Pretty chill place to watch the game. We went to catch the Jets play and they loss but that's besides the point. Loved that fans of a bunch of other teams where there cheering their team on. It was a fun atmosphere on a Sunday afternoon.

Great service. Great chicken pot pie homemade. Ny strip, best flavored steak. Love the $2 martini! Mango is great. Also love the shrimp scampi. Large portions and worth every bite! The prime rib special is usually tasty. But you get what you pay for, not a big portion, but it's under $10 still a great value. Our new go to!

This place is a gem! The staff is down to earth and friendly and the chef makes and creates some of the best menu items! It changes daily so you have to either call or check out their Facebook page if you want to know the daily specials ahead of time. I highly recommend their shepherds pie, open faced Meat loaf sandwich, pig wings, and grown up ham and cheese with tomato basil soup...but then again anything I've ever tried here is delicious! 
The only downside is that you may have to wait a while to get a table if you go on or near the weekend especially after 6:00pm... 
Last Thursday we attempted to eat there and it was about a 45 min wait.  Would I say it's worth it? Absolutely.

Have been to Crowley's, quite a few times, and every time I never walk away unsatisfied. For me, this is like a slight spin on pub/ all american food. When I am stomped on where to take a picky eater, who likes to eat, this is my first choice. They even have a good menu for kids.

The service, consistently is pleasant. Although the servers look rushed, I have never felt I am being rushed for an order. Everyone is very helpful, and checks on you routinely about how you are enjoying your meal. There is also a nice selection of beers and ciders.

First, I have to start by saying that whatever you do, you have to do yourself the favor and order the Reuben Egg Rolls. This is hands down these best starter. It is so much of what is good about a Reuben with melted cheese, meat, and cabbage. This has never disappointed anyone I have introduced to it. If you are looking for comfort food, the chicken pot pie is next. This does not have a biscuit based crust, but instead, mashed potatoes. It is filled as traditional pot pies are, with carrots, celery, and peas, and offers nice lump piece of chicken breast. 

If you are looking for a burger, they will more than satisfy that need, as well. Honestly, I have never had anyone order something they haven't thoroughly enjoyed. This is definitely a place that you repeat going to. Do yourself a favor, and go.

We were in town on vacation and had just finished touring the National Automobile Museum when I asked at the gift shop for a lunch recommendation. We were referred to Bertha Miranda's. I am so glad! The chips and salsa were great. The entrees were amazing. My husband said it was the best Mexican rice he's ever tasted. I'd have to agree. The rice and beans were tasty. I got a plate with a chicken enchilada and a shredded beef taco and he got the machaca. Delicious! Seek out this restaurant and definitely stop by if you've visited the auto museum.

We stopped for Sunday brunch and second time for Sunday dinner. Fresh Harvest has so many choices. There is a great selection different kind of foods available for everyone, even those on a special diet. It would be difficult to leave hungry. Delicious food at a fantastic price, all served in a friendly atmosphere. The service is good too.  I would definitely return again.

Wonderful food!! I have ordered just about everything on the menu and have not had a bad meal. This is my brother's preferred take out when he comes home for college breaks.
Restaurant is clean, and the menu is clear and fun to look at! 
Great spot for Vietnamese food!
Try the Vietnamese egg rolls!!
Food was excellent, but the server MCCoy was the best part of our experience. He was engaged, attentive and took our annoying orders with grace and ease. 6/5

This place is incredible. Such a great tasting healthy fresh option for lunch - my favorite is building my own bowl. Everything is amazing and I love the dressings. Not much to say other than I love it. Definitely go :)

I've been here twice in the past couple weeks, and tried a few different things. My thoughts:

Appetizer: I tried the buffalo wings. These were pretty good. The sauce tasted good, the wings were plump and juicy, and there were good quantities of everything.

Main: I tried the pizza with double pepperoni. It was also relatively good; there was plenty of pepperoni and the pizza itself was cooked and seasoned well. 

Main: I also tried the chicken parmesan. Unfortunately, the chicken was very tough and dry. This dish was a lot harder to eat than the other things I have tried here. I like a good chicken parm, but this was one of the poorer attempts at that dish that I've had in the city.

Dessert: they have a few containers of ice creams, (in fact, their menu is in general very large), so I tried a cup of cookies 'n cream. It was good, although not as much as a specialist place like Ben and Jerry's.

Price: Reasonable for what was offered.

Service: Good. They let me switch the TV channel when my show came on, which was very nice of them.

Overall, this is a decent restaurant. I would have given it four stars except for the bad chicken parmesan. As a place for just pizza and wings, it's probably one of the better offerings in the neighborhood.

Food: The Mac & Cheese is a must try. My mom got the Pork Mac & Cheese and it was truly spectacular. Cheesy with a sweet barbecue that was so good I ate the leftovers for breakfast. I had the roast beef po boy which was good and had generous portions, but reminded me of a French Dip sandwich. My sister got the Florentine Mac which came in a white cheese sauce instead and was much lighter, but still tastier, than the Pork Mac. 

Venue: Located on Frenchmen street, this is one of the few full service sit down restaurants in the area. They DO accept credit cards which isn't the case for all establishments in the area. They had live music playing when we were there which was a bit loud, but still enjoyable.

It's all about the mushroom soup with a fresh slice of bread and butter. Thick and hearty before an afternoon at Longwood Gardens is just the ticket. A flight of beer is a fun way to try four different types, but steer clear of the meatloaf sandwich (with poutine sauce) and salads that look as unappealing as they taste.

Omg delish. Reading the menu started the journey - so much to choose from and the next thing sounds better than the last. I finally settled on a hot pastrami sandwich which was tender and juicy on super soft rye and spicy mustard. Slap yo mama good!! My friend had a montecristo sandwich with French toast bread. Delectable and buttery. Yum. And the people working were just as awesome. Thanks Yelp for another awesome surprise. Can't wait to go back!!
This review is for the chicken tender: it's more to the salty side. The batter is crunchy but not hard. It's greasy though. When I heated up in the oven I could see some grease on the pan

Came on a whim looking for vegan options. Enjoyed what we got. Mostly wraps, burrito and bowl type offerings. Weather outside was nice so we sat in the outdoor seating. Would have been more comfortable on level ground but it is what it is. I'll go back again no doubt!!

Still a great place on the northside whether for lunch, dinner, or special events.  Last couple of visits during the pandemic have been great experiences due to service.  Only a couple mishaps due to a fatty piece of steak (ribeye special one night) and an okay-ish pork chop.  

My favorite item is still the prime rib sandwich.  And H&Z has some of the best salads you can find. I'm sticking to the Oven Roasted Beet Salad these days.  If you actually have room after downing cocktails and those amazing rolls, the bourbon bread pudding is one of the best!

Was very hungry having missed lunch so i stopped in for 2 sicilian slices.  They were heated up just a minute with a little portobellos and a little more cheese so they stick.  I was shocked.  They were absolutely burned all the way from the bottom. Super charred.  Nothing else was in the oven? Maybe too hot.  I returned them to get a replacement.  Meanwhile the smoke detectors started going off.  It took a few minutes of the loud noise but they admitted the ovens too hot.  They forgot to put the exhaust fans on.  Not sure what i should pay for this experience, but they opted to not charge given the experience.  What happens with more customers than me?  Oh and the staff all sat down with lunch bags.  Guess they dont eat what they serve.  As a concerned trappe resident,i will skip this joint.  MJC

We loved all the Indian food here. My friend dining with us spent two months in India, and she also said it was excellent. I was not so impressed by the Thai dish we tried but it was not bad at all. The Indian food was just the real stand-out for us. The service was also good. So happy we found a nice place for Indian in this area!

Just a block away from the craziness of Bourbon St. with better prices and service. We were there on Thursday night and sat on the upstairs balcony. So sorry I do t remember the girl's name who waited on us but she made our night with great service. She said she hadn't even been there that long when we complimented on knowing the menu and what didn't contain pork. The music was great and the food was top notch. We got to sample a bunch of local favorites.

Mmmm.. I can tell if a pizza is from Sal's or not just after one taste.  They have one of the best marinara sauces around. Bet!  And the people, everybody is always friendly and chatting it up with you when you come in. I cant always understand what they are saying but we both smile and never had any issues with them. I really like it because it's a true pizza restaurant unlike all the chain stores that just focus on delivery and don't really have a dining area. Sal's will sell you a slice or an XXLarge pizza, whatever you want.  Plus, you can grab a beer with it and chill in the dining room watching TV. Where else you gona have a $10 lunch buffet with everything from pizza to fajitas. Mmm. Shit! I'm going to Sal's right now. That's how good it is.

I just finished eating a small Canadian bacon & garlic pizza and was so impressed, I figured I would write this review. The pizza was delicious and the ingredients were fresh. The garlic was chopped up small enough so it covered each bite.

The antipasto salad was great as everything was shredded. Even the lettuce & ham were chopped.

We also ordered the meatballs. The meat itself was cooked perfectly and the sauce had a nice kick to it.

The guy running the place came out with a water dish that he had created from a empty container, for our dog. Yes, the outdoor seating is dog friendly here!

Petra has become my "it's 3am and I'm starving" go-to spot. As far as I know, they have the latest hours of any other restaurant in the area. If they were closer to my job, I'd check them out during normal waking hours. I'm a big fan of their shawarma and I recently snagged a piece of a friend's lamb kabob - it was amazing! I've heard good things about the gyros, so that's next on my list. The pita bread is very soft and their portions are large enough to have leftovers. Petra is a great find for Mass Ave, as most of the other restaurants are more American-style cuisine. Service is fast, though the two guys who operate the place seem to be short on words (not that I'm complaining). Since my first visit I've been telling everyone I know to check them out, and now that includes you!

If you need something to do on a Friday night, visit La Maison. 

The funky band made me wanna jump on stage and dance with them. There is a cover charge *cringe but worth it. The guy on the drums...looks like Lil Wayne but plays the drums like Travis Barker. Unbelievable!!! The hype man is also pretty entertaining. 

Take a trip to La Maison before 2012!!

I love this place! I've been coming here since the early 70's.  Once in a while a miss but for the most part they are spot on. Solid good eats and nice kids at the window.  Only consist drawback is iced tea,  Bad!

My friend and i stumbled upon this place while exploring St Pete. Needless to say, we were very disappointed. My friend and i both work and have worked in many restaurants that specialize in seafood. I myself am from Maryland & have lived in Florida for the past 4 years. I ordered the shrimp dinner and requested it grilled. I had a choice of two sides so i chose the veggie of the day which was broccoli and then French fries. When my order came, I'm not lying when i say the shrimp was tiny & Luke warm. It was not grilled at all. It was exactly like the frozen shrimp you buy at Walmart that you put in shrimp salad. They were that small. My broccoli was cold & also frozen as well. I could tell because the color was very pale green and it was cut in a way that made it look mass produced and frozen. The french fries were standard restaurant quality fries that are quickly thrown in the fryer. Again, luke warm. They wanted $15 for this meal... All in all very disappointed.
 Our server was great and very sweet. The service was fine however i felt compelled to save people from coming here and getting ultimately disappointed with this seafood place.

The smells coming from this place make it hard not to order everything on the menu. I enjoyed my bowl of ropa  veija (shredded beef) with black beans, rice and tostones. The portions were generous and the ingredients were fresh. 

They also have red and white sangria, the red was delicious but a little too sweet for me.  Do yourself a favor and order the Salchipapa, I'll definitely be coming back for more of those.

Get to know your neighbors.

I really wanted to like this place.  I love Mexican food, especially well done tacos with homemade tortillas.  However, the experience just wasn't very inviting.  The service was great and the food was ok, but the tables are so closely placed to one another. 
 
My girl and I sat down at what would be a four top.  They parted the two top tables by about six inches.  We watched as they attempted to sit another couple and they refused.  They finally were able to sit another party of two, and we were literally elbow to elbbow.  We could partake in their conversation and visa versa.  On top of this was loud music and hipsters as far as the eye could see.    

The food was ok, but it is not worth another visit for me.  Give the patrons some breathing room.

This place is exactly what you want in a bar.  Great food, and an amazing beer list.  Really, these guys are experts when recommending a great beer to fit your palate.  If your grabbing a bite, the Saint Lucifer Burger is other worldly. They use locally sourced beef and produce for this creation.  Back to the St. Lucifer, it's actually a habanero spice / table condiment made by some guys in the area.  Saw it once in a restaurant in Philadelphia.  Stuff is legit.

I had to rate it one star.. but y'all should pay me $5 cover charge so I can make it ZERO stars. WHO CHARGES A COVER CHARGE?!? This location does. THIS LOCATION. FIVE DOLLAR COVER CHARGE. Nah I'm already paying for water down drinks and half *ss games that didn't even work! Plus the employees are rude! Almost had to backhand somebodies mother. I'm usually not this mean.. but F*ck this place!

Gave it 2 tries.  The first time they shorted me a quarter pounder and the second time we ordered through the app and they lost the order. The manager, Corina, acted like it was our fault and was very rude.  Never eat there again...
Fantastic Tapas and margaritas.

Decided to finally try this bbq! I was NOT disappointed. Service was phenomenal and the food was even better. We ordered the 4-meat dinner; pulled pork, pulled chicken, brisket and ribs, BBQ baked beans, cole slaw, and mac n cheese. We loved it so much, we decided to order bulk pulled pork and pulled chicken and sides for gender reveal party this weekend! Thank you for an outstanding experience.
Food was average nothing special, the female staff was ok but the male guy delivering food just tossed it on the table with no care.

Love this place. Service is top notch. Everyone loved their food. Onion rings, grilled cheese, salad, burger, and parm chicken on fries were ordered at our table and everyone loved. We were at the hut but weren't happy about the food options. So glad we decided to go upstairs.

Really delicious pizza. Thin crust New York style. We had the florentine which was so good - anything with ricotta, garlic, and spinach has my vote. The supreme was also amazing - had like 8 different types of meat on it and veggies.  It'll definitely be our new go to place for delivery. So much better than a chain.

This is as generic as it gets without actually being a chain store.
Service was ok.
The chips were good, the salsa just ok.
The Nachos grande with chili con carne were pretty bland, with cheap tasteless cheese.
The chimichanga with pork and tomatillo sauce was banal with nothing special about it.
They asked for 2.5$ for a table spoon of tasteless, mushy guacamole. 

This place tastes like it serves TV dinner mexican food.

We ordered food through door dash. It showed up with all the containers smashed, which wasn't a good sign from the start. They forgot our cheese dip, called and got 'credit' which is great. But we are from out of town and are here for a hospital stay. The elote was tragic...took one bite and couldn't muster another. Also got arroz con pollo, but it looked like they had gone to Walmart and grabbed a vegetable medley with broccoli, cauliflower, carrots, and just huge veggies and tossed it in...won't be back
Well Done excellent hot beef good portion a excellent value. Friendly people who know good food!

A four star steakhouse by Sarah's standards is one you at least come back to. Plus, they are famous for their shrimp cocktail with sinus clearing cocktail sauce. Seriously, this stuff is the devil's dirt. Someone even told us they think it's made with wasabi it's so intense, but I promise you it's not. 

SO many delightful surprises during this meal, like when waiter thought I wanted Topo Chico without the tequila in it because I asked "what is Topo Chico?" while perusing the cocktail menu. No guy, I definitely want the tequila. He didn't speak very great English to be fair, but that led to some of the delightful surprises. Like another thing! When he asked if I wanted to upgrade my side from tomato juice or beans (I think? Who pairs that with steak?) for something "lobster," and I assumed I was getting a lobster tail with my steak but no, it was lobster bisque. IMO, this is too heavy to bring out before someone devours a $50+ steak. Another star bites the dust, you know what I'm saying?

HOWEVER, there were Parmesan cheese crisps in the bread basket and peppercorn in my butter. This was the type of butter that made me stop and say, "I feel so bad for vegans," and the type of Parmesan cheese crisps that forced me to eat all of them without Future Husband even getting a taste of one. Yes, these crisps literally said to me, "Sarah eat us all right now." The wedge salad was probably one of the best wedge salads I've ever had. In fact, I liked it (plus the cheese crisps) more than I liked the "world famous" shrimp cocktail. If you're going to boast about an appetizer, make sure it's good and that the presentation ensures guests that there is, in fact, shrimp underneath that cocktail sauce. (There were only 4 so waiter asked us if we wanted two orders of the shrimp cocktail). Dude, it's really not that good. I would've paid for two orders of the Parmesan cheese crisps though.

We got the creamed spinach side because Future Husband always wants that as a side at the steakhouse and I said OK because I checked Yelp and saw that it came with cheese flakes on top (yes! More parm!) but later when we were gnawing on our leftover steaks cold in the hotel room, I couldn't stand the thought of putting that spinach in my mouth. I ate my leftover steak with pretzels as a side. 

The green beans with brown butter cashew sauce came with my meal and they were quite a disappointment. Well, nothing with cashews is a disappointment, but don't you expect a brown butter cashew sauce to cover your buttery beans and make them mushy and sweet like a Thanksgiving side dish? No, these were just thin, French cut green beans blanched and then painted with a tbsp of oil (seriously didn't even taste like butter) and topped with some crushed cashews. I ate them all, because she likes her veggies, but it's probably just because we (I) ran out of the Parmesan cheese crisps.
Love the burritos and the friendly service here. Food cooked to order and fresh no fast food here!

Don't let the looks fool you. They put their money into the food. Great place to talk and graze. Friendly, expedient staff. Made great menu suggestions.  Try it if you want something besides fried American food
Great happy hour prices ! Good spot to go watch any type of sports games . Chip and salsa bar
Had be fantastic meal with the family the other night. The food was great and the wait staff was fantastic. It is now the top of my list for Italian cuisine.

Excellent service from the moment we walked in. Excellent small place with character. Awesome menu. I had the biscuits and gravy and it was extremely delicious. Wife had the grilled cheese and was very happy with it.

Excellent place to go for breakfast anytime.

THE BEST FRIED PICKLES I HAVE EVER HAD!!! No clue what they put in the batter but I loved it.  The slaw I wasn't to crazy about but that's because I am from Jersey and we have mayo in ours but my boyfriend loved it.  The burger was HUGE!!!  The staff was amazing!  I can't wait to go back next year.

I really enjoyed the music. As far as the food. The humus was amazing. The salad with goat cheese, strawberries and pecans was weak. Pretty much all lettuce. Found a few pecans and cheese sitting at the bottom.

Never again! I went here against my better judgment at lunch today b/ it was expedient and I was hoping to keep it uncomplicated. BIG MISTAKE!
I wound up paying for the experience. Seated at a table for two against the wall (no problem) we immediately sensed that all was not right. There was an ongoing frenzy, wait staff running, hastily delivered "greetings", repeated messages-"that comes with dressing on the side, etc"-I gave the waitress my choice the first time she told me that. Lots of excuses, "we didn't know about all these large parties", "there are only 4 of us here" yadda yadda. A long delay in receiving our order  and I finally told my friend, 'if the food doesn't come in the next 5 minutes, I'm leaving a few bucks on the table and leaving.." So lunch arrived within that time  frame but it might have been better had it not. Oh, yes, before I continue- "Italian" restaurant, right? So, I ask the waitress if any of the pasta is fresh and she says "as fresh as the day is ." No understanding of "fresh" vs. dried and GUESS WHAT! they do not offer one fresh pasta dish.  B.S!!
Okay, Im gonna take a breath here.
While we're waiting for the lunch, we noticed lots of things about the ambience, in addition to the chaos all about us: There are e.g  food boogers on the wall next to us (I hope they were food) and the carpeting is filthy and old.  I'll bet not one penny has  gone into real renovation of that space for years-just a few boring decor changes. PLEASE! How about a fresh coat of paint for goodness sake!
Fettucine Alfredo (my friend's choice) arrived gummy and dry. Yech.
Salmon cakes-the salad part was fine but the cakes were so uninspired, so blah, so lackinig in seasoning, I ate a few bites and left the rest. Neither of us felt like sending our food back and having to go through that process again- we just gave up and got out. BTW I feel I must mention the Bread? Must be the cheapest "italian" bread one can buy-a miserable loaf. How insulting to Italians to call this an Italian restaurant.

Bottom Line: if you want authentic Italian food, go to Brooklyn N.Y. or best of all, save your money and go to Italy. I give up on even passing Italian food here in Tucson.

Ciao

P.S. Just reviewd my credit card statement and see that LB added $0.50 to my tip, which under the circumstances was a decent tip. I won't contest it for the small discrepancy but it's another bad business act.
Great venue, scrumptious and the best classic Italian food!!!
The bbq and hot pot are so overpriced for the quality of food. Go spend the same amount at a place like Morimoto or Fogo De Chao and get high quality ingredients prepared for you by a chef.

I used to go to the Crepe truck while I was at Temple... I always went with the pizza crepe.  How could you go wrong pepperoni, spinach, broccoli, mushrooms, yum! I miss this place. I might just have to stop by soon! I've still never tried a sweet crepe, they all sound so good!

I had never been to Sawasdee before, but the guy I'm dating swears by their food, so we checked it out last week. It's an intimate and casual place. Quiet and tucked away inside a strip mall. The menu seems rather large. 

I ordered the Pad Thai, Crab Rangoon, and hot and sour soup. All three were delicious! The Crab Rangoon is a large portion, plenty for 3-4 people to share, and more crabby than most I have had with a really good side sauce. The Pad Thai could have been shared between two people as well, but I had yummy leftovers instead. I ordered mine with shrimp, which adds to the cost, but didn't really seem worth it. There were maybe five shrimp in what was otherwise a massive plate of food. The most interesting thing was the the hot and sour soup. It is very good but very different from anywhere else I have had it. Super tangy and flavorful. 

Our waiter was attentive in making sure we always had a full glass of water, but he wasn't over so much that it felt intrusive. He was polite and helpful with suggestions when I was trying to decide what to order. 

I'll definitely return, and this time with a bigger appetite!

It was my last night in Santa Barbara, and I was looking for a place to kill some time before my plane left.  I walked all around trying to pick a place that had outdoor seating, nachos, and beer.  I discovered this place, and thought..."surely, they're going to have great nachos."  I even asked how they made them...but I was wrong.

The service was pretty lame.  I was there on 2 for 1 drink special for happy hour, and they brought me two beers at the same time.  The nachos were so below mediocre that I didn't even finish them.  (And I LOVE nachos.)  

The reason I give this place three stars is because they had Pacifico on draft and outdoor seating...and because my total bill came to $10.

When I first found out that I was spending a week working in the Warehouse District I was disappointed that I wouldn't have time to get to my favorite NOLA spots. Turns out it is just an opportunity to find some NEW FAVORITES! Lüke is definitely that. This was an awesome meal in a wonderful setting with top flight service. Shout out to our server Kenneth! 

Here's the long story. When I took the included photo my dining partner knocked his Martini to the floor shattering the glass and causing a minor scene. The waitstaff handled it perfectly. Then I said to Dan... here is the test... is this a good restaurant or a great one? Kennth had replaced the Martini within 3 minutes! That is a great restaurant. As he placed it on the table he said, "Usually when this happens the second one comes in a sip cup!" That's FUNNY!!  The oysters were perfect both raw and stuffed. My etoufee was spot on and i loved it served over pasta. This was a great night at a GREAT restaurant.

Have lived in the area for 8+ years and Tims has always been our go to for donuts. I've tried them all too (north side and dowtown) and Tims is by far the best. None compare no matter what anyone else says (including Indys most famous donut place).

Get there early (like 6am) for the best selection. Staff is super friendly and it's easy in and easy out. Their Apple Fritters are AMAZING.

Tucked into a small Harahan strip  is a very good restaurant offering genuinely tasty smoked meats.  The restaurant is a family venture that is very friendly and efficient.  Pricing is fair.  We ordered Pulled Pork, Brisket, and Ribs.  The pulled pork was flavorful and you have the choice of five sauces to add to your meats.   The brisket was thickly sliced, very tender, and moist.  It seemed to be lightly seasoned with salt and pepper during the smoke and it had a smoke ring.  The pork ribs were very tender to the fall off the bone stage.  They had a nice sweet glaze and were delicious.
The restaurant offers six different sides of which we tried the baked beans and Brussel sprouts. The beans were sweet and good.  The brussel sprouts would be better with some smoked meat flavor maybe from some smoked meat debris, but they were ok.
The desserts were blueberry or peach cobbler.  Both were excellent.
This is easily one of the best smoke meat restaurants in south Louisiana.   Recommended.

Love this place! I tried my first poké here and have been going at least once a month. Staff is super friendly and have been consistent with the portions & presentation. Highly recommend trying it out! GroupOn usually has sweet deals for this place too; helps out with saving some $$.

Good food with not so good service. While it should be noted that it was a holiday and they were pretty busy, the operations were very much out of whack and employee moral seemed low. The hostess appeared new to the business and unsure about how the phone worked when we called to confirm the reservation. Her lack of experience became more apparent when she struggled to check us in and find us a table. The manager while slightly overwhelmed did take time to find our server when know one else could. And the staff was nice enough to try and serve us our neighboring tables appetizers and then again their main dishes. Then shrimp and grits were really good, though.
Great food, a little more than the chains $, but better quality. Mostly a take out place, not really set up to dine in comfortably.

My boyfriend and I were visiting SB and went here for a date night on a Saturday. When we arrived at 8.50 for our 9 pm reservation the place was packed! The bar was absolutely slammed. We waited there for ten mins before getting our table and had no chance of being waited on but no worries we were about to sit. We had a great table inside which I requested since it was chilly out. Our waiter came over right away. We ordered our drinks then a bit later our food. When our first course arrived our drinks still hadn't which we pointed out to the waiter. He apologized because the bar had been so backed up and rushed to get the drinks over, which was appreciated. The manager even came over at some point and apologized for the drink wait and comped our bill for them. It was a great gesture. Now for the food: Apps- squash blossoms- were an absolute hit 10/10, meat charcuterie plate- was also great high end meats. Mains- lobster pasta- maybe one of the best pastas I've EVER had. It's that good. Must order! Mussels and clams- good but a hard act to follow after the lobster pasta. The waiter promptly got over our subsequent drinks and they even offered dessert on the house! We got ricotta fritters and thought they were great! Overall excellent experience. It's really crowded on Saturday night but hey it's the weekend!

I have wanted to try this place a bunch of times, but because of their hours I never made it down. I was a bit worried this would be yet another "trendy, hipster ridden, overrated" type of place that seems to be the common theme for most restaurants popping up in the valley. They make honest good food without being smug. My wife got the turkey and brie that several people spoke so highly of in the reviews and I got the reuben. Both were fantastic. The reuben isn't a traditional reuben with sauerkraut, but still hits all of the right notes and is perfectly balanced in my opinion. Not too heavy, not soggy, not dry. Yet still enough savory to make it satisfying like a reuben should be and a very good twist on what you normally expect a reuben to be. We also tried their simple side salad and a cup of tomato soup. Both were good, but outshined by the comparatively awesome sandwiches. We also tried basil lemonade and grapefruit rosemary soda, both were good. Portion sizes we're not small but not obscene. I can eat a fair amount and I was satisfied. Pricing is about right in my opinion. Service was friendly, they were packed so we had a small wait but they were quick to get our food. Highly recommended if you can make it out to try.

What a great little gem to find nestled across from a shopping center on 19. Coming from NYC, it was super cool to see so many awesome New York pictures and items! Everyone here is really nice and helpful- our server was very attentive and sweet.
The food was pretty good. The mussels were decent (I got them in the red sauce)... A bit dried out / overcooked , but the tomato sauce was good. The "knuckle sandwich" wasn't that great... I thought it would be pink roast beef but it was cooked all the way through ... It was ok. 
The star of the show was the flatbread! We got the peto one with cheeses and spinach and we added shrimp. OMG amazing. Can't wait to order that again!
The Brooklyn bakery attached to lucky dill has so many beautiful cakes and pastries! I will have to try some next time I come in for sure.

Our marching band was visiting St. Louis for a Bands of America competition.  We contacted a couple of BBQ restaurants ahead of time and Bandana's jumped at the chance to serve us.  They agreed to close down the restaurant over a Saturday lunch hour to serve all 140 of us!  The food was so good and the service was amazing.  A huge shout out to John, the Manager, for running a great restaurant and having such good staff on hand to make our day even better!   Thank you!
The "long board" rocks! Look forward to it on Saturday nights. Fast good food w/o the processed food taste!

It's a great place for a lot of reasons!  Lively but not loud atmosphere. Charming friendly host. (said his name is Antonio Bandaras) and he was fun and funny!! 

Beautiful array of very fresh fish. Lots of great combos of long rolls and hand rolls in addition to the usual fare. Excellent service and friendly, fast sushi chefs. No waiting. Very easy parking. Smiling, friendly servers who were attentive at the sushi bar. We will definitely return. We rate sushi restaurants with either a shark bite (bad) or Japanese good luck kitty. This place gets a kitty!!

The wife and I got in really late to Glen Mills on a Friday. We found out that Inge close early in the town. Blue Fin was open so we tried it out. They had only a few patrons left when we got there and we closed the place up. Even though we were last, nobody rushed us at any point! So the service was top notch.

For the food... We had a few appetizers and some rolls. We had spicy edamame... Awesome... Rock shrimp... Awesome. I know the wife wanted to go to pf changs and get chicken lettuce wraps. I overruled and chose Blue Fin. Amazingly enough... They had chicken lettuce wraps... And she liked them better than pf chang's! I couldn't believe it! They didn't taste as prefabricated as pf changs... Again awesome ! The rolls were great too... And it's BYOB! Overall ... Awesome! Will definitely return if we are in town!

Great place to get fast food that's actually worth the money you pay for it.  Their milkshakes are great and their tenders are the best.  I recommend the Buffalo Bleu chicken sandwich, simple and tasty.  Good fries too.  It's a clean restaurant with friendly fast service and they have the soda fountain with the touch screen where you can get like a billion different drink combos.  Perfect spot for a quick easy meal.

WARNING: These cookies are addicting. I'm slightly embarrassed to admit I have basically every flavor. My favorites are the chocolate chip walnut, harvest and the wilbur peanut butter. They are always soft and delicious. Perfect for when you are looking for a little treat.

Quick stop for dinner to go. Sweetie likes them, and you know what, so do I. Good sandwiches, good service. Prices are a little high, but for the quality it is almost worth it..

She got a cheesesteak and fries, and liked it. I tried the chicken teriyaki and some cheese bread. The sandwich was great- tender, tasty chicken, and lots of it, on good bread. The cheese bread was better than expected, just based on cheese bread at pizza joints, etc. Same good bread, and real cheese. The lemonade is pretty good. Service here was friendly and fast (though there is of course a wait while they make the sandwiches.)

Best pizza in town.

Amazing crust light flavors and very well baked. 

I will have to try other things from the menu.

We had a great time here.  In fact, we didn't get our tickets at the call window since it was our first time and totally forgot.  Once we got to the check in, one of the employees walked us back and then right back up front again to a table.  We were served quickly and the show was super funny.

The Mud House should get ten stars!! Found this gem through other reviews on Yelp and we stopped here while driving back to Wisconsin which is home. Since the few days we've been home, I've been thinking NON STOP about this place as no coffee shops in the Milwaukee area comes close! 
Outstanding food! I had a bite of my spouse's breakfast burrito and I ordered the granola which had greek yogurt and the perfect amount of honey drizzled on it. Extremely friendly and non pretentious service and the lavender mocha has set the bar for all future mochas I will consume along with the Gibraltar! 
Any time we drive through the St. Louis area, it will be mandatory to stop at the Mud House!
Loved the bathroom decorated with board games!

I really like their food, I have eaten at good ones and bad ones, but this location is one of the better ones in the chain.  I usually go there when I want a huge burrito, without a Baja Fresh around this is what I am stuck with, no complaints here.

You walk in and hear, "Welcome to Moe's" that kind of sets me at ease.  The staff is super friendly, accommodating specialized tastes and also will let you know if something contains beef for all of those vegetarians out there, which my mother in law is.

I usually get my usual home wrecker, but somethings I would change if I had my choice.  For example the olives are way too salty for their menu and sometimes the chips taste like they have expired.  When you are in a slim margin business which all restaurants of this type are in I will go back over and over again.

I hope they do not get decimated by the five guys which just opened next door.

Far too expensive for average food and beer.  Wife and I each had a Boston Lager burger.  "Samuel Adams Boston Lager beer-braised mushrooms"...what a joke...we had to look real hard to find three mushroom slices each.  Plus, although we had to wait too long for the burgers, they were not even hot, and were waaay over-cooked. Fries are anemic.  So, 2 burgers, two beers for $38...then add tip (server was ok).  $45 for two people to eat.  You can get much better food for a lot less.

Every dish was delicious. Highly recommend this place. Short Rib, fried game hen, bone marrow, deviled eggs, filthy fries, brussel sprouts, grilled Caesar, caprese salad, and croissant bread pudding waffle. Outstanding!!!!

I ordered a Chelada. I had to describe to the bartender how to make it. It's not difficult. He was unable or too lazy to follow my instructions. He'll not be going to the Chelada World Championships anytime soon. You'd think that a bartender at a Mexican joint would know how to make something as simple as a Chelada. 

I witnessed the same bartender drop a glass while stocking glasses, pick it up off the floor and proceed to put it on the shelf with the clean glassware.

This is what you're up against.

This is my favorite wing place, but I have to say the service here at this new location is HORRIBLE.  The staff is very friendly, but it just seem like they have very limited training.  You constantly have to tell them everything you need, even the obvious.  And the food comes out VERY SLOW.  

I was very excited for this new location on the westbank, but looks like I will just be coming back here for to-go.  If you plan to dine in, you have been warned.

Trash dirty inside as they make the pizzas.... pizza horrible sauce is not good...not good quality at all...the wings were where the cold sodas and that a no no...not the best area to eat but just go down the street to the Vietnamese spot....thats good food

Good food, if they would ever straighten their act out. The last three times I ordered online they claim I didn't. I have to show them the email, then they get real apologetic and furiously make the sandwiches. I even gave them 20 minutes to make then, then I have to sit in here and wait another 20 while they make them.
Fantastic mole.  This is real mexican food.  I can't wait to go back to try more of the menu.
Had the Honey BBQ Burger ... maybe the best burger I've ever had.  Period.  Jamie, our waitress was outstanding.  Definitely recommend this place!

I came on a night that they didn't have a buffet because of a party starting soon. Nevertheless, I had a good experience! I've eaten Indian food in many places (including difference countries) and this place might be my new Philly favorite. My friend and I had samosas and both thought they were meh. The sauces that came along with them also lacked flavor. The entrees however were AMAZING! I had the chicken tikki masala and my friend had a vegetarian dish of mixed vegetables. The naan was standard. I can't be sure which one she got, but I know it's one that specifically doesn't have a creamed based sauce.

The food here is absolutely wonderful! I have deducted two stars for the small size of the place, which results in a lengthy wait. My friends and I love to go to brunch on Sunday mornings, but the over an hour and a half wait for the  6 of us (plus the lack of parking in the area) deters us from going very often. I would love to try every item on the menu!  The lemon donuts they bring to the table are amazing!  Would love to see another location open with a larger dining area and much better parking options!

Update March 2016:  Found out that the donuts I mentioned in my original review are not something they typically bring to the table for free and had probably been brought out due to the super lengthy amount of time we'd had to wait when we were there.  This time, for 2 people we "only" had to wait for 50 minutes at 11 am on a Sunday because we were seated at a 4 top with 2 people we didn't know.  Awkward!  Plus we were really wanting mimosas and they were out of orange juice - seriously?  How difficult could it be to make or go get more?
Dickey's is ok. The food is pretty good but really greasy. The prices are very expensive. Dickey's was really dirty when I went. The floors were really sticky. I do not recommend this place!
The Sampler is $20 but two people can easily split it and have a great taste of NOLA cuisine. Bartender was super nice. Great atmosphere!!  Also, the Gumbalaya is really good!!!

white trash hash. so good!

Really busy during brunch-but worth the wait. They also have 2 for 1 drinks during brunch!

DO NOT GO HERE!!!   We arrived around 8:23pm. At first it seemed promising. We waited about 10 minutes for our waitress to come give us our menus or take our drink order. We ordered 2 sprites and 2 cokes. It took about 20 minutes for our drinks to arrive. At this point we were getting annoyed, but we were still trying to give them a chance. She finally took our order and we waited. We also ordered calamari for an appetizer and waited for about 20 minutes. It arrived and was rubbery and very untasteful. After awhile we realized that everyone else had dinner rolls and we did not. We were finally given some after about 40 minutes of arriving. Also our meals were supposed to come with a salad. We waited and waited and still never received our salads until we finally asked for them. I ran out of drink several times. I asked her for some more sprite and she said she would get that right away and after about 10 minutes I still had no drink. Finally a nice young man filled my sprite for me even though he wasn't our server. After close to an hour our food arrived. It looked promising at first. It had a very beautiful presentation. But... after trying my food, which was just a simple lasagna I then realized it wasn't that impressive. We arrived at 8:23pm and finally left about 9:53. The food was overpriced and not impressive

Just finished eating at Harvest. Great experience!  Great local craft beers on tap. Wait staff and kitchen was able to handle a party of 15. Service was very attentive. They asked about nut allergy concerns. Food was fantastic. Seasonal specials are always a favorite. Salmon was delicious. I liked that they offered healthy options and nutrition information on the menu. I would recommend Harvest.

My girlfriends and I went on Tuesday night. We got there at 5:15 pm so there was no wait. 

We ordered the following:
Flash fried spinach - extremely greasy. Turned my stomach.
Fish sandwich - outer coating was good. The fish was mushy.
Chicken pot pie - it's OK. Good hunks of chicken, the crust was flaky, but very few vegetables. Save your $ and buy Marie Callendar's - it is way better.  
Fried chicken dinner - Chicken was very good. Crispy outside, juicy inside. The green beans were bland. 

The service was very good. But, bring a sweater if you go. It was really cold in the restaurant.

Taco Tuesday night dinner and the place was a mess. More than a half hour wait and we still didn't get seated. Then came the bad news people couldn't sit at the bar because it was too hot and worse of all complaining and leaving because the service was too slow. So sad because we were here once before on a Saturday night, granted the place was empty but the service was good and so was the food. Very disappointed!

PlantPure is an amazing lunch spot for those who work, live, or play in the Gayborhood/Market East neighborhoods. Expect to pay anywhere from $7-12 depending on item. But don't worry -- portions are HUGE! I'm not a big fan or go out of my way for oil free foods, but this hit the spot and didn't leave that tired full feeling -- or as some call it -- food coma.

Vegan soft serve is also available! That automatically grants 5 stars for me, as there aren't ample vegan ice cream sources in the vicinity. Delicious and totally recommended from this vegan!

The restaurant was almost empty when we arrived. We were seated right away. We ordered and it started to fill quickly. A very loud group was seated next to us when there was several other areas where they could have been seated. I complained about the ice tea not tasting right. The server took it away and never brought a return drink. I ended up paying for something that tasted bad. It was never replaced or taken off the bill.Didn't notice until I had left the restaurant, ..NOT Happy...

We went Sunday afternoon around 3ish. We were the first ones there. No line, no wait. Then, ppl started showing up. The place did not disappointed! We picked the Drunken noodles, Similan noodles, a plate for our kids (forgot what's called, just have a pic), order of sticky rice. It was Delicious!!! Great service. Clean place. We will go back again to try something different. Their Instagram page have a bunch of pictures of the dishes. That helped us choose our dinner.

Typical decent brewery with a well-known name. Nothing really stood out, except for the quality and variety of brews they have. Great price/quantity for the flight if you want to try multiple. Victory is one of my favorite brewing companies. The food is good, especially the fried pickles. Waitstaff is pretty friendly. Large space. Side take-out beer area where you can get booze to go. Specials around. 

Rating: 7/10
Pros: BEER!!! Good variety and quality!
Cons: Very ordinary

This place has changed Ownership many times in the last 5 years

I think ALDO's is best but Amy's not so much.   How hard is it to make a pizza?   I mean for real?

It was pretty clean for a Chinatown hot pot place. My only issue is that the prices are a little high. 6-8 dollars for a serving of meat... With that said, their condiment bar was very well stocked, the service was great, and if you check in you get a free order of meat of your choice. There were plenty of veggies to choose from which I loved. Also, they have full bar. with three meat plates and assorted veggies it ended up being 42$ in total. I would come back here for a special event only.

Food was delicious and the menu is thoughtful. However, a bit overpriced. That's not why they're getting one star, however. After leaving New Orleans after eating there on Saturday, 3 of the 5 people in my party were hit with fraudulent charges on their credit cards. That's a big inconvenience for non-NOLA natives on vacation. I am happy to have been in the 2 of 5 who paid with cash. 

I'm sure this goes without saying, but I won't be dining there again.

Great little breakfast place.  I ordered the French toast wth a side of hash browns and hubby ordered the cheddar omelet with pancakes.  All of it was very good. We drink decaf coffee and that was just okay- not as delicious as the regular coffee according to previous reviews. 

The restaurant is big and comfortable. The staff was friendly and fast to refill the coffees.

Right off the bat, their Salt and Pepper Calamari is TOO. DIE. FOR.
I have never had anything so exquisitely and expertly crafted and seasoned; it was beautifully plated and expertly balanced within its flavor profiles.
I got their Beef and Potato Hotpot which incorporated ginger in the most delicate and surprising of ways - I was incredibly pleased with my choice.
I forgot to take pictures like an idiot but would recommend this place highly.

Chiefs has made my list of must go places for any of my out of town visitors who like this type of food. Or even those who only think they might like it.

Last visit my group included two people I consider to be food experts. They have eaten a variety of food all over the world. They pronounced Chiefs fabulous and authentic.

As a non expert and one who initially could have been characterized as being in the category of might like it I can say fabulous and rely on my companions opinion about being authentic.

The decor is lovely and has character. The staff is super attentive. There is a choice of a formal dining area, tastefully decorated and with character, and an outdoor dining area. The focus of the outdoor area is a fountain and there are many plants. An iron railing and gate provides privacy for the outdoor dining area.

Currently alcoholic beverages are not available but BYOB is welcome. There is a convenience store across the street where alcoholic beverages can be purchased.

There is ample parking behind the building for those who, unlike me, are not close enough for a nice pleasant walk to Chiefs.

Edomasa is the my favorite Sushi around. The service is fantastic. They are just so sweet here and yeah they have screwed up a busy times but they still know how to make you feel happy. The Sushi and the Enoki mushroom appetizer is OFF THE HOOK! They are the only ones in SB to have a real Japanese menu, like some crazy stuff that I am still afraid to try lol.  I live in Carpinteria and will drive to Edomasa for my sushi fix (about 15 minutes). They never disappoint me and my kids after eating here about 20 times and are open crazy late...till midnight I think. We love you Edomasa!!

This is my 6th visit, and I always have a great experience here!  Except for kids yelling, but I do my best to avoid them!
Food is very good and my servers have always been on the ball!

Still a go-to fav for pizza and all things vegan. This coming from a meat lover. I went with the special...kimchi pork belly pizza. Wow spice and delight. The kimchi was crips and the sauce was filled with spice and flavour. 
We started with the spinach and artichoke dip. Great starter but go heavy on the dip as there are only a few pitas to spread. 
The wife had a fav mac&cheese pizza. Classic and never disappoints.

Very cool spot with an eclectic menu of amazing variety: baby octopus, antelope, hangar steak, pot pie, liver mousse, etc. Food was excellent. Prices very fair. Tap list was all local stuff, although a lot of the beers were subpar tasting: diacetyl batch of Troegs Sunshine Pils, odd Yards and PBC stuff, other weird breweries I've never heard of. Nice to have a local focus, but the tap list needed some work. Service was excellent. Outdoor patio seating upstairs was awesome. Loved the ambiance.

My family and I eat at this location quite often without any issues. On our last visit they burned our first two pizzas and it took quite a while to get our dinner. I understand that problems happen everywhere and I'm a firm believer that it's how you handle them that makes a huge difference. I'd like to personally compliment Zach on a great service recovery as it was suited for the issues we had, he was extremely personable and very professional. The entire family enjoys the pizza and we will definitely be returning to the Saint Charles location from now on due to the outstanding customer service and smiling faces.

Based upon the very successful and delicious Foo Truck, I am excited to see a permanent location for the Asian fusion 'Foo-rritos' we've come to love. Just above Chinatown, it's a quiet spot with an inviting design to enjoy some old favorites, and, in the case of rice and noodle platters, welcome new additions to the menu. The beef burger 'Foo-rrito' is all you could ever want wrapped into one big package (the kimchi and noodles really add another dimension I've never before experienced). Very excited to come back again!

Bird & the pig - surprisingly good, loveeed the sweet bread and the slices of apples. The chicken was a little dry. 

Slaw & tomato bisque - pass

Flan - different but a good different ! Graham cracker type crust and very dense. Not overly sweet
Exceptional service and food.  Appetizers divine as were cuts of beef & desserts.  Best meal of entire trip to New Orleans & a well needed rest from gumbo and shrimp.  On the list for next time!
Very fresh tostadas. Excellent flavor and sauces. In addition, the salsa and homemade chips are great.

Nice neighborhood bar and restaurant. SouthHouse has a good beer selection. Anything from pale ales to deep, dark brews - they should have something to satisfy your thirst. If cocktails are more your thing, they have a well stocked bar. 

The menu is better than it should be for a neighborhood bar. SouthHouse has good appetizers, soups, salads, burgers and entrees. The onion soup was pretty good. And the fish tacos were just right. The jalapeño cornbread looked great - sorry I didn't try it.

Delish sushi, sashimi and Ramon!  Hubby had the tuna roll and tuna sashimi, very fresh and tasty. I had the shrimp Ramon and after taking a taste, hubby had order envy. The broth was so creamy and flavorful! I got mild spicy and it was perfect, not too overbearing. Super duper nice staff.  Great place. We will definitely be back!

Only tried the cupcakes. The frosting is fantastic, light and sweet, exactly like a cloud. The cakes are just average for cupcakes, and were lacking in sweetness. The chocolate bliss was a little too bitter for my taste, and some of the others were even a bit salty. Even though I got there 2 hours after opening time, the cupcakes weren't displayed and some flavors were still not available as they were reportedly still cooking.
soooo good! prices are reasonable. customer service was great. very clean. and a good happy hour deal, 4p to close daily

Fried shrimp and Maryland crab cakes are outstanding.  Ate here twice this week and the food was wonderful each time.  The plates are big and fill you up. Loved the southern green beans as a side. The place has a lot of character, too - something you would not expect from the outside.

I have tried Green Eggs 3 times.  The food is fine, but the service is so spotty that with so many other choices just steps away there is no reason to ever risk the bad/nonexistent service you chance every time you go here.

My first experience was a brunch.  The side I received was wrong.  No biggie, just fix it & move on.  Once they fixed it, our waitress completely ignored us.  I don't know if she thought I was mad or something.  She also never asked me what I wanted to drink and I had to keep asking servers to please get me coffee or water or just something to drink.

My second time, assuming the first was a blip because they are so popular it couldn't be the norm, went just fine.  Just a normal restaurant visit.  Nothing bad, but nothing exceptional, just normal which is perfectly fine with me.

During my 2nd visit (above), they had no issue seating me before my companion joined me.  On my 3rd visit, I arrived with a 70 year old friend (a 3rd person was on their way).  We asked to be sat (the majority of the tables inside were empty and cleaned/reset) while we waited for the 3rd in our party.  We were told we could not be sat without the whole party was there.  We tried to explain given my companion's age, sitting was pretty much necessary.  They need to get the hostess to make that call.  Approx 10-15 mins passed before the hostess appeared and said we could sit.  Again on this visit we had to continue to chase down anyone to take our order and gets drinks.  We were literally ignored.  When my companion asked if the coffee being brought was fresh & hot, she was told yes, but it was ice cold - obviously had been sitting around.

You might get good service, it's a crap shoot, but with excellent places all up & down 13th Street at the same price point who consistently deliver great food AND service, why waste your time waiting and chance it?

We are visiting family in Philadelphia for spring break. Headed to Eastern State Penitentiary and stopped at Mugshots for a bite and coffee. The coffee was so good, but the cheese platter, pastries and smoothies were an amazing surprise. I loved the healthy options while on vacation. The staff were all friendly and kind.  I highly recommend Mugshots!!

1. COLD as ice crystal alligator appetizer...sent it back!!!!
2. Long wait for our orders to be taken.
3. Worst food ever in Bourbon St.

I had the trout and he had steak and fries. my trout was very salty and was served with one sliced tiny fingerling potato and three croutons. I'm not a big eater, but I felt the dish really needed some more depth of flavors. I can't imagine what I was supposed to do with the three croutons. His steak came with béarnaise sauce and fries. the steak was great and the sauce was a success.

I recently went to Max Brenner and it was the best experience I've had in a restaurant. My server's name was Kyle and he went above and beyond to serve my friend and I. He had a great personality, was very welcoming, and made sure to keep us happy and comfortable. You can tell he really enjoys his job and isn't just there for the money- he wants to make sure you truly have a great experience! If you ever go and want to make sure you have an AMAZING time, ask for Kyle!

I really enjoyed Cantina Dos Segundos, and was referred by my bartender to join yelp and write a review. 

Excellent margaritas, tacos, and absolutely love the salsa verde.

Can't wait to go back!
The customer service is too slow. And then food is just okay. But the decoration of food and the environment of the restaurant is great. However the grape is not washed.

The shakes and onion rings are good but overall not worth the high prices. I know people love the burgers here, but though they are better than your average fast-food burger, I really don't get all of the hype.

I was looking for a place to have lunch in Franklin yesterday and Pucket"s menu drew me there. I sat at the bar, as I was by myself, and was lucky enough to have Mercedez Patterson be my bartender. She had great suggestions made great drinks and just gave me such an overall excellent customer service experience that I had to call the manager aside and tell him how much I appreciated her excellent customer service. Customer service is very important to me as dining out is a hobby of mine and I appreciate it very much when I get good service. I had the cream of asparagus soup which was excellent and the catch of the day was a grouper with a crab white wine sauce that was very good. I had never had grouper before so I was not expecting it to be exactly as it was but it had nothing to do with the preparation, it was very good. I also had the Assagio mashed potatoes and Caesar salad both very good as well and took home a piece of the triple chocolate layer cake, I believe it was called and that was fabulous. The food was very good but the customer service was excellent. I will definitely go back and hopefully have Mercedes brighten my day again.
Hands down the best coffee in the Treasure Valley. They roast all their beans locally.
mary was a savage dealing with three tables 9+ people!!! she was fast, consistent, and funny!!! and thats on perioddddd. we love you mary!!!!!
The bottomless mimosas were AMAZING! Our waitress Lenna was the bomb. Highly recommend:)
Really enjoy this place! Great veggie burrito, special burrito was awesome too. I like the toppings, sides and salsa they offer and I like how the burrito comes with chips too!
If you don't live somewhere with a White Castle you are missing out!  This one was not terribly cleaned or stocked but the burgers tasted just fine at midnight.   Best after drinking food ever!

Always way understaffed and way overpriced for subpar food. Today it took 10 minutes of waiting to order and another full 15 minutes from time of ordering 3 subs to checkout... they did not have turkey meat or ham ready for the afternoon crowd, this was at 4pm on a Wednesday.

Came here for dinner this time. What a great experience. We made reservations ahead of time as this place can get very busy. Upon arrival they have a touch-less contact tracing QR code you can scan with your phone and fill in online. This is very sanitary option. 

The staff were extremely pleasant to deal with. Kind and informative. The manager sat me down and told me about their daily specials and the local farm to table suppliers they use to create the specials. It's nice to know they truly care about the ingredients they use to create these beautiful dishes. 

We ordered a bottle of wine, the arancini (which changes daily and it's VERY delicious), and tried the salmon dish for dinner which was so tasty and delicious, highly recommend. When we finished our dinner we were able to cork the bottle of wine and take the rest home with us which was very nice! 

I am always pleased with this little local gem. I always have a great experience here, great food, great service, and very clean. Will definitely come back again.

Phenomenal food! Ordered the wagyu beef satay and edemame dumpling -- both were unbelievably delicious. They were small plates but so good that my partner and I were happy to split. We also ordered the shrimp pad thai small plate to split. My partner wasn't thrilled with it, but I thought it was really good. Also had the good fortune of being gifted dessert by a couple seated near us: mini ice cream cones that were both tasty and cute! Finally, the cocktails were tasty. Was especially pleased with the Ming Mule.

I enjoy Brick & Brew. I have had some pretty good food and some sub-far food, and even worse service (sometimes slow, sometimes feel rushed). I think the highlight is really the drinks and bar staff. It's a very unique atmosphere and I recommend coming for craft beers and great cocktails.

Really excellent Vietnamese food.

 We had a big bowl of pho, Spring rolls and vermicelli with grilled pork.

 Usually to get authentic Vietnamese food we we have to drive all the way down to Philadelphia to the usual spots.

 We are very pleased to say that we now have a place that is much closer to home and totally hits it on all cylinders with really good fresh authentic cuisine in a modern Clean setting

Was there last week. One of the worst places.  Staff stood outside on the street chatting while we waited to be served. We felt like we were in the twilight zone. Creepy guy playing music. You may wait ten minutes before being acknowledged at your table. Food was not great. Mushroom wine sauce tasted like it came out of a can. Very gross!  Overall atmosphere was off and strange.

We were shopping in the area and found this place on Yelp.  We are sooo glad we picked it.  The food was absolutely delicious!  Staff was very polite.  The building was clean.  The only negative comment would be their horchata.  I've had much better elsewhere.
The best sushi and service you'll find in Murfreesboro. Do yourself a favor and eat here.

It was super weird when we stopped by on a Saturday evening and were the only customers the entire time. The place looks like it could hold quite a crowd, and the food was great! However, it was a little hard to get to due to some nearby roads being closed for events downtown, so perhaps that was the cause for the slow evening. Nonetheless, we really enjoyed our time, for starters, the soups were absolutely delicious! Won ton, sweet'n'sour, and egg drop - YUM!!! Would totally go back just for those!

We also had the half peking duck and an assortment of dim sum plates. Tbh, the dim sum wasn't all that amazing and I wouldn't get it again, but the duck was great, and there were plenty of other menu options I'd like to go back to try.
The owner was very hospitable and gracious. I only had the hummus and Baba ghanoush; they were the best I've had. For dessert I had Turkish coffee and baklava! I will be going again

Really great ciders on tap! Ordered 10 tastings (WeHo is not GF) and appreciated the varieties in flavor. I REALLY liked Resolution. The spicy hot wings were really good. Facility is open (architecturally noise will travel), bathrooms are neat! Kid and dog friendly.

Our last meal of our trip to the south and we purposely pass by Philly and ate lunch here.

They have lots of yummy food in this place but the best dish is festival fish soup, or N-1, in the menu for $6.5 a bowl.

Big eater will need 2 bowls.

Ask for more fried garlic and inion to enchant your bowl of noodle.

The best burmese festival fish noodle soup in the northeast.  Period!

I love the clever rabbit! If you ever have a vegan/ vegetarian friend come into town go and give this place a try. The servers are always so friendly and will give good suggestions if you ask. They have amazing vegan pastry's to go and a big selection of tea. Their coffee is sub-par if I'm honest so I would advice you to avoid it. The decor is super neat, all psychedelic animal accents with french- mid- century furniture. They have large tables for big groups and comfy window chairs for intimate gatherings.

Don't even know where to start this place amazing.  Once you realize the owner came from Mazzaro's and Alessi's it makes sense because the food here is fantastic.  Unassuming place tucked into the Airport Business Center by the St Pete-Clearwater airport, this place rocks. Great breakfast options, awesome pizzas, and they have great sandwiches and burgers too. I am slowly making my through the menu!  And they deliver.

went here recently... maybe it changed owners or managers or something...  wasn't as good as before.  And you know I'm a coffee snob type of guy so I was pretty bummed with the coffee drink I received.   it was also kind of full of smoke in the air or something...  think I need to find a new crepe place.

Very turned off by how rude they were. We called before leaving since it was fairly late and they are about 30-40 minutes away to verify that they were indeed still open. Upon arriving, we entered and people were inside eating. We sat down and waited. A gentleman came out and said they were closed. I stated we called and were told they were open, he came back with a "who did you talk to?" Does it matter who I talked too, no one gives their name when you call. He followed by saying they closed ealy cause it was dead in there, yet they had customers eating!! No, "we are sorry for the inconvenience", nothing what so ever!!! Just rude and very passive aggressive!! 

So we walked out feeling very disgusted, and went to 55 South again, they remembered my husband being related to Elvis, which was funny, and got us a table right away and we were treated with respect and awesome service!!! I will not be going back to Papa's after being treated like my business was nothing...

FYI: Maybe your business is slow and dead because the way you treat paying customers!!!
I've come a few times for the lunch buffet (9.99). It's decently good food but not spectacular. Clean, well-lit, comfortable, convenient.

Attempted to eat here last night at 8:30pm, despite multiple open tables we were told 45 min to hour wait.... They were not even close to being slammed/overwhelmed.  As we stood in the lobby deciding where to go next another waiter asked if we had been helped yet and looked to be ready to seat us until the original waste of space we dealt with chimed in that he had already told us it would be an hour wait.  I hope the owner of this establishment knows the waitstaff is turning away paying customers at 8:30pm on a Saturday.

Great food!  Especially sushi! They have a ton of different verities of sushi. We just had lunch at their location in Philadelphia over the weekend and it was great as well!  We always leave stuffed and happy with the meal. Staff is friendly and attentive as well.

Tried this place out tonight. Very nice place, clean and nice people. I ordered the Philly beef steak and specifically ask for ONLY cheese and onion. Specified no mayo!!! Get home and what do I find; lettuce, mayo, tomatoes and pickles!! Needless to say I did not eat it!! I'm allergic to mayo and would needed to get an injection had I eaten it!! Thank God I checked!!! So I surly will not go there again.....!

It's a sports bar. They've got beer, food, and TV. 

The food wasn't exceptional by any means, but gets the job done on game day.
Bottomless Mimosas for $15! The food is decent. The staff was friendly and funny!
Order to go twice and always give me an excellent meal. Love the panang curry duck

First visit there for me. We were celebrating a triple family birthday. We ordered four different meals and had four disappointments. The exotic mushroom soup was anything but. It was "blenderized" and had little taste. Shrimp tostada needed something to bring out the flavor. I can't say what would do it. My brother-in-law had the lasagna and said it did not taste like any he had ever had. He ate about one third of it and gave up. Two of us ordered dessert and were served what amounted to a $7 pop tart with a small portion of ice cream. The apples were not cooked sufficiently and the pastry was bland. I will not be returning to Buckley's any time in the foreseeable future.

The atmosphere is somewhat snooty.  Nice looking, but you can feel the attitude of the employees and the patrons.  Our server maybe thought he had seen me before and called me by someone else's name.  (This was our first time there!)  
The server was reasonably attentive otherwise.

While my dinner (crab cake burger) was really good, as were the tater tots, my wife's sliders were inedible.  She asked and confirmed catsup on the side, but it was on the burger anyway. The meat was dry and there were peppers which was NOT stated on the menu. (Big No-No!)

But here is what really had me annoyed:  we both ordered margaritas, on the rocks, with NO salt.  My wife watched closely as the bartender made them.  He loaded the rims of the glasses with salt and poured the drinks from the shaker.  Then, after discovering his mistake, he poured the drinks back into the shaker allowing much of the salt to go in there with it.  Then poured it back into new saltless glasses. Guess he thought no one was watching.  When the server brought them to us, we mentioned the action.  He offered us fresh drinks, but we declined.

While he did offer new drinks, we do not know if he said anything to the bartender.  Given the feel of the place, and the actions of the bartender, we will not return. 

Grossly over priced.  You are paying for the pleasure of dining with the cream of society.  I'll wager my tip was far greater than the guy with the $90 golf shirt.

Great food. Family-run business. Expect a very casual, low key, not fancy type of place. Remember family-run business. Authentic Thai food. Sushi is not their specialty. Feels more or less like you are in a local place in Thailand. Delicious food!

Best pizza in the area! This is authentic NY pizza and the $5 lunch special for two cheese slices and a drink can't be beat. It's always quick service (the guys that run it are great), incredibly tasty, and there are a handful of tables inside if you want to sit down to eat. Perfect for a time constrained lunch during the work day or grabbing a quick bite to eat. I have tried the pizza and the garlic knots, and both bring back fond memories of time spent in NYC. I come here regularly and love it!

It's about more. More coffee choices. More fountain drink choices. More gas pumps.

It's about better. Better cleanliness. Better friendliness.

It's about what no one else does. Restaurant quality sandwiches and sides made fast to the customer specifications.

Is Wawa a carry out restaurant? A sidewalk cafe? A gas station? It works as all three with none impeding the others.

We started off with a pitcher of the Mojito and a pitcher of the Sangria de Cava which were both fantastic and they make the pitchers table side which is neat for entertainment. 
Then the table shared some croquettes de pollo and devil crab croquettes which were both good with some hot sauce added. The table unanimously preferred the chicken to the crab.
My main course was the sampler style between three meals on the menu. The pork and round eye were decent and traditional. The empanada de Picadillo was much more enjoyable but It was worth it to try three different courses.
The perfect end to the trip was the bread pudding, which I saw recommended by many others. It was incredible with the top layer being so sweet and the texture was not too soft like others are. I ended up eating the bread pudding again the morning after since we took it home and it was still amazing, prompting me to make a review about it.

You have to ... have to ... get a pie from "the pizza box" inside the market ... we've been back daily at some point to enjoy another creation ... fresh ingredients, nothing canned, clean and neat! 

Make this a regular

Think Bon Air and you know it's about Fast Eddie's!

Where else can the food for two people be less than $10 and tasty! 

Grab a table, order a Big Elwood on a stick and a cheeseburger then go enjoy the coldest beer in town!

Bring CASH as Fast Eddie's is CASH ONLY!
The food is absolutely fantastic. Truffle fries are very tasty. Didn't bother taking a picture because it won't do justice of what it tastes like.

My boyfriend brought me to Texas Roadhouse for our late date night. Our server, Joel, was pretty kind and helpful. I really appreciate his customer service. Im pretty sure that we will be back again. Thank you again Joel for making our night a good one even though you guys were about to close.

I was in the mood for Korean food and needed to meet up with a friend downtown, so we decided to try Miga, a fairly newish Korean restaurant in Center City. We had to wait briefly for a table, and then were taken to a semi-private room off of a raucous main room. In another situation I might have felt exiled, but we had a lot of catching up to do and the private room was nice. We started with vegetable vegetable tempura, presented in a tall fried vegetable tower of a thicker-than-average cut. I especially love the zucchini tempura. 

Before our main course arrived, the waiter brought this amazing selection of pickles. I'm still thinking about the hot pickled garlic scapes. mmmm. I know I should get more creative, but I had a craving for Bim Bim Bop, and so that's what I ordered, in a steaming bowl. The soft fried egg arrived on the side, with chili sauce, which I promptly dumped all over everything. I loved the mushrooms, and such pickles with each different bite.

Miga is not BYOB, and more expensive that some other Korean restaurants in the neighborhood with similar food quality. But if you'd like to be waited on and feel a little fancier, give it a try.

The thin was PERFECT, as close to Vito & Nick's as you get. In fact, Vito & Nicks is a bit greasier so we actually liked this better. We are far northside lakefronters that would drive all the way to the far southwest side (84th & Pulaski)  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=94aYUljniPI  to get that treat on occasion. so driving to Indian Rocks Beach from Holiday isnt too bad in comparison. The stuffed was like a cross between our two all time favorites, Giordano's and Edwardo's. No need to order "extra sauce" here.
The first time we ate here in October, we were blown away and loved that they had TBB's pumpkin on tap, even though the glass size is small. We wanted to try it again before leaving a review and the pizza this time was even better than we remembered. The Shipyard Island Time Session IPA (tropical) was a perfect pairing! 
WARNING: IMO, the deep dish (pan) is NOT what I look for in that style of pizza and be sure to "season" your pies with the shakers of parm, crushed red pepper and ask for oregano

I am giving this restaurant two stars, not because the food was bad--in fact the food was pretty good. It was the absolute horrific service that appalled myself and my boyfriend. We love nothing better than going to eat on Sunday nights after an incredibly long work week. We are both in the service industry and now a thing or two about service and food.
To begin with, we sat at the bar because there were few people up there and we wanted to give the bartender a chance to make some money too. There seemed to be three bartenders working, so there was no reason for the terrible experience we had. I ordered a martini after asking about vermouth (I received a very lackluster response--almost as if I was bothering him by simply asking a question). I received the martini, and the bartender took another 5 minutes to ask if my boyfriend wanted anything to drink. We ordered a salad and two pasta small plates after that. The bartender brought out some bread-- ice cold and with no olive oil. Bread should never be ice cold no matter the situation, but we ate it anyway and did not complain. We had to interrupt the man next to us to ask if we could borrow his oil. The man sitting next to us ordered the same salad and a baked lasagna. He received his salad a few minutes after ours came, and his BAKED lasagna followed almost immediately.
