Apparently the owners of this establishment read their reviews (very smart on their part!) because shortly after I wrote my review they re -created their dinner salad to one that consists of romaine--not the iceberg lettuce that they had served originally! The food here is remarkable! I'm so glad that I live within walking distance to it, because I plan to frequent it regularly!
Checked in via Yelp, was seated quickly once we arrived, good was excellent but a bit pricey. Amazing service
Really awesome to walk down at night.  No where near as crowded as Broadway although these bars can get pricey.

I'm not sure how people find this place, as it's tucked away a bit, but when they do, I am sure they come back again and again. We were around the corner at the growler beer bar and the owner recommended it as a quick and healthy dinner spot.  

I found the food to be a healthy alternative to the bar food choices we had in this area at night. The staff were great and helpful to us at the counter where we placed our order. It was our first visit, so they walked us through the drill. Portion sizes were large and I didn't feel guilty eating the food.  

I loved all the cycling decor and walked around a bit as if I were in an art museum. My kind of place!

Tequilas is a bit hit or miss.  

The decor is interesting for an upscale Mexican spot to say the least, and you will either like it or hate it.  I didn't enjoy getting seated in the weirdly lit bar area with people bumping into our chairs from time to time.  The chandelier has to go.

As for the service, I found it a bit odd that the waiter wouldn't take an appetizer order and insisted that he takes the meal and appetizers orders together.  That's the first time I've ever heard such a thing.

As for the food, it was decent overall... but pricey.  My friend had the grouper and the wife had the cochinita pibil and those were the highlight dishes in my mind.  The bacon guac was excellent too.  I ordered bacon wrapped shrimp with rice for my meal.  The shrimp just came out way too salty for my liking.  

As for the drinks, they were pretty strong and tasty.  I would say this is an area where they shine.

I'd probably stick with El Vez if I happen to be in that area, but this isn't a bad alternative.
Menu was average at best. Service was decent, atmosphere was just ok (really bad lighting) and the drinks definitely were weak. There are much better places to go and spend your evening then here.

Ok, Juicy Lucy's is not the best burger I ever had in New Orleans.  That honor still goes to Port of Call and here's the reason.  Juicy Lucy's forte seems to be stuffed burgers.  Its kinda of slider.  You can't get it cooked rare, medium rare.  That's a real downside for me.  The place is welcoming in a kind of kick back Mid City feel which is upcoming.  The service was attentive but nothing special.  The french fries.  I like 'em.  However, I don't like them rationed.  I want a mound of onion rings.  They were good all 10 of 'em.  French fries pretty standard but nothing special.  The burger was good but I kept thinking this was something my grandmother used to do.  Cook it till its done and cook it again.  Overall, I liked it.  I didn't love it.  It does what New Orleans does best......you're in what used to be someone's home.  That I like.  Putting anything in a strip mall automatically leaves a bad taste of "Anywhere America but not here".  I don't think Port of Call is as good as it used to be but I still believe it does what does and what it does is better than anywhere else in the city.

Went for the first time on Saturday eve. Met a friend I hadn't hung with for a while. Sat at a table by the bar. New covid rules. Service was fantastic. Great selection of beer. Atmosphere was fun. Importantly we felt safe and all covid rules were enforced. Had cheese fries earlier in the night. Initially served incorrectly (my buddy doesn't eat bacon) but was quickly and correctly rectified. I ordered a burger to go which also didn't disappoint. Wife and I had been wanting to try but now we're definitely making an effort to stop by regularly.

I love this place.  Fresh fried fish tacos!  Freshly made chips!  Delicious, not too sweet, fresh lemonade and aqua fresca!  The food is so good.  It's fresh, hot, and cheap.  What else can you ask for!  Do yourself a favor, get there.  

My favorites are the fried and grilled fish tacos and carne asada.  But the cervice looks amazing, too!

What a great little place!

Since so many reviews have already detailed the adorable old train station tucked away, the delicious sandwiches, and truly yummy fries, and warm service, I won't go into detail.  I'll just offer another enthusiastic recommendation - CHECK THIS PLACE OUT!  It's really a hidden gem (very hidden - no sign until you're already off the road). 

We tried the fried pickles as an appetizer - fun!  I had the truffle hand burger, which was juicy and awesome, and my man got a hamburger which was supposed to be paired with an onion confit (we're not sure if it was there since we couldn't taste it).  Both had awesome fries that completely lacked any greasiness and were perfectly seasoned.  We left full and happy.

We'd go back in a heartbeat. Although this is close to 5 stars, it's quite expensive for a sandwich lunch, and the boy's burger lacked the onion flavor described on the menu. However, it's worth it for an occasional treat!

The food is tasty the portions are average the soup was nothing special the decor is very nice but I think this place is EXTREMELY OVERPRICED!!! Sai Ba Dee in Upper Darby is has as good or better food for a fraction of the price of this place. Thai food shouldn't be this expensive bottom line and there sushi is mediocre at best. For the price you won't be blown away

DO NOT DINE HERE FOR ANY REASON IN THE WORLD!!! 



Okay so where do I begin??!!! We anxiously arrived to the fiery crab ready to dig into some sea food boil, oysters and many other things we had scoped out on the menu before we arrived. Upon entering and approaching the hostess stand we were greeted with a rather bothered attitude filled hostess . Waited on a 30 minute delay to be seated, understandable neww restaurant, packed, everyone is eager to try. Our number was called we were sat then the real experience began.  Filled with angst to eat at this point we promptly gave our waitress our food order and drinks verbatim, 2 Louisiana mules, one order of chargrilled oysters, crab cakes, order of raw oysters, and an order of cheese sticks for our daughters. Waters arrived, our daughters coke arrived and our appetizers, then we gave our waitress the entree order which wasn't taken until apps were dropped. Okay so we are one chargrilled oyster in and my 12 yr old daughter requested to try her first oyster, when I go to serve her oyster I noticed  there wAs a hair in my oyster, a short hair possibly already charred a bit. Soo I politely tell my server and request for a new one, just to not run the risk of any more hairs on any other oysters. Here is where things took a  turn for the woRst. Our waitress took
My oysters to the kitchen came right back and said "just our luck there was another oRder in the window" so me and my untrusting self proceded to count the oysters as they come in a doZen and I counted 9!!!! Soo 12 minus the one I ate, minus the one my daughter tried minus  the one with the hair equals 9  and half the bread was missing because our kids ate that before we sent it back as well. Also my bf's raw   oysters do not come shucked and turned over like at any other decent seafood place. Thenn finally those mules y'all forgot about, yeah us toO, arrived. Low and behold with a blaCk substance in it, more dirtiness. Sooo at this point I think it's time to go as we are a family of 6 kids and eating out always is a treat Soo it has to be money well spent. Okay no problem, I calmly request a manager and tell her my reason and tell her I will pay everything we   consumed. They then argued me down about having to pay for everything including alcohol. Something that had some strange filth in it. We finally settled after I told them I had photographs of the hair and we quickly left and went right down the street to Don Jose Mexican grill and had an amazing dinner.  If I may suggest fiery crab, you may be new and booming but it isn't about how many heads you can get in your door it's about how many heads will come back always choose  quality over quantity....great service,  and most of all quality hairless food. 




Our waitress was: Shaeh -Lynn
Not very traditional flavors. The navarati curry has a strong garam masala flavor . Too bad, I was craving Indian food. I wish Reno had better indian food.

Amazing food, great atmosphere, and great owners! The crepes were outstanding.  I had the "Apple Garden" crepe that was just AWESOME! The owners took time out to joke around with our three year old and have good conversation with us. We will come back for sure!

Love the food! Butter Chicken and Chicken Tikka Masala with Naan and Fried Rice was exactly what we needed. Best Indian Cuisine I've had outside of Malaysia! Service was a bit slow, but the food was very much worth the wait!
I've loved everything I've had here. I've had 4 or 5 different drinks, ramen, and the chicken wings. I would go more often if I lived closer. I definitely look for excuses to head that way.

It was bad enough that I could not get a space at the almost empty bar, because no one could bother cleaning up from the previous customers, but then I had a useless bartender who knew nothing about the beer menu. When I asked her if she could tell me what beers they had available since providing a beer list was too much of a burden for the management, she honestly said., "I don't know, they are all in the coolers, name one."  I thought to myself, Ah, Bud Light????  Have you heard of it? Later I asked if they had any unfiltered beers or craft beers. She didn't know what those were. Check!!!  At least the Thai egg rolls were good. I shouldn't be surprised by this kind of experience in Nashville, a city of amateurs.

P.S. Get some paper towels in the bathrooms. Don't know if you've heard, but there's a pandemic.  Some  folks here need to do their jobs and some need training.

My first Shack Burger was at Madison Square Park so I was thrilled to have one pop up in Philly! I love Shake Shack! The food is consistent and delicious! My orders have always looked like they've come out of a magazine, fresh bright colors on the plates, fluffy buns and crispy golden crinkly fries and or course piping hot.This location is always popping. My favorite is the classic Shack Burger with red onion and a side of fries. The milkshakes are delicious as well.  Once you get through the queue line, you will be handed a buzzer to notify you when your order is ready for pick up. There is a nice sized dining area in the back of the restaurant and tables outside when the weather is nice.
I love that there are treats for the pups as well, unfortunately I've only gone for lunch during the work week so I haven't gotten the paws up from my furbabies on whether they love the offerings or not!
If you have not eaten here, you definitely need to add it on your to do list while in the city!

We chose to do take out and it was a waste of money. I ordered the buffalo chicken wrap and it was an embarrassment. Small, no pico, and falling apart. You could tell it was put together in haste. I have been to the pub for dine in but after this, I do not plan to go back.

If you are a tourist and are looking for a good cheesesteak do not go here. It is a tourist trap and cheesesteaks they hand out are sub-par. 

Save yourself some time and go somewhere else.

Living in Southampton for several years now, I could have kicked myself for not trying Panda sooner than I did.  This is a bare bones, no nonsense, no surprises Chinese takeout joint that has never disappointed me.

My usual order could be chicken with mixed veggies, general tso's, crab Rangoon, and/or pork fried rice.  If you're craving anything similar, you'll be happy you went to Panda. In addition, staff has always been fair and direct, and provides abundant condiments typically.  I've never waited more than 20 minutes for a pickup order and the food is hot.

Though closed for awhile during the COVID era, Panda is now reopened with safety precautions in place.  I typically pick up my order with very minimal contact to staff. Go Panda Go!
Our favorite Italian Restaurant in Reno. All the food is really good, but we always go back to having the Carbonara, best in town.

We went New Year's Eve with a reservation for 7.  They sat us at a table for 6 .  Manager noticed right away and made an extra effort to move us to a bigger table.  She succeeded.  The food was delicious and serve was excellent.  We definitely returning.
Consistently solid sushi and terrific service, especially during the pandemic. Love that you can ask for "nothing extra" to reduce takeout waste!

It took about 10 minutes before anyone greeted our table, and had to get the attention from someone else to let a server know we were ready. Drinks took forever... Once the food came out, no napkins or silverware were given. Seriously? We then had to ask for napkins from our server and refills! Worst part is, when they brought us our new drink our old ones were left behind on the table!!! No body ever picked up dirty plates. I am well aware that this is a chain and not so much of a fine dining restaurant but basic serving procedures are done in order  to have napkins, silverware and clear plates for any establishment! Desert was never an option for us, maybe because we were never given a menu.. What had happened to Applebee's?! Throughout our meal, we also heard servers and bussers throwing out "sorry's" left and right. Wow. Also, the carpets were dirty! Do they ever vacuum or sweep? It is disgusting to sit at a table knowing theirs SHIT below. I guess it represents theirs service and food.

I got a Montecito burger and a small chocolate shake. The burger was really good and it came with fries. The shake was not thick at all, which was disappointing. It was like drinking chocolate milk. My biggest qualm was the price. My friend and I got two burgers and two shakes and the total bill including tax and tip was $40. It just seemed a bit pricey for burgers. Overall, the food was good, service was prompt and the ingredients were fresh/local. I will definitely come here again.

Super good. I want some right now haha. The money you spend is worth it here. The gyro plate is amazing and you can choose your side and you get a drink. Very satisfied and super yummy. It is also quick.
Keep in mind, it's McDonald's. My food was made appropriately, I was treated satisfactorily, and I didn't wait long. That's a gold star for the place. Remember, it's just a McDonald's.

One of my favorite spots in Philly. If you like a diverse beer selection, great burgers, and exceptional mussels, you will love Monk's. Monk's also has a fun and lively atmosphere with that is anchored by a friendly staff. Overall, I highly recommended Monk's to everyone.

I came here with my parents and we had the jampong, naeng myun and galbi dolsot.  The banchan was simple but very good (good kim chi and that is important to me).  Portions are large but more importantly, the flavor was larger.  My jampong broth was delish and it was heartily filled with seafood.  The noodles were perfectly cooked.  On the other spectrum, my mom's naeng myun was also flavorful and filled with beef strips, cucumber and radish.  The broth was also terrific.  Lastly, my dad said this was the best dolsot he's ever had.  He loved how the onions and carrots were cooked and became caramelized.  The galbi was also well marinated and very tasty.
We came at the end of their lunch hour and it took a while to get our food.  But the wait is worth it because the food is sooo good.

Had a really nice time at dinner at Broadway Oyster Bar.

They had a jazz band rockin, the oysters were fresh, and the cajun food was pretty damn good.

I had the sample platter. The gumbo was definitely my favorite, but everything else on there was tasty as well. My first experience with an etoufee was a good one.

The girlfriend had the fish tacos and she really loved the avocado on there.

Overall, service was great, price was reasonable, atmosphere was fun. Would definitely go back if I am in STL again!
Great Japanese and Chinese food.  Never been disappointed.  Been in business for years.  Very attentive service.  Highly recommend.

We have always loved Pierre Maspero's and have visited every time we are in NOLA.  Today, we arrived for a late lunch and were disappointed. They were very busy, but still seated us right away.  We ordered seafood pistoleros, shrimp & grits and a muffuletta.  The muffuletta and shrimp and grits arrived first.  They guy who delivered it just said he didn't know anything about that. The shrimp and grits were cold and it was a different recipe from what I'd had here before.  The waitress worked hard to make things right but it was disappointing.

I'm in Trejo more often than I'd like to admit due to working at the Montgomery County Courthouse, but for good reason. Be warned, many lawyers and law enforcement officers are in the restaurant daily! 

The quaint little Mexican restaurant offers great authentic Mexican cuisine at a reasonable price. The portions are generous and I am usually stuffed after coming out of Trejo. When eating in, they give you some of the best chips I have ever had. The complimentary chips almost remind me pita chips; they are thick and very crunchy! They also come with a killer salsa verde that is extremely flavorful. I often save some of it for my tacos or burrito. 

My favorite thing from Trejo has to be their burrito. The unique thing about this place's burritos is that the contents are somehow well mixed in the tortilla, so that every bite you take has a bit of rice, meat, beans, and cheese. In fact, they bring it to you hot off the grill when eating in so when you take a bite, all of the content meld really well together along with the cheese. My mouth is drooling just thinking about it. Combined with the salsa verde, you've got a flavor packed meal. 

Compared to the other Mexican restaurants, Trejo is a tad on the pricier side, but well worth it. Check it out next time you're in court!
The Hot Sausage Po Boy was Da Best The sausage is fresh and homemade, and so are the Onion Rings, fresh and homemade, will absolutely be ordering from here slot. Menu is on my cover page
Food was great and staff was friendly! Emma was very helpful and patient with me as I asked for recommendations. Will be back again!

Took a friend to dinner at The Grill for her birthday.  Had a nice glass of Pinot at the bar before she arrived.  Very stylish/comfortable bar.  We had a wonderful dinner.  I had one of the specials, Sea Bass w/shrimp & fennel on top.  Very delightful.  They brought my friend a birthday dessert without all of the singing.  That was the way I had hoped it would go.  All and all a very nice experience.

Bar louie has some of the best burgers in town. Especially when you can get them for $5 on Tuesdays!!! Our server was Kristen and she was amazing!! Exceptional service, definitely recommend her! They also have my favorite beer on tap, (blue moon). They have an outdoor patio as well with a gas fire pit which was another nice aspect. 5 stars all the way!!!!

Awesome! Taco Tuesday could never be better. Wish there was one in Arizona! We had our favorite tacos and not so favorite such as the mole could U.S. some work when the Carolina and oyster and brisket could stand alone or make up for what mole lacked. The crispy or flaked fish could use more seasoning

So good! We sat outside and the space is so lovely! The trees keep it nice and shaded so even on the warm morning we were comfortable. The food was good. My little guy had a biscuit and gravy which he devoured. We all split a French toast and it was just enough sweetness. I had a basic scrambled eggs and toast with fruit. The potatoes that came with it were so good as well. They came with onions and peppers, I could have made a meal out of them! My boyfriend had coffee and he enjoyed it and j had a couple of mimosas (always a good choice!). If/when we make it back to St Louis this place is on our must visit list!
The tacos and sweet corns were awesome, but the soup was the best ever!  The prices are great. If you go to Nashville you have to visit this place.
The fact that this place has a high rating bemuses me. The nastiest food, not just cheesesteak I've ever had. You couldn't pay me to try this ever again.

Went with some folks from the office.  We were all in from out of town.  The wait was a hour but the 4 of us found a place at the bar.  Service was good and our bartender was good but food was just okay I had a pesto pasta dish with shrimp and crab meat.  There was very little crab and the pasta, especially for being pesto, really lacked flavor. I could barely taste any basil.  When I asked the others they felt similar.  It was okay but definitely not as good as we expected.
Another Franklin staple. Particularly on warm weather nights when music is playing on the square, this restaurant can become an excellent Franklin experience.

Absolutely amazing. Their specialty sushi menu is not only incredibly diverse, but every thing we have ever tried has been truly delicious. Probably the best sushi at this cost on the west coast, and maybe the best sushi at any cost. The regular sushi leaves a little to be desired so we recommend sticking To their specialty menu. But we were delightfully surprised by this Santa Barbara gem

Not sure why there is such a range of reviews, or more accurately, so many less than favorable reviews.  I ate here a couple of times four years ago in my pre-Yelp days and ate here twice on this year's trip.  On all occasions the food and service were exceptional.

The selection of sandwiches, soft drinks, water, fruit juices, tea, snacks, and healthy food is pretty large.  I had the hot pastrami sandwich one day, and it was very good. The meat had the right balance of lean and fat, which is key for pastrami.  The next time I had the Cuban sandwich.  What made for an interesting Cuban sandwich was the addition of salami, which you do not see many other places.  It actually made the sandwich a little better than average.

You can find a good selection of chips for your sandwich.  They serve breakfast sandwiches all day, but I never had a chance to give them a try.

You can eat either inside or outside, depending on the weather and your plans.

Overall, a nice place to walk to when visiting the area and a short walk from the local hotels.

Probably the best BBQ in Nashville! I went to Leg Porker, but they were mediocre. It was all hype that made that place sound good, but I have to say Martin's topped all the BBQ joints that we went to in Nashville. Super flavorful and the meat fell right off the bone! The place had a lot of room to find a place for a big group and this place just had that fun vibe surrounding the place. Awesome eclectic vintage looking decor, lots of TVs for sports.  Definitely recommend stopping by here!

We always get something different when we come here and it is always amazing. They have the best garlic rolls. They are great for catering too. The catering is very easy, our guests always love it, and the prices are very reasonable.

Elaine and her crew keep our bellies full on our almost weekly trips down from our office. We never hesitate to bring our out-of-towners here for a quick bite, and they are always impressed!

They have a great menu of sandwiches and wraps, and fantastic rotation of new/limited items season to season.

Definitely check them out the next time you are hungry on Cherokee Street. (And if you like to discuss dogs, they are your crew, and they can give you the DL on all the Doggie gossip, so don't hesitate to ask ;)

Cheers,
Mike Wyrock

This place is a gem. They have indoor seating and a cute little outdoor patio that is covered. You can easily make a reservation online. 

We got steamed dumplings, shrimp toasted, and shaved ice. The entire experience and meal was delicious and casual and fun. It is really reasonably priced too.

This is easily in my top 20 meals ever and probably even in the top 10. As with any tasting menu they are going to be some courses you like less than others, but when your least favorite course is a ridiculously good sashimi flight, you know it's one heck of a meal. And speaking of flights, I highly recommend the sake and wine pairing. The sommelier is young but ridiculously educated on such matters as each pairing went impeccably with its respective course. everything was fresh, flavorful, and very inventive. Since the menu changes monthly, I won't go into the details other than to say everything was 10 out of 10.

A grilled cheese sandwich with pickles and tomatoes is one of my favorite comfort foods and GourMelt does not disappoint. Super friendly service and even with an extensive menu of grilled cheese creations, they're happy to "customize" your sandwich. Be sure to try the tomato soup...and split an order of their yummy garlic fries with a friend! The menu is creative and the prices are fair. Visit the website to view the calendar on where to find them each week.

Christina is an outstanding waitress, however the food is not so much. The chicken tacos were heavily over salted, bland, & ridiculously expensive. You can tell there are problems with management as it took over 20 minutes for the appetizer to come out in a completely dead restaurant... We were like the only ones there. I think if this place lowered their prices and got new management/ kitchen staff, this place could really do good. They already have a great beer selection going for them so if they just revamped their management and staff, this place could be a hit!

I consider myself quite the breakfast sandwich connoisseur, and I LOVE RJs. They make the most gigantic, delicious sandwiches around, and offer turkey meat selections too. (I know, you're thinking it's like ordering a diet Coke with a Big Mac, my stomach can't always handle regular bacon.) So good. No complaints.

Great food; large portions.  Chicken was flavorful all the way through and loved the fried plantains.  Rice was bland was once beans on the rice- it was fine.
First time there confusing where to enter - cluttered near door.

OK so I was trekking on my hot rod 2 wheeler (Schwinn) the other day and found myself out of steam in not the best 'hood as far as stopping on the sidewalk/street whilst alone.  I spotted this cozy corner rest area and parked it.  Good idea, Al....why - thank you!

First - the set up is pretty rad.  Plenty of space and types of seating to cater to your butt needs.  Local artwork on the walls that you can actually purchase if you so desire.  Electrical outlets for your technology needs and in my case...battery vampire phone.  I also am going to go out on a limb and assume they have Wifi.  

I needed protein and got an overdose.  They have two of my all-time favorite things on the menu - a peanut butter & banana smoothie w/soy AND bacon wrapped dates..Wha-what?  Now before I get ahead of myself - I opted out on the dates that day, but I will surely be back to give them a go in the near future.  I actually ordered the cheese quesadilla because I was looking for protein in a snack-based form.  It was quite delish, cheesy, and took care of my dietary needs.  The sauce was zingy as well - a nice additive if you choose to dip those tips. I also enjoyed a delightful iced latte with espresso (added) and caramel, which certainly recharged my energy cells.  


The peeps...they were so very informative and helpful.  I had a chat with a nice gal about the big biking event going down in Dutchtown in May and a brief history of past events - MoPro...look it up and enjoy.  The sweet gal that actually took my order was very helpful considering I had never dined at Urban before and had no clue what to order.  She actually hand made my super awesome PB & banana smoothie.  I felt the love.  She also informed me of their Sunday Brunch - dim sum style, which I was very intrigued by and intend to experience in the near future.  Always looking for new and exciting brunch adventures on the weekends.

Overall - I really dig this place.  I intend on coming back so I can explore there other dining options AND get some of those bacon wrapped dates....and another PB & banana smoothie, of course!
This place was hyped up, so I decided to try it.  Mistake.  Small portions and not very flavorful.  The tacos were very dry.  Rose cafe kicks this place's butt

Delicious! 

We stopped in after hearing about it in an Uber pool and were not disappointed. Everything was delicious. It was a bit awkward at first sitting with a group of strangers, but everyone was really nice.

The fruit tea & sweet tea are so good!!

The pecan pie is the best I've ever had. Nobody ate theirs and I wanted to take their plates and run it was that good.

We stopped in on a Sunday- we were offered bean salad (delish), cole slaw (very good, mashed potatoes, Mac and cheese (so ooey gooey good), bbq spare ribs (did not try them, but they looked good), Cajun catfish was sooooo good!!! I should have ate more of it, and fried chicken which was very good. I had two pieces lol. 

We left very satisfied. We didn't eat again until 7pm and we had Monellis at 11am. It was $25/pp which felt pricey for a lunch, but it was totally worth it.

I really love Ike's Love and Sandwiches! They have the best bread ever, great catering for lunch or dinner, really flavorful sandwiches with tons of meat or vegan and vegetarian options. The staff is friendly and the vibe is great! Totally worth trying out!

I really enjoy Antonio's every time I come to eat here. It's too far from me to make use of the carry out side of the restaurant, so I can't speak to that but the sit-down part of the restaurant is excellent. It is BYOB so be sure to grab a bottle (or two) of your favorite vino before going. I've got to admit that I'm pretty boring in my orders. Every time I go I always order the vodka rigatoni because it is the best I've ever had. I have gotten to enjoy tastes of my friends' and family members' meals when they order something other than the vodka rigs and I have never been disappointed. The atmosphere is nice and most times we eat there Anthony is either in the kitchen or making sure everyone is happy with their meals. The owner being a regular presence really helps maintain the standards of the restaurant, I believe. If you're in the area, you should stop in for some delicious Italian food!

Hmmmmm let's see where do I begin?
The HANDWRITTEN signs that taped on the windows are unwelcoming and the Customer service wasn't the best. 
The younglady that took our order gave us the impression that she doesn't like her job or people. The  weren't done very well and there was NO seasoning on them whatsoever. Also who sells  and doesn't have Ketchup packets? TNC!!! (how ridiculous) and the coleslaw (which we did not eat)was HOT  
( I'd choose KFC over TNCS) AND the kicker isssssssss spending money on food and  drinks (they were out of lemonade) so I went old school and order a Hawaiian Punch my bro got a bottle of water.  When I asked for ice that heffa said,"25 cents". I expressed my disappointment WTH!!  And other customers couldn't believe it either.
The 2 stars is ONLY because our fish and shrimp was enjoyable. Other then that, I'll be in NO hurry to return to TNCS.

What a let down. This place was recommended by the concierge at a hotel my out of town guests were staying at. The first thing the waitress did was inform us of what that were out of... On a Saturday night! Out of ribs. Out of shrimp. Seriously? Are you going out of business? Things for progressively worse from here. The chicken was grossly undercooked and when we complained the manager said it was smoked and supposed to be like that. Are you kidding? Also the steam pot was very short on the seafood and long on the sausage and potatoes. This place is going down the tubes and not too soon. Vacate the space and make way for a restaurant that gives a dam.

So my boyfriend and I sat at the bar, ordered drinks and chips and salsa to start. We got our drinks and menus and decided what we wanted. Menus closed we sat and waited for over 15 mins while the bartender talked to old men trying to make her tips by being flirty. We had to yell for her attention and still had no chips and salsa. We ordered. She barely wrote anything down and we had to repeat ourselves twice. Another 15 mins goes by and my boyfriend asked her if she forgot the chips. She lied directly to our faces saying "they were coming". She brought them out and we watched her ring in the chips after the fact. Thus lying because she did forget. Our orders came out and both were wrong. My boyfriend went to wash his hands as I explained what was wrong and she lied AGAIN saying he asked for it that way. I was sitting right next to him and NO he didn't ask for it that way. We are young professionals and I have never felt so discriminated and disrespected in my life! She thought we were dumb kids and not worth her time. Never coming back!
Manager did handle the situation professionally after though as she continues to ignore us with no apology while she cleaned our drink glasses.

Super personal as I walked in. Explained the menu. I got the Italiano and It was delicious. They made it to order exactly like I requested. They also have a pepper bar that you can get your own fixings!! Love that. I will be back and they deliver
Great authentic Mexican . The former La Ha still kicking out the Flavors. The Chicken Soup is always a great go to. It was nice to re visit my old favorite.

I was recommended to go here by a friend for a tarot reading and was pleasantly surprised! Ashley was amazing, kind and really personable! Although I did not try any food, the tea was great and my tarot reading was well worth the cost. This was my first time having a reading and Ashley was incredible! Will return in the future. 
The only reason I am giving a 4/5 is because of the parking! It was hard to find parking near the tea room as the street was incredibly busy.

Wonderful. Starting with the young lady receptionist who is extremely polite, patient and helpful. Sushi is great for take outs but the poke bowl will always make the trip worthwhile. It is like a sushi assortment in every bite.  Excellent every time!

This place was only okay. I have high expectations for a brunch place, especially one in Nashville. I ordered a salad, which was $13 dollars. All it had on it was about 4 blackberries, arugula, two cubes of cheese, and a teaspoon of granola. No meat or bacon or anything. Disappointed to say the least. We were also rudely kicked out by the male worker in the front by the hostess stand when we were trying to purchase a T shirt. No explanation, just told he was clearing out the restaurant. Won't be coming back here and you shouldn't either.

Easily the worst pizza shop in Hockessin. The cheesesteak crust is very bland has like 0 flavor it's a very dry pizza. The garlic knots are a tad overrated, usually I just get soggy soaked knots if I've ordered them. Today I tried the cheesesteak absolute joke. So I've heard bad things about the cheesesteak before how it's a small like dinky sandwich. And wow people were spot on, the sandwich is only like 10 inches so already under the typically footlong standard. It is 8.25 it makes sense now. It is made with the pizza dough. I got it and literally I thought there was no cheese on the steak. The cheese was melted into the roll with the steak put on top of it. What a absolute joke of a sandwich. I mean the absolute worst. 2 cousins has a attitude even with the employees thinking they'e the best. Nope not even close

Food was excellent, so fresh! I love breakfast food and was NOT disappointed. Coffee was also amazing. You can take some to go which I liked. It was so good I bought some for home as well! Service was good and did not wait long for food. Would definitely recommend this place for breakfast.
On vacation and this place is close to where I'm staying. The atmosphere is great and very diverse. They have a live local band which is really good. Nice little local spot to check out.
The strip mall that it's in is kind of scary looking but the restaurant is not.  Delicious pho and nice, attentive staff!!

The only reason I even left "ONE" star, is because you can't leave a review without one. I have waited a long time to write an honest review of this (hole), I guess I always thought to myself to overlook all the health code violations, and drunken staff being in charge of my "well-being". 
After tonight I know now it's ok for me to post the pictures I have saved in case this ever happened.
All establishments have health codes and violations. Such as "You cannot wear open toed shoes while working!!!"
It's disgusting seeing this establishment get away with no excise even present. I can speak from experience that there shouldn't be open- toed shoes, or drinking alcohol behind the bar, or bottles of booze covered as "mystery "shot?!!?
We realized very quickly after finding out we were out of place. 
Being a neighborhood bar....I worry about the neighborhood, and over serving.
Be careful coming here!

After doing some research on where to buy the best muffuletta in town, we settled on Napoleon House. Their Po Boy received rave reviews so we decided to give it a try. So we ventured out there to give it a try. 

We ended up getting the roast beef po boy which was so so and the shrimp po boy was good. The customer service however could have been a bit better. Although the food came out quickly, we didn't see our server until we requested the check. A quick "how is the food?" would have sufficed.

All in all, it wasn't worth writing home about. You might be better off looking at other places to get your po boy fix.

Went there for RW last night and am definitely a fan.  There were three of us, so we got to try 12 different dishes (not counting dessert).  Of all of the dishes, I'd say the pork belly buns, mussels and the one salad with edamame were hands down amazing!  My least favorite dish would be the smoked shrimp spring rolls, which just had a strange texture.  I also liked the fried brisket, but wish it had some kind of sauce or flavor. 

The coconut curry mussels were so good, and I loved that the waiter offered us more bread to dip in the sauce, however the bread had huge holes in it, so it just fell apart in the sauce :( 

The dessert was a big disappointment, but I wasn't going there for it, so it's not a deal breaker for me.  The red miso with the coconut cake didn't really fit in, and the ice cream on top had no flavor.  The lemon meringue was okay, but nothing great.  

I think I'd return for a beer and some mussels and salad sometime.  I'm glad I tried it during restaurant week with friends so that we got to try a little of everything.  The atmosphere and service is great!

The veggiemuffilino here is mmm mmm good. If your wondering what that is. It''s a veggie panini that is trying to be a muffelleta. 

This is a small icecream shop/ restaurant. They have a good sounding menu especially if you are looking for a cheap healthy option, but it isn't too nice inside, salt was nowhere to be found and they don't have a bathroom in the place. However there is some seating outdoors. Some of the sandwiches and salads are pre-made. I saw them sitting there after I ordered. Luckily the veggiemufalino wasn't one of them. 

Service was far from stellar. The guy working the counter was confused by the Yelp check in offer. He then didn't give us a receipt and charged us double for a sandwich. Mind you that he also needed to be summoned by bell to work. 

My sammy was really good. So I say take your chances, but don't be expecting 5, 4, or even 3 star dining at this place.

It was our first visit and it was AMAZING!!! OH MY WOW!! The food was delicious. All made from scratch to order. We consider ourselves Foodies, so we ordered 4 entrees, apps and dessert to try different things. We were NOT disappointed in anything. The Mango Chicken was heavenly...if you like (love) mangoes like I do.....this is the dish for you.  The owner works tirelessly and was so kind and friendly. We WILL be going back. We have found our new go to place!!!
It makes me sad every time I go there now. What used to be the best poke place in town, now leaves me unhappy since their expansion. More expensive, smaller portions, and lack of familiar employees.

New to the area and recently tried this place out. Since then I've been going back weekly, sometimes even twice a week. Great taste every time, fresh ingredients, amazing juicy meats. To top it all off they are one of the most reasonably priced places in the city!
This is my favorite sushi spot. The quality of service is impeccable. The best sushi in town. Everyone should try sushi sushi at least once. I promise, you will not be disappointed.

Couscous is probably my highest recommended restaurant.  I've been lucky to have moved around and to have traveled internationally, and I have to say the quality of food, service, and atmosphere at Couscous is amazing compared to a lot of the places I've been.  The ambience is extremely relaxing, ideal for a romantic date or out with friends.  I'm in love with all the food I've tried, especially the vegan Moussaka: it has perfect spicing, perfect texture, generous portion, and it's one of those foods that is both delicious and healthy -- amazing.  I recommend it with the Tzaziki, also one of the best things I've ever had.  The Harira soup is out of this world, make with chickpeas, lentils and spices in a tomato base.  My husband is addicted to it and I get it for my toddler son all the time.  I haven't tried it yet but I hear that the Moroccan Lemon Chicken is extremely tasty.  Probably my favorite dish for non-vegetarians is the Chicken Shish-kebob.  I've also tried the Appetizer Sampler which I highly recommend!!  Really, check it out.  Without fail all of the dishes and entrees are remarkable.

I had dinner at Ruth's Chris this past Friday night. I've tried their Center City location before so I already knew what to expect. I knew it would be expensive but I also knew it would be good :) 

I was with a party of 9 so we decided to share appetizers and sides. I think we ordered one of each side. The lollipop lamb chops were amazing! The asparagus was another one of my favs. The garlic mash was awesome as well. Oh and I cant forget the crab cakes! Nothing was bad but those were my favorites. 

For my entree I ordered the T-bone steak. The steak was to die for. It was cooked perfectly and was very flavorful. I knew I wouldn't finish the whole steak so I decided to save room for dessert instead. 

For dessert I ordered the molten lava cake. This is a chocolate lovers dream come true. Chocolate within chocolate with ice cream on top. :) It was much bigger than I thought it would be so I ended up taking that home as well. 

Although the service was great at the start, it diminished quickly. We had to call our waiter over to place our orders for the entrees. Towards the end, I had to ask 3 times for a refill on my soda.

After a very bad experience a few years ago, my daughter and I decided to give Desi Tadka another chance. We arrived a little before noon, for the lunch buffet. The decor of the place is really in need of an update (the yellow tablecloths are blinding), but we were here for the food.

The buffet items were hot and fresh and my daughter and I really enjoyed our meal. The naan was fresh and at one point when a new batch was ready, the owner stopped by every table to ask if they would like one. This was a nice touch. (I should note that this appears to be a new owner, different from the one I remembered seeing last time.)

Our server was attentive and friendly, refilling our water at appropriate intervals. We ate several dishes, including the butter chicken, vegetable rice, aloo gobhi, and another chicken dish. All were suitably tasty and well prepared. Best of all, we had no stomach issues this time around. 

All in all, a big improvement. Kudos!

Great new find! Went with a friend for brunch/lunch on Sunday. Decided to sit inside since it was ridiculously hot. Interior decor was very neat! Sort of like a gentleman's library at an old manor house, but not at all stuffy. One wall was covered in different framed photos and pictures, another wall had large glass cabinet/shelves filled with interesting chotskys. Taxidermied animal heads, but not creepy, very dignified. Anyway, I thought it was a cool vibe. Dining room is pretty small though! Service was very prompt, very attentive, and very friendly. We took our time, about 2 hours, and never felt rushed or like the waitress was resentful about our lingering. Lots of delicious things on the menu. Really wanted to try the short rib benedict, but healthier choices won out. Shared the chicken and feta salad, short rib tacos, and street corn appetizer. Salad was well-balanced, creamy feta but refreshing vinaigrette. The tacos were a bit of a letdown, however. Tortilla was nicely charred and about medium sized, but there was only a tiny, tiny bit of filling. Proportions way off, needed more meat and slaw or a much smaller tortilla. Left us feeling a little jipped, especially for $3 per taco. Street corn was delicious though, very generous portion, we even took some home. Overall, I was very pleased, and plan to return again with my husband.

I am a fan of the other Trias but not so much of this one.  I'm not sure if the bartender was pretentious or just shy and clueless but he seemed to be scoffing at some of our general questions about the menu and the venue. Veggie dishes were much smaller than necessary, a few more leaves of lettuce would have made me forget about the bartender's attitude.

When it rains, it pours. We arrived at 9 AM for breakfast, and we got our food at 9:45 AM. One meal was good, the other was so-so. We didn't get one single refill on our waters, and when we asked for extra hollandaise sauce, by the time we were finished and told our waitress about the lack of the extra sauce, the only reaction we got was "oh, didn't they bring that to you?".
We asked for a manager and waited for him to come out after 15 minutes. He picked up the bill, but I can only say, never again!
A bunch of people suggested this place for cheese steak. We were underwhelmed with our cheesesteak. The fries were fine, but we wish we tried somewhere else.

Taste of India! I haven't had Indian food in a very long time. I brought my mom to this restaurant and it was pretty good! I like the immersive culture as you enter the restaurant, the smell of cumin, masala and curry tantalizes your senses immediately when you walk in. Also, there was an Indian film on their televisions that was extremely entertaining.

We made sure to try everything and it was all quite delicious. Some of it I hadn't eaten in years! The samosas were great and were accompanied with quite a kick. It was a great mixture of spice along with other prominent tastes. 

The naan was delicious, the light crisp texture along with the other condiment options, was great for experimenting with flavors. 

The culmination of meat and fish was oh so good. I can't say enough about the place. I know they're under new ownership so the place is still slow moving. We were the only customers for a while but the staff gave us a warm welcome. 

Everyone! Please come check it out. I think this is a great representation of Indian food, so please come and try it out!
Beautiful ambiance. Great brunch menu. Highly recommend the burger, which was cooked perfectly. Tender and juicy burger.

We have been here several times and have never been disappointed! The restaurant is often crowded and very loud - so if you need more quiet, wear something warmer and sit outside under their heat lamps! I LOVE the clam fettuccini and their clam chowder is delicious! The head cook is quite a chef and watching him prepare the food is very entertaining. He does bang the pots LOUDLY - so be aware of your ears are sensitive. The restaurant has a nice ambiance to it and is cheaper than many in town. The wharf is fun and we love going for lunch as well - they will allow your dog at the outside table and even brought ours a fresh bowl of water - and I didn't even ask them! We will be back!

We LOVE THIS PLACE!!! Food always fresh and unique, margaritas are delicious  you only need 2  
Awesome services and food, high recommend!

Great brunch spot! This restaurant sits on the corner of a pretty busy area in New Orleans so its no surprise that they're always packed for brunch. So, there's basically two things you need to know about what to eat and what not to eat here. Number 1 - you NEED to order the bananas foster waffle. No need to even look at anything else. You're welcome. Number 2 - absolutely do not order the gumbo. The roux was soooo dark and the flavor was horrifying. I hope no tourist eats it and thinks that's what all the gumbos taste like here :(

Looking for a new watering hole. Reviews on yelp were mixed. The Village Pup is close to home it has been under several ownerships and we have tried them all. They have a great location in the township. They layout of the restaurant is great for a sports bar. Plenty of tv 's to view. Lots of good seating. 

The first new feature is the QR code on the menu for beer selections. Problem is it would not work unless my phone was connected to the WiFi. When I tried to connect it required a passcode. I asked our server for the code she could not provide it. Instead she used her phone to display the 41 craft beer selections. 

We started with the hot wings. They were over cooked and dry. The grown up grilled cheese was not as advertised. There was nothing special about it. The chicken filet sandwich was not as good as one I could buy at chick-Fil-a. The beer choices were great the place is great. Enjoyed the excitement when the flyers scored a goal. I did not enjoy the food.

My favourite place to take my family and friends! I like the Jerk chicken dinner! The portions are large! The Caribbean atmosphere is delightful! Listen to the sound of the islands
while you dine!
Mediocre food this time and subpar service. Our usual server is great but we didn't see her this time.

Located on the 3rd floor of the Hyatt regency. At first glance the menu seems weird because it has sushi listed and the bar food but it kinda works well for the all types of taste buds you get
Coming in and out of a hotel. The chargrilled oysters here were way better than expected. I really got aquatinted with this place when I was here for a week for work.

Are all the servers at Horizons trained origami masters? Scoff at my ignorance, I'm baffled by the whole "napkin thing". Every time you get up from your table, a member of the wait staff dashes over to fold your napkin back up into a triangonal pyramidal geometric configuration. I've tried hiding the napkin in various locations, but they're always able to hone in on the cloth with such speed... I'm almost anticipating the next time I dine at Horizons for magic tricks, you know, rabbits pulled out of a hat. 

The decor is a bit dated, and everyone always seems a bit too small for their chair, however, their food is exceptional and inspired. I like that they tend to steer away from faux-meat, however, I would like to see more vegetable, as opposed to soy-based, dishes on their menu. The last outing, my boy and I split an order of the sliders, he order the mushroom pub plate, while I got the paella (which should have been more accurately named a risotto). We always get the crème brûlée for dessert. Their beer selection is always on point, which is a huge bonus. The portions are generally small and a good pint can help to fill that extra space in your belly. 

I wonder how accessible the recipes in their cookbook are.....

for Midway Games only

decades later and this place looks almost the same as when I visited as a kid.  Some big differences:
Fascination is gone. 
They added a ticket-redemption area since there are lots of games that give out tickets.

Games have not changed, prizes are a little newer.  Shrek and Despicable Me were some that I recognized, that's how "current" they are.

Some games are still 5 for $1 but many are $1 to $2.  $1 for the "Horse Racing" games where you roll a ball into the hole to advance your number.

The center circus performance area still doesn't have a viewing area so people just crowd around the side watching, that can be a major pain.

Husband and I cruised the options around Newtown after a hike in Tyler State Park on a beautiful afternoon. MOD spoke to us and in we went. It was our first ever visit to this chain. We didn't scan any reviews.

Ho! MOD (for Made on Demand) offers salads or "assembly line" thin (round flatbread-style) crust pizza custom topped with an enormous (30+ item) list of traditional and not-so-traditional toppings and a choice of cheeses and sauces, available in sizes to please a single diner or two? In addition to custom pizzas, a handful of pre-suggested compositions are available. Ditto on the salads. Each pie/salad (by size) is a set price regardless of the number of toppings.

Since the other half and I didn't need to share a pizza (the "mini" size was truly perfect for one modest muncher), I gleefully loaded my pie with toppings that would make my husband cringe to eat on a pizza: pesto sauce, arugula, gorgonzola, vegan sausage, chick peas, broccolini, and more, while he ordered a pie with pepperoni, sausage, and mozzarella. The pies were done quickly in a quick blast from the wood-fired oven. We both enjoyed our creations immensely.

Freshly made caramel-pear iced tea, sweetened with a light hand, was a refreshing beverage to accompany our pies.

Staff were great at explaining the concept and pointing out the various options and crust sizes as we approached the counter. Everything appeared fresh and appetizing in the ingredient bins.

Cool concept and a tasty product. Two thumbs up from us!

We always order delivery from wing king and the milkshakes are to die for!! It's $5 and so delicious. I also ordered the mini cheese steak and it's a pretty large size for a mini, filled me up well. Fast delivery!

We only stopped in for a quick lunch once, but we WILL return.
Good food, good prices. Friendly staff.
Right at the train station, how convenient !

Ok, ok. I'm not a fan of anything chain-y (c'mon I live in New Orleans!) BUT I was surprised by this place! The Harahan location was busy, but quick! I ordered a salad made into a wrap and it was delicious! Price isn't too bad, considering most salad places are overpriced. I definitely didn't expect the quickness. Place was also clean and sleek and great for a quick drop in for something healthy. Thanks for the delicious Beet Street salad wrap, City Greens!

Showed up with a group of 9 people and was sat almost immediately. Food was great. Had the caramelized salmon with Parmesan cheese and saffron rice with green beens. The salmon just melted and tasted so good. Service was so so. They took the order, delivered it but never came back to see if we needed anything.
They have great blizzards. They even show you that the ice cream does not fall out of the cup. I come here every time my kid gets 100%on his school work.

They have decent seafood, although we waited a while for our food.

We went around 10 pm or so, and a lot of people were still there eating. 

I recommend getting the Peking Duck, jellyfish, shrimp, beef and mixed vegetables.

We live nearby and love Adobe Cafe! The pros:

Always quick service. 
Fair prices. 
We live the salsa. 
Generously sized salads. 
Tasty quesadillas. 
Nice little outside seating area. 
I like the artwork I the restaurant. 

Definitely a hidden gem in the area!

Tourist trap that I wasn't inebriated enough to enjoy. This place has all of the hallmarks of a classic, homestyle restaurant, but the food was bad and overpriced. I order a large shrimp creole and received a small bowl full of watery sauce with no shrimp and mediocre rice. My brother ordered fried catfish and fries. The catfish was okay, but not very well seasoned and the fries were limp and soggy. After a 45 minute wait and $40 later, I left sad and hungry. I would have had a better experience at say, Popeyes. Best thing I ordered was the red cream soda. Sorry Mother's!

I have been so eager to try this place since I saw them building it across from Sprouts. Ramen spots are becoming more popular here in Tucson and I was excited to see if this would make it into my top favs and it certainly did. We arrived on a chilly Saturday night (perfect weather for Ramen) and they had both drive through and dine-in options with outdoor seating. We opted for dine-in since it was chilly. Only two other couples so we sat on the opposite side where the bar was.

Ambiance:
Now the inside decor was amazing, very traditional. My husband who has been to Tokyo Japan said the set up reminded him a lot of the Ramen spots there. Very minimal design with pops of color. They have bar seating and booth seating. We didn't sit outside but I did see they had booths out there as well.

Service:
So sweet and wonderful. Our server I can't recall his name was not only super kind and helped recommend dishes for us but his energy made the experience so much better. We didn't feel rushed, he knew the perfect time to come and check in. I feel like it's hard to strike a balance not feel like your overwhelming guests but making sure they have what they need and he did that perfectly. 10/10 for service.

Food: 
To start we got a vegetable Gyoza. The dough was a green color which I never had before and I think whatever they added gave it a great garlic flavor. The dipping sauce was unique, it definitely grew on me but not crazy about it at first. It didn't taste like just soy sauce, it had a more tart/ sour flavor. They were steamed gyoza but fried on one side. It was nice to have both soft and crunch at the same time, I liked the texture it added. My husband and I both ordered the Kiwami Aka, a spicy pork broth but asked for no pork on top. As I mentioned My husband had been to Tokyo before and said the noodles were just like the Ramen spots there. A more brownish flat noodle compared to the white puffy noodles I find at the other Ramen spots in Tucson. The spice level was at about a 5. I love spice so I would've liked a little bit more but forgot to ask but it would be a little spicy for someone who is spice-sensitive. The flavor was super rich and flavorful. It combined well with the accompanying bamboo shoots, pickled onion, seasoned egg and green onion (tasted so fresh by the way). One of my favorite parts was the ladle they give you to slurp up the broth. It is so big which is perfect for adding a little bit a noodle and a little bit of egg for the perfect bite every time. 

All in all the place was wonderful. Great ambiance, fantastic service and even better food. It's not too big of a place inside so keep that in mind if you go during busier times. A great date night spot!

Would've given 4.5 if I could have. Only negative is the size of the building. Today was the 4th ave street fair and my coffee came out in about 30 seconds. Not too hot either! And a great selection of syrups and pastries.

Another great meal from that crazy Cubano. We love this place and start thinking about the fish and sandwiches from the moment we leave Orlando. Try  it once and you'll do your best impression of Arnie.... "I'll be back!"

F*** Yes. Ok my lips are still black from the squid ink from the massive amount of seafood paella ingested. I went with a group of friends who ordered half a  pig which made me want to go back to eating meat so bad. I'm getting ahead of myself, to start off the tapas were unreal. First the chips and tuna spread to start was beautiful and subtle but way better than bread and butter. The baked goat cheese and arugula salad was an awesome  mix of flavors. The octopus was the perfect mix of smoky and salty and cooked PERFECT. The crab stuffed peppers were small but held their weight because they were STUFFED with a huge chunk of crab. Not that canned BS either. The cheese platter was phenomenal... truffle honey... Nutella... figs.. blue cheese... manchego and apples (enough said). The bacon wrapped dates were gone before the waitress out the plate down so you can be the judge. The suckling pig was beautiful and hand carved right in front of us, I never saw a pig get demolished so quickly. I got the seafood paella which the hostess challenged me to finish because it was a disgusting amount of food... she never met a foodie like this though We got one of every dessert for the table and they were all equally extravagant. The staff from the manager to the hostess and waitresses were amazing. Beautiful place, amazing people... I will be back.

This location for BJ's has given me a few good laughs since it opened. The first time I went here, the service was the single worst thing I've experienced in my life at an established chain restaurant. Food was old, stale, sitting under a heat lamp and dried out until tasteless. And their servers were incompetent at best, weren't even familiar with their own beer menu (They tried to tell me they didn't carry Rogue's Dead Guy Ale, even after I pointed it out to them on their menu, took a manager to finally figure out that they did carry it). 
This time around the service got a lot better, but I keep feeling like my food is sitting under a heat lamp for a half hour before it comes to me. I think it was the fact that my Sante Fe Spring Rolls were lukewarm when they arrived, kind of gross. 
I think the funniest thing that happened to me was this last time I was there: I ordered a Union Jack IPA (mainly because their indigenous beer menu is OK at best) and 10 minutes later, some random waitress comes up to our table and says "Who ordered the Union Jack?" 
I raised my hand, then she attempts to hand me what appears to be a screwdriver or some other type of orange juice based cocktail. I said "no, no, I ordered the Union Jack IPA" 
She said "Wait, what did you order?" 
"Union Jack IPA" (then looks confused and again attempts to hand me the cocktail) 
"No, I ordered a beer...that is definitely not a beer" 
(Walks away without a word) 
About 20 minutes later, after I actually got the beer I ordered, I still see this waitress walking around the restaurant with the same drink in hand, trying desperately to pawn this thing off on someone. It was so sad, I couldn't be upset, so I just laughed. 
I guess the point I'm trying to make here is, go to the other Tucson location of BJ's, they actually know what the hell they're doing there.

This trendy little bar is truly "six feet under" as you have to walk downstairs from the sidewalk to get in the door. It is decked out in a spooky little theme, from the lighted shovels on the wall to the eerie music that is played. It all ties nicely together without being cheesy. 

We were only two of a few people here - mainly because we were drinking in the early afternoon; don't judge - but the allure of this place is undeniable. The bartender was friendly and helpful as we asked for tips on where to go for dinner that evening. She knew her way around a bottle of bourbon as our manhattan and old fashioned were dressed up just right. We ordered the hummus platter to snack on and were pleasantly delighted that the "bar food" was fresh and tasty. 

All in all, a great experience that I would return to have again and again. Six feet under gets two thumbs up!!
I love taco bell but i just think their missing sum kind of sauce but in my review i give them 5 stars.This taco bell doesnt taste like the rest its like they put a foot in.

After trying this gem in a strip mall on with west side of Oracle road, near Orange Grove, it was so good my husband and I returned again for dinner two days later.  On Sunday the small place was elbow to elbow with patrons watching football, on the 6 flat screen TV's behind the beautiful wood bar. Since I don't watch sports I think i'll stick to midweek dining. The first visit we started with sazeracs which were wonderful! So good we both had two rounds. The appeal of this place is the creole dishes on the menu.

The hushpuppies with crayfish is wonderful! They can be added as a side to any entry for a small charge.

The "pit" flavored hot wings were excellent. Last night I had the Spicy Haitian pulled pork and immediately had a runny nose and a smile on my face. It was pouring rain outside and all my woes were forgotten. My husband loves their gumbo! I had the Big Hippie (eggplant burger) my first visit and it was great. I especially like the buns  on their sandwiches; nice and glossy, buttery toasted before assembling the sandwich. The menu again is pretty limited, with about 6 appetizers, a few salads, a few entries (the Gumbo being one) and about 6 burgers/hot sandwiches. They  provide the option to make several of the dishes vegetarian, such as their lamb flat bread.  No desserts on the menu, but the owners assured us this will be changing in the new year. I'll keep my eyes open.

I am certain we will be back soon.
This place has a lotta fancy stuff but the food is just boring and bland. Way to over priced. Sucks and wont come back.. Good thing i live in Cali

I loved this place 2 years ago. We went to enjoy their happy hour and were disappointed to find their tacos and beans to have a significant amount of food modifiers and salt enhancers. The queso cheese dip jiggled like it was thickened with   Xanthan gum. You don't need to pull these shenanigans wit mexican food. I know your clientele has tender taste buds but my gosh the salsa is so bland and lifeless. Drinks were good, service was rushed and impersonal. You can do better Blanco.

Space: large and open with amateurish décor, feels like eating in a warehouse or school cafeteria.
Service: not so good, had to flag down servers.
Food: healthy menu of very bland food
Price: Inexpensive
Recommendation: walk less than a block south and eat at Sup for more flavorful fare served in a nicer space.

My hubby and I stopped in for some pizza. I was impressed that they offer a pizza without cheese on their menu! I can't have dairy so that works for me. My hubby had his with fresh mozzarella cheese on his. We also tried the meat platter for an appetizer.

My review is this: everything tasted good but the downsides were the bread on the appetizer was burnt and the pizza was soft and doughy. We expected crunchy pizza because the bottom crust is so thin. The dough also had black stuff on it that tasted burnt as well - I guess that's supposed to be from the wood burning stoves but I don't get it.

Our server was attentive but our pizzas came out before we finished our appetizer - luckily the table next to us was free so they parked the pizzas there until we finished our app. 

Another weird occurrence was a young man who seemed to be directing the staff. He was in a chefs outfit that was filthy dirty - I mean gray/ black dirty - not food dirty. Front, back, sides - not sure where he had been but I'm positive he should not have been directing the front of house dressed like that. 

Overall: It's pretty good and I might go back again but it's definitely not the best.  Much room for improvement.

The food is always good, but the environment in horrendous. It always smells like sewage or sewage+cleaning solution (if you're lucky) and the bathrooms are disgusting. I love Panera, but this restaurant is subpar and needs a lot of work. Also, you're either freezing or sweating. There is no in between

This is probably the best example of a local cult chain gone bad. The fact I've been forced to eat it 3 times today helped me provide my first yelp review. I had the food truck first, then thankfully the airport allows this place to corner the market on being one of the only places that serves alcohol. Yelp should have a negative star based on this fried trash. Or a special place in hell for people who like it. It's obvious the employees hate the place. Cheers.

Not that they need the additional pimpage (60+ reviews!), but Taco Bus is authentic goodness.  I missed an opportunity to go to one of the many taco buses in Oakland/San Francisco on my latest vacation, but I'm glad to have found one in my own 'backyard'. 

The 'guac' is fresh, tacos are yummy (hooray cilantro), and even the Hibiscus Lemonade is interesting.  Of course, you can't go wrong with a Mexican Coca-Cola (much better than the 'American' version).

From now on, the only places I'll go for good Mexican food are Taco Bus and Casa Tina in Dunedin.

Your run of the mill Chinese takeout place. It's been here forever so they must be doing something right. Decent, cheap and fast. Get a combo which includes egg roll and rice. They also don't deliver their food in styrofoam which is always a plus in my book.

This is the first time I ordered food from this place. Price is decent and the taste is great. They don't have a lot of vegetarian options. I ordered a bulk order for my  work team. Everyone in my team enjoyed the food. We will go to this place again. Currently, they don't offer sit down ag the restaurant. Only take out. They are very conscious about COVID precautions.

Went there based on reviews and was a little disappointed.  I ordered a burger and fries. The burger could have been seasoned more since it was homemade and not a patty.  The service was extremely slow. I was not overwhelmed by their customer service

As I paid for my bill I realized they did not give me the home made pickled wedges. When I asked he said oh we are out of them.  Could you have told me?

I was worried because the place looks super pretentious, but the food was outstanding, and the presentation was top notch. The part that surprised me the most is that even though they were very attentive, they were also very nice and personable. A very good experience all around... and the dishes are very different/interesting... but delicious!

Wait wait wait, I have not reviewed Nomad yet?? I am embarrassed. I have eaten here many times, most recently last night. Whenever I am craving crispy thin crust, I know I need Nomad. The crust is so thin- almost cracker like. Its great! 

Last night was Wine Wednesday (1/2 off bottles of vino!). We tried the Trenton pie, which we believed was cheese then sauce. There was cheese, but then the "sauce" was just clumps of plum tomatoes. Although not what we had envisioned, it was tasty and garlicky nonetheless and I would order it again. I do not like Nomad's Margherita nor plain pizza. The sauce is too sweet for me. The Spicy Sorpressata is a good bet as well, however it is not really spicy, so prepare to ask for red pepper flakes. 

Last night we had an issue with the table next to us (or should I say, they had an issue with us). Apparently we were being "too loud" (I promise you, we were not, and I am constantly cognizant of that fact). They felt the need to rudely scold us and ask us to pipe down. Hands down this is the most obnoxious thing I have ever experienced in a restaurant!!! Nomad is by no means a place to take your family for a quiet dinner. The walls are brick & the floor is tile; there is no noise canceling aspect to the place.  If the snob who felt the need to be the noise police is reading this, then you are a fun-sucker and you put a terrible damper on our mood! 

For this unpleasant interaction, the staff PROFUSELY apologized. They agreed that what the other party did was completely uncalled for, and re-sat them very far from us (thankfully!). They were so sorry that they brought out a complimentary Nutella Banana pizza for us to share. 
I have been wanting to try this for a while, and it definitely lived up to expectations. So delicious and crave-worthy.
 
I cant give 5 stars because its simply not the best pizza in Philly. Its good, but does not compare to my other favorites. Overall, great service, tasty pizza, and a good place to catch up with friends (and get a little loud doing so!)

You can't disagree with a great burger EVERYTIME!  On your next visit, please talk to Johnny he is the most positive man with a smile that hits the soul.  We leave there feeling great every time!  This is our go to place for burgers & fries when we have family and friends in town.

A great breakfast spot located in the french quarter. They had a lot of interesting and delicious options. I had salmon and avocado toast, and the rest of my party had brioche french toast, bbq shrimp and grits, cinnamon pancakes, and cinnamon french toast sticks. Our server was friendly and helpful; and they had paper straws!! Would definitely suggest stopping by for breakfast or lunch.

Everything that I have had from their menu has been awesome.  

The wings, hoagies and salad bar are all delicious.  

On Tuesday all of their platters are $2 off.  For $7.25 I got a large cheese steak (with onions and Whiz - Yup the real stuff), a larger order of fries, cherry peppers, coleslaw and a Cesar salad.  It's enough food for two lunches.

I have to say that the cheese steak was best I have had in a long time.
Good pancakes, great ice cream but nothing special. Waitstaff was friendly but not overly noteable. The view was outside Jackson square which wad nice. It was average.

Came to this well known local establishment on a recommendation of a friend.  Casual atmosphere and friendly staff.  I ordered fried chicken which was juicy on the inside a crisp non-greasy crispy crust.   The sides I ordered were Mac and cheese and collard greens. Theses were not my favorite. The corn bread was great.

So I've got two conflicting opinions here. I recently went to Katie's on Clayton and wasn't sure if this place was the same. I'm thinking no because I liked the food at the other place better, but I will admit I did not try the pasta here yet and that is my own fault.

Went here for lunch with my bro and I got the lunch special with the salad mista and the pear pizza. The salad was decent if not a bit small but I wasn't impressed with the pizza. Just thinking about pear plus procuitto should be mouthwatering but it was a but off for me. My brother had the pizza margarita and was blown away. I tried it and I will be the first to tout its freshness but I wasn't as excited as he was.

What stood out to me were the home made pastas (which I curiously didn't try) and the home made bread which was pretty fantastic. The wait staff was also great but it was kind of hard to tell who they were sometimes since they were all dressed like me: jeans and casual top. 

Because of the location, and because my brother will most likely want to come back, I can see myself here again. I'll be sure to try the pasta. But for what I'm paying I really did expect a bit more wow factor.
Very friendly staff amazing food and environment we just moved here love downtown great place to hang out

Has a pretty good selection of foodstuffs.  Like the interesting meat and fish department--especially that you can actually buy living fish.  The only drawback is that most of their employees don't speak good English so it is hard to communicate with them.  Also, a manager I spoke to the day I was there didn't seem to have a grasp on how to treat a customer cordially.

Most of my dining experience here is ordering pizza to go.  It's excellent!  The few times I've been in the dining room have been a very pleasant experience.  This is an upscale restaurant - not a run of the mill chain restaurant.  I expect better treatment here.  See review by Priscilla G.  She was generous with 2 stars.  

A nice touch I've seen at some chain restaurants is that the manager walks around and checks on the guests.   Maybe Piccolo Trattoria should try that.

Great bakery - have it all - excellent pastries, great bread as stated by other yelpers, the coffee was also first rate.  A bit small and sometimes crowded.  Either was a big step up from Starbucks and they don't even have expresso.
Food was delicious and the atmosphere was enjoyable. Service was slow and it was difficult to get the servers attention at times.

This place is terrible! The place smelled, the service was terrible, the food was not good at all. You can't advertise you have gluten free options when you do not. It's basically false advertisement when it says ask your server for gluten free options and the server and manager and everyone says we don't have anything but are leading towards that way. Our server seemed annoyed that she was even working. We had 4 ppl and all the food was mediocre. My husband got French toast that was plane Jane  looked like it was made from wonder bread aNd could be done at home- what a rip off! Not worth the wait at all!

I always come her for the pizookie! Tonight I also had the fish n chips and the sliders as an appetizer. BJ's is always a fun time. The atmosphere is always buzzing. Tonight I had an extra sassy waiter named Adrian. He was very attentive to my table's needs. 

Bj's is overall average in terms of food. Everything I've ever ordered has been just good, but I feel a little reluctant to pay $15 for an entree there.

One of my favorite bars in Tucson.  Really friendly staff and for how busy this place can get, the bartenders are always very attentive.  Lots of beers and drink specials to choose from... and I should probably suggest you try the Harry Potter shot at least once.  The shot itself is mehhh but the presentation is pretty epic.  Related: this place smells amazing because of these shots.  They set those suckers on fire and they're topped with cinnamon so there's always an aroma of French toast in the air. This place is great and I would love to give it 5 stars but the bathrooms are atrocious.

I'm sorry for writing a bad review such as this but my food seriously tasted like they are not trying to be authentic but trying to convince the masses to eat here. We went to a place called Border Cafe and that was also a huge spot ... but they were at least good. This spot seemed like ketchup was their mother sauce. The service was exceptional but that wasn't enough to save the lunch for us. I did a bit more googling and realized the owners also have other local restaurants that I absolutely love so I'm not sure how this location's food is so off? Side note ... my coworkers liked the food so maybe I'm too picky.

Favorite Sonic. Decent food (what do you expect?), great service. One employee here, I think her name was Grace, was an absolute pleasure. My order came back slightly wrong, and she was very apologetic and gave me the correct food I ordered plus a voucher for a free meal! Great customer service. Give that girl a raise!

Don't waste your time and money. $54 for a burger, fries and one old fashioned. Service was very slow, burger was ordered medium rare and was well done.
With all the great food in Philly this was a real disappointment. The only thing cool about this place is the name.
