I came here the other day for a late lunch with a girlfriend and ordered the Bahn Mi with pork.The staff were very nice and there was a quick turn around for food. I have to say I wasn't super thrilled about the Bahn Mi though, which is unfortunate because it is one refreshing meal if it's done right. The difference with this Bahn Mi and the traditional ingredients is the hummus that was put in (usually it's just pickled veggies and meat). To the restaurant's defense they did have it on the menu as a veggie Bahn Mi with the option to add pork. The other ingredients were good, but I think I would skip the hummus if you're looking for the more traditional style sandwich. Our server was really kind and offered us a donut for free each since they throw theirs away at the end of the day every day and we took her up on it. We split one cinnamon and one traditional with icing and it both were delish!

I ate at the Maya Cafe on a Friday in late April with a friend.  We did not have a reservation, but were able to walk in at 7:45 and be seated right away.  It was a little loud until the two tables nearest us cleared out.  Our waitress must have felt busy, because she handed us some menus without a smile or an introduction, and disappeared.  I'm not very outgoing, so I usually prefer the less chatty servers, but this girl's behavior verged on rudeness.

We received our salsa and chips quickly.  I liked the chunkiness of the salsa, but I would have liked a little more depth to the flavor, instead of just tomatoes and onions.  Nonetheless, it was quite good, and the chips had the right amount of salt.  My friend and I also split a guacamole appetizer, which many reviews have called a "large" portion and "bland."  I can't agree with either comment--there was just enough for the two of us, and it was well-seasoned, although simple.

We both ordered the fish tacos as our main course, and these are responsible for the star that brings this restaurant from three to four.  Three soft wheat tortillas wrapped around crispy, perfectly hot, perfectly cooked, flaky white fillets, with a little guacamole and pico de gallo inside each, seasoned perfectly with something that mingled with the lime juice I squirted over it and transported me to food heaven.  The rice served with it was bland and unremarkable, until mixed with the delicious juices dripping from the tacos.  I hated to finish that meal.  I dream of going back.

We also ordered a margarita each, which I liked but was not overwhelmed by--it was good, but not spectacular.  However, I do not drink much, so i can't compare it with other establishments' margaritas.  Maybe it's the best in St. Louis, I just wouldn't know.

The food came readily, and our waitress, while taciturn and unfriendly, was at least quick and efficient.  However, I was more than a little annoyed when, as we were talking after having finished our meal, we were left over twenty minutes without water refills, as though now that we had paid, our waitress had completely written us off.  Finally, just before we got up to go, she stalked over from the bar where she had been lounging with a water refill.  As we left, she failed to acknowledge us with a farewell or even to make eye contact.  I have rarely encountered that level of coldness in a server.  Maya Cafe can thank their fish tacos for making me overlook her poor attitude, because I would definitely like to come back someday.

We were here for a Saturday night dinner Dec 30th, with another couple. Made reservations online. When we arrived we mentioned we preferred to sit in the bar area, online reservations don't offer the option to select. The hostess stated there were no available tables, we saw at least five. They were several in the back. It had snowed all day and it appeared not very busy. We felt she could have made a little effort to accommodate us, we felt she was a tad rude.
The decor is fun rustic and where we sat was very nice. Our waiter was satisfactory. Twice we had to ask the young man cleaning tables to get the waiter to order more drinks.
The food was wonderful. Most of us had the BBQ pork tacos, red onion slaw, delicious! Not too sweet. The guaq was perfect, very creamy. Our margaritas were very small, ice filled, very expensive. For a table of four our bill was 250. Not including tip. Three of us had three margaritas each, they were the specials. They were $11 each. Remember they are small. The one guest had a few drafts. So the poor rating is a reflection of the hostess being short with us and the overpriced, very small margaritas.

Opal was a great place a few years ago. We believe it has stepped away from greatness with exorbitant prices. I'm happy for the owners that the place gets very full, a lot of people like it obviously, but it's very noisy as a result and we're not hot on sitting for long periods in a lot of noise. I see we're not the only ones who find it noisy. Maybe they need to do something to the walls?

I raised my original star rating to 3, because I'm new to Yelp and Opal's food is better than "Meh".  They won't get 4 or 5 though for the reasons I've already stated. I got a long, friendly message from the owners, demonstrating that they are serious about social media. Sites like Yelp have certainly added hours to the work restaurant peoplehave to do now. 
I don't think its' realistic, though to expect a restaurant to fix the noise. It's just people talking too loud in groups, which is common in the US anyway. Another idea would be seating groups in a different room, but again, not really practical.

Update: walked by there this summer and it was so loud there that the waitress was literally shouting to be heard... at the sidewalk tables! I know this is what some diners like, it's part of the vibe they enjoy, but it isn't for everyone so be warned, go there with people you DON'T want to talk to.

The food was 5 stars but For me the initial treatment drops them to 3. The food and service was impeccable (once seated). They were super friendly. I do admit that it is one of the hot spots in the city right now and we did not have a reservation. That is my fault. 

What I did not appreciate is the fact that the host made it sound as if I could quickly get a seat at the bar when I called expressing my concern because it was a birthday dinner. Further more our wait for a place to sit was an hour and a half for two. Again my fault for waiting that long but after the 25 minutes we were told it would take it was hard to just leave. It did seem to me the common theme was they would tell the potential customer 25 minutes regardless of what they thought.  I mean they should have a more truthful expectation for they customer rather than trying to keep the bar seating full. 

I would say if you don't have a reservation don't waste your time. There are so many other places in the city to eat. 

My real hope is that the management sees this and they give more attention to what they tell the customer about the bar wait or consider making the bar reservation as well. 

With a reservation I would go again.

WARNING: IF YOU PLAN TO DINE HERE, MAKE SURE YOU HAVE SOMEONE WATCH YOUR VEHICLE WHILE YOU EAT.

On 1/12/2014 evening, we parked our car in the front parking lot of this restaurant and dined for about an hour. Upon reaching our car to go home, we found our rear passenger window broken into and several items were stolen from the vehicle. One of us ran inside to notify the manager. She came outside to inform us that this was the THIRD incident of a vehicle break-in of THIS WEEK! She said she would go back inside to notify Tucson Police Department and noted that there were no security cameras on the building. Not even sure if she called because she went back inside and never bothered to come back out to reassure us or anything. As a restaurant manager, I might assume she'd try to save face by offering her sympathies, but all she said was that this was the third time it has happened and I can call TPD for you. End of story. Not at all impressed with the lack of safe parking lot or lack of caring service.

Food is good. Have really good drinks and food come out very hot and fresh compared to most restaurants. Only reason I am giving 4 out of 5 is because their greens are frozen and I expected the mardi gras pasta to be a bit more flavorful considering this is NOLA. Overall service was good.
Great place to eat!  Long lines though if you get there after 1000. Had the biscuits & gravy, bonuts, mimosa, iced coffee, and the blacklock(?).  Not disappointed with anyone of them!

The food here was ok but definitely not exceptional. The waitress was nice but the food took a long time to come out. Coffee was just ok. I probably wouldn't rush back here with so many options in town. There was nothing to make it stand out...

Great place to spend an afternoon.  

They need a few more shops to browse, but we didn't have any trouble spending an entire afternoon here.  There are a variety of activities and the aquarium is next door.

We spent most of our time at Wine Design, Tina Tapa's and watching the Carnival cruise ship in port prepare for departure.

I loveeee fresh kitchen and I love it even more now that there's a closer location and bigger! The parking in the south Howard area was really annoying but this one is more accommodating. I genuinely like every side and base they offer and most of the proteins. The sweet potato noodles and kale slaw are my usuals for the base. I switch up on the veggies always because they're all cooked so perfectly and seasoned well, but this time I see the with the green beans for a nice crunch and the mushrooms of course because I have a clear obsession lol. The almond baked chicken is a MUST I need to try to make that at home one of these days because it's such a good idea as a Panko replacement. The BBQ chicken is a little saucy but still good. They have an array of sauces to chose from as well which comes with one complimentary choice. It's hard to chose between the coconut sriracha and cucumber jalapeño for me. They also have an extra bar of add ons and I pick the salsa to add on top. I don't think they should charge for the extras considering the price is already pushing it but it's understandable. Cheese and avocados are a little pricier to provide I suppose. I also got "The Boss" fresh pressed juice from their daily beverage section. Super fresh and not bitter for a green juice. There's quite a few to chose from including coffee choices. All around this is a great healthy choice for lunch. I'm always craving it after a good workout!

I was very impressed with this  restaurant. the omelette was very delicious and the potatoes were very crisp. the only reason I'm not giving the restauraunt a 5 is because my food came out 20 minutes after my parents food.

I've been going down to St. Clair County with my boyfriend to visit his family every summer for the past 4 years. We always do different things when we stay out there but one thing doesn't change: We go to Show-Me's.

The food is always tasty and never underdone. The Toasted Ravioli aka T-Ravs are awesome. Perfectly seasoned and never greasy. Always a treat for this Chicago gal who can't find a place up here for them. And their wings: some of the best I've ever had! Get them with Hero Sauce. Great flavor and heat to them.

What's also great for this place is that it isn't gouged by Cook County tax and such which means me and the bf can each get 10 wings each, an order of T-Ravs and a huge mug of beer each and walk out with our pockets still intact.

See you in July, Show-Me's!

The brisket here I found to be a little dry but the ribs were good. I found the place clean and the staff was friendly enough. I do really like the way the place looks with the wood decor and the actual fire place is a nice touch. I don't know if it's a great place to go out for dinner but it's great for a quick lunch with coworkers. It's a little pricey for lunch but it's worth it every now and then.

Service started out great then slowly declined as the meal went on. Food was all good, I wouldn't say great but good. Slightly overpriced id say but probably right along the lines of red lobster. Service definitly lacks tho. We waited for over 15 minutes to get our bill. Then another 15 for her to take and run the card. A table was seated next to us and got up after 10 minutes no one coming to there table. Very unorganized place. Food was cold in some spots, you could tell it was rushed together but all in all good. The place was hardly halfway full too so I'm scared to think of what a night would be like when it was.

I was really psyched to get some Puerto Rican food. I've seen this place under the El, and wondered how it was. 

I had a friend tell me it was decent, so I went there one day.

The girl at the bar was very sweet, but I just really couldn't get over the flipping around on the prices. I felt like I was right back in Puerto Rico having to scrutinize every bill to see what they slid on there. 

The receipt was not itemized, so I really came out unclear as to why my meal was 4 dollars more. The meal itself was pretty amateur. The cerdo frito was ok, I guess. The rest of the sampler, the quesadilla was soggy and amateur. The tostones were tostones, and I just expected so much more for close to $15. The fried chicken were like little rubber balls. The presentation was bad too. They through it in a styrofoam container that I would get at a papi store for $4.


The food alone would be 3.5 stars, but the fact that they are still handing out menus with false (old,) prices is what got me. It would have been one thing if she handed me the menu, and let me know in advance that the pricing was off due to pandemic inflation, but they were very "islander" about it, and handed me a mystery bill with no explanation. Slick and slimy.

The neighborhood is changing - you guys can charge $15, but you gotta be on point, and up front, and step your game up in general. Sloppy!

On our last night in New Orleans, we decided to live it up and eat somewhere new an a little higher end.  

We decided last minute on the Chophouse and therefore decided to just walk in without a reservation. While I understand this was 100% our bad, the hostess was a bit rude about it. 

Moving beyond that, the food was hands down amazing. I had my steak cooked "cajun style" and it was perfect. Not too spicy but something I'd only be able to track down in New Orleans.

What made the meal a solid 5 for me was the loaded baked potato, wheeled to your table on a cart and prepared exactly to your liking. 

Definitely a little pricier but absolutely worth it.

The food was good and the wine wasn't overly priced. I got the fillet, and my fiancé got the burger of the month. The fillet was good, but the burger was way better!! The burger was very tasty, and juicy. We got a bottle of the prisoner, which was fabulous. My fiancé refilled our wine glass the whole time, which I do wish the server paid a little more attention to. Other then that we enjoyed ourselves, and will be back, especially for the burger!!

I just can't get enough of this place.  

We just went back for the first time since I became a Vegetarian.  I got the Vegan Steak Strip Burrito and Butternut Squash Tostada, and oh my GOD.  I was so happy there were no children around, I was seriously having a When Harry Met Sally moment, only I wasn't faking!

Ok first of all, the tostada is topped with butternut squash, onion, tomato and cilantro and is just so fresh and perfect.  

Next, the burrito... I have become accustomed to making sure there's no meat or dairy on my food since I know it will make me sick.  I opened it to find what I thought was ACTUAL steak.  I had to make my husband taste it just to let me know.  Turns out it's a seitan steak strip and I couldn't tell the difference.  

For vegans and vegetarians, they also have vegan steak strip tacos, tofu fajitas, vegan tamales and something else that I can't remember.  Hmmm... wonder if they'd make a butternut squash burrito.  

Anyway, the prices are still high, but for what you get.... the vegan burrito is $8.  I'd still pay it.  

They are also now open 24 hours on the weekend.

The food was alright, but the service was the real winner. The server tried really hard, and he was wonderful. The staff was devoted to getting us exactly what we wanted. Service like this is worth another visit.

The spicy wings were good. The spice hits you right away but doesn't linger too long so you're not dying the whole meal.

The soy could use more soy.

Both are much tastier the next day straight out of the fridge!

Gerst Haus is a fun dining experience and has tasty food, if you like German fare. However, the Gerst Haus is less about the food and more about the atmosphere.

The atmosphere was fun with a tuba, drum and accordion trio which doled out some fun musical ditties and sang happy birthday twice. Watch out for the forced chicken dance. It can be irritating.

The staff, from the front door to our server, was aloof and seemed very disinterested in us. Our server didn't want to offer suggestions or even explain what the different items were. Perhaps it fit with the "German experience". Vee don't care vat you like. Just order somesing. So authentically German, that I felt like I was in the motherland.

Our server Barbara was aces, steered us to all the great choices. Started with 10 wings, 5 garlic Parmesan and 5 Honey garlic. Wow great wings, crispy but not dry with fantastic sauce. I decided to go with the grown up grilled cheese with a slice of tomato and bacon with crispy Tater tots.  Delicious, the combination of provolone and cheddar has great idea! Oh yes I forgot about the Beer, it was perfectly cold. 
Great place, nice atmosphere, & great service and staff!

What happened? 

We order the same thing every time, we used to pay not long ago, $45 to $50 including the tip. A month later,$58 or so.  Today I was going to order,
And it was $89??? Sorry, your sushi is o~k , but it's  made out of rice, not Gold!

Navigating through the parking lots that connect this restaurant to the outlets is a nightmare. The Texas Tea was very good but the burger I had simply didn't leave anything but an average experience.

My husband and I enjoyed a date night here! It was amazing food and the service was great!!! The food was fresh, and cooked perfectly. I highly recommend this restaurant! They accept reservations through open table.
This place is simply amazing, especially if you have a family with small children, and it is a nice sunny day. There is wonderful outdoor seating, and the pizza is great, too. Highly recommended.

I come here for business lunches or coffee meetings a couple times a month.  There is ample seating and the dining area is nice and bright.

Panera food is Panera food is Panera food is Panera food.  So, nothing to write home about, but they do have a nice selection of sandwiches and salads, and I do like that you can see how many calories each dish has in it....helps to make your choice a little healthier, I think, that is, unless you are craving the Mac n Cheese....in which case, those 600 calories are worth it!

Plenty of parking, friendly staff, and they are quick to clean off and wipe down the tables after someone gets up to leave.

I love love love this place. I love the Louisiana and seafood influenced meals. The drinks are great. My favorite are the spiked coffees. The biscuit beignets are tasty. If they ask if it's your first time there say yes and you might get a free order or beignets!

We made a reservation for my birthday at 5:00 for 10 of us. 7:00 rolled around and we were still enjoying ordering drinks, food, and visiting; we were told we needed to leave because they had a reservation at 7:00. Fine, have your reservation but at least let us know at the beginning we only have a 2 hour time limit. Put a sour taste in our mouths. Won't be back.

This place fucking sucks. The employees are slow as fuck. The food sucked. There was about 3.5 pounds of half cooked, fake grilled peppers and onions on my breakfast burrito. The manager and cashier were both rude to a Spanish family. Fuck this place.

I placed an order through the Little Cesar's website on 12/31/21. They use Door Dash for deliveries, which I was not aware of. My order was never delivered. I called and received a confirmation number for a refund. Now, almost 2 weeks later after waiting on hold for customer service for over an hour to check on my refund, I'm told that I will not receive a refund. They stated I entered the wrong delivery address and it could not be delivered. This is complete bs! I spoke to a supervisor and am now waiting for a manager with customer service to call me (which I'm sure they never will). I will NEVER order for Little Cesar's again! $54 may not be a lot of money to this company but it's a huge amount for me to spend as a special treat for me and my kids.

I am super picky about bread, and typically do not like sandwiches - but Middle Child was really good! I had the Turkey Reuben, with lots of turkey and really good toasty bread. My husband had the Phoagie, extremely tasty and also vegan friendly. The portions were large, I had enough to take home for a 2nd meal. I was hoping that they would be served with chips or a pickle but there were no sides. As for seating, are a few tables available but they are first come first served. Also FYI they do not serve breakfast sandwiches after 11:30am.
All the people in my group who ordered burgers had terrible stomach aches for the evening, including me. Makes me wonder if they use beef with pink slime. I will not go there again.

I am a not Thai food fan and I don't think I should have authority to judge this restaurant until one day my friend brought us there.
it was a mid week day night the restaurant was not busy.
the server Ed sit us and ask for us the drink. since they have bar. I order a Thai beer ( $ 5.00). It was not bad at all. we order Thai summer roll with peanut sauce. it was so good. and the dinner for me was Pai Thai with Beef  which rice noodle with beef serve with Thai special sauce. it was really out of this world.
Our waiter Ed is a nice guy with all profession. he give us a good service and knowledge of Thai food. and he also mention the restaurant can free delivery the food to your house. I think this is one of my regular spot for my dine out place.
I Love Pai Thai Restaurant and I love there food.
Good Luck Pai Thai and Good Luck Ed.

Jake

From Philadelphia
Tried the Westchase version of this pizza place and it was even better then the one downtown! If you haven't tried this place... You gotts!

of all the places i visited in nashville, the soda parlor was definitely one of the most unique. we stumbled upon this newly-opened hidden gem while exploring the marathon mall before heading into corsair distillery for a tour and tasting (if you're visiting from out-of-town, you should do both of these things). 

we met olan. (be jealous)
he's the coolest. he's super friendly, kinda odd in the best way, and has an incredible approach to business which is especially admirable given today's economic climate. i LOVE to support awesome businesses and genuine business owners/ good peoples. you should too. (and look him up on youtube. prepare to LOL)

we met some super cool employees who chatted with us about soda, ice cream, olan's videos, and nashville tidbits. the soda parlor was still pretty new, so i'm super excited to see how much of a following and community it's cultivated over the last year or so. 

i'm not the biggest soda drinker, but i thoroughly enjoyed a cold root beer while perusing the fun shirts for sale. boyfriend loved his float... the vanilla ice cream was yummy.  

we bought a few shirts and sweatshirts for ourselves and gifts for friends. really good quality, super comfy, and i want more! (good thing they're available for sale online... doooo it). 

i adore this simple, quirky concept. arcade games. indoor and outdoor seating. a comfy friendly environment. some clothes, in case you spill soda on yours. and the community gaming events and movie nights are a splendid addition. i really can't wait to return (too bad nashville is so far away from nj).

Hotel food, but the wings were just what I needed after a week of eating . . . not wings.  

I'm a wing fan, but I readily admit that I've never been to buffalo, I don't frequent bars very often, I've only fallen in love with blue cheese over the past few years (the Amish make a great blue cheese, FYI), and I don't really like super hot wings. 

What I do like are juicy wings that aren't overly breaded or fried, which is exactly what Champions provided. 

I don't drink, so I can't comment on the drink selection.  I can say, however, that for a sports bar this place delivers--you'll find more TVs than you need.  The service was ok as well . . . nothing to write home about, but prompt and quiet.  

I also tried the veggie burger on a second visit and found that pretty good as well.

A longtime valued customer of Rose Cafe. This is a local favorite. They know exactly what I like. I don't even have to ask. Being Mexican coming from the best Mexican cook (Grandma) their Wuevos Rancheros con Carne is the best. I take all of my out of town friends here for this masterpiece. And they all come away satisfied and happy! The restaurant is alway clean and inviting. The chips are fresh and yummy. The staff always has the nicest smiles. Food time is fast and the food well that is the BEST!

We came to Philadelphia with no plan and a dying iPhone.  This night could have turned bad quickly.  After driving circles around the city we decided to quit and park near some strange pregnancy building with blocks exploding out of it.  Pretty sweet.  

I decided we needed to walk towards the water.  That seemed like the area to be.  And oh hot damn it was.  DAVE AND BUSTERS!!! i screamed with delight.  We scampered past some awful smelling places and into D&B searching for the shooting game with the best price and best graphics.  AHH!! Card not AUTHORIZED?!? Oh it's ok, just go to the front and if you bought your card in another state they'll authorize it to work there and then u can shoot it up til dawn! ok until 12am on Sundays.  

Unfortunately like all Dave and Buster's, there's an issue of messed up guns not reloading or shooting nowhere near where you're pointing it because some crazy ass kid smashed the game to death.  I had a big issue with a shotgun.  But maybe if enough people go they'll replace their damn guns and I can get to killing zombies.  Or dinosaurs.  Or bad GIs.

Excellent lunch menu!! My husband was raised in Argentina and this is one way to make him feel like he's dining back home... today we tried the lunch menu.. perfectly proportioned meals at a reasonable price..the Picadillo was a little salty for my taste as was the Milanese ( hence the 4 star rating) but the black beans were amazingly delicious .. We started off with empanadas beef, spinach and ham and cheese.. love the baked dough !!!! Will be back again for dinner next visit...

I have been to Mi Nidito several times and I have never been disappoined. Everything you order is delicious and very, VERY filling. Yesterday I had a shredded beef chimichanga enchilada style (where the chefs cover the chimichange with enchilada sauce and cheese then melt it under a broiler) and was satisfied and full for about 5 hours. My two sons (who can be pretty picky) love the open cheese crisp. My husband had a chimichanga too with red chillie and was pretty good, but not as good as the shredded beef. If you do go, make sure you go while working up an appetite, usually pretty long wait, and in Tucson in July, it sucks to wait outside, although I did kill the time while ordering a delicious margarita. The only downfall was our waitress was really slow and forgot our rice and beans......If you are in tucson, def a place to try.

HORRIBLE SERVICE!!!!!!!!!!
Its friday feb 13th and we are here with the kids and waited in line for 25 minutes for the lady to forget our order THREE times!!!!! How do you screw up 2 salads and a cheese quesadilla order....  The staff was all screwing off, not changing gloves after handling RAW MEAT...  "I dont have steak, we are out if that" blah blah blah...
Completely unprofessional and rude. 

Then they turned down TWELVE people!!! Because they were out of meat!!!!

WE WILL NOT BE RETURNING HERE

I love their sangrita margarita! It's fantastic. I wish it was like $1 cheaper though ( it's $9). There queso is a must with chorizo and the pickled peppers. If you only get one app get that. I love the salsa and guacamole. Very fresh which is great. The tacos are delicious. Usually 2 does it for me! I love the shirt rib one. That's my fav! You must try them if you haven't yet. I love sitting out in the patio in the summer time!

I have been working at 3 Days for the past three years (irony I know!!). What folks don't know is that I actually change what college I was attending just to stay here. I have thoroughly enjoyed my years here and would repeat my decisions a thousand times over. The owner, Colleen Dobbs, sincerely cares about her employees and her customers. You need only look at the local meats from Goose, the house made sauces, the fresh pour over coffee, and the handmade catering display to know that tie heart and soul goes into this place. I can honestly say I have beer gotten tired of eating these delicious goodies and simply love to share them with my friends. It's been an honor and a privilege
Very friendly. Consistently good food. Great lunch buffet is a nice way to try new dishes.

Worst steak ever. To think I came to Philly for that.
They just slapped some seasoning-less meat on bland bread and serve you the whole soggy mess and expect you to love it. My cab driver called it a tourist trap yet the line was long out the door.
Oh well, love and learn. Go to Ishkebibbles instead.
Just very yummy food.  Everything on the menu is wonderful.!  Wonderful sauces too....and that Crack Pie is YUM!!
Really great space and wonderful food. The octopus and seared okra were my personal favorites. Highly recommended if only for the atmosphere alone.
Best Irish coffee on the planet, ask for Brent to make it! Awesome food too. Cool building that is over 200 years old!

so happy there's a thai place in chalmette now!! it's really convenient especially when i don't feel like driving out for food. i mainly order take out from here, because it's just faster for me. but the food here is great. you can adjust the spiciness levels (probably necessary for this area... if u know what i mean ;)) and it's really quality stuff for the area. portion sizes are huge, i'm always guaranteed to have leftovers. so far i've had the pad thai, the pad see ew, and the yellow curry. they've all been super good. i'll have to say, it's not the best ever thai food i've had, but for the location and price, i'll take it.

Recently I had the pleasure of being invited to the Capital Grille for a friends birthday. I didn't really know what to expect, so I went into it with an open mind. We arrived for our 8:30pm reservation and were instructed that our table would be available shortly and were told to wait at the bar. This was somewhat off-putting, I mean what's the point of having a reservation, right?
 
 Before we got to the table, the bartender asked for our party's name in order to transfer our tab, WOW! They earned points with me for this, definitely.  I hate waiting at the bar, then having to pay my tab when I'm just going to eat anyway.
 
 The menu had a large selection of items, I would say leaning heavily to the seafood/steak items than anything else. Their wine list was quite extensive, even though we didn't order any it was nice to see that they were very well prepared had we. The different kinds of bread at the table were all delicious, I could almost eat my weight in all of them. Now, the food...

 The prosciutto wrapped mozzarella was AWESOME! The mozzarella was supple and complimented the prosciutto very well along with the tomatoes on the plate. For the entree I had the Porcini rubbed delmonico with 12-year aged balsamic. This was probably the best steak I've had in my entire life. It was juicy and fully of flavor. Paired with the mashed potatoes this was a knock out.

 Unfortunately, I was too full to sample their desserts after this behemoth of a steak, but I'm sure it's just as good as anything else on the menu. I would recommend this place to anyone looking to have a wonderful meal with great service. They would also have to not be afraid to spend some money, our bill for 3 people was about $300.

Came here for a weekday brunch around noon, and the place was relatively quiet and empty. Atmosphere was low-key and the interior has somewhat of a rustic feel. There is plenty of street parking as well.

For brunch, we ordered the egg scramble with bacon and potatoes, the buffalo chicken crepe, and decided to share the apple crepe. It was the perfect amount of food for two hungry people. We were so hungry we forgot to take pictures of the food, but the presentation was simple and appetizing.

If you were to order one dish, we would recommend the crepes, which appear to be the Rooster's specialty. The apple crepe was actually our favorite. Very simple, but it was a delicious combination when added with the cinnamon syrup. The buffalo chicken crepe was very delicious and quite unique. Flavor was great and I really enjoyed the savory crepe. 

Overall, the Rooster was a great, intimate setting for brunch which we would highly recommend. Prices are reasonable, and while portion size is slightly on the smaller side, it was not bad at all. Try it for yourself!

I was recently diagnosed with some food allergies and have a very difficult time dining out. Stephanie in the lounge was amazing with my issues, found me a delicious meal that didn't make me ill, and kept the drinks rolling without being intrusive. It was fairly loud and crowded, but in the Christmas season on a Friday, it's to be expected. Overall, one of the better restaurants in the Common.

this is my first time dining in here and we absolutely loved it. the outside is a little off putting but the inside is beautiful! dark, spacious, quiet, and comfortable. there is even a button to press so they know we're ready to order! we got the tt roll, Alabama roll, and pork gyoza. it came out quickly and tasted great. our waitress Jenny was very kind, everyone was very welcoming. We will definitely be back for more!

Been craving for banh uot and I honestly must say it's pretty good...I just wish the have varieties of stuffing but meat will do just fine for now. Their sandwiches is pretty good besides the pickles being a little sweet for me....sugar cane was yummy and banh batexo was definitely good, it tastes fresh and the seasoning was perfect.

I have not eaten at enough Korean restaurants in order to compare to this place. However, what I can say is that the meat was mostly fat so I gave up after not being able to chew the first five bites. I ate the sides instead, which included white rice, various fried items, and a small portion of iceberg lettuce with a soy dressing. I was not impressed and another member of our group who has more experience with Korean food also said that his food was not good. Maybe we went on a bad day.
This place is nice but the service sucks!!!! It needs better management for that location!

Our first time there and the food was great.  Great 'fusion' cuisine.  The wonton 'crab rangoons' with sweet chili sauce were an awesome appetizer.  The entrees were also very good.  We'll definitley go back.  I was a fun chance of pace over our standard steak houses and chain restaurants we normally patronize.  My wife said her martini was excellent and it looked like a very well stocked bar.  The server seemed a little alouf at first but she softened up and became a very good recommender of what to try and share. 

Supprt downtown Nashville businessess!  Domo Mr. Roboto, domo!  Cya there.
The food and staff are both incredible! One of Indy's hidden treasures. True authentic Mexican food. I loved my experience here!
For some reason the service has gotten so bad over the last few months. They're so slow and our waiters have been bad. It's sad cuz we have loved this place.

Best.Mussels.Ever!!!!!
Enjoyable atmosphere and very friendly staff, including the owner. They never disappoint when it comes to the food and excellent customer service! #KotoSushi #ShrimpTempuraRolls #Mussels

What a great surprise.  After others in my group did tons of research to find the best places to eat  I found this place on a forum where someone spoke about their recent trip.  Plus, it didn't hurt that you could find a $50off certificate for $10 online.

Conveniently located in the French quarter and there was no wait to be seated on a Thurs night.  Started with the oysters and crabcakes both of which were delicious.  I went with the fried seafood platter which was also good and my friends went with the Grilled Tuna "La Boheme" with barbecue shrimp.  The waitress was extremely nice and quickly brought us over our free refills.  

After hearing about all the other restaurants we just had to try while in New Orleans and all the specialty foods we had to taste, Oceana was one of the best at a fraction of the price.  

Would highly recommend without the certificate but with it, I say Run to Oceana!
Some of the best St Louis style pizza in the area. Forget Imos, this is the real thing.   Consistently good every time I go there.

I've heard so many good comments about Morrow's that the first place I thought to suggest for dinner for my sorority sisters was it! We went for happy hour and stayed for dinner. The drinks were good. I definitely enjoyed my extra dirty martini! 
I decided to get a poboy ... oyster and catfish poboys that I shared with my Soror. The bread was more like a pistolette instead of the usual french bread but it was tasty nevertheless! Other entrees my group got was the Salmon, fried chicken, greens and accompanying salads and rice. Everyone enjoyed their dinner and the service was great! Oh, I also got an order of Cajun Crawfish Pasta for my daughter. She said it was great! I plan to return to try some of their popular dishes!
No seafood (and no seafood) in the main  dining room?!?! Used to love Salmon over pasta in a blush sauce specials. This will seriously reduce my number of visits.
Great brunch!  Smoked salmon Benedict was super yummy. My husband got the meat omelette and it was really good. Beautiful inside but we sat outside because weather was so good.

This place is so great. They had valet parking because that is always a chore in itself. The portions are huge so be prepared. I think almost everyone in my group had a Togo box. The sauce / gravy that comes with the food is amazing. I had the veal parm and the veal was extremely tender. The prices are actually reasonable which because this place a perfect combination of great food and great prices! You can't go wrong here
Good authentic Chinese food at a Fair price I got the chicken and lo mein shrimp and the sweet and sour chips we're really good but took off one star because they were a little skimpy on the meat.

So, they fire a manager with 30 years at Eagle Tavern. And they just let go (read: made it miserable so they would go elsewhere) two of the best bartenders I have encountered. They wanted to 'spruce up the place'...they succeeded....now it looks like a cafeteria bar. And they wanted a younger crowd. Lets see how that business approach shakes out for them. For me, I have no desire to go back. Now, its just another bar. And there are enough out here where I can spend my money and not have to deal with new management. 

Oh, and whoever said in their review that the fish and chips were good, must have had one too many brewskis. I tried that plate a few times, as it was a favorite at the old ET. Not anymore.

Kathy lured us in with her friendly New Orleans manner and did not disappoint.  Experience guidance all through the meal with great suggestions to complement our Muffaletta sandwich.  Excellent BBQ shrimp, which Kathy showed how to peel.
Nice pairing with Big Easy IPA.  A thoroughly enjoyable lunch!

Saw that this place had one of the best cheesesteaks in Philladelphia and I decided to try it during my short visit. I ordered it with Cheez Whiz and I have to say that it was OK but a bit disappointing. Bread and meat were fine but it just wasn't as flavorful. Maybe I had higher expectations but I don't have plans to visit this place again during my next visit.

Id recommend getting the trifecta seasoning if youre getting the boils. Gallic goodness will repel any vampire near you. Huge dinning area and nice bar area as well. Be careful of ordering the clams, they might come out ice cold haha they fixed it but we weren't compensated...oh well...still a yummy place to eat.

The best lamb burger in the world!! you will not regret your visit! The service we had was amazing even though it was late at night.Traditional Avgolemono Soup Cup had such an exquisite flavor ans was so smooth. We also tried the NYC Style Reuben the taste was delicious! The bread was crunchy and the meet was so tender and juicy. After this wonderful meal we tried the cheesecake they offer, hands down the best one we have ever had it was so creamy and felt just made.
Good happy hour, delicious small plates, strong tasty drinks and friendly staff. Nice end to a pleasant Sunday.

I SO wanted to really like this place, not even love, but a strong like. I came out with a strong "meh".

Made reservations on Open Table (this marked my 10k points!!!!)

We walked in and it looked like it was once a Perkins or a Lyons and had been refurbished into a family owned restaurant. It was clean and felt fresh inside.

Seated quick, and our server came over (she had a mask, but it only covered her mouth, and she pulled it away from her face to talk.... why wear the mask??!!)

Ordered:
Cajun Mahi Mahi w baked potato & broccoli- the broccoli was the best thing, the fish was way dry and the Cajun was a forced flavor

Spaghetti & meatball-  good 

Cesar salad- looked great, it had a lot of dressing (which may turn some people off)

**originally my son was over the moon that there was a chocolate chip pancake on the menu, but when he ordered it our server said, only for breakfast (maybe a little * on the menu, served only for breakfast)

I felt the food came out a bit too slow.

Anyhow, not offensive, but there are restaurants with in 2 miles of this place I would rather go.

I stopped in to grab a nourishing smoothie, before a night of alcoholic drinks. Yup, let's coat our bellies with the good stuff, before we add all the stuff that rocks our body in a not so great way. I have found this to be a great way to prepare for a night on the town. 
The staff here is patient and knowledgeable. I was having trouble deciding & explained  my logic of health liquids, prior to not so healthy fluids. LMAO, she knew exactly  what to whip me up! Some kale, banana, & I really don't know what else.
Bottom line it was delicious & the next day, I was no worse for my night on the town. This is by no means supported by any scientific logic. It is female logic. Healthy foods cancel out unhealthy ones, LOL. I know it doesn't make a lot of sense, but if I believe it works for me, I'll continue the process!
What's a girl to do? Follow female logic at all times!
Absolutely delicious brunch here. Best meal we had in NOLA and that's saying something. Good service too. Little Gem salad was my favorite. Perfect amount of salt.

May Day!  May Day!  Who ever owns this restaurant needs to get their butt in there and get some training done.
Waitress  - fail.
Food / Brunch - fail.
Service - fail.

****** (Notice this is the only review for Brunch) *******

I will wait a few months and see if the person that owns this place gets it's problems under control.

20 minutes before waitress acknowledged us.
35 minutes until food arrived cold.
food sent back.
food arrived again - cold again. eggs undercooked.
First plate had nice sized slices of ham. Second plate had a tiny portion of ham.
I would have loved to have gone back into the kitchen and stuck my finger in the Hollandaise sauce, to see if it's being used cold.....
Cold sauce made for cold breakfast.
and the price was a tad high for portion size.

I'm hoping the owner likes this place enough to make some vast improvements.
**** (I noticed another review 1 YEAR after mine - complaining about the cold eggs benedict.. I guess they haven't improved on the cold hollandaise sauce in 1 friggen year)

Absolutely wonderful, this is my go-to comfort food place. Sesame beef and walnut jumbo shrimp are my favorite, but I love so much of their menu (wonton soup - also incredible!) 

I also just love the feel of the restaurant, it feels cozy, it's never too loud, and the owners are nice. It's almost never crowded, but I wish it was, because I love it and I want them to always have tons of business.

The service was really bad and they did put EXTRA bill on us.

We went there for raw oyster and other NO food couple days ago. But what we got was a plate of oyster with live worm. Seeing the worm moving on what we were gonna to eat was really disgusting, so we just canceled the dish (I think we should just walk out there, although the other food was fine) and ordered the other cooked one.  However, they didn't remove the item from the bill and enforced us to paid 20% tip for a group of 5.

We went back to correct the charge and they still hold the original amount of "20% tip" to the final check.

This is my first review because I think they really deserve for the low rating!

Always loved stopping here, except yesterday, when I encountered the rude bouncer dude at the bar who yelled at me "I said move!"  What a dick...
We walked over and ate in the restaurant.  Great food.  Won't be back tho

This place is complete bullshit. I can tell from the reviews that out of town people think they are getting some "real" New Orleans experience or something by going here. What a waste of money this place is.  Went there this morning with friends and ordered 4 mochas. The mochas tasted like they were made with hot water, a splash of coffee, and some cocoa sprinkled on top. After complaining about the lack of coffee in them (they really should have been made with espresso, but whatever) they told us that is pretty much exactly how they were made. Then the OWNER told that if we didn't like it then we didn't have to come back there. Rudest woman I have encountered in this city so far.  In fact, all the women behind the counter were extremely rude.
Got carry out tonight - almost choked on this giant bone in my buffalo chicken pizza.

Once my favorite. But not after the New Year's Eve.
Lot to complain, idk this is place is enough to describe.

Chill Out Cafe provides a quality meal in a warm, casual setting.

Atmosphere - 7/10

Nothing super special about the atmosphere. It was pretty cute and lended to a relaxed experience. I thought it was a bit but my sister disagreed, and really enjoyed it. The outdoor seating is awesome if the weather permits it.

Food - 7/10*

Food is okay. Everything that we ate was satisfying but didn't blow me away. Shumai was a bit rubbery and everything else, the ginger chicken and tofu red curry, was a bit mild. If you ask, the servers will bring you Thai chili which elevates the meal completely.

Service - 10/10

Our waitress was extremely attentive and beyond sweet. Despite being the only server, we got what felt like undivided attention. Her personality accentuates the atmosphere which the restaurant's name, Chill Out Cafe, describes. 

Price - 9/10

The lunch specials are extremely well priced, at around $9 a plate. Some of the appetizers are a bit steeper in price but not without reason. No qualms here.

Overview - 8.25/10 

Chill Out Café is a perfect place to go on a chill (get it?) morning. It will hardly blow anyone way but the service and price point make a strong case for it.

I'll be back!

Several visits here have been rewarded with celestial food.  If the Tournadoes of Beef are on the menu, ORDER THEM.  This is a must-go on our annual visits to New Orleans.  We look forward to our next one.

Circles has fantastic Thai food for a reasonable price. They were also kind enough to allow us to use a deal marked as "dine in only" for take-out when I accidentally didn't read the fine print and came to pick up my take-out order. The food is fresh and everything is well-cooked. We felt that it was definitely on the spicier end for "medium spice" and we'd probably order with a little less spice next time. Overall, a great place with a huge delivery radius. Don't miss out!

Ah ! Cajun Mike's ! It's been too long. I used to visit this bar every night after work for about 3 months. The staff and bar tenders are very nice and attentive. Service is very fast and beers are very VERY cheap. Guinness on tap ? Thank youuuuuuuuuu !

The food here is very good for bar food. Sandwiches and po boys taste great. The only reason why I marked this place for 4 stars is because sometimes the consistency of the food isn't on par. 

Can't really blame them though. It gets pretty damn hectic in here. Thanks for all the good times Cajun mike's. The old Domenica Crew (4 years ago) Used to love coming here after work. I still wish I worked closer just so that I could come here more often after work.

First Timer

Arrive around 5:45p and was told an event was going on later (comedy show) and that we had to be out by 7:15p *blank stare*
Party of 3 sits at bar...order drinks and appetizers (fried shrimp, gumbo, catfish nuggets, baked mac & cheese, shrimp & grits; all of app menu).
Drinks-garbage
Food-Idk bc my catfish nuggets and M&C never came.
Service-garbage
The gumbo tasted sour from what I heard, never got my food, shrimp and grits were bland, drinks tasted like juice, even with an extra shot.
Received bill, 18% gratuity added for party of 5 or more...Um...we only 3...then the gratuity was added after tax included instead of before AND the gratuity calculation was incorrect. "Manager" slash hostess who told us we had to be out by 7:15 comp my bill bc my food never came. She also took off the gratuity but said when they have events they automatically charge 18% gratuity to bills. Stop it. Because you said we had to be out before the event started, so how are we...never mind. Then had the nerve to say there are signs on the tables that say this. Stop it. Because we sitting at the bar and there are no signs AND you should've said that when you were telling us what time we had to leave! Oh, I forgot, a couple arrived after us and ordered WHOLE meals and their food came out before our apps.
The only good part were the clean bathrooms. 
When were leaving, like literally out the door, like we were outside(!), the "Manager" slash hostess gave us coupons for free apps talking 'bout "next time ya'll in town free apps on us." She almost made me cuss. Stop it. I give it a -0.

I have been to C'est Cheese a total of four times, and every time the service was outstanding.  I don't recall who helped me the first time I went in, but there was nothing bad that stuck out in my mind.  The other times I've had the privilege to be helped by one of the owners.  

My most recent visit to C'est Cheese was a week ago, on a Friday afternoon.  There were four people working, and I had one of the owners help me out.  I like that she remembered me, and she was patient to allow me to sample many cheeses.  She was also a big help in picking a good variety of cheeses as well as a salami.

The cheeses at C'est Cheese are the right temperature and flavor.

Regardless of how busy the store is, someone will greet you with a smile.  I also like how C'est Cheese doesn't portray itself a some pretentious business.  

If I get married some day, I'll have C'est Cheese cater my wedding, and then I'll write another review.  =)

We had a bridal luncheon for 30 people. Mauricio did an amazing job setting up our lunch. The food was fantastic and the atmosphere was perfect for that size party. Everyone had a fabulous time. I will definitely spend many evenings back at Los Serapes.

Good place for seafood  good music  and every waitress ive have had always been nice  
Gets pretty crowded but they are fast

Decided to try someplace new and laid back for my birthday tonight and I am SO happy we chose the Black Barn! The atmosphere is comfortable, and the guys are super welcoming and friendly. As we were waiting for our sandwiches we were saying how we hope the food is as good as the energy and we were not at all disappointed! Between the four of us we had the Philly cheesesteak, chicken pesto, Monte Cristo and pastrami, along with the mac'n'cheese side. Even my picky kids were impressed with everything! Looking forward to coming back for sure!!
Hole in the wall. Great sushi. Great price! Super sweet couple. Don't be turned off by the appearance. Yum yum! Some of the best sushi we've had at a very reasonable price.

Wonderful Thai restaurant right in my neighborhood. Great food-nice service- lovely atmosphere. Loved my Pad Thai my hubbies Pad saw ew  was yummy as well. Just beware that a level 2 out of 5 spice level was as spicy as we could go.

Fine dining but simple food.  I had the fillet (steak) and my place was clean - no shame.  blueberry dessert was good, the bread pudding is the move though.  OMG tasted so goooood.  Ambiance is the best part of this establishment, that and the 100+ history.  Historic neighborhood as well.

Two words: piggy mac.
After a morning touring the Ryman, a guide recommended Puckett's for lunch. A short walk away and we entered the large open dining space with old southern memorabilia all around. We were seated quickly and drawn to the pineapple jalapeño margaritas (we opted for no actual jalapeños and it was refreshing and delicious). 
Though we only wanted lunch, the dinner options had been lauded on Yelp, so we opted for larger portions to try them out. My boyfriend got the chicken fried chicken with red skin mashed potatoes and onions rings. The all white breast meat was moist and fried superbly. A delectable option.
When I read about the piggy mac, I knew i had to try it: pulled pork with Mac an cheese in a cast iron skillet. Probably my favorite dish from all of Nashville, and maybe the best pulled pork I've had, which is saying a LOT coming from NC! So creamy with a bit of a spice (paprika?) tickling the tongue. It was definitely a dinner portion which made it a challenge at lunchtime, but probably shareable for lunch maybe with an appetizer.
Definitely an experience worth the hype for quality southern dishes!

Very disappointed. Simple review. Atmosphere too bright, and the tables were uncomfortable barrels that your knees hit. Staff was young and inexperienced with no personality. Food average at best. My son and I had very dry tacos. Very expensive $$$$10 for a white wine spritzer. Taco bell would have been a better choice.

I have been to HopCat a couple of times and definitely enjoy the beer list and their food. They have a huge selection of great beers! I definitely recommend getting their Crack Fries! They are really good!

They are definitely not the cheapest place to go for a pint and dinner, but they are good for beer and food on occasion. 

My most recent visit came with good beers and food, but some sub-par service. We started our stay off by being walked to our table all the way in the back of the restaurant, past a bunch of empty tables, right next to the restrooms. If it was crowded and this was the only table I would understand, but there were quite a few empty tables that we walked by on our way to the restroom... I mean our table. From there, another group was seated next to us that ask to change the channel to a specific game (a typical question I imagine for sports bars/pubs) to which they were told no. After some other awkward encounters they had with our/their waiter they decided to leave. I understand their frustration, but they were being a tad obnoxious so I can understand our waiter a bit too. The problem I had was when our waiter came to us and complained about it to us. Then on of the obnoxious people's phones was found left behind our waiter joked about messing around on it to us. Kind of unprofessional in my opinion and kind of disappointing from a well-established bar.

Overall, I find HopCat's beer list and food impressive, but after my most recent visit I feel like that's where my good impressions end. I hope I can go back sometime and get a new perspective.

The restaurant has a beautiful atmosphere--that's about it.  The food left a lot to be desired.  

I've been there twice and Cuba Libre left me disenchanted.  The drinks are weak, the food is blah (kinda fatty, heavy, and over-salted).  I've had the pumpkin ravioli--they were ok, and the levantamuerto, or "wake the dead," soup (it wasn't levanta anything-- a thin little broth with a dash of coconut milk).  Traditionally, these soups are full of veggies and resemble a more soupy goulash or a stew with latin american vegs, like yuca. My friends had some pork dish and the cuban sandwich. The pork dish was really salty and the cuban sandwich was difficult to chew... the food wasn't worth the cash paid.  

Also, the bathroom was gross (there were waste papers on the floor and the sink wasn't draining the water)...
Does what it says in the name and does it well. Very delicious and well presented noodles. The pork belly was succulent and the broth is very good. Highly recommended for a casual meal.

Went for the buffet on a Sunday evening with a group of 9. Service was nothing special. But given the size of our group they charged a standard gratuity charge of 15ptc. Food menu had decent options ranging from standard appetizers, ramen, udon noodles, sashimi and sushi. Sad part was that was just ok and Nothing seemed to stand out in particular. The beef tataki was extremely thin and did not taste fresh...Felt like it was preprepared.
Everything we had was awesome.  Eggplant App. Chargrilled Oysters, Mardi Gras pasta, Blackened Redfish stuffed with seafood dressing.  Natalie was an awesome waitress.  Dinner was fab!

I don't go there as much as I used to, as we moved a while back, but we went there today, and it was as good as ever.  Best Cubans, and devil crabs anywhere. My wife and I have known Dana, the owner for years, and her and her staff are always great. I actually used to got to the original store in Ybor years ago, and it is the same now as it was then. If you want catering, they have the best food for that too.

I went in this past Saturday and had an amazing time. Savannah was great, she made sure I was always taken care of in a timely manner, and was very entertaining. The food was delicious and she recommended the flaming lips and I really enjoyed the drink. The atmosphere was great and Savannah would be somebody I recommend to dine in with. I really enjoyed my time at The Cruisery, as a whole was great and I recommend it to anyone in the area.
Fenwicks has great coffee from Bongo. The Monte Cristo is delicious. They have excellent, thick-cut bacon and the beignets are on point!

This is definitely one of my favorite Mexican restaurants in Tucson. Their food is great, there is usually a wait at the restaurant between 30 mins -1 hour so be prepared, but I would say it's worth it. Also don't forget to try their micheladas or margaritas w/ the president plate or shredded beef tacos.

This is not my first time dining with Piazza Gavi.  We ordered through ubereats and the delivery took about 60 minutes to get to my door.  We ordered pepperoni pizza, cheese ravioli with a side of meat balls, garden salad, and minestrone soup for about $71 with tip.  You can't go wrong with ordering the pepperoni pizza.  It was our favorite, but this is not the best pie in Tucson for the price.  The meat balls are huge balls covered in red sauce and pair nicely with the cheese ravioli.  For some reason, the garden salad did not come with dressing.  Luckily we had some Italian dressing in the fridge to keep the theme going.  Overall the food was good, but can be pricey for the amount you get.  Pair this meal with some hard kombucha.  Cheers!

The chicken was juicy and pretty good. The skin wasn't as crispy as I would have thought. I usually prefer dark meat, but at this restaurant enjoyed the chicken strips more. Being able to select the spice level was a great touch. I grew up on a once a day fried chicken dinner, so wasn't super impressed with this one. I think Gus's in Memphis may be better. Worth the experience once.

I bought samosas and chili pakoda from the store on 03/11/21. Chili pakoda was very hard and didn't taste that well. On the other hand, samosas were very stale and once tasted them, I realized that samosas had gone bad

Initially I thought it's just one bad samosa but it turned out all the samosas were bad and could have given you food poisoning. 

I called the store to let them know that their samosas were bad, however, they seemed very indifferent as it happens everyday. They told that no one else complained. Well, it looks like they want people to fall ill before they will take any proactive action. 

I am writing this review because another friend of fine went through the same experience and also complaint about the quality of their vegetables. 

Thanks to the other stores in the neighborhood, I won't be visiting this store anymore.

I have never been disappointed in the Harrah's Steakhouse in the 15 years I have been visiting it. I try to stay away during the big events downtown as I am a local and know it gets insane. On my last visit, I had the Pacific Grilled Salmon and my friend had the Fillet Mignon, Oscar style. We both had the Cesar salad to start. All were prepared wonderfully and the service as always was excellent. Bananas Foster for dessert. Delicious, not rushed and worth the money. I will continue to go back and suggest it to anyone. Good job!

One of our favorite spots in the Rittenhouse area. Bar staff is quick, friendly and knows their stuff. I think $9 for a martini or old fashioned is extremely reasonable and they are always made really well. Tried the cheese plate and lamb chili Saturday, and thought at $16 and $11 they were priced fairly too. They were both great! It was packed but service was not an issue at all. I wish the bathroom wasn't down a flight of such steep stairs but I have no problem overlooking that for such a great experience.

Prices here are like your local Whole Foods or Trader Joes, but that's because they're advertising and selling a lot of locally grown and made products. Which is pretty awesome for people that want to support local vendors. 

I loved the homeopathic/organic product section for medicine and makeup. I'm pretty conscious about what products I put on and in my body, so this is a great place for all that. I'll be coming back soon to check out the entire store next time. It's worth coming in to.
Had dinner there tonight.  I can only recommend this for carry out if you're not too particular.

Went to this restaurant the other night and now I'm highly jealous I can't find anything like it in Raleigh, NC. Ordered sweet and sour "chicken" and General Tso's "chicken", as well as veggie dumplings and spring rolls - absolutely amazing. I've been craving sweet and sour chicken but no longer eat meat so this was the perfect substitute with seitan instead. The waitress was extremely friendly and food came out fast.

If you absolutely need breakfast on the Causeway, this place will do.

Things that bother me:  canned mushrooms and low-grade Swiss cheese, and this place delivers on both.  

Homefries are on point, and the service is stellar.  Outside of that, it's just a-ok.  There is a 100% chance that I will not return though.  3 stars for cost effectiveness. My meal was only 8 bucks and change.

We love Nimbus because the food is really good. They offer a gluten free pizza crust which is important to us because my husband can't have gluten. Their portions on most everything are huge and can be shared. However, don't expect fast or good service. The past 3 or 4 times we have gone there we have had slow servers with little to no personality. One time we waited for over an hour for our food and an additional 30 minutes for our bill in the same sitting. (and no they weren't busy) If you can get past bad service to get really good food...this is the place to go.

Of course 5 stars... We went on Kentucky Derby Saturday for jazz brunch and are still talking about the food, the drinks, and the music. We had a large group and the service was impeccable. We can't wait to go back!  Now if we could just figure out the Big Daddy cocktail... We're getting close!

A comfortable spot with delicious noodle soups rivaled only by a select other spots in Philadelphia's Chinatown. This place does get VERY busy, as you'd probably expect being right next to the famed tourist destination Dim Sum Garden, but it is famous for different reasons.

Curiosity led me to this place, and I was blown away by the quality of the food I ate. Of course, I had the get the house special noodle and was pleasantly surprised by the flavor and appearance of the soup.
The slowest Dunkin' Donuts ever! They never get your order right and it takes 15 mins for one cup of coffee every time

Redemption! After letting some time pass, we decided to go back to Tequila Sunrise to see if we'd have a better dining experience than last time at the bar -- and we did! 
Our bartenders/servers were very attentive, helpful and friendly and the food was delicious. For a Friday evening (~ 5:30 until 6:30 pm), we thought it was unusual that we were the only two people in the entire bar area during our visit -- and maybe that contributed to an improved service experience this time? Regardless, it was nice having the area all to ourselves! 
If you like fried avocado tacos with a kick, try theirs ... we did based upon a server's suggestion of this new menu item and we loved them! [Tip: ask for a side of sour cream to temper the heat level of the delicious, yet spicy, jalapeno cilantro crema on the tacos.]

New Bawarchi is located in the same spot previously occupied by the much maligned (at least by me) Bombay High in the shopping center known for ShopRite and LobsterClaw on Germantown Pike.

As I mentioned when reviewing Bombay High, I've been a fan of Amans for quite a while, and they are my usual choice in the area, but I decided to give New Bawarchi a try tonight and was very happy.  First, the person who helped me was very friendly.  We chatted for a few minutes and he seemed excited to have a new customer.  

I thought of New Bawarchi on the way home and just looked up their number, so I didn't know that they focused on Southern Indian food.  (If I did, I wouldn't have ordered my usual saag paneer.)  The saag paneer was quite good, and different than I'm used to, but I feel like I should have tried the dosa.  (In fact, the gentlemen who helped me did say I should come in some night and get the dosa.)

I had saag paneer, roti,and naan, and each item was quite tasty.  The saag was smoother and the paneer firmer than at Amans.  

I think I may have a new favorite Indian restaurant in the area.  I hope they survive a lot longer than Bombay High because they are much much better!  Go check them out.

I don't think they have a website yet, but here's their Facebook page:
https://www.facebook.com/pages/New-Bawarchi-South-Indian-Cuisine-Catering-Banquets/285921618192464

This restaurant offers great seating, cool atmosphere, and pretty good service. I came here twice. First time ordered by the menu and second time ate at the brunch buffet. Both times, I was very satisfied with the quality of the service and food. Overall a great place for brunch/lunch/dinner. There is also a bakery located under the restaurant. While the food is a bit on the steeper side in terms of price, they make it up with generous portions.

I recently moved to the St. Louis area and have been trying every bbq place that I can find. I've tried all the main staples like Pappy's, Bogart's, Sugarfire, and Adam's Smokehouse (and a few others). Beast Craft BBQ is my favorite so far.

All of their meats were awesome. I really like the number of meat options and the awesome selection of sides.

Unfortunately, I couldn't find the picture of the food that I took. Between my brother and I we ordered most of the meats and sides on the menu. We both left stuffed and extremely satisfied. I would highly recommend that anyone in the St. Louis area try out Beast Craft if they have the chance.

I ordered some chicken pad thai to go Last night from Tum Rub Thai. I wish I had gone in to eat. As soon as I opened the door a great aroma was in the air. The decorations looked great and when I got home the food was good. 

I will be back to eat at the location. Another benefit the gentleman working the counter was super friendly. 

I know that I didn't have much to say in this review but I will edit it after I eat in the restaurant.

Wow. For about $10 you can have a very filling meal. In had the Angus beef brisket dinner plate with mac and cheese ,fried pickles, corn and a biscuit. The beef was good...but very salty. And so were the fried pickles. But the corn was amazing,it had some spicy flavoring to it. Also , the cherrywine soda was good. I had this place at a solid 3.5 but what made it a four is the bakery. We had the coconut cake and white chocolate dipped Oreos. Superb!  Its as if this place wants to fatten you up ! I would definitely make another attempt at the pulled pork next time. Hopefully it won't be as salty as the Angus. Overall , not bad 4rivers.

I love this place! It's a tiny whole in the wall with no real signage other than a wooden skull with cross bones high over the front door. Very easy to go right by.
The menu is small, but oh so good! They use fresh ingredients and make almost everything from scratch. I go there specifically for their sweet potato & greens Po-boy. Adorned with black eyed pea walnut spread, it is delicious! I love that I can eat something moderately healthy in a city where that's a rarity.
The service is also so good! The people who work there truly seem to care about their product & their customers experience. You order at the counter & grab one of the limited seats & wait a short time to indulge your tastebuds. So good! I make at least one trip there every time we're in the city!

It's your basic fried everything seafood restaurant. It's not the best in the area, but it's not the worst. I had the fried fish and shrimp platter. Everything tasted the same and there were only 6 tiny shrimp, so that was disappointing. Also ordered the crab claws and boom boom shrimp, both of which were really good. Perhaps the appetizers here are what you should get. If you're looking for a decent bite to eat, this is the place.

Definitely not 4.5 stars. Deceptive for the price, not to mention our food was served in tin foil and a paper carton. My bahn mi was OK  but tasted like a $5 sandwich, not $11!! Have no idea how this place has a one $ symbol. Should be $$. Bf had fried rice. Said it was nothing special, not worth $13. Other than that it's open late and it looks like a chill hangout but I wouldn't go solely for the food.

Good food and good service once again. They had a different menu since the last time I came here. I started with the sausage and lentil, which was served hot the way I like it and with a little spice. I had the chicken carrabba w/fettuccini for my entree. It was good but I would try something else the next time I come.

My fiance had been bragging about how great this place was for a couple of years now. To be honest the only thing holding me back from going there was my less than adventuress pallet. It had been a long weekend and I asked her where she wanted to go she said here. So off we go! We started with Calamari it was your general fried calamari. It tasted great and the spicy mayo that it was served with was good. I had the pan fried noodles with pork. I was shocked at how delicious it was. The noodles were crisp and after you let them soak up the sauce a little bit they were the perfect combo of crispy and sauce. She had the beef soup. It was a traditional Vietnamese soup it was also great! The jasmine tea was good too. The restraunt itself was unpretentious and clean the service was great. We will definitely be back. I have her again to thank for my expanded pallet.

Ordered pizza by the slice and it was okay. Crust was thin and crisp however served luke warm. Also ordered a small salad - portion was huge, enough for 2 or 3 people to share.  Staff was very friendly and attentive.
Placed on online order. The woman working said they never received it. I had the confirmation in my phone. Proceeded to tell us "oh well" and didn't take our order.

The Stillery, Midtown is the place to go in Nash for good, casual food without a crazy wait. The patio upstairs is seat yourself, and the perfect spot to listen to live music and people watch the bars below on Division Street. The fried pickles and the pizza are my personal favorites. This is without a doubt one of the most underrated restaurants in Nashville.

Solid food and drink downtown. I had them make me an off menu poboy. I asked for oysters instead of shrimp and they made it happen, no fuss. They loaded me up with 10 oysters! Had myself a pimms cup and a few sazeraks. Surprisingly good food from the kitchen of what looks like just another ho-hum tourist trap. Recommend you stop in for lunch on a Sunday and you won't leave hungry!
Best pancakes ever!! The pecan banana pancakes are a must have!!! I'm never eating pancakes again because no other pancakes could live up to the pecan banana pancakes !!!!!!

Absolutely worth the wait. Go early and the line moves fast. It started raining while in line and they gave out umbrellas. Once inside, they are a well oiled machine and really keep things moving. Latte was perfect and not too strong. The nasty was delicious. The off-menu nasty princess was also very good. My absolute favorite item was the churros with chocolate sauce. My favorite thing ever!!

If you think that chicken fingers are just for kids, think again! McDougal's serves up pieces of chicken so good that people of all ages flock here to get in on the poultry action.

I think the secret to McDougal's is that when it comes to the fingers, they use 100% breast meat, nothing that's been reconstituted. Whether you get your fingers fried or grilled, you are guaranteed to get tasty, fresh and juicy chicken that will have you craving more. There are also plenty of sauces available for you to gussy up your meal, from ranch and blue cheese, to chipotle barbeque and hotter buffalo-style hot sauces as well. They're all good, though I admit a personal preference for the ranch and honey-mustard myself. Get yourself a combo basket (three fingers are plenty! The portions are really huge!) and your chicken will come with fresh-cut shoestring potato fries and a slice of Texas toast as well. Another thing I like to indulge in occasion when I can resist the siren song of straight-up chicken fingers is the chicken finger sandwich, which is really nice because it comes on the grilled Texas toast and can be topped with tomatoes, lettuce, mayo and mustard (and any combination thereof). 

To top everything off, every meal comes with a free cup of soft-serve ice cream at the end. The portion isn't huge, but after filling your belly with all the delicious chicken, you won't have room for much anyway! Plus, it's free, so what are you complaining about?!?

The Coop is no-frills eating at its best. Probably the only thing to complain about is that parking on Belcourt Ave is generally a bit of a nightmare, but I think there is a lot around back. The atmosphere is super chilled out, and this place is truly at its peak during the summer months when you can dine al fresco on their big wooden deck and enjoy the weather. This is a fun place where the simple, delicious food really shines. If you're craving fried chicken in Nashville, few places will do it better than this.

Very, very good BBQ! We came here after church one Sunday for lunch around 12:30 & it was a line, but not a long one. We both ordered the brisket cheese steak sandwicj; that brisket was soooo tender and good. However, they had waaaaaayyyy too much cheese sauce atop. And i love me some cheese. Their sides are always delish and fresh; baked beans, coleslaw and cheesy bacon potatoes were the ones we chose. They were all yummy!

There are so many things I love about these donuts. They are low fat, low carb, low sugar and packed with protein. All donuts are under 107 calories. The concept is fabulous and the execution is even better!

Keep in mind that these are not your typically fatty greasy  deep fried airy donuts. They have more of a cake-like consistency, dense and heavier. It's more like eating a protein muffin, still rather delicious. You probably want a fork; they are pretty dang crumbly. My favorite was the chocolate with chocolate frosting and sprinkles. It pretty much just tasted like a chocolate cupcake, but heathy! I also greatly enjoyed the lemon raspberry flavor, it's one of my go-to flavors. 

My only criticism, much like other reviews, is that some of the flavors leave a chemical-like aftertaste from what I assume is the artificial sweetener used in the donuts. I once tried the cookie dough donut, and while the toppings and frosting were great, the dough itself left a strong, unpleasant taste in my mouth that was hard to get rid of. I hope they try to experiment with alternative, natural sweeteners! This place has so much potential to be the best in its area if it can get every donut to taste as delicious as the ones I mentioned in the paragraph above.

I will still continue to drop by here occasionally but I will stick to my usual order. Great place!
The food was great, the view was pretty, and our waitress, Judie was really nice. The coconut bread was killer. I thought it was gonna be a mistake to get a $4 margarita, but it was really good!

Beer was good but food not so much. As a group we ordered a few apps that were all pretty unfortunate. Hot dogs were actually very good though! Good place to have a few drinks as long as you don't plan on having a meal there.

My husband wanted to go out to eat so I told him to find a Groupon since we're trying to save some money. He found this place so we bought the groupon and off we went. I remember the food was pretty good. It was very unique food which is what will make this place warrant another visit. The service was superb. We went during a normal dinner shift, so we'll have to go back to try brunch some time. I would recomment this place.

Consistency. That's pretty much it, Don Pedro's never lets you down. My Bf and I discovered this little place about 4months ago, and when ever he's in town he demands we go there. Service is pretty great, Rebecca our usual server always recommends something different and it's nothing short of delicious.
