All the dishes are great, but let me say that the Lomo Salteado and Ceviche Mixto are by far our favorite. The sweet potato goodness they add to the ceviche is just to die far!! Great little gem in south tucson, by El Super for those Tucsonians.

Tried to go to Dandelion for brunch for my 21st birthday. I looked at the menu online and saw they had scones and other classic breakfast-y foods. Showed up at opening time at 11:30 on Memorial Day, but they only served lunch. I saw another yelp reviewer had a full English breakfast, but when I asked the server about it she was very confused and said they did not serve anything like that. Still, I decided to eat lunch. I had fish and chips and my friend had bangers and mash. Both were super tasty and authenticly British but heavy for 11:30. I also ordered a 5oz beer from the tap that was also tasty. Was very full, but the desserts sounds delicious. I got a chocolate cake with earl grey frosting. They brought the dessert with a candle which was nice. Would highly recommend for lunch and dinner

Can't believe I forgot to leave a review earlier. I'm a big Vietnamese dessert fan, and I've tried the Bambu in Philly, another one in NJ, and NYC but the Pennsauken location is by far my favorite. The drinks are always on point and the customer service is exceptional. 

On my recent trip (we drove over an hour to satisfy our cravings), I called about 45 minutes to closing and ordered about 16 drinks, the lady who took down my order was professional and I got all the drink exactly as ordered. 

All their drinks are amazing but a must try is the REFRESHER! None of the other Bambu has it!

Short Stop Po-Boys has been turning out yummy sandwiches and fries for 50 years. They are actually the first Po-Boy shop I visited when I moved to New Orleans in 1997. I always compare debris style roast beef to Short Stop.

The ordering system is a bit confusing for first time customers. You order your food at the tall counter, then you mill around near the counter until your food is ready. Then you go to the short counter to pay for it. The staff isn't super friendly, but truthfully, they are very busy. 

It helps if you have someone with you to grab a seat while you are waiting at the counter because seats go fast! So do the parking spaces at peak hours. Sometimes there are people parked on the neutral ground or on the side of the road.  Don't let this discourage you from trying them, there is a great reason for the crowd, and spots open up fast.

People are in and out of here ALL DAY. The sandwiches are excellent, they have a wide variety.  I have never had one that I didn't like. (Except that one time I accidentally got a roast beef with mustard. Who does that?)   When they call your name and you get your treasure wrapped in layers of paper, it is time to eat! I love the texture of the bread and how the meat falls out. I love the smell and mmmmmm the taste. They have the ratio of meat to bread down to an art. The po-boys are pretty close to perfection. The French fries are always fresh and they are never skimpy on anything.   

If French fries are not your style they have chips on a couple racks. My favorite drinks are the unusual ones they keep in the coolers by the register. They have drinks I have never seen anywhere else. 

The restaurant is simple, clean, no frills. The walls are lined with booths so you can lean over the table and keep your shirt clean.  Short Stop has been around for 50 years for a reason. They are excellent!

My husband & I went here for our 2nd anniversary. It was a quiet Monday night. The service was friendly & the food was good. I wasn't particularly amazed with any of the dishes we ordered but it was good enough to make me want to come back to try out some of the other options.
Really good restaurant! This was my first visiting and I enjoyed all the food! Nice service and clean environment. If you wanna try some delicious Chinese food, you must try here!

Made a reservation and got the table I wanted on a Saturday night!

Had the calmari and shrimp imperial apps.  Both were good. Calamari were generic (I like to have a mix of rings and legs). Entres were crab cakes and strip steak. Both excellent!  Strip steak was ordere med rare and that's how it was served. Crab cakes were full of flavor and crab meat. Shared the creme brûlée for dessert and it was good but I have had better. All of the food was brought to us piping hot including there delicious asst of bread.  

Wait staff very friendly and informative. It was busy, therefore, service suffered a little. 

Lighting could be dimmer for an extra cozy feel. Wide range of clientele.

My husband and I came for brunch while on our honeymoon. It was so much fun and we enjoyed ourselves. Out see her was fantstic and ON IT. And the queen was hilarious and did a wonderful job at keeping everyone entertained. This was different and fun. I will say bring some extra cash to tip the queen. Had I known, I would have and I felt bad that I couldn't go e her a little love. Our food was great, although, I have to admit, I was disappointed that the egg on my skillet was overcooked. I guess it say in the window for too long or something, but regardless, friend rice is always better with a runny egg. And that was my only complaint. Everything else was great and I can't wait to be back.
Hadn't been to this location in years, loved it once again when we were there last week! The service was awesome! Will be coming back in June when my fiancé and I take our annual trip.

Cold Springs is awesome. You have to make sure to go if you are just visiting. :)  The best atmosphere around in a gorgeous setting. I actually had my wedding party dinner after getting married here. They were super accommodating.

Was surprised that this place was now a Thai restaurant.  It was very fresh, authentic, great flavors.  Nothing dressy about this place but some of the best Thai we have had in Reno.  The spring rolls were very fresh and loose wrap with large shrimp.  I love the Thai tea. They also will refill Thai tea for 1.50 when everyone else makes me buy another full price.  The yellow curry had so much flavor instead of just pure heat that many places serve.   I want to try one of there classes. You cook in groups and then eat all the if all dishes.  With wine the price looks reasonable but have tried it yet.  Don't miss the mango and sweet rice desert. Best I harbor ever tried.
The wait was extremely long for such an informal restaurant with overpriced food. It's not worth your time. You can find a much better place to eat in the area any day of the week.

I went to Reilly's with a big party, and the service was great! Big parties are so hard on servers so I was really impressed.
    The hot sauce Brussel sprouts are seriously the best thing I've ever had... Seriously so good! They also have a pizza with an egg on it, and it's really good! 
   Finally the building is absolutely beautiful, its a place I want to spend time in. Try it out, they are a business worth supporting

Much better selections and quality compared to Panera.

The food items are fresher and made better. One of the best chocolate muffins I've ever had came from this place. 

The crew is OK, not the nicest, yet not rude either. 

The place is clean, however seems a bit cramped and may confuse someone going in for the first time. The coffee station is better assimilated with toppings depending on the person, but it's a little cramped too.

Coffee's better compared to Panera, which means it's astronomically better than Starbucks.

If in the area, give this place a shot. You might just become one of their loyal patrons...
20 burnt wings and No seasoning on The Philly cheesesteak The place was empty you guys have to do better

Difficult review to write!! 
Pros: View can't be beat! We were shown to a table by a friendly hostess as soon as we walked up. She took us to a table right on the dock as we requested. Hooter's provides a canopy over the sun exposed tables so it was perfect.
PROS: Drinks were cold and delivered quickly. I tried the Dragonberry Mojito which was FANTASTIC and fresh made. We also had white sangria which is always very good. 
          Buffalo shrimp is my go to favorite thing here, I order them medium, and were fantastic as always. Very crisp even after being tossed in the delicious sauce! 
          Fries: I always order some with cheese sauce to break up the seafood flavors. They do great curly fries here.
Cons: I only have one but it is a biggy. I have eaten oysters at Hooter's many time. Always steamed and always served on the half shell. We ordered a dozen and I was surprised to be brought a plate with oyster shucking knife and towel. I thought it was odd but didn't say anything. Then I got my oysters. In the shell. Closed. Umm.... They want me to shuck my own oysters? OK. I'm a local and Florida raised so no problem, I guess. But what about our visitors? Is this part of the experience? So I start shucking. We ate half a dozen perfectly steamed oysters. I mean PERFECT! This is not an easy thing to do and the kitchen should be commended. Then I got tired. And I looked down at my shirt and I was a mess from shucking. And I smelled like a dead fish. I told the waitress to take the rest back and give me half credit on the bill because no matter how good they taste I was done opening them. She shucked the rest for us and we ate them cold because she was so nice. BEYOND UNACCEPTABLE!
         SHRIMP!!  So so so very very over cooked!!! Dead as all hell. Shells so soft they were almost impossible to peel. TIP TO MANAGEMENT TO SHARE WITH THE KITCHEN: Never ever ever put peel and eat shrimp under a warming light!! That is just one of those things you can't do with seafood. The shells turn to mush in 30 seconds! These shrimp sat under a light for a few minutes. Dry as a bone and so hard to peel. The seagulls got half our order.

Excellent experience totally spoiled by a weird corporate/management decision. Why in the world would any customer want to shuck their own oysters?? My oysters are just as fresh with a guy doing them to order in a kitchen 20 feet away without me making a mess of myself at all. Not to mention the fact that I paid $12.95 for the dozen! Shame on you for that alone considering where we live but don't charge me that and make me shuck the damn things!!! I can't stress what an epic fail that is!!

 Service was fantastic from the hostess station to our waitress to the bartender who told me how to make the Dragonberry Mojito.

Expect to pay. We were 3 people. We had the 10 buffalo shrimp, a dozen steamed oysters, and a small order of steamed shrimp. Side of fries with cheese sauce. 2 beers, 1 large white sangria and 2 dragonberry mojitos. $70 before tip

They have all your normal breakfast foods at a reasonable price. The service can be a little slow on a busy weekend morning. But early morning weekdays they are quick and you can be in and out in about 20 minutes. I have become a regular and I am never disappointed. Every time I order the breakfast sampler with the pancake and bacon. The waitress's remember regulars and it's a nice homey feel.
Staff here are great.  Food was delious.  I had the oyster and the grill shrimp sandwich And it was at a perfect price.
Every bit as great as it's sister restaurant Sampan. I come here for lunch all the time and it's always a great crowd. Trendy, great service, and unique brunch menu.
Wendys has always been my favorite, but now that the spicy nuggets are back I frequent it even more now

Ok came here CRAVING a milkshake. After waiting on the drive through line for 15 minutes she said "I will be with you in a minute and we don't have ice cream".
WHAT?! You don't have ice cream?! The name is literally steak and SHAKE!!!! And its not like they just didn't have chocolate ice cream or something, they had NO ICE CREAM?! I guess I saved myself some calories
Although maybe a little pricey for Mexican food. Definitely our favorite in town for Tex-Mex. The staff is always great and the food is always awesome.

I'm surprised this place has "only" four stars. It was my favorite meal in New Orleans, which is really saying something. I had the fried green tomato eggs Benedict, which I believe was a daily special.  If this is on the menu when you come you MUST order it. I love fried green tomatoes so as soon as I saw this I knew I had to order it, but the execution exceeded my wildest dreams. The perfectly breaded FGTs, runny egg, creamy Hollandaise and flaky buttermilk biscuit (a wonderful twist on the traditional English muffin) went together perfectly. Brunch dishes come with a side of potatoes or grits and I had the cheesy grits, which were fantastic. I also had a chocolate iced coffee (a coffee blend with chocolate, not a mocha) and it was phenomenal as well. The chocolate flavor was distinct but not overwhelming.

The prices are surprisingly reasonable for such a popular spot - my dish was around $10. 

Like many restaurants in NOLA, you can get in line with the Yelp app, which was very convenient. Come early - when we arrived at 10 am on a Sunday they were quoting a 15-30 minute wait, when we left at 11 it was an hour or more. 

Thanks, Cafe Fleur de Lis. You've doomed me to a lifetime of visiting Southern cities in search of restaurants that serve fried green tomato eggs Benedict!

Photos + my NOLA food recap here: https://destinationsanddesserts.com/2017/02/24/new-orleans-food/

If you come here, do not leave without getting the garlic knots!!! Seriously. They are amazing. They always have slices of the day and lunch specials! And if they're too busy in the dine in area, just walk next door and order there!

Had a wonderful dinner here on Friday night. The bacon cheese bread was like eating a slice of pizza. It was tasty. I had lobster bisque. It was so good. There was plenty of large chunks of lobster in it. I had salmon that I think was cooked in hoisen sauce with lemon grass. Very good. My wife had sauteed sea scallops with shitake mushrooms. I tasted hers and I wanted to swap meals. Just eat there early before the bar area fills up with loud music and drunk young people that act like its the first time out drinking (typical downtown).

This place is fantastic! We've order lunch and breakfast a few times and each dish has been delicious. I knocked off one star because the taquitos were a tad over done the last time we ordered. However, the service is great! The food I ordered was a bit too spicy for me and the young man at the counter graciously allowed me to order something else (think his name was David). Can't wait to go back :)

This hotel was very conveniently located to all the things my husband and I needed to do in Philly during our last visit there. Close to many historical sites, some live music venues, our friend's art gallery, shopping, and great food. The doormen were always on top of their game, never missed a beat. I felt looked after and safe. It was really easy to get a taxi or rideshare to-and-from the hotel. Inside, the lobby was comfortable where I found a mix of tourists and business people. The front desk and concierge were all smiles (which is so appreciated!) and ever-helpful. I really felt like I was a regular treated with such kindness and respect, and that they recognized me. The elevators were quick and in good working condition. Our room was spacious, clean, and had a nice view of the boulevard. Though it was humid and hot outside, it was nice and cool inside. I appreciated that the desk working area was large and plentiful. And I always appreciate hotel rooms where electrical outlets are placed thoughtfully. I would definitely stay here again!

No other restaurant in the area has been as consistent as Anthonys.
Certain things like the chicken parm have become very expensive but then again the quality is always there. 
Family owned and operated. I would recommend highly.

This place is utterly fabulous.  It is not the *nicest* looking place but really who eats AT a pizza place these days...most of the big boys are counter service with no dining anyways.  We always get the supreme pizza large (the small just doesn't seem to work right proportionally with the toppings) and often get a Philly cheese loaded which is to die for.  My husband and I don't go out much as we are home cookers and are more often than not disappointed by eating out between the cost and the quality of food, but this place is a no brainier for us every time.  Locally owned rather than a big chain and the difference is clear.  Wings are pretty good for breaded style with a tasty sauce...I just prefer mine to the point of almost burnt so they aren't quite crispy enough for me...haven't tried anything else but imagine it's all on the same level.

After visiting Tir Na Nog about 10 times, it's high time for a review!
We are Sunday morning people who really enjoy the early opening they offer. We have had nothing but good times, and MUST attribute that to Lucky, a most amazing bartender. He is friendly, talkative, wonderfully smart...and that makes all the difference!
Always great food and the service at the Chesterfield location is always top notch. Especially great for large groups.

Huh??
What a strange experience.....
Went there on a Saturday afternoon for a mid afternoon snack and beer.
Walked in to a nearly empty bar / dining room. Sixteen of the nineteen TV's were on to an assortment of football games and a couple of network shows. Ok.  But the only sound in the room was the blaring volume from one of the TV's that was tuned to a football game on Fox. It echoed thru the entire place; all of it....the game, then the car commercials, the drug commercials, the insurance commercials...... everything. We (all 20 of us) were bombarded by this. Why?? 
Meanwhile the lone bartender was slow to see me.....slow to offer menu..... and never checked on me once I received my beer and appetizer. Oh, yeah....the appetizer... Supposedly a specialty...Chicken wings with caramelized onions in a balsamic glaze. The three strands of onion added nothing to the shockingly bland, thin glaze that coated the puny wings. Nearly tasteless. 
Meanwhile, two miles down the street, PJ Whelihan's was packed.

This is a sports bar (kind of) saloon good to meet for drinks in a group setting. Food not so tasty...typical pre made lower end bar food. Fish and Chips looked and tasted like Gorton's from the frozen section and Burger was pre package, but better than average.

We're lucky in Indy to have some really excellent options for Thai, and Thai Spice is one of the best. I have yet to find a dish here that doesn't meet my expectations, and I've tried a lot... appetizers, soups, salads, curries, noodles, you name it. My favorites here are the curry puffs (curried chicken, potatoes, and onion in a flaky fried pastry dough), spring rolls, the pla goong spicy shrimp salad, and the me ga tee coconut peanut noodles. The menu is extensive, and it's my goal to someday try everything!

The prices are very reasonable, about $10-12 for giant entrees, and the staff are very attentive and friendly. Like someone else mentioned, I recommend starting at "medium" heat and moving up from there if you can handle it. It's also good for groups.

Great food! We got the platter for lunch and loved it.

The place is extremely simple (if it wasn't for yelp, you'd guess the food would be pretty mediocre from the set up). It is shared with a cheap grocery store. The service was a bit slow. But it was all worth it! Open 24 hours.

If your idea of a date is going to a thrift shop... this could be a great follow up!

Truman and his son Kurtis have amazed me by making me feel like a true part of the family. I have nothing but great things to say about this restaurant and it's employees. The food is phenomenal, the atmosphere is pleasant, and the all around dining experience is one that I couldn't put a price on. I take all my out of state friends here. If I could give it more than 5 I would!! SAKE BOMBS WITH TRUMAN ARE MANDATORY!

Finally made it in to the new location.

Location: In a little hidden drive off of 96th, kind of a pain getting in and out on Sundays.  3/5

Food: The best salsa ive ever had, just fantastic. If you made a visit just for the salsa noone would blame you. My go tos are the Quesadilla Mazatlan and the Fajita Fundida, both are great. Arroz con camarones are good too. 4/5

Cleanliness: Didn't see any problems here but that revolving door at the entrance is a mess. Get a couple nice wooden double doors that fit the theme and you would be gold. 4/5

Value: You can usually find a coupon but be sure to PRINT it off. They started not accepting phone coupons. Prices went up again recently on some things but its still pretty good value. 4/5

Service: Always fast and polite. 5/5

Overall: If you want good solid mexican food you can't go wrong here, I'm a big fan of Riviera Maya.
Pretty creative menu and wonderful fresh oysters. Everyone is super friendly and helpful as well.

Ah!! Words are not enough to describe the simple, delicious and SO colorful dishes. Vegan friendly! I always stick to the platter, cauliflower and Brussels sprouts, and the portions are amazing to share. Aaaaand the staff is wonderful!!! Best of the best

We went at 12:30pm on a Saturday and it seemed that we were the first customers for the day! We were happy to have found this gem.

There were two men working and they were really nice and patient with us. They may be slow with their service but we had a lovely time! 

They brought us three sauces with papadum (lentil crackers) to munch on. I never had them before, but it was simple and solid for snacks. 

There wasn't a lunch special for Saturday. 

Chicken briyani is spicy enough to stop for a second and admire the flavors. You taste raisins and cashews and can't help but keep munching on. ($13.95)

Chicken tikka masala is on point, perfect to eat with naan (we ordered garlic naans which are super garlic and fantastic ($2.95?)). ($13.95)

Chicken korma is rich and hearty - i had never had it before so I was glad that Jaffron made a great impression for me. It was my favorite. ($13.95)

All the portions are generous. I thoroughly enjoyed all the dishes and hope to come back!

3 sisters gave great portions for breakfast and the food was great. I had 0 complaints with the service (Keke was great) or the food. My only issue was the space in between tables, I felt as if we were eating on top of the family next to us. 

I ordered the breakfast burrito and it was amazing. I was able to save some for later as well. This brunch spot has been in a couple different news articles and all of them were correct. I highly recommend this spot.

Short wait for a delicious lunch. Wanted something different than the food court and this hit the spot! 

Started with the Pot Roast Cheese Fries. Incredible. If you don't order this, you're doing something wrong.  There is lots in an order and it's absolutely delicious. 

The Caesar salad is huge. Comes with whole romaine leaves, croutons and Parmesan crisps. It is very good. 
The omelettes are fluffy and delicious. The egg whites aren't funny and they can put lots of toppings in them. 

Service was good. Our waiter was friendly but he kept disappearing. It took forever to order and then to find him if we needed anything. 

But the food is really good! And the wait was only about 20 minutes, we could keep shopping while we waited!

I work around the corner from Siam Pad Thai and I'm pretty sure I will not come back again after today. I've been here maybe a handful of times, But here's my explanation:

Normally when you go to an Asian restaurant, you get bad service but the food is amazing, so you find yourself coming back bc the food is good. However, I only came back bc the restaurant is close by my job. I've also gone to Jasmine and Fuji which is close by as well, but sometimes you just get lazy to go that much further. Today I walked into Siam Pad Thai and told the male server I would like a table for one. He said ok. I told him I was going to wash my hands first in the restroom. He said ok again. After coming out, I sat next to a table of 5, where the server was bringing out their food. Then, I noticed a lady walked in and sat herself across from me next to a table of 3 ppl with t-shirts that says "my". I proceeded to watch her as she sat by herself. The server walked over and greeted her, he brought her a menu and some silverware. They continued to talk, she sounded like a regular (a repeating customer). He then started walking towards the kitchen, didn't even bother to look my way. 

Now, most people would think, maybe he didn't see me? That may be a little impossible, considering I sat next to the table of 5, where he was bringing food out to, he had to avoid certain areas when dropping off their food bc I was blocking his way.

However after all that, he didn't even bother to come greet me, give me a menu, or silverware. I sat there a little shocked and confused, but decided to walk out. 

I was craving some Thai food so I called jasmine made an order than picked it up. 

Good luck to you guys who decides to go there. I hope you have a better experience than I did.

Ate at Court of Two Sisters on Sunday 10/9. Spent $160 on 4 buffets, 2 sodas, and the tip. The courtyard looked pretty and fun, too bad we were sat in an almost empty room with no music. Awkward! Also, while the hostess was seating the 4 of us, a waiter from the same room rudely cut us off. Apparently, where he needed to go was much more important than where we needed to go. $160.00 later when it was time to sign our credit card slip, a waiter (not ours), dropped off the slips of paper and TOSSED the pen at us, said no words, and walks away. At least the food was good.

Great place! I've only been to their lunch buffet, twice, but both times were delicious. Its such a good deal: $10 for all you can eat, FRESH food. AND you get unlimited ORGANIC sodas. I don't even like soda, but here I am spending several sentences raving about them. They're good. The food is not at all like your typical buffet food - they only put out around 3 main dishes, 3-4 kinds of gourmet pizza, a couple soups, 4 types of salads, and a selection of breads. But everything they put out is like something you could order as an individual dish and since they make them in small quantities, the food is constantly fresh. It's like being able to try everyone's dish at your table. The breads are freshly baked and delicious as well. All for only $10 - its a steal. 

Not to mention - you can start eating as soon as you arrive - no waiting for servers or orders to be taken!
This place deserves a five star review. The only place I would ever eat a crab cake, filled with real crab. Amazing sauce to pair with the seafood dishes. Good drinks. Absolutely love this place!

I know some would turn their nose up at a franchise "chain" bbq joint but I been fortunate enough to eat in many of the establishments that are considered the best like Kansas City Joes, Central BBQ, Pappys, Franklins, ect and this place is legit. Has been my go to in Indy area since they arrived. Im a brisket guy but have  had most everything they serve and havent been disappointed. They have some great sides as well, my favs are the vinegar slaw and sweet potato casserole.

Mediocre service and we were asked to leave our high top at the bar before 3 out of 9 of us were finished drinking our drink because they said they had reservations. (We were in the BAR. That was a first for all of us.) The appetizers were not very good; the chicken quesadillas had chunks of chicken in them that were inedible. We had to ask for plates, spoons, etc for the appys. Also very loud. There are many better places in the area for Happy Hour.

So disappointed. Place was empty at dinner time, should have known there was a reason for that. We got an appetizer - "fried" mashed potato balls. While this was tasty, they were obviously a frozen item and fried waaaay before we ordered it. We got steaks for the entree, mine was about 80% fat. Got carrots and string beans on the side, they were bland, and there was only two string beans. Nothing seemed fresh or particularly tasty. The cook/owner spent most of the time running down the street to their new Mexican restaurant. So bummed out because we always wanted to try this place and it turned out to be extremely overpriced for mediocre food.

I originally visited here when it first opened a few years ago and had a bad experience but I've heard so many good things lately I decided to give it another go and am so glad I did!! Been here twice in the last few weeks and wow is it SO good! Pizza is my favorite, you get so much for the price! Fish is also very good, the salmon with risotto was delicious! Great service and great ambiance and don't leave without a cannoli!!
Food was wonderful.  bacon wrapped scallops were buttery and yummy.  They make a mean drink too!

My husband and I have been here twice now. I finally am coming around to writing a review. Our first time there, we were with our 3 children and it was awful. The server/bartender completely forgot about us. My wine glass sat empty for over 10min. The food was mediocre and way over priced for what it was. We were there for over an hour. Bc our first experience was so terrible, we decided to go one more time, without kids. Our server was wonderful. The wine flowed quickly. The food came out in a timely fashion. But once again, the food was just alright. While everything was ok, I highly doubt we'll be back. I was sooooo hoping this place was going to be good but we were not impressed.
Tiny restaurant with huge flavors! We shared meatballs, pork loin and agnilotti and all were wonderful.

This is a tiny little place across the street from the convention center. The coffee is delicious, but my favorite thing I've had so far is the serra honey lavender. It's absolutely amazing. 

Despite the fact that the staff was absolutely swimming with customers and orders all of them were friendly. 

Might need to be a regular for me when I'm in the area.

This is one of the Best Steak Places in Town!! Took my Wife there For our 11th Anniversary. We were Greeted at the door By the Manager Troy who Promptly seated us at our Table. We were treated great by all the staff. I had the Lobster Bisque soup, shrimp & Steak witch were all very Amazing!! I would highly recommend it!!

My Wife and I decided to try the fried chicken at the Firehouse Bar & Grill. We were very pleasantly surprised. Our server, Jennifer, was very prompt and attentive at getting our drinks and taking our order. We asked about the fried chicken and we decided on the four piece meal. It came out fairly quickly and included green beans, mashed potatoes with chicken gravy,a piece of French bread with garlic butter and four pieces of perfectly cooked and seasoned fried chicken. It has been a long time since we have had chicken that was seasoned well enough to make us want to come back for more! All pieces were cooked perfectly, crisp savory coating outside and piping hot juicy inside. the portions were ample and we were able to take home a couple of pieces to have for lunch the next day. We will definitely be returning soon to try some other menu items but wouldn't hesitate recommending the chicken to family and friends.

Got into New Orleans late to catch a flight early morning. This is one of the few places that was still open when we got in town.  The place was semi-busy, and the menu looked promising, unfortunately, it did not impress.  We had the following:

-Five Pepper Calamari - lightly battered fried squid tossed with jalapeños, red & green bell peppers then seasoned with salt & black pepper - loved the texture and flavor was good

-Sizzlin' Squid - whole squid grilled then served on a hot plate with teriyaki - buttery and thick teriyaki, was decent

-Pumpkin Seed Plum Duck - Peking style crispy duck battered with pumpkin seeds in a pool of rich plum sauce - "crispy" is loosely used here.. it was very much the opposite, and the sauce, thumbs down

-BBQ Pork with Vegetables - tender boneless strips of pork marinated in Asian BBQ sauce, stir fried with mixed vegetables - sauce was really overwhelming, could not taste the and the mixed vegetables were overly drenched, meh

-Hoshun fried rice - combo (chicken, pork & shrimp) - rice was good

Definitely would not be my choice of place to eat again for late dining.. or at all..

I came with a friend for dinner late last night . The restaurant look very nice ....no really crowded in there , the price not cheap too and the menu don't have too much for choose .
    My appetizer was lobster mac-cheese , little salty but good though I only found 3 small pieces of lobster  in big plate . I got my cocktail drink's name ' key lime martini ....I love it . 
  My dinner was fish ... Absolutely I forget what the heck is fish name but they don't let me down ...I love they make with tomato with garlic and white bean I think so ....
   Anyway hockessin doesn't have much good restaurants around . Red fire is nice place for you have some drink with friend or  a date . They usually closed 1am . 
P/s they don't accept you bring wine to restaurant

My co-workers have been coming here for years, yet I have not come here until this week. I have been missing out!

They have plenty of options for chicken or tri-tip. I wanted to try both so I picked the combo plate which comes with plenty of chicken, tri-tip, beans, rice and tortillas. Oh....and also your choice of many different kinds of salsa on the side. For less than $13 you're getting an amazing deal (especially by Santa Barbara pricing standards). 

I enjoyed it and ended up going back the next evening....just because. The cuts of meats are tender and juicy, and bbq'd to perfection.

I really wish I could write a 5 star review of The Libertine. Josh Galliano is an incredibly talented chef and I've been a fan of his since he started out in St. Louis at An American Place. But, I don't know what's going on at his first sole venture. 

I've been in twice and waited to write a review to see if the kinks were worked out. It's improved (the first time I went the food was so bad we only ate a couple bites of each dish), but we went from one or two stars to three ... which was a disappointment. 

The Good: 
Service is great, bartenders are exceptionally friendly. 
Nice beer selection 
The beef cheek ragu was very tasty
The pig tails were pretty good
The Citrus dessert (Orange Curd, Lemon Cake, Dreamcicle Sorbet) was light and airy, enjoyable

The Meh: 
We were in for restaurant week so we ate at the bar, I had to keep my coat on the whole time because every time someone entered the restaurant a gust of polar vortex wind hit me. They should really put some heavy curtains up between the entrance hallway and the entryway to the bar. 

The Escabeche (Olive Oil Poached Fish, Lavash, Asian Pear, Roasted Beets) didn't have much flavor at all. 

I thought the sunflower seed fried rice was an interesting concept and tasted ok, but it's a rather small portion and more of a novelty than a solid dish. 

The Red Velvet Cake (Cream Cheese Ice Cream, Candied Cocoa Nibs, Dried Beets) was just ok. The cake was quite dense and I couldn't taste the slightest bit of cream cheese in the ice cream. 

The cocktail list appears inventive, but honestly, if I'm going to pay $10 for a cocktail I'll go to Taste. None of the cocktails I've had here are worth $10. 

I'll probably keep going back to The Libertine every 6 months or so in the hopes that Galliano is making his signature eyes-roll-in-the-back-of-your-head-it's-so-good food.  But right now, no high hopes =/.

I stopped here after the beach for a early lunch. I got the Don pressed sandwich and potato salad. Both items ordered were excellent. It tasted so good. Very fresh. The establishment is small and quaint. The employees were so friendly. Do yourselves a favor and make this Deli a priority stop! I will be back for more!

delighted at philly's ramen renaissance, i HAD to try ramen boy even though i only had 10 minutes left till i had to be at work. coming from nyc, i didn't know when i'd be back again! the waitstaff was super accommodating, being as i told them i was short on time. the waitress brought me my water, & menu immediately and put my order right in with urgency, which i thought was nice of her. it was about half full at 2pm on a wed afternoon.

i ordered the tonkotsu (ramen boy classic) since it's my personal favorite. who isn't in love with pork?? the broth was tasty enough, but didn't have enough depth to last the whole meal. it started getting bland mid-meal. the egg was nicely soft boiled which was a plus! i get so annoyed when i get a hard boiled egg....i know, i'm crazy, but i love me some soft boiled egg in my ramen =) and the noodles....i can't quite describe it but they had a funny texture. unlike any ramen noodle i've had. it felt al dente, but maybe it wasn't fresh ramen? i can't put my finger on it, but i know i didn't like it. it really brought the dish down for me. and another minus- no hot tea at the end. it's just one of those nice touches i've grown accustomed to after a hearty bowl of ramen- a nice, light, steamy mug of green tea to seal the meal. so i gulped down some ice water, and ran off to work. i will most likely be back to try the rest of the ramen on its menu. hope for a better experience, as i love to see philly's food scene thrive!

Everyone always raves about this restaurant. 
I really did not enjoy the food at all. I ordered the turkey pesto sand which and tortilla soup and I thought the food was very bland, my mother ordered a grilled cheese and broccoli cheese soup and it tasted like nothing. There was no flavor at all. I would not recommend.

My wife and I have lunch here every few weeks and have never had a bad meal. The seafood is always fresh and delicious, and the seafood linguini and lobster ravioli is amazing every time. Despite the Yelp description, there really is nothing "Asian fusion" about it, apart from the owners being Vietnamese. The owner is very friendly and has a great sense of humor. It's obvious that he takes pride in his business and it shows through the stellar customer service. This place is a real gem and has become our little Italian restaurant.

The decor is very inviting and immaculate.  I had a rum and coke with their wine based rum...it did not disappoint. The oxtail dish was excellent and the cocoa bread was the taste of the Caribbean i was craving. When I'm in the Tampa area, I will definitely stop back in for more deliciousness!  The staff was extremely friendly and attentive. A very enjoyable experience overall!

Holy cow, their donuts are amazing! I'm not exactly sure what a vegan or "vegetable" donut is, but they were hands down two of the best donuts I've ever had. Just wow! We stopped by in the afternoon around 12 and the donuts were still fresh. We had glazed and maple and I can't wait to go again and try more of them. If you're in Tucson and you like donuts at all, this is a MUST!
I has the blue cheese burger, what a delicious thing, the service was excellent, definitely I will come back again.

Spiro's Restaurant is our favorite place to eat in st Charles.. the food is great, no matter what menu item you order. But, the stuffed filet and stuffed pork chop will blow you away...
The staff are all friendly and do a great job of everything you need to have a great night out for dinner.. you will not be disappointed.
Our only negative is we don't go there more then we do. 
Also a special shout out to Deian who always makes my wife and I feel special and welcomed like we were going to his own house for dinner.
Food was fine. Prices were fine. Service was a joke.

I've been here a few times and it was just ok. This time it was completely different though. Seems like they might have gotten a new chef and/or management because it was like going to a new restaurant. The food was over the top good and service was a million times better. The oysters and mussels for appetizers were incredible and nice portion size on the mussels. I ordered the sweet potato gnocchi for my entree and by far one of the best I've even had. The butter cream sauce it came with was so good I could have drank that on it's own. My husband got the chicken dinner which came with coconut rice wrapped in what looked like plantain leaves to hold the flavour. Again, portion sizes for both of these entrees was very good and we were stuffed. Definitely recommend this spot!

This restaurant is really great, locals recommended it to us and I'm glad we went there. The service is great, also the wine and the food is just amazing. The place is kinda small but very cozy. The portions are very big, so you'll be full after, the price is good for what you get. The food is really good. 
Will definitely come back.

WOW oh WOW!  This is the place,  awesome selection of rotating brew on tap!  Also from time to time their own home made brew!!  The pizza and salads outstanding, and of course the home made ice cream, doesn't get any better.  Great place to go to watch Wildcats BB game.  Nice touch to have one of the owners, Eric to come around and greet his guests, I feel like a celebrity even though I'm a bum!  Always come here when in town, usually ones a month, and thanks to "Ryan" for promoting this place, my mouth is drooling as I write this, the craving is getting stronger, time to take the 500 mile drive to 1702!  Also order 2 samples at a time to enjoy and bring your friends.
My bread was stale which was disappointing. Although, I went during their lunch hour rush and was out the door within 5 minutes!

Good sushi, good service, and chill atmosphere. Everything I've had, has been good. 

They have am outdoor seating to watch the night go by in a residential part of the marigny.
Excellent service and food. Great for business or a nice lunch with a friend. Quiet and pleasant dining rooms. Moderate piece. Easy parking in the public lot for 75 min free, or vallet.

Tried this place for the first time last night. I gotta say I think after twenty years of looking in for a true Northern/ New York flat style crust pizza.... This is it!!!! The crust/sauce/mozzarella was amazing. The staff was super friendly in fact I told them I had other business in the area ..... so the told me to call when I was on my way to insure I would get a fresh hot pie. Definitely coming back...

First let me say that I waited a few weeks after dining here to write this because I was actually angry when I left and I didn't want to sound like a Karen. I also desperately wanted this to be a great experience as I was told by many people that this place was excellent. 

I know that most restaurants are dealing with being understaffed but if that's the case then don't take the reservation.

Our evening started with waiting about 10 minutes for menus. We gave our drink order at that point. They were out of one of the drinks so we had to reorder. It took 5 minutes for the non alcoholic drinks to arrive. We then ordered dinner. Shortly after the rolls appeared. They were hard as a rock. They weren't day old, more like days old. That's when we were told that they were out of prime rib. We then had to re order as everyone in my party had ordered the prime rib. Shortly after that we were informed that they were out of NY strip... This is a place that has steak in the name. 

Finally on the 3rd try we were able to order dinner that they actually had. The salads were served that's when I asked about the wine and mixed drinks. The waiter said he forgot. My wife ordered wine but I ordered a gin and tonic. What I got was a gin and water because when I sent it back I was told that they were out of tonic. So I just drank water for thre rest of the night.

The steak was actually amazing. It was probably the best I've had in years. The problem was that again they were out of the sides we had ordered. So we just cancelled them. 

We skipped desert because I couldn't take being told they were out of something else. 

It was a pretty disappointing night as this place has excellent reviews and my hopes were high.

We had an excellent experience.  The blue cheese stuffed olives made a fantastic martini.  We also really enjoyed the octopus salad, the grilled asparagus salad, and a "hog fish" special.  Peter was our waiter and spot on, with his service and advice.  It's a favorite spot in St Pete Beach and we will definitely be back!  Thank you!

As someone who works in the wellness industry, I greatly appreciate the addition of Sliced to our Nashville market.  It is hard to find good healthy food at lunch time.  I sometimes drive from Franklin just to eat lunch.  The meats are awesome.  They have only 3 ingredients.  You cannot get this healthy of a sand which meat in your local grocery, at the cost that Sliced charges. I would suggested you look at the ingredients in the deli meat you are purchasing.   I often buy it for my family for the weeks lunch.  I love the salads, too.   If you don't want to eat healthy, you may want to stick to fast food.....but if you are looking for a healthy spot to eat, I suggest you try some of the best food in town......Sliced.   You can't beat the adult grilled cheese and tomato soup!  My niece is addicted to the Classic (Up East) Italian Sand which.  Again, it is nice to have a new healthy option in the Nashville area!  Thanks Sliced!

If you want authentic creole food, this is your first stop. Come in to support owned business but you'll return over and over because the food is amazingly delicious. 
Our waitress Trisha was the best. I was so hungry I thought the extra side of carrot soufflé passing me by was for me and ended up eating two. Omg was that good! I'm 2k miles away now and still thinking of that delicious carrot soufflé and the fried chicken. I only had enough time to take the photo of it before I inhaled it.

Served my wife's food without ribs and told us they were out. Then 30 minutes later they served someone in next to us ribs. What the heck. Poorly ran establishment. We've never been here and had everything perfect. If it wasn't close to home we would never eat here. Don't waste your time, it's worth the drive going somewhere else

Update- 5-2-2018
Ate here again and what a mistake, this place is poorly managed. Took over an hour to get food, no refills, manager apologized and continued to make excuses. It's not the customer fault if people don't show up for work or someone is new. We expect decent service for the price we pay, not perfection. 
I left more money than we should have on the table just to leave. Never received a bill

First let me preface with the fact that I used to be the manager at local movie Theatres and I've never had to pay to watch a movie. I've also been to the cine bistro in Hyde park previously so my expectations were pretty high. 

I received tickets as a gift from one of my patients recently and she raved about her experience so I decided to finally go check out the Mockingjay Part 1. The theatre itself has a modern upscale feeling when you first walk in but that soon dwindles when you see the three lines in front of registers and people arguing who got there first. If the cashier would just focus on her line then it could have been avoided. 

The theatre seemed to be large. However when I decided to "check things out" it took me all of 2 minutes to see everything and I was not impressed. 

The theatre screens are too high and the seats were stiff and reminded me of a computer chair. 

The service was was not impressive. The waitress took everyone in the theatre order except for us. We did not get the opportunity to order until the movie started and took 30 minutes to get our soft drinks. Our meal came very close to the end. 

I was not impressed with my margarita flatbread. It was more like a thick slice of cheese accented with a few tomatoes. The chips and salsa were good and the strawberry lemonade was delightful. 

I guess it was an experience but for the price of the food and movie interruptions I will not be returning anytime soon. I would much rather head out to cinebistro where there are no children allowed and the food and service are higher quality.
Very good BBQ, great sauces and amazing sides! I will definitely be coming back. The layout is very inviting with lots of TVs to watch your favorite game.

So surprised at the negative reviews for this place. I'd never been to the Rec Room before and we were looking for an all ages venue to go for dinner that was also entertaining for my mum and my daughter. 
We arrived hungry so went straight to THREEten, one of three eateries inside the Rec Room. We watched the Oilers game on the enormous screen above the bar and enjoyed a caesar. 
The Caesar was really good and came with an incredible garnish of salami, pickled egg and gherkin. The clamato was very pickley too - yum! 
I ordered the deviled eggs to share with the group and they were bacon topped, really creamy and a nicely presented appetizer. I had the salmon salad and it was massive! It came with asparagus, and was drizzled in a yogurt dressing. The flavours were fab together. I really enjoyed but like I said... it was HUGE. I left a lot of the leaves so the server enquired if I enjoyed it if she could get me something else. That's great service, guys! At one point, the manager just popped over to say hi and check we were all good.  
Then we went to the arcade area, we got $15 worth and played a few games. It was super fun and a Monday night is the perfect time to go. Not too busy and you can pretty much walk up to any game you want to play without needing to wait. You get a card pre loaded with your tickets and if you win those tickets automatically load onto the card. It's pretty hi tech.
There is a virtual reality area and axe throwing, plus the other two eateries to check out next time.

Seriously good food!! We stopped in here after a movie at the Riverside and had an amazing dinner! I had the Luau Kalua Pork sandwich turned into a salad complete with coconut cilantro rice. Husband had the tres tacos and was more than satisfied. No alcohol served here, but you are welcome to bring beer or wine from the wine bar across the courtyard or from the store on the corner. Be sure and say Hi to Sabrina who is working hard in the kitchen making sure everything is just right!  Great experience all over --,
Great staff, great food and always accommodating. We enjoy our brunches, breakfasts and more.
Best raw oysters I have ever eaten. The horseradish mixed with the cocktail sauce was superb. This is a definite must at happy hour for .75 cent oysters and half price drinks.

Super packed, tons of beer, great food. It is a must go if you're touring breweries like we were. I'm not a local so I don't know the scene but I had a great time here and plan to come back. Philadelphia has a great beer scene and feels more laid back than at home.

I'm not in any sense a vegan gluten free or anything like that kind of guy. But I do enjoy eating healthy and i really like this place. It's kind of like a healthier version of chipotle with more and better options. Lot of cool delicious food and it's very quick and affordable. Great place for lunch or early dinner.

The Texas luau and Lockhart legend are my absolute favorite burgers. They're so juicy and full of flavor. The jalapeños in the Texas luau are just the kick I need without completely overdoing it. The onion rings on the Lockhart legend are perfectly cooked and so crunchy.

Their fries though are AMAZING!!!!! Whether they're just skinny fries, cheese fries(with or without chili), or the luau fries, they're a must have.

And lastly, they're milkshakes. Spiked or not, they're still scrumptious. My favorite non-spiked milkshake is worms & dirt. And my favorite spiked milkshake is the mint chocolate chip. Try. Them. All.
I received a half rotten salad tonight when I ordered delivery. I have a picture of the completely BLACK lettuce that the kitchen staff OKAYED to go out to a paying customer. Absolutely disgusting.

How is it that I've been sitting for an entire hour at the independent and they bartenders/servers have walked around us multiple times without so much as looking at us while servicing other tables.

...might the reason be that we are the only Poc in the entire establishment?
Absolutely hands down the best Bank I know. All employees are included in being the best too. FYI this review was by my own free will. I highly recommend banking with Suncoast

Had breakfast there last Sunday and the atmosphere is nice and our waiter was very good and personable.
The food was ok.  The best part of the food was reading the description of each entree... it made your mouth water and I was so looking forward to what I ordered.  
The food was very bland and not near as exciting as it's description.   I wasn't the only one at our table that wasn't impressed ... there were a few others that were like ... meh... it's ok but not great.  As a side note ... Along with my entree order I asked for coffee with cream ... and received cup of coffee with what looked to be skim milk... I was told it was whole milk and was informed they didn't have any cream!!!  What!!! I Thought that was pretty humorous considering where we were!

My husband and I made a visit on a Saturday evening. It felt lovely outside so we sat on the patio. Our waitress was very pleasant and extremely helpful. The only thing I would say about the service was that the food took a really long time to come out. My husband and I prefer the spacing of our meals but the time it took for each meal to come out was a bit too long. Another table next to us also complained of the hour wait. Hopefully this isn't a reoccurring thing. 

The wine was delicious and my husband had a Manhattan. He enjoyed it very much. We started with the spicy Italian & kale soup. It was hearty and flavorful! We also had the shrimp and pork dumplings. They tasted very fresh. For our entrees, I had the salmon dish on au gratin potatoes filled with cheddar cheese accompanied with crispy Brussels sprouts. It was SO good! It was savory and indulgent! I will come back surely for this dish! My husband had the pork chop and even though it was very good, it wasn't as good as the salmon. 

We opted out of dessert for that evening. Even though the service was not amazing, I would surely give it another try. This restaurant has four stars for a reason!

Great beer list and awesome gaming area! I only wish I had more money to pour into the gaming machines! And maybe a little more money to sample all the drafts on tap:)

I played a little old school PAC man, some Simpsons (which brought me back!), shot some hoops and played giant connect four (and lost!!).

It's super spacious inside, so it's easy to move from one game to another. I also like that on some games they have cup holders. Who doesn't like to drink and game? Dang, that sounded super nerdy!

Extra bonus points for the free popcorn out of the large popcorn machine in the back.

Well, here I am again, ashamedly caught up in going back to the same restaurant for the second time in a week. But, for the record, that just shows how good this restaurant really is! 
Nice atmosphere, good food, and pleasant service, they really have it all.

I've even began calling this place the Cheesecake Factory of Thai Food, because thats how large the menu is. The first time I came here I was overwhelmed with the vast amount of choices the menu had on it because, It features a Thai side as well as a Vietnamese side. Both sides of the menu seem equally enticing, but I choose mainly of the Vietnamese dishes such as the Grilled Pork Banh Mi, Chicken Pho, and the fried spring rolls. The food exceeded my expectations, and the portions were generous too. When I went back I sampled the Thai Tea and the Chicken and Shrimp Vermicelli Bowl (highly recommended). Everything was fresh, hot, and had great flavor as it should be. 

The only unpleasantry I have to add is that sometimes the service can be a bit slow, but I believe that is because they just opened and have few staff members. Perhaps they should look into hiring a few more people, because their reviews have been mostly positive and I'm sure that they will start picking up some more traffic in the restaurant soon. I know I'll be back again! I'm so thrilled that there's finally a good quality Thai/Vietnamese place close by my location; but my waistline won't be.

This is a great place to grab lunch. The menu is limited in my opinion but enough to have the usual -turkey club, burger, salad options. This place is a little expensive although it is right on the mainline.

I've been obsessed with this pizza since they were operating out of Win Win coffee bar. So happy to see he's got his own place now. This is seriously the Best pizza I've ever had in Philly. 

Look at the photos... they speak for themselves! The crust is so fluffy on the square pizza, which is my favorite. Every pizza on the menu you can't go wrong. Add toppings, customize, whatever you want. This pizza is a delicious work of art! 

Cash only. You need to  arrive approx 30 mins prior to doors opening or the pizzas will be sold out within the hour. Also, not much seating inside, so carry out or take your pizza to nearby Philly Brewing to eat it. So delicious!! Worth the wait. 100%

Need a hip/contemporary space to get work done or catch up with a friend over tea or coffee? Foundry is a great place to go! There is plenty of seating, whether its at a bar top, booth, comfy chair, or outdoor seating for those nice warm days, there is a spot for everyone. Not only do they serve coffee/teas, but they also have breakfast and lunch items! Open until 1800, and wifi is free! I had their bacon scone and woah! It was just what I needed! And of course any bacon treat I can try I will!

Ordered pizza at 6pm showed up at 845pm at the front desk at fair field in willow grove. Pizza was cold and shared with a coworker. that night we were both in the bathrooms all night and few times at work. Good god how in the hell do you screw up pizza?

Omg this is the grossest Chinese food I have ever had.  I am not sure how they make the sweet and sour sauce but I spit it out.  Smells like ketchup.  The crab rangoons are so bad I will not eat them either.  Crab rangoons are usually my favorite.  These taste like carrots with cream cheese.  I am so disappointed.

This place is ridiculous! I ate in, and the service was amazing. As were the unlimited sides. The po boy was HUGE! My roommate and I are both big eaters and neither of us could finish ours. You definitely can not ask for a better meal for $10. I wish they'd put one in Broad Ripple...

Great atmosphere, but even with reservations, we waited for about 30 minutes, so that was a turn off.

The service and food were excellent which made up for the initial, poor service.

Really good food. Friendly staff. Had the seafood bisque, clam chowder, baked clams, and crab imperial fries. Portions were huge, didn't need to order an entree. Will definitely come back if I'm in the area

This was one of the worst dining experiences I have had. We were seated immediately on a Friday at 6PM... in what could only be called the "family section". It was a back room with several LOUD arcade games and six other families. The children were all running around and our table was closest to the games so we were constantly hearing parents attempt to referee their children or corral them back to their table. I don't mind children at all, but it was absolutely unenjoyable for a meal. 

The food was mediocre. I had a burger that was clearly frozen and burnt. My daughter's kids' grilled cheese was so unappetizing and dry, she wouldn't even touch it. 

The waitress and even busboy were very kind, however the service and wait times were ridiculous. We didn't get our drinks for almost 15 minutes and weren't even asked for our meal orders for another 10 minutes. 

Finally, the bathrooms were disgusting. Worst than a gas station bathroom. I didn't even want to wash my hands in there. 

We would never go back to this place and would r suggest it to anyone.
Amazing food. Every. Single. Visit. Grab a Cuban sandwich and head over to Green Bench for a beer!

We visited this location for early breakfast on a Thursday morning. As soon as we arrived, my toddler needed to use the restroom. Unfortunately, all 3 toilets in the women's bathroom had noticeable feces on the outside bottom of the toilet and in the toilet. The bathroom floor was absolutely disgusting. This should have been enough reason to leave, but we stayed and ordered. 

My daughter's milk was delivered spoiled with chunks of rotten milk floating in the cup. When we shared this with our server, he just offered to remove it from the tab with an apology. 

I would not recommend visiting this restaurant. Outside of being understaffed like almost every other place (this is understandable due to continued strain from the pandemic), they are not clean and clearly have an issue with spoiled/rotten products.

The atmosphere is beautiful. Warm reclaimed wood with community long tables or individual high-tops. This is a great place with a date, catching up with friends, or coming in for an after-work drink solo.

Must Dos:
1) Cocktail or Wine flights. 3 for $20. The cocktail flight is amazing. They are very generous with their pours. And you can to choose 2 reds or 2 whites with your wine flights too. 

Pros:
1) Did I mention the cocktails already?
2) They also have a 2 Plates plus Entree for $30. Considering the entrees are like $20, this is a deal! But, the plates are probably slightly smaller than normal. The trick is to get the 3 for $30 deal and then order more plates to share!
3) Bread Plate. Choose 3 or 5. You can't go wrong and I love the apple jams.
4) Kale and Pigs ears. This was my favorite dish. Large enough to share.
5) Devil Eggs. Very Good here, but it wasn't that overly special.
6) Collar greens. There was a hint of some fruit in it.
7) Chicken and Waffles (good, but the peanut butter was a little weird)
8) Fried Oysters were good

Cons:
1) Shrimp and Grits were my least favorite. Or maybe b/c it was 3 pieces of shrimp and the grits were just okay. Do not get this. I expected more from an entree.
2) Pricey for comfort food. It will be around/at least $50 a person. It's good food, but it's simple comfort food. 

Honestly, the best part of the meal was the cocktails and atmosphere. The service was great/friendly. I would come back for the fried chicken meal, BLT, and some other large plates. Plus- always the wine or cocktail flight!

I ordered Uncle Bill's Skillet and my partner ordered the blueberry pancakes.  The pancakes here are worth a try.  Large and covered in copious amounts of fresh toppings. The bacon strips are also thick and huge. This place fills up fast, however, we were there on a Sunday morning and only waited about 5 minutes for a table.  Staff is all kind. Typical favorite breakfast joint.

Came here yesterday for a late lunch/early dinner. Our waiter (forget name) was the man, very funny and did a great job. To start, we got the spanakoptia which was really good. For my main, I got the lamb chops with tzatziki and potatoes (essentially fries). The lamb chops were delicious and cooked perfectly. The potatoes were a bit unseasoned. The person I went with got the lavraki (Chilean sea bass), which they enjoyed too.   We got the salted caramel baklava and the autheneus cheesecake for dessert. The cheesecake was really good and the baklava was solid. Cool place and would consider coming back.

I love high tea.. it's truly a passion of mine. I've had high tea in England and since then almost every "tea house" experience I have is vastly disappointing. 

This place really tried, I could sense the effort but in almost every aspect Royal Tea House fell short. 
-You didn't get to pick your tea - I don't like being forced into any libation I didn't choose 
-The scones were moist and the clotted cream reminded me of flavorless yogurt 
-they had the right idea with the sandwiches I suppose, but they weren't by any means great - I mean it's a sandwich it's not that hard to mess up 
-the sweets were way TOO sweet 
-Also I'm not sure if this is just me but the whole establishment felt like a bed and breakfast in the middle of nowhere with a bunch of cats (even though royal tea house had no cats) 

I feel like I have unrealistic expectations for high tea since I had the real thing but hey I will always continue my quest to find a tea house that doesn't put me in a bad mood 

*on a side note I did hear another women having tea say it was the best tea place she's been too!

Found prasino in yelp reviews and decided to give it a try! The hostess was friendly and server was equally friendly and promptly took our drink and food order. We ordered the hummus with crudités, to start off with and it was mediocre. For entree I ordered their lobster roll and salad, husband ordered short ribs. The roll was a little different than I expected, the lobster was chopped up into little pieces mixed with celery, almost like a salad but with a very vinegary dressing. I was told I could pick a side so I chose their prasino salad which was a lemony dressing, pair that with a vinegary sandwich = very tart meal. Husband's short rib was okay , more like braised meat then short ribs. What bothered me most about this experience was our server, Not so much the food. She was sweet and attentive in the beginning then just completely dropped off towards the end of our meal. She was no where in sight what seemed like eternity. It was later in the evening, literally 3 tables left in the dining area and no server. Perhaps busy doing side work to try to leave early that evening which is fine but give us our check and we'll be off our merry way! 
P.s, sides do not come with the meal as she explained earlier, they charge for sides.

Food was mediocre at best... Food was extremely overpriced for what you received.
would not go back.
would not recommend.

I had lunch at Murrieta's last week with a couple of girlfriends. The food was really good. Two of us had the cobb salad, one with shrimp and one with chicken. It was presented very nicely and was just the perfect amount. The other had a chicken sandwich with really yummy looking fries.

The service was pretty lack luster though. I think we had a pretty new server, not just to the restaurant, but to the industry. She was pleasant, but no the sharpest knife in the drawer. Overall, the service didn't take away too much from the experience as the food still came out quickly and there weren't many other diners there at the time.

Good day,

First time going to the restaurant went to the bar a gentlemen in a company shirt came up and asked if we were eating in.  We said no just grabbing a drink.  The gentlemen who I assume was the manager or owner just walked away in the middle of the conversation.  Wow did that really just happened?  I expect a little better customer service for a business that JUST opened.  A simple, "the gentlemen behind the bar can help you" would have sufficed.  This business will NOT last if you don't respect the people from the community.  Remember you're a guest here.  Ohhh and this happened approximately 2/14/2020 5:10PM EST

Regards,

2.5 stars.

The sandwiches are almost ok. It lacks flavor but if it is late at night and you absolutely need something to eat, this place is an option. They certainly aren't gourmet. They also sell day old bread for $.50

Amazing queso Biria tacos ! 
Really good chips and guacamole .
Also tried the street corn.
Service was excellent. 
I would definitely return!

Exceptional experience.

This place hasn't been open very long, and people are crowding in to give it a try!  The lobby was pretty full when we arrived.  We were expecting a party of 7 so we put our name in and were given a 15-20 minute wait time estimate.  It was probably about 25 minutes before we sat down, which was still faster than I expected.

We sat and began to go over the menu.  There were about a million different things I wanted to try, so I can't wait to go back again.  We were told about the coffee off the day, a key lime coffee.  Naturally intrigued, I had to order it.  It was really a normal nutty brew topped with whipped cream and a lime twist, but was good nonetheless.

For my meal I tried the potato head casserole.  Hash browns with onions, held together by sour cream.  Topped with a queso sauce, mushrooms, breakfast sausage, peppers, and an egg your way.  I substituted chorizo, which was a great choice.  You know any type of casserole in a restaurant will be totally pre-made and basically just heated up to order, but this was still delicious.  Well done.

I would highly recommend giving it a try.  I know I'll be back!
mostly adequate if not a bit gimmicky food.  The pastry can be fresh or it can be a bit stale.  Get there early for the former.  Best brunch in town?  methinks not.

Yet another slow meal service including the usual completely undercooked steak, followed by "let me know if there is anything else I can do for you" after you're table has waited ten minutes for your meal to arrive while thiers is now cold. The service continues to worsen as well as the customers.

Not a couples spot, definitely not for kids...if you are rowdy drinkers looking for overpriced food served with free peanuts, I guess this is your place. I'm done with this nonsense. See you in a couple years for a new review.
Wonderful place and wonderful food. We came all the way from Washington to try this place well worth it.
We had a chocolate croissant and the bacon egg and cheese croissant, a delicious way to start your day next to the beach.

Once you step inside you are immediately greeted with that southern hospitality which is terrific. There is lots of seating inside which is great, and helps the waiting time go fast! I ordered the crawfish and grits which is served with a slow cooked egg. This was my first time trying crawfish, and I wouldn't want to try it for the first time other than New Orleans. I also got the fried chicken sandwich to split wit a friend, and it was delicious. 

The cocktails here are on point as well. I suggest getting a frozen cocktail you will not be disappointed! The bakery offering looks to good to turn down. I ordered the banana bread after I was clearly full, but I'm glad I did it was amazing!

Winston was wonderful! I highly recommend the garlic rock shrimp appetizer. The crab legs were also great, as was the crab trap drink. Overall, a great experience. Wonderful views of the beach behind us. Fun experience.

This place was amazing! this was the first place we stopped in NOLA. 
they accomadated all 8 of us and ALL of our luggage. 

Our server was knowledgeable as well as friendly. 

I split the seafood platter and a side of the cajun fries, which were delicious. 

For checking in on yelp, you either get a free glass of wine, or dessert. So we went with the dessert. Got the Banana Foster Ice Cream cake. which was seriously tasty. 

There was only one bathroom, which was hard to get into, someone was always in and out.

Was on my way to wegmans and thought I would try this place as I saw all the glowing reviews.  Maybe I got the wrong thing as everyone raves about the pizza but I didn't think the so called Italian hoagie was very good.  It was edible but doesn't measure up to Carmines.  Roll so so and the ham was nothing special.  Only had a few slices of salami.  To be honest it didn't really taste like an Italian hoagie.  Guess they never heard of capocollo.
Steve's is in Glendora!!! Holy $h*t!!  No more driving to Sea Isle City for the best mac n cheese grilled cheese EVER!! The only complaint I have is.... it's TOO close to home. Lol. ;)

Update on my last review.. I was contacted by the owner and the issues were resolved. And she was very polite and mailed me a gift card to give the restaurant a try again. Which i appreciated. So my husband and I gave it a try again the day before vday (2/13) and it was GREAT like how it was before the previous visit. Hostess had our reservation, our waitress was amazing...and of course the food was fantastic. And the place was PACKED! I do recommend you make a reservation to come here because it gets full here. (Which is always a great sign) food wise I recommend for the appetizer black mussels..entree the salmon or steak..dessert ALL OF THEM cant go wrong lol.

Quite a disappointment. Went to the Bistro for anniversary dinner. When we entered the restaurant there was no one at the hostess stand and no indication to wait or seat yourself. After waiting for several minutes a waitress zipped by to say she would be right there. Once seated I was sorry to see such a small menu. The flatbread was very good with fresh mozzarella though. I ordered the Bistro salad, which ended up being nothing more than I could have made at home, and was drowned in dressing.  My husband's pork was fried and very thin , not very tasty. Will NOT be going back.
Perfect balance of flavors and textures! We split the halibut sandwich and arugula salad! Service was spot on, thanks Matt!

Went here for the first time tonight! I had never tried Indian good but my friend who is from India invited me and recommended it so with an empty stomach and open mind I happily trailed along! 

Firstly, the place is super clean and nicely set up. There was Indian style music lightly playing over the speakers that was actually very catchy. 

Secondly, the service at first was a miss. My waitress spoke too softly and mumbled and slurred all her words together and I didn't find her to be especially polite. Not mean, but also not the type to give you warm fuzzy feelings either. BUT the service was saved during checkout when the gentleman working obliged my five guests by splitting our bill 5 ways after the original waitress put it all on one tab and he did it all very quickly and with a smile! 

Thirdly, the real reason you're still reading this review: the food. I ordered the chicken tikka masala (you can order it different levels of spicy-mild, spicy, extra spicy, etc) I got mine spicy and didn't find it spicy at all (although I am from a Mexican family where habaneros are topped on food like its salt). And it was delicious! It's tomato based but to me tasted a lot like red chile chicken. I added a side of steamed rice and one piece of naan (naan is bread and is a very good size). My friend ordered chicken curry and that was equally as flavorful but I still have to say my dish was my favorite! Can't wait to go back here perhaps for the buffet to try more things!

Friendly wait staff and bartenders. Drinks are great and reasonably priced (get a double for $3 extra!).

The assortment of Eggs Benedict looked great and I think I made the wrong choice and picked the shrimp omelette which was just OK.

Finally found a TRUE pizza place in Nashville. Stopped in for a late lunch and had such a wonderful visit! The pizza was perfect! Fabulous crust, thin and crispy, but still filing and tasty. The sauce is delicious, so flavorful and full of body. 
The manager, Douglas, was so awesome! It was great to find out he was from Chicago, and we knew of some of the same spots up north. Overall we LOVED this place as did all our kids (who are VERY picky). The prices are great and the service is wonderful. If you want REAL pizza, not that crap that the "chain" pizza places crank out, DEFINITELY stop by Bellshire Pizza!

Went here about a week after opening. First, we stood at one of entrances as employees walked by us, not telling us where to go or who wohld seat us. About 15 minutes in, finally someone takes us to our seat. After getting cheese dip the server disappeared for another 20 with out taking our order.  If this place was crowded I would understand but it wasn't even half full.

I really had such high hopes for this place. I love the ambiance of the restaurant and I will come back possibly with a group and have a drink. We ordered a lot of different i teams and enjoyed the queso and what they call their walking taco it has a few interesting ingredients peanuts, and bbq pork but I really enjoyed the flavors. The tacos fell short. All of our meat was really dry and flavorless. With all the different toppings I thought it'd help but I really found them terrible. My husband and I both ordered a drink. We found them to be overpriced for the size. A few interesting flavors but wasn't blown away. Service wasn't that great and there were only a few customers in the restaurant. Got the vibe we weren't really welcome. We got there an hour before closing.

A well kept secret, the MFA of St. Petersburg is a small but exceedingly well-curated museum located in a beautiful neo classical building reminiscent of the old Getty Museum in Malibu, CA.  Indeed, it has many similarities with the old Getty.

Each room seems to bring a different era into focus--buddhist, Indian, classical Greek, American School, impressionist, wondrous sculpture, Rodins, Manets, a magnificent Georgia O'Keefe, spectacular photography, et al.

All in all, breathtaking.  

There is a neoclassical courtyard open to
the public adorned by several sculptures, also reminiscent of the old Getty.

The museum store is cute and full of surpises such as Keith Haring Dominoes.  

The Dali will always be the big attraction in St. Petes, but the MFA is a big cleanup hitter.  Definitely stop by!

If I could give negative stars this particular location would earn a negative 5.  Service beyond horrible.  Was in a couple weeks ago with the family and after a family who arrived minutes before us were greeted and seated we waited nearly 30 minutes with a fairly empty dinning room while staff members continually walked by without recognizing or acknowledging we were there. My wife and daughter got fed up and went to the car. I stuck my head near the side entrance to the kitchen and asked for a manager.  She was right in front of me and I informed her of the situation and she was rude and could care less that she inconvenienced my family.  

Went back last night for Ice Cream and the girl on the counter was lost in space. I actually waived my hand in front of her to catch my attention and she was like a dear in the headlight.  I gave her a coupon and she was confused then shouted to the same manager who I dealt with the week before for some kind of card and the manager yells back she doesn't have it.  When my order was ready it literally was thrown on the counter in front of me, without our a word she turned and walked away, no bag, no thank you..... NOTHING!

This place should rename themselves SLOW & UNFRIENDLY!  Will never step foot in this franchise again! Stay away, go to Rita's or if you want ice cream go to Richman's (old Jack Frost in Glenside)

Great sandwiches. Absolutely love the roasted Brussel sprouts! Just a short walk from the World War II Museum. We have eaten here a few times and today we brought my mother and grandmother and a couple of our kids. Did not disappoint!

My dining partner and I have been going to Outback at least a few times a year for many, many years.  Outback gets awfully busy on the weekend, so we try to get there early or go during the work week; otherwise the weekend wait can be over 30 minutes (and they're good, but not good enough to wait 30 minutes for a table).
