I've never been disappointed with my meal.  The food is well-prepared, served hot, and tastes good.   The bloomin' onion is good, but it's huge and best shared with at least 4 people.  The coconut shrimp is really good.  The salads are always crisp and fresh.  On our last visit, we started with the the fresh baked pretzels with the cheese dip, and they were hot and fresh.  The cheese dip was good, but honestly, both the pretzels and the dip didn't have a whole lot of flavor.  I'd get a different appetizer next time.  We both ordered the ribeye, which were cooked perfectly and very flavorful, with a loaded baked potato on the side, which was also very good. The service was prompt.  Our drinks were refilled quickly and our check arrived promptly.

This has become the must stop on our passayunk happy hour crawl (which we admittedly have done too often). They have solid drink specials and a pretty revolving mix of food specials.  Order a few specials with some of the normal menu and you will leave very very happy.  The crispy lamb rolls, soup dumplings and pork bao buns are definitely the must try items here.  We have never been disappointed with the food or service...this is definitely a must for not just passayunk but any philly food fans.  Highly recommend...so much so that it compelled me to leave my first yelp review ever.

I eat here 2 to 4 times each week.  The octopus salad, octopus maru balls, and the yakisoba are great.  They make for great lunches - I do the yakisoba and one of the others and it's about 10 bucks.  

All that said, I have been underwhelmed by the curry burrito and the don mono.  

Note that delivery can take well over an hour at lunch times.  

As for the interior, get over it.  The guy is cooking street food and the vast majority of people do takeout or delivery.  Most importantly, the place is very clean.

I was visiting New Orleans for the weekend and had a craving for Vietnamese. Pho Tau Bay (literally meaning "flying boat" and is an archaic Vietnamese word for "airplane") is located near the medical school and most of its customers appear to be students and hospital faculty/staff.

The restaurant is very clean with a modern decor, but has a real gentrified feel to it that is out of touch with a traditional Vietnamese American restaurant. First off, the ordering process is more in tune with a Hardee's: order and pay at the counter. Condiments are dispensed into little paper cups similar to ketchup at a fast food joint, and drinks are self-service (they carry Coca Cola products here).

I ordered a Pho Dac Biet "Xe Lua" size, which translates to "locomotive size" and normally comes in a very big bowl at most other pho restaurants. However, at this Pho Tau Bay, "locomotive" size is the equivalent to a small bowl at most other places. I joked that the "Xe Lua" here must be in HO-scale ;-) The broth is acceptable and can be made spicier with Sriracha. There is plenty of meat in the pho, but the variety of cuts is more limited compared to a more traditional Vietnamese restaurant.

Being a big eater I also ordered a combination Banh Mi sandwich. This sandwich is actually more on the mark to a traditional Banh Mi, with generous amounts of vegetables, pate and cold cuts. The bread is fresh and lightly toasted. I would recommend the sandwich.

Personally, when I think of the name Pho Tau Bay, I think of small grungy Vietnamese restaurants with a lot of personal service which I am accustomed to (there is a place by the same name in Houston that fits my description). This restaurant, however, seems sanitized, sterile, and gentrified, and has lost a lot of its traditional charm in the process.

I was extremely happy with this place. It's on the RiverWalk a couple blocks from the Hilton hotel. Although very tourist-y, the food taste just like it would at the local spots. They have a live band and also next to the water. I purchased a bucket for 2 and no I didn't eat it by myself. It came with 2 full lobster, 2-3 snow crab legs, 1-2 dungeness crabs, sauteed red potatoes, corn on the cob, a crazy amount of shrimp, crawfish, mussels, and clams.  By far the best meal I had here in New Orleans. 

WARNING: Very messy and will leave an odor on your fingers for a couple hours. LMAO.

So, I am a big JJ fan and hubby & son #2 love this place. I was forced to go - full disclosure. 
We ordered our food and my bad, totally, I didn't realize there was cheese on the sub I ordered for two of the kids to split. One of which refuses to eat cheese (DNA test pending). Well, I sucked it up and paid for another sub. I asked for ONLY turkey and lettuce. It came out with turkey, lettuce and cheese. Argh!  My little one was trying to scrape the cheese off of the lunch meat and was miserable. My sub was good. I had the turkey/mushroom. Hubby loved his Italian sub and they do have a fun drink machine there. One detail I noticed that was off-putting was the pickle. Totally gross, neon green cheapie pickle. Not what I would expect from a good sub shop. I mentioned it to hubby and he said he tells them to leave it off the tray. He agrees they are gross. Oh well, I've tried this place 3 times. Not really impressed and will stick to Publix & JJ from now on.

We had French Onion Soup, terrific . The broth was more than just the usual soup stock. 
Flounder Franceis and Tallapia. Both were great. 
Good coffee and good desserts. 
It's just a great all around neighborhood eatery. 
Service was very on top of it as well.
Thanks for a great dinner! We shall return.
Well went back and to much dismay it was just plain lousy. Parm encrusted tilapia was actually in a pool of butter. The free app of pasta and broccoli was like salt lick. 
It's really a shame considering how cool of a building they have and it's rich history. They need a complete kitchen make over.

A really nice property. The location is great for being close to e French quarter  without being IN the French quarter.

Rooms are comfortable and we had an awesome view from the 35th floor.

The elevator system is pretty cool. You punch in your floor on the ground floor and it tells you which car to get on. Cool indeed, as long as it works. On our last day it was not working and there was a group of us trying to figure out how to get upstairs. I ended up hopping on a freight elevator. I'm not sure  what everyone else did.

We had drinks in the bar. It was a nice way to wind down. Drinks were reasonable considering it was a hotel bar.

Been here twice.  The only thing I would go back for is the clam chowder.  The rest is pretty run of the mill.  Husband had the grilled swordfish...it was way over done.  I had the grouper bits, which were pretty disappointing as they had a cornmeal like coating.  The salad was just ok, and the crab cakes were just ok.  Probably won't go back.

My family and I have eaten here for about 10 years for dim sum. I only get to frequent it when I come home for the holidays. But I hope we don't ever have to go back. The quality and variety of the dim sum used to be exquisite, and could be comparable to popular dim sum houses in Chicago and Seattle China towns. In the past 2-3 years, I've noticed the quality of the food has started slipping and this time it's at the point of no return. 

The fong zao (sp?--chicken feet) were dry and bland, and worse of all, spoiled. We had to return the dish, and cross our fingers that we didn't get food poisoning. We also got the pepper steak dim sum. My dad described it best, "one pile of s***." The layers of steak were stuck to each other, between layers of hardened cornstarched sauce. It lay on top of old disintegrated caramelized onions and green peppers. When you peeled the steak off, the middles of the meat were pink and cold...Eek! It makes me sad to see this quality of food. Redeeming dishes were the siu mai (pork and shrimp dumplings wrapped in a thin egg wrapper) and steamed shrimp dumplings (rice wrapper around shrimp). Both were hot, fresh, juicy, and flavorful. But they were missing some essentials: ha cheung fun (steamed wrapped shrimp noodles), ou yuen (beef meatballs), congee, etc... We also ordered a freshly cooked fish and vegetables, which was ...okay. 

I can forgive food flukes at a familiar family haunt, but bad service needs to be accounted for. After we returned the fong zao, we didn't have any carts frequent our table, and the cashier (the owner's cousin) was not very polite. 

I think my family continues to go here because they knew some of the friendly staff "aunties" (whose turn-over rate seems to have gone up) and because they offer unbeatable coupons. I will obviously do whatever my loyal parents want to do--because I'm a good Asian daughter :) --but I really really hope we never have to go there again! You get what you pay for!
Alright. If you're looking for women this ain't the place for you. However, if you're trying to hang with friends then by all means go and have a wonderful time!
LaSpada's has the best pizza in Plainfield. Hands down! Everything is tasty. Buffalo logs are so good! Fast and good quality.

Feels like home. BEST and most authentic LATIN FOOD in the city! As a NJ/ NYC native, it has been hard to find consistently quality good, at a good price. As an El Salvadoran finding great pupusas has been just as hard but macarena nails it! Their breakfast "Centro Americano" and the other typical breakfasts are AMAZING and just that: typical. It is out new go-to... Thankful for this gem!!

My wife and I have been missing the crawfish they serve in China terribly, and when we saw that Red Kings serves them at a reasonable price we decided to drop in and try them out.

As usual, with a Chinese restaurant in the States, my speaking Mandarin resulting in a lot of oohing and ahhing, and service was excellent.

The restaurant storefront itself is nothing special but the food is really good and completely authentic. The crawfish were a little bit milder than they would be in China, which is a good thing for the average American, and the pepper broth-boiled sliced fish was spot on. 

Anyone who can stand some spice should try this place out!

Not your usual Thai restaurant.  I was so happy to find my fav Thai dishes I can't find at other Thai restaurants.  The food tastes like what I get in Thailand.  They are known for their noodle dishes. Tom yum noodles are soooo sooo good.  Pad Thai tastes what I get in Thailand.   Nam tok Thai grilled beef or pork salad is also great. Finally a Thai restaurant that's not Americanized!

Poor seating options for couples. Choice was directly In front of the speaker for the live singer or out on. The front porch at a table in the corner with screaming kids jumping all over. They seamed to cram as many tables as possible and with out proper distance as required. When we were sat our table, it was filthy dirty from the last people who were stuck there. No menus, not that we could read them anyway as it's very clearly at the end of the porch. Table wanted and was slanted way too much. Been there many times and never this bad. I would recommend going anywhere else unless nothing else is open. Oh yea we left after no one came back to clean our table or get us menus.
Yum. The bear claws. The glazed. Yum. My daughter loves the sprinkles. Husband loves cinnamon rolls. Come early because they are popular. Bring cash too because no credit cards.  Did I say "yum"?

The place is a real dive, that being said my wife and I love the place, the diverse clientele from homeless Karaoke singers to suit and tie types never fails to entertain us. The gambling is great with loose machines in all areas, pretty good comp program and great bar tenders. If your looking to people watch this is the place to go, you will see obese women in yoga pants and homeless guys wearing sport coats and everything in between. If your looking for a 5-star experience better go to the Peppermill as this place is not for you.

I am honestly shocked by so many bad reviews. I order delivery from this spot pretty often and always receive the proper meal. The food always tastes great, and arrives quickly. I have been inside before the pandemic and picked up food in person and also had a quick experience. There are better things that need to be complained about instead of taking it all out on a food establishment that's literally staying open to keep everyone fed during a pandemic. I know I appreciate this chipotle and have never had an issue. Thanks for making me burritos when I'm too lazy to cook myself!

The waitress was very sweet but the food wasn't as flavorful as I hoped. Had the blue drank and it was very sweet, the manager insisted it was strong when I asked to add a shot, I ended up full off the sugar and felt no buzz. However, aesthetic is lovely.

Awesome! You definitely need to make a reservation, and you should be aware that there is a dress code. 

I had the Blackened Drum - it was perfectly cooked, and spicy in the "amazingly flavorful" way not in the "too hot" way. The mashed potatoes were buttery delicious and out of this world good, and the veggies were tasty as well.

The best part, though, was the bread pudding. It was by far the best bread pudding I've ever had. 

Service was impeccable, it was obvious that the staff is exceedingly well trained.

4 stars because I've only been there once so far!  Was actually looking a restaurant that served Boba tea, and came across the reviews for this place, and it happens to be a few blocks away from my house - so off I went to try it.  It's in a strip mall - zero parking really because of the starbucks, subway, and sushi place in the same space.  With about 10 parking spots - so you might have to park and walk. 
It's clean, and no frills inside, but I like that modern sparce feel it had.  The waitstaff was attentive, and friendly and greeted me right away.  The place was packed.  
The menu is authentic - and different - and really interesting. I saw some of the plates coming out, and although I played it safe with Taiwanese Fried Rice with chicken (which was delicious - I'm looking forward to trying some of the more adventurous food next time.  I tried the boba milk tea also and it was wonderful!  The tapioca pearls were fresh and so good!

Never been to Tucano's?  Here's what to expect for all my friends who are wondering if it's worth that high price tag.  Today I made my return as promised but this time to dine in for lunch, I have heard much from others who complain quality is not as good at lunch time.  So I bet your thinking why and how could you give this place 2 STARS??   Let's try finding a hair while biting in to your turkey wrapped with bacon! (Pictured on my plate) 

  **Service- We had a great server and she made sure we lacked nothing, the meat servers also were pretty prompt.  Given maybe 8 tables were in for lunch the speed between them could have been faster. 

**Food-   
 ** Salad bar- was Meh the main reason being my friend and I each got a roll, from the same batch the lady set down he got a hot one and mine was cold completely,how does that happen?  AGAIN as my last visit items were Luke warm and lacking flavor.  I.E. alfraedo sauce, lobster bisque, next time I come in I'm gonna temp the food.  

** MEATS- I enjoyed quite a few meats that were usual quality as the top sirloin, turkey, garlic sirloin, white fish, etc.  Where the quality dropped was with the parm chicken, (sadly it was over cooked and dry) The hanger steak was way to salty for both my friend and I.  This never used to be a problem, WHAT DID NOT slip in quality is the grilled pineapple.  

  Cleanliness-  THIS IS WHERE I had the biggest problems, keep in mind we went at lunch literally 1130. I noticed walking to our table behind the hostess the floor was sticky, I found that to be very odd.  During our experience a slice of pineapple was dropped from a server and workers just walked past it as it sat on the floor.  I also observed tables being cleaned and the condiment bottles, cues, shakers, not being cleaned AGAIN.  If you followed my first review this was one of my major complaints and it's STILL not fixed.

Best wings ever! And pizza! And burgers. Lol. You get the point. The happy hour specials are good and service is always friendly! It's a nice sit at the bar, have a conversation on a Sunday afternoon type of place.

Amazing Cheesesteaks!!! We drove all the way from NYC to try some good cheesesteaks and this did not disappoint!! A tad pricey but expected. The cheese fries were perfect too!! We will be back for sure!

Wait staff ignored me for over 20 minutes to even ask my party size for seating or let me know how long the wait was. Seating Waitress looked at me several times, and never said a word. I asked cashier for wait time and she "oh" and that's all. I left.

We had a very bizarre experience over the weekend. My husband and I invited friends out for dinner before a show. My friend ordered a Southwestern Chicken salad. Three entrees arrived -- the salad not one of them. We waited. And waited.  The waitress would not make eye contact. When we finally got her over, she said they were "working on it'. She finally delivered the salad, and it was lettuce, dressing and NOTHING ELSE. No protein, no beans no corn, nothing that resembled the menu description. Was she not supposed to notice???? We complained; she said they could not make that particular menu item. Brought out a substitute after some time but by then we just wanted to be gone. Lots of sports bars in SE/Bench area -- no reason to return

This place is one of my favs. Three servers that are outstanding, Madison,  Micheala & John. I can't believe they remember my wife's & my drink order every time. They are so  accommodating they even get game shows on for us as we're not sports fans so much. The buffalo chicken dip is to die for. With pub chips; please keep the pub chips so much better than reg chips!!!!!
Take out the crap. I'm in!!!! This chicken tiramisu is amazing.  Chicken tortellini is great as well.
Good food - good service & great location. The wait time on Fridays and weekend may be long ( there is call ahead seating FYI) . Our wait time was 45 minutes! But definitely worth the wait .

Was visiting Tucson and I decided to try out Ermanos.  Very cool scene.  Unique menu with good selection of wines.  Not good for mixed drinks as no liquor from what I can tell.  Pretty good selection of bottled beers.  There was a small band set up to play on Thursday night and they were pretty good.  I really liked the layout of the bar. As a solo drinker it was easy to find a spot at the bar to drink.  But there was a good amount of seating throughout for groups.  Had an outdoor patio area as well.  They had a really nice super sharp tv for football watching.  More chic bar on the college side of the tracks.
Adorable place. but food is pricey and taste is mediocre.  Had chicken pot pie which is served in a black personal sized skillet; very thick and creamy.

One of my favorite sushi places in town. Samurai Blue ha been around for several years and has never fallen short of hitting the mark both in flavor and in service.  They have a variety of fresh selections as well as carefully thought out specials. It's right in Centro de Ybor, upstairs across from the Muvico.

My mom and I stopped in for a quick bite before our movie time and were able to get seated right away on a Sunday evening! They have a good menu. We decided to try the black and white pizza, which is a new item that features their roasted garlic white sauce, mushrooms, sausage, cracked black pepper and lots of cheese, it was delicious! We also ordered the sangria and a strawberry Italian soda, which were super yummy! They also have a gelato stand by the front door. We ended up getting strawberry and creme brûlée on the way out, also fantastic! The service was excellent. The prices I felt were a bit on the higher end of the spectrum. For example, a family size (18 inch) specialty pizza runs $30+, a bit too much imo. This was our first visit, so we'll definitely be back to try more of the menu!

I'm a fan of Rusty's pizza. There isn't much that's particularly unique about Rusty's vs others. I like the sauce and flavor of the pizza, which draws me here over other places. 
I order relatively simple like hawaiian. It takes a typical amount of time from order to completion. A bit toasted around the edges, which I think adds some extra flavor. 
I can't speak to the salad bar quality.

Overall, I look forward to Rusty's when I visit home. 
:-)

Tasty Tampa Cuban. Highly recommend it! The cheesecake flavored iced coffee was also delicious! The atmosphere was casual and quiet. Be careful opening the door to the restaurant because if anyone (kids especially) are standing in the doorway you will hit them. They will be looking at ice cream standing there. 

Great place for lunch. Workers were friendly. I would go to this place again.
Bagel deli has helped me many of hungover mornings. A lot of people complain about the wait but it's worth your time! With so many different bagel combinations, you can't ever get tired of it.

Purchased vanilla confetti buttercream mini cake and chocolate mousse mini cake.  Both went in the trash after a bite.  Cakes were flavorless.  Frostings were subpar.  And they tasted stale. $12 wasted.

Carlucci's is a wonderful Italian spot tucked away in the corner of Mount Laurel. There's a reason why it's been around for decades! The food is fantastic, the view of the Rancocas Creek is pleasant, and they manage to have their spot near the Turnpike/295 and yet, you can't hear the highway. That's straight up magical, Carlucci's. 

If you have the chance when ordering there, get the Pasta Fagioli for a starter, AND the house salad - both options are definitely homemade, and freshly prepared. Any seafood dish served there is wonderful - we haven't been there in a few months, but whenever we go, at any time of the year, their seafood is excellent.
I love this place.. falafel and tahini sauce are the best.. must try their tea and it is complimentary

I love their spicy pork tacos. They are true authentic tacos served just like you would get them south of the border!  And they also serve Sol beer here.  If you are looking for delicious authentic food from Mexico, I highly recommend this place.

I've tried some of the hyped up donut places(VooDoo donuts and Duck donuts) and they never gave me the "omggguuhhhh" reaction. Tried Hole in One donuts for the first time in Tampa one morning and I don't care for any other donuts but Hole in One. The glazed crossiants!!!! 
Super excited that one opened around Tarpon Springs (lives in Spring Hill). Thank youuuu!!!

Please open one in Spring Hill!!!!

We always seem to come here after shul, not sure what the connection other than it is near West End and there is a nice park across the street.

They have great sandwiches.  It doesn't matter how many times I eat there, but I always end up getting the reuben or the corned beef sandwich, I always get the large size, and always end up eating the whole damn thing and feel gross afterwards.  Not the the fault of the sandwich or Star Bagel, I just can't stop eating delicious warm corned beef, even if my wife is in my ear nagging me to stop.  So, do yourself a favor, listen to my wife and stop at half if you order a large sammich.  

They also have a bunch of vegetarian options too, if that is what floats your boat.  The fruit tea is also quite tasty and has free refills and the coffee is excellent.

Service is pretty good, they get people in and out fast, seating can sometimes be an issue, especially in the colder months when you can't use their outside seating.  Parking is a beast, too.  You basically have to back out into three semi-busy roads and it is limited to start off.

Good place for a nosh.

Amazing crabs! These are the best tasting crabs that I have ever tasted. I got #1 combo with the Hot N Crazy Crab "mild" sauce. It was amazing and I couldn't even finish my meal. 

The restaurant was clean and the staff are friendly and welcoming. Ask for Harrell as a waiter. It has only been opened for three days. They just opened on 7/16/19 and are already getting great business. 

So now there are three major crab restaurants in Brandon- ( Crafty Crab, Mr. & Mrs. Crab and Hot N Crazy) and I can tell you that I have tried them all & this one is the best. Let me know what y'all think!

Been there twice in the last few days. First time was mediocre, second time, tonight was lousy. First time a friend and I were ushered into a back room restaurant although there were seats in the main dining area. The bbq chicken sandwich was terrible. Tough chicken with little bbq sauce that had no real flavor. Tonight the receptionist was busy on the phone when I entered and finally suggested that I sit at the bar. After sitting for quite a while a waitress, loaded with dirty dishes, came by on the way to the kitchen, asking if I wanted a drink. I asked for a beer kist and got ine about 5 minutes later. I found a menu sitting around nearby and made a selection but never heard from the waitress again. I finally left, still hungry.
Wonderful food! We sat outdoors-the atmosphere is quaint and inviting. We enjoyed the stuffed pork chop with an appetizer of shrimp and grits as well as gumbo. As was fantastic! Highly recommend!
Great atmosphere, amazing beer selection.  Very friendly and knowledgeable bartender with a great sense of humor. Highly recommend for anyone who likes to go to bars for good banter and great beer!
Have dined here several times over a period of eight years.  Always great service and excellent prime rib and an awesome salad bar.

I live in the piazza so I thought this place would be my usual spot (yeah pyt gets too ghetto on the weekends for a skinny white boy).  Gunners definitely has overpriced drinks and food (especially food, horrible menu).  If they want business, they should just make an awesome drink special that people will start spreading the word about (e.g. $3 kenzinger pints, 1/2 priced well drinks from 5-11, $3 pbr pounders, anything geez!). Stop trying to be so upscale and turn into a classic watering hole for NoLib residents, business will be sure to follow.  And throw in a pool table and a buck hunt, get with the freaking times gunners run, turn yourself into gunner FUN! (and dont play hip-hop, all the pyt people will start destroying your place).

Stopped in to Café NOMA for the first time to grab some breakfast. I've been watching construction take place around it for a year or so. It looks so nice and new inside in the little eat-in courtyard. You can access the cafe without paying the entrance fee to the museum.

That staff were very friendly and masked up. Pineapple mimosas were a surprise as I've never seen that before. The lemon icebox pie was delicious. Sweet and tart with a chewy crust on the bottom. I bet all their pastries are great. The kitchen doesn't open until 11 so I'll have to go back to try some of the other things on the menu like Thai fries or Spicy Shrimp Poké bowl.

Fabulous food, fabulous people, and a fabulous find. While there, I was offered to try about 5 different things, and all were delicious! Please try the sandwiches - they're superb, and they're very cheap.

Ok this is Chipotle but w pizza.. Pie and ingredients were fresh and it was made quickly. Thry have specialty pies or custom where you can pick your ingredients.. A lot to choose from. The only negative I can think of is the price point of $9.99 for a personal pizza w three ingredients more. A little high for a food court joint.

Overpriced, overpriced, overpriced. 

I have been waiting to experience this new CWE hot commodity for a week now and the perfect opportunity to skip the 45-minute line presented itself at 3PM on a Wednesday (we only had to wait 10 minutes to order!) The restaurant itself was clean and had an interesting decor scheme. The staff were efficient and what one would expect at a typical fast food restaurant. 

The food, while decent for diner food, is FAR too overpriced for decent diner food. I was extremely excited to try the vegetarian option: the fried, cheese-stuffed portabello Schroom' Burger. Unfortunately it was hard to taste the small mushroom with all the cheese and fried breadcrumbs, so the mushroom sandwich turned more into a mozzarella stick sandwich. It was also a little too small for what one would expect to get for $7. The crinkle cut fries were crispy. I wasn't a huge fan, but my friend, who loves crinkle cut fries, thought they were excellent. The 'pie oh my' pecan concrete was far too small for what one would expect to get for $5. 

All in all, it was a fun experience but I probably will not return unless others suggest it because of the price of the food compared to the amount and quality of food I received.

Customer service, Food Quality and the Vibe is OUTSTANDING The bartender was the bomb, the guest whom I met this night were awesome. It was fully packed but the vibe was still low key and chilled. It was just a beautiful night full of great people.... I had a wonderful experience

Simply delicious. It wasn't that busy inside for a Thursday night, but the outside seating was pretty full. I ordered the coconut key lime pie martini....yes please! And hubs ordered a Jai Alai. We shared a Fire Roll for a starter, excellent choice! For my main course I ordered the Guava Salmon with Cuban Black beans as a side. I wasn't too keen on the beans, but since it was the first time I've tried that style beans, it's likely just my taste preference. They had tomato flavor and I'm used to baked beans with molasses. The salmon was wrapped in bacon and cooked perfectly. Hubs order the Thursday night steak special with grilled veggies. Only thing left on his plate when he was done was a silver dollar sized piece of fat. He was happy. We've never been to the shops in West Chase so we  walked around a bit after dinner. Many of the shops close early, but it was still a nice stroll. Great atmosphere for a date. We'll definitely be back.

Okay.  I don't toss 5 stars around lightly, but last night I had one of the best meals I've ever had in my life at this place!  The escargot was so good I wanted to get two orders and have them dump it over a bowl of pasta.  Then my main course came.  Veal Scotty.  Every bite was perfect.  The artichoke hearts were very tender and the veal was melt in your mouth perfection.  The food is so good that it is worth running the cigarette smoke from the Apple Barrel gauntlet to get up the stairs and inside the door.  It's like jogging through purgatory to get to heaven.

A friend & I came here to "try something new". The sandwiches were good - the bread very good. The side of sesame noodles were TERRIBLE. Tasted like burnt salt, if you can imagine that. (Should know better than to order ses noodles from a non-Chinese restaurant!). The tomato soup tasted like tomato sauce. I give only 2 stars because prices for anything but the sandwiches were not prominently  posted & it came to $42 for lunch for 3 people. That's with only 2 sides and 2 drinks. Could've gone to a sit down restaurant for that.

This is what vegan food should taste like.  

I'm not vegan but many of my friends are and a lot of vegan food tends to drift towards new-age hippy-dippy fusion food because these 2 or 5 things work together.  Not that there isn't a place for that, but sometimes you just want honest, good food. 

Our party of 3 was sat in a nice table in the quaint dining room and our server was wonderful, explaining a few things we had questions on and always swinging by to bring a new bottle of water or top off our glasses.  We sat shortly after 8pm on a Thursday night and it was packed, usually a great sign. 

From memory we ordered: 

NACHO DE MACHO - maybe the one thing I wouldn't order again, as it was more of a deconstructed nacho with only seasoned tofu crumbles to replace the cheese.  When I think of nacho's, I think of a towering heap of gooey cheese and jalapenos, both missing from this.  

YUCA FRITA - these are not my go-to but a friend likes them so we ordered.  Best I've ever had.  Anywhere else these taste like fried air puffs. Here, they had a really nice taste and the dipping sauce was great.  Presentation when brought to the table is also beautiful. 

PINCHOS - not my choice for an app but was very tasty, the sauce on the bottom of the plate had a really nice kick. 

For dinner I ordered BRÓCOLI, and while you might not get that excited over a broccoli taco, you should.  Do not sleep on this! Side for this dish is rice and beans, and they are both amazing.  

I also ordered a CUBANO CLUB which I split with a friend.  The bread was more of a cheese steak roll, and not pressed, but the flavors were all there.  This is something you could hand to a carnivore and they'd be hard pressed to know it was vegan.  The mustard used in this is wonderful.  Shining star on the plate, the sweet potato salad,  Bright and amazing!  

My friend ordered a CHIPOTLE CHICK'N BURRITO which I split and this was much heavier, had a nice smokey flavor from the chipotle and while the root veg wasn't listed on the menu, it doesn't have the consistency of a tortilla with a bunch of veggies inside.  There's some weight to this thing.  

Rounded out with TRES LECHES CAKE, and while a bit heavier than others I've had, the taste and fresh fruit that came along with it was spot on.  Really kind of amazing. 

This is a great little spot that has a core menu of amazing food, one you could go back to 3-4 times and not eat the same thing twice.  My understanding is the menu is tweaked and changed as seasons change, too, so something new is always there to look forward to.

The staff is always friendly and helpful and accomadating. Will is great at the front desk. The best rooms are in Building 4 and get the rooms facing the pool/mountains. Gino in the Cafe is also awesome and great service. The food and breakfast buffet is great. There cocktail prices are a little high for my taste, but I guess you have to pay for the view of the beautiful mountains. Thanks to all the staff and making every stay here enjoyable.
Very friendly staff and excellent food. Here's a hint if you see the special on the board outside you had better stop in!!!  Can't wait to try another special!!!

We were looking for a brunch place in Santa Barbara that served great food and didn't have a crazy long wait time. Dawn Patrol followed all our guidelines and the food was fantastic!

Ordered the famous Build Your Own Hash with Corn Beef, Poached Eggs, and the Herb Aioli. The dish was massive and came with so much food included plenty of toasted bread. The Corn Beef was cooked perfectly and tasted divine dipped in the Herb Aioli. Do yourself a favor and try the corn beef hash here, it might not be the healthiest but its worth the calories!

Coming from San Francisco, I thought the prices here were quite reasonable and way cheaper than the Bay Area. $14 for a Corn Hash with plenty of food and bread is a great deal. I seriously can't complain!

Get past the fact that it's in a gas station. I was able to and now I'm a frequent customer. I just wish they opened before 8am so I could get my smoothie fix before work. 
My fiance gets the peanut paradise with whey protein every time. It's delicious but it's too rich for me. I prefer any of the fruity ones.
We usually split a buffalo chicken wrap and thai chicken wrap. Both are great. I've also heard the chipotle chicken panini is a hit. They're not very fast at making combos (food and smoothie), but if you have the time, it's worth the wait.

They ran out of fancy donuts and chicken at 5:15 pm and they close at 7 pm!   However, the few donuts that they had were excellent.  They would have received five stars if they didn't run out.  The manager said need to be here before 11 am to try the fancies.  Why don't they plan to have more of them later in the day?
A little bit overly expensive now. Everything is $1-$2 more than they should be. The service is still solid, and the food gets the job done, but the price is a bit off.

After the Ballon Races E-Dawg, H-Man, and me went for our traditional breakfast- we had thought about Archie's but if I'm not drinking, why would I go to a bar?  So we chose this instead, I was hoping they had outdoor seating...

We became members of their Eggheads program and were able to take advantage of the Early Bird menu from 7-8, don't know when I'll EVER be awake that early when I'm not going to work and actually be headed out for BF again but it was worth it.  If I was drinking, I would have tried the mimosa, but alas... 

Best 2eggs in Reno!  Asked for the pots crispy and they ACTUALLY WERE!!  Not just with a few deep fried cracklins' thrown on top - I mean EVERY potato was CRISP.  E-Dawg got the biscuits and gravy half order for everyone to share and it was plenty. 

Plus - hula hoops for the kids to play with?!  Awesome. 

Next time I might try an omelette but just wasn't feeling it.  The little monster inside of me wanted an English Muffin and crispy potatoes, and S.I. delivered.  THX, we'll be back!!
Pretty good Sushi Buffett, two people ate with beverages for under $25.00.

I had the Crawfish Boil Hot Fried Chicken Sandwich,  Rosted crab cake "on the half shell," and a frozen Pina Colada. The sandwich was good but I didn't taste any crawfish. The Rooster crab cake was a cute appetizer and the Pina Colada was a good drink to get me tipsy  . Overall the vibe was nice, as they had light music playing in the background, the prices were not high and the servers were very attentive.

I was excited to try American Social, but was heavily disappointed in the food. We got the Lobster Benedict and the Strawberry French Toast. The Lobster was so rubbery and over cooked that we literally couldn't eat it. The rest of the Benedict didn't have flavor. Strawberry French Toast was burnt on the outside and soggy on the inside. Atmosphere and service was good. This place has potential to be great, just work on improving your cooking staff. Definitely not returning and wouldn't recommend.

I am not a fan of this bar after a Saturday night outing. The male bartender with dark hair was very unfriendly. He also barked at my friend when he was giving him his tab. We were waiting on him to get another bottle of champagne to fill our glasses. My friend turned away for a second to say hi to a friend. Then he impatiently yelled "Sir, SIR!". Stop being such a tight ass and mellow out. You are waiting in patrons not the other way around. There was no beer list out on display so when we asked him about beers he seemed annoyed. Please list your beers on the wall or on your taps like most bars. I also asked the bartender a question about a beer and he was so wrong. Bartenders should know their  bar products. I asked for a non hoppy beer. The imperial red ale is disgustingly hoppy and probably one of the worst beers I have had. I left my half finished glass on the bar and left.    

The place is too narrow when it gets crowded. The waitress seemed bothered that we were standing in the way when she tried to deliver food and drinks. There is no where to stand out of the way when it gets crowded. HINT: They should make an opening ar the end of the bar near the door so the wait staff doesn't have to plow through patrons to deliver food. 

I did enjoy the DJ that was sampling old 70s-80s music. It was a fun small crowd dancing with some mommasitas sprinkled around the dance floor.
This place is the worst place in town. Food had NO flavor. Took two bites of my giant plate full of no tasting BS.

Terrible service and quite possibly the worst cappuccino I've ever had. Walking in, instead of acknowledging the customer, I had to flag the barista down. When asked about their hand poured coffee, I was given the three bags if coffees they were offering. No suggestions, no description of each. The cappuccino was pulled for too long and there was no foam. It was basically a latte. What a bummer.

Delicious food and drinks. This place was recommended by a friend, and I'm glad we went! More upscale place which comes with a price, but it was worth it. We got the seafood risotto and snapper, okra, carrot ribbons, and charbroiled oysters. Everything was tasty, I would return!

The Red Lion Burger is the ish! The burger of my DREAMS! It's that serious! 

The Red Lion Burger...AWESOMENESS on a bun! 1/2 Beef, 1/4 Lamb & 1/4 Pork, bacon, caramelized onions, soft cheddar cheese and BBQ sauce...gosh my mouth is watering writing this! They also have the best sweet potato fries. Crispy on the outside, meaty,slightly sweet and piping hot on the inside!

The service is horrid(hence the 4 stars) , but I deal with it because the burger is soooo darn good!
We were probably one of the first clients. We have never been disappointed with their food & hospitality.
Omg the food was amazing service was impeccable. Just an all around fabulous place my new favorite spot

A totally disappointing experience.  I have been visiting NOLA for years and last night's dinner was dialed in. The raw oysters were served warm and flavorless.  The French fried sweet potatoes were cold but burnt on the outside.  Will not be back.  What happened to you Acme?  So many other great eating options in New Orleans.

Actually went to Felix's across the street the next day.  Amazing , similar items but oysters were served chilled, potatoes were generous in portion, cooked just right and staff was super friendly and fun!

Stopped in here with some friends the other night and enjoyed it like any other trip to Scotty's. Service at this location, as well as others, seems to be a little hit and miss, but we lucked out that night and had a good experience. My wrap and tater tots (one of the best combos on the planet) were both delish and washed down well with a good beer. The only reason I wouldn't come back here is because they're a little more out of my way than other locations, not because they failed to live up to what I've come to expect from Scotty's. I left full and happy, what more could a guy want?

My fiancé and I were checking out wedding bands and decided to try this place out afterwards upon reading Yelp reviews. The fish was very fresh-- I very much enjoyed the salmon roll and fried oyster roll. I tried the shrimp with spicy mayo and cucumber but it was just very bland. Otherwise, everything else was great-- salad, soup, and complimentary red bean ice cream. Our server was so kind and helpful. I would definitely return here!

We received a comped night and I am not complaining about free but I wouldn't pay the full price. It's pretty similar to a comfort suites not a resort hotel. The casino is fun but doesn't pay out well. I like the casino outside of Chandler better.
Best beef bulgolgi I've had in Missouri, that being said I have had better but you won't find better in the Midwest. Beef fried rice was good as well.

i definitely enjoy lenny's on occasion. pretty much the best sandwich around conshy. obviously the roast pork is the main attraction, but i am partial to a club and it's great as well. 

only negative is that it's not open later. a post-work sandwich is virtually impossible unless you are right down the street.
I'm going to try to keep this simple: the staff is very courteous, the food is amazing, my kids loved the place, oh and the beer... great selection. Would recommend to anyone.
I've only had tacos there but they're so good I don't want anything else. Nice service and great salsas.

My husband went for coffee at rogue wave's new location and could not stop bragging about it so naturally I went to check it out. The Almond milk flat white I had was absolutely delicious and I could see myself making many more returns. The space is big (considering their old spot) and parking is ample which is great compared to some of the nearby places on 124street.

I've been here a few times and it's just right for pool. I usually go after work, so it's not really crowded, especially considering that they only have about 4 pool tables. They do have skee ball and a few video games for anyone who just wants to add a lil fun tot heir evening. I like that they have TV's all around so you can watch whatever sport you like (the Olympics was on so that kept me entertained in between shots). I've only eve had the fries and drinks, which are really hard to mess up. Upon entry and the little seating area there was an unpleasant urine like smell, but idk if that was in the furniture or if someone had an accident. FYI- on Monday's there is a pool league that reserves one of the tables, but another table opened up just in time so we didn't have to get kicked out (lol) Overall, it's good for a nice afterwork wind down.
Food was sooo good! Ordered curbside bogo deep dish and regular thin crust, side of sticks and dips it was so delish
Phenomenal food, phenomenal service, phenomenal dining experience. We left feeling spoiled!
I love that I get exceptionally stellar service here, they remember my name and are SO positive, makin' me feel all special. ( ^_^.)v

I am pretty partial to mom and pop shops, if only bc they are usually cheaper, have amazingly delicious menus that you wouldn't find elsewhere and usually decent service.  As we eat at home most of the time, when we go out we want it to be a treat and something we wouldn't necessarily make at home. Barbara's literally checks ALL the boxes.

We walked in on a Sunday, albeit a bit early for dinner time, and found it to be largely empty. The space is huge, tables are comfy, restaurant is well lit, but it's not fancy. As we sat down, our waitress brought us a basket of delicious bread that seemed to be rye.

We started with the mushroom stew over spatzele, my husband had the paprika chicken stew over the same noodles (he loved it). The mushroom stew was so good that both the friend and I who were splitting it ordered a whole order of ourselves before we even finished it. It was THAT GOOD. Thee stew had that delicious Hungarian paprika taste and basically perfect mushrooms. Also on a bed of delicious noodles.

We also tried the cabbage noodles and the stuffed cabbage, both of which were perfection. In a rare move we even got coffee and dessert. The cherry and apple streudels were delicious and the coffee reminded me of Turkish coffee in Istanbul. 

I can't wait to go back here, even hungrier and fill my belly. 

So good, great service, decent prices. Go here!

Thank you! I relocated to Philly from NY and while Im not going put alot, I do order in. (I used Door Dash and they were great) I tried delivery from other places that ended up in the trash. I love the name of place and they were my last hope of finding old school Cantonese food. The food was delivered hot and on time. It is a little pricey but the good news is that you can eat this for a few days and its still great. Chicken Corn Soup is perfect, dumplings are fantastic. Please remember if you are ordering in to ask for your sauce or you wont get it. Its not the restaurants fault, the online ordering via door dash makes you spell it out. Its a must try!

Food was excellent! They were extremely busy and the manager took the responsibility of helping by hosting, serving and bussing the tables. We will definitely add this to the rotation. Highly recommend fish and chips!

This place has very good desserts and a very nice atmosphere. It is decorated beautifully inside and the people are very friendly. It is a very authentic café. I would give it more stars if I could. I have been to Paris, Normandy, Toulouse, Marseilles and Bordeaux and this café looks just like the ones in France!

Hugo's pays attention to your allergy concerns which is absolutely incredible. They have a separate fryer for us celiac folk and don't up-charge for the gluten free crust. The place is absolutely adorable inside too. All that being said, the gluten free pizza crust just didn't do it for me. It was a little too dry and lacked any real flavor or crisp. I did enjoy the topping choices like the hot chicken and the loaded French fries. I'll maybe give it another try once the menu changes again but I'm not rushing over.

I've eaten here at least 50 times. The food is always delicious. Cheesesteak is delicious, and so is hot n spicy chicken. Only flaw is the service is bad sometimes, but I'll give it 5 still for being reliably good

Great little coffee place. 

I saw there's going to be a Dunkin Donuts put in right next to it, even somewhat covering it from the street. I think it's very on-the-nose to have a big chain place come in and try and hide a nice local place.

I just recently moved back from Northern California and had yet to find a delicious noodle spot, and this is the place. Although there isn't ramen on the menu, it didn't matter! 

My beef noodle soup was made extremely fresh, the beef was tender enough to rip with my chopsticks and the broth had so much flavor I couldn't get enough! 

The customer service was absoLOUTELY amazing, the cashier's were extremely friendly and helpful. Ambiance was chill, so chill I asked for the playlist they had playing while we ate because I needed that vibe to go with me! 

Overall great experience, we will definitely be back!
Probably the best sushi I've ever had. Everything is alway fresh, restaurant is clean and well maintained. Staff is courteous and the food is spot on.

We were driving from Tampa to Lakewood Ranch on the i-75 and needed a non fast food option for lunch. We saw the mostly positive Yelp reviews for this place and decided to give it a go. The building is a stand-alone roadside eatery beckoning you in with flashing lights promising soups, sandwiches, and the best pies.

The interior reminded me of an old school DQ with red moulded plywood booths, neon lighting and large over-counter menu. You can do dine in or take out. There is a self serve fountain drink area. The bathroom is hard to find despite the handmade sign directing you to it. (although a very helpful employee guided me -- clearly i was looking lost) You basically have to walk into their kitchen and the bathroom doubles as their furnace and supply closet. An employee was dividing up a cake in the hallway to the bathroom as I went by. Not a great first impression.

The menu offerings are also extensive (which to me is always a sign of danger...it's impossible to do that many things well). Under the counter is a massive dessert case featuring pies, bars, cakes and cookies. All look fantastic. We ordered a tomato sandwich ($6), a chicken salad sandwich ($8), chicken noodle soup ($4) and a Reuben ($8). And cannolis and a napoleon for dessert.

Positives: the bread was very fresh on all our sandwiches. The soup had interesting ingredients (zucchini). Portions are large. Sandwiches are the size of a small dinner plate and stuffed thick with whatever inside you ordered.

Not so positive: all sandwiches were severely lacking in seasoning. Tomato and chicken salad sandwiches had lots of mayo, zero salt or pepper. Reuben was a bit more successful because of the cheese, sauerkraut and thousand island dressing. Oddly the chicken noodle soup was very very salty. And the noodles were crushed spaghetti which I find hard to tackle with a small plastic spoon. Not a deal breaker, but a peccadillo.

Desserts were a disappointment too. Cannolis had a nice cream. Napoleon tasted frozen. Not surprised if they were as it would be hard to keep the amount of choices they had fresh.

Good concept, but I would prefer a shortened sandwich menu done well and a few fresh favourite desserts instead of trying to have something for everyone.

Terrible service! I woman at the counter when I was paying was EXTREMELY rude! I asked to see my bill when I went to pay and she gave me a nasty attitude. I would NEVER come here again! The food wasn't even good! Even a customer behind me commented on her attitude. Unreal.
Pretty good burgers, perfect size for me; not so big it's hard to eat. Good variety, great prices. Not taking cash at this time. Also, the bar drinks were a bit pricy.

I usually give some leeway for waiters/waitresses but the only downfall to this place was the waitress/service. Granted we had a large party and the place is very loud causing some commotion I'm sure , on top of the fact the waitress has to go all the way downstairs for all drinks and checks. It could of been run a little better. Perhaps supplement the waitress with a runner and split the tips of some sort. The waitress did mess up almost every one of our kids orders and gave us an extra plate of wings which is never good. 

Now with that aside. The families and kids I was with all seemed to enjoy the food. The wings were great, Mac and cheese was great and pizza was good as well. I personally got a burger and will be honest it was one of the better burgers I've had in my lifetime (only 22 y/o) but I've encountered some solid burgers.  

Food and service aside the live music was a treat. Daniel Bell and some other lady I don't know the name of really did lighten up the place and get the whole crowd involved. Definitely recommended this place but don't come to hungry or wanting a drink as it may take some time for both to come.

If I could sum up my visit to this location it would be one big.... "MEH". I was thoroughly unimpressed with this restuarant, but unlike several places I have been that I gave similar ratings to, I think this is one that I will return to to give it a second chance.

Let's start with the (limited) good parts about my experience. 

First off, the atmosphere is very well done. Quite a ritzy look with elegant decor without a doubt. When you walk into the restaurant it's pretty awesome. Well done on this part. 

Second, the appetizers we tried with quite satisfactory. We had the Tapas, Brie Potstickers, as well as the Thai Chicken Meatballs. Without a doubt the meatballs were the best hands down. The Brie was so so and it was wasn't warm at all when it was served. The Tapas had some good cheese, but olives aren't really my thing (it was my girlfriend's birthday, and she loves olives, hence why they were ordered). Overall the appetizers were decent and actually pretty good starters to a meal. That pretty much ends the positives though. Let's get into the disappointments.

To start, the prices for the entrees are quite outrageous for the quality of the food. My girlfriend ordered the Cedar Plank Verlasso Salmon and it was a giant letdown. The salmon was bland, the "chef's potatoes" lacked any flavor at all, and the "pesto crust" didn't even taste like pesto. We were fully expecting a succulent flavorful dish, and this was absolutely not what was presented.  A little flavor would go a long ways. 

I ordered the Bistro Burger which the description paints as a magical burger bursting with flavor, and it simply was not. The burger itself tasted like I could have ordered it at any fast food chain for sure. It was nothing special and well overpriced for sure. It is definitely not something I would recommend.

To continue, the waitress we had was super nice, but not very observant of her customers. We finished our meal and wanted to check out a dessert menu, but for about 10-15 minutes we could not get her attention. We didn't want to be rude and wave her over or call out her name, so we sat patiently and tried to make awkward eye contact as she went to other tables. It wasn't incredibly busy in the place either, so I am honestly not sure what was going on there. In the end, I asked another waiter who was helping out the table next to us to see the dessert menu and he brought it over right away. All of these experiences pretty much left a bad taste in my mouth, and it wasn't just the flavorless salmon.

However, the silver lining of Bistro 7 and possibly (hopefully) it's saving grace is the fact that it advertises an excellent happy hour. We were not able to make that, but I definitely would like to try that out as the appetizers were by far the best part of the meal for sure. I would love to try some of the others ones on the menu without a doubt, and I think another trip to this location may be in order. However, I do not foresee myself being fooled into ordered more overpriced entrees. Fool me once, shame on you, fool me twice, shame on me.

I hope to return to this review and have a much better experience to share, but for right now I am definitely not impressed at all.

I tried Cowbell a while back when it was on everyone's favorite list of new places to go and it was obnoxiously busy.  I had to sit at one of those community picnic table like tables with people I didn't know all up on my hip.  I ate the supposed best burger around and was underwhelmed.  

Fast forward 2 years or so and this time the girlfriend wanted to give it a try since she had not been.  This time the place was steady but we were able to get a spot at the bar and my semi claustrophobic issues were solved.  She loves a good burger so she order one and I got the Carne Asade tacos.  My tacos were pretty tasty and came with a side of beans, pico and slaw to add on top if so desired.  I desired.  She wasn't talking much while eating but after we left she said she kept biting into pieces of gristle.  That's not cool.  It's especially not cool since they charge 13.00 for this burger.  I'm anti the whole gourmet spend an ass loud of money for a hamburger guy.  Especially in my expereince, the cheaper ones are usually better anyway.  I will say their homemade ketchup is quite good.  I thought it was just a gimmick but it has distinctively smokey sweet flavor which was perfect for their hand cut fresh fries.

In closing,  I like Cowbell during non busy times but I'll stay away from the overpriced burger.

Was craving tacos so my bf and I decided to come here. I've been here plenty of times and i must say they have some of the best tacos around. Food is always hot and fresh and tasty. The asada con queso is my favorite, the steak is juicy and there is SO much cheese! I think the next time i'll try the queso fundido! If you are on the west side of Indy and are craving authentic Mexican food come here!

Fantastic fried oysters! I have been craving these for some time and Blupoint did an exemplary version. Light batter and fried a nice golden brown, then served piping hot in a few minutes. The interior a sweet,  soft and slightly briney kiss from the ocean. I also tried a trio of  oysters on the half shell. They came served on a bed of crushed ice. Slight saline taste, shucked a minute earlier. These tiny Great Whites were very good. A trio of mignonettes- cocktail sauce, aquachile and champagne vinaigrette were offered as well.

Great restaurant. Ordered the filet, oscar style. Cooked to perfection and the crab was super fresh. Had the creme brûlée for dessert and it was to die for. The server was friendly and versed in the menu. I felt like the whole experience was worth the high end cost.

I'm fortunate enough to live only two blocks from Sapori-- my husband and I are frequent patrons.  Sapori offers true Italian cuisine.  We frequently bring friends and family to visit and encourage them to try their specials, the chef is always creative and serves incredible seafood.  While we come here for fantastic food and beautiful ambiance, I have to say that Sapori has my favorite wait staff. They are such professionals that it creates a truly special dining experience, something that far exceeds all of the other Collingswood restaurants.  

Sapori, you're my absolute favorite!

(And yes, you can often look forward to a complimentary shot of limoncello, chocolatecello, or some other creative flavor.)

I have been here twice now with friends.  Once for brunch and once for dinner.  Both were excellent in terms of food quality and service.  They only take reservations for 8 or more.  My only caveat is it gets very loud in the dining room.  They did install sound baffles but it didn't help.  We still had a great time though. 

I have to give a special shout-out to our server Stephanie who was so much fun.  She has a great personality and kept our glasses full and the table cleared all while covering a lot of tables. 

Brunch has an excellent and inexpensive menu.  I had the spicy scramble and it is VERY spicy but delicious.  If you prefer less spicy, I would suggest asking them to lay off the chile sauce. The housemade peach bellini is very tasty.  They are working on having a bottomless mimosa but for now, it is $7 per glass.

Dinner was great. We had a party of 8 so we always order lots of apps to share.  The stuffed jalapenos are delicious but VERY spicy.  We also tried the cheese balls and chicken pops and they were good. My pork steak was excellent and enough for a couple of more meals.  Everyone enjoyed what they got from filet to steak sandwich.  I recommend checking out this family run place. It is on the Hill with two parking lots along with street parking on Shaw.
Nice people but the donuts are horrible and tasteless. Probably one of the worst donuts I had. Also tried the apple fritter which was another huge disappointment.

i recently went to this restraunt. the place was very busy. the staff was very nice. i really enjoy the meal i had,the place was verfy clean.and best part was you didnt have to wait a long time to get in.it was worth the trip,and i will go again for sure

The sushi at this place bumps the rating up from 3 to 4 stars. The sushi is comparatively cheap and more seafood and less rice than other places which is nice. Great flavor too. I've also had the steamed dumplings (good), Four Seasons specialty (bland), General Tso's combo deal (good). The fried rice is just okay, what you'd expect for drive thru fried rice. I was excited to try their bourbon chicken but after one reviewer said it wasn't like the mall food court version but more like terryaki, I'll have to pass. Overall, it's a good place for a quick chinese food fix and the sushi is really good for the price.

Note: Apparently, they do buy one sushi roll get another half off from 11-2 (cash only). I wish they would've told me this before I paid with a card...Cmon chopstick express help me help you with those credit card fees.

This place was SO good! I love that you can substitute the burger with a vegan patty or impossible burger patty. Also got their sweet potato fries which were great! They are open until midnight so this makes for a great late night meal.

We ate at Curry Leaves four times during our stay in Tampa and we absolutely loved it! We eat Indian food all the time and cook it at home as week. This was by far some of the best Indian food we've had during any of our vacations and it far exceeded the food we get at restaurants back in MN where we live. The food was delicious, the service was quick. They treated our daughter like a princess and made sure she was accommodated, even bringing her rice out right away! We will definitely be going back our next time in Tampa! We completely forgot to take pictures, each time our food came we dug right in!
Great food, nice and fast service very close to home made Mexican food only wish they had parking spaces since parking is so limited at Carpinteria
Went to dinner at this place that was recommended to us by locals! Absolutely great dinner with good service & a nice bar staff! A little pricey , but you got what you paid for.
Wow .....Food is great here...Honestly this is the first hotel i felt like a home food. So colorful food with no impact .... I love to come anytime i get an opportunity ...

The food was fine by New Orleans standards (I'm a native, so, yes I have spent my 10,000 hours in NO restaurants). Not great, but not bad. What I can say is that I have never been so rushed through a three-course weekend dinner anywhere, especially not in our gracious city. No sooner had our cocktails arrived than our soup course was unceremoniously plopped on our table. My husband had gotten up to wash his hands, but that didn't matter. Soup was served anyway. Who in New Orleans doesn't take a moment to savor your Sazerac and reflect on the day? Not Muriel's, that's who. As I was spooning up my last bite of curried bisque, a waitron appeared over my shoulder and actually took away my soup plate whilst I was putting down my spoon. Seriously? Her robo-colleague dropped our main courses before she cleared the room. What about a pleasant breather between courses? My husband and I soon figured out the reason:  The two front-door workers were patrolling all the rooms, one of them with a tablet. He was clearly noting empty tables or other infractions. The waitstaff had been reduced to automatons on an assembly line. What a waste of an otherwise lovely evening.

I was so looking forward to the shack opening. It looked very fun and the menu looked really good. My family went a couple weeks after opening and said it was so so. They said hashbrowns were extremely greasy. Finally a day off work and I get to go, I took my daughter. Walking in the place looked very cool and I was excited! After being seated we waited 10 min before anyone coming to our table. Finally a girl asked if we had been helped, we had not so she said then she would help us. Food was nothing special, my omelet was overcooked, and yes my hashbrowns were very greasy. Yuck. Sadly I'll m not impressed and wont be back. It's clearly one of those cool atmosphere restaurants but don't go for the food!

Visited friends last evening and decided to order delivery from this restaurant- highly recommended by our friends. I was impressed with the large selection of items on the menu, and it took awhile before I could decide . . . it all sounded so yummy! Finally chose one of their specialties called "Saraceno" because I am a seafood LOVER and this dish featured shrimp, scallops, clams, mussels and baby octopus! WOW! My mouth was watering and I could hardly wait for the food to arrive! However, much to my disappointment, they sent something called "Pasta Terracina" instead of the "Saraceno". The Terracina was all veges on pasta- probably fine for a vegetarian, but a HUGE bummer for me!! My friend had called in the order, and I was sitting right next to him and distinctly heard him order "Saraceno". Yet when he called them to let them know about the mixup, they blamed HIM and said he had ordered the Terracina! Not cool!! My friend orders from them all the time- yet there was no offer to correct the mistake or accept any kind of responsibility on their part . . . not even an offer for a coupon or discount on his next order . . . nothing. Just left me with a meal that was not at all what I had been anticipating- and not even something I could bring myself to enjoy as I am not a vegetable fan at all (especially for tomatoes and zucchini, which the Terracina was loaded with) The veges were mushy, and they didn't include any parmesan cheese or red pepper flakes to help enhance the flavor. My husband shared his clams and spaghetti with me, and I did my best to forget about it. Just wanted to write this review to advise anyone ordering either of these dishes to specify "the one with the SEAFOOD" or "the one with the VEGES" . . . or better yet, perhaps in the future the Tuttorosso staff should confirm with the customer to be sure they're going to get what they want. And if a mixup occurs, at least make a gesture to try and make it right rather than blaming the customer.

Hookahs and drinks are amazing,  very friendly and great service. 
They make really good hookahs (this is coming from a middle eastern guy who smokes hookah most of the time and own 3 of them at home lol). 

Go there you won't be dissapointed.

Really dislike a lot of their food. Chicken cheese steak have a lot of meat but it's flavorless and chewy. The pizza isn't too bad for the price .... But it's pizza, not the best I've ever had and not the worst. Truly dominos and Pizza Hut have more flavor :/ anyway I love their fries and their quesadillas!!! They truly are amazing but really how hard is that To mess up ???

A holiday dinner at Wine Exchange Bistro was wonderful. We had a party of 6 and sat outside. Food and drinks we highly, highly recommend to all of our friends and family. Everyone of my party will recommend this restaurant; however, the server was not someone whom I would recommend.
Checks were just plopped on the table, a tad bit on the sarcastic side when asked to explain degree of spice, response was a bit short tempered and condescending at multiple points of the evening.
All things being equal we will be back but definitely
never again in her station.

Went on Sunday night (yesterday) and wanted to wait till today to post. The restaurant was not crowded but the noise level was extremely high. We ordered the calamari which was tender and cooked perfectly. The appetizer plate was nothing special and the roasted peppers were from a jar. Our waitress was attentive and even made an adjustment on our son's meal with ease. 
I had the gnocchi with sausage added and it was good but the sauce was a little bland. My wife had the veal Sinatra which was a good portion size but needed more seasoning. I can't believe for a small byob Italian restaurant the pasta is not home made. That was real disappointing. 
Overall not a bad experience but one of the other waitress had her young daughter chasing her around the dining room crying. I don't ever mind eating out with kids but this just seemed a little over the line. 
We won't be going back. I was really hoping it was going to be a go to BYOB in NE Philly. Our search will continue!

Went on Sunday with the family. The food was typical American diner. Ordered the brioche pancakes and they were quite delicious. My cousin ordered the southern friend chicken biscuits with gravy and he really enjoyed it. The only thing that wasn't great was the coffee.  Otherwise I would recommend for a Sunday brunch.
It's a fuckin WaWa, they are all the same. Flavorless sandwiches and over priced coffee and soda.

My husband and I went to dinner for the first time last night. The food was great and all the staff was very nice and out going. Our waiter Andrew was awesome. He was super attentive and had great suggestions! We definitely will be back!

Fun events like trivia and karaoke

Food: A (deliciously prepared, well seasoned, and a good selection.)

Drink A (full service bar and happy hour prices ex: "$2 drafts". Beer selection is semi typical of all the local bars Rogue dead guy, sam Adams seasonal, sam Adams lager, DFH 60 min, yuinglig, Guinness, Victory hopdevil... )

Atmosphere: B (the hard wood areas are nice, but in the back bar where they host events they have very uncomfortable chairs... and it is very strangely laid out: almost sitting on top of everyone elses table.. yet its such a big room with a lot of empty space, cant they just move the tables a little? You'd think they would........)

Service: C (depending who you get you could be there with an empty glass with your tongue hanging out for half an hour or get filled up in 30 seconds. Geez, one time I went in with my friends (5 of us total) and I got completely ignored since i was in the corner seat.. my friends had to order me beers.)

Overall: good food, nice atmosphere

The first time I came here I had just turned 18. I was literally a culinary dunce. The only thing I knew was hometown Mexican and Vietnamese food. 

I made the chef cook my salmon sashimi which apparently was suppose to be eaten raw. At the time I didn't know. The chef was so nice and accommodating. 

Now, I've been to the best sushi restaurant in New York, Chicago, San Francisco, Bangkok, Los Angeles, and Miami. This place does not hold up. 

On a side note, a fellow Yelper thought it would be appropriate to send me a hateful message about how dumb I was. I guess he was born with sushi in hand.

Cheers!

we had to wait 10 minutes for a small Mocha Frappe that was sitting on the counter ready to be served the whole time. I was late to pick up my child because of this. The manager was extremely rude. She was upset and shouting to employees looking for her big mac, and then she grabbed my bag of food and dug through it looking for hers. After i told her the food was mine, she continued complaining to the employee, who then also decided to dig through my food. This is why everybody is quitting their jobs there. The manager is rude and disrespectful and the employees never smile.
This place is very good with a very neat atmosphere and a large menu with a lot to choose from! I highly recommend. It has quite a lot of healthy options as well!

For a such a  high class menu and prices to match, I expect some DAMN good food. I love duck. I love risotto. And guess what? The risotto topped with duck was proclaimed to be one of their best dishes. Well, my risotto was delivered cold and tasted like it was dessert and not and entree. There was so much lemon and it was so sweet that it could have been topped with whipped cream and served as a twist on a lemon cream pie. Now, I was a little confused about the duck being cold as well, but the dish is intended to be topped with 'cool' duck. Meh.

Customers RAVE about that $12 mac and cheese appetizer with truffle oil. Hell, over Thanksgiving I made an entire casserole dish of fancy mac and cheese (made with gruyere, parmesean, fontina and cheddar) from Pioneer Woman's website that blew Firefly's out of the water. Maybe even out of the entire ocean.

Firefly must be doing something right because the tiny, quaint, quirkily decorated restaurant was booming with customers. I will say, the primary demographic of customers were age 50 and older. I wonder if Firefly was once the hot place to eat and has since gone downhill and the original customers remain loyal?
yummy breakfast sandwiches and a great selection of iced teas/coffees. always friendly too!!

Tap House is an overall great restaraunt. The food is a 10/10, fun and comfortable atmosphere and service is impeccable. I have gone a few times over the past couple months and the service has been top notch. I have had Deja as my server a few times and she has always been extremely kind, personable, and a helpful waiter. Will definitley be back soon!
Food's always great everytime we dine. Live the multitude of choices on the specials menu. Service is a little slow.

Im sure anyone who is locals knows that you will wait 20 plus minutes in line, the employees are incredibly rude and your order will be wrong. You would think since they are throwing any food into a bag and clearly not reading order tickers they would at least be fast. Or that the orders would be correct given the abysmal wait times. Not the case. This Wendys breaks every sin for a fast food place. Slow service. Incredibly rude employees. And incorrect orders.

Was visiting from LA so I wanted to try something different and new. Right when I saw Turkish delights, I knew I had to try them. I went in and was not greeted nor was I offered any samples. It was obvious that I was confused on what to get and I also didn't know how it works. Unfortunately, I wasn't able to receive that excellent service everyone received. This explains why I only ordered two since I had no idea what I'm getting myself into. 

The baklava was a bit on the sweeter side. So if you're into sweets, this snack is for you. It's also on the higher end of the price considering how it's $3 for a piece. If you've never had Turkish food, I would still recommend experiencing it. Would I come back though? Probably not.

Very nice decor. Kyle was quite pleasant and knowledgeable so ask to sit in his section during lunch!!

They serve "crab boil red potatoes" in lieu of bread. OMG! I couldn't stop eating these wonderfully delicious, salty, spicy little fellas. Kyle even brought out a few more (with real butter)...perrrrrfect! 

The stuffed flounder was quite good. Perfectly seasoned, light, flaky and served with a savory stuffing. The seafood platter with shrimp and fish is HUGE! Plus, it's perfectly fried, delicious and well seasoned too!

To me I like their pizza. They always have different pizzas and you can even get your own personal pizza. You can bring it home and pop it in the oven and done. I feel like they should build more because I have to drive 30 minutes to just get a pizza.

Staying here at the hotel and didn't not want to go out in the rain. Had soup, salad, dessert and cocktails. Excellent service, food is fresh and well prepared. Cocktails were good. Pleasant adult setting.

Tried it for the first time last night and was sadly disappointed.   I ordered the bbq chicken platter with mac and cheese and green beans.  I got some smoked chicken in water with collard greens and some inedible mac and cheese.  I had expected pulled chicken with bbq sauce.  The chicken pieces were tiny bits of chicken scraps. 
Husband got ribs and they were really good...and did have sauce, great sauce too.  
We got two slices of cornbread too.  They were really tiny, but tasty.
Overall, for the prices, it is not worth it for the platters.  Maybe just the ribs, if we go back.

I came here to try out the flavored boiled seafood. I've been making my rounds to all of the seafood places in Nashville so I was looking forward to Crab Fever opening up. FYI they do not have their liquor license yet so wet your whistle after you leave. I shared the combo number two with additional crawfish. The combo number two is snow crab, shrimp, corn, potato and pork sausage. I chose the fever sauce and mild spice level. The seafood was perfectly cooked but was not flavorful. The sauce does not deep into the seafood like it does at other restaurants. The sauce here is a lot thicker than other places which may be a part of the issue. I also strongly dislike pork sausage. The service was really quick and our server was attentive so that is a plus. It's worth trying out again once I can get alcohol with my seafood.

Monty's is located right on Jackson Square, across from Cafe Du Monde; its prime location for refueling whilst exploring New Orleans. 

We walked in just before the lunch rush. Since we had a larger party, we had to wait about 10 minutes for a table to be available.

Service was decent. Our food was delivered in a timely manner, however, the waiter was difficult to find at times.

Food was meh. I had the crab cakes and they were slightly over seasoned, however, I appreciated the large amount of crab they used.

Every time I visit this gem, I never regret ordering. Their food and variety of flavored bubble teas are always a hit . I also appreciate their social distancing rules they have set in place and precautions they take to make sure their staff and customers are protected. Very appreciated!

Hong Kong house has the best dim sum ever! We tried five types: fried shrimp, stuffed tofu, fried pork dumplings, steamed tofu, and coconut milk pudding. All were amazing. The only negative I could find with hing kong hose is the fact that they don't brew their own iced tea. Its lipton on tap. The prices are absolutely fabulous!  Lunch cost us less than $20!  For dim sum!  Excellent!  The restaurant is clean and beautifully appointed and the staff is wonderful. They are very helpful if you want to try something new and aren't sure about the ingredients in a certain dumpling. It was so good I've already picked out which I'd like to try next. Pleasantly surprised!!!

These guys REALLY need to advertise better. I was complaining to a coworker just last week that I haven't had good barbecue since the last time I was in Austin.
