She told me about this place and swore up and down that it was Texas good. I walked in and immediate fell in love, well before I ever got to order any food.

Back story time! Three generations of my family have been military and police. So walking into a place that celebrates EVERY branch and every first responder, took me back to being on a military base. Bravo guys just bravo. 

So onto the food! They have a caveman style menu and it rocks. You can order ordinary things like a rack of ribs and a pulled pork sandwich, or you can do like me. Walk up, grunt the word MEAT, and they'll ask how many :)   I ordered three meats (brisket, smoked turkey, and jalapano sausage) southern mac and cheese, and a sweet tea. Best meal I've had in ages. It's 90% close to texas good, the brisket could use a little more salt, but champagne problems!

If I had any slight criticism, I wish that they'd stay open a little longer. The 9pm close time means that I can only get there on days off, but again with the champagne problems. I can't wait to go back. And again THANK YOU FOR ALL YOUR SUPPORT OF OUR SERVICE MEN AND WOMEN!!!!!

It's a build your own poke bowl. Topping selection is great. You can get 2 different meats, and they have a large amount of sauces. Ingredients taste fresh and for those that can't make up their minds, they have recommendations

This is HORRIBLE Thai food. My fiancé and I used to order from here once every two weeks for about 3 years. We recently moved to palm harbor so it was no longer close enough to justify going frequently. However coming back into town I was so excited to get take out since we were driving back by there.

I ordered what I always do, chicken Panang cure with broccoli. He ordered chicken pad Thai. It was AWFUL. there was no flavor in either. Very disappointing because it used to be great! 

I don't know if they changed hands or chefs but it was so horrible that we decided to toss it and go somewhere else for dinner. 

I wondered why there was no one else in the restaurant when I went to pick it up. Now I get it.  

If I could give this 0 stars I would. We will NEVER go back.

This is probably the most cool, laid back beach hang out around! It's casual- you see anything from bikinis to shorts, etc/ it's got great bar, music, food, and scenery! Great for families, too! Cabanas, beach chairs, corn hole, and live music! They even have a water toy box out on the beach for kids!

Staff at this spot was very friendly and patient with us. We were visiting on business and just wanted to grab some bites in which this place is tapas style. How can you go wrong? Tapas and a full bar. Sounds great to me. We ordered several dishes to share at the table and a few were fabulous and a couple were mehhh, take it or leave it. To note, the brussel sprouts were cooked perfectly in texture and BACON!!! The onion and pepper addition was good too but I got a hot bite one time that torched my tongue. 

Tasted great, the brussel sprouts and thai chicken wraps

Ok may try again, crab cakes and mac n cheese

I'm good not to order the meatballs. The sauce however, was awesome!

Only had breakfast at this quaint little place. (several times)
The food was awesome each time,staff and management is great.
Very busy and rather loud but worth the wait. Next time I am in the area I will go back.

I threw an 80th Birthday party for my mother on September 28th at The Mansion. I spent $6000 dollars and invited 75 guests. I just got off the phone with the new owner asking if he was going to honor the $125 gift card that my mother received as a gift. He told me that he was not!! This is ABSOLUTELY DEPLORABLE. THE BEST OF LUCK IN YOUR NEW BUSINESS!! I do believe in KARMA!!

Karl Daniel
NYC

Hillary is the best server literally ever!!! She made our experience so great. I didn't like the first drink I ordered and without even saying anything or taking it back, she took it off my bill. Went above and beyond for our group of almost 20 people and hustled so hard. Thank you Hillary we love you!!!

This place is called EdgeWild. I wasn't expecting it to be a restaurant.

I mean, EdgeWild sounds like the name of an assisted living center for elderly swingers...

or a line of Oakley sunglasses....

or the long-awaited follow-up album by The Spin Doctors...

or a model of mp3 player released by Zune...

or a WWE diva's dildo...

or a hipster bar in Wyoming...

or a roller derby team in Wyoming...

or a Christian metal band...

or a venture capital firm that specializes in juicers...

or the nickname of a tattoo'd Christian youth pastor who will later be jailed on statch...

or a show on the WB centered on a young logger in Vancouver and his love of bestiality...

or a hip, new tampon for urban youth...

or a new drink made with Wild Turkey and Apple Cider Vinegar...

or a roller coaster at Dollywood...

or weed-flavored, THC-less gummy bears for the children of hippies...

or a pill you take to keep from scratching your fungus ridden testicles...

or a hairspray company owned by members of Cinderella and Motley Crue...

or a particularly painful anal piercing...

or a social media dating app that centers around abstinence...

or a masculine appliance for those worried about urine seepage...

or the brand name of a hemorrhoid pillow...

or a condom company exclusive to whorehouses...

or a standardized test for pro wrestlers...

or a vaginal rejuvenation clinic...

or a cream you would apply to your irritated taint...

... not a restaurant. But whatever. The food is pretty good. The seats are surprisingly comfortable and won't irritate your taint (aka irri-taint.)

Always love my time at the Brewery! 

The Fish Tacos are amazing and unexpected at a brewery , the Brewte salad is great and I love the Pretzel Bites! 

They book a great number of fabulous bands and have awesome events as well.  If you are in town, check it out!

Great new addition to the neighborhood.  The atmosphere is great and kid friendly.  However, the food was such a disappointment. I ordered the chicken sandwich and potato wedges and received half a sandwich and 4 potato slices. It's evident Dock Street it trying to be something it isn't. Where is the pizza? Add French fries and a burger to the menu. Know your neighborhood. Will be back for drinks because it's so close to my house, but definitely won't eat here again.

3rd stop on the Flavors of Philly Tour, by City Food Tours - Each tour guest received a one-half of Philly Cheese Steak sandwich and a plate of Cheese Fries to share among two guests. I have had different Cheese Steaks along my travels, but never a Philly Cheese Steak from a real Philly restaurant. Now, I know what all the hype is all about...

If you want a simply fantastic experience this is it!!!

You can find a coconut curry soup that is quite elevated here...And the dishes and appetizers take you away to canopied lands and romantic times.

My other half and I ate here and actually hung out for a bit afterward...we never do that! We are always busy! The service was good even though there was a wait, and we found the reason for that wait explained in our first bite.

Atmosphere was clean though the restroom is a little shady and pushed back by the kitchen. The dishes were large and we were able to share. 

The Panang and the pad Thai chili chicken thing were both amazing. Had mango sticky rice for desert which is a MUST at Thai dinners and they did it right! I ate a large soup almost completely myself because I could not stop myself so...wow!

So, true to my word, I gave this place another try after they've been open for a few weeks. I am so glad that I did!

The falafel recipe seems to have changed a bit and my wife says that it's much better and is no longer dry. The tabouli had bulgur in it this time, and was just delicious. Seriously. I don't often like tabouli, and I ate the entire portion. It was just that fresh and wonderful. 

They had the shawarma this time, and it was amazing. Even my 13 month old approved (also worth noting, she had some of the rice and shoveled it all into her mouth, and then demanded more - 3 times!) The pita was so good!

All of the things that I liked before were still delicious - the rice, the hummus (which my kid also ate, by the spoonful!), the grape leaves, and of course that BAKLAVA.

The staff is still friendly and accommodating, the place is clean, and I will definitely be back.

Oh, also worth mentioning, I did try the french fries. Not something I would normally order from a Mediterranean place, but glad I tried them here. They are seasoned perfectly and I'm pretty sure they were hand-cut.

Great neighborhood spot for a beer, a snack, or a few of each. They do a great job of rotating the draught and can selection to keep things fresh and the servers are generally friendly and knowledgeable when you ask about their current selections. The food is just as strong as the beer selection and there truly is not a single thing on the menu that does not hit the spot. The Buffalo chicken spring rolls and chicken fingers are fan favorites but everything from the kitchen is solid. 

The Collar is truly a gem and is worth stopping by any time you're in the neighborhood. Looking forward to being able to sit at the bar again as the bar tending staff are all exceptionally friendly. In the meantime their tables are a great place to start or end any night out with friends!
Great service, nice ambiance!  The bread is so delicious!  The flounder was excellent.  Jambalaya was meh.  Gumbo was good.

Ive been here a few times and every time I go its always a treat. I heard about the place when they catered an event at my old job; I was impressed with the fact that they were the ONLY Mexican joint that I loved the refried beans. The wait staff is always very friendly, and always make good suggestions. This last time I went for the happy hour which you get free chips and salsa and beans (which is always a winner).  I had the chicken fajita wrap with some sour cream on the side, very yum. The chicken was juicy and I'm an onion gal so I was very happy that the cook wasn't scared to pile on the caramelized onions. Oddly enough I didn't Ive never gone to the bathroom the few times Ive there so I couldn't tell you the status on this. The seating is not bad pretty comfy chairs and lots of leg room so no complaints there.
This is one of my favorite local spots for breakfast or lunch. I usually order online and pick up. Love the chocolate chip pancakes and the avocado BLT.

I order the "hot" chicken sandwich and was largely unimpressed. Wendy's spicy chicken nuggets have more kick than these oversized chicken tenders. They weren't bad per se, but the fact that they were touted as "hot chicken" set my expectations high. My friend said the same of the hot chicken bites. The fact that the sandwich came with American cheese and aioli should have been a red flag. The fries served with the sandwich were excellent and made up for the hot-chicken letdown. Next time I'm at Acme, I'll definitely look elsewhere on the menu.

Went to Booker's with a large group (8). The restaurant is located in a gentrified area- safe with easy parking. Overall, we had a fantastic experience and would absolutely return. 

The service both at the bar and during our dining experience was great. The cocktails are reasonably priced and the happy hour menu has a nice selection of small bites that are priced accordingly. 

Once seated, for appetizers, we had wings, crab cake sliders, Brussels spouts and buffalo cauliflower. Our main entrees were very enjoyable. We all had some type of fish-salmon, trout or cat fish. They were all delicious. I wish this establishment much success.

Perfect dining experience for dinner tonight at Rocco's.  It all came together...service, food, ambience, wine, timing, and noise level (no overbearing loud music).  In fact everyone raved about their meals and everyone wanted to taste each other's.  "Yum...yum...yum"...that's what we said with each bite and with each taste of each other's food.  Steaks cooked perfectly, salmon was the best I think I have ever had.  Our server was right on.  It was way better than our first time here early on...they definitely have their act together.  Can't wait to go back!!

Our first night in New Orleans and we wanted to grab a quick bite. This spot is not too far off of Bourbon Street the area is dark not too many street lights kind of a warehouse district feel but hey we still had a good meal. The bouncer checks your ID and you order at the bar. We ordered crab balls catfish po boy and beignets. All of the food was good and seasoned well. I don't drink sodas often but this root beer was pretty good.

Headline: Good food, needs some ambiance. will try again, and probably again.

Like a few others, I was excited to see a new Mexican restaurant opening up. the outside isn't really telling, I don't recall what was there prior, but that is what it still looks like. so from a curb appeal point, it wasn't really pulling me in. the reason I wanted to go there, was the appeal of Mexican food.
walk in, and really still not feeling it. it is just some tables and chairs, spread out as it would in any cafeteria. a mexican statue in the door, was really the only thing that told me it was a mexican style restaurant. 
We were quickly seated as the place is kind of big inside. our drink orders were taken, they have a good selection of beers and wine. not great but good enough to cover most folks tastes. the server seemed new, and I have to keep reminding myself that the place is new. he seemed unsure of the menu and like me, no idea how to pronounce some of the items on the menu. which, tip to would be servers, learn the menu. how to pronounce items, what they are, what options you have.... he wasn't a bad server, rather attentive, but you could sense the newness and also the short lived tenure of his time as a food server. meaning I don't think he had any plans on doing it for more than a month or two.

Ambiance.  it didn't really have any. my assumption is that it being a new place, they did not want to spend too much on fixtures and paintings and building remodeling. which is likely a smart business idea. put the money into getting the operation going, and, I hope, mold the place more as the revenue comes in to support it.  which is cool, but maybe a touch more sooner than later. for all I knew I was sitting at a table in the middle of a shoe store that oddly had a bar, and a mexican statue. It wasn't bad, per say, but it wasn't good. It just was.

Food. so I tend to tense up and feel a need to punch folks when I hear "it isn't authentic Mexican".  1 how would you know? 2 from what part of mexico. 3 from what era? Mexico isn't a place that has had a static culinary system for eons. it has been influenced by visitors (and invaders) for ever. with each "visit" a little taste of their guest remained, not in a cannibalistic way. what I truly enjoyed was that the menu was not the usual array of things you can do with a tortilla, cheese, meat, and rice.  they had other foods, believe it or not that did not include a tortilla... I admittedly do not have any idea what would constitute authentic mexican food. but I can tell you this, the food here was good. the portion didn't make me feel like I need to go outside, purge, come back in and eat more. nor did I need to go home and microwave a mac and cheese. 
The Guacamole, I found to be very good. My GF was less enthusiastic about it. but she has bad taste, look at her BF.

reading some other reviews, perhaps I did not see the place as well as others did. I didn't see any paintings of the countryside. so my comment on the ambiance might be widely incorrect, it does happen, and I hope so. I want this place to do well, I enjoy the semi diverse food options we have here in Conshohocken. I was sad to see the indian food joint go away.

in summary, I will be back, and will perhaps increase my rating. of course it could go the other way, but I'm optimistic.

Great restaurant! I've been coming here for years and the food is consistently great, portions large, service perfect, and price is right!

And they deliver
Great beer choices, good food and had some pretty good service. Went out on the balcony during a time at lunch and it was a great time with some friends. Definitely recommended
Found this on yelp but unfortunately when you walk in it's very not up to par. Very dissatisfy

Don't make the mistake of coming here to use the Gift Card you got for Christmas. The food is great - much bigger menu than I remembered - and our server was friendly. Highly recommend the Thai chicken pizza. We also split an order of buffalo cauliflower and a power bowl. Everything was great.
Know before you order here. Be sure to read the latest health inspections. They have very bad reports numerous of times.  My house ordered here and we all got sick.

I fear these types of restaurants.  Hibachi *can* be done well but every one that I've been to (this one included)  muddles it down to "if we set things on fire, perhaps they won't notice that the food is bleh drowning in some form of sauce.".

Well, I noticed.

We had the cheesesteak and smoked wings. The cheesesteak meat was very tender, loved the bread it was served on. I'm not normally a fan of chicken wings, but the smoked wings with the dry rub and buffalo sauce for dipping were amazing. Can't wait to have them again.

When I was 2 years lesser of the man I am today, I came to this establishment, drawn in by high reviews and the appeal of fresh seafood I could not find anywhere else. Of course, expectations were high given the price. But that experience blasted my ideas of good oysters out of the water - I had to come back and review this place.

Here I am, ready to take on the challenge of writing about Oyster House, the next place receiving my utmost praise. When going inside, it was busy as always. But a pro tip if you're with a small group of people: SIT AT THE OYSTER BAR. It's a nice view of how they prepare the oysters, and the vibes are immaculate.

With excellent service, especially for how busy the restaurant was, we ordered numerous smaller items alongside around 20 oysters and clams of various types.  Furthermore, we also had Fried Oysters, Grilled Octopus, New England Clam Chowder, and a true Fisherman's Stew.

I'm going to save you some time. While I write long reviews for a majority of restaurants, all you need to know is that this is a MUST TRY. Everything I had was amazingly tasteful, and was demolished within seconds. The freshness of this seafood is unparalleled from what I've seen in Philly - would love to hear if anyone has better option.

Best Pizza Ever! And nicest people too. We literally called at close time and asked if they could make us a pizza. Not only did they do it gladly, they gave us some freebies and thanked us for shopping there.
Loved it! Beautiful restaurant, love the location/water view. Ordered the mahi tacos and they were great! Server was also great. Will be going back for sure.
Excellent burger! Juicy and loaded with flavor. Fantastic onion rings. I loved the mayo bar. Definitely a great burger.

The Cheesecake Factory is a mix. The food can be amazing. There have been a couple time where I have had something that is just OK but never bad. The Cheesecake is so awesome that is has ruined me for other cheesecake. The downside, is that is always packed and also so LOUD. The other downside is that is always an expensive dinner out as well.

So, I'm a local. I live here in East Nashville and love it, but when it comes to a slow, drippy Saturday afternoon and I need to relieve my boredom and satisfy my hunger, I stop into this place. True to it's name a lot is battered and fried, but this place offers a great selection of sushi rolls, sides and cold beer. 

I have to admit that trying to find a place that serves food worthy of repeat patronage and service that matches is hard to find anywhere, but here. As I write this review, sitting in the bar area  I'm watching one young man, StevN literally jog between tables checking on his customers, handing out menus, running credit cards, stopping at each table to ensure all of his  guests are not only satisfied, but genuinely happy with their experience today...this is not unusual for StevN, he by far and hands down is the best bar tender/server/bus boy (I say it this way because he is doing it all) I have ever seen in the food and beverage industry. There are currently 32 people sitting in the bar area and this guy has not only maintained his professionalism, he is showing one table at a time what it's like to have a great experience while dining at Battered and Fried. 

I'm having the fish and chips, lightly breaded cod and fresh, hot, hand cut fries with a cold draft. It doesn't get much better than this. Even when I order something other than my "usual", it arrives piping hot and fresh. This is why I continue to come here, I know that, with out a doubt I will have a fantastic dining experience that exceeds my expectations every time.  Thanks, StevN for another great meal, cheers all!

Excellent service and food. I had the pappardelle bolognese and my partner had the filet with mushroom ragout. Not a scrap of food left behind. Attentive and friendly service by Adrian. We will return!

What a disappointing dining experience.  1st let me say that our waitress, Felicia, was very nice and did a good job.  

However, the food was just bad.  I thought this was an upper (not highest but upper) level steakhouse.  I was expecting something on the level of Ruth Chris, Sullivan's, Maggiano, etc. instead it was akin to a fancy food corral.  

I ordered this $41 seafood grill.  The sweet potatoes were GREaT!  However, the asparagus were not even cooked!  It's like they forgot to blanch them & instead just put them on the plate.  Plus my fish was undercooked.  I hate sending food back so I ended up only eating the sweet potatoes & putting everything in a to go container.  I even told the manager my fish was undercooked and showed him the pale fleshy part and he just looked confused and said he would get me a container.  Additionally everything took a really long time.  

My kids ordered fruit punch w/their kids meals and that had to be sent back because it was flavored fountain water.  Hubby ordered the filet and it was so tough and looked like a different cut of meat.  

The $14 calamari appetizer was good but you only get a small portion.  The tomato and mozzarella appetizer was also just bad (how do they mess that up) as the cheese did not taste fresh and it had no flavor.

For the cost and the poor quality I would say skip this place and head to KOP to Seasons 52 or one of the better restaurants as this was not worth the $160-$170 for a family of 4.

I love poke, but I live in Roxborough now.  I used to go to Poke Ono in Ardmore which is great.  Now I am starting to go here.  I fill out the slip of paper with what I want (tuna, salmon, brown rice, and lots of other yummy stuff) and it's great!  I will probably be going for pick up A LOT this Summer!
Longest wait. Incorrect order. Unprofessional and rude employees. Don't bother coming here.
I have eaten at Luke's a handful of times. The food was great every time! The Trio was delicious. The Poppyseed Coleslaw was a perfect side. I even enjoyed the root beer and chips.

I finally made it after finding out about this place in February! I came twice and they were closed during COVID :( and after a 4 month hiatus they are open again!!
To make up for a 4 month delay I got 5 croissants to eat myself today my croissant sampler was delicious. Their plain is the cheapest I've seen in philly and VERY good. Blows hipster joints like Tatte in Boston/DC out of the water. 
Although the plain croissant is the true test of lamination, my personal favorite flavor is almond and so had to get both the chocolate almond and plain almond. These were truly mind blowing. There is rich, thick almond paste permeating the flaky buttery crusts. I'm not sure I can eat other almond croissants after today, after having eating 2 of the frozen Trader Joe's boxed croissants yesterday...

We came here to have brunch....service was great and the food exceeded our expectations...of note was the tomato salad/burrata, red velvet pancakes, and the veggie burger. Would definitely return and recommend to others.

honestly, not my favorite coffee shop in the area. can rarely find a table, so it must be pretty popular with the neighbors, but I prefer cafe clave or manakeesh for my coffee-infused studying needs. food's okay, service is okay, basically everything is okay overall.

Dean was the most amazing waiter. Me and my best friend were doing a road trip and stumbled across Goata Beard. Dean was so helpful with telling us what to do and instead of judging me for getting two creme brûlée's he encouraged it! He was hilarious and made the experience so fun! Then Katie, a different waitress came up and helped us find a place to do karaoke and texted her friends to ask for some advice. They both went so out of their way to help. Also on top of all of that, the food was the best we have had this whole trip with no exaggeration. Thank you guys! Next time we are back in Philly, our first stop will 100% be here! Highly recommend!

They sold me uncooked rotten food!
Save yourself the food poisoning and don't go there.

Jimmy John's menu is nothing fancy but the sandwiches are very good. The meats are really good quality and I love their tuna. The regular 8" sub isn't packed with meat as stated in other reviews but is just the right amount for me and for $5.29 you can't beat it. If you want a fatter sub get the giant club sandwich. It isn't really a club sandwich but just a fuller sub with a lot more meat and that's only $6.79. The rolls are baked fresh there and is very good. You can also get it on their fresh baked thick 7 grain bread but I haven't tried that. They also gut the roll unless you ask them not to. Bottom line, great prices and great sandwiches. I recommend giving it a try.

This is definitely a solid restaurant. In the multiple times I've been to this location they always do seem to have a bit of a wait so don't plan on a quick meal. The ambiance is casual and can be somewhat loud, but there's lots of cool stuff on the walls to look at and the menu is nothing short of extensive. They offer every type of food one could imagine and although it can be a little pricey the food has always been good.

Being a total fan of NY-style pizza, I was very glad that the Yelp app led me to Brozinni's!  Their pies are without question the best NY-style pizza I've had in Indianapolis thus far :-)

Tip: At lunchtime you can get individual slices, just like at your favorite back-alley pizza joint in the Big Apple.  At dinnertime they sell only whole pies.

The signature pies they make here are named for areas and points of interest in NYC, which is a nice touch.  On my first visit, I enjoyed Long Island, which is made with Pepperoni, Sausage, Bacon, Diced Ham, Mushrooms, Black Olives, Green Peppers, Red Onions & Mozzarella.  The toppings are obviously premium quality, the sauce has a nice kick to it without being overpowering, and the crust has both the taste and shape of an authentic NYC pie.  The pizza was totally Legit, and completely delicious!

Their salads are fresh and tasty, and we very much enjoyed their garlic "knuckle" starter.  

Tip: When you get the garlic "knuckles", keep the serving tray when you're done so that you dip your pizza in the garlic butter sauce - it's a great combination!

I look forward to returning to try more of Brozinni's completely Legit NY-style pies - highly recommended!

Since I'm following the TV show Glee which made numerous reference to a chain restaurant called "Breaksticks" (wink wink), I suddenly felt the urge to visit Olive Garden, which could be a smart marketing plot on their part. Of course I have been to Olive Garden before and I too have been shamed for doing so because alas we live in Philadelphia where there's a large Italian population who will take their time to tell you how unauthentic Olive Garden is and in turn I will share my view on most American Chinese food but I digress.

Surprisingly, I've experienced a bit of attitude in Olive Garden, I'm surprised mostly because I only get this kind of attitude either from highly expensive restaurant or fast food places where they get paid so little that they just don't care about customer service. I like to brush that off by saying that the staff are just "colorful", but a training session or two could improve the corporate culture. Or maybe the standard here are generally low and our expectations should be lower.

I've heard so many people mentioning their unlimited breadsticks that I've higher expectations and got disappointed by these greasy, flavorless breads. The salad is tasty but drowned with dressings. I did like my pasta e fagioli soup and it's possibly the more solid course. The eggplant Parmesan is pure bullshit; The eggplants are dry and very bready, almost like chewing on crackers and I swear the tomato sauce on the spaghetti comes out of a can. Any jar sauce would have tasted a lot better. My stuffed chicken marsala has a sharp wine tasted instead of a rounded one and pairing it with mash potatoes is the opposite of ingenious. At this moment, I'm suffering with an upset stomach.

I feel like I was cheated when two blocks away there's Maggiano's and Buca di Beppo where they give you big portions for the same amount of money and much better quality of food. Also the service would have been much better. Though for some reason, my friends love the trashiness of this place and I love my friends, but I'm not looking forward to come here anymore. Screw the breadsticks.

I absolutely love this cafe. It's bright, airy, clean, trendy and has an insane amount of games in good condition. They make great espresso drinks, lattes (coffee and tea) and teas. They have a selection of pastries and desserts. The staff here are always friendly and polite. Best of all they have beer and wine! I usually stop by here for a hot drink and to people watch in the sunny windows. I have yet to play one if their games but the game selection is STACKED. During the weekdays it's nice and quiet and there's plenty of space.

Only place I know where you can get a good hoagie in less than five minutes. Small corner shop that's been around forever and rightfully so. They're good, the prices are reasonable, and they're fast. What more could you want?
SOME Ting-Wong please. Please is there SOME Ting-Wong? Does any one know if SOME Ting is Wong? I think there is some Ting-Wong here.
Great food!!! It was a beautiful night so we were able to sit on the patio. They are doing a good job with the COVID-19 stuff.

Coming from New York City, finding good and quality Chinese food here in the Tampa Bay Area is a difficult task. New Bamboo Express is my new favorite Chinese spot. The food here is unique, tasty, and authentic. They are not overpriced like Tokyo next door! This place takes a stomp on Tokyo and is 10 times better!

Lately I have been a regular at the Cyrano's happy hour, and I have found it to be quite the hidden gem here in the Maple/Brent/Webster Wood/Groves area. They happy hour specials are awesome: half price beer and wine and $5 martinis - some of the best deals in town! The bar is a little small, but it fits the ambiance of Cyrano's very well - cozy. This is a great place to bring a date or just come and chill and sit back and sip on a martini. They have a good selection and the bartenders are always friendly. 
The food to me is just average, and the menu is fairly limited. I have only had dessert once, and I don't really remember it. I have had the burger, and it is pretty good - not great though. Happy hour goes til 7, so I prefer to come here for drinks and try somewhere else for dinner.

Amazing is all I can say! First of all EVERYTHING on the menu sounds delicious, it was so hard to choose! My husband had the oysters appetizer which were HUGE and came out sizzling on the shell which I had to ask how they did it bc the oysters were perfectly cooked. I had the tuna tacos appetizer and I asked for extra wasabi which they must have mixed with something bc it was the best I've ever had and I'm a wasabi junkie. For my meal I went with their signature dish, the scalibut and it was SO good! Buttery scallops and the sauce it sat in was out of control. He had the parmesan crusted catfish which was so flavorful!  For desert I had the salty malty and it was DELICIOUS! Alan was our waiter and he was engaging, funny and excellent!! I'd give 6 stars if I could!

I do not often go to breakfast buffets. But I have been to enough to make a decent comparison.

This has to the most god awful breakfast spread I have ever seen or tried to eat.

Do you guys have a tub of salt you let the food sit in before you put it out on the line?

Nothing and I mean nothing was good, even the fruit was completely devoid of flavor.

The service too was beyond bad.

It was so bad that I did not get angry but just sat there chuckling. 

oy never again....

I still don't think that El Rey is the best Mexican food in town, but I can't complain about their skinny girl margs, the brisket tacos or the fact that it's about 3 blocks from home.

The 'secret' passageway to Ranstead Room is quite superfluous.

Went to Smokin' Thighs tonight for the first time after wanting to check it out for some time.  Food was delicious and service was great!  The kids were with us and they had a great time and loved the food as well.  Patrick, our server, was awesome.  Great selection of craft beers, lots of sports on many screens and plenty of tasty choices on the menu.  You can customize your order with various sauces and toppings to keep things zesty.   I will be back soon with co-workers to dive deeper into the menu.  Can't wait to come back!

Awesome food. My husband and I were looking for a place to get a deli sandwich and had seen the shop driving busy. We decide to stop in and try them out and were not disappointed at all. The sandwiches are made with quality products and great bread and because without that your sandwich will be nasty. Try them out if your are looking for good food and support a great local business.

Yum, yum, yum!! Went here on a Friday night after having a hankering for sushi! We've been on Sunday for the half price special, but enjoyed it so much more this evening. 

The service was phenomenal, as they were extremely accommodating to allow us to sit outside with our dog. It was slightly chilly and wi day, so they turned on the heater and pulled down a tarp to allow us a more comfortable experience. 

We ended up ordering the playboy roll, shrimp roll, and spicy tuna roll along with miso soup to start. The miso soup wasn't my favorite, but I think it was because I was just really excited to have my sushi!!  The rolls we ordered were great! Flavors and portions were just right.
Breakfast here is surprisingly delicious. I tried their chicken egg and cheese biscuit sandwich and it was good. Staff is always friendly

Made my reservation over the phone, confirmed for 4 nights...arrived and my reservation was only for one night. Luckily they weren't overbooked, but this mistake could have been a big problem. 

The wifi is practically non-existent, don't even bother. If you need to work, go to a coffee shop. 

Bed was pretty comfortable. Unfortunately no mini fridge or microwave.

This place is good. Small dining area, but their food is easy to take home. I usually call ahead, grab, and go.  Don't expect to be waited on, they don't have a large staff. They only take your order at the front counter and then deliver the food to your table. You have to get your own drinks too. 
Don't let those things deter you from eating here... food is good. Enjoy!
The best god damn chorizo tacos I've had IN MY LIFE. This place is no joke. If you aren't eating here once a week, you're doing it wrong.

I don't know if I'm more disappointed with this restaurant or the many yelpers who led me astray. So many five-star ratings and I can only wonder if maybe they changed management or chefs or what...

For reference, we ordered, the hot and sour soup, spicy basil fried rice, paht ka pow gai (basil fried rice), paht kee mao (drunken noodles), and massaman curry. I asked for no shrimp in any dish because my wife is allergic and 6 months pregnant.

We got shrimp in the drunken noodles. C'mon man.

Hot and sour soup -- overly flavored with something like soy sauce? My tongue was burning from the sodium (and I was a deer in a past life).

Basil fried rice -- tasted like plain rice.

Drunken noodles -- tasted like plain noodles.

Massaman curry -- decent. I didn't hate it, but I'm an optimist by nature.

Like any good optimist, I thought maybe it'd taste better the next day. Sometimes food can absorb more flavors overnight. Maybe the salt of the hot and sour soup had ripped away all other taste buds, and all I needed was a temporal palate cleanse...

And, yes, the food tasted better. But not great. And I didn't buy food to eat the next morning. 

So in summary, Mama Thai loses 3 stars for trying to kill my wife with shrimp (jk, I know it was nothing personal, but what am I going to do? call and complain and drive out to get a new one or wait 30 minutes for you to drive it out? Idk, maybe I should've called, but my wife was fine not eating the drunken noodles anyway, since everything else was so beige).

Mama Thai loses another star for being weirdly salty and over-soyed (hot and sour soup) and bland at the same time.

All that said, the service was friendly and the place was clean.

In a city with so many great Thai places, might as well avoid this one.

We were in town from Phoenix, found this plave on yelp.  I had the Prime Rib dinner and my wife had the Red Snapper.  Both were delicious!!  Great place to get a nice meal without the pretentiousness of a dress attired restaurant.  Dinner includes soup,/salad, entree, and Desert.  Very friendly service!  Most definitely would recommend.

My friends and I are staying across the Cafe for spring break, and we were so excited about this cafe. We decided to swing over there around 9:30am, and let me tell you- they did not disappoint! I was so impressed with the politeness of the staff and the quality of the food. We both ordered the Avocado Toast and mimosas. The eggs on the toast were delectable, and the avocado was at a perfect level of ripeness. The mimosas were great as well- the orange juice had a little pulp in it which I, surprisingly, found enjoyable. Overall, we had a great experience here, and we plan on visiting a few more times before we leave this weekend.

I love Jamaican food. A little known fact about my hometown (Toronto) is that it has the 2nd biggest West Indian population outside of the West Indies next to Brooklyn, NY. I grew up around Jamaican food and culture.  Imagine my excitement when I found this joint at the farmers market!

As far as Jamaican food goes this joint is spot on. It's a for real Jamaican joint after all. The jerk chicken, oxtail, curry goat, curry chicken (all with rice & peas and callaloo) are the dishes I generally go for with a jamaican beef patty on the side.  Go for the kola champagne or a bottle of ting an you'll be good to go.

Another joy was the fact that they have roti, which is a West Indian flat bread like tortillas but in my opinion is way better. It's got crushed chick peas and is as good as it gets. 

As for the beef patties, they're good, but not as hot (spicy) as I like to have them, but being in Nashville with only one other West Indian joint, I won't complain.

Tell the good dude Kamal that eyejammy says "what up." I highly recommend Jamaicaway. 

Likkle more. seen!

No more needs to be said.  Pho and ramen reign supreme here.  Masters of the Pho universe. MPGA
(Making Pho Great Again)

My friends and I stumbled upon the Clover Grill while walking on Bourbon from the Blacksmith bar a few blocks away. We decided to head here the following day for lunch.

The burgers and fries were great. The meal was much needed after a late night with many drinks. The food hit the spot! Some of my friends went back there 2/3 times during the trip 3 day trip.

The place can be a bit dirty (floors, counters, table tops) and can take a while to be seated. We had to wait about 15-20 minutes to get seated. There aren't many tables to sit at or space at the counter. The check took awhile to get to us after we finished eating. 

Don't expect great service, but you'll come away with a pretty good burger and that's what we were looking for!

I had never been to this location and just stopped in for a quick burger to go. I ordered the 1/4lb I believe it was...it actually was very dry, not seasoned and bland. 
I just couldn't believe it, but maybe just an off day! Only one other customer in at 1pm when I stopped by. The woman at the counter was pleasant, took no time to get burger. I'll go back at a later date and have a redo, when I can sit inside and have aa shake as well!

Last week, I entered a Facebook contest, and was contacted that I had won a VIP dinner for two. For a single mom, recently divorced, this was a real treat. I took my friend Stacy and we ditched our plans to go to the movies to drive nearly two hours to the Clay Terrace location because that was the one that came on the GPS and the FB message I had gotten didn't specify that there were two. When we got there, the place was really nice-like upscale but with a welcoming feel. I loved the clean lines and the decor-it wasn't cluttered and was well lit. We ordered a small Ceasar salad and we were pleasantly surprised that we could actually share it and even had half a plate still left of the salad. It was the absolute BEST Ceasar salad I have ever had-literally it was so flavorful and we later found that they make their own Ceasar dressing. We decided to get a large pizza 1/2 Pine n Swine-which was a pineapple bacon, feta cheese, onions, and tomato sauce. The other 1/2 was their Classic recipe which was Pepperoni, sausage, roasted mushrooms, banana peppers & tomato sauce. Both were scrumptious. Both were an explosive of flavor in every single bite. It was like every taste center on my tongue was awakened and given the gift of flavor. The crust was crunchy to the bite yet soft in the middle just like a great crust should be. It would have been worth the money if we had gone on any other night. Our server was great and I wish I had caught her name. That young lady brought our food out, was ready to explain anything we might have been unsure about, and she even gave some great suggestions, like the Ceasar Salad. When our bill came, I mentioned the promotion we were there for and she got her manager. Clearly we had gone to the wrong location but the manager was AWESOME. He saw the inbox message from their other location and explained. I was ready to pay our bill because we had clearly enjoyed our food and service, but he honored their promotion and even took care of our drinks. We took care of our waitress. It was worth the near 2 hour drive and even getting lost a few times on the way to go. We did not try any of the craft beer-because, well I was driving and I know that one beer can have me a little tipsy. I will say they have a huge selection of craft beers and I saw other patrons enjoying them. They even have employees on hand, like our server, who can explain the different beers and the manager can even give suggestions to what one might want to try since there is such a huge collection. For the pizza lover-this is the place, this IS the place to go. For the craft beer enthusiast-this is a must stop. Don't pass up Pies & Pints at Clay Terrace Blvd in Carmel, In.
You'll wait 10-20 minutes on hold before someone picks up the phone to tell you its a 2 hour wait for pizza. Save your time and go to the Papa Johns on S Emerson!

I have been patronizing Beef'O'Bradys for years, and I must say, I am very conflicted about this place lately. The food is great, no doubt.  The service during the week, especially at lunch is 5 star level - again no doubt!  But I must suggest sticking to the weekdays.  I'm not sure if it is strictly a staffing issue, or what, but this place has a definite Jekyll and Hyde feeling.  The level of service and quality of food rate a 1 star at best.  So that is why I give it 3 stars, but totally suggest eating there, just not on the weekends.
Great place to shoot a rack on well maintained tables. The food is surprisingly good especially for a bar. Liked it so much we joined a pool league and are now regulars.

I cannot say enough good things about this place! The food is amazing, fast and so fresh. You can tell they really care about the quality of ingredients used in their food. I always get the hummus wrap and have never been disappointed. The service is impeccable. I've been going here weekly for the past year and the staff is always super friendly and helpful! Mickey's is simply the best!

Square on Square has really cheap lunch specials..soup, rice, and veggies for under 10 bucks.  Their egg drop soup is delicious and the service is very quick. Portions are large too. Their mixes vegetables are great, as is the sweet and sour chicken.  It's conveniently located right near my office so it's a go-to Chinese food stop for me.  Nom Nom.

I only went here once, during Tampa's restaurant week, and I had been very excited when it opened it a few months earlier. Their food might have tasted very good, but I'm not sure as the taste of it was soured by two things: 
1) Service- I had gone as a group of six. Some of us ordered off the regular vs promotional menu and there were quite a few drink orders, yet nothing to change our behavior from friends dining out to impossibly demanding or badly behaved clients. As a server, I would have calculated a very nice tip, even if it was only at 15%. Although the restaurants ambience is about recreating hospitality and warmth, it was in short supply coming from our waiter. I couldn't tell if he hated us or he just thought he holier than us. Questions about ingredients or how the food is prepared is a great way of establishing rapport with your table, not an inconvenience! I wish I could remember his name other than recalling a red head with a beard. At the entree price points of around $35, I refuse to settle for any newish restaurant that says they are still working out their kinks. There are other restaurants within armature works that are competing at the same price points.
2) Restaurant week promo for $72. My boyfriend and I decided to try the promo menu which was dinner for two, a three course meal including appetizer l, dinner and dessert, which was a pretty great deal. We received one full size appetizer to share, one full sized entree to share, and dessert. It's a good thing we were both on a diet and the smaller portions we had a result of sharing everything was good for our waistlines. But it weirdly and stupidly deceptive as the combined price of the same appetizer and entree from the regular menu was $72, so they just threw in a dry cake slice for free. It was a bizarre and frankly dishonest way of marketing a meal, and we laughed it off.

Oak and Ola has a beautiful, IG worthy decor, and uses the same general parking available to all of armature works. To their credit, we appreciated seeing the owner go to everyone's table, as well as ours, and spend a few minutes chatting. Everyone enjoyed their food and sharing and sampling each other's dishes. But no one in our group has been back.

We are traveling we stopped in for a quick bite.   We love Culver's they offer a snack pack for less than $5 which includes butter burger, fry's and a drink.  Plenty of food.  We greeted when we entered the restaurant.  The staff was friendly and appeared to really love what they do.  My other favorite part of Culver's is the frozen custard.  They have vanilla and chocolate made fresh every day.  And as a bonus they always offer an additional cold creamy flavor of the day.  Today the flavor was Double Chocolate Decadence and it was was rich and delicious.  We always stop at Culver's when we see them when traveling because we don't have one where we live.   Always a treat.

Dang they no longer have the hot dog thing that I love so much. Anyways don't buy too much into the crappy reviews. A lot of them were written during the Heffe's first few weeks when they were figuring out how to properly run a restaurant. They've got it sorted out now and the service is just fine. More importantly, the food is excellent. Really innovative and delicious. Just go there and eat already.
The Thai tea with Boba wasn't strong enough and just tasted bland. Was definitely not worth the money :(

I'm a brand new Tower Grove East resident - Grove East Provisions is a revelation. Why? 

Setting: Grove East is the perfect spot for a meal to go, a relaxing sit down breakfast or lunch, or a place to meet a friend for coffee. Walk up to the counter and order your food and beverage, and they will bring it out to you. (Bonus tip: there are outlets available in the seating area if you need want to bring a computer and get some work done. This pairs nicely with their bottomless coffee.)

Food and Beverages: They use high quality / fresh ingredients, and that makes the sandwiches, salads, and breakfast items fantastic. I had the club sandwich during my last visit and I couldn't help myself from eating the whole thing in all its beauty. Grove East serves a variety of beverages including coffee, soda, wine, beer (draft or bottle), and bloodies/mimosas during brunch. 

Service: I've had nothing but positive experiences and I've always gotten the sense that they care about what they do. 

Go here!

I've been here a few times now. Overall, the sushi is just ok, nothing spectacular. I did take out a few weeks ago for a special roll that was pretty much just a california roll with salmon, crunch, and spicy sauce, and it was ridiculously over priced. Good for large groups if you're looking for a last minute BYO, but otherwise I wouldn't recommend it.

Horrible service. Yes we were greeted friendly but that was it. I ordered a side and it came without any utensils! Then they just left us there so I couldn't even flag someone down to get utensils. It's taking forever to pay because they're still not back here. It isn't even crowded or anything.

Next to Lipscomb University, The Well turns water into coffee. Well, in the most poetic of ways. My friend and I stopped by on a gloomy Saturday evening and our moods were significantly improved upon stepping into the sepia-toned enclave. The baristas were approachable and friendly, offering patient recommendations for their favorite coffee brews. While there was a short wait for our beverages, we watched the whole process from the bar, and it seemed the staff concentrates on providing a high-quality pour over the most rushed service. These drinks are meant to be sipped, not downed. 

In terms of coffee, I recommend the Cuban. Condensed milk poured into fantastic espresso? Yes please.

The venue is full of warmly lit, open spaces perfect for studying or doing light office work. Visitors seem quietly productive and only occasionally chatty if you're looking for a proper place to work on the weekends that's not the library.

I've seen this particular venue crowded during the week, so I would recommend coming at an odd afternoon hour during a Saturday or Sunday. I'll definitely be back.

Was thrilled to go back to this place and take my family. The POKE bowl is to die for....super fresh super packed with deliciousness...and so good for you.The staff was so great.... 
Sauces are great
The Pad Thai was fantastic. I wish I had this place near me as it truly is a masterpiece.

Excellent good fresh real Mexican food prepared with awesome ingredients and great perfect portions. Why anyone would ever go to street taco and beer when this is just around the corner is crazy and dumbfounding.
At least the server said they weren't serving food but their late night menu says "midnight to close"

My wife and i went this morning for brunch out of the blue. We probably will not return there early on a sunday. 

She ordered coffee and a breakfast burger, her coffee was cold....no big deal, easy fix. The burger was described as having andouille sausage, fried mac and chees, over easy egg, chipotle marinara. As she was eating it she started pulling out chunks of chicken and mushrooms. She asked the waitress about is and she said "oh sorry i forgot to tell you the fried mac and cheese has chicken and mushrooms in it". I personally have never heard of fried mac and cheese having other ingredients. Her hating mushrooms, she was finished after that. Leaving 3/4 of the burger on the plate you would think it would be questioned, ah no, not there.

Maybe if there wasnt as much yelling and horseplay in the kitchen, they would have remembered that in the burger description.

It's my mother-in-law's favorite place and it was her birthday, which is what brought us here. After relaxing at the bar with happy hour drinks ($5 sangria, certain wine, margarita, and other stuff) and utilizing the yelp check-in for free chips n salsa (score!) we headed to our table.  All the in-laws ordered steaks, which looked delish.  I ordered the frisee salad and hamachi as my entree.  The frisee tasted a little off to me, but the hamachi was top notch. 

The restaurant is nestles atop a hill with lovely views of a golf course.  The setting is spectacular and definitely sets the tone for a lovely meal.

The gluten-free hot dog bun was surprisingly good, it looked like a shortened baguette. It may come from Tote bakery in the Italian market, not sure. If that's where they're from then I'm screwed in about an hour because their baguettes contain honey and chickpea flour which I'm not supposed to have.

I opted for an original hot dog combo with spicy mustard on the dog and malt aioli for dipping. The hot dogs are really substantial and meaty- I couldn't finish it. I'm not a huge hot dog person so the largeness of it was a bit of a turn-off. The fries were excellent, though, much like 5 Guys does.

My coworkers got a few hot dogs to try: Coney, Chicago, 9th Street, and the Smoker. Favorite was the Coney, the Chicago a runner-up (be warned that the peppers are pretty hot), and neither really cared for the Smoker hot dog. They said it was the sausage itself they didn't like, not the toppings so much.

The place was pretty full the whole time we were there, from around 12:15 to 1-ish on a sunny Friday. The line moves fast because they take your order while waiting in line, then you pay and by the time you're done there your hot dogs are ready. If you snag a table they'll bring it right over to you. We lucked out and got a table, but there are only a few.

Overall, though, $6.25 for an allergy-free solid lunch combo near Rittenhouse is nothing to complain about.

Miso happy!! Nothing like having a yummy ramen place to go when you get that craving! Ramen is always a good choice when you want something fresh, hot, filling and relatively fast. Haru has alot of good options on their menu for ramen, cold noodles, yakitori, don buri rice bowls, CURRY (my favorite) and they do offer a variety of vegan choices with miso broth! 
The inside is bright, open and clean with a super friendly staff. Check it out!

Decent food, horrible service.  Both the hostess and our server oozed negativity and never missed an opportunity to condescend us, whenever they actually came by the table that is.  Just skip this place.  Cydnee is an awful waitress

Yay, Sweet Tomatoes! You have finally gotten rid of the "Premium" toppings! We've been back twice since you came to your senses. Now if you could just be a little more consistent with your menu and actually have available everything that you advertise for that week, I will graduate you to a 5 star rating! Thanks!
Definitely my top 5 places to visit in Tampa bay. The rooftop, drinks and food makes the subset views WORTH All the while. This definitely a spot i bring ALL MY Tampa visitors to. M.bird never fails

Good God Almighty! I was really hoping the "Executioner" heat level was the perfect step up that I needed from the "Stop Drop and Roll". SDR heat was awesome but not quite got enough for me. I'm a chili head so rarely is anything hot enough for me so the average spicy lover would probably be content. 
Well I just tried the Executioner level whole wings and it's not a step up in heat; it's TEN friggin steps up.  I've never found anything that I couldn't eventually eat despite sweating, tearing up, and burning pain but after one bite I was all done!! I'm hoping that somebody just made an accident today and tripled the pepper power cause there ain't nobody that could eat that. For a point of comparison I would give the usual SDR level about a 7 and in today's case Executioner would be a 12. I could smell the pepper when I put my order in the car. Even if it wasn't inedible because of the heat level, the flavor sucked. Way overpowered by the pepper power to the point the chicken wasn't good. It was also over fried which is a common problem here. (I try to specify "light fry") But when they are on their game there is NO other hot chicken placethat can touch Big Shakes. 
I guess I got two wings that will be thrown away.  Thank goodness I at least got 2 SDR that I could eat. I would have bet $1000 there ain't nobody that could have eaten the wings I got today! I dont care how bad ass you think you are.  
BIG SEAN, you got to put a heat level b/t SDR and the E if this is truly how it's gonna be every time.

I have gone to P. F. Chang's before and it has been great, but I went Today (6/23/18) our waiter lied to us and told us that my food was done  and it was coming.  Then the next table got their food but not use. she told us that ours wasn't done. It was packed but some people in front of me got their food before me and the came 30 mins after me.  So much for a reservation... it didn't do any good. I have been at the restaurant for over an hour and all I have got is water, also my waiter was refilling my water and spilled quite a bit on the table then walked away. I had a reservation at 6:45 and I did not get in till about 7. My reservation was useless. The waiter I had checked on me about 2 times. I have been to this P.F. Chang's before and it was awesome but this time it was pretty sucky. I am seriously thinking about going to the food court at the mall just to get some food. People all a round use have not got their food and they are leaving. Are waiter has been avoiding me because I had asked where my food was. I also wish the their was a 0 star option. Never come here unless you have lots of time and when I says lots I mean a few hours. The food was ok but I was sooo hungry that I just ate it all. I hope the next time I go to a P. F. Chang's every thing is good.

This is a great place for a low-key lunch on a vacation. It was decently priced and had very unique flavors, along with other traditional items. The Smokey Bleu had awesome Worcestershire mayo (unexpected) and the meat was thinly sliced rare roast beef (loved!). Paid $2 more and got the Brussels; heavy basil, but good flavor. The rustic was made with white cheddar (so good!) and I added ham and tomatoes, which put it over the top delicious! The mac and cheese with bacon bits is legit. 

Best part ... they're honest people. We accidentally left our wallet. Huge relief to call and realize they had kept it safe until we returned!

Probably the worst value for dollars at a hotel I've ever had.  I've stayed in a wide variety of accommodations around the world, from huts and cabins to luxury hotels.  The price point of Tanque Verde was far in excess of the value offered, like at least double, if not more.  Staff was okay, but not "over the top."  Food was poor.  We arrived about 20 minutes before "closing" time for dinner (9P) and were told by front desk staff they would ensure we could still get dinner.  We got dinner - not hot or fresh at all.  It was buffet style and the dishes had not been heated for some time.  Selection was not good.  I will say the prime rib was pretty good, but nothing else was really worth eating.  All that for $75 for the two of us.  Breakfast the next day was better - pretty good omelette and price was decent.  

Room was okay - nothing special.  Poor job with making it feel welcoming or homey - lots of empty shelf space that seemed like an empty apartment or cabin.  The decorations were dated.  Carpet was like indoor/outdoor stuff.  Linens were worn - towel ripped when used.  

We were given the wrong type of room initially.  While they quickly corrected it, further delaying our effort to race to dinner, I had to go back to front desk to switch out keys and move my own stuff to another room - a place like this should come and bring you new key and offer to move your stuff.  

Checking out there was a line, which was not moving, so I just threw my key on desk and left, figuring I didn't need a receipt. 

Having said all this, the property and location is great.  Beautiful views.  However, I would recommend finding something better.  Not worth the cost.
This place has really improved since I last visited. Food & service were great. Mattie was amazing.

My wife, son and I are glad we made the effort to come here! We're from Memphis & were planning to visit Nashville's Parthenon on a Sunday, & used GoogleMaps to find restaurants open for lunch on a Sunday. Castrillo's was on my radar quickly, and their website showed a great menu at great prices, very close by. But the GoogleMaps "street view" at the address showed what looks like an empty lot, and around the corner a "K-Market" convenience store. We almost gave up, until a photo here at Yelp by "Jacob G." made me realize Castrillo's of Sylvan Park WAS the building K-Market used to be in! So we drove to Nashville yesterday and went straight in to Castrillo's Pizza before hitting the Parthenon..

Menu (and pricing) was as awesome as their website led us to believe, and the gentleman in there was as nice and friendly as you could hope for. Sure, it had a "hole in the wall" kind of atmosphere, but that only added to the charm of the place, honestly.  Main concern was that there's only two booths to sit in, and no other obvious seating, but I gather most of their business is take-out.  We ordered a pepperoni personal pizza for my son, a meat lover's personal pizza for my wife, and a spaghetti with meatballs (add mushrooms, please) for me, and some bottles of soda. I ran to the restroom (very nice and clean, by the way!) and as I came out I could see our man in the kitchen working hard on our food.

Not long after he brought our son's pizza, then soon after my wife's, then my spaghetti.  My wife and son had super-high marks for the pizza. LOVED it! I took a bite and was impressed; worth going back for just that! My spaghetti was good, too; I'm more of a meat sauce (bolognese) loving dude, but if you prefer marinara sauces that are veggie-filled and sweet then you'll enjoy it heartily!  The bread sticks I got with my pasta were great, too. My wife and son wanted to try the delicious-sounding Sweet Cinnamon Sticks, but we decided sticky fingers weren't a great idea when visiting the Parthenon, so we decided to try them next time. And there WILL be a next time...when we visit Nashville next, we'll go out of the way to this place. Well done.  As we finished & paid, the man there (bearded fellow...I never caught his name, but he was terrific) made friendly chatter with us and it was clear how familiar he was with Memphis as well as Nashville. Great time, great food.  Must eat there again.
Great In-N-Out! The line can get long, but it goes by pretty fast and the food is always super fresh. They do a good job organizing the drive-thru, and all of the employees had masks on.

I couldn't dare give them one star just because of the history and reverence I have for black-owned businesses that have been able withstand the test of time; but I have to say that I was truly appalled at the level of distasteful service my party received when coming here to dine.  

We had a very large party, 14, to be exact.  At 2 o'clock in the afternoon on a Friday, we tried to call ahead, but they weren't taking reservations; but we wanted to try anyway because the tour guide on the City Bus tour that we were taking told us President Obama ate here so we had to come too.

We expected an hour wait, and a tasty gumbo; both were true.  But what we didn't expect was the absolutely horrible attitude that we were greeted with by the hostess.  Turns out she was the Assistant Manager (it's a family business, and I'm not sure if she's a cousin or what), but she was terribly rude at our every effort to get seated.  

At one point during our wait, I approached her to get a menu to look at and pass around to my party get a head start on our order and she refused to give me a menu, stating that she didn't have enough to pass out because they were meant to be used for the guests who were being seated.  Mind you, I had asked for a single menu; not 14.  

Then when it came time to seat our party; she approached one of the men in our party to inform him that he wouldn't be permitted in the dining room because he was wearing a tank top.  Apparently they have a very strict dress code that is only advertised with two small signs (and not on their website).  She pointed at one when rudely refusing his stay (see picture).  

This would have been understandable if they closely followed this "code" with all diners; but they didn't.  It was a hot day and there were at least four females in our own party with short tops and shorts; but she didn't say anything to them.  Never mind others who walked in and got seated immediately because they were with a smaller party.

This has been my longest review to date, and with good reason.  An establishment is there to serve it's customers; not to make them feel like they don't belong.  If you have a large party, don't bother.  You can get better chicken and wayyyy be service at Neyow's instead (see my review on Neyow's).

My boyfriend and I had this when at the Geekfest near his house. At first, I knew that it looked super familiar, from seeing it online. I ordered the BÁNH MÌ THIT BÒ and my boyfriend got the VEGGIE PH. Let me just say that was the BEST banh mi sandwich I have ever had! Also, the pho was super delicious as well. 

The prices are super reasonable, and the food is to die for. I couldn't ask for anything better

To sum it up in one word, incredible. I ate here a few times these past 2 weeks and the food and service was spot on. The guy behind the cooking table is quick, friendly and knew exactly how spicy I liked my food. The sushi chef was amazing as well. The rolls were always fresh and he was always asking if there was anything special he could make. I really didn't eat the buffet stations offerings but I'm sure they are equally as delicious. 
 If I'm ever back up this way for work, I'll be sure to pass by and enjoy their incredible food and service.

If Jesus Christ were a restaurant, this would be the culinary incarnate of his holiness.

I really am going to try not to be blunt or biased but this place is everything I have ever cared about or love about a restaurant.

Firstly I have been here for a few occasions, lunch, dinner and a holiday buffet.   ALL of which are 5 stars and perfect.

Let me start with my lunch occasion.   I stopped here with my wife and had the calamari and a sirloin rubbed in Kona coffee.     The calamari were both flavorful and tender and amazingly specially delicious.   .  I mean coffee on a steak...what will they think of next and let me tell you this...that sauce...that creamy sauce.   OMG.

The dinner.   I stopped in with 3 of my best friends for a mans night out.   Everything was perfect.   Again, had the calamari which was downright beautiful.   Next was another perfectly cut/cooked rib eye medium rare and simply orgasmic.   We had the lobster mac and cheese and the corn which has bacon in it.   Everything here I ate with the guys was perfect the spot on and my friends could not rave more about it.

The buffet.   Stopped here on mothers day with my mom, and my mother in law.   It was again oral sex for the food mouth.   The buffet featured all of the breakfast goodies, eggs, bacon, sausage french toast.   However, the thing that took this up a level and only the capital can do this was the MADE to order (and included in the buffet price) a lobster eggs Benedict.  This was beautiful, large pieces of lobster on top of eggs...NEXT they had a raw bar with oysters and shrimp cocktail and stone crab legs...again this was ALL included.   If you get the chance, stop in and enjoy the buffet which also included tenderloin covered in Kona coffee .

Overall this was one of the top 5 places I enjoy a meal in the world.   I love the capital and this place pulls it off FLAWLESSLY.

Go here, thank me later!

PS - One thing I forgot of amazing importance.   Make sure you go to the bathroom here.   I am serious!   The bathroom is beautiful and make sure to wash your hands.   They have the nicest napkins to dry your hands ever.   Again this place even goes to that level of detail to have QUALITY napkins to dry your hands!  Again go here and enjoy the can too as it is even supremely better then elsewhere!

This experience (outside of the trouble I had with UberEats) was slightly better than others I've been having! They offered a nice BOGO on certain appetizers, and the pork gyoza did not disappoint. Had it arrived hot, I imagine it would have been much better but was cooked thoroughly and nice, crisp outside with a good dipping sauce. The shrimp tempura was unique from other places as the tail had been removed which was SO NICE to not have to try removing the tail from a roll with no knife. I usually struggle, but this time was easier. One piece did contain some tail which caused me to choke slightly, but got through and it was the only issue I had. The California roll was exactly as expected, nothing less and nothing more though everything tasted fresh. Was pretty happy with this experience, however a good egg roll would have been the perfect touch and I'm confident this place could do it after trying the gyoza. I'd recommend eating in over delivery, not too bad!

Michael & Michelle Le are the owners of this new business on Dryades. They personally greeted me when I walked in. Such a warm and inviting Café. The menu is pretty extensive and the seating is ample, with the ability to accommodate small, medium, and large groups. The location is great and there's lots of free on-street parking in the local neighborhood. 

I had the Vietnamese Coffee ($4.50) and the Shrimp bahn mi (Vietnamese Po Boy; $9). The Coffee was rich and quite strong. Part of the lure for this beverage is the brewing process, which completes at your table. It's basically an espresso with condensed milk over ice. A nice summer drink, which was perfect to support my study group plans after lunch. The shrimp bahn mi was totally unexpected for me - it was not at all like the typical New Orleans fried shrimp Po Boy. Instead, it was a healthier, lighter version, with sautéed shrimp, fresh coleslaw, jalapeños, and a house-made remoulade. Quite delicious and not too heavy. 

Both Michelle and Michael stopped by to check on me and whether my meal was to my liking. Great service! I'll be back for sure!

Yoshimoto i see you rolling homie, i stay pigging out on your Sushi definitely the best in the area not just the sushi nut the environment you offer is pretty unique and classy with touch of flames here and there to make it even more interesting. Will be back constantly thanks for the chow. Arigatō

This place is NIRVANA!!!!!!  Not a Kosher deli, but outta sight Jewish style deli.  The food is always fresh and plentiful, so much so that a take home container is pretty much a requirement.  Never had a stale piece of rye, or bagel.  Never had vegetables that were questionable. All if it looks fresh and appealing.  My wife and I went for breakfast on Easter Sunday, also around the time of Passover, and it was quite crowded. They accommodated us easily.  And the food was well worth the 30 minute drive.  I would love to rent a room there so I could be closer.  I think I can safely say that this is my most favorite restaurant this side of the the Atlantic Ocean.  The servers are just great (if you read my reviews, I am seriously into great service) and I can't say enough good things about them.  If I could eat 3 meals a day here, I would.
I tried the place once but its really worth the 5 stars. I really liked the shrimp po boy that I had for lunch and would be back to try more varieties. The staff is so nice as well.

Good dinner! The location is new and very tastefully executed. The attention to detail in the decor was nicely put together. The menu basics are solid and I'm sure the rest to come is still a work in progress but you can tell the staff cares about the product and bring a high standard. Great ingredients, great cocktails. My only drawbacks I can take away is that our cheese plate needed a protein or a fruit (cherry comes to mind). I would also work on dressing up the crustinis and add a honey or a sweet jam. The guava paste didn't really fit on the plate to me.  The only small detail I had to add about the beef patty melt was that there was twice as much bread as burger. The patty was juicy and simply amazing, the bread was perfect but the portion of bread didn't match the patty. The fries were good, I feel less fries and maybe a tiny bitter salad as well as opposed to an option (fries or salad) with arugula would have wowed me.

Don't get me wrong, the food was incredible. I would go back again tomorrow. 

Overall GREAT PLACE TO EAT. I'm just being critical to give feedback as it just opened. 

Well Done!

La Hacienda was delicious! My husband got three chicken enchiladas and I got a cheese quesadilla with the Texas margarita!  You can truly can judge a place on their margaritas and it did not disappoint!! LOL. The waitstaff was very courteous and prompt. They were busy but still handled it with grace including the minimal seating due to Covid restrictions. Would definitely recommend! Hidden gem!

This is a generous two star review, based on the food that tasted decent. Steak 'n Shake as a franchise has declined steadily in cleanliness, service, and promptness. This location is no exception.

I was in the drive thru for 15 minutes. This wait time is unacceptable. If a company cannot service a drive thru customer within 5 minutes, that's bad news. 

I stopped here because I specifically wanted Steak 'n Shake food, nothing more and nothing less. Sure, I got it, but it shouldn't have taken this long.

Words to the franchise - step up your game or let your business suffer.

UNCOOKED EGG WHITES!!!!!  Ordered eggs benedict, twice had to ask the eggs be cooked so the whites were not snotty.  I don't eat snotty egg whites because... well, it's disgusting... and because I am not Rocky and real humans can get salmonella.  30yo manager was huffy about how long he had been working in restaurants and seen eggs cooked that way.  Only when I told him I had been eating Bennies since before he was ALIVE were my eggs cooked correctly - a little overdone but at least the whites were not runny.  Husband's breakfast was OK but more than one person could eat.  Server was apologetic and very nice, but manager was nasty little brat.

La Ha is my favorite Mexican restaurant of all time! I've been going there since I was a kid and they've always had a friendly staff with great food. I love the ACP, fajita nachos, frozen margaritas, and of course their queso dip! Every time I come home this is my first stop. They consistently have tasty food. My husband jokes he almost proposed to me here because I love it so much! Definitely a must have!

Been going to El Minuto for over a decade. Moved out-of-state for a few years and finally landed in Phoenix. I would love an authentic place like El Minuto anywhere in the valley. Finally made it back home and stopped in to see Teresa and wasn't dissapointed.

For those who think El Minuto is "Amerimex for the masses" or not original enough, El Minuto has been cooking the same great stuff for generations, the same way. If this style of food has now been "Americanized," it's only because all other places have copied El Minuto's winning recipes, and they all try and taste like El Minuto. I have never left El Minuto unhappy, and I have never left it hungry!

Some of the commenters saying it's quite possible the best burger are only partially right IMO. I had the single cheeseburger, and while yes it was good - I wouldn't say it was the best ever. Could definitely tell it was fresh, not a frozen puck, but mine was smashed a little too thin (making it too large for the bun). The French fries were also good, but I would like to try the seasoned fries next time.

It's definitely a great meal and fairly inexpensive as well! I will definitely be back if I can get there during open hours!

Great food and coffee. I don't care for super bitter coffee found some international chains...so I always get the light roast. We have ordered breakfast and lunch  recently and both were delicious. Last week was the breakfast burrito, lunch was a fajita wrap. I've had the breakfast sandwiches, pancakes and omelets. All great! And the owner has made a great effort to meet the needs of her customers during this difficult time. Help out a small, local business and drive through for a treat!

Be prepared to get SPOILED at NOLA!! The chef is so attentive to detail...everyone works like 1 unit!!
The lady that manages the Brick-Oven always has a smile on her face! I'm here on business & stayed walking distance from NOLA...so of course I'm here 3 nights-in-A-row!! I want to try EVERYTHING on the menu. They do not disappoint

I had low expectations when I strolled in this place and left with a great experience to write about.  First off the waitress helped me get my baby stroller up the steps into the restaurant, very cool.  Then she watched my baby as I ran downstairs to use the ladies room, awesome.   I dont know if this place is great for kids but there were two babies in the restaurant in the afternoon and they seemed to like it!
 The menu is short and sweet with a few good vegetarian and vegan choices.  I got the chicken burrito and loved it.  It was piping hot, worderfully tasty and just the right size.  For a burrito it is a little pricy - $10! But I guess that is because the place is in Northern Liberties?
Great service, high prices, tasty food.
Giant delicious burgers. Service was slow, BUT it was a busy Saturday night and we weren't in a hurry.

I have tried Richboro Coffee several more times and happy to report that my first experience might not have correctly reflected this little shop. The price of the coffee ice-cubes is indeed listed on the board of prices. The board hands high and  is not very visible if you are right at the register and do not look up.
