Buttery rice, corn tortillas, a salad and condiments galore on the table rounded out the plate. If only I could figure out what was in that sauce...

My buddy had the Camarones Rellenos. Well, let me tell you these aren't your mom's rellenos. The same plump Mexican shrimp stuffed with cream cheese, wrapped in bacon and fried... ain't nothin' wrong with that. We did a shrimp swap and I gave him one of mine and he gave me one of his. If I were a shrimp, I don't think I could decide which was a better way to go.

Service kind of brought the whole thing down. We had to beg for our check and, even then, ended up having to go up to the counter and just pay there.

The food was good but service, the cash only format and the price point is enough to take this out of our lunch rotation.

Good Mexican
I believe that they are trying really hard to overcome the problems the chain experienced earlier. I found the food fresh, very tasty and rather large portions. The service at this location was fast and friendly. Very clean for a fast food place. The prices are reasonable, they have a large menu and the food is pretty good.

I come to Boise on business a few times a year.  I had read the reviews and decided to give The Modern a try.  True to form it is a redone motel.  The room was of decent size, and the bathroom is ultra new style.  I came here to work so the free wifi was a plus, but the "work space" area in the room is a countertop just deep enough to fit my laptop with an uncomfortable wood chair.  There are no refrigerators or coffee makers in the room.  I agree with most of the reviews on the bar: friendly service, good cocktails, and very good food for a bar.  My only real complaint is the NOISE.  The walls are paper thin (I could hear the person's cell phone vibrate in the next room).  The noise in the hallway echo, and there is a lot of road noise as well.  The bed was comfortable, but it wasn't a good night's sleep.  Hip factor: high, location: good, bar: big plus, value: you get what you pay for.  I might stay again but only for 1 night.

They have the most amazing Veggie Stromboli! I add onions. If you order one, here's a tip: When you get it home, flip that bad baby upside-down onto a few paper towels to let some of the juice drain out before cutting into it and it'll be perfect.

Mashed potatoes and green beans on the side was super flavorful. The pecan pie is a must. The good was good but not overly special. The sweet tea was very sweet! It was a great place to stop in at. The lunch lady style of it kept the line moving so quickly I didn't even have time to look at the menu behind the servers. Very respectful service.
$5 Build Your Own Bloody Mary Bar... Need I say more? Only wish it were available all week not just Sunday!
Last night was my 3rd time here, and my last. On all 3 occasions my Pizza came out cold. I cant understand it, was not busy. They must be premade because at 550 degrees wow can it go cold so quick ?
Love this place. Very good food. Never had anything that wasn't good. They get very busy so you may want to call ahead. Highly recommend.

This place is awesome! They have great food and a pretty nice variety of craft beers. My boyfriend and I love trying out new places especially ones with 1000 points on open table. We have been here for dinner several times and it has yet to disappoint. I'd recommend this to anyone looking for a relaxing night out at a reasonable price. The only reason I gave it 4 stars was due to the parking. It's an unpaved parking lot and when it rains it gets very muddy.

I liked this place. When we got there, it was pretty empty so we were able to sit at the table outside.  There were plenty of options on the menu to choose from at decent price points. We started with the white bean hummus which was really tasty. It came with veggis and toasted bread which was great.  I ordered the Risotto which was really delicious.  It was cooked really well and very tasty.  My husband ordered the meatball pizza and it was very tasty as well. It was a thin crust pizza so it wasn't too filling. The only negative was that the food did come out really slow. We were the only people there for the majority of our meal so I wasn't really sure what happened. Our server was really friendly though so no complaints there. I'd definitely come back to try something else, but hopefully the timing gets worked out.

We had a lovely brunch at Yolk. When we arrived we were told it would be a 50 minute wait, but it was actually 15. We're glad we stayed! The waiting area is really cramped and small...especially considering the large number of people waiting to get in. 

We ordered an omelet and breakfast wrap (both yummy) and I had a tea, which was fabulous. I point that out because if you're a tea lover you'll appreciate how rich and flavorful the tea is...and it came with a dollop of honey - perfection. 

I really enjoyed the layout of the space. The breakfast bar is great for a super casual breakfast, but the booths (which we had) were sectioned off in a way that made our experience feel more private. 

The menu had a great selection of specialty items, including French toast deliciousness that I'll have to get next time.  Overall I was really pleased with our selection. I had heard so much about this place and it was worth the wait! 

My only critique is that our bill for two was 40 bucks before a tip. So paying nearly $50 for breakfast is waaaay more than we would normally pay, but when you consider that most add-ins are $1 each the bill creeps up quickly.
Masons was a last minute decision for carry out and turned out to be one of the best decisions we made while in Nashville. Ordered for 8 and everyone was satisfied.  Meatloaf is especially good.

This Bonchon location is great because it right in the heart of Chinatown, however the quality of the wings varies. When I first came to this location the wings were big and juicy. However on my second visit on a busy Friday night the wings were too salty and dry.

This is a wonderful Italian grocery store in the heart of the Hill. Its located on Marconi just south of St Ambrose Church. 

I just came to browse before going to happy hour at Steve's hot dogs on Friday. I ended up purchasing some pastas, sauce, and meatballs for dinner(I can report that they were all delicious. We ate them last night). 

There is a great selection of frozen raviolis and tortellini in all sorts of flavors from cheese, beef, mushroom and spinach, lobster, and much more. 

There is also a full deli with meats and cheeses as well as a decent alcohol selection. 

The people seemed friendly. 

This place has a similar selection as Vivianos down on Shaw.  I like them both. The prices are higher than you will find at a big box grocery but there are some things here you won't find beyond the Hill. 

Its worth checking out.  The Hill is a great place to spend a few hour walking the streets and stopping in the different stores and restaurants.

Everything that I've tried here is good, I love that they have salsa bar with description in every salsa and aguas frescas  the best...
My suggestion is... they should have super quesadillas with corn tortillas as the normal quesadillas, I was sad about it and I hope they will have soon.

I'm not a complainer but this food must be inconsistent because some people say it's good and some say it's bad. My steak was okay. My calamari had absolutely no flavor. The mashed potatoes were an odd texture, they weren't smooth. My mom and grandpa ordered the salmon and it was dry and had an odd taste. My steak was more soft than the salmon. 
Our waitress was very kind but the manager was kind of rude and aggressive when asking what was wrong with the salmon & doesn't really seem like a people person or someone with good customer service. WE WILL NEVER COME BACK BUT THE WAITRESS WAS NICE; AND THE MANAGER SUCKS.

Average coffee and unwelcoming environment. Seating wasn't too big and was taken by young college kids studying. I prefer more hang out friendly coffee shop with a vibe and welcoming atmosphere. It's just coffee, no need to be so serious.

We were referred to this restaurant by Leo at Ponchartrain Landing RV Park. It's not really all that close to the RV park, but it was worth the drive. The food was awesome and very generous portions. I had the Red Beans and Rice with Sausage and my husband had Catfish and Shrimp. Both were very good. They were a little stingy with the sauces, but would probably have given more if we'd asked. There is apparently an issue with getting towed if you park next door at the cleaners (they have a recording playing outside and sign inside warning customers about it). We parked a few doors down on a side street and walked over.  A lot of locals come in and get take out which is usually a good sign. This place was really hopping for a Monday night. There was a line, but didn't take all that long to get our food.

Delicious. Great food, good portions, fair prices, cool decor and music, large wine list and really friendly service. We got a bunch of appetizers. Cured meats were great, fries were really good and I also got some dish that had baby octopus/pasta/sausage. It was really good. For my meal I ordered the Hanger Steak. absolutely amazing. The price was really good to considering the quality and portion size. The dessert was cool, menu created by the owner/chefs son. I had peanut butter parfait. The salted caramel was good but a little rich but again, really good and great price for the portion size and quality. Definitely worth checking out. (get the Hanger Steak. I got mine medium rare and it was delicious. I can't wait to go back)

Sushi and Sashimi for 2, as good as it gets! We have been to MANY sushi restaurants, and this is the best one yet as far as taste, cleanliness and service go! The Sashimi is served on a bed of ice which makes a big difference in taste. This is our 2 year old son's favorite place (loves the vegetarian fried dumpling appetizer). We ordered the same menu items the first time, loved them so much that we order the same time and time again. Green tea is great with your meal too!

I enjoyed it here! Cute little place in media. Was nice and casual to have Sunday brunch. Not sure how great it would be for bigger groups because it seems to be more for smaller groups of people. I had the al Monty which was good! The grilled cheese we also had was so so. Many other options I'd love to try. It's BYOB which is a nice plus.

FINALLY! A nice restaurant in Nashville that actually enforces a dress code. I came here last week in a nice suit but had a flat cap on. I was pleasantly surprised when the host asked me to remove it and informed me about their dress code. My biggest complaint about Nashville restaurants is that even the "nicest" of places, most people will be in flip flops, cut off shorts, "wife beaters". (maybe the other M Street restaurants will take a step in this direction)

The over all atmosphere/decor is absolutely amazing and well suited with the staff being very friendly and knowledgeable while providing great customer service.

I had a couple of cocktails that I would rate 5 stars, both on price and overall quality.

For a starter, we had the Edamame which was really not good at all and give a 2/5. I'm not sure if it was cooked incorrectly, but it was extremely hard/woody. The seasoning/flavor was fantastic though.

We sampled numerous rolls and sashimi and they were all very fantastic and would rate the taste a 4/5.

As far as price, I'd also rate that a 4/5.

If you like Sushi, you probably won't be disappointed.

"Dreadful!" is the word I would best use to describe the "Tennessee Cuban" served at the Whiskey Kitchen located in the Gulch. At first, I was quite curious to try said sandwich as I somewhat consider myself a "Tennessee Cuban." However, this probably rates the worst out of all the Cuban sandwiches I have written about thus far. As you may see from my picture, the ham used here was cut twice as thick as you would expect to receive at a Thanksgiving dinner making it a chore to chew. The "TN Beer Mustard" (which is simply a marketing term for "stone ground mustard") was served in a container on the side. Using my butter knife, I applied a generous portion of the mustard to the lightly toasted underside of the non-pressed bread. (No one can ever seem to get the bread right!) Lastly, the sandwich was messy. The juice from the pork dripped all over my plate and hands. Good thing I asked for extra napkins! At $14.50, avoid ordering the "Tennessee Cuban" at this tourist trap! As a "Tennessee Cuban," I'd like to think of myself as much more enjoyable than this loafy sandwich!
Very good barbecue, if not slightly overhyped. Not the best I've ever had, but certainly near the top.

Great place for lunch. Generous portions and freshly made to order.

Worth the price!

Although I've been to TJ's on multiple occasions.. this visit was not as pleasant as the rest. Brought my parents here and we sat in one of the comfy booths by the bar. If you want a waitress who lacks personal skills and couldn't produce a smile if she tried, then this is the place for you. It's unfortunate too because the quality of food is great. TJ's I highly suggest you reconsider who you hire because I won't be running back!

Service took a long time, but the waitress was really nice.  Ordered their cod fish burger and got a massive stomach ache after that. 
Looks like a nice place to go to if you want to eat by yourself, read a good book, and sip on a glass of wine.

Interior and atmosphere was beautiful! Hardly anyone there at 6pm on a Thursday and it felt like we had almost the whole place to ourselves. The food came out really quickly, within 5 minutes, which was reminiscent of Han Dynasty. Pricing is definitely better than that of Han, but food equally as good. Not the most outstanding food I've ever had, but solidly comforting. Service was amazing!
after they changed their menu, i am not a fan. bland food, no more mango tea, too many unwelcomed changes for me.

Food, beer, ambience...all three in a great package.  If you have never been to Belgian place, this is an excellent introduction and example.  Pick any one of the mussel pots and of course copious amounts of pommes frites.  That combo is some of the best stuff you'll ever had, but be sure leave room for sausages or hearty sandwiches in addition to an excellent beer selection.  If you want to extend your palette further, be sure to try a Monk's Flemish-style Sour Ale, though the depths of dubbels, tripels, strong ales, kolsches, and lambics will be sure to please any palette.  My buddies took me to this place in a large group and had an amazing time; I intend to go back whenever I get back to Philly.

Very clean buffet & friendly staff.. 
amazing sushi bar. Dessert section is kinda bad but they have fresh fruit so it makes up for it.

Super fresh lettuce and veggies with a variety of salad types to choose from. You can substitute the recommended salad dressing easily.  We would easily and happily pay a couple dollars more per salad since they are fairly large and so fresh. The strawberry lemonade is very tasty and not too sweet. We'll be back for sure!

I met the owner at a car dealership and he told me to come check his New restaurant out . So for date night took my wife I was very impressed. The staff was attentive and Extremely Nice and the owner checks on you throughout the night to make sure you're enjoying your experience. Food was awesome 7 course meal for a reasonable price.  Just one pointer before you go "Bring a huge appetite" and definitely get the lamb, we left stuffed and sleepy. I highly recommend the Restaurant

I came on a Friday noon and they were offering a brunch menu. Hands down, the chicken and biscuit was the best I've ever had. Cool decor and nice outdoor patio area. Staff were courteous and attentive. The cocktails were super tasty. I look forward to coming here again the next time I'm in town.
Absolutely delicious food. Prompt service. Delicious soups and delicious spring rolls. I definitely recommend this place!

Currently in Tucson for training. Came across this restaurant and I have to say it was an amazing experience! Started off with the order to Chips and guacamole. Then followed with the catch of the day (highly recommended!). The service and atmosphere was the cherry on top.

Cool coffee place.. not just coffee but he have breakfast and lunch .. smoothies atc ... 
inside feels relaxed .. I had chocolate smoothie and pretty good :) ... Owner actually work and not just some guy hidden in office. 
I like it here! Good job

First of all, I love the ambience.. It really is a cool looking restaurant.. If you are looking for something other than traditional Cajun/Creole food then you will love this place. I really wanted to taste the Cajun taste so I was somewhat disappointed after seeing the great reviews I expected to be wowed. They have small portions unlike the other New Orleans restaurants. The menu changes daily apparently .. I thought that was cool.

Shrimp & Grits- Okay not spicy how I wanted it. && the grits had corn kernels in it. Very different .. I haven't decided of that's a good addition or not.

White Sangria- drink of the day. NOT GOOD !! 

Cajun Poutine- Very good. A unique appetizer that was really tasty!!! 

My friend had the Crawfish pasta && it was not good. She ended up leaving it there. Disappointing. The bread && butter was tasty. 

As an entree I had the Lamb burger.. It was fantastic. Juicy, flavorful, and delicious. I highly recommend it.

Great food and service. Had the bone in Rib-eye and it was cooked perfect. Wife loved her salmon and the granddaughter loved her Wagyu hamburger. Clam chowder was great and the salt pepper wings were a great starter. Plus they have Innis and Gunn beer to top it off 
Perfect value. Lovely atmosphere with friendly staff. 
Will most definitely be back!
Very, very average with regard to the regular a la carte menu. No texture to the rolls and everything felt hastily made. Much better sushi elsewhere in Nashville, I'm afraid.

I can't help but like any restaurant where the chef owner visits the table to ask how I liked my food and seems to actually care about what I have to say.

The food here was fantastic. Service was a little odd but I think we came in just before closing and the wait staff may have already taken off for the night, leaving part of the kitchen staff to tend to us. 

The whole staff sounded like they have a good time with what they do and it shows through in the food. 

I never would think to order wings in a NOLA themed restaurant but these were wonderful and completely unique. 

Shrimp and grits were phenomenal. 

Beigniets were good but not what I'm used to; someone from New Orleans might hold these to a higher standard. 

I'll definitely be back.

We waited 2 hrs for a table for 2 on a Friday night. Ended up at bar. Ordered drinks, lemon drop martini was awful. Bartenders subpar. Food was not great...meat in the tacos tasted weird. I'll stick with El Maguey.

We had a wonderful experience here! The food was good, portion size just right, and the human connection on point. We love to visit small, neighborhood spots where the food is good, and ambiance is just as good. Our server, Sara, was so real, so friendly, and thorough with our order. We will definitely be back!

Im a sucker for BYOB.  Isabel was a google search Mexican find.  The restaurant was plain and oddly shaped but had some charm.  The service was slow at first but swiftly picked up.  The restaurant was crowded and everyone seemed to be enjoying the fare.  I had a pollo enchilanda and it was great seasoned well.  Overall a 4 star place.

One of the best poboy I've ever had was from here and the service was good as well. Ordered a combo shrimp, crawfish and oysters poboy and they use these crunchy but soft in the inside leidenheimer bread. Mmmmm.

This is by far my favorite resteraunt in Philadelphia! Our dining experience from start to finish was superb! Be sure to try one of the side plates, the polenta. The setting is much like an urban farmhouse. My oregano fettuccini was exquisite. The farm fresh flavors just seemed to burst in my mouth like the fireworks on the Fourth of July

Wasn't really my favorite Ramon spot. The place looks nice and gives you an authentic vibe that your in Japan. But over all the service was slow and the udon broth in the noodles where too salty. I wouldn't come back here any time soon but I hope they add more to their menu because it was very short.

My personal taste in hot chicken leads me to frequently tell visiting friends that Hattie B's is my favorite.  They truly have a wide range of hotness options and their chicken is always of the highest quality.  I can get mild - medium and get some heat while actually having some flavor.  Unfortunately several other hot chicken places focus on burning your taste buds off and not much on flavor.  Hattie B's has a great mix of both.  You also get very hefty portions which makes it a good value.  Their side items are also excellent.  The line at this location gets very long on a frequent basis but you can now order to go online which is helpful for a local like myself.  There's another location off Charlotte which is also great and may have a shorter line.  This is definitely a must visit if you are experiencing Nashville for the first time!
Very good neighborhood taproom and restaurant.  Great selection of beers, and a well-varied menu.  The kitchen is slow, so plan time accordingly

If someone asks you to drink a bottle of red wine at 4pm on a Wednesday in 85 degree heat, you say yes.  You say yes, and you drink that wine.  And while you're at it, why don't you get off your high horse and some eat some Italian meats and cheeses?  If I could live at this restaurant, I would.  It has everything I need.  More wine than you shake a corkscrew at, expertly aged dairy products, thinly sliced layers of exotic, cured meats. 

The bar is a giant slab of marble.  Cool to the touch, expansive and welcoming.  Two friends and I chose to sit here and were greeted by our friendly and enthusiastic bartender, Sarah.  I have not met a person more knowledgeable or passionate about wine in my life.  It was a delight to be served by her.  After much scrutiny and many, many samples, we selected a bottle of red to split while we munched on our cheese and charcuterie.  My dining experience ended there so I can't speak much about the entrees.  I will say that as a tourist in St. Petersburg, I was thrilled to stumble upon such a great restaurant.  I hope to be back soon!
The best place to eat seafood. The employees in this restaurante are very sociable. The food wow very delicious this why I give them 5 stars.

After reading all the reviews I was anxious to try this place.  Just walking through the door made us all ready for a great dining experience because of the great aromas, beautiful food being delivered to the tables and the unique use of the old diner.  Unfortunately immediately we were met with a group sitting next to our table that was so noisy that four of us couldn't even speak to each other across our table.  We asked for our seats to be moved but it was a very busy in-season Friday night so we couldn't change our place.  That's ok because maybe the food would be worth it.  I ordered the grouper with shrimp and there wasn't one shrimp to be found on my plate.  Oops, said the waiter, I guess the chef forgot to put them on - they adjusted the bill. (This is their most popular item on the menu so you would think he would remember!) My husband's seafood trio was mediocre at best.  My friend's mashed potatoes were cold and his mahi was overcooked and his wife got her salad when we all got our entrees.  All in all a very disappointing experience considering the rave reviews.  I would consider trying it again when it's not in season and it's not so crowded but for the price I'm not sure I want to take the chance!

Holy cow, what a find.

Went there for a quick lunch. The place is beautiful inside, terrific lowkey, bistro atmosphere. 

Got the Honey Almond Chicken for lunch. Simply superb food. Great service and price.

Seriously, this place is a must visit and a total hidden gem. Would've never expected it.
Honestly, you can't mix up your pancakes at home for about $5, including real maple syrup and fruit?  Again, another Princeton hype that is not worth it.

Amazing food and service. Fish and chips was a large portion. The crab cakes where made to perfection. Blackened cod tacos where so good. Coleslaw was not over marinated. The drinks where delicious. Service was impeccable. We Will go back. Atmosphere is wonderful for the whole family we had family from eight to forty.

This place was FABULOUS! We were first time diners last night and from beginning to end, everything was wonderful. Our waitress, the ambience and the food were some of the best we've had in a while. For COVID protocols, they do require masks and we felt completely safe. My husband and I shared the ahi sushi roll, the steak frites and the lobster Mac and cheese - which you have to get! We are still talking about the Mac and cheese today and it will likely turn into my new craving as it was the best restaurant lobster Mac and cheese we've ever had 

Overall, we highly recommend the Hangar and as locals we are thrilled that something this great has moved into the plaza. We hope they have great success!

Wow this place is amazing and I regret not trying it earlier! If you're looking for a quick, cheap and satisfying lunch, this truck is your answer.  I've only been here once and got the chicken bowl, which was really great but what I really liked in the bowl was the purple/pink cabbage stuff! It was really surprisingly refreshing! Basmati rice was BOMB! Never had a rice that smelled so good, and I eat a lot of rice (perhaps because I'm Asian or maybe I just love rice).  Service was really fast and the workers were nice. I will definitely be back for more when I'm nearby.

Great place to eat breakfast on a Sunday morning in SB, and easy to find.  About a 15 minute wait, but they have self serve coffee out front.  We ended up getting seated way in the back by the bathroom, at that point we might as well have been at IHOP.  It was so loud inside.  If its a beautiful day, I would recommend waiting for an outside spot, because without the beach view, the price premium is not worth it.  I overheard a local say that there are much better places to eat in SB, but they tolerate Sambo's when their friends visit.  The coffee was good, and I had the California Benedict.  It really was delicious, with fresh hollandaise.  It was pricey, about $13, but something I have not seen anywhere else, I would go back for it.  My wife was disappointed with her French Toast, and the syrup was watered down.  Home potatoes with the green onion was nice.  Service was prompt once we sat down, and the mini muffin appetizer was a great way to keep us happy while waiting for the food.  The water had a horrible aftertaste.

I've always loved this location, and went a lot when it was Loves. The patio and outdoor area is still amazing, and great to hang out on a nice day. The outdoor bar was up and running, and they added a nice stage for live music. The food was pretty basic bar fare. We had the nachos, shrimp appetizer, wings, and the sloppy burger. All the food was equally good. The nachos were layered so that the chili and cheese was even throughout the whole dish which I definitely appreciated. The cheese sauce was just nacho cheese sauce, and I'd love for them to upgrade to a good queso. The wings were all drums, so if you're a drum person you'll be excited, and they were delicious. The shrimp was almost exactly like the bang bang shrimp at bonefish and was really good and nice sized shrimp. My husband slammed his burger before I could try it, so I take it he enjoyed it as well. The menu was pretty basic, but  everything we had was good so I foresee us spending future Saturdays hanging out on that beautiful patio!
Hidden gem! Food is affordable and seasoned! We loved every bite and even had some to take home for dinner.

Great local place.  Garlic knots were excellent, a subtle garlic flavor but not harsh like some I have had.  Very good.

Our group had a couple of pizza's and a sandwich.  All very tasty.  We will definitely come back if we are in the area.

Let's go to El Charro! We said as we entered Sahuarita. Alas, it's no longer there. But this new place, 3 months now, is there and it's actually owned by the El Charro family and  is their first foray into non-Mexican food.

I found the food quite tasty...I tried the grilled cheese with tomato and avocado. It was accompanied by a tasty bowl of chowder with apple bits.The sandwich was done perfectly but the soup could have been a bit hotter in temperature.

We sat outside with my pup, dogs are welcome,  and it was very pleasant. Pretty fair number of people eating there.

My only complaint deals with the service: I think they have a lot of rookies who have yet to learn the ropes. They were friendly just not attentive. We had to ask for our  utensils and napkins. We waited a while to get our drinks. We had to take our bill inside in order to pay. I wondered if they were also short-handed.

All in all, it was a pleasant  enough experience on this weekday afternoon. Just hope they can get the service up to snuff and it would be  very fine.

One of the best steak houses in the country.  I have been to almost all of the expensive steak houses in the US from Seattle, WA to Miami, FL and Boston, MA to San Diego, CA.  My job required me to visit clients in almost every state in the US and wine and dine them.  Dempsey's Steakhouse is one of the best.  The table side Caesar salad is prepared in front of you which is a lot of fun.  The steaks are always cooked perfect and the creamed spinach is fantastic.

Awesome concept, everyone who works there is really nice.  I keep meaning to go there to do some major record shopping.  Decent food, amazing coffee.  I see they have a lunch menu that will be in effect soon, can't wait!

2014 UPDATE:  Just FYI - they have the BEST iced coffee I've ever had.  So smooth.. need one right now!
Skip them and walk another block North , The Gyro Shack is soo much better and I gave them 2 chances.

The food was delicious. Full of rich flavor. I had their version of the mushroom Swiss burger with pepper jack cheese instead. I also ordered a side of the crawfish cornbread dressing. 

It would have been a full five stars, but the wait to get seated lasted too long. There were periods of time where empty tables lingered with patrons waiting to be seated. The staff was also very nice and welcoming.

Yummy rye ipa.....good enough to assuage the inner demons wishing to slay those responsible for what passes as an airport in philla-hell-phia..not the lovely city...or its well behaved and classy sports fans !

I'll begin this review by saying that I've been visiting this place for the last couple of years, and up until 6 months ago, I would have given this place a 5 star rating without a second thought. But not any more.

I remember the first Burrito that I had here: Fresh, filled with guacamole, sour cream, flavorful and filling. Then about a few months ago, they raised the prices. "Fair enough, inflation hits everyone", I thought. But I wasn't prepared for the drop in quality. The burritos now are usually dry, too salty, overstuffed with beans more than anything else. The guacamole is still in the burritos, but in token proportions, while the sour cream seems to be on a permanent vacation from this place!

Just today, my girlfriend ordered a burrito from this place. She specifically asked them to go easy on the beans and for extra sour cream. She got a burrito chock full of beans and with no noticeable sour cream. She took apart the burrito and sure enough, there's no sour cream anywhere in the burrito.

To sum it up, a burrito from this place is dry, salty rice, cheese, lots of beans, a token amount of guacamole, with hit or miss meat (misses more often than not).

If you're looking for a place that USED to be great, then this is the place you're looking for. As for me, I'll be walking the four or so more blocks to the Qdoba when I fancy a burrito from now on. At least they don't skimp on the guacamole and sour cream even if you do have to pay extra (and hey, even with the extras, it's cheaper than this place, with their $9.75 steak burritos!)

Great place to play poker but sux for food. Parx poker menu might be the worst food I've ever eaten at a casino. I mean seriously how do you screw up a chicken noodle soup??? I seriously think the horses are being fed way better than the customers.

Layla is an amazing go- to place in the Grove. Their burgers are delicious and their hummus is unique and unmatched. I love that I can rely on this place when it comes to taking out of town guests to dinner. Their brunch is also amazing. I would highly recommend Layla to anyone! The service is sometimes lacking, but the food is worth the wait!

I've actually been here a few times, but have forgotten to check in.  I hate it when I do that!  Anyway, i have only been for breakfast and its a great place!  i'm an early riser, and Stanley opens at 8am.  I love the walk in The Quarter that early in the morning.  Everything is quiet and peaceful and its not hotter than Hades yet.  The servers there are super friendly and the food is so freaking good.  Its a charming little place in a great location.  You have to give it a try.  It will become one of your favourite places, for sure.  Dont forget to grab a bloody mary to go, you'll regret it if you dont!

Why on this green earth is this actually advertised the same as 'Oceana' with the same logo and dinner menu layout. I get if it's the same owner but stop making me feel I'm eating at the same restaurant twice. Several people got out of line because they associated it with eating at the same restaurant as the night before. REBRAND for goodness sakes!!

So first of all, just wanted to set expectations for the Viet crowd or grew up on eating authentic Viet food reading this review; that this is VERY different in my opinion to the Viet food I've eaten. I would say it's Viet styled/inspired while infused with American breakfast and flavors. The food was good don't get me wrong - but a bit pricey for what it is. 

I ordered, the TBD Breakfast Rice Bowl, spicy popcorn chicken, fried pork belly bites, Ryan's fried chicken sandwich, and Viet iced coffee. The best item was definitely the rice bowl. The sandwich was a bit dry and the spicy popcorn chicken and fried pork belly bites just looked so simple and plain and honestly seemed like it was just small leftover pieces that they turned into a side order for the price. The coffee, was the worst. It tasted like burnt coffee and water-nothing like what Viet coffee should taste like.
Delicious food. Prompt service. Had toys for my toddler, family friendly. The apple fritters were very good. Coffee was very good per my husband.

Usually this is one of my favorite places to eat at home, but the newly scaled down menu was a bit meh. I think my visits to cheesecake bistro are coming to an end as I wasn't really impressed with the offerings and our lunch was lukewarm at best, and there were a total of 8 people dining while we were there. The service was good, but I can't say much else was.

Angry old man speaks. 

I think this restaurant is the most mediocre over priced food in South Jersey. But my beloved wife and apparently the rest of South Jersey love it. 

Tonight the GM should be fired. The place is a shit show because apparently there was a banquet he couldn't handle. 

My waiter was awesome but embarrassed by the wretched service. He was awesome. A+. 

Don't rest on your laurels G. I could see you tanking badly with this food quality and service.

My first impression was "man they keep this place clean!"  The dining area was super inviting with items for sale along the walls.  They have little information flip cards for different foods and whayntheir benefits are.

The staff was really attentive, patient, and friendly.  They gave us a few of their samples of protein blends and allowed us to take our pick from the menu.

I ordered the cold coffee with coconut oil boot (XCT or something like that, I don't recall the exact name.)  I really enjoyed the coffee.  It had a smooth, bold flavor.

I also had the avocado wrap.  It was pretty good, but I was hoping for a little more flavor or seasoning.  I still give it 4/5 but for me it was lacking something maybe like a salsa or hot peppers-I do not know if they offer hot peppers but will definitely ask next time.

I will venture back and try a new item and see if there is something else on the menu that bumps it up to 5 stars for me.
Not my typical spot as I like meat for dinner however, very good and  will be back fir sure

Okay. I'm going to put this simply: Capital Tacos could and would thrive in Austin, TX. Just the fact that these two locations aren't lines out the door all the time sort of baffles me. What food is today, and well worth a little drive North from the Tampa bubble. Great food, fun vibe, and a good value for  inventive quality food.

At this point we've had the Besa Besa shrimp, a well executed bang bang shrimp, the Seared blackened and sesame tuna dinner which provided a tuna steak prepared two different ways with buttered veggies and fluffy yellow rice. We've gotten lost in the wine options, and downed some 7-layer chocolate cake with a side of cool creamy milk to pour over it. We've had the cedar plank salmon with wild mushroom mashed taters that blew my socks off, and an acceptable key lime pie. The poblano relleno burned itself into my face, and my heart. The guac sampler is always a table favorite. The service has never left us wanting, so I have to give it the all too elusive five stars! Don't forget the drinks, always something new and tasty to try with a complimentary layout and decor!

Went for brunch and had the steak and eggs. The steak and eggs were cooked right on and the hashbrown casserole had a fantastic kick. Coffee was good too. Our server was attentive and nice. The only downside is no bloody mary's or mimosa's (no liquor) but hopefully that'll change at some point. I'll be back.

I cannot rave about this place enough. I had my first Japanese whiskey and it transformed me from a total Tennessee whiskey gal. The chicken wings were to die for. Everything we tried was superb. My new favorite spot in town!

Love to eat in or order out.  My top two choices are the boss has gone mad pizza, and the vegetarian calzone. The yam fries are pretty great for a side and the bar serves really good chasers. The boss has gone mad pizza is made with spaghetti on it!! Seriously you need to try it is downright amazing and will change your life! Servers here are super friendly couldn't ask for a better run pizza/pasta place :)

Never again this place needs to close the sandwiches were horrible the Bobbie which we like was so bad the roast beef was so dry it was like it was there for days and ham was bad I spend 28.00 fir crap never again to bad it use to be a nice place if it has knew owner they better wake up the good and service was horrible
The most immature and rude staff. Only let's you in "if they know you" and then makes up lies saying they cops won't let anyone else in. GO NEXT DOOR TO LOSERS!!! Not trashy either and fun people

This is by far my favorite place on grand!! I have been here twice this week and only have positive things to say. The decor makes you feel like you're on vacation. The staff is friendly and is always welcoming. The food.. I could eat the whipped feta on the lox and bagel every day. I have never had something I did not like.

We came in last Friday and opted for the beloved Chef's Tasting, as we were able to sample all the Chef's best dishes.  Think of it as a 'Greatest hits' for the Vicia kitchen.  My wife has a pork allergy, but they had no issues accommodating to this.

My favorite dishes in this five course bonanza?  By and far, the braised lamb shoulder.  The fresh seared scallop was a hit as well.  The beet salad was different, but still had great flavor and texture.  There were so many other tapas-style dishes that were 

We also opted for the highly-recommended wine tasting that pairs quite well with the entire experience.  I loved how the sommelier walked us through for each wine for each course, as well as the region and house in which the wine originated.  With that being said, my wife wasn't a fan of some of the dry red varietals offered.  I didn't mind, as they complemented perfectly with what we had that night...

We also had our 7yo son with us, but thankfully, he is not a picky eater.  We opted for the fried chicken thigh, pita bread, and goat cheese spread for an appetizer; mushroom risotto for his entree.

The dessert was a mousse ice cream that was delightful; we accompanied this with the sorbet selection.  Quite delectable.

I would not have thought that we would have enjoyed that experience, considering that it was a bit off the beaten path as far as what we usually do.  The fact that this establishment won some James Beard Foundation accolades doesn't hurt either.

Last night, my friend and I turned around for a minute to close our tabs and our jackets were gone. We asked the bartenders if they knew anything about it and one of them pretty much immediately talked to one of the other customers like this was a regular occurrence. He more or less confessed and she offered him six packs for their return but seemed to not be surprised nor really care. I won't be going back. Keep a super close eye on your stuff there
Great food. Wish they were open for weekday lunch. Highly recommend the Mie.  Duck confit was fantastic. Chicken wings were decent if a bit messy; nothing wrong with that.
It's quite expensive compared to Terakawa. I think they have really good ramen and I'm absolutely coming back.
Yum! Great wings and great burgers. The Italian burger was substantial and a great mix of sausage, and the sauce used was slightly sweet, blending perfectly with the spices in the meat.

My first thought of this place was, "so this is where the attractive people gather!" honestly I felt like I was back in Richmond Virginia when I was here. It was a collection hipsters but it was awesome! The shops they have range from cocktail bar - Ramen - butcher. This place is right next to the river too so going from a scenic walk with a drink is totally doable!

When this place first opened, my family went there to give it a try since it replaced Fuddruckers...a place we often visited. The food was horrible and service just as bad. I decided to give it another shot with some friends and head to the bar. The bartender was pretty attentive and drinks were good. Love the selection of beers. My boyfriend ordered the alligator bites although I warned him the food wasn't good. Soooooo glad he ordered them because they are awesome!! Best thing on the menu! I've gone back to HOB several times since then. Once ordered nachos to switch it up, and it was literally 15 chips and not much of anything else. Barely any meat, cheese, beans...anything. I think this place is great to sit at the bar although the cover kind of sucks considering the bands that usually place aren't very good. I always have a good time when I go there so I am still rating this place a 4 star.
We had the worst meal we've ever had at Fogo. Many of our favorite cuts were too tough to eat. The prices are also much higher and the quality of the food is very low. We will never go back.
The food is always fresh and hot. Five star service team. The toughest part of eating here is deciding what to eat. It all looks delicious.

I always like it here. The service has always been good for us and the food is great. The pineapple margarita is amazing and not too sweet, great for breakfast. They make the guacamole fresh at your table, as it should be. In terms of value for dollar try the quarterly tequila dinner!! Top shelf tequila shots, a few specialty tequila drinks and 3 courses $100 for 2.

Party of 8 and we all had a great meal.  Starting w the olives and cheese plate. Amazing yet so simple. The French onion soup was a fav at the table as it was chilly out. We sat in the outdoor tent that was periodically super warm then cool pending when the heater kicked in.  It was ok as the food was so amazing. We also had the escargot--is anything ever less than perfect w garlic and butter?  And speaking of bitter, the warm crispy roll and French butter was out of this world.  Worth every carb calorie. Who is this chef?
And of course the duck confit w lentils was perfectly done and the pickled red onions offset the crispy duck.  
Definitely will be back.
This was our first time coming to a Dock's las resort. And Aleigha S. Made our visit fun!! Thank you!!

I was here many years ago and went back tonight for dinner. Everything was delicious - I had the 86 West Roll to start, the filet oscar and the flourless chocolate torte. Service was attentive and it was a great meal.

Okay, first things first.  We've been looking forward to this restaurant since we heard it was opening.  We heard the one in the warehouse district had delicious food.  We live 3 blocks from this restaurant and we usually like to eat around our neighborhood since we have really great restaurants.  We went to La Casita on the second day it opened.  It was me, my husband and our 2 girls.  Like the Margaritas, but it took 20 minutes to get. Food was okay, but it took a long time for it to come out.  We spoke with the waiter and manager and told them that the whole neighborhood had been waiting on its opening and they were probably going to get slammed and they need more wait staff/bartender.  We went a second time with some friends. Drinks took 30 minutes to come out and food even longer. Then we went last week on April 14th for my husbands birthday.  Drinks took 45 minutes to come out, Food 1.5 hours.  We got there at 6:00 and left at 8:30. we had friends and kids with us.  Waiter brought wrong orders and said that the guacamole wasn't going to happen.  We spoke with the new manager since the original is no longer there (don't what happened to him.) They have only been open a month and a half maybe and already a new manager.  It's such a shame.  I really wish they make it, but they have to have better trained wait staff.  I worked as a waitress in the past and I know that it shouldn't take 45 minutes to get a drink.  Good Luck La Casita.  Maybe we'll visit in the future, but y'all gotta get your act together.  Jazz Fest is right around the corner and y'all are going to get slammed.

I Love steak'n Shake but this is the WORST in the area. I've eaten at this location more than once to give it a chance but it's filthy so I'm never returning. My last visit, there was a huge roach crawling on the window by our table and the waiter did nothing, asked to see a manager, was ignored. Finally spoke to a "Manager" and he casually told me the roaches come out when they exterminate and shrugged me off. There are plenty of restaurants on fowler, save yourself the hassle and eat somewhere else.

OMG I WILL BE DREAMING/CRAVING THESE BAGEL SANDWICHES FOR THE REST OF MY LIFE!!!

Stopped in after a crazy night with friends while visiting Indy.  I love bagel sandwiches and they have SO MANY options!  We had such a hard time deciding what to order.  I customized my own bagel sandwich (two meats, cheese, garlic & herb cream cheese on a cheese bagel of some kind, I think) and everyone else ordered something different.  Nobody left hungry or unsatisfied!

Their bagels are great; nothing like supermarket blah bagels.  I hope I visit Indy again so I can stop by- meanwhile I'll be trying to recreate something similar at home!

I eat at this place all the time whether I'm on my boat on my motorcycle or in my car off I lived here 20 years and that is absolutely the most comfortable and most enjoyable food I've ever eaten downtown

For a tea house? 5 stars
First, the view and location for enjoying an iced or warm tea-based beverage can't be beat- this is why we live in Florida. Daytime brings views of the water, sailboats and the beautiful parks along Bayshore Dr. Nighttime bring people watching, all ages, all kinds together.

The tea selection is plentiful! The walls are adorned with 60+ varieties of loose tea, mix n match or go with your std chai or other popular drinks on the menu. I enjoyed the ginger-lime iced. You pick, stevia, rock sugar or agave syrup to sweeten if ya like: 

The service, while slow at 10:30am with only 1 girl working, was with a smile, so approachable and generally happy to serve you. Yo could feel her good chi when you walk up to the counter.

Oh and there is FOOD! Vegetable quiche for me with cheese and tomatoes, meat for Momma with sausage. Served with bite size fresh fruit salad and a mini, warm, fresh cranberry muffin- the quick was light and fluffy, and the most important part a flaky crust, edges AND bottom! 

Try it out, enjoy Florida at its best
Three out of four plates were filled incorrectly. We asked for a box for the one plate. It was too small. Not worth the money given the poor service.

I heard great things about this little barbecue place. Unfortunately it does not live up to their reputation the wait staff and hosts are very prompt and friendly however that did not make up or the subpar BBQ. I would not recommend this place to anyone.

I really had high hopes for this place. The smell was good enough to slice and eat, and unlike a lot of barbecue places it had a spacious and comfortable dining room. Unfortunately my hopes were dashed with the Smokehouse Chef's Salad I ordered. The menu read "Mixed greens topped with a generous portion of smoked ham, pulled pork and turkey, cheddar and swiss cheese with sliced egg and tomato wedges", but in reality the smoked ham was generic food supply presliced sandwich ham which had been julienne cut, as were the flavorless white and yellow cheeses which started off life as sandwich slices. The pulled pork and turkey were cold flavorless lumps of yesterday's leftovers that nobody had bothered to break up or fluff before dumping onto the salad. The mixed greens were commercially chopped iceberg lettuce topped with a small fistful of commercial spring salad mix. The apple (cider?) vinaigrette dressing I chose was flavorless until I added a large quantity of the bottled "BJ's Hot Sauce" which was conveniently made available at the table.

Shattered hopes.....

Pros - Great smell, plentiful parking, fast and friendly service, clean bathroom.

Cons - The food, the greeter who was too busy on a personal telephone call to seat me. 

I'm tempted to give the place another try for an actual plateful of barbeque (I had a long-distance drive ahead of me and didn't want to get the heavy meal sleepy's, henceforth the salad) but really have my doubts.

I tend to forget about this location because it's located in a shopping mall that I tend to avoid. My last visit here consisted of a quick to-go order. Rylee took my order and was very nice throughout the process. She repeated my order back to me and made sure it was accurate. 

During my wait, I noticed about 4-6 people were waiting for their food along with me. That's unusual for Chick-Fil-A as they are usually very prompt in getting out orders in a timely manner. A few minutes later the food started to come out of the back and the manager gave everyone who waited an apology, a bounce back card and their food.

This is typical to wait for a while at most fast food places, but Chick-Fil-A really goes above and beyond when the little things aren't right.
This is a great bakery!! Not only the bread is delicious, but the sandwiches and pastries are as well. I highly recommend Great Harvest Bread.
Good variety of food options to choose from on the menu. Staff was friendly and quick with service. Plenty of seating.

Holy cow! This place is delicious and I wanna come back for more!! First off, I should say my hubby and I were driving on the westside to do some furniture shopping. We were both needed a little snack to get us going for the expedition ahead. Somehow we both had the same idea. GASP! Go to The Tamale Place!!

So after turning sharply into the parking lot and rushing inside-dude we were starving. No one wants to go furniture shopping on an empty stomach! We ordered our tamales and enjoyed very very much. They look small but man they pack a lot. They are super delicious with all kinds of meats or peppers in them. They are such a hot commodity that by the time we were there, they had sold out of a lot. Which is cool because it tells me people dig this joint.

Either way, I think I have to say every time I drive Rockville to go to the westside, I'm going to have to stop here for a little tamale action!!

Enjoyed the concept, the food was fine (of course we cooked it, so there's that) but the service was horrible. At a restaurant where YOU are cooking your food the one thing that should be easy is the service. This seems to have alluded Pfunky griddle. 
It took forever for someone to come to the table to take our drink order and then finally bring checks and cash out.  I will not be back and I cannot recommend the place to anyone.

Wow! Refreshing sb experience. I was in town for a night and decided to give sandbar a shot, and it turned out to be a great night. Such a friendly and lively crowd that gave me hope that downtown sb is not doomed forever. My bartender was Justin, and even though he looked young he seemed like a very experienced bartender. I've never seen anyone multi task that well because somehow he managed to make drinks for the entire restaurant while staying engaged and giving great service to everyone at the bar. Drinks were great (I recommend the spicy pomegranate margarita) but service was even better, I can't wait to return to Sandbar next time I'm in town. 5/5!

This place was absolutely amazing!!! The service was impeccable and the food was delicious!! I do not usually leave reviews and I am very picky when it comes to good food!!! BUT this place was worth every dollar spent!!!
This restaurant has atmosphere, is romantic, good wine list, great menu with ample specials, makes a great cappuccino, and extensive dessert menu. Ask for Gigi- fabulous nice server. I'll be back

Came back since I been craving for their Thai food hmmm every time I came back this place remind me more and more of my grandmom back home. They make the food just the way my nany did. My order this time was green curry which i love!!! and i have tried many place but it wont beat this one. Their food have just the right taste and spice into it. No mysterious blank spot where you have to wonder ' what is this suppose to taste like? Or why it doesn't seem to taste like the food I ate in Thailand? ' NOPE! It was NONE OF THOSE!!! I'm glad every time I eat there it's just keep getting better and better. The chef are great if you get a chance you can ask if the chef can come out to talk to you because he 'Will'. All of the food and sauce and dessert and drinks he made it himself. He is a very hard working man and along side the owner of the restaurant they both are such great people. Any question you have just ask! Everyone there are so nice and love what they doing. See you again soon Ratchada ;)

Our experience was frustrating and it may have been due to the COVID restrictions. I do appreciate Barbacoa working hard to remain open. However, the point of a reservation is to secure a time and seating area. I had called a week in advance for a reservation for my best friends birthday, the person I spoke with took down my info and said everything was set. I asked what their policy was for adding additional seating and decorations. The staff member said that I could call ahead to add seating and that decorations were okay. I thought she was nice and helpful because she offered the staff would be able to decorate the table if we wanted. 

The day of the birthday dinner reservation I called a few hours before to make sure balloons were allowed, the staff member said it was allowed. I asked if it would be okay to seat most of the party at the reservation time in order to surprise the birthday gal, the staff member said yes! The reservation time came and went but our party waited almost 30 minutes to be seated. The balloons that we had brought were questioned and discouraged. 

The entree and drinks were delicious although it took two round of appetizers to arrive. Our server was very nice and by the end of the night we had a great time. 

I do think that because of its reputation, I held Barbacoa to a higher standard. It was completely disappointing to experience so much frustration from their lack of communication as well as knowledge of their own policy.

Decorated super cool.   Nothing was outstanding but it was all good.  I'm probably a little pickier than the average person.  Food I ate had some spice but just not the flavors I expect from really good Cajun.  It's good if you're looking to satisfy your craving for Cajun.

The taste of the food was quite good, but ALL dim sum dishes served to us were ranging from warm to cold in temperature at 11:15am (which is a big minus), and after visiting their bathroom I really question the cleanliness of the kitchen as well as the whole restaurant.
Somehow none of the dim sum places in Chinatown Philly didn't convince me that it's possible to have a good dim sum experience here.

My absolute favorite place for breakfast!  Servers are always friendly and like family.  Food is consistently very good.  Addicted to the biscuits with sausage gravy.  Greek salad to-go is another winner!  Their Greek salad is fantastic and always fresh. Makes living around here a pleasure.  My family from Davis Island doesn't mind the drive if we are going to the Riviera.

I don't tend to frequent hotel restaurants.  It just so happened I attended a function in April and won a gift certificate for this place for $50. So, I was willing to try it out. Seeing as how I owed someone a dinner, we made our way out there on a Sunday night to chow down and see what this place had to offer.

When we walked in, our first impression was "Is this place even open?" It was 7:15pm and you would think there would be more hustle and bustle. Nope.  There were about 4 taken tables but the rest of the place was free and clear. There were a few dirty tables that looked like they had been sitting there for awhile, which skeeved me out a bit, seeing as how the place was practically dead.  When we walked in, there were 5 people drinking beers and talking at the bar (Zinc) that is attached to the restaurant.

Our waitress was nice, but young. She didn't seem to know how to wait on a table. She didn't ask questions and came back to us after 10 minutes (twice) to tell us our beer selections were out. There was no beer list and the excuse we got was "Well the bartender is busy."  Really? Because inbetween the first time she came to tell us our beer was not available and the second time, I went to the restroom and there wasn't one person left in the bar (the football game ended, everybody left). It was 7:45pm when she finally came with beers and to take our order.  We both had the same thing and ordered and appetizer. Our app never came. The waitress did offer to have an app boxed, but what we had ordered wouldn't work out well in a microwave.  We both had the Maryland Crab soup -- ehh, was run of the mill out of a can. Nothing fancy or different than any other restaurant.  For our entree, we both had the Filet with Lobster Mac and Cheese.  I couldn't find one piece of "fresh Maine lobster" amongst the elbow macaroni.  The sauce was way too greasy and sat in my stomach all night like a lead balloon.  For dessert, we were comp'ed because of all the errors happening (very nice of them to do).  We had the carrot cake and the caramel apple pie -- both yummy, but we had to ask for coffee with our dessert.  It wasn't offered and it wasn't fresh, either.

I'm sure this place COULD be good, but I would hate to see the bar and wait staff if they were REALLY busy.  Good luck.
It is a neat location. Decent food. Wasn't overly impressed. We came durning lunch-the smell from the entrance to checkout was terrible. I was underwhelmed by the taste of the food.

You know, it took me twenty-two years to visit the most popular diner in my hometown. But I was definitely pleased with my experience.

I ordered a chicken salad sandwich-- it contained a perfect chicken to mayo ratio and the chicken was in manageable chunks. My companion's omelet was enormous and was filled with bacon-- it looked quite unhealthy, but she seemed pleased with it.

I'll definitely have to return. Good service and good diner food=happy me.

This place is completely adequate.
Decent sake, very nice. Okay food, though some people have told me they were unimpressed with the freshness of the tuna.
I, personally, thought the tuna was totally average.
I enjoy the octopus balls the most, and they have deals on Wednesday, that makes it very worth it. Otherwise, most of the food is too little food for too much money.

I enjoy the music, and the friendliness of the servers, even though service is super slow, especially considering they are very small and on weekdays often very empty. One server even just totally forgot to put in half my order.

I had a completely average time at this middle of the road place.

What a great find.  The staff was very nice and accommodating, but did not hover.  The food was innovative and delicious.  We shared the mini-Mexican corn on the cob and the seasoning was fantastic.  For an entrée I had the salmon platter, which came with a small salad and rice & beans.  The salmon was chargrilled with a dry rub - very tasty and nicely cooked.  My friend had the chicken burrito which she enjoyed, and took home half as it was enough for two meals.  We hope to get back and have room for dessert next time!

While planning a girl's trip to NOLA, my friends and I knew that we wanted to go on a tour or two as this is a pretty historical city, especially compared to the cities in our relatively young state (California). There are so many tours to choose from; we honestly decided on French Quarter Phantoms due to the $30 for 4 people Groupon that we stumbled upon. I wasn't sure what to expect because sometimes the discounted activities are a little lower quality, but French Quarter Phantoms and our tour guide (young lady, I am so sorry I cannot remember her name) really blew my expectations out of the water. She was not just informative, but also very spunky and engaging. She seemed to be really passionate about New Orleans' history and the preservation of the cemeteries.
 
I had an idea of why the tombs are above ground in NOLA, but I didn't know the process of the natural cremation or the trial and error over time that it took to get to that point. I honestly learned quite a lot and appreciate the process even more. It never ceases to amaze me how humanity has adapted over time.  
 
There is quite a bit of walking, so definitely keep that in mind. I think someone who requires a scooter would be okay, though I'd call to be sure that they are allowed in the cemeteries.

I need to first start with the fact that I am not a fan of poke.  We only went here for my husband who LOVES poke.  I was blown away by how delicious it was.  All I can say is GO!!!  You will not be disappointed.

My wife and I had lunch there yesterday. The restaurant is upscale with modern "Bistro" type decor. Our service and food were excellent! I had a fish stew (can't remember the name) it had 7 different seafood selections in it. The broth was rich with flavor the vegetables were crunchy but cooked just enough.  Wife had a shrimp dish with a cream sauce, rice and a salad it was rich, creamy and very flavorful. 
Both dishes came out hot (temp) which we enjoy.  Highly recommend this restaurant.

The pretzel appetizer had a unique dipping combo. Allowing both spicy mustard and a very viscous cheese sauce provided a balance of options for each member of the meal. 

For the entree, both the mango special and the provincial were tasty but the sauce had created a soggy burger. My favorite, the banging ketchup enhanced the seasoning of the fries. 

Toah approved.

Vince's does pizza right. I go far out of my way to go here.

Nothing fancy, but the pizza is amazing. Kind of reminds me of shore pizza.

Amazing crust.

Lucky's is awesome. Great good, great staff, lots of fun. Interesting and delicious specials. My favorite dish is the breakfast burrito as a quessadilla. Amazing. 

They have outside seating available because of COVID.
Tried t great veggie burger here. Nice local joint to frequent with friends and family or for a quick bite.

One of my favorite Southside restaurants. The Bubba's 33 hamburger is one of the best I've had. Very similar to a hamburger I've had in southern CA. (Slaters) & I thought that was the only place to get that burger. Bubba's however "does more than burgers", that is where the 33 comes from, but I will leave that as part of the Bubba mystic! LOL! They have a great menu and really great tasting fare. I have gotten the grilled chicken salad probably a dozen times. They also have a southwest fried chicken salad that very tasty also. They have great tasting Pizza as well. It's a great place to watch sports,  have a couple of beers, and one of the many, great tasting menu offerings. Haven't been disappointed at all.
I have used their on-line and pickup/carry out quite a lot  since the onset of CoVid and quarantine! Ez-peezee!

Dined at Grace perhaps four or five days after opening.  First impression is that the staff are all fantastic, and plentiful.  There were always staff coming and going, and asking if we needed anything.  Zero complaints; the service could not possibly have been better.

Short version of the review: fantastic staff, fantastic entrees, huge helping of lobster on the lobster bolognese, absolutely accurate temp and perfectly prepared filet, scallops were melt in your mouth.  Some of the signature cocktails may be your thing, or maybe not, but they're expensive, so choose wisely.  The sides came out a bit cold, probably just something the kitchen will work out on timing with, no pun intended, time.  As far as deserts go, the key lime pie is admittedly not home made, but wasn't impressed with the chocolate option so perhaps the key lime is the way to go.

Longer version: dined on a rainy Sunday, were greeted at the door by the owners (husband and wife, I think).  Entire staff were very friendly and attentive.  The establishment is modern / contemporary, lots of white/gray tables and floors, accent walls, blue-lit bar, numerous seating options.  Arriving at 4pm right as they opened, it was like a flood gate of staff were released into the dining room; there was never any moment where we couldn't have asked for something that was missing, so incredible service.

Had the Pastrami Salmon Taquito and Pan-Roasted Sea Scallops (Dinner Entree) as appetizers.  Contrary to the name, the salmon doesn't have pastrami i the mix, but was a great appetizer regardless, and great value for the price.  It was a generous portion of smoked salmon on top of the slaw/onion mix, and a crispy tostada, topped with caviar.  The scallops were ridiculous; huge, fresh, perfectly prepared.  I could have eaten about ten pounds of them.  The bed of rice surrounding them, nothing to write home about, but that's not why you order that entree.  

Entree time; had lobster bolognese and pan-seared cab beef tenderloin (aka filet).  OMG the lobster bolognese was incredible.  You get a tail (in the shell) on top, and then a mix of pasta and lobster claw in your bowl.  For the price, you'd be surprised at how much lobster is in this dish; so good, no complaints.  The filet was prepared perfectly, rare, and my wife is picky about the temp.  It was an excellent cut and cook.  Only minor complaints, no Béarnaise sauce, and the great tasting truffle-oil infused mashed potatoes came out cold; so they were probably plated before the entree was ready.

Desert, ordered the home made chocolate souffle versus the admittedly (local) store bought key lime pie.  It was a bit runny, more like chocolate pudding, had a strawberry and some blueberries on it.  In hindsight I'd have gone with the key lime as I love key lime pie and could care less if they didn't make it in house.

Drinks: the signature "Grace" drink is a bit on the fruity / light side, and not very strong.  I'd recommend a custom margarita, which was their limeade syrup and milagro tequila; pretty light, tasty, and reasonably strong.  Also had a Bacardi & Diet, was kind of weak, so may not be the kind of place to order well drinks.

All in all, pretty fantastic experience for a restaurant that is four days old.  Will definitely be back.

I visited the restaurant this past weekend for dinner and was incredibly impressed with how well they are handling the crowd capacity due to covid. The staff was super friendly and food was not only delicious, but the service was amazing. Highly recommend and we will be back soon!

This place really surprised, never been a JJ fan before but their new 9grain sub roll bread is amazing! 

They also have vegetarian friendly options which is a plus :) 

I went there this past weekend and got the veggie sandwich #6 and my love got the totally tuna. Both came with cucumber lettuce tomato and mayo, mine also had provolone cheese and avocado on it since it was just veggies. 

The only small complaint is the cashier didn't tel us about all the extra "freebies." Not being a previous avid JJ customer I just thought the sandwiches came how they are, if I'd known I would've gotten vin&oil and pickles on mine too. But the staff wasn't overly excited or friendly either.

The atmosphere was clean and updated. The signage was a bit much but overall a nice place to sit and enjoy your sandwich. 

So great food, great price and great atmosphere. Maybe just a slight "pep in the step" of the workers and this place could be a 4 or 5star which is amazing for a normal chain sandwich shop. 

Yum yum!

My favorite farm to table spot.  Everything they make is so fresh and tasty.  Chef Matt does a fantastic job of shopping locally farms, finds what looks good and creates a tasty dish.  The biscuits are aMAIZEing and homemade ice creams are to die for....especially salt ice cream.  We just went Friday night and they restricted their menu to a 10 course tasting menu.  It didn't disappoint.
Great atmosphere, warm bread with a pesto oil, and a nice meal. Service was great. Very sweet sauce style.

Sundays are way too busy, but it makes sense since the food is good. This place usually draws an older crowd, but it seems like it caters to locals. I like how there is outside seating. However, when it gets busy... the service goes down because you end up waiting so long for your food. I suggest the skillets. The price is ok, but i mean cmon it's breakfast, so it shouldn't be too expensive. The one thing that brought this place down is a "food share" fee. Which i never heard of. Usually asian restaurants charge for a "food waste"but that's rare. but a SHARE CHARGE? what cuz , i don't wanna eat all my food so i wanna give to my wife? it's ridiculous. I guess the locals don't care about that which keeps them coming, but this one thing definitely brings the rating of this place significantly. I do suggest going on a slow day, but other than that, go find another place.

DO NOT EAT AT THIS LOCATION!!!!! GO TO THE ONE IN SPARKS.

I am new to the area and erroneously called the Reno location for a to-go order not knowing there were two locations.  I thought I was calling Sparks.  When I arrived at the Sparks location I was told I had ordered from the Reno location.  I called the Reno location and the guy who answered the phone was very nice and said he would cancel my order and thanks for calling.
A couple of minutes later, the bartender called me back and starting yelling at me for ordering from them and cancelling.  She said that I better get over there and pick up my order and that the Sparks location was not allowed to serve me!!  I handed the phone to my husband and she started yelling at him, swearing at him, so he hung up.  The food at the Sparks location is outstanding so I can only assume the food is good at all locations.  However, I will never, ever, ever go to the Reno location because of the B--ch who called me and screamed at me for making a mistake.

I have always loved this place. No matter what I order, I know it's always going to be delicious. (My current favorite is the chopped salad, but you truly can't go wrong with anything you order.) They have great beer on tap and a garage door that is opened during appropriate weather. The inside is all dark wood, which makes for a cozy feel. If you've never been, or haven't been in a while you should get there. Or at least order takeout!

Sigh.
I have been searching for a Thai restaurant that hasn't "Americanized" the menu, that doesn't offer everything with a "1-5" choice for spice.

OK, pet peeve aside, it was a solid 4 star experience. We got there around 7pm, and got seated right away, which was nice. Hot ginger tea, and we both ordered "medium" which was right around "3" on the 1-5 scale. (I know, put it aside)

Started with Veggie Tempura, small portion to share, but very tasty and nice selection of vegetables.
Paradise shrimp showed up as promised, bright green fresh tasting snow peas with tomatoes and a half dozen big shrimp. 

Don't let the lack of that fifth star keep you away, I'm stingy with stars, 4 means really good, but not the best I've ever had. That would be Thai Landing in Baltimore on Charles.

We were visiting friends in Oro valley and went here for lunch.   Three of 5 peoples food were bad, one was just ok and the other ehhh. 
So,  my spinach enchiladas with sour cream and cilantro sauce was literally spinach and cream sauce enchiladas.  There was almost no spinach inside the tortilla!   WTH!   I would have sent them back but our gal didn't come back till I started to try to pick it apart.   My husbands carne asade burrito was so dry I almost spit it out when it picked out some meat.   When he doesn't eat his steak burrito that is not a good sign.  Our friends foods were also not good .... pork burrito with so much tortilla tucked in, and the chili  rellonos  were mediocre at best.  They did have good rice n beans with a tiny
 Side salad on the plate.  That was nice.   But my goodness....main entrees were bad. And Itold the waitress when I handed her our credit card to pay that my spinach enchiladas were terrible, and all she said was sorry.  No comp at all.    Not cool.

I'll admit that I'm getting tired to Southern fare so I compromised by having pizza at Louisiana Pizza Kitchen.

Service is SLOW as death here and their pizzas are decent but nothing that would make me trek out to the far end of the French Quarter for again.

I shared their garlic bread and their 3-sausage pizza (Salsiccia) which was unique with alligator, italian and andouille sausage.  I've never had alligator on a pizza before!

Everything tasted fine and prices are reasonable ($12 to $15 each) but the service was pretty bad and it wasn't busy.  Open for lunch and dinner.

Stumbled upon this place on the way home across the bridge. (Through a GPS yelp search actually) This is truly a gem. 

At the time that we went, it was lunchtime. They had a two for one cocktail deal. I chose the rum punch which was tasty, but both served at the same time. I would have preferred to have this served one at a time to prevent ice melt in the second one. 

Aside from that, the food was great. That blue crab Mac n cheese was the best with chunks of meat galore! The Rasta Pasta with seafood was awesome. There was plenty of covered outdoor seating. 

As expected, this restaurant had a very casual/tropical ambience. This place gives you a high level of environmental comfort.  The wait staff was very friendly and informative. I highly recommend this place if you happen to be in this area.

Beautiful place / ambiance. However due to not making a reservation the only place to sit was inside or outside in the front under the porch. It was a beautiful day so we wanted to sit outside! However in the front they make you go to the counter and order everything. You have to stand in line to order drinks (which took a while because so many people were sitting outside in that area), then go back and order food. There were about 10 servers inside doing nothing, I'm not sure why they wouldn't have the servers serve that other outside area? It wasn't a good experience. So sad because I wanted to love it but this ruined it for me and I won't be back.

Google "St Louis BBQ" and most likely your first hit is Pappy's Smokehouse. Between having just read a friend of mine's hunger inspiring steak blog and my roommate's heating up of some father's day leftover pulled pork on a lazy day off work, I executed such a googling. I saw from the get go that the readers of the local weekly rag here in town have voted Pappy's best BBQ joint in town four or five years running. It's been featured on cable television shows... and conveniently it's only a few miles from where I live. I decided to check it out. 
 
After pulling into the parking lot and stepping out of the car, I was immediately a little worried. I could smell nothing. Even the most mediocre BBQ joints smell AMAZING from 3 blocks away. I decided not to worry about it too much, as it was a pretty windy day and took consolatory relief in the fact that even at 2 pm on a weekday the parking lot was pretty full. 
 
Walking into the place the first thing you couldn't help but notice was THE BLUES. Dear god, I get it, you're a BBQ joint, you're allowed to play the blues, but it was way too loud to be anything other than absolutely obnoxious. There was not too long of a line that kept me for about 10 minutes. Again I figured this was a decent sign mid afternoon.
 
Waiting in line though I began to be bothered by the amount of children under the age of, oh say, 12. My favourite singular man made spot in the universe is at Arthur Bryant's at 17th and Brooklyn in Kansas City. I began to wonder... Do I like Arthur Bryant's so much because of the food or the fact that no one brings their bratty white kids there?  (Actually it's both). 
 
My turn to order came up. I decided on the beef brisket. Sandwiches came with the choice of 2 sides. I ordered a fountain drink (PEPSI4LYFE) and my total was $11. They took down my name, I got my Pepsi and sat on a stool at a counter looking out over the downtown skyline. My sandwich appeared rather quick (five minutes?) and was brought out in a plastic basket with my sides in little styrofoam cups and a plastic fork and knife. It didn't LOOK overly fantastic, but looks aren't important. 
 
I ripped off a piece of the brisket, which was drowning in too much sesame seed bun. I chewed. It didn't taste like much other than cow. Well, I thought, maybe their sauce would set it off. Without tasting it, I put a liberal amount of their original sauce and took a bite into my bun heavy sandwich.
