I'm relatively new to writing about food. I'm usually a bit of a garbage disposal when it comes to food. If I really like something I grunt and moan euphorically (and sometimes cry) and eat the whole thing. If I don't particularly care for something I just eat most of it and shrug my shoulders. My pallet is undeveloped simply because developing a pallet requires a conscious effort to do so. I was considering this as I was chowing into my sammich. 
 
What do I say about this? The meat just takes like meat and the sauce? It wasn't spicy (not even the one labeled HOT was very spicy). I decided to pile on more sauce for the sake of forming an intelligible opinion of it. I chewed. It was boring. That was all I could come up with. I had a vague sense memory of being six or seven years old and eating chicken nuggets in the grade school cafeteria. I remembered how i hated BBQ sauce up until I was 15 or 16 because I figured that all BBQ sauce must taste like that shit they served in the cafeteria. Holy shit, this tastes like cafeteria BBQ sauce... a big upfront taste that seems to mushroom in the front of your mouth like an untasty bullet hitting its unfortunate target. 
 
The two sides I got were slaw and beans. I am aware of the fact that some places with boring, flavorless meats and sauce often have fantastic sides that keep the place afloat. This was not to be the case with Pappy's. The slaw was slaw. I feel like there's two kinds of people when it comes to cole slaw. People that like it and people that don't. I happen to like it and ate it all, shrugging my shoulders at the empty styrofoam cup.
 
The beans tasted much like the sauce. Too much like the sauce.  I couldn't finish them. I had flashbacks to my destitute mid twenties, struggling to finish the can of Best Choice baked beans that was constituting my one singular meal for the day. I started to realize that the most satisfying part of my meal was the Pepsi (I don't drink much pop). I took a moment and really thought hard as to what comparison to draw.
 
Here it is:  I could have had the exact same sandwich experience but with better sides, for $4 less at a HyVee cafe. 
 
If this is the best Saint Louis has to offer, I'd recommend just saving your BBQ adventures for a trip to Kansas City. Go Royals!

Why is this five stars you may ask?  Because it's an Boise institution that has been in business forever, and the food is just as good as when I frequent this place before Yelp existed. Simple deli sandwich but with quality ingredients.  I got ham and Swiss on Rye and it was delicious.  My husband and I ordered a side of steak fries and they were  also delicious . They don't skimp on meat with their sandwiches which makes for a filling sandwich.

Perhaps the best french fries I've ever had - cooked in peanut oil! I also really enjoyed the blueberry & port chutney, and the pickled beets, but the fries alone are more than enough reason to revisit this restaurant! I did not overly enjoy the salmon, but I'd really like to try the maple butter pork belly and one of their flatbreads at some point in the future!

Oh my. They have the donuts. 

I will definitely be back. 

Do not miss coming here if you go to New Orleans!!!!

Get there buttermilk drop. Please go. It's incredible. They also have other breakfast items such as eggs etc.

A fine restaurant in Nashville, but something I ate here got my stomach churning for a couple of days.  

Wife and I had the Kansas City Steak, which was cooked to our requests perfectly.  The seasoning was uneven.  I subbed a side of pasta with a sauce and this was too oily for me (maybe this was the problem?)  It tasted OK.

Staff service was quite friendly and attentive.  The bar staff (got drinks while waiting) was pretty funny.

I ordered through grub hub and this was my first time having it. Omg first off the presentation was really nice and the portions were nice. The food tasted amazing. I'm not a fitness person or anything but I'd order from here again in a heart beat.

Never been to New Orleans this restaurant was reccomended to us.    Our waitress was Trina.  She was great.   I had the beef gator with pepper jelly very tasty.  Was able to try a sample of the turtle soup.  The flavor hits your taste buds about 6 seconds after the bite.  Never having turtle soup I would defiently get this so if you come here try it.  Trina suggested the bread pudding.  Never having this before it was excellent.  When you come ask for Trina she is the best.  Very patient if you need help with what to order.  Im from Arizona so this is a very different experience and having super nice people like Trina makes such a different.
Carlos had Great customer service, he made delicious  micheladas!! Will be coming back forsure

I consider myself a chowhound - lover of all things exotic, cheap, hard to find and I don't care if it is dirty. Why am I giving this over-priced, hipsterfied, trendy place 4 stars? Do we need any more carpet bagging celebrity chefs here in Nashville?
Well, it was pretty good, and we need more South Asian offerings, even in this category.

Now to the review:
A few of us shared some appetizers:
Kale Pakora: Fried Kale chips. Can you get trendier than that? Well, they do a nice thing with garbanzo beans and yogurt kind of like a seven layer dip underneath with a little heat stuck in. The suprise? It was served cold.
Gol Guppa shots: these were a flavorful mix of potato and garbanzo beans ground up in a semolina puff ball that you could drizzle green mint sauce onto. Some sweet and salty and crunchy/chewy of the semolina. The suprise? They were cold. 7 to the order.

We got a couple of their Desi fare - add a protein and a sauce. We were so glad they were served hot.
We got the chicken with yellow moilee cocunt curry, which was a nice, savoury sauce without much spice. The chicken chunks were fine, a touch dry. A $16 curry dish. We also got lamb vindaloo which was hotter, but not oppressively so. Chunks of lamb and potato, lamb a bit dry for an $18 lamb vindaloo!

On the side we got their raita, which had chunks of curd? in it. Not typical, but very good. We got one of their chutneys of the day, with fermented serrano chilies. I have eaten Thai-spciy Sri pha pai in Queens, a blow your head off Sichuan huo guo in the summer in China and this rivaled those in heat. Wow! make me cry, sister. That actually helped them get 4 stars.

Naan for $3 a serving? Good, fresh out of the tandoor-oven fresh, but nothing special, except the high price.

Beer list was fine - a good range of $5 and $6 bottles including Boddington's in a can - not common in town. 
Wine list was fine and expensive. $64 for a $16 bottle of Owen Roe Sharecropper had me shaking my head and sighing, but hey, I didn't order it.

But go, take your friends who want to go downtown and have something slightly more on the exotic end of the things (for Nashville) and slightly nicer South Asian (for Nashville). Take friends who are used to paying carpet bagging celebrity chefs for slightly overpriced, but fairly good food in Nashville and you and they won't be disappointed.

And you can look across the street, mourn the loss of 12th and Porter and know that you and your yuppie support of celebrity chefs are part of the problem.
Like me.

I still feel this is Philadelphia's finest bean and that the Baristas are well-trained. This location started selling sandwiches a couple months ago. A Veggie sandwich - , Ham and cheese and Chicken Salad on Ciabatta roll for $7.00. I also think this is my favorite La Colombe location. it is the original location and I have been coming here for as long as I have been in Philly (13 years). What has also changed since my last review is La Colombe had the cold brew iced coffee way before chain coffee places like Starbucks and also started doing pour over before chains etc, caught on. 

The espresso drinks are still top notch, quality. The pastries (most made at their Fishtown location) are still very good. Baristas still knowledgeable and friendly. I like this location because of the ambience. It's great to kick back, hang out with friends, or alone reading, writing, people watching.
The smoked chicken bowl was alright. The chicken was a little dry but the rice and cauliflower rice were good. The sauce was just ok.

Although there appears to be a problem among management for retaining enough service staff, you can't go wrong with this spot for breakfast. My favorite omelet is Rockefeller $12.95     
Fresh creamed spinach, oysters, onion, bell pepper, and cheese. Don't get put off by oysters with your eggs as it's really delicious. Just be prepared to wait for it and you need to climb steps to the second floor to use the customer bathroom.
Paid $6.95 x 2 for overpriced egg and ham on a brioche bun, but once I got on the plane and opened them, discovered it was just a hamburger bun. Dishonest bait and switch.

"Marissa, what was your favorite meal in New Orleans?"
"THE RUBY SLIPPER, DUH, RANDOM QUESTION ASKER"

Ruby Slipper came highly recommended to us, so I, in turn, highly recommend it to you.

The best biscuit of my life.
The best Irish Coffee of my life.
The best cheesy grits of my life.
The best scrambled eggs of my life. yep, I just said that.
great potatoes.
mediocre/too chunky belini but like WHATEVER

I've been to engine rose a few times now. They have an excellent selection of craft beers.  To be expected they have many of the same great burgers as engine 9, but they have some great upmarket dishes as well.  Pork wings, short ribs are both done very well. Staff was attentive and friendly.  The only drawback is I can't figure out their hours of operation.

Came in to Reforma 12/09/21 , I'm not one to give out negative reviews or criticism but this will probably be the last time we visit.  Here's what we ordered and I will explain why the low rating . 
Nachos with carne asada - the meal over all was inedible. Guacamole not fresh . It should have been a bright green not brown . Every bite of the nachos was over salted . The chips were just dusted with too much salt . We didn't even eat our complimentary chips and salsa due to the heavy hand of sodium from the chips . 
Tortilla soup - probably the best thing on the menu. 
Calabacitas - First, they forgot my order. When the Calabacitas arrived I waited to receive something similar to the picture they displayed on their QR SCAN menu but it was not even close . Messy presentation that showed it had been forgotten . 
Bunuelos - expected warm discs of fried goodness . What my 8 year old got was a bunch of cold cracked pieces . I displayed pictures of the QR scanned items on their menu and what I received on the review . 
2 draft modelos , and horchata - two stars go to the draft Modelo beer and the nice waitress that took it off the bill .

This was our first time ordering from Voorhees Diner, through Door Dash, and will be the last time.  When the driver arrived he was told they never received the order.  Ok, I suppose there can be glitches.  The driver called us promptly and said he was waiting for them to make the order.  After waiting over an hour, he calls again and says the diner gave us the wrong food and he was going back in to straighten it out.  He calls again and says, the manager refused to give him the missing dinner salad and our order also contained another door dashers order, which he took back into the restaurant.   We finally get the order and half our order was missing.  Called the restaurant and the manager blames the door dash driver and refuses to even address the fact that after an hour and a half, half our order was missing.   She was rude, completely dismissive and totally unhelpful.  While the order was placed through door dash, it's the restaurant that should care how its customers are treated. Maybe they should stop taking orders through door dash if they can't fulfill the order and do it correctly.   Very sad that the supposed manager who answered the phone could not have cared less, and had no intention of trying to do something to help make this right.   Door dash did give us a credit, but this was not about the money, it was about the total lack of interest in a customer.
Chile verde was covered with raw onions and the sauce had no flavor and was thickened with corn starch. So bad I sent it back and ordered pork tacos- dry, dry, dry. Just say no.

Delicious garlic bread steak with provolone and spinach!  Onion rings are standard issue frozen beer battered, but fries were crisp and yummy. Gluten free sister ecstatic about her steak and the roll.  

Took star from no bathroom otherwise tiny 2 table place is definitely worth trying!

Consistently delicious food. Inexpensive to try new things. Great new location with more space. Reasonably priced & delicious lunch specials. 
If you like spicy food - go authentic!

Ippolito's is my go to for fresh fish in the city. From sushi grade (made Thomas Keller's salmon coronets) to humble smoked trout (shredded into a cracker spread) this place always has what I need at a reasonable price. Quality is always high - just yesterday I picked up some great snow crab legs cheaper than what the local supermarkets were advertising (Ippo's had it on sale for just $3.99) for a great Valentine's dinner. Staff is always super knowledgeable + friendly as well.

Love supporting local businesses and if it's good enough for most of Philadelphia's restaurants (they also own Samuels + Son wholesale) it's good enough for me. Thanks guys!
We now have a new favorite breakfast place. Nothing fancy, just nice people and good food.

This review is for a Sunday 4pm happy hour experience.
I ordered "Two Fish Tacos" which was presented nicely.  However the fish tasted like it was leftover from a previous day that had been boiled or steamed to revive it.  Do you know what old boiled fish tastes like?  Horrible!
I could not finish my meal.......

This place is really gross. Sushi tastes like grocery store sushi that's a couple days old
The ramen is flavorless and to be quite honest made my stomach hurt after 2 bites. definitely over priced and no food quality.

Just has my boyfriends birthday party at the karaoke lounge upstairs of Fuji mountain. The red room comes with a bathroom and a doorbell (to order drinks when you want it). The servers came promptly and it was definitely a good time for the price paid... Perfect for a group of people looking to sing karaoke stress free in an enclosed area!

If you're ever on South St and you need some late night pizza... THIS IS THE PLACE!! 

It's a small establishment so the idea is that go in one door and you go out the other. There's a small standing area if you want to eat your pizza quickly before heading to a local bar, but most of the locals grab a box and chill out on any available stoop on the street. 

It's cash only and cheese slices only, with the exception of Toppings Tuesdays. At $3.50/slice you will get your monies worth! On another visit to Philly, I will DEFINITELY try them again.

Disgusting. Total wast of money. You're better off going to the store and buying a sandwich. The eggs and grits were sooo watery. The pulled pork was flavorless and the bacon was paper thin. Waste of money

Tacos: to die for!! I really wish I would have gotten like 10 of the avocado tacos, such a great texture and creaminess. I am SO obsessed with the steak salad with cilantro dressing now. I literally went back two weeks later to eat it again!!

I am not sure about other items on the menu since I've only been here once but the pizza was very delicious. I am actually from Delaware but I was in Philadelphia with a family member of mine and we stopped by Rex Style Pizza. The owner was really nice and he's very sociable with all his customers. I saw him talking to a customer of his about sports because apparently he's a huge Philadelphia sports fan and it shows from the Philadelphia sports teams theme that permeates the restaurant. I would definitely come back again. I loved the atmosphere and I highly recommend this place to anyone else who may want to come here either in the future as somebody who like me just happened to be in the city for a short time or even someone living in Philadelphia who has yet to experience it.

Place is fantastic. Probably too good, which is why the line is constantly busy.  Most of the time I have to end up ordering from somewhere else bc I simply can't get through. Talk about frustrating. To sum up my review, best pizza in SJ... please hire another person to answer phones, can't imagine how much business you're missing out on.

WOW!!! The sushi slices are massive. Really, I was astonished when they brought my nigiri order. The slices were way bigger than most places. If you like sushi you gotta go there. And I also ordered the egg drop soup with shrimp......OMG, OMG I've never had anything like it. It's totally unique to Nama. If you love soup, you gotta try this one.

First timer & will go again. Went at 7:15pm, easy parking and no wait to sit. Food was quick and hot. Atmosphere was nice, really interesting structure. Salads, steaks, baked sweet-potato and veggies were all perfect as we ordered. Too full for dessert. Waitress was great!

Second visit July2019, updated to 5star. Everything was perfect. Got there about 6pm, still some parking up front. No wait to seat 2 people. Waitress was great, food was absolutely cooked perfect. Steaks were exactly as ordered, steamed green-beans tasted fresh like just out of a garden. We were seated within sight of the large  mesquite grill. The cook had a lot going on and off the grill but he seemed relaxed and attentive to his craft. Great atmosphere.

Last night my husband and I drove across town to eat dinner at Miguel's at the Summit. We have eaten at their locations so many times and have never been disappointed until now. We ordered our food and I always get the Chile Rellenos because I don't like spicy food, my husband ordered the special fish tacos. I know at times you get a spicy Chile but mine was so hot my throat and mouth were on fire. I asked my husband to try them, he said "they were packing some heat". The service was the terrible part of the evening and this particular man is always so wonderful (I believe he is management, owner, co-owner) last night he was just rude! He came back after we got our food to ask ONLY how my husbands meal was, didn't even acknowledge me, then filled my husbands water while my soda glass stood empty waiting to be filled. After he left I was in disbelief, my husband said sarcastically "How is your meal"?  My husband said all night it's like your invisible no acknowledgment what so ever. So where we were sitting I could see them making the fried ice cream desserts all night and I kept saying they look so good I am getting one of those maybe that will cool off my mouth. Well the waiter came again just looked at my husband set the check down without asking if we wanted any dessert and my soda glass still empty!  My husband said she hasn't had her glass refilled all night she has been waiting. So he finally takes it and fills it part way. Needless to say I said forget the dessert I was so disgusted with the service and left dinner feeling hungry. Usually we love this place best Mexican food but tonight we left with a very bad taste in our mouths. Disappointed in Miguel's!
Super good! I'd even go as far to say this might be the best taco I've ate here in Tampa! Carnitas and Al Pastor were not disappointing!

Great food, atmosphere, clean, friendly workers and nice decor. Even had security. Not much meat and very pricey. Felt like cafeteria style restaurant. Liked the fact it was established the year I was born 1976!!!

We took the birthday girl here for her 22nd birthday and had an absolute blast. Our chef, Harold, was absolutely amazing and really made sure we had fun. He also speaks Spanish, which is a great plus, and really furthered the great experience we were already having. 

The chicken hibachi was fantastic, the steak hibachi was equally as good, and the shrimp hibachi was spectacular. Everyone in our group had a fantastic time, I could not emphasize this enough. This experience let the children in us come out. 

To make things even better, the staff were so kind and attentive making sure we always had water and that our food was good! 

Thank you for a great experience. The birthday girl had a great time and everyone in the party shared the same sentiment.
You can't go wrong with the salmon tacos. Seriously the best tacos I've ever had. Great service and amazing food.

Been there four times now and the service has gotten worse every time. After we got our drinks didn't see waitress for 30 minutes. Food also came out lukewarm. Great atmosphere but not good enough to overcome the terrible service. Won't be going back

Words do not describe how wonderful The Salt House in New Hope is. The atmosphere is incredible, old school colonial pub with a fireplace, candles, and perfect seating. 5 STAR! At great prices ... Duck meatballs, fried brussel sprouts, scallops, burgers, short ribs, crab, chowder are favs ... drinks are perfect! Great house drinks and an excellent beer options. A MUST for all ... Mike and Kristan do a tremendous job! Thank you !!!

My experience at both Agave restaurants, the one on Milpas and the one on De La Vina has always been a good one. 

The food is always good and innovative and fresh. My fav for Mexican food!

Wow! Wow! Wow! After my mom and I shared a good time at Superior Seafood, I talked about the food I had there for two days straight! We had the chargrilled oysters for the appetizer and my mom is a oyster person.. I'm not too much of one... but we both enjoyed them! My mom made the comment they are some of the best oysters she has ever had. For entrees, we shared the filet and blackened catfish. Both plates were "SUPERIOR"!! I could not wait to eat my leftovers, Haha! We ended our time at Superior Seafood with the crème brûlée and I have to say that was some of the best brûlée that I have had in a whileee. Also, we had the frozen French 75 drink, really good as well as everything else. I think this is now one of my favorite restaurants in NOLA!
Sandwich was excellent. Nubs were great. Cheese pretzel could have been a little more fresh(warm)

My Friend found a hair on her piece of pizza. She almost threw up. Never will I order from this place again. Always I will let the people I converse with know not to order here. I'm in Philly ALOT.

A BIG CLOT OF HAIR, not just one strand.
Good, cheap, and fast. Yum. Teriyaki burger is exceptionally tasty.
The food was excellent and the owner was very kind and personable!  We can't wait to come back, the food was exceptional!!  Can't wait to go back!
I love this spot. You can tell that their sauce is made from scratch. This is definitely a go to spot for excellent Italian food.
Very friendly owner, reasonably priced, great atmosphere, friendly staff, and very consistent, albeit simple, choices.  Ideal spot for a quick bite with your kids after Mr. Johns or InMovement

I think the best way to enjoy the food here is to not come hungry. The food is tasty, yes, but a bit expensive and portions aren't that big. I think next time I'll aim for a post lunch cookie break and try one of the huge chocolate chip ones they have up front!

On a different note, baby-friendly? YES =) I was here with two other new mamas, so 3 high chairs between us. The staff was super nice, helped us park our strollers in the back, and the babes were able to hang out and be noisy without worry. We were at one end of the big family table and there were two more moms with even younger babies down at the other end.

I don't know if I've changed or the food has. The new location is great, clean and nice. Our first visit here, the waiter was more interested in being entertaining to his friends than being attentive and the food was meh.

Our last visit, the service and food was better, but I think I'm not a bread and pasta fan anymore. It's yummy, but I had unpleasant reactions to the wheat. Never had that till this last time.

Saraga is the best international supermarket in Indianapolis! Almost any ethnic food you
could imagine is there. We go to visit family every summer and winter, and we never leave without going to Saraga.
I've had fun sitting at the communal table.  It's on the expensive side for SB, but definitely one of the best restaurants in town.

My husband and I had a great experience here.  Although, there was not a lot of help offered in the wine side,  our service was incredible on the deli/market side.  The cheese man was very knowledgeable and made great suggestion.

I would recommend this place for sure.  Great cheese, great deli, great soups!

Pat O'Brien's is a classic when it comes to entertainment in New Orleans. I've been here many times and all were very different experiences. What I love about this place is all the different rooms and patios you can enjoy. From the beautiful garden patio, to the boisterous piano bar, to the other quieter rooms - there is a place for everyone here!

Pat O's is known for their hurricanes and there is a reason! Served in a huge commemorative glass, these can be dangerous, but delicious. Also if you're feeling kind of over the touristy drinks, try a Cyclone! 

During this visit, we were lucky enough to get a front table in the piano bar and it was a BLAST. It was a super rainy day, so the place was packed (which usually can be overwhelming, but with sing-alongs and alcohol it was bearable haha). Usually the piano bar can be impossible to find a seat (Especially with a large group) so heads up! Because of how raucous it can be, the service is decent - but pretty typical. The table service was lovely (all men with green sport coats), but the bartenders were AWFUL (hopefully she was just having a bad day!) 

This place is definitely a must if you are first time visitor! Also - make sure to sign up for their newsletter and receive a complimentary drink for your birthday!

This DJ y'all!!!! Wow.  Wow wow wow.  Slater Hogan killed it.  I've experienced a lot of DJs in my day and he's definitely of a different breed.  Mixing the old school with the new just *perfectly*, bringing back memories while still remaining relevant.  Just amazing!!! Shout out to Jade at the bar - he was amazing as well.  They all really made me feel like family for my birthday today.  I will definitely return, no matter the day of the week!  

This bar is casual but has such great vibes and an overall inviting atmosphere.  They have awesome weekly specials and staff that want you to enjoy yourself while you're here.  They're so much fun.  There's more than meets the eye here, because I was skeptical at first - but, give this bar a chance, I promise you'll be glad you did!

Been looking for an excuse to try this place, and found it after I returned from Miami and had a couple hours to kill before I picked up my son. If you like Omelettes (and I do), this is definitely the place for you. Well over 150 options, plus regular breakfast and lunch fare. I had the pizza omelette with all the fixings of a normal loaded pizza, without the added carbs of the crust. My lady had the South Carolina omelette filled with fried shrimp, grits, and cheddar. This place is definitely worth the occasional 35 miles up 295 from Delaware. I will be back!

I can't believe the prices here. A lot of the menu is food with unique twists to it and always pulled off to have great taste. There is a little play area for kids and some outdoor seating. And friendly speedy service. Try a bunch of things and split them!
delicious with a wide variety. doughnuts are a bit pricey but they are a welcome change from the coffee chains.

Love this place !
If you are looking for a great spot to watch the game with incredible food and awesome service look no further . The wings and smoked chicken tacos are out of this world . 
We've been here 7 or 8 times and it is consistently great every time . I highly recommend it and will definitely be back .

Looking for a vegan spot with some flair?
You should check out this chic spot in the market east location in philly. 

I went to this spot this past weekend and let me tell you, it was deliciously yummy. My friends and I ordered a variety of different meals from off the menu. The dishes are on the smaller side and they are considered to be tapas. 

Just something you should know: 
I really enjoyed this place, but I prefer to have a larger meal. Even though it was fantastic, you will be spending about $30 for a meal for one. 
This restaurant is definitely one of the most accommodating locations that I've been to for dinner. They had both, gluten and soy free individual menus. It really made it easier for my friends to have more options to consider. 

My order- 
PLEASE PLEASE, you need to get the bao bun with eggplant, it was so divine. The sauce is what made it, it was finger licking good. My second dish was pretty good, I got the potato gnocchi. 

You really should go, we honestly had a tasty experience. 

Just a tip: MAKE A RESERVATION.
And if you order the risotto, it's about 20 mins wait.

Went to see Craig Shoemaker on Saturday, November7, 2015.  This was the funniest time we have had in many years.  The entire audience was laughing so hard our jaws hurt and stomachs ached from all the laughing.  Craig was on stage for an hour and 45 minutes, with non-stop laughter.  If he is in our around your town make sure you get to his show.  Best comedian we have seen ever, and we have seen Seinfeld, Lewis  Black, Kathleen Madigan, and others, he's up their with the best.  Be wary of The Helium Club, when you go to the show floor you have a two drink minimum, which we didn't know and had already had drinks in their lobby bar first, but still great time because of Craig Shoemaker.
Great food. Wait staff very friendly and alert. Prices are good. Atmosphere very nice.
The lily is the best thing on the menu!! Many of the items sound odd but they taste heavenly. The line can get a bit long but it is totally worth it. Great atmosphere, food and staff.

Great food again.  Just too much food...amazingly, as we left my wife said "one less fish and something with artichokes..."  

That was what we said the last time we went!
Wait is a little long but it is well worth it...I recommend calling ahead with your order if you don't want to have a long wait...

Don't do it.  The dolma taste canned.  The hummos is just so average.  The prices are way too high.  If you have ever eaten good Greek food you will be so disappointed.  I don't get how this place stays in business and has been around for so long.  I really love Greek food and this is in my neighborhood.  I wish it were better.  

The regulars (owners?) who sit at the sidewalk tables during the day belch choking cigarette smoke that you can smell from doors away.  However, they are so sweet and super nice to my dog.  Really good seeming people.  I wish I had something nicer to say about the restaurant.

YUMM! I don't know how else to describe this place. Everything we had here was fantastic. Get the banana pudding, although I had no stomach space left it was worth leaving 10 pounds heavier to stuff my face with that pudding after the delicious chicken. Next time I'm in Nashville this will be a staple stop for sure.

Have been here twice, once for a business lunch and once during happy hr. Both times I was very satisfied with not only my food but also the service.

When I went for lunch, the restaurant was quite busy, but we still managed to get our food in a reasonable amount of time. The menu is similar to the Cheesecake Factory in that it's pretty extensive and you're likely to find something you like.

I ordered the Jambalaya lunch special ($8.95). Portion size was nice, and came with large pieces of chicken and shrimp, along with a side of garlic cheese bread. Delish! And just enough of a kick that I needed a few refills of my drink.

During happy hour, they had great deals on appetizers and beers, along with a burger special. Burger, fries, and a beer, for around $6. Can't beat that! Any place that serves a pretzel appetizer with different cheese sauces is a winner in my book as well.

Would definitely recommend the Elephant Bar if you're looking for a tasty, casual meal.
Best bbq chicken ever.  Reverend Mel is so kind and boy can he cook.  I bought the last of his chicken and have been pinching it.  Collards and Potatoe Salad not bad either.
Good oysters at a reasonable price.  Fried shrimp and oyster po'boy was really good too.  Definitely a place worth checking out.
Love it...wish they would deliver.  Pizza and antipasto salad with the best dressing.

I went here on Mothers day for lunch and my experience was very poor. The restaurant was empty and the employees clearly did not want to be there. It food took forever to get ready and the emplyees were not welcoming at all. I will not be returning to eat here again.
Excellent pizza, turkey club sandwich uses real turkey not that luncheon roll stuff, they have scoop-able Richman's ice cream and some homemade desserts that are delicious. Great takeout service.

A beautiful sunny Saturday morning in Tampa and California tacos go hand-in-hand!

I just arrived back in from Costa Rica last night and was looking expectantly for more fresh ingredients in a taco today. I decided to swing by California tacos and was not disappointed! The amped up tacos give you extra vegetables like shredded cabbage and pico. Choose from fish, chicken, Carnitas, carne asada,  beef, etc. nestled between double corn tortillas to hold it all together. The staff was super friendly and helpful! My tacos were overflowing with fresh ingredients and topped with guacamole and cheese. Excellent!

I also love the really casual picnic tables set up just off the road. It really makes you feel like you're kicking back and relaxing!

Cute little cafe off the 101 on the way to Santa Barbara. Good selection of sandwiches and a decent kids menu. The Indian Summerland chicken sandwich was decent. Came with some good veggies including mushrooms and spinach and Swiss cheese. The cheddar broccoli soup of the day was pretty average. They have outdoor seating which is nice on a sunny day. The charging for water thing was a bit annoying but understandable due to the drought.

This was always my go to Chinese Buffet when I lived down the road from it. Its a smaller buffet compared to some of the others around, which I like because they seem to keep the food fresher. I also like that I can get my own drinks here and don't have to worry about a waitress. Also I like that they have the traditional shaped Crab Rangoons here instead of the triangle shaped ones. If you go here I do recommend going as soon as it opens or shortly after. That's when the food is the freshest and they'll have everything you want available, but that goes for all Chinese Buffets. I tend to stay away from any Chinese Buffets during dinner because I don't know how long the food has been sitting on the buffet and sometimes they are not as good at replacing food that has ran out during dinner. As far as the Chinese Buffets I've been to this is one of the better ones and I'll will be back to it for sure.

Celiacs beware!
Well, the service was great. Our waiter was attentive and quick and was able to answer all of our questions and offer gluten free options readily. probably because there were very few options. To be fair, he did offer that there was gluten Free pasta available but that it was not very good and he had received numerous complaints from customers. I've had bad gluten free pasta and its awful so I trusted him.

I ended up ordering the "Mixed GrillSkewers of grilled steak and chicken marinated in Italian herbs and extra-virgin olive oil. Served with broccoli and grilled vegetables.". It was below average. I ordered the steak medium rare, it came medium and the chicken was overdone. The broccoli was raw and the grilled veggies were slimy and too soft. The usual salad was fine and fresh and our server was kind enough to put the croutons on the side somy companions could have them. 

Admittedly, if you walk into an "Italian" restaurant- chances are you're looking for pasta; if the Olive Garden would invest in a decent gluten free pasta I would go back but until then, it's not an option for me.
Only place around open past 10. Ended up tasting pretty good too. However I asked for the house hot mustard and I got honey mustard instead.. that was not pleasant.

I spend 50$ today on my order they forgot my taco and I also order a steak burrito which I was really looking forward to eating they gave me chicken burrito the chicken was dry there was no beans in my burrito when there was supposed to be. My jalapeno poppers were surrounded in grease and had thick nasty grease stuck to the bottom of it. This was not a good experience for me at all I will probably never order food from here again. I was really disappointed.

This place was wonderful!!! I am in love!!! So I walked in and the decor was warm and inviting.  I was serviced by the owner and she was sweet and accommodated my requests.  I ordered a Caesar salad and it was so fresh and filling.  The salad dressing was organic.  The owner gave me a free organic soda and I must admit that it tasted wonderful!!! I recommend that everyone go to this place because this is a true treat!!!

I have been here dozens of times without issue, several for pickup, but the last couple of times I've tried to get a pickup order (one via the web, the other via the app), I walked in to find a ton of people waiting and no food on the pickup shelving.

Nobody said anything to the people just waiting around, many without masks. I asked the guy behind the counter, he tried to find my order, but after scrolling through dozens of orders, he couldn't find me.

I didn't feel it was safe to hang around and get it sorted out, so I left.

I've had many good experiences at this location, so I tried again the following week. I placed my order via the app and I arrived to find the same scene - dozens of people waiting. Nobody said anything to me, but the lady behind the counter said they had over 100 orders they had to get through. 

Is the problem with the software or the people who don't know how to fill orders? I don't know. Either way, something needs to be fixed at this location. 

Regarding the people here, everybody I've dealt with has always been very nice, even on the last couple of visits.

Meh is right. I took Erika K here so I could get a couple drinks in her so she would forget about all the things I didn't finish on my 'list'. The margaritas were fairly decent and BIG, which was awesome. They taste like standard margaritas, nothing special but good enough to quench our thirst on a hot evening.

The patio is really nice. There were fans everywhere so it was fairly cool on a 90+ degF night. We really liked the atmosphere. It was fun to sit at the bar and munch on chips and salsa. The salsa was OK. I am starting to think every Americanized Mexican place in STL gets there salsa from the same place or uses the same recipe...

We were seated inside, that's when things went downhill. It was packed, loud and hotter than outside. We were seated in an isle and servers were always flying past us but no one stopped to bring us water or anything. We had to flag a guy down to take our order. 

The food was just OK. Standard American Mexican. Nothing memorable...

Next time I would never leave the patio and guzzle margs all night...

Tavolino continues to be one of our favorite Happy Hour locations in Tucson. Kudos to Benjamin, our waiter, and to Jonathan, the resident sommelier, for their exceptional service!

Bob & Candi H.

Not for me. I ordered the special of Pork Belly with grits and an egg and it just didn't belong together and was below average. The pork belly was tough and the grits with the egg just didn't have any oomph to it. Weird flavor and while edible, not really enjoyable.

My wife had the eggs and potatoes with turkey chorizo. I tired the chorizo and same thing...did nothing for me.

My kids had the French toast...boring and bland, just a soggy sponge.

2 breakfast entrees, 2 kids meals, 2 milks, 2 coffees with tax and tip = $52

And served in a eco-whatever container. I'd like a plate please if I'm gonna shell out that kind of $ on meal number one.

No one really checked the cream for the coffee, so that ran out. No one checked the coffee either, both huge kettles ran out too. And it's a small place so people waiting for tables hover over you because there's no waiting area.

I'm not returning here.

I decided to try this place out since it was nearby, knowing nothing about it, and was pleasantly surprised to receive the best pizza I've had in a while. Castrillo's should be a frequent stop for anyone in the greater Sylvan area.
Great selection of local beers on tap. Friendly attentive service from the owner.  Food was good, will be back!

Dropped in for lunch & ordered the bento box w/ BFC.  Two pieces of fried chicken with a sweet and spicy sauce on a bed of macaroni salad, two fishcake balls, pickled daikon (I think), broccoli & tomatoes, and steamed white rice.  Everything tasted like I imagined it would, but the fried chicken was a little tough and dry.  The rice was also tough, dry, and chewy; it seemed like it was held too long or maybe cooked with not enough water.  This is an Asian restaurant...the rice needs to be cooked and served correctly.
The coffee is always wonderful, the service is always friendly and warm, and the atmosphere is perfect for this introvert that still wants to be out of the house.

Just happened to wander by this place, and am happy we did. Friendly service, comfy chairs in the back, and food and beverage wise:

4 stars for the cinnamon muffin
4 stars for their sweet chai latte

The sticky buns looked great ...

Because Yelp requires at least one star. It does not deserve one. I LOVE caribbean food whether in the states or in the Caribbean....LOOVE LOOVE....this was NOT LOVE. Had the wait ONLY been the issue I would have called it a bad night for them but this was far beyond it. Having been in the F&B industry it's rare I write a bad review, but this needed to be said. 

1. I waited for my food to be delivered it took 2hours and I live 10min away
2. THE ORDER WAS WRONG! I asked for cabbage AND mix veggies, no rice and peas, but instead they gave me ONLY mix veggies which by the way are freezer bag bought from the grocery store and tasted like it. 
3. All of my food clearly was COLD and Roti SOGGY
4. An order of plantains was 4 small pieces, wasn't cooked through
5. Curry Chicken? I didn't even realize there was curry on the Chicken....maybe it was because of the microwave....I doubt that. 
6. I order the large portion...NOT large at all had three pieces of chicken only one piece was average size. 
7. I definitely will not be going there again. Only thing I didn't regret was the tip to the delivery guy, he was cute.
It's great to have such a high quality place in Jefferson Parish.  When I'm looking to pay "restaurant prices" for something in a plastic box in the refrigeration section, this is my go-to store.

This place used to be pretty good, but tonight I got a banh mi sandwich and it was awful. No flavor and the bread was rock hard. I know it's hard to keep bread fresh, but once it's stale, just tell folks sandwiches aren't available.

The bomb. Chicken wings and fried catfish... yum. Delicious fries.. just the right thickness and well seasoned. Nice employees. Cool murals abound. Ran out of sweet tea (must be good), but happy with fruit punch. Great, hot food.

I ordered the Graham Central Express, which is a Graham cracker blended vanilla ice cream. The mouthfeel was smooth. There was just enough dryness from the cracker blend to be interesting. The texture was varied between bouts of smooth ice cream and sugary chunks. Very good.

Tei too is a great place to stop by for lunch or dinner! Great prices, and generous portions.
 The staff is very alert and helpful! My favorite dish they have is their pineapple fried rice with tofu! The pineapple adds just the right amount of sweetness, and the cashews and green onions add a great texture. Definitely recommend, like I said generous portions so you won't leave feeling hungry.
Food is delicious! So are the drinks! If you sit at a table the wait staff is not that great. Sit at the bar, Tara is awesome!

The menu doesn't do this place justice. We did 3 appetizers and 2 entrees and none of them were disappointing. The meatballs were juicy, the 'Nduja toast was the bomb, the local tomatoes were delicious, the pizza was out of this world and the shells well if I could get a bowl of that cheese sauce I'd be in heaven. 

Go try it out. We had a great server and the food was delicious and came out of the kitchen fast.

Quick version: I'm going with two stars because the service was excellent, kids meals come with the sides in a paper boat that will entertain a three year old for a bit, and the fact that they use text message to tell you when your table is ready so you don't have to sit there.  Pulling it down; paid parking, tourist trap, very weak and expensive drinks, bland uninspired chain food.  I'm not giving it stars for location partially on the water because you can go across the channel to Gators (five minute walk) to get the same view, much better and cheaper drinks, free parking, marginally better food.  If you don't need to redeem or accrue Landry's loyalty points, Gators would be my recommendation.

Anyway, how does this place stay in business?  Tourists apparently.  Went on a early Wednesday evening and it was packed with a 10 minute wait, and I know no locals that have ever gone here twice.  Only reason I went is because I had my $25 annual Landry's Club birthday dollars that were going to expire the next day, so it was a choice between come here or drive 45 minutes to the great Mitchell's Seafood in Tampa.  

You know this is a tourist trap as soon as you walk through the door; that's when you run into the gift shop selling every Bubba Gump-related item you can think of from clothing to tumblers.  Forrest Gump nostalgia must be a pretty powerful force if people want to wear it.

It gets worse when you open the menu.  Most of the drinks here involve 'souvenir' cups, or if you want to go over the top, 'projection light' souvenir cups that both light your drink up and shine the Bubba logo down on the table when you lift it up.  Are there really people who want to spend $18 on a weak drink to get the light up cup?!?!?!  Apparently yes since this place has been here for years now.

Okay, enough of my rant.  Drinks first; like I said, expensive, and weak.  Hell, a 20oz Bud Light draft is almost $10.  I made the mistake of ordering a long island; tasted like a mix of Pepsi and lemonade with no discernible booze, and I paid $14 for that lack of enjoyment.

Food, had shrimp scampi, pizza/fries kids meal for my kid.  The shimp scampi had what appeared to be capers, but I couldn't taste them unless I ate one by itself, no real hint of garlic either; the whole dish was just completely bland like the ingredients had been thrown in last minute after cooking the pasta.  Perhaps this is because old folks don't like strong tastes and were sending it back to remove the flavor?  Who knows, but to me it tasted like generic pasta with mild hints of butter and shrimp.  The kids meal was like what you'd expect from any Chili's, TGI Fridays, Applebees, etc. but the sides do come in a little paper boat that my three year old found fascinating, so there's that.

The service was excellent, no complaints there.  I feel bad for the servers, part of the theme involves them memorizing obscure Forrest Gump trivia and asking if you want to challenge them.  Ugh; gave a 25% tip because I think they deserve extra for enduring that hundreds of times a day.

Last but not least, leaving reminded me of my last complaint; parking.  Bubba's is served by the John's Pass Boardwalk establishment, and their parking garage is paid, with no validation by the restaurant.  They charge $1 per 20 minutes and they round up.  The garage is very cramped and slow, so you will literally waste about ten minutes from the time your ticket is printed until the time you check in with the hostess at Bubba's.  If you go during a busy time of day, I estimate you'll spend about $5 of time amongst the garage, waiting for a table, waiting for food, and leaving.

I am so mad at my wife. She lived in Miami for many many years and was entrenched in the Cuban culture down there. And she didn't tell me about this restaurant until three years into our marriage. 

Came in, restaurants clean bathrooms are clean. 

Got empanadas for the appetizers, the chicken version completely amazing Chrispy  flaky crust, seasoned chicken. I got the Imperial polo dish. Covered in cheese that rice was spiced perfectly the chicken was cooked to perfection l. 

In closing I ended up buying three more empanadas to go home with me my wife bought enough to go home with her to have for dinner. 

In short absolutely amazing no complaints no issues waitress was great. It's  beyond perfect.
Their traditional gyro platter and chicken wings are yummy. I would say the only criticism I would have is the tzatziki sauce is very thin and not a lot of flavor.

Excellent food and service

A tip - order a spice level lower than what you would generally order as medium had my eyes watering and I eat spicy food on a regular basis (desi)
This is an awesome place! The pickle soup is delicious. Their egg salad and all of their green salads are delicious. I dream of their Almond Joy Sundae. Can't go wrong !

Although the customer service was phenomenal, a basic cheesesteak is not worth $9+ at Liberty Cheesesteak. 

 I basically paid $9+ (not including side) for a dry cheesesteak with very minimal amount of cheese.  I had to keep opening the sandwich and taking bites at parts where I just might get to taste cheese.   After all, it is a cheesesteak and if it's going to be called one, the customer should at least be able to taste cheese.

I suggest that the  owner  take a trip to Jersey Mikes or J Michael's in Wilmington, North Carolina to get ideas on a) what a cheesesteak is supposed to taste like and b) how to minimize or even maximize market price with customer satisfaction and expectation.  For instance, I pay around $7 for a cheesesteak at the abovementioned restaurants.  At Jersey Mikes, I received a gracious amount of melted Provolone cheese, peppers, onions, and the sandwich wasn't dry - not to mention it was bigger & cheaper than Liberty's.  At J Michael's, I also received a sandwich the same size as the one at Liberty's, except it comes with lettuce, mayo, other condiments of your choice, a liberal amount of melted cheese, etc - not to mention the cheaper price.  

I must add that you should still try Liberty Cheesesteak if for nothing more than  to support the young staff and small business owner.  They were extremely nice and good looking.  

That way, you can make your own observations and conclusions about whether you would visit Liberty again or recommend it to a friend.

If you have 35 minutes to wait for a simple burger and fries, this may be the place for you!
Didn't order anything fancy, just a burger with cheese, onions, lettuce, tomato and mayo, a large fries, and a bottled water. Why oh why should any burger place take 35 minutes to serve up the food????
Checked on it after 20 minutes - was told they got backed up on fries. When the other person in our party checked on their order 10 minutes later, they were told they were backed up on onion rings.
Decent food but NOT WORTH THE WAIT. Never again, BurgerFi, you blew your chance!

This Burger King is beautiful but the staff  is very bad.
The staff is grosero ,  adicional my orden is wrong. Bad staff
I have always heard good things. Took a long time to get the food, Fried Chicken was horrible and the hush puppies tasted like seafood. First time and last time.

I love kolaches! My favorite is the pizza one, because I LOVE PIZZA! It is best to stop by early since that is where you'll get the best selection possible.  The cost does add up if you're buying some for work, but everyone is happy when they're eating it. 

Another reviewer said to try the sticky buns - YES! This is a must! It reminds me of the rolls my dad used to buy from the local bakery back home (but they weren't sticky buns). 

The service is not that bad for the times I have been there. If you go there close to closing, maybe you might feel a little horrible.

We were getting a little cabin fever with this week's dreary weather and decided to get out and watch the Blues Blackhawks game. They have a $5.00 special on Busch pitchers during the game. The wife had a Rueben sandwich and I had their black and bleu burger. She's had better Rueben's before but this one wasn't bad either; she's a bit of a Reuben connoisseur. I thought my burger was really good, cooked perfect with a tasty blue cheese spread and thick cut bacon on top. The top bun was a little dry, but not that big of a deal for me. I like this place; it has a beautiful dark wood bar up front with three large tv's over it, there's exposed brick and a large room upstairs with more seating.  It's not an overwhelming menu, but has a lot of good choices and delicious sounding nightly specials. Form what I understand, the chef here used to be with Monarch before it became an event space. We'll see you guys again.

Great service, great food, great view not sure why there are some not so great reviews it was beyond what I expected but all Lombardo's family restaurants I've been to are top notch. We will return, with friends.
Great food at this Thai restaurant.  Decor is very tired.  Could use a little freshening up.

Loved peche, but I wouldn't expect anything less from the team that brought us Cochon. We got to trya. Bunch of things and although I'm sure there are a lot of other great items as it is. Wonderful menu, this will makes. Great meal

Catfish smothered with white rice.
Drum
Tuna dip
Cappelini w/ crab
Fried bread- this might be one of the best things I have ever eaten.
Artichoke and crab fritters
Squash bacon rice casserole

The Shrimp toast was a little bit of a let down as were the red shrimp. But they might have just been overlooked.

A new must for Nola.

Copper Kettle, what happened? Went to brunch yesterday and was highly disappointed with the food. Burnt bacon with the texture of a kettle crisp and dry sausage patties, runny gravy and hash brown casserole, dry, tasteless salmon and stale bagels all for $17 a pop. This is the same thing that I would expect from a school cafeteria in which you would be charged much less. Saving grace, as always, was service but really, how much work can one do on a buffet except remove plates and keep glasses of water filled. For food that is highly unhealthy and evocative of school trip memories to Shoney's breakfast bar from the late 80s, early 90s should not be priced so stratospherically. A suggestion, improve on food value by hiring a cook who doesn't sacrifice quality for quantity and creates and serves food that is good value for money yet tasty and somewhat fresh. Yesterday's brunch should have been served by middled-aged women with questionable moods and hair nets gussied up in processed food-stained white aprons asking for your meal ticket to stamp. Bad form Copper Kettle, bad form.

This is my new favorite Nashville BBQ joint. We got a platter for 4 so we got to try a little of everything! Our absolute favorites included the pulled pork, brisket, dry rub ribs, and the broccoli salad. That being said, we ate every last bite on our plates (even though we probably shouldn't have). We also got a redneck taco which was my absolute favorite by far - great combo of flavors. Our least favorites were the mac and cheese and potato salad; the wings were pretty standard as well - although we did like the rub on them. Definitely check out Martin's if you are in the area. We will be back - hopefully soon!

Tried Jerry's Bar for dinner this time. I ordered the Fried Chicken Sandwich with fries. The chicken is dipped in hot-n-honey sauce then topped with charred scallion aioli, lettuce, and tomato all on a brioche bun. I found the chicken too thin with mostly breading and the sauce had a nice tang, but a little too heavy. Maybe the classic slaw and pickles would be better topping than the lettuce & tomato as they did not add much.

My 400th review goes to Cajun Kitchen! This review is long overdue and definitely worth mentioning. It is afterall one of our most popular spots in town for breakfast. 

I don't come here as often as I'd like, because the weekend is my preference to dine here, but that's when it gets really busy. Long lines and wait time, no thank you. I highly recommend coming here on a weekday if you can swing it. My son was craving beignets and their California benedict, and luckily it was on a weekday so I called in the order ahead of time. That would be the other option if you are coming here on the weekend and pressed for time. 

Outside dining is available in the parking lot, where a nice little parklet is set up. As of right now 6.15.21 indoor dining is also available with limited seating. 

The food was nicely prepared and still warm by the time I got home. I loved the beignets! I'm glad they didn't go heavy on the powdered sugar. They were lightly dusted and the warm strawberries n banana topping was excellent! 

My son also enjoyed his California Benedict and hash browns. As for me I didn't order anything on my latest visit here, but the meals I've had in the past have all been delicious. Looking forward to coming back sooner than later, now that I know their food to go is just as well prepared as dining at the restaurant.

I wanted to like this bar. I was excited when it opened and helped bring life to its little alley. I'm also guessing it's locally owned, so it makes me feel sad-- even guilty--  to give a poor score.  But maybe this feedback will help!

Five times, I've gone and the following have been consistent:

1. Bartenders are unfriendly. I always approach with a smile, but I'm always met with a frown, as if I'm inconveniencing them with my order. I understand the pressure of bartending, but I've never had trouble smiling at my patrons or acknowledging them with brief eye contact during their order. Here-- consistently, the bartenders are almost defiantly unfriendly. 

As a girl, I understand sometimes it's easier to be stone faced so that patrons don't mistake friendliness for flirtation. But I've never ordered a drink there and felt it was a positive experience. 

I see other reviewers saying the service was lovely, so I'm just confused-- maybe it's a just a dice roll? Maybe I've just caught people at bad times? But I can only speak to my experiences. 

2. The outdoor bathrooms are filthy and never have soap and usually only one or two stalls have toilet paper.  I seriously hope the staff have their own private bathroom, because in all my visits, there has never once been soap in the bathroom. Not once in my 5 visits. 

Since they are unisex bathrooms, there's also the delightful adventure of dodging pee puddles on the floor from very sober and clean people who forget to aim. There aren't hooks in all stalls to hold bags, so it's interesting to hold your bag, tiptoe hop to the toilet, and pray that nothing touches the pee soaked floor. 

Photo included for your pleasure. From Sat, Aug 25th @11:24 pm. (I shutter to imagine what it looked like upon close.) and don't forget the fun fact that there is never soap. Wish I had taken a picture of the defeated SoftSoap bottle that had been decapitated, used up, and left thrown on the counter by about 10PM. Mind you, my first trip to the restroom was around 10 (no soap then) and my second trip when I took that picture was around 11:30. Still no soap. No one could wash their hands that entire time. Or probably the whole rest of the night. 

The drinks aren't particularly well made. 

I've given two stars because one time they had a great DJ outside, and it made me happy. 

Note: they used to have an attendant for a few hours working there passing out paper towels, but in exchange for passing you a paper towel, they expected a tip. Normally I wouldn't mind, but for such a dumpy bathroom, with no soap, with pee on the floor, down a Tucson alley, that is comical to me that I'd have to tip for a paper towel. 

I'd still say go here rather than any of the chains downtown-- Support Local Business! But that's where my recommendation would end at this time.
Great family run business. Awesome food, great service and a nice family friendly place to eat.

I feel like I can't give this place an accurate rating and am willing to come back out to eat here again to better review this place. In Tucson, I am traveling with two Puerto Rican's and a Colombian. So of course this place was picked come dinner time. It was cute to see them so excited for the food. 
I'd like to think I'm pretty cultured. I always enjoyed carne asada so I had ordered that with plantains and fries. I guess I'm used to the Americanized version because I wasn't expecting what I got. The meat was almost sour tasting due to the seasoning they used. I'm used to the steak being grilled and topped with some vegetable or onions. The plantains were pretty good. And the fries were average. I was underwhelmed with my food. However, my friends thoroughly enjoyed their food. 
I had a couple of bites of their food and it was flavorful. I definitely just ordered the wrong thing.
The waiter and waitress we had were both very nice and the wait for food wasn't long at all. I'd love to see how this place night life is like. If I have time to come back before leaving Arizona, I will definitely give this place another go.

Our second visit in the hopes that it would have improved since just after opening. Our server was a really nice guy, not very attentive but overall pleasant. Our menus were torn and covered in food stains - not nice at all. The place looked dingy and dirty - and way worse than in the Crust days. My husband's burger and tots came out about 20 minutes before my pizza and my daughter's calzone. He liked his burger but it was nothing special. When the other food finally came out my pizza was soggy and the slices drooped like no pizza I have ever seen. The cheese was orange despite being called a mozzarella blend. It was huge but not at all tasty and very greasy. I only ate 2 pieces because I was starving. The dough on my daugter's calzone was raw so she ate very little. The server did explain that it was the cook's first day and they did comp the calzone, but who was supervising the new cook? Evidently no one. We decided to give them a second chance but there will definitely not be a third.
Not bad for the price. Problem I have is the amount of salt they have in the sauces. There are tons of options and a Lot of sauces you can add which lets you make smaller bowls and test often.

I love the happy hour margs for$5, but someone has to tell some of the servers that you can get blended margs on happy hour just not frozen I guess? I always eat too much, but you can't go wrong with the nachos n fajitas!  I am staying next door I just wish they still had margs to go

I've been here twice now. The first time was when they first opened. The beers and the food were good and reasonable prices.  Great drink specials.  But the service was slow.  Understandable for a new restaurant.  

The second time I was never treated so rudely In a restaurant in my life.  I opened a tab and had a few drinks. When I went to close my tab there were drinks and shots on my tab that I did not order or consume.  I let the staff know and the manager came over and told me he'd take care of it.  Then my boyfriend closed his tab ( as he got there before me and had opened his own ) and the items removed were put on his tab ! We had the manager come back over and he said " I think you drank too much and don't know what you had and you're both liars !" unbelievable!  I have better things to do then waste time arguing over 15 dollars.  It's the principle of it.  They should no be adding things to anyone's tab without them giving their name and authorizing it.  I could not believe he was a manager.  That is terrible customer service.   The bartender was a doll though.  She was polite and wasn't condescending.  I made sure to leave her a generous tip so she wasn't to blame or thought I was trying to get one over on them.  Basically they need to be more careful there and realize that they make mistakes.   My advice - being cash for the bar. Don't open a tab !

The atmosphere is completely opposite of most Caribbean restaurants. It is the Perfect setting for a romantic dinner, wedding party, etc. The food is immaculate and had great presentation (I ordered the oxtail). The owners really catered to my experience and I will be revisiting this restaurant in the future.

my family has been in love with their chicken w/ eggplant in garlic sauce since i was a child - this dish alone merits 5 stars. and thanks to my workplace, i've recently grown fond of their curry chicken & potato, pan fried dumplings, filet fish w/ tofu, and the rest of their totally cheap, totally tasty menu.

can't say much about their dining-in service as i've only eaten in a small handful of times back in high school, but their take-out service is great. my favorite hole-in-the-wall place in philly!
Went in yesterday for lunch, noticed none of the employees were wearing masks so took my business elsewhere.

I was visiting my parents and decided to check out a place close by. The reviews looked great so I took a chance.

I ordered the Calamari to start. It was WAY OVERCOOKED and too salty.  Ordered the half rack of ribs and fried shrimp combo. Ribs were dry and covered with too much sauce..almost to hide the fact that they were dry.

But the server was great. And the beer was cold. 

Will I come back? Don't think I will. Not based on my experience. But it may be fine for someone else. Just not me.

I've been to Philadelphia twice, and I've been to Tequilas twice. This is such a great place. The atmosphere is vibrant and fun. More upscale decore, but not pretentious. I've always gone with a party of 4 so we can try different foods, and I haven't had anything I didn't like. Nice portions. And they're guacomole is amazing. I can't believe how many mexican places can mess up guacomole, but Tequilas does it right!

Their margaritas are in a class of there own... the best margarita I've ever had! You can actually taste the agave. And it you are thirsty :) or go with a gruop, be sure to get their tower. It serves 8 drinks at about half the price of order single margaritas. Very good deal. 

If you have the chance, make sure you eat here!

Amazing food at a pay what you can cafe. The different themes make a fun assortment of different kinds of meals. The deserts are always amazing and supplied by CakeNV. Don't miss this meal, it comes around once every two months.  Volunteers serving are very kind and the social environment makes meeting new people fun.

Honestly not sure why this place has gotten such horrible reviews. I've been going here for years and have been happy with the buffet which had tons of options. I just went here a few days ago and ordered baigan bharta which was delicious. I also really like their chicken biryani. I've had a lot of Indian food around the area and this is one of my favorites.

Wonderful place in downtown Tarpon Springs!  Delicious food and quaint atmosphere. Their paninis are so good and made even better with all if their olive oil and balsamic selections. Cheesecake is SO yummy too!  We will definitely be back!  :)

So the food here is pretty interesting. There is a nice mix of different types of Asian cuisines represented here. The Roti Canai was delicious. The sort of delicious where I wanted to order three more. Just for myself! I split the Mango Tofu with a friend. The tofu is cooked with mango, peppers, and some delicious sauce. It was great. My friend ordered the Thai Basil Curry with beef - and she was definitely happy with it. 

I'd go back again to try the rest of their extensive menu. 

Word to the wise: they are a huge restaurant - and they seem to have a small staff. You may end up waiting for a while.

I really was excited to visit the taco bus I heard good things about so I was anxious to finally visit. Unfortunately, I thought my food lacked flavor and my tacos were very watery and messy. I had the beef flour taco along with the shrimp and was not blown away by any means necessary. I will say however the ambiance was very nice and I enjoyed the area and how it had character.
Best eggplant parm in the city. Great service, once they learn your name, they'll never forget it. And the desserts are heavenly.
Get take-out from here about once a month or so but randomly like to dine-in. Very friendly & food is wonderful. Love their pizza, wings, & lasagna. Prices are great.

Really liked the pizza. Had 2 pieces of the pepperoni pizza and a drink for the lunch special for just $6. Some of the best tasting pizza I have had (I had the thinner hand tossed), very suprised how good it was. Just visiting in the area, but wish they had this in the Twin Cities area.

This was such a cool cafe with not only great coffee but some interesting choices for breakfast. My chicken strip waffle and my wife's breakfast wrap were the best breakfast we had during our trip. Seriously, we were pleasantly shocked and commented same to the wait staff. The place is a must see during any stay in Nashville. Place was super clean and staff super friendly. This will be a regular stop for us.

Yummies is by far the best thing I have had in the Compton area yet.

You wouldn't really even know its there either. Its right at Compton and Shennandoh, but tucked away behind some tree's or hedges. 

They have a menu that changes everyday that is already made and hot and ready to serve. Its amazing! This feels like the home cooked meals you have when you go to visit your parents down south. I just love it!

I have been there on a Sunday and a Friday. The Sunday had a turkey dinner, complete with dressing and the works! On any given day they give you a choice of what main course you want then you get 3 sides and bread! Its soo good. I walked out stuffed and with a smile on my face both times. On Fridays they had a huge array of BBQ items to choose from. I had the BBQ Pork Steaks, Mac n cheese, corn, potato salad and corn bread. AMAZING! 

I highly reccomend this place. That atomosphere could use some help, theres a lot of mismatch going on, but their a small business just starting out, so give them the benefit of the doubt. Its really worth it. The staff is super friendly as well!

Ran in here tonight to pick up some dice & look at some minis. 

The good: Several tables, have a large war room downstairs for private events(didn't go downstairs to see it though), locally owned, have a cafe onsite for gaming munchies, the arches/architecture separating the kitchen from the main room, & the Fountain Square neighbourhood

The bad: Small selection(They'll probably order stuff for you though.) No used minis for sale, food selection is stereotypical gaming stuff- hamburgers, nachos, pizza, soda, ice cream, energy drinks,( Nachos w/o meat & mushrooms on pizza only vegetarian options) & the guy who rang us up seemed indifferent, non-talkative & bored. 

Bottom Line: OK if you need to grab something common like a  D&D players' handbook or dice & aren't particular about styles or colours. While they do have some oddities & unusual card games, & having food onsite is a brilliant idea, the slapdash nature of the endeavour leaves me wanting more, & closer. Why are there not really any awesome gaming places inside the loop?
Eh, it's ok, for getting Mexican specialty items and a taco to go but I don't think it's any more than 3 stars...

This places service sucks. We been coming here for 4 years about 6 times or more a year and this is the second time they lost our reservation. Do not come here if you want professional service even if the food is good. Service sucks. We been waiting an hour now for our reservation that we were early for. We have watched 6 groups come in after us and already get seated ahead of us.  Go to shoguns restaurant better service and same exact food in St. Louis also more locations.

I have been at the PUB several times over the past 22 years, almost yearly.  My husband was born and raised in Merchantville, so we have came back to the area quite often.  We have NEVER had a bad experience.  Yeah there might have been a time where our steak was not cooked to our preference but never complained or sent back.  Besides that the steaks are quite large, no complaints.  Tonight our experience was exceptional!!!  Started out with pre dinner cocktails at the lounge before heading to the dining room.  A little pricey, yeah but boy were they strong.  Into dinner.  The salad bar was fresh and clean!  The Caesar salad was awesome.  I had the burgundy street sirloin and husband had the manager's special prime rib.  Medium rare on both.  They came exactly that.  Again, only complaint was that the steaks are large.  Service was excellent.  Patti was on spot.  She popped from nowhere and took glasses and plates when they were emptied.  The PUB is an old school steak house.  It's really an awesome experience!!  Yeah the outside appearance might scare you off but try the restaurant out!!  Our UBER driver said the exact same thing.

Bluebeard! Come to Denver! Here's a list of things you'll need to pack...

- Sexy atmosphere including vintage typewriters
- Amelia's fresh baked bread (so I guess Amelia needs to move too)
- the elk and pork salami
- the roasted beets salad (with oyster mushrooms, mixed field greens, feta, marcona almonds, balsamic truffle vinaigrette, crispy shallots)
- brussels sprouts agrodolce 
- roasted cauliflower, anchovy, pine nuts, capers, mint, parmesan
- your great craft cocktails

Listen, with your love of craft beers you'll fit in just fine here in Denver. Don't worry about making friends, I've got plenty that I know would just eat you up! 

What's that? You love Indianapolis too much too leave? Okay, okay, I guess I'll just have to visit you when in Indy, but if you ever change your mind give me a holler. Until then I'll just be jealous of Brittany S....

If you are looking for a beautiful space with delicious food and excellent service and happen to be in Indianapolis I would highly recommend checking out Bluebeard. It's a lovely spot for lunch, dinner, or a snack!

This is the absolute best breakfast in Louisiana!!! My husband and I were sad to see they had moved from the New Orleans location but did a search and found them in Metairie!! I tried something new and got a mushroom omelet with cheese, YUM! My husband got his usual from years past Mexican Omelet, not a crumb left!!!! Was Great seeing Ricky and Lou, made our honeymoon even better!!!

Tasty coffee, baked goods from Whisk Bakery, inviting atmosphere. 

Ask for the Honey Latte.
Pretty good steak (had the Sirloin).  Cooked right and the usual trimmings (spuds and bread).  This place can get loud (bad acoustics) so be aware.  Worth the stop when in Tucson.

My wife and I ate here twice last month while on vacation. We had gumbo, oysters, fish of the day, cold beer. The food was good and fine and so was the service...the first night. The second night was a Saturday and the guy rushed us through the meal apparently in an effort to turn over the table. So I deliberately stalled and ate very slowly...I eat somewhat slowly anyhow. Ease up! Is this not the big easy??
Good food and a good atmosphere.  We come here every time we are in the city for a doctors appointment

I'm a tenure track professor at Penn who's lived in NW Philly for the past two years.  After living in Ann Arbor, MI, I was used to having a wide variety of cafes and bookstores to work in, but hadn't yet found a great place in Philly. After a VERY productive four hour Sunday afternoon work session, I have to say that Chapterhouse is that place!  I found a table near the window easily near an outlet, and first ordered a nice latte, then decaf and oatmeal.  Staff was friendly and knowledgeable about coffee, and encouraged me to hang out in order to finish work, even offering the wifi password without having to be asked.  I like a little background noise (it becomes white noise and makes me way more productive!), so the atmosphere worked for me.  Be warned -- the place is dog friendly so may not work for those with severe pet allergies.  It definitely lived up to all the Yelp reviews and my high expectations.  I will definitely be returning soon.

I love Duck donuts. Nice fresh warm donuts! I visited the location in KOP. I love smores do when i saw they had a smores version donut it was a no brainer. They staff was grwat as well. They had to make more donuts so the wait was a little longer than normal. So the guy gave me a extra donut for the inconvenience. Great gesture.

Over involved staff and underinvolved preparation. I am always skeptical when they tell me dishes will come out "as they are ready" to ensure that they are super fresh. No, what you're saying is that the kitchen doesn't know how to pace the meal and so you, the client, will eat whatever is put in front of you no matter its logical sequence. 

Sure enough, we had our appetizer in about 5 minutes and our entrees about 5 minutes after that (with appetizer still happily sitting in front of us). 

Then, the various staff took turns interrupting our conversation to see if they could clear our plates! They wanted us out in about 35 minutes. Literally, servers we never saw before would swing by and try to clear the plates. It's like they were keebler elves ready to swoop in. 

The effect? A rushed, impatient, (although pleasantly quiet!) experience with average execution on the food. Was it bad? No, not bad at all....just not memorable or noteworthy.

The food at Himalayan is reasonably good, but they can't get a takeout order ready on time - EVER.  Add 15-20 minutes to whatever they tell you, or you will sit listening to background music and looking at the carpet that desperately needs cleaning.  Time for a new place for Indian takeout.

Ordered on app (no curbside?). Gave my order to someone else...took 4 calls for someone to pick up phone in store...Mike, made my mother, who went to pick up order, wait In the lot (15mins) and didn't ask if she would like a drink, also offered No freebie, etc...I called later and I asked what he did after giving wrong order to someone (prepaid $52) and he said "we remade and and took it out to the car and everything."  The "and everything" made me laugh. It was already paid for man! 

And below is a veggie bowl and chicken bowl??? Terrible service and was cold and lacking any flavor. 

You can do better chipotle!

We worked all day and were in the area around 7pm on a Tuesday night.  I was starving to the point of falling over.  Yelp to the rescue!  This was the restaurant closest to our location at the time and off we went!

Upon entry we realized as middle agers we were the youngest clientele in there - no worries!  We didn't feel out of place and were quickly seated.
