It's on the louder side but still a great place for a catch up to a celebration!

I went to this restaurant for the first time last night, I wantend to try it for a while and I wasn't disappointed. All the dishes on the menu sounded really yummy, unfortunately, I have a dietary restriction and I couldn't find anything to suit my needs. I asked our server, Kelly, and she went above and beyond to find me something gluten free. The Chef was very kind and put together a special dish for me, it was very tasty and it was gluten free. I coulnd't have asked for more. Thank you Kelly and thanks to the Chef, you guys are great!
We have been to Jamaica several times, this food {at D's} was authentic.  The curry goat and jerk chicken should not be missed.  Very good food and service

If you have not been for happy  hourthen you must go it is truly fabulous ~ Champagne Danny is one of the best bartendars around and offering great reduced priced drinks and free noshes  6 days a week. Great Bar menu and if you wish to stay   they are child friendly and relaxed dress code~~
  In the dining rooms you can get dover sole meniere or a burger with a bag of fires whcih are both award winning
They are not French by the way they changed the menu over 5 years ago

Brunch for the win! 
An order at the counter style resturant that offers brunch all day, this place serves a smaller menu which clearly ensures top quality and care. The food is delicious! My friend got biscuits and gravy with over-medium eggs and I got a traditional breakfast with scrambled eggs, toast, turkey sausage and two potatoes. 
The potatoes were served in a style I'd never had - small yellow potatoes served whole but crispy and so well seasoned on the outside. Similar to a breakfast baked potato. YUM. 

We also got lattes which are served in to-go cups so that you can take them with you. They have both dairy and soy milk. 

The smaller, intimate atmosphere is clean and well kept, the bathroom is large and offers a changing table, and the staff is very friendly. I would recommend this place to anyone who wants quality breakfast food!

I'm only reviewing the location and the sushi, have not tried anything else. The sushi was really good, surprisingly good. The location was spacious and mostly empty. The staff was friendly and the presentation of the sushi in the plate was great. I would highly recommend this place. I had the spicy salmon roll and the eel avocado roll.
Food was excellent and reasonably priced.  Scallops were delicious.  Escargot was awesome.  Wish the early bird special was just a little longer!  Tough for working people to make it.

I like the consistency of Outback restaurants and this one hit the mark.  Filet was cooked properly, good cut.  Wedge salad  was fresh and tasty.  Sides were  good.  Service was attentive and filled my drinks without prompting.  Solid Outback in my opinion.

OK I've seen the reviews so far and quite frankly there isn't a place in or out of Tampa that I would consider to be great Mexican with the exception of one surprising place (Mekinitas) that I have to go back to to see if it was a fluke.  Anyway, back to Cantina Laredo's.  Yeah, it may not be "gourmet" but the Camaron Poblano Carne Asada is really delicious and enough that my husband and I end up splitting the dish.  We also really enjoy the guacamole made at the table so I think if you are going for taco's then yeah, it's probably not any different than going to any one of the 100 other mexican places in Tampa.  Now as for the margarita's....  I am going to disagree with whoever said they weren't fresh or good.  The margaritas are one of the major reasons we go there... They use fresh squeezed lime juice, Patron Silver...  and after two of them the night turns into a party.  We go at least once a month.  If I could give 3.5 stars I would.  I definitely think it's better than OK.

I was here fir a kinda wedding party.  I liked the look of the place but the service was a little to be desired.  Since I love my buffalo wings and truly how can you screw them up.  I order and order if hit wings, I told my waitress that u wanted them well well done, I guess to some that means raw.  I had to send them back to have them done some more after 15 min I got them and truly I was disappointed.  The so call hot wings were more like vinegar wings. I only had two and could not eat more.  Once I had to go to the bathroom I found myself walking on a river of pee, toilet water and who knows what.  I don't know if it was a bad night or what but really, really.

Must admit, we only wound up here because the place next door is a DD&D place and, contrary to their Yelp, were closed! Happy to report that Lebanon assuaged our disappointment! Food was delicious and generous and service excellent. Wife & I split a shawarma combo platter and couldn't finish it. Super creamy hummus! Wonderful!

Dont understand the hype about this place. The beet salad was primarily bitter endives than beet. The farm board was nothing special . The zeppoles basic fried dough. The only redeeming dish was the lamb meatballs. Will never return

Omg what a great find for a local breakfast spot! The options alone are amazing. Everything from eggs and bacon to custom bagel sandwiches. Ordering is easy from the touch screen monitors. Bagels are fresh and delicious!

Took my mom and girlfriend here for Hibachi on mother's day. I made reservations but the place was a little overbooked so there was a short wait. The staff we're pleasant and since we were the only people waiting they comped us each a drink which was cool.

Being a designer myself, I'm a big fan of interior design and restaurant aesthetics so with that said, Ooka is a great looking restaurant. The look is very modern with but with an Asian flair as you would expect but its not over the top. Some places with Asian decor tend to look cheap and packed-in like a Chinatown gift shop. Anyway, there is great use of different kinds of wood in very angular shapes all around. The bathroom was clean and cool as hell.  Lastly the lighting is very intimate. If you visit Ooka, what I'm talking about will be obvious. 

We had an average waitress during Hibachi but the chef was out of this world in terms of cooking and humor. We actually had Chef Tony from the picture here on Yelp. The guy was riot. Between my gf, mom and the chef I was laughing so hard I was tearing up. 

The food was the best Hibachi I've ever had. To some of you foodies out there that may not be saying much, but I loved every morsel I was given. We all ordered something  a little different and we tried eachother's food so I can safely say it was all delicious.

I haven't been back since but the thought crosses my mind all the time. It can be pricey but no more expensive that what any special occasion could warrant. Honestly I think I'd rather save going to this place for special occasions so I don't ruin it with familiarity and further scrutiny. Ooka comes highly recommended by me.

From the service, to the food, to the ambiance, Il Pittore was top notch.  The staff was extremely attentive and friendly.  The food...outstanding.  We had the lamb sausage appetizer - so flavorful we wanted to lick the plate.  We split a pasta course - homemade pasta, need I say more?  I had the braised short rib dish as my secondi - they were cooked perfectly.  Braised short rib is one of my favorite dishes to order out but it can be so easily done wrong.  Il Pittore did them so right!  We will definitely be going back!

Love BKs. Always have and always will. They are crazy expensive compared to the stands on the side of the road but I still think it's worth it. I love that they started that way and have grown to a b&m which explains they're high prices. Out of the 20-30 times I've been there, I've never been disappointed. LONG LIVE BK!
Service was good. The food was ok. The portions were laughable for the money you pay. I am struggling to think why this place has decent reviews.

i haven't had pupusas since i lived across from a Salvadoran place of the same name in San Francisco. The pupusas here are so good! i always get the combination with beans and rice. i pile on the coleslaw and am in heaven.
Excellent restaurant, not much more you can say.  Great steaks, great service, little pricey, but well worth it.

Upon my first visit, I ordered take out. I was told it would be 20 minutes. I arrived to pick up my order at about 15 minutes. I then waited roughly 30 minutes for my order to be ready. I received my order and only half of it was correct. They fixed the issue within another 15 minutes. Half of my food was cold, the other hot---and ended up without 2 of my sides. I spoke w Jacob the manager on duty that evening who was extremely apologetic and stated he would email me some free meal coupons. Now we are at least 2 months out and I've yet to receive my email. 

I attempted to dine in another evening. The service was mediocre. I'm not impressed w the food enough to go back. With or without my free tickets

We jpicked up our holiday pie as we ordered a French silk. It's supposed to have a Oreo crust and it had a regular crust that tasted stale, salty and thick. That was a disappointment.
The filling to crust ratio was way off as the filling was way too much and way too thick and rich. It almost resembled a frosting type flavor and texture.
I can not recommend this as my family and I are very disappointed.

UPDATE: 
Owner contacted me and apologized for the French silk and offered to make another or a different pie at no charge. We are eating the mixed berry as I write this review and it's delicious. 
Highly recommend this business.

Caffe Luce is a regular stop for me while I'm in town. Not only is it right in the heart of downtown near my hotel, they have a good amount of seating if you need to work/study too.

The coffee is great and the staff is friendly. I usually go for a cold brew or an iced almond latte with one of their syrups. Vanilla is good, but I'm a fan of their lavender option as well - it's sweet, but not overly fragrant to the point where it tastes like you're drinking a candle.

I haven't had any of their food, but it always looks good when it comes out--next time I'll have to have a snack to see what it's all about.

My only complaint is that it can get REALLY warm in there, even on the chilliest of days. So if you're not into heat, your best best bet is to probably take it to-go, especially during the summer months.

Do yourself a favor and give this place a try.  It will become one of your favorite spots in south Tampa for fast, delicious meals.  
I've had the burger, the chicken sandwich, and the delicious desserts.  (Not to mention the delicious sides!)
Can't go wrong!  Everything is delicious!
Highly recommend!

Really great spot.  Grabbed dinner for me and husband.  Ordered many different things and enjoyed it all.  Egg rolls are outstanding.  Location is in a Asian grocery.  Once inside, the entrance to the restaurant is between two freezers.

This place is my SPOT. I love studying here and the coffee in on point. They have outdoor seating which has been so essential for mixing up my studying lately- the only problem is they don't have outlets out there- but there is rarely a problem getting a seat inside to study. There are plenty of windows so it's a very bright study spot and it's pretty open so you don't feel like you're sitting right on top of other people. They have a mix of tables, comfy armchair- type spots with tables, and a counter. So whatever your study style is, you can find a spot here. 

The baristas really know their stuff when it comes to coffee and I'm really picky so I appreciate their recommendations. They also have some very cool iced teas- most recently I got one with chestnut and grapefruit. And I can't forget! They have this AMAZING new affogato that I am obsessed with and probably would bathe in. So there's that. 

There are also a bunch of pastries and quiches for sale but my gluten free and nut free self doesn't have any options. Luckily it's a short walk from a bunch of gluten free spots in Haddonfield so it's never too much of a big deal. But Jersey Java, if you're reading this, a couple of gluten free snacks would push this review from a 4 star to a 5 star and you would have a VERY grateful and loyal customer on your hands
My favorite Mexican spot around. Mushroom quesadillas are amazing. I've ordered from here countless times both from their website and from Uber eats. Great place

Tonight I went to the location on Hillsborough Ave by 275 and I had 2 orders. Burger with cheese and boneless wings and shrimp with black beans instead of fries. When I got home I found out that I did not get the burger and the boneless wings were regular wings. When I called to let them know she told me that me burger was there and I could come and get it and she would put down new boneless wings. She did not tell me that I had to bring the incorrect order back but I did anyway. I drive back up to the store and they were very rude to me. I showed them the shrimp and wings and they insisted on taking it and remaking the shrimp instead of just giving me the burger and boneless wings so I could be on my way. I had to wait another 10 minutes while they remade shrimp that had not been touched and as I'm walking out the rude woman offers me a cup like I should be grateful. This restaurant has a lot to learn about customer service.

The food is AMAZING!! Or waiter was equally as amazing. He was very attintive! You would never have known the restaurant was full with people waiting to be seated. I made a reservation an hour before on OpenTable and when we walked in we were immediately seated.

Delivery took almost 2 hours from when I received the confirming email. At the hour mark, I called the store. "Yeah, we're busy, it just left". At the 1:20 mark I called back. They put me on hold for 5 minutes and then told me it was on the way. Took almost 2 hours. The store is 2 miles down Dale Mabry. Never again.

Pizza was obviously cold.

Went to Antoine's without reservations on a Friday night...so they suggested we go here while we waited and they'd get us.  Big mistake (for Antoine's...).  We were originally just going to get drinks, but then the caprese salad looked good, and then the duck and andouille gumbo looked good, so we ended up ordering these as well.  The duck gumbo could have used more duck, but except for that, it was quite tasy.  The caprese was good, though it suffered a little in the presentation (thick slabs of mozzarella...).

This placed was fun about 10-12 years ago.  It looks like they haven't dusted, mopped, or cleaned anything since then.  The place is filthy, and the food is horrible.  I'm surprised the health inspector hasn't shut them down.  I would give them zero stars if possible.

Eat here at your own risk!

Oh. My. Gosh. You gotta go here. It is amazing and the food I had was flavorful and just so good. I've been vegan for a while and this is one of the best places I've ever eaten at. Sadly, I'm just passing through but if I wasn't I think I would eat here for lunch and dinner everyday lol. I had the bbq wrap and chick pea salad.... I'll be dreamin bout it
Delicious donuts and very friendly staff. Everyone at work enjoys them and ask me where the donuts are from. Po is very friendly and very helpful. Will continue to visit Alvernon Donuts!

Sucks suck sucks food service employees everything. I ordered chicken and fries both were ice cold when you bring it back they act like they don't understand you oh yah no ketchup or bbq for the chicken .Save your self 12.00 stay away
Did I say it sucks

The beer here was very good however the me Lai receipt which was the muscle dish leaves a lot to be desired many of the mussel shells were MD many of the muscles were overcooked and all of the muscles were extremely small in terms of bodies this might just have been a bad batch but this is all I have to go on service was good

Chorizo huevos rancheros was so good. Comes with green chili sauce and avocado. Friendly down to earth service. Good coffee... 2.50 free refills! Great tortillas. We left properly stuffed. Can't wait to try more of the menu.
Great place with great people. The phill cheesesteaks are fire. They have cheese wiz! The people are even better and always feel welcome there. If you like cheesesteak, skip the fake places

I Love Hoong Kong Bakery and since I am in chinatown mode it gets 5 stars but seriously their rolls are delightful even my son likes their cookies!! woohoo good bye Nabisco!!! Go for the rolls and the Triangle Sponge cake and the awesome pork buns. Hong Kong Bakery goodies are a staple take home on a visit to China Town bad thing about em is that they do not accept plastic but its only 70 cents to 80 cents worth of dough bread so its fine with me .

I love love love Hong Minh Noodle House. I come here for 3 things. 
1. Duck wonton noodle soup. The broth is so flavorful and reminds me of how my mom makes it. It's really a big bowl enough to share for 2 people. Just add in the herbs that comes on the side and a squeeze of lime and voila! 
2. Fried chicken wings! Comes with a side of rice or fries. Don't want either? A dollar off! It's so tender and well seasoned. So much better than the popular Manchus! I like the jalapeños added to it too. It's mouth-watering just thinking about it. 
3. Beef chow fun- rice noodles sautéed with beef. Idk how to explain this dish but just get it. 

Thanks for whoever posted the picture with the menu! Who need to go menus when you have yelp or smartphones. First time I went here, I made the mistake of wearing jeans. It use to be Jade Apple (Chinese to go restaurant) with an open kitchen so it gets stuffy.The second time I came in with shorts and a T-shirt and the A/C was working better.

The owner is a sweet older vietnamese lady. She reminds me of my mom who just loves to cook. I like to support the mom and pops restaurants.

So I'm not going to completely dis this place. But come on.... no AC? It is so hot in here!!!!! Stale chips, one serving of beans for two people, the beer drafts broken, the steak was not that good, the prices are ridiculous!! 
The kitchen staff, no masks, talking giving high fives, flies everywhere. This place is not what we expected. Get it together charro steak or you won't be here much longer... sad!! 
*** this is not MEXICAN FOOD.

Oh my God  is what  I literally screamed tasting the red beans! It felt so good to taste new Orleans food the way it suppose to be. Living in Houston I have to defend my opinion when I say, the so called Authentic New Orleans resturant food don't have that NOLA taste. There is something  special about an original NOLA cooked dish. This place gave me this in so many ways. I mean the gumbo was right, and I screamed yes for the juice. When I tell you i scraped the bowl, and ate every drop inside. I also had the fried chicken which was really good, the mac and cheese was rolling ,and the rice was great. I also was psyched, because I got to taste the original new orleans-style French bread, which absolutely melts in your mouth. I also had the salad which was really good and fresh. Did I mention that this all was a buffet, yes all this great  buffet-style food for only $15.99. You can order from the menu, you don't have to do the buffet, but you get the most value for your money if you do the buffet. Now the décor of this place isn't the most elegant, but this is a place you go to for great food. If you visit New Orleans you definitely have to stop by this place to taste an awesome meal,and be greeted by a cool staff.

We are in the steak house portion of the restaurant and it did not disappoint! Jessica was a server and she was simply amazing. She was attentive and friendly and provided us with great service. Our food was delicious! A great little gem on Broadway!
The owner is so nice, the pork was okay, but chicken seems to be what the people go for, will try that next time. The Mac and the cheese was good, but the GARLIC FRIES ARE THE BOMB!
It was very delicious, and they are very accommodating as well. They took care of our luggage.

LOVE THIS PLACE!!!  Visiting Clearwater during spring break and needed to find a local place for lunch. Glad we chose The Raven. The poutine was some of the best we've had. Kids loved the pizza. They had personal sizes and larger. Of course, the kids wanted something different so each kid got a personal pie. The wife loves veggie burgers and their homemade veggie burger was great. Chelsie was our waitress and took great care of us. After a long day in the sun, their food hit the spot. Exactly what we were looking for. Thanks to Yelp users for the recommendation.

This place is awesome! We go maybe 3 times a month and we are never disappointed. We usually go on Sundays, and the staff is wonderful! The new spinach dip is amazing, and they offer bloomin petals now, which we love. The bloomin petals are the same as the bloomin onion, but a much smaller portion, it's the perfect amount for a family of four.
If you are looking for a great drink, the bar here does not disappoint! I definitely recommend the frozen margarita, a great drink and a reasonable price! 
If u want to have an even better experience at outback, make sure to utilize the call ahead seating!

I almost forgot about Vito and Michaels! Very tasty pizza with a crisp crust and loads of veggies! Fast, fresh and friendly. The only reason it's not 5 stars is due to the dingyness of the front room where I ate because I was on my bike and had to bring my bike to the table with me. The front room with two little tables is a bit dirty and could use a once-over with a broom & a cloth. I suppose they wouldn't let be bring my grimy road bike into a super clean dining room, it's prob a good thing they have this front room otherwise I'd have to eat out in the heat on the benches! The main dining room is very clean as is the restroom. Overall a great place for quality pizza at a great price. Loaded slice and a drink less than $6. Definitely stop in!
Heard great things and we had high hopes. It was just okay. 5 of us ate here and none of us felt our food was above par. We left disappointed. Staff seemed great. Food not so much.

This is by far my sushi spot in tampa. It will please any kind of sushi lover. I am more of a specialty roll kind of person with the new tampa roll being my fave but I have tried at least half of them. My boyfriend goes for more of the nigiri but also loves their rainbow roll. All in all I love this place!
Finally a good Vietnamese restaurant in Countryside. Outstanding Service. Delicious Bahn mi.  Perfect Boba.  I can't wait to take my family there. I think this will become one of my ATF's.

This is my favorite sushi place by far! It has wonderful staff, and so many different sushi and appetizer options, even if you don't like sushi, it's all you can eat kitchen items too! They are quick, and the food is always very fresh. I've never had a sushi roll here that I didn't like! If you love sushi, this is the place to go, I come here at least twice a month!

We loved sitting outside in the late afternoon, (shaded from the blazing sun by an umbrella) drinking sangria, and munching on our cheese and meat plate (2 of each).  We LOVED the La Tur soft cheese!  YUM!  I wish we had ordered two!  Unfortunately, the other cheese we had, the Ubriaco Prosecco, was boring.  We liked our meats:  Prosciutto de Parma and Coppa Piccante.

The food here is actually good for being all veggie and I actually liked my friend's torta the best. 

The service is horrific. Sojourner should have an "order at the counter" service because it took at least 10 minutes to get a waitress and another ten to get our water and take our order. She brought the wrong wine and was seemingly out of it the whole time. 

I get it. We're all supposed to be relaxed, not eat meat and enjoy life, but Sojourner's not cheap and I really expect more.

Awful, simply awful. I should've just gone to Shake shack as at least I would've known what I was getting. The food was average at best, overpriced for sure and the service was simply awful. Will never ever go there again. Beware this is not the pinks of LA for sure

My girl and I have been here a handful of times now, and each overall experience is better than the previous! The staff is always so helpful (and attractive?? not that that's actually relevant??), doting, eager to please. The atmosphere is super chill. The food is best thing about it though, as it should be!!

I want to like the restaurant as its literally in my back yard however I have been here many times and have left disappointed every single time. The food is expensive and not of good quality. Ive had sandwich and burgers all which has way to much bread to meat ratios, there drinks are watered down too. Ive had lots of different pasties out of there window and all have been bland and stale. I did have the Hazelnut iced coffee once and it was good. Im also not a fan of the indoor seating, but the outside patio sits on Dakota right in Hyde Park village so its a nice area to people watch.

Awesome burgers and sandwiches!  We eat here every Saturday.  The best french fries in the world and great burgers and sandwiches.  Tommy is a trip and Al is the greatest.  Marie is a great cook and Shelly and daughters are wonderful.  We can't say enough good about this little treasure.  Great for birthday parties or any other family occasion.

The food was amazing! Really inexpensive and delicious. Something for everyone in the group to enjoy. Recommend going for happy hour because the deals are even better. The service was also good and our server was telling us NOLA facts and made it fun!
Perfect spot for a drink with colleagues and friends. Happy hour wines are very good. Walking distance to businesses in downtown. Beautiful decor and friendly staff. Love it!!

First time there at the suggestion of a friend.  The most exciting thing about the place was our server, Nick.  He was amazing!  The food is just ok and miniature and does not warrant the high prices, but I think the ambiance is what makes the people come here.  We sat outside in one of the bubble dining tents and it was cute and cozy.  Loved the fact that we had a mini fire pit on the table.  It was chilly on Saturday.  Let's talk about the attitude of the staff:  The dude at the security checkpoint outside was a total jerk.  He asked for ID and I asked why and he said "because." I asked again and he finally said "contact tracing."  Just say that in the first place when requesting the ID.  Get a personality and grow some manners dude.  Secondly, the young ladies at the reservations desk (when you finally make it in) need to pay more attention to the patrons as opposed to gossiping amongst each other and trying to figure out which one of them is the Next Top Model.  Third, please tape up the peek-a-boo holes in the tents or replace them.  They are a little war torn from the elements and a little birdie friend actually dropped his business inside ours.  LOL!  I think I am going to sit on the other side (garden) the next time.  I noticed the patrons were grown and sexy and it's less noisy.  Great concept but do better...

Great service and oh my!! So happy we found this gem while running down Magazine yesterday. It is right down the street from my sons school so we decided to come right before pick up time. Man oh man! Everything is authentic. I had the media noche with an iced bombomb coffee infused with Malta! My husband had the ropa vieja which is his favorite dish. There were so many items we wanted to try like the Havana sampler with croquettes but we were pressed for time. Definitely coming back and bringing family back with us.
Way over priced, came here because of the reviews, theres much better around this sandwich cost me $11.00

Everything we had was really awesome. Borscht was so flavorful. We sampled a number of their soups and appetizers. We finished the meal with a phenomenal desert called Napoleon. So very different from anything I've had which is what we were looking for when we came here.
Great space large enough for group party's. Frozen Paloma was delicious. Friendly staff with fun fresh feel.

I love their pizza and have tried several local pizzerias in Nashville with similar fare and none came close to the deliciousness of S&H. They don't skimp on toppings and they cook the crust so well. Their dipping sauce are also great.

I was really apprehensive about checking this place out. It has bomb reviews, but nothing on the menu itself looked appealing to me. After finally agreeing to go with my friend, I ordered a G and Tea to drink and a bologna sandwich. The drink was absolutely amazing and the bologna sandwich was pretty cool. The staff is nice.

"Yay! I'm a fan" perfectly sums up my experience at Zydeco. I had the day off from work and because all of my friends work the old 9-5 Mon-Fri schedule, I went by my lonesome. I walked into a new, clean, and fairly empty brewery around 2:30 on a Tuesday and was greeted by a friendly and chill bartender named Mike. I asked about happy hour times and he said they didn't have that set-up yet (a bummer and the only reason I'm not giving them 5 stars) but he did offer me a "locals" discount which was very generous. I ordered a flight based on Mike's recommendations and was blown away by the beer. The red ale was excellent but what really took the cake was the "Champagne Wishes and Caviar Dreams." It weighs in at a whopping 7% but is as light and fluffy as a light domestic beer or unsurprisingly, a dry champagne. I ordered a pint of that after I downed the flight and my total was $15 before the locals discount. The food looked good but I was on a liquid diet at the time so I did not indulge. I will be back. Parking in Ybor is always laborious but it is what it is.

I'll probably get death threats cause I'm not huggin Jose Garces nuts this time like all of Philadelphia; and yes I'm breaking my rule of yelping after only dining once, but I have decided I should be saving more $ these days if I plan on making some plan trips in the near future, plus the recession is still rockinandrolling. About a month ago I took my pops, the legendary Chiman to dinner. He mentioned he was trying to eat lighter so instead of our usual steak dinners I brought him to Amada. 

First thing first we were raised w/ only a few simple rules at the dinner table by the Chiman: only pussies didn't finish your plate and get seconds. So why may u ask I bring my dad to tapas restaurant like Amada's... cuz I had a gift card and he said he wasn't that hungry. 

Crab stuff peppers= bangin, so were the wild mushrooms. I thought the stuff lamb was tasty, but my dad claimed the cheese overpowered the very little lamb. We got another dish that wasn't memorable enough for me to remember. Review is going pretty good so why the 3 stars? The chicken paella was pretty bad. First off ,no la soccarat, come on Jose for 40 bucks a pop u can't skip out on the best part. Secondly, it was way over salted, I felt like I was eaten rice shaped salt. Thirdly (if that's a word), my pops kept on say "in ironbound in Newark u can get thees mus cheaaper." Fourthly ( still not sure if a word) I had to eat the whole platter since if u remember Chiman's #1 dinner rule: only pussies didn't finish their plates. Fifthly, I think chicken paella in Jose Garcia's language means ex lax cause I had one way ticket on the porcelain train for a bit and my pops was ok. In all fairness chicken was cooked very well....

Happened to stumble into this restaurant for happy hour (5-7pm at the bar every day of operation) on a decently busy night. The tables were fully reserved for the night, but there were a few empty seats at the bar throughout the evening. The happy hour menu is very minimal; 2 drink options and a few food items. Additionally, there is a full tasting menu as well as an a la carte menu with individual prices. 

Upon ordering the Montreal Short Ribs, I was informed that it would be about 40 minutes for preparation. That was fine by me, and the kitchen even treated me to a complimentary entree of the roasted chicken, which I assume another diner had ordered and sent back. It was good but nothing to write home about (or praise in a review). I felt similarly about all of the food we ordered, including the latke fries and short rib. The short rib was a little undercooked even for short rib, and the latke fries were a hefty price for just 4 fries that were just ok. 

I'd come back for happy hour, but it's unlikely that I would return for a meal due to the prices.

Everything we had was so delicious! Obviously a little pricey, but it's a steakhouse, so that's to be expected. Good for celebrating semi-special occasions, and you can get a tasty (and strong) beverage to help you celebrate! Great ambiance, and excellent wait staff. Get your steak estilo charro (with melted manchego cheese and sauteed bell peppers on top). You won't regret it.

Holy cow! The food served out of the side of this truck is some of the best I have had. I got the spicy tuna burrito and the tuna nachos, which was pricey, but well worth it. Also, the burrito and nachos together were way too much food for one normal person to eat. If you have the chance to get food from this truck, do it. For what you get, the price is totally reasonable even if it is a little more expensive than what you might expect from a food truck.

Maybe it was the anticipation of being in a long line with the scorching sun beating on us that got us ready for CCK's famous malt shakes, but this  time around was better than the first.

I was happy to join a friend as she took a visitor on a Man vs. Food St. Louis tour (CCK, Pappy's, + Iron Barley), & we waited in line for ~35min. at 1pm on a Saturday afternoon (make sure to bring quarters for the meter). 

I had the regular chocolate shake last time, but all I have to say is that i've gone malt (chocolate banana), & there's no turning back!

On another note, I noticed a bit of construction on the street across from CCK & am really excited to see the end product. It'll be perfect to get a CCK cone on the go & walk around!
Has some customer service kinks to work out as a new restaurant...Seafood Gumbo needed more seasoning and not quite jalapeño poppers.

great food but awkward stares from staff.
this place is delicious and very friendly though the waitresses passed  by a few times and to busy and friendly with other customers but neglected us.....our food was delicious after all it was close to closing time and they seemed in a hurry for us to leave a little uncomfortable.

Ordered the carne asada fries and two mini tacos, tell me why ONE mini taco had 2x the amount of meat in it than the carne asada fries??? Paid 9 something for the fries and $2 for the mini taco, such a rip off.

Four stars for price. 
I drive truck, so I've eaten bbq all over America. This place is better than most, but it's certainly not 4 star worthy. I'd say the food is more like 2.5 star. 
The cheeseburger was quite large and the meat was tasty. (Be advised: if you don't stop them they'll automatically put that disgusting invention called mayonnaise on it.) I got it plain so I can't comment on their lettuce/tomato game. 
The pork bbq sammich was soggy on the bottom. Moist is good, but this was just plain wet. The meat itself was bland but not bad. 
The bbq sauce is pretty good but not great. 
The Mac & Cheese tasted ok but the noodles were way overcooked. It'd be much better if it were baked and had a little crustiness to it. 

If I lived local I'm sure I'd come here occasionally.

This is a really fun spot for lunch if you're in the area. Ordering is quick and you're given a number. Head to any spot to sit. Lots of servers around cleaning up which was nice to see! I loved my black and white shake. Wow - definitely not a McDonald's creation. Great flavor. My husband really enjoyed the adult caramel bourbon shake - mostly the caramel and whipped cream on top. My Crunchburger was medium rare, which was perfect. I felt the chips make it a little too salty though, so if you're watching your sodium, don't crunchify. The fries are terrific. Get a regular size even if you're sharing as it's a big order. I was partial to the chipotle ketchup rather than the BBP sauce it comes with.

The place was really cool to look around, but the burgers were not great. Plus they seemed to be understaffed because the waitress was constantly running from table to table. She barely even stopped to take our order. She was moving away from the table as she took it.

It's just not as good as before the new owners took over. It's still OK, but I miss the homemade chips, the variety of salsas, the homemade tortillas...overall it has more options now, but less satisfying. Would have given it 4 stars one year ago. There are better taquerias closer to Washington (and still in the same delivery area).

If you haven't been downtown in a long time you better run!  HUB is a great place for happy hour, dinner, appetizers, or late night fare!

The bar is amazing and the selection of tap beers is a little overwhelming a good way :-)

The Tuna Noddle has become my favorite, just sayin'

The Beer Braised Brisket with their special bread is on point. I took one bite and felt in love with the sandwich. Home made chips as a side item is worth it. Fresh and crunchy chips yum! I will be back.

Pretty nice for a quick service restaurant. Staff was friendly and helpful! The vibe of the place was laid back and the food was brought out with minimal waiting time. I ordered a salad and my boyfriend got a burger. All of it was good! The reason I'm giving out four stars and not 5 is because I think it's all a bit overpriced. The small burger was $10 and the salad was $8. I wouldn't necessarily complain about the prices if a side or two came with it but Burger 21 sells everything individually. Personally, I wouldn't recommend going out of your way to check this place out but if you're in the area and hungry for a burger, go in! Like I said, the food is delicious and the staff is great. Enjoy!

Our group meal here was excellent. Not sure why there are so many negative reviews below. The staff accommodated our group of 9 people, separate checks for each person, with different people arriving at different times, very professional, no problem, they weren't fazed at all (why do people spell that word incorrectly?). They took our drink orders (they have an great bar serving pisco sours, capharinas, etc) and had excellent recommendations and gave us plenty of time to figure out our entrees. 

All the entrees were excellent. We had 2 vegetarians in the group, but there were plenty to choose from. I had a sauteed fish entree that was flavorful and authentic, with multiple layers of flavor. Several others got scallops that were seared and served with their shells. The beef saltado and beef stew were both great as well. Warning, the entrees here aren't enormous, despite this being the Midwest and all.... Go figure?
Fattoush Salad with Chicken is excellent! We get takeout at least once a week. Great addition to the area.

Delicious! I love that they have vegetarian options. I usually opt for the bean burritos though. Guacamole is an extra charge but it's freshly made and delicious. 

The location is great with a very cool vibe. They do dine in and takeout. Takeout option is great if your heading over to one of the two breweries around the corner for a drink.

I'll break my "don't review it only visiting once" rule because in my party of eight, I think I tried almost every sandwich they make here. Located in the tourist-turgid area of the French Market, I find the quality to be top-notch for what could have been a trap.  A simple stall, they offer a pretty impressive selection of sandwiches. Two-cheese grilled cheese sandwiches for $4 is about the cheapest you'll find something to eat in the French Quarter, and doesn't feel cheap when you have choices like Gouda and Havarti to melt.  The smoked salmon sandwich with Burgos cheese makes an excellent lox bagel approximation, with smoked salmon that had flavor and red onions give it a good kick (no capers though). The Asiago roast beef was dripping with melted cheese and the horseradish in it is real-deal, powerful stuff. The Serrano ham and Manchego cheese sandwich is also very good, but that might be because I'm a sucker for the garlic condiment that is sure to ruin your breath.  On either wheat or white baguettes, toasted, all of them were excellent, and I can say that you're safe getting a decent sandwich here. Sure, it was almost ten dollars for some of the fancier ones, but they're hearty and I was not left wanting for more despite skipping breakfast. If there's a next time, I NEED to try the Brie Belgian waffles.
Amazing dining experience. One of the best tasting menus in Philly. Absolutely do the wine pairings! Friendly staff and excellent food.

Some of the best food of our first- time trip to NOLA in a relaxed friendly lively setting.Starting out with tasty cocktails (iced tea with vodka and fresh mint from their garden),we then loved our entrees, baked fish fillet with crawfish etoufee and braised short ribs, really excellent well-prepared dishes.

The service was beyond good,  very kind and thoughtful. We went there in the first place because we wanted to see Zydeco night at the Rock n'Bowl next door, and I just bought the show tickets on line, without realizing that I could have gotten a discount by eating at the restaurant and buying the tickets at the door. That was OK with us, one of perils of travelling and not knowing stuff, but the staff at Ye Olde were concerned enough about our not being able to get the discount that they called the manager of the club (owned by the same people) and asked them to give us free drinks. We were then met practically at the door of the club by the manager who directed us to the bar and served us our drinks. So sweet! No way did they have to do that, just generous customer service. Zydeco night was fun too.

Ive been coming here for over a year now and i absolutely love this place! The food is always on point! And the oysters are out of this world ! The manager Jennifer was there and she was super sweet! She checked up on our table to make sure everything was perfect and it absolutely was! We Will definitely continue to come back ! I definitely recommend coming here!

This was our first time at Lilac after hearing that it was a gluten free bakery. I was excited to try it out. When we were in line, it seemed like they were pretty understaffed at the register. My mom and I ended up ordering the Vegan Carrot Cupcake and Vegan Apple Cranberry Crisp to go. When I saw them boxing the crisp, it seemed like they just took the leftover bits and scooped it into the takeout rather than giving the crust topping. When we opened it up to eat it, it just looked like a serving of mush, so soggy. The crisp tasted like soggy fruit too, and definitely not worth the $7.50. I would have returned it, cause I had opened it up earlier in the shop, but the cashiers seemed so overwhelmed by the line of 5 customers, I didn't feel like waiting. The vegan carrot cupcake was average. I did feel like consistency of the cake was pretty moist, which is nice for vegan/gf baking. However, the taste of the "cream cheese" frosting wasn't right. Overall, pretty disappointed.

I catered sandwiches and salads for my daughters U of A graduation party. Mixed sandwiches, green salad, potato salad, fruit platter. Food was delivered in a timely fashion. This was super but the "wow" came with the presentation and the spectacular sandwiches! I'd ordered a mix of sandwiches. Each one was absolutely delicious and fresh. All of the guests were excited about the food and wanted to know where I'd ordered from. 
Thank you so much! The food was awesome and presentation was beautiful! I highly recommend.
Love this place.  Great for take out or eat in, always my first choice for Thai in Sherwood Park.
Quick service. Good food! Bar available! Staff friendly and respectful...Good music but you must pay the jute box ...

I've been on a bit of a Chinese train lately, and after doing some googling stumbled upon TKO, a very fortunate stumble that thoroughly satisfied my taste buds.

Ordered via menufy and the process was simple and quick, got my order in without ever leaving Instagram - I've dealt with some annoying online ordering and glad to see it was so simple l

Being in quarantine, was really happy to see how seriously they took curbside pickup, process was really smooth and I had my food right when it said it was going to be ready 

We got the Bourbon Chicken Fried Rice and the Pineapple Tofu - both we're very good. My one wish was that there was some sort of sweet add to the fried rice, I threw on some sriracha mayo I had at home but some sauce would've helped, nonetheless then flavor of the chicken was good and the rice was superb, the tofu was also cooked extremely well, but what sold me was the pineapple glaze/sauce, really elevated the dish for me and made it stand out.

There is not a lot of good Chinese in nashville, but TKO should definitely be near the top of your list!

I've been here twice already and it really just doesn't get any better than this. I've been having a bingsu craving ever since my trip to Vancouver last summer and have been trying to find a place that matches Vancouver quality and this is it! The interior is super cute and the bingsu are reasonably priced and super delicious. I have a pretty severe nut allergy and they were really accommodating. I've tried the matcha bing and the mango bing. The matcha is my current favorite and you get surprises as you go. The mango bing was also delicious but I will have to try again later in the summer as mangos aren't in season right now and were slightly sour in my bingsu (but hey, it means they use the real stuff!). They also have a variety of other cute snacks and drinks to choose from. I'm definitely going to be frequenting this place and making it my go to place for bingsu!

This place is right near all the bars in broad ripple! Accessible parking. It's a cool place to check out for breakfast or lunch. I can't remember the price but i went 2x that I can recall so it must be good and affordable for me to have gone again!

Had hummus with gluten free bread was told there would be a couple dollars up charge turns out the small serving of hummus was $9 and the bread was $5 so essentially $14 for a small appetizer where an entire pizza gluten free would cost this much or less at Sauce. this was the lunch menu... just feels like getting gouged.

Just ordered lunch, not only is the food amazing but the service is too. I could have sworn I ordered a salad, but a quesadilla came by accident. Not sure if I put the wrong thing in my cart, but the manager Ben was so amazing he rushed a salad right over to us. They were so fantastic and I mean, can you get much better then a massive quesadilla! Highly recommend!!

I absolutely love this place! It has adorable rustic decor, the staff makes you feel like family, it's clean, the plating of the food made it look even more appetizing and everything that was placed on our table was amazing! They had the best grits I have ever tasted! They were rich, creamy, and savory. You won't even think about asking for salt or pepper here and their Arnold palmers went perfectly with everything. I live two hours away from Tampa and would have no problem driving here to eat and spend a day In Tampa.

Food is good but the atmosphere is one of they weirdest I've seen in a restaurant. They make you feel uncomfortable about being there when they are about to close. Like you are holding them up from going home even though they do not close for a hour.  It sounds weird but we live close by and have been there probably 30 times since they've opened a year ago.  They are always "early" cleaning and putting up chairs hours before they close. One time we were at our table an hour before the closed. They turned all the chairs upside down on the tables around us, then swept around us like we were in the way.  As I write this we are finishing our drinks with a large group on the patio and they turned the lights off at 11:01pm on a Saturday night.

We were VERY intimidated after we received our food... we had never been to a Shabu Shabu restaurant (only ever tried it at home where we make our own rules), and when our food came out, it looked nothing like the other tables.  Every other table had a big pot of broth in the middle, and ours came out as one tiny bowl placed in front of me.
We tried to ask the waitress why ours was different, but she was a) impossible to get a hold of and b) confused by our confusion.  We eventually just ordered a second tiny bowl of broth and we ate separate meals.

It was delicious food... it was just intimidating when we didn't understand the menu or options.

The perfect place to try a boil. We were visiting this past weekend and had people with us that had never tried crawfish before. This was the perfect place. Multiple options for boils. Incredible flavor. We got the Taste of New Orleans with Boil house flavor and medium heat. It was perfect! Our server Jo Jo was very friendly and helpful. We will bring others here in the future!
Outstanding! We had the taco and tamale combo. Flavors were on point! Ample servings. Quick service. Clean and cute inside. Definitely worth a drive.

Seemed pretty low staff for the business level, the whole time we were there. We waited a few minutes to be acknowledged and then seated. The server was decent, but seemed annoyed to be there and complained to a number of guests and co-workers (we could hear) about various complaints, from management to customers. She was a fine server mostly, just seemed annoyed with everyone and everything (including us). There was a young gentleman there on the other side of restaurant and I wish we had been seated there- he seems genuinely nice and friendly and less agitated.

The food seemed to take a bit but wasn't horrible. The salad was fresh and the food was decent. Chicken nice and moist, burger was fine. Nothing out of this world but solid, especially for a Dennys. I felt the cooks cared about it at least, better than can be said at some places!

Not our best visit there but could have been worse.

Went here to try the burgers, was not disappointed. They have a great variety of different burgers, plus a burger of the month. Not only was there a ton of options, the final product was great too. Accompanying the burger varieties, was a decent variety of beers as well.

Grabbed a salad for lunch a  few weeks back and loved it. Had them cater a breakfast and lunch for a business meeting for 19 people everyone enjoyed the food. I had several people tell me how good it was.  With 19 people, I ordered a variety of wraps and Panni's and not one was bad.  Went back to try the 2 day juice cleanse just finished.  It was also good. Looking forward to trying the protein bowls and smoothies.

Stopped by at this place by sheer chance, we were actually looking for another Indian place nearby and finding it closed we decided to give DBN a try, and glad we did !! The lunch buffet is served dine-in style which reduces wastage of food and you can get more customized selection than a one-size-fits-all buffet offerings you get at other Indian restaurants. We had veg pakoras, tandoori chicken, fish pakoras, curry chicken and saag paneer with fresh naan. I esp enjoyed the fish pakoras among all though our party of 5 generally agreed all the menu items we tasted were good in their own. The owner/chef was pleasant to talk to and receptive to suggestions. Will go there again if I happen to be in Tampa sometime in future.

I avoid this shoprite at all costs. Small aisles and the two times I've been there, there has been crap muddled all over the floor and I've left with sticky shoes. Prices are the same as other shop rites. 
I'll go to a different one from now on.

So my first party group I was going with met today at Latitude 360o.  I received my e-club coupon for my free appetizer for up to $8.99 just in time.  So I ordered the chicken tenders, fries, and BBQ.  

How could I ever expect something to go odd with something so common on a menu?
I offered a friend some of my appetizer.  As I was eating, my face was getting hot.  I asked if my face was red.  So my checks were flushed.  After a while of eating, I gave her the rest of my appetizer.  She was fine until she tried the BBQ sauce.  Apparently, the restaurant makes their own sauce and added cayenne peppers.  

The appetizer was not appetizing at all.  The fries were not all that great; my friend said it had Cajun seasoning on them, but I was used to having Cajun which was not the same.  

The size of the appetizer -- 4 tenders and fries -- could be worth it but a little large for an appetizer.

So, I am giving the place an OK because although the food just did not settle well with me, they did change the channel to the Olympics games -- which were awesome.

Good pizza, good customer service, open late. What else is there to say? Ladies were very friendly and cook my pie to order. Perfect way to finish off a long work day. I'm going soon again to try their grilled bologna and fried tenderloin sandwiches!
Absolutely delicious food, unique menu choices, great portion sizes, hospitable staff... loved it!! Will definitely be back

Pretty good sushi rolls. Pretty bad service. It was very clear that everyone working here was completely miserable and probably wanted to kill themselves rather than provide good service. You've got your typical unexplainable decorative choices to go along with the random smooth rock radio station that both equal about what you'd expect from a local spot like this. Except in most places like this the staff is very friendly, unlike Toyama where I had to ask my waitress for chopsticks. Don't waste your time here. The sushi is good enough but not worth the price and horrendous staff

Zinc is classic, upscale food. It is clean, simple and always very tasty. They have a broad range of menu options that allow for a less expensive sandwich or entree salad to more elevated seafood and beef dishes. It is a small setting so the volume can be boisterous.

Quick business lunch.  Order at the counter, grab a seat, listen for your number.  Pretty standard.

Sandwiches are huge.  For me, the half & half makes the most sense.  Half salad plus half sandwich is plenty enough to fill me up.  I went with the house salad.  Very good but a bit long on the dressing.  The acidity in the dressing also gave the lettuce a slight wilt.  All in all, a very good house salad.  For the sandwich I went with an Italian beef on Italian bread.  The combination was very flavorful but slightly dry.  A bit of au jus on the side or drizzled on the sandwich after baking would hit the spot.  I really liked how baking the sandwich caused the sesame seeds to brown slightly, enhancing their flavor.

I'll certainly give these guys another shot.  Next time around I will ask for less dressing on my salad and more au jus on my sandwich.

Not the best pizza I've had in town. The salads are excellent and several choices. Good pizza and ingredients on the hand tossed pepperoni I had.

Restaurant ambiance was casual, but still nice. Good and kid friendly at the Delmar location.

Chef Michael was amazing! Asked us what we wanted more of and kept checking in on us, the fried cheese and honey was OUT OF THE WORLD, as stupid as it might sound... I will never forget it! All the meats were prepared fantastically. We will be back!

Came here for Valentine's day and had their custom menu set for that day. The food was fire and afforable. All the workers and esp the woman who was i believe the owner, super nice and welcoming. This place is fire.

This is a good restaurant to stop by after shopping at the mall, but I'm not sure I'd choose it over the surrounding restaurants. We ordered the grilled chicken sandwich and the sesame salmon, both of which had good taste. The salmon comes with a side of mashed potatoes, which were way too salty- they were hard to eat. 

On that note, after advising our waiter of this, he was very accommodating and took $10 off of the bill. The service was lovely and the restaurants boasts a welcoming atmosphere.
We love this hidden gem!  Crab rags and pot stickers are delish!  Our favorite is special fried rice with extra bean sprouts.

Have eaten here multiple times. Food is usually good, but they consistently mess up the order. One star for service!

Have been shorted several pieces of chicken. Wrong sides were given. Incorrect sizes of the sides. They give you packets of honey that then leak all over the rest of the stuff in the bag.

But last night...those kids forgot to give us the biscuits with our family order. That gets you a review on Yelp. Why even go to Popeyes if you don't get the biscuits!

Word of advice, always check the bag before you drive away!

My wife and I realized it'd been far too long since we'd eaten at Monarch so we rectified that situation on a recent Thursday night. We planned on just getting a couple dishes, but then the words "tasting menu" were floated around when our waiter came by so we couldn't turn that down. We ended up have a fantastic meal that was all the more fun because we didn't expect to have so many different dishes.

We ended having:
An amuse of a potato croquette with shallots and onion.

-a toasted ravioli with black garlic sauce containing a sausage of a type which I can't recall. The flavors were great as the sausage had good spice and the ravioli has great texture and was also well-seasoned. Only nitpick is that the filling could've used more meat.

-the pear salad with a roasted pear working as a "faux" foie grois. A nice simple salad that was made more interesting with the roasting of the pear. 

- the pear and truffle risotto. Damn, I enjoyed this. Great earthly flavor from the truffles and nicely offset by the pears. 

-the final savory course was the red wattle loin with spinach, carrots and spatzle. I loved the pork as it was tender and full of flavor as it had a crispy crust on the outside. One of the best pork dishes that I've had in awhile.

-Finished with a chocolate souffle. Simply delicious with an intense chocolate flavor while maintaining the proper light texture. 

I need to make special mention of my wife's courses as Josh really did an excellent job with her veggie tasting. She let me try each of her courses and they were damn good.

As noted above, she had the same amused as I did.

Her next course was a traditional gougeres with a quail egg. Wow. I could handle a plate of these. The gougeres was so light and the flavors worked so well together.

She then had a radish/goat cheese ravioli in a dashi? broth where the ravioli was made of radish slices. A beautiful plate and the cheese was pungent (in a good way) with flavor. The portion was just right as the dish could'v been overwhelming.

She also had the pear/truffle risotto and enjoyed it as much as I did.

Her final savory was cedar smoked hearts of palm. The plate was delivered with a cloche that was full of the cedar smoked which was a lovely smell when removed.The hearts of palm had absorbed the smoky flavor nicely. 

For dessert she had a lemon financier with a yuzu sorbet that I enjoyed more than I expected as I'm not usually a fan of citrus based desserts.

A great meal with excellent service throughout.

Miles Table is a great spot if you're looking for a quick brunch on the weekends. Order, pay, and tip at the counter, grab your number, and your food is brought to you at your table! Don't be fooled by its easy system; Miles Table has no shortage of traditional brunch dishes like French toast and eggs benedict, and it also has more creative ones as well, like divorced eggs. I love how quick the service is, and every meal I've had here has been great! This is a great hidden gem that I'd definitely recommend to anyone who wants to avoid the lines at the more popular brunch places in Center City.
Real Korean BBQ! Service is good! Thai food in SB is not original Thai but this is Korean if u wanna try

I liked this place a lot. 

I had the KFC (korean fried chicken) wings. I got half soy and half spicy. They were super crunchy and meaty and delicious. You only got 6 which was an odd amount in my opinion. My boyfriend got a beef hot pot dish that I tasted and it was really good. My only complainant was that the sesame oil stood out a little too much. But all in all it was good. 

They have local beers here from across PA which is neat to see. We sat outside despite the hot temperature. From what I could see inside, it looked very nice. A little small, but nice. 

This place is in a residential area so it was quiet, I liked that. 

Although while we were sitting there I could help but notice a man walking down the street looking at bikes with his flashlight no doubtably checking if they were locked. I of course yelled at him from where we were sitting and told him to go buy his own bike and that all the ones on the street are locked ;)

After that, I began eating again. Just a few minutes go by and my police officer senses are tingling. I see another male standing on the sidewalk watching very closely as people walk past him. I know he was waiting to either grab someones phone or wallet out of their hands. Luckily he gave up and walked away. 

I say this because it is in a nicer area but still be careful!

This place use to be a amazing, affordable deal. We use to love to eat here.Not so much now. We came in got sat down. I ordered water and my boyfriend ordered a soda. The soda was flat and my water glass had indistinguishable grime on the inside rim. Our tempura appetizer had literally skinny shrimp and one each 6 veggies.  We saw our rolls sitting in the bar. By the time we got them,  our rolls were sticky and soggy. It has really gone down. We did end up getting new soda, but it took a bit. Our waitress was nice, but we will spend our money elsewhere. Go somewhere else.  We will be.

Degas is a wonderful French bistro with a charming neighborhood bistro location right on Esplanade Avenue. It has has become a family tradition as we live in the neighborhood. It is true un-creolized French (except perhaps for the grillades and grits on the Sunday brunch menu) with a hanger steak with pomme frittes for anyone in your party who doesn't go for that sort of thing. Do try the excellent soups (the onion is heavenly) and the mussels appetizers but you had best split the mussels if you're going to leave room for dinner.

Wow this place is great.  My wife saw it while walking by and after looking at the reviews we decided to stop by.  For appetizers, we had the both the Yuca and Papa a la Huaincaina both of which were delicious.   The yuca was perfectly cooked, and the potatoes in the other dish were also super soft.  We also ordered fresh juices- a papaya, mango, and strawberry.  Most of the time when you see fresh juice you expect juice fresh from a cartoon- this was not the case.  They blend all of their fruit fresh at the bar for you and it is awesome. 1 I honestly would go back here just for the fresh juice- I am shocked that they don't just sell these out on the street its that good.  My favorites were the strawberry and the papaya but all 3 were really excellent.

For entrees we had the Quarto Pollo, the Aji de Galliana, and the Seco de Carne.  The Pollo was amazing with a crisp skin and chicken that fell off the bone.  It was seasoned perfectly and the amount of fries and salad would have been more than enough even without the appetizers.  The Aji was almost like a curry with shredded chicken that was excellent- it was my Father-in-law's favorite dish of the night.  I would also highly recommend the Seco, it tasted totally unlike any other dish I had ever previously had.  The best part about the Seco was that you could actually taste the steak itself!  We unfortunately were too stuffed to have any dessert, but I really wish I could have as all the choices looked yummy.  This restaurant is well worth multiple trips if you live in the area, and definitely worth a trip out from the city.

And now for a story: A burger and a burrito met and fell in love. As is natural, soon a child came along... and the burgerrito was born.

But this burgerrito had higher aspirations than just being the child of two famous foods. So, he thought about how to make himself better. He traveled far and wide and came upon a place called Hatch. After a wild night in Hatch, he found himself  lying in a field covered with green chiles, surrounded by pigs. After his head cleared, he had an epiphany. He would cover himself in a rich concoction made from these two items and people would adore him. Further adorn himself with cheese, onions and lettuce and he would be even more irresistible. He became known by his celebrity name - Burgerrito Deluxe.

Sadly, there is no happy ending to this story. He was stabbed with a knife and fork, entered a huge black hole with destructive enamel walls and never seen again.

It's Reno Bites Week! My friend and I decided to go to Zozo's for lunch because they are offering so many interesting $10 specials this week: Honey Pecan Crusted Sea Scallops; Grilled Halloumi Cheese; Prosciutto San Danielle and Fall Melon; and Brown Sugar & Cider Braised Pork Belly. Wow! So many to choose from!

When our server overheard that we were there because of Reno Bites Week, she kindly and patiently brought us each a passport, explained what they were offering for their daily specials and their upcoming magic show, and was generally very attentive. 

We decided to order the scallops and the grilled halloumi cheese to share. Neither of us had this cheese before and it was fun to try. It came out nicely browned, firm and it has a salty bite (in a good way). They served it with cut asparagus, arugula and sliced cherry tomatoes mixed with a lovely pesto sauce. There were only two scallops, but combined with the halloumi we had a nice, light lunch. Besides, we also planned on sharing a dessert and needed room! 

It's always hard for me to resist Crème brûlée, so when I saw it on the menu, I was thrilled that my friend wanted to share this, too. It was delicious- yummy custard topped with torched, caramelized sugar.

My friend and I are both happy that Reno Bites Week brought us to Zozo's for the first time. I told my husband about it and how nice it would be for a romantic date for us. It is a cute, intimate Italian restaurant complete with checkered tablecloths and enticing menu. I hope to get back there again soon!

3.5 stars is what I'd like to give Peg's. We had great food when the food finally came but they definitely seemed a little under-staffed in the kitchen. While the overall experience was quite pleasant due to friendly service, ample portions, good food and the fresh squeezed oj helped, we waited about 30 minutes to get our food. Don't come here if you're in a rush.

I especially enjoyed my homemade corn beef hash served temporarily with home fries, 2 slices of toast, and a slice of cantalope-$9.50. My husband enjoyed his biscuit & gravy deluxe - $9.00. However, next time we may just go with a half order instead.  The majority of our group ordered the Eggs Benedict Special of the day and apparently the hollandaise sauce was dead on. Overall, I'm a happy camper but I was feeling faint by the time the food came - longer wait then expected.  I will be returning but probably after giving a couple other breakfast diners a try.
Nice small cafe. Great food for a decent price. The oyster benedict was delicious. The tomato and avocado in the avocado bowl were perfectly fresh. Loved it.

Can I just say the soft shell crab BLT with bacon jam is the greatest BLT I have had in my entire life. I also highly recommend the shrimp and grits. Great food and great service are pretty much a constant here.

I really like brunch, and I'm into trying out new places, trying to find where I want to regularly eat breakfast.  Simply put, Carmen's is at the top of the breakfast game, possibly the best place in the whole city.  The menu offers four choices that change daily.  Each is $12, a side of meat is $2 extra.

I had the scallops with eggs, toast and potatoes.  I really like seafood, but I'm not a scallop lover.  These were the best scallops I've ever had.  My housemate and brunch partner Jonny had a lima bean omelet that looked delicious.  Despite having a limited menu, most people, including vegetarians, shouldn't have a hard time finding something they want.  

The service is unbeatable. Carmen's is a tiny little place, there are about five tables, and then a small bar.  Reservations are required.

Carmen's will become a regular stop for me.  It's one of, if not the, best breakfast places in the whole city.  Do yourself a favor and wake up early, make a reservation, and head over and see what Carmen is serving up today.

I wish I could give this place 2.5 stars. I went here with some friends after having drinks at Bearded Iris and left feeling pretty underwhelmed overall. Full disclosure, I am currently on a 'no meat' kick, so I cannot speak to the quality of most of their menu items directly; but the people I was with ordered a fairly large assortment of tortas, tacos, and burritos. Overall the consensus among us (I had their veggie bowl, which was one of only two non-meat options that I saw on the menu) seemed to be that the food was okay, but not anything to write home about. To me this seemed like one of those places that relies on creating a super hip/cool environment and charging 'casual-premium' prices for their food to trick you into not noticing that you are mostly overpaying for mediocre food. That being said, if that sort of thing doesn't bother you as much as it does me, I reiterate that the food wasn't bad, it just wasn't great. What was great here was the atmosphere. The restaurant was very clean with plenty of seating both indoors and out on their covered patio, everyone on staff was quite pleasant and helpful, and they had plenty of televisions to distract you from your friends. So while I did find this place to be a let down foodwise, it was nevertheless nice in terms of ambience. For my money, though, given that there are so many other restaurants in Germantown that do both well, I probably will not go back here again.
Food is great I look more forward to the Dominican menu like la band era with pollo guisado. Most Dominican restaurants are bars so yes you will experience the loud music and everyone drinking.

I went here last Tuesday with a girlfriend and her parents. Ordered the tuna tartar.. That was a mistake as it was fishy and had to return it.  After that the service was terrible. I ordered a steak salad. Had to ask twice for a napkin and steak knife... Which never came after 10 minutes. I finally had to go to the kitchen and ask another server to get me one so I could eat my meal. When the server came by to check in her comment was.."oh I see you got a steak knife". Really no sorry or anything. In addition, no water refills and requested the bill twice and waited 20 minutes before we got it back.  I won't go back.

So excited for Idaho to finally have a self-serve fro-yo shop! One of the biggest things my family missed from Cali. Note to others: the price is by weight so you are in complete control of the cost of your cup. I would like to see more tart flavors but the ones I'd cut seem to be a big hit with the others I see visiting the establishment. Good variety of fruit toppings.

I am always looking for good sushi on the main line. Despite there being multiple options, I am usually left feeling not quite blown away. Ginza, however, never fails to impress. This sushi place is delicious, with great service, a large and varied menu and the best part... free edamame! 

This is the #1 sushi spot on the main line!
I ordered the raspberry cheesecake shake and it was one of the best shakes I've had since a cruise a few years back. The staff inside of the food court was nice and the service was fast!

We have stopped by the 4th Street Burger King on several occasions.  We use the drive through on our way to our store in the mornings, usually just for coffee.  The gal taking our order and at the window is extremely unfriendly, at first we thought everyone has a bad day.  We have always had the same lady serve us at the window and have absolutely never seen her smile.   But today we ordered an actual breakfast with coffee and a smoothie.  This lady was yet again very unfriendly and when we requested that the smoothie be blended again, as there were many large chucks of ice, she gave us a very hateful look and when she returned with the the re-blended smoothie and we thanked her, she made a rude comment. A kind smile costs nothing and goes a long way.
Lovely ambiance: big, bright and cozy. The quality of the food is the best I can imagine. The coffee is great too. Loved it!!

I had lower expectations of this place to start with but was amazingly surprised. It's new and touristy but the food help up. My wife and I both had specials (Yucatán Shrimp & Doc Ford's fish sandwich) and the food exceeded our expectations. The atmosphere was outstanding. Parking is easy. Will come here again.

The wait staff was friendly and knowledgeable about the menu, and the desserts were tasty. However, everything else left me wishing I had just ordered some pizza and stayed home! This is my second time, and I must say there will never be a third. 

Unlike the first visit, reservations were made, so my party and I were seated immediately. There was water, silverware, and menus laid out on the table for our perusal. The server immediately introduced himself, explained the menu, and kindly answered our questions about the dishes that were listed.

For an appetizer, my party received a cheese dish which had three different cheeses to sample, meat (ham?), nuts, and fruits in different forms. They only thing that everyone enjoyed was the toasted bread that came with the platter. Because some people in my party either weren't familiar with the dishes being offered, or didn't like the sides being offered with the main dish, steak and chicken were the safe entrees for most. I decided to go with the pork belly pasta dish, but halfway through eating it, I felt nauseous. There seemed to be a good bit of oil drizzled on the dish, and whatever cheese was used made my taste buds revolt. I think I drank more than I ate, just trying to get the weird taste out of my mouth.

Also, I've developed really bad headaches over the years, so stepping into Firefly's extremely bright scenery was very jarring to say the least. All I remember thinking is, "This must be where all my broken Christmas lights and old photos come to die." My boyfriend agreed, who joked about the decor's "sensory overload" effect.

That being said, their dessert dishes are great!

I don't know if it has switched owners or if maybe the owner isn't there anymore but we ordered 2 baked ziti and a calzone to go . When my husband got home I literally thought they gave us the wrong food. The ziti  was a hard square that was reminiscent of a middle school lunch in size . The calzone looked like two rolls with some cheese in it. The total weight of ALL THREE meals was under 1.5 lbs . It was a $28 fail . I would have listed pics but I don't want to embarrass the owners . Honestly I would give it a 0 if I could. It was like eating stale leftovers.

I ordered the wolf st sandwich and it was amazing. I am not vegan but was craving something vegetarian and it was awesome . I urge anyone to try their food and open up your horizons to healthier options in South Philly. Also ordeted a broccoli salad with green goddess dressing which was delicious. Definitely going back soon.
It was a good visit I don't know why people hate on this place so much but they stepped there game

The food here is pretty damn awesome and I really like the aesthetics and ambience and overall casual but not slow or sleepy feel. I got the p&k burger with cheese and bacon AND they added fried egg which is basically greatest meal ever. It's pictured. It tasted so awesome. 

The waitstaff is also really nice but our particular waiter, while he meant well, he didn't seem too knowledgeable about the food. But no big deal, some people don't give an F.

First, let me say that buffets scare me. Like Dickens wrote, you have to know that or nothing that follows will seem magical. I come by my fear honestly- having worked in restaurants and with caterers. Honestly anyone whose been at a buffet and been victim to the over-sauced mystery fillet, the squishy pasta, or the picked through iceberg salad can relate. Now that I've set you up, let me get to the magic...

This was a wonderfully done Mother's Day surprise! Whoever chose the spread knew what food does well hanging out over a burner and what doesn't. I can't attest to later in the day, but it looked as though the buffet was being sufficiently worked to maintain the quality and availability of each dish. Segue to food!

Best dessert was the limoncello cake. Yes, eat dessert first! The cocktail shrimp was cooked well and plentiful, and the prime rib was available in a range of doneness. (Spoiler alert!) Restaurants use au jus to make a less well piece a more well piece. Someone was commenting negatively about that while I was ladling some very tasty horseradish sauce on my plate.

Buttermilk garlic potatoes gave me both a new idea and restored my faith in buffets- mashed anything is a tough buffet food. The turnip greens were amazing. A tiny bit salty for me (the salt sensitive), but was that a tiny ring of jalapeño I saw? Yum! The francais fish was very good if a bit spongy on the coating- anything fried would get that way with sauce or steam. Bit of forgiveness granted. Less for the roasted eggplant in the antipasto salad that turned out to be beef! Looked like eggplant! Should have been eggplant! And mozzarella instead of loads of feta! There has to be a bit of the real world creeping in so that the magic stands out!

As I write this, I realize that the magic is really not in the perfectly good food but in the attention to detail that made the buffet work as a method of service. I love tasting everything and then going back to fill up the corners- yes, I'm a hobbit! Thank you for the bit of magic it took to make me question a long-held fear of the buffet!

The

We stopped into Bensi last night for dinner to give it a shot on our search for a new go-to Italian restaurant. Bensi is located directly across from the Olive Garden in Montgomeryville, which seems like a location scouting error as it'd probably do better at the North End of Montgomeryville where the main competition would be the crappy Macaroni Grill. 

On first walking in we were a little nervous because it was damn-near empty at 7pm. Obviously we were seated right away as there was plenty of room. The waitress was over quickly with fresh bread straight out of the oven and took our drink order. She was friendly and very attentive ... although it's not like there were others vying for her attention.
