For an entree I ordered the Chicken Sorrentino, Chicken Breast topped with Eggplant and Mozzarella Cheese served with a side of pasta. The chicken was very good and the portion was good. They gave me plenty of pasta on the side so I didn't have to worry about going home hungry. 

My wife ordered a salad with grilled chicken added. The salad came out a was plenty large and had quite a bit of chicken on top. She enjoyed it quite a bit. 

In all it was a good experience and we'll give it a shot again in the future to see if it becomes a regular for us.

Very upscale and friendly, but not the foreign experience we were looking for. The buffet was very well laid out and had TONS of things to choose from that were thankfully labeled. For Indian food I was expecting spicy, but the buffet was mostly sweet, which was off-putting. If I could give 5-stars for service I would, but the atmosphere lacked any link to this cuisine experience, and I'd have preferred to eat the spicy food India is known for. There were no curries at the buffet, which is an Indian staple. I left happy, but disappointed.
Extremely dissappointed! The Lobster roll that I pick up yesterday was Pathetic! $22.00 for 3 1/2 oz. It did not look like the one in the photo. Not a good value! A few bites. I felt Ripped Off!
Sooo many beers on tap and a great place to bring the dog!

How do you not stop at a place with a name like this? The location itself is a cute little roadside stand with VW bus hanging out of the side. It surely catches your eye. They offer various hot dogs and they all sounded great. I went with the rebel yell as I enjoy spicy. It was a perfectly prepared hot dog that hit the spot. The service was fast and friendly. They offer a few picnic tables to sit at next to the stand. Overall, I really enjoyed my visit and would recommend it to anybody that enjoys a good hot dog.

Ordered food and drinks off the tablet menu, paid for it . Then the server came over and they didn't have the hot tea or almond milk. Waited 15 minutes to get water. The roe cucumber cups were good . Hamachi was very thin and not super fresh. Veggie ramen was filled with noodles but the egg wasn't good. Imagine a hard boiled egg cut in half and placed on top. No flavor

Bridgid's is not an Irish pub but rather it's a Belgian eatery and beer haven. 

The food is unique and very good.  It can get crowded at times and the service is touch and go. This is a wonderful Irish pub with a short menu of good food. Definitely take a look at the beer menu which is the size of a short novel.

The food is very inexpensive considering the quality. Try the tough steak, which really isn't tough at all. The place is really small and can get a bit uncomfortably crowded at busy times.

Nice warm little cozy place, food is delicious however portion sizes are small. So expect to order quite a few dishes. The Brussel sprouts are one of my favorite dishes. The cheese and charcuterie boards are very good as well. It can get quite busy here so expect to wait for a table.

Tasty! Tasty! Definitely must try ALL of their signature drinks. Not only were they beautifully crafted but awesome flavor combos.  Definitely shows that there's a lot of love put into this place. Too bad we couldn't take any to go. We'll be back again to try other creations!

Fast, cheap, very fattening, and delicious. 

Fries and shakes are amazing!

It's a cute atmosphere and a classic Philly location.  I prefer the one on Grant to the one in Bensalem though.

Finally got to make a stop in after opening every time we came it was just way too busy so luckily the lunch rush was slowing down when wr visited there was no wait.

After being sat we were able to go over specials and order some drinks we took some time to look over the menu but when the drinks showed up we were ready to order. A burger some delicious tender with raspberry chipotle sauce and a kids meal it took about 20 minutes for everything to come out. 

The food over all was good no complaints and the margaritas were good the mango was very artificial flavored but I managed to get past it with a strawberry rum

Food great, service is not so hot.

I've always walked out of Nadia's with a full and happy stomach, they have a way with noodles and seafood that is inspired.  It's a bit too complex for kids, but a great little restaurant to take you wife or date.  If you call ahead you can get a reservation for a bigger table, I was able to get six people 'snugly' ensconced mid-week at 7pm.

This place would be perfect if not for the irritatingly slow wait staff.  Ordering isn't always easy but leaving is near impossible, I've had to go flag down a waitress twice for waiting over 15 minutes to get my check... and it's a very small restaurant.  Could be they're watching soap operas in the back or something.

If you're not in a hurry and want outstanding Thai, head to Nadia.

Full disclosure - I've never eaten at this restaurant.  HOWEVER, I do order delivery from here at least once a month.  DELIVERY! IN ST LOUIS!  This place is a gem for delivering their delicious, homemade calzones to my door.  Their pesto sauce is to die for and the customization you can do on "The Fold" always puts me in a good mood.  Haven't had a bad calzone combo yet!

The food is good, but their prices are high for the quantity they serve you. That's the reason for 3 stars
They either need to serve larger quantities or reduce their prices
$9.99 for a cup of rice , one spoonful of black beans . I cup of raw tomatoes, 2 pieces of plantain green spicy sauce and mustard sauce, Seriously  that should not be more than $5. It would not cost them more than $2 and they still make a profit. 
The owner is a very nice man but please reduce your prices or give more quantity for what you charge.
I sure was immediately hunger when u got back home.
Delicious food! Even bought a bottle of their hot sauce. Purchased the corned beef hash and just wished there were more chunks of corned beef. Strawberry orange juice was delicious!
Out of town and stopped by after the day at the state fair.  Found this to be a great place.  Above average service,  tasty appetizers and nice cold beer. . RECOMMEND...

Had lunch there Saturday May 18, 2013 about 2 PM. Husband had a veggie burger. I had a falafel pocket and salad of spring greens. Had iced spice tea to drink. The side carrot salad with the falafel was so sweet that it was like a wonderful dessert, so we didn't try dessert this time.  All delicious. Will return again soon to try other items on their large menu. I ADORE that this place is so peaceful; there is no rushing around, yet the service is cordial and attentive. Recommend to anyone who likes good, hearty, nutritious, and beautifully served food in a lovely environment.
They make the best Kimchi jigae here. I especially love it when they serve my favorite potato salad side dish. Service is excellent. Always leave with a smile on my face & contented appetite

this place was absolutely delicious! i went the other night, and let me tell you... if you're looking for TASTY SEASONED indian food & want to stay safe COVID-wise, this is the place. they have ample outdoor seating & it's so cute at night. the staff was super nice & we received our food in a timely manner... TRY IT

We were there on Tuesday night we got there around 6:45 and there were two other tables. Cute restaurant very clean. We got the Veal meal with the mushroom gravy and the cucumber salad. I got the mash potatoes and my hubby got cube fries. It was good. We got strawberry crepes for dessert and I'm use to having them with fresh fruits and this  was just a strawberry jelly. Not that good. But we will probably give it another try in the future.
Went here in 2019 and this isn't normal Mexican food, they used American cheese for enchiladas but their drinks and guacamole are fantastic

I've been here for both lunch and dinner and both times were great! The first time I ordered the Caprese Panino and the second time I ordered the Flour Tortilla Bowl. I was extremely impressed with both and want to keep returning to try more items on their menu. 

The atmosphere was very quaint, cozy, and casual. Service was a little slow because there was only one waitress, but she was very nice and still checked on us throughout our meal. 

My boyfriend's dad had to wait for the black bean soup to be prepared, but it wasn't a long wait at all, and the chef, Sabrina, even came out to greet us and apologize for the delay. Sabrina is the only chef in the kitchen, which is so impressive since everything tastes impeccable and the food comes out relatively quickly!

Overall, great service, great location, and great food, especially for such a reasonable price. I will be returning!

Service took forever! It's like I physically have to go get someone so I can get service. Out of all honesty, the dim sum idea is great, but for the quality, definitely is over-priced. I could taste the dim sum are coming out from a frozen package. C'mon, if you are going to serve dim sum, at least be authentic, I can go to K&S next door and get me some frozen dim sum and make it better than the restaurant. If I am going back, the only thing I would order is some yang chow fried rice to go (which is one of my favorite dish), I will not waste my time to sit in again.

Second time to Mod was another good experience. Everyone helping me was friendly, it was fast, and the food was good. I ordered the same as I ordered previously, a regular Mod pizza with ground beef, roasted red peppers and fresh tomatoes. The crust was a little overdone and a bit lacking in cheese, but still tasty. Like before, the perk of the meal was the marion blackberry lemonade. Mod should seriously sell it by the gallon!

This is the best Mexican restaurant around. The food is amazing and fresh and the staff is very friendly and accommodating. They have great prices and large portions!  The bar is beautiful and the drinks are fabulous! This is the only Mexican place I visit!!
Great customer service and wonderful, cozy place to work or just hang out. We're from Seattle and visit very time we come to town.
We Luv'd stepping in here. Cerveza draft. MAGAZINE guacamole is a deliteful mix of guacamole, bacon , cilantro & pineapple. Endless fresh chips + salsa. The decor es bueño

High prices, low quality, and supper slow service!!

If only the employees would focas on the job at hand! Every time I've been there they never stop talking to each other and that involves one talks while the other stops working and listens while people are waiting!

Don't think this place will be around long?

I love 24 hour diners.  This place is very affordable also. Had two eggs grits and a pancake for 6 bucks.  The pancake was big and delicious.  I regret not getting something more adventurous.  It's too bad I'm rarely in Chalmette, because I'd be a regular here for sure. Love that it's a golf themed diner also.  Really unique looking place.  I'm gonna find an excuse to come back!

The service was good & our server Leigha was very friendly. The decor was unusual & I really liked it. The food was good. I had a Cobb salad & tried the spicy egg rolls which is really good dipped in the sauce. My daughter just had a burger which was average but she lived their mac n cheese. The great thing about this place besides their happy hour & daily specials is that they have a 20% discount for military! I would have given 5 stars but the table was sticky.
The roast beef po'boys are the best, but I agree that the BBQ shrimp one was disappointing.
Sat at the bar and had dinner. Service was great.. I ordered the chicken parm and while it wasn't like mamas it was very good.  I definitely will be back.

My goodness, where to begin.. its 3 AM in the morning and I feel compelled to give a 5-star review. My office has bought lunch here 3 days in a row. Really, the food is incredible. I got the shrimp & crawfish pasta after many mornings of THE CITY'S  BEST DONUTS (there I said it) and man let me tell you.. I've eaten a lot of the city's shrimp pasta (I'm a Kenner boy Semolina's was right around the corner) AND THIS IS THE VERY BEST. I can't stress enough how good the pasta is. It's miraculous. I know if I ordered anything else off the extensive menu everything would be great. And it's 24/7. This is a special restaurant. It's worth a trip to take.. I just absolutely love everything about it.

As a Whole: BRGR Kitchen+Bar is part of the modern-style Treasure Island Beach Resort. The restaurant itself has really trendy light fixtures and accents, such as lettuce and basil plants on the table! It's a clean and comfortable restaurant to grab lunch or dinner in. 
Food: I'll be back to try a veggie burger for sure! I tried the   House Luau Shrimp salad bowl and found it refreshing. I wasn't a huge fan of the pina colado-ranch dressing it came with so I requested the white vinaigrette instead. We began by trying the edamame pods, grilled honey habanero wings, and the smoked fish dip. All 3 were highly enjoyed I'd recommend these starters. 
Parking: Located underneath the hotel; covered and free *yay*
Location: It's a little bit hard to find, at least we had a hard time finding it. There is a smaller sign with the restaurant name on it but it took us 3 drive-bys to see it. I love the views from the hotel itself. Absolutely beautiful! 
Enjoy! xo
Fall off the bone meat and a Strong drink! What more do you need? It can be busy, so plan ahead.

Forever and a day I felt cheated for never having this mystical dining experience they call Elizabeth's. Every time I tried to go there, it was closed or there was a tremendous wait, too long for my growling hung over stomach to wait for. Now I have had breakfast there TWICE and a dinner there that rivaled any Brennan's or Emeril establishment in the city.  Dublin Lobster with Jameson cream sauce. Sweet breads. Barbecued shrimp and leg of lamb. Unbelievable. And the upstairs bar is a nice retreat complete with TV's, a pool table, and a dining room overlooking the levee for special events. Try a Corpse Reviver if you like a strong, sweet but not too sweet knock you over cocktail.
For breakfast I love the Redneck Eggs with fried green tomatoes or the shrimp and grits with a homemade biscuit. I have heard great things about the waffles and plan to try that next time. I hope there are many next times. One hint: if you plan on a weekend brunch there, get thee to Elizabeth's before 10:30 am. Otherwise plan on waiting, waiting, waiting.

Flatwater is a great little restaurant in Broad Ripple - great food, casual and comfortable atmosphere, and great service! Another perk? I went around 7pm on a Friday night and it wasn't too crowded/there wasn't a wait!

I had their Moscow Mule that was made with tequila instead of vodka - it was good but seemed a little watered down - maybe I waited too long to drink it?! The food was great - my table split some apps, the hummus platter and the lettuce wraps. The hummus platter was a good, basic hummus platter. The lettuce wraps were FANTASTIC. So flavorful and delicious. I will, without a doubt, be ordering these every time I visit Flatwater!

I can't wait to come back in the summer to enjoy their patio (it's right on the canal!) and try some other things on the menu!

I had stupidly ordered from Uber eats and they completely dropped the ball... not sure her name but a woman from 1000 Figs called me to let me know no one had picked up my order. She had me cancel my order and then re entered my order on her end and it was delivered in 10 minutes. Unbeatable customer service, very happy with everything. Oh and the food is FIRE
The latte art was EXCEPTIONAL!!! Also, Philly muffins! What a concept! 10 out of 10 for sure

The food would get 1 star but we had great service. Rene was a phenomenal server. The restaurant was clearly old and in need of upgrades. The menus were falling apart and dirty. The carpet was really worn and dirty. The clam chowder was not good at all. Definitely overpriced.  We were all pretty disappointed.

Absolutely love the food and folks here.  The price may seem a little higher than others but you get a larger portion.  I really like the banchan that come with you order.  My go to place when want Korean food.
We frequent this Outback because the service is awesome (thanks Barbara) and the food is a good quality. If it's not 100% they have no issues making it right.
Much like fight club I beg you not to tell anybody about this place! It is that incredible. Neighborhood burrito better than anything in a 10 mile radius! I highly recommend the Azul burrito.

This place is one of those local gems that has remained special because it remains authentic. No pretense, no hip vibe, just legit local food. There were three in our party and we all had different types of Po' Boys. Everyone was quite pleased with their choices. I had the Shrimp and Oyster Po' Boy, and it was OUTSTANDING. The shrimp was battered and fried just right and the French bread was on point. They have a small bar inside, so I was able to wash my huge sandwich down with an Abita Seersucker Summer Pilsner served up in a heavily frosted goblet. Bam!!

I have had several dining experiences in New Orleans, mostly in the French Quarter and the Garden District. This is the only place where I felt like I was having an experience that one could only have in New Orleans. 

Good stuff at reasonable prices, given the ingredients they use and the amount of food they serve you.

Very expensive and when we got Greek salad, chicken wings and a gnocchi for take out it was close to $40 and sauce on gnocchi were burnt when we started eating it at home.  Obviously geared to the rich and famous of the $500,000 homeowners of Valley Forge.

First impression was terrible.  Order you food on a tabletop ipad.  Waitress very snooty when we asked for directions.  Then...the bill was $48 for two bacon cheeseburgers, fries and bottled water.  Upcharge for each item on burger.... $3 for bacon, $1 for tomatoe-1 slice and !1 for lettuce.  Very expensive. 

Food was good but not worth the  cost.

Expected tip during order/pay process. . How can I calculate tip based on experience  before I receive service or food.
One of my favorite pizza places in Riverview. Make sure to try the Cappy and get it deep dish! I've been to Chicago to get deep dish and this is better!

BEST breakfast in Reno. Considering I usually skip breakfast....this is a huge compliment. They're working on opening a new location in South Reno as well! The crab eggs benedict is amazing as well as the french toast. My bf could eat both of those and still down the huevos rancheros, that's how good this place is. The owners are super friendly, as well as all of the workers!

Easy to walk past, but once you've stopped by once, your life will never be the same. This place makes me justify driving 20 mins for Taro boba but I have to because now every other boba place in Tampa pales in comparison. The sushi, salad, and miso soup are phenomenal here, and the atmosphere is upscale but not stuffy.

Some friends took me here because they wanted to go to a vegan place. I agreed to go because I saw that I can still have the tuna sandwich on the menu. Unfortunately when we got there, we were told that they were out of it. Who's out of tune?? Normally I would just pick something else but that's really the only thing on the menu that I wanted as I'm kosher and not really a salad for lunch kind of guy and none of the other options appealed to me. How hard is it to go to the store and just grab some tuna temporarily until your normal supply comes in? Definitely need to run the kitchen a little more efficiently. Gave them three stars because the veggie sandwich wasn't filling but good. NEGATIVE the juices tasted watered down.

Visiting Tucson for the gem and mineral show and was looking for a nice place to take bae close to downtown for Valentine's Day. This place was highly recommended by the locals. After having dinner at this place, I will say Tucson is killing it when it comes to high quality eateries!

So when we arrived they told us they were just serving a "Valentine's Day menu". It was a 3-4 course menu or you could do al la carte. We decided to do the 4 course. #Yolo! Everything was to die for. We both got the beef rib-eye as the main entree with soft shell crab(we both got this one), beef tenderloin, foi gras beignets, semolina cake, and a Nutella tart. I was in food heaven for the night! It was perfect for Valentine's Day! The service was prompt considering it was Valentine's Day night. The ambiance was also very cute and romantic.

All in all, I had a great experience at Downtown and can't wait to come back and try their regular non Valentine's Day menu.

Great little spot in the Pythian market. Coffee is good, service was helpful and friendly. They don't take cash, but they do take every other imaginable form of digital payment, so not a problem in 2019. Great new addition to the area!

So, we live in Austin and as such, you get access to a lot of good TexMex. While visiting Tuscon,  we Yelped this place and decided to try it. It has good reviews and some that aren't good, but, that kinda makes it more real.  So here you go fellow Texans...
Chips:  thick and crunchy, multi-colored. Very good.
Salsas:  2 were brought to the table, one mild, one hot. They are not similar to what you find in Texas.  The mild one most closely resembles pizza sauce.   The hot one , spicy pizza sauce.

Ordered a side of guacamole.   Very tasty.

I ordered the carne asada burrito,  grilled.  Came with rice and beans.  Pretty good actually.  Lots of steak. Good tortilla. 

My wife ordered a combination plate:  taco, enchilada and beef tostada.  The enchilada sauce was the pizza sauce again, the tostada and taco had very mild ( and my wife commented it was mild, and she prefers mild, but this was closer to not seasoned) beef filling. 

The service was excellent. Very attentive.

I think if you are a native Tusconian, you'd probably think it was excellent.   But, it's different and yet similar ti TexMex.

So, no insult to Tuscon, but I like TexMex way better.

Barista Parlor is a beautiful place to get outstanding coffee. Apparently it's not for everyone and most people have cultural issues with "hipsters" and changing models of customer interactions. We walked in and were fascinated by the vibe, giant mural, stylish mad scientist coffee siphons, beautiful long wooden tables, and grungy masculine vintage auto and motorcycle decor. It took us a few moments to figure out where to order, but we enjoyed just walking around. Our barista was very friendly and helpful. We grabbed a fun booth and unwound as we had been on the go all morning and needed to caffeinate and decompress. Mission accomplished! We sat by the turntable and I loved their selections, opting to listen to their music for the most part over my headphones. I had a fantastic pourover and I guess my wife loved her iced latte. I don't do those drinks! It was the perfect place to relax, read, do some planning for our weekend and just enjoy a beautiful place and a fantastic cup of coffee. Yes it was a little on the pricey side, even for pour-overs, but I will gladly pay a bit more for quality and incredible ambiance. Would love to have a place like this in my hood.

They say hole in walls have the best food. I found  that to be true. This place was ev-er-y-thang! The food was outstanding.  I had the fried crab and shrimp. My husband had the fried grouper. Everything was we seasoned and fresh. The fish tasted like it was marinated in butter and the texture was perfect. Very little sauce was needed. I really wish I'll could take this place back to Atlanta with me. I was highly impressed.

THE GOOD:
-Food is very tasty and lots of it is actually authentic Irish cuisine (I'm a snob about places tacking "Irish pub" on the end of their name and doing absolutely nothing else to go along with the theme)
-They have Irish bacon (almost like ham), which is delicious and goes well on a burger
-Relatively cheap; good for smallish groups
-Can be fun late-night
-They can pour a pint of Guinness the CORRECT way (and some of the bartenders can even draw a shamrock in the foam--AWESOME.)

THE BAD:
-The food used to be better when the old owners were running it
-If you're local, you'll see at least 5 people you know here. If they're people you don't particularly want to small-talk with, then that will put a damper on the meal.

Overall, it's still the place I go when I want to go out casually with friends or take my Irish friends to when they visit.

Used to come here on the weekly to enjoy happy hour and small plates. But the last few times we've been at Cassis the service and food have become lackluster. Our waiter, young, tall and dark hair pulled into a short pony tail, should not be involved in any form of service industry based on the way he treated us. I had a friend from out of town with us and had to keep assuring her that the waiters are usually not nasty like this. And the food came out in portions that were half their usual size from when we usually order small plates. Very disappointed to see Cassis evolve into this and hope they can do better in the future. In the meantime we'll be taking our business elsewhere in the downtown area.
Had beers and french fries and a burger here. The food was really good, beer choice on tap was great, and had a good happy hour environment.

First time here love the energy music playing ... busy ...staff eager to serve and not have you waiting to place orders.  Food flavors awesome I had whole wings with stop drop and roll spice, my friend had Rambo tenders.  The tenders were the juiciest not greasy but the juiciest I've ever had.  Flavor was throughout not just in the crust. I also had mac and cheese and Cole slaw ... both were well prepared and seasoned.  Fish (cod) not cat was good as well.  Made pepper sauce and Louisiana hot sauce available now tables.  Will definitely go back when passing through town.  Next time I'll go all tenders and no wings.  There was nothing wrong with the wings I just avoided ordering tenders this time because they remind men of fast food (zaxbys)

Really good tableside salsa! Mariachi played both of our requested songs, chorizo fundido was awesome. The lobster enchiladas are so freaking good!
 
Another great restaurant find in Tucson.

Another surprising win for Indy's food scene. I was skeptical about good seafood in landlocked Indiana. This place delivered! We started with the edamame. You have to get this! The caramel soy sauce coating is delicious! I then tried for the tuna, but they were out. Huge bummer! I was torn between the crab stuffed shrimp and the grouper. I went with the grouper. It was good but really regretted not getting the shrimp. My colleague got it and I was drooling over her plate. She said it was so good and it looked like she maybe wanted to lick it clean. Maybe. She also had the mule while I went with a basic glass of Malbec. Both solid choices. 

There was a guy playing music tonight, which was a nice touch.  The decor was perfect for the seafood. It was beachy, but not tacky or overdone.

Since I'll likely be back for work in the coming months, this makes the to-revisit list.  But shrimp and crab, I'm coming for you next time!

Finally there is one place in center city to enjoy south Indian food. Not so authentic, but what the hell, I will take it. Stopped here on an evening stroll around the city. The Dosa stuffing are obviously designed to be hipster friendly. 

Ordered Masala Dosa, Gobi Manchurian and Medu Vada. Medu vada was good. I wish the size of Gobi manchurian is bit bigger. Coming to Dosa, I think the batter might be a day old. Dosa batter gets fermented and if you keep a couple of days more, the sourness increases. So I could taste the sourness in Dosa. Masked it with Sambhar and Chutneys.

The major minus point for me was Sambhar is not complimentary, and they give you only one choice of chutney. But again if I am longing for Dosa when I am in the city, I guess I have to come here.

Why of all places in the world does this city not have more late night food? This astounds me. Maybe everyone here is seriously getting toasted and can't have food getting in the way.  Anyway, New Orleans, just a thought, but maybe there would be less vomit to clean up off the streets if your wonderful city had more 24 hour cheap eats places like Verti Marte. 

The All That Jazz sandwich is great, even though we all wished it had any other kind of cheese besides American. Shrimp and oyster po'boy and all the hot dishes like dirty rice and buttery ass vegetables were great. Cash only is annoying, but we survived.

First off- I live in a dry town. Who'd of ever figured that. If I walk east, this is the first bar I come to and the only one in comfortable walking home distance. The drinks are cheap. The beer selection is decent. The take out beer is on point and the food- damn if it's pretty good too. Oh, and the jukebox is insane. I can play Abba to Zappa and everyone enjoys it. Speaking of everyone- this place is full of regulars. No worries though- by the second round you are treated just like a regular too. Occasionally, there will be impromptu pot luck lunches- which, if you are me means free deviled eggs! Am I gonna bump into these folks at the James Beard Awards, no- but this is a solid, never fail, local joint with everything you want in bar and then some.

Dear Bacon; your half sandwich and fry combo is the best value in downtown Boise! Delicious choice of sandwiches, piles of seriously amazing fries and out of this world fry sauce. For $6.36!? Whaaaat? Well played. Also thank you for the loads of napkins you gave me because my bacon Brie was messy. And thank you for the Brie melting not only on my sandwich but in a perfect little Brie pile next to my fries....hello fries dipped in Brie. Can't post a photo because I already ate it. Oops.

Got take out order during the covid19 and a soda , it had no bubbles just tasted like water and some flavor went back he said what do u want me to do that's all we have the guy didn't come to fix the machine ! So why u selling it I wonder why u charging for soda if ur machine is broken :/ just to make the extra few bucks , I changed it for a tea that tasted horrible he gave me some sugar to put inside and seemed annoyed and careless  I hate when bussinesses don't care what they give out as long as they get their money deserved a bad review for not just saying sorry our soda machine is temporary out of order we don't want to sell u crap

I love sushi, and presumably so do you. And if you love sushi, you'll love Fat Salmon. 

I finally made it out here with my boyfriend after hearing many good reviews from friends. We were looking for quick, good sushi with a casual vibe. Fat Salmon was exactly what we wanted. The restaurant itself is gorgeous! It has a dimly lit, ultra modern date night atmosphere. Whether you're taking out your honey or your bff, this is an ideal spot to grab dinner. 

Style's important but we came for one reason: the food. Their menu is extensive, and it was a nice touch that their signature roll menu features pictures of the rolls. Normally, I go straight for signature rolls but none sounded that interesting so I kept it simple with a tuna roll, a Kai roll (an oversized roll with eel, tuna, shrimp tempura and avocado, and an order of salmon sashimi. Nothing too fancy but man, was it good! Their rice is a little firm and has good flavor. The fish was very fresh, even late on a Sunday night. My boyfriend kept it simple and got a yellow tail roll, a spicy tuna roll, and a shrimp tempura roll, all of which he loved. 

We also started with grilled baby octopus as an appetizer, which was great in a ponzu sauce over a bed of veggies. Complete with two glasses of wine, and a MASSIVE ball of tempura red bean ice cream (that tasted like it was coated in a light fried sugar cookie!!!! yummmm), the bill only came to $80, which is a steal in my book for that much sushi! 

I would give it 5 stars if the signature rolls were more creative but for freshness and flavor, I'll definitely be back soon!!!

Finding an appropriate restaurant for six (including a 3-year-old and an infant) in the French Quarter at night is a challenge. A lot of walking, reviewing wall-posted menus, and deciding to move on. Pere Antoine wasn't the first choice, or even the best choice for our group, but it won because we were all exhausted and starving.

I shared the combo crawfish/shrimp etoufe with my 14-year-old. The crawfish side was pretty good -- that was my side. The shrimp side was too bland. The portion of food was decent, and the service was excellent. I think the temperature of the food is my biggest gripe, as I expected to need to wait until the food cooled down before digging in. Instead, the dish came out tepidly warm.

I think the bar is set higher in New Orleans for any restaurant, perhaps unfairly so. In any other town, I would have given 5 stars.

Viet Tokyo Cuisine is a new restaurant on Haines Road, Bristol, PA.  Its doors have been open about ten days, offering Pho (Noodle Soups) and Com (Rice Dishes) from the southern part of Vietnam as well as Sushi.  It is owned and operated by a lovely Vietnamese woman and gentleman who are anxious to please customers with authentic beef broth noodle soups with a variety of thin sliced beef,  meatballs, or chicken.  The environment is utilitarian with about six booths and a few tables around the single dining room.  Decorations are sparse, but the house is clean and the service is solid.  

I ordered a bowl of their Pho Bo Tai (Round Steak).  For $8.95 I was served in a large square bowl of a decent beef stock, nest of noodles, and 8 - 10 thin slices of the rare steak that I separated with my chopsticks to allow each to finish cooking in the heat of the soup.  I added Thai basil, sprouts, jalapeno slices and lime juice to taste, and set out to work my lunch.  The noodles needed to be pulled apart, but that was easily done. The beef was very good, especially when dipped in a mix of sriracha and hoisin sauces. I could not finish the pho. 

Finding a pho shop in this part of Bucks County was a pleasant surprise.  While there are a few others around, they remain few and far between.  I found that the broth, while good, needed more time in the pot to simmer and reduce to a more complex spicy finish.  This is normally at least a 24 hour process, and this one was not quite mature. Still, I enjoyed it, as well as the labor of working the noodles, beef and consommé.  That is one of the best parts of slurping pho. It can be such a hands-on experience. 

I will likely check Viet Tokyo out again to sample the rice options. It would be great if they also made Banh Mi sandwiches, but they were not on the menu.  Still, maybe they could do them as a special once in a while. If good it would guarantee my faithfulness. 

3.5 Stars. 

Can't speak to the sushi.

So fun!  We happened on this place while trying to avoid going through Philly to get to Wildwood.  Stopped for a breakfast sandwich which was perfectly fine if a bit large but HAD to buy one of the Giant Eclairs!  It is truly ENORMOUS!  Two pounds of amazing pastry!  This thing lasted us for two days for breakfast and was yummy to the last bite.  The diner is done in fifties style and is clean and homey.  The staff and owner are very friendly.  We will stop there every time on our way to the shore.
(There is a picture on the wall of the owner with Guy Fieri of Diners Drive-ins and Dives but I'm not sure if this place has been on the show.  It should be.)

Food items were delicious, the atmosphere was upbeat but very loud, and the service was meh. In fairness to the restaurant we went within the first two weeks of opening so I'm sure there were some service areas they have since streamlined. We will definitely be back!

Came here with my girlfriend and sat on the side walk which was nice on a cool, sunny day. It was a little weird at first because there's a slope and you sort of sit at an incline, but you stop noticing after a while. As for the pizza, it was just okay. It was a decent pie but seemed a little light on the meat for the Salsiccia, which consisted of fennel sausage, roasted fennel, tomato sauce, mozzarella. I wish I had gone for the special which had mussels in it. I would come back to give it another try but there are too many places in Philly to try!

I'm very happy to say I have finally came to apricotstone all I hear is good things about it, and it is the best Armenian and Mediterranean food I have had.  The staff is customer friendly and educate you with type of food they have and what they are made from.  If anyone wants an amazing Mediterranean food I recommend apricot stone without thinking twice you will NOT be disappointed

Mediocre hotel, bathrooms are dated and lighting is bad. Staff is nice, beds are comfy and overall room is good. However this hotel is located near a Champs bar and often has issues with the noise from the bands at Champs bar. For example, right now it's 11:15pm on a Sunday night and the drums/music from the bar nearby are so loud I can't sleep. I'm on the 10th floor and the staff at the front said that hopefully the band stops soon.  They said people complain often and they are sorry, I understand it's not their fault and there's nothing they can do but I have a full work day tomorrow and need sleep. I will find a new hotel for my business trips to Indy. This one was great due to its convenience to upscale shipping and restaurants but there's others nearby that are farther from Champs and hopefully quiet at this time of night.

Amazing BBQ in a town full of great BBQ. The sides are all good also--the corn pudding was spectacular. Spouse ordered beans but could not eat them because they were spicy, so I obliged. Mac and cheese was also excellent. Brisket is tender and smoky. Fried green tomatoes are crispy and tangy. I wish I had tried the "pb" banana pudding but could not have eaten another bite. 4* only because the small sides are $2.75 and overall check was pretty high for BBQ in my opinion but I am finding every meal out is $5 higher per person in Davidson County than surrounding counties . Parking and access is typical Bellvue One hit and miss but the inside is a cool BBQ joint washtub and chalkboard ambience.

We are Italians living in Philly just for few months and this is our favourite spot for authentic pasta in town. So far we tried lasagna, cacio e pepe, genovese and gnocchi sorrentina and everything was just as our mothers would have made them. Also don't forget to start your meal with their Focaccia Barese and end it with their Tiramisù, we loved them! This is definitely the place where Italians feel at home

Wow! That was Yummmmy!!! The atmosphere was laid back and fun! Our server was very great and the food was to par, but the sushi and soup WOW was it beyond my expectations. We will definatley be back for more... Loved it.

DELICIOUS! Very affordable menu items with a majority of options under 10 bucks! I had the falafel and it was delicious with tons of topping options. The staff were so nice and friendly and the food tasted so fresh. Best falafel i have ever had!

Disappointed with the prices and portions. I felt this place was way overpriced for the tiny portions they give you. The food was good, but not worth it. We tried a variety of things (mainly because we never felt full). We sat outside which was nice, but I don't think I'll be returning.
Last week, my parents were in town and wanted to go out to lunch. We really had a great experience at Matt the Miller's - very eclectic menu, and server was EXCELLENT!

The food was good. There was just one server for a very large group. Service was not good. Got my drink when I was done eating, and no napkins or refills. Didn't bother to ask cause I knew it would take too long. There should have been more servers

Nice little spot in the Philly suburbs. I was excited to try this location as I love Peruvian food (being Peruvian, it is also a must). The ambiance is awesome and authentic; I loved the side room with the Andean dolls and dresses! 

Papa a la huancaina was good.

Pollo a la brasa, I must say, was too salty for my taste. Great crisp, though!

The beef from the seco was tender and juicy but I felt as if the dish was missing some much needed flavor. 

My main problem was that the lomo saltado was not cooked on the wok, therefore we missed that smokey flavor that lomo saltado usually has. 

OVERALL - Good atmosphere, good service, decent food. Come check this spot out!

OH.  MY.  GOD.  If you want to try the best donuts in the world (at least in my eyes) you HAVE to go here!!!  Literally melt in your mouth.  As I type this review, my mouth is watering and now I want donuts.  I love this place.  My dad has been taking me here since I was old enough to eat donuts.  I love telling everybody about this place and hearing what they think.  And they all agree.  

My personal favorite is the glazed cinnamon twist.  YUUUUMMMMMYYYYY!!!!

THE BEST DONUTS EVER!!!!!
Fantastic menu!  Brunch was fantastic! Had the bacon chorizo omelet! Great service too! Our server was attentive and sweet! Will absolutely come again!
Wow, I've eaten tons of Mexican and South American foods, but this is probably the best I've had in the states.  Excellent flavor.  Some of the sauces are very hot (and I love hot stuff with flavor).

If you're in the mood for freshly made NY style pizza, whether Napolitan or Sicilian style, Pina's is the place in Doylestown.  They also have good sandwiches, buffalo wings and mild "crispy" wings.

Unfortunately I can't say the same about their pasta dishes.  Most of the time the pasta appears to have been precooked and thawed and the sauces don't have the flavor you expect.  Too "out of the can" for my taste.

The atmosphere is romantic or family oriented it depends on seating location and how loud you speak. The host, staff and owner/manager are professional. He even comes around to make sure your meal is excellent. The ambiance is subdued and not over the top. The most important is the quality of the meat and ingredients. Exceptional if I must say. I haven't been in Philly long so I'm appreciate that my numom Katherine exposed me to this wonderful restaurant. Thank goodness I won't have to experience other Indian restaurants as I'm a loyal patron unless duly disappointed which I highly doubt. 

This is my second visit and because I'm a creature of habit I'm ordering the exact meal. Saag Lamb was amazing my first visit and I expect nothing less than quality. The garlic naan bread is a favorite of mines. Dessert rice pudding with green raisins and slivers of almonds. I'm going to eat good before NYE beverage consumptions and they give plenty of food so I'm sure I'll have a nice snack for later tonight or lunch for tomorrow. 

Come and see for yourself  I'm certain you won't be disappointed either.

We went to Bristol's for their Sunday brunch today. We've been before and it was wonderful, as always. The oysters on the half shell were small and very fresh. Smalls are my favorite and are sometimes hard to get. They had a hot shrimp Mexican dish that was fabulous -- sorry, I can't remember what it was called. Service was great. My only complaint is that they put sugar in the grits. NO PLEASE! Sugar does NOT go in grits! Would you put sugar on your corn on the cob? Nope....grits are corn; they get salt and butter. Sadly, they were cooked perfectly -- no lumps, well cooked so they weren't grainy, but inedible because of the sugar! Everything else was perfect. The carrot cake is divine with the coconut pecan filling. If you just want a nibble of dessert, they had key lime pie shooters and tiny creme brulee servings. Overall, very good.

Crow's Nest is one of our local hangouts that never disappoints- the drinks are affordable and poured well, good beer selection for Dan, and friendly service. They are always playing some older movie on the wall, which is fun and a conversation starter. Definitely a dive atmosphere, what really surprises is how good the food menu tastes. They have eclectic options for noshing, that does not disappoint. They have amazing fried pickles which are spears paired with jalapeno-sriracha sour cream, delicious hummus, and some of the best fries in town (according to one of our good friends). This is a great place to be if you are looking for a fun, affordable, and delicious night out (and who doesn't look for that?! ). Happy Eating!

Capedeville is a sweet little gastro pub that got its' start a few years ago before the gastro-everything craze really hit New Orleans. 

I finally made it tonight after wanting to try for years! It feels unpretentious with just some posters on the wall, a jukebox, a bar and an open floor. I loved the relaxed vibe and our server was so sweet and efficient. 

The menu looked fantastic:  highlighting local and seasonal produce (and without annoyingly blasting its commitment to doing so, everywhere.) Blueberries, asparagus, fennel, tomato, arugula, summer squash and zucchini, basil pistou. I was so excited to sample what seemed like smart twists on comfort classics with fresh ingredients! 

We ordered the happy hour blueberry duck wontons with pickled vegetables, the Parmesan frites, the espresso rubbed steak with tandoori cauliflower, and the tomato fennel soup with basil pistou. The delivery was so sad: watery soup with no fennel (or tomato) flavor and a thick layer of basil oil posing as a pistou (also strangely flavorless), the wontons had NO hint of duck and had stale, soggy shells, the steak did not have the smoky, almost chocolatey flavor I have enjoyed when trying other espresso rubs, and even though cooked to temperature (perhaps a little rarer than the medium-rare we asked for) did not have a beef flavor at all. The cauliflower, while clearly roasted with spices, was dry and the spices were indistinguishable. The frites came to the table cold and the Parmesan was chalky rather than the slightly nutty, melty goodness I would expect. The portions were well-sized, however, and the aioli was good. 

The desserts look excellent from other folks' reviews and I would come back to try them. I wish this hadn't been such a confusing experience! Perhaps I caught them on an off night.

The claim chowder was very good as well as the prime rib. The crab mac and cheese was very good. The sauce could have been thicker, but very tasty. Larry, our server, was GREAT. He didn't over bug us, but took the initiative to meet our needs. All around very good experience. We couldn't believe we were in Reno.

We came here with a group of 8 and were able to make reservations in advance. They take reservations by phone for parties of 6 or more. They also automatically add gratuity, which wasn't a big deal as most places do that for larger groups and the service was good. 

One of the nice things is that the restaurant is set inside a Victorian style home, so we actually ate in a room by ourselves. It felt very cozy. There is also outside seating on a porch which is great for groups of 6 or smaller. The porch has a roof, but is open otherwise. 

The beer selection was great. We went in late summer and they had a selection of some IPAs and Belgian beers, which were all made onsite. A few were hand pump, which means they are served at room temperature. They recently won 3rd place at the Philly's Craft Beer Festival for one of their Belgian brews. I can see why as you don't get the run of the mill beers. If you like the inventiveness of brewers like Victory or Dogfishead you'll enjoy this local spot in Ambler. 

Now onto the food. We got some appetizers, specifically the bacon popcorn and the cheese plate. Both were delicious. If you like bacon and you like popcorn definitely give the bacon popcorn a shot. It goes down well with a beer. 

Everyone in our group got something a bit different and the menu is seasonal. Most of the items use local ingredients. I got a burger which was one of the best I've had anywhere. Portions are balanced and everything was seasoned very well. 

Overall this is a great place if you want a break from your chain brewery restaurants, something a bit different in a beer, a rotating menu with local ingredients and a cozy setting. I'm looking forward to our next visit!

I had never been to Blue Ocean before but I was prompted to try it out by a Yelp elite event. This order was to-go and I enjoyed it at home with my dinner date. The rolls we sampled were the Blue O, the Spicy Girl, and the Cardinal which were part of the event. I also ordered a Rainbow Roll and a Crunchy California Roll. Blue Ocean threw in 2 Crab Rangoon which was very nice. The guy in front of the house packing up the orders and expediting is super friendly and nice and it was nice to see a few tables of people dining in. There was ample room to wait in front for your order to be ready and I enjoyed looking over the selection at Blue Ocean's bar because I had never been here. If you're in the Loop and you want sushi this is for sure the place! The maki rolls were beautiful and the fish was fresh. I'll be back to try the ramen and the udon! Thanks Blue Ocean!

The employees at this Wawa are rockstars. Its always really busy, and the line wraps around the coffee station, but they get people in and out the door super fast. The sandwich makers are quick too.

I frequent this Wawa at least 5 times a week... usually lunch, sometimes breakfast. I think I need rehab or something.

The grilled cheese here always seems to satisfy me.  Unfortunately, I feel bad since every time I come here with my father, his meal tends to be so-so.  I got the frazer grilled cheese which had pepper jack, chicken breast, jalapenos, onion, and chipotle mayo on ciabatta.  It was pretty tasty and I had no complaints.  My father however ordered the cambridge (which I was pretty close to getting) which had roast beef, cheddar, caramelized onions and horseradish on ciabatta.  I tried a little bit of the cambridge and it really didn't live up to the expectations on how good it sounded.  The sandwich was very dry and there was barely any sauce.  there was a tiny hint of the horseradish that was put on, but you really couldn't taste much.  This is grilled cheese, it's "gourmet" grilled cheese, but it should still be melty and delicious...it was a real disappointment that the cambridge was dry.

The service I noticed was not the best either.  I've come here before and the waitress I had was pretty good while the place was pretty busy.  It was busy this time on a Sunday afternoon but the service was pretty poor.  Call me picky, but I believe that if a beverage glass is empty or close to empty, the waiter/waitress should kinda be on top of that.  I don't believe that the beverage should be replaced immediately, but I don't think that it should get to the point that I'm looking for the waiter/waitress to refill my beverage.  This time, the waitress never asked for a refill.  We had to ask whenever she came by (which wasn't much at all).

One of my gripes is how the 5B's grilled cheese is more expensive than the others and comes with a side of fries.  I think that this sandwich should be reduced in price and the mandatory side of fries should be taken out.  If you plan on getting that sandwich with fries then it's fine, but what if you're not?  You're stuck paying extra for food you don't want.  It's probably priced higher and with fries because the 5B's is a version of the Bobby Flay sandwich...and why not increase the price on an item that most people outside the local area will order since they're heard or seen it on Throwdown?

I'll probably come back because I enjoy the grilled cheese here and the ice cream.  The service and inconsistency with some of the food that irritates me....

Terrible,  couldn't sit outside  like before without reservation.  Waited 20 min after being seated, 9.00 for a shot of Jamison.  And raw mussels. That's 144.00 per bottle and 2 orders of raw mussels  that we had to send back. It used to be a favorite spot

I live 4 blocks from here and wouldn't go unless every friend of mine who visited asked to. If you google things to do in philly these cheesesteak places pop up before the liberty bell. I think there cheesesteaks suck and you can get a better one at an airport.  If I go get American wit out. The onions aren't always cooked well.

Excellent ambiance with candles at the table that drip wax straight down. I had the lobster soup and the pork belly sandwich. Very filling and delicious. My friend had the fried chicken which was WAY more than we expected. The mashed potatoes were a huge portion as well. All in all a nice restaurant. I'm dinging them one star because they changed our reservation time without telling us. I called and got a confirmed 8:30, but when we got there they said it was down for 8:45pm. Oh well I guess that happens when staff are lazy or forgetful. Food was good, though, so I'll go back.
One of the best happy hours, if not the best, in old city. Home to also possibly one of the best burgers in Philly! I love The Gaslight!!

I have eaten here 3 times and finally decided to review. 
Very clean restaurant, attentive staff and came in a timely manner. Interesting cow décor and big booths. 

I have ordered the Rise and Shine burger (Egg, bacon, onion burger) and the South of the boarder burger (jalapenos, avocado, pepperjack cheese, and salsa) and I have to say I am blown away. They were decent size and not your average burger taste wise. The fries were really good and also the fried dill pickle chips are a MUST!

10/10 would eat again.

Came from California and my AZ friends took me out to this place. It was really neat inside and all the staff were very nice. They were welcoming and answered any questions we had, even though our friends had been many times. They offered suggestions on what was super amazing. We split the pork nachos and the pretzels and fondue. Both were really, really amazing. 10/10.  We went during brunch and they didn't really have an extensive menu but I'm sure the regular menu would've been longer. Anyways, would recommend and would go back.

Went to the buffet about 30 minutes before closing. (8:30) Knowing we would probably not get the best selection. Didn't realize it was 36.00$ on a Tuesday! Also didn't realize the manager would not able to give the $3.00 military discount to one of the guests because they didn't have a players card. Employees were nice and food was good,  but not 36.00$ a person good. I don't think I'll be back.

Great appetizers especially the scallops and the crab cakes, I would give it a 5 stars if the entrees were as good as the appetizers. We went there on a weekday for dinner and they were out of lamb. My dad ordered tuna and my mom ordered seabass but they were so-so. I ordered the pork chop and I think it was good. For desserts, we ordered a chocolate lava cake and lime pie. The lime pie is excellent and I recommend it. I would give this a 3.5 stars.

I love this place and have gone since I was a kid.  It's solid and consistent everytime.  It's not high-end gourmet, but it's good quality family dining.  The pastas are large enough that you'll usually have enough to take home for lunch the next day.  The service is always good and the prices are around what you would pay in a restaurant not anywhere near the level of quality you get here.  My overall favorite is the tortellini, which is what I order most of the time, but the chicken or veal parm is also great as well.  Just be aware, it's packed after ballgames!

This is legit the worst McDonald's. I go here from time to time because I live right around the corner... But they have the worst customer service and I always get sat in one of the waiting areas. I went there today and got a large Fry, a side of Mac sauce and a small Coke... I sat in the waiting zone for 15 minutes.
Their early morning shift is much more pleasant.

I love this place. Hip, funky, eclectic and always good. Whenever I am Ian town to visit my daughter at U of A I make it to Time Market.  The breakfast is really good but I love having lunch here. Sandwiches, salads, healthy options and pizza....whatever you are in the mood for they have it.  The best is to sit and have a glass or two of wine while people watching.   There selection of gourmet foods is awesome too.  This is just a really different low key place that anyone, no matter your age, can appreciate.

I put a star so my review can go up. However, it is completely unacceptable and shameful that such a "landmark" with subpar sandwiches (by the way) is still popular despite what is a blatant hateful, offensive, racist, and xenophobia sign that says he wants "his America back." Ignorance gives me indigestion.

The food is good people. The prices are high.

The determining factor of satisfaction for me therefore was the service, which was piss poor. I just got bad attitudes all around at the Kirkwood location.

Where do these people come off being snotty? You work at a sub shop, and not even the original one in my home neighborhood - Little Italy.
These people are at a strip mall in the suburbs.

Next time, it's Yatz' or Casapulla's.

I won't go pay high prices for bad service. Get outta here!

Good stuff! We had avocado toast, pro bowl and Dark Magic smoothie. Loved everything! So much goes into each item - fantastic flavors! Friendly staff, nice decor- will come again next time I'm in town!

Visited: Monday - September 7, 2015 ( Labor Day ) - 5:15 PM

Normally, I'm home grilling mass quantities of meat however, there is always a first. My lady friend and I had no firm plans but, since dinner time was approaching, we decided to enjoy the last unofficial day of summer searching for a suitable eatery. We drove to Lancaster Ave in Ardmore where it appeared all the eateries were closed. We continued our lazy drive up Lancaster Road and found Azie on Main.

There was no indication that Azie was open but, I drove to the rear of the building where Azie is located and parked. We were greeted by Azie employees that granted our request to dine outside on the inviting patio.   

 We chose a table covered by shade but, with a prefect view of the sun-drenched patio. It wasn't long however, when a persistent wasp forced us to dine indoors.

Inside was a beautifully appointed decor. We sat at a booth where we ordered Kobe Spring rolls, crab spring rolls, seaweed salad, avocado salad, Filet Toban Yaki. We were happy with our food but special attention is reserved for the Filet Toban Yaki - it was cooked to perfection with a taste hard to surpass. The service was expertly handled by an attentive Raymond. 

......not a classic way to spend Labor Day but, an enjoyable alternative.

Love this place! I've been several times and the owner has always been super friendly to me. He's a funny guy and has good recommendations for me whenever I ask. He's got some personality, which I think is why others have responded negatively but I think it's endearing and fun. It's far and away the most authentic Italian food I've found in Boise, so I'd definitely recommend it.

Good BBQ with attention given to sides, but I believe the price point is a bit high.  $10 for 4 ribs is a bit much, in my opinion. 

So, if you're willing to pay quite a bit for decent Q, then this is your place.

Excellent!  Great patio dining. Flavorful, complex dishes. Highly recommend.  This is our go to dining place for Tampa.  

Make a reservation on OpenTable.com.  No waiting!!

Good eating,
Albert
Giving it 4 stars for being open at 4am....or think it was 4am.  Solid late night food.

had a delightful cheese plate at red owl tavern. good people watching from the outdoor tables and friendly service! our server, Matt, even gave us some useful information on the building itself, which is over a hundred years old.

i will recommend this spot to friends visiting the tourist attractions nearby.

If you get the Farmer's Crepe with a side of fruit you won't be sorry.  It is so good you will be taking small bites of it to make it last longer. Also, our waitress could not have been sweeter. She had that special ability to smile the whole time she was talking. This was an especially nice dining experience.

The food is ok. But it can be a pain to remember to bring cash to it there. And the food is not worth the effort. It can be a nice place to go for a drink when the weather is nice out. But during the summer it is just way too hot to eat outside. Even with the awnings draped overheard. There are better burger places all around st Pete. So Yelp it up and check out a place that's worthier of your business!

My boyfriend and I have tried steak and eggs from casinos throughout Reno and Vegas, and Bonanza has remained our favorite. We have become regulars and love that the waitresses remember us and always give great service.

This place is awesome! I had no idea the offered brunch. A friend recommended it for brunch, we went on a Saturday morning around 11. They have a great brunch selection and they offer it all day. We got the ez up platter and I'm glad I got it because it gave us a chance to try so many different thing. It came with sweet potato tots which were really good. It also had doughnuts!! There is this maple creamy dip that came with the tots but I used it for the doughnuts and it was a good pairing. They also have two dollar mimosas! Two dollars! I love mimosas and they filled theirs to the brim. Bonus points. We loved this place so much that we came back on Sunday. The very next day. On Sunday we got the BEC sandwich. And 6 donuts. It was a lot of food. We weren't ready. We could barely move after. Their lime watermelon fresca is delicious and refreshing. Needless to say, I will be coming here regularly.

Wonderful food with fun ambience, but expensive and very loud. We live in Santa Barbara and like to try new restaurants. This one was in a good location, at the edge of the Funk Zone, at State St  and Yanonali across the street from the railroad station ( we parked in the railroad station lot). The food was delicious -- rich, unusual flavors without the heaviness of Mexican food. The decor was attractive and simple with white walls and a tile floor. The inside area was very lively and packed with people as was the lovely outdoor, heated patio area with fireplace. The only problem was that the noise level was off the charts loud.  I had trouble hearing the person sitting next to me as well as those across our little table and we were in a quieter corner area. But it is a hot new restaurant and the place was hoppin'. The prices were also expensive -- $12-$14 for drinks and $60 plus for 3 tapas and a dessert per person.

I'm from NY and the one thing I'm in shock in Tampa about is the lack of decent Italian food and pizza. I was referred to Nabruzzi's by a coworker and I'm very happy I was. The service was excellent, you could tell the food was freshly prepared and the prices were great. The vodka sauce was great, they do their own spin on it and I liked the toned down flavor of it. The red sauce was a bit too tangy for me but that's  a personal preference and you could taste the freshness, so I don't take any points away for that. We had a great night with great food and we'll definitely be back, hopefully to try the pizza and dessert next time.

Had a nice dinner here. The food was awesome but for some reason I can't say it's more than 3. It was a lot of food too for a good price. We had chicken biriyani and lamb curry. It still isn't the best Indian food I've had. I'll definitely be coming back to try more and explore Indian cuisine.

One of our favorite places whenever we visit Phillie. The mahi mahi tacos are DELICIOUS!! Best Ive ever had! Not authentic Mexican but a pretty trendy/interesting twist on the food. The service and attention are top notch! But stay away from the enchiladas... Oh and if you like strong drinks this is def your place.

We came here since it was close and we were looking for something quick in between games at the Scottrade Center. We decided to get the pizza buffet which came with a drink for $11. They had mostly pepperoni and cheese and two different crusts, extremely thin and somewhat thicker. They also had an Alfredo pasta fried chicken mashed potatoes and salad. I tried some of the thin pepperoni and cheese and a slightly thicker crust bacon pizza. The extremely thin crust wasn't that great. It almost rd tasted like freezer pizza you make at home. The slightly thicker one wasn't too bad although nothing special. I also tried the mashed potatoes and chicken. Those were good. Overall it was great since we had limited time but the food was just average.
First visit and the pork entree was delicious. Egg roll: meh. Friendly service, nice atmosphere, will definitely be going back!

Order combination rice, it was fantastic, if you like garlic and fresh hibachi taste. I ordered it without heat and it was great. Also order the garlic and peep chicken, the sauce was great. I over ate, but was so good, I ordered again the following week. The portions are a good size, had left overs the following day.

First let me say that I am a fan of breakfast. That being said, this was one of the best breakfast meals I have ever had. Portion size was huge. Quality food. Wait staff was on their game. The coffee just kept flowing. 100% would definitely go back.

My husband and I chose this restaurant as our first stop on our Clearwater visit because of how much it's raved about. We had a 30 minute wait, they were great about communicating where we were on the waitlist. The busboy did a great job wiping down the table and bottles, disinfecting. Our waiter Christopher was quick and courteous. Here's the sad part... the food was terrible. I ordered a Cajun grouper as an entre and crab Rangoon appetizer. Both were badly cooked, chewy greasy wantons and the fish was dry and smelled very fishy, like it wasn't fresh. My husbands stuffed grouper was a little better but chowder disappointing. Will not go here again and suggest you don't waste your time either

The barista here was incredibly friendly and the decor was cheesy but charming. The owners obviously really put their heart into both the floral shop and cafe. Service was fast and the customer service was great. A decent alternative to chains with similar or slightly lower prices.
Great food and drinks. The staff is super friendly and welcoming.  They are very attentive. Also, it's a great location for a beach view!!

This visit to Philly Plava was prompted by our trip to Philly a few months ago. Typically a Philly cheese steak wouldn't necessarily excite me but after our food adventures in Philly my mind is forever changed. 

The prices here are good. The usual suspects are on the menu but they also offer Italian subs too. Skip the wings, although they were cooked nicely there was no flavor whats so ever on the hot garlic. The garbage fries were great. Real bacon, jalapenos, whiz. Do you like your Philly wit or witout? I can tell you I like mine wit cheese whiz, chopped onions and hot cherry peppers. Philly Plava does a good rendition. The meat is chopped very finely. Could use a bit more whiz bit overall very good. My son loved his hot Italian too. He gave it a 9 out of 10. 

Overall for 3 or dinner was $40. No bad when we had 3 meals and wings. I will definately revist.

I had a great experience here! They have delicious New Orleans inspired breakfast dishes, suitable for meat eaters or vegetarians. Our group had 2 vegetarians and we both got the Garden Slammer and then the meat eaters in the group got a mix of fish and chicken dishes! 

Great diner experience and I love the decor.

2nd time in and they have really got the hang of things now. Ignore the low scores people need to give new businesses a break and let them get it together before they completely dismiss them. I think the service issue was that the booths are so high ( which we really like with Covid and why we are ok with sitting inside) was also their challenge. They can't easily see if people need anything. Solved this week by NR having an assigned staff member cruising up and down the aisle and the manger asking if people need anything like refills etc. our waiter was amazing as well and paced our meaL nicely and gave great recommendations. Table were being well cleaned between customers and the food was really good. Even the cinnamon bread stick dessert was good and my daughter was excited to have vegan pizza out for the house and it tasted really good. So for vegan or non dairy folks this is your place with friends. They also have cauliflower crust avail. Seriously try it out for yourself, there is something for everyone on the menu. This is not the NR from when you were a kid. PS: you can still watch them making pizza's though :)

Two of my sisters and myself  drove over to St Louis to vist Sweetie Pies  Upper Crust on Thursday, 07/12/12 and it was well worth the trip.  The staff was upbeat and friendly.  They were taping while we were there so Ms Robbie, Charles and Andre were all there.  Charles is cute enough to be a model and Andre is a doll, as well. Ms Robbie is a fabulous old girl like myself.  The chicken wings, mac and cabbage was to die for and the southern styled cornbread was wonderful.  I tried the Pear Cobbler but I didn't fall in love with it.  My sisters and I enjoyed our visit so much that  we went back on Saturday before we drove back to Indianapolis and bought some dinners to bring home for our families to try.  We put the dinners in a cooler for the 3 1/2 hour drive home.  This time, we tried the banana pudding and it did not disappoint.  It would be nice of the City of St Louis would invest a little money in upgrading the sidewalks and the streets at the front of the building but in a nut shell--Bravo for Sweetie Pies' Upper Crust. Thanks for the good food, good time and the pictures.

My review is based solely on beverage consumption as we waited out a storm. I had three drinks from the speciality menu. All good, but the Flip Flip blew me out of the water!  If you like sweet, creamy strawberry and banana flavored drinks, you are in for a real treat!  The people who work there are friendly, Sarah, our bartender was super fast and friendly as well!   Live music and great location on beautiful CWB!

This place is hands down the best bar in Montgomery County. The food is always held to high standards and the service is very attentive. Not to mention every man who works there is a total babe. They are the kind of place that remembers your name and your usuals. They are clearly passionate about their jobs and teach me something new about beer every time I'm there. It's nice to have a place around here that doesn't carry the same beer everywhere else has. It makes you get more involved with the bartenders and waitresses and really opens your pallet to new beers.

- Atmosphere is bright, lively, and trendy with a vibrant and modern color and design
- The waiting staff is extremely pleasant and checks on you the perfect amount of times
- Water canteens on table
- Strongly recommend the omelets and skillets, especially the 'CountrySide Skillet'
- The coffee is delicious and bottomless
- Number of pleasant side choices ranging from fruit to pancakes
- Great place for a fun family get together or a casual date or to just catch up with a friend
- The price is slightly greater than more chain-like competitors such as Bob-Evans or I-Hop but the quality of the ingredients and the flavor profiles are an obvious upgrade
- Most meals range from $10-$15
- Has both Breakfast and lunch but I have only had the breakfast and it's evident that is the specialty
- The landscape and location of the establishment are perfect
- Best place for a moderately priced breakfast in Indy 
- One downside is how busy it can get on the weekends...have waited up to 30 minutes...but during weekdays we've never experienced a wait

I live in downtown Philadelphia and have had my fair share of high quality vegetarian and vegan food in the city. With that said, I was blown away by how good Blue Sage was! After reviewing some local spots, I visited last night for the first time with 2 other people and we were all blown away. 

We split the Kale Salad and an order of the new tacos on their menu for an appetizer. The salad was MASSIVE and extremely tasty (so big we had to have it boxed so we could save room for our main entree) and the tacos hit the spot with a large topping of guacamole! 

For entree, I got the "Chicken and Waffles" which was essentially mushrooms, waffles, a fig jam as a syrup. and plenty of other little toppings that truly brought the dish together and actually made it feel like a true chicken and waffles. My Mom got the empanadas and my girlfriend got a sort of dumpling dish. I'm sorry I can't recall the names of the dishes, but they recently changed their menu and the updated one is not online. Both of their dishes were equally as fantastic, although I wouldn't have traded my chicken and waffles for either!

I'd highly recommend checking this place out, and the added bonus is that it's BYOB so you won't break the bank! Great food, good prices, great quantities! You will leave feeling full!

I am befuddled by the positive reviews.  I wanted so much to love this place, but almost every single thing about our experience was downright awful.  Even though the restaurant's website touts their discounted happy hour drink prices, and even though I asked our server to confirm the happy hour - she said, "oh yes!  We have our happy hour from 4-7", when we got our bill, our drinks were not discounted.  When I pointed it out to our server, she said, "oh, yes, we have happy hour, but the drinks aren't discounted."  Huh?  What?  Do you know what "happy hour" even means?  

The bill was for $27 and change, but then she came back to say, "oh, I made a mistake.  It's $31."  When I said, "wait, what?"  She said, "I'll bring the bill back." When she did, it was exactly the same.  When I looked at her quizzically, she started doing the math, none of which made sense.  

At this point, we just wanted out.   It wasn't until we were in the car driving home that I realized they had shorted me on my change on top of the bill debacle. 

OK, now for the ice-cold food that was utterly lacking in every way.  Even though we were one of two tables in the entire restaurant, the food took 23 minutes to come out (the clock is right there for all to see.) So you'd expect it to be perfect, right?  But the rellano was vastly undercooked. The breading tasted raw and was utterly unappealing.  The "giant" burrito was the size of most small tacos, with literally nothing in it but the meat.  No lettuce.  No tomato. No onion.  Nada.   

All this is partly our fault - we should have sent everything back.  It's just not something we typically do ... and we had been there for awhile already and wanted to get on with it. 

The chips and salsa were the highlight of our meal.   Oh, and our drinks were good, but the non "happy hour"  left a sour taste in our mouth.
Affordable generous portion of well balanced variety  high quality fresh fruit. The 2 women working are very pleasant. Will definitely be back.

"America's worst fried chicken" is what it should be called. Went on a quest to find good fried chicken and found a bunch of hype for this place. My quest was a complete fail.

We get there and there's nowhere to sit which seems like a good thing. Perhaps their chicken is that good right? Wrong. We order our $12 3-piece chicken with red beans to go and join the wait. About 30 minutes go by and a couple of guys next to me complain saying, "I placed my order 45 minutes ago, what's the deal?". Apparently their ticket system got messed up somewhere. The employees in the kitchen and the servers kept looking frustrated and lost. They were taking chicken from to-go boxes (with no gloves) and placing it on plates and vice-versa. Whatever, I can wait for "America's best" I think.

We finally get our food around 40 minutes later and head out. First thing I notice is GREASE! The chicken looked like it just ran 10 miles. No attempt to dry it whatsoever. So I pick up a piece and the batter pretty much falls off and behold, I find long strand of black hair caught in the grease storm. I eat it anyway. The red beans were okay, nothing fancy.

Overall: over-priced, unsanitary, and average (at best) fried chicken. I would have been much happier paying $5 for a KFC 5 piece or whatever. I feel like I have to barf now, goodbye.
I recommend ordering the prime rib... delicious!

You can play your own music from the electronic Jukebox and there is a pool table. The best part about this bar is their tapas menu. You can not come here and not have the goat cheese and manchego toast or the goat cheese empanadas. It's a great place for groups and the staff is super friendly.
Exceptional service and great great food! My family and I really appreciate such a wonderful experience. BEST Chinese restaurant in Nashville. Thank you and see you again!

Since I wrote my first review about this

Great staff but I received pre-made spicy tuna and it smelled. Not the real deal if they choose to do lazy mans sushi; the chef was embarrassed they pre make it too.

Accidently came here instead of Cochon Butcher (was pretty buzzed). Cochon Butcher is actually right next door, woops. Waitress was SUPER NICE and kept giving us generous portions of bread and water even though we didn't order very much for 4 people. 

Fried alligator - AMAZING sauce
Braised Pork Cheeks - MUCH tender
Mac & Cheese - LESS memorable

My family and I came here for brunch for Father's Day.  Overall, I would say they handled a group of 10 rather well for having  a packed house and being down servers. That's the reason for 4 stars instead of 5. Food was great and will definitely return. We had the curried sausage sandwich over grits. Best addition was the cornichons to the grits! Standard brunch items were also delish! Will come back and try out the dinner menu next time.

This place was just average for me. It was really cool to find a hot pot restaurant, and they do a decent job of serving this style of Chinese food, but because it's the only restaurant that offers it, they're over-burdened by customers. We probably waited 30 minutes for a table on a dark rainy night. We were starving. I think we arrived close to 8:00 pm with grumbly stomachs and high expectations. We couldn't decided if we wanted to stay and try out the hot pot, or leave and grab some quick food at nearby Guero or BK. 

I'm glad we stayed, but the food was just mediocre for the price we paid. The spicy soup is a lot of fun, but a bit impossible to eat/drink. It's definitely HOT HOT HOT Hunan-style! (And we only ordered medium spicy.)  My mama, a native of Hunan, China, would be proud.

It was a fun experience, but the wait and the lack of service left me ambivalent at best.

Service was great
Setting and ambiance is nice.. pretty dim and there was a live jazz band.. music was relaxing and everything today is great for a date

Food was great and fresh but I just wish it was more on the menu.. its very limited

I ordered the Brussel sprouts and burger
Always such long waits for mediocre food. Customer service is bad and majority of the time get the wrong order.
