We've been there plenty of times before, but this could slow our rate of return visits really substantially.

I actually had a good experience here.  When I cam - about 7 PM on a Wednesday night - the place was nearly empty and I had a great cooked to order chicken cutlet sandwich.
The food was great and the side salad I also ordered had fresh (iceberg) lettuce and lots of nice tomatoes and cucmber slices.

I would definitely pick up another quick meal here.  Npot sure about the pizza - the slices didn't appeal.  Maybe a whole pie - freshly baked would be a better option.

Anytime I come to the Nashville area i stop at this place immediately after my flight lands.  I could eat it like every single day.   I loooooooooooooove the extra hot fish with wings and their fruit tea is amazing as well.  The service is a bit slow but the food is well worth the wait.  I wish there was a way to have their food shipped to the DC area

Went to Pizza Brain last night... they were getting ready to close but they welcomed us as if they were open all night:) great pizza! Great service!! We had trouble finishing our pizza... the slices were huge!!!! We will be going back there soon!!

We just finished having breakfast for Mother's Day.  We had made a reservation through Open Table, though apparently it was not acknowledged (I just received an email from OpenTable stating that we were a "no-show.") We indeed were there.  I did check in a bit before 10am and requested we sit outside (though I had messaged to sit inside as the weather was not great this morning).  We were told we could not go outside (the restaurant was virtually empty when we arrived). We  read in the restaurant's profile that seating preference was done on a first-come basis....so not sure why our request was not honored as there were many seats both inside and outside at 10am.  This initial confrontation made the beginning of our experience unfortunate.  Thankfully the wait-staff was excellent.  The food was good, but my poached eggs (with the veggie and grits item) were absolutely hard-boiled....unfortunate again.  We plan to return, as the atmosphere is lovely and hopefully we will be greeted, in the future, with more grace and professionalism.  A work in progress.

Did I just eat at the same restaurant others are reviewing?? This place was horrible. When you walk in it's smells musty. The decor sucks. It's not charming in any way shape or form, it's just old.  And the food sucked! My son and I went there for lunch. He got the gumbo, which he ate less than a half a bite of. It had a really strange taste to it. In fact, he said it tasted like King vitamin cereal. Which is really odd!! But also 100% accurate. That's exactly what it tasted like. For our appetizer, we got the seafood pan roast. It was nothing more than a bowl of mush. Highly seasoned mush. Why this is even on the menu is beyond me. But then we finally got what we had really come for, the barbecue shrimp and grits.  What a huge disappointment! The grits were lukewarm and had absolutely no taste to them. The shrimp were just medium sized, peeled shrimp in a brown gravy. Maybe they do it differently because we were at lunch, but I was expecting a plate of huge, shell on shrimp. However, what I got was pitiful.  And unappetizing. I would have given this place zero stars, except the service was excellent.

We've eaten at this Carrabba's a handful of times, but after the last two, we will not return.  A few months ago, my husband was sick hours after eating a pepperoni and sausage pizza at this location.  We boycotted the place for a few months, but decided to give it another try this weekend.  The food is usually good, and we had a gift card.  Well that was a mistake....  My husband ordered the seafood canneloni, and I had Pollo Rosa Maria (my favorite!).  Our order took 45 minutes, and when it came to the table the canneloni was burnt (and I mean it was Black!) and my chicken was dry and crunchy.  :(  Disappointed, we sent it back.  The manager was apolegtic and discounted our bill.  The reorders came back and were cooked fine this time around.  My husband wasn't impressed but my dinner was good....so I thought.  We left the restaurant around 9:30 and by 1:30, I was as sick as a dog!  Food poisoning 2 times in a row?!?!  We will never return!

First time dining here last night and it was just okay. I wasn't missing much. 

I tried a couple of sushi rolls so I can't comment on the hibachi. The rolls weren't anything special and just average, not bad but not good either. Service was prompt and good. 

Also, I came at 9 and toward the middle/end of the meal pretty much the entire staff were out on the floor wiping up the tables and cleaning. Felt sort of awkward since I was still eating and felt like one of those annoying diners who the entire staff wishes would just hurry up and leave. 

Would I come back? Not for sushi, but maybe to give the hibachi a try.

When it comes to fried chicken, Hattie B's is as close to perfection as it gets.

I was introduced to Hattie B's and hot chicken just about a year ago and quickly became a devotee - I've probably eaten here at least once per week ever since. I've tried just about everything on the menu and visited at all hours - from brunch to late night dinner.  

The chicken is always juicy with a crispy, crackly crust. As is expected, the dark meat is the most tender, but if you're a white meat fan, you still can't go wrong - I've never been served overcooked or dry chicken here, just moist, juicy deliciousness!

My favorite sides are the pimento mac & cheese (it's the gooey stovetop kind), the baked beans(smoky and tangy all at once), and the red skin potato salad.  There's nothing particularly special about the potato salad, but it makes an excellent condiment for the hot chicken. The cold, creaminess pairs perfectly with the hot crunchy skin.  Try it! Two sides come with every plate, but you can add a 3rd for just .50 - totally worth it.

Want to avoid the long lines? Go for an early dinner around 5pm on weekdays or if it's the weekend, grab some late night fried chicken any time after 10:30pm. 

Hattie B's is a truly outstanding casual dining spot: friendly service, fun ambiance (love the motown and funk music!), and exceptionally good food at a fair price.

Consistently great food, good location and cool atmosphere. This is the perfect place for lunch during the week especially during the summer because of the outdoor seating. All of the food is locally grown and their daily specials include different seasonal fruits and veggies. They are vegan and vegetarian friendly but also have a good selection of meat dishes providing an experience that anyone would love.

6 weeks we have gone here for breakfast 5 of those weeks they have not got our coffee order right. 2 milk 1 Splenda should not be hard. Would recommend checking your order before you leave because they don't seem to double check it for accuracy

Just as a heads up to vegetarian friends out there....

Despite being labeled "vegetarian" (both in name and being coded with a "v" on their menu) the "vegetarian enchiladas" come with rice that is made with chicken stock. Additionally, the staff, including the manager, have an unclear understanding of what a vegetarian is.  The manager tried to convince me that chicken broth was not made from animal. 

I contacted the owner and, to his credit, he tried to remedy the situation. However, when I turned down his offer to a phone call, he requested that I "be human." I suppose he was afraid of nastygrams online, but I only want to make sure that people who care about what they eat are in the loop. Seems unfair otherwise. 

Anyway, this is the second time this happened to me at El Charro and I've eaten their chicken based rice once before, having been told that it was vegetarian. I won't be going to any of their locations, including the new plant based one, Charro Vida, that just opened up on the NW side. I ate there once and loved it, but I just don't feel good about giving them my business anymore.

I can not say enough good things about this place! They understand the concept of quality over quantity and execute their menu impeccably. The tonkatsu and steamed buns are some of the best I've ever had. The broth is spot on with those delicious homemade noodles and tender chatsu pork that almost melts in your mouth. And I could eat those steamed buns every day!

We lived in Runnemede for years before ever trying Marino's and we are so glad we finally did. Coming from South Philly it feels like we are back home. The cheesesteaks are so over looked when people are reviewing cheesesteaks. Apparently they haven't tried Marino's... Now if they would just get Liscios or Aversa bread we would never order anywhere else.

When Georges Perrier stepped away from Le Bec Fin he did completely leave the food industry. Instead he opened up a boulangerie/café in the heart of the Main Line that delivers fresh baguettes, decadent pastries, intriguing sandwiches, and Illy coffee. I had the chance to finally make it down for a quick lunch today and it definitely channeled fond memories of my the time I spent indulging upon the boulangeries of Paris.

Upon walking in I was instantly tantalized by the numerous pastries of the day that sat in a row that tempted me to order and eat every single one of them! But while I could have just have easily gone for the rich looking raspberry and dark chocolate cake that my friend picked up, I had to go with the one that touted pears and sea salted caramel in a vanilla cake; which says a lot since pears are something that I normally avoid with a passion. But the bitterness of the pear paired nicely with the sweetness of the caramel, sponginess of the cake, and sea salt; and especially went well with my coffee.

With quiches, tartines, hot sandwiches, and just about every kind of bread and euro inspired pastry that you could possibly imagine ordering would of proved to be no easy task. But upon good recommendation the Croque Madame with ham, melted gruyere and goat cheese, caramelized onions, and a gooey sunnyside sitting on top of an open faced sourdough was the only thing on my mind. And it was as incredible as it sounds, especially since it came with a salad with a creamy Parmesan dressing and a brownie for good measure.

By the end of my lunch I was pleasantly stuffed, and already plan to come back when I'm looking for a breakfast pastry, quiche, or flan tart on the go. But it also does double over as one of the only feasible coffeehouse options in the area with its inviting decor, awesome croissants, and plentiful amount of Illy flowing.

Just mediocre -- meh...
Had the new Rosemary Garlic Chicken. It was just so - so. A little too much garlic. Think 6 cloves is a bit overboard. The Zuppa Toscana was so salty I actually had to spit it out in the napkin. Can only imagine that is what a salt lick in a petting zoo might taste like? The garlic bread was old and crusty. Asked for more and the second round was even worse. As if the meal was not bad enough....the toddler behind me was screaming bloody murder. (I have two children and believe me -- they were far from perfect, however if they misbehaved when we were trying to eat a meal out at a restaurant -- my husband or I would take them outside. Let people eat in peace and quiet). Apparently the parents of this screaming toddler thought it was cute that the child was hitting notes higher than Maria Callas, We could not get out of this place any faster. I will give it two stars because our drinks were filled numerous times and our waitress was friendly. Will we be back? No thanks :(

LOVE Dewey's! Outside of NYC, this is the best pizza I've had. The crust is fresh and chewy and the sauce (both red and olive oil) is equally delicious. I've had a huge range of toppings at various times and have never been disappointed. A big plus is their house salad which is SO good and not the crappy iceberg lettuce + huge slices of onions and tomatoes that most pizza places offer. Wouldn't hesitate to recommend to anyone.

This place is such a perfect date night locale, every couple at the other tables was there for a special occasion. We decided to drop in for our first date since getting married, and it was delicious.
I had the steak bearnaise that came with lobster on a heavenly buttery cream sauce. My hubby had their pork special of the day. Everything was well made and consistently good.

The lobster turnovers were also to die for, and my cocktail was flavored with earl grey and tasted amazing.

It's definitely too pricy to stop in all the time but for a special occasion, it's pretty darn good. The ambience is very dark and cozy and I kind of felt like we were in a wine cellar of a fancy person's home.

Laxmi's is a marked improvement over the very poor cuisine at New Bombay Grill, the last Indian restaurant to occupy this spot in Ardmore. But it's not especially good.

Laxmi's offers a weekend lunch buffet for $12.95. At first glance, the buffet looks somewhat promising. There is a nice selection of vegetarian and non-vegetarian entrees, several fresh and colorful salads, an array of chutneys and pickles, and two dessert selections.

I tried small amounts of : Chicken Tikka Masala, Chicken Curry, Yellow Dal, Aloo Palak, Mushroom Paneer, Samosa Chaat, Three Bean Salad, Naan, Kheer, and Gulab Jamun. I did not try the Mixed Kabob, Vegetable Pakora, green salad, or various pickles and chutneys that were also available.

I'll start with the Gulab Jamun. Often, Indian restaurants screw this up by serving it cold, making it too sweet, or serving cheese balls that are too mushy/soft and fall apart. Since the Gulab Jamun was the last thing I tried at Laxmi's, after a long line of mediocre dishes, I did not expect much. So it was a very pleasant surprise to find that the gulab jamun had a good texture, with contrast between a more firm, fried exterior and a soft interior. The syrup was delicately flavored and not too sweet. It was great, actually.

Unfortunately, the success of the Gulab Jamun makes it decidedly an exception to the general mediocrity of the food.

The interior of the samosa tasted for all the world as though the spices had come out of a jar labeled "McCormick curry powder". The flavor profile was out of place in a restaurant serving actual Indian cuisine.

The sliced mushrooms in the Mushroom Paneer had the rubbery texture, acidic flavor, greenish color, and suspiciously uniform shape and size of jarred mushrooms.

The chicken in the Chicken Curry and the Chicken Tikka Masala was dry and overcooked, and the sauces in both dishes cried out for salt and more spices in general.

The Yellow Dal was bland, even watery-tasting, and again, needed salt.

The Aloo Palak was decent. It had adequate seasoning and the spinach was fresh-tasting.

The Kheer was extremely thin--it took dipping the serving spoon all the way to the very bottom of the serving bowl in order to find any rice. On the menu, the Kheer is described as a rice pudding flavored with cashews, almonds, raisins, and green cardamom. I encountered no cashews or almonds at all, and counted literally two raisins in the entire cauldron of Kheer. The rice in the Kheer was unappealingly dry and chewy, as if they were using leftovers to make the Kheer and had not paid adequate attention to how this would affect the texture and taste of the dish.

The Naan was crispy, made hot and fresh and delivered to the table. No complaints.

Verdict: I couldn't shake the feeling that Laxmi's is targeting a diner who is accustomed to fairly tame, bland food and wants a version of Indian food designed to suit that simpler palate. I would never recommend this to someone attracted to Indian food for its bold and vibrant tastes. Saffron in Bala Cynwyd has a much better weekend lunch buffet for a similar price, and I would encourage a person to drive out to Shere-E-Punjab in Drexel Hill before I would recommend Laxmi's in Ardmore.

Laxmi's is a vast improvement over New Bombay Grill, but that short-lived restaurant (itself essentially a reincarnation of Khajuraho) set the bar inexcusably low. I could see this Trader Joe's-like version of Indian food having its appeal, but I myself won't be hurrying back.
_____

NOTE (added Nov. 12): On Nov. 10, my two-star review was the only review for Laxmi's. The very next day, Nov. 11, two five-star reviews show up, *both* written under accounts that, to this date, have reviewed no other establishment on Yelp? Things that make you go "HMMM."

Strange location - check 
Variety of menu items - check 
Kinks to be worked out - working on it 

Decided to give the new Japanese Tapas style eatery a try. Starting with the vegetable gyoza, I'd say this was a lovely starting dish. Fresh tasting and pan fried these could present a problem if I had a craving. The presentations is simple all six placed on a white place with a little spot for pot sticker sauce. There really isn't enough sauce to saturate your gyoza, but if you're like me then you don't really need the sauce. 

We tried the Shrimp Tempura roll on the specialty menu. It was good, and I'd say that it tasted as good as other places in the STL area. We had to request a side of pickled ginger, just can't eat enough of it! And we also need to request low-sodium soy sauce, the tables are not stocked with it. 

The skewers, yakitori tare (with sauce) yakitori (salt & pepper) both chicken, we also opted for a 3 piece shrimp skewer and the bacon wrapped large prawn. You really CANNOT go wrong with the skewers, the price point is excellent and really when I return I'd order about 6 skewers of shrimp and chicken! 

Our waitress did recommend the bulgogi wraps (Korean beef in lettuce) as well as the Japanese style pizza or pancake (Okonomiyaki) maybe on my next visit! 

The decor was appealing and simple, very dark. Black ceiling, floor, walls with accents such as tan chairs, and silver and white on the walls. I love the hanging lights, reminded me of Chinese New Year. They do pride themselves on being a sake/sushi bar, but be patient they are still adding to the menu, revising and hoping to add more to the menu in the way of sake and sushi. Oh and we did recommend for the ease of ordering they should look into providing customers with a paper ordering guide, that way everyone is happy.

Five Star Dirty Diner Food!! Relegated to One Star for the abhorrent service. I mean this guy, Barry, our server, may think his 'tude is endearing or possibly even charming. WAY OFF BASE BUDDY!!

The greeting at the door...wait that didn't happen.  We had to walk back to the server station to ask if we could sit outside. It was nice of them to allow us and Deich, the dog, to sit outside and traipse through the restaurant on the way. 

The mosquitoes were on time, our server was not. He showed up a while after we were outside, asked what we wanted to drink then darted off again "just whistle if you need me". There is a door and fifty feet of hall in-between he and our whistle. Not likely heard. 

Brought our coffee and waters out on a filthy tray, set it down and stared at us. We just got the menus buddy, come back in a sec! 

Ten minutes and fifty mosquito bites later and no Barry! We took the dog and tied him out front and sat at a dirty table for another five. Barry, from across the restaurant, "you guys ready?" Our table still filthy I nod accordingly.

He comes over to a dirty, nay disgustingly dirty, table and doesn't wipe it up. He just says, "Dude, whatdya want?"  I commence with my order, followed by what Kim would be having - two pancakes and a side of bacon.  Barry, "Is that it?" Inferring her meal wasn't enough, or big enough. 

Well apparently that was all the service we would be getting. He came back with a gnarly wet rag and wiped the crumbs off the table, INTO MY LAP!!! Not nearly clean, the table decided to give up the fight. We sat for a while, our food came. By that time it was lackluster, to say the least. 

My Crawfish Etoufee Slammer was only barely delish by this time. It's memory was more fond than the actual dish.  Kim's pancakes were nice. The "THICK CUT BACON" was nothing shy of a sliver. Oh well. 

Atleast Barry wasn't to blame for the food. 

Would go back again only for the good memories I maintain from days long lost. 

Au revoir Slim.

I finally got to Nada!

This place was absolutely adorable and the food was delicious! We came here for a work lunch, as a party of 9, and although the service was slow - everyone really enjoyed it.

The meals were smaller, as I expected for such a fancy little place - but the food was very good and high quality. For lunch we each got two tacos, a side, and a small doughnut (for dessert) for $9-14/ per person. My vegetarian lunch was fried avocado tacos, and it was amazing! (How could it not be?)

The menu was good, the restaurant was clean and cute, and the price was decent. We will be returning!

Went for $6 lunch to be disappointed that they took off the 3 piece tender as an option. Wasn't told why just was blocked off the menu. Asked if we could still get tenders she said yes. We got the 4 piece meal which is supposed to come with 4 tenders, toast and fries. We received the smallest tenders and both did not receive any toast. Now who would complain about not getting toast? Well when you're paying full price not even getting a drink or sundae you expect to receive the full meal. I also looked up on the website the $6 buck meal deals and everyone else seems to still have the chicken tenders available.

We were out and about, and the only thing my husband wanted was potato soup and everyone was out.  We stopped here and they just stopped serving lunch, my husband said I just want some potato soup, so the lady said I will go talk to the cook to se if they put it away, they didn't so she brought him some out!!   GREAT CUSTOMER SERVICE!!
Every time my husband and I visit Santa Barbara we make sure to eat here, our favorite! We especially love the bone marrow bruschetta
Banana fosters is a must. Bartender was great, cool story, good service and got a little birthday gift from the restaurant. Drinks we got were also very good

My boyfriend and I happened to stumble upon this place last minute for a dinner date. The service was absolutely amazing, the lady helping us was extremely kind. The food was delicious as well. We were very pleased with our visit and will definitely be back soon.

I've come twice to this Han Dynasty and both times I was extremely happy. I decided to come here the other night after a seeing a movie down the street with my friend. After the movie, we sat at the bar at Han, ordered a few beers and ordered one small plate appetizer and one main dish to split (it was plenty of food for the both of us and we didn't even finish everything): 

BEEF TENDON APPETIZER: This dish was absolutely amazing. I can't remember if I had ever had beef tendon before but I would definitely order it again after trying this version of it. The dish was very spicy but it was balanced nicely with the Szechuan peppercorns in the dish. The beef tendon is cut into very thin long slices and it is surprisingly fresh tasting. It has great spice and flavor. 

MA PO TOFU: This dish is also great. The tofu is served with some ground pork and comes with a lot of broth. I definitely always ask them to make it spicy and they Han definitely delivers. 

I love Han. The food is great and I have not been disappointed yet.

I've been reading about this place for a while and finally got to try Dim Sum Garden. Looking forward to the famed soup dumplings, I was sorely disappointed. They were pretty much like all of the other dumplings in Chinatown. The rest of the meal was okay, if a little salty. If you're really looking for phenomenal soup dumplings, check out Yang Yang Express in Upper Darby.
food was a surprise good food right where we wanted to be and the cost was great thisdoesnt happen in  nashville  very often

This place is a great addition to the Philly chinatown food scene.  As total n00bz to the conveyer hot pot game, gotta shout out our waitress Abby who helped explain the menu, ordering style, and how to consume the delicious meats and veggies. We had a group of 4, and the meat skewers+edamame appetizers, meat+veggie+noodle combos + a side order of Udon were the right amount of food. Wagyu is a must try. Overall this jawn was tasty, entertaining, unique and accommodating. Can't wait to come back after the bar opens. Warning - the spicy dishes pack a punch.
Went sat dec 8 , 2018 . For my husbands birthday . I ordered nachos BIG MISTAKE ! They hardly had anything on them . Dry no cheese , 2 jalapenos !!! Should of sent it back !!!!! Horrible

This place makes me SOOOOO happy!  I met a friend there for breakfast and the food was great, the service was terrific, and there is plenty of parking.  I can also walk there from my house if I wanted to get a good walk in. Pedestrian friendly!

It is immaculately clean with a lovely set up!  I ordered the breakfast tacos - enough to feed my whole family and delicious!  My friend ordered an omelet and enjoyed it very much.  Coffee and toast also terrific!  I really hope this place stays open!  We love it!

TL;DR Good food, clean place, friendly staff, high wait times depending on what time you visit, no reservations, great combo options, decent quality meat, plenty of sides

Decided to try this place out while visiting the STL area with my man this past weekend. I grew up in a culturally diverse part of southern CA, and around lots of Asian food so I'm a little picky. I had my favorite KBBQ places back home. I moved to the Springfield, IL area which has no KBBQ whatsoever. 

I picked Wudon ultimately based on Yelp rating & reviews. We arrived at 7pm on a Saturday night and were told it would be about an hour wait. Given the drive to get there, we decided to put our name down. We checked out the Asian Market next door and got a few drinks at Murphy's Bar to pass the time.

We were sat at a large table for just the two of us which I did appreciate. We ordered the small Marinated Beef Combo which was more than enough (we intentionally did not pick AYCE as we wanted to take leftovers). We ended up spending about $70 for two people (the combo was $61 plus we had beer as well). Thought this was a good deal considering we would have spent around $60 on the AYCE but not been able to take any leftovers. The combo included marinated galbi, LA galbi, boneless beef short ribs, and beef bulgogi. The meat was really tasty, my favorite always being bulgogi, but the short ribs were a close second. Sides were decent, although I always look for the spicy pickled cucumbers which were not present, but other than that the sides were plentiful. Sides included kimchi, veggie pancake, rice, lettuce, soup, scrambled egg, and a few others. 

The staff was all very friendly and the place looked clean as far as I could see. I didn't check out the bathrooms but our table and underneath it were clean when we sat down. Mostly the staff hung back which is to kind of be expected at a place where you cook your own food. However our waitress was sweet and made sure to check on us a few times and brought us jalapeños and extra spice. 

The only cons I can think of would revolve around having a way to reserve a table or call ahead to put your name down though, especially for out of towners. Some people may be deterred by long wait times if they've been traveling. Additionally, when you Google the restaurant, clicking the "website" button takes you to the Wudon YouTube page. While this is interesting for a restaurant to have, I think they would benefit more by updating that link to a website or even a Facebook page where all business information and possible reservation opportunities can be posted. Lastly, it would be great to see some seafood options as well, like maybe a Land & Sea combo with chicken and shrimp or something ? 

Overall it was an enjoyable experience, and I would go again next time I crave KBBQ.

This is probably my least favorite coffee and breakfast shop in Downtown. The drinks are lack luster. The bottled drinks are expired so make sure you check the date. I asked for a breakfast sandwich, they cooked it the wrong way - noticed it was wrong, said oh well and still handed it to me. Definitely my last time going here.

#1 fo' sho' - food was definitely on point! Best pancake I've ever devoured. The Old English omelette was delicious! But best of all was the service! We had a sweetheart named Debbie serve us and I appreciated her loving disposition and genuine care. We found out after paying that she was the owner. Now that is a servant leader for sure! She didn't just help out at the tables, she served the customers and loved on us. We are lifetime customers!

Good, I mean GREAT, BBQ in Affton? Who woulda thunk it? This place is great! Ordered here twice and it's been so amazing that I broke my "try 3x first" rule and decided to review now.

Granted I only had pulled pork and smoked turkey, but I can tell that everything has to be good by how neither of the two meats need any sauce. The dry rub on the pork is absolutely great. I found myself wanting more of the "burnt" pieces. The turkey is so tender and smoky- very moist and flavorful.

I will definitely find my way back here and bring a friend or two next time. This place is def in my top 5 STL BBQ joints. 

And next door is a shooting range??? You can't beat that!

I got the crab cake Benedict and Side of grits! This meal was phenomenal and filling. I was worried I'd still be hungry when ordering it since I didn't see any photos from other reviews. The reason I gave them 4 stars is because the waitresses were rude and made it such a big deal to make a move to another table when we had someone unexpectedly ask to join us.

I moved to Indiana a year ago so I've enjoyed shopping here for local goods for Christmas presents. So many goodies to choose from: Just Pop In Popcorn, De Brand Chocolate, Frittle, Chef Jeff S'mores Balls, The Best Chocolate in Town, Goode's Candy, Groomsville Popcorn Ear, and soooo much more. They create/sell gift baskets but you can also buy individual items. I love that you can buy individual items because I usually create my own themed gifts, plus you can make this a one stop shop to get/try all kinds of goods. You can stop here to try a whole bunch of stuff and see if you like it before you venture out to each individual store. The staff are all very friendly and helpful. Definitely check out this place!

Unfortunately, I wasn't able to eat here. On the web it is advertised that they were open until 8:00 PM. As we got out of our Uber, another group was standing in front telling us they are closed. He said they just got there themselves and someone inside told them they will not reopen until Monday. We arrived at 6:30 PM. Thank goodness our Uber driver didn't leave and he brought us down to the French Quarter. I cannot believe I came all the way from South Carolina to eat at this place and it was closed. 
Our Uber driver that took us home told us this was typical for them. Close when the food is gone!

I think this place just needed a little bit it figure things out. When it first opened I was eager to go because of its sister restaurant being los agaves!  And was a little disappointed.  But now I'm loving it. The margs are on point.  The main menu is a bit expensive but there happy hour is probably one of the best in town.  THe ahi bites are incredible. The nachos as big as my face.   Street tacos can't go wrong.  Service is always attentive and friendly.  In a nice day sit in the sun and people watch on the patio! Definitely check this place out if kit around between 2-5 (happy hour).

I've searched the South Jersey / Philadelphia area for a spaghetti dinner that compares to my mother's home cooking for 27 years. Finally, at Spitalieri's, I found it. Pasta was delicious and you could put the sauce in a bowl and I'd eat it as soup. 

Dino's bites + spaghetti with meatballs. 

I've been there twice in the last 5 days. 

P.S. If you see my mom, don't tell her I said that.
Any restaurant that doesn't have a sink available for customers to wash their hands before eating is a place I won't go back to.

These guys do a great job, good burgers and very friendly service.  We try to stop whenever we are in the woodbine area. Great prices too! 
They have an extensive menu but all we've tried are the burgers.

I love this place for 3 reasons.

1.  Very polite and funny employees
2.  Best hummus and pita that I've had in St. Louis by far.
3.  Black and White cookies

My wife got a turkey wrap and it was just so-so as others have said.  I have gotten the hummus and pita appetizer as a meal and felt satisfied.  The hummus is exceptional and very tasty.  The pita is well seasoned and so soft and fresh it must've been made that day.

As for the black and white cookies, they are a DELIGHT.  They are imported from NJ so you know they're authentic.  They are mass produced which is ok, but I'd really rather someone in STL start making them fresh.  That being said, best place to get these delicacies in STL.

The outside seating by the water offers a great view. The food is always wonderful. The menu has something for everyone, even my picky mom loves this place! The grouper sandwich is my usual choice for lunch and never disappoints. We have never had an issue with the salads before, but my side salad and husband's Cobb salad were overloaded with dressing, so much that he couldn't finish his after a few bites. Next time, will get dressing on the side.

The closest you can get to real soup dumplings out in the burbs! Honestly, this place is nothing special and would not survive in center city - the scallion pancake is way too thick, the soup dumpling skin is also way too thick, and salt baked squid is pretty soggy. So why the 4 star review? Location! This is the only place you can even get such items in this area! Plus it's clean and there is parking - not the same glamour you'd get in Chinatown.

What can I say but that the pizza is always fresh and great.  Cowboy is our favorite and we also add extra onions and mushrooms before baking. 
Always a fast and easy dinner.

This is right around the corner from my office.  The entire office orders about once weekly, and we all love the place.  The burgers are always a huge hit, but have always been happy with my food.  Very friendly staff, also!

Putrid food
The first appetizer we ordered, steamed vegetable dumplings smelled like rancid garbage and tasted putrid.
The cold noodles smelled horrible, as was the replacement.
At that point we decided to cancel our order for the main course and leave still in good health. Disgusting experience, will never return here. Who serves 3 out of 3 spoiled dishes to customers? You can't smell that it has turned and is not fit to eat? If we could give negative stars we would. The health Dept should close this place down. Horroible!!

Brugges Brasserie is one of the great local staple restaurants of Indianapolis.  It is something quite unique and special which I encourage everyone to try out.  If you live in Indianapolis you should be quite familiar with Brugges since it frequently tops most metro area restaurant ranking lists (Yelp, UrbanSpoon, and best of Indianapolis Monthly).  I had the opportunity to travel to Bruges, Belgium a few years ago and this tavern does capture some of the charm of its medieval Belgian beer Mecca namesake.  The beer selection is what anchors the restaurant starting with their own Triple (of which there is a 2 beer limit since they are around 10% ABV).  They have some of their own and feature specialty brews of other regional breweries.  This is one place I always find myself drinking a different beer with each order just to keep trying something new.  The style of pub food is great here as well.  My favorites are mussels in herb de Provence broth, the braised meatball sandwich, and the fries (with mayonnaise of course).  It's a small space so there can be quite a wait, I would come early if you are not ok with a wait.  They have a nice deck and outdoor space in the summer months.  This place is truly as good as it gets.

Great little restaurant in northern libs. It's a mix of good bar food fused with savory deliciousness. The atmosphere is laid back but with hilarious artwork. We sat in front of a picture of breasts, which we thought was hilarious. For food we tried the truffle cauliflower and fries to start out, both were delicious. We also tried the wings which were pretty okay (I'm very particular though). We got the special house sauce which was a pretty good buffalo sauce, but our friends got the Asian sauce and loved it. All in all, this place is a nice casual restaurant that accommodates large groups if needed and we were all content with our meals!
Very disappointed in the food and service. We ordered the trio and 1 dish out of the 3 was hot. Waiter didn't check on us, nor did he ask if thing was OK when he removed the half eaten food.

So delicious. So fresh. Such great service! 
Bastilla was heavenly- crisp crust, sweet and salty 
Falafel were perfectly made and flavorful. 
Loved the eggplant dip and lamb tagine :)
This place is a family-owned gem

I tried their normal pizza, and it was decent. Tbh their country time lemonade in the soda fountain was a big selling point for me. My date got the elote pizza which he liked. You definitely have to ignore the fact that they are located downtown and there are some crazy people around but there is seating in front which is convenient and the staff was friendly

Maybe my rating isn't fair since I'm from Vancouver. But I this place felt like someone had heard a a seafood bar described to them and had tried to open one without ever having been to one. It has all the right things on the menu, but they're all a little...wrong somehow. Like the crab comes already bathed in the butter--who does that? And the Brussels sprouts come with these bizarre lumpy chunks of meat in them, and are way too sweet but not at all crispy. The signature ceasar is almost too spicy to drink but also nothing really special. It was a decent meal, and may be some of the best seafood you can get in the city, but it was overpriced and just didn't blow me away.
Good food, EXCELLENT garlic bread.  The seating was a bit strange, but we would go there again.

Love! Love! Love!
The food is always delicious. The portions are generous and too much for me to eat in one sitting. So, take a friend and an appetite. I appreciate it being pet friendly, but my dogs are too wild. Great addition to Germantown. Oh, if I could make one suggestion, they could post their hours on the doors.
I'd eat this daily if I could! Only wish the hours were better.

I had been wanting to try the Cobb salad that I had seen on social media but originally it was only available on Mondays. Now it's on the daily menu and it was fantastic, one of the best salads I've had in a long time. Sorry I didn't get a picture before I ate the whole thing but it was a working lunch and didn't have any time to get a photo but trust me, it's great!

Panda Express in OFallon, IL

Panda Express store number 2102 charges for Crab Rangoon and then does not put it in the bag. After speaking with the Manager Alisa and explaining to her that the Crab Rangoon was not in the bag, she stated to come back to the store with the receipt and an employee will have the missing food. Manager Alisa then refused to honor the fact that it was paid for and refused to give the Crab Rangoon even with a receipt.  
Furthermore, the white rice was old and dry. The orange chicken was extremely spicy. The Lo Mein noodles were not fresh and chopped into little bits. I asked for the General Manager's information and all I got was initials CJ. No phone number, contact information, or even when the GM will be in the store next. Panda Express owes me for 3 orders of Crab Rangoon's

After a visit to Longwood Gardens, we Yelped something close...which turned out to be really close.  This pub has a great atmosphere that belies it's location in strip of stores.  The food was excellent!  I had Carnitas Tacos that were incredible.  Before dinner...the pretzel braid was amazing.  The chips and guac were somewhat disappointing, but it didn't dampen the rest of the food.  For dessert...the mint choc cheesecake...wow!!

The service was top notch, too!
We ordered a "Provo with" and "American with" and they tasted great - tasted better than I recall from other places.  It was a win in our book.

Foodie Call: always there when I turn around, at a cool dive bar. Or my homebase for bama gamedays. The burgers are always the  best. My boyfriend and I like to split them just as a nice hearty snack. Just tell them to cut it in half if you are splitting a burger with someone. I've had the #1 and it's always amazing and we just had the jalapeño burger bc my bf loves spicy things and it's his bday and omg this burger is also perfect. I'm not surprised. I probably wouldn't have been able to eat a whole one because it's so deliciously spicy and I can't handle much spice. But it was still extremely tasty, like always!

Yes, the fried chicken is fine, though not anything exceptional. Yes, the red beans are good, though not anything exceptional (mine came with crunchy rice too...really?). I suppose if you go for those 2 items it might be fine. Major problems arose however, with overcooked fried shrimp (if you can't cook shrimp in NOLA you have a problem) and completely inedible chicken tender kids meal. Dry, flavorless, not consumable. The kids Mac and cheese was equally bad. Chicken Alfredo sandwich was less than impressive. Drink specials were fine. Service was very slow. I would never eat here again and I recommend you spend your money elsewhere.

WOW!  Very nice restaurant slash live music venue.  Awesome staff and drinks.  Food was also impressive.  Try the mescal drink, it's terrific!  The gumbo, alligator po' boy and Cajun crawfish dip were all exceptional.  Clean restrooms as well.
Great architecture and beer selections.  The location was great and the server friendly and helpful!  I will go back!

Have you ever had one of those places that you want to keep secret so it is just for you?  In your head, you think "If everyone finds out about this I will never be able to  get a table."  This is that place.  We went to to their unlimited brunch and every single dish was better than the last.  The Mexican Chocolate Waffles blew my mind, and the Biscuit & Gravy was a brilliant new take on a classic.  The $3 Mimosas helped wash everything down and we ate our fill.  This ain't your mama's breakfast taco...its a new mainstay in the crowded Broad Ripple food scene.

The delivery service is terrible. I made an order and only part of it showed up.  And when I called to try and get the rest of my order I was treated incredibly rudely. The customer service is incredibly sub par. Don't order delivery from here. Ever.

First...  You have to get a sense of the layout of this place.  The complex has a main central "Philly Marketplace area."  In the front is the "NBC Sports Arena" with a bar and tons of TVs above it including the biggest HD TV I have ever seen (32 foot diagonal!).  The TV admittedly looked phenomenal.  Behind this is a VIP seating area, another bar you can hit, and then a another VIP bar area that annoyingly blocks foot traffic.  By the way, it was $20 to sit in these VIP areas on the main floor during the game.  Uh, what?

Around the outside of this is attached 4 separate pub/restaurants: The Victory Beer Hall, Broad St. Bullies Pub, PBR Bar & Grill and the Spectrum Grill.  There's also a Chickie's and Pete's, an anonymous cheesesteak place ("The Original Philadelphia Cheeseteak Company" what?), a sports shop, etc.  In the back (towards the Wells Fargo Center/Linc) there is a big outdoor area also with a huge TV.

The Victory Beer Hall looked nice inside.  They had tons of their good stuff on tap as well as Dogfish 60, Weyerbacher Merry Monks, oh, and Blue Moon?  Anyway, I think these were all $7.  When we left there to wander we had to trade our pint glasses for plastic cups.  Seems each establishment is run differently and they don't want you stealing their glassware.  On the main floor they had more standard tap selections though we did drink some Yards Pale Ale at $6.

We were there on a Saturday afternoon for the last Flyers game of the '11-'12 season vs. the Pens.  It was an away game but it was PACKED.  A bit of a challenge to get around and grab a beer.  I don't know how often this will be the case, or if it was for this particular game, or if it's because the complex is new, or a combination of the former, or whatever.  But, overall, it was a good atmosphere for watching the game because that's what everyone was there for.

It's hard to say how to feel about this one.  The design is kind of neat though it could have been larger to accommodate more people, since if you're not at the game or tailgating and aren't at McFadden's, this is the only other option.  Victory looks likes a nice space and a place to get some good beer.  I was hoping for slightly cheaper beers, but I knew that was a pipe dream...  The outdoor space looks like it could be fun, then again, you might as well tailgate right outside and watch their big TV.  It still has an overall douchey feel, and a douchey name, but what else would I have expected from something named after Comcast?

Overall, I would have given it 2 stars, but because Victory is involved and for lack of other options by the stadium, I'll give it three.  (Let's just get a real cheesesteak place in there for chrissakes.)
If you're looking for authentic Italian, this little place is definitely the spot! Live music, amazing pasta and Italian dishes and affordable wine.

This place is a good pit stop for your soho pub crawl. They have a good beer selection. But no liquor so that is a downer.. 

Bartenders are friendly and down to earth, music good. Crowd seems to be mostly younger.. 

They have darts and above patio area but other than that it's just your typical bar..

Ugh this place smells so bad. As soon as I walked in the door it hit me. It smells like they have been reusing the same dirty wet rags over and over to wipe down the menus and table tops. Literally the whole place smells awful. The only reason I stayed was because it was a work lunch. I went there at 12pm today. It's now going on 7pm and I can still smell it in my hair. I literally threw all my clothes in the wash as soon as I got home and will be washing my hair right after this review. The servers are very sweet but omg someone needs to do something about the stench. I will NEVER return. PLEASE CLEAN YOUR RAGS!!!!!

Excellent restaurant. My co-workers and I came here on a Monday night after a long day, and this place hit the spot. We came later in the evening after the rush when there weren't a lot of patrons, but I am so glad we stayed. The bartender, Rick, was very helpful and prompt about seating us, and our server, Dom, was excellent. Very attentive and friendly. The corn hushpuppies appetizer is SO. GOOD. And so are their drinks, I had a frozen mango margarita that was amazing, and my friend had a sangria that she quoted as "the best sangria ever." Don't even get me started on the tacos. We got the family style 12-taco dish, and holy crow we all loved our tacos (omnivores and pescatarian alike). Highly recommend stopping by for a bite.
The service was a little slow although it wasn't many patrons present. I'm a fan of the food but the rolls are quite a bit pricey

Really good authentic mexican food, right in the middle of the italian market. My real estate team and I grabbed lunch here after volunteering down the street and we came hungry!

It's hard to mess up chips and Guac, but it was very good, and I was a big fan of their salsa verde. I had the beef tongue tacos and they were delicious! This was my first time trying beef tongue and I was a really big fan. Would definitely go back!

Delicious meal! I have many allergies (gluten onion dairy) and my meal was amazing - gluten free pasta with shrimp and vegetables, still flavorful which many restaurants have trouble with when you ask to eliminate garlic and onion. Husband had chicken parm and pasta and loved it. Great experience!
Great Place. Great Service, spectacular drinks and wine list, and great food.  Will be coming here again!

So look, I eat at the best places around the US. Berns and Council Oak have the best steak. Malios, donatellos are great places too. But....... Sometimes you just need waffle house. You don't come to people watch or see attractive workers. You come for eggs, t bone and a waffle. You can get it at 4am if you want too. This location is cleaner than most. Service is waffle house. Im happy with a server with teeth so I can understand them. There is no substitute when your in the mood. This is not health fare and I do eat healthy. This is my treat, my Mcdonalds. Lots of parking, near the highway just incase of a shootout. Bon Appetite!

ALWAYS a great experience. Have been here multiple times and have always left very satisfied. I love the atmosphere and Ocean Prime is a favorite for date night. Recently, my girlfriend and I went for our good friends birthday dinner. It was a large group of about 11 and had the glass room reserved. When we got there we started at the bar while we waited for others to arrive. Their drinks are very well prepared but somewhat pricey. I ordered a generously poured Hennessy and a splash of cranberry and my girlfriend got a water lol (she is pregnant). When seated we were immediately greeted by our server and waters and bread not to long after. The food took some time to come out because of our large group but when it did we were in heaven. I ordered the crab cakes, my girlfriend ordered the filet and we shared a side of brussels spouts. The crab cakes were delicious. Very meaty, fresh, and a large portion. The filet was ordered well but was still pretty tender and flavorful. Not the best filet considering it had to be ordered well done and we have had some well done filets that were still mouth watering (Middle Grounds Grill was without a doubt the best) The brussels spouts were perfect. A lot of bold flavors and complimented our entrees. Looking for a trendy ambiance with amazing drinks and food for a date night? Definitely give Ocean Prime a try.

We come here frequently for lunch. The lunch deal is $8.95 + tax + tip for soup, small appetizer and an entree. The food here is decent but I've had way better. But since it's a good deal for lunch I can't complain. It satisfies our thai cravings if we can't make a drive to Philadelphia. Only bad thing is that if you come during peak lunch hours (12-1pm) you're going to have to wait a while to get your order taken and food to come out since there is only one waiter for the entire restaurant and it gets pretty packed during peak lunch hours. Try to come early or as soon as they open.

Amazing all around. Best fajitas we've ever had. Sam was our server and was incredible with our dietary redirections. And we sat outside under the heater and brought our little dog and was the perfect stop on our way back to LA. We will be back.
I've been to Kitchen 519 a few times now, and I've always had a good experience. The food is AMAZING! I'm looking forward to my next visit!
Loved this place!  Food was delicious and service was great!  We were having breakfast ahead of a long drive so no cocktails but they all looked delicious.  Highly recommend!

Excellent food, service, and quality in the heart of Nashville. 
I came here on a Sunday afternoon with a friend after a night of ruckus in downtown Nashville. It was very obvious that we had a rough night given that I was in ninja turtle pajamas and my friend was wearing sweatpants and a hoodie. This is a very classy establishment and we stuck out like sore thumbs.

We were still given a five-star treatment despite our given disheveled look which I truly appreciate. We entertained our waiter with stories of our debauchery the night before and got to ordering. Lots of water was had while at this fine establishment. We asked our waiter to please just leave the pitcher and he obliged kindly. Fantastic water. 

The food was just as amazing. Both my friend and I ordered steak and biscuit Benedict. The eggs were cooked perfectly, not too runny to where it just oozes out. Perfectly soft boiled. The steak was cooked as asked without any issues. Seasoned well and delicious. Also there was an assortment of green on my plate. I'm not sure if this was strictly for display purposes or to be ingested, but they were delicious. 

What I found unique and very tasty was their assortment of ketchup/sauces. The assortment of condiment sauces was heterogeneous and delicious. Especially the Texas ketchup, which seemed to be a mix between a homemade ketchup and salsa, both sweet and spicy.

Lastly, I have to comment on the staff. A vibrant group of individuals who were very attentive to our needs/wants, with equally hospitable spirits. From the servers, to the hostesses we were treated like royalty despite looking like paupers. I would recommend The Southern Steak & Oyster for any occasion. Looking forward to coming back.

Some really good things and a few not so good.  First it is by far the closest to authentic Chicago deep dish in Nashville (apart from my homemade version which rocks!!).  So many places call themselves Chicago style but all they do is make a thick crust and throw on toppings (in the wrong order by the way).  If you know Chicago pizza then this is most like Giordanno's.  We've been here many times but the most recent deep dish we got was too "soupy" if that's a word for pizza.  What I mean is when they dished out the slices it was very runny and spread out all over the plate.  It was no longer a slice of pizza but a puddle of pizza.  Deep dish pizza needs to rest, just like lasagna.  Because they take so long at 312 to make their deep dish they probably just want it out on the table ASAP.  I understand that but they need to come up with better organization in their kitchen to allow for the deep dish to rest several minutes.  When you go to Gino's East or Lou Malnati's in Chicago they get deep dish out in 45 minutes and it's perfect.  Here you can easily wait an hour.  As much as I love Chicago deep dish my favorite is actually Chicago thin crust.  312 has excellent thin crust pizza, one of the best in all of the state.  

The dining room is nice with a number of things honoring the great city of Chicago.  It has just enough Chicago décor to give you a Chi-town atmosphere, yet not too much so they don't overdo it for those who couldn't care less.  
I wish they had fountain Coke.  They have the Mexican Coke in a bottle, which is good, but can be pricey if you have to wait an hour for your deep dish to cook and you drink 2 or 3.  Even if you go with their copy-cat fountain Coke (which isn't that great) you still pay for refills.  On a visit back in 2015 I complimented one of the owner's on how authentic the deep dish was.  I then mentioned that I had in my freezer at home several frozen pizzas from Gino's East and Lou Malnati's (the top 2 deep dish pizza places in Chicago and the world).  In response she said her crust was better and made some snide remark about those places.  First of all, respect the originals and the best.  Second, what competition are they to you as they're both 400+ miles away?  Sounds jealous to me.  Regardless I'll continue to visit 312 periodically and pay for refills.  I'm glad to have them in town, but would love it if they had some competition.  Rosati's (a Chicago pizza place) has a location now in Knoxville so maybe they'll eventually find their way to Nashville.  That would be great because Rosati's is a little better than 312.
We had dinner at Il Palato the other night. The new space is open and light. Waiter was great. Food was very good. Check it out.

The good: My falafel burger wrapped in lettuce was REALLY good. I don't even really like burgers, it was damn good. Everyone at our table of 8 enjoyed what they had. They can cook good food. 

The bad: The place was overly crowded and very loud. Our server was obviously overwhelmed. The worst part was they started packing up our things and  seemed visibly annoyed that we hung around for a few minutes after.

My wife and I live in Hermitage and visit about once per month.  The atmosphere does seem  slightly dated, but that's part of the charm.  I would term service as slightly above average, but steak quality is well above average,  bordering on excellent.  The potato, however, was disappointing.  Although hot, the potato was hard and grainy.  Needs better quality spud (from Idaho - yes, it does make a difference) and baked longer.  Salad bar was fresh, clean with good variety.  And finally, pricing was fair for a quality steak.  We will be back and would recommend.

We come here often, and love the prices as well the servers! The food is usually pretty good, but we almost always get appetizers. I've heard complaints about some of the entrees, but we've always had a great meal.

This is my go-to coffee joint in New Orleans. The prices are reasonable, especially for what you get in this foodie/tourist city. They're increased their prices a little since I moved here, but not enough to be a deterrent. There's space upstairs that is regularly used for meetings, and there is patio and indoor seating.

Busy hours are kind of annoying. It sucks to be pushed out onto the patio most of the year because New Orleans is a fickle mistress. If it isn't sweltering, it's raining. For the other month and a half of the year, it's too cold to enjoy sitting outside (says the lady from Florida). They are dog friendly, and it's common to see dogs enjoying patio space with a water bowl next to them. 

The coffee is very good. When I lived in Midcity, I made it a point to walk here for a few hours of work most days. There is free wifi, and the baristas have mostly been friendly and chatty. 

I've seen people conduct job interviews, work at tables, and have game nights and meetings. The biggest drawback for me is that they close so early.

I was in the area so I figured I'd check out Cheung's. Satisfactory but not outstanding. The egg rolls were a bit heavy on the sesame oil & the crab rangoon were pretty disappointing. Everything else had generous portions & were okay.
Fresh, flavorful and one of the best baba ganoush I have had. Tabouli delicious, greek salad dressing light and tangy, and the owners are so nice.  This will be a regular stop.

The first thing I did before starting to write this review was check the rating on the Applebees across the street (2.5 stars).  I did this because if I didn't know any better, I would swear they are using the same kitchen.

My whole family was not impressed with Max Brenner.  Great on concept, lacking in execution.  We were so excited to try this place, but it was a downer from a flavor perspective.  I really think their desserts are not any better than those you get at any chain, but they cost more.  

Someone said in another review an "upscale Friendly's."  That pretty much nails it.  

The service was very friendly, but inept as well.  I received my diet coke at least 5 minutes before the rest of my family received their waters.  It took a long time to get our bill etc...

This place is ok if you're sitting at the bar.  If not, don't expect to get great service.  The beer is ok, but I'm not a big fan of the food.  It's not awful, but I find myself coming up with reasons not to come here and go elsewhere instead.

Spent almost $60 on three plates of food and all three were sour. I called and they offered me a new plate, which I took but soon discovered the new plate was sour too. Stuffed pepper, and macaroni on my other 2 plates were sour as well. My family just threw them all away. I'm so disappointed, If they knew the food had been sitting out all day they should've just offered a refund.

Just from outdoor branding, I didn't expect Salt to last long and put off making a visit since I knew it was pretty pricey. A visiting friend expressed a seafood craving last weekend, so I finally used it as an excuse to give it a try. I was VERY impressed. We were able to make a reservation just a couple hours in advance. Our server was a delight and provide friendly, thorough, and informative service throughout the evening. Our rock shrimp appetizer was amazing. My tuna entree was delicious and I couldn't resist the watermelon Caprese salad. I was much too full for dessert. Environment was very peaceful and pretty. Only comments would be that a bread basket or something would be a nice addition and that total bill is a bit expensive after ordering multiple items. Delicious food, though, and I hope to return soon.

I'd been wanting to try this place out for a while and finally got a chance to last night. I loved it! I had a tough time deciding what to order, a whole menu of options for a veg is awesome :) The person who took my order was very friendly and the order arrived faster than they said it was. Food was delicious and filling. I love that the delivery minimum is a realistic $10 so if you don't want a huge meal you could get away with ordering appetizers. Definitely ready to try more dishes from this place.

I'm so sad and sorry to report we can no longer stay here. There is a serious mold problem here and I really really want to pick up and leave my room at 11:30pm! My eyes burn horrifically, I literally can not breathe. The hallways on floor 3 (where we're staying) have mold over every single air vent. The carpets in the entire property are completely disgracefully shameful. What a DUMP. I hate saying this because we've spent so many birthdays and anniversaries here. One of our favorite places is beyond trashed. 

We called around 3 to have someone come to empty our trash and bring more shampoos and towels. We were leaving the room to let him come in to clean and he only brought towels. My husband asked for more shampoo and asked him to empty trash. We come back from a walk and there is soap on our doorknob outside our room and he STILL never emptied our trash. We have trash and food everywhere. 

What a shame that such a world renowned property does not live up to such expectations. What a mesmerizing beautiful property that has not been kept up. Truly sad.
Okay so I totally love this place. This is the real deal it is authentic and this food is awesome!! It's real fast food at a decent price chicken tacos are a 1.25

Well. Where does one start. We sat outside and then asked what beer was on tap and our server mentioned yards and dogfishhead. So we asked which ones and she wasn't sure, we figured she's not a beer drinker, it's ok, so we walked up to the bar to ask the bartender, who proceeded to look around for an answer, look at the actual tap and said she didn't know either. so they know what breweries they have beer from, but not what types. We went for yuengling. We ordered some food and two members of our party ordered a gin and tonic and a whiskey sour. after a 10-15min wait we got the beer and a red drink that instead of a gin and tonic was what we deduced was a tonic water and grenadine. when our other member finally got his whiskey sour it was mostly sour with a splash of whiskey. however the kicker that made us get up and leave was when my friend who received the incorrect gin and tonic got a replacement of a neat whiskey and got back to the table with it she realized it had bugs in it. not one bug. not something flew into her drink, several little beetles (like you might find in with your rice or pasta). We got up to leave and brought the drink up to another server who was very kind and offered to right the situation, but we were done at that point. not sure if they had a bad day or they are normally that bad. but we will definitely not be returning. p.s. sorry to the waitress, you were also very nice and we regret not leaving you a tip for your service. but the bugs. I have never seen that. We could not stay.
Small menu. Know what you want. Busy place. Friendly workers.  Try the soup of the day, in season.

O

Best food ever!! So glad they made it through Covid and can still serve the best breakfast around town!  Ya gotta have the jalapeño cheese grits and the ultimate egg sandwich is da bomb!! We love the food and the peeps!! Enjoy!!

Pizza was fantastic, service was friendly even though we strolled in 15 minutes before close on a Sunday night.  Bonus: didn't feel like crap afterwards.  You can tell the difference in the ingredients they use, especially when you're done, although scarfing down 4 slices at 11pm is not good for you no matter how "healthy" the pie.  But the pizza itself is delicious.  I can now see what all the fuss is about, and I wish their Texas investor would get the ball rolling.  What are you waiting for, Cuban?
Their lunch buffet is scrumptious! I wish they were near my home instead of my work so I could go for dinner too! Delicious food!

Wanted to try this place forever. Waited outside on a beautiful day for about 20 min. We got the sweet potato pancakes with non wet whipped cream (acts like butter). Then you pour the cinnamon cream on top...HEAVEN!!! We also got the Santa Fe corn cakes. These were also delish. Not sweet at all unless you add the provided maple syrup. If you love cornbread, you will love these!!
I would gladly come back here. Also eggs and non breakfast sandwiches available. It's a sit down place. You just have to wait in line for a table. Good service. Good was served hot and fairly fast.

Way not the best pizza on sand key, that honor goes to original pizza in reddington. Most like famiglia's. But the bar is great and the service is great too. And walking distance to lots of other stuff. Definitely  a fun place just north of the narrows

I went to website to do call ahead seating. I entered all information & drove to restaurant, approximately 1/2 mile. When we got to hotel, I went in just to be sure we were on list. The lady with short hair & blue top told me that they had not received my information. She asked if I called in. I told her no, I had signed in on website. She told me that they don't do it that way, you have to call in. I said that they should remove that option from website because I almost didn't go in to check since I thought we were already checked in. I never raised my voice in any way, She told me not to yell at her! I said that I wasn't yelling, but it should be removed from site if you can't use it. Again, I was told not to yell at her. They lost our business tonight! That was a very rude way to address a guest!
Love this place! Great food! Nicely done Caribbean jerk and sides! Nice location and outdoor seating too.
Great place got the TriTip sandwich was good all do I wish they had more of a variety of BBQ sauce but other then that it's a great new place! Would highly recommend it to a friend !

This is the first and last stop for the beer connoisseur!  With more beers on tap than I've ever seen in a single bar, no fan of beer can be disappointed, unless you're a bud light guy.  If that's the case, just buy a six pack and stay at home.  Crum's is only for people who appreciate good beer from across the world.

The best deal at Crum's is it's flights.  The flight allows you to get four four ounce beers for just $5.  With such a large selection, there's really no other way to go.  Of course, if you love one specific beer, you can also order the full size.

This is a great bar for the beer connoisseur, but the atmosphere could be better.  The bar has incredibly limited patio seating.  Additionally, the interior often smells of cigarette smoke.  Moreover, it always appears to be night, as the windows are tinted and barely let in any light.  Obviously, this is the ideal atmosphere for the heavy drinker, but as the beverage selection seems to be geared for the beer connoisseur, the Crum's atmosphere somewhat misses the mark.

That being said, the staff is wonderfully brilliant in beer.  They can tell you so much about any beer they have on tap.  Usually, they also allow you to sample the beer.

Overall, Crum's is one of the more amazing bars in St. Pete.  If you love beer, you need to stop here!
We just had a wonderful dinner for our first time at the Vine!  Waitstaff and owner very attentive to your needs, great view of the city and the food was outstanding! We will be back, and soon!

I'm from Kansas City, the barbecue capital of the world.  Don't question that fact either.  St. Louis, Texas, Memphis, Carolinas...all of them ain't got nothin' on KC.  With that said, I'm a big fan of BBQ, but also a big critic.  So...

This place is pretty good, but misses on a few key points.

MEAT: The meats are definitely the thing they do best, which is obviously a good thing.  Their dry rub is nice.  The meats are cooked to perfection: falling apart with fatty tenderness.  I had the pulled pork, the pork belly, and the brisket.  Also, the chicken wings are great.  Overall, good meats.

SAUCE: The sauces are all pretty weak in my opinion.  They have a traditional, a sweet, and a hot.  The traditional is too tomatoey.  The sweet isn't that sweet.  And the hot is too vinegary.  I found the best flavor to be a mixture of all three (roughly 1/2 original, 1/4 sweet, 1/4 hot).  Yay for my mixology skills.

OTHER:  
Solid: Mac n cheese, jalapeno cheddar cornbread, sweet potatoes
Weak: Carrots, the fact that they DON"T SELL FRENCH FRIES!!!!!!!!!!!! Unacceptable.

I'll be back when I'm cravin' BBQ.  However, if they'd strengthen their sauce choices and they'd add fries to the menu, I'd be a more frequent customer.  

Solomonov needs to head to Oklahoma Joe's in KC, MO.  His head will freakin' explode...BBQ at it's finest.

Frida bakery has mixed reviews from my friend. I like to find out myself for my own experience. The bakery serve lunch and breakfast. The breakfast included many item with bacon. The lunch also good. When I was there, many come in for the soup, I did not try that. 

I got to pieces of their dessert for the my late snack. I have cassada torte and the carrot cake. The cassada torte has a cannoli place on top. The middle has two layers of cake and mousse and a layer of chocolate. The cake is moist and has syrup in it. It is tasty. 

The carrot cake is good. It is top with carrot icing. Layer with cake cream. My experience here is good. No big wow factor. They have outside seating good for the current weather. I was serve quickly. Seem like the customers who eat there enjoy it.

My boyfriend, Matt and I were in the city at the Barnes Foundation and wanted sushi for lunch.  Most of the places we knew of are only open for dinner.  So we turned to Yelp and Dasiwa was open for lunch and everyone was giving it great reviews.   We were not disappointed and loved everything!

We walked in and were greeted promptly and were seated.  We were told to look at the lunch specials on the board.  Matt and I both decided to get the maki trio for lunch.  It consisted of a california roll, salmon roll, and a tuna roll.  Matt also ordered miso soup and I ordered a sashimi salad.  The salad was served in a martini glass and had a little bit of heat to it which I liked.  Matt's soup was also great and he enjoyed it.  We both enjoyed our maki trio and it was priced at $17.  While we were there a few customers stopped in for coffee and a pastry and there were 2 other tables.  The staff was friendly and our waters were kept filled.  Dasiwa is a BYOB and would be a great place for a nice dinner.  

I will definitely be back!
Slowest service of any sonic I've ever been to every single time. Drive through is the worst.

No Remedy for this Doomed Restaurant!

Il Rimedio opened on the site of the former Rx on 45th & Spruce.  So much going for the place; so little coming out.  It's hard to fail in this West Philly neighborhood:  Penn students tend to flock toward novelty; the regular residents like to support neighborhood businesses; and there's quite some foot traffic.  So all a new restaurant has to do is provide reasonable food at  reasonable prices with vaguely competent service, right?  Il Remedio gets it wrong from the beginning, and there was literally nothing it did to remedy (ha!) itself or to suggest it cares to do so throughout one incomprehensibly bad meal.  

Let's start with the decor:  white tablecloths in a neighborhood restaurant--  with ill-cut curtains that sort of crunch over at the bottom of the windowseats-- fine if you're going for the grungy down-market dorm look, but somehow the two just create grotesquely contradictory curb appeal ("we want to be fancy [tablecloths] but we're lazy and sloppy and couldn't get our curtains properly sized at Ikea").

But who goes for the drapery:  let's get to the food.  I brought 7 friends in on a recent Tuesday.  We had plenty of dining options:  I dragged them here to support my neighborhood.  We ordered all the items on the appetizer list and were uniformly disappointed.  Cockles w/sausages sound great if they had something other than shells; the sausage in that dish seemed like it could learn a thing or two from Hebrew National (you know, taste, texture, complexity).  The radish salad had a few industrial looking pieces of white something and we're still debating if it was cheese, filler, or what.  The scallops with beans and "bacon foam" would have been nice if someone had bothered to add beans and to drop the foam (a few driblets).  And the "greens" on the dishes had that same industrially grown and processed feel-- heck, Trader J's might provide better produce (and no, that's NOT a compliment).

The housemade pasta was what I was looking for and it arrived lumpy, with the linguini actually angel hair. When the error was pointed out to the  waitress, she first berated the cook ("I told him to put linguini!") then came back and insisted that their "house made" linguini actually resembled that angel hair on the plate.  Our party dissed the risotto as well, and the pork on the menu (or was it lamb?) was tough and disappointing. 

But wait, there's dessert!  Aah:  lumps of more industrially prepared and cut gelatin appeared ("berry terrine").  The wafer had been sitting in the cream so long it was a sodden fan; the cheese platter ("we don't know the cheeses since we buy them the day of serving" informed our helpfully non-compos waitress)-- well, it was more of the industrial stuff that again TJ's could do better.  The profiteroles looked like they came out of a plastic can and did not  taste much better.

All the growing pains of a recently-opened restaurant, you say?  Maybe.  But in this very forgiving neighborhood, a lot might be overlooked for a competent, intelligent waitstaff.  Our party was one of 2 (yes, two!)  in the restaurant that evening, and our incompetent and inept waitress seemed ignorant of every single aspect of her job.  At one point, we actually had to phone the restaurant to get her attention ("sorry, you're missing half our order, and could we please have that corkscrew you promised about 40 minutes ago.")

So, friends, support your neighborhood.  Eat at Honest Tom's down the street for a fraction of the price, or head to Kanella (10th & Spruce) owned by a W. Philly resident for superlative food and service.  But caveat emptor on this one:  there's simply no remedy for the horrors you'll find at Il Remedio!

This place sucks. Got some kind of open faced sandwich which was horrible, fries were cold, server was terminally unavailable..on a Tuesday, when I told her to get the manager,  he was too enamored with a bartender to talk to me. Applebees is across the street. Go there.
Curry chicken is epic! Sweet Tea is really good! I do not like Sweet Tea, but there's is awesome. Also, they have Bruce Lee photos!

This location is close and convenient; never a line compared to the Overland and Five Mile location. They're quick and efficient. However....last night we ordered two pizzas. They tasted fine. This morning hubby and I were vomiting and diarrhea. Both of us... that's the only thing we've eaten in common. Gonna have to ask our dinner guests how they're doing today...and I'm not looking forward to asking... teenagers that man this store may not be up to speed on food safety??
Orders filled promptly. Curbside delivery is handled well. Turkey and brisket are great and can be frozen for use later

Highly recommended.  Sort of a typical neighborhood Italian restaurant with pizza and cooked dishes like spaghetti, chicken parm, etc.  Only thing is, the food is much better than average for a neighborhood joint. 

I had spaghetti with sausage and peppers, and it was excellent, just like mom used to make.  My partner had a pizza, and I tasted a slice, which was excellent too.  Salads and garlic bread were fine.  

Service was polite, friendly, and helpful even though busy, stopping by several times to see if we needed anything.  

Would definitely go again.

Exceptional Surprise!  Beautifully decorated interior, friendly staff, quick service.  The surprise was that it was happy hour(Sunday). 50¢ smoked wings and half priced cocktails.  I ordered plain wings , glad to enjoy full smoked flavor and froze'.  Then had the City Park burger, shredded cheese, caramelized onions and hickory sauce. Next surprise was that it was a double patty with the Pontchatoula cocktail.  My friend ordered the 'Let the Beet Drop" cocktail... Not a good idea, but we did give out input on how to improve it only to find out we were the first to order it. Our server was sooo helpful and friendly.  Definitely returning.... soon!

SUMMARY: Hey, at least the beer's good.

My wife and I came here for dinner on a Sunday evening. It probably wasn't a good sign that there were only a smattering of people inside. Still, for some reason (namely my wife), we decided to eat here.

First of all, we had no idea where to sit because no one greeted us. So, we stood there awkwardly until one of the bartenders decided to call out and tell us to sit anywhere. I noticed that one of the bartenders was eagerly texting away and not looking up or cleaning the bar, which was noticeably dirty.

When we finally sat down, we ordered a lager and an imperial stout -- both quite tasty. Unfortunately, that is where the tastiness ended. My wife ordered the shrimp and grits, which came in a pool of liquid fat. Please see the pictures for more detail. The bun of my po boy fell apart which made it quite messy to eat.  Because my wife hates to leave an empty plate, she took the remainder for leftovers.  Still, she looked disgusted and I can't blame her.

If I wanted to go to Ybor to grab a beer, I would head to Zydeco because their beer truly is good.  Otherwise, I would not visit again for food.
Ask for Bambi! Great restaurant and wonderful service. Salmon was great. Avocado toast was amazing.

As my daughter said, this is the perfect restaurant for us - chicken for me and ramen for her.

You can order on line or drive through, although you don't order at the drive up sign. There is a small note on top of board directing you to order at window. When you get to window the menu is repeated, plus they have helpfully listed out what everything means, so easy to order.
