Lots of students, it seems, and near a lot of restaurants. With more people in line, service can be super slow, so unless you come at off hours, expect a wait in the cramped area up near the counter when you walk in.

If I could give it ZERO stars, I would. I ordered a small meal, soft taco, nachos (chips & cheese) & a bean & cheese burrito w/o onions. It took 30 minutes to get my simple order. They weren't busy, 2 other people besides me, also they were ahead of me. The absolute worst customer service I've had at a Taco Bell. They were pumping people out of the drive thru but ignoring the lobby guests. Finally, there were people who ordered after me asking for refunds. I WILL NEVER GO THERE AGAIN!!

I went to Solaris Grille this past Friday. While I was waiting for my cousins arrival I decided to buy a drink... $8.80 to my debit card and I laid a cash tip on the bar. I discovered today the bartender took it upon himself to add an additional $2. I called the restaurant they told me to come in and they would refund the "oversight" $2 is $2 but it's the principal. I waited awhile to be served the drink so it was not worth a $3.00 tip. The food is Ok not tasty. If you are looking for a decorated plate this is not the place. If you are out for a lonnnnggg leisurely dinner this may be a fit for you as the servers are on tortoise time if not then you may miss your movie or show if that was on your agenda for the night. For a Friday night Solaris was bare and that is unfortunate because it is a great capture for the 25-40 crowd base. The only thing Solaris has going for them is the decor. Management needs to step up their help or return them to McDonalds.

Great service the FOH staff are very courteous! The food comes out in average time and is good and filling.  Get the cheddar drop biscuits and chorizo gravy it's only $5.  The BLTA and waffled French toast were good too.

I love this place. We had such a great time. Danced, laughed and enjoyed our food. I wish they had unlimited mimosas or a better price on them. But other than that...we would totally come back... Thank you Bitches

This was my first experience at Freddy's. I knew one was being built on Broadway and had seen snaking drive-thru lines at other locations. I love cheeseburgers and fries. Freddy's puts an interesting spin on both. 

The employees and management were congenial and attentive. My husband ordered the double steak burger with bacon and I did the double with cheese. I thought it would be too heavy as a double, but the cashier said the double was roughly equivalent to a quarter pounder.

The meat was unlike any other burger I've had. Very flat, which I'm assuming allows for the fried effect on the patties. I really liked the fries. Well seasoned and crispy with fry sauce, an Idaho must! Lastly, I tried a concrete: vanilla custard mixed with a topping. It was rich and smooth. Yum. 

Interior is retro with pictures of the founder's life. They play oldies. Clean and comfortable enough. Good choice if American fast food is the meal you're craving!

This little gem is just fantastic! Service and food is exceptional. The kind of restaurant that you love to eat at with a beautiful story! Owned by Immigrants who came to the US escaping the travesty of the Middle East. Mother is in the kitchen preparing truly authentic, delicious dishes served by her daughter who was just delightful! You can taste the love and feel the hospitality in everything about this place. It was the best food I have eaten in St Louis...period and the best Middle eastern food ever! Highly recommend!
I can see why this place always has a line out the door waiting to order. Best fried chicken I have ever had. Caution on how spicy it is.

As far as cheesesteaks go, this place is Philly's top spot, I just don't really like cheesesteaks.

Meat is freshly sliced daily- not a frozen steak-em. There cheesesteaks are always juicy and tasty. I like mine with onions, mushrooms and provolone. Sangwich is loaded with meat and can be a bit messy- but I don't mind. 

Bread isn't great and usually gets soggy by the time you reach the second half. Mushrooms are canned, and i never like that over fresh mushrooms.
Cold coffee, over cooked, dehydrated bacon and undercooked, soggy,nasty, raw egged french toast with a crappy attitude to boot....later guys, wont be back...

If you've never had a lobster roll in New England or out in the Hamptons, please go now.

The atmosphere is fantastic.  You'll fall in love with the shanty-esque feel of the place rather quickly.  You'll peer into the cooler and see the Luke's Brand Root Beer and Sarsaparilla and want to buy a case or two. But ultimately, the lobster roll needs to win you over.

My lady friend and I ordered the Noah's Ark.  A tasting trio for two of the lobster, crab, and shrimp rolls.  It came with a beverage, chips, and a pickle.  We did not opt for the crab claw special.

I decided to work backward and try the shrimp and crab rolls before taking on the lobster roll because, in my mind, the lobster roll had to be good.  So let's get the possibility of disappointing me out of the way.  With that said, keep in mind this: this is the only lobster shack I've been to that had sriracha sauce on the tables.

The shrimp & crab rolls were, well, flavorless.  They didn't taste like fresh seafood or the fixins on them.  I applied an ample amount of sriracha to each and that made them somewhat palatable.  The pickle and root beer rescued me from this mediocrity fairly quickly.  I wasn't upset, though, because I had this fantastic lobster roll to look forward to.

I was sorely disappointed; almost offended.  I've had the privilege to eat at Lunch in Amagansett in NY and at a few great lobster shacks in Maine.  Most places serve a warm lobster roll or, as Lunch does, serves both a warm and cold 'lobster salad' lobster roll that puts Luke's to shame.  I would've been happy with an imitation of either, but I can't even feign satisfaction.

Luke's lobster is obviously not fresh.  I saw no boilers or steamers anywhere in sight.  They definitely didn't cook the critters on site or you would know from the smells and equipment present.  The lobster meat tasted salty and was a little too firm to be same day fresh.  That typically indicates that it was shipped frozen in a briny solution.  Our cashier told us the lobsters came in twice a week fresh from Maine.  I don't think so.

The lobster rolls aside, I'd had out in the place for the root beer and chips.

To reply to the two people that left the "blegh" and "mediocre" reviews - 

Clearly, "Miss Blegh" you have no idea what true hospitality is, in any culture... thus perhaps you should stick to what you know best, and apparently expect, in your "dining experience" - the drive-thru at McD's. We fellow Yelpers did not mislead you, you simply have no manners (oh and juvenile taste in TV as well - shocker) and none of us will miss your "blegh" attitude at GSH. 

Now, to "Miss Mediocre" - Not sure what happened here, I, like many others eat here at least once a week, if not more, and well, this is unfortunate, as I have yet to get a meal as bad as you say yours was, and I'm sorry to hear that. Out of curiosity though, did you happen to talk to your waiter about it? Every seaweed salad I've had there, is well, fresh seaweed, which is, well, wet... and the "puddle of liquid" is dressing mixed with, you guessed it, water from the seaweed.. because it's fresh, not freeze-dried. So perhaps it's just a different style of salad that you haven't had yet - perhaps there was too much dressing on yours and it was just a mistake - just a thought on that. As for your spicy tuna roll - tasting funny and overstuffed... again, not all tuna rolls are the same, with exception to the tuna, of course - but each sushi chef has their own method of pairing with certain veggies, sauces, spices, etc - again, perhaps this was just a different version than what you've had elsewhere? I know Cali Rolls are basic fare everywhere, but I have no expectations that they taste exactly the same everywhere, because they just don't - they're  going to be different and there's no other way around that fact, unless you just eat at the same place and never go anywhere else. Just sayin'... every thing is gonna be different, even if it's all called the same thing. If you do happen to ever want to try it one more time, may I suggest the Firedragon Roll as a start... hands down, it's heaven in a roll. 

Ok, so about me? I've been a regular customer of this establishment, even prior to it being GSH, when it was Kashima, and I have NEVER had a bad meal here. Get to know the owner, she is an incredible woman, with a huge heart for her amazing "sushi family", all her regulars that come back time and time again, not only for the incredible food, but for the warm hospitality, the feeling we get that we are literally in her home, where she shines, along with her wonderful staff, who have been with her since day one. Get to know these people - and it's not about "getting an in" with them, it's about being decent fellow-human beings towards others, who happen to be serving you some of the best sushi in town. If you find something distasteful on your plate, be proactive and let them know, they can't read your mind. Maybe your taste-buds are having an off-day b/c you've got a cold, or on an Rx that is messing with you... Or perhaps it's just a different version of what you're used to from some other establishment... Or maybe you're absolutely right and that dish isn't what they ever intended to serve... everyone makes mistakes from time to time, and unless it's brought up, how does anyone know? 

That's my eleven cents on GSH, I was there last night and I'll be there again in a few days... just like the hundreds of others who love it there as much as I do - and it's OK if you don't like it, or won't come back - I say "to each their own".

Michael was amazing.  Came here for dinner the night before my daughter's birthday.  He found out and finished her meal off with happy birthday, and an ice cream with a candle.  She was beaming, it made her feel so special.  As someone that also works in the service industry, he was in tune to our needs (we had two small children with us) he was excited to be there and you could tell he takes pride in his work.  Thank you for the great service!

I am excited to have Suraya in the neighborhood. Staff was very friendly, decor is beautiful, and the cafe counter is well stocked with delicious looking treats. Unfortunately, I won't be visiting too frequently since the cafe is a bit expensive - the cruller and a mint tea, although a heavenly combination for the taste buds, was hard on the wallet ($9). I am excited to try out the restaurant when it opens in 2018 and then revisit for special occasions.

Great daily drink specials and happy hour! Have plenty of indoor and outdoor seating! We love to bring our pups here and sit outside! Love their fish dip, street corn , and wings! We also tried the camp fries for the first time and thought they were delicious and definitely big enough to share! Friendly and attentive service!
Delicious! The place is so modern and fashionable! Músic was amazing! Loved the place!!
This is a simple no thrills dinner.  It doesn't need any.  The food is great and prices are perfect.  The place is small and it was crowded, but this is just a testiment to their business

Beautiful view of the Bay with nice beach area! The food is terrible like really bad and service ain't great. We keep coming back because it's close and location on water is awesome. My wife and I have tried many items off menu and I can honestly say they all sucked. So if your wanting good food look elsewhere. If you're willing to sacrifice food for a pretty view and live music go for it.

Good food, good prices. today I had the beef taco salad for lunch very filling and good deal for $6.50

Yesterday I had a chimichanga, delicious also, 
I will definitely return if in the area.

This was a great family experience with extended family. The service was great and the food was delicious.    We will return again very soon.   Everyone liked what we chose and we are more full than we need to be.  Great place for celebrations.
Perfect sandwich with amazing bread, amazing pickles, and an amazing owner! Everything was super fresh and I'll definitely be back.

Showed up for a take-out order, and 2/3 chefs along the line had masks below their noses. Very disappointing. I commented to the host who had the chefs correct their masks... and then 2 minutes later, masks are down below their noses again. Ugh!...
That and they shorted us 3 rolls on our order. Refund was issued on the shorted order, but so far no comment from management on the masks below the noses.

Well thank you again Yelp for making me aware of Taqueria Pico De Gallo. Simply amazing tacos!! We ended up trying the carne and fish tacos and I loved them both. The fish tacos were probably the best I've ever had.  Very cheap too. We had the 3 fish taco combo with a drink and added 2 al a cart carne tacos and we were out the door at about $12. We will totally be back here on our next trip to Tucson!

Leave the French Quarter to visit Neyow's! You won't be disappointed! Asked several locals for food recommendations and most of them mentioned this spot so we had to check it out. It's super easy to get there via trolley. 

The restaurant is really cute and the staff is friendly. My friends and I all ordered the Bow Wow drink which is a strong punch that they're known for. If you finish it they'll give you the next one half off. My friends and I all finished ours and got seconds and we were tipsy as hell... definitely worth it. The food was amazingggg. Got the charbroiled oysters and the pasta on the bayou (shrimp and crawfish)... seriously the best pasta I've had in a long while. 

Definitely will be returning here on all my future trips to New Orleans.

I don't want to write this review. In fact, I've put it off for weeks. But I've been to both Patterson House and Holland House several times in the last couple of months, and since Patterson House is the bar against which Holland House is generally measured, I have to weigh in again. 

On the one hand, Holland House is amazing. I've never had bad food there. In fact, it's always been quite good. The drinks, too: incredible. But I have had so many bad service experiences here that I just can't abide it any longer. In early June, some friends and I tried to go to HH for brunch. I'd sung its praises to them for months and we finally ventured to the east side one Sunday. When we got there, my friend went up to the door and found it dark inside. He asked about getting a table and if they were open. No, he was told. Not "I'm sorry." Not "We're not open for brunch anymore." Just No and a closed door. 

Because I love this place so much, I wanted to give it another chance. A friend and I went a couple of weeks in a row for happy hour and early dinner. The first time, we wanted to get a seat at the bar. Because we generally sit at a table, when the hostess asked us whether we were eating dinner or just drinks, my friend said "Oh we can just sit at the bar" and started to walk over there. We didn't realize they seat the bar just like the restaurant. An honest mistake. The hostess gave her a withering look and said to Wait, she had to check. And then came back to take us to the bar without so much as a smile. 

Next time: we come in to the restaurant after another couple. Somehow the hostess completely ignores/overlooks the people before us (which they were clearly and understandably upset about) and asks if we're OK sitting in the lounge area. After we were seated, it took about 10 minutes for the server to ask what we wanted, despite the fact that he kept walking by us again and again since we were right next to the back bar where he was getting drinks for other tables and would stand and chat. When he finally acknowledged us, I made the mistake of being hopeful since he seemed nice. But from that point on, it only got worse. We were ignored for the entire three hours we were there. All four of us had to wait at least 15 minutes after we ran out of a drink for him to come and ask about another. When our food was brought out (separately, at two different times), it arrived without silverware. The server didn't come to check that we had everything we needed and we were forced to ask other servers or runners for utensils when we finally gave up waiting for him, by which point the food was well on its way to cold. 

I am sorry to say that I think Holland House has lost my business. By comparison, the staff at Patterson House I have found to be nothing resembling elitist or neglectful the last few times I've been. Holland House seriously needs to re-evaluate its staffing decisions if it wants to keep its customers. As for me, I'm tired of being treated like I don't deserve to be there. It's just not good enough to treat people like crap. Nowhere is.

If you're in search of a delicious unpretentious, non greasy cheesesteak...the search is over! Greeted by a cool, friendly guy dressed in a fun outfit with overly nice manners he took out order. Simple menu...just get the Classic cheesesteak. Fries are delicious. For what this place is, and what it is trying to be...just a great place for good, fast food I give this place a four.
Typically a go to for me for iced toddy.  I enjoy the funky flavor and company found around 4th ave

I don't give this rating lightly but the service and every course of the meal was excellent.  The taste and presentation from appetizer, main course and dessert was impeccable.  Out server, Colt as well was top notch.

I was craving tacos so much especially since I'm from the West Coast. I know my tacos. namsang? After watching Ugly Delicious, I was like okay. Let me give this place a try. The restaurant is pretty small. It's packed, you will touch other people. So if you're claustrophobic, good luck! 

You stand in line towards the front to order your tacos. You eat first then pay. CASH ONLY. I believe I ordered two pork tacos and a lamb taco. The pork tacos were just okay because they felt a little under seasoned, but the lamb was amazing. I had never had lamb taco before and it was so just so delicious, juicy, tender, and delicate and packed full of flavor. In terms of price, the tacos are on the pricier side of what I am used to. I'm used to paying less than $1.50 per street taco. However, given what they stand for and given these are probably the best tacos you will get in Philly, it might be worth it!

The food was mediocre. There was only 2 people working in the front on a Sunday brunch and the place is packed. It took the food 2 hours (no exaggeration) to come out. Food for different people at our table came half an hour apart. Only come here if you have 3 hours to spare. The waiter is nice at least.

Slow and rude. Twice I've called in to-go orders, both times after arriving and paying for the food, I find out the orders were never placed and I'm left waiting 15-20 more minutes. More than one occasion I've been charged extra for items never received, just to met with eye-rolling and smart ass comments when I ask for it to be corrected. Staff is rude and does not care about your time. The food is mediocre at best.

I am in love love love with the ambiance. It's so beautiful, fun and vibrant. The staff were phenomenal and very pleasant. We laughed and enjoyed the waiter so much. 
The food was also tasty we enjoyed the Fruit bowl, Pain Perdu( which literally melted in our mouths) the Poulet Frit( probably one of the best chicken sandwiches I've had in the city. A little heat and the bacon and cheese were a excellent touch! I would surely get this again), Justine Burger( which was cooked well done and was a good take on a burger).  We had the bar make a special non-alcoholic drink for the minors that was very very good. 
This was surely one of the best brunches in the city.

Checked out this place last night with a friend.  Little slow (business wise for them)for a Friday night but we got super fast service- so bonus for us!  The dining room is quite small. But it is clean and well lit. A little confused by their 2 front doors and we ended up taking the one that put us by the bar.  Not sure if that was the right one but we got seated right away.  

Our server recommended the sausage platter appetizer.  They were all delicious.  It comes with 3 sausages and is served with a side of saurkraut and rye bread .  Only wish the server had told what each sausage was.  So my friend and I used our culinary knowledge from garde manger class in culinary school to figure out the sausages from our menu.    

For our entree I had the schnitzel with a mushroom burgundy sauce.  I fell in love with that sauce!  The braised cabbage was also delicious.  Just be careful not to wear white when eating it, has lots of juices and is served in a heaping bowl- had several close spills on my white cardigan.  The spaetzle was a little bland to me so I poured that mushroom sauce over it and nearly finished the bowl.  

Now the dessert... when we walked in one of the servers passed us carrying a cake dome of Opera Cake slices.  They found my Achilles heel!!!  

What is Opera cake you might ask?  It's technically a French dessert and could be a cousin of Tiramisu.  It's an almond sponge cake, soaked in coffee and then with layers of ganache (swoon!), and coffee buttercream.  Although with this particular cake I could taste hazelnut as opposed to the usual almond flavor- which was very tasty and a pleasant surprise.   

The dessert and the sauce sold me on this place.  I look forward to going back and trying their potato salad (they were sadly out that night), sausages, and of course their Opera cake.  Probably a good thing that Centennial Park is next door.  Might need to walk off all the Opera cake I will most likely be eating.

It was best experience in STL, I live in Michigan and was t visiting my brother!!
we decided to go try new food, the waitress suggested Mousakhen (half chicken) it was so  tender and juicy!! My favorite ever, my brother had lamb kabsa he loved it. 
We shared the combo and their Hummus and falafel are THE BEST!!! 
My advice give it a try!!! You will like it

Went for lunch and tried their lunch special for Bahn Mi and Pho. Bahn Mi was cold cut meats, it tasted okay. I personally didn't enjoy one of the meat in there but it was ok with sriracha. Summer roll was with pork & shrimp however pork wasn't actually pork, it was some pre-sausage type which was not what I expected but it was good. Pho was great! A lot of meat and broth was on the citrus side but I didn't mind. Customer service was good. We'll be back!
Had great chillie chicken and samosa. You don't need anything else, is fulfilling. Eat here almost every week. Staff are very welcoming.

After walking around in the city park, this place is just right inside the park....
The coolness and looks so historical makes me feel like I'm in the 1800ish dinning.
Sit down and the waitress come to u and its quick order and eat.
Inside or outside both are good

Went here on a Friday night to hear Irvin Mayfield in a new trio. Quality entertainment, quality drinks and quality food in an environment I could enjoy with the kids! Kids enjoyed chicken fingers while the adults enjoyed something more sophisticated. Early sets mean I can go to bed at a reasonable hour  but still get my culture fix.

Fantastic steaks. Top sirloin to die for, great filets. The service was wonderful. They got the steak temperatures perfect. The salads were delicious. 
Here's my only complaint: cheap silverware, tiny plates, bad presentation, no bearnaise sauce. Other than that, if you crave steak, go here. Do not go for the salmon - overcooked and not the freshest. 
Good steakhouse atmosphere, and the best beef around.

While the restaurant interior does look like KFC: Days of Future Past, it is at least clean. However, I wouldnt really eat here unless youre a single dude who is famished.

The biriyani is quite good;however there are 2 main problems:

1) Price. 
The biriyani dishes are mostly 12-13 dollars. 
Reality Check: this is Tampa, not NYC, not Chicago.
If I go to Ghareeb Nawaz in Chicago, I can get awesome chili chicken biriyani with enough for the country of Somalai for 6-7 bucks. That is also  a hole in the wall dive, but the food is scrumptious. I dont know how rice with bits of egg and chicken are so expensive for Tampa. Quelle surprise!

2) Wait time.
 Last time, I ordered one chicken biriyani for takeout, and it took( deep breath)         ...  1 hour and 40 minutes!!!!  WTF!
After asking every 20 minutes about the dish, the cashier would just make up some pathetic excuse and only after harassing them did I get my food.

Tampa's Indian food has gotten really abysmal or maybe I'm spoiled by Chi-town.
If you dont mind throwing money away eat here.
IF you want some good biriyani and can eat meat, go to Jai Ho (the one near Amscot) during the weekdays, they have a more flavorful one and you get some other stuff with it for 10 bucks!

Don't let the exterior look fool you. The restaurant is actually very nice and clean inside including the restroom. We tried Nam Khao (crispy rice salad with pork), Kapoon (coconut noodle soup) and for banana desert. Everything is very flavorful and rivals Laotian/Hmong places in Fresno, CA, and St Paul, Minnesota. Waitress is also very friendly and attentive. Highly recommend this place!

Not another place like it in Indy. Bartenders are very knowledgeable on their selection of beers. Food is decent. I have only had a variety of appetizers. The atmosphere and artwork brings the experience altogether!
This place is pretty cool. Right down the road from the office and it's perfect when you need a good ol' greasy burger. Great easygoin' atmosphere.
What a great place to eat before the game! High quality food!  Nice bar! Great service. The Crab was yummy!

I'd like to start my review by thanking the manager John. I walked in to the restaurant earlier today to beg for a reservation for my parents and I. My dad had his first round of Chemo yesterday and decided he wanted to see me sooner rather than later, especially because sickness and hair loss can turn stressful quickly. John promised to get us in, and when we showed up he had made sure a table was ready for us. It was such a kind gesture and meant so much to me. 

My dad and I shared the Alligator bites (his first time having Alligator) and they were SOOO good. I would go back just for those. Our main courses were delicious, including my mom's BBQ shrimp which, if you're in the mood for some protein, are excellent. We also shared the Bread Pudding. Again, delicious. I'd like to try many more things on the menu.

The restaurant is really pretty inside with exposed brick, gas lamps, and a lovely bar area. I had a wonderful time, but honestly, the kindness and accommodations having been a last minute reservation was enough to make me recommend Roux and go back again. Thank you to everyone at the restaurant. You gave us a wonderful family night.

This is the trifecta of tasty, interesting selection, and great atmosphere. I have had a ton of things on the menu, and never been disappointed. Sandwiches, soups, flatbread, sangria--interesting choices, yummy specials, and consistently fabulous. They have an interesting urban-homey vibe that fits perfectly with the area, and good prices to boot. I adore them. 

What to have, you ask? I say have it all! I am particularly fond of the (slightly nontraditional) pho, the lobsta seafood chowder (served with a side of fresh Cuban bread, of course), their meat-loaded chili, bacon baked potato tsoup, and most of their paninis. Oh, and one of the best Cubans in Ybor, let's not forget that. Top it off with beer or, better yet, sangria, and you have a place worthy of even out of town guests--my vegetarian friend from NYC is still talking about it a year later. No, really, it's that good--at prices they make me want to come every time I drive by!

Walked in after the Phillies game on Sat March 30 with my wife and 2 small children.  They told us sitting at the bar area would be quicker than waiting for a table.  Ok - it was getting late and we were hungry.  We sat in the middle at a pub table with  4 chairs. We waited longer than 5 min before a server finally walked up to us.  He apologized for the wait and said he didn't see us sitting at the table in his area.  Really? What??  It gets worse.  We ordered drinks.  I ordered a tall Sam Adams.  Kids and wife's drinks came first.  Ok - mine was from the bar.  Whatever.  So I waited...and waited...and waited.  Finally he brought it over - Not a tall Sam Adams.  Regular size.  I rolled my eyes - whatever again.  We ordered the food.  Kids got chicken fingers.  Wife and I ordered All American double cheeseburgers.  I can be a finicky eater - So I made it simple - Just make mine with buns, cheese, meat, bacon and lettuce.  That's it.  Easy right?  Not so for them.  Kids chicken fingers were dry and hard.  He brought my burger back with...mustard, mayo, ketchup and pickles.  At least he immediately realized that it was completely not what I ordered and took it back.  Then 10 min later he came back with a super greasy burger that still had pickles in it.  WHAT??  At that point I was upset and finally said something.  He was nice and did apologize, but they messed up so many things it was too late.  I ate 2 bites of the burger and some soggy fries.  Slop.  The manager came by and then offered us coupons for next time we come.  NEXT TIME???  I told her there would not be a NEXT TIME and was again upset by this weak attempt to make our experience better.  Then she said she would also give us 25% off our meal.  I accepted because I just wanted to go.  Awful.  The whole meal should have been FREE for that garbage food and service.  They finally decided not to charge me for that garbage burger after I told them it was inedible.  I was foolish.  I had heard bad stories about this chain in the past and thought "let's try it out."  HUGE MISTAKE - NEVER AGAIN.  TOLD ALL MY FB LIST - many said "yeah we heard horror stories about BWW too!"  At least the Phillies won.  HUGE FAIL by Buffalo Wild Wings.  PJ Whelihans in Newtown Square is like the Capital Grille compared to this hole.

Had xmas eve dinner with family.  The dishes did not blow me away for the price they charge.  My kids ordered the beef wellington.  We were notified it was not the actual wellington but rather the deconstructed version of it.  It was just ok.  The porkchop with blue berry sauce was not very good.  The pan fried chicken was good.  Dessert were ok. I must say, service was very good.   Overall, i still prefer the steak house and most likely will not come back here.

My husband and his friends have been here before and they had great things to say so I was excited to try this place out. I enjoyed their drink selection, it was extremely creative and it all looked delicious.  The atmosphere was perfect for a late night dessert bar, and would be a lovely date spot. We ordered a cake and our friend got a brownie. The cake had the right concept, but it was a little bland. Our friend's brownies were completely dried out though, they couldn't even eat the edges because they were burnt to a crisp. Overall I think the experience is okay, and I will probably be back in the future.

This is a spot that I regularly visit. There are more and more Japanese and ramen houses in Nashville than 6 years ago when I moved here, and two ten jack is one that has had its name in the top 3 ramen places for years. I've worked with Japanese flavors quite a bit and two ten jack does not disappoint. They take classic Japanese cuisine and put their own hip spin on it, like the takoyaki (octopus hush puppies). The small plates are shareable and yummy, sashimi and nigiri always fresh and the perfect temperature. They have several robota grill options, and several noodle dishes. I personally go for the ramen. I'm vegan (WAH WAH) and still feel like there are multiple options here for me. The yasai ramen packs a lot of flavor - I mean the broth itself is incredible. Overall, it's a wonderful spot with a beautiful space. Is it my favorite ramen in town? No, but it's definitely worth the visit.

Ordered take-out for a lunch.  All three of us ordered the shrimp wraps. Each wrap was prepared just as we had ordered and the shrimp tasted wonderful.  Excellent!  The food was well prepared and still very warm when I picked it up.  All the condiments were included.  The person who took the order and provided it for me when I arrived was great -- great personality, great service!  This is a gem on the edge of the golf course!  Well done!

Great sports environment with good tasting food. I wasn't going to eat here because the low rating in Yelp but I'm glad I did. The service was great and the food options was to be as expected. Standard sports bar type food and tasted great! The nachos were perfect to share and the fried shrimp poboy was perfectly seasoned. The devil eggs were a great find. Wasn't expecting that on a restaurant  menu with crab in it.... Money!

great happy hour specials and quality food. love the dollar malpeques when they have them--and their white balsamic is amazing, easily my favorite oyster accompaniment of all time. not a ton of seating downstairs, so arrive early !

A friend was able to snag a last minute reservation for four on Monday night. If you check throughout the day, sometimes cancellations come through and you can get a table! I have had a reservation in March, but was dying to get in sooner. So glad it worked out because the entire experience was worth the rave reviews.

As a table, we decided to do the Tayim option. This is a "for the entire party" option, so everyone had to be willing to eat this way. This is absolutely the way to go your first time at Zahav! 

Wait staff was incredible. Our waitress explained everything in great detail and provided her recommendations. I was in the mood for a cocktail so she suggested the Z&T, saying it was savory option. I had three of them. Delicious, light, refreshing!!!

Two friends went for the wine pairing and, although I loved my cocktail, I'm going for that option next time. Each glass was explained in great detail. I took a sip of the "Zahav" dessert wine (named Zahav because of it's gold color, no connection to the restaurant) and it was the most incredible chardonnay I've ever had.

Now for the food, the saltim was great. My favorite was the eggplant. We went for the Turkish hummus - which is served warm. This is the best hummus I have ever had. If you have 4 people, you must get one of each of the Mezze plates. Each one was better than the last! Favorites include the cauliflower, mushroom schnitzel (I do not like mushrooms at all) and the haloumi. When it was time for Al Ha'esh (the mains) we got four items that we agreed upon and shared those. We did the chicken, steak, eggplant, and branzino. I felt the chicken was a bit undercooked, may have been my piece or the "grilled over coals" cooking. Not sure. It was still flavorful, but a bit chewier than I prefer. Everything else was perfect. Easily the best eggplant I have ever eaten - so tender! It literally melted in my mouth. The steak was incredible. The branzino was my favorite and I do not like fish. I typically avoid it at all costs, but I had to try it because it was fish from Zahav! I am so glad that I did. It was so light and the crisp skin was perfect.

For dessert, I split the Malabi Custard and Hazelnut cake with a friend. This combination was incredible. I took a bite of a friends Chocolate Konafi and, despite how delicious my dessert options were, I wish I had ordered that instead. The Chocolate Konafi was crispy and moist. The pistachio ice cream was the perfect flavor pair.

I am really looking forward to my upcoming reservation in March!

My first visit to Spice Box.  The food was prepared to taste. Spices were just perfect.  each dish had its own flavor. The hospitality of the owners was amazing. They answered questions. Sat with us for a minute to explain things. Being new, I request you all to go & try them out. The atmosphere was very inviting & I felt very safe. Butter Chicken & Chilli Chicken with garlic naan was a very safe bet. Will be back there again soon.

It's been a few years since I was in the Chadds Ford area, but it to to Longwood Garden necessitated a return trip to Firebird.

Can I say this restaurant is close to perfect? We arrived 30 minutes early for our reservation. No problem; we were graciously seated. Our server was terrific. Our food was perfection (we both had grilled salmon, baked potato and delicious veggies). I asked a passing staff member for directing to the ladies' room, and she said she would show me the way. I thought that was super in a crowded restaurant. The food was hot, the service was outstanding, and the meal perfect. My only note would that the noise level could have been a tad lower.

I hope to return again to this marvelous place!

Went here while visiting Nashville for the weekend. Honestly, I don't think I've met a friendlier staff in my life. Besides the fact that the food is AMAZING, Kristin was the sweetest person ever. I wish I could come back here every day to try everything and hang out with the great people. Thank you for an amazing meal and service!
This place has it all; the atmosphere, the food, the people. The best part is driving new people there since it's tucked in the mountain it's always a pleasant surprise. Love love love.
This is a gem. The workers are always friendly and the service is prompt. The best choice for Mexican food on the main line by far.

Say hopapalooza to the guy behind the bar...then say hi to the monkeys looking over the bar, when someone asks if you would like something to eat, say mushroom bruschetta and let the evening melt away ...

Ok my bad I didn't yelp until we sat down. Heed the warnings don't eat here had the corn beef hash. It was god awful in fact I didn't eat it. Way to many other places to eat, no idea why it's so busy.

Wow, a lot of negative reviews on this place.  Well, I've got two words - Smokehouse Burger.  It's worth the trip.  Go on a Saturday afternoon, sit at the bar and have an excellent burger.  It's that easy.

I would give this Burger King a half star if I could but I can't. I went there twice in two months and both times they got my order wrong. On my last and final visit I specifically asked for my Whopper with no sauce (dry), and cheese. I even avoided the drive thru so there would be no confusion. I went inside and at the time I was the only customer in line. Ten minutes later (seriously) my order is ready and by then there's a large line. (One customer even came inside yelling they got his drive thru order wrong). I go to my car and proceed to eat the whopper in the car. Bad idea. Ketchup and mustard are oozing out of the burger and onto my pants. The burger itself -the one that I patiently waited 10 minutes for- is cold and lifeless- not to mention the slice of cheese thrown on top of the burger has absolutely no chance of melting. They even forget the only veggie I requested. Pickles. I immediately take the meal back in and have a nice talk with the manager. The manager assures me that he is working with the recently hired cook and to give him time - he's learning. The manager then proceeds to replace my burger with a fresh burger and upsize my fries for my inconvenience. I go back out to my car. This time the burger is piping hot and sauce less. However, the pickles are missing again. On top of that, the new fries the manager gave me are stone cold. I have all these remaining Burger King coupons. I'll just have to find a different Burger King to use them at.

Service is SLOOOOOW.  Took 30 minutes for a bowl of dry granola to get poured into a bowl. They do not allow outside drinks but do not serve soda or sparkling water. They are very serious about this policy.

We were disappointed to eat at Bravo November 4,2018. They have been sold and changed their menu. Two of my favorites have been changed. I loved chicken caprese. It no longer has any resemblance to its name. It now is broiled chicken on angel hair pasta with small stewed tomatoes.No more delicious spices, rice, and vegetable.We were told another favorite is no more-chopped salad. 

It is too expensive to be disappointed. If you liked these items, too, they are no longer made the way they were. I hope a good restaurant does not die because of new owners.
Gayle K.

We went thinking this was Gaspar's Patio and who knew that Tampa has a Gaspar's Patio AND Gaspar's Grotto? I just thought the Grotto was indoors and Patio was...well, the patio!? Anyway, we stayed, of course, hoping to have a specific porter that was listed online for the patio but they didn't have it. No big deal, they had something just as good!

Then, you can't have beer without wings...so, we tried a couple different flavors - regular buffalo and parmesan. Both were wonderful and just what was needed!

I've been here before, but usually on a weekend when it is quite a bit busier and louder. If you're wanting to try it in a quieter setting - I would highly recommend a Sunday afternoon! They have a brunch, which we didn't try but I'm sure is good, and it was very calm and a nice atmosphere for a Sunday!

Parking is also a breeze on Sundays - if you can't find something right on 7th, which we did, just go behind the building and there is a parking lot.

First experience with Napoli 3 was great. My husband and I went for a date night dinner on a Saturday and had a wonderful time. Service and food were excellent. We ordered the oysters for an appetizer and I had the Seabass for my main course and my husband had the pasta special. For dessert we had the tiramisu. Everything was delicious! No complaints here

Great food, great service. Had the Moroccan chicken, which was spicy, flavorful and juicy. It's right next door to Campo and can be hard to find, but definitely worth it! The food is Mediterranean and I really appreciate that they have kept the flavors complex and strong, instead of feeling they have to make it bland for American palates. Pita and hummus were fresh and the server was knowledgable, friendly and attentive. Went there for a girls' dinner, but definitely will return with hubby, as he loves spicy food.

Excellent place to go... Was there with a party of 22 and we all had a blast!! The waiters were a little unorganized for such a large group, but the service afterwords made up for it. 

The food of course is prepared right there in front of you with a lot of flare and fun. The food was great of course...and fellas,  man was it some eye candy at this place...wow!!

Pats was my least favorite after my Philly Cheese Steak challenge.  We went to Philly last weekend and tried Sonnys's, Geno's, and Pat's.  The lines at the latter two were ridiculous! I opted for American without onions at Pats and it was ok.  The bread wasn't great and the cheese wasn't melted.  Sonny's was the favorite!

I see you, Portillo's.

I waited as long as I could, but finally had to give in after 2 weeks of Portillo's officially opening here in Fishers. I knew the lines would be long. I understood that it'd be congested due to traffic, so for anyone looking for complaints where that's concerned, look elsewhere because it was exactly what I expected. The biggest line I saw was for the drive-thru, so just be prepared if that's your plan. The parking lot is huge with more than enough spaces. My husband and I ventured in and at first we were confused as to where to start because there are several lines. The line to the left was for pick-up orders (fyi download their app, order ahead, and pick it up just inside the entrance...I heard there's a special $5 off $15 code upon ordering). The line for the main dining is to the right and the crowd you see in the middle is everyone who is waiting for their food.

The menu is large but what makes this place famous is their Chicago hot dogs and Italian beef sandwiches. The cake shakes aren't half bad either! I set out to order the Italian beef with extra gravy. My husband did the same, but had his dipped (i.e. they dip the whole darn sandwich in gravy so it's extra moist) and he also ordered their Chicago dog. Everything was delicious as expected!

We will travel to Portillo's several times and start ordering different menu items just so we make sure we try everything. Worth the wait, worth the lines, but if you want a more relaxing visit, maybe think about visiting Portillo's a year from now :)

Go Cubs Go!

Awesome locale for a rooftop bar. Definitely made for some good people watching. Tiny slice of NYC/South beach in western Florida. Will definitely be back next time I'm in town! (Had a great waitress experience- very funny and helpful with drink suggestions).

I really wanted crab legs for dinner but after a full day of fun in the sun my kiddos were in no shape for a dinner out. So we ordered take out from here. He crab legs were really good and the corn on the Cobb (locally grown) stole the show! It was sweet and tender,some of the best I've had! The Amberjack fish was delicious! Very mild and flaky. Would love to experience the restaurant next time but the take out was fantastic!!

Overrated, service was extremely slow considering the fact they and only 3 tables to attend they had 3 waiters on stand by. We went at 2:30pm barely anyone was in there. More importantly their traditional sushi ( nigiri) is truly horrible. I had the white tuna, first the piece of fish was such a huge portion compared to the rice underneath. The fish itself fight was so tough and chewy. I can't speak for the sushi rolls but I would never come back and order sushi. I'm truly shocked at the high ratings of this place.

Today was my first experience at Naf Naf Grill. While the food was good, the service seemed rushed. The staff seemed like they wanted to place the orders as quickly as possible and did not want to engage in a positive customer experience. That being said, the falafels were the best I have ever had. The chicken shawarma dish with hummus was good, but by the time I got back to my destination, it was cooler than I would have liked (through no fault of the company). The pita bread was delicious. I will most likely order from them again, maybe next time through the app and try their delivery service.

This is not Tony's. Andy and Dee Dee Kohn are the proprietors. You can frequently see them smiling and greeting customers in a most friendly way. If something is not right, they make it right. The menu has something for everyone: the fattest juiciest wings in town, kinowa and kale salad, 35 way cheesey cheese noodles, flatbreads, burgers, healthy, heart stopping; you pick your poison. Great beer choices, decent and FAIRLY priced wine list, and all the Diet Coke you can drink.

Don't miss $5 burger night on Tuesday. Excellent burger and unmatchable.
Pfg. What's stopping you? Come on 

Had my first brunch here. Amazing!!!! Something special for everyone. S'mores pancakes for the kiddies, avocado toast for vegans, lots of  meat fOr carnivores . People stand In Line at other restaurants for less. 

Support this place. It is well deserved.

I would like to respond to Mark D. You are sooooo wrong. The club has fabulous food. You might want to ask the 700 members who enjoyed our Easter brunch. Can 700 people be wrong?????? Believe me they had many other Establishment's to choose from.

Chirashi.  I've never had a  good bowl of chirashi in Tucson but stoopidly I keep on trying.  This one was  total rip off.  Took forever for the waiter to bring it and then quick as a flash he vanished.  No wasabi, no ginger, no tamago, no roe, no nuthin'.  What he brought was a big bowl of plain white rice with a big glob of cheap filler on top consisting of seaweed and pea sprouts.  Under that they carelessly  tossed some little slivers of fish which was totally mediocre and some pieces were just cheap smoked fish.  That was it.  

Look, it's not that hard to make a good chirashi dish.  Give me a knife and put me behind the counter and I'll show you how.  The problem is all these dives want to save money by not putting any of the good stuff on it.  Zero stars rounded up to 1 because that's as low as I can go.

PS This is the first time I've been back here since the fire.  I don't know, maybe they still do Korean good.  The sushi sucked before the fire too, but the Korean food was good.

First, as I said before,  I'm not a big seafood fan, but this restaurant really seems to go all out for their customers. I went there in the middle of the week for their $12.95 lunch special. The food was plentiful and very tasty. It was all you can eat off the menu. I ate a lot. I had soup, pork rolls,  steak and chicken,  and three different types sushi. Then I had a dish of ice cream. It was all good. I'm not sure why this place wasn't packed with people but I will go back. Their servers all worked on all the tables and they kept the food coming. I really like the Volcano sushi roll. I  saw people from the LA Fitness in their too. I guess after working out, they have to put on the feed bag too. As I waddled out I noticed they have Happy Hour too. Go here to eat, drink and be merry.

Great family place. I initially came here to check out their burgers. I heard they used hamburger from Dickmans and that their hamburgers were very good, so I had to check them out. It turns out that their hamburgers are very good. I had their basic hamburger with cheddar cheese and  a side of cole slaw ( which was vinegar based). I wished I would have had the fries instead, they were thin almost like shoe string. Their ice cream is pretty good too.

This is a great place to go to after work to get drinks for happy hour and to sit outside on a nice day, but that's it.  Their food is not good, and I have experienced this on more then one occasion.  The server I had last time I went was just the rudest most pretentious individual i have ever encountered.  I could get much better mexican food for far less money.

Wish I had a picture but we finished our cheesesteaks before we could snap any pictures. Waited in line for about 20 minutes and it was well worth the wait. Very efficient ordering system, 6 people fully masked allowed inside at a time. Ordered our steaks and watched them work. From grilling the meat, to dressing the sandwiches, to wrapping it up they were fast and efficient. Waited about 10 minutes in total and it was well worth it.

One of our favorite dinners in New Orleans. The whole fish was amazing. It could have fed 4 people. Large portions. The Brussels sprouts were so good. We are outside. Very good advice. Amazing oysters. Great drinks! I'd come here again! Thanks!

Quick service, Stellar dishes!
This is a go to for Real Food!
(Low carb)
A hidden gem, so don't miss it, downstairs from where the Pneumatic used to be;)

Sit at chef's circle/table watching the kitchen action!

What a wonderful experience, fine dining and getting a show watching the action in the kitchen!!!

A diverse menu, with excellent presentation.  I will return for more, please!!!
Very good and fresh fish. Beautiful presentation for the sashimi dinner on lighted ice. Nice staff. We will return again. Ivan, the owner, was very good at making us feel welcome and comfortable.

Steer clear! We have always enjoyed this location since they opened UNTIL tonight. Ordered tomato pie and a cheesesteak, both were cold and soggy and they increased the prices out of nowhere. $26 for both.  The owners of this location needs to take a good long hard look at themselves and their greedy attitude. We will definitely be finding a new weekly pizza joint. Good job ownership, turned a regular customer into a critic. Thanks for ruining a good thing!

I went to Bee Roasters for the first time based upon the wonderful reviews. The location was fairly easy to find. When I entered the establishment I was greeted by one of the baristas. I was excited to learn that they offer loose leaf tea. I am a tea fanatic, so I was stoked. They had at least 5 different flavors to choose from. I opted for a rooibos. While my tea was steeping, the pastries  in a nearby container caught my eye. They had an assortment of muffins and an odd looking iced cookie. Nothing was labeled so I asked one of the baristas what muffin flavors are available. I chose the pineapple upside down. I was excited to learn that if you check-in at this location on Yelp, you recieve a discount, which is AWESOME. So everything cost less than $5. I took my goodies then I was out the door off to my next destination. I couldn't wait to try the muffin. There were pineapples at the bottom, which excited me even more. I took a hug bite, and I found the muffin to be just ok. I think in my mind I thought it would be a bit sweeter. No fault of the establishment, just a personal preference.  I don't know if my expectations were too high or because I didn't have coffee, but my first visit was just okay. I am still going to give them another try.
Average food. Not particularly high quality or interesting flavors. Not very clean. The most interesting food item was the spicy ketchup sauce. Everything else was pretty boring.

Came in for dinner last night. It's a type of place where you order at the counter, sit down, and then they bring you your food. Pretty low key place! The patio is shaded very well. The chips and salsa don't come with your food but you get a lot and they have a nice salsa bar. I liked the mango salsa. My Hailey Burrito was so good! My husband liked his Ketchum burrito as well and of course my daughter enjoyed her kids quesadilla. The margarita was worth the $5. Overall we had a nice low key dinner here. The burritos are not your normal taqueria burrito but they felt healthier and fresher ingredients. We'll definitely be back.

AMAZING Italian restaurant in every way possible!

Beautiful interior - first floor is a coffee / bar / grocery store with interesting and super cool things from Italy - condiments and sauces, pastas, chocolates, sweets, snacks, coffee, etc - wish I can buy everything here! Upstairs is an incredibly beautiful dining area with a retro vibe. The skylight adds to the whole Mediterranean charm and you can watch the scrumptious food made in an open kitchen. 

Now on to the food - WOWOWOW!!!

First of all, in addition to the already well-diverse regular menu, they have a special menu that changes every WEEK to celebrate the 52 cities of Italy! It was Elba when we went - so of course we had to find out what this amazing Tuscany city has to offer!

All the dishes were just DELISH!!! Flavorful and yet all the ingredients shined through! It was my first time having gelato that accompanied savory dishes and I was totally blown away!!! The gelato was savory with hint of sweetness and the gelato texture added a phenomenal sensation to the dish - just when I thought gelato couldn't get any better, it did!!!

And of course we had to get the famous gelato as well - again very good, even the wafer was delightfully crunchy and made a good match with the gelato.

Service was super friendly too- our waiter was so nice and patient and explained everything on the menu to us. Very attentive throughout the meal.
Very attentive service. Good place to fulfil traditional Italian cravings. Don't forget to top off your experience with Philly's Best Gelato, it's home-made!

Per usual asked for pizza to be well done, as often it's doughy and gross if you don't. The pizza that came is a brick. Could break your teeth on it as it's completely charred. Had 1 slice and trashed the pizza. Grossest pizza I have ever had. Completely disappointed in the food lately, rarely a good experience and ALWAYS ALWAYS ALWAYS late by at least 15 mins. Sorry I wasted $20 on Mina's food, I can promise you this was the absolute last time I'll order from this establishment.

Gave it another shot; glad I did.
freshly made Belgian waffle +maple walnut ice cream was delish....apparently they use a batter with actual pearl sugar (=authentic belgian waffle).

Something I really appreciated about the maple walnut was that the nuts were toasted (it's the little things!), and you could taste the freshness of the ice cream.  Nothing kills me more than when I go to an ice cream shop and the ice cream tastes anything like freezer burn...  There was absolutely none of that here.

The shop is small, cozy, but comfortable.  

Docked 1 star 'cuz I feel the price I paid is a bit outstanding for a waffle and 1 scoop of ice cream, at a little over $7..

(but at least it didn't disappoint, right?)

Great breakfast spot for families or solo! The service is always on point as is the quality of food. 

It's known to get crowded on the weekends so come with patience.

I've been here twice now and am happy to have a reason to grab food downtown. I really enjoy their voodoo chicken, however get it as a po-boy as it is good and spicy and you need the bread to cut it.
Their staff is very nice and friendly, the help you select what you'd like and even with a large crowd were very patient as their menu is much larger then you'd think it would be for a quick downtown stop.
They will ask you several questions to properly customize your order so be paying attention. 
I wish they would add shrimp to their menu as an option as it is mostly chicken dishes. Also their rice is nothing superb, add some salt and it is good but on the okay side.
Fun fast place that offers more filling fare then other locations downtown.
Save your time and money and go to the Tampa Palms location. Waaaay better service and food.

Came here for brunch last weekend. It was pretty fun. They have mimosas and bloody Mary's. I ordered biscuits and gravy and added two eggs on top! The gravy is very good with loads of pepper and the biscuits are big and fluffy.

All the other brunch food looked amazing. I will have to come back here for dinner. The patio is massive and on a summer day I hear this place is litty. 

I'll have to be back when it's warmer to drink on the patio and get Wiggity wild.
First time dining here for breakfast. Staff was really nice and attentive. I had the eggs in a nest it was really good for a sweat and savory option

This place was mediocre in all aspects.  The food was decent pub grub but dressed up fancy.  The prices were fair-priced for the college crowd that frequents there.  There is a dining area for the more mature crowd on one side.  Hi-tops and a large L-shaped bar for the revelers of a decent size. It got crowded pre-game and thinned out (Hawks game at Hagan Arena - walkable).  Good sport watching venue.  Service was consistent but not fabulous. 

I did have an issue - I switched to draft beer ($3) halfway through our visit.  I ended up getting a headache and feeling sick.  A hangover ensued but while I was still drinking.  I think this is due to the draft beer being too full of air - it has happened to me before.   I think it is the opposite of flat beer - likely, how it is poured.  I usually steer clear of draft beer but since it was a happy hour deal, I rolled with it.  I am not sure what the solution is or if I am the only one that experiences it but maybe there is a remedy.  Just a notation for you. 

I think the draw of this this place is its prime location as a drinking establishment for college students and not much more.  Expect to be underwhelmed a bit.
I love love this place ! Always delicious and I haven't had such a great Indo-Pakistaní food in years !! The owner and his staff are so sweet !

I have always been a fan of Chick-Fil-A it brings back childhood memories of trips to the mall.  My home town still does not have a Chick-Fil-A.  And I adore that the staff reply with "My pleasure!"  Nuggets with honey are where it's at!

went there pregame to a hockey game.  They had a decent selection of beers, but the musician they had was horrid.  It was such a downer that we could only last for the one beer.  I think Hooters is a better option before games.

Had a family lunch at Milito's after my daughters baptism a little over a year ago...to put it mildly the experience was unforgettable. We had a party of about 20 or so people. Wait staff was very inexperienced, food was not real great and the service was pretty poor. It was very evident that our servers had no idea how to provide basic food service as simple things like silverware are needed to eat and bread is not a dessert item and so on and so on. Also, if you screw something up apologize...don't huff and puff. We are not an inconvenience are we? We emailed the restaurant manager to give some feedback on our experience because this was a disappointing experience for such a special occasion. Well it's been over a year and no response and not one person in our party has returned. Quite frankly,  most Italians would be embarrassed of this place.  And more than anything it bothers me that our email went without a response...nothing rude or unreasonable in our email. I'm also kind of offended that the management their actively seeks out yelp reviews to respond to but didn't respond to our email.  Nothing says you don't care about customer feedback than that. I would have never wrote this review if they would have acknowledged our email.
Food is okay, portions feel like not worth the price. I ordered Togo and the total came out surprisingly high and the price is not adding up to it even counting tax. Menu prices are outdated.

This place gets three stars because the service was so great and the food...not so great.

We ordered the smokehouse chicken sandwich and the chicken pasta (I don't remember what it was called, but it had a BBQ Alfredo sauce). The sandwich was a chicken breast and two pieces of bacon smothered in BBQ sauce, between the two halves of a Costco-esque burger bun. That was it, except for some diced red onion and grated, really orange "cheddar" (which I didn't eat, since I generally don't put anything that glows in the dark in my body).

My mom had the pasta, which seemed to have the exact same ingredients as my sandwich, except on pasta. It was not very good.

The redeeming element of our Firebirds experience was the service. Our server was friendly and attentive, and the manager came by to make sure we liked the food. When we told him it was just alright, he asked what they could have done to make it great (ahem, kaiser roll, lettuce, tomato, decent SLICED cheese). He ended up taking my mom's pasta dish off our bill... They get big points for that. 

All in all, the food was pretty mediocre, but the service is what I would expect at a much more expensive restaurant. In a while we'll try them again and see if the kitchen got the memo.
Pre-COVID, this place had the best brunch events on the weekends mixed in with a live atmosphere with a DJ and hookah. I miss this place!

HA ha...she didn't know what head cheese was till it arrived! I took the munchkin there for the lunch special--three courses on the cheap. Of course we added the Shrimp Rémoulade. If you're a lowbrow Dallas tourist, which I am, you have to add the house specialties to the meal. 

She ordered the Homemade Hog's Head Cheese and Ratatouille. I had the Smoked Salmon and Pork Chop. Imagine her surprise when her cheese is meat from the hog's head. But she liked it. She said it tasted like really tender pot roast. 

My food was excellent. We both had the Banana Bread Pudding for dessert. This is a great deal for $24 a person! We arrived early, even for a Wednesday the place fills up for lunch. It's pretty. And I'm fairly sure there was someone who IS someone dining across the aisle from us. There was a great deal of whispering and special service going on.

Not the Drago I remember!  Had a dinner here with 5 people from our company and it was sad. I remember Drago for its great service and killer chargrilled oysters. Found both to be a huge disappointment on this visit. Oysters showed up after our dinners were placed even though they were ordered 30 mins before the meals. Chargrill was down for maintenance so they tried to do them outside on a grill which was no where near the same. Raw oysters were also ordered but we were told 30 mins later they were out so we took more chargrilled as a sub. Those never showed but after the disappointment of the first batch they were not missed. The rest of the food I would classify as 'ok'. The service from the hostess to the server we had were all particularly slow and disorganized. Too bad. I was looking forward to this visit. Trying acme oyster house tonight as I hear that is the much better alternative now.

Really nice place for a quick lunch. The food was great and fresh the service was quick and friendly and the place was exceptionally relaxing... i sat outdoors with the beautiful view. I would definitely come again and bring friends .
You can't go wrong. I would have to rate it as one of the top ten most impressive restaurants I have ever eaten at. It is somewhat pricey, but you are guaranteed an amazing meal and fun experience.

I stopped by this location and was in the mood for this appetizer. The waitress was Dani Very she was very informative writing me with providing me with a special special member discount and save me five dollars. Mark she was even so kind to enter the discount coupon for me. We ordered a triple dipper which was very good. The presentation was neat and the food and the food was heated properly. Overall The food tasted fresh and delicious The restaurant was clean but there was but there was a couple areas in the roof that dripped onto the floor next to our seat. Atmosphere in the bar area was casual.Therec were sports on the tv.
Lastly they have good drink specials and happy hour.
The end result was an enjoyable experience.

This truck is staffed by friendly people. The Carnitas is insanely delicious. The burritos are gigantic and the Nachos are fresh. I can't say enough good things about this Food Truck. If you are on Spring Garden during the day make sure to give El Tlaloc a try.

Such a cool location and courtyard! Went for lunch on a Monday and the staff was super friendly. Great atmosphere and solid beer lineup. Food was good, nothing crazy amazing but it was a great lunch! We were more impressed with how friendly the staff was and how cool of a environment they have created.

Horrible experience. Ordered the deluxe bento box Waited 20 mins for the food. The people came in behind me already got their food. So I walked to the counter asking for the progress.  the cashier give me a dirty look as It is my fault for being impatient. Never once apologize for it. The food is cold and very mediocre. Rice is dry. Never again return.   Warning: really slow and cold service. The cashiers are just couple of high school kids. So If you like bad service and crappy food. Please drop by.

The pork belly ramen is rich & satisfying. The addition of corn & green onion give it freshness to balance the richness. I love that the menu is not overwhelming, just tried and true items for anyone who loves noods.
Average food, slightly above average prices.  Service was fine.  Alcohol is beer/wine only.

Horrible service. We went for happy hour and ordered the brulleed goat cheese appetizer specifically asking for the toast without the garlic oil. When it arrived without the garlic oil- it turned out to have enormous pieces of garlic in the cheese(!) We couldnt even eat it because of garlic allergy, and when we told the waitress - she had an attitude.

A friend recommended this place to me. Just in town on business. After being in town for a week I haven't had a pleasant experience going out. Everyone has been kind of rude. Until coming here! Lauren was a pleasure and was very sweet and helpful. And the food was amazing as well. It was a definite turning point in my trip. Thanks Lauren!

Really had high hopes, very disappointed. Ordered crab and shrimp boil pan and stuffed lobster and crab cakes pan. The shrimp were mushy and the lobster was tough, hard with no taste. The deviled eggs were good and the service excellent.

The food is good, with a varied menu. Start with the complimentary, home made potato chips, yummy. Some recommendations are the burgers, mahi, and salads. The only item not recommended is the steak. And BEST of all 2 for 1 drinks and a good kids menu. In the past the service has been horrible, albeit pleasant. The past few times the service was good.
Perfect location for a cafe. This is not a cafe. Little to no attention to detail around decor, ambiance or creature comforts. Lame thermos coffee. Owner is grumpy and far from cordial.

Mashed potato pizza. Oh.Em.Gee. Cool space, I'm just happy there's another close-by bar that also has good food to add to the list. Really crowded but hopefully it dies down just enough that you're not on top of everyone.

Came to Brio for brunch, but they only had two items on the brunch menu, Which neither two peeked my interest. For starters we ordered the Calamari that came with a red sauce and a white sauce. The Calamari didn't have much flavor. I ordered a Arnold palmer made with peach syrup. This was really good. I ordered the Wedge salad which was good I just needed more blue cheese dressing. I ordered the Flatbread Margherita, but it was way too salty and asked the server to remove it. We also had the Spinach dip. My dining companions didn't care for it. I found it to be ok. We were going to order the shrimp and eggplant, but decided against it. Our server seemed to be new and had to be asked to refresh waters and our drinks. Visually the establishment is beautiful to look at. I left feeling like I didn't get what I was looking for.

First impression was that it's a cool little diner. They definitely have a Greek influence, but the menu is huge! They even serve breakfast all day, and lunch from 10:30am - 9:00pm. I was overwhelmed by the number of choices on the menu. They serve everything from gyros to broiled fish, to chicken piccata, and strip steaks. So whatever you're in the mood for, or I if you don't know what you're in the mood for, this is the place to find it. Honestly, I was really surprised at the variety of the menu, I mean they even have Schnitzel. Once we arrived we were seated immediately, and our server took our drink order. I ordered the chicken piccata, with pasta on the side, and a bean soup, and potato skins to start. Wifey ordered a Caesar salad to start, and the chicken francaise. Everything was great, but my piccata was a little bland to my liking, but I understand that it will appeal to more people this way. It wasn't a big deal, I spruced it up with a little lemon juice and salt and pepper. Another cool thing is when you get a dinner entree, you also get a soup or salad, and dessert! Oh did I mention that the prices are really reasonable? This place is really a great value for what you get. For dessert I got the chocolate pudding, and wifey got rice pudding. Both were very good. In conclusion, food was good and fair priced, service was excellent, and the ambiance is comfortable. I wouldn't hesitate to recommend this place, and we won't hesitate to come back.

I can't say enough about how great taco mar is! From the customer service to the food... it is all amazing. I recently started eating Mexican food and trying new places. My boyfriend called in an order (first time) and the man who took our order was so friendly and helping us decide what to get and what are interest we're. So patient and helpful. We ordered the fish and shrimp tacos. Highly recommend, he offered two different sauces, a white garlic sauce and a chipotle. We got both and they were delicious. Their guacamole is hands down the best I've ever had. It's always so fresh! If you haven't had their food yet, you have to go!

Food is absolutely delicious! You can tell it is very fresh and high quality. The menu was easy to navigate and the staff was friendly. 

I would give 5 stars, but it is a bit pricey for roasted vegetables and protein that I can make myself at home. However, when I'm in a time crunch, it is a healthy and delicious option for downtown philly. I'll be back!
They were okay...nothing I would Rav about . They had great deals but average chicken. Havent really though twice about going back

Total customer service failure. I used to order from here for delivery all the time. Food was decent. Your usual pizzeria food. Wings were good. Called tonight and was told they no longer deliver to my address. Mind you I'm 4 miles away. When I asked when the policy changed they told me a month ago. At that point i explained that they had delivered to me 2 days ago. The response was "well no, sorry we can't." 

I manage a large business who also used to use this place for parties. I explained this to the owner on the phone and he said that he would still do it for big orders. So he won't deliver for me, but if I make it worth his while......no, sorry. I can't.

Come here fairly often because we know lots of the staff, and we've always had great service. Full bar and GREAT food. I would warn that the food takes a while to come out, especially on busy weekend nights. But if you're wanting to spend a couple of hours over food, beer, and live music with the family, it's a great choice!

Love this place.  Good food, friendly and helpful staff, and ... mere feet from the water.

We often drop in for a cup of coffee to take for a walk on the beach, and a bit less often treat ourselves to a nice dinner on the patio.

Update:  While we've never had a bad experience here, our recent visit was off-the-charts great.  Our server, Dom, was exceptional.

You'll be very happy here on a date, family dinner, or to treat yourself.

My favorite go to local Tampa place to get some delicious BBQ. I love sliced pork and always find it so hard to find at BBQ places as most do chopped. They give very generous portions here and delicious homemade pickled pickle slices if you eat in. They also offer a drive thru option though I would recommend ordering online and just picking up through the drive through so you don't wait for the meats to be prepared. As for sides, I love their green beans, Mac and cheese, onion rings, and fries! This is an OG cute BBQ spot that was revamped a few years ago.

A delicious meal served by such adorable staff! I stopped by for an early dinner before going to school and it was just perfect. They didn't mind at all when I stayed after I was done eating & caught up on some emails. I'll definitely be back

Had the spring rolls. Standard thin ones without much filling. not quite worth the price.

Pho was good. Soup is on the light side. The rare meat was cut paper thin and delicious. The brisket was thick cut and had that good fatty flavour. The meat balls were very nice.  If the soup were richer I would give it a much higher rating.

Our party of 5 arrived close to opening and didn't have any wait. The famed chicken was much lighter than I anticipated it being! Tasty without being overly salty. We also tried the veal, which was surprisingly good. The butter beans were yummy (I've never tried them anywhere else before). The fried okra comes in a HUGE portion. Pro tip if you go with a kid: order off the kids menu. That thing was almost as large as our adult order and also comes with a side. Waiter was very nice but also very forgetful. Would usually take 2-3 times reminding him before we got what we asked for (sweet tea, cornbread, hot sauce, etc.)

Had dinner here with a few friends this past weekend. Service was excellent - friendly & attentive. The restaurant atmosphere was great, although i think it would have been even better if we could have eaten upstairs (suggest requesting upstairs seating prior to arrival). Food was excellent! Great flavor and portions. Really enjoyed our meals and wine (Oregon Pinot Noir was excellent!) Will dine again

GMG is my absolute favorite lunch spot in Oro Valley. They offer a very generous lunch portion (about 25 dishes to choose from) for between $6.50-7. The lunch combo includes soup (egg drop or hot ans sour), wonton crackers, fried rice, and an egg roll. I've tried the house chow mien, chicken and broccoli, beef and broccoli, and shrimp and vegetables. All of it's been delicious. Like all Americanized Chinese food, it's very heavy and rich, but makes a great treat! Plus, they pack your leftovers for you, and it's usually enough food to need a to-go box. It reheats beautifully and the container they put it in is microwave friendly. My leftovers don't usually last through the afternoon.

This is probably the best lunch value I've encountered in Tucson. The food comes out promptly and the service is good. The restaurant is usually half or more full with customers during lunch, but I've never had to wait for a table. The interior is very clean and the decor is kind of neat, with a big lighting fixture installation on the ceiling that changes colors. Highly recommend!

Went here tonite and it was wonderful. Food was delicious and plentiful. They will spice it as you like, and it seems to be made to order. You can make it a meal and get naan and a drink for only a bit more. I think this is now our favorite Indian restaurant. Give it a try- you won't be disappointed. And try the iced tea. Really special blend of tea and spices. So refreshing.

Found some good Pho in Reno! 

Not only is the broth good, but the toppings are abundant. I would definitely come back to try the Bun and Bahn Mi.

I would not get the porkchop lunch special again though, too sweet, small, and kinda dry. The service was really great!

Updating my review to reflect the new, reduced quality of the Old Eagle. It's quite clear everything that is going on here is aimed to increase profits. They got rid of the bottles of domestic beers and only have cans now (don't care really, but they should be cheaper, but alas, they are not). The menu has been substantially reduced and many nice items are no longer available. The fries used to be phenomenal and they cut back to some cheaper kind and you can tell.

Come for conversation, go elsewhere for food.

Ordered for takeout last night, and we were very pleased, overall! We got the Thai Fried Rice-so good! We will be getting that every time we order. 
We also got the Yellow Curry and the Chicken Pad Thai. The flavor of the curry was great, but it had a little more bamboo shoots than we'd prefer. Still great though! 
The Pad Thai just seems to be missing something. At the other Thai places I go to, they ask me for a spice level and this place didn't do that. There was no spice at all. It was kind of citrusy, even though I didn't add the extra lime. I like spicy, so I prefer my Pad Thai that way. This one was still good, just not the flavor that I'm used to for a Pad Thai. They also threw in some almond angel food cake (?) cookies and they were really good!! We will definitely be back soon!

My first review was glowing, but I had a chance to go back last night- a Saturday, and people outside- all of them including me, had to wait a VERY long time for service.  I never went inside, so I don't know how slammed they were, but in any event, they we under-staffed.  People were upset, not me really, but it was awkward.
