Food was so-so too compared to prior vists- the expensive guac was a smaller portion, and the chorizo burger was very dry- it's always been incredibly juicy.  Maybe an "off" night, but there is so much other competition, I think I'll pass on this place from now on.

It is a small restaurant. 
One in our party enjoyed their gyro and said it was good.
One had chicken strips with eggs. The biscuit, eggs and gravy were satisfactory. The chicken strips were heavily breaded and fried hard. The chicken strips had some tough meat areas, so would not order them again.

Rude! The food is ok, but everytime I call to order they are rude. One time, I called and placed my order and asked for a total. The guy I was talking to yelled to someone else and asked for a total. The other person said, "tell her $ 3.95 for the fries, $8.50 for the sandwich and $2.00 for delivery". I asked for a total, not an itemization. I can look at the menu and do math, apparently they can't. I asked for the total b/c I wasn't sure if I had a current menu and what the delivery charge was. Then when the order arrived, the total wasn't $14.45 it was $15 and change. They also have no patience when taking the order and no manners. I say I want to order and they say "what do you want" with an attitude like I am bothering them. I am sick of it and won't be ordering anymore. A sandwich with cheep, sinewy meat on it is not worth it.
Had the carbonara. It was ok. The sauce was really thick. My favorite part about it was thr poached egg. 2nd favorite thing was the bacon. The free bread was good. The server was a bit overeager.
Excellent food - good service. Several vegetarian options. I had the vegetarian paella -- it was very good. White chocolate bread pudding for dessert--plenty to share with a friend or three!

Ok the place fooled me.  Thought out was a retro burger joint.  That's how it was described.  No it's a modern-day industrial burger joint with turkey and vegetarian options.  They have old fashioned soda pop on tap.  I'm convinced that it doesn't matter what you order here...you'll be well pleased.  Parking can be tight, but it's worth the effort.  Get in line...order your food and they bring it to you.  Get your own drink.  Might have to look to get a full bottle of ketchup or fry sauce.  They also offer regular mustard and honey mustard.  I got the burger and it was just plain delectable.  I swiped a couple fries from my wife...they are the old fashioned ones with a soft center.  My onion rings were battered and nicely fried...not greasy.  They have plenty of tables. I quickly learned why the locals favor this place.  Expect great food...Oh yeah.

First off the owner was super nice. I mean the kinda humble niceness that New Orleans has in spades and gets right. 

The food was exactly what I wanted for a local neighborhood place. Cheap check. Good check. I had the fried shrimp po-boy and it was spot on. The bread and the breaking on the shrimp were awesome cooked perfectly. 

Do yourself a favor and grab the lunch special 5.99 for a po-boy and fries.

Went out to trident grill for the first time last night. It's a cozy sports bar with well sized menu. I was so impressed by the good and services we had a lovely waitress named Aida that went out of her way to make sure we were happy. The food was delicious. The drinks were fantastic. I would definitely recommend and will be returning!

Cons: mediocre pizza. Pros: after waiting an hour and a half for it, you'll be so hungry you'll eat it all anyway. 
We went on a Friday night. The place was packed. Long wait to sit down.  After we ordered and paid, they informed us that one oven was broken and the pizza would be an hour. We rolled with it. Our hunger grew and grew as we waited. When the pizza arrived, it was mediocre. Good toppings but a firm, tasteless crust. If you hold a slice out only by the crust, the tip will point straight out without bending. Very similar to what you get if you make pizza at home on a pizza stone. After living in New England for a time, I'm a pizza snob, and I worry that there probably won't be anything better in Boise. How I yearn for the crispy (but pliable), flavorable crust I once knew. My search continues.
Best breakfast in the area and very reasonably priced esp for the portion size .. Hungry man breakfast is highly recommended

We stayed in Santa Barbara for a long weekend and sought out Mesa Verde, though we were staying downtown. I am vegan and my boyfriend eats vegan most of the time. We arrived when the restaurant opened, so the service was relaxed and attentive and the owner was just lovely.  We ordered way too much, too excited about the options to narrow our choices, but enjoyed the leftovers.  Everything that we had was delicious, beautifully presented - and the portions were substantial.  We had the Latkes, BLTA and Macro Bowl (plus chai and lemonade).  Admittedly, though we were stuffed (and had leftovers already boxed to go), we gave into the offer of baklava with vanilla ice cream and were blown away.  Insanely good.  Don't miss Mesa Verde, especially if you are even remotely interested in seeing how good plant based food can be...

It's been a while since I've had a good Chinese food experience out here in Jersey since I've moved here in august. My husband really wanted Chinese food and I was trying to change his mind... glad he didn't listen to me (for once ). 

I ordered delivery through Uber eats, accidentally put the wrong address for some reason and they were really friendly and made sure it went to the right person. The driver dropped it off on someone else's porch ( contactless delivery) and after calling the restaurant, he came back and i was already crossing the street to meet up with him. Very friendly service and the food was still hot. 

I think I found a Chinese restaurant I like here! Soooo good

An exclusively vegan restaurant with a wide selection of creative and tasty selections.  The menu follows a New Orleans theme, with vegan interpretations.  Well prepared and artistically presented.  Casual setting and busy with what looks luke local clientele.  Off rhe beaten tourist parh, but in a bohemian part of Uptown known as the Lower Garden District.  Walking distance to streetcar line.  One of the best vegetarian rstaurants I've been to.  Well beyond the "grainy" quality of most places, with no hint that patrons are grazing.  Preparations need more attention to seasoning to impart more taste.  Basically roasted vegetables, needs some rosemary, sage or something.

The only reason I'm giving two stars and not 1 is because of the atmosphere outdoors and live music was good. Food, service and cleanliness were not so good. Great for outdoor drinks and live music but not recommending eating there.

I have visited this restaurant three times, now - and always find the same problem.  When you go for the butter chicken, vegetable korma, or other dishes with sauce, you are hard- pressed to find the chicken, vegetables, etc.  On Thursday evening all they should have called those dishes was butter sauce and korma sauce.  In talking to a friend, he said that seems to be true at the northeast location as well.  My Thursday dinner partner ordered a chicken masala or something similar from the menu and had the same complaint as I had from the buffet food - just a large helping of sauce.  All was not lost however.  The mango sweet potato soup was terrific and I really enjoyed their pakora, naan bread and saffron rice, so did not go home hungry.  Can't say the same for friend who ordered from the menu!
By the way, they don't bring your bill to the table so you will be there a long time if you are waiting for it.

Why go to Geno's? Really, why? Cosmi's is very close to Geno's and is a top 5 cheesesteak. I don't think either Geno's or Pat's is superior, but Pat's isn't bright orange and doesn't have neon all over it.

Pretty average pizza place in most respects, but they make a really good vegan pizza! The wait is a little long but my guess is they never have vegan pies on hand and have to make them after we order. I prefer theirs to PWS, but I wish they had more vegan options (like the seitan wings at PWS). Overall my experiences here have been good!

Today was their first day of business at the new location in Palm Harbor so we HAD to go. We went with a crowd of seven for lunch and all seven left happy! It was exactly what we wanted. We all wish them best of luck in this new location.

I don't even know where to start with tableau. The ambiance is very chill. We sat outside on the balcony and enjoyed the wonderful view and great people watching. It was our anniversary and the staff more than took care of us. They were so nice and really went out of our way to make our day so special! We would come back here every year if we could! For food, we ordered the gnocchi, market fish and bbq shrimp. Everything was excellent and we can't wait to come back!

alright i love qdoba but this location is an exception. i just moved to the area and before would frequent the hermitage and west end stores which are delicious. 

the first time i came to the brentwood location they were completely out of ground beef. it was later in the evening (around 8) so i figured the day had just took its toll and it was fine. i ordered chicken instead to go. 

the chicken was tough, dry and impossible to bite through so i ended up throwing my meal away, but again i chalked this up to just a bad experience. 

so tonight i came back. ordered the tacos again. this time they had the beef which i was pleased about. i began paying while the girl finished up my tacos, which were completely wrong. swimming in sour cream which i didn't ask for and no tortilla strips or corn. again no big deal. i walk up to the counter and mention my order was wrong. i even told the girl she could just scrape the sour cream off and i would still enjoy them but her manager insisted on a remake. 

the cashier snatches my plate out of my hand and begins heavily sighing, eye rolling and in general bad attitude. she remakes my tacos and hands them back to me, still sans tortilla strips and corn. i ask for them and she says, "they're already on there," with the most attitude possible as if i didn't watch her remake them and no they weren't. she begrudgingly adds more, and i'm so annoyed i just take my food and leave. 

the beef was cold and i paid for queso i never got. i ordered 4 tacos and they only remade 3 of them. honestly i would rather drive 20 minutes out of my way to not have another garbage experience here.

Sooooooooo good. Great service. Want to go back everyday. I ordered the peppercorn steak and it was really really good. I tried their signature blueberry lemon cocktail and that was really good as well. Tried their strawberry basil and wasn't a huge fan but it want bad. Their Flemings potatoes was probably my favorite side dish offered at any steak house. I've been to many of the steak houses in the city and never been the Flemings before but I'm glad we went. The highlight that puts Flemings above the others is their attention to detail like the complimentary parking, Coat check and the car being brought to you by the time you're outside the door. You don't see that kind of service in a lot of places so it's great to see how much they are thinking of their diners. Can't wait to be back!
Stumbled in on a Sunday afternoon, very pleasant surprise. Food was superb and our waiter was very good, perfect recommendations for app, meal, and dessert. Will be back

What a pleasant place. Has an upscale vibe to it. The staff here are remarkable. My waiter Anthony "little Tony" is an upstanding example of what an employee should be. The menu is opening, inviting and exciting. We started with the classic wedge. the bread here is nice and crispy on the outside but soft on the inside. We had the pistachio pesto orechetta for the main entree. The chicken was nice and tender, the pasta had plenty of flavor. We are having our first Christmas party here in December and looking forward to it.
My new po-boy stop when traveling between Florida and Texas. Split the fried shrimp and the alligator po-boy with hubby. Excellent!!!!!

I've been coming to Cate Zone for years now and have never left a review. I've been singing their praises by word of mouth but now it's time to go virtual as well. 

Best Chinese food in St.Louis, I promise it does not get better than this. Our last visit was on Christmas Eve and a 45 minutes wait..... end up only being 35 and so well worth it. Their space is small but with food this consistently amazing I hope they can expand or open a second location. 

Recommendations: sizzling eggplant (this dish is a must every time I go we eat it as an appetizer), the Szechuan boiling fish or hot fried fish are my favorites. My fiancé's loves the beef skewers or their lamb cilantro rice.

Very tasty. I like that there is so much variety. You literally can create any pizza combo and not be looked at strangely lol 
My fiance and I dined in last week and while there was a line, it was not unreasonable. 

Overall, the pizza was fresh and tasty and we received good service. We'd definitely return.

i will review the plainfield indiana location for you. i ordered a burger and onion ring. i had to pay a extra dollar to sub the onion rings instead of fries. i only got 4 onion rings that where pretty good and hot. this is all that was good the rest of my visit. my burger was only warm with a stale bun and no mayo like we asked for. my food was in a basket which always make me think its a plate that everyone uses and don't get washed. for $9.00 can't they wash a plate that i eat off of? my wife ordered tenderloin with iceberg lettuce and mayo. and fries. they where cold and had fancy lettuce and no mayo. she sent it back since it was cold and tasted bad and was chewy. she wanted a burger to replace it and iceberg lettuce with mayo. the girl brought her some iceberg lettuce while they made the burger. the manager come by and took her lettuce away to trash. when her burger come finally she had to wait for more lettuce and mayo. lettuce in one trip and mayo in second trip. the girl waitress would disappear for 5 to 10 minutes a trip. all the employees where high school kids and always missing in action for 5 to 10 minutes. if there was a emergency nobody would know for 5 to 10 minutes. this place is in metropolis mall and parking is terrible but thats not there fault its the designer of the mall fault. i was not happy at all and for $9.00 i can get a steak across the street or a $9.00 hamburger that is good with better service, better taste, better parking. if you want to watch a football game and drink a beer, eat cold $9.00 burgers and park out back of the mall this is your place. i would have to be paid to eat there again.

We are so glad this place opened.  The BBQ, pulled pork especially is awesome.  The grits, mac and cheese, cole slaw, all top notch.  The only reason I give it 3 stars is they just have to get their act together with service.  The last 3 times we've gone, they've been out of something critical (at a very early hour).  Last Saturday night, we called in our order about 10 minutes before arriving and proceeded to stand and wait for it for another 30 minutes while some very large take out order had everyone scrambling.  One of the items that had run out was corn bread.  Corn bread?  A staple of bbq?  There were definitely people standing around that could have made some more!  
Come on, guys.  We want this place to knock it out of the park but service is key!

Really interesting tiki spot to stumble in to. Lots of variety on the menu. Prices range from like $8 to $16 for a cocktail (if I'm remembering right). Staff were super cool and attentive. Didn't try the food but will next time I'm in Philly.

Made my way to Jim's because my friends from Philly said it was a must. Most reviews will tell you that the line is always out the door, and it is. Sometimes it'll wrap around the side. It does move pretty smoothly. They have a good selection of bottle drinks and beers. There is very limited seating upstairs, it's not good for big groups. 

The main reason why Jim's gets a 3 star review is because the meat lacked a lot of seasoning. I did have a little high expectation for this cheese steak, but the blandness of the steak was disappointing. The onions were flavorful and the bread was fresh. But I have had better seasoned cheese steaks.

You know I've been a customer for over 15 years and now I see how small portions have become and how expensive the food has become. Last time the food wasn't that great and now it's a small Stromboli for just shy of $15. I can go to pats and get a large for the same price! Very unhappy. Never will again will I order here. It's like burning money.

If you like being seated close to the noise/activity of the hibachi grill when it's just two of you and the rest of the dining room is empty, and if you prefer to receive your appetizer after your entrees/rolls have arrived, and if you don't care if your order isn't correct, and if you like waiting 30 minutes for the check, this place is for you. The food is good. That's about the only positive thing I can say about this place.

Small, trendy place with a great atmosphere.  Relatively inexpensive, but also somewhat limited menu.  We typically order the flatbreads and a glass of wine.  The wine selection is very expansive.  

Overall, I would HIGHLY recommend Tria for a weekend dinner or late night meal.  The combination of social atmosphere, good food and wine, and moderate price make it an overall great experience and one of the best restaurants we've been to in Philly

My friends and I came here for a birthday party just tonight, and it was alright. It was my first time back at the Cheesecake Cafe since they burnt down a few years ago, and it was surprising to see how much they've changed. They've totally revamped the place. It used to have a more family restaurant feel to it, resembling the Olive Garden's atmosphere, but now it looks all modern glam like Moxie's. 

They don't take reservations on the weekend, so I had to call in an hour early for our party of six, to get us on the waiting list. We got there, and no one came to take our name for several minutes, so we were just left standing there. Finally a hostess came and told us it would be about 10 minutes, even though I had called in an hour earlier. 

Their booths are very roomy, and ours was able to seat all of us comfortably. Our waitress was great, coming every now and then to check on us, and also helping us take group photos. 

I had the french onion soup, because I didn't want to be too full for the cheesecake -- we were mainly there for the dessert. The soup was alright, a bit salty, but it usually is. The cheese on top was one big chewy mound of cheese though, not soft and stringy as I like it. 

We decided to order a bunch of different cheesecakes and just share them all. I was rather disappointed that the Bailey's cheesecake tasted really light; you could barely taste the Bailey's in it. The raspberry vanilla cake was the thickest, and also the heaviest. The white chocolate was okay, kinda bland and nothing really special about it. The Very Berry cake was the best, because the berries make the cheesecake not too sweet. 

Cheesecake Cafe offers a lot of Asian fusion cuisine on their menu, which I was surprised to see. I'm not sure if a dessert place like this could do Asian food that well though. I have my doubts, as you can see. I thought a few of their appetizers were also kind of expensive for appies. I mean, they're not entrees, but they're almost the same price! 

I was also surprised to see a lot of families with young children there too. I guess it's a common place for families? They have an open bar and their tv screens were tuned into football. The overall ambiance of the place seemed to clash a little, with the sports channels playing, Top 40 music in the background, and little kids running around everywhere. Still, I guess it's a place where everyone comes for the dessert. I'd say the food was okay, but I've had better, and that includes the cheesecake.

As a native Californian it's hard to find good Chinese spots. But this place is now my go to favorite place for authentic Chinese takeout. I got the chicken lo mein and duck egg noodle soup. Huge portions. Healthy, not greasy. Definitely returning.

I was visiting Nashville for the first time. I wanted to try something the locals like, and I found Hattie B's. The workers were all friendly and helpful. The line was fairly long, so I was sure the food was good. I ordered the chicken sandwich and sweet tea. I was convinced to try the Mac and cheese as well. I was not disappointed! I don't think I'd ever eaten as fast as I did. To be fair, I was really hungry as well. I thought I was going to have to wait a long time for my food, but it came out within a decent amount of minutes. 10/10 for the sandwich and Mac & cheese. The sweet tea wasn't as sweet as I'd have liked it so I'll give that about a 6/10. I definitely recommend this place, especially if you're all about seasoned fast food!

My son has mentioned Uzbekistan numerous times. He chose it for his birthday dinner last night.  Having Russian/Western European heritage, I expected heavy food and much bloating. I was delightfully surprised.
As a party of 7 (who tasted everything), 3 of us ordered beef stroganoff--accompanied with real whipped potatoes and a salad. Others had kebabs that we tried and enjoyed. Lamb ribs, bread, varenikis were all a delight. 
Unlike some of the other reviewers, I can tolerate a little delay with service. It didn't affect my enjoyment in the least. All the staff were pleasant and helpful.
My wife--a light eater--wolfed down her stroganoff and varenikis. We agreed that we had to return and try other items that called to us from the menu.
My son ordered the chicken (stew, I think).
In all, a great introduction to a new restaurant with an enticing menu to explore.

Pretty good, but honestly I was a bit disappointed. Everything looked good and was cooked well but lacked lots of flavor. I got the French dip and my husband got the salmon. There were other things I should have tried but everything was lacking salt and spice. Service was fine, he misunderstood my friend's order and was decently attentive.

We did sit outside which was really awesome but the creek.
Old school style pub! Great food and has a great selection of brew! They even have Hoegarden on tap! My wife and I stumbled in here on a Sunday afternoon and we both cant wait to come back.
Great place in downtown Tampa. Casual drinking in the afternoon. Music, dancing, live bands at night.

Ambiance- 4 stars
Wait staff personality- 1 star
Food - 3 stars
Tap beer selection- 0 stars

Sorry to be so rude but did not feel welcome here.

Must try the Downtown Salad~ an absolute favorite!  Also Grandma's Pie~ a huge favorite of ours.  So nice to finally have a great pizza shop~ they have inside and outside dining and a BYOB.  Always very crowded on a Friday night~ actually not just Friday's either!

Suggested by our Uber driver when we got into town. Brisket and pulled pork were spot on delicious. Subtracted a star for organization and side options. Would definitely go back because it's all about the meat!

My girlfriend just ordered at this restaurant through Postmates. she ordered Chicken and Waffles with a side of collard greens, a Vegan BBQ Sandwich, and three orders of Vegan Mac and Cheese. When the postmate arrived at the restaurant, she called to say they were out of the side of collard greens. We told her that we would take corn on the cob instead, no problem. When she arrived at my hotel, we received: Three pieces of chicken (no waffles), NO Vegan BBQ sandwich, two corn on the cobs, and the three vegan mac and cheeses.

When we called the restaurant to ask why they didn't contact us about all of the things they were out of, they completely blamed Postmates and refused to take responsibility. I travel all over the country for work and use Postmates all of the time. When a restaurant is out of something, they usually call to tell me. They don't tell the Postmate to tell me. The manager placed ALL of the blame on Postmates and told me that "if I would've contacted them directly, this never would've happened." To which my response is, "Then why would you offer your services on the Postmates app? 

The manager was clearly upset with Postmates, but directed that anger towards my girlfriend. I am ABSOLUTELY disgusted with this. We waited two hours, only to be given less than half of what we ordered. I leave town tomorrow, so luckily I wont be seeing this restaurant again in the upcoming future. If you don't like Postmates, then DO NOT offer your services on the app.

Thanks for ruining dinner!
Love this place, reasonably priced, open till 10 during the week 11 Fri & Sat, fresh, fresh!

Love is all I have to say. Good for vegetarians and meat eaters alike, the food is not bland and most of my carnivore friends have been all for this place. I come here when I want to treat myself. Their long weekend Friday buffets are to die for. A++

Went for lunch,loved the menue selection and prices....was wanting to love this place . Ordered the lasagna. The portion was 1/2 a normal serving so guessing for lunch that was ok,but now not so reasonably priced . My first bite reminded me of the canned spaghetti O's from my younger days on the military base or from the embassy comisary. I ate a little more and sure enough...the sauce is as was my recollection of the canned spaghettios... glad my portion was so small ...when we got home  I had a proper lunch. Will give this restaurant  one more try, but won't be ordering the Lasagna or anything in a red sauce for that matter....wish me luck!.
       The decor is very nice as is the service and staff.Nice ambiance.
best in the city by far and the people have a heart of gold i go thier all the time .

I just walked out if this place, it SUCKS!!!   I am Cuban and expected good food just like the previous reviews say.  I had picadillo with rice & plantains and couldn't eat it.  It was cold & tasteless.  My hubby had a Cuban sandwich and it was worst than my plate.   Never again would I go back here.
The food is fine. Unfortunately they don't live in this century where phones work. Good luck if you need to call them. They won't answer. Poor customer service and the food takes FOREVER.
Came in today for a quick bite and a drink! Pizza was delicious and the service was great, Vance did a really great job taking care of us. I'll definitely be back!

This place was so good that my friend and I came here twice during our 4 days in NOLA. We ordered the seared shrimp and sweet potato. As expected the shrimp was so good but we were blown away by how good the sweet potato was!!! We ordered the potato salad which was a little too spicy for our taste but definitely would recommend the braised greens. We also tried the bbq chicken poboy at our next visit. All in all, this place is great for the price and service was excellent!!!

I have been hyping PJ's wings up for a few months to a couple co-workers who have never been. We finally go on wing night and now the wings are so small?! Maybe due to Hurricane Florence or maybe PJ's is finally turning into a sell-out franchise/chain. I don't know. Anyway, wings used to be the best and large. Now it's a rip-off. $4 copper lagers are the only good thing going on there apparently.
Amazing!!   The Mexican Char Oysters were the best oysters I have ever had.  I highly recommend the tacos too. This is a must try restaurant, we will be going back!

The reason for the 1 star is that when you walk in, the atmosphere is nice and friendly.  They also sat us quickly after requesting to wait for a booth to become available.  The rest of the experience was not worth any stars.  

We decided to try this place after seeing many good yelp reviews, unfortunately I am unable to write a good review.  We ordered the Smoked Wings for an appetizer and they came out pretty quickly.  There were 8 smoky wet wings that looked great on the plate, but first bite was disappointing.  They were cold!  We are not ones to take plates back or have them redo the order, so we decided that we were just going to take them home. 

We decided to get the Slow Smoked Pit BBQ platters, which came with two sides of your choice.  My wife ordered the Chopped Pork Shoulder with house fries and mac n' cheese. I ordered the Ribs with fried okra and sweet potato waffle fries.

The platters came out as quickly as our appetizer had, and were as disappointing or if not more.  All the food was cold, like it had been just sitting and they just place it on the platter when ordered.  The worst was the mac n' cheese, the center was refrigerator cold....inedible.

We asked for boxes, so we could take our dinner home and heat it up ourselves.  This was by far our worst dining experience ever that all the food was not up to par.  We spent $35 on take-out food.

Fusion Bowl is a nice laid back spot. This is the second time I have been here. I must say I do love just sitting on the couch. Last time around I got the breakdown from Rico Suave Mel R. on dominoes. 

Last time around I had the beef teriyaki, and this time I had the Japanese udon noodles, chai tea latte, and a nice sample of vanilla ice cream and Vietnamese coffee. All were delicious!

I can't say enough thank you's for the owners of Fusion Bowl. They are very friendly and welcoming! This is a great spot that I will definitely come back to!

I'm not gonna lie, I've been to Penang several times back when I was a college student about 5 years ago and remember being blown away by how good the food was. 

This time, I still loved my go to appetizer Roti Canai, and chicken sate was full of flavor and the meat was super succulent, but the mains we got just didn't have the same impact. Partner and I got prawn mee and cantonese chow fun. I enjoyed the savory broth of my prawn mee and appreciated the generous shrimp inside, but the noodles were overdone. Pork slices were dry and tough. It was just okay. 

My partner was really disappointed with his chow fun. He went with the "safe" option and ordered it thinking it would be similar to chow fun you get at a Chinese restaurant. What came out was a goopy and soupy concoction with chopped up wide rice noodles floating in it. On another note, portion for this dish was generous- lots of squid and greens, etc. It was just so not what we expected based on the description on the menu. 

Service was excellent though and it's a plus that the place opens until late. Even though the main dishes were a let down this time, I will probably return for the roti and skewers.

I love B.Good. This location is a bit iffy though. There are generally long lines/wait time. I enjoy the almond ginger bowls the most. I also do love knowing where my food is coming from, it's important! 

However, their smoothies are strange. I have tried each one on the menu. The ingredients are delicious don't get me wrong, but the smoothies come room temperature, which is a little off putting. Other than that B.Good has a lot of healthy alternatives, everything is made to order, and they offer customization when it comes to your meal. The staff at this location is nice and always helpful.

Simply the best authentic Mexican food you can find in the Tampa bay and Zephyrhills area. Affordable, small, and delicious. Their Pastor and Shrimp tacos are amazing. My mother in law loves their Chorizo burrito.

My favorite place to dine and hang out in St. Louis. The beer selection and quality is of course outstanding. They constantly rotate their offerings, but not too frequently. They have to categories of beers: faithful productions of the classics and contemporary editions. For example, they have an excellent Czech Pilsner, a great Marzen, and a very, very special Bavarian Oktoberfest. They also have very tasty contemporary varieties, like modern IPAs. Bottom line, the beers are truly excellent. 
That said, I really love the food here. The food selection is written on a caulk board and rotates selection often. The focus seems to be Central European fare, but they do it well. While I try to mix it up with variety, I find that the Bratwurst Board is magical. The presentation is perfect. Two perfectly prepared brats, with spicy German mustard, and the best German potato salad ever. I had to educate a coworker as to the difference between southern mayonnaise based potato salad and the authentic German stuff. Trust me, the German potato salad here is authentic and awesome.

A great place for everyone! The pizza is the best pizza hands down! The staff is great too
 We will definitely be back.

I have tried crab all over south Jersey and this place is my favorite yet! The service was amazing & the crab was perfectly cooked and seasoned. It was so good! You get a bread basket before your meal with several different types of bread which were all great. We went on a Wednesday evening about 6pm and they weren't very busy at all, so it was perfect. Their dessert display looked really good too, which I definitely want to try the next time I go back! Full of cakes, cheesecakes, and more. Loved everything about this place! Can't wait to come back to eat again.

We were in a road trip and stop here from New York on our way to Virginia. One because there were only 2 open at 2/3am. I didn't choose this spot. I just went with the flow. It seems that people was coming from the club here to eat and there were actually lines. Pat's which was down the street had a smaller crowd. The process was simple. I was a little confused at the selections. The sandwiches are sold separately from the fries btw. The place is well maintained and looked like it's in Vegas or time square but cleaner. They have a merch store and everything. 

I had a few fries - since I only eat organic food. Everyone I was with had different sandwiches and the response was dry and I wish we went somewhere else. One person said it was good. So that's my review on the food. I put it up on my food page and the response was why did you go there.. lol

I absolutely love this place and wish I could give it more stars!! Came here on a snowy Saturday! The place was packed. We were still immediately greeted and brought to our table. 

Staff was lovely and well informed. They had a wide variety of teas and the waitress not only helped me, but my children pick the best tea. 

On the tea-- it was amazing. I have several friend who drink tea who would be thrilled to see such a varied selection. The finger sandwiches were yummy and soup simply delicious! Everything had a home made feel with focus on every detail. 

My children had a wonderful time and we will definitely bring back other to enjoy. We live in philadelphia and have been searching for a great place to have tea. You cannot find anywhere in the city for a place so quaint with food and tea that was so delightful!! 

Will be asking to make a reservation for Mother's Day and will be certain to keep it in mind for parties in the future!!!

Formerly Schmiemeir's Bakery (founded by my old college pal Roy, now retired, and operated until a few years ago by his family).  Haven't been there under the new ownership, but if it's as good as under the Schmiemeirs, I'm sure it's very good.

Went here before seeing a show at the Santa Barbara Bowl. Service was great, with a decent selection of seafood. There is was nothing special about the seafood other than being difficult to eat. We got a medium seafood sampler which had rock crab (recommend by our server), but like the name, it was hard as a rock and hard to eat with little meat. not worth it!! Also, the oysters and clams could have been clean better. fresh doesn't need the sand with.

The highlight was the churizo and clams. Hearty and unique.

I go to this place for breakfast almost every Sunday. It is unbelievable the amount of food you get for such a cheap price. And it is absolutely the best breakfast I have ever had, hands-down. The staff is amazing, you will get the small town vibe here. The cream chipped beef and scrapple are to die for.

Les Bon Temps had an appealing menu, and the food was pretty good. In the beginning, I hated it (the menu, the chef...), but they really started to come around when they replaced the leader in the kitchen. And just as they were starting to get good, now they're closing! I'm sorry, I mean CLOSED...

 The owner (Howard Taylor, also of Carmine's Creole Cafe) sold the retaurant to a chef from the Borgata who will now turn it into an Italian place. Good for him. Too bad for the staff who apparently were given less than one day's notice, including the chef who JUST got there a month ago. They knew yesterday that the restaurant was being sold, but not when.  In near-Brasserie-Perrier-fashion, they were told four hours before doors closed that the deal went down. I think they got a better deal than BP staff, though. Oh, well. Anybody been to Cafe Nola lately?

This place is so tasty I'm salivating writing this and thinking about my last meal there.  Standard Steven Star portions...overflowing plates of goodness that are easy to share b/w two people and great for bigger parties.  You will leave with a full stomach and a doggie bag or two so don't plan on going dancing afterwards.  It's a tad noisy (specially at the communal table in the middle of the place) so if you wanna propose or breakup with your sweetheart, chose another locay.  Try, do try, to save room for dessert as they should not be overlooked here.
I've lived in Tn and lived in Williamson county for 28 years and never even heard of them until we passed it.

Chipotle is Bae. However, the long lines for this place is ridiculous! I have seen more efficient staff in other chipotle's, and they are so stingy with their guacamole. But chipotle is bae. So there really isn't much else to say, whatever qualms I have with this place will deter me little from getting a dank burrito.
The food was very good. The service was outstanding. Danny and Skyler ensures we had the best possible night and we did. Come here and you won't regret it
Great tasting food with a very affordable price. As a Peruvian myself i highly recommend meanchi's
Charbroiled oysters here were WAY better than the ones we had at Drago's yesterday. Plump and delicious.

We had an outstanding dinner at Rebirth. I really enjoyed my Red Snapper special. It was perfectly prepared and delicious. Our outstanding server, Mary was friendly and fast. She was knowledgeable about the menu and made excellent suggestions.  Rebirth also has a full bar and impressive wine list.  Their gumbo is also excellent. Highly recommend.

Came in for the first time tonight, just driving by. Staff were very nice and food was delicious! I would highly recommend this restaurant and am very much looking forward to going back in the near future!

We ordered the boiled 3lbs rock crab for 25 bucks and lobster tacos for 19 bucks. Foods amazing and the service was good. It was busy and packs, we was on the long line before get sit to the table. Love it, will come back again when i visit SB.

Everything is fresh and from scratch. Maybe not the best food you've ever had, but absolutely the best you've had in White House. Service is fantastic. We walked right in, but the line was out the door on our way out. So get there early, because the secret is out!

I recently went to Nonna Giovanna's with my wife for dinner. Let me tell you that I made reservations for a table for 2 at 6pm on Friday 4 days earlier. When we arrived at about 6:05 our table was not even ready yet. So we waited for about 10 minutes at the door looking like fools. Finally we were seated. Our table was not very clean and it was also soaked in water and soap. Since it is byob we brought our own bottle of wine which by the way we had to open ourselves. After about 7 or 8 minutes our waitress finally arrived I believe her name was Emily. She was somewhat nice but was not focused and on task. So we placed our order and then waited about 20 minutes for our food which we got and the person who brought our food was not even our waitress. I ordered pizza and it had to be the worst pizza I ever had. It was Dougie and cold. The old lady who was the owner kept coming over to the table and nagging us she had to come over about 5 or 6 times. Asking if we were ok. Overall they can not keep up with the dinner rush.

Our go-to dinner and lunch place in south Tampa. Despite occasional minor issues, always concerned with resolution, (i.e. didn't like entree, misunderstood something on menu, happy to replace or take off)
The atmosphere is fun and breezy, people dress nicely (unlike some overly casual places nearby, ahem)
Interesting versatile menu.

If you have one menu item, it better be amazing. Well the chicken tenders are nothing to write home about. On top of that, it is overpriced and the portions are very small. Just when you think it can't get worse, they don't have dipping sauces like ranch or buffalo sauce. What?????? 

I'll be going to the Chick-Fil-A next door.

This place is not what it once was. The atmosphere inside is all anime, which is amazing but not what it used to be. The bobas lack flavor or made incorrectly than before. & EVERY TIME and I mean every damn time I go in and get a milkshake I have the shits and pukes that night and regret it. It's like they don't properly wash their milkshake machine or milk is constantly bad. Get the same ice cream regular, no problem, once it's a milkshake it's a stomach sore about 6 hours later. Kept going back for the bobas and now they are unenjoyable.

This is the BEST Chinese I have ever had!!! The vegetables are always fresh, the meats are not fatty and not over breaded! The quality is better than some fancy options out there. The ladies who greet and serve you are sweet, fast and the food always comes out steaming hot! My husband and I make this a stop at least every other week. Addicted!

Food is great. I could definitely do without the cook yelling at the high schoolers all day. The older woman at the counter kept interrupting me while I was giving her my order. 45 min wait in line and then another 30 is what you should expect here for breakfast if you don't get there early.

Food was extremely good. Service was great. Server was super friendly and knowledgeable!

So why 3 stars?

My wife and I had the hummus with lamb appetizer and then we both got our own dinner plates.

Bill was $65. 

I had to stop for tacos on the way home because I was still famished. As good as it was the portions were so small that we would have needed to order four dinners to be satisfied. 

Please increase your portion size or at least advertise them as small plates on the menu so we know what we're getting into.

Disclaimer: I only eat 1800 cals a day. Not asking for much.

I ordered pizza and mozzarella sticks for delivery while in a downtown Wilmington hotel.  Ordering process was great, the staff was polite and warned me that it would take 45 minutes to get my order.  The food arrived in only 30 minutes and the delivery driver was even more pleasant than the guy on the phone.  Food was hot, very good and exactly what I wanted.  Overall, a great choice.

Visiting from WA and this place was great!! My wife had the rosemary chicken formaggio, I had the steamed clams and seafood fettuccini. The chicken Formaggio was amazing for both our tastebuds. The steamed clams were also great! They had a lot of garlic with a spicy style broth, it was so good we would dip our bread in it. The seafood fettuccini was pretty good. A healthy amount of seafood, clams, lobster, shrimp, and scallops. The fettuccini was the only down side just due to the fact I like my Alfredo sauce to be a little more thick then runny. All in all it was great!
Good quick and healthy meal on those days when you don't want to cook normally get take generally prettyfast

This place just opened up in the former Route 6.  Have now been three times in about a week and a half.  Space is very open and they have two rooms essentially - the main dining and bar and then a separate enclosed jazz lounge (full dining).  I've had drinks, full dinner, and happy hour - and all have been awesome.  

The food is blowing my mind.  I was skeptical of southern / New Orleans type cuisine as its not my favorite but this is a modern twist - everything has just a hint of the south.  Everything tastes rich but is not over sauced or covered in cream.

The scallop crudo is awesome - slightly smoked and comes with some chilis and avocado.

The crawfish fritters are exactly as they sound - amazing.

The gnocchi is a cornmeal take on it with a soft egg and some bitter greens - really tasty.  

The fired oysters are one of favorite things so far.  They are smaller in size than the typical one - perhaps this is why they are so darn tender.  

The best dish I've had so far is the corn soup.  It's a massive bowl and comes with two blue crab beignets.  This dish is rich without being too creamy or heavy.  

And don't forget the bread. You get corn muffins and bacon biscuits with sweet cream butter.  So awesome.

They have a solid beer and wine list (seem to be figuring this out as they go along) and they have a lot of bourbon based cocktails.  

Happy hour is 4-6 and you get $2 off beer, $5 glasses of white or red wine and a deal on the cocktails but I don't exactly remember.

Haven't stayed for jazz but my neighbors did and liked it.  

Check it out!

New location open just a few doors down from the original location. The cafe inside has authentic food - if you like spicy food, this is it! Good selection of interesting international grocery items. Love it.
Got take out a couple weeks ago and it was very tasty.   I got the garlic shrimp...good sized shrimp in a garlic sauce with veggies and white rice.   We also enjoyed the veggie spring rolls.
Food was ok but was not worth the price! Trying to be a five star restaurant but not living up to the hype! Really dish towels for napkins that leave residue on your clothing!

Great Taiwanese food. It's similar to Chinese but has far less sugar. I've been to Taiwan and the food at 101 is authentic. Try a mixture of different dishes and share them with other members at your table, Taiwanese-style.

We absolutely loved this place. All the food was really good. The staff was extremely friendly and attentive. If your in the area this is a must try. We will be coming here every time we come to reno. Great server,great food and drinks. Very clean. 5 stars from us. Wish this place was in sacramento so we could go more often

My girlfriend and I went here to celebrate our anniversary and it was wonderful! They food was beyond delicious, after 4 courses we were stuffed! Beyond that the staff was just incredible. Our waiter Stephan was incredible, he made the experience so much more amazing, definitely great at what he does. I was really happy that everyone we encountered was LGBT+ friendly and didn't even second guess that we were on a date to celebrate a special night (this is rarely the case when we go out we usually get sisters or roommates...) all around very impressed and cannot wait to go back! Thank you for a fabulous experience!

I don't think I've eaten food this bad in my entire life. Pizza is like card board and I couldn't have made a worst tasting salad if I tried. And the worst part is their prices are outrageous. How they lasted this long is beyond me. Many people are echoing exact same sentiments. It will be closed down in less than a year. No doubt.
Decent asian food! Not too expensive. Menu has all the traditional items.... Give it a try! We are glad we did!

Royal China was recommended to me by a co-worker.  I'm not usually a big fan of Chinese, but I wanted something different.

The inside is very nice - not fancy schmancy, but warm and inviting.  

Our server was very nice and friendly and was kind enough to offer that sharing one large bowl of the best won-ton soup I've ever had was a much better deal than buying two small bowls.

We had spring rolls, which though perfectly fine, were pretty run-of-the-mill.

We also had cashew chicken and I'm giving it mixed reviews.  Thumbs way up for very fresh veggies (which were not overcooked), and for a nice-sized portion.  Thumbs down for lack of flavoring and so few cashews.  It also came with a very small bowl of rice.  We had to ask for more rice, but they were very accommodating and didn't not nickel and dime us on that one.

It was a tad expensive, but not outrageous for getting fresh food, nice environment, great service and did I mention the fantastic wonton soup???  Overall, it was a great experience.  I absolutely will go back and will try something different next time.  

Due to small signage, the building itself, even though it is on Vets, was difficult for to me find and.  At first, I mistakenly went across Vets to the China Buffet place.  I had to call Royal China for help.

This place is pretty pricey for the experience I had. First, it's seriously understaffed. Thursday night the place was packed for dinner and they only had two servers. This caused our server to forget about us. I had to end up getting my own fork cause she was taking so long. Secondly, my meal sucked. I ordered the Greek lamb chops and it was incredibly fatty. I ended up having to cut away most of it leaving me not much to eat. The potatoes were the only decent part of this whole experience.

The food and service was good like always. Compared to other steakhouses, Capital Grille food quality does not match the price. While still good, the food does not leave you amazed like other top steak houses in the city. If you haven't been, definitely need to give them a try. Now if this is your third visit, I highly suggest trying the other top rated steakhouses in the city.

They  made us wait for 2 hours. we kept asking every 15 min and they would say it's nearly ready. they took 1 hour to give us a table. once we got inside we saw that there were many tables but they were mismanaging the seating. they didn't know how to prioritize between those who placed a takeout and those who were waiting as it was quite unfair. The communication was lacking. overall a terrible experience

I agree with an earlier reviewer in saying that I much preferred the sides to the BBQ itself. Where as the brisket and burnt ends I had were certainly serviceable, Holy Hog's sides were a treat. In particular, I enjoyed the jalapeno mac and cheese, as well as the Brunswick stew. They had a nice complement of tasty sauces, including a mustard-base.

Seating here is all outdoor, so beware inclement weather. We did really enjoy eating at the bar, which had a good representation of local/craft beers on tap.

Caramelized onions, chicken, and cheese sounds simple, but with the pink aoili...wow. Everything was cooked perfectly and the corn cakes weren't dry. Worth the price and the drive, although the neighborhood made me nervous about parking.

Another chicken joint with TASTELESS chicken! People not to stop with the nonsense and saying this is great chicken or that this is the best blah blah blah! Huge difference between TASTELESS and just plain old BURNING YOUR TONGUE HOT! Why in the world would anyone want to pay for burning on your tongue spicy food over taste , beats me! It should be a combination of both!!!!!! For that , stay home fry yourself some chicken and add the spiciest hottest sauce you can find at your local supermarket ‍ . Let me also add that the fries aren't up to par.

Went here for a quick dinner and We ordered full rack of ribs and a 20oz. Bone inn New York steak, that was pretty good. With Cesar salad that they forgot to put sauce in it, a full load bake potatoes, and broccoli on the side.  The only thing that is wrong is they put too much onion butter on top of my steak. The appetizers that I ordered needs more dips sauce  instead of bread. The Oil and vinaigrette needs to be more authentic. That I don't  like the taste of it. But overall the steak and ribs are perfectly cooked. That was great.
This used to be my favorite sushi place to go to.  Ownership has definitely changed, the menu is different, the service is horrible and the food is sub par.  Don't waste your time.

Fuel is the perfect lunch spot! Healthy, hearty, and delicious. Everything on the menu is under 500 calories and I don't know how they do it. The panini's are very filling and most come topped with gooey melty cheese. Great smoothies as well, whether your looking for a protein boost, more energy, or just a healthy snack.They usally offer $10 for $20 deals so be sure to buy one before going with a friend! Staff is always friendly and you don't usually have to wait too long for your food. I see myself becoming a regular here. topped

Having tried bbq from all over the United states, even the world...this place left me speechless. Btw, I've got this app just for this place. Dont miss an opportunity to have you tastebuds exitedly pleasured.TRY THE MAC N CHEESE!

Been there ones the food was good specially the curly fries  those are amazing. I went during my lunch break,The service was fast staff was friendly, I have no complaints I do have to say the sandwich looked bigger in the picture than what they actually are, but I believe that for every fast food restaurant .

My sister and I went there today to grab coffee and go but the atmosphere was so charming we decided to grab a bite and stay. The lady who was helping us was really friendly and their cruffin and mocha latte were equally amazing. Will definitely be going back

I love this place!! They make the perfect, most beautiful cakes. They are absolutely delicious! Their pink champagne, red velvet, and chocolate strawberry cakes were a huge hit at my daughter's birthday party. I can't forget about their yummy baked goods either. They are do good, I'm willing to drive from Twin Peaks and Silverbell just to have them. The staff is very friendly, hardworking, and willing to do all they can to help. Anyone who would have an issue with them or their service is just ludicrous.

Gravy fries and Yuengling, a more perfect Philly pair doesn't exist. There are gravy fries and then there are these; not  soggy fries and gravy with a few meat flecks but sturdy, crispy  fries completely covered by a beef blanket. The famous roast beef had a robust meaty flavor and did not let us down. I'd probably add cheese next time to make it even better/ less kosher.

The other thing to get is the roast beef sandwich (the combo, meaning with cheese). The same slowly cooked, moist beef is sliced into a thick sandwich. Another fine way to enjoy the namesake product.  And in case you care about their weight of your meal, this sandwich contains 1/4 pound of meat. Horseradish is ready for you on the side.

Nick's has been around since 1938 and they obviously know what they are doing.

Ordered takeout because I previously had food from here with a friend and it was good. Ordered pad kee mow, fried rice and pad Thai. The pad kee mow was absolutely disgusting. The noodles were soggy and way overcooked without any flavor and the chicken was not cooked properly. Pad Thai was overly sweet. Fried rice was okay. Will not be ordering from here again. Never had bad Thai food until I ordered from here. Called them and they had nothing to say and were unapologetic. Absolutely ridiculous.

I feel bad doing this because of the praise heaped on this place, but in a way that is part of the dissatisfaction here.

First, the food.  Had the fluke crudo first.  I grew up down the shore, ate a ton of flounder and this is the first time I've had it raw.  Not a particularly notable fish, but I was interested to try.  The fish itself was barely distinguishable from everything else surrounding.  Flavors didn't play well at all and the whole thing was bitterly acidic to me.  Beautiful yes, but so are flowers and I don't want to eat a flower.

Had the poulard (chicken) as a main course and again, flavors didn't play well and nothing stood out for me.  Have had better meals elsewhere int he city for far less.

This leads to my main beef with this place, and something you may be thinking after reading my admittedly amateur review here.  I felt out of place here.  Like people were looking down on me, including the staff.  Now I've eaten at some of the best restaurants in Philly and a few elsewhere and have never felt this way before.  I know how to dress and eat properly, but Mica seemed to be filled with old-money geriatrics who didn't want a young man such as myself dining next to them, picking apart the crown jewel of beautiful Chestnut Hill.  Never felt comfortable.

I felt the same about the food here as I did at Ela so if you like/dislike that this will probably follow suit, although Ela was much more welcoming for me.  Visually it's great, but call me old fashioned but I like to enjoy my food, not feel uppity because I'm there.

Chicken wings are good but ............
 I want equal amounts of drumlets to the other pieces.
I don't want what ever you happen to dump out of the frozen bag.
Think about it! 
 Put the same amount of each.
Im sick of 9 drumlets and 3 of the other.
It can't be that hard.
 Get it together or loose a customer.

Food is okay but I'm not sure if it makes up for slow service (takes 25 minutes for one meal, than another 25 minutes after the first one comes for the other persons meal), loud atmosphere (can't hear the person next to you) and absolutely no phone service (wasn't even getting LTE).

I came here once to meet up with some friends once and just like Bill M. Says its like a college party. Every one there was wearing nice sweaters and fancy shoes and drinking PBR as if they were trying to make their best attempt to be hipsters.

The Shrimp and Grits are STILL to die for! I timed my trip back to Chicago so that I wouldn't miss this gem.

If you have to choose something to try I recommend the Shrimp and Grits and a stint at the oyster bar, hands-down.

The only gripe is about their to-go food packaging. Shrimp and Grits out of a "dish" deep enough to hold two CHICAGO style pizza slices is not appropriate for the golden Grits dish (smile). Management please get us lovers of all things Grub some decent bowls to-go.

We ordered take out on the first day they opened. The place was very clean, the fish was fresh and the service was very friendly and polite.

The food was mostly bland though. I got a custom bowl with their noodles, a scoop of tuna and a scoop of yellowtail with their "spicy" sauce. The taste just wasn't there. Same thing with most toppings. The only redeeming things in the plate were the raw jalapeno slices.

I really wanted to like this place and become a regular, but I wasn't blown away. Pure Poke will remain an economic alternative to the slightly pricier Chriashi bowl at other sushi restaurants.

I work down the street from Basil Leaf so we'll order take out from them every now and then.

This is a pretty typical Thai restaurant. It's certainly not going to blow you away, but it hits the spot when you have a Thai craving. I've had the pad thai and the curries and both are pretty average. When you take out for lunch they give you an egg roll with your meal. It's a nice little surprise :) And I like how they pack the food in actual plastic containers rather than Styrofoam or tin containers that can get messy and hard to handle.

I've only actually eaten inside here once, but it was nice. I'm actually really impressed with the transformation they did to this place (it used to be an Irish pub). They really have given it a lot of character with some classy decor. The service is also pretty average.

If you're on the beach and have a serious urge for Thai I'd say give this place a try. (There's also Nori Thai, but I've never been there.) Otherwise, if you can wait another 15 minutes, take a drive downtown and stop at one of the many Thai places there.

Wonderful ambiance and terrific service! Maggie made my experience at the newly renovated restaurant easy and fun. This is my favorite Asian restaurant. Same owners as Sakura, with the same authentic Asian flavors I've come to love.

First time here and loved it. I ordered the aloha chicken sandwich, and was not disappointed. The chicken was well seasoned and not over cooked, the green Chile added a nice touch( I'm a sucker for green Chiles though), and the jack cheese was melted and yummy. The service was great, and she even came out to check if I liked it ( I told her it was my first time there). The store was nice and clean and had a chill surfer vibe to it. Overall an enjoyable experience, I will definitely come back again.

Best BBQ I've had in a long time!!  Thanks for catering the HCA family picnic.  Can't wait to come in and sit and have a meal and see you all again.
I have to tell everyone to come and eat!!
New place from owners of Holden's in the old pastovino space. Decent happy hours. 3 food choices. Nachos, sliders, wings. - good prices
The food isn't bad, but we order almost every week from work, and they have yet to get my order correct, despite the fact that we send the printed order via fax.

So disappointed in the way I was treated by the older gentleman. I've been a customer for over a year with time off for cancer treatment. I believe in supporting local businesses and tried to pick up my order. I could not understand what he was saying behind his mask. I asked him to repeat and for some reason he stomped off into the back room. Ignorant behavior and a lost customer.

I ordered a Whopper and a value french fries. . HOW DIFFICULT IS THAT? A WHOPPER AND FRIES! I got my order and there were NO FRIES Give me a break! Maybe the girl who served me should take the black rag off her head and pay more attention to her JOB. This will probably be the last time I buy from this BK.

Also - there were only 3 cars ahead of me in line. Car #1 took 3 minutes to order and 5 minutes to fill the order. I saw only 1 bag of food passed from the window to the driver. What could possibly take so long? I was in  line for 10 minutes.

I am suprised that yelp has given Modo Mio $$$, because if anything, this place is very affordable for the size, creativity and elegance this restaurant offers. $33 for a tasting menu is incredibly affordable, and you get to try dishes that are different and delicious. 5 stars for sure.

SOOOOO GOOOD! First, the staff is so incredibly nice and accommodating. They gave us great recommendations because is was our first time. We got the beef and steak bahn mi, which were both great. We also got the Cajun crack fries-- AMAZING!  Def will ve back soon.

WOOOOOOOOOOOOOOWWW first time eating in a Mexican restaurant and I'm glad it was here, I'm from Miami/venezuela and their food reminds me back home miami and Venezuela I was very happy for the SIZE and AMPUNT of food I was served, I work on a 5 stars dining restaurant in New Orleans as a lead cook and I was very But VERY happy for everything I had on my table DEFINITIVAMENTE COMING BACK TO THIS PLACE AND WITH A LOT MORE PEOPLE ! keep the hard freaking work!!  I LOVE IT

RJ and I have been here several times since our first visit. I either get the shrimp or fish tacos, and he gets either the fish tacos or the turkey sliders.  I really want to try something new but the tacos are just so good!  Love Rum Punch is fantastic, and we enjoy the popcorn as well.  I plan to try something different next time! Cromwell's is a consistent 4 each time!!

I just moved into the area and have been looking new places to go with good coffee. A friend turned me onto La Colombe. The coffee is great! Better yet the staff are very friendly and talkative ( not used to that). Now I'm in there so much, they already have my drink ready. Sweet! Thanks to te people of La Colombe

I came here and got the baked cheese (Provoletta Parillera), Reno's Parilla, and a Milhoja for dessert. The beer and wine was so standard issue that it's unmentionable, however a personal tea-light fueled grill to keep your meats hot is worth a mention. I also sprung for an extra- the Morcilla (blood sausage) so darn tasty, and of perfect consistency. The baked cheese, tasted like hot delicious cheese flavored bubble gum, and  the charred external portions of all the meats and the Chimichurri sauce complimented them all wonderfully. I loved that all the meat didn't all taste the same, and the cuts weren't too fatty (a little fat while cooking on that small grill is great) The coconut macaroon and empanadas looked attractive, since they have a meat shop, bakery, and wine shop all included in the same space. I only gave three stars because being blitzed with greasy meats, I really needed a great side to hold it all up- a vehicle if you will. I did choose two sides, the spinach (awesome, but with huge onion chunks) and the potato salad, which did not even exist to me and wasn't worth the stomach space. So I basically had a grill feast heaping with meat, and nothing to accompany it with. TOO MUCH MEAT! (says no girl, evar) I'll be back for a fried egg dish next time. I really liked that they spoke Spanish to us as soon as we walked in as well!

Hands down awesome bar! Most notable is the very unique atmosphere and decor! I liked the vibe.  I wasn't able to try the food this time as we got there pretty late on a Sunday...but I definitely plan on coming back to try it! 

The draft beer was a good and the bartenders were very friendly. HUGE deck out back. 

I know this place is new but it's definitely packed with potential and I will be back. Glad to see a such a unique addition in East Nashville!

I stopped in at the spur of the moment after an appt I had .  Audrey greeted EVERY single customer by their first name when they entered.  She personified customer service!  As others stated, I was given a cup of soda while I was waiting for my take out.  The wonton soup was PACKED with wontons. These are good people that own this business!  They restore faith in locally owned merchants.  I happened to meet Franco who was the contractor who did their remodeling work who stopped by, which was very classy; I plan on returning with my husband for the Friday Night buffet.  I even liked their takeout containers. No metal handle to spark in the microwave.  Audrey made everyone feel like they were welcome and at home.

Went here for dinner and got the Shakshuka. It was very spicy but very good. Very good service and it's BYOB. Definitely want to check it out for brunch one day but I know it's crazy at those times. Come for dinner and you'll be pleasantly surprised

Friends who are frequent visitors to New Orleans suggested Bayona to us, as we had one night for a great NOLA dining experience. I will need to send them flowers, or at least hand-written thank you notes, for the recommendations. What a wonderful experience: classy, delicious, exquisite!

We arrived early for a 6:30 p.m. reservation and elected to sit outside (one word of warning: if you sit outside, wear some bug spray on at least your feet -- some evil insect devoured my husband's feet, leaving ugly bites and distracting him through the whole dinner!). I figured the courtyard would be lovely and picturesque, and it was, with banana trees, beautiful foliage, lovely tables and charming views everywhere one looked. As usual in New Orleans, the service was attentive, professional, never overwhelming and gracious, always making us feel like they were happy we were there and wanted us to love every minute of the dinner.

I started off with a glass of champagne, which was the perfect cocktail for a warmish NOLA spring evening.

We had reviewed the online menu, which is separated into the menu items of Bayona fame as well as daily/weekly specials to reflect seasonal offerings. We ordered:
Chicken, andouille soup
Crispy smoked quail salad (OMG! I want some right now!)
Duck breast with duck confit crepe
Panko-crusted salmon with choucroute (saurkraut) and Gewurtztraminer sauce
Mango-cheesecake flan

We will definitely return to Bayona and I unreservedly recommend it to anyone looking for a special -- an unforgettable -- meal in New Orleans.

First let me preface this with our original intent.  Our intent was to eat next door at Riverstone Café.  I had called up a few hours prior to make a reservation for 8 for an early dinner (4pm).  It was my father in-law's birthday and we couldn't find many places to server at such an early time.  The happily took my reservation with no issues.  When we showed up, they stated there was  a private party and we had to go next door to "doc watsons".  We were a little pissed that nobody failed to mention this to us. But, away we went to the sports bar next door. We walked in and instinct should have told us to leave. But we were on a time crunch so we stayed.  The place was dead, 2 patrons at the bar and our table of 8.  Waitress took our orders and was quite slow to bring out our drinks.  After not coming over to update us at all we sat for a long time waiting for our food.  Finally, after just about an hour they brought it out.  However, they  didn't bring out a dish that my mother ordreded.  Waitress said it would be just a minute.  Ok, that's normal.  10 minutes go by and no food or update.  Finally she comes out and says it will be 6 minutes.  6 more minutes ???  that would make it 16 minutes after the rest of us got food. WTF ??  Turns out she forgot to put in the order.  Now, if this was a crowded restaurant or a Friday/Saturday night, I might understand.  But when it is your only table in the restaurant, how can that happen.  How can the service be so slow ?  Sure, they comped us the one dinner, but nobody seemed that apologetic.  I had the short ribs, which weren't bad, but when I got home, I felt like I was going to vomit.  Something wasn't right in that food.  I never get upset stomachs or indigestion or anything.  I would never go back to this place even for a free meal.  AVOID at all costs.  I would either go to Asian place Z Wei, the pour house or hell, you're bound to have a better experience at McDonalds.
One of my favorite pizza places in Philly and NYC. 5 stars for food and the service has always been great.

I like to eat outside.  
Unfortunately, I live somewhere (New England) that really doesn't support this habit four to five months out of every year.  Try as I might (and I have an outdoor firepit) I'm bound to the indoors and the conventional table and chair/couch balance dining. Boring!

Naturally, the first thing I want when I get to New Orleans is food; and gobdangit, I want it outside.  My friend M and I are shopping a bit around the FQ (it's her first visit) and I asked a lovely young shopkeep in Faulkner House Books where we should go, keeping in mind that I need to enjoy my food without the confines of four walls and a roof.  She suggested Green Goddess and I agreed, toting M happily off to Exchange Alley.

We arrived early, but already almost all the tables outside were full of happy diners.  I said *almost*.  We got one.  Probably because I *almost* flung myself across it in my excitement.

Our waitperson was wonderful, offering excellent suggestions of the menu items which I will highlight below:

Sweet Potato Biscuits with Orange Honey Butter-Amazeballs. Seriously.  We received three light and flaky biscuits the color of sherbet accompanied by a sweet butter drizzled with orange honey.  There was only myself and M dining, but she graciously offered the extra biscuit to me.  I went to split it and felt absolute agony (sort of like when King Solomon told those two broads to cut the baby in half?  It's in the Bible, folks and it is CRAZY) so thankfully she spared me that. 

Vegetable Platter:  Isn't it amazing when you receive something so simply prepared that you realize how much you love that item?  This platter did so little to the vegetables on it, that it really made them sing.  Simple, sweet heirloom tomatoes (yellow) were flecked with sea salt, as were thinly sliced radishes.  Roasted fingerling potatoes and asparagus benefitted from light dips into Romesco and Garlic Aioli.  The only item on the plate that didn't blow my skirt up were the hearts of palm, but that's just because I'm not a fan.

Roasted Vegetable Salad: Vegetables, mixed greens, Goat Cheese and spicy little pumpkin seeds...
Q. What's not to love?
A. Nothing.

I drank a couple of Bayou Teche beers and had some Chicory coffee (all outside!), went to the bathroom (very clean.  *inside* in case you were wondering).  And left with nothing but good vibes for the Green Goddess.

Love the freshness of the food here.  I wish they would either make the portions of the black beans with the jerk Salmon a bit larger to accommodate the large price.  6 ounces for 8 bucks is a bit steep.  

Great food and service.

Really amazing food, but go hungry. 

I strongly recommend the sweet onion crepe, which is truly amazing. It melts in your mouth and fully caramelized. The explosion of flavors was simply impressive. The dish has been on for over 100 years. Love the history too. 

My second favorite would probably be one of the pasta dishes, the garlic capellini with sweet Maine shrimp. Great mix of flavors, both savory and sweet. The shrimp is sooo good.

All of the pasta dishes are quite astounding. I like the wild boar pasta too. Almond tortellini and spinach gnocchi are both okay, but not up to my expectations. I think they are a little bit oily actually.

Service was so perfect too. There are lots of olives and bread going around. When I got too full and asked them to stop, they packed my desserts for me. I was very happy with the place and hope to come back soon.

this is my first stay in Philadelphia and it has been a good one. Like other reviewers, the parking is hard to find or easily miss, had to drive around twice to find it. When I go to the front desk I was given my room and when I went to go check it out, the room was not ready yet, I returned to the desk and met a very nice employee named Ducky, who I think looks like Olivia Munn, made corrections and made my stay a great experience when I finally arrived in my Junior suite. On the 7th Floor, there is a 3.5-4 ft standing pool with a hot tub adjacent to a gym. On the 10th floor there is a restaurant called 10th floor grill which has a terrific view of downtown.

We were looking for a place to take the kids to play some arcade games, have a few beers, and pizza. We showed up on a Friday evening at 8:25 and they were closed...Wow..I was very surprised to see they weren't open. It's a Friday night and perfect (if you can find it) for a family dinner with young kids.  Whoever decided to open this restaurant better prepare for failure. This is poorly located, poorly advertised, looks closed every time you pass by it, and obviously poorly managed.   Will never know how the food is, but can tell you Fortell's is very good:)

Amazing food and a great Reno eats gem!

Always wanting to try somewhere new, the family and I decided to dine in at Fat Cat Bar & Grill on a nice Friday night while in town. We arrived mid evening to a mostly quiet restaurant, so we pretty had pickings of where we wanted to sit. Since the outdoor dinning was completely open in the back patio area, we decided to sit out there and enjoy the night. After looking over the menu and talking to the waitress I realized Fat Cat is a very, "Farm to Fork" style restaurant like it is where I'm from in Sacramento. Hand crafted burgers, 100% organic, grass-fed beef from a local ranch, turkey and beyond meat patties, fresh greens for burgers on request, gluten free buns, local beer options. This is what you can expect from their overall menu which I like.

My girlfriend and I ordered drinks for ourselves, her the Frisky Kitty and I got an American Mule. And we all shared the Mac & Cheese which was delicious. It's their version of the classic with Parmesan and white aged cheddar, topped with Parmesan and panko bread crumbs. So it was both gooey from the warm fresh cheese, and crunch when eaten with the top layer of panko bread crumbs. My youngest loved it so much he ate most of it. For our actual meals the boys each got the kids cheese burger and kids chicken tenders meals which were well sized portions. And I had the Cowboy burger which comes with sweet-smoky hickory BBQ sauce, bacon, a jumbo onion ring and melted cheddar. It's definitely one of your "knife" burgers as you'd have to unhinge your jaw to eat it without cutting it in half first, lol.

Overall we had a wonderful night here, the back patio was really nice as the sun went down and the lighting came one. The service was awesome and the food for great...I'd definitely come back here when in town.

Solid 4 stars! The waitstaff isn't the most glamorous or overly friendly, but certainly get the job done. The buffet is huge and you shouldn't ever leave here hungry, or broke. The prices are great, especially for great Japanese food. Informal dining and lots of room for everyone.

I really enjoy this spot baby
I'm jacked now 
Great park across the way
Staffers are super friendly...

I just cane again to get the drip coffee with free refill and of course 3 credit cards I tried were declined....it was truly embarrassing and yet a tall blonde lady was patient and allowed me to save dignity by giving me a cup of coffee! No charge and I hid in a corner to use my phone apps to check balances....of course I was at fault....I had made a payment on time earlier in the week which had not cleared...long story short....I went to pay and a red haired barista chatted me up and these guys are so nice....he asked me about my work and was interested.....they allowed me to save face! 
I truly love this place. 
2.75 for two great coffees' 
Nice park and quiet location! 
Ty vm! 
N
Great coffee, and great people! I ordered a cold brew and lets just say it puts starbucks to shame, this is the real deal.
I was refused service 10 minutes prior to closing time. Just lazy I guess. So when this place closes at midnight on a Friday I guess it means that's when the employees get to go home.

Very romantic restaurant with the exceptional service and great food! 
They have indoor and outdoor sittings, outdoor fireplace and beautiful garden. I've been there about 5 times and it was always great experience!

Absolutely awful experience! There are maybe 100 places to sit and 300 people in the place. I understand it is busy, but we waited in line for a beer for 20 minutes upstairs and none of the 3 people behind the bar were helping anyone for the 20 minutes we waited. We decided to go downstairs to try our luck, after a 10 minute wait we finally got attitude from a bartender who brought us 2 of our 3 beers. We asked for the third, assuming she may have forgotten, she snapped back with "yea I heard you the first time". We expect to be treated politely as we are always polite to workers in an industry we have all worked in. Other people next to us at the bar had similar stories of waiting 30+ minutes to be served and were also shocked by the attitude the staff had. The beer/food must be excellent otherwise this place would be empty, but if I was the manager I would actively be looking for a new staff. A few extra chairs or benches wouldn't hurt this place either I'm sure. Maybe we ran into some lazy staff on an unexpectedly busy hour, I don't know.
