I went into this location while on vacation in the area as I remembered McKenzies/ Taystee as a child. I had several donuts, a breakfast burrito, and a coffee. The donuts were as good as I remembered, but I had to wait nearly 30 mins for the burrito. 

As often the case in and around the city of New Orleans, the service and customer service were horrible. The lady working the front was rude at best and lacked communication. I stood there as people came in and place their orders and leave before me and when I asked her about it I was rudely told that some of them placed their orders online or by phone. Still, the this was not the case for (all). 

Nonetheless, If I was told that the burrito would've taken as long as it did. I would've been prepared, but to be greeted that way and treated with such disrespect, and the lack of communication and wait for a cold burrito with no explanation or apology was not okay and I will not be returning to this location.

I saw the reviews for this place and decided to check it out. There aren't too many diners in Delaware anymore and the ones that are around aren't that great.

As I was walking in, I noticed an employee helping an elderly man out the door. I was seated in a booth and ordered a glass of skim milk and their "Lucky's Breakfast" (2 eggs, home fries, bacon and a homemade biscuit. I substituted the bacon for some scrapple.) As I waited for my order I took out my point and shoot camera to snap some pictures; my phone's battery died.

The scrambled eggs were fluffy, the home fries were good, the biscuit had some cinnamon/sugar sprinkled on it, the scrapple was a nice thick cut and had a nice crisp outer layer. The only thing I have negative to say about this place is that there was something black floating around in my milk (picture included.) Although I don't come to Concord Pike that often it is nice to find a place that serves breakfast all day.

Went there for the first time tonight on New Years Eve drawn in by a bluegrass band playing from 6 -9. The place was very crowded with lots of families and little ones running around- picnic table seating mostly. You order food and drinks at the counter.  It's a free for all and we were glad to find a 2 seater near the band in the midst of the chaos.  But literally moments  after bringing to our table our first  drinks (not an easy task), a staff guy came over and told us we needed to go up and get in line for food immediately or  "we will have to swap you out." We told him we did intend to order food but just wanted to have a first drink and sit for a bit but he looked unhappy with that.   We would have stayed  longer to hear the music and ordered more drinks but I  complied and went up to wait in long line for food as  insisted and missed most of the set and after that decided to beat it.. Will likely never go back.  Maybe it was because it was New  Years Eve but it was quite bizarre.

How in the world does this place get 5 stars?  And we ordered food tonight because of a Yelp referral. Awful!  Have had Thai from many different restaurants in many different cities. And this place is across the street!! We ordered dumplings which we are certain were frozen. And very spicy. Then, 2 orders of  Panang chicken. My hubby likes medium. I have to have mild. They were both terrible. Spicy and the veggies were sparse. The curry sauce is very thin. It comes w/barely enough rice for the dish. The entire experience was really bad. I barely ate. This is definitely our 2nd time there. First and last. Ugh......

This New Hope nightspot has an impressive, somewhat classic exterior, and a large outdoor patio. It's one of the larger venues in the neighborhood. I have friends who meet up here - there's usually a crowd, and how - to listen to musical performances held here. Parking can be a pain, but that's New Hope in general. I ate at Havana once for dinner with family, but it was such a long ago I don't remember what I ate (I don't remember being disgusted, so that's worth something). Their menu covers an entire range of dishes, from small to large, Thai to Mediterranean, but everything is pretty pricey. There's a bar too, so I usually just stop in for drinks. Worth a try if you're in the area.

WOW!!!!  Best lobster I have had since leaving new england.  The loster roll was jam packed and very flavorful.  I was excited to see on the menu they serve haddock and that will be my next try.  Helpful staff and very friendly.  They lost as star - we have been trying to go back but they don't seem to keep regular hours and open when they want.  The chef informed us they will no longer be open for lunch.  I don't imagine they will last very long like this.

Wawa-think 'Buckeyes' of the north except much smaller and cheaper. 

Wawa is a convenience store riddled across philly and in my honest opinions definitely a must go to in philly. Locals will groan at mention of it but don't mind them.

Wawa was a saving grace for last minute meals and supplies. They serve your standard gas station items but also make fresh sandwiches and smoothies. In my time, I got an avocado bacon sandwich, chipotle chicken sub, spicy italian sub, mango smoothie, mango peach smoothie, mango sorbet and lemonade sorbet. All amazing!

5 star quality for reasonable prices. Sandwiches were $7-8 and smoothies were only $2 for 24oz. To be honest these smoothie prices were the best part of this while experience. Philly is a walking city, why not pop in grab a cheap, high quality smoothie to keep cool?

I probably went to Wawa 5x in my entire trip. I don't regret it. I recommend you go as well

Food: 4/5
Bang/Buck: 5/5

If you ask any REAL sushi eater in town, Tokyo sushi is by far the best. If I happen to go to a different place for sushi, I feel I just didn't get my sushi fix. The miso soup, egg shooters, and nigiri options are perfect. My go to place. My favorite place in all of Reno.
The best burgers and salads ( my fave is the Thai peanut with chicken) and the staff is always great!

I stayed in a former firehouse and this sandwich shop was 2 blocks away. It was busy from open to close. I had the fried bologna sandwich and it was superb! It combined slightly sweet Texas toast with spicy mustard, crunchy potato chips, chewy bologna and gooey cheese. Perhaps the finest sandwich I have ever had. The sandwich is enough for 2 people. The deviled eggs with chicken skin were nicely seasoned and the crunchy chicken skin was a nice touch. Served with hot sauce, what else? A gourmet meal for under 20 bucks.

I wont write a TOO lengthy review, but was in N.O. visiting family and an uncle recommended this place to me and my mom. I trusted his wisdom because he will not steer you to a place in New Orleans if it doesn't have his stamp of approval, lol. We went ahead and took the plunge. We found this place and while the neighborhood may make a few less adventerous souls hesitant, this is New Orleans, baby and my hometown!. This neighborhood in particular suffered heavily as a result of Katrina, but things are bouncing back here.

We arrived, were greeted and seated promptly. The decor is simple, yet warm and inviting. It may have been either a family home at one time or another eating/drinking establishment. It's evident some work was put into the building and it still retains it's old New Orleans style charm.

 The bar is off of the main dining area and the kitchen is located in and elevated above the main dining room. In fact, the sounds of food being cooked and the kitchen crew conversing back and forth with the servers adds to the ambiance, but at the same time is not overwhelming to the point you can't converse with your fellow diners. The clientle at the time we were there (post Noon Saturday) was a mix of neighborhood residents and tourists enjoying their food.

Our server greeted us and was very attentive. I ordered a beer (They don't have beer on tap) and looked over the menu. While the selection is limited, care and effort is put into each entree, as another Yelper mentioned. I ordered the fried shrimp platter and mom ordered the fried catfish. We both ordered sides of red beans and fries. Shortly thereafter, our food arrived piping hot. The portions were generous, but not overwhelming. The shrimp were large, crunchy and tender insdie. These were indeed Gulf shrimp and IMO, the best shrimp on the planet. I also sampled mom's catfish and it was a large filet, crunchy on the outside and tender inside. The red beans were excellent, and reminded me so much of my grandmother's red beans and rice. 

We skipped desert as we were both pleasantly full. I did want to try the bread pudding, but didn't have room. We then got a chance to speak with one of the co-owners who was very pleasant and inviting. We told her how much we enjoyed the meal and would return.

Dining here was a very enjoyable and uplifting experience. Why uplifting? It's great to see a family owned business start, thrive and bring residents and tourists alike together in pre-Katrina New Orleans. I wish them many years of continued success. There is no pretensiousness or snootiness here..just down home New Orleans cooking and hospitality.

If you have had a bad experience here before, please at least give it another try.

Best sushi I've ever had!  It was so fresh and tasty.  My favorite was the Itsuki Sushi with chef's special sauce - perfection, and so much love in that dish!  The second almost tied for first dish was the Tiger Eye-Eye sushi...sooooooo good!  Coming in for a tie for third was the octopus sushi and the freshwater eel with eel sauce sushi.  All very delicious and husband and I left so satisfied.  

My son gobbled up the entire sizzling shrimp and vegetables dish which had 4 shrimp (my son's favorite) -- that amazed me since he wouldn't normally put onions in his mouth even when hidden - but there he went, chopstick after chopstick , eating all those onions and scallions.

I feel very special when I eat here whether I'm alone or with my family. or on a date night...that's the vibe of this place, it's homey, friendly, great food made with love and enjoyable music playing -- what more could you want?!

I came here after a wickedly long day of travelling & was craving homemade fresh pasta after being overseas for 2 months.  Word of advice is to not get the pasta here.  It was a plain & simple dish.  Get the sandwiches, which I should have done in the first place.  D'OH!  My boyfriend's sandwich looked sooo damn good & delish!  Tiny hole in the wall, but well worth the drive.  Quirky & cool ambience.  You can sit outside too when the weather is good.

if i could rate them zero stars i would! terrible service. the place wasnt busy at all. myself & my friend sat at the bar ehich was empty but full of dirty dishes. after she cleaned the bar she literally took, 20 mins. to take our drink order in which my friend asked for a extra shot that never came. our food was so bad! rib was tuff! the bar tender friends were seated at the bar so she spent all her time with them.

Omg this place is super cute! We've been to different Daisy Dukes before and always enjoyed them. This one, however, had an old time diner feel to it. The food wasn't as good as other ones we'd been to but the atmosphere made up for it! the bloody mary was on point as usual. The waitresses we're very nice and helpful as well! I'd go back if I'm in the area.

Awesome drinks.  High quality ingredients.  Friendly service.   SUPPORT LOCAL!!! worth going out of your way to support these people that offer organic food personalized service.  

Blueberry hot tea and coffee were amazing.

Sit at the bar. Been in NOLA 3  nights and by far the best meal since we have been here. My wife hade the raw oysters and we split some onion rings. I had the shrimp platter and she had the shrimp and oyster platter. Was enough food for 4 people. The female bartender ( sorry I can't remember her name)
gave superior service and made it a memorable experience. Highly recommended.

We're ordered a Chicago stuffed pizza and there was almost no stuffing inside. We ordered they say 15 -20 minutes but in 45 mins you still have to wait for it to be made. We refuse to go anymore after the repeated rudeness of the management here. So we go to the mccarran one which has always been great.  It's worth the few extra minutes drive.

Terrific spot with dedicated chef's that are faster (and better) than anyone I've experienced in Reno.

Their products are very fresh, and the combinations will make your mouth happy.

If you get a chance to give Sushi Minato a try... do it!

Hosted a donut tasting (with rating sheets and all!) for some friends. Frangelli's was their choice for donuts. We only rated the glazed for the tasting and those were, sadly, not my favorite. The donut was tasty, but there just wasn't enough glaze and/or the glaze was too thin. You can tell these will hold up well when filled though! Glazed just might not be their thing and that's okay.

The vanilla frosted and chocolate frosted made up and some for the lacking glazed. The vanilla frosted might have been an old fashioned (maybe?). Whatever it was, it was very good. The chocolate was so fresh and tasted a bit more like a dark chocolate to us. These two were great.

Love this place! Perfect option for HEALTHY vegan food! I am absolutely craving their soups and cheesecakes! Guilt free, of course. They usually have 1 soup option and a few cheesecake options. I recommend the lemon ginger turmeric cheesecake...it's so pretty and full of goodness! Try going on a day with their broccoli cheddar soup or curried lentil! (Both are a tie for first for me). Yep you may have to wait a bit (unless you order these because usually they're ready to go) but your food really is prepared with love and worth the wait!

Possibly the best vietnamese food that I've had in the area. Definitely the best outside of downtown. Wish we lived closer, but when errands or work take me this way, I'll make the trip. Operating very efficiently for take out orders under the current circumstances.

This is by far the worst Chipotle there is. This is the like our third or fourth time eating at the one in the mall food court and every time it sucks. This time I ask for chips and gauc, she rings it up and hands me my food, I ask where my chips are, we are out she says, I'm like then why did I pay for chips and gauc. Also their coke machine was out of everything but lemonade. Ok no problem I'll get sweet tea. It was sweet for sure like grains of sugar still undesolved.

I love Chipotle but I will never eat at the one in the food court again!

Never really liked this place since it opened ... Stopped here 'cause I wanted a cheese steak and didn't feel like driving further down the blvd to Steve's . I'm glad I stopped in and gave it another shot, the cheese steak, fries and soda combo was a really good deal and was surprisingly awesome,  the cheese fries and steak were loaded with cheese and the portion was pretty insane. I felt my heart stop a few times during lunch but that's just part of the experience. 
Only complaints : the pickles suck bad (bread and butter pickles ?? Also cut too thick)
Fries and napkins were scattered on the floor...

My experience here has always been consistent with staff hired for their pleasing assets ignoring the fact my beer is empty or I'm waiting for my check.  

One night in particular, my table had to continually try to flag our waitress down to get her to bring our check.  Finally, when we got her attention she said she would bring it.  And she did, after a fifteen minute conversation with her friend at the waitress station.

Why two stars if the experience has been so bad?  I enjoy their food.  It's just typical bar fare, but it is done well.

I would totally give five stars if they would institute an alternative to YELLING out everyone's name and food type when their order is up. 

I visited during a busy lunch hour and granted, it was loud enough already. I sat near the counter, so I was able to hear when the order for every. Single. Person after me came up. I've visited before and sat elsewhere, when it wasn't so busy. 

It's a reeeeeally annoying practice. 

Especially because we live in an age of buzzers and tented plastic table numbers and whatnot.

Also, they've been open almost a year now and the pies are still a bit inconsistent, as far as doneness. I'm guessing that with the way that they are cooked, depending on toppings, and where in the oven they are  placed, as well as the dough used, along with the cooking time...many factors go into  how the finished pie is presented.

Being a pizza blogger, these are the little details that matter to me! 

Barring those things, I love it. The roasted garlic is amazing. No matter how many toppings you put on it, it's still the same price.

It appears they do a lot of business from the college right across the street, Lindenwood University. It took about 15 minutes from the door to the counter, plus about another five minutes to get my food. Overall, very satisfying and I will definitely be back.

Maybe if it's not a rainy day, I'll just sit outside...

Picture this:  It's 100 degrees at 11AM, I don't know my way around town, and the spouse and I (and the dog) are starving.  We're also in a bad mood because we spent over an hour the previous evening trying to find some place, any place, decent for dinner, only to end up with mediocre casino restaurant food.  (Note to self: Reno casinos are not Vegas casinos).  

After driving around aimlessly looking for something that looked safe, appetizing, and with shaded outdoor seating, we came across Beto's.  I still salivate at the thought of the chips and salsa.  

Now, my tastes may be a little skewed, so please keep that in mind.  I live in San Jose, and despite the city having a large Mexican population, the Mexican food there is absolutely horrible, except for a few hidden gems that I'd prefer to keep to myself.

With that disclaimer out of the way, I can tell you that Beto's is the best Mexican food I have ever had.  The salsa (verde?) was a complex blend of spice and a hint of lime that perfectly matched the puffy, crispy chips.  We shared carnitas and carne asada, both awesome.  The meat was tender and juicy, and seasoned perfectly.

The place was packed, and most people inside were eating seafood soups.  It looked great, but it was a little too warm outside for soup.  I'll have to try it next time I'm in town.

I found this quaint little poke restaurant on Yelp and had a strong craving for some fresh food on my business trip. 

The restaurant is in a nice little strip mall and was very clean and bright inside. The menu was easy to understand and the staff were all so friendly and helpful. 

The poke choices all looked very fresh and clean. I loved the variety and definitely feel like there is something for everyone's taste preferences.

The boba tea was sooooo good and refreshing too!  You have to order it!

I would strongly recommend this restaurant. You won't go home hungry- and that, folks, is all she wrote.

consistently yummy and generous servings. green eggs is a philly staple that visiting friends from out of town request to return to every time. i chose a savory breakfast - breakfast burrito with a side of tomato soup. my friend had the famous red velvet pancakes. we were both delighted with our food and had plenty left over to snack on later in the day. we came on a weekday and avoided having the monstrous wait that the is inevitable here for weekend brunch.

I ordered two identical sandwiches at this location and both orders were 100% wrong. I ordered "bell peppers" and received huge mounds of banana peppers. I asked for tomatoes and cucumbers and received neither. Additionally, I paid for avocado but "they were out". They did not offer to refund me the extra charge for avocado. Terrible service, terrible sandwiches. I had no idea making a couple of sandwiches with the order written down inches in front of your face was so difficult. Won't be returning.

Owner is SUPER nice!

I have loved every sandwich that i bought! mmm and the greek salad is perfection (add grilled chicken for extra bit of happiness)

I think this place is super cool and its right across the street from Webster University DWTN Campus! (perfect)

YUM - I RECOMMEND IT!

They have the best Axxess card 2 for 1 deal in town.  Tasty food (I love their pork chop and was really happy with the kale and salmon salad) and a nice classy atmosphere.  Overall it was a fun staycation dinner date spot.

The woman owner is very rude. My husband went in yesterday to get me lunch as a surprise. We haven't been there for lunch in a while just pizza take out for dinner. He asked her if they had any lunch specials and she yelled at him for asking! She has been rude before but we have tried to look past it thinking she was just overwhelmed. Being yelled at by her was the last straw for him. BTW won't let me post with "0" stars had to give it 1 to post review.

I know Don's is an institution, but we just couldn't help but feel like we were being shuffled through a Cajun swamp-tour ride.  
 
The service was okay.  We sat at the bar to avoid a long wait time.  Our waitress was nice but overwhelmed with business; there didn't really seem to be too much of an attempt by her coworkers to help her get caught up.  

The catfish was good  The chargrilled oysters were okay--perhaps a little above average and pretty fresh.  But the fried shrimp lacked the freshness and crisp texture you might expect from a Cajun seafood place like this.  The cheesecake dessert COULD HAVE been good because it was unconventionally white and fluffy, which I found refreshing and kind of interesting.  BUT, in the long run, it tasted like a gigantic sugar party; it was so sweet that it was difficult to taste the other ingredients.    

The price was atrocious for this kind of standard Cajun fare.  We had only ONE entree and ONE appetizer between the both of us.  After the cheesecakes, the order came to more than $60.  When you add the tip, you're paying $72 for standard fried seafood, and remember, just ONE entrée, and that's waaay too much. 

All in all, the 50/50 success of the food makes me wish I could give 2.5 stars, but when I factor in the price, two stars really does become the right choice.

By far the worst restaurant experience I've ever had. Almost comically terrible. We came in and had to wait to be seated for over 15 minutes even though the restaurant was basically empty and the bartender made eye contact and stared at us for most of it.

We were eventually seated where the bartender served us and overall had a very poor attitude and took ridiculous amounts of time to serve us despite us being the only customers in the bar room and him being 10 feet away from us.  And doing weird things like placing our drinks on the other end of the table where we couldn't reach them and thus forcing one of us to get up and grab them and hand them out ourselves. Instead of, you know, the drinks being handed to us by our sever. And of course, none of our drinks were refilled the whole meal even though he was a few feet away watching us. 

The food took RIDICULOUSLY long. Relative to how few people were in the restaurant it was once again, comical. By the time we ordered were probably the only food order in the whole restaurant. Took about 40 minutes. Then of course when it came out it was only for half the table (5 people). One of us had to sit for 10 minutes and watch everyone else eat until our food came. Then I had to wait another 10 minutes on top of that for mine, as everyone else at the table was nearly finished. So it took an hour for me. Food was cold and incredibly dry. We all usually love B Dubs and were very excited to go. But this was just terrible. Would not recommend AT ALL.

We came here Saturday afternoon, August 28 for my granddaughter's birthday. There were 8 of us. We were not greeted at all by the hostess but instead she barely looked up and said it would be a 45 minute wait. We went and purchased our game cards and just as the kids were playing their first game, we received the text that our table was ready. It wasn't 45 minutes, but maybe 15 minutes. When we approached the host stand and gave our name, the hostess didn't say a word but grabbed the silverware and took off walking to the dining floor. We assumed we were to follow and when we approached the table she tossed the silverware onto the table and again, didn't say a word. 

This is NOT the type of person you want representing your establishment as the first person you come into contact with!

Another rude employee was the young woman working the ticket exchange counter. Extremely rude and not helpful.

I will add though that our waitress was pleasant and attentive.
Incredible breakfast, huge portions! The wraps are enough for 2 people. All the bakery stuff is amazing!!
Stopped in on a Saturday at 1:15pm and they were closed.  All the reviews looked good but they were strangely closed during reports open hours, and what works seem to be a normal time to get lunch.
Beginning to end great experience. Attentive friendly service. Clean lines in a bamboo-walled space. Sushi chefs working a few feet away to create perfect standard rolls and nigiri.

On Monday, 1/21/19  my girlfriend and I went to this establishment. This was my second time being at this restaurant and a first for Kelly. I was somewhat disappointed in the quality of the food and the service that was provided on Monday considering they were not busy and had been really happy with my service the last time I was in which was about 8 months ago on a Saturday evening.  What brought us in on a Monday was for the devour menu considering it was a good deal.  We had the two, four meatball choices and both of us picked our own four which was nice and mixed and matched the meat with the sauce. For our side item we had brussels sprouts and noodles with the banana pudding dessert. The meatballs were so so not as good as the last time. Didn't seem as "fresh" compared to the last time I visited. The  brussels sprouts were way disappointing as they consisted more of theleaves vs having more of the brussel sprout itself that I'm used to having (you'll notice from the picture they did a good job about putting the few sprouts at the stop and all the leaves that had broken apart at the bottom). The noodles however were really good and the banana pudding was great. The other disappointment was our server didn't explain the devour menu at all actually, we had to later on ask about it and the server also  forgot about our dessert. So we had to remind him about that. However, one good thing to brag about is if you go on a Monday it's half-price bottles of wine which did get. So overall I would have to rate my visit as below average this time which is a disappointment since I was very happy the last time I visited. Hopefully this was just a fluke.

Usually order delivery but the pizza and wings are average at best. Nothing special. At these prices, I wish for more oomph. Luckily I found another place close by in the neighborhood. They don't deliver so depending on my laziness, I'll choose one of these restaurants.

Pancho & Lefty's has a cool little rooftop hangout right across from Bridgestone Arena. We setup shop on a few of the barstools and had fun people watching. We came on a weeknight for drinks and an appetizer. My friend and I both ordered the Main Squeeze Margarita to drink, which was a really unique take on a margarita and in fact didn't really taste anything like a margarita but it was still good. This drink has tequila, orange agave, lime and orange juice. For food, we ordered the Big-Ass Nachos ($13) to share which had refried beans, roasted corn, queso, pico de gallo, jalapenos, crema and cilantro. We added adobo chicken ($3) and this was a great choice since the chicken was flavorful. Instead of ordering entrees my friend and I just shared this and this was enough for dinner for two people. The food and drink were all really good here and the rooftop vibe was relaxed.

15 minutes before we were supposed to leave for a concert at the Ryman I was going to get a second drink but I had trouble getting any of the servers over to order. Our server disappeared and probably over 30 minutes went by that we didn't even see them. We finally had to go over to the bar and ask someone for our check so we could leave. This is the only reason I am not rounding up to a 4 even though the experience was more like a 3.5. I would come here again and give them another shot because of the food and the convenient location.
A must go to place to eat love it Seaford is the best dessert is good to very romantic atmosphere prices are reasonable

We've been meaning to stop in, and tonight, we finally did. And glad we were!

There isnt much different to say that everyone hasnt already said, so I will just reiterate some of the reasons why Taste of Havana will become a regular spot for us. 

I had the Pan con Bistec, and my wife had the Cuban. We loved the bread (and everything between it). Usually we take home half our sandwiches to eat for a second meal, but I just wasnt ready to stop eating for the night, so alas, I dont have another meal. Guess I'll just have to go back! 

And the company was just as inviting. We chatted with Diana (Dayana?), for quite a while after we ate, and she told us how she and her dad opened the restuarant, and how it really is a labor of love. 

Try it out. Order a sandwich, have a seat, chat them up, and enjoy! I'm already looking forward to our next visit, and thinking about who else I want to bring with us.

Thank you for a wonderful evening!

I came here on a date the other night and was looking forward to getting a milkshake. I was a bit let down to see the options they had for shakes, so I settled with a float instead. The sofa was so so good and my boyfriend really enjoyed his shake. I think it's a bit pricey for the portion size, but it was good to try! If you like a fun stomps here and friendly service as well as some good drinks, check this place out!

This is the best carrot cake I've ever had in my life. Though, the hosting staff is beyond rude. I've been multiple times, had a wedding cake consultation, and a private party consultation over the years but felt that they treated me as if I was not worthy of being there each time. We didn't get our wedding cake from here because they were so off putting. The experience is fun, especially for young girls, and the bakery team, bar tenders, and waitress have always been awesome. But The hostess team is far from genuine and unhelpful

The best brunch food I've had so far! This is my favorite spot now, the food is farm to table, it's fresh, flavorful and absolutely delicious! I had the crispy potatoes and the biscuit sandwich and for dessert the cinnamon roll.  Everything is large in portions and decadently flavored.  Awesome place!

The food and the service was excellent! Definitely worth a visit if you come to Philly. Great location by University City. Came here to enjoy a solo brunch and had a great time enjoying the food, checking out the decor and chatting with the server about the neighborhood.

Food is great. But for me it's all about the overall experience. Having dinner at the bar and the ignorant, self-centered prick of a manager knocked my chair over 3 times!!! 3!!! On the second after i mentioned it he said "Sorry, boss. I have a small place here." Third he did not even acknowledge. I am not you boss, pal.  If I was you would've been fired on the spot.

I have been to Billy's 3 or 4 times and have enjoyed to food each time. This trip I was so disappointed, the stone crab was stringy and expensive, the shrimp, scallop and grouper was tasteless. Everyone at the table felt the same way.

Highlights:  Great value and attentive staff.  Amazing roast beef sandwiches in a bar setting.

I came here after work and sat down at the bar to enjoy a roast beef sandwich and some fries.  I was looking for something cheap but also delicious and wasn't thinking much about healthiness.  

I ordered the roast beef sandwich and fries and was amazed at the tastiness that this sandwich had to offer.  It was DRENCHED in au jou that they put on top and the fries added a nice addition to the overall meal.  It's a pretty sizable meal for around $9-10 and I highly recommend this place.

Keep doing what you're doing.  I love this place and I love the food.
Great view, food horrible, fish under cooked, grouper fingers were soggy, service slow, unbelievably slow.
This has got to be the umpppteeenth time I had Pats over Gino's . Its juicy overall. Made pretty damn good. Eagles up.

The pad thai is pretty good and the crAb Rangoon's too. I ordered red curry fried rice and it was too spicy to eat. I can eat spicy but it was too Much as I ordered it planning on sharing with the kids and there was no chili symbol next to it to indicate it was going to be hot. Also there was a foul Sewer back up smell that was in the dining area that make me want to barf.

I must say that I was not expecting to like this place as much as I did....but I did!    We were seated promptly ,  and some one came and made the most delicious salsa for my wife and I, it  had the perfect flavor and heat!    (this alone is most excellent).

The drinks were delicious, and we talked to our amazing waiter, and he was SO kind and attentive.  
The food...was truly  5 STAR!   The unique flavors of each dish were so complex, and there is no way to describe with words how AMAZING the 2 meals we ordered were.     If you have a chance to eat here while in Tucson, please do!    You will not be disappointed.   There is something for everyone from vegetarians to meat eaters!!
Solid Vietnamese restaurant, and really affordable too. I was definitely surprised to find this place right by the hospital.
Food was awesome!!!! Service was a little slow but overall a great experience!! We will be back for sure!

The signature bagel is a hidden gem in Fairmount. 

Thinly sliced avocado, perfect spread of cream cheese. Chocked full of crunchy almonds drizzled with honey and dashed with a signature spice.  If you don't know, now you know.

I dined here for Valentine's Day dinner and was only slightly disappointed. The good was that the food here was pretty good for fine Chinese American cuisine. They offer the basics which usually include fried rice, chow mein, egg rolls, etc. My partner and I shared a family meal which included an appetizers share, soup, choice of rice (fried or white), two entrees, and two desserts (pictures to follow). With it being Valentine's Day, it was slightly busy so service was a little slow to keep up the demand of diners. Our sever (I can't remember her name though) was very calm during the rush and was constantly checking back with us to ensure we were doing okay. We had cocktails which were very delicious and minded our stomachs until our food arrived. The environment was very open as it being in the GSR but the authenticity was not there for being a Chinese American restaurant and sushi bar. All in all, the food was delicious and the service was dependable. The bad was that my expectations were not met. This is my first time here even for being a Reno local and I had no idea about their sushi rule. Apparently sushi is only served at the bar and not at the table for all you can eat. They have it only a la carte when dining at the table. I had discussed with my partner prior to eating here that I wanted sushi and he can eat whatever else he wanted because his appetite wasn't as big as mine. That's where the one star is lost due to that one thing. I wouldn't eat here again only because it's more of a tourist attraction if you're staying in the GSR. There are a lot of other places similar to Rim which are more affordable for Reno locals.

I was on a short roadtrip to Santa Barbara and after a bike ride along the beach I was hungry for seafood. I greeted by Jonny and was seated at the counter overlooking the open kitchen. I was looking at the oyster selection and Jonny gave me run down on the oysters they served. I ordered a half dozen oysters mixed variety.  They were very fresh and tasty along with a nice mignonette sauce and seafood sauce with a dollop of horseradish an addition of both a lime and lemon wedge. Looking over the menu and with the recommendation from Jonny I ordered their house Cioppino which was loaded with shellfish (king crab, mussels, clams,scallops, shrimp) in a very flavorful broth set inside a bread bowl. I barely finished the shellfish and could only finish some of the bread that soaked in the great broth.
Jonny was very helpful, courteous and very alert to the needs of his guests. 
When I'm back in the area again I will definitely stop in for great food and service!

Drool. This is my favorite burger place in Tucson. I'm gluten free, and they are very accommodating and have GF buns and lettuce wraps. The hippie soda is great, and I love their variety of sauces and dips.

Good food, Like the concept of local and healthy.  Just remember to keep up the customer experience.  Making a reservation and then showing up to be told that there is a 45 minute wait???  Not a good customer experience.  But in the end, I nice place to go for dinner.

Yeah, don't go there. Created an account just to write about how shitty this place is. Honestly, the guy who helped us is a complete dick, the hookah quality was terrible and not worth the ridiculous price they charge, and the atmosphere makes me cringe. Damn, what a waste of time and life.
It is always crowded and that is fine BUT they really needed the air turned on today! It was SO hot in the there!

The foods always good there, but service was awful--new GM doesn't look like he knows what he's doing, and amidst the coronavirus pandemic he didn't even bother to wear gloves while handing out the drinks and taking payment. Nasty stuff.
Really good traditional German food.   Great bakery and store for German products.  The schnitzle is awesome.

I ordered the burger and it was excellent.  The menu was well priced and the selection was very diverse.  Most yelpers will say to get the steak but unfortunately it was lunch so that might have been too heavy.  The appetizers looked great but I did not partake.  Enjoy the food, ambiance and good service.

This is probably my favorite chicken spot in Tucson. The customer service was great. Destiny went above and beyond and made sure we were taken care of. Not to mention the food was delicious. Definitely will be coming back.

It really takes a lot for me, a fat chick, to not like food but *Ding ding ding* Melrose wins the award for having the most bland boring food since my mom killed a roast. 
Ordered: a Patty Melt. Side of O'Rings and a slice of their butter cake. 
Patty Melt: hard to mess this up. Even IHOP gets it right. But Melrose managed to by having a flavorless patty, over cooked onions and a semi-burned rye bread. I even added some sea salt in hopes it would improve. Nope. 
Onion Rings: how they got this wrong was a big mystery. But they managed to achieve it. I tried dipping it in BBQ sauce but even its Que-y goodness couldn't mask this greasy flavorless mass. 
Butter cake: Meh. Betty Crocker does it better. 
I'm sure there are blue plate special folks who prefer bland food. This would be their mecca.

Ordered here during COVID, but I hear that it's typically an all-you-can-eat sushi restaurant. To be honest, I never order from all-you-can-eat restaurants in general, because I find the quality to be subpar. This was the case here. One of the rolls tasted kind of fishy and the others didn't seem to have the quality that I'm used to. The order was packaged on time and pick up was easy at the door. I would order from here again but it was not terrible.
Found a finger nail in my salad and they got mad at me like it was my fault. Ended up getting a full refund but would never go back nor would I recommend eating here.

Why don't more places like this exist? Excellent food that is always delicious and for a great price.  Not only can you not beat the value for product but you have a great quick serve atmosphere to boot. go here now!

Great food - busy even during a miserably terrible downpour!  Tacos and Torta ordered.  Tacos and Torta devoured - 
Mucho Tasty!  Haha - sorry could not resist the gringo spanish.  I mean, really - 4.5 stars with over 1k reviews - why are you even reading this?  If you love great tacos and a mexican coke - stop reading and git cho fanny over there and gobble up!

Stay hungry.

My husband and I visited Nashville with the one intention to try Nashville Hot Chicken. We ended up dining at three establishments in one day with this being the second we tried.

We arrived on a Saturday late afternoon and the wait ended up lasting approx 50 mins in the hot, burning sun (just to order). We both shared the large dark chicken plate. We opted for "Hot" it ranged from mild, medium, hot, damn hot, and shut the cluck up.

We got Hot at the last place we tried and it KILLED us (but damn it was good) We got half medium and half hot here.

Additionally, we got the Mac and cheese and greens as sides and added the creamy coke slaw.

There weren't any tables free inside so we dined in the patio (which is opened to take out diners). In hindsight, I would recommend you order ahead online.

As for the food. It was just ok. Good amount of crispiness. As for the spiciness...it was weak sauce. Didn't hit any radar at all. If I knew they would be that tame we would've gone spicier. The medium was basically less than mild to me and the "hot" wasn't close.

As for sides, the Mac was ok. Greens were unmemorable. And we both didn't enjoy the cole slaw.  Maybe too creamy? It didn't taste refreshing.

We also got the banana bread pudding which was ok.

Also, you can tell this place is just a hype beast restaurant. All the other diners were tourists like us. Probably half were from California.  (We heard two large group talk to each other about being from California.) No locals were here.

The food is tasty enough! But wasn't our favorite of the three hot chicken we tried and not sure it's worth that wait. Order ahead than maybe.

The hipster hot chicken spot.  The hype beast got me. And I left vaguely disappointed.
The food is always excellent but the noise level is intolerable. The tables are too close together and the sound level in the room makes conversation almost impossible.
i enjoyed this place very much! did not stick around to eat in, but it looked very clean. and my california rolls were delicious.

Friendly servers, great beer selection and interesting menu. I love the brick oven pizza. Not only was the crust awesome but the sauce is some of the best I've ever had, seemed the closest to Italian pizza than anything I ever had before in the US.

Such a delicious meal and such a great addition to the neighborhood! This is definitely getting added to our pizza rotation. They do sourdough Neapolitan style with great topping options. Ordered the soppressata (wonderful after burn from the fermented pepper jelly) and the clam with leeks (so creamy but not too rich). Did a side of the roasted cauliflower and broccoli which was also delicious but the pizza is definitely the star. Excited to try more of their topping combinations with our next order!

Excellent customer service. Staff enforced mask wearing while guests walked throughout the restaurant. I felt safe and comfortable while dining. Brunch was delicious. I wasn't a fan of the candied bacon but everyone else at my table enjoyed it. I had the country breakfast and it was great.

I know the great service at the store when I stop by to purchase groceries ...... But lately I have been unable to actually go to store .... I used another food delivery service ...... at other stores ... but not quite the same. When I found out Raley's has their own delivery ( ECART ) and for only about $5 ( first time free ) I had to try it. It was wonderful. I could place order on line and note what to replace if out ....could make notes about address and time to deliver ... And when order was being filled they called to double check about replacements ... All in all a much better experience. The young man who delivered was prompt and friendly .... the items were sorted and dated well ahead ... and there was even a sample product in the bag.  I will use again and stick with a known quality .... Since first time is free of delivery charge why not give it a try.
Always loved Cafe Bistro! Ever since it opened, it has been one of our favorite spots. Staff are very helpful, and friendly. Food is great and you can always get a seat. Great environment.
They have the best bubble tea!! Everything I've tried on the menu is very tasty and the service is quick

I also bought the Travelzoo special and wish I would've read the reviews first.  The food was ok, but they served the drinks in plastic which doesn't seem quite right when drinking a $14 glass of champagne. They added 20% on for gratuity even though there were only two of us in our party.  They told me I needed to use the online system to make a reservation.  I used PayPal, which was recommended and when I arrived they had no record of my deposit.  I checked my credit card today and they charged $21 over the signed amount on my receipt!  I will not return and recommend NOT going here.
Awesome great service delicious food for the last ten years and never falls short of amazing

Sueno was an awesome stop on the way along our night out. Fair prices for food and drink and really tasty menu choices, the burrito was insane. Abby our server was attentive and super helpful and we all loved her!! Our group will be back!

Voted by our entire family of 5 as the best meal in Nashville. Something for every person on the menu and the flavors.... oh my gosh .... my very picky tastebuds were super happy. 

It just tasted like the food was actually crafted with thought and love instead of cranked out for the tourist crowd. The chef has done an amazing job of keeping a simple menu with phenomenal tastes. 

The building itself is lovingly restored and the staff were all kind and attentive. Sivon, our waitress was so kind! Food runner Zack made sure the kids were fed first - so important! 

Sweet potato pancakes were AMAZING. The biscuits were also our fave of the trip. Husband said the fried chicken was also best of the trip (he ate fried chicken all over the state). 

Special note to the proprietor.... it was amazing and refreshing to see the love in restoring this special place. As the city gets more and more modern, it was beautiful to walk into a restored place of history that was obviously curated with love and attention. Beautifully done.

We were in Chestnut Hill for the #nightoflights exhibit and wanted a quick bite to eat. It's been awhile since we've been here due to Covid.  The brewery has expanded into the space next door adding a dine in restaurant. Previously seating was inside the farmers market and outside. Of course the outside seating has also expanded. 
It was chilly to be outside but the hostess and manager found us a table next to the wall that was ok.  I didn't see any heating lamps but we could feel some heat from the bar area.
One of the reasons we go here is because of the free beer with Yelp check in!!! My husband had the seasonal Festbier. It was tasty with lots of spice. I had the Apple cider which was also good. Beers and drinks also come in half pours which I like because I'm not a big beer drinker. Cocktails are also available now.
We had the regular pizza It was good. Very cheesy! I prefer the Margarita but I let my hubby choose. I like the pizza sauce no matter which one I get!  
I have to shout out our waiter, Sellus! He patiently helped us pick our drinks, gave us several tastings and was so nice!

I grew up in this area and never knew of Blue Sage's existence until they were featured in Philadelphia Magazine for their sliders a few years back. (This was just on the brink of "sliders" popularity) Both were new to me and I headed over the next weekend to give Blue Sage a try. 

I must say, dining vegetarian and trying funky new things was DEFINITELY not my style but I was incredibly impressed and delighted. I then referred the spot to my parents.. mom was a little curious but skeptical.. dad (a big guy) raised on meat and potatoes was fearful the "froo-froo vegetarian food" wouldn't even fill a cavity for him. They too were impressed, delighted and stuffed!

Sweet, cozy spot, amazing food, friendly staff and more food than I can usually handle. Can't wait to go back again!

I don't get the bad reviews. I thought the pizza was solid. Better than any of that flat pizza that most St. Louis people seem to fancy. Pizza had great flavor. Waiting staff was very pleasant. It took a little bit to arrive but that's ok. It was fresh. I'll definitely come back and try the pasta because it looked really good
Always a great meal.  We've eaten there several times. Service was a little spotty tonight, but the grouper and shrimp with risotto was excellent.
It's a great diner-type breakfast. Had a huge omelet and hash browns and couldn't even finish it all. Thanks Joe!

Don't come here. A while back a lady crashed her car into one of the walls and since then, nothing has been the same. Most of the time they are out of Oreo and chocolate ice cream. Also, the customer service is a joke. We waited 17 minutes for our ice cream to be "handed out otherwise it has to be remade." I ordered a small order of cheese curds and one fell out and sat on the counter. This sounds like an honest mistake but when you only get a certain amount, it's annoying.
The ice cream sat for so long that by the time it was "handed out," it was melted. The girl handing them out had half a brain. She couldn't manage 5 ordered of ice cream. I kept up with the orders better than she. Once she started handing out the ice cream, she spent 20-30 minutes "throwing away napkins." 
This is a mess. Seriously just go to baskin Robbins, it's around the corner.

Planned and organized my friends bachelor party at this restaurant. It was beyond successful. They have three menu options for parties to choose from. We chose the most expensive one which gets you a choice of three meats, three sides,and a dessert. Did I mention it's unlimited??? Yes... unlimited and the price is fantastic, about $35 a person. We received five-star treatment all night and the bbq was just top notch. We were constantly checked in on by the manager who was extremely attentive and helpful. The food was delicious, the service was quick and fabulous, I would recommend this place all day.

One of the very few chain restaurants we consistently visit. A very nice mix of healthy eating and classic entrees on the menu. Both indoor and patio seating available. Both the indoor and outdoor areas can accommodate large groups. I usually get one of the omelettes, they're always good.

YUM! I ordered a New Orleans sandwich and it was delicious. Definitely captured a Cajun taste.  Atmosphere is nice and the lighting made the place look nicer.  This was my first time here and the lady taking the order was nice and I will definitely be back again. If you come, try the New Orleans!! Pretty much all sandwiches are under $10!
Great breakfast spot next I will try their lunch good service too. The French toast and blueberry pancake was delicious

If a friend asked me for great Italian food I wouldn't say here. But, if they said that they wanted a fun place this would definitely be the place I recommend. The food is good but it's just a fun place to have a  casual dinner, and play some bocce ball. You come here with friends, drink, eat, laugh, and make memories. Not many places create that atmosphere.

Met friends at the bar. Drinks on point and all yummy. Unfortunately the night we went the restaurant was closed.
Will come back again for dinner, drink, and possible a room to look for
Colonial Cafe a hometown bar , good food, good drinks, good people and GREAT owners!  George and Leslie are terrific...they make you feel welcome and they truly appreciate your business.

We come here once a year because the kids love the midway. 2 o clock on a Wednesday afternoon and we had to wait over 30 min to get our car from valet. No one even asked for our ticket or apologized to say they were short staffed. They just ignored us. I tried calling customer service and was not warmly greeted. This is a management issue if only 2 valets are working. There were 4 families also waiting over 30 min with us. Very not happy right now.
Another nice spot to drop by if you are in the neighborhood. Varied menu and drinks.  Hipsters and regular folks.

BEST WINGS EVER!!! The scooter wings double tossed are awesome. Every time my daughter comes down from Alabama, this is where she wants to go.  I have ordered to go, UBER Eats, and eaten there. If you have leftovers, start up your grill and throw them on. Just as good the second time around.
Excellent food. Their pork ribs are fantastic. Great service. Highly recommend this place to others and will certainly return.
Excellent experience today. Quick seating and service.  Sit down meal comparable to fast food prices.  55+ menu and kid's menu is awesome.  Food tasted great!!

My family comes every year to this place whenever we come to Florida during vacation. 

The staff are really nice and the food and drinks are just perfect. Me and my sister usually get the ice latte with the "Le Parisian" sandwich which are so good! It's simple but sometimes the best things in life are. 

Defiantly give this place a drop by if you ever need a pastry fix or just want something small and light to eat.

Excellent family owned business.The service was excellent,so was the food.Good home style cooking.The decor inside is super inviting and tastefully set up. If you are in the mood for European specialties and tasteful desserts, have breakfast, lunch or dinner at the Sunset Grill.
Service is always great! You never run out of chips and salsa. Food is good and reasonably priced. My favorites are the burritos and tacos feast for two.

Horrible customer service from the manager/owner. I've never complained about a restaurant's food before, but honestly it was terrible. Complained to the manager/owner and her attitude was disgusting. Do not recommend.

Normally I love coming here (mainly for the view) but this past experience will have me staying far away.  First the service was horrible,  the waitress had to come back 3 maybe 4 times to verify our order. At one point she just walked away as I was about to order a drink.  

The breaded shrimp was ok but the breading itself was blah.  The rice bowl was decent but after a large roach landed on our table I was done. Sure roaches are everywhere but we told the waitress after we had to hunt her down and she ran away. Then we told the bartender/manager who said ok and continued to ignore us.  We had to practically beg for the check. Other patrons started to apologize to us. We could not get out fast enough! I even called back the next day to report it to someone else.  I received an apology and was told I would be taken better care of next time. I'm not convinced there will be a next time.  

I left hungry, thirsty and annoyed.
Love this place. Their drinks are amazing (especially the iced chai) and also their breakfast sandwiches are delicious and cheap. Highly recommend coming here for breakfast or lunch!

Great diner food!  Sodas that they make are great!
We drove 45 mins to get here and it was worth the drive.  Milkshakes are a must.  The disco fries are good.

I have been there twice. I had the turkey and avocado sandwich on the first visit and the Cobb salad on the second. Both were excellent. The staff is great. This will definitely be a regular stop for me.

This is a touristy waste of calories, a rather average burger place. I had the 96 burger, which was just ok. I'm giving it two instead of three stars because there are so many great artisanal burger places everywhere now that the average bar is higher than this. The milkshakes were generic as well and my two kids were unimpressed.

The waitstaff messed up two dishes. Also one of our party needed to be strictly gluten free due to Celiac and the waitstaff/kitchen was not knowledgeable regarding cross contamination. If you're Celiac, you are rolling the dice.
Not so vegetarian friendly. Their cream cheese wontons has crab in it and they tried to give me fish sauce.

Nice cozy place. A bit crowded but it was great that they take your name and number down so they can send you a text letting you know your seat is ready. I got to check out local businesses around the block instead of waiting in the restaurant. The workers were friendly and nice! Very unique style and food was amazing! Every taco cost $3-$4 each - it's just a taco. They did have some meals, but nothing too big like a typical Mexican restaurant. The tacos were different and delicious! I high recommend this place!
I'm not a huge fan of buffets but this one was excellent. I highly recommend this place if you are in the mood for Mediterranean food.

Moxie's get's a good rating from me because of the MENU. They literally have one of the best menus. I love the options and variety. My favourite is definately the beef vindaloo! absolutely delicious! love the white chocolate brownie! med bread yes!! avocado springs rolls scrumptious! steak also deliteful! The menu is definitely a 5! However i dont like that the food is dependent on the location. For example the beef vindaloo is usally excellent at the Bourbon Street location but crappy at the Kingsway Location. I find that with moxies, you actually have to find your favourite location. Other than that i'm a fan.

Came here for lunch on a whim, and man. I was not disappointed. Bacon wrapped shrimp appetizer? Yes. Easily one of the best meals I've ever eaten. Staff was courteous, friendly and helpful. Will definitely be going back here.

I was told that Columbia Restaurant is the oldest restaurant in America! Is that true or was he BSing me????

After hearing that of course I had to take advantage of stopping by here before taking off on my flight back to California.  

I ordered the crab croquettes and the Cuban and will say that most were not very memorable.  Both items felt dry and lacking flavor.  

I really wanted to love this place and will be happy giving it another shot on my next visit back into Tampa.

BOMBBBBB!! The boo/I were in Reno for the lantern festival weekend, AND after a magical night - we were hoping for a yummy morning after BRUNCH to complete our trip...and came upon this tasty place!

Two Chicks is a relatively medium size, cute, local joint that seems often jam packed with people. We settled for outdoor seating and waited probably no more than 15 minutes, but def. knew others waited longer than us for indoor seating. Service was nice and fast overall, even while sitting outside.

Let's dig in:

(1) Steak breakfast with hash browns and eggs - the steak was a tad bit overcooked, but still very tasty, well seasoned, and juicy AF + standard yummy sunny side eggs and hash brown were perfect in completing the meal.

(2) Biscuits and gravy with sausage and eggs - homemade and highly recommended - it was so damn good! The biscuit was nice and soft, easy to cut through with a fork but still substantial enough to hold up all of that rich, thick, and tasty gravy! Perfectly cooked sunny side eggs and a side of sausage BC more meat is always a must...

(3) Side of veggie fritters - this was a house favorite and was well worth the hype! All the string veggies are compacted and panfried to a beautiful crispy fritter. Def. unique and very tasty!!!

(4) Mimosa is a brunch necessity and this one was so good and refreshing, their house squeezed OJ was perfectly cold and even had light pulp + champagne = the perfect morning wake me up! 

Not sure when I'll ever be in the area again, but def. would be sure to pop by here!!

Went for dinner on a saturday night. Service was quick but my server did nothing when i complained about my over cooked food which he recommended to me. My buddy got some pasta swimming in sauce and over seasoned.we shared a bruschetta appetizer which was bland. I found everything overpriced for the quality and dont plan on ever returning.

Pueblo Solis has become one of our family's favorites over the past few years. In my opinion, the food has gotten so much better since my first visit several years ago. My sons love trying all the different types of salsa, and we always end up ordering way too much. I love all of the combo options, and also the chile rellenos.

The staff is really friendly and always engages with my kiddos which makes them feel super special. We can't wait to get back and visit in person eventually.

Very good food. This was my families first time here and we enjoyed everything. Great service, great food. I had the taco and chili relleno combo, so good. All the food was hot and fresh. We will most definitely be back.

Good hotel. Decent and friendly staff. Clean rooms.
And a bar named Winthorphe & Valentines?!!
On top of that great deal on Orbitz...

but beware... $55 for Valet parking???
I mean... that's almost half the price of what I paid for the room on Orbitz guys!!!

Fellas, the service isn't bad but arm em with something worth bringing out that doesn't taste like Hamburger Helper bread crumb packets sprinkled over an Olive Garden dumpster.

Wahlburgh's? Naw it's Philly.
Staff service is always pleasant. However being McDonald's you still have to request that the meat is made fresh, otherwise you get the hours old warmed up stuff which is

This place has such potential. The food is good in my opinion. Overpriced but worth it every now and then. Definitely not an everyday place. The service is however horrendous. The hostess is the rudest little thing. She has pushed me to the point of no return a few times but then I remember the wasabi bloody mary. Suddenly I remember why I love this place. Great cheese platter, great eggs Benedict and great bloody mary. I'm thankful the hostess isnt a server. Otherwise I'd cross this place off my list.

Best sushi in the south jersey area - fantastic staff and very homey environment if you dine in.

YUM!

The food here is excellent and well prepared. amazing flavor. I would go here every night at the calories allowed. The line is worth the wait. hold onto your receipt though as it is the only way of the staff  knowing your order. highly recommend the shrimp and ham dishes. The sides especially the greens are great.

Ive been here a few times and I have to say, you really can't go wrong with this place. The first thing I want to mention is that the service here is superb. They can speak English well and they can also speak Cantonese and Vietnamese fluently. They are friendly and prompt whenever we need their attention and, really, this place deserves a 5/5 for service.

As for the food, it is always consistent whenever I come here. I've only ever ordered pho from here, so I can't say a lot about the other food, but my brother says the rice platters are really delicious. Even when they brought it out, it smelled delicious - I kind of regret not stealing a bit of the food from my brother! Anyway, the pho here is really good. The broth is flavorful (the broth is what makes or breaks pho and this place definitely does a good job in the broth department) and the bowls do not lack in quantity. A couple of other pho places I've been to would only give, like, 2 strips of beef and half a cup of noodles (exaggeration). The serving sizes here are enormous. I would say that the small bowl is the size of a regular bowl.

You really can't go wrong with such a solid place like this. I highly recommend coming here if you're ever craving a little bit of pho!

Was great until they took away online ordering.  Now the lone is out the door , you have to wear a mask and they claim it's faster?  For who?  Before I could order on my drive over and it would be sitting there waiting for me!  That was the best.  This new wait in line method is so annoying.
Not very good service food good but came out in pieces. Like my meal together, veggies came out after I was done with main course. They are veggies not a dessert. Don't know if I'll be back
O i always wanted to check out this place. Great place. Great food and service. Best noodle place in town.

My family of 4 ordered breakfast food (eggs & pancakes) at 7pm.  The restaurant was not very full - maybe 7 tables w/ customers.  After 45 minutes we still did not have our food.  Nor did at least 2 tables that were there before us.   After asking the waitress (1 of 2 on duty) when we might get our food, she told us, 'I don't know - I can't make the chef go any faster'.  Other tables were complaining about the wait as well.  At that point we finally got up and walked out.  --  On a brighter side, we drove to the IHOP near Grant & Swan.  There we had a perfect service and had our food on the table exactly 11min and 30 sec after placing our order.   We will NEVER go back to this Coco's.  Coco's used to be a great place.  The Coco's at Campbell Plaza was a favorite for many many years before it closed.  Sad.

We have been traveling for over 2,500 miles (from CA). The food on the trip has ranged from mediocre to poor and we have been eating at 4 star yelp review restaurants, however this meal was exquisite. Both creative, fresh and more than reasonable priced! This restaurant completed our New Orleans adventure.

Very impressed! We happened upon this place for a quick bite between appts. Great selection of wraps, hot or cold, 6" or 12"; plus homemade soups, 3 or 4 daily from a selection of 8? soups in their rotation plus salads!  Happy employee at register offered us generous tastes of their soups, and explained the menu. They can customize ANYTHING to your liking, and we didn't see anything about additional charges. Unusual & healthy choices too: nuts, sprouts, avocado, craisins, all on any of three different tortlla flavors. Great for take out. Clean, fast, & cheery. That's everything I want for fresh food, fast instead of 'fast food'.

The smoked turkey, bacon, cheese, avocado, spinach, tomato & scallion "bolo' i ordered hot, was perfect! They have a way of keeping the wrap wrapped! No seam, no mess! Seriously, perfect for what we wanted & needed at the time.

This Thai restaurant does everything right! Crispy spring rolls served with a delicious sauce, coconut chicken soup that is full of flavor and Tofu in chili sauce that is perfectly spicy but not hot! The Amazing Chicken entree is yummy too.

The service is friendly, fast and efficient. You will love the food, atmosphere and service. I'll return often.

Veterans day just picked up new glasses and noticed this restaurant.  Decide to get lunch at the last minute.  Told as vets we get a free entree from lunch or diner menu. Anything we wanted. Wow, great service great food.  Will go back.  One of the few place I have eaten in Indiana that I can say that about as a combo of service and food.
Great food and a wonderful experience the was polite,helpful and recommend some excellent dishes  great

Second time eating here since August, when I moved to Tucson. First time was fine. This time, not so much. First, the menu has changed in format and seems to offer fewer options. Stephanie, our server was nice, but slow. We had the Spanish Omelette and Eye-Opener breakfast. Omelette was fine. Asked for crispy bacon on the Eye-Opener, didn't get it. Waited to eat until bacon came back and when I did, I noticed pancakes were uncooked all the way through. Whole plate was taken back and returned with crispy bacon and cooked pancakes but way overcooked eggs. I'm not a picky diner, but the eggs had a brown crust and were really rubbery. Manager and server apologized and offered to remake again. My friend had already finished her meal, so I was over it and asked for the check. Nothing comped, not even my soda. I didn't ask for it to be, but just assumed if you've messed up my order twice, I should at least get a free soda. The cashier, however was very nice. He gave me a fully stamped diner's card so I can at least have a free entree on my next visit. He salvaged the experience.

This was our second visit to twisted ranch. Our server was Kyle and we both ordered big kid Mac n cheese's with loaded fries to share. While waiting, I witnessed Kyle taking a fry from a tray of fries at the window that were meant for a customer and sneakily try to eat it. Not sneaky enough. After over 30 minutes Kyle brought our food out, and there was only one Mac n cheese. He argued rudely about not hearing me order it and finally turned around to ring another one in. After another 20 minutes my Mac n cheese came. I asked for our bill and a box. He charged me for the second Mac n cheese and I asked him nicely if he would take it off our bill. He argued with me AGAIN. Finally the manager came over and was very kind and took it off the bill for me. If it wasn't for the food and the manager I would have given Twisted Ranch one star.

I did the lunch special and got a slice of pizza, three breadsticks, and a drink all for around $6! 

The breadsticks are soft and delicious! They are cooked just right and not too crunchy. I could have eaten them for days! 

The pizza was fine. Not bad, but nothing to write home about. 

I thought the lunch special was a good value and will be returning.

Husband and I spent the day in Philadelphia and found Cuba Libra by serendipity. We assumed he could get a good rum and coke (his favorite) there. We ordered lunches that were combinations of three or four different items. I ordered the Del Mar - which started with shrimp ceviche, next course a coconut milk-based seafood soup, and grilled mahi-mahi with black rice and seafood for the entree. Every bite was an exciting combination of flavors and textures. Husband ordered their Cuban "bento" special which consisted of an Angus beef slider, guacamole that included fresh pineapple, an empenada, and a mini-portion of tres leches cake. I can't overstate how delighted we were with our selections. We found the decor relaxing after a day of festival crowds. We look forward to returning here on a future visit to the City.

I went here with my boyfriend after a really stressful week, and the atmosphere was exactly what I wanted, and not at all like I expected. It's definitely not super fancy or trendy, kind of like a south Philly thrift store exploded on the walls. It was homey and comfortable, something that can be kind of lost in a lot of the really overwrought hipster places on Passyunk.
     As for the food, the menu is somewhat standard Italian American, though tastier than other places in the area. The specials are what really stood out, especially the pulled pork, mandarin orange, and arugula bruschetta. My boyfriend got the chicken parm sandwich with extra sharp provolone, which was HUGE and OUTSTANDING. Overall, the tiramisu was probably my favorite, giant and covered in buttercream. Our server was Nik, who hooked us up with extra spicy mussels and kept the drinks coming.

While I couldn't convince my lady to go to Cooter Brown's Tavern during our time in New Orleans, the words "vegan hot dog" was enough to get her to accompany me to the similarly innuendoed named Dreamy Weenies at the tippy top of the French Quarter. 

Despite the silly naming marketing ploy, this place takes their hot dogs seriously.  Offering five different kinds of veggie dogs (and many kinds of dietary restriction meats), this is a herbivorian hot dog fanatic's dream.  I got the "andouille sausage" made "pothole" style since I had never heard of putting potato salad on a hot dog before.  And them covering it with veggie chili and cheese on top of that made it irresistible.

I'm amazed that no other place tries this fancy combination.  At times the potato salad overpowered the dog, though the textures combined to make an interesting eat that's as unique as the city itself.

For a little over $10 after tax, I also got a drink and some waffle fries.  The fries were spiced perfectly but they were slightly soggy (and I wanted some crisp compared to the gloppy, delicious mess that was on the plate next door due to the overstuffed hot dog bun).  I left slightly less than filled (the hot dog is larger than the average back yard griller big but not huge by any stretch of the imagination) but more than satisfied.

The staff here is super friendly and I get the feeling they really care about the neighborhood and want small businesses to succeed in it.  So I'd gladly give them my patronage again if only to try another one of the five kinds of veggie dogs.

Great pizza place for takeout! The online ordering process is really easy. The food is excellent. I'd recommend the margarita pizza with mushrooms or the ravioli and meatball entree if you are looking for a treat. They also have excellent wings. Food was hot and affordable and ready very quickly. Will definitely be returning!

Me and my hubby were visiting from out of town and craving chinese. We decided to come here. 

So far unimpressed with the service.  We both asked for water and after a "look" and about five minutes later they were delivered. 

I ordered the shrimp lo mein. and my hubby ordered the chicken lo mein.  I would have ordered a cup of wonton soup but the sever rudely cut me off. His loss.

The food came fairly quickly.  The lo mein was all oil and no sauce.  But still pretty alright. 

The ambiance was lacking. No audible music in the backround. I like asian places to play asian music.

So this is my new favorite place. I find the restaurant to be easy to navigate, clean and very well organized. However, what amazes me the most is their food. I've tried almost everything on the menu and I can attest that it is all delicious! My personal fave, similar to others on yelp, is the chicken basil pesto. The angel hair pasta is perfect, the basil pesto is on point and the sauce, although creamy, is not too heavy. Next time you are near a Piada I highly suggest you try it... And if you have to go out of your way, it is well worth it!

Have been going here since I was 5 yrs old and I'm currently 23. Nicest people but not the nicest part of town. Donuts are absolutely delicious. They sell out fast! Don't go there at 9:30-10 expecting to have top pick.

Really terrible.  We were staying at the Atlantis, so the Sunday champagne Brunch was an easy choice.  I wish we would have gone anywhere else. The food was cold, easy things like scrambled eggs were crusty and gross.  For the price for one person, you can feed two people at a cafe down the street and walk away happy.

This was one of the best experiences I've had in terms of service in a really long time. Me and my wife just wanted a quick bite to eat before checkout, and we were quickly greeted by Michael at the bar. He had amazing recommendations and he would anticipate our needs before we could even say anything. Even before we left, he offered to refill our coffee to a Togo cup so we can have something for the road. The food portions were very large, and it really was the best way to end our little getaway from LOS ANGELES. Thank you for that Michael. We will definitely be back!
One of the Best Indian restaurant in philly... Buffet rate is economical...  Don't miss the lamb curry..

Some of the best tacos I've ever had. They have a good selection that you can have in a taco, burrito, salad, or bowl. All ingredients are fresh and they put your order together quickly. People who work there are really friendly as well. Every time I'm in the area I make a couple stops here for tacos.
fantastic chicken gyro with fresh lettuce, tomatoes and red onions the portions are large , I will stop here whenever i visit Temple University"

Nom Nom Nom!

My friend and I came here for the roast beef, but it wasn't ready so we opted for the club po-boy which included bacon, root beer glazed ham, and chicken with a side of onion rings.  The large po-boy was HUGE!  Even split between us, it was still ginormous.  You definitely get what you pay for because these po-boys are fully loaded!  It also doesn't help that I'm a messy eater! Haha.  The onion rings are awesome!  They're literally thinly sliced onions that are fried, and I loved it!  It's perfect for putting in your po-boy to add some extra crunch and flavor.  The sandwich was actually really good.  I like that you could really taste the root beer flavor, but it wasn't overpowering.

The only downfall was waiting for the po-boy.  It took longer than expected, but the wait was well worth it!

Gotta be honest - I'm pretty surprised there's a good Asian restaurant in Avondale.  We've been here many times and have never been disappointed.  Great food, atmosphere,and  service:  a real treat in this neck of the woods.

This is the first Greek place we have tried in the area but we got take out from here and it was excellent. We both got the beef and lamb platter and the food was great! The meat was delicious and moist and the tzatziki sauce was some of the best I have ever had! The fries were also amazing! We will definitely be getting food from here again and can't wait to try other dishes next time!

Been going here for years.
Always a GREAT meal.
Been to Buenos Aires and these match up!

Sweet ones are great too...

The service was lacking in all areas, very neglected by the server, walk by numerous times with out following up on our beverages. The server would walk up ask a question then walk away without time for our response. I get the place was decently busy and kitchen back up. But I know as a fellow service worker that it could have been way better. The food came out after a extra long wait cold the fruit on my plate was warmer then the eggs and potates. Over all wouldnt reccomend to others as a new local this isn't my place to go.

The Dish is a quiet little place with a very relaxed atmosphere. The interior is simple and cozy, and I walk right past it pretty much every time I go. 

The menu is mostly variations on comfort food. It's not huge, but every time I've been they've had a number of specials and I usually end up getting one of those, although the sweet potato shepherd's pie from the regular menu is nice.

They've also got a decent selection of wines, and last time I had an elderflower cider with my meal. 

The most outstanding thing about the Dish is their patio. It's cute and quiet, behind the building and sheltered from the traffic noise on Stony Plain road. 

While nothing here has every completely knocked my socks off, foodwise, it's still a perfect spot for catching up over dinner. They also do dinner and a movie once a week, which I think is a neat idea.

My first experience with Vietnamese food...and I regret it. The Pho was decent, ordered Chicken. However veggies were very sparse.

The worst part of this trip was by far the Pork BBQ Sandwich. there were very few pieces of meat in the bread, and my first bite was actually into a piece of bone. At least 50% of it was fatty gristle. Yuck. Also very little veggies on this sandwich too.....isn't that the cheapest part to fill a sandwich with? I won't be back.
