Much better than what some might call their counterpart "Taco Mamacita"  Local Taco's  ingredients are much better and they are way more creative.  Better put together all around. 

Anywho..very fun place to eat and get some good grub!

This place seems a little overrated to me. I think by far the best reason to go there is the view. That being said, if you are going for the view it's imperative that you ask for a table by the window. I didn't ask and was seated in the middle where it's like being at any other restaurant that doesn't have a view. The ambience is extremely romantic - very dim lighting (almost to a fault in my opinion) and the booths are really nice. Almost lounge-esque. 

All of that being said, now everything else. I just didn't think the food was worth the price. Don't get me wrong, I got the butchers fillet dish with the chilled shrimp salad and the cookies and cream for dessert. I enjoyed it. But didn't think it was anything groundbreaking flavor wise or creativity wise. Certainly not worth the cost. 

Our services was incredibly mediocre, in fact, at times frustrating. It took over 15 minutes before someone even took a drink order and another 15 minutes for bread and taking food order. The whole night I felt like I had to keep my head on a swivel to get the waiters attention. 

Likely wouldn't go back again, unless I wanted to be showy with a date and have a good view.
Excellent food at cheap prices. Even the buffet was surprisingly great quality considering it was $12.99

WOW.  Everything about this place is fantastic!  As soon we (my son and I) walked in, the atmosphere was casual, exciting, chic and elegant all at the same time. Our server Elizabeth was fun, cool, efficient, attentive, genuine and beautiful through and through. The service was pretty quick and the food was out of this world. Every single thing from the burger on a "mac n cheese" bun with homemade chips to the chicken Cobb salad with their sweet Italian dressing to the tastiest onion soup I've had in the past 10 years, unique and delicious. Of course we could not go home without buying a piece of cake from their bright, eye-catching desert case to go. 
AND just when we thought it couldn't get any better, after we got home, we ate the huge piece of confetti cake made by their famous pastry chef. OMG....you have no idea...to die for.  All in all the most pleasant dining experience we have had in many years. DO NOT miss the chance to enjoy this fabulous outstanding establishment.

Hubby and I wanted to see get away from our Resort and see what the strip had to offer...We entered Salty Island.Ordered adult beverages which were tasty! Then decided to try entrees on the menu hubby crablegs n shrimp...me shrimp n grits!! The food was flavorful and portions were plenty.We were very satisfied for $$$ and social distancing atmosphere!!

Been going to El Charro Cafe for years for lunch and dinner but was never in the bar. 

The bar...go to the bar. 3-6 pm happy hour every day.  The cheesecrisp with grilled poblano green Chile's is excellent and goes well with any margarita but the margarita made with Casamigos tequila made by our two favorite two bartenders Jerry and Robert is off the charts!  Of all the places to go when downtown we continue to gravitate to this place.

Went there twice in one day on a recent business trip.   Had the Bill Clinton Presidential Plate the first time, then Carne Seca tacos the second time with a margarita.    Outstanding!   I will be back.
Cafe Amelie is beautiful! The Bloody Mary was one of the best I've ever had, and my catfish sandwich was delicious. The service was also fantastic.

This joint was on point!  Delicious chicken stew (Pollo Asado) on top of the red beans and rice, was a hit with the  family.  The sauce from the bistec ensabollado along with the rice could be a meal in itself.  Portions were enough to   have lunch the next day.  Brought me back to eating in the down home spot back in Northern Jersey.  The pernil is next on my list of things to have there.  Excellent family owned establishment that has even better food.  Tomàs knew everything about the dishes and was helpful throughout dinner ensuring we were settled in alright.  The empanadas were freshly made to order as well as the plantains.  We caught them before closing, (my apologies) and still didn't feel rushed even as we spoke about their one year anniversary coming up.  We wish nothing but the best for their business and family!  Thanks for a great experience, we'll be back soon.

My husband and I ate here on Nov.4th 2014.  Draft beer $2 a pitcher and the best pizza ever.  We had the "Reginelli's Gumbo pizza.  the toppings are Andouille sausage, spicy smoked tomato sauce, crystal hot sauce marinated shrimp, roasted egg plant, pickled okra and the holy trinity.   So So good.

The servers were great! The food was incredible! The atmosphere was very romantic! It was our first time to Nashville and this was a perfect place for a romantic evening with my wife! I highly recommend the restaurant for everyone and anyone!

Service is great and the restaurant looks nice but the quality of the food is subpar. Came here with the family for a birthday and everything was very salty. It's like they dumped a cup of salt onto every plate
Love the atmosphere!  Food is great!  Service is also top notch.  Expect to wait a while.

My daughter and I were out and about for a daddy-daughter date. She needed a dress for homecoming. I love my daddy-daughter dates and searched for a good place for lunch. She is 14 now, and still loves hanging out with her old man. Go us.

The menus here is a bit on the small side, but that is about what you would expect from a fast casual place. I would have liked to have seen  build your own options, and add ons like Guac. 

The problem with build your own is that it slows things down and this place was already pretty busy. Guac, Sour Cream, and other adds on though would have been nice.

Also missing here is a salsa bar with various kinds of salsa. The only options here are a house salsa and a couple others that are in large squeeze bottles up at the main counter.

I wanted to try a few options, I had their Texican,the Brisket and the Fajita. My daughter had the bacon egg and cheese from their breakfast menu, which they serve all day.

Being that I am a Texan, now transplanted in Idaho, anything that says Texan on it is a no brainier or me.  This place might as well had something on the menu that said "Phillip, this is the one you will order so get on up here and put your thing down,"

My daughter raved about her breakfast Burrito. I took a bite, and it was good, but not really any better or worse than any other breakfast burrito I have had. I think by daughter raved so much because she was hungry and had always shunned Breakfast Burrito. 

Its like trying a food for the first time that you had always turned your nose up at. Once you tried it, you wondered where it had been all your life. 

For me Id give it a 5.

The Texican was good. I could not place the favor of the meat, but I liked it. My only real complaint on this one was that there was not near enough meat. It was a bit like that old commercial, "Wheres the beef".

But I did like it. Due to the beef being MIA, Id give it a 4.

Next up in the batting order was the Brisket. In no universe could this be called Brisket. It looked and tasted like Roast. It had no flavor at all, and for me, was a huge miss. On my 1 to 10 scale, I give this one a -3

Now for the big winner. This one saved the day for this place and won me over. The Fajita taco was outstanding. The chicken was a bit dry, but it was flavorful, and spicy. It packed some heat which for anyone from Texas that loves spice, is a win win win win win.

On my scale, this one gets an 8.

If it was not for the Fajita, this place would unfortunately be a failure. I had to downgrade by review to only 3 stars due to all the other negatives. 

I will be back for the Fajita taco for sure.

Tried out this Italian place for my birthday meal.  The service is impeccable. We received a long speech about several items on the menu and the attention continued.  The owner came out and greeted us as well.  Everything is made from scratch. 
      My family enjoyed our dinner. Salads and bread were very good.  Chicken Marsala sauce lacked wine taste.  Chicken was good, according to my Wife and Daughter. My Shrimp Fradiavlo was tasty.  I am still partial to Joey's as the Italian food leader. The shrimp was fresh.  Will we return? I'm not sure.  I think as a regular stop for dinner, likely not.
Soggy wings , salty philly smh the worst wings I ever had in Tampa. Idk how they still in business . Gross food. Oh yeah horrible customer service as well to match the horrible food

Been here one other time as friends told us that it was great bar food. It is. I love the fried pickles, right up there with the best pickles I ever had(the Avenue). We had the wings, my husband loved them and now his go to place when he wants wings. Lots of TVs with sports on if you want to catch the game. Tough when you are on a diet but if you know it's bar food you don't expect low cal options. Servers always fast to greet you and bring you drinks
Ask for Jimika! Great service and excellent food. Had the red beans and rice with blackened chicken. It was cooked perfect.
I went when this establishment first opened and found it a bit over priced. The food was delicious. Seating was odd, had to sit at the food prep bar. Will try again.

Being a NYer I'm incredibly picky with my pizza... This place is amazing!

I've been on a diet for at least 5-6mo....I think I just gained all that weight back from eating all the random slices being brought around.  :-P

The pizzas come in any variation you can think of,  they are freshly made,  and you can tell.

You can request a pie,  and choose how many slices you want,  and what's left gets walked around, meaning you get to try the various flavours that have been requested by other diners.

The pizza DO NOT. sit on a hot bed to rot, like you'd see/expect from Ci Ci's.

They have only been open for a few weeks, but this place is already getting packed.

It is kid friendly
$8.99 per adult 
pizza, salad, and a drink, all endless, I think that's a good deal. :-)

I will definitely be going back, and bringing along some friends. :-)

This place is my go to all you can eat sushi! It's great for large parties and it's also BYOB! I've been coming here for the past 10 years celebrating birthdays, graduations, and going away parties! This restaurant does take reservations, so if you do have a large party on a weekend, I'd recommend making reservations in advance to avoid any long waits. 

The cost per person ranges from $30-35 after too and tax depending on if you come on a weekday versus weekend. You're given a kitchen menu (appetizers) and a sushi menu, where you list the quantity of what you want. They have a great selection of appetizers and soup options in additional to tons of sashimi, hand rolls, & sushi rolls. 

MOST of the time, the sashimi is fresh / good - however, there has been instances where some of the sashimi isn't as fresh; but generally we've had great experiences here and have always been coming back here! So if you're looking for a All You Can Eat sushi restaurant, I highly recommend Sushi Kingdom in Marlton, NJ!

The service is mediocre, some days it can be better, but if they are busy with a full restaurant and a long wait, expect a delay in getting your dishes and less attention from the waitresses.

Mi Linh is delicious!  My husband and I love Vietnamese, but usually stick to the places that we know- Grand area and Mai Lee.  We happened upon Mi Linh and were pleasantly surprised.  These are the best spring rolls either of us have had...by far.  I had the curry chicken, which was perfect!  It had the perfect amount of heat and sweet- delicious!  

Service was great too.  We will definitely be back!

The Eagle is a nice place in Downtown Indianapolis. My dad suggested that we go there on my last day in Indy because it has the best fried chicken in the city. I will say that though I enjoyed the food, I wouldn't say it's the best fried chicken that I've ever had and the overall experience was just okay. My dad, bother and I all ordered the fried chicken sandwich with a side of Mac and cheese and fries. My dad and brother had the bourbon punch and I had the eagle tea which is a play off of a Long Island iced tea. Some things that made this experience average is though the hostess was pleasant, when it was requested to sit in a booth, she sat us on one side of a booth that had a wobbly table. When our server arrived, I asked if it was possible to use the full booth and two tables and asked if the expectation was to share the booth with new guests. We were able to move how we liked, but coming from hospitality, the employees of the restaurant should anticipate the guest needs. Also, our server could've been a tad more attentive. Again, food was decent, but I wouldn't say good enough to really want to go again. I'd go if I was invited by someone else, but not necessarily from my own desire.

I disagree with most of the negative reviews below and I frequently visit this location. It's a chain salad restaurant, not sure what y'all are expecting. At this store, they have friendly service and all the fruit/veggies are fresh. I typically get the Sophie with green goddess dressing.

I went here just to try it out. I had the country fried steak dinner the steak was very good and moist mashed potatoes are decent my wife had the fried chicken special the chicken was beautiful my seasoned and was moist on the inside the staff was friendly I love the selection of pies will come back for sure

My second time here and service is still slow. the last time was take out and that was slow too, primarily due to new staff. A month later, service is even slower!
The burgers are good and well priced. I'd still go back to Bobby flay in a jiffy

Costera wasn't busy on a rainy Sunday night.  We had a reservation and were seated immediately.  The Spanish sunset cocktail ($12) resembled a French 75.  
Four of us shared dinner.  Service was a combination of our waiter and the owner/sommelier.  Our dishes included:

Blistered Shishito Peppers with Arbequina and Maldon   10
Cumin Roasted Cauliflower with Yogurt and Mint   9
Octopus a La Plancha with Heirloom Bean and Herb Salad   17
Scallops a La Plancha with Saffron Fideos and Bacon   16
Seafood Paella with Shrimp, Clams, Calamari and Mussels   26/person

The octopus consisted of a single medium-sized tentacle, which seemed skimpy, although the bean and herb salad helped to fill out the dish.  
Seafood paella was fair.  It contained a lot of shells, but that's shrimp, clams, and mussels, isn't it?  

We washed our meal down with a bottle of 
Mencia, Raul Perez "Ultreia, Saint Jacques" 2016 Bierzo  55

Overall, ambiance exceeded food, partly because of portion size.  It was a good meal and I'm glad we ate there, but there are many other NOLA restaurants I'd try before returning.

I have tried Portillos before in Chicago and really enjoyed my meal so I was looking forward to trying the Brandon location.  I tried to come in on a Saturday right after opening but it was way too crowded, so my husband and I came back for a week day lunch.

The inside is a bit overwhelming.  I was confused about where to go to order, but once I figured it out - service was quick and friendly.  We had a really time finding a table and there were people everywhere.

I went for an Italian beef sandwich with fries.  It was  definitely a tasty sandwich.  My husband got one of their specialty hot dogs and enjoyed it.  These are the main Chicago type items on the menu but they also have an array of salads and other foods to munch on.

So why the 3 star review?  I just don't get the hype.  Yeah, the food is good and the atmosphere is fun, but this place seems to always be insanely crowded and the food we have sampled is not really something to write home about.  While I really enjoyed the home grown feel of the Chicago location, this one just doesn't have that feel.  Will I be back?  Probably - but hoping some of the hype dies down and I don't have to fight for a table!

This place single handedly kept me eating greens during the work week! Fresh and delicious salads--my favorite is the avocobbo + steak + goat cheese instead of the blue. Love that you can order online and pop in to pick up, because I could always find somewhere to "park legally" for 5-10 min to pick it up rather than stalking people for parking forever (Clayton, I love you, but you need more free parking).

Why the 4 stars instead of 5? Like others have mentioned, it's quite expensive. It's a once a month splurge kind of a place, rather than a daily choice.

A friend who visited Nashville before we did recommended the spot to us, and we are so happy she did. We really love tacos, but we're both picky about them. Everything we had here was amazing and so incredibly inexpensive! The place filled up fast and I could see it being difficult to find seating for a big party, but it was a great outing for just the two of us as a date night. Staff was really friendly, even when there was a mixup with our order because another guest grabbed our tamales by mistake. Far and away our favorite place that we ate in Nashville.

Food was good when we finally got. They are still understaffed.  Great on food but overall just too long of a wait.  

Their comeback sauce is good stuff. It is like a horseradish sauce to dip your fries in.  Definitely must try 

Burger and wings were also good

I admit I've always felt odd visiting East Nashville to grab a burrito at Nuvo. There I am, Mrs. Suburb-Mom - generally sporting a tee, jeans, and ponytail or a preppy summer dress - sometimes with my suit-and-tie husband fresh from his 9-5 downtown - mingling with the hipster-glasses-wearing, skinny-jeans-clad, wild-haired youngsters.
Sweetly, the owners and employees (I like the young guy with the faux-hawk thingy) always make me feel like one of the "cool kids". I used to try various menu items until I got the 90210 (minus artichoke hearts - yuck), and I haven't strayed since. I'll concede that it's a bit greasy sometimes, but hey.. what goat-cheese-laden, hot, delicious comfort food isn't greasy?! My husband always gets the Berkeley. Every once in a while we splurge on some cheese dip; it's pretty good - not the best I've ever had but totally hits the spot if I'm craving that. The salsa is just so-so in my opinion.. But really, if I wanted perfect salsa I'd go to a Mexican joint. This place is all about the quesadillas and burritos. Oh, and the new Charlotte Pike location is way closer AND they have always had FREE cinnamon sugar tortillas when we've visited. :-)
I'll agree that the music is obnoxious, and the videos are weird. But I'm not really a music nerd so I don't mind as long as I can keep shoveling great food into my face.
For my life I can't imagine how people keep getting soggy burritos: in over 2 dozen trips neither my husband nor I have ever had this experience. And concerning the price, I will gladly pay $1.50-$2 more for a burrito made fresh in front of me with quality ingredients, and made my local folks in a local business. As a small biz owner myself, it means a lot to me to support people who are doing a great job and employing their neighbors and peers. Go Nuvo!
This restaurant has consistently good food and large portions.  The prices are reasonable, and the service is always friendly.  I especially like the Greek inspired dishes.

Pumpkin - I really wanted you to be in my top restaurants in the city, unfortunately it was not the case. The place is small and you are sitting awfully close to the people next to you, but that's the case in most place in the city these days. I got the strip steak which came with maitake mushrooms and root vegetables. The steak itself was pretty tasty and flavorful but it literally came with one tiny piece of potato, one piece of mushroom and one small piece of carrot and they were not exactly flavorful. I would suggest sautéing the vegetables so they can complement the steak better. Also for $30 for that entrée, it was definitely a little overpriced, don't get me wrong the steak was good, but for that price I expected better. Overall my experience was pretty average, I guess I had my hope way too high. Oh just a little head's up its BYOB and Cash only.

I am so glad to finally see a Thai place in the Norristown/KOP/Collegeville area.  It's BYOB, which is even better.

The restaurant is housed in a cute house, with a wrap-around porch.  The inside has a friendly cafe vibe upon entering, and the dining room has a spa-like ambiance.

The food is good.  I didn't realize that they were related to Chingmai in Conshy, which was a stable lunch spot for me when I worked in Conshy.  They have great pad thai, which is a must for me at a Thai Restaurant.

I'd definitely come back.  I think it would be great do dine al fresco on the porch in the summer.

Great experience, food was fresh and super
Tasty! Cooking the steak over rock is a cool experience to anyone who hasn't tried it and you can cook it to your satisfaction. I am a steak lover so this was fun. I decided to cut it in 1/2 so I can enjoy each half nice and hot. Make sure not to leave the shrimps on too long as they can over cook and taste rubbery. We have a great time every time we visit this location.

I had to choose between this place and another place and honestly only chose this one because of the design and atmosphere. Once I ordered and ate my food I was ECSTATIC with the choice. Delicious, fresh and fulfilling food. Happy I stumbled into this place and will definitely be back and recommend to my vegan and non-vegan friends :)

I honestly wanted to give this place zero stars!!! I waited over an hour for a well done steak and it comes to the table COLD!! Both the steak and fries were cold. The waiter was cold.  He avoided our table for a good 30 min.  I was at the point of almost walking out.  

Please try another restaurant!  Do not waste your time nor money coming in here. I've been here for two hours HUNGRY AS HELL!  Very disappointed.  Willie's Chicken here i come!!!

By the way. Our server's name was Chris.  Avoid his section if you can. He's gonna twirl around the whole restaurant without checking in on you. If you have a problem he is definitely not coming back.
Loved this place ... stopped in for a snack and had the queso and the parm fries topped with crab ... both were outstanding!! Also the Cajun mules were delicious!!

This location is not wheelchair accessible, no buttons to open the door. I'm not sure about other locations but I'm a senior caregiver & attempting to push my client in the door was extremely difficult. The walkway leading to the door itself is narrow and obstructed by pillars. I turned around to leave out of disappointment & frustration, but a customer inside ran to help me .. long before an employee came. I love A&W but this alone is enough to make me never return to this location again. With or without my client who is in a wheelchair !

Find your way to this local favorite to enjoy awesome po-boys (the roast beef is the best), debris fries, and the best frozen Irish coffee I've had (my friends who don't like coffee like this drink). The staff is friendly and the environment is true to a New Orleans neighborhood place. I recommend eating in the bar area for the best experience.

Let me start out by saying that I LOVED this place and I am honestly very sad to give them a poor review, but there is good reason for this which I will get to in just a moment. Their food selection is very diverse (same with the beer list!) and has never been anything short of excellent, the atmosphere is very cool and low key and the service has always been on point at both the restaurant, the bar and the pick-up room. We would frequent this place on a regular basis, until our latest experience this past Friday. 

My fiance' and I were here on Friday, 8/7/15, and we had a server by the name of Jack. Jack was a strange guy- he seemed way too comfortable with us right from the get-go calling me baby and stealing french fires off of our plates when he would come to check on us. It was a little uncomfortable, but we just chalked it up to him being overly confident/friendly/comfortable as my fiance and I are pretty friendly, down-to-Earth people and easy to have fun with. All was well and good until the end of the night when we had asked for a to-go bag. Jack brought them over to us and wrapped up my food and then my fiance's. He asked what my fiance's name was and I told him. Thinking he was writing his name on the bag, he set the bag down in front of us and walked away. He wrote "DICKHEAD Thanks for eating at Rons!!" on my fiance's to-go bag. WTF?!? SERIOUSLY??? Joking or not, that is NOT cool. The picture of the bag is posted here as well.

Needless to say, we were both fuming. We found the floor manager, Steve, and told him about it right away and showed him the bag. Steve looked at me in disbelief and I told him this way over the line and uncalled for. I explained that we are all about having fun with people, but this was completely inappropriate and that Jack did not know us at all to be joking around with us in that sort of a way. Steve said he understood and I asked him what was going to be done about it and he replied that this will cost Jack his job and then we were ushered out the door. No profuse apology or offer to comp our meal or speak to the owner, etc. 

Your employee just blatantly insulted a regular-visiting, paying customer by calling him a dickhead on paper and all we received was a non-concerned apology and were showed the door. Not satisfied with the way this handled, I called back and spoke with a female manager. She did apologize to us more than once which we appreciated and told us that this was unacceptable but we didn't need to hear the obvious stated again- the option to allow us to speak with the owner, comp our meal, or follow-up as to how this would be handled would have been the right way to handle this. Very disappointing and we won't be back.
Because I can't give less than a one star. A coating of grime on everything, hamburger poor quality, hundreds of other places to eat instead of here.

The food is good but not great. Portions on all dishes except for the ravioli were large and the ravioli was adequate. We could have split the other dishes and had plenty. 

We were seated promptly and the service was good. Drinks were refilled regularly. 

The prices were on the high end and seemed high for the experience and quality of food.

Worst customer service, once visited the restaurant during evening, waited for around half an hour for order then to surprise worst taste of food and very less quantity. Not worth the price and time. I wouldn't recommend anyone to go there again.

We have been trying to get in here for a few weeks now.  The buzz and reviews have been very good.  Last time we tried to stop in it was full with large tables and had a 2.5 hour wait.  We were not prepared to wait that long but this time we had a plan to go somewhere elsebut then come to find out when we got there they are taking reservations now so give them a call before heading there.  

As i mentioned the buzz has been very good.  The food loos delicious so we were excited.  

We didn't exactly have reservations but were told that if we could be done in 1.5 hours we could have a table that was reserved for 8pm.  We decided to chance it.  

Looking over the menu everything sounded so good.  Our server was someone we knew so we trusted her suggestions on wine parings and food.

We started with their version of a wedge salad. Very tasty with lots of great flavors. 

Next we decided on the scallops and pasta. This was the chef's selection. Both were cooked perfectly. Very tasty dish. 

Finally we had the Steak. It was cooked perfectly. Loved the presentation. Side of corn risotto was delicious

We had our server suggest wine for each course and she was spot on. A really great experience.
Excellent drinks and food, sometimes line is a little long but well worth the  wait. A welcome addition to my childhood neighborhood.
This place is amazing. The tortillas are next level. I recommend the Yaqui taco and the Sonoran Hot Dog.

I have eaten here a few times and get take out for their wings pretty regularly. The wings are great if you get them well done. I have also had the nachos which are so good! The French onion soup is also very good. The only thing I didn't like was the sliders which I only ordered once. Overall this is a solid place

Food was ok. Service was subpar, and they started closing an hour before they closed. Literally vacuumed under my table and were changing out condiments while we were eating. There are far superior places in Boise to spend your money.

Stay away from this place!! 9:00pm on a Sunday and the absolute Worst service ever. They were not even busy! I now know why! We ordered BBQ wings and they were so spicy we couldn't eat them! Our curly fries tasted like they had been sitting in the kitchen for 2 hours. Impossible to get a beer or soft drink refill. Our waitress was more concerned about her phone and the guys working in the kitchen than her job. The bartender did nothing but talk on the phone the entire time we were there. WHERE is the management???? This place needs closed ASAP! We will never go back!

Good, fresh food. Ordered the Croque Monsieur. Could be a tad bit crispier and less mustard but overall it was pretty good. Salad was crisp and rverythibg tasted fresh. Service was excellent and the food came out fast! Fir the price its a good value. I will be back when I'm in the area.
Cute little spot for coffee and breakfast! The pumpkin spice latte was delicious for a cool rainy fall morning, and the breakfast burrito was wonderful. Would definitely recommend to a friend.

I am a sucker so I bought a Groupon - but silly me - I didn;t read the not-so-fine print and the groupon was for DINNER ONLY.  Thank goodness they honored it at lunch but you had to order off the dinner menu (no cheapie lunch specials for the groupon.).

That was fine by me.
I started my meal with an OK version of Tom Kha Gai (Thai Chicken Coconut Soup).  This is my favorite soup ever so I have to say this version was very nice - not too sweet and not overly rich with too much coconut milk.  4 stars.

An iceberg salad (gloppy ginger dressing on the side) came next.  Meh.  Fine.  There was ONE cherry tomato and ONE cucmber slice buried at the bottom. Whatever.

Next I got a specialty sushi roll (I can;t remember which one - I think it was the Lotus Inn Roll) that was just OK.  The sushi fish here is just OK.  Not bad and not great.  I also got an order of sake (salmon) sashimi ($6.50 for 3 thin slices) which I never should have gotten.  Meh.

For $14.95 I expect more than an alaskan roll with a few slivers of Escolar on top.  Escolar is NOT white tuna.  Albacore is white tuna. Thank goodness I remembered to get the sauce on the side.  Fish was good - but not superb. 


But whatdya expect?
Meanwhile the party of 6 next to were raving about their chicken & brocolli and shrimp chow mein.

Maybe I oughta stick to cooked foods here.
Or the Salmon Lovers Lunch ($14.95) which I have gotten a few times.

Atmoshpere is relaxing.

Fact: one of the few places to get brisket in town that's worth anything. 

Opinion: absolutely the very best BBQ in Greater Nashville area. 

This is the hidden gem of south Nashville!

Placed an order and my husband went to pick it up on the time provided and apparently got treated with a bad attitude. "It will be ready in a minute!!!!" My husbands like "I was just letting them know I was here." Oh my ‍ I do think they should treat their customers a little better. When I go in I don't think they are overly nice.

My wife, our daughter, our grandson (4 months old) and I went to a local farmers market in the morning and decided we needed something to eat for lunch!  Decision, decisions....Elle (wife) looks up local restaurants and food-joints in the area and sees Hooters is very close among other places; Here's my logic....I was invited 16 years ago when I married my wife to go to Hooters for my stag night, but we ended up not going....And let's face it the 4 month year old grandson loves boobs, that's where his lunch comes from.

Anyhow, you may think it sounds wrong and seedy but it definitely wasn't.  We had a wonderful waitress called Hannah, who was friendly and helpful and made sure we were all happy with the service and our food.  I had Chicken salad, our daughter had Chicken wings and curly fries, and Elle had a burger with curly fries.  All the food was delicious and served quickly.  Yes, you wouldn't really think that Hooters is a good place to take a child, but it turned out to be a very good choice.  It turned out to be some of the best food of our two week holiday!

I've eaten at Horn's several times over the past two years, almost exclusively for brunch, and they have never disappointed me. I cannot for the life of me figure out why they aren't super busy every weekend morning. Sometimes we can just go in and the place is practically empty.
Do NOT order any of the noodle dishes, the noodle dishes are cooked to the point of being mush, and then are covered with goopy sauces.

My one experience at HUB for a late lunch was so-so. Service was adequate, but not good (just WHO exactly was our server, anyway? we were traded off-and-on through every step of our meal so that we had no idea), and two out of three meals were OK (the one that seemed best, my friend's chicken pot pie, she now remembers not as fondly as it seemed at the time). 

The atmosphere of the place is fantastic, and the ice cream is truly outstanding, so I do have high hopes that things have/will improve and will update this review after my next visit...

Amazing. Great drinks and food (appetizers and entrees)  was awesome. Prices were right. Good size portions. Great neighborhood atmosphere and best of all, kids are welcome.  My favorites: crabcake entree and tuna appy and the crab dip was great too.  We will be going back again and again!
Ate there again and it was not up to par. Also, the wine glasses are almost less than half full which is very disappointing. They should either get smaller glass or make the portions a little larger.

This was a great find! The pasta was delicious! They have the best spicy marinara I've ever had. My parents are visiting from up north and we were just passing by and decided to stop in here for dinner. I'm so glad we did! They also give you fresh warm bread when you come in which is always nice. The staff was so friendly too they gave us some really good appetizer recommendations! We loved the mozzarella and peppers.
Food is very good and many items not on your typical Greek tourist trap menu. The owner is always there and the staff are on their toes as a result. Try the Greek meatballs, excellent

They yelled at us for sitting in. Reserved table after telling us to sit anywhere. The rest of the dinner was equally disorganized. The apology we received was pretty annoying because it wasn't for the miscommunication but rather for the fact that the reserved table was never used after all. The food was overpriced.
This place is the *slowest* coffee shop I have ever been to. The coffee was fine, unremarkable. But the pace was like a slow motion movie.
Not the ordinary fast-food pizza place. The modern interior of this restaurant is so instagramable. I'll surely come back again for their artisan pizza with upscale toppings.
Just grabbed a jerk chicken combo, everything was fresh, chicken was moist but still had a crisp to the litter layer. A must have if you are in the area!

The reason for five stars-Gringo's is consistently good.  Every time I have come here, the food and drink have always met my expectations.  Tonight at the bar Sam took care of us and we never lacked for anything.  From the chorizo dip to the taco salad, everything was outstanding. 

Yes, I'll be back.

Our waiter was fantastic, super great with communication, and although he was busy , he made didn't have a rushed vibe at all!
Clam chowder was amazing and the teak salad 10/10 recommend! 
My sweet potato fries were cold , but there was a party of close to 20 right before us , so I think that just kind of messed up our foods timing.
Others at my table had the shrimp po boy, kids cheeseburger (which was the size of a normal cheeseburger!), and the fish and chips. Also had a side of the whipped potatoes which were good !

The fries were yummy and homemade. The burgers were very tasty and a great alternative to eating at fast food chains. Prices are good, but the ones on the photo here on yelp must be old because it wasn't that inexpensive. My peanut butter milkshake was yummy!I never would have found this place if I did not see it on Yelp , I would definitely come back.
Good food but not great.  Plastic utensils made eating a little difficult.  The staff was very friendly.  Keep in mind it is cafeteria style.  Overall happy I ate here.

Not all chains are created equal, and Chipotle does a solid job of offering more healthful options than its competition.  

Our fave is the vegetarian fajita bowl, ordered with extra black beans, extra rice, corn salsa, hot salsa and guacamole.  Squeeze some fresh lime (near the soda fountain)  over all and you are good to go.  If we are feeling particularly decadent, we may ask for the cheese and sour cream.  A bowl is more than enough for two meals.   

Both the black beans and guacamole could be better spiced and the salsas should be zippier.   When your repertoire is as limited as Chipotle, every item should be exceptional.
The food was delicious and flavorful! I ordered my food through UberEats and I'm so happy my food was hot and came with utensils!

I have been to Juniper twice and the cocktail list was certainly the highlight of both visits. The Hipster is my favorite (despite the name) and I enjoyed their signature gin and tonic as well as the Southside. 

We had a reservation for Valentine's Day and were disappointed with the table because it was right next to the drafty window and door and was shared with another couple. The fries were a wonderful appetizer and I thought the bison meatball pasta was decent. My husband ordered a tenderloin off of the specials menu, however he had to change his order when we were later notified that it had run out. 

The atmosphere is nice and the bartenders were great. Overall it was good.

It's a pub! How can you go wrong with a pub? Sure, it's no haute cuisine, but what are you gonna do? 

Hubby and I came here on a Saturday night and sat outside. Staff was really friendly and helpful when we asked for another table that was a little less dark. 

We had the cheese steak spring rolls. I thought it was a really creative way to mix two totally different dishes. Definitely nice as a snack. Then I ordered the meat lovers pizza, which was really tasty! All I'm thinking is they should serve it on a normal plate instead of a cake platform lol. My husband had a burger and fries, which I believe was just OK as he didn't know that bacon etc. was an add-on. 

Overall, nothing wrong with it. There was live music going on, and it was just what we needed for the night.

With dozens of restaurants in this high end mall area why come to Mission BBQ? That's a great question. There's plenty of good spots nearby - almost too many good ones to choose from. On the other hand, for BBQ Mission is the go-to spot. Mission is no longer a secret, though. Their locations litter the East Coast - and greater Philly area. 

Fortunately, their quality hasn't plummeted with expansion. The BBQ is better than average and consistent, at least has been in the two dozen locations we've been to. Why Mission? Take into account the food isn't cheap (but you shouldn't expect it to be). Nevertheless, there isn't a meat on the board that doesn't hit your plate better than average. A meal here (and we tried about everything) is much better than chains like Famous Dave's, Smokey Bones and Dickey's.  

Mission doesn't have table service. Visitors walk to the cashier, order and have their food in minutes (but they do clean up after you, even though we decline and throw our own trash away). The chore can be choosing a meat. In our more than a dozen visits to different locations we've opted to pile on most of their meats (brisket, pulled pork, turkey, chopped chicken, regular & jalapeno sausage, back back ribs and spare ribs) and opt for the XXL Combo (where you can choose three meats). 

There hasn't been a meat we didn't enjoy. The pulled pork, chicken (doesn't come on the bone - it's pulled) and brisket were good enough to eat without sauce sometimes, but I wouldn't recommend it. The turkey can be a challenge here (it's sometimes dry) but the sausage packs flavor. 

There's an impressive variety of sauces available. There's a flavor for everyone and while some are average, others are awesome, like the Smoky Mountain, Bay-B-Que and KC Classic, which were my favorites. For you first timers here's a list of the bottles we found on our table (and across from the drink station). 

  Memphis Belle
  Smoky Mountain
  Texas Twang
  KC Classic
  Alabama White
  Bay-B-Que
  Tupelo Honey Heat
  Carolina Vinegar
  Georgia Mustard
 
We only tried two of the sides and the cornbread, which is as sweet as cake. The french fries were clearly hand cut and well seasoned and the beans are worth ordering, too, although we prefer them well done and request it that way. The downfall: their side salad is poor. It comes with iceberg lettuce (yawn). Change it to mixed greens, kale, romaine, etc, and it'd be a good as the BBQ. 

If you're in the neighborhood shopping - and eat meat - this is a good lunch or dinner spot. There's something for every - meal lover - here. And, an open parking spot with your name on it.

Excellent! I've lived in south-east Asia for 22 years and this is some of the best quality, most authentic Malay / Thai / Indian fusion food I've had in the United States. The Roti prata and Roti canai were excellent in texture and quality. The beef rendang curry was melt in your mouth tender and the chicken satay appetizer had excellent flavors. Two in our group had the Kue Thaow soup and raved about the superior and complex flavors. Excellent and friendly service was another plus! Wish I lived nearby - I would come here ALL the time!
This place is excellent. The people who work here are very nice. No problem coming solo they welcome you.  Beer is cold and food is very good. They deserve 5 stars but I give too many of them out.

We took our Daughter and Grandson there last night and enjoyed ourselves.  The espresso crusted beef medallions was tender and tasty.  My question is, why do you have to ask for bread rather than it just being brought to the table like every other restaurant?  After I asked (seeing other tables with baskets of bread) we got some that came when our food was served.

Best restaurant in Philadelphia. Unpretentious, fresh food that's aggressively seasoned. AKA, food with huge balls. Fantastic menu options, great philosophy, great service and BYOB. Grab the dips of the day and whatever else sounds good to you. It's all delicious. Food isn't meant to be eaten wearing ties atop a white table cloth. Praise everything that this place exists to keep proper food perspective alive. If you want to be pampered while eating fluffed up "cuisine", head to Avance. Oh, wait....Avance is closed...
Celebrating @NickyP901 's #Birthday at her favorite Restaurant here in Tucson. Pasta, Chicken, Trout, Brussel Sprouts, Wine, & an awesome Desert Platter.
Nothing we had tonight was less than amazing! I will recommend this place to any and everyone. Cool vibes and our server Jackson was super knowledgeable and helpful with every question we had!
Love coming to eat here. The oysters are great. I always get them raw. My family and I are always well taken care of when we go!

Crack thy name is Hope's Cookies!

Now sugar is my one true vice, and more often than not it comes in the form of a cookie. I've probably eaten 3 times my weight in cookies during my life, so I have a pretty vaste frame of reference when I say that Hope's Cookies are the best cookies...ever! Look no further than the Kahlua-infused White Russian cookie.

To be fair, the punk colleged-aged employees can sometimes have an attitude, but I guess I would too if I was constantly being taunted by the unrealistic temptation of constant cookies.

If you get your Hope's Cookies fix at the Reading Terminal, you might like to know that the storefront has about twice as many cookie varieties as they have at the Terminal.

So I suppose after eating little beyond dusty cliff bars while camping in the desert for over a week, anything would have tasted good, but I still think Sterling's was amazing. 

We kept it simple-- steaks. Mine was a medium rare filet. My dining companion got his pepper-crusted and with a cognac demi glaze. Both were incredible. We added the fontina mac and cheese to our meal, which was piping hot and crusty on top. 

No cocktail menu to speak of, so I hesitantly ordered any kind of champagne cocktail and the bartender happily obliged. 

The service was supreme, and we had a memorably delicious meal!
Flat beer. Undercooked burgers. Disintegrating buns cold from the refrigerator.. When all you sell is burgers and  beer,  this is a problem.

Good food, not as much wait time as other hot chicken spots.  The hot chicken isn't the best in town, but it's more than serviceable.  The Deconstructed Cobb Salad is excellent, and will be my go-to meal when they open their Donelson location.
This place has decent food, it was our first time here and we really liked the service. We got different plates to try out different dishes and everything was excellent.

I can't get enough of this incredible cuisine! Not only is it filling but always makes me feel like I have tons of energy and is guilt free! I love all their gluten free options and their accommodating staff! Highly recommend if you are a local or visiting Santa Barbara! Try their Matcha for an extra energy boost in your day!

Delish!  I love all of their pasta dishes.  My favs are the spaghetti confetti and pollo Milano.  I drive up from bradenton just to eat here.  Nice wine list and good cocktails.  If you get here early, you can miss the crowd.  Otherwise, be prepared to wait at bar area or outside.

Stopped there Sunday, 6/21/2020 for a family meal and get this.  They had NO CHICKEN NOR MEATLOAF. In fact the only meat that had were PORK RIBS. My family doesnt even eat pork.
Now this was a 1st.  A home style restaurant with NO meat prepared on a Sunday no less

Ate here with coworkers after a conference at Loews around the corner.  It was absolutely delicious.  We ordered the spiced ribs and bacon wrapped dates.  The presentation and taste were spectacular.  Ordered the chicken dish and it was perfect.  I had the white chocolate cheesecake and it was amazing.  5 stars for sure.

I love McShea's. This is definitely my favorite bar in the area around SJU's campus. It's so much closer than Manayunk and it's an easy train ride away (no cab needed). That being said, it's not really a college bar-- it's Narberth, I'm not surprised, but the crowd tends to be more middle-agers than young professionals. The bar has a great cozy vibe and the back room is great to bring a group of people. However, I find the wait service tends to be a little slow for larger parties-- I tend to go early and start my own tab at the bar, because that's much faster. Some of the bartenders are really quite friendly as well.

The beer selection is really quite good and varied; there is a beer card called the "Full Fifty" or something-- if you finish the list, you get a pint glass with your name on it. It's a great incentive to try new beers. But the prices tend to be more "city" prices than what you would expect to find in a small town. Again, I'm not surprised-- a lot of the beer is imported (you'll find Chimay, La Fin du Monde, various Troegs etc). But remember this or you'll be extremely put out when your check comes.

A final note about the food: get the fries! They're well-battered and come with their own special mayo dip. I really don't like mayo on my fries, but I do love salty fries that are crunchy on the outside and softer on the inside. These are the fries for me.

Overall, McShea's is an enjoyable trip, especially with a group of friends. It has a great local vibe and a great selection of beer. Quizzo is not a must (it tends to vary, depending on the week).
Horrible people horrible service, I've never wanted to climb over a drive thru window more than that joke of a restaurant,

So glad to see more options in strapped tight Metairie area. 
Best in town hot and sour soup. 
Fish fillet is delicious. Pork meat balls are exactly what they make in Nanjing-China. 
Would definitely recommend this place to Chinese food enthusiasts..

You can't go wrong here.  Chicago Deep Dish pizza is to die for.  Love the sauce.  Their Sicilian pizza is awesome.  The crust is very light and crisp, not weighed down and doughy like other Sicilian pizzas.  Their wings are decent but are a little chewy.  We like our wings not so jerky like.  Their mild wing sauce was delish.  We will be back!  (The owner is extremely nice, makes you feel like you're part of the family!)

To-go order took a long time, and they messed up the rice. The walnut shrimp was practically floating in a sea of mayonnaise. It's disgusting to have to wipe each shrimp with a napkin before you eat it.

The summer rolls are disappointing; there are a couple strips of charbroiled pork and not much else - just a lot of fluff.

Went here around 11-1130am for a brunch. Ended up ordering a hot chicken sandwich with a Caesar salad. 

The Caesar salad was pretty good- I don't like a ton of dressing and their wasn't a ton on it. 

The hot chicken sandwich was very good. I liked the sauce they used and the chicken was perfectly tender with the right amount of crispiness. 

We also had mimosas and they were good. This was a reasonably priced restaurant.

Food was all cooked perfectly. Had the fries, onion rings, cilantro lime wings and house sauce wings and the gyro platter. Wings were good and meaty. They put plenty of extra sauce on the wings so dip your fries in it. The taziki sauce was fresh and after 11am you get the cucumber salad. Really good. I took home 2 desserts to share later. Strawberry cheesecake and carrot cake. It's a fun place with really good food and very nice people who are friendly, accommodating and made it a great meal.

What a shame. The food and servers were great but absolutely NO ONE was wearing a mask and we didn't realize it until we sat down. It's not only dangerous but so disrespectful to all the patrons wearing masks as we should be doing in the middle of a PANDEMIC. Will not be back. Wasn't worth it.

We hit Philly on the front end and back end of our vacation.   We hit two cheesesteak places each day.   At the end of our trip, we hit Dalessandro's and Sonny's.

At Dalessandro's, we got sharp provolone (extra, which is 5 slices instead of 3 slices normal), fried onions, and mushrooms.

Of the four cheesesteaks we tried, Delassandro's easily has the best roll.  You can tell from the first bite the roll is better than the rest.  Perfect consistency, holds the meat and juices well, and has the best flavor of any roll as part of the overall sandwich.

The meat, fr'd onions and shrooms were piled on generously.  Meat had good flavor and was moist throughout.  

A drawback, and the reason for 4 stars - even by getting extra portion of sharp provolone, the cheese got lost.  We could see it between the bread and meat, but were expecting it to be more in the taste of each bite.

Also, the mushrooms look out of a can from the grocery shelf and not grilled on the flat top.  (see attached pic.  Color and texture indicate can.)  Grilled mushrooms would take the steak to another galaxy - maybe they don't have room on the flat top for a pile of grilled mushrooms next to the meat and grilled onions...they should make room, you know?

So yeah, 5 stars on the bread, 4.6 overall,   The meat, bread, and fried onions carry this sandwich.   We got mushrooms on all four steaks we tried, and wanted to keep the ingredients consistent for an apples to apples comparison.   

A solid steak overall.   Would come back again.

Oh!   And don't believe any "they messed up my order" reviews.  They've fixed that.   They take your phone number n name (to text you when order ready if you don't hear loudspeaker).  The order taker reads your order back to you to confirm.  

Then, when you pick up, the person in the window asks your phone number to confirm, then reads your order back to you.   They get the orders right.

Went there yesterday for my daughter's Christening and the family loved it.  This is a pretty good compliment considering that we are all Italian and one of my family members owns a catering hall that spealizies in Italian meals.

The staff was great and the food was amazing like usual.  We also went home with a TON of food.  I have breakfast, lunch, and dinner for at least a week.

I have been coming here for years and never have been disappointed.

Keep up the great work, 12th and Filbert, Maggiano's!
Good bagels, mediocre everything else. I've ordered delivery a few tikes and its always kind of cold and unappealing. Won't be back for anything but bagels.

Excellent food. We shared a cheese plate. The sausage tasted just like the real deal. The Gouda nut cheese was excellent, and it was served with plenty of crackers, hummus, olive tapenade, and dried fruit. 

We both had the Impossible Burger- it tasted just like a real burger and was delicious. The sweet potato roll was very tasty.

The service was also very good, prompt without being fawning. The waitress was very personable.  It's great to find good vegan food locally, and we'll definitely be back.

We had our Rehearsal Dinner there, and it was really good. We looked at a lot of places, and this was the best value for the money.  

Scott and the others made it incredibly easy for us to arrange a dinner for 107 guests.  All we had to do was pick the menu, give them a head count, and bring some orchids to decorate.

They really kept the wine flowing, and it is was a great value for how welcome they made our guests feel.  The food was really excellent as well, but what really set them apart was the high level of service and how well the place is managed -- especially for an event.  Other notes:
- The pastas are really good.
- Great craft beer selection, including local beers.  They also rotate their selections.
- Their fish is really, really good, especially the blackened snapper.  The best fish tacos ever.
- Brunch is amazing!

| L O C A T I O N & P A R K I N G |
Right off of the popular State St and in the same building as Rebar Coffee. It's easy to miss Yankee Noodle since their sign is a banner on the wall which is laid inside of the outside patio, so look for Rebar's sign and you're in the right place.

There's a lot right next to Yankee Noodle & Rebar for another establishment but they're currently under construction and not open so it's ok to park there. However, there's a good amount of free street parking on the other side of the bridge if you don't mind a short 5 minute walk.


| D R I N K S |
YN has a great selection of beers, wines and cocktails. The inside bar is nice but sitting on the patio and sipping is even nicer.

This has one of the better beer offerings I've seen at a restaurant. I recommend Chimay Blue. (:

+ Lychee Mimosa ($10) - This wasn't served in a champagne flute and I feel like I got double the amount of a normal mimosa [score!]. It was sweet, fragrant and bubbly. I much prefer this to its oj counterpart.


| E A T S | 4/5 Stars
It's foreign to see an upcharge for levels of spiciness. And it kind of sucked that the 'basic' bowls of ramen didn't come with an egg.. another $1.50 upcharge.

[Level 0 - free | Level 1 - $0.50 | Level 2 $1.00 | Ramen Fury $1.50]

+ Level 1 Miso Ramen w/a perfect egg ($14.95)
 Not spicy at all but salty. The perfect egg though was indeed true to its name.

+ Ramen Fury Miso ($14.45)
 Disappointed in this level of spiciness. Mild in spiciness at best. This also was too salty.

+ Fried Chorizo Dumpling & Kimchi Nachos ($12.75)
 This was good! The only complaint/issue is that they ran out of kimchi and was needed to complete the taste of this dish. Also, this is not a traditional pile of tortilla chips with cheese and other toppings. (see my photo for reference)

+ Spicy Dan Dan 3 Cheese Beef & Pork Mazeman Ramen ($15.75)
 Interesting take on a popular Chinese noodle dish; it tasted nothing like the dan dan noodles I've had before but I liked where they're trying to go with it. I personally love cheese and think the more the better. But I could see why this could be too cheesy and heavy for others. 


| S E R V I C E |
5 stars for the service here! Every server we encountered was friendly but Catherine was the hero of Yankee Noodle. She made sure that we were well attended to, our water glasses were always refilled, the food was timed perfectly and even gave great recommendations for things to do in the area.

There was a small mishap of no kimchi for the nachos and my table wanted to order something else since they felt it was necessary to the dish. Catherine and her manager went above and beyond to let us order another dish we wanted and let us keep the kimchi-less nachos. I loved how the situation as handled; she was so sweet and accommodating. Big thank you's to her for making our experience great.


| O V E R A L L |
With this being a new business and all, I assume that they're still working on recipes and what not. However, a couple of months from now I fully expect YN to be one of State St's hottest spots; from their great selection of drinks and creative dishes to their amazing service. Hell, I may drive here from LA every other weekend to sit on that patio with my beer and bowl of cheesy dan dan noodles!
The Ryman is a must see if you are in town! I do wish we booked the guided tour to hear more about the history.
Nice place for quick lunch, the Itailian hoagie was delicious, just enough add on and the roll was soft and good. Seating area is very roomy and cleanl

I don't enjoy writing bad reviews, especially of a place like this.  I really want to see these locally owned non-chain restaurants have success.  In three years though, we haven't had a single smooth experience here, yet we keep coming back....because in the end, the food is (usually) pretty good, and it's never too busy.  In fact, it's a Saturday night and the place is virtually empty, starting to think that's no accident.  40 minutes passed between the arrival of our first and final orders.  Every order was wrong in some way.  The veggie burger was (for the fourth time) frozen in the middle, the grilled cheese was a burnt cheese, and all the food was in general cold and limp.  Amazing too because as the plates were being distributed, the girl warned that the kid's plates were "piping hot" due to the heat lamp they'd been sitting under for the last half hour.  Not ok.  

I get that this isn't fine dining, it's fro-yo and burgers.  None the less, consider that some people can only afford to take their family out to eat for special occasions, a few times a month at most, and they chose to spend their limited time and money at your place.  If you can't figure out how to consistently provide people with a vaguely positive experience, you won't be around for long.  It's not rocket science, a little care and some training would go a long way.

We are so excited for this new establishment!!! It's right around the corner from our home here in Seminole Heights. This concept is so unique, I've never heard of anywhere like it. We came in for lunch and got the catfish sandwich. My goodness, it was cooked to perfection!! It literally melted in my mouth as I ate it. The portion was HUGE (ended up taking half of it home). It came with crispy Cajun fries which were perfectly seasoned. Their house-made pickles are exquisite! Hopefully I can steal the recipe ;) we also had the jalepeño hush puppies with pimento cheese and those were just as amazing as the rest of our food. Everything from the sauce to the bun was delightful. Great price for 2 meals, a few sides, and a couple of drinks. The staff is super friendly and looks like they are happy to be there. Joe, the owner, was the person who took our order and he was very charming and professional. He even went out of his way to visit our cute little table in the back patio and checked in on our experience. You can tell the whole staff cares about what they do and are passionate to serve great food in the Heights! Great job!!

There is something called Kick Ass Fries! Which by the way takes up to its name. It is hand cut French fries topped with hand pulled pork, cheddar cheese, sour cream and whatever you want on it, you can ask for it. You get a good amount of fries, only for $10.95. I know that must sound a lot. But I think it is definitely my money worth.
Best Conch Fritters and Curry Goat I have ever had. Second picture is the scialatielli with shrimp clams and cauliflower.

Excellent, excellent, excellent. Authentic New York style deli eats. Better bring a big appetite to the table cause otherwise your gonna bust! Huge sandwiches and I can speak with expertise as this weekend I went on a Corvette rally and I saw over 50 of these sandwiches an a majority of people only got thru half of thier food in one sitting. Quality was top shelf with plenty of flavor. Will definAtely be back for more! Try it you'll like it!

The fish tacos were good but expensive for the portion size. Two tacos and 1/4 cup blacked beans. Crab cakes were okay but nothing spectacular. The ambiance was nice. The white sangria was good and being able to sample local craft brews on tap for the flavor was nice.

Worst food in southern Il. Corporate management doesn't care, I emailed twice no response . Server was busy with a large party of eight. He took our order delivered our food (the wrong food ) redelivered our food . Worst chicken fried steak I have ever not eaten.  Delivered check . No manager no how was your food  won't be back
Only been there for lunch, but these are some good freaking sandwiches. Great relaxed atmosphere too. Clearly Anne or whoever runs this place cares about the experience.

Had the quesadillas which were essentially cheesey big tacos. I did mix and match. The flavor is great and typical of a good side restaurant in Mexico. The atmosphere in back is nice. Def hit the spot and what I was looking for.

All three quesadillas were great! I recommend chicken tinga if you like spice. If you're less adventurous the queso one will do. 

I would have taken pics but I ate every last morsel within minutes.

Always good. The brandy milk punch is one of my favorite drinks in New Orleans, and a great addition to any brunch. We got there as they were opening at 10:30, and a long line was already forming. Despite this, our party of four was seated promptly, and well fed and out the door within an hour.

Great burger and fries! Love that it's kid friendly.  Kali was super helpful and went above and beyond to make sure we had a great experience.  We just moved here six weeks ago and it's one of our go to places so far.

This was a great place to end an evening in the Central West End! We planned on going to a few other places, but we ended up staying at Moonshine - almost til close. Fun, laid-back and a bit quirky. Great prices. Friendly and informative staff.
Their infused moonshines make delicious cocktails and shots. Drinks served in Mason jars for that extra touch.
I only had drinks, but can't wait to go back to try their brunch and dinner. The food menu looks just as promising as the drink menu.
Small place, but it wasn't too crowded when we were there on a Saturday night. There is also outdoor seating. 
There's even a table set up for beer pong. We also enjoyed the TouchTones jukebox which you can buys songs using the phone app.

My Family and I come every once in awhile and unless you don't make your order complicated like asking for a medium done egg on your royal burger it's pretty good...So today I see download our app and get a free milkshake. I go to pay and am told you have to put in a debt card on the app to get the shake for free....WHAT! I'M NOT DOING THAT! Instead of saying ok you weren't told that will give it to you this time,  but next time you'll know...Nope and this was a manager...Wow

Let me just warn you, there is something very wrong with this restaurant. We started out finding dried blood in our napkin and when the waitress told the manager, she NEVER came to our table to give any apology. We instead got plastic wear to eat steak!! Our shrimp appetizer was dripping grease and overcooked, all of our meals were overcooked and tasted like they had been frozen for months! The worst was all of us ate something different and all if us got food poisoning afterward. I don't believe they clean as they should, and have no care for their food. Take our advice, there are way too many restaurants around, don't waste your money like I did.
Taste is great, but don't order the Sirloin steak...it's just a plate of vegetables with a side of steak slices that are over cooked. It's a little too expensive for the portion sizes
Love the all American burger!! Plus the lemonade raspberry with vodka was so good!! The fish spread was okay but nothing spectacular
I expected worse given the bad reviews. Had breakfast; no different than Perkins or any other local breakfast place.  What place doesn't use frozen breakfast potatoes?  Not extraordinary, but fine.

I'm glad I finally got to try their donut! I love a good cake donut and theirs were delicious. It was so fluffy and airy. You could tell how fresh they were. They also do have yeast donuts if that's what you prefer. 

My husband tried their mango fruit tea with lychee bobba and loved it. I tried their milk tea and it wasn't my favorite. I did come in expecting Taiwanese style bubble tea and theirs is Thai style. The straws they provide were not wide enough to get the bobba through which was unfortunate.
This place is always good. I have eaten here about three times in over a year. The sushi is about the same as most other places but still good. The servers are usually friendly too.

My best friend and I are both a sucker for some tasty BBQ so when we were in Nashville this was a no brainer. We walked in around 3 or 4pm to a line out the door. This was instantly a sign that we have found the right place but don't fear the line, it moves fast. 

The food list was super minimal showcasing they knew their barbecue and they did it well. While you're waiting in line the menu is well displayed above to order and pick-up counters. Both of us being huge BBQ fans, we were so excited to dig in and compare to our hometown taste of Eli's.

We both went with the pulled pork sandwich plate that comes with two sides which can be smoked green beans, cole slaw, French fries, bbq beans, Mac and cheese or potato salad. After some long deliberation, I ended up going for the bbq beans and French fries.

When placing your order they have a wall full size of their sauces and products you can buy and my friend ended up getting one of their dry rubs to take home. After placing your order they call it out on the other side when it's ready and that's much faster than expected too.

Now don't go in expect a five star spot, this is real country BBQ and their environment calls to that. The food is also super spot on. A LOT more smoke incorporated in the food than Eli's for all my Cincinnati people but so good and definitely work a stop next time your in Nashville. Oh and the cups you can take to go as a piece of your trip! Which is always fun.

Another great birthday celebration at The Melting Pot!!!  Nick was our server and he was amazing!!!  Nick was polite, attentive and prompt. This time, because we had a party of five, we had two burners so I was able to try the Bourgogne cooking style and creme brûlée fondue, both amazing!!!  I can't wait for my next birthday!!!

I love to go to small family owned places for food because the quality and the customer service is usually phenomenal but that was not the case here. When I walked in the older gentleman was talking with another man who was sitting at the table. I walk up to the counter to ask about specials or popular items because this was my first time. He continued to just chat with the other man as I'm clearly looking at him waiting for him to finish. He made eye contact with me and continued to talk. Finally when he was finished he took my order and immediately went back to chatting with the other gentleman. I wanted to ask if he took card or cash only and I tried to ask multiple times but he ignored me-I was not even two feet from his face and he just ignored me. I stood at the counter for maybe 4 minutes and even tried to ask his wife but she just went about her business in the back. After about 10 minutes I got my sandwich and when I went up to pay I saw these two signs on the register. I get the humor but it doesn't make me feel welcome in an establishment when I see "different day same shitty attitude" and "nope not today" it makes me feel like I'm bothering you with my business. Well don't worry Frankie's Deli, I won't bother you anymore.
Absolutely love their meatballs!  On pizza or in a sub, you just can't get better than this.

Awesome yellow curry chicken. So many good flavors. Also tried the pad Thai chicken with a level 4 hot. Oh boy. That packed a punch. Little too much heat for me. It still tasted great and would order both items again. Just less heat. 
Little pricey for Thai food but definitely will go back for another try.

This is the second time I stayed here this year and it will be the last.  The first stay was in the skyline tower.  Good but not great.  The second stay was at the smaller older dirtier tower.  The room smelled of cigarette smoke. The carpet was filthy and next to the bed someone had dumped a soda and it was sticky.  There is no security because the door had a gap big enough to slide a screwdriver in to pop the latch.  You get to listen to the air conditioning all night long.   Spend your money elsewhere and enjoy your stay.

Wow this place has been awesome since the new young  female manager took over.She is so good at her job and seems to be on top of everything.I think with good leadership you get better service. I noticed the tables are cleared immediately so the wait time to be seated is now shorter and the atmosphere just seems happier?? She gets right in and helps with chips ,drinks ,cleaning plates. 

That was not how it used to be and although the food has always been great the service was hit or miss. I love any of the dishes with Mole on them and the pico de gallo is so healthy and fresh that I steal it off of everyone else's plate in exchange for my cheese.. The salsa is outstanding with just enough texture to not taste commercially prepared. I'm told it is made in house each day. The Happy Hour deals are good with strong cheap Margaritas and tasty tacos.

Came here (hotel) for a business meeting and was early, so I decided to eat at the restaurant.  I got the cornmeal breaded shrimp to start and the "Eat Salad" as my lunch.  Both were really good.  The shrimp came with two sauces and I preferred the avocado one.  The salad was goat cheese, strawberries, boston bibb, cornbread croutons and ranch dressing.  The waiter was super friendly and attentive and the place was very warm without being "formal".  Not what you would expect for your hotel "offering", but a great surprise!

Fun place, great food, fantastic people watching, COOL BIBE, great valet parking! Down sides are that the acoustics are challenging if you want to hear your friends talk, the portions are on the small side for what you pay and it's really hard to get a nice table on busy hours, long wait!
Well the crab cakes were a nice size needs more seasonings if you ask me, the French fries was nasty how can u mess up fries? Carmelized apples delicious over all it was ok

4+ stars for my first Spot Burger, the Charlie Brown.  Burger, Fried onions, Bacon, Whiz on what appears to be a potato roll.  VERY good burger, easily the BEST burger I have ever eaten from a truck, but I have not eaten burgers from many trucks in my time...be that as it may, this burger will stand up to any brick and mortar burger and is better then any chain burger I've ever had...Five Guys, Elevation Burger, Jake's Wayback, and even Cheeburger Cheeburger...SPOT burgers are ground sirloin, not chuck, and you can really taste the difference.  I actually wanted a cheesteak, because they do slice their own steaks, but they sold out by time I got there.  

Walk up to the cart and there should be one or 2 order takers on hand...Give them your order, your money, and sit back and wait...Prices are pretty good btw, 7$ seems fair for a burger of this quality\quantity.  Beverages are 2$.

Overall, given the quality of the burger and the price, I'd say they deserve 5 stars.  The reason I did NOT give them 5 stars is due to the long wait for food!  This is not a food truck, but a cart.  There is room for one small person inside and one small grill which looks like it can hold about 8-10 burgers at a time...which is fine if you only have 8-10 customers, but when you have a long line with 30+ people and more coming the wait times become almost unbearable.  Some people waited over an hour to get their lunch today...I waited till they were all gone(literally placed the last order of the day) and my order was done in about 10 minutes, however they had also ran out of cheesteaks by this time.  

I wish there was something that could be done to speed this up!  A second grill?  A second cart?  Hopefully they do well and can upgrade the cart to a truck and turn the tables over faster!  That is my only beef with this burger truck, the burgers are outstanding and worth the wait, if you have the time!
It's ok, I'm not going to say it's extraordinary and it's the best Chinese food I'd ever had,but it's better then most places in reno.

Walked in on a Tuesday night and they were able to seat me right away. The server gave a great description of the menu. My choices:
-Fingerling Fries- terrific, the mustard sauce was exceptional
-Spicy Tofu- the tofu was amazing, but had a sauce that I wasn't too fond of
-Gold Beets- my favorite choice I made, had smoked tofu underneath and had excellent flavor
-Chocolate Uber Chunk- have to say it was probably my worst choice, but was still very good 

Vedge is definitely A MUST GO if you're in Philly. Like go. Now.

Super casual place to grab a quick lunch or a cold beer after work.  While not posh in any way, the food is consistently good and the servers are friendly and efficient.  My husband enjoys the meat-and-three - the creamed corn in particular, while I am partial to their grilled cheese and soup lunch special.  On a cold, dreary winter day, you can't go wrong with a hot grilled cheese and a delicious (and big) bowl of vegetable beef soup.  Yum.

While I'd never think to bring guests to Dalton's, I'd definitely return for a quick and tasty lunch or dinner.  We'll be back!
Amazing food. Always a new good beer to try - my favorite was Mago Tago. One of my favorite spots in the Philly area, for sure.

Nice clean modern looking inside.  The servers were attentive.  I ordered an assortment of skewers. Nothing tasted right and one was unedible.  I couldn't wait to brush my teeth to get the rank taste out of my mouth!

This is what I've been looking for. 

The moment I entered Philly's Italian Market, I turned to my bf and said "It reminds me of Italy!" I lived in Florence for over 4 months and have greatly missed some aspects of that culture, especially the old world vibe that persists throughout the cities, most noticeably in their markets. This place is similar but for obvious reasons quite different and unique, and that's what makes it fantastic!

The stores that line the streets and whose wares inevitably spill out onto the sidewalk as well offer a large variety of items, ranging from produce, fresh seafood and meats, cheeses and pastas, and home goods. It seems like some of the Italian places import certain items from Italy, which is awesome since now I can get a few of the things that I used to live off of in Florence right here in the US! Of course, its not just Italian businesses here anymore, but also Mexican and Asian. Some might complain that its losing its original identity, but all things must evolve in our global economy and the transformation that the Italian Market is undergoing can only mean good things for its future.

Even if you have no reason to come down here, the Italian Market is worth it even to just walk around and explore. This is one place that is truly, truly a major part of the heart of Philadelphia.

wow. love the servers there. they are witty, pleasant, and they do a little 'yay- dance' if they find out you loved the oyster shooter they recommended :) 

stop by for the plentiful oyster crackers, or raw oysters with to-die-for cocktail sauce. oh, and sit at the bar if you'd like to see all the shucking action... you'll be glad you did

I use to love this place had been going for years. Then one night I'm walking from another bar with a plastic cup of tea (not alcohol) in my hand and as I'm getting closer to the door to go in the bouncer tells me he cannot let me in with the drink so I said no problem, threw away the cup and he still doesn't let me in, I'm asking why and he couldn't give me an answer! Then 3 girls get up to the line all with cups in there hand and the bouncer just lets them in right in front of me like nothing. I was in shock! I asked why he allowed them in and not me and he kept saying they work here! I was in disbelief and other customers behind me saw how I was treated and left. I still till this day do not know why he didn't let me in. I think it was cus I didn't look like the other girls in short dresses etc. but after my experience I'm never going there again.
i haven't been to this place in about a year, but i still dream about their raw flank steak appetizer.  and their pho, rice dishes and other noodle dishes ain't so bad either.

This is an unassuming little gem with a Tampa address but very convenient to Riverview. Good southern comfort food for a reasonable price. Really good hushpuppies, fish  and gumbo. The food is cooked fresh and always hot. Would recommend

SUMMER TOUR means a different part of the world inspires the menu during different times of the summer. we came during the Singapore inspired menu

they've got a big dining table in the back for large parties, perfect for us

took them a LONG time to take our orders and give us the complimentary bread, but eventually our food came out. they serve smaller portions so i'd suggest sharing an appetizer or dessert!
