--beach babe cocktail: best part of the meal! so fresh & delicious w/ the passion fruit flavor
--complimentary focaccia w/ olive oil: liked the crust on this!
--banana leaf grilled basa: the fish was flavorful but the "pandan" flavored rice was soggy & did NOT taste like pandan
--dark chocolate jalapeno ice cream sundae: yummy chocolate ice cream... the jalapeno give an interesting kick at the end that wasn't too overpowering (we got this dessert FREE w/ yelp check-in)
--pineapple almond tart w/ coconut ice cream: buttery crust & yummy ice cream

3.5 stars because the appetizers and desserts overshadowed the main entree & i expected more for the price point... maybe i'll come back for HAPPY HOUR

Is that okay if I give 10 stars?? Me and my hubby just had the best dinner experience in here!!! So good!!
It is a place in the corner of the streets and has a lot of windows and doors which is so romantic with the streets lights around us...The whole place feels nice and comfortable. Our server Jessica was very friendly and welcoming us. She recommended the pork chop which is AMAZING! gosh! How can a pork chop being so juicy and tender?? It's too good! I lost my words when it comes to good food... we ordered the steak Frites as well and this one is also amazing! The side fries are so good!! And the bone marrow... gosh... so good... I don't even have another word to describe... so good... oh and we also had the oyster as an appetizer. It comes with 6 small oysters. They were raw but warm, with a tint of Lemmon juice, butter and some spicy sauce on top.. perfect portion for 2 people to start dinner. I just love the way they cook it and also the plates, the containers. Everything was so good. 
We highly recommend this place! My husband was keep telling me how satisfying he was for the whole night while chewing his food lolll... the price is really good(comparing to the place we went last night) and the portion was big as well. In all, it was a really great experience tonight! :)

Im the cook here at Tequilas we have yet to start are a full meun but be sure to look out for vegan/vegetarian options and added side with your meal we have a great staff and our head chef (Chef Dave) is a very strong leader/ funny guy always full of energy and rocking a smile

Located in the heart of the grove, this bottle shop and bar is the beer snob's craft brew oasis! Gezellig may be a hard name to pronounce, by it's music to my ears. I love going and getting lost in the copious amount of beers in their cooler. They offer such a wide variety of your local favorites, from 4Hands to Urban Chestnut. They also have a vast catalogue of national brews as well. So often you find a brewery that you've never heard of. Additionally, they have a selection of imported beers as well. 

What I love about this shop is the flexibility. So often when you go stores that force you to purchase between four and six cans of beer, you take the gamble of not liking one of your selections. This is not the case at Gezellig! You can pick a can based on it's name, or it's can design or just because you've never heard of the particular style. This allows you to broaden your brewed perspective and taste imbibes you may have never sought after. 

Insider tip: always check out the draught menu as well. If there's a beer that sounds interesting and the inventory indicator is red, GET IT! If your beer is the beer that blows the keg, your beer is free. I have had this happen before on a pricey stout. I had a mostly full glass, but got it for free because it was the end of the keg. 

Right now they are only offering window to-go service because of COVID. Before the pandemic, this was a great winter hangout because you are allowed to bring your pets into the bottle shop. It's a great opportunity to spend time with friends, both two and four legged! 

And as for food, two words... Pie. Guy. This New York Style pizza shop is attached to Gezellig and offers "delivery" to your table. I highly recommend the "knotchos." Imagine everything you love about a slice of decedent pizza on top of warm, doughy garlic knots. More on that in a later review!

When I come home to STL I crave Chinese food, actually I leave the airport and head straight to the restaurant.  Press for time I could not go to my favorite Chinese restaurant so I headed to this restaurant because I know they have good food.  Anyhew, when asked could I get chopsticks they cost .25 each, then I asked for fortune cookies I had to buy a pack of 5.  I've been eating in STL Chinese restaurants for YEARSSSSSS and have never been charged for chopsticks or fortune cookies.  Needless to say I will not use this restaurant as my emergency to place again.

Asparagus as a side dish is an extra two dollars and it  was overly large and tough. Food piece of fish but didn't bother to read the description of the salmon and was surprised to see a sweet honey glaze on my salmon. Next time I will have request it not be put on my fish.

Two big thumbs down on Wilko. We ate there on a recent Sunday night before show at UA presents. We placed our orders and waited for one full hour. I chased down the waitress and insisted on knowing what was up with our order. It came out another 10 minutes later and it was completely average. We wolfed down our dinners and left feeling completely dissatisfied.

The food is pricey. The $16 chicken confit is a chicken leg, cous cous and some carots.

The noise level is so loud that you can't sit at a table for six and hear everybody. 

For a bad time, come to Wilko for dinner.

Meh. My chopped chicken salad was pretty good but the other entrees at our table were mediocre. Guacamole did not taste fresh, in fact avocados tasted like the kind you can buy wholesale pre cut and cryovaced. Drinks were also meh and overpriced for what they were. Not at all an authentic Mexican meal nor even a good Mexican-American meal.

Went on Christmas day and ordered from the regular menu. Chef was extremely accommodating with my niece's food allergies. Portions perfect size. Very fresh ingredients. Also a good kid menu. Jerk chicken was great. Pasilla pepper also excellent. Friendly staff.
The food is excellent and the owners are friendly, generous and kind. Highly recommend!
Great service , amazing food and happy hour :) couldn't ask for more ! Try the ceviche, bang bang shrimp, ahi tuna  for appetizers ! You won't regret it !
Very good. The sushi chef we had was amazing to watch and very quick and efficient. Wonderful experience, will very much go again.
for the price, this is best pizza place i've been to in the area. Highly recommend the pepperoni pizza, thoes things are huge!

Made a 7:30 reservation a month in advance for party of four for New Year's Eve 2012.  They gave us a horrible table upstairs off a hallway that was so noisy due to wait staff going up and down hall, and bright lights shining in our eyes.  The food was  just ok.   We were rushed through the first 4 courses then waited an hour for desert.  Not even a courtesy of complimentary coffee as we waited patiently.  The service was not good.  They served lobster tail with no utensil to remove meat easily and we had to ask for steak knives.  Never again.
lack of vegetarian options was disappointing. also, long wait time and judgmental looks from staff and other customers for being youngsters.. I just seemed out of place and not very welcome
Came in tonight to grab a quick burrito and the staff was so amazing. Joey, Josh, and Matthew were so chill and hooked us up with great portions. The food was insane! Will definitely come back.

This place is a few blocks down from where I'm staying & I'm a sucker for donuts. So I figured I would take a walk & try it out. 

The place itself is super cute & minimalist. White walls, a donut sign, and a few plants on the shelves makes up most of the spot. It works out really well though bc the main focus is the donuts & the take out boxes with their blue & red really stand out. 

I got the peach fritter, coconut cake, blueberry cheesecake & spectaculoos to bring back to the house for us to try. I am not vegan or vegetarian so there really wasn't any particular reason for my choices other than they looked good and were really well reviewed :) 

I blueberry cheesecake & coconut cake was probably my favorite. Both had good flavors & the donut itself was good. The spectaculoos had good flavor but was definitely heavy. I was a little disappointed that the peach fritter tasted nothing like peach :( just tasted like a regular cake donut. 

Overall not bad- $3 for a donut & $5 for a fritter ($18 for half dozen)

The manager ( cannot remember his name started with B) was over the top and sanitary towards taking our orders. Even though my husband made his life more difficult than needed he kept his composure and never broke professionalism. We will definitely be returning to this location thanks to his patience and orderliness.

I have been a student in St. Petersburg for three years, and for all three of them I have wanted to visit Ceviche.  I only have heard good things- and those good things proved to be very true!

The past week, after a visit to the Dali Museum, my friend and I were hungry with some (rare) spare time, and he asked me where we might be able to find some good tapas.  I suggested Ceviche.  At first, the restaurant was crowded, but that was because most everyone was sitting outside on the covered patio.  We chose to dine inside and had amazing and prompt service. 

My friend had the Ceviche which he enjoyed, we had sangria and I had several of the tapas.  The food was authentic to southern Spain.  The tapas I had were a higher end version of the tapas I had in Granada last summer and just as good if not better.  The papas bravas were excellent - and heavier spiced than the the variations I had in southern Spain- which I liked. 

The prices were reasonable, and the atmosphere fantastic.   I will be making it back to Ceviche!

Commendations to our server Ruby. The restaurant was way understaffed and she hustled.  The food was more than disappointing. My wife's arugala and watermelon salad had 4 small chunks of watermelon. The salad was the size of a soup bowl and just filled with arugala and tasteless dressing. Nothing else. My prime rib dip was not good. Meat slices were burned crispy on the edges and many slices were just unrendered fat. The sandwich was sloppily made and half off the bread.  For the money we paid for lunch the chef should be totally embarresed. Shame on you.

The Tagliatelle is a little bit undercook, flavor was normal but not bad, I like their dessert, very Italian, the Panna cotta could be softer in terms of texture, and lack of lavender flavor, the sabayon was quite a lot and tasty

I love Datz I just wish my visits were more enjoyable! For this visit I took my family but they were not impressed unfortunately. I order the bravacado toast and the guacamole could have used more flavor and less guacamole, the plate looked good but didn't taste nearly as good, I also order a cool drink but can not remember the name but that was delicious! I will continue to be a Datz consumer and try out more plates so stay tuned! @eatwanderandslay

We have been here several times, because the food is really good!  But, this week's experiences have left me very frustrated.

I called last Monday night around 6:00 to order take out.  Sadly, they were out of 95% of their menu!  Not sure what that was about.

So, since we hadn't gotten our fix, we went last night to eat there.  We learned that while we waited for our table, we had to wait in a line to order drinks at the bar.  This would not have been a big deal, except that I got in the line at 7:24 and it was 8:08 when I finally got my drink!  The bartenders were clearly working a quickly as they could, but obviously there were not enough of them.  They mixed a lot of specialty drinks; perhaps a "beer and wine only" line would help?  

When we finally got our seat, our service was good, and so was the food.  They were only out of chicken egg rolls and one beer.

I will be taking a break from here, though.  There are clearly some management kinks that need to be addressed.

I grabbed some lunch with co-workers here and we were all very satisfied with the decision. The meal was absolutely delicious and service was pretty fast. My only complaint is that the portion size for the dumplings is a tad small. Other than that, I'll be visiting them again in no time. I recommend the Hand Torn with an egg. It's pretty incredible.

Came in for dinner, really recommend it. Amazing meals.. had the calamari for appetizer, the seared salmon + green pea cousin, and the chocolate coffee cheesecake. 

My coworker had the chicken tortilla soup and the stuffed chicken breast.

We were both really impress by how the delicious the food was and the service was amazing. We ven got to talk with the chef about the food.

In summary if you are in town, is worth stop bu
Quite good rarefied Mexican.  I couldn't help wondering--did El Vez rip-off their menu for the tuna tostadas or vice-versa?
Caribbean chicken, fish tacos and Mahi was great. Gatorade bites yummy. The sides were OK, but main entres good

The place is quaint and the food was great. I had the Mac n cheese with hot chicken. My husband had a pizza. We were warned by the very nice server that the portions were generous and this was especially true for the pizza. With so many places in a close proximity it was tough to choose but I'm very happy we chose The Stillery it was great!

Burgers are consistent, good beer selection, good location. Too many kids, too many suburban people thinking they are being all cool on Mass Ave. I will keep going, but during off hours when I can get a table in the bar.
Place sucks. ATM steals money and service is piss poor slow south service. The rumonade was good though.

We actually had a good time here. It was our cheat meal and we decided to try something new to us. We had fun with it and tried every sauce they had to offer. I recommend the fry sauce and their house sauce. It was a great experience. The custard was delightful as well. 10/10 for customer service. I've never eaten at a casual/fast food dining place that was so nice and courteous. They came by our table multiple times while we were eating to check on us. They are awesome and the food was great! Try the cordon blue checker sandwich, it's flavorful!
We came here for brunch, and it was the most mediocre food I have had in a long time. It's hard to mess up brunch food- I just had a simple frittata and potatos but it had no flavor at all.

food is excellent.

my cuz had the crawfish -- it was delicious. i had the redfish, which was also very good. the veggies were cooked to perfection -- this is something that many other area restaurants lack the ability to do. my only complaint was the food was a little cold.

they have nice selection of wines by the glass.

the big minus is that the service was dreadfully slow.

I would agree with how wonderful the food was one month ago but on our second order tonight I couldn't believe it was the same place! Both the gyro and shwarma seemed tough like reheated meat! Even the hummus changed! What a shame! We thought we had found a gem!
they regularly screw up the order! i'm done! i'm not sure why it's so complicated to make fast food correctly.

Went there for the first time last Friday.  Sounded like it could be good.  Ordered a ribeye, cooked medium.  When it came it looked partially blackened.  I was hungry, so I started eating.  This was one of the worst pieces of meat I ever tried to eat.  Never saw so much grizzle and fat.  Definitely would not go there again.  Service was OK, salad and appetizers were good.

I love going to Sushi Land!!  The service is always good; they are efficient but still serve you quality food. All of the sushi rolls are tasty but I prefer the specialty rolls especially the Hurricane.

I truly can't wait to go back to the spot! We went for dinner with friends and had to race over there for lunch before we jumped on a cruise ship! The fish tacos are insane, it's great being right on the water and the service is decent, better at the bar.

This place sucks. The food that I have tried is good so I will give them that much, but they are horribly inefficient. I have been here twice now. The first time I tried to order an item off the specialty menu. I was briefly told that they did not have the ingredients to accommodate. Fine whatever, they're a small business so I'll give them a pass this time. I ordered pho and it took like a cool 45 minutes to come out. I was annoyed but whatever it is what it is. The second time I eat here I try ordering the same item that was not available the last time. I am given a different excuse about how they do not want to because they would need to make a whole new pot. Excuse me but that is not my problem, and aren't you a restaurant? Making more of a food is literally your business model. Whatever I don't want to get into it so I begrudgingly order another pho. It takes another 45 minutes this time and I'm fed up, I want to know their deal. I ask the guy behind the counter and he said they had to MAKE A NEW POT. You are reading that correctly, they denied me the first dish because they needed to make a new pot so when I ordered pho the solution was to make a new pot. Cool thanks, I'm never coming back.
This place is great. Large portions and the best hot sour soup we've had up here. Staff is friendly and the restaurant is really clean.

How have I not written a review of this place yet! I've been coming here since I was in college (2007 was when I started).
This place is the best. They have the best Chai in Reno, I haven't tasted anything better. Service is always impeccable and the staff is always peppy and kind. Parking can be a little challenging sometimes as it's right by UNR and some students think it's ok to park there for free parking. But I go at odd hours, so I haven't had too difficult a time. They don't have WIFI which is so nice, to just get work done off the grid and only use data if you absolutely have to. I love meeting friends here, there's plenty of seating, outdoor and indoor. And they're pet friendly! I was there with my best friend and her 2 dogs right around Christmas time, and it was a nice winter day when we decided to sit outside. One of the baristas made his way outside and let us know that if the weather turned crappy we could move inside with her Rhodesian Ridgeback Pit and German Shepherd (not small at all!). I was so pleased! 5 stars to the best coffeeshop in Reno!

Seriously I'm not much of a sandwich and fries type of girl but that's what I ordered and I'm glad I did. I had the chicken and goat cheese panini which was pretty amazing and whatever dipping sauce that comes with it was sooo good. It was a black olive dip. Weird but like I said sooooo good. Service was really great and I will definitely be coming back.

Who was today years old when they found out that Jill's Place is related to Shalhoob's? Hence the Butcher's Daughter! Such a cool local connection. 

This is a solid place for lunch - my coworkers and I come here often during our monthly lunches out and Jill's always leaves us full and satisfied. I've only been here at lunch time but they've got a great menu.

Don't sleep on the fried chicken salad! It's like fried chicken in a southwestern salad and hits the spot!

If I were a seafood-liker, I would probably be giving this place a 5-star rating based on the feedback and comments of my family when we had lunch there.  Since I don't eat seafood, my choices were a burger, hot dog or chicken sandwich.  I opted for a cheeseburger for like $7.00 (lettuce, tomato, onion are extra, like 50-cents or so.)  It was a big burger!  Not thick, but from side to side!  It almost filled up the small plate it was served on.  The only thing that came with my burger was a pickle spear.  There are no fries, onion rings, etc.  Just German potato salad.  Mind you, I never order burgers when I go out to eat (as I'd rather order something else and fix my own burgers at home) but since I did not eat seafood, and this is 99% of the menu.  That being said, it was an excellent burger!  Perfectly cooked, maybe medium or medium well.  Delicious!

There aren't a lot of options here (and that goes for beverages as well) but what they do have, they do it well!  Highly recommend.

An indianapolis staple, I try something new every time! Everything is delicious. Today, I had the Indiana corn cakes, with avocado and beets. I ate the arugula side salad and corn cakes together in a bite to add an extra crunch! Their coffee is always delicious even on a hot day!

Service and wine were excellent. 
Food is terrible. 
Beautiful building but not coming back. 
For these prices I can go to Osteria natalina
Great service, great food. Highly recommend this place. I don't know what else to say, other than that it's solid and you won't be disappointed.

Charming little hotel with excellent staff and comfortable rooms. Enjoyed the afternoon wine and cheese, along with the excellent breakfast each morning.  There are also lots of restaurants within walking distances, but the specials at Molly Darcy are very good.  A shout out to Esther and Michael for making our time there so special.  The parking is 17.00 a day.  If you park on the street it is 1.50 an hour for two hours and free after 5pm.  We were not there much during the day, so we chose to park in the street.    If you sleep in you need to go pay the meters by 8 am the next morning.

We received a recommendation from a friend-of-a-friend who lives in the area to come here, and we're so glad we did.  Had an outstanding family dinner.  Every single thing we ordered was delicious (we tasted everything around the table): soups, salad, pasta, chicken, wine, and desserts. Our server Ortega was attentive, helpful, and pleasant.  Best meal of our visit to the area.

This place shouldn't even call itself a restaurant. Unless you constantly ask the hostess to get seated you will never get a spot. Food takes 45min - hour to come out, even appetizers...so don't expect to get anything first, it all comes together...an hour later. The staff hate working here and you can tell. Miserable experience. 1/10, Highly recommend not dining here.

Maybe I am not being fair but when I think of bakeries I use Termini's Bros. as my measuring stick.  Although the same initials are shared, TB, Testa's is not Termini's.  But they do get their marks for being convenient, friendly, and reasonably priced.  

I have had their cakes, cannoli's and cookies (not all at the same time) and all are fair.  An easy to get to location with ample and convenient parking options.  The kids that often work the counter are always cheery and eager to  assist.  Bring cash though as plastic is not an acceptable form of payment at Testa's.

When you need some baked goods and can't make that trip into the city you have Testa's.  Nothing wrong with that.

Hello!! Yummy baked potato, burger, and strong drinks!! Definitely a great place to eat and I enjoyed myself. :) the monsoon was what I ordered to drink and I was feeling good after drinking that during my 1 hour or so wait! Must go!

What a quaint gem in the middle of Edmonton's little Chinatown. Yes the neighborhood is a little shifty at night, but date night was oh so awesome when it ended with an adventurous menu! We watched the fish in the tank and some Chinese TV programming while we waited for the items to be prepared. I had a couple of random things that I do not remember the exact names of, but both item were awesome! I will be back there for some delicious treats in the near future!

Do it. The food was very good however the oysters took 30min to show up. When they arrived they were great. Stay away from the blackened boudin. Not to tasty. The crab ravioli was good and spicy  as well and the shrimp and grits were great. The stuffed shrimp was very good but small. Only three. Bread pudding is good but hard to share. Will return.

I have no shame in saying that one of my favorite sandwich shops in town is the Subway on Thompson Lane.  Before you make fun of that, go check it out.  That said, I like the selection at Which Wich better, but I like the actual quality here less.  

I think that the concept here is ok, somewhat akin to eating at SatCo, but it isn't for me. I'd rather just tell someone what I want to eat. If I wanted to write, I'd do a review.

I made reservations here for my anniversary, after two previous unsuccessful attempts to get in.  I took this as a sign it was a good place to eat.  What I didn't know was they have a policy of overbooking which means my husband and I were left with no where to eat on our wedding anniversary unless we wanted to stand over the other diners and watch them eat, for a lengthy, undertermined amount of time. 

I have no idea how the food is, but would not recommend that anyone go through this experience when, even if you made a reservation, you have no guarantee you will even be able to have dinner at all when the owner seems to be nothing more than greedy enough to overbook his reservations at a rate to be sure his seats are always full.
Food is pretty much par with all US Chinese food. Everything we ordered was very good and it was very quick service. Certainly I would have no issues coming here again.

Small dive bar with great music.

The music the night we were there was fantastic. We heard Mark Box and Dreamwolf. Both were awesome. I could listen to Box over and over again.

We initially walked by and heard Mark singing and loved his voice. But since we had just gotten here (Nashville) we didn't want to walk into the first bar we passed so we kept going. We walked down Broadway and heard very loud music coming from all sides. At times (most) it was too loud and we were on the outside. What was it going to sounds like from inside? We ended up back at Loser's. And we were glad we did. We had a great time.

This is a great little venue for music. There is a small stage at the front and a narrow seating area on the main floor. We never made it passed the first floor. 

We were in heaven. Live music in a dive bar. What more could I ask for? How about a drink and maybe a menu... We finally realized we needed to go up to the bar to get what we wanted. No one was going to come to the table to get our drink order. 

We would also learn that we needed to go pick up our drinks at the end of the bar as well. My drink... Well that appeared to be really weak. I ordered way too many drinks to be able to see straight but my eyesight and all other facilities were just fine. So all I could assume is that there was little to no vodka in my vodka sodas. 

I'll be back for the music, the venue and intimate setting and I'll be sure to watch the pour next time. Either that or I'll order a beer.

The naked smoked wings were pretty darn good too.

The food was amazing and the service was awesome! We were seated fast and received our drinks in record time. I went into the restaurant hungry and walked out with a satisfied stomach. The cinnamon roll pancakes had a delicious crisp on top with a soft mouthwatering bottom an absolute delight to eat. My eggs were made to perfection, the bacon had the perfect crisp, and the hash browns were the right amount of crispy and fluffy. My husband had the omelet which had the perfect balance of ingredients and a nice thick piece of toast, toasted to perfection. This restaurant is a diamond in the rough and a spectacular place to eat. Highly recommend for folks visiting who want to have a good brunch experience.

The star is for the pizza, great. I don't think they have a manager in the place. Most unorganized place I have been too! Give yourself a couple of hours if you are going to sit and eat, 15-20 minutes for a slice of pizza in the back.

I've long thought and oft said that pizza is pretty hard to screw up.  Think about it, it's dough, sauce, cheese, and if you really want to get crazy, meat.  Jockamo's doesn't break this fine culinary tradition.  The pizza is fantastical.

From what I know about Jockamo's, it was put together by a gentleman that had once worked for Bazbeaux's Pizza, a downtown fixture.  Both are fantastic and I'm going to refuse saying which one is better, partially because I don't wish to stake any future election bids on this review (haha) and mostly because I haven't been to Bazbeaux's in a while.  Anyhow, they're both awesome.  Eat them both regularly.

Back to the gist.  I had the the Luau pizza, think a BBQ/Hawaiian Pizza.  Pineapple and GT South's BBQ Sauce? I think yes. It was absolutely fantastic, though I could have done with a few more pineapple bits and a few less red onions..  My brother, Jake, got a pepperoni pizza, it was also tasty-licious, but needed some more pepperoni, the pieces were a little on the small side.  

The atmosphere was very nice, nothing too overwhelming though.  They had some cool local art for sale on the walls and in what may become a trend with me, they had interesting bathroom art (see my review of MacNiven's).  This particular piece was of all the different characters from Three Floyds' different beers.  Robert the Bruce, Gumball Head and all the others, arranged in a sort of Last Supper set up.  I enjoyed it quite a lot. 

Service was good.  We went for lunch, and I think that our server was in charge of about seven tables.  She handled them quite well, with the help of her SA (server's assistant, for you few that haven't worked in a restaurant).  The SA was very awesome, he worked his tail off and never seemed to get stressed.  Made me feel like I was in good hands.

The bar looked well supplied, though I didn't partake (in an odd move on my part).  Plenty of Indiana and other craft beers, as well as a fine selection of 22oz bombers.  So it's a great place to grab a pint or six with you pie.

The only really big issue I have with Jockamo's is that it's motherblanking Irvington.  I like Irvington, but that sum'bitch is out there on the East side... way out there.  Of course, I live just north of Greenwood, so everything really worth going to is far away.
Quaint old train station that seats about 20-24 people.  Arrived during Sunday brunch.  This is not fast food.  Go when you can linger.  Service and food were good albeit slow.

The best thing about this place was their drinks!! The service was good and it's a quaint little spot but I was totally unimpressed with the food. The shrimp on my po'boy was small & rubbery (hard to chew), not to mention there was only 5 on the whole sandwich. We chose this spot due to location and we could get a table without having to wait over an hour. Would we go back?? Likely not based on the food quality alone.

We came here after a long evening in the funk zone. It always catches my eye when we are in SB but I always forget to make reservations. 

We were able to get a table on a busy Saturday night but we did have to wait an hour. It might have been a shorter wait for the bar or communal table. The waitress must have said five times that it was family style restaurant and that her job was to make sure that we didn't order too much or too little. I've lived in So-Cal long enough to know that this just means they make dishes that are a just slightly too small to be a full entree but definitely the price of an entree. That way you are tempted to buying three plates for two people on average. I wasn't too hungry so I ended up getting the scallop dish which came with this amazing corn polenta. Note that they call it a "platter" and charge $34. It's not really a platter, more like three large scallops spread out artfully on a plate. Unfortunately they were out of the pretzel which seems super popular as the people at the two tables next to us also tried to order it. 

Anyways, the flavors, ambiance, and drinks were excellent. Definitely met my expectations and all the hype.
Came here based on other reviews and we were not disappointed. Home cooked deliciousness.  Super friendly service and large portions. You will not leave hungry!

Heads and Tails-Either Side Is a Winner

A couple friend of mine and I went to this establishment, this being my first visit, but my friend had gone here before and enjoyed it. We order the char grilled oysters, oyster Rockefeller soup and I ordered for my entrée the featured Heads and Tails surf and turf po boy. This particular sandwich is served on the locally familiar crusty po boy bread assembled with tender thin sliced roast beef with light gravy and friend shrimp on it. I ordered it  with the usual "dressed request". "Dressed" is a local New Orleans slang means lettuce, tomatoes, pickle, mayo. This was all excellent food. The po boy was unique to this place, as far as I know. The soup is not to be missed. The char grilled oysters are as good as any place else.

I ordered for delivery via Uber Eats. Never will I EVER make this mistake again. I've requested a full refund. This place is awful. I got ZERO chips with the TWO meals I ordered. I got 1 cookie instead of 2 and it was NOT chocolate chip...it's berries and white chocolate. My child's sandwich had lettuce instead of spinach. And my sandwich may as well not have had any toppings at all. What a joke!! This place needs new employees and obviously new management because the reviews show that nothing has changed.

The food is very good:  well prepared; spiciness is upon request based on a scale of 1 to 4; and, ample portion size.  The satay tofu with a spice level of 4 was excellent and the ginger tea delicious.  Service is fast and aims to please.  Prices are reasonable.  This could definitely become a regular stop when in the mood for Asian food.

This place is pricey but really good! I can get authentic ramen, curry rice, and Hawaiian bbq. I am from LA so I love Hawaiian bbq but this place is pricey and they could be because there is no competition in the area.
Stopped in yesterday for a drip and a vanilla latte.  I've had much better lattes - this had a watery taste and the espresso did not have a good flavor.

The best food I think I've ever had. My mom literally gave the waiter a hug as we left. 
We tried the tasting menu, honestly not that much of a price difference, but totally worth it. We tried the Brussel sprouts and the Scallops to start and both were fantastic. The Lollipop lamb chops are delicious and super tender. The goat was very interesting but the Pondicherry Ratatouille is the best thing we had the whole night. The bread basket was very worth it but was a little confused with the chutneys. 
The waitstaff was super attentive and very knowledgable. 
We will definitely come back again and again. 

10/10

Overpriced food. You can go buy wagyu organic burgers and brioche buns and feed 10 people for the cost of 3 burgers. Also I have measured the fries after 5 orders and the average length was .4 inches after 5 orders. Its sad.
Worst service ever ever ever!!!!! I waited for two coffees for over 30 minutes if I hadn't paid for them yet I would have el
Great place, friendly staff. I am truly surprised that it's almost never busy when we go. I love the meatball pizza, my wife loves the wings.

Cute coffee shop vibes but exceeded my expectations like no other. The food was fantastic here! Highly recommend the cauliflower & the yam fries. I could go on and on about the food but check it out for yourself- highly recommend this place!

Came here while in the area for work. I ordered inside and walked out to my car. When I opened the chicken package up I found a weird grey string/hair something gross wrapped around the chicken. 

I Went right back inside to tell them and foolishly expected the normal chic fil a service I'm used to (smile on face and friendly attitudes) yet instead I was greeted with employees who appeared annoyed I was returning the food that they just gave me which clearly was inedible.

No one apologized for their mistake or the inconvenience or gross factor of having to find that on my food.

Will not return to this location!
Urban No Grub.  Waited 45 minutes during brunch today with many promises the food was arriving.  Decided to just leave.  The ice water was good.  :)

Just don't seem to want customers.  They do a Wed special for burgers.  Great idea.
Limit what sides you may have, (onions cost 50 cents extra) wont cook under medium, (was told that's because they precook them on Wednesdays), won't serve any cheese other than provolone, pepper jack, or american. Are you kidding?  No cheddar on a burger!  Complaints to management are a waste of time.  I live a half mile away and don't go anymore.  Too bad, great location. Raised the price of the beer special as well.

Alright, so if you haven't experienced the weenie, its about time.  I don't care what you're doing right now, just get up and drive to East Nasty and get you some weenie!  The chili dogs are out of this world (and I stopped eating meat 4 months ago!), they are even better topped with slaw!  YUM.  They also have tofu dogs, for you soy loving, meat friendly people :)

One of the best things about this place is you never have to wait for your food longer than 4-6 minutes.  Usually you pull up, get out of your car, order without a wait, eat your dogs and are on your way in like 10 minutes.  Take that McDonalds!

First time here but definitely not the last. The other restaurants in the area will have to step up their game in order to compete. 

Al carte menu and a buffet menu, WHAT?!

I did the olmette station vs al carte but the menu was extensive and no one complained. 

Party atmosphere but still chill and plenty of TVs if you want to watch.

this was a good last minute brunch find for us. we miscalculated timing of when we needed to leave for the airport given saints traffic, so we bailed on our reservation and headed around the corner to Luke's. 

Server was very nice and the brunch menu had several appealing options. i enjoyed my shrimp and grits though could have used a larger portion (maybe it was just bc we had eaten nonstop during our trip and my appetite was extra big). i ordered a glass of prosecco that was just ok and my friends both said their bloody mary was just ok as well. 

overall was a good, quick brunch stop near our hotel before leaving town.

My family and I loved Riverbend Restaurant. All of us are native New Orleanians, and found the food very authentic. The owners were amazing, and the same can be said for the ambience. Overall experience was very warm and inviting.

This place deserves all the accolades it receives. Thee best 18 oz. Delmonico I've had bar none. It was definitely closer to 30 oz. perfectly cooked, seasoned and tender as could be. All accompaniments were excellent. We did the kitchen and wine cellar tours and then headed upstairs for the best macadamia nut ice cream ever. Great classic steakhouse atmosphere and service.

The food was truly awful.  The extra star is for the wonderful server who tried to make it right.  First, my "gluten-free pancakes" were listed as a two-ingredient pancake... They were straight mush and revolting.  I ate them because I was starving and we waited 45 minutes for a table (we'd been told 20-25 when we signed in).  My husband tried to eat his chicken fried steak, but the "breading" was burned and didn't stick to the shoe-leather they called a steak.  The hash browns were cold.  He explained this to the server, who offered a fresh round of hash browns (tasteless and cold in the middle), and took the steak off the bill.  If the food had been even halfway decent, the wait may have been worth it.
The service was outstanding and the food was awesome as expected. I love that they had my turkey bacon and french vanilla creamer!

This is a great place to get great Chinese (Mandarin) food. I was a huge fan of the Hong Kong Inn here on the east side and don't think I'll ever find another place that matches their food. Ever since they have closed, my desire has been to find some place that could duplicate their egg rolls (it's 8 am and I'm drooling just thinking about them). No place has even come close, until I ate at Yen Ching. Now they are not a duplication, but they are far better than the egg rolls you'll get at ANY other Chinese food place. The food here is fresh and very delicious. It is definitely my "go-to" for Chinese food from now on. It's no Hong Kong Inn, but it is a far better substitute than any other place I've tried!
We ordered the Princess Chicken because of the previous reviews I've read. My wife favored it and I thought it was very tasty. We also order our default General Tso's chicken (known as General Zoal's chicken here). I preferred this dish. I would also never eat fried rice anywhere else! The fried rice here at Yen Ching is AmAzInG, and I rarely eat much rice!

My buddies and I stopped in for the first time right before they closed for lunch. We were impressed by the quick service, professionalism and the quality of the sushi. Even the house salad was great. Will certainly be coming back in the very near future.

Good for a quick bite. Service was friendly and fast. Penne rosa was much spicier than I anticipated, but they were very nice about replacing it with Japanese pan noodles when I asked. $1 soup/ salad additions are a good deal. Overall, above average bang for your buck.

Been going to Tino's for years and love their pizza and it's usually consistently good, but this was the second time it was not up to par.  The edges of the pizza were WAY too thick.  The middle was just fine but it seemed like there was more dough than needed for the large pizza. Had to throw a lot of the crust away.   My half white pizza was okay, but lacked that fresh garlic and olive oil flavor that I'm used to.  Couldn't hardly taste it.  My husband's other half was lacking on the sausage.  A bit disappointing but maybe it was an off night.  Will try them again in a few weeks on another Thursday to see if there's improvement.

We we went based upon the recommendation from our Italian teacher who raved about it. Honestly you will feel like you were in Italy as soon as you walk in. Downstairs is a coffee gelato bar upstairs is a very nice restaurant area it is deceptively  larger than you think. 

I husband and I split the Casa salad which was very fresh and dressed lightly and just perfectly. I had the spaghetti vongole which came with several clams in the shell on top of the spaghetti. Such a simple dish prepared perfectly and presented beautifully. My husband and I split the broccoli Robe which was also prepared perfectly-  not too tough, not overcooked. For dessert what else can you have but gelato? There is a reason why he is the gelato champion. It is the creamiest gelato I ever taste it and I tasted many a gelato while I was in Italy. And the meal was complete with a beautifully presented cappuccino.

The service was great- very attentive, very friendly and the prices were not bad at all.  I wish them buona fortuna. You can stop for just coffee, dessert, gelato or meal.

newest viet place in sj area. save the toll $. this place is a contender. pho stayed hotter than the others around the area. liked this place cause its CLEAN. hope it stays that way. waiters seemed a bit confused at times (need to work on that), they congregated with each other quite often. the one waitress needs to learn limes/lemons!! prompt service, food came out quick and tasted fresh.

small sized pho looked like a large compared to let say pho so 1. salt baked squid was pretty tasty too. the bf got the pork chop rice meal. he was satisfied and stated that his entree def beats philly. 

glad this place opened up and replaced the previous dead beat restaurant that occupied the space previously. 

they just need to work out the kinks....doesn't take credit cards yet  (get on that) and train their servers better. 

def will be back here again. great place for a cheap bite for a group. money well spent.

The food was good, the service left much to be desired.  Everyone else in the restaurant waited on us but our server.  He never once cane to check on us.  We had to flag other people down to get service.

Chili cheese etoufee is awesome.  Prices are awesome.  Eating on plastic-not so awesome, but see #1&2.  Jambalaya is so tasty, spicy, and full of sausage, it is a perfect compliment to the etoufee.  Was actually looking for the spinach etoufee, but I am convinced these guys could make etoufee out of anything and it would taste...awesome.
Always get a half and half, and always go to Yats.  It is ...what else?  Awesome.

What a unique and welcomed addition to the growing neighborhood! I love being able to come here for a great cup of coffee and a pastry on a weekday, meet with a friend for a fun, social brunch on a weekend, or come here any evening for a cocktail and delicious appetizers! Service is great, albeit no frills and fits with the classy, edgy hipster vibe of the place. So glad they decided to invest in this neighborhood and have subsequently inspired other to do so as well!
Really cool shop off the beaten path. Great espresso and nitro cold brew. Would recommend to anyone.

Once again... great great great.  I really love the gnocchi and I rarely order anything else.

We were a table of two and sate at the front by the window since the rest of the restaurant was packed with large groups.  Our food came out exceptionally quick and our server was great.

**********
Edit added November 27 2014.

I'm not going to "update" my review, because the rating stays the same.  But I feel it necessary to add more detail to the first review since there really wasn't a lot to it (I was still a newbie Yelper back then).

Pazzo Pazzo is a fantastic Italian restaurant located next to City Hall and is by far my favourite spot for dinner downtown.

For the first couple of years that I was coming here, all I ever got wast he Gnocchi with Gigi sauce... I was absolutely hooked on it.  But lately I've been spreading my wings a bit.  There's been good dishes and bad dishes along the way.

My least favourite was the Carbonara.  I know this is an odd thing to say, but there was just too much pasta in this dish.  There was really no balance to it.  I didn't eat very much of it and would not order it again.

My new favourite dish is the Chicken Breast Alla Panna.  This is a HUGE dish and I typically get 3 meals out of it.  It's a 10 oz perfectly cooked chicken breast, covered in sauteed onions, the most perfect broccoli, adorable mushrooms and a cream sauce.  Oh.. and the chicken breast is marinated in olive oil and cognac.  It's also served with the most delicious roasted potatoes and peppers.  I don't know how they do it, but it tastes like the potatoes are infused with the  pepper flavour somehow.  Amazing.

And, with all entrees, you also get a "side" of pasta or salad. I've never gone with the salad option, and the pasta option is a huge bowl with your choice of sauce.

I miss my gnocchi... but I've had so much fun trying the rest of the menu.. one day I'll get back to it I'm sure.

One small complaint... although it's really not from me, but from my mom, and a few other patrons that I've overheard.  It's very dark in this restaurant.  I love the ambiance that that gives, BUT it is extremely difficult to read their new menus and their specials board.

That's okay though... I just read the menu to anyone who needs help hahaha
I love this place!  Food is great, service is great.  Great beer selections to compliment the oh-so-delicious bbq!

Bottom Line:  My favorite restaurant of all time. 

Bastion is the holy grail by which I rate all other fine dining establishments.  

Here's why Bastion wins:

(In order of the chronological experience)

The staff!
-Thank you Josh and Lauren for treating people right, for hiring the right people, and for creating an atmosphere where the patrons feel special special. 

The private bar
-The service and quality of cocktails are best in class, yes, there's a private bar before being seated to dine. 

The vibe
-Amazing vibe, decor, and music (played on vinyl)

The experience
- watching the chefs work and do their thing is so inspiring and gives so much appreciation for what you're about to eat. 

The FOOD
- as good as it gets, think "Chefs Table" and you'll have an idea  of the quality, creativity, and plating. 

Bastion is a MUST TRY

We had to leave because they never brought our food after an hour we even talk to the owner an old lady white hair she didn't do shit worse place ever.con todo el dinero k asen debería Contratar más cocineros.

In town to see some friends and stumbled upon this new bakery downtown. Definitely a gem! The chef is a Nashville native who worked in NYC before coming back. The Tennessee prosciutto with ricotta  and ginger orange pull apart are ridiculously good. If it's nice definitely hit the outside porch.

"You're not our target customer" is what the gentleman standing outside smoking just said to me. He stopped me as I was walking home and asked what I thought of the barstools...from outside (huh?). I replied that they were fine, and that I hated the music, which blares outside at an unnecessary volume. It's crappy music as well. But regardless of my musical taste, his response was pretty careless. Not only have I lived here for over 23 years, but I operate a very successful, local business and have served on the board of the Manayunk Neighborhood Council for years. I frequent many of the restaurants and stores on Main Street and often give recommendations to visitors, friends, etc. Some people jokingly call me the "mayor" of Manayunk (only because I know so many people). So if I'm not your target customer, who is? I have been in "the Hotel" many, many times...my cousin's wife and her father were previous owners, another cousin and my sister in law held jobs there, I've eaten and drank there. However, this new owner seems to only cater to those who like his barstools and way to loud, shitty music. No doubt you have plenty of business to ensure your success, but you won't have mine.

Viva Pueblo Real!

Sure. Go ahead and stick to the normal combos and the food is a good step ahead than the normal fare (Las Palmas, Mazatlan, Cinco de Mayo). But where Pueblo Real really shines is their Pollo Verde. 

The chicken is grilled well and accented by a wonderful poblanos, cilantro, and cheese sauce. The dish garnished well with avocado, pico de gallo, and comes with rice and beans. It's the best dish.

The Fajitas are ok, but still don't compare to the mastery of Casa Fiesta on Bell Road. Go with the Pollo Verde. You'll love it.

The servers are all fun, sarcastic, and make for a great time. Don't forget to say "Hola" to Jesus. He's the fun manager. You'll never lack for chips, dips, and drinks...they hustle.

Amazing potential with inconsistent service/food.

I came to Bar Lucca for the first time with three of my friends on a Monday night. The waitress was very attentive at first, but steadily began paying less and less attention to us which was unfortunate. It got to the point that she was at the bar with the rest of the wait staff basically waiting for us and the two other tables left to leave. Annoying.

So let's talk food.

The meatballs? Meh, kinda dry and in a lack-luster broth

The burrata? Delicious! Could have easily eaten three dishes of it

The prosciutto pizza? Boring. I wish the prosciutto was sliced thinner, the crust was crispier and that it was seasoned better

The gnocchi? Delightful! The green onions added a nice zing!

The Brussels sprouts? I've had way better; definitely could have been crispier and more flavorful. They tasted mostly like olive oil.

We finished with Nutella donuts which were actually very yummy!

The ambiance is nice here and if the food and service were more consistent, my rating would be higher and I would be more likely to return but right now I'm not in a rush to do so.

Pub 1905 is questionable and draws a diverse crowd. I regularly bump shoulders with both grandmothers and bikers when entering through the angled doorway (watch your step, by the way). I ended up here by accident one evening on a dating misadventure. The guy & I never went out again, but ever since Pub 1905 has become a place I frequent at least once a month. The burgers here are incredible -- seriously! Nachos aren't bad either. Staff is average and the venue is nothing special, but trust me on the food, it will exceed every expectation. They serve up monstrous hotdogs because hey, sometimes that's just what you need. The point of all this is don't be deceived by appearances, Pub 1905 is a worthy stop... I just wish they'd reupholster the furniture.

I love the ambiance of Ciros!  The food is average some things better than others. The lamb lacks flavor but we love the duck fries and burgers are good too. Chicken and waffles just ok.The drinks are fabulous! Not only do they have unique names but are taste great and pack a punch. I would recommend for drinks and maybe an appetizer but not for a meal. Make sure you call ahead for the password, it's all part of the fun of the atmosphere!

wow... portions are big & tasty... my fiancé & i could have easily split one omelette...

staff is energetic n fun...

parking kinda sux but peg will validate...

enjoy...

Rolled in craving some Alfredo. They had the option I wanted and they even customized it to what I want. When I got it I wanted a little more sauce andtheir very nice observant employee bo instantly saw I wanted more sauce without me getting out of my seat and brought me some. This place has good food, good environment and awesome employees. Keep it up guys

I highly recommend this cafe if you are looking for the best shrimp and grits. I had the best shrimp and grits I ever had there! They have a wonderful brunch menu, daily specials and delicious coffee too. The staff was also very friendly and helpful.

The first time I came to this restaurant, I had a spectacular experience. The restaurant was jam packed and we walked in with no reservation. Nevertheless the hostess was very pleseant and offered two seats at the oyster bar. Our waiter was super helpful, made some wonderful recommendations and was extremelly accomodating when we had to rush out to catch our movie. The food was delicious, particularly the pan roasted mussels and we left very happy. 

Last night my boyfriend and I went back hoping for another taste of those mussels. It was about 11pm when we headed out for dinner and I chose Mitchell's because I knew the kitchen didn't close until midnight. To be sure, I asked the hostess when we walked in at 11:12 and he kindly reassured us that we had plenty of time since the kitchen would be open another 45 minutes.

We decided to sit at the bar rather than the main dining room. The bartender didn't so much as look in our direction for the first 10 minutes that we were seated. He stood at the opposite end of the bar and talked to three waitresses who appeared to be counting tips and checking out of their shift. When I finally waved him down, he muttered that he'd be with us in a minute and exited the bar area towards the kitchen. He returned 5 minutes later with a crate of cranberry juice to stock his bar.

When the bartender finally came over, I jockingly inquired if he was busy as I gestured around to the empty room. He returned my humorous comment with a cold stare and a pointed remark that he was 'busy with his close out duties." Wow. I looked down at my watch and it was 11:27 with more than 30 minutes to go until kitchen closing time. Not to mention that we had now been sitting there for 15 minutes without so much as a greeting.

Much to my boyfriend's dismay the restaurant was out of mussels that night so we weren't able to order the dish that had brought us back here. No biggie. We understand the concept of fresh foods and the fact that it can run out. The bartender impatiently tapped his fingers against the counter as we quickly scanned over the menu looking for a replacement. After hurridly taking our orders, we didnt see the bartender again until it was time to drop off the check. He never bothered to offer us bread, dessert or a drink. We weren't notified of last call and we certainly weren't checked up on as would be expected even at a lesser quality restaurant.

We ate our meal quickly and quietly as the bartender wiped down the counters, closed up all the liquor bottles and mopped the floor around our feet. We clearly were not wanted here and it didn't make for a comfortable date environment. Once we had paid our check and were ready to leave, my boyfriend calmly asked to speak to the manager in charge. The manager came a few minutes later bearig a look of impatience and indignation. We explained our disappointment with our experience while he stared back blankly only to finally say in a very flat voice that he is "sorry about that" and hopes we "try them again". No explanation and no offer to make it up to us somehow.

I normally would not take offense to the rudeness of a bartender or restaurant manager, but I'm baffled by this experience because we had 45 minutes till closing when we walked into this place. Had I known we would be made to feel so unwelcome, I most definitely would have stuck to my normal choice and gone down the street to Ocean Prime, where they know how to treat customers. I don't believe that Mitchell's will do well in the future with this poor level of customer service. An avid food lover and recommendor of restaurants for all my friends and clients, I'll be sure to let everyone know this restaurant does not deserve any of our business. There are too many other amazing options out there to waste $100 on an average meal and downright rude service.

I've never been a believer in online reviews, however, I felt the need to create a profile after visiting this establishment. My girlfriend and I just dined here earlier tonight, in celebration of our 5 year anniversery, to see what the fuss was about. Let me tell you...CIROS DELIVERED!

The night started by a knock on a huge wooden door (speakeasy appropriate). The gentleman (which we later found out was the manager) opened the eyehole and was very animated. We gained entry after the password for the evening was presented. He asked us if it was our first time here, and our first time at a speakeasy. He was very accomodating, and really played into the part of the speakeasy.

The cocktails were superb. Im a bourbon drinker and I had the best Old Fashioned Ive ever had. Ive had quite a few Old Fashions in my day as well. My girlfriend ordered a Moscow Mule. Although it did not come in a copper mug, it was still outstanding. After trying the cocktails, I personally had to make my way to the bar to shake the bartenders hand. He was very courteous and gave me the historical run down on both cocktails. I did not know my dining experience would also include a history lesson. Best history lesson ever.

We ordered a few dishes. We had the cheese fondue, chicken and waffles, and beef tartar. the tartar was highly recommended and I can see why. Not the biggest portions but full of such unique flavor and fusion.

Just when we thought the night couldnt get any better, the manager (Eric),   came to our table with 2 glasses of champagne! He really didn't have to, but he said on behalf of himself and the house Happy Anniversery. 

Our dining experience was flawless, and the staff made us feel so welcomed. I highly recommend this establishment to anyone living or visiting in the Tampa area.

I honestly can't believe I'm just discovering this place. What a gold mine of deliciousness! I happened by this place with a hankering for Vietnamese food. I'm always skeptical of chains and I know there are several locations. But I was hungry enough to give it a shot. 

The inside isn't super impressive, but I could care less. I was quickly greeted by a very friendly man and ordered what has since become my "usual"...18A....crispy tofu with rice noodles. I got the order to go and went back to my office. 

Opening the clamshell, I was dismayed. White rice noodles on white styrofoam with some off-white bean sprouts on the side and off-white fried tofu. I poured the little container of vinegary type substance over the noodles, sprinkled the peanuts that also came on the side. Mixed. Ate. My eyes rolled back in my head and I immediately didn't care that the food wasn't as visually stunning as Vietnamese cuisine typically presents. The flavors were SPOT ON. Bits of anise flavor, garlic, all of the deliciousness that I'd hoped for. Even the tofu had fantastic flavor. 

The kicker? The amazing plate of food only set me back $7. Can't wait to go back and sample more dishes. But for now, me and my 18A would like to be alone. No you can't have any. Go get your own. Now.

Eggplant pizza was delicious, but service left something to be desired! A group of my friends and I went to 24 one night for dinner! I ordered the eggplant pizza and was able to split it with a friend! They offered us a complementary wine spritzer, which was just okay. I enjoyed the ambiance, but found our server rude. He actually took the menu out of my hand while I was reading the drink menu. I would go back for the pizza!
Brunch was delicious and the staff is so nice! I would recommend the Trenton Benedict

I just had the BEST wings I've ever had!!! They were absolutely incredible! This place continues to amaze me! They've been here 5 years and always keep fresh items on the menu so there's always something new to try. As great as the food is, that's not the best part! The service and staff are phenomenal, and the manager Jorge is very personable and really takes care of his guests. They also have the BEST Steelers Fan Club I've ever been to! It's amazing how many Steeler faithful live in Florida. They have games and prizes, special guests, and even a cash raffle! I've been to many Steelers bars, but this place is the best. Very well organized (reserved seating), and VERY family oriented. I can't wait till football season and watching the Black 'n Gold at Glory Days Grill!
If you're in New Tampa you need to check this place out. AND they just built 2 cornhole courts! Life is GOOD!
Go Stilleerrzzz!

Tina ROCKED our night! We brought in a table of 14 ladies for a bachelorette dinner - which had the potential to be very annoying for a server... - but she kept such a positive attitude and was THE sweetest / most attentive server. We were so lucky to have her! Excellent service, for sure! #outofthered

Food was mediocre. They had good drinks options. I got pot pie potatoes was undercooked. When ordering a drink I got glared at as the waitress looked at my ID. TERRIBLE. TERRIBLE service. We ordered were never checked on and took 15 minutes after we were done with our food to go ask the bartender for dessert & our bill. Creme brulee sugar was burnt. Wouldn't recommened especially if you're getting served by the girl with black hair. Much better options in town

The service here is incredible!  They remembered our names, anticipated what we might need and were very friendly.   Everything is made from scratch and you can tell by the flavors.  So happy we ran into this gem.  Very plain and simple and clean - they put their energy into the food and service, not the atmosphere.  This  would be awesome for a family dinner or work lunch. :).
Had the double bacon smash burger and it was delicious! Reasonably priced for a fancy burger and I i was stuffed when I rolled out. Yummmmm

We were a little non-plussed by only 1 egg roll on the appetizer platter and that the crab rangoons were just deep fried wonton wrappers. No filling, just a dorito shaped triangle of fried flour. We also both ordered the Yaka mein. The pork was good but the broth was just a basic chicken with no traces of hangover suspending flavors or spices. I could have used some ketchup and worcestershire to help this along. Service was great and the restaurant was clean and inviting. The menu looked good and i'll try some other things in the future.
Best Thai food in all of Santa Barbara! Can't go wrong with anything on the menu!

Great bay view, greeted and was able to be seated with no wait. The restaurant was busy and my server was professional, helpful and recommended my entire dinner. It was a great selection of the sea bass top with crab meat, balsamic rice and asparagus. Delicious! I will have to come back and try the salad they are known for another day.

Was really craving an açaí fruit bowl during a study sesh downtown so we stopped by. I ordered the Classic Açaí Berry Bowl (açaí + granola + blueberries + strawberries + bananas + honey) and a scoop of PB. It was pretty good! I wished the açaí was a bit thicker but the bowl overall was still pretty good.

The store was very clean and nicely decorated with a couple seatings inside. They had a grab 'n go type of stand for easy salads, yogurts, or juice. We thought the staff could be a little bit friendlier and inviting, but they were nice enough and got the order done :) will be back again for more of your refreshing bowls

The most delicious lemongrass tofu bahn mi ever! Loved the flavor. Only wish the sandwich was a little more substantial. Will have to ask for extra filling next time around. Many vegetarian options. Looking forward to trying their smoothies and Vietnamese coffee/tea. Overall, place was cute, small and clean. Great addition to Washington Ave

Outstanding food and selection!  Worked all details with Charlie thru text and email and he was ALWAYS fast to respond. Served over 100 people and everyone had nothing but 5 star reviews. The truck's inner kitchen was spotless and obviously was reflective in the pride Charlie had of it. 
Highly recommend as the pulled pork and mac-n-cheese were a couple of the faves.

I was staying in downtown Nashville, but wanted to get away from the mayhem - I grabbed a bike share (and then a scooter when that annoyed me) and sought out Bartaco for something different. 

Fortunately, it was a Monday night and there was room at the counter. I grabbed three tacos and a non-alcoholic drink. I got 2 or 3 tacos and they were all excellent - the perfect antidote to the conference food I was offered during the day.
The teppan dinner was soooo good. I have gone to a lot in SoCal (Daimons, Matsu, Bennihanna, etc) and this was better than any of them!! All the food was super delicious!!

I always like coming here, great drinks, good pastries that even include the gluten fee variety, cool decor, the hippest kids Reno has to offer, what's not to like? It's generally really clean, well stocked and sufficiently staffed. The employees have a tendency to be a little snooty, but, as a coffee shop worker myself I have to say, it goes with the job. It's only a few blocks from my apartment so I frequent this location and they're always very consistent which is a great quality. They also have sandwiches which awesome, although I've never had one, they look awesome. Definitely worth the stop to little midtown coffee stop

Let's face it, we go to Dave & Buster's (hereafter D&B) for the games. The food is okay, but most people like to come here for the fun Vegas-lite atmosphere with all the Midway games you can play.

I went to this D&B several times as a youngster. I remembered the fun games, the great food, fun times, and you came home happy. If you were a big winner, all the better. 

Those were my memories of D&B. Then something happened along the way, I grew up.

Several years later, that same excitement does not run through me like it used to. The games lack the "more" factor. There is a blandness to the whole experience. It feels less of you feeling in control and more that you are in a controlled environment, much like, well, a video game. 

When I wanted something to eat, I found an empty seat and waited 10 minutes. I looked around to see nobody was even close to the vicinity of helping me. Realizing I was never going to be helped, I thought, "screw this", got up, and walked out. 

Another thing. I remember them being real strict about bringing minors in here. Now I see them running everywhere. Has this rule been laxed? Also, I noticed employees were more like babysitters, and less hands on with the whole experience. It is good that they want you to have fun, but other customers complained to me, and in my earshot, about the lack of staff willing to assist in customer needs. That is definitely no bueno.

Basically, D&B is now a shell of it's old self, and unless they dig deep and find what made themselves successful in the first place, they will become something less than a shell, they will become a fossil.

I am a tough reviewer so I don't give out many 5's. I do thoroughly enjoy Ahi as the quality is excellent. The food selection good and the creativeness in the rolls is definitely there. I highly recommend for lunch and dinner both.

Loved sitting on the shady patio this morning, people-watching across the historic square as the birds sang from the trees. Coffee tasted like New Orleans and the no frills southern breakfast was beyond filling. The biscuits were a 5.

Well there may be numerous sushi joints in the area, it's difficult finding one you would want to frequent.

Enter Ichiban. After eating here a 2x I can officially say it has made it into rotation.

First things first... looking at the sushi chefs here and seeing that the majority are of Japanese descent is a plus. Maybe this makes me a snob, or maybe not, but having Pablo make my sushi isn't exactly my idea of authentic.

Located on the Mesa in a strip mall setting with other restaurants. The decor at Ichiban is simple and plain. I do enjoy the tatami style seating offered.

Service is polite and friendly. A little forgetful with refilling waters and such however they check in on you often so all you need to do is ask.

The menu offers quite a few Japanese entrees, standard rolls, and a limited number of specialty rolls. Sashimi is offered despite not printed/priced on the menu. Favorite rolls include the Ichiban Roll and Box Sushi. Cannot wait to try the short ribs on the next visit, look delicious!

This is what happens when hipsters open a Pho joint. Vegetarian pho was mediocre at best. Broth had a strange flavor and was mildly reminiscent of vegetarian broth. The greens were a bitter addition and don't blend well with the broth. 
My friend who got the beef pho said hers
was good, she's had better, but it wasn't awful. 
Bummer guys. Seriously.

Not only is this our constantly favorite local favorite for ourselves and when we have out of town guests.  But, they're customer service is above and beyond.  We dropped in for an order to go after an unfortunate at home dinner incident as they were closing.  And they graciously took care of us with a delicious pie to satisfy and make up for our failed at home plans.  So grateful to have this place in our neighborhood!

My family always has a great experience coming to Panera for breakfast lunch or dinner but this last time the breakfast we ordered did not come as we specified , but the management and staff went above and beyond replacing our order and even giving us another free breakfast on the upcoming weekend.   I just wanted to update my review to let the people at Panera know that you're doing a great job keep it up. Thank you

Came here for Sunday breakfast with the family this morning.  We got there and we only had to wait about 10 minutes which I think is pretty decent since usually on Sunday's it takes forever!  Let's be honest this place is run down.  I think I should try another location and compare.  My son got the cinnamon roll and hash browns.  The cinnamon roll was splendid however the hash browns were bland and undercooked.  My daughter and I had the waffles mine came with scrambled eggs which were bland as well.  My waffle was really good though and the syrup wasn't too heavy.  My fiancé god the square meal I believe it's what it is called or the square breakfast.  Again his was bland as well.
We decided we would most likely not come again unless we were coming for cinnamon rolls.
The service was pretty good and we were pleased by how attentive the server was.
In my opinion this is not the breakfast place to go to in Tucson.

I've been many time to the nada in Cincinnati so I was uber excited that the restaurant made its way to Indy. 

Get the Rojo Sangria. It is by far the best Sangria in Indianapolis.  Beware, it's strong! Especially the fruit. 

I've tried the salmon and pork belly tacos. Only downside (compared to a restaurant like Bakersfield) you can't mix and match the tacos. Go with friends and each get a different taco so you can share!

We walked in & were seated but the server didn't come back to take our order. We went to the front & noticed that 5 of your staff was just standing in the front chit-chatting. We then left and were pretty disappointed with the customer experience.

I just had my wedding here Saturday night, with my rehearsal dinner here Thursday. I don't even know where to start. The food on both nights was absolutely amazing! all our guests raved about how delicious the food was! Al was accommodating with literally everything we wanted. The weather was iffy, but we got it figured out because of Al and Nora. Jennifer was amazing to work with throughout the entire process. Al treated me like his daughter throughout everything- he truly wanted to make me happy and make my husband happy. Bogeys was incredible. The bartenders melts the drinks flowing, and everyone had a fantastic time! I honestly can't say enough good things about this venue. Nora, was so caring, kind, and was there for anything and everything I needed. Thank you Bogey's, for making our dream wedding a reality. Truly something I'll remember forever!!

Honestly, I woke up this morning wanting breakfast and a burrito, and I decided why not get a breakfast burrto, at noon haha!.. So I figured I may as well try someplace new and yelped for a veg friendly breakfast joint! Hinge popped up.. I genuinely didn't notice the "E" for east when looking at the address and thought Hinge was on the west side of the city, lets just say while driving down ridge looking for somerset I finally realized this. I already had my mind set on going here, so we hopped on the e-way went to the east side and finally found hinge. let's just say it was well worth the trip.. 

I had the breakfast burrito.. It was AWESOME! and HUGE all for only 6$!!! I also had the cheese cake, which i trekked around center city back to home and didn't eat until about 6pm and it was still AWESOME! YES YES YES!! my partner had the challah.. and some eggs. I tried his challah it was frigging amazing!! I'm more of a savory person for anything breakfast related,  but they were definitely worth ordering. 

The space is pretty quaint, cool decor, super clean bathroom, and although the staff seems to disappear frequently ( I suppose with only 2 people working and the dining area taken care of they were trying to handle multiple things like writing the lunch specials... or something.. idk.. I don't care either. If I go again I'll definitely order ahead, the wait was quite annoying, but the food was well worth it.... all in all I'm in, but this place is SUPER FAR!

We have been to the Prime Rib twice, and have really enjoyed it both times.  It is pricey, so not a place for a regular Friday night dinner, but more appropriate for a special ocassion.  It has an "old time" feel, which is neat for a change.  Excellent service, suberb quality, and the prime ribs are top notch.  Although we were 30 years younger than the average guest, the night was thoroughly enjoyable.

We have been here a few times and have liked the food each time.  We just went over the weekend and there must be a new chef and/or manager.  It was horrible.  Our wine glass were dirty and didn't match.  My bowl of soup had a clump of gunk or the rim, takes a second to wipe it and make a nice impression.  My wife's Cesar salad was flavorless.  It had a watered down dressing on it.  How do you mess up salad?   I got the veal Brandi.  The veal was freezer burned that sauce was a brown tasteless goo.  My wife got the scallops and shrimp.  One scallop was barely cooked the other was raw.  The shrimp were just barely cooked she couldn't eat the thing.  Rather than a waitress seeing it uneaten and asking if there was a problem.  Nothing.  Really went down hill.  It's a shame the area needed it.

My family came out from california and we decided to take a trip to Tombstone. We left early in the morning and on our way there we all got really hungry. I looked up breakfast spots in Tucson. Bisbee popped up and looked amazing. It did not disappoint at all! The breakfast was amazing, hot, delicious literally everything good you can say!!! I highly recommend this place for sure!!!!! Portion sizes were out of this world!! Biscuits and Gravy was fantastic. The french toast is huge!! Bacon and sausage was the best!!!

If you interested in being verbally abused by the staff,  this is the place to go. I literally got yelled at and a staff member had to restrain one of her co-workers from coming at me all because they forgot to ask what kind of chicken pieces I wanted in my meal. CRAZY RIGHT,  but all true . This just happened to me 30 minutes ago. This place is always dirty and smelly.  Extremely smelly. Definitely the very last time I go there.

I live behind stewartsboro elementary and I've known this store to be slow before, but the one across from Nissan is out of my way from work, so I come here. However, this morning, 4/7/19, I send for my order when I leave my house, say I am ready to pick up as I'm passing Almaville Rd on Old Nashville, about 10 min away. I arrive and neither items are ready. 2 people in the drive thru, 1 person in store. After the guy that was waiting on his order in front of me, this young lady asked if I had an order, I advised her I sent for my mobile order about 10 min prior. She made my coffee, handed it to me, proceeds to the back to get the items for my sandwich, I asked how long it was going to take cause I had to be at work in 4 min, a reason why I sent for my food to be ready way before I arrived to give them plenty of time to prepare it, she said 30 seconds, and then when it was done, she came to the counter, threw my order across the counter, and said in a hateful ton, "have a nice day and here's your order, we only have one register and we are busy." I told her I didn't ask for the attitude that I was just going to get a refund so I could leave quick, and she said "get out of my store, you have your order, now go." I asked for her manager and she stated she was the manager. I asked for her DM name and she said "get out of my store."

Mexican food is one of my favorites, so this place is always a treat. The food is pretty decent, doesn't "knock your socks off", but it will satisfy any craving you have for mexican food. The salsa is very good. But where they may fall short in food, they more than make up for it at the bar. I have been going here for a few years and I have NEVER had a weak drink. I know I will always get my money's worth in this area. They serve quality alcohol and the mixed drinks are always on point. Portions are amazing and the drink menu is extensive. Mixed drinks are my favorite, and I've had my share - no disappointments here. Their menu even enticed my super masculine husband to order "girly" mixed drinks - they pack a punch!
