Okay everyone loves a good Cuban and one of the biggest factors imo would have to be the bread and the pork. I ordered the media noche basicallly a Cuban with sweetbread instead of the typical Cuban bread . The bread itself was soft somewhat chewy and the pork wasn't moist or flavorful as I was expecting . I hope it was an off day because they were quite busy but either way the sandwich is a 6/10 for me . The positive is the lady at the front desk she genuinely seems to want to connect with each customer and make them feel good. Maybe next time !

I love the Panera chain. The food at this location is consistent with the quality you'd get at any good Panera location. We went for dinner on a weekday night. It was moderately busy, but we got our order quickly.

Came here about 8 years ago to try this new place we found, still quality ingredients still just as good as ever
They've grown they now have three locals way super cool
I concur with other yelpers best pizza hands down

Every time I'm in philly and crave soup dumplings this where I go... 

It's located right in the heart of Chinatown, so expect it to get very busy during  brunch and dinner time! 
Usually service is decent here but everyone knows when you come here, you come for the food and not so much for the service.
The soup dumplings were amazing! 
The crabmeat and pork soup dumplings were good but the pork soup dumplings were better in my opinion. 
We also had the Chinese broccoli with fresh garlic and the shrimp dumplings. Both dishes were yummy! 

It's also a BYOB restaurant, but they charge for a corkage fee! And it's a cash only restaurant so bring cash or else pay the atm fee and use their atm right by the front door!

Everything we're tried off the menu has been great! Especially like the pretzels and Mac n cheese. Cool atmosphere, like to go during off hours due to the fact they do get busy, which is understandable--they have great a drink selection. Bartenders are always friendly

Went here some months ago. The sushi itself was pretty fresh, but also pretty average. Definitely not the best, but certainly not the worst. Presentation is nice, not pretentious like Osushi (disclaimer, haven't been there yet, but looking at the pictures from courier post and fb, it isn't hard to tell). So sushi overall is pretty good. Great for Cherry Hill, but just good overall.

Ramen was highlight. Broth was light, but seasoned nicely. Miso soup was awesome, the best I've ever had. Many other places season it too heavily, but this one is light. Katsu was meh, I could only taste the breading, but I've never had Katsu at any other place, so can't comment too much.

I think it's slightly overpriced considering the portion sizes and quality, but still within reason.

The best sushi place in Cherry Hill definitely.

I came here in the late afternoon with my 4 year old daughter, who brought her beloved stuffed animal with her.  We forgot it on the table when we left, and when we called first thing the next day, the woman who answered the phone said she remembered us coming in with it, but that it was not turned in.  As tables are bused immediately after people leave, I can only assume it was taken by our waitress or another employee, who kept it for themselves (it was brand new).  I hate to leave this review, as the food is actually very good and the owner is incredibly nice, but the apparent dishonesty of someone working there - particularly when it involves taking a little girl's toy, leaving her in tears - is pretty low.
I've only had a salad here but it was huge and delicious. My roommate loved the flatbread. Look forward to trying more on the menu.

Very authentic flavors and presentation. I had two different chicken tacos, each with its own unique flavor. Both really tasty. There are two bottles of salsa on your table. One tomatillo based (milder) with bright flavor and the other a smoky chipotle (little hotter). Both were also unique, and tasty. Service was quick and friendly. They charge for chips and salsa, which put my lunch with a drink and two tacos at $12.25 before tip. Therein is the reason for 4 stars instead of 5. Tacos are about $4 each and rather small, so free chips to go along with the salsa already on the table would get 5 stars from me.

Very disappointing dinner tonight. The food was good -- but the service was off the charts bad. After we arrived, our server took our drink orders and then disappeared for nearly 15 minutes. By the time we saw him again, 3 other tables that all arrived after us were already enjoying their appetizers and food. Once we finally placed our order, we waited another 15-20 minutes for our appetizer to show up, and then another 20-30 minutes for our entrees to arrive. Our server and the manager blamed some "glitch" on the problem, but every other table in the restaurant seemed to avoid this issue. Although our server and the manager both assured us that they would "take care" of us because of the poor service, when we received our check, it was for full price. We are long time customers of Rock 'n Sake and love the food, but we won't be coming to the Metairie location any more. I STRONGLY recommend that you avoid this location and instead visit the Warehouse District location -- where service is far superior.

Taste Bar is an incredible cocktail bar. They have delicious fries and I highly recommend the brussels sprouts. However, they have very limited entree options. With two entrees to choose from - (a pork burger and brick chicken), this isn't really a place you can eat at too often. My partner and I both love fries and brussels sprouts, unfortunately, both are fat-heavy dishes, and we find ourselves choosing other cocktail bars due to the lack of menu items at Taste. 
The other update I wanted to tack onto my original review can be construed as both a positive and a negative. Taste frequently updates their drink offerings, which is awesome if you love trying new cocktails. Unfortunately, it's sad to see your favorite drinks disappear from the menu over time. 
My final verdict? Taste is the perfect destination for trying creative, unique and high-end cocktails. You won't find drinks like these anywhere else. However, if you are hungry, eat somewhere first, because there won't be much to choose from.
The infused vodkas are super duper good, if you are not sure what to get go off the list or ask your bartender/server what they like. Only $3 a pop during happy hour you can't go wrong.

No good, employees/ owner or whatever you wanna call this guy was so rude at the front window. The menu is NOT vegetarian friendly AT ALL! My friend found a bug in her food and told them, they then gave her a different meal instead. My food did not taste fresh, the salsa tasted like they got it from a can then watered it down. DISGUSTING! Don't waste your time here! The pictures are really deceiving. Don't get me wrong the pictures of the food look really delicious but the pickled veggies in my taco reeked like gym shoes and were far past their best by date. I couldn't even finish my meal.

So never having an authentic cheesesteak before in my life beyond Subway in Texas, which by the ways gross, I began sinking my teeth into this Prince of Steaks sandwich. At first I was thrown off by the said use of cheese whiz and then the bread was a little chewy, not soft like an Italian restaurant type bread. By about the 3rd or 4th bite, my brain began saying, "heck yeah baby!" I scarfed down the entire sandwich that I applied extra pickles to and a piping hot bag of fries with spice and warm cheese........soooooooooo good! You won't find these baby's in Texas!! I am sure going to miss this when I go home......... :-(
Sushi burrito was so good.  It's inventive and fresh.  Love this addition to KOP.

Was in search of a sweet treat after walking all day and stumbled upon this little place. Wish we would have eaten lunch here too, but we had stopped elsewhere before! Carrot cake cupcake was so good!

The food was hot. That's all that was good. Speaker at drive through is waaaay too loud. Didn't get my order right and there was a fly, yes a fly, in my Sierra Mist. Prob more than one but I didn't notice until I had drank it(them) all.

I've had friends who ordered their cakes from here and it was pretty good. On the other hand, the lunch items we had when we dined in were pretty average. I ordered the chicken salad with a side of okra and the boyfriend ordered a Reuben sandwich with fries. 
The chicken salad was good, but nothing I'd come running back for. The okra was bland, but I guess there's not too much you can do with it. The roll that came with it seemed like it was taken out of a bag of rolls you get from the grocery store. The Reuben sandwich was tasty, but you can never go wrong with that. The fries actually had some flavor to it so I was satisfied with those. They brought out a square jello type thing. I'm not sure what it was and our waitress didn't tell us. I tried a bite and it wasn't terrible, but I just pushed it off to the side. 
Other than that, our waiter was prompt. The restaurant is clean. I can finally say I've eaten here, but not rushing back.

This was a favorite place but nowadays its hit or miss at best. Ever since the chef that put this place on the map left there is a new cook every week and the food reflects that. Good beer? Well you can get that anywhere in Seminole Heights with service to go with it. I'm a local who dines out frequently and I must say the Mermaid struggles to compete with other establishments at this point in its life span. A place that started off strong can no longer keep consistent staff and in my opinion that reflects ownership. Spend your $15 for a burger at another trendy hot spot.

We came late late.on a Sunday night and had a great time!  We were quickly greeted upon entering and were sat at a nice clean table.  We quickly placed our drink and food order since it was late.  The drinks were what we expected but the food was another story.  It was unbelievable.......fresh crisp condiments with an awesome flavor, they were quickly explained by our server so we knew what we were eating and extra Kimchee was brought to the table as it is my favorite ( it is made in house and was so good I bought a quart to go home with me!) The beef and shrimp were well marinated and very flavorful and the rice was perfect not gluey or sticky awesome for it being the end of the day.

I would have given the 6 stars if possible.  Definately worth a visit.

Margaritas by Zach were 5/5!!! So delicious, but the food left something to be desired. The spicy shrimp tacos had this bizarre sweet sauce, as did the mahi mahi tacos. This sauce made the tacos barely edible. We had guacamole which was made with avocados that were not ripe at all...stop trying to use avocados that aren't ready people!!! The salsa was straight cilantro which left it almost bitter. I'm only giving it a 3/5 because of the margaritas and good service, the food was pretty bad.

AWFUL!! Do not waste your time or money. I wish I could give 0 stars instead of one.

-My food was served 15 minutes after everyone else at my table.
-Price were high for the quality.
- A large number of menu items were not available "Coming Soon".
-Water not refilled
-Now 3 hour later I feel very very sick.
-The list goes on...

I like like like this place.
I've only been here once but that was such a relaxing enjoyable breakfast.
Reward your hard working taste buds; go here.

BYO.

Ample and creative cocktail menu with real attention paid to mixing. One of the bartenders, Stephen, isn't letting anything subpar get into a customer's hands. We sampled about 6 of the drinks on their cocktail list and all were awesome, especially the Creole Coffee, Sheilavsit, and the Absinthe Suissesse. 

Atmosphere is welcoming and more on the modern side (but still homey) for most places in the French Quarter. The food is also a more modernized take on traditional Louisiana cuisine. We had the hoppin' John crawfish salad and an order of cracklin's at the bar with our drinks, and both were very good, offering some traditional New Orleans flavor but being very light which was perfect for a pre-dinner snack.

This is a great place to spend an evening. My GF and I thoroughly enjoyed our visit. The service was excellent, the music was very good and the food was delicious. We started with cold-boiled shrimp. Diana opted for the scallops for an entrée and I had the clam basket. Both were excellent. The clams were the best I've had, the scallop I stole was great. 

This is a wonderful place for a couple's night out. I don't give out five star reviews very often, but Ricky T's earned this one. Pay them a visit, you won't be disappointed.


Will and Diana
Seminole, Florida

We discovered this place while staying at Innisbrook. They had the best country fried steak that I've ever eaten.  Also the seasonal pumpkin pancakes were out of this world! Nice clean interior and good atmosphere. Would definitely come back!
An hour for a a box of melted cheese.  Somehow the crust is way undercooked on the bottom and thinner than the fork.  Not worth the hefty price tag.

Came here only once while in Philly for the SIOP conference. 

First impression was that it was very clean. 

Second impression was that the guys behind the counter were all kind of tough looking. But they're damn good cooks so who cares. 

I loved my chicken cheesesteak. I took a bite of my friend's regular cheesesteak and I thought it was really good! My other friend got a hummus gyro and she said it was good. Saw the guys making a sexy looking salad behind the counter and felt food envy. I would love to come back here if I'm ever in the area. Definitely underrated as far as cheesesteaks go.

I am sorry but the bill was $160. The food was just awful and the ambiance was 0 being exactly what it is a low-mid range Best Western Hotel Restaurant.  We were staying in the Hotel Roosevelt and wanted a quick meal. The ratings were high enough and we were like OK. What a bad decision, the food across the board was just not tasteful and the preparation seemed like they were trying to make a statement but it was just a mish mash of ingredients that did not work. I had a New York Strip that came smothered in spinich and half cooked mushrooms. It was just awful. The Lobster appetizer was just some lobster with butter  on top of a cut roll for like $20. Come on. So disappointed. The chicken was fine nothing fantastic but it was very small and $30 bucks. This was so over priced for such low quality dining experience. Really left me upset. 

We ate at Red Fish Grill the Night before which is no high cousine Center with a group of 13 and everyone just reveled in the meal, kids, parents alike. And the total bill for 13 was $200. Tonight we had 3 adult meals period for $130 and the meal was terrible.

When we are in a new town my husband (a Chicago pizza lover) has to try the local version of their pizza and Mona Lisa was the perfect place to try New Orleans twist on it. Our travel guide said it was the best place in town for pizza, and they weren't wrong: we loved it!

The pizza was a thin crust and they offered more than the usual pepperoni and cheese pizza, but had some finer ingredients, such as goat cheese and pine nuts. One can create their own, but even several of their specialty pizza were vegetarian. Even our meat eaters ordered veg. My favorite was the spinach pizza (we tried each others). One medium pizza can feed two average hungry eaters. 
I was in a pasta mood and had a vegetarian spinach lasagna. This was by far the best lasagna I have had on this continent!

The atmosphere was very casual, the walls are creatively decorated with every possible version of the Mona Lisa painting, prizes were reasonable, and the staff was extremely nice and helpful.
Very good service and food. Lots of GF options. Would highly recommend to anyone with vegan, vegetarian, or GF diets

Renato catered my wedding and did an absolutely phenomenal job!  The food was beyond amazing, people are still saying it was the best lasagna they have ever had. On top of that he coordinated our rentals and brought along his really charming catering staff.  He was really flexible with staff, they cut the cake even though my brother made it and the staff even helped clean up decorations after the event.  A lot of wedding caterers are always trying to up-sell or nickle and dine you.  Renato treats the event like a wedding for a family member.  I explained that we were on a tight budget and he worked with me to find a menu that met our budget and was still a full meal of really amazing food.  He made the event really special by going above and beyond in every way, including putting together a really beautiful buffet display.  We will definitely be making a regular pilgrimage to his restaurant to get more of his delicious food.  Honestly, I can't recommend Renato and the full Via Maestra 42 staff enough!

EH.
Everything was "almost there".
Geno's is better with provolone cheese.
So you can pretend you are in a local 'cheesy' (unlike the cheese steaks) deli and not at a place where they are supposed to dare compete with Pat's King Of Steaks.
Don't you get that hot sauce from the pumps either. It's deadly! It ruins the whole thing.

The seatings are comfortable because it's spaced out well around a nice ghetto corner facing (yay) Pat's. Neon lights and framed pictures with the whole world.

Maybe that's what did it. Oh no wait, maybe it was that crazy gut aura I got from those signs that read something in the likes of "SPEAK ENGLISH! THIS IS AMERICA!" Okay a beloved police officer died because of a foreigner and you own some harley's across the street. Doesn;t matter to me. Get some class and better food.

(Too bad because the service on the line was pretty great. HAHA the irony!)
A pretty decent place when you absolutely musty have Chinese food.

They get 0 stars from me as far as pizza is concerned.  I stopped ordering from here several months ago.  I would order a large plain pizza for pickup at a price of $6.99...not bad, huh?!  Think again.  The crust was always rubbery and the sauce had little to no flavor.  But for the price, I guess you shouldn't expect much.  Well, the last visit I arrived for pick up and was told my pizza was not ready yet.  After waiting approx. 5 min I got my pizza and headed home, just around the corner.  When I opened the box I immediately noticed the pizza was not hot and had apparently been sitting for awhile.  So why did I have to wait for a cold pizza?!?!  I won't be back.

Came here for brunch before heading up to chop our Christmas tree down. They are the perfect little breakfast stop! I had the pork belly Benedict and as a Benedict lover I was thoroughly impressed. The bread they use is amazing. Great service from the waitress who helped us- we had a good laugh about a handsy couple just inches away from our table. Thankfully it didn't ruin my appetite lol! I told my bf from now on that needs to be our tradition before we get our tree. And will definitely be back before then!

I really want to like the Royale!  So many of my friends love it, the owner has sponsored many civic events and causes through the business.  This is worth at least one star in my book.  In addition, they have a decent beer menu and limited, but decent menu, another star...

I just can't get past the "too laid back to serve you," and "too cool to care" attitude that comes from staff.  I leave ticked off everytime I go.  Not good.

BTW, The Owner of the Royale as asked me to convey they they prefer groups smaller than 6.  Large groups cause delays in their kitchen.
Called them & they literally hung up on me mid sentence. He said something, when i asked him to repeat himself, he literally sounded frustrated & just hung up. Extremely unprofessional.
I got the Greek omelet and there was a bone in it from the chicken, which after tasting/biting down in it I was turned off by the whole meal. The sweet potato tots were good though.
Price was high, but I was very tipsy after only two chocolate covered cherry drinks and they were good. Crab and artichoke dip was very good.
Service was slow and inconsistent. Food was under cooked. The sausage patties were rubbery and my fried eggs over well were runny.

I have been to this location 2 previous times with no issues. Today I ordered smoothies for my wife and kids and my wife's smoothie had a large hairball in her smoothie. I immediately called and they refunded my money but that is unacceptable!
The food is always good here but the employees are very very slow. There's always a massive line,  of because of an influx of people but because of sluggish service

My coworkers and I placed an order for Capriotti's. I've been to different Capriottis locations before, and have always had stellar sandwiches. My experience here did not disappoint my stomach. 

In total we ordered 13 sandwiches/salads and 2 bags of chips. They forgot a sandwich and both bags of chips in our order. This was frustrating, but we figured it out. Their sandwiches are massive, so luckily we had enough to share!  The Bobbie is a fan-favorite, and my personal go-to. It features Homemade Turkey, cranberry sauce, stuffing, and mayo. It is basically Thanksgiving in a sandwich. The BBQ Chicken Salad is another one of my favorite things to order. It comes with a chipotle ranch dressing that literally makes you want to lick your bowl.

Food: 5 stars.
Missing food: -1 star

Even amidst a pandemic this business SHINES! I heard they started doing deep dish pizza as takeout became so necessary and so I had to scope this out of myself. 

It is TRUE. The menu is super abbreviated  at this time (considering how big it was before especially) but the addition of pizza is a total game changer. Now I can indulge in a proper martini AND pizza. My 2 favorite things. The deep dish itself is great, its a build you own style, so we love that! I chose to add onions and spinach. They let us do a half and half so that my husband could also add sausage. Overall it was solid. There was about 30 minutes between placing order and receiving pizza. They did give us that heads up. We had plenty of boozy martinis to savor while waiting, and so it wasn't even an issue. 

I genuinely have so much respect and adoration for O'Bistro. There are zero gimmicks or trends or cool points. It's just simple, timeless, and lovely.

Our first time trying this place. Ordered the thin crust pizza with pepperoni, sausage, onions, olives and mushrooms.  Crust edge was cooked great but the pizza itself was soft and somewhat soggy. We tagged more cheese, onions and mushrooms than pepperoni, and the sausage was so thinly sliced we could hardly taste it.  Don't know of this was because we came in at 830pm since they close at 9 but we were just not thrilled. Ordered a garden salad consisting of only iceberg lettuce chunks hit it had plenty of veggies on top. Not worth 5 bucks though. We will not be coming back.

1. It's a good cheesesteak, not going to lie.

2. The line is not worth it. I feel bad for tourists. 

3. My first time I stood in line and when I left I had to wash my clothing because the cheesesteak smell was IN my clothing.

4. Indoor dining, upstairs a plus. Who wants to sit outside when it's chilly and the weathers changing like today...

5. I felt unbelievably pressured to order quickly my first time around... I don't like that feeling.

6. only 3 stars because I've had better for cheaper.

Let me first state that I am giving one Star, as that is the lowest that I could give.  Our "eating" experience was less than good, and there is no way we could call it a "dinning" experience!  Our server approached us immediately and got drinks and took the order of all seven people in attendance.  We were promptly brought our salads, within two (2) minutes of ordering, which I later found out that this is the policy of Carrabba's.  Two to three minutes later, before I even got the crushed black pepper on my salad, our dinner arrived.  We all had to push our salads aside to finish them.  My dinner, which consisted of Grilled Chicken and a Cavatappi Pasta was brought to me undercooked and pink.  I proceeded to grab the waiter, who was very apologetic and he brought it back to be recooked.  When they brought my dinner back to me TWENTY minutes later, it was the wrong dish.  The manager/Expediter came over with the usual apology and proceeded to tell me that they are rebooking and it takes approximately 14 minutes to recooked, and that they were taking the charge off the bill. Ni wasn't looking for a free meal, however, I wanted a pleasant dinning experience, which apparently you can NEVER get at Carrabba's, S their company policy is to get the main course out within 14 minutes of ordering, according to our server.  When they finally brought my food out for the third time, it again was pink and under cooked.  This time I sent it back, not getting anything.  The manager came again and apologized, along with a $25.00 gift card, and the same undercooked dinner in a to go container that was microwaved to finish off the raw chicken.  I don't want the card I wanted to enjoy dinner with my guests.  I doubted that I will ever use the card, and gave it to an older gentleman next to our table, so that they might use it.  I won't be going back to Carrabba's anywhere in the world, as if I want to have in and out dinning, I will go to McDonalds, where at lease the food is cooked, and I'm not rushed out of the facility!  So much for CHAIN RESTAURANTS
Try the chicken pesto sandwich it was amazing!!! Great happy hour prices and excellent beer selection. It was a little crowded but they can't help that they're popular! :)

Ok so our waiter was nice and the food came really fast. I got the cajun Alfredo and if you aren't feeling adventurous and wanna play it safe GET IT because if was soo good and it came with really fluffy bread. When i went i was kinda sick and I still ate all my food because it was soo good :) Highly recommend if you aren't sure where to go.

I eat in here at least once a week! I live right down the street, so I'm within walking distance. The food is always delicious!!!! The service, however, varies on who is working. Sometimes it is really fast, other times very slow. Sometimes you get a ton of rice, beans, meat, etc. Other times, they are very skimpy and you have to ask for more. Some employees are really friendly and others are cranky. But I love the food and I live very close, so I keep coming back. Free refills on soda is great. The burrito bowl is my favorite thing to order! I like Chipotle more than Qdoba because Chipotle is spicier.
Place is pretty good.   Good service.   Good Italian beef sandwich.  Cool atmosphere.

Only place in this city where u can get: 
1) a fish sandwich
2) a set of queen or full size sheets
3) and a bootleg DVD
All while having a drink at the bar. This place is SUPER hood, but I think that's part of the charm...lol

Two friends and I wanted to eat some where new. We are all long time Santa Barbarians, eat out frequently.Came here at 7:30, probably because of Restaurant Week place was completely packed. Noise level was considerable. Old Fashion cocktail was very good. Onion soup may be the best I've ever had. Obviously made from scratch. One friend had the fricassee  salad and the special with a battered Crispy Rock fish in a delicious white cream sauce with a distinctive almost smoky flavor. Other friend had onion soup and a salad. I had the soup and the wagyu beef special with frites. Everything was very good, the Onion soup and the Crispy Rock fish special were stand outs. I am looking forward to going back again to try some of the other menu items, but probably on a week night when it would be just a tad less noisy. Recommended.

Didn't have a great experience here, but seems like a really popular place. Came on a Saturday night and it was super crowded, but was able to get a spot at the bar. Both drinks we had were really good! I think one was a grapefruit cocktail, and the other was a pumpkin spice ale which was fantastic. 

We order the Paneer Relleno entree which was decent, but nothing special. I was bummed because it wasn't served hot, it was just warm.. which to me is a major issue. 

Also ordered the dinner special. The avocado chicken curry was some of the worst indian food i've ever had. It tasted like a strange flavor of chicken soup, but was really bland and just really not good. I did enjoy the yams which were flavorful and cooked well, and the yogurt, rice, dal, and naan were fine. 

Overall it is a pricey place for really mediocre Indian food, but the ambience and location are great. There are way better options for food in Nashville, and I wouldn't recommend this place.

We love NOLA! And possibly more than that...we love Po-Boys! 

Night three two of our four day adventure finally led us to Mahony's. This joint was recommended to us by many. Supposedly the best po-boys in New Orleans! I think that's a pretty hefty title, but they were definitely yummy! 

We ordered fried green tomatoes with pimento cheese spread and they were NOM. The po-boys hit the spot and had a great amount of filling! I always find po-boys to be a bit dry, so we asked for some remoulade on the side and that was very helpful! I think if they had put more sauce on the sandwhich itself we'd be reaching that "best po-boy in NOLA" threshold for sure. 

You could really tell that the staff was proud to work there and passionate about customer service. The decorations were fun and Mardi Gras-esque and the whole place felt very alive. 

I definitely recommend if you're in search of a delicious Po-Boy that you can sit down and devour!
Go here - fun location, good sushi and great outdoor patio.  Check out their happy hour too!

My family has been coming to the South Meadows Wild Garlic since it opened, and it has gone so downhill over the past year. The past two orders we've received (ordered through Door Dash)  have been lukewarm at best, always are missing items, and any bread (pizza crust, knots, etc.) have been burnt to a crisp. These are the knots we received tonight that were literally black and tasted like char. We threw the entire order of knots in the trash and were offered $2.47 back for the almost $8 we paid. We got $0.18 cents back for the 6 sauces we ordered and never received. I don't know if it's just to go orders that are this bad or is it's this bad in person also. We won't be returning. It seems quality is no longer of concern at this restaurant.

I have been to many of the specialty burger places in town , but have not yet found one to top Port of Call. 
The huge burger , cooked to order, is served with a huge baked potato with all the fixings. The burger is nice and juicy and the baked potato compliments it well. Port of Call has been on Esplanade for many years and still served quality food.

We stopped by Cochin Butcher after our excellent tour of the National World War II Museum, it's only a 5 minute walk.

The look and feel of this place is like hipster central combined with real butchers and great grunge and alternative classics playing loudly in the background.

The atmosphere and food is very good here, the prices are not.

Ok so we had 4 excellent sandwiches, all were excellent.  The Pig Mac, Pork Muffuletta, the Cubano and the Moroccan Lamb sandwich.  We all thought the sandwiches were absolutely delicious and generously proportioned.  They definitely hit the spot and had great flavor.

However, I thought the prices were really high or I tipped too much.  Since when does 4 sandwiches with no sides, tap water and tip cost $60?!?

Anyways, it was a sandwich experience and I do understand why Couchon has the hype it does.  And management has certainly extracted full value of that hype.  Enjoy!

I have been to Taqueria Feliz on three occasions--once when they first opened, and twice to give it a second and third try. 

My first visit to Taqueria was just okay. My fiancé and I were seated in front of the windows near the canal. This was unfortunate, because the sun was going down and was glaring directly into my eyes, to the point where I was tearing up. There were no shades on the windows at the time, so we moved to a different table where the sun was less annoying.

I understand that the place had literally open about two days prior, but our waiter clearly had not studied the menu or the specials. He told us that all of the apps during happy hour were half-priced. When we received our bill, we come to find out that they were not. When we discussed this with our waiter, we received no apology and no price adjustment. He just gave a shrug. 

On my second and third visits, the waiters were definitely more knowledgable. A general statement about their food--the tacos are very small with a little bit of meat/veggies and the price is a bit high. I recommend the brisket tacos, which are spicy with a good flavor. Start with the guacamole and have 1 1/2 taco orders per person.

I noticed on my third visit, when sat next to the windows on the canal side again, that they had added shades onto the windows! Hallelujah.
Food and service was great. I had the pork chop which was off the hook. Place is small but it was enough. I do highly recommend for a higher quality meal in Treasure Island. Ry the carpaccio.

I'm honestly amazed that this restaurant got good reviews. I've tasted a lot of pho, and this is one of the worst. The broth does not have any flavor at all and the noodles do not come apart easily, but rather stay stuck together like glue. I personally have had way better pho than this place; I would say it is below average. The spring rolls I am not much a fan of either. I do like their bubble tea, however.

Hands down, must try!!! Great spot, very flavorful food! I tried the hand  pulled noodles and fell in love! Broth was rich and embodied every part of what I was expecting. There weren't  many people, but it was perfect vibes. I can see this spot becoming a local favorite quickly. Definitely come and try!!

Today's experience left me a little hot under the collar. Although I am still a fan of Sasha's delicious salmon & trout crepe, trendy decor, extensive wine selections and it's gorgeous Demun location....the service has got to be better! The same flamboyant (bold) bartender/server who waited on me my previous visit waited on me today as well. He does not say "hello", he does not say "goodbye", he does not say "thank you", he does not ask if "everything is alright", he does not inquire if you "need anything else".

In short he does nothing aside from place the order and deliver it to the table. This could be a personal experience; I did notice he was a bit more social with other patrons on both occasions. I'm not certain if they are regulars, friends or just the right color.  Whatever the case it made me extremely uncomfortable. I enjoyed my crepe and even though I wanted to ask for other items I refrained from calling him over to make any additional requests. 
After dropping my food off he never returned. I even had to get up to ask him for my check. Then I had to get up to give him the check so I could finalize my stay and carry on with my day. 

The next time I visit this Sasha's location; if I decide to visit again at all, I'm running for my life if this guy is working. It's a shame for such a great spot to have left such a bad taste in my mouth. Service over everything!

~Christy

Okay, let me just put this out there...

I would go here before Chipotle or Qdoba any day. The service was quick, the food was delicious, and it was cheap! I'm a gal living on a very tight budget, so to be able to have a great meal for under $10 is possibly the highlight of my week.

Chips and queso are only $2, and you don't want to pass it up. Worth every penny to have that cheesy goodness in your belly.

I went simple with a cheese and carnitas quesadilla, and the meat was so flavorful!! It was a party in my mouth. 

So overall I give Pancheros 4 stars, the only thing keeping them from a 5 is that it isn't a sit down restaurant so the service is obviously not as good as sit down place would be.

Came here with a reservation but waited 20 min to be seated. We have the breakfast bite, seafood paella, and churros. All of them were well made and delicious. The lighting in the restaurant was soft and dark which created a intimate ambience.

Came here with a group of coworkers on a Friday for lunch. We work down the street and wanted to check it out. This was a while back so the menu could be different now. I tried the gumbo and it was pretty good but I was sort of weirded out by the fact that it had greens in it. It was also served with potato salad, which I thought was a cute, cultural nod to Louisianians who eat gumbo with potato salad. I got the catfish as my meal and it was pretty good. I wasn't wowed but it was a good lunch. My coworkers were all satisfied with their meals as well. The place was empty so we had it all to ourselves. I like the setup and the decor. I will have to go back for dinner and drinks and update this review.

The best cheesesteak... I had whiz and onions on mine.  So flavorful, they have a great selection of drinks and sodas. Service was friendly and efficient. Much better than gino's and pat's (over rated).  Plenty of seating upstairs.

801 is really, really great.

Everyone knows that not all steakhouses are created equal. I can truthfully say that I had the best steak of my entire adult life recently at 801. This place is worth every penny, and you're going to need some, because it's expensive.

I am usually just here for drinks because I love the bar and they make a mean dirty martini (all the stars for blue cheese olives.) The staff is always wonderful, and it's a great spot to grab a cocktail or a glass of wine and catch up with friends. Beware of the smells though, because you're going to end up ordering something, even if you aren't hungry.

I've had dinner here several times as well, and the food is some of the best I've had in St. Louis. I ordered the 8oz filet on my last visit, and it completely blew me away. I had a glass of red zin alongside of my steak, which was the perfect choice. The mashed potatoes and asparagus (family style) were almost as good as our entrees. 

Service is always wonderful, the valet is easy, and it's a really beautiful establishment. I'll obviously be back very soon!
Very good masala dosa... and generally really good food. And I am Indian, so that says alot.

In from out of town, I came here with two girlfriends. We had a great time, good food, fun setting, and they have cocktails. This place certainly has a fun, rustic vibe that veers on hipster without being pretentious or any negative aspects of that word. Large portions on my pesto pasta and the waiter was really great, keeping our water refilled. Located in the heart of the french quarter - we walked back to Bourbon to engage in debauchery! Also surrounded by great galleries and cute shops. Will return next time I'm in town!

This is a review for Metro as an earlier spot. As in coming here before 8pm.
We were walking down Mass Ave and finding every place packed with a 30+ minute wait for two. A lot of the restaurants that had the wait were not worth it. Enter Metro, which appeared almost empty and advertised a barbecue chicken sandwich special.
Two female bartenders and some friendly, chatty patrons. Decor overall is a little dated, particularly the carpets, and the whole place reeks of stale smoke.
What's funny is that this didn't come up on Yelp for this area when I searched "restaurants" even though they serve food, and actually have a pretty good food menu. Nachos, burgers, a balsamic chicken pesto sandwich, mac and cheese, boneless wings, etc. And weirder is that there is no indication that this is a gay bar from the outside, and even the interior is hard to figure out. My wife noticed a penis bottle opener, and most of the patrons and staff seemed to be gay, so we just assumed and, reading the reviews later, just confirmed it.
It's weird because, in most other cities, gay bars fly the pride flag on the outside, or at least have something inside to indicate what they are. Maybe this place doesn't want to turn anyone off? Maybe they're more worried about harassment in Indiana (the gay bar in Bloomington also is pretty discrete)? I don't know...
But the food was actually pretty decent. The chicken was dry and the fries weren't great, but I was happy to have something to eat that didn't taste awful and didn't require an hour wait. They did use romaine for lettuce (nice) and everything was generally well-cooked. Plus, they were really quick, and we were able to get to our show at the Murat without being too late. I really appreciated that. Food was pretty cheap too. Both of our sandwiches were $8 with a side, and everything else was under $10.
Draft beer selection wasn't great: Stella, Flat 12 Walkabout and some domestic swill. But they strangely had a really good craft bottle selection with about 15 options. Definitely on the pricey side. I think my Widmer black IPA was at least $5 based on the total bill. The specialty cocktail list looked really, really good though, and we may end up coming back for that at some point.
This would be a 3.5 if I could give it out. Certainly not a bad option on Mass Ave, but there are other places with better food, for sure. We may come back here later at night one time, more for the bar and club scene, and have a fantastic time. I just wanted to put it out there that this is an earlier option.

This was a stop in my never-ending quest to find the perfect Oyako donburi at a local eatery.  This place definitely didn't fit the bill.  I ordered Oyako Ju; the sauce was pretty good, on the sweeter side, but the chicken was extremely tough and dry.  I might have rated this place lower, but a friend ordered a teriyaki/roll combo and liked it.

This place seems to have a community of regulars.  When we were there, the majority of patrons who came in (altho not together) knew each other as well as the waitress.

We stopped by sweet 16th on our way through Nashville and OMG - the breakfast sandwich (egg and cheese on a savory scone) was legitimately the best breakfast sandwich I've ever had. Not too greasy, just the right level of salt, and so fluffy but filling. The price was also super reasonable! We also tried the brownie, a cookie (or two), more scones, and a pecan bar. I'll definitely want to come back anytime I'm in town.
Very nice place, the food is good and they have daily specials. The priices are incredibly low and the servers are very nice. They have alot on the menu from seafood, steak, chicken eyc.
Amazing ! Will definitely be back, Ribs were very good.  Brisket Better , and Turkey was to die for ! No Sauce needed . Had to order a second round . Will def be back

Stopped in for dinner last night. We were seated right away. I was pleasantly surprised at the healthy options on the menu. My turkey burger in a lettuce wrap was well seasoned(maybe even a little too peppery for me but I'm picky) and juicy. I also like the variety of better choice sides. I had the cole slaw. It's nice to know I can indulge my family but still stay on track with my own food choices. I took a star away for the pepper!

Absolutely great food and environment. Great location to with many cool little stores to shop at after. Some fun bars down there as well. Also, service was phenomenal. Highly recommend the steak sandwich and chicken nachos!

Clearly, I stand behind their mission but I can't continue to help through them when they offer a terrible product. I ordered my favorite soup, matzo ball soup and got a caesar salad with it. The salad was soggy with dressing and it tasted like someone threw fish oil all over it. Old fishy oil. It was disgusting. If the croutons were not drenched in that, they would have been tasty. 
Now the matzo ball soup. The broth tasted like a powder packet broth and the matzo ball had a thick film over the entire thing like it had been sitting somewhere developing a callous. It was far too dense and while they called it "smoked", it tasted like weird sausage.
Ugh, I don't know where these positive reviews are coming from, I was so disappointed.

Great hoagies, quick and friendly service.  I'm not sure how this can "tacky up" the neighborhood, since at least from the outside is the same as the prior french bistro.  No, it's not trendy like Middle Child, but it doesn't have an absurd set of rules just to eat an egg sandwich.  I like Lee's.  They make good quality old school Philly hoagies and cheesesteaks in a nice, clean setting.  Lee's is perfect when you want a good sandwich at a decent price without any pretentiousness.

First time back in months and they have a new menu.   Over all very nice visit.  Very good burgers and Patty melts.   Saw an onion ring tower go by and they shrank.   Boo.   Fast serving service as usual.   Only negative is fact that waiter was not fully attentive in keeping our drinks full.
I ate here on a Sunday for their buffet. I was very impressed with the food all around & will definitely be coming back to order off the menu.

This place rocks.  Well, unless you want to get a loaf of bread at 6 pm when they are gone for the day.

This is the traditional french bakery run by a French-Canadian family.  They show up at 2am to get the place going, and by 9, the lines are out the door to buy the $0.85 demi-baguette, the $1.55 baguette, or the most expensive boule they have at $2.85. Come early though, as they sell out almost every single day.  The prices are that to be expected of a traditional French bakery, where people buy their bread every morning.

Stopped there for lunch since I enjoy Asian food and never visited this place. Had the Ginger  Broccoli with chicken and it is served with rice (brown rice for me). Ordered the small for $6.99 which was just the right amount of food. Food was very flavorful but I think a bit pricey. However, I will return and try another dish in the future.
First visit, clean, staff friendly, the food, aaahhhh, the food! Tuna ceviche tasty, light. Hummas bruschetta had a pleasing texture, the naan perfect temp. Definitely a repeat visit in order

I have been looking for an authentic creole restaurant in the bay area for a while and was lucky enough to stumble upon Chief's Creole Cafe. The first thing I noticed upon entering the restaurant is the incredible ambiance of the place. The dining area is adorned with antique furnishings which gives the place a "homey" feel. The building once housed a bar in the 1930s and the owners wisely kept restored the original decor. 

As for the  food, I chose the Creole Gumbo made with chicken, large fresh shrimp, crab, crawfish, okra, and andouille in a rich roux sauce. Be warned that the dish is spicy so you will be drinking a lot of water!  The entrees come with a nice sized house salad with homemade dressing and delicious freshly made muffins. I finished the meal off with a pair of beignets, one plain and one "dirty." Like everything else at Chief's, they were freshly made and absolutely tasty. 

During my meals, the owners (Mr. and Mrs. "B") checked on me to make sure every thing was to my satisfaction and the rest of the staff was very nice and personable. On my way out I walked through their outdoor seating area which is nicely furnished with beautiful plants and cozy lighting. 

Do yourself a favor and visit the wonderful Chief's Creole Cafe for truly authentic Louisiana cooking.

I will admit I have been to Baxters several times and have yet reviewed the place yet...my bad!  The place is not much to look at, but they have great food and friendly service.  Larry the bartender is always ready with a trivia question and really makes you feel welcome.  

I have come with business colleagues for lunch about 6 times and have never been disappointed and I recommend the cheese steaks, chicken salads, and turkey plate.  You won't be disappointed if you look past their appearance of just another bar!
Amazing food, my favorite thing right now is the Jax salad with steak, never disappoints!!!

I don't go here much anymore due to the long wait times for food, but I gave it a shot again. I ordered 12 tacos. 1/2 crispy and 1/2 soft. I got home and they were all soft. I called and told them and they said they were going to put it in the book. I called a day or so later, and told them I wanted to put in the order for those 6 crispy tacos. I specifically called it in a while before I was leaving because they are really slow getting food ready. They said 15-20 minutes. I arrived about 25 minutes later to pick up my tacos. When I arrived, I told them my name.  About 5 minutes later, the guy I told my name to went and got someone else and started talking about me saying "that girl who complained is here" The other guy started typing an order into the computer, and then came to me and said your tacos will be ready soon. My tacos were out in another 15 minutes. My guess is they didn't even put the order in until the guy was typing it in while I was standing there. And make me feel awkward in doing so. I mean, stuff happens. But it should NOT take 45 minutes to get 6 tacos. Especially when there were only 5 other people in the restaurant. If they could be more efficient, then I'd be there a lot more often. The foods good.

Grounds are lovely and lots to do while you wait - and you're going to wait. Biscuits are overrated. They're more like buttery dinner rolls. Service was excellent, they had lots of friendly and attentive staff. But I wouldn't come back for the food. Fried chicken was underwhelming, and the pancakes and waffles were very sweet. However, the pork was really good. It tasted like sweet, smoky pork - it didn't need a sauce or any other cover up.

Stopped in for brunch this morning just before 11AM. I was surprised that we were seated immediately, then I learned that we made it just in time before the late morning rush. The specials are listed on a chalkboard on the wall, and our waitress described them to us and gave her recommendations. They all sounded amazing, but I already had in my mind that I wanted a carb heavy meal.

I opted for the Amaretto French Toast. I was nervous because I feared it may be too sweet. I hate when I get a "sweet" breakfast item and then feel nauseated halfway through the meal because of the overabundance of sugar. This french toast was PERFECT. It was french toast with an almond crust on top, rather than slices of bread infused with sugar. The vanilla bean maple syrup was also a nice touch. The portion size was excellent. I was able to finish my meal, but didn't feel like I had a food baby erupting. 

Overall, I think this is an excellent spot for brunch. I'd recommend going earlier to avoid the wait. It also appeared that they took reservations (which is rare for brunch). I will definitely be returning, and possibly with a bottle of champagne for some mimosas (BYOB!).

Delicious burgers! Plenty of toppings. Good selection of beer. Burgers are big, my sister and I split one. Also had sweet potato fries that were great. It is a little dark in there even in daytime. Small TVs at each table. Lots of bar seating with a few tables in back for 5 maybe 6. Very friendly and helpful staff. This place is very close to Haslam's Books and Mazzaro's Italian Market.

I have to admit I still miss Miller's Marketplace in Woodstown. Their stuff was just incredible all around and it was the perfect size shop. On the other hand, The Amish Market offers a circular purchasing format with so many delectable goods that I often just get overwhelmed/anxious and leave with the most fattening items. It's super healthy.

So here you'll find doughnuts, baked goods, candies, nuts, wine tastings, a small eatery, deli meats, salads, cheeses, chunks of meat, fried chicken, pretzels, more cheeses, soaps, produce, and smoothies. Did I forget anything? Like I said, overwhelming!

I prefer shopping here to visiting a traditional supermarket, but the prices can be a bit higher so you gotta be careful and monitor yourself. I also like visiting during off hours, like closer to closing on Friday evenings or Thursday afternoon. Saturday at any time can be utter madness.

This market is close enough to my current residence (which is always changing, let's be real), so for the time being, I'll continue to patronize when I can.

I really love this place 
The WonTon soup is sooo good 
Mongolian Beef is so awesome 
The waitress is so very friendly 
I  found this place last year while visiting 
my Son and family!!!  First place I ate this 
year

Well as one of the residents have said to me many times. The pizza here is like the best addiction you could ever have, and you crave this pizza at all hours of the night. I really like their fresh ingredients & unique pizza style. I had the garlic basil. Absolutely loved it. It's got this great hometown feel & it's perfect for a quick pizza fix or a date night. It feels like it's been around forever but the pizza always feels like it's new & different. Probably thanks so much for being apart of the Nashy community!!!!!
love this place. dream bar!! Great bartenders specifically Brooke. Saturday nights are perfect for a family dinner

My experience at Divvy was okay.  First, I'll lay out the facts.  Our reservation was for a large group (fourteen people) on a Saturday night at 7:20 pm. The restaurant was busy, but we were seated prompted (which I DO appreciate, especially when there is a large group because that can be difficult on a busy night even if you have a reservation). Our server was very nice, and she explained how ordering typically works; small plates...everyone shares...there are typically four rounds of ordering...start from the front of the menu and work towards the back.  That was fine but it's difficult to coordinate that amount of organization with a group of fourteen. Nevertheless, we tried just the same. The food was good, but I felt (and I sensed other in the group as well) rushed to get it on my plate and pass it around to the next person as quickly as possible because there was so much coming out of the kitchen at once.  I can't say if this was because we were ordering and passing it around like the server told us to for sure, but I think that was probably the reason.  Had we been able to order for smaller table sections (groups of four or five - having discussed what that set of particular people wanted) I think it would have been less pressure to pass so quickly and we could have just enjoyed the four courses of small plates within smaller groups of our large groups. 

Anyway, the decor and setting is very modern. It's a pretty hip place. It lacks acoustics and it was pretty noisy. I struggled to hear what the person across and two seats down was saying.  After an hour or so, I stopped trying to engage in conversation because I was getting tired of talking over the crowd.  

So, all in all, it was okay. I will go back.  I may have just had an off night.  I may have just been because our group was so large.  The food was good, and there are items on the menu that I want to try next time. 

I do recommend the bacon wrapped apricots, beer cheese fondue, olive tapenade, and calamari. The coffee and beignets were enjoyable after dinner as well.

Ugh. This place is awful.

Mulate's, first impressions are SO important.  You should think about hiring a hostess who will make a great first impression, because the one you have now made a terrible first impression.  She asked us how many in our party and told us the wait was 15 minutes, then asked if we would like to put our name on the wait list. We did not answer quickly enough for the hostess and she gave us a death stare that spoke of how much she wanted to squash us like little bugs beneath her feet.  We opted to wait since 15 minutes is not bad at all considering the busyness of New Orleans this weekend.  I started writing this review in my head as we waited.  The rude hostess was a -1 star automatically.

The wait ended up being less than 15 minutes, so that was a plus.  Unfortunately, it was the only plus for Mulate's.  Our waitress was nice and professional--not super friendly or helpful/attentive, but she was pleasant enough.  Not enough to make up for the rude hostess though and not enough to be considered a plus.

Now, the FOOD.  I hoped the food would be delicious and awesome and amazing.  It's priced in such a way that I expected good, quality food.  My dad ordered the Crawfish Cajun Quartet and my mom and I split a Seafood Pasta and Stuffed Mushrooms.

The food came out within 30 minutes of ordering and we were immediately impressed with the size of the stuffed mushrooms.  The breading looked good and the mushrooms were HUGE.  There were only 4 of them (for $10.99!!! Ridiculous.), but the size and quality seemed to make up for the lack of quantity.  I bit into a mushroom expecting a mushroom with crab stuffing and ended up...with mush.  Yep.  Mush.  I don't even know what it was.  The GIANT stuffed mushroom we had been served was about 90% breading and mush and 10% mushroom.  I couldn't taste the supposed crab stuffing at all and had to dig through thick mush and breading to even find the actual mushroom.  It was terrible.  I ended up cutting the second one in half and digging the mushroom out, leaving the breading and mush on the plate.  Also, pointless bed of iceberg lettuce under the mushrooms was weird.

The seafood pasta smelled cheesy, which was to be expected since it was an alfredo pasta.  I took a bite and it tasted like I had eaten a whole stick of butter.  I took another bite and consumed another stick of butter.  I stopped at 3 bites, because I have a personal rule to consume no more than 3 sticks of butter per meal.  The pasta was limp, squishy, definitely overcooked (probably boiled in butter, then tossed in butter and cheese...), and COLD.  We asked the waitress to reheat the food and she very kindly took it back for us.  The seafood in the seafood pasta was miniscule and didn't taste fresh at all.  We left more than half the pasta untouched and didn't even consider packing it to go.  Our family is a "eat every last bite, don't waste any food!!" type of family, so that's a big deal.  

My dad did not enjoy his meal either and described it as "not bad" and "so-so".  The two bites I took of his crawfish pie and twice baked potato were unimpressive, so I'm inclined to agree with him.  

TL;DR--pleasant waitress vs. angry, mean hostess and expensive, nasty food?  Sorry, Mulate's, you suck.

I parked and immediately noticed a new kid on the block.  God damn am I glad I came in!  

Cappuccino is amazing.  According to the owner (these guys just opened last week), they started this place with a guy who was voted #1 cafe in Italy before an earthquake wrecked the store.  Normally I'd scream bullshit, but I think these guys are legit.

A break from traditional burger joints. Texas Meltz do not serve traditional Burgers and Sandwiches...They are Melts. Over the top quality, and flavor....Made To Order... Many sandwiches to choose from...Had the Cowboy Burger on Texas Toast with grilled onions and choice of real cheese... Meat patty was thick and tender and lightly salt and peppered. The onions fried. Again, you have a choice of what "real" cheese you want..The Texas Toast fried and buttered. The Chipotle mayo was mildly flavorful. Simple as that. You could taste all the different flavors of the melt without it being a mixed together mash up of flavors. Can't wait to try their other sandwiches. One might actually call these Melts...Comfort Food. They have house made potato salad, and coleslaw, neither is the sweet version..Their prices are comparable to other restaurants that serve quality burgers and sanwiches verses the fast food crap. This place is a little hole in the wall place. The owners are very nice and are real and pride themselves in having quality food....I marked this down as a find for the Reno area.

The visual display of wood, lighting  and open ceiling was really enchanting when you walk in. I was super stoked about having dinner here because of the ambiance. We had a reservation which was a plus. But the food was not as exciting as it looked. Great presentation but just ok taste. I think I would go back just for drinks.
Excellent option for a quick bite at the airport. Made fresh and perfect meal.for.vegetarians as well. We had margharita and veggie both we excellent.

Wanted to update my review to reflect my recent visits.  I've noticed recently the owners (older couple) no longer there.  It appears their daughter is now running he restaurant full time.   While the food is still good (no longer great) I've noticed the service has went downhill.  It seems like they just don't have enough staff to handle the large amount of patrons.  Still a great friendly Thai spot!

I like Mexican food, but this stuff is only so-so.  It can hit spot if you're hungry, but the variety of dishes I've tried here are kind of bland, especially for the price.

Caveats to the above: Chuy's has a solid happy hour, generally good service, and the patio is excellent.  If you go for happy hour though, beware: although ads for happy hour are laid on every table, the specials only apply to people sitting in certain areas.  This rule is mercilessly enforced, so double check with your server before you launch into the $1 tacos and cheap drinks.

Eat out most of the time in many different cities around the world. We spend a couple months a year in Reno . This month we decided to go to new places in town to switch it up. We usually go to Pegs for breakfast but thought a new place would be fun. Service was great but food very mediocre.  I ordered vegan eggs benedict and vege hash .  Vege hash was a bit tasteless,  burnt cheese, hollandaise sauce wasn't hollidaise it was butter. My friend ordered the regular Benedict.  She felt the same. Husband had the breakfast burrito. He thought it was pretty good.  Decided to return again on another day to give another chance and had a similar experience. I would only go back for breakfast if nothing else was open. Ingredients is key and I felt the quality of ingredients was definitely lacking.  The  prices were too high considering the low quality ingredients.

Wonderful dinner in a really cool, quaint establishment. It used to be a factory where they made women's high heels. (Fun fact from our super sweet bartender). We started with a board: prosciutto and black pepper cheddar served with dried apricots, fig jam, walnuts, apples and the best homemade cheddar crackers. Everything was fresh and delicious and not too filling. Great started while we waited for our table. On to dinner: I ordered the special. Pan seared trout with arugula pesto, lentils and topped with a cabbage tomato slaw. It was delicious. Great flavor combinations. I don't care for lentils but decided to try the fish as is and was a fan after that. Husband ordered the ribeye with Gorgonzola butter and cheddar potato gratin. Folks, this was one of the best steaks we have had. We are from Dallas and have experienced many steaks in our travels but it was smooth as butter, perfectly seasoned but that butter. Oh man! Let's not forget the yummy potatoes too. They were delicious. Everything was fabulous.

When you want to treat yourself to Great French Thai Food in South Jersey, Siri's wins hands down. Had the escargot in the puff pastry cooked to perfection without the overpowering of garlic butter that you usually find. My date loved the Ostrich and the Pad Thai I had was the best I've eaten. When you want to celebrate a special occasion, this is the place. Be SURE you have reservations

This place is by far the best Indian chaat place I have been to (and I actively seek out chaat places every state I visit), and I do not understand how any one can say otherwise. I would even go to say that some of the chaat I had here was better than at most chaat stores in India. Clearly, I'm a fan.

On my multiple visits, I have tried their pani puri, dahi aloo puri, paapadi chaat, deconstructed aloo tikki and samosa, pav bhaji, ragada patties, paranthas, chole bature, masala chaas.. all brilliant. Recently, they added Dabelis to their menu (I couldn't believe my eyes, as I have never found dabelis anywhere in the US!), and they were the best dabelis I have ever had.

The service is a bit slow, but it is SO well worth the few minutes extra wait. The owner seems like a very genuine and sincere man, who clearly works very hard, and really cares about this place.

Enough said! - Visit once, and let the food speak for it self!

I made a reservation at Blush on open table for 12/27 at 6:45pm. It was "promoted" as being a 1000 point reservation and we thought we would try something different. My husband and I arrived at the restaurant and I informed them I had made the reservation on open table. 

We were seated in the patio and asked the server if the fireplaces worked. She told us they did, so we asked to be moved next to it. She tried to turn the fireplace on but wasn't able to. Someone else came by and we asked them to turn it on and we were informed it didn't work. 

The service was extremely slow and we were originally served us someone else's entree. When we eventually got our meal, the food was decent. If we were just reviewing on food alone, we could give them 3 stars. Unfortunately because of the service we can only say the overall experience was a 1 star.

I paid for our dinner with my credit card. The next day I reviewed my open table app and I could not find any record of my reservation. I looked in my email and found that the restaurant had "cancelled" my reservation. I called the reservation desk to inquire and left a message asking that someone return my call. Five days later, I have still not heard back from Blush, nor did I ever get the promised 1000 points!  

A couple days ago I sent another message on the Blush website asking for them to correct the issue and I have still not heard back. It is obvious that this is a failing restaurant that does not care about its customers. It is sad because they have the potential to rival The Lark, which has excellent service, food and atmosphere.

Just go! Food is great. Service is awesome. Valet parking is Free! My husband said, in the middle of eating, I'm glad we stopped here!! Chelsie, the bartender, us fantabulous!!!! She was also our waitress and made great suggestions on what to eat, and how hot to get it. She is friendly and treated us like family!!! I had the hot chicken with beignets, based on her recommendation ... lemme just say...OOOOOOOO MYYYYYYYY GOOOOODNESSSS!!!!!!! JUST GO GET SOME!

I had a wonderful catering experience here. I ordered the 3 course meal for 30 and it was fresh and well prices for what you get. Will use EPL for catering again.  It was every packaged well and you can order online.

Drive past this place daily and wish I could eat there every night ...if I could afford it.  :-(   I went there a few times for special dinners and once with a group from work. 

The food is not cheap, portions are small - but worth it for me! My wife is Japanese and also enjoys it. I usually get some sashimi and the Kobe beef everything I ever had is delicious. 

I also like the bar, the atmosphere, special room for a larger (louder) crowd, servers are great and obviously the chefs know what they are doing! Will return ...when I get a raise at work.

Four of us went for drinks and food after bartending a Banquet at a hotel close by. We wanted to sit at a table, but the Hostess insisted we sit at the bar even though there were two available booths. We asked if we could sit at a table upstairs. She said we could only sit at a table if we were having Dinner proper. I had no idea this dive bar was so formal. Dinner proper sounds like something fit for the Queen of England. We told her we were leaving. She shrugged her shoulders. We were disappointed as we have had many after work drinking sessions at Good Dog while sitting at a table. We went to Fado and decided to make it our new after work place.

Im still unable to find a better happy hour deal in Tampa. So don't waste your time trying. Ashley the bartender is always awesome!. She  is always smiling even under her mask. They now have happy hour on Sunday also. Keep up the great service and food.

We came at an awkward time, 3:30. Dead time for a restaurant where it's hard for the server to either be too attentive or not attentive at all lol. Ours was VERY attentive. 

We ordered and shared the meatloaf with grits and Mac and cheese. Meatloaf was super good. Almost teriyaki like in taste but I duuuug. Neither of us is a true grits fan but tried it anyway and still not fans lol. Husband though the Mac was ok but I wasn't a fan at all. It was like melted cheese on dry noodles. One bite and it wasn't worth it to continue.

For dessert, we got mini bread pudding and mini pecan pie. Both were good, but the pecan came with a chocolate sauce that I preferred without.

The staff and owner here are wonderful. The food is amazing.  They have great lunch and dinner specials that include three rolls, soup, and salad. 
The fish is always fresh and they will do anything to make their customers happy. Heads and heels above other sushi I've had when I'm in Nashville, including the trendy spots down town and in Brentwood.

Consistently amazing and fresh!

Another amazing meal tonight.
My husband and I had the chef special which ended up being a hot ham and swiss cheese sandwich on brioche topped with a creamy cheese sauce and a fried egg. DELICIOUS!

Cafe Ponte is one of my favorite places to dine. 
They have creative and  delicious dishes. I haven't had a bad meal the 4 times I've been here. The service is great and the staff are very helpful if you need suggestions.I generally eat fowl or pork so I've never personally had any of the seafood or beef items but my friends who have dinned with me have and they have also enjoyed their meals here.Looking forward to going back and trying their tasting menu.

This East Nashville power-couple has got the whole Kolache thing figured out! Very interesting, imaginative, and super-deeeelicious! The muffins are amazing as well...and that yummy East Nashville Original Spice makes their breakfast casserole the best in town! ;)

Man oh man, this place is legit. Once you open the door and smell the inside of the resturant, located in a blink-and-you'll-miss it strip mall along Rt 313 in Dublin, PA, you'll know you're in the right place for good bbq. The place is small, very clean (bathrooms too!) and has a friendly, no-frills atmosphere.

Great selection of meats here, from the standard ribs and brisket to double smoked ham and chorizo. They also have specials on Friday and Saturday from 4:30pm on...on the weekend that we stopped in (2/22/14), the special was a 1/2 pound burger made from their own blend of beef including brisket and chuck. You could even add pork belly! Other specials include a smoked ham steak. Unfortunately we got there about an hour too early. Next time...

As for our lunch, we had a half rack of ribs Dancing-Pig style ($12), a brisket sandwich ($7), a chorizo sandwich (with a house-made garnish made with jalapeno and cilantro, $3), a side of beans and slaw (about $2 each), and the cornbread.

Oh, the cornbread. Spongy, sweet and delicious. Best of all, The Dancing Pig gives first-time customers their cornbread for free!

The ribs were small but delicious; "Dancing Pig" style means the house spice rub and a light brushing of sauce. Very flavorful. They also have two kinds of sauce at each table: a vinegar-y Carolina style as well as a thick, sweet bbq sauce. Both are excellent. We were also given some of their "dust", which is a spice blend that includes habanero and ghost pepper! I used the tiniest bit on my last rib and got a nice bit of heat. I imagine using alot of this results in exploding heads and profuse sweating. Use caution.

The brisket was great! Somewhat thick slices of brisket (see photo) served on a brioche-style roll. Nice to see a substantial sandwich roll like this instead of the cheaper potato/white burger rolls I've been getting at roadside stands.

I was a big fan of the chorizo sandwich! It's not something I often see at bbq places in the area. It's just one sausage split and served on a simple roll (plus that garnish!), but it's damn good and only $3.

The sides, particularly the cole slaw, were also great. The slaw was really creamy but we couldn't figure out what made it special. Good stuff.

Prices overall were very reasonable; the ribs are the priciest item and they have a great variety of sandwiches (chorizo, cubano, brisket cheesesteak) that range from $3 to $8. 

If you're in this area and want good bbq there isn't really any question that you should go straight to The Dancing Pig. The nice woman who waited on us (the owner's wife, I think) said they've been rated highly amongst local eateries and word-of-mouth has been great, but that in general people in that area don't want bbq. Those people are insane. This place is a must.

This place is one of a few good choices on the Treasure Island Causeway for a casual dinner.  Lots of space, live music but not disruptive.  Our service was fast and friendly.  Grouper sandwich, cole slaw and green beans all good and decent portions.  Try the hush puppies as a side they were great.  Avoid the seafood bisque it was very salty.  Sangria was just ok however only $3.50!  Recommended place to eat.

We found a pretty good deal on Groupon that we took advantage of and after going, it was an even better deal than I initially thought.  If you are a Johnny Cash fan, even a casual one, I would say that visiting this museum is a must!!! Heck, I think that even if you've never really listened to Johnny Cash that this museum would be a great experience, as long as you have an appreciation for music.

I had a wonderful experience here. The staff was attentive and very professional. I ordered the Prosciutto Wrapped Chicken Breast, and it was really well done and delicious. The polenta was light and cheesy. The ambience was inviting and relaxing. It checked all of the boxes for me.

I asked for just a rail bourbon at the bar, and got charged $11. Apparently they're rail bourbon is Buffalo Trace... If I wanted a more expensive bourbon, I would have asked for it. To be clear, this review is just based on that experience. I was watching the game and didn't grab any food.

Was visiting a friend in Indy and she wanted to check this place out. IT WAS A+. Awesome service, excellent food and the server offered us whipped cream on our iced coffee, can't go wrong. Potentially best omelette I've ever had..... I got the surfer girl and my friend got the mushroom egg Benedict dish.

When I heard that we were getting a sushi restaurant that wasn't AYCE, my first response was GREAT! Finally, I don't have to pay high prices for a la carte, and I don't have to "get my money's worth" by making myself have a stomach ache. And with all these great reviews, I knew I had to give it a try!

My first impression was about location, it's a little bit confusing as far as where to park, but once you find it, it's a comfortable parking lot out back. It's also a smaller restaurant, which isn't a negative but I can imagine it getting pretty cozy at peak hours. 

From the moment I walked in, the staff was so friendly and welcoming and helpful. As it was my first time, they explained how the menu worked. One thing that I loved is that, as someone who doesn't really eat desserts, I was able to double-up on appetizers instead of getting dessert at the end. I LOVE THIS! So I went with mussels and calamari. The calamari was pretty standard but YOU HAVE TO TRY THE MUSSELS! Nothing like any mussels you'll get in town. I got mine baked, not sure what the fried option is like but...so so good. 

I also went with the 2 roll combo, opting for 8 pieces of nigiri and one "Sunrise roll". Both were very fresh and tasty with beautiful presentation. 

Everything here was incredible and I guarantee this will be one of my new hangouts. 5/5 food, 5/5 service, 5/5 ambiance. Just a great business to have new to us in Reno!

We can go with 4.5 stars! I've eaten here before and their food really gives that seafood, creole, savory deliciousness that you are looking for. The Bloody Mary is top notch and I cannot brag on their oysters enough. I always get the oyster duo (Rockefeller and Royal) and a dozen fresh! They also will make you an oyster shot! This time we just had appetizers and and drinks on an extremely hot day during the pandemic. The manager's energy made me smile. Someone with that positive energy in such trying times is irreplaceable. He had the staff smiling even though I could tell they were miserably hot and disappointed about the money they won't make because of the current circumstances. The 4.5 stars was because the air vent kept spraying dust on us and on our food at first but the manager moved us and apologized. I recommend sitting at the upstairs bar or the balcony when all of that is open again!

My beau and I came here for a fancy dinner out. We both got the single porterhouse, which is dry aged for roughly a month. I got medium+, which was cooked perfectly to my liking. It was delicious and not to mention... HUGE! 
Unfortunately my boyfriends porterhouse came out a tad bit too cooked. He ordered a medium rare and ended up getting something more cooked than medium. After telling the restaurant manager, he was very accommodating  and made sure we were satisfied with our meal. 

Great steaks, great service and amazing baked Alaska!

I usually receive amazing service at this location. I maybe caught this employee on a bad day because it was apparent that she was upset at my daughter's indecisiveness, among other things. I work in customer service & know that no matter what, the customer should never know that you're having a rough day. She was an older lady, so I think she's just done. Very frustrating to drive 1 hour for this amazing coffee and get this horrible service.   If you see this... I hope you have better days ahead

We love this place!  I'm not a golfer but my husband is a golf nut and we both have a great time!  I love the sectional couches so we non-golfers can relax and hang out while the golfers hit balls.  Drinks are pricey, food is ok... but it's fun for the whole gang!

This place is worth going too for great ribs, creamy mac n cheesiness , sweet and savory baked beans , mash potatoes are worth having . Green beans had a great smokey taste . Only thing I  didn't have the corn bread and there was no 
"home made " desserts 
Don't  forget your free hand rub

Bought a breast meal last week at the drive thru.  Server had an attitude as if doing me a favor.  Got home chicken was very dry, not fresh.  This as been going on too long, has to be because of the location.  Won't be back!

Our meal was horrible..Seam like chicken was previously frozen. Sauce in Curry dish had separated.  Stuffed chicken wings was Blah.
Service was very good!

Excellent selection of sushi rolls. We ordered 3 different sushi rolls. All 3 had beautiful presentation and were delicious. Service was excellent and pleasant. Overall very good and we would definitely come back.
