I give it points for a VERY veggie friendly menu. Beer list was very good too. We went in when NO ONE else was there for lunch. The bar tender was a cliched hipster chick who was rather unpleasant and not the least bit helpful ( I don't need a new BFF but you don't need to act like you're too cool to offer me even semi-civilized service. I'm sorry my presence annoys you, maybe you shouldn't be in the service industry?) Given the awesome vegetarian menu we'll probably try it again sometime but if the service is typically like that forget it. Descent people be ware.

Well I only write reviews if it's insanely great and the staff is awesome or if it's really poor. Fortunately the bartenders were awesome! The food just way below par. Zero flavor on the fish, seemed thawed although was told it was fresh. Broccoli and potato's terrible. Should have gotten a burger. Too bad. Great location
Best sushi ever! They have a vast selection of sushi and full bar. Love their bulgogi sushi and poke bowls. Great service and ambience! Highly recommended!

Another absolutely wonderful meal with friends at the finch and fork. Great appetizers- the brioche and schmeer with hot smoked salmon and spread was great, as were the perfect Kushi oysters. The raucous pink deviled eggs with smoked trout were outstanding. 

Main coarse? It's Tuesday, so we had to have the fried chicken- and what fried chicken it was. Super quality Jidori chicken, fried in a tasty crust. A full half chicken of golden goodness. Crunchy outside, juicy inside, delicious. With perfect mashed potatoes (with gravy) and homemade sweet pickles. 

And then dessert- you sometimes have desserts that are creative, and sometimes have dessert that are good. Chef James Siao's desserts are both. We were pretty full, so each couple split one dessert: the s'more pot de creme, which sounded ipretty good. It was better than that. Three simple elements, each taken to a new level: torched homemade marshmallow, rich silky chocolate pot de creme, and an ethereal crunchy topping that started life as graham crackers but evolved into a higher plane. Our friends shared the Fire roasted milk shake made with banana ice cream and, among other things, salted caramel. They too were very very happy. 

Round it out with great service, and some first rate cocktails from a skilled bar, and you'll have what we had: a perfect dinner

Was lured by a supposed Neapolitan pizza...  close but not quite. Very high end Italian with first class presentation. Nothing disappoints unless you go with a particular expectation (like a certified VPN pizza).
Really liked the ceasar salad with its classy presentation

I will never, ever go back to this dump again. Worst service I've ever had in a long, long time. I don't think they even care considering this is the second time,  we tried to give them a 2nd chance in less than 30 days. We ordered sushi approx. 6:50, after confronting waitress at 7:30, was told they ran out of rice, be 5 mins., walked out at 7:45 never to return again. You guys suck!!
Great food and amazing environment. Staff was very friendly and quick to bring our food. Loved the decor.

Corn beef Ruben: 4 Out of 5
Meat loaded sandwich fresh off the griddle! Make sure you have some liquids to wash down all of this richness. Perfectly seasoned brisket & it melted apart as I picked up to grab a bite! The only thing I wish was that they gave us more of the of the sauerkraut and a pickle on the side. 

Service: 5 Out of 5
The guys that helped us were on point. We were waiting for about a couple minutes and one of the line men took our order & got us rolling. Within 10 minutes we put in our order and left to eat our hot of the press ruben.

Environment: 4 Out of 5
Busy environment on the weekends. It's a grab and go situation most times I come here. We chose to eat outside in the Marriott courtyard across the street. 

Overall:  4 Out of 5
The sandwich itself was $12.75 out the door. Coming back to try the pastrami Ruben!
Cuban sandwich's were delicious. Parking is a little difficult though, you may have to park across the street. Overall really cool modern atmosphere.

I was here for the first time a few weeks ago and loved it. Everything is made fresh to order. The staff is unbelievably friendly and helpful. Everyone there was "our" server and was ready to help with anything we wanted. I got The Runner Omelette which was egg whites, turkey, roasted veggies and brie. It was absolutely delicious. I usually shy away from omelette with roasted veggies because it always seems to be bell peppers and onions. This was a pleasant surprise. The blend of vegetables were carrot, summer squash and onion. Perfectly roasted so they were cooked through but with crispy edges that really gave it so much flavor. I also got a side of creamy grits with cheddar. My server noticed that they were delivered without the cheese before I even did. She quickly rushed out another cup in seconds and had us keep both. The food was on point and so was the service which means I'm sure to be back.

I know most people come here for the coffee drinks, but you can NOT pass up the pastries. I came to HiVolt earlier this week and ordered a lemon raspberry muffin. This muffin was HUGE. I told myself that I would only eat half of it and bring the rest home, which didn't happen. Before I knew it, the whole thing was gone. I couldn't help myself.

The muffin was full of fresh raspberries and packed with flavor. It was a perfect balance of tart and sweet, and I haven't stopped thinking about it since. HiVolt, will you start delivering these to my doorstep?

Worst service I've ever had! Waited 22 minutes just to get a drink, ask for a chips and salsa refill and then never get it l, only to finally get my dinner an hour later and it was wrong! I usually love to come here but this time was worse than ever!
Might have a good atmosphere to hang out but the coffee is disgusting. When do you ever make cappuccinos with brew coffee and not espresso shot.
I keep coming back even though it's a tourist trap. Food is mad expensive for what it is, but hey, how often do I come to Philly? I like it better than Pat's.

When the place I wanted to go for lunch was closed, I decided to try this place.  It was great to find a restaurant with a lot of veggie-based, but not all strictly vegetarian or vegan, options.  The salad I had (Wild Child) was excellent.  The rest of the menu looks great too.  But one thing kept me from giving it 5 or even 4 stars:
WHY IS THE MUSIC SO LOUD!!!!?

I like music.  In fact, I love music.  I play music. I go to music events.  I have accepted that no restaurant can tolerate, or thinks its customers can tolerate, a quiet background.  So, there's music. But this was so loud it made me feel anxious and rush my meal. Is that what restaurant management wants?  There's no need in this case, because it wasn't at all crowded, I could have lingered and relaxed without a tiny bit of guilt over making others wait for a table.  But yet I couldn't, because it was too loud.

I have been going to Uncle Rodney's now for 7 years. I love this place!
If you want the best barbeque in town, this is the place. Chicken is great, Ribs are great and Rodney takes pride in how he does things and the quality of the meat he buys. Very casual, drive up type place, indoor/outside seating. Don't get dressed up and get prepared to get messy. Yummmm

Give me bread or give me death. Croissant D'Or Patisserie is THE mecca of yummy croissants and pastries. Fresh, made in-house, delicious, buttery dough filled with your choice of decadent sweetness. I am extremely indecisive and love to be a fatass whenever given the option so naturally I ordered one of each. (I did share, ok!) Out of the apple, raspberry, chocolate and almond my favorite was the raspberry. However, I would be happy if I woke up and any of those croissants were magically in my kitchen.  My iced coffee and milk did not need a grain of sugar, it was already smooth and delicious. 

Since I am a bit of a history buff I am completely enthralled of the interior of this place (formally the original Broccato's) Architecture and design just aren't what they used to be and it truly feels like going back in time. 

The bakery had a constant flow of people almost the entire time that I was there. The workers remained as fresh as their pastries as they helped the ever growing line. 

The only drawback is that since it is in the middle of the charming french quarter it does pose an issue if you have to drive there since it only really allows for street parking. Still worth the possible parking ticket hazard.

In n Out is always a go-to! Their menu hasn't changed and the quality is always great! All of the employees are very friendly and helpful. 
PRO TIP - always ask for your fries well done! 
They get fried twice and become super crispy.
I always get the hamburger protein style because it's gluten free.

Brazilian restaurant in the heart of Arabi....shooting through in between house showings. Yes, I'm a realtor and YET I'm somehow largely normal. Just ask me. This place is a combination coffee shop, bar and restaurant - covering most of the major options. I only had a limited opportunity due to time constraints but loved the look, the service, the vibe. Ordered the cheese bread because - hey - it's cheese bread. And OH MY GOSH. It was perfect. Hot, freshly made, filled with cheesy goodness that was delicious and not overwhelming - nicely balanced appetizer. I could have eaten 30 of these. I would come back here JUST for the cheese bread. And for a drink I had the Passion Fruit Caipirinha  which was perfectly made and presented. And it went down very easily. Will definitely be back to try more of their fairly expansive menu!
Great service, poboys are excellent, gotta have the red beans and rice. Was great for an in and out lunch at the French Quarter. Service was fast and friendly!!

Another great dinner at Wycombe Publick House - Chicken Parm Grinder.. The atmosphere is always friendly.  The staff is attentive and always making sure that you are taking care of.  Never disappointed in my food choice and a large variety of beers to enjoy.  I will keep going back and will try different dishes to let you know.  Go and have a great time.

Tradesman's is a delicious new full-service barbecue place to spearhead entry in Philadelphia's Midtown Village.

My induction was to choose it for a first date I was on, and it really impressed us both. The spacious 2-floor dining room is warmly lit, and has plush red seating with beautiful wooden tables. We were able to carry on a great conversation, so the music and white noise wasn't too loud at all. 

It didn't initially occur to me to call this a barbecue restaurant, even though staples such as smoked chicken, brisket, pork belly, ribs, and cornbread are on the menu. Barbecue restaurants in Center City are such a rarity, especially one as modernly-elegant as this. But it truly is a bona fide barbecue - the nose knows, and you can't help but be taken aback by that delicious aroma while inside. 

We started off with the Potato Skins appetizer; I recall there being 5 of them on the plate. It probably would make a better impression to even it out, especially when the waiter knows there are two people there; however, the plate was big enough to take the hungry edge out of both our bellies - so there is not much room for a worthwhile complaint. And the Skins were delicious, topped off with juicy pork belly on each one.

We both had heard about how good the Smoked Chicken entree was, but it had already been sold out at 5:30pm on a Friday - that does not bode well, being a signature entree at a new place. But I'll extend grace that this is a new restaurant, and management will need to tweak their stock orders better for the future.

So we both did get to try a couple super-delicious entrees. My date had the Housemade Sausage and loved it; I'm not a sausage fan at all, but it had a delicious flavor...for sausage. Hey, it was smoked - and I love most anything smoked.

I admit to being surprised as to how delicious my Brisket entree was, and I'm a barbecue snob! The brisket cut was plentiful, it was a little on the fatty side (as most brisket tends to be served), but its scrumptious smokey flavor was a bell-ringer to me! Heck, even the brisket fat was delicious. Isn't it always a good sign when you try something new, and your mind goes wild trying to size it up to where you think you've might of had it better? Trademan's brisket really is up there for the best brisket award, against all the places that I've been in the past. You just won't go wrong choosing the brisket here.

Entrees are typically served on a bed of white bread, and you'll have to order the sides à la carte. We were too full for either sides or dessert, and we both still want to try that Smoked Chicken, so I look forward to coming back here again.

The staff were fantastic even though we had to hunt down our waitress a few times, thinking she forgot about us.

There is a definite bar area if you just want to get your drinks on, or don't need a proper table, and it is really cool. In fact, they bill this as a Whiskey Hall; you'll have to read others' reviews about that since I'm not a drinker. The bar extends right to the open front wall of the building, with permanent seating right there on the outside of the wall. On a warm night, this place is lively from the outside to the inside. I left admiring the way the whole place was set up. 

This is the kind of inviting place that I always thought Center City should have more of.
An amazing place that has an amazing menu. The seafood is awesome. You have to try the calamari or the tuna tower.

Uva used to be one of our favorite restaurants because food was always wonderful. However, after  biting into a piece of glass in the packed up leftover food that we took home with us after dining there last night, I don't think that we will be going back. I'm fortunate that I didn't cut myself or swallowed it. It was a good 1 cm piece of sharp glass.

Exploring Edmonton and we landed on 124th street. We decided to try this restaurant as it appeared on our searches for restaurants nearby.  As soon as we entered, the staff greeted us with a warm smile and arranged a table quickly. Our server was excellent, he walked us through the menu and then also suggested dishes for us. My husband ordered the coconut curry rissoto suggested by our server and boy oh boy that rissoto was delicious.  I ordered a Salmone E Limone and it's was tasty. Our son enjoyed his Mac and cheese.
Overall it was a great experience. Thanks to Tiramisu Bistro team!!

I wanted to try this place a while back so we went last tuesday and even tho I still want to try everything else I was delighted with the visit. 
.
Nice,clean place, there was only one person serving and she was the sweetest, was fast serving us. She brought the banchan (korean appetizers) which I loved them all,a nice touch to welcome us and taste different things. We ordered the king steam mando and they were out of this world. Big,well seasoned. I loved them. We also had the kimchi stew, interesting dish,the flavour reminded me of guts stew,a nice spicy dish. We also had the spicy chicken and asked them to be "less spicy" ..still spicy but delicious, the way you want a "sweet and sour chicken" to be. Chicken strips with this amazing sauce.  Both plates came with rice. A decent portion . Cant wait to come back and order just appetizers and have a taste of a few dishes. They have ramen,waiting for some fellow yelper to let us know how good it is.

What kind of hotel/casino does not give free water bottles?! Everywhere we've stayed they give at least 2 water bottles a day. Also when we called  room service, Vicky picked up. She sounded like I had just woken her up from her nap or something. Her tone was rude and unacceptable. Our first time staying here and we are so disappointed. The hotel itself is old and worn down.
The English muffin sandwich with egg and cheese was very good. Iced coffee was a smooth tasty blend. Definitely recommend this place if you are looking for a light healthy breakfast

Omg I really enjoyed this place. The chicken Marsala was my favorite. I have been looking for a place that hit all the right spots and man this place did it. Unfortunately it is 2 hours from home! But best believe I will be going here when I am in town. The price seemed fair and the buffet was plenty.
Horrible service. Waiter ignored all of our needs and reached across my face constantly to grab food

Really enjoyed having a brunch/ lunch here with friends. The balls at bigger than you think! The staff was very friendly and attentive. The atmosphere was kinda different, reminded me of a New York Italian restaurant that mobsters go to ha. But I really enjoyed eating here and would suggest to everyone to go try this place out! I can't wait to go back for dinner some time.  The menu looks intimidating but the waiter explains how it works and its kinda fun because you get to use a marker and check off what you want. The only thing I didn't really care for are the family style sides, but not a deal breaker by any means! This place is delicious, try it out, you will not be disappointed!

Ordered from uber eats on a busy night. Cheap but seriously amazing bahn mi.

Try the pork belly with quail egg bahn mi, as well as the honey glazed pork roll (which actually contains char siu). Packed with flavor. The bahn mi are 8 and 6 USD respectively, which to me is a great deal.

The concept is great and the staff is friendly! I ordered pickup through their website which was an easy experience. The store is laid out well for COVID, and it was easy to pickup without much interaction with the staff or others waiting in the store. As I entered I was greeted and directed where to go, so kudos to the store for being awesome! Even during a dinner rush. Also, the baking instructions were easy to follow and accurate. What I wasn't overly excited about was the actual pizza. The toppings were fresh and piled on, but the sauce and dough just weren't that good. It reminded me of a frozen pizza. I think there is something to be said for baking a pizza in an actual pizza oven vs my mediocre home oven. For the price (14" two topping pizza was $13) I would have rather picked up an already cooked pizza.

I work near Mr. Baja Fish and we have slim pickins' in this 'hood when it comes to restaurants. I was so excited when they took over the building, and it doesn't disappoint. 
They have awesome grilled shrimp tacos. Battered fish and grilled chickens tacos are good too and reasonable.  Chips are fresh. In fact all the food has been fresh. I've been 3x in 3 weeks and its now a new favorite!

Excellent Chinese food! Best in the StL area. The quality of service varies UNLESS you have NOAH as your server. It's a 2 for 1 if you're lucky to get him...dinner and A SHOW! Food is great, parking can be a challenge sometimes. If it's traditionally a high traffic Chinese food time ie: New Years, Christmas, Thanksgiving, call ahead for reservations.

Only thing i love is my server had a beautiful smile.

Cashier was chatting with chef in Chinese language loudly.

The food was nothing wrong but it was not authentic at all.

Actually they listed all kind of famous Asian food. They sell Vietnamese pho, Korean soup, Chinese Tofu. Shogun is Japanese cuisine though.

And the restaurant exactly looked like Modern American Pub.

One sentence.
This is new shit.

My boyfriend and I went to Dekes for the first time last night on a whim and man was it a good choice. Best BBQ I've had in a long time. We decided to try the buffet and I added on a half rack of spare ribs. Everything was delicious. The buffet is definitely a good choice if you're looking try some different meats. The spare ribs were amazing. I can't wait to go back again.

I happened to find this place by chance today.. I was driving back from Chicago to Southern Indiana and searched for a good Desi restaurant near Indianapolis and this place showed up on google with 5 stars. I ordered a take out for Chicken Biryani, Aloo Tikki Chaat and Falooda Kulfi! This place didn't disappoint. They were not only quick in preparing the food but the food was delicious too!
Décor of the place is modern and has multiple carrom boards - pretty surprising and impressive! If I lived in Indianapolis - I could see myself coming back to dine in with friends for a relaxing evening, catching up with them over a few games of Carrom!

Yeah, it's good. And the menu is enormous. It's not high-class; it's not "five star cuisine;" it's just darn yummy. You can get anything they make to go, and if you need to walk with it aways there are some sandwiches that they can prepare cold so your food doesn't have to get lukewarm as you walk with it. Be sure to get a side of their house-made potato salad. It's disturbingly good. 

The employees are super-friendly and they take all major credit cards. Score!

Plates are best to share so order a lot of medium plates to try everything! 

Unique flavors, and fun spin on Asian classics!
you can't go wrong!!! reasonable prices! real good food!

Amazing food! We had the meatloaf, fish & chips, pork chop and Brussel sprouts. All of it was so delicious and fresh! Service is a little slower than usual, but all of the servers are so pleasant. Would definitely recommend dining here. Would recommend a reservation, as it fills up fast. The bar is open seating.

I am a HUGE fan of their fish tacos! My fiance' and I come here every Wednesday night at 7:30pm because they have a Trivia League that takes place. It's a lot of fun, challenging questions and of course, there's always a game on the TV's. The service is pretty decent, but then again, during Trivia, it's packed. The sangria is good, the fish tacos are great, the wings are delicious (with the signature sauce of course)! Great staff and Aaron is a great guy. They do their best to make your visit to this Beef's a memorable one. Highly recommend. 
Park in the back or next door in the Salvation Army parking lot.

Pretty good authentic italian.  Great service for lunch and I had a stuffed pepper special which was basically a giant meatball inside a bell pepper covered in their marinara which was really tasty.  Ceasar salad was good too.  I would definitely eat there again.

We used to come here all the time when I was in high school.  I recently moved back after being gone for 15 years...  Now Avon has a ton of Mexican restaurants and this place is still my favorite.  Great chips & salsa, flavorful entrees with huge portions.  

The only downside is parking is not great.

We stumbled upon this place after renting a car at the airport. We thought it would be nice to have breakfast at the lake. We saw a sign for Messina's Runway Cafe and thought we'd give it a try. First, the cafe (there appear to actually be three dining establishments in the premises) is a renovated art deco private air terminal with gorgeous murals and embellishments. Second, the menu is five star. I had the Shrimp and Grits which featured a creole sauce that is the best I've ever tasted. My wife had the Eggs Boudin and loved it. Our server was attentive and jovial. To top it off, there's a great view of private planes taxiing and landing. Even if you're staying in the French Quarter you should take a side trip to Messina's. It's well worth the trip.

There is no better breakfast in town. They have amazing monthly specials but it is difficult to pass on my favorite, the eggs cochon.  Inagine: A large biscuit turned into two Benedicts but with tangy pork instead of Canadian bacon, a side of incredible potatoes, and a special side of candied bacon that must have been prepared by God, himself.  My mouth waters every time I think about it.

Found this little diner on Yelp. It lived up to the reviews. The food was simply excellent. The service is what will keep you coming back. My server, Scarlett was A-FANTASTIC. I enjoyed the western omelette with loaded home fries and a pancake (hey i had to cut back somewhere). All the ingredients were fresh with that certain homemade taste. Did mention MS. SCARLETT, she was the best.

If you haven't been to penn station you're missing out all their subs are phenomenal! Got the Philly cheesesteak and the bread is so soft and the sandwich just melts in your mouth. Customize your sandwich if you want good pricing it will fill you up.

Sahara Grill is a middle eastern restaurant that is a informal, less pricey restaurant. I came on a Thursday night around 8pm. The ambiance is not upscale but quite regular and plain - almost too much so. It was half full when we arrived with 2 people in our party.

We ordered the Tabbouleh ($6) as an appetizer and I got the Chicken Shish Taouk ($15). Water came in small plastic clear cups. The tabbouleh was decent. It came with pita bread and a small salad. Honestly the salad wasn't great and was just very plain. I seemed to be complimentary, which might be why it was so plain. The pita bread was a little cold and not soft when it came out. I did like the tabbouleh but perhaps they could have added other flavors too? Maybe I don't like this dish itself, but perhaps there could be more tomato and other ingredients in the ratio between veggies and parsley.

The main course had some parts I liked and some that I didn't. I did enjoy the roasted parts of the dish - the zucchini and the chicken had great flavoring and were smoky and spicy. They were really both grilled the right amount just to be crispy but not burnt. The chicken came back pretty tender and had a nice orange-ish color too. This dish also came with rice. I wish the rice were a little hotter and less mushy. The tomato that came on the place was also huge and could have been cut to a smaller size.

Overall I think this place is decent but I will probably not come back as I want to try other restaurants and I think greek places like Kanella Grill though a different cuisine, serve sort of similar food done better.

Finally, the service. The waiters were friendly but we didn't ever get water poured until I asked, so my cup was empty at a point. They were nice though.
This is really great pizza. It tastes so fresh, and I don't feel guilty eating it. I love that they deliver, I will definitely be ordering Naked Pizza again.

Stopped by because of the great reviews. The black guy who helped us out was the rudest welcoming to New Orleans. I say his race because there were only two guys working at the counter and the other was white. So hopefully a manager can fire his ass. We asked what he suggested and he literally said "how am I supposed to know, I work here?" Yeah, I'm as confused as you. Then he says he skinny and he doesn't eat much, another reason why he doesn't know. I have a muscular build but he proceeded to almost fat shame me even though I'm not even over weight. He said I look like I like food, so I should know what I want. He was a horrible reflection on what could be an amazing city. He said this in front of other customers.

Staying in nearby hotel and walked over to grab to-go breakfast for my family. I was very impressed with the quality of food. Pancake stack was one of the best I've ever had - large, brown (not tan) and delicious! French toast was great. The topper was the cheesy jalapeño hash browns - unique and awesome! Service was quick too.

Came to opening night of this fun and lively neighborhood restaurant in Fishtown.  The large windows in front let in great light and the youthful interior offers ample enjoyment from the upbeat music, pool table, stadium seats for waiting and quirky artifacts throughout.
Then there is the food and drink!  So good!!!! The dinner rolls were hot and served with a brie butter.  We were a large group and shared latkes with ginger and roe, vegan patty melts, hamburger, two kinds of fries with aioli, broccoli and shrimp with shishitos.  We drank organic wines (red and white) and a Dixie cup ice cream cup for dessert.  
And of course the staff was beyond helpful, friendly and enjoyable to chat with!  It all comes from owner, Matt Cahn's vision.
Can't wait to return!

Meh. Nothing to write home about. The Chinese food server here is below average.
Every time I eat here I end up with an upset stomach. Just go somewhere else to eat.

Roast pork banh mi
We came for lunch on a Friday because we heard that they make banh mi with crispy roast pork belly on the weekends.  The banh mi was very good - made to order with fresh cilantro, carrot, cucumber, pork loaf and roast belly pork.  We did think that the roll was a just little small though and be warned - it's cash only!!
Then make wonderful food and nice waiter! If you want to taste traditional Chinese food you should go

Not bad, it's a great lunch spot for those working in the area.  I wouldn't go out of my way to get sushi here, but it's decent for the area.  My personal peev is with the bathrooms (any place that wants to be high end needs to make a great bathroom impression).  I almost got locked in one of the stalls because the doorknob was faulty and the toilet seat was a bit 'rough'.

I am from Bowling Green, KY where we also have a Wild Eggs. While staying the weekend in Nashville, I was so excited to see that there was a new Wild Eggs location just right down from where I was staying! My friends and I were very pleased with the short wait and the attention the staff paid to every detail. 

I ordered Breakfast Nachos, which is my regular meal at our location and my friends ordered their favorites as well. Our food was great, we had a positive experience and can't wait to visit when we are in Nashville next.

I just didn't like how the sides were presented with the meal. There wasn't much to choose from when it came to sides, like an option was sautéed bananas. I asked for all of my meat to be well done and didn't get that so after the 5th slice of meat I was over it.
This place is amazing!  Bartender is so nice and efficient.  Crawfish boils are fresh, meaty and a reasonable price.  Best crawfish in the Quarter!

One of the best meals I've ever had. I've eaten at many restaurants but wow this place is fantastic. It's the food and service of a white tablecloth fancy restaurant in a more laid-back atmosphere. Highly recommended

A recent Yelp chat thread was heralding the re-opening of a Village Inn in the Westchase area Tampa, and extoling the virtues of their many different types of pies. I realized that it had been quite a while since I had eaten at a Village Inn, and so in an effort to take one for the team I popped in to the Village Inn on N Dale Mabry in Carrollwood for lunch.

You'll find Village Inn located right alongside the road in between Busch Boulevard and Waters Avenue. As with most Village Inn's they are open 24 hours a day, and there is a steady stream of people looking for round-the-clock breakfast, sandwiches, entrees, and pie.

In all honesty, the first thing that you'll notice walking in the door is the damp, musty smell of the carpeting. A good vacuuming and carpet shampooing would go a long way towards removing the scent. Even though this place stays busy, there are normally piles of dirty dishes sitting on empty tables waiting for someone to come along and clean the tables. It's not an especially attractive first impression....

As mentioned before, the menu is primarily breakfast options available 24 hours a day -- omelets, crepes, pancakes, waffles, French toast, steak & eggs, hash, biscuits & gravy, skillet goodies, and all of your usual favorites. VI also serves soups, salads, burgers, sammies, and old school comfort food entrees. The food is simple, and good.

A big part of the VI business are their pies with over 20 different varieties available by the slice, or by the whole pie. If you eat at Village Inn on Wednesdays, you'll receive a free slice of pie with any dine-in meal.

For my lunch I had the Chipotle Chicken Ciabatta sandwich which was grilled chicken breast, mixed greens, red onions, sliced tomato, and chipotle lime vinaigrette on a grilled ciabatta bun. Served with a side of fresh fruit instead of fries.  And of course I had a slice of pie -- spiced pumpkin with whipped cream.

This place is in serious need of a thorough top-to-bottom cleaning, and perhaps some staff training on clearing the tables and sanitizing the tabletops instead of just picking up the dirty dishes.

The first thing you will notice as you walk into this restaurant is the incredibly friendly service.  We were greeted so enthusiastically that I felt like I was a regular customer, even though this was my first time there.  And the experience was just as nice from that point.  The chips and salsa were great, and a nice added touch is a bowl of bean dip to go along with your chips.  This is especially nice if you have a little one.

The menu is really varied with a lot of interesting items.  We were trying to keep it cheap today, so we had to pass on the more exciting and enticing dinners and stick with cheaper and more basic fare.  Husband really enjoyed his burrito, and my Enchiladas Suiza were delicious.  I was using the remaining chips to scrape up every last drop from my plate.

With good food and service, I'm not sure why I don't want to give them five stars.  I think it may be the discrepancy between the atmosphere and the prices.  The restaurant's atmosphere seems really casual, but the prices seem pretty formal.  This is a problem with a lot of Mexican restaurants, though.

NOTE: I think this place used to be called "Si Senor," if you were wondering.
This is a great Vietnamese restaurant!  The pho' is excellent as is are rice noodle bowls.  The only down side is you can't get a beer or glass of wine so bring you own.
Awesome food with great service. This place has the potential to be a market leader in Indian Cuisine.

Hey what can you say.. they're your run of the mill pub place with decent food selections and decent beer selections.  Food is a bit greasy for my taste but was cooked decent enough to eat.  They have tons of HD tvs around so if you're into watching games while eating it's a decent place to go.  I've never had to wait for a table here but I usually go during the day for lunch.  If you want a comparison.. I would say it's like going to TGIF with a personal touch.

Unfortunately this review is long overdue. I decided to treat the women in my office to a galentines day dinner. None of us have been to the melting pot and we read the reviews online and looked at the special they had for this event. 
When we arrived our table was not ready. Which was odd but I digress. We were told they could not serve alcohol because they were in the process of getting their liquor license. Understandable however we should have been told before we arrived. 
Our server took a while to greet us and then close to 30 minutes to get us our drinks (which were sparking cider) our first course took about 45 minutes to get to us. And by that time the restaurant was almost empty. 
As soon as we got our first course we asked to fire the second one so we didn't need to wait. 

It was our understanding that this event was an appetizer, salad and dessert. But our waiter told us it was that plus and entree. We thought that was cool! 

By the time our salads and entree arrived it was already 10pm we had work the very next morning so we decided to take our desserts Togo. 

We go our bill and we're shocked at how much we were charged. The waiter lied that the entree was not included in this event and was actually extra. 

I knew one of the GM and I messaged her explaining how upset we were with the timing and the service and the shock of the extra fee we did not know about. To which she gave me the corporate answer that they were in the process of training new staff and sometimes people stay even longe than we did that evening. That they were working out the hiccups and that she'd talk to that server to correct his mistakes. This did not solve the fact that we were still upset and getting a corporate answer did not help at all. 


If you are going to dine here it's going to be an all night thing. Make sure to carve out multiple hours for this.

Similar to the user above, I came in here on my lunchbreak as my office is located nearby.  The location isn't great, and the building is a little shabby, but the food is worth it.

I got a gyro salad, which was essentially a greek salad served with strips of gyro meat (lamb?), pita bread, and cucumber dressing.  Very tasty, and at $6 the price was right.

We came upon Persona while exploring State street. We were attracted by the twin wood-fired ovens clearly visible from the entrance. The diverse selection of pizzas, salad and tasty drinks (local craft beer and wine was very appealing) what exactly what we were looking for. The service was very helpful and hands-on to describe us through their ingredients and offerings. 

The pizza and salad was delivered quickly and turned out wonderfully tasty. A very nice and subtle crispy crust with just the right amount of chew to it. Combined with the craft beer it was super memorable.

We look forward to a return visit and to enjoying your pizza when you expand nationwide.
Pretty solid coffee shop. too much cream cheese on the bagel but awesome pastries and good coffee selection.

Returned again last week for dinner with 21 people and what a treat! Everything was great, and the service was very accommodating. My favorites were the mushroom ravioli, the baked oysters, and the seafood risotta. The star of the table, though, was the short ribs. They were fabulous! Our group had it's own area, but we were not closed off in a separate room. We were in an elevated area that looked out over the main floor and the entertainment. Can't wait to go back. I will get short ribs next time, it was great.  Oh, and the $2 parfaits for dessert hit the spot!

I went on Wed 7/15/2020 and was so happy to see them open as the location in Westshore was now closed.  I always loved them but unknown what happended on this day, I ordered takeout and ate in my car minutes after picking up a supposed Hot Cornbeef on Rye but it was cold, the bread broke apart (old) so I took the bread off and just ate the cold cornbeef with the pickle.  I then ordered about $40-$50.00 in the bakery. I love in Zephyrhills so when I got home to show my family the treats it was very disappointing as the éclair was hard as a rock and the custard inside was hard. The Cannoli was definitely old, the shell was very soft not crunchy and the cannoli crème inside was hard and a little sour. Threw out Cannoli and the Éclair. I also ordered 2 Napoleons and they were delicious and were fresh.... 1 pound of Apricot cookies with the chocolate and sprinkles and they were fresh and delicious.  Disappointed in my sandwich not as thick as prior orders, cold and bread not fresh at all.. The girls at the bakery were wonderful. I hope for a better experience next time.

I only came for late night drinks, so I can't speak to the food, but this was such a fun spot! I have noticed the Crow's Nest for years when I'm walking around in Maplewood, but I just recently made it in. I was so pleasantly surprised. They have done a great job mixing that traditional dive bar atmosphere with a more up to date drink list. Pair that with a selection of arcade games and this is the perfect spot to head out with friends on a Friday or Saturday night! I'll definitely be headed back next time I'm out in Maplewood!

If you like a very loud atmosphere and overpriced food, this is probably the place for you.  My husband and I took my parents and it was challenging to hold a conversation over the noise level.  The guys said the steaks were good, but I ordered the chicken and it had no taste whatsoever, which is not an exaggeration.  Even though we had a $150 gift certificate, we still paid an additional $200 which is so frustrating given the great restaurants we could/should have gone to.  Anyway, I'm trying to be fair here, so let me just say that if you like a loud, rock-concert type of establishment with decent (not great) food, then you will likely be fine with it.  Our expectations were evidently too high.

I love this place very much. When I went to NO for the first time, I ate lunch at this place. I ordered BBQ Shrimp and I was a fan right there then. In my second time, the very first night in NO I directly went to this place. I ordered BBQ Shrimp and my boyfriend got Jambalaya Pasta. Both were delish!!! I was so happy with the food. Please if you visit French Quarters EAT HERE! :D

If you are ordering for take out maybe go here. The food is not horrible, but for the price no bargain. However, as a restaurant experience, I personally had a horrible experience. I had a long wait for everything. The order was wrong and the atmosphere was bad. I feel like I was robbed after dining here, time and money.
Great BBQ! Brisket some of the best I ever had. Jalapeno Mac N Cheese is awesome. You wont be disappointed!
This place is great... they have a nice antique interior with a fun atmosphere. I highly recommend Meat balls and the house "pesto" salad dressing!

This place has the best beef brisket you can find anywhere... we always get the 'fatty' because it's way more tender and just, well, delicious!  I'll be honest tho, i haven't really tried much else on the menu because we have a tendency to buy the brisket by the pound and take it to go and cook up our own sides at home.  

At any rate, you won't be disappointed!
Just had my first sandwich from Vivola.  Enough for lunch tomorrow as well!  Delicious hot roast beef.

This is my favorite place for ramen in Nashville! However, I need to come back like 30 more times to be able to try all of the small plates and meals and drinks on the menu. The bar is super cool and the drinks are unique. The ramen, as expected and recommended to us, was incredible. Such a fun dining experience! However, they do not take reservations, so make sure to come early or allow time for waiting.

My friends/colleagues and I were just discussing how we've all been looking for a location away from work that has both bistro food and crafted cocktails.  John and I often find a location with a signature drink menu that have true mixologists, but then mediocre food or they're a bar only.  

We finally made it into Wild River Grille.  Ask and ye shall receive.  Delicious and generous small plates for sharing, great service, AND a great seasonal drink menu.  They incorporate the local farm to table approach with the Chef preparing well seasoned items with great balance of flavor.  The spice-rubbed pork belly on savory french toast with a savory, mild Bing cherry sauce had to be one of the best dishes I've had this year.

I usually reserve a review five star review until I've patronized a place more than once, but this really hit the mark.

This place is really good if you are looking for good pizza in the Philadelphia, Head House District. 
The place is classy, but not pretentious. They have a full bar and the staff is attentive and nice. 
They offer outdoor seating and I have always been blown away by the quality of yummy italian food here. 
I am a pizza snob and this place does pizza right!

Post race energy depletion meant I needed some noms, and I always turn to Yelp for reliable advice. My padre was hesitant as always, but of course he caved, and he was very pleased he did. We both went ahead and had prosciutto included in our dishes. He went with the breakfast sandwich, and I the omelette (also with onions and feta). The omelette was incredible. I feel as though restaurants don't normally sauté their onions for flavor first, but Tuscany really pulled through in that regard. The prosciutto was also no super chewy, and we both agreed a great quality meat. The hash browns now.. you can see the chunks of garlic.. I am Italian ladies and gents. I bleed garlic and olive oil. This made me V happy. 

Atmosphere was cute, quaint, and very welcoming. Minus this strange musty smell I noticed. Only advice would be to fix that up, and possibly more options in the omelette area. It's a make your own, but sometimes I like to not think and have fun creations presented right to me (I can be lazy after winning my first bike race back in years, can't I?)

We went there a few times and had a great experience each time. The food is simply amazing, I can highly recommend the spicy garlic edamame, the salmon poke and the mexicali roll. We always sat at the bar and felt that the chefs could be a bit nicer, that's why I am not giving 5 stars. If you like good sushi in a nice and cozy ambiance, you should give it a try!

This place is not to be understated. These tacos are freaking DELICIOUS. The freshly made corn tortillas and the freshly grilled meat, THE HORCHATA (and I typically don't care for the stuff)!!! Everything was amazing. We had #1, #11, #9, and a Coke and horchata. 

Be warned that your taco comes quite plain...you need to order guac separately ($3.50!!), but salsa is free, and it's good. ALSO, it's cash only!

I'm getting the chilaquiles next time (saw someone else eating them and they looked incredible). 

Go and try this place. It's worth the wait in line.

I have been a fan of all other Sabrina's!! Soo Excited this one opened in NJ, for days I don't feel like crossing over bridge, this location is perfect.The inside is great, original Woolworth's , & chalk boards up top, hallway for waiting ..as the hosts have tablets -to get on the lists..

It didnt disappoint, we went  2 weeks ago, as the waitress said it was their 1st weekend with brunch& waitress did say not All items were available on menu-just yet!!
WE got the Apple & gouda omelete, with potato & bacon..was Great!!! Course the coffee was GREAT!! 

Return factor: Of course
Its right in heart of Haddon Ave, great window shopping!!

Sabrina's is always a solid choice for brunch. I tend to take friends here when they're visiting Philly because it's consistent, delicious, and the wait is not too long when you use their call ahead option. They're BYO which is good or bad depending on your drink preference for brunch, but they take credit cards which is awesome. I also like that they have outdoor seating for when the weather is nice. 

Their prices are reasonable and I haven't had anything I haven't liked. The coffee is good and they have iced coffee for those warm summer days. My favorite meal is the huevos rancheros. They're just the right amount of spice, but super flavorful with runny egg yolks just like I like them! There's a veggie option which I sometimes opt for since the chorizo is heavy and the dish is already pretty filling. It's topped with lime sour cream and guac and it makes for a perfect mexican brunch dish. Their pick your own omelette is also another good choice since you can pack a lot of different veggies in and some cheese/meat for a decent price. Their home fries are also delicious.

Definitely would check this place out for brunch. Use the Yelp app which estimates wait times or call ahead so you don't wait for hours there.
Great dinner tonight.  Our server, Patrick, couldn't have been more helpful and efficient.  Food was tasty and filling.  Drinks were good.  This was our first visit and we will be back.

So I may or may not have gone here twice in 24 hours ~don't judge me~. 

The risotto and butter lettuce salad are the main reason I come here again and again, but the service and decor just tops everything off. This restaurant is absolutely beautiful. Very Alice in wonderland. 

I would recommend going for tea as well, as the prices are fair and let's be real, the instagram pics are pretty cute. 

The only caveat here is how loud it gets. To the point in some rooms where you find yourself yelling across the table. 

Otherwise, I highly recommend if you're visiting the Rittenhouse district.

The blackened grouper was very tasty. Wonderful fries. We saw dolphins off the back deck and watched the pelican swoop around in the water. Limited draft selection and no corn tortillas for the tacos. Friendly waitress.

This was the best place for our Thanksgiving dinner.  My daughter and I loved the service. Though we were not given sanitizer we were given hot towels to wash our hands before eating. They made sure to social distance us. The restaurant is beautiful no matter where you sit. The cosmopolitan was the best I've ever had. The lamb was perfectly cooked. We had a great time. The lobster bisque had real lobster not just cream base. It's a must to dine there.

Was in the area toady and decided to try this restaurant. I love Mediterranean food amd I have to say that Shawarmaji is one of the best in Edmonton. I ordered their chicken shawarma lunch special. Was so tasty and fresh. First time to taste the Lebanese coffee and I liked it. The person in charge was so friendly too. Resto was clean. Service was great. Will definitely come back.

In a town of outstanding food, this place stands out.  Why?  Because it's awesome, that's why.

If you're a tourist, get the f*(#k out of the French Quarter and go to the Garden District, wander around looking at the stately mansions, and end up here for the BEST FREAKING SANDWICHES you will ever eat in your life!

We split a half-and-half with shrimp and catfish.  Holy!  Everything was perfect - tender, fresh, flavorful seafood, perfectly seasoned and delicious light batter, the bread with soft and just melted away, leaving the seafood to take center stage.  I want that sandwich.  I love that sandwich more than is normal.  

Atmosphere is super chill and very cool.  Self-service iced tea.  Order at counter.  

I wish every person who visited NOLA would stop in here.  Such a great experience.

I can't believe no one has reviewed this place. I'm only giving a 4 because I have never sat down to eat, but their muffins are so good and their prices are great. Also the owner and all employees are the nicest people in the world.

Really enjoyed our first visit, gyro was delicious, steak wrap very good also. Not crowded, has outside seating which we enjoyed.  Greek fries were also hot, crispy and good with the cheese on them and of course the delish tzatziki sauce with them.  Only one disappointment, no masks on staff.
Seems like the times have been hard on this place which used to be our neighborhood staple for Chinese. The menu and the venue could both use an update. Really nice people.
i literally paid almost $40 and got the wrong order on uber eats - the driver said that's what she was given! then when i called the phone didn't work! worst place ever!

Food is great. I love that they make all of the food from scratch. If your looking for a great spot to have brunch Sabrina's is a winner. I also enjoy their breakfast potatoes. Pancakes are nice and fluffy and you can't go wrong with their French toast.

In case you haven't heard, Sidecar's upstairs bar/dining room is open for service! We swung by last night with friends to check it out and everyone agreed that the exposed brick, retro banquettes and tables and large windows with a pretty view of the skyline were on point. It's a totally different vibe and yet somehow the same old Sidecar. Great servers, awesome beer. Two thumbs up.

Lovely small and intimate with great food! Friends and I popped in one Friday evening. What a treat! We were welcomed with open arms and the graciousness continued from arrival to departure. We had empanadas and various dishes and they were all delectable. I'll visit often.

After days of eating buttered, sugared, and creamed everything, we wanted something clean and lean. This was a great choice. There was a delicious looking selection of raw, gluten free, vegetarian, and vegan options. They also had crab cakes, eggs, and cheese options, too. I delighted in my veggie egg white omelette, wheat English muffin, vegan sausage, and wheat blueberry pancakes. The pancakes were perfect, the staff was fun to chat with, and the atmosphere was relaxed and casual. I'll have to come back to NOLA just for the vegan gumbo.

This is my go to for a quick healthy lunch. There are many options on the menu. There are also some good healthy  non soda drink options. What most people don't take advantage of is adding freebies to your salad like cucumbers or greens. I have Panera rewards card and after anywhere from 4 to 6 visits I get a reward. It can be anything from a free drink to a free sandwich.

Our first time in Nashville for our 10 year anniversary.  Location was great. View was great Construction didn't bother us at all. Under the skirt of our beds was a dirty sock, earplugs, an empty bottle of water and an empty mini bottle of vodka. What else wasn't cleaned. Then we went down for breakfast. We were seated and were passed by for 15 minutes while every other table was served multiple times. We left.

FINALLY, new location opened in Nashville. Nice location and not bad service. They also have Chipotlane for drive through pickup which i have never tried before. You can order online and drive through to pickup your food.
I would really appreciate if the staff is a bit more friendly.
Also we recently order online for delivery through Doordash and they totally missed the instructions we gave and did not add rice at all. 

A slight improvement in service would go a long way.

Still giving a 4* for the location.

Want good pizza late nite? Come here!

They have a good selection and different sizes! 

I got there special which have lots of toppings.  The veggies tastes fresh.

They close at midnight and we came in at 11:15. It took awhile for our pizzas, but they were hot and fresh.

This is my new lunch spot for BBQ. It's good every time. Even though the menu is limited everything is delicious including pork, beef, and chicken, but my favorite  is the Turkey and the Rib eye . It's was deliciously  smoked and flavorful. Worth the visit!

Yummmm love the cool new flavors, 
"Home means Nevada" and Licorice my Favorite!!! Fresh and creamery!!

I'm a frequent customer to The Journey who will be a lot less frequent. I usually have a high tolerance for crappy service, especially at ethnic restaurants - it's one of the things that makes them more authentic (I'm ethnic so I can say that). But The Journey doesn't just have crappy service - they have aggressively hostile and rude service.

Try this experiment... Go to The Journey, go to the sushi line, pick up the tongs, grab some sushi rolls, and then put the tongs neatly back onto the plate of sushi rolls instead of the Plate That Is Reserved for Tongs.

OMFG. If you didn't know better, you'd think that you just took a huge steaming dump onto the plate of sushi rolls. The sushi-making dude who speaks no English will grunt in your general direction, gesticulate angrily, and then put the tongs so hard onto the Plate That Is Reserved For Tongs that it makes a loud clangy sound and everyone within eyesight of the circus sideshow turns to see it. Translation: "MF'er!!! put the f'ing tongs back onto the f'ing Plate That is Reserved for Tongs!!!!!!!"

After you're done with that experiment, try this experiment: Go to a plate of sushi rolls and, instead of picking the one that is in the very front - maybe because the one at the front is smaller, has too much rice, has a booger on it, or maybe it's just because you're the paying customer and you don't have to have an explicit reason - pick another one. The reaction from the sushi chefs will be more severe than if you had just burned down an orphanage full of screaming orphans using cute furry puppies as kindling. 

What's amazing is customer after customer were either visibly insulted by the above and/or laughing at the stupidity of it, and they don't get the message. In addition, it's not just the employees - I saw the owner of the place do the same things.

How long can you display contempt for your customers before your customers get the message?

I can't say enough good things about House of Kabob. My fiancée brought me for lunch and I am hooked.

My go to is the Jr Chicken Tika with rice and a grilled tomato. The chicken is so tender and the flavor is amazing. The steak skewer is good too, but the chicken definitely steals the show!

They are moving to a new building soon with better parking. Thank goodness for that because during lunch, parking is extremely hard to come by.

The service is always pretty good. Drinks are refilled and the food is brought out promptly.

Talk about a unique experience! In the rare (or not so?) event that you're in the mood for a hot dog, look no further. I was blown away first by the atmosphere, since I'm usually enjoying a hot dog at a ball park or picnic. Here, you're in pretty sleek bar setting with tons of options for boozing with your meal. They really bring some surprising sophistication to the dog game. 

In terms of variety, there's something for every mood. If you're feeling extra meaty, go for the Kansas City. Or venture to a city abroad as you enjoy another geographically themed delicacy. If you're not getting a hot dog, you probably will be getting some side eye, from me at least. I wouldn't come here to order a salad. 

As for my first experience, awesome all around! I tried the alligator and shrimp dog, and was definitely feeling the New Orleans flavor. The bread they use as a bun really brings it to the next level, and I would like to see them do more in that regard too! Maybe they could play around with some sourdough, a seeded bun...the skies the limit (or the Destination?), we'll see! Service was fantastic too; our waiter provided some great suggestions, and the food came out in no time.

Great atmosphere and staff...but missed the mark on the most important aspect. 

We were a party of 6. Our appetizers were very good, the drinks were great, the restaurant ambiance was spectacular, and the vibe was superb. However my medium rare steaks were cooked almost well done. Our waitress (who was awesome) and the dinning room manager offered to have the steaks re-done, but I didn't want my party to wait on me and I absolutely hate to throw away food (especially steaks). In a restaurant like this I don't expect this kind of huge error to happen (maybe one level to the right or left, but not all the way to well done). The staff did send us a free desert to share, but that didn't really fix my $65 well-done steak. So there goes 3 perfectly cut steaks down the drain (along with my $65). We were having a good time in the restaurant, but the main event (food) lowered my "fun-level" a lot. 

Next time I want a good steak I will stay with the regulars: Charley's, Burns, or Council Oak.

Let me start off by saying that I/we truly enjoy the spirit and energy that is the Hamburger Mary's franchise.  We try to frequent these eateries whenever we find ourselves in a city which has one, as was the case this past weekend in Ybor City (Tampa).  We didn't have a reservation but the reception staff, who was very accommodating, found us a seat.  We thoroughly enjoyed the atmosphere; it was as festive as always.  Our waiter "Michael" was a blast; we had a great time with him as did his other tables around us.

The above notwithstanding, I must say that the food and show were lacking, at least in comparison to other H.M. stores we've enjoyed.  The food came out almost cold and although it was replaced, it all just seemingly took forever.
 
The show at other stores have always been just that, finely tuned performances; 1 maybe 2 songs per performer. Sure, the ladies collected their tips along the way but in Ybor the shows were nothing more than endless medley's, seemingly protracted to insure maximum collection time; it went on and on and on!  Even the DJ, who we sat next to, seemed bored out of his mind.  He did serve another purpose though; he counted the money as the ladies wandered the floor.
  
I'm sorry to make this sound like a downer, but despite the excellent wait-staff, the evening and the medleys just seemed to drudge on forever.  These folks should take a drive over to Orlando and see how it's done.  Just sayin -

Indy is really upping their food game since I've been there last.  Met an old friend here for breakfast.  It was cold in June so we sat inside. It was cold inside.  Or maybe I'm just turning into one of those old people that is always cold.
Greeted by a very friendly guy who told me to sit where ever I wanted.  My friend came and the very friendly guy was also our waiter.  Very chill guy...very cute, very nice.  I might have fallen in love...just a little.
I really liked their menu. It was eight in the morning but he said we could order anything.  I still wanted to try their biscuits and chicken gravy.  Got a half order with two over easy eggs which was still really large.
My friend ordered the chicken sausage and, gosh I forget what else but she loved it.  The coffee comes in a really cool cup that you'll want to steal and it's good!
Recommended for sure.

We love this place!!! The sandwiches are so unique and so flavorful. And don't get me started on the house made pickles!! Yum. We went today and only finished half of our meals. A waitress came, took out sandwiches and had them individually wrapped and even added a little container of pickles!!! Very happy!

Acme Oyster House offered a gut busting seafood menu. The space is big: there is a bar for drinks, oyster bar (for shucked raw oysters) and tables for people to sit and feast.

This was our first night out in NOLA. We were excited! We waited for a table and the wait was about 20-30 minutes.

We sat near the bar. I could see everything, the TVs playing the basketball game, the bar, the oyster shucking station and all the tables. There was so much noise: talking, laughing, clattering of dirty plates behind the bar, and people dancing. 

We ordered: 2 Medleys (gumbo, jambalaya, red beans and rice + fried soft shell crab), 1 dozen chargrilled oysters, 1 large Ettoufee with fried crawfish tails, 1 Jambalaya, and 1 cup of chicken and Andouille Gumbo. 
Dessert: 1 bread pudding with scoop of vanilla ice cream. 

The Good:
The chargrilled oysters were buttered, garlicky and so plump and delicious! I loved it! We took the bread to sop up the sauce. 
One oyster had some sand. They weren't the best chargrilled oysters that we had in NOLA but they were a close 3rd. 

Protip: dip that bread daintily in the oyster sauce. Don't sop up a large amount of that sauce bc it is super salty!!

The fried soft shell crab was juicy, crispy and so light. The flavors were simple and the texture and cooking was well executed. 

The bread pudding was delicious! It was gooey, sweet and had a great flan texture. Even though we were stuffed from all the food, we still devoured the dessert.


The ok: Andouille sausage. It was grilled in the medley. It was a good sausage. The large ettouffee had a little bit of seafood. The fried crawfish tails added more seafood and a bit of texture.

The red beans were buttered and broken down. They were ok. 

The gumbo was a little salty and tasted nothing like what was made in the New Orleans Cooking School. 

I would definitely return to eat a plate of chargrilled oysters. 


instagram.com/snackchatnyc
the to-go specialist was amazing. We will come back solely because him he. He had a great smile and was energetic.

BEER CHEESE SOUP.

They have it on Thursday's and it is to die for.  I've never gone on any day other than a Thursday, but I've heard their crawfish on Friday's are pretty swell as well.  But once again, BEER CHEESE SOUP.

Chargrilled oysters chargrilled oysters chargrilled oysters!!!! I just can't say it enough. I'm usually a fan of just plain steamed oysters, but after reading the reviews of the chargrilled variety I decided I had to try it. I can still taste the garlicky buttery goodness. The oysters are cooked to perfection and served in a delectable sauce, with bread on the side for dippin. It took a little longer than our entrees to get to us, and even combined with the 20 minute wait for a table, these babies were still worth it! I wished they had an option to get more than a dozen.

For my entree I had the shrimp poboy and jambalaya. Both were pretty good, but the oysters were def the highlight of the meal.
Corned Beef Hash was amazing! Fresh & tasty! For a Saturday morning we were able to get a table fast. Service was excellent!
The staff is pleasant and the food is delicious. I was hungry and forgot to take a picture, but the chicken flaunts were yummy.
Top to bottom the best dining experience I have had in years. All at a hotel restaurant!  Completely unexpected.

Let me preface by saying: WE ARE IN GLOBAL PANDEMIC AND I WILL COME BACK AGAIN!

While I am extremely thankful that Sabrina's Cafe was open and available to feed me in a time of need. I gotta keep it real. While the dine in experience may be significantly better the take out experience was not that impressive. 

Let's start with the ordering process,  very smooth and simple. I'd recommend you have your form of payment handy and available. Once ordered the food was done in 15mins.  

Now here is my issue. The transportation of the food from the restaurant to home was problematic. I'm assuming due to the packaging and the temperature of the food. By the time I got home, the waffles and chicken became soggy. 

I know this isn't 100% their fault but when you are charging $15.00 for breakfast, I need the packaging to be right for take out and not lose out on the experience. Again, I will be back when things return to "normal" to provide an update. Hopefully this is can help others as well. In the meantime, thank you to the staff at Sabrina's Cafe for providing great customer service.

Went to lees on a whim after drooling over their Instagram page for a few weeks. Got a shrimp and chicken Alfredo cheessteak with spinach. It was aaaaammmaaaazing. The food is good the place is clean and cheery. The price is up there but the quality of the food particularly the bread and seafood is  worth paying more than I would normally. Mr Lee and staff are very friendly and patient while you choose from their endless selection.  Make it a point to stop here if you are in u city and on the prowl for good eats!!

Great seafood and atmosphere. I like most of their food the bang bang shrimp is my favorite. I thought the sushi was just okay. The inside is nice with tables and a very large bar. The inside bar has lots of tvs. It open up to a great view of the lake. There are also tables outside!

It was the monopoly of any restaurants being open.  Took them 15-20min to even take my order.  Then I told them to box it up.  That took a while, too.  I had to board.  Take a look at the picture and tell me how that's a turkey club sandwich.

This is a really nice place to grab soup, salad, or a sandwich. The ingredients are really fresh, the portions are filling, and the staff are very helpful. 


The ambience is very welcoming. This place is also perfect for a informal business lunch.

The food was great! I had the bravehart and my husband had the cast iron eggs. The hotel potatoes were delicious and crispy with just the right amount of salt. The service was lovely and the patio seating area was perfect for a late morning breakfast. I would recommend Cup Cafe to anyone
Food was ehhh. The atmosphere was AMAZING. Worth the trip to just hang out and have a few drinks.

I've been here a couple of times and loved it each time. Pumpkin curry and pad thai is my favorite. Their appetizers are good too. I had the spring roll thing, coconut soup, and fried banana. Delicious.

I give it a one star because of the dishonesty of the help.
We were a party of 6 for an anniversary. Delicious food! Great service
One of the party lost her sweater, no one found it, and I forgot to to
pick up a gift that I had left next to my chair. No can find that either.
Hard to believe.
Love this place ! Great food great prices friendly service ! And their pancakes are to die for !

The best priced Cajun food I've ever bought! I had the amazing red beans and rice with blackened fish, cornbread, and a salad for $10! They also have have. Groupon which is helpful for large groups. Every food item tasted amazing and had the perfect amount of seasoning; the food is made with love and our server Nyce was AWESOME! They also have a house fruit punch which is REALLY worth a try. I would highly recommend getting this food to-go. My family and I ate outside and that was not a great choice. It's not in the best part of town and there are crazy amounts of flies. There is not nearly enough seating. Even though the atmosphere is horrible (says a person who absolutely hates eating outside), I still rated this place 5 stars because the food and service is just THAT great. 
Overall: I'll for sure eat here again, just to-go!!!

By far the best sushi in Tampa. 
The restaurant does not give justice to the food. 
It is small, simple, and clean, with marginal service....but my god the sushi is amazing. 

The Buccaneer Roll is yummy, even though I typically don't eat Americanized rolls. 
The only sushi that I truly enjoy in Tampa Bay. 
Nothing else gets that self talking "mmmm good" reaction. 

If you are on a date, then get it as take-out or get a date who doesn't care about ambiance.

Price was reasonable and taste was decent!
It was super busy saturday dinner time.. told to wait for 25 mins but i think we were seated earlier than that 
Thanks to other reviews , i ordered free margaritas which wasnt my cup of tea but its free afterall. Lol. 
They do check your ID. 
Two of us ordered burrito with chipotle sauce and tacos tortas and two tacos. Delicious! 
Check came out $23.80 total. Pretty good deal for dinner!

It's roots are in the Tamales, and there's no mistake in saying they're arguably the best, Green Corn and Beef tamales in town! You can pre-order by the dozen to take home, or they're part of their humble, but very, very good Sunday buffet. It's a quaint setup but it stands big on those tamales.

I have been coming to Little Anthony's for years, I however have never had the food just always enjoy the fun ice cream creations and retro atmosphere. Always fun entertainment and great classic cars. Music is always on point. Friendly staff as well. I love all of the fun cut outs for pictures and there are Poké stops near by for anyone who plays Pokémon Go.

Delicious brisket and ribs 
Same location as brewery where the pb stout was delicious. Had to try the southern BBQ

Wine selection was large with a good variety of Italian wine from northern Italy. The pasta is made daily and our meals (burrata tortellini and chicken pesto) were amazing. Making me miss Italy when I lived in sacile and this just made our return list.

I remember waiting in line on weekends for one hour to get table and back then the food was great! The service was high tempo  and good.
Last week I received guests from Europe and Asia so I decided to show case American breakfast. 
My experience was a désastre it started with how the waitress poured coffee holding  her container high it splashed the coffee  all over the saucer . The silverware was not polished  that's just the beginning!! Food was served cold and tasteless prepared with out any care.
I kept apologizing to my guests and telling them how good it used to be. 
Sad sad sad ....
Well next time I will just stick to regular diner at least I can get better service and decent food for 1/3 of the price...

Decided to go to Kimswick and support a local business. I honestly cannot believe I waited an hour to eat here. First off, our waitress was terrible. If we asked for more than one thing at a time, you'd only get about half. Had to constantly look for her to get something. Had to ask three times for water and it wasn't overly crowded. 

Second of all, the food..... What happened to all their home cooked items? A turkey club is not something I'd write home about. Our table also had 5-6 nats constantly flying around and when we told our waitress she said "I'll be sure to tell them"..... Okay, great. We then waited about 15 minutes after we finished eating to order dessert. I think they forgot to add cinnamon to their Apple pies. It was missing something. Wouldn't order any of this again. For an $80 tab our table was severely disappointed. 

Still laughing at myself for waiting to get into this restaurant. Wanting to support local but I'd also like to enjoy the food/experience. Very unlikely to return.
Such a joke of a zaxbys, 15mins to take my order. Another 15mins to make. Forgets the zax sauce. Y'all need to fire the whole staff. The place was empty

This is your typical Cheesecake Factory food chain restaurant and it is located inside a mall plaza. I think the location is very convenient too.

I really like Cheesecake Factory because the menu selection is huge and there are so many options. Plus I have a sweet tooth for cheesecake like fresh strawberry, red velvet and anything chocolate or white chocolate. The service was good.

Wonderful dinner to celebrate our 1st anniversary. The tomato pie was surprisingly the star of the meal and the beet salad was refreshing. We ordered the halibut which was cooked to perfection. The desserts- the homemade ice cream and skillet cookie were delicious. To top it off, the service was fantastic!
The real deal!!Tamales and tacos made with all fresh ingredients even the tortilla's!If you've been to a taco stand inTexas or California you know what I'm talking about!

3.5 stars. 

So, who knew the Vietnamese restaurant would have the absolute best French fries in Fishers?!?!

They are beer battered, thick, curly cut pieces of golden delicious heaven. You must try them.

The first time, I ordered the full chao fries with the lemongrass pork and picked carrot. The second time, I just got the fries (and grabbed some Buffalo wings on my way home!) The pork and carrot really make the meal, but the amount of pork on the fries felt kinda minimal... disproportionate to the amount of fries and carrot...and I couldn't justify the price.

I also got the pork egg rolls, but I was disappointed that I paid six bucks for two tiny, overcooked egg rolls. Definitely overpriced.

Service here is great. Parking is plentiful. COVID precautions were observed. They have kids meals. And they have curbside delivery, too. 

I'll have to try a smoothie next time!

I grew up on The Flying tomato Brother's & other deep dish Chicago pizza, so you really can't compare! 

It's the only pizza joint in Indy where I can get sun dried tomato's & goat cheese on a pizza...this is why I go. 

the sauce & crust are at best forgettable.

Super average sandwiches. This place looks exactly like Gourmet Bagger in San Diego but the quality is not the same. The bread on my BLT was toasted so much that it tasted like a cracker. I question the quality of the bacon and the other ingredients. If I was in the mood for a sandwich I would choose Beyond Bread instead.
Good food & service. Great healthier option for on the go, or to chill while you enjoy the scenery in the heart of the French Quarters

Cant go wrong here.  Its a fun experience.  Any negative reviews of this place are suspect.

Have you ever been invited in for a kitchen tour at another restaurant? My guess is that if you have, it was an exception, not the rule.  At Bern's it is the rule...and it's fun..  

Service is almost always excellent.  Suggest you avoid Holidays, Fathers/Mothers/Valentines days, and go on a weekday when the Tampa Bay residents/locals go to Bern's. 

The wine cellar....I could spend hours in there! Wine selection is the BEST in the world - don't take it from me, read the Spectator, Advocate and Enthusiast....Take the tour and you will see.

Desert room(s) are old school and wonderful, and the deserts are second to none.  

Coffee roasted and ground on site, and then brewed in Illy coffee machines....the best you can buy.

This place is a must see for everyone, and it is an EXCELLENT value.

I suggest the 6 oz Chateaubriand tips, Not only do you get three perfectly grilled "chunks" of  the meat,, you get that char-grilled crust on the outside,  that in my opinion is the best part of a perfectly grilled medium rare steak.  It is the best deal on the menu, bar none.

Say "Hi!" to Marco at the bar, he has been there for years, and is a really nice guy.

Quit reading and just go!

Update: Have consistently gotten great food and great service, but still wanted to update my previous 5-star review with another 5-star review after the following incident:

I told a friend at work that I wanted to take her out for dinner/drinks anywhere she wanted to go, to celebrate her upcoming retirement. She chose Granite City. From the moment we walked in, the hostess, who was also our server, was really upbeat and friendly and knowledgeable. In joking about how we were there for happy hour, it slipped out of my mouth that we were also celebrating the friend's retirement. Our server later surprised us with a special dessert for my friend, with "Congratulations on your retirement" written in glaze on the plate. It was a really nice, thoughtful, and generous gesture. Thank you for going out of your way, and for the top notch service! We will definitely be back.

Excellent steak. Comparable to Ruth's Chris.  Large salads.. My son had the Caesar and I had Caprese (biggest Caprese I've ever seen!).  Nice atmosphere, but loud.  I agree with others in that service was very efficient but not overly friendly, which together could lead you to feel a little rushed.

I'll never go to this restaurant again. My first time attending and the owner came to my table and asked our party what our issue is because we made her server cry. Our only interaction with her at that point was my friend asking for a short stack of pancakes and cheese on her eggs and the server saying she's new, she doesn't think they do that. I don't feel in the restaurant business you should go to a table and tell your guest they're the reason your server is crying. It made us feel uncomfortable, targeted, and bad for the server. When my food did come, it was cold and my glass was dirty. I've been to way better brunch places in the city.
Food was good, service was great to me personally, but others at my table had a lot of problems. I suggest coming with a small group, large groups confuse the order

Overall very Bad experience. 

Worst Thai Food & to top it bad service. 
Visiting Santa Barbara from Bay Area where we have a plethora of Thai Restaurants - so we are spoilt with Thai cuisine options the Bay Area has to offer. Nevertheless- based on other reviews - we decided to order take out from Zen Thai. 
- we ordered 
Tom Kha - overpowered by Coconut milk. Lacked the galangal, Kaffir & lemongrass flavors in it. Very watery too. 

Green Curry - very spicy, and again very watery gravy with cut jalapeño in it.  We asked them to keep it as mild as possible. So disappointed. 

Plain vermicelli noodles for our toddler. Over the phone we asked specifically if they have them as our toddler loves it. Instead the take out had flat write noodle! 

To go with the green curry - we ordered 3 serves of rice. Ended up getting just 1 serve!! Since we were staying at a hotel - we couldn't make extra rice so instead ended up having the green curry as a soup! 

Overall very Bad experience!
The Key Lime Pie ice cream was amazing! Best ice cream I've had in Indiana, by far.
