The service was the only thing to write home about. The food we ordered was all mediocre. Beef was tough and bread was soggy. Spend your time and money elsewhere unless you want to step into another tourist trap.

Favorite of Our professional athletes and business people.  Very, very good food. Friendly service.  The owner is always on premises and he is very affiable.  The food is served fast, hot and fresh.  Great luncheon menu.  This is a reliable and consistently good choice for excellent Chinese.

My wife brought me a slice on her way home from work. I was hooked! The pizza was so good. The flavor and the size of the slice!! We went back and I ordered a slice of pepperoni and their Sicilian. Man, that was some good pizza. Good value too. It was made to order but didn't take too long. Their pizza and a cold beer, perfect combo!

I will preface this review with the following fact: the employees here are great. They listen to your order with intensity, key it into the POS at a quick to rapid speed and the burgers, fries and other assorted feed is heated up to edible temperature as fast as the laws of thermodynamics allow. For this prompt and valued service, I have levied seven (7) stars. This is in combination with my food review, which follows. If Yelp got with the "program" of a "21st century website" there would be separate reviews for food and service, and I award the service a standard five (5) stars. The food receives -5 (negative five) stars.

Regardless, this review is primarily to address the longstanding advertising campaign of Five Guys that plasters their greased inner walls with claims from local papers, websites, fans, celebrities and more of how wonderful, delicious and world class their burgers are. It is all a pack of lies. I have visited this Five Guys, and two others in the Greater Philadelphia area over the last three years. Never have I enjoyed my burger. I have ordered it, and eaten it, and  felt nothing in my heart but misery, pain, grief, sadness, frustration and anger. I read reviews online and I shake my head, gnash my teeth, I ball my hands into fists and pound on my work desk like a petulant child, shaking with rage...thinking, "Why?!" Their burgers are overcooked, even for Big Food Industry safety standards, mealy, chewy and most damning of all, flavorless. Tasting of boiled, reconstituted beef gristle, you could fish better meat out of the cloning vat reject cesspool. The toppings can barely save any number of patties, and the cheese resembles a car's finish that's melted and softened under a heat lamp and slowly pried off with a paint scraper. 

The fries (again acclaimed in reviews both in the store to fool consumers, and by blinded "real" reviewers") are over-salted, over-cooked brittle fingernails slowly wrenched out of the fingertips of a veteran "WORLD'S LONGEST NAILS" $1 freak show performer. Even a "Tiny" order of this is only tiny by lesser abyssal plane dwelling standards, the charred husks dumped into a grease laden bag in a frenzy, with barely 17% of the fries making it into the cup they provide.

All in all, one of the most woebegone meals I've ever had.
Absolutely love potluck!!! Such amazing food and amazing owners! I follow them on Instagram and it's fun to see all the different places they go to each night!

Just got back from our first try of this place and we were generally impressed! The menu was totally different from what was online, so just be aware that it does change. My husband got the baseball-cut steak and I got the ricotta-stuffed pasta. The ingredients were extremely fresh and high-quality, from the meat to the veggies to the pasta. The steak was a bit overcooked for my husband's taste, he said it seemed like they cooked it at too low a temperature, but it was excellent quality and he enjoyed the balance of flavors in the dish very much.

The best part of the meal was something we didn't even order-- none of the desserts on the menu appealed to us, so we were just going to forget about it. The chef sent us out a flourless chocolate cake that wasn't on the menu, though, and it was AMAZING. They should definitely keep that around, because it made our meal! The chef also sent out samples of a soup earlier in the meal, which we liked. It's nice to feel like you're trying things as they're being developed!

The waiter was a bit formal for such a quiet neighborhood place, which is part of the one reservation I have about the restaurant: it's quite expensive and a quite upscale atmosphere. If the prices were, say, five dollars cheaper per entree I think it would have a better chance in this neighborhood. There are too many inexpensive options competing with it, and it won't get many walk-ins like it would in Center City-- I think it would do great over there, but I'm worried about it over here!

Then again, Marigold Cafe does fine in the neighborhood, and Rimedio's food was much less fussy and just as interesting, in my opinion. So we'll have to wait and see-- but if you're looking for a lovely, quiet, high-quality date-night BYOB in University City, give it a try!

Came here a couple of times, once for dinner and another for a night out of drinks.
Cool little spot.
The food is good, and has good vegetarian options. Lobster mac n cheese, white mussels, and oreo beignets are great

They have a good number of drink cocktails too. Unique martinis too
I went for Valentine's day this year, it was amazing. I loved the food and the concept of the restaurant! Def worth the price and the experience. Another restaurant checked off the "bucket list!"

There's a reason everybody gives such a high rating to this place. The sandwiches are made to order and the thin sliced, fresh roast beef contained in them couldn't be better. I'm pretty sure the owner made my sandwich while his daughter took my order. It's great to support local businesses, especially when the food is good.

Perfect spot to grab lunch and take to the park on a nice day.  My boyfriend actually brought me here after getting a "Fajita Wrap" on his own a few times and genuinely thought that it was real chicken, so I had to try it.  I typically detest imitation meat products, but this was delicious! Can't wait for spring to be sprung so I can plan another take out picnic.  

One star deducted because it was pretty cramped and there were a few employees hanging around in peoples way, but it was popping off at lunch time so that's a good thing for business.  No restroom-- they suggested we use the Barnes and Noble Bookstore.

I've been a few times in the past with a group that just ordered drinks at the bar, and that's about all I'd recommend this place for. 

My dining experience there recently was pretty mediocre. Do not order any of their flat breads!! I'm not sure how to describe what ends up being served, but it is not good- very soggy, skimpy toppings, and the dough has the weirdest texture. The pierogis were fine in comparison, but I think they were the frozen, boxed variety and were just reheated. The folks that ordered burgers and sandwiches seemed to have the right idea. Nobody raved about them, but they seemed good. 

Ordered two rounds of drinks during the meal, and they do definitely have a really wide selection of beer. 

We were sitting in the back, underneath the stairs, and mid way through the meal, the pipe above our table starts leaking. Not just an occasional drop, but a steady stream along a couple feet of the piping. Two of my friends got their backs soaked, and we ended up all moving to the other side of the able. A couple of them are in construction management so they actually walked up the stairs to see if they could identify the problem as we tried to flag down a staff member. Our waitress claimed to not be able to see the water leaking, and then once we flagged her down a second time, her response was "That's weird, that usually only happens when it rains" and then walked away a second time????? Our group had been joking about it until that point, assuming we'd be offered to relocate to another table. When an alternate table was not offered, we just asked for the check to get out of there. That's when the manager came over with the check, and he had taken a round off the tab. Appreciated, but kind of a weird reaction.

I'm being generous with 3 stars because I'm basing it on one visit.  My wife ordered fish and didn't like it. She never complains about fish.  My hamburger sucked.  If I had to guess it was a frozen  patty.   I was asked how I wanted it cooked.  I asked if they will actually cook it the way I asked, because most places can't seem to do it.   She said yes they do here.  I ordered it medium.   We did a takeout and jumped on the boat.  The hamburger was very well done.  It was a big diameter hamburger, but very thin.  Maybe the thickness of a McDonald's quarter pounder. That's probably why it's well done or nothing.   I certainly will not return for a hamburger.

Let me begin by saying my family and friends call me the hamburgler. Do not be fooled by my 5ft 4inch 110 pound frame because I can throw down with most 260 pound guys....

And THIS my friends is it. I've probably eaten more hamburgers than anyone I know and at places famous like The Pantry/umami/apple pan in Los Angeles, port of call here in New Orleans, brindle room in NYC, and about a zillion infamous places in Texas, Nashville and the like.

But this place trumps them all. Fresh, steaming, gooey happiness...simple and totally out of this world. I love the fact that there are only a few things on the menu because these few things they do flawlessly! The homemade condiments just are just the icing on the cake. The onion rings are the best I've had in years and word on the street is the owners mother bakes all the deserts that, by the way are delish! If you want reasonably priced, fresh and local hamburger perfection really they can't be beat.
place js the spot too go for a good slice, I'd give it 5 if the girl working the register most days didnt seem like she wants to die

Ya know, you want to try all cheese steak places, to really see if Pats is the best.

I do concede that on some days, Pats is "not on their game" and Geno's is better...

But a good "C minus" steak from one of these two places is usually better than any place that is on their "A game".

Sorry for that dissertation... and now Philip's Steaks.  I was really hoping I found something here...I was asking my self "why did I never hear of this place?".

Well the answer might be that it is just average.  It is not bad, but not excellent.  If your in the Passyunk area...try it...maybe they will be "on their game that day".

Meeting friends and relatives for a cocktail and quick bite. Generous serving of my favorite single malt scotch. I  had an early fare of shrimp Remulade, salad, crab cake and peanut butter pie. All were in keeping with Feelings I have come to know.The crab cake was especially good. Both bar and wait staff were exceptionally friendly and helpful. Not at all intrusive
best cheesecakes in town! it wouldn't be a birthday celebration without a peppermint cheesecake. I'm not kidding when I say that it is the tastiest dessert- you gotta try one!

So many amazing things on the menu I had a hard time deciding.  Went with the breakfast burrito and chips and queso.  The burrito was large and stuffed full of fresh goodness and smothered with cheese sauce and a spicy red sauce. It was fantastic!  Can't wait to go back and work my way down the menu!!
Love this neighborhood gem! Fun time with great surroundings ! Great service with Rachel ! Definitely coming back!!
This place is huge, bright, and the menu has something for everyone. Very fresh food featuring local ingredients. This was the first of many visits!

Do not come here. You're better off going hungry. This place is deplorable. It's 8am on a Sunday, before the crowd/rush. Not busy at all. We waited at the host stand and someone had to wake the host from the room behind the stand. We sat and ordered. About 10 minutes later they came back and said they were out of sirloin tips. 10 minutes later they came back for a replacement order. 10 minutes after that, everyone got their food. Cold. 

Everything was awful. We sat in the booth by the front restrooms and smelled bleach the entire time. We got our check and they had not removed the sirloin tips. Waitress said they would take care of it at the register. We went to pay and they had no one at the register. When someone did come, they couldn't "find our check" on the computer, but we had a paper copy in hand. They walked to the back and came up and said "your check has been paid" so we asked to clarify and they just shrugged their shoulders. We went to leave, thinking someone did us a favor, but our waitress quickly corrected that misinformation. 

By now, someone else was paying at the register so we lost our place, and when we got back to the register they said "they don't take cash". 

Get it together or just close for good.
Food, drinks and service was excellent. Love the new larger location. Looking forward to going back soon.

LOVED Sampan. 

Yes, there was a long wait even at 6:00 pm, but it was definitely worth it. Plus we just got drinks and small plates at the bar while we waited.

The food was fantastic, and the service was really nice. Pork Bao Buns and Cheesesteak Dumplings were phenomenal.

True Food Kitchen is my Happy Food Safe Space! I love this place from the first visit to this location!

Atmosphere. The colors, it is just colorful and warm and promotes a great mood. You just want to be in a good mood when you visit! Along with this, the staff is just so sweet, happy, knowledgeable. They are helpful and know the menu and can give some great recommendations. I appreciate their staff. Every visit they always are friendly and welcoming!

Food. First the drinks! I live for Beets! They had a cocktail called Beets by Jon! They let me change the vodka to whiskey in this cocktail and it was exceptional! I also love the Adaptogenic Tulsi Tea, their lemon to the honey combination was perfect for a nice tea. It's great on a sinus type of day. I also like the Bright Eyes Juice which has an apple, ginger, beet, pineapple, Tumeric, and carrot. It was tasty and fulfilling, not too sweet, it was just right. Honestly a great dessert option in my opinion.

As for food, as of right now my favorite is the chicken sausage pizza. Omg, the gouda and chicken sausage was phenomenal! It's a pizza you could share but honestly self-care and don't share. You need this pizza love for yourself. I have also enjoyed the Korean Noodles Bowl with shrimp. The glass noodles with the shrimp were exceptional. In addition, a great starter was the Roasted Beet and Goat Cheese flatbread. Great item for sharing especially if you about this beet love.

This is a great location for small or big groups, dates, self-care outings, friend outings and more. They honestly can accommodate it all.  Street parking is available and I honestly have never had an issue finding parking in a one mile radius.

I don't know how Amish people feel about the movie Witness, but I imagine it's something like how people in West Philly feel about the Fresh Prince of Bel-Air theme song. Regardless, I think of Witness when I go to the Dutch Eating Place, which not only embraces its Amish heritage but outdoes even the filmic Harrison Ford in an Amish hat images that swirl around in my brain from time to time. 

The only reason I'm giving the Dutch Eating Place 4 stars, as opposed to 5, is for the sake of authenticity. My gluttony has been limited to only the apple dumplings, which are phenomenal, so until I have tried a fuller selection of their breakfast and lunch options, I don't feel comfortable giving it the full 5. I do anticipate, knowing what I know of the menu and its delicious-looking pancakes, that this could be a 5-star staple, the star of Reading Terminal and the envy of other Dutch-inspired vendors in the sprawling market. 

Do me a favor: give it a try and tell me whether it's worth waking up early and grabbing breakfast one of these days. The reviews are strong, but mixed, and I'd love to hear a second opinion before setting my alarm for 6:45am one of these days.
A tasty burger, a ton of variety, great atmosphere.
Best pizza in Idaho in my opinion. The staff is very friendly and location in Meridian is very clean. The pizza is outstanding! I love that place!!

Best authentic Mexican spot in Metairie! The drinks are so good and they are overly generous with their alcohol to mixer content. The tacos are huge even on Taco Tuesdays when they do their 5 tacos for $5. They have a beautiful courtyard with hand painted murals on the walls and a Tv outside. There are also string lights that make the whole experience cozy. Service is quick and the food is always delicious, I recommend for anyone looking for great food, great atmosphere and ALOT of parking which is always a plus for me.

The food is always good, but service and noise take away from the experience. During busy nights when the patio doors are not open, it can be very difficult to hear the person speaking next to you. If you are going for a more intimate dinner, wait until outdoor seating is available in spring/summer/fall. However, if you want a loud place to meet up with a large group of people, this would be a good place.

We order from Bonu at least once a week from our office in Exton.  The food is always fresh and good.  The owner is a really nice guy that is there almost all the time who clearly takes pride in quality and ensuring it all the time.  Keep it up !

My husband is from NOLA and on a recent visit we went to this place upon my request. Although he knew all of the BEST places in the area that we could get a bite he gave it a chance and we were NOT disappointed. EVERYTHING we had was FANTASTIC! Would love to try everything on the menu eventually. A MUST try!

Really good food, I eat here often.  However, buyer beware.  I recently ordered a large pizza with sausage & also asked for extra sauce.  I was surprised when it was almost $20 dollars.  I learned that they charged me an extra of almost $3 for the extra sauce.  I did not consider a condiment to be an extra topping.  Very disappointing.
I love this place. I got great scallops and shrimp here. I like how you can take their stuff and cook it at home

If you don't know it's there, there is a good chance that you might miss it. It is a little spot in a busy shopping center. When I first started going here it was consistently fabulous every single time I went. However the past few times I went my order came out wrong and had to be sent back a few times. I don't live as close as I once did so I only go every so often now. If you are in the mood for a quick and cheap sushi meal this is a good place to try

How did I work in this area for so long and never know about Ruth's Café? This place is so cute and, moreover, is the perfect place to have breakfast or lunch with friends!

I went with a group of 11 on a Friday morning. We called ahead by a few minutes and the staff at Ruth's we're super accommodating to our group. The environment of the restaurant is so cute! There are tons of decorations and brightly colored things all over the walls, the tables all have different designs on them as do the chairs, and every mug in the restaurant is different. Talk about a perfect brunch spot!

The menu has some thing for everyone because they serve both breakfast and lunch the entire day. I had such a hard time picking what I wanted but I ended up going with a skillet with corn beef hash, scrambled eggs, and fried potatoes. The taste of everything was delicious, but I do wish that there had been more corn beef hash and a little bit less potatoes in my skillet. I know, I know less potatoes? Don't get me wrong, I love potatoes, but this is a lot of food and I wish I could taste the corn beef hash a little bit more.

The service was excellent and all of our food came out in record time, which when you consider that we were a group of 11 people is especially impressive. They had no problem splitting the check 11 ways and anything that we needed, they made sure we got. 

Long story short, go to Ruth's Café! Maybe I'll see you there because I certainly plan on returning soon!

I ordered a French Dip to go.  The wait time was short.   Got back to my office, opened up the container, and it smelled GREAT.  Immediately had co workers asking where I purchased the sandwich.  The roast beef was very flavorful, so I almost did not dip it in the au jus.. but I went ahead... and wow.. amazing flavor!.   

I can't wait to go back and try their breakfast sandwiches.

This restaurant sets itself up to be amazing. It has built in ambiance and I think they hang their hat on that and don't worry about much else. I will say that the first time I came here, I absolutely loved it. The food, the service, the atmosphere was perfect. So when my family and I decided to return for a birthday, we were all looking forward to it. We left a disappointed and settled on the fact that we wouldn't be returning any time soon. 

It started out poorly with a waiter who didn't even attempt friendliness and approached without so much as an introduction. It took about 20 minutes to even get offered a drink, let alone get them on the table. There were more slip ups by this guy (bringing the wrong beer to the table, saying it was "on him" and then charging us for it anyway) but I will move on... 

The menu is not much to talk about. Its quite limited and definitely not what is listed on their website. They now have a reasonably priced 4-course prix fixe however everyone at the table must agree to do that or a la carte, they cannot do both at the same table. This must have something to do with timing but I think in a fine dining establishment they should be able to accommodate all diners in whatever they choose. 

Our food was good, nothing knock-your-socks-off great though. I chose the one salad they had on the menu to start and duck for dinner. The duck was good and beautifully cooked but it fell in the too-sweet trap that duck often does. I understand the pairing of sweet with duck but this was just too much. 

Other good choices at the table - crab cake appetizer - 3 nicely sized crab cakes of pure crab, grilled branzino and the side order of sauteed spinach. 

Desserts were yummy and maybe the best part - beignets (our tables favorite), their take on s'mores and the house made gelato. 

All told, there are SO many other better restaurants in town - for both food and service that we won't be visiting Water Works again anytime soon. I know people who haven't been will probably want to go to check it out - maybe try it for brunch so you can see the view in the daylight and not spend as much!

I'll keep it simple. Small dive-ish restaurant in the French Quarter on Decatur St. Both husband and I came for the fried chicken. It did not disappoint and neither did the red beans and rice we got with the chicken. It was delicious, crispy, juicy, tasty and the red beans and rice were bangin!

Here's the thing, the service was sloooow and often times seemed non-existent. The servers were nice and courteous, just painfully slow. We saw at least one couple leave the restaurant because no one came to take their order, not even a drink order.
Couldn't get eye contact to even ask how to get service. Host standing at merch 5ft away while ppl waiting at host stand for help.

Soft Opening:: 9! 
Staff were friendly and professional. They knew what they were doing and what they were all assigned for. Food was good. Their 'spicy' is not at all spicy. It definitely needs more heat. 
For their price, there can be more options. However I may be speaking too soon as this is only their soft opening. They mentioned first or second week of December for their grand opening and will then have their liquor license too!
Will visit again!

Tonight was one of the best dinners out I've had in a long time! Kirsten our waitress was phenomenal! Food was on time, drinks replaced before we noticed they were low, and over all was able to be cheerful even though the restaurant was fully packed. You have to appreciate hard work when you see it and she was the star of the evening! Even the manager Morgan was sweet and very glad to hear the positive feedback of her team member. Strong team, strong service and great food! I would highly recommend smoker bones any day! Thanks for the lovely night Kirsten!
Chicken gyro! So good. Fresh ingredients and great flavor. I added a side of lavender lemonade, it was good and the lavender did not over power! Give it a shot!!

I will not eat here again; it's an unequivocal fail IMHO. Most or all of the employees are Millennials who don't know-- and don't care. I flew into Boise and was staying at a hotel near the airport. I attempted to order a delivered pizza from the Broadway location. The young male who answered the phone said in an irritated voice, "Well, delivery is at least an hour and a half out."  When I said that would be fine, he then replied, "Oh, you're calling the wrong location, you need to call the Overland store." So I did. This time I'm told by the Overland store that only the Broadway store (the one I had just talked to) delivered to hotels by the airport.  Apparently, they've not had time to complete the complex task of accurately divvying up the City into delivery zones for each store. 

Frustrated, I Googled the address; it was only 3 Miles away from my hotel so I made the misguided decision to go to the Broadway store and get a take away pizza. The place was staffed with giggling teenagers who know *nothing* about running a business , and apparently, have never heard of, or do not believe in, the germ theory of disease. I will address the infectious indiscretions in a moment. 

I attempted to order a pizza with green olives but was quickly informed by the 20-something clerk that they don't offer green olives on the menu. I resisted the urge to ask sarcastically, "Well then, why don't you remove it from your menu?" I ordered a medium thin-crust pizza with sausage and black olives. Over the next 30 minutes, I sat and watched what can charitably be called a ridiculous circus. One clerk waiting on customers while 3 or 4 employees chewed the fat or attempted to fold pizza boxes. It would have been funny if I weren't so hungry and annoyed. 

The most horrific thing I saw was that when each customer orders, the clerks touch the eating surface of the salad bowls with their nasty thumbs. They then take stacked plastic glasses and put them upside down with the lip-and-teeth-touching-rim directly on the surface of the tray or countertop where the masses put their hands, wallets, purses, car keys, paper money, coins, etc. The clerk did it over and over. When one woman quickly turned her glass right-side-up with the business end in the clean air, the giggling Millennial actually turned the cup down again, as if to scold the customer for being hygienic. Over thirty minutes I didn't see anybody wash either their hands or the grubby sticky counter. 

Despite the place being mostly empty, it took a full 30 minutes to get the pizza for take-out. Naturally, it wasn't the thin crust I ordered but I sure as hell wasn't going to wait another 30 minutes for them to make another pizza. Overall, the pizza was very mediocre with scant topping but enormous helpings of aggravation. I saw it as an overpriced disaster. I won't be back.

-----------------
UPDATE: I appreciate response from IPC and have upgraded review from one to four stars. Will try again next time in town for business. Thank you.

HORRIBLE!!! Do NOT eat here. You will get food poisoning! I went to this restaurant before my bachelorette party went back home. We came from Houston for the weekend for my bachelorette party and Sunday afternoon we decided to treat ourselves to a restaurant that supposedly was nice. We come in to the place it was EMPTY there was one person in the corner and that's it! We figured - nice it'll be great service since there's no one... WRONG!! Service was nonexistent after 50 minutes we finally get our drinks and order taken. The food took 70 minutes and it was GROSS. NOT WORTH THE WAIT!!! It's 10 of us and we ordered 12 dishes (2 to share) 10/12 dishes had horrible taste almost inedible and we found shells in plates that didn't even have any shellfish/crab! The gumbo is horrendous! We sent back 4 plates since there were extremely cold, and when they brought them back out they were cold still! The crawfish were bad!! Many of them had gone bad and had a bad smell but they though they were good enough to serve. At the end we talked to the manager who said he did heat up the plates and wasn't sure why they were cold and that crawfish was like that (like we had never rated crawfish before). Many of us couldn't even finish the plates and keep in mind this is NOT cheap. The total bill for all of us was about $540 which hurt paying so much for that horrible food none of us really enjoyed. DO NOT EAT THERE!!! Out of the 10 of us 6 of us ended up with food poisoning which was unfortunate since my wedding was only 5 days from the bachelorette party. To say the least they routines the week of my wedding and many of my bridesmaids week as well. I wish I could give it 0 stars!

Looking for a late breakfast and wound up with what we thought was our last chance. We were so wrong. Great food, made in house. My wife and I shared a side of pancakes which were crip on the outside with a perfect interior. I had a cheddar and ham omelette. The ham was cubed from a grilled  nice sized ham steak. Eggs were well prepared. There were spicy cube shaped breakfast potatoes. I asked for my English muffin to be well toasted and it was. 
Friendly service
Ill be back to check out lunch.  On the beach with a beautiful view
Recommended 
Slainte

This is my favorite Thai restaurant in Reno.  They are always so friendly and welcoming.
I usually get the mango curry.
They have the traditional fresh spring rolls but if your feeling frisky try the avo fresh spring rolls or my personal fav the mango fresh spring rolls! 
Great! Now I'm hungry  
Enjoy

Delicious food that served quickly and professionally.  Unbelievable bargain for the quality and quantity of food served.  Love the pho, spring rolls, tofu skins stuffed with ground pork/shrimp and the rice dishes.  And I'm addicted to the iced coffee - some of the best I've had.  I probably eat here at least 2x month.  Love it!

Waited 15 minutes after being seated for our drink order to be taken. We had to flag someone down. It was around 8 PM and not busy. A different waitress came over and took our food order, she wasn't pleasant or act like she was happy about being there. We got our food and my carrots and Mac and Cheese were cold as if they had been sitting out. Got one drink refill. The table beside us was complaining because the waitress never came back. Had to flag someone down to get our check! I mean come on! Is it really that hard to provide decent customer service? On the bright side, the food that was warm was delish!

I had seen this place a few times driving past on the 202 but never had a chance to stop by.  But then I saw an internet add about the place and it's hot dogs and I made a special trip for a late lunch (small parking lot).

There is a large number of menu items including various types of hot dogs, burgers, sandwiches, and sides.  But of course going to a Dog House for the first time mandates hot dogs.

I went with the New York Style Classic with spicy mustard and red spicy onion sauce.  The bun was grilled leaving a nice toasty interior to prevent sogginess from the onion sauce and increasing the flavor quotient.  The hot dog was well cooked and a bit of crispness to it.  No soggy limp dogs here.  I could not tell if the dogs were grilled or fried since it was smothered in sauce.  However, with the additions and the rich dog flavor I doubt any type of cooking would make much of a difference for the dog itself.  Mustard was fairly standard, doubt it was custom made.   The onion sauce was nice and spicy with a mild tang to it

The Chicago style dog was excellent.  The bun again was grilled to prevent sogginess which makes a huge difference.  Mustard and relish were standard fair, suspect straight from the jar/bottle.  The mix of chopped raw onions, tomatoes, and sport peppers was excellent.  Ingredients were fresh and crisp.  The onions had a nice bite to them and the tomatoes were firm.  Sport peppers imparted just the right amount of heat.

As a side note make sure you watch your bites as the sport pepper is just the right size for a big bite and then tickle the back of your throat.  Pickle slice was crisp and vinegary without overpowering the other toppings.

French fries were fairly standard and unimpressive.  With limited gastric real estate I am not sure I will waste the space for fried again.

Overall the dogs were excellent and the toppings fresh.  This is my new favorite hot dog place to eat.  Just be warned there is a small parking lot and limited seating.

Absolutely love this place. Staff friendly always! I first found out about Woods donuts when I would go to local gas station and they sold Woods donuts there, but at a higher price. (Third party pricing) So I asked the gas attendant about the donuts and she told me whom the baker is. I would definitely recommend this backery to anyone looking for good pastries and friendly, smiling faces!

I was first introduced to Chapati at a Yelp event, and I can promise I'll be back. I got to chat with one of the owners of the restaurant (his mom is the main chef, simply cooking what she grew up eating and cooking her whole life- so cool!), and he explained that the cuisine is a fusion of Pakistani & Indian flavors. While I can't attest to the restaurant itself, the food was out of the world. Spicy, fresh, delicious. 

I only wish that they were located downtown Indy as opposed to out near Eagle Creek. Maybe one day they will have a food truck?!

Shitty Food! They will make you wait so long and serve you nothing but crap. I ordered an aloha chicken burger. First, it was cold. Second the chicken was raw-completely raw. Third, the bun was not toasted but just glazed with hell lotta sweet sauce. I had to dump my this burger after 2-3 bites because I did not wanted to get sick.

With a name like Chicken and Watermelon, in what many would consider the "ghetto," you know you gotta serve some tasty wings to stay in business. And that they do! 

I found out about the place through a friend. She works at the radio station, and they did a parody about this place and had themselves and listeners posing in front of the sign and their wings. What started as a joke and potshot at the blatant racism in their business's name ended up being C&W's best marketing strategy: getting people to buy their chicken and eating it! And once you taste their chicken, the joke's on you! 

So she and many listeners became obsessed with this place and now dream about their wings day and night. With their extensive menu, it's hard to not convince your friends and family that wings are on the menu for every meal. Everything I've had here is good and their wings are known to be big and juicy. I wish they would give you more sauce since they're all so tasty and varied. I love their Boogie which is a spicy fruity (pineapple maybe) thick concoction. Their Jamaican BBQ is also spicy and savory. Both are complex sauces that leave you wanting more. 

Their fried liver is only $2 and is a huge amount of food- way better value than their fries. But you can't have wings without fries which need the cajun season and ranch dressing to complete it. And watermelon, of course, for only $1 for a huge slice.

Seafood options now (Disclaimer- I haven't tried any so can't vouch on its tastiness nor freshness.) And tons of different desserts. 

Fried corn is batterless and so good when the oil is fresh. Cakes and pies are big enough for two. They've got a Groupon right now so their cheap prices are even cheaper for a limited time....Wonder if it's because Claiborne in front of their store is a current clusterfuck. Yet another smart marketing strategy! The owners seriously know what they're doing!

Whatever the case, brave the neighborhood and the parking nightmare to grab some of the best wings in the city.  

This place is a definite take-out joint. Even though they've tried with the interior, the few times I've attempted to eat in there, I've been panhandled and had a general sense of unease. Don't remember the condition of the bathrooms. Star taken off for not hiring someone to take care of their dine-in patrons. The girl behind the glass is already handling the phone and all orders coming in. They need a host/server which would deter non-customers from going in. Not cool.

So call ahead if you can. It will save you precious minutes between you and your wings. 

Note: for anyone interested in the news behind the "joke," the story can be found here: http://www.allaccess.com/net-news/archive/story/132580/wrno-parody-jingle-turns-into-real-ad-client

Sad that you can't see the music video anymore. The commercial was pretty funny and a true classic for John Osterlind and the Assclowns. Top 5 performances.
Perfect little place for when you get the knashies. I especially like the awesome italian sodas. Great flavors and the service is nice.

Wow, let me just say I've never been to a restaurant where the food was so good but the service was the worst and most uncomfortable things I've ever experienced. Our waitress had no clue what she was doing. We ordered drinks first and I order a Riesling. When she came back with it I had a Cab. We put in an appetizer and it didn't come out u til after our food had already come! Never once asked to come anything. Server was awkward and made the whole experience miserable.

On that sunny Philadelphia late morning, it seemed that everyone in the city was shrugging off home confinement to be on the streets, outside.  That meant that our party of 5 had to wait quite some time to get a table at Cafe la Maude - but less than the 1hr we were told we'd have to wait. The Cafe was very busy and for a good reason.  First outdoor seating remains in short supplies in Philly and suburbs (unfortunately), and second, because the food was as good as the atmosphere.  We ordered and our food came promptly - a surprise.  We ordered the Mediterranean platter, the Po' Boy, the Petit Steak, the Brisket and the Saumon Fume.  The food was very good but sometimes too salty especially our fried cauliflower side.

My boyfriend found this place on Facebook. We are always wanting to try new places so we decided to come here. 

We did not know what to try, so the waitress assisted with some recommendations. To drink I had a Vivita. It was the perfect portions of alcohol not too strong not too sweet. Great presentation. He had a michelada. Not many places know how to make them, but she did a wonderful job. 

To eat he had the Puerco guisado with yuca guisada and white rice. The pork was very tender and melted in your mouth. The yuca with viva sauce was delicious. I had shrimp with viva sauce and white rice with fried yuca. Shrimp had great flavor not too salty or unflavored. 

Overall the experience was great it's a family owned restaurant part Colombian part Dominican. Gives a great feel of the Caribbean. Definitely will come again.

Just had breakfast and it was wonderful. Some of the best customer service I've ever had in my life. The customer definitely comes first here and the food exceeded my expectations in every aspect. I definitely recommend this restaurant to everyone looking for a good breakfast meal. Brittany treated us like family.

excellent service! we made reservations for the outdoor seating and it was gorgeous out! the fire pit & lighting outside were amazing.
I got the New York strip steak... VERY salty. the atmosphere was great but very overpriced.

If I could give this place 3.5 stars, I would...but it wasn't deserving of the 4stars. I we really wanted to like this place...and maybe under other circumstances, we would. It was a Sunday @1130 and although crowded, there were multiple tables available. Although our waiter was helpful and friendly, the timeliness to receive water, then drinks, then food was a little slow. 
She got a salad with chicken and the 2 for 1 Bellini. She enjoyed all of it and said cumulatively it was a solid 4.25 out of 5 stars. 
I had the chicken and waffles with a chocolate milkshake. The waffles were average...there just wasn't anything special about them. The chicken was a solid B/B- . It wasn't outstanding, but wasn't bad.  Even the milkshake was a solid B/B- The taste was good, not great, not bad. She felt it was not as thick as she would like...I thought it was fine (no jokes please). 

Like I said, we wanted to like this place...fun potential vibe... We will give it another shot at some point.

Location location location. If you are lucky enough to find a parking spot anywhere near downtown Kirkwood on a nice evening, sitting outside at their bar is pleasant. Oh, a few quirks. We met friends there who already ordered drinks and apps. We waited 30 minutes for waiter, never came, went to the bar to order. Also, although main menu and bar menu were on the table, we were informed we could only order from bar menu from this side of the outside section. Hmmm, so they want to make less money? Kitchen too small? We ordered the pretzel bites, which were really good, and laughed that we should call in for a to go pizza and bring it to our table. So our table ended up with a few drinks, two apps, and we left to give our money to another venue that wanted to let us order. Wait for a dinner table on the weekend literally hours ...

We came back here after a long break. I have been so busy trying out so many new places and I wanted some comfort food so I came back to Mi Quang again. I didn't think it was possible but it taste even better than before. If you're tired of the same old Vietnamese food like pho or rice then come try this.

Mi quang is central Vietnamese noodle dish with many complex flavor. The dish is composed of shrimps and pork ribs that's been marinated and cooked separately before coming together in the bowl. It also comes with quail eggs and Vietnamese ham. The noodles are flat and very soft yet retains elasticity and does not fall apart. 

Another highlight here is their bun cha Ha Noi, which is a northern dish. It is lemon grass pork and pork patty grilled and is marinated in sweet sweet sauce with scallion oil and daikon radish before coming out to be served with a side of vermicelli noodles and vegetables. The grilled pork has an amazing charred flavor to it. The patty has the texture of a tender meatball and is packed with lemongrass flavor in every bite. If you are here, make sure you get these 2 items first before anything else, make it a priority, they are the best in the east coast!!

I love me some Papa John's! Love that they are embracing social media and trying to create a friendly community environment. I look forward to engaging in the dialogue on FB and ordering lots of pizzas!

I am so happy that I found this little spot hidden a couple of blocks off of Mass Ave.  I had heard of Kaffeine but I just happened to be driving down a side street right by it.  I knew I had to return! 

The inside is so cozy.  They've done a great job with the interior.  Their coffee selection is simple by design.  Personally, I love my large iced drinks and there wasn't any of that.  I went with the Spanish Latte, iced, and loved it!  It was only a 12 oz drink, but it was so tasty.  I don't know if I would go out of my way to return, as there are so many options around the city, but I am so glad I stopped here. I recommend it!
Simply the best. I will dream of the The bene St Charles forever and ever and everrrrrrrrrrr

Artisan-Resto cafe does a good job of giving a bit of a contemporary twist to its general rustic prairie feel.  Although the decor is largely of a classical style, it isn't jarring or dated per se in its feel.  The omelettes, fruit, and other food items are generally of a high quality, with the eggs and potatoes sourced from local farmers in Alberta.  Their fruit is, understandably, imported from the US, but since Alberta has a much colder climate than California (where a lot of the fruit in North America is grown), it's to be expected.

The staff are also quite nice, and they add to the overall vibe of the place.  They are also attentive and helpful with food recommendations.  Overall, I would return whenever I feel like having a large breakfast in Edmonton.

Such a delicious breakfast place! The drinks took the cake for me! The cocktails and mimosas set the tone for a fantastic brunch. The crab cake and omelet I ordered was just okay, nothing spectacular, but the powdered donuts were perfectly delicious!

I'd probably have given Rick's 3 stars if I had gone in the winter but the view alone gets a star.  We ate out on the deck at Ricks overlooking the water.  It was such a nice day and the only thing that could have made it better would have been an ice cold beer...but we were on the clock so we had to do without.  

The lunch menu at Rick's is a great deal.  Everyone received a mass quantity of food on their plate.  I ordered the fish and chips which were good (though not better than Broad Ripple Brewpub's which I still think have the best fish and chips).  A friend of mine ordered the chicken salad quesadilla and loved it.  I might have to try that next time I go.   

We decided to split the mudd pie for dessert and even split between 3 people, we each had a huge amount.  It was delicious and reason enough to go back.  

I wish that Ricks was a little closer so that it could be a lunch place we opted for more often.  But I suppose those are the sacrifices you make to get a great view for your restaurant.

In my honest opinion, some of the worst "food" I've ever suffered in my life! I should have gone with my gut instinct and the fact that there were NO other customers in this place!I took 3 bites and left the rest.In the 3 bites of spaghetti I found a large piece of meat-gristle, very disgusting! The sauce wasn't just flavorless or "off-flavor" it actually had a BAD taste to it!Actually repulsive!I saw the "cook" making this mess in a fry pan (First Red Flag), meaning the sauce doesn't simmer for a time in the pot, the way sauce should.I saw the owner pop something in the microwave oven (Second Red Flag) as he was making this obscenity and then dump whatever into the fry pan, the "gristle-meat" perhaps?I took one bite of the meatball - pure mushy disgust!
I asked the owner if there had been a change in ownership or management in the last year or so (since I had last eaten here) and he defensively said "Why you askin'?", like maybe he was tired of hearing this question.After more attitude he admitted he took over the restaurant about a year ago, he asked me if it's better or worse. I told him it was bad, I couldn't eat it. In a desperate display of self-embarrassing bravado he told me "My sauce is twice as good as anything Max (the previous owner) ever made!!!" 
Yeh, well, all ZERO of your customers and my own taste tells me otherwise!I spent $11.00, took 3 bites (all I could stand), and the owner didn't offer a refund or another dish, he said "I can't do anything about it!"
Well, I can do something about it, drive right by and go to CiCi's next door, they have better food for half the price.
I left and went right to a McDonalds for a couple burgers- #1) Because I was still hungry, #2) To try and get the disgusting after-taste out of my mouth.
Worst place I've ever seen.

Follow this link to see Health Dept. Violations.

http://www.city-data.com/fl-restaurants/PIZZERIA-BELLA-NAPOLI.html

Rules For Restaurants-

http://www.flickr.com/photos/30759108@N08/7130324763/in/photostream

Took 2 tours with drench quarter phantoms during our visit to New Orleans: ghosts and vampires (tour guide = Ducky) and St  Louis One Cemetery (tour guide = Sam).  Ghosts with Ducky was a great and entertaining tour. We learned a lot, and thought Ducky has a great personality for a tour guide. the St Louis One cemetery tour was a great way to see so much history, and Sam clearly knows a lot. Just wish he didn't complain incessantly about Nicholas Cage. It was such a negative distraction, and keep putting the attention back on himself, and not the cemetery's great history.
1st time and it was awesome!  Had the best prime rib I've ever tasted.  Will be going back when we visit Boise next time.  Service was equally of the highest quality.  Highly recommend

It was late and I came here for some food. I had their Southwest Chicken Tikka and it was great.  Savory and on point.  Chicken was not dry and the sauce had more flavor than just tomatoes, which is an issue at some places.  What makes it Southwest is the grilled corn and cilantro added to the dish, and it works!  It was an excellent idea and executed well.  The sweetness of the grilled corn only added more flavor to the dish. 

It was given in a little to-go tray as only the front of the restaurant was open this late.

1st visit (because my intended restaurants were closed on Mondays). South of Gandy in a strip mall on the east side of SDM. I ate at 3 pm ("dinner" menu) last Monday. I was the only customer for a while. 
The cafe is dark inside and uninspiring. 3 TVs were showing sports/no volume (I'm not a fan of suchlike). A long bar, well stocked. Service was matter-of-fact.
App: Tom Yum Chicken soup - very tasty but much too salty. Surprisingly large bowl for $ charged by other cafes for a cup. Entree: Garlic with chicken - very good, large portion (2 meals). Based on this trip, I'll go back.

This is the best Korean restaurant in the Tampa Bay Area. The kimchi is fresh, plentiful and authentic (I lived in Korea for a year), the staff is friendly and kind, the pork bulgogi tastes just spicy enough and is consistently perfectly cooked, while the beef and kimchi pot stickers are the perfect first course as they are the perfect balance of crispy outside with a fresh inside. 

I've been here 10 or so times and it never disappoints.

The hostess and my server was extremely attentive and met all my needs. The menu was simple but seemed to have at least 1 thing for everyone. What I was surprised about was the lack of steak cuts on the menu for a restaurant called The Steakhouse.

Why only 4 stars? 
1) Bread presentation; if I'm planning to spend $75-100 for 1 meal I expect something better looking and better tasting than a brown and serve roll. I was very shocked this was their choice for the first food item to be on the table. It came in a very adorable cast iron dish that clearly was used for nothing more than serving.
2) short wine list; also did not seem to embrace more modern wine trends 
3) the main reason I'm writing this review is Restaurant Managment. The gentleman walking around checking with guests to ask about their meal was extremely selective in who he spoke to and put on an heir of arrogance. I watched as he chose who he spoke to and who he simply smiled and walked by without saying a word. He never once spoke to me or walked by my table. Every customer is important and should be treated the same.

The ribs and the brisket were absolutely wonderful. I travel all over the country for work and always love to try BBQ at different places. This has to be some of the best dry rub ribs I have had in years! The staff was polite as well

Fun time. This year it seems as though everything was spaced better which maybe my imagination but it did not seem as wall to wall as last year even though it was crowded. The ice skating rink was packed even though it was a bit warm and the "ice" was melting away. I love that that they added the racelette shed and it looks like a couple more German food vendors. The schnitzel and red cabbage dish looked wonderful although finding a place to eat is difficult.  Sorry but I really question the Waking Waffle as being German.  
I love that that they have music which the Chicago Christkindlmarkt has.
They also have heaters and a nice fire pit area. 
The pyramid and the variety of mulled wines and beers was a great addition.  My only complaint was pricing. For about $8 in Chicago, I can get a nice cup with mulled wine in it. Here the mulled wine was $7 or $8 and it was in a paper cup. If you wanted the Christkindlmarkt cup it was $10 and you didn't even get the mulled wine it!

Tried this place during Endymion parade day! We needed to fuel up and got it to go to eat while camping out for Endymion. I got the grilled chicken ceaser salad and my fiancé got the Cochon de lait poboy with a side of fries. They were both very good. I feel as if we were over charged a bit. The poboy alone was 14$ that didn't include the fries. Other than that everything was good. Next time we will eat inside.

Another late review but definitely well deserved. I was taken to this place on the night of my birthday, Thanksgiving eve. All I can say is this is probably  the best meal I have had in a formal restaurant in Tucson since I moved here! The food was absolutely outstanding, kind of a new twist on traditional Mexican dishes. I really loved the  ambiance , interior and design. And the service was excellent! From the time we arrived to the time we left there was never one minute that we didn't have someone checking on us, refilling our drinks or just making sure we were enjoying themselves. Definitely a must for my Tucson foodie crew!
The service is horrible, delivery time can go over two hours, but the pizza is unique and pretty good.

I've never had chicken "nuggets" for chicken Parmesan and then the server tried to convince us that a muffuletta sandwich comes on this soft bun
 I tried to explain that it comes on a more dense bread.
Mahi Mahi tacos, cheeseburger, tomato grilled cheese, and shrimp sandwich were all excellent. Price is very fair for the amount of food. Will be coming back.

Cute little restaurant in Peddler's Village. Stopped in for breakfast and everyone left happy and stuffed.

Breakfast sandwich with eggs, smoked bacon, avocado, and cheese on a brioche bun was great, the fried chicken special sandwich was awesome (although the piece of chicken was a little too big), the breakfast burrito was simple but good and we also had the dollar pancakes and they were also tasty!

It's a little country style restaurant in one room and the other side of the restaurant you can order food at the counter. 

The service was also very nice, attentive and friendly.

Great little spot to stop in for breakfast in Peddler's.

It was my first night in Indy and a few colleagues and I not-knowingly stumbled into what turns out to be one of the most famous restaurants in town. The dinner experience had fairly mixed results (3.5 stars) and so a pros and cons list can do this justice.

Pros: Amazing Service - really friendly and welcoming waiter who was attentive and polite, Proper setting for drinks and socializing, Nice crispy sear on steak, Shrimps had great texture 

Cons: Taste... on just about everything... Shrimp Cocktail was just a bit too loaded with horseradish. Steak was not seasoned well so for a 12 oz strip, it can get pretty thick and without much flavor, even with Medium Rare it gets rubbery rather quickly. Also, there was a giant strip of tendon running down the middle of my cut which added to the chew. Sides were average.

Overall, there is a lot of things going for this establishment and I can see how people really like it but after my experience, I'm pretty sure I won't be go back. With that being said, maybe your culinary experience will be different so its worth a try.

They advertise pickup and delivery. I call and ask if I can place an order for pickup. The girl on the other end of the phone tells me to hold. I wait for almost 10 minutes. Finally, the girl picks up and says "We're extremely busy, there is no one here who can take your order". I felt like asking her if she didn't know how to read and write. Needless to say, I'll never give this place my business again.

Great pub, great food, bottled beers can be pricey but a great selection. This is probably more of a restaurant than a bar, but it's good for either. The carpets seem to roll up at about midnight, so it's not a late-late place. Staff is great.  Televisions are permanently set to sports channels.

Stoney was somehow in the music industry in Britain, so the bar is covered with photos of him and rock stars. Music is pure old Brit from his iPod. This is the only place in the world I've been to actually get into difference of opinions on the origins of bands like Foghat and Montrose (I was the one who was wrong). This place would be perfect with the addition of a jukebox (and if my favorite Frambois wasn't $13 a bottle - I've gotten it for less in NYC). 

Go on Saturday night for the Yorkshire pudding (making this at home is a difficult proposition in a typical kitchen), either alone, with roast beef, or as toad-in-a-hole (yum). There are sometimes leftover Yorkshires on Sunday. They have great desert puddings. Fish'n'chips is great, but bangers and mash is better.  The marvelous bartenders have been fantastic in working with me when I wanted a drink with more than two ingredients, but save a martini cocktails are not the forte here. 

Probably leave the kids at home. There is a kids' menu, but I don't think I've ever seen children there, it may just be for folks with the munchies. Kids might be fine at the early end of the dinner hour, but in my opinion it becomes less child-friendly around 8. 

I've never been thrilled with the bands that come in, but it brings those who are not regulars to the bar and keeps it in business, so it's a necessary evil. There are lots of holiday special events and charity fundraisers. 

Make sure you park behind the bar, not behind the hair salon next door (owned by Stoney's ex-wife who is grinding an ax by towing cars even when her business is not open).

It's a very energetic feel coming into the restaurant. Bright colors and pretty cool music. I went for brunch and the unlimited drinks were awesome. Sparkling Rose and mimosas, pick your poison. Food was great, portions are small. Not to worry, it's still filling
the best ...unique taste...fresh.  gluten. free..reasonable. $$  be specific....double check. If take out items

Waiting time and the attitude in restaurent is very bad. They did not even apologies for the wait time they made us to. We waited roughly 40mins just for a single biriyani pickup. However the taste be , i would not sugggest my friends there to try.

Came in on a Tuesday afternoon.
Food was good .
Service was prompt .
I will be back at this location .

This is a different beast for those who have visited the Fermentaria. Both locations are unique in many ways. The original brewery has more character whereas the Fermentaria has the feeling of mass production and each location brews different beers, odd but true. The brewers at the original location focus more on Saisons, and the Fermentaria tends to reproduce beers that have already been made. 

After being both locations I don't have a favorite. I like them both equally and in their own way.

We stopped in here for a quick lunch before checking on a boat we were looking to buy. I order the trifecta burger and must admit it was one of the best tasting burgers I have ever had. My bro of over 30 years ordered the crab dip and the fish tacos and they were stellar as well. Our waiter was fantastic as well. I believe he said he had worked there like 20 plus years. Overall excellent experience. BTW we finished with the key line and it rocked as well!

Service was great! Food was ok. The Mac and cheese was made with a slice of American singles....I think they should try a little harder than that. It is definitely over priced. The lighting is terrible, extremely bright. It also smells like partical board.

I came here for dinner with my fiancé last Friday. It is a small place with about 20 closely positioned tables. It was very packed.  We had reservations for 7:15 pm. Overall, the food was very good. The service had some high and some lows.  We were quickly seated at a table in the back. There were two tables for two in the rear near the bathroom. There was a table close to the window and a table close to the walking aisle, just inches from the server station. The tables were practically connected. The table near the window was occupied, but the couple left a few minutes after we seated at the table close to the server station.  One of the servers came up to us and said that we're going to want to move to the table closest to the window because it's more comfortable. I really appreciated that gesture. 

However, the service was less impressive from that point. The gentlemen who seated us was not our main server. The main server did not immediately bring water to the table. We she first approached the table, she abruptly asked if we were ready to order. She did not introduce herself.  There was absolutely no greeting. It looked like she just escaped a tornado. She was flustered. I will say though that once we placed our order, everything came pretty quickly. 

We ordered the meatballs and tomato mozzarella appetizers, and a pizza with sausage and roasted peppers. The food was mostly very good. The meatballs and sauce were delicious. The order came with three medium-to-small meatballs.  I think four would be a better number to split between two, but I guess the portion was fine. It came with three pieces of bread, which was essentially delicious pizza dough. The tomato and mozzarella appetizer was lacking. It also didn't look very appetizing. They may have been going for the rustic look but the appetizer just looked sloppy.  

The pizza was definitely the star of the show. We got the marinara sauce, which was a cooked tomato sauce. They had a Margherita style sauce as well (which was more like the traditional uncooked pizza sauce), but we wanted to try to cooked marina sauce. It was very tasty. The pizza dough is one of the best in Philly. I only wish they cooked the pie a little longer to give it more of a crunch. 

Overall, I recommend this place. The pizza is very good. It is also a neat spot right on Spring Garden.

Haven't been to Reading Terminal in years, thought I'd stop in for lunch. Started with the fresh made iced tea. Then got one of my all time favorites, Snapper soup. It was delicious, full of flavor and lots of Snapper meat. Also they had those huge Oyster crackers I love. Waitress was nice enough, the place was packed though so I can't complain. Talked to the small but very informative manager Dave, he recommended  I try the Oyster Sliders. Perfectly fried, great sauce and the oysters were huge. I liked it a lot and I left stuffed. Definitely a place I need to stop at more often for lunch, I'll have to try some of the raw oysters next time. I can see why this place is a Reading Terminal staple, fresh delicious seafood and relatively inexpensive considering I went next store and payed $5 for an ice cream cone at Bassetts afterwards. Make sure to give this place a try if you're every in the Market!

The Cuban with salami was mediocre. From what I gather, traditionally a Cuban does not have salami, but I like them both ways. Actually, I probably like a Cuban better with the salami. I think it just makes for a more full tasting sandwich.  Although, sometimes simplicity is best; I'm torn.  It was okay, not the best Cuban I've ever had, but not the worst either.

Spicy chicken sandwich not that great.  Breading fell off, and just didn't taste that good (like it was frozen).  The lunch sandwiches come with your choice of "kettle" chips, coleslaw, or potato salad. We choose the kettle chips, and french fries for an upcharge, but still had to pick one of the three sides I didn't want. So, I choose coleslaw.  

The coleslaw I didn't want was not good. It was basically white cabbage in a water down mayonnaise dressing, but I was forced to choose one.  I don't really like potato salad and chips are never a good idea at a restaurant (maybe one exception).  My wife wanted the chips, and I'm pretty sure they opened one of those tiny individual bags, and put it on the plate with the chicken sandwich.  My fries were good!  I'm glad I ordered those, even for the upcharge.

The service was fast and friendly, and the place is pretty clean. Also it's located in a great place to go walk around after having lunch or dinner.

Just one more thing about the chips. For the money I pay at a restaurant, I want something cooked, not opened. I can get a bag of chips at any grocery store, convenience store, or gas station on any block in any part of town.

Our party of ten was easily accommodate by a reservation. Food was delicious and well-priced. Had a bit of difficulty getting our drinks refilled but it was fairly busy. Very friendly staff. Appreciated the offer of half size orders for some entrees.

One of my favorite spots in nashville, not because the food is magical or authentic but because it's fast good cheap food. 

Called Satay by the Vandy students, this local Thai place is definitely a gathering place and a very reliable food source. This was our favorite spot to go after tailgating all morning/afternoon and just wanting some food that hits the spot. You don't come here for the vibes, but for the quick cheap filling Thai food. We would come at least once a month. It's quite a small store, but the tables turn over pretty quickly so by the time you order and actually get your food, a table will open up. It does get packed on Friday nights and the weekend so be prepared to wait. The line sometimes goes out the door. 

I cannot say good enough things about this place!!

We live right around the corner, and iMunch has become a staple on Saturday and Sunday Mornings. Great coffee, hot and iced, and great breakfast sandwiches, and also occasionally we stop by for lunch, which has also been great. The only down fall is that it's a little pricey, however, we clearly still frequent so this is not a deal breaker. Just FYI, $5 min for credit card chargers, but they have let me slide at $4.50. 

You can also call ahead which I recommend, there can be a longer wait depending on time of day.

I have to give Tony's only 2 stars. The soups are very good, but I prefer Pizza Amore for pizza. We tried the place a few times and one of my issues is when ordering a dinner, whether there or take-out, the you don't get any side salad, and the rolls they give you are very tough. My husband didn't like the hoagies either, the meat was sliced too thick. I'll only stop back for soup, but that's about it.
Wonderful place - waiter and owner were fantastic.  Food was good but the bread pudding was disappointing.

This place takes farm to table to a whole different level. You can see the vegetables they use right outside their location. If you haven't been there before please let the host(ess) know, it is a little confusing. I ordered the Zucchini Salad and Red Lentil soup. The best part of the ordering experience is that they asked if they had any food allergies (never before had a restaurant been so accommodating). In the menu, they also list Gluten Free, Vegetarian, Vegan options which is great. The food was amazing, I felt healthier just looking at it. Can't wait to keep going back and try their menu throughout the seasons (I heard it changes with the seasons). If you want an accommodating diet, sustainable, wholesome, and healthy option, this is definitely the place to check out!

What is a hamburger? Is it a concoction of exotic meats, greens, artisan breads, and cheese from a faraway place?  NO!  I'm a bit tired of the continued re-inventing of a common man's/woman's meal. When I get salty about fancy burgers I go to Buds. Chargrilled meat, grated cheddar cheese, and secret sauce on a bun. Friendly service if you're friendly and sufficient enough to get food inside your stomach. It's better to go when it's busy because the charcoal will be really hot but it's still good when it's slow. One of my favs.

Excellent food and service. We have been twice and loved everything. I have had their ribeye, scallops, tuna crudo, salad and a pasta dish. Can't wait to go back and try more. Nice outside patio If the weather is nice.
Love this place! I have been trying to stay away from bread, so I haven't been going much. Favorites: pastrami reuben, the french dip and the pickles!. I am going to have to go soon for a cheat day.

Great place, everything I've tried is very good. The almond croissant is my go-to here as many others have mentioned. They have a few different coffees available from light to dark roast and they are good also.

I don't even know how to explain how beautiful inside was ... loved the piano that was on top of the bar .. First we had sushi as an Appetizer and was very surprised how good it was ... me and my bf loves sushi but didn't expected to be that good especially from a steakhouse but was amazing.. our main we wanted porterhouses steak but they ran out that night, so we shared cowboy steak.. omg !!! Portion was big enough to share and the meat was melting in our mouth ... sides were Mac and Cheese which was recommended and it was great !! Loved it ... also mashed potatoes was good too !!! We also had Goo Goo Cluster Icecream cake and it was sooooo goooood !!!! People there was so sweet, friendly, helpful, and professional... especially our server Logan was so amazingly helpful ... I really loved everything about the this place!!! Definitely would go back when we go visit Nashville again ...

Many brews and a friendly crowd.

Located inside the Eldorado and hoppin' at night and on the weekends.

Nice spot...check it out.
Still fantastic!! They are as good as ever. Remodeled interior is beautiful. Sandwich is delicious.

This place is great but can be really crowded, super loud and if you do the tasting menu, you're dining experience can be super rushed. I love the food. I've had dinner here twice, both times getting the tasting menu. Some highlights were the Chilean sea bass, wagyu beef & crab wonton tacos. But, when you get the tasting menu, the food comes out one after the other and $100 + later, you're back out the door in under and hour. If I'm going to pay that kind of money for dinner, I like to take my time and have a couple drinks too.
Delicious pork tacos , quesadillas, and the chicken burrito was awesome. Great customer service , very friendly

Cafe Ponte is by far my favorite restaurant in the Bay area.  It is one of the few restaurants that consistently offers superb food and service.   My husband and I have had the opportunity to try some of the highest regarded restaurants in the area, and we both agree that Cafe Ponte surpasses them all due to their high quality unique gourmet offerings and outstanding service. Additionally, surprisingly, they are reasonably priced and we have yet to leave hungry (We have left hungry at a quite a few places where they believe minuscule portions equals gourmet).  Cafe Ponte would definitely make it in NYC.
Great local takeout with fair prices and quality dishes.  Noodles and curries both pass the mark.  Recommend takeout over eating in.

Fabulous  Sangria! Great chips and very flavorful salsa! My chimichanga was excellent! The service was very quick and pleasant. This location has been several different concepts - all ok but nothing great. This is really good Tex mex - I hope they make it! Based on my experience- they should!
This place has the best po'boys!  Service is great and the food is mouth-watering delicious.

Cool place! They could up their craft coffee game a little, but it's still a cool spot and the coffee IS good.
Reminds me of a spot in the Hollywood hills oddly. Laid back..wood paneling...kinda Californiaish.

I want to love this place more, but my wife and I just seem to prefer the other local breweries.  When we make the comparisons, we feel the taste of the beers are on equal footing but found the other places had friendlier staff and more of a comforting atmosphere.  The indoor space is very big, almost too big as it seemed to take away from the friendliness and make it more cold.  The staff at the bar just did not seem overly interested in talking about the beers that they were serving as I get the from the other local places.  I like when the staff show pride in the beers and really talk them up.  Again, decent beers, just wish there was a bit more to the place.

For a first time, Sisters was AMAZING!  The decor and the lighting really set the mood, and everyone from the door staff to the bartenders to the coat check attendant were very friendly.  They do have a $5 cover, but it does end up being worth it.  I love that they don't make you pay extra to go on the dance floor.  The DJ happened to be spinning boy band/girl group music which made the experience all the more fun, and what's more, I enjoyed a custom mixed cocktail, ran into a few friends, and danced like I'd never danced before.  I will FOR SURE be back for one of their parties, hopefully their upcoming 90's party!

One of my favorite restaurants in the city. My go to place for celebrations, to take out of towners and to grab a late night drink. Love their salads, cocktails and small plate options. Service is always great. I am not a huge cocktail person but never miss ordering their french farmer (better than anywhere in the city).

Returned for 2nd visit already! Updated with photos and got to see our wonderful, fave server Liz! 

Stopped here after a long day of shopping and running errands. I was exhausted and starving, so I opened up Yelp to find something close by and Berlins Doener was literally walking distance from me. I looked at their Yelp
Listing and visited their web site and thought it was a great choice. I apologize for my lack of photos! My exhaustion combined with hunger took over and I neglected to take any. I will certainly update on my next visit! 


Driving up 5 minutes after finding it on Yelp, my first response was a bit hesitant because it's a non descriptive building in a strip mall. I felt a little worried about the authenticity of the German food I was hoping to eat. Well, thankfully, I was wrong! Don't let the storefront fool you, once you walk in there's a selection of German music playing and a nice, casual feel to the place. 

We were seated immediately and served our drinks quickly. The staff were great and answered all of questions about the menu since this was our first visit. Our server, Liz, was incredibly friendly as were all of the staff we encountered. 

As you know if you have read some of my reviews, I'm always trying to keep a Keto friendly diet, so both my boyfriend and I went with Doener salads (only $8 each). They were huge and plenty to eat. My boyfriend added feta cheese ($1) and extra meat ($1!) The $1 up charge for each is worth it if you are hungry because his salad was packed with Doener and a nice helping of Feta. I was not at all disappointed with my salad and I didn't add the extras. I had plenty. We loved the salads and had some left to take with us. 

I also ordered a bowl of Goulash Suppe ($6). I absolutely love Goulash and I wasn't disappointed. While it isn't completely Keto friendly having potatoes, it was delicious! I ate a few potatoes but had plenty even leaving most potatoes in the bowl. If you aren't avoiding carbs, please eat them! The only advice I might have is to add an option for the heat level. While this was delicious and I could definitely taste the heat from the paprika, I would have preferred it just a bit spicier. I certainly understand the owners choice not going too spicy since some folks like no heat or simply can't eat spicy foods. My boyfriend doesn't like anything too spicy and was very pleased with just a little heat. I will definitely order it again! 

We also decided to share a sausage. I think it might be a requirement at a German restaurant, right?! We actually decided to add it after starting our meal because there is a large crock of the restaurant's homemade mustard sitting on each table. That mustard kept calling to me! I could hear it gently singing my name through the crock, tempting me to eat it! Along with a sausage! I know what some of you are thinking and you should just stop... 

We couldn't decide which sausage to add. The server explained that the difference between Bratwurst and Knackwurst is that the latter is smoked, and the third choice Käse Krainer has jalapeño and cheese added to the sausage. I was feeling the Krainer but since my boyfriend is always skeptical of food being too spicy, we went with the Knackwurst since we both love smoked foods. It came out a few minutes later on a bed of sauerkraut. Yummy!!! It was delicious with the homemade mustard! We decided on our next visit to get more of the sausage and I'm looking forward to trying the Käse Krainer! You can add a sausage to any meal for just $3.50. 

They also offer several other traditional German dishes and promote themselves as being German street food. While we didn't partake that night, they have an entire menu of German beer selections and wine as well. 

The food prices are incredibly reasonable! Our entire meal including an iced tea each was around $30 before a tip. The service was fast, the food was yummy, the restaurant was immaculate (including the ladies restroom), and the staff was very friendly! Everyone including the cooks said warm goodbyes as we were leaving. I told our server how much we enjoyed our meal and she said she would tell the owners. I got the impression that this is a small, local restaurant with very involved owners. I always enjoy supporting local businesses. We will definitely be back when we are in the St. Pete area!

i ve tried a lot of mysore masala dosa at different restaurants...THIS place has the best mysore masala dosa i have ever tried. even the crepe part of it near the ends had a masala taste (which i rarely find at other restaurants)...sambhar was above average...

their samosa was spicy and big.

I would go back

We have been visiting economically priced Buffets in Las Vegas and Reno this week. The Buffet, in the Eldorado, was the best by far. The salad bar had very fresh fruits and vegetables! The meat station had a large variety of high quality cuts of meats. The pork chops were extremely moist and flavorful. The brisket and BBQ pork ribs rival any BBQ in TN and states to the west. If you like salads, meat, with all of the fix'n then this the place for you. All for the low price of $20 on Sunday nights.

Cozy dark atmosphere with a modern twist, I was with girlfriends but I would recommend for a date night. We really enjoyed our meals and had great service. The Angel Bacon Burger didn't blow my mind, it was just okay. I tried all my girls friend meals and everything was very good, we also enjoyed the caprese bruschetta.

I live in the neighborhood and was very excited for this diner to open. I've been there 3 times now each time giving this restaurant a chance but I don't think I'll be back again. This place had a lot of potential but the service is slow and the food is not good. I got a buffalo chicken cheesesteak. It came out cold and missing ingredients.
