The decor is that of an older steakhouse.  I would recommend it.  Very nice dinner!

I wanted to try this place after a rave review from a good friend and he didn't even mention that this place is vegetarian/vegan. I went for the first time with another good friend - a hardcore carnivore. 

We ordered 3  items between us and each plate was both brilliantly presented and absolutely delicious. While I normally eat a vegetarian/vegan diet, I was not only satisfied, but absolutely amazed at the attention to flavor and texture that these dishes provided. Many vegetarian restaurants tend to be bland and boring. Not the case here! My friend said that the meal opened his mind to the possibility of 'good vegetarian food'. He didn't miss not having meat/dairy one bit. We both agreed that the pulled mushroom sandwich was dynamite!

We did go a bit overboard with our ordering as each plate was a good portion and we also got beers and deserts. While this meal was a bit spendy at around $90. I think even a hungry couple could get away for under $50 after tax/tip.

The service was very friendly and helpful. The atmosphere on the patio was also very nice.

No more smoking inside!!!! YEAH!!!!
We can now have dinner & drinks without coughing up a lung or washing our clothes when we get home!!
LOVE the Shrimp Appetizer!!!!! Wings are good, especially the trashed wings.  The burger with soft cheddar is amazing!!!!
Service can be a bit slow at times & some staff should watch their cell phone usage & texting & focus on attentiveness to customers. More attentive & prompt service = happy customers & bigger tips!!!

But overall, still love this place! Good food, nice bar, big patio, HH specials.

Went for a cruise on bike this past Saturday and as we were making our way toward Broadripple via 62nd we decided to grab an appetizer at Taverna (We both had never been ). We were there early afternoon and they still had their lunch menu but we were able to order off their "bar bites" menu, which starts around 2:30pm-3pm (ish) We ordered the pulled steak sliders and avocado corn salsa queso with chips. And of course I paired the queso with a margarita (el jimador tequila was on special and this margarita was SO GOOT!) best margarita I've had from an Italian restaurant :) When we were perusing the menu earlier we noticed they also have a brunch menu on Sundays (you may need to call and double check though as this was Mother's Day weekend and they could have just been serving brunch for this occasion but EVERYTHING on the menu sounded so tasty, AND they accept reservations AND you can make them online via Open Table. I love technology that makes everything so durn convenient!!! This restaurant has been around for a year or so and based on the lack of guests when we went (ie, we were the only ones there) it seems that not many have discovered this little gem yet... Slightly happy and sad at this realization. Super happy because I'm selfish and want good food to myself but still sad because this restaurant has not yet been recognized for their unique and fabulous dishes! Oh and they have a big outdoor patio area for dining and I hear they hire live bands certain nights! MUST. CHECK. OUT. Oh, and one MORE interesting thing about this restaurant-No freezers. All fresh. All the time. :) Yummy!

Looking for good food in Reno and we found this.  The portions were huge and they have a good selection of food items.  I eat Middle Eastern food a lot and I would say this place is like a ME Fusion.

We had the hummus sampler and it was awesome.
Not your standard "Hawaiian" lunch plate food.  Very fresh ingredients!  The staff, to include the owner, were very happy to have us as customers.  Would go back in a heartbeat if back in the area.

Wow! This place is the real deal for coffee & breakfast in Hendricks County. It's close to me and we rarely go (that will change now), but today I decided to treat myself. I got the Vietnamese Cold Brew & Barts Journey breakfast sandwich. It hit the spot! Again, highly recommend - extremely kind, clean & welcoming!

So I'd like to share some good pictures, but we ate too fast for that!  The place is small, and although it's been around for about 9 years, we usually pass it by because of the line. Today we got there early -around 8:30. I got a Bloody Mary (regular, bacon, or cucumber) and coffee. Good strong coffee with cream. The Bloody Mary was good-not Zing Zang, I think a dash of olive juice. My husband had the Americano with bacon, potatoes, and a pancake on the side. He said the pancake and the syrup were good and he ate all the breakfast.  I had the tomatoes Benedict.  It was so good y'all.  Tomatotoey with garlic.  Not a traditional hollandaise sauce.  So good. I ate every bite-it did take me a while. The meal came with the home fries. Tasty. So...moral of this story, if you have the time stand in line. We'll be back!

Nice folks with lots of good local brews on tap! Locally sourced food too. Food looked good, but just there for a few beers this time. Will definitely be back to eat!! Sat next to the owner.  She's awesome!!

We have been to Edison several times and usually enjoy the experience. Unfortunately our meal last night left us concerned for the quality of the restaurant. We ordered a filet medium rare and the first time it came out well done. Normally we would never send something back but when paying $40 for a steak you want it to be right. Second time it came out and it was still over cooked, more like medium well than medium rare. We didn't want to send it back again so we ended up taking a few bites and just asking for the check. Our appetizers were delicious and I was hoping to stay for dessert as the brown butter ice cream is a favorite of mine but error on the steak was something we could not get over. Our waitress clearly felt bad and was wonderful but at this point I am not sure we will be back again as there are several other restaurants in the area for the money that can cook a steak correctly. It was also a little frustrating that when they noticed we did not enjoy our meal they ended up taking the cheapest component off our bill as a way to make up for it (which we had not asked for) instead of the steak which was the dish we were not happy with.
Food was awesome!  Great atmosphere, not too noisy.  Really enjoyed the tacos, especially the Baja Fish one.  Highly recommend to anyone in the area.  Definitely am going to be coming back.

We got there at 5:30PM on a Friday, and there was already a line.  Fortunately some of our group got there at 4:30, and had found a table near the bar.  The waitress brought me the wrong drink at first (I think this was the bartenders fault), when I told her, she brought me the right drink and comped it.  The staff is very friendly, obviously they make their tips from their outfits and personality.  The drinks came in glasses, everything was good.  We left the group and went to an event down the street.  

We came back at 10:30pm to rejoin the group.  The place was still packed, with people waiting outside.  We sat at the table and waited, and waited, after 20 or so minutes, we flagged down a server from another table, who informed us she was not our server.  We told her we hadn't seen our server in a while, and wanted drinks.  She did bring us our drinks and our server, who apparently thought the whole table had left.  My complaint isn't with the service as much as it was with the $7.00 mixed drink in a 6 ounce plastic cup.  

If you want some eye candy, and fun conversation with flirty waitresses, this is your place.  If you want some value, or just to drink, there are plenty of other bars nearby.  Including Kilroy's right across the street which treated us great the last time we were there.

I suspect that in a few months, when the newness wears off, this place might be okay.  I've heard great stories from the existing chain locations, maybe this one just needs some time to grow.

We did not eat there, but I've heard the food is good.  Of course, I've heard the same thing from many of my married male friends as justification to go to Hooters.

I decided I'd give this place a try after seeing it plastered all over social media. The pictures of the coffee and food looked great and it also showed several students/young adults working on computers there so I figured I'd try out the coffee and bring my work there. That was my mistake. I met up with a friend and we walked up to the host who asked if we were sure we wanted to stay for the wait. It was only 10 mins so we looked at each other and said sure. So we stood at the end of the path and waited for the host to send us a text with the ready table. We got the text about 15 min later and we walked up to the host stand and she led us inside. She sat us inside and my friend and I sat across from each other at a pretty uncomfortable half booth half table. There wasn't any space to work on our iPad and computer so we just shared my iPad because that's literally all the room there was. The waitress (her name was Emily) came up and brought us waters and asked what she can get for us. My friend and I weren't ready yet so we scanned the QR code for the menu on the table and she walked away. She came back about 5 mins later and took our order to which she literally rolled her eyes when all we ordered were 2 coffees. She came back with our coffees about 5 mins later and asked if we wanted the check. We were kind of taken aback because we planned on being there for an hour or two to work on some things and maybe get a refill on our coffees but my friend said sure I guess. Emily brought us the check and we never saw her again, except as we were leaving she was hugging on another employee behind the counter. At one point I had to use the restroom and wasn't sure where it was. It's pretty hidden  so you'll most likely have to ask an employee where it is. The hostess walked by at one point so I said "excuse me, where is yalls bathroom?" To which she responded "it's back that way" and kept walking. Didn't point, didn't look back at me or anything just kept walking the other direction. I laughed and walked in a circle until I found it tucked into a corner. You'd think frothy monkey would be polite to a couple 20 somethings because clearly that's the audience they're trying to reach. With wine Wednesday's and college students all over the area, I guess I wish I would've felt more welcome. After I came back from the restroom my friend and I decided to leave and work elsewhere. I probably won't be coming back. The coffee was good, but the service and the stares we got from staff just wasn't worth going.
Love this place! Great food and prices. Every person that works here is beyond friendly and I always look forward to coming here for lunch or dinner!

3.5 stars. I honestly can't say I am a fan if this place, but I certainly think its better than a-okay. I can see why others think so. First of all, we came late...just before closing time, unbeknownst to us. The waiter politely clued us in that the kitchen was closing soon and we should get our orders in, unfortunately our last and most important member had not arrived yet, but they were still able to accommodate us. The restaurant is huge and is like a maze. It felt like room after room of tables.

I thought the food and drink was okay. The pitcher of mojitos sounded promising. I was excited because it was going to be prepared in front of us; I rarely see a mojito prepared the classic way. I was disappointed to see him just pour the ingredients together rather than crushing the mint with the sugar. It may not seem like much but it make a world of difference. The empanada I ordered was also good but perhaps not what I was expecting.

Mmm delightful milk tea, great Thai tea, a little on the sweet side but the super friendly staff will probably make it less sweet for you if you ask.  Great service pleasant waiting space.  I am so excited I just saw this place today and it said grand opening so I had to try it and I'm super impressed!  Can't wait to try more flavors!  They have lychee milk tea OMG.  I haven't tried it yet but I will.  Cash only.
Overall great drinks, service, prices cheaper than surrounding shops ($3.50 for milk teas) and nearby my house, so five stars!

Mr. B's Bistro is a very charming restaurant in the French Quarter.  It's classic New Orleans with a touch of international and southern flare combined into one great restaurant.  Some good menu options to taste and enjoy include the jumbo lump crabcake, the bistro burger, shrmp and grits, and my favorite the hot buttered pecan pie.  The service is friendly, prompt, and nice.

Long time since I've been here, but we were on the West Bank craving fish.  I had only ordered boiled seafood from Sals before which was AMAZING!! We thought it was worth a try.  I'm so glad we did their fried fish was so good!  Seasoned well, light and crisp and plentiful.   I have a doggie bag for dinner.  My fiancé ordered white beans w/fried catfish.  He also loved the fish & gave the beans 3 stars.  We both had a beer and our order came to $23.  Great price for the quality and quantity of food.  Highly recommend!
Best beer selection ever! Very limited food menu for vegetarians so don't go hungry if you don't eat meat.

Food was good and service good despite the place packed and a waiting line.  My only complaint was getting a switch in meals ad paying twice the price.  Special was a lobster in ginger sauce for $16.  Waiter told me they were out of whole lobsters but would a tail be all right?  I said yes but was charged $33 for the tail.   Not right so make sure you ask the price if they are switching.  Waiter came back after taking order and giving order to the kitchen so it seemed like just a straight switch. Wrong

The food is decent. Most of it is ok, a couple things are really good. Their in-house/affiliated craft brewery Big Lug makes beer that is... not nearly as good as so many other micro brews around. It's not necessarily bad, it's just not really that good all-in-all. They have a regularly-rotating selection of beers, though, so you can always find a couple to your liking.
Here's the rub with this place: the service is bad. BAD. I work nearby and have been here many times. It's consistently bad. I stopped going unless I get carry-out. Just not worth it. It's too bad; they honestly deserve a 4-Star rating if it wasn't for their terrible bartenders and servers.

If you are craving Pasta this is the place! Wow! I had the Shrimp piccata and it was sooooo delicious! It comes with a piece of garlic bread to dip in the sauce yum! The flavor is amazing! They are consistent here which is great! I eat here 4 times a month it's that good! They have great salads too! A must Pasta place to try you won't be sorry!
Finally. Good chinese food in Stl. Steamed entrees and moo-shu were amazing. Very fast delivery!!! Will be my weekly go-to!!
Outstanding food. The menu was great with plenty of options. Everyone in our party ordered different items. Everyone raved about their food. Definitely going back.

My boyfriend despises seafood but on a rainy afternoon, on the way home, he let me stop here to grab some take-out. I had the fried clam meal and an order of the smoked mahi dip appetizer. The smoked mahi appetizer was AMAZING! It came in a little dish and was served with the freshest lance crackers I've ever had. The fried clams were like none I've ever had before. You get a choice of two sides and I chose the cheese grits and cole slaw. Both were delic! The clams breading was not as heavy as I am accustomed to. It took a bit of getting used to but was thoroughly enjoyable. I live in Mira Lago so I drive by every day. They are only open Thursdays, Fridays, and Saturdays which breaks my heart because I crave the smoked mahi dip all week long. When they are open the place is always jumping! All seating is outside though and you sit on picnic bench type seating. Since I live so close I'd prefer to do take-out but on a nice day I could see sitting outside enjoyable.

Ok so here's my 2nd review... and I'm writing reviews so people like me (who enjoy good food, good atmosphere, good times, and a good bargain- on occasion) can find reliable reviews for the hot and not so hot places around Philadelphia.  All that said lets start the review...
Can I review the HAPPY HOUR 1st and then do another review for an average night out at Harvest for dinner service?  Ok that's all right you'll allow me to do that.  Your mothers did raise you smart and right I guess.
HAPPY HOUR- I like a good deal.  I'm not cheap.  There's a difference.  

1/2 price deals are a value and are pretty damn good but not great.
1/2 price mixed drinks are pretty damn tasty and thats all I have to say about that.  Keep the liquor flowing!
1/2 price beer selection is limited but even beer connoisseurs and beer brats should be able to SETTLE for a beer such as a Troegs that is on special.
What did I forget....? Service.  Go to the bar and order drinks and food yourself unless you're sitting down for dinner.  Hey I'm a casual guy and they did give me plates and napkins when they delivered the pizza pies so I was happy,
Atmosphere is nice and the music they play during Happy Hour is great as far as I'm concerned and I know I have good taste in hip hop- you'd say so yourself if you flipped through my tape collection- jk I'm not that old but I did collect cd's!
Ok I planned on doing the sit-down dinner part here but it almost makes more sense to write a completely separate  review for the same restaurant (only not Happy Hour) and here it goes...
5...4...3...2...1...
Great service food was amazing I had the brisket tacos 3 of them all had a nice portion of brisket which wasn't dried out it was nice and juicy. And the drinks are even better !!!

Good food, great service. Located in Village Shires, this location has been many different failed restaurants, usually bars with lousy burgers. 

This place, 100x better than what was here before! Business is booming, and I except this restaurant to stay open for quite some time. Have been here on several occasions, always a pleasure.

Husband and I were very much looking forward to this place, as we liked the "quaint", "charming", etc. type comments here on Yelp, but we were so, so, so disappointed. The place gets a star for the excellent service (our waiter was very sweet). 

We ordered iced coffees first, which came with a couple of ice cubes that promptly melted. The coffee then sort of bumbled along into lukewarm territory the remainder of our stay (about another half hour). 

The food...what can I say? Husband, as soon as the food was set in front of us, said, "Ordinary in the extreme." That was how bad it was, that you could tell by just looking at it. He had the quiche, and was served the saddest slice of tasteless pastel yellow wobbly triangle. Its miserable existence was topped only by my salad, whose pitiful appearance made the quiche look like haute cuisine. The poor salad was just a layer of wet chopped romaine, a layer of sliced watery tomatoes, a layer of goat cheese slices (weird), and some pine nuts and olives. It looked like a salad you get from a bad food truck. I know you know what I'm talking about. 

Food doesn't deserve to be treated like this.

My boyfriend and I were visiting family in St Louis and decided to try Eleven Eleven after reading the reviews on Yelp.  We had a chance to eat outside and everything was absolutely delish from Appetizer to Dessert.  We tried the Wild Boar Ravioli, the sauce was amazing!  My grandmother and boyfriend ended up having the Catfish special while I had the Roast Chicken special.  Mine came with cilantro pesto which I was a little skeptical of and never tried but couldn't stop eating when my entree was brought out.  For dessert we had the warm apple "caramellate" that we all devoured!  The Ambiance and staff were also 5 stars!  I would highly recommend this place to anyone who enjoys food and having a good experience at a restaurant!  Well done!

This place = yummers !! I will defy come back!

I came here to celebrate Peru's independence day July 28th! I needed some home loving!!
 
Only 4 stars?! Well the food was great (I had better - but not in the Tampa area) but the decor and atmosphere is really blahhh and boring! I had Bistec a lo Pobre (steak, fries, rice, plantains, fried egg, and beans) The portion was huge! So it was well worth it to take some home. I had some yuca and huancaina because I just love it! I order that anywhere I go :) ! My mom had Arroz Chaufa (Chinese fried rice peruvian style) and it tasted so good! Just like home! 

If they work on how the place looks they would have 5 stars in no time! 

Another HUGE thing I didnt like, is that only 2 people were serving the place. When it got full, they locked the door and people outside were knocking and couldnt get it. Sometimes they would ignore them. If that would had happen to me, it would be probably 2 stars, but I had excellent service! 

Just a heads up !!!

I went to the Crispers in Orlando when I lived there so I decided to give this location to try. Had to have a salad and sandwich combo....Bottom line it's similar but not the same. Prices were higher and IMHO quality was lowet.

My cousin and I were visiting New Orleans for my birthday and looking for a good brunch spot. Happened upon this randomly through a website. I was a little concerned due to the low volume if yelp reviews but the menu sounded great and bottomless mimosas sounded even better. When we arrived the outside was full but we waited at the bar and enjoyed mimosas before being seated. The view is incredible and the interior ambience and design is amazing (always very important to me). The best part was the food was WOW! My smoked salmon breakfast was spectacular my cousin's croque madame was amazing also. Our server, Daisy, was the best! When talking with a local they were surprised we found this place so if definitely is a hidden gem! I think most people must assume it is just the bakery below. We were only in New Orleans for 3 days but actually came back on Sunday for happy hour because we loved it so much!! We both will recommend this restaurant to any others traveling to New Orleans and will certainly be back on our next trip!!

I was recently in and just wanted to express love for this place. The service was great, wonderful selection of drinks including seasonal specialty cocktails. The food was amazing and management was very friendly. My only question is why are the fans never on...like ever.

I came here last night and I'm coming here again today for take out. It's a fun place with a good bar food menu. Inexpensive food not the healthiest but still good. The house salad is the best!
They have a ton of tvs so its a great place to catch sporting events.
Tons of parking. 
They have a big patio so I'm assuming Summer days are pretty fun here. 
That's all I've got for now. Oh, they also have a location on the hill too.
This was my breakfast stop on my way to SLC. 30 minutes of waiting and my order never came. Services is slow despite not being busy.
This place seemed empty when we came and wasn't sure about it but my first time eating a Gyro amazing! So so so good! Highly recommended!

Had a really lousy meal mostly due to an inattentive, incredible bad waitress. My husband and I both had salads, my cobb was good and the portion size was fine. however my husbands caesar salad with chicken was full of almost rotten romaine and he could barely find the chicken. Although the chicken was easier to find then the lousy waitress. We enjoyed a beer sampler and I had a Rocktoberfest, which was great. Although we had to remind the waitress to bring it. What really set us off was when we waited a good ten minutes for our change and she only brought the bills, did not give us the additional 75 cents we were owed. Hey, if she doesn't think change is important then give the customer the extra buck, not yourself or the house! She had gotten lost again at this point so her tip reflected the service and our missing $. I made sure to tell the hostess to fill her in as to why her tip was not what it should have been. Refrained from complaining to her manager.
Bottom line this is probably a place better suited for beers and apps at the bar.

Quick bite on Saturday before the Fox. Chico took care of us. Great service, excellent food, in and out just in time to make the show.  Salads, mussels, grilled cauliflower and a succulent order of calamari. A few glasses of wine and out we went. All and all, just what we needed.
Add on: realized the next day I had lost my credit card. Called and stopped by and they had secured it in the register. Made my day. Being before Christmas it could have been bad. Chico: you Rock !!

I found a hair on my McMuffin as I opened it to eat it, IT WAS IN PLAIN SIGHT. I immediately took it back and the Manager or Assistant manager asked me what was wrong I showed her instead of making a scene ( thought I was doing her a favor and not making them lose customers) and, I didn't even get a sorry. PATHETIC. I don't even live a mile from there and I will not be eating there anymore.

What a great breakfast place. Various locations in the NOLA area, this was a phenomenal breakfast. I had the St. Charles Benedict while my wife had the Nutella French Toast (which we split both for a great savory and sweet pairing). Waited about 30 minutes but we'll worth it. You will leave full garonteed.

We came here on a Sunday. 7 adults and 2 kids, 1 of which was an infant. We made reservations of course, just in case. 

We were seated right away. The place is narrow, but definitely have ample amount of room. Very nice atmosphere. Friendly and warm.

We ordered 2 Mix Mezze appetizers, the calamari, 2 mix plates, the lamb kebabs, and 2 seafood casserole. 

I wasn't too impressed with the mixed mezze, but it wasn't bad. My favorite was the eggplant - and the never ending pita coming of course is a plus. ;-). Other than that, the other dips were really just ok.

The Calamari was good. Crispy on the outside and tender squid on the inside. Not too chewy at all. Very well executed if I do say so myself ;-).

The mix plate and the lamb kebabs were also good. The chicken was juicy and not dry. I didn't try the lamb, but I'm not a big fan of lamb anyway, so I wouldn't have been able to tell if it was good lamb or not.

My favorite was the seafood casserole. Tons of seafood and the sauce is delicious. Probably not healthy, but who cares, it was so good! 

Definitely a place you'd wanna try. The food is pretty darn good =)

Service is fast but the sandwiches can't beat subway vegetarian options...
It's good but as compare to price and flavour i will prefer subway.
Excellent sandwiches! Nice laid back ambiance . Fast service.good prices comparable to the chain sub places. Definitely will be back to try more of the sandwiches.

So yesterday  i went  for lunch with my girlfriend and it's Best food I ever had for a long time. I'm in the food sales business for more than 35 years and I am just simply impressed with the food and the service. The cleanliness was impeccable. The prices of the food is what shocked me the most; they were incredible. I will definitely be spreading the word about this great place!

Delicious pizza. Went on a Friday night around 9ish and got seated just fine. Patio is the place to be here! Garlic & Cheese bread was not what I expected but a delicious surprise.  Love the sautéed onions on the pizza. The crust is a bit sweet but perfectly chewy and delicious.

The quantity of food is above average. Though, the coffee seemed a bit watery in taste. The place did have quite a bit of people, but we acquired a seat quickly. It's an ok restaurant. If they could improve anything, it would be the coffee.

Had the Vegan Piccata & was quite surprised at how delicious! Seated right away, got here just in time - it's packed with a little wait now @ 7pm on Friday night! Service was spectacular & we'll absolutely be back! Great quality food & excellent service. Love that it's right here in our own backyard!

First time at Bam!Dog today and WOW! That is the best hot dog ever! (And the tots are their own hero!)
I had the Texas Throw Down. Perfectly cooked jumbo hot dog in a toasted onion roll with all the best fixins, cheese, chili, chopped red onions, jalapeños - heavenly!

Loved it. Adventurous dining. Excellent wine by the glass and Delicious Pasta dishes. The rabbit-chestnut starter was pure decadence. Fresh baked breads. Attentive staff and a beautiful new restaurant on the Philly dining scene. Impressive.

Today I got a gluten-free sandwich for takeout. It was tasty. What most impressed me about this place were the vegan and gluten-free offerings.  My criticism is that this place feels underrated. It Needs to make its presence known a little bit louder!

Traveling a little further for lunch than usual, I headed here based on a recommendation from my customer. We're really close to to Philadelphia so there are cheesesteaks galore and that's what I opted for today.

I found it their "medium" size (with provolone and onions, not "wit wiz") to be plenty. It was not greasy and maybe that's why it was a little dry. I put ketchup on it. Don't hate me.

The restaurant is showing its age, but that's okay. Sometimes the best food comes from the hole-in-the-wall spots.

This place has the PERFECT setting!! Destinee and her Employees are AMAZING! Support local and support them they also support first responders! Take your pooch and introduce them! You may even get lucky at times and meet a K9!! You MUST try this place! I give it five stars

i need to put my review in because i eat here every week. i know this is a controversial opinion but i think this is the best pho in the city. fresh noodles, basil, jalapeños, and bean sprouts every time. pho 75 stopped making chili oil post covid so that was a big let down. they got all the fixins here. you cannot go wrong eating at pho cyclo!

TERRIBLE SERVICE!  Our waiter was literally grumbling to himself the entire time and said he validated our parking, but he didn't. We went in to grab a beer and get our parking validated. This was a bad decision. 

The table behind us couldn't get his attention and finally walked out on their check. Usually, I wouldn't be ok with that, but I had watched them wait 20 minutes trying to get his attention. 

We got an app and two beers. The food came out quickly, but the beers took forever. And only one beer came out. If I hadn't been paying attention to what he grumbled to himself, we would not have known he knew we were expecting another beer. He grumbled quietly that the keg needed to be changed. I understand that, but he did not communicate that well at all. Also, I was a waiter for years. If I have a delay like that, I bring the customer a water and have two back up choices that are similar for the customer to switch to.

Zaytoon is my favorite restaurant in Santa Barbara. The atmosphere is so romantic with the live music, twinkle lights covering the greenery, and the fire pits in the center of the tables. I choose this restaurant for any and every special event that happens in my life from birthdays, graduations, new job promotions etc. 

The food is decadent and the drinks are delicious. I highly recommend the chicken schwarma and their raspberry mojito- hands down best mojito in SB!
Thank you Stephanie. What an amazing restaurant. Everything was delicious. The US Army endorses the lost Cajun. Fried catfish was the truth.

Chicken. Waffles. Peach Butter. Syrup.

If you want to chow down where the locals go, hit up Maxine's for some good 'ol fashioned soul food. I hear their fish and collard greens are delicious, but I have a hard time not ordering the traditional chicken and waffles (because of course).

The service is excellent and it's nice that there are still restaurants out there where the managers walk around and chat with customers. Everybody's a member of the family at Maxine's.

Texas de Brazil hits all the marks, fantastic service, good salad bar, great food, and good atmosphere. The meat selection is good, but the quality of a few of their cuts is fantastic. Their sausage was the best I've had at a Brazilian steakhouse! The meats rotated quickly and with good variety. If you are going to pay the $ to eat at a Brazilian steakhouse you should not be disappointed with Texas de Brazil.

Great place to stop for some food and a beer! Had the orange, fig, and prosciutto pizza as well as the steak tacos. Both were phenomenal. Was surprised with how well the different components of the pizza worked together. Service was very friendly and attentive.

Happened upon this place on our way home yesterday.  The inside is definitely more impressive than the outside area. The food was decent, but our service was not.  We had a waiter that, for some reason, was not friendly or attentive to my friend and I.  They brought my chicken with rice dish which was over-spiced to the hilt; almost too much to eat.  My friend got the shrimp cocktail and a taco and said all was good.  After getting our food, our waiter never came again to ask how everything was,  or if we needed anything.  Instead, he sat at the BAR talking with another patron totally ignoring us. We engaged another waiter walking by as my friend was totally out of coke. The gentleman waiting on us wore glasses. I believe he was the only one that was, so he should be easy to identify.  Benjamin was the waiter that took care of our needs the rest of the visit.  I made a point to the hostess as we were leaving that my $10 tip was to go to Benjamin and NOT the original waiter as he failed miserably at his job.

Was really impressed with this new spot.  The first thing I noticed was the huge outdoor patio seating - great for COVID (they were spraying and cleaning down the tables regularly), but also just a really nice space to enjoy the weather.  And since the patio is right next to the creek at Aspen Grove Park, it felt like you were separated a bit from the hustle and bustle of Cool Springs. All employees were wearing masks as were most customers while ordering, and it felt very sanitary.  The line is marked so you can social distance, and I never had to be within 6 feet of anyone.

Food was delicious.  You can pick from a variety of rice bowls, noodle and broth bowls, and salads, all with fresh ingredients, made salad bar style so you can customize.  Calories are listed too, which is nice.  I got a tuna poke bowl, which had purple rice, sushi grade tuna, avocado, pickled cabbage, kale (which I added) and a delicious spicy sauce, and a coconut curry soup.  Food was definitely filling and felt nutritious and very fresh.  They have a lot of not-your-ordinary soda fountain drinks too, beet lemonade, fig and vanilla, mint green tea.  I will be coming back for sure to try more, this place definitely fills a void in the high calorie fried food corridor of Cool Springs.

After hearing great things, I tried the Suya bowl with jollof rice, chicken and cornbread with medium spice.  I didn't know what to expect, but I have to say it's flat out delicious.  The other reviews (sans the dry chicken one which had to be a fluke) sum up my same positive sentiments.  Definitely going into the rotation.  It's really that good.  If you have been debating it give it a shot you won't be disappointed.

SICK...  We stayed there January 2016 and ate at Rosie's cafe as a group of 25 and ended up with what I think was food poisoning. We were very sick and had the EMT to our rooms and hotel security. There was about 10 in our party that became violently ill over a small period of time that all ate at the same place. I have called many times and we all left a report.  Day manger was supposed to call back but never did after many calls to the Hotel. After filing a report with the health department, they stated that many people were sick on that date and reported the same issue.  You would think that this could have been easily rectified with a simple phone call and owning up to the situation. At least to make sure that we were all ok after they knew we were all sick.  Some of the kids had to go via an ambulance ride to the ER.  After five years of staying at this place we are done!

We did the sunday brunch the second sunday in Feb.  Outstanding service and food. I had a pizza carbonera as a app, the pastry stuffed with scrapple and poached egg and my partner had the pasta with trumpet mushrooms.  two carafs of house wine and coffee plus two deserts which were awesome.  Price $124 with tip and worth every penny of it.

they get 4.5 stars from me, only because i've gotten older and i don't think that anything is as good as it gets anymore. ;) it's been well over a year since i've written a review, but vietnam palace, specifically tracy, deserves a lot of good 'press'. 

i've dined at vietnam palace many times in the past and already knew that i was a fan of the food. i don't have a marked preference for it over vietnam restaurant (both are delicious), but VP definitely has better pho  and grilled meat. anyway, my organization hosted an 80 person banquet in their upstairs private dining room, and not only was the food amazing, not only was the service amazing (people went out of their way to complement the service at a banquet, where people are varying degrees of tipsy and usually only paying attention to their own conversations. amazing), but the event coordinator is also a top notch human being. she patiently coordinated all sorts of business details and last minute changes and couldn't have been more pleasant or accommodating. the event went off without a hitch and people are still telling me how much they enjoyed the food. well done, and thank you!

highly recommended dishes: any appetizer (seriously), papaya salad, pho, hue style soup, i prefer vermicelli to broken rice, but they do both dishes very well, stir fried flat noodles, country style beef and their salt battered seafood is not heavy and very nice. and they can sub tofu in almost anywhere (my favie dish at the banquet was a tofu stirfry. excellent and clean).

Everything here was excellent! My family and I decided to try Nagasaki out for dinner. We ordered a few appetizers including the monkey brain (deep fried spicy tuna stuffed avocado), vegetable tempura (delicious and light), and the age tofu with smokey fish flakes (my personal favorite). 

We split a few bowls of ramen and some rolls for the main course. The ramen was huge and delicious! I highly recommended the tonkotsu miso. The pork was incredibly tender and flavorful. The rolls were all excellent and beautifully presented. I usually scorn vegetable rolls but the peanut roll was extremely good! I highly recommended that for anyone who is a vegetarian or just afraid of raw fish. 

They surprised us with some mango cake at the end of the meal. So tasty!

Try this place! If you like authentic Japanese food you will love it.
The drinks were on point and the food was delicious. I got the pulled pork sandwich with the pulled pork nachos. I highly recommend this place!
Come on, a 24oz $5 Margarita!! The Deep Fried Mac and Cheese and wings here are amazing. I try to hit this place up at least once a week after work for drinks and food.
Bad service, hour and  a half wait for large party to have our table given to the latest walk in. Forgotten drinks, dinnerware and rude waitstaff.

excellent food and good service.  i've been going to tiffin for a long time now and always love it.  had dinner there again tonight and it was great.  the onion bhaji is awesome, so is the chicken korma.  try the peshawari naan.  it's yummy and almost like dessert!

When birria tacos blew up, I wanted to go to a spot that had both the tacos and ramen. This place came highly recommended by a friend so I went and ordered; was not disappointed. The tacos were delicious!  the ramen was good too, but I definitely preferred the tacos. I've recently learned that they have $1 al pastor tacos for Taco Tuesday. I will definitely be going back to try those next.

The food is always good, I love their coconut shrimp and the vegetables are always on point. The outdoor seating is great so these always keep me coming back. This is the only location I've been to but I consistently have issues with the service here. It's not terrible, and it's not always, but definitely more often than not the experience is sub-par. Food/drinks/patio make up for it though!

GLUTEN FREE AND VEGANS REJOICE!


I have visited the restaurant 6 times for breakfast in the last year. We were originally drawn to the place because my wife is gluten and dairy free. Our meals have always been very good, closer to fantastic actually, and the service polite.
We took out of town guests there today and were served by the owner herself.
The food was great as always. One of the comments was "your body says thank you to you every time you take a bite", and these were not vegans!
The true pleasure of the day was talking to the owner! To listen to her speak about the care and passion she puts into her restaurant was quite honestly the best interaction I have ever had with someone in the business.
Gluten free, let alone vegan items are for the most part average at best, and cross contamination is always a concern when eating out. She has figured out how to make good food that is healthy and safe for those with special dietary needs taste hands down fantastic!
Be sure and don't miss the carrot cake cupcakes!

From the parking lot walking into the restaurant, you may feel like me and be second guessing your decision to come here. But once inside, the people and the food make this place wonderful. Shrimp pad Thai was excellent. Tom yum gai soup, very good but maybe a touch too salty. Won ton soup excellent. Chicken satay was great. Service was great and always love happy servers. Makes the experience better.  
Price was very fair and I would definitely come here again.

Who knew Cajun pork rinds served instead of bread as a starter could be so good?! The food was great, oysters were big and inexpensive. Our waiter was friendly and made some good recommendations. It's inside the Intercontinental Hotel so it did lose some ambiance due to having to walk through the lobby to use the restroom, but other than that it was great! It was our first time having gumbo, because well NOLA, and it didn't disappoint!

So I have eaten hear 4 times in the last two half weeks.  The service has always been fantastic (Lindsey is the only severs name I remember). We have had a lot of items off the menu and everything has been great.  I am so glad that they have opened on the West side of Carmel as I have been visiting the Hamilton Town Center location. I will probably be back one night this week!

Employee: "How was it?"
Me: "Honestly, the chicken was so dry I couldn't finish it. I want to give his place another try, but this was disappointing."
Employee: "Cool, thanks man."

So it would have been cool to either get a freshly made meal with fresher meat, or a refund, but instead my lunch search continues. Fuck this place and the hipster vibe they tolerate, I will NOT be returning to support this establishment. Even if the chicken wasn't dry, the rest of that shawarma wrap flavor was janky AF - tasted like they put tabouleh in it, lol

From outside nothing special 
Inside Food GREAT 
Service GREAT 
VALUE GREAT 
Sangria GREAT 

We had Pork Chops and a Salmon Special
Had to take half home 
Apps were wonderful octopus as well as empanadas 

Just go there

Best in Philadelphia, hands down. Been to the typical Geno's, Pat's, etc but there's something about Jim's that's different from everywhere else. Frequently travel to cover shows at TLA next door and now I'll be frequenting Jim's after as well.

A friend and I stopped by for a late lunch.  We both had salads. They were very large and nicely done. I had the chicken on mine and the flavor was wonderful.  I would however liked it to be a little more done.  There was some light pink in the thicker areas.  I am old school and feel that chicken should not have any pink whatsoever!  I am not a complainer so rather than telling the server I just did not eat about 1/3 of the breast.  Other than that the food was very good and the service was nice.  The location and atmosphere was very pleasing.  Enjoyed sitting outside and taking in the scenery. I would gladly go back but, I would ask for the chicken to be cooked longer or order something else.
so happy there's a great pho restaurant in north Delaware

I ordered Ramen expecting an approximation of the popular Japanese meal in a bowl. Instead I got Korean rice cakes with ramen noodles in the traditional spicy bright red Korean sauce. Be warned only the beef ramen on the menu will get you what you might expect when ordering ramen.
Fantastic, authentic curry. Absolutely delicious and just the right amount of spice. Can't wait to come back.
The salmon was ok, the tuna was not fresh so I didn't eat it and the service was slow. Perhaps they have a better Chinese food.

Great place with a good hearted manager who actually has ethics. Ordered a 20 piece boneless wing dinner and some came out smaller than a quarter. He saw it and stepped up to fix it and even agreed that shouldn't happened for the overall cost. Glad this manager Rick  was on top of his position. I recommend if there is a problem let Rick be fair and objective. This is a place I will continue to support and enjoy because Rick works hard to make his customers happy. He even acknowledged that he believes all customers 
"should get what they pay for" Rick I appreciate you and I will return

Amazing!  I happened to be in the area for work one day recently and stopped in at the Shawarma House for lunch.  The place doesn't look like much from the outside, but it is brand new and super cozy inside.  I tried all the classics: badrijani, khinkali, and khachapuri.  All were really very delicious.  On top of the amazing food, the staff and service were also top-notch.  I can't recommend this place enough!
Like why go to any other Mexican restaurant. Great food, great atmosphere. The best pork carnitas! And the menu says they are a favorite. Could use more parking.

I work across the street and go almost everyday! Atmosphere is probably the cutest place in Metairie. The maple bacon doughnut is TO DIE FOR. Love the owner, all the staff is friendly and know their regulars.

Wow, an amazing breakfast spot. Portions on all the food are great. Ingredients taste fresh, the kitchen creations are wonderful. Self serve coffee station is great for an impatient coffee drinker who needs his fix STAT! 
Music is modern/inoffensive, staff is on it. Give this place your business!!!

The Wild Cow is a casual, vegetarian restaurant in East Nashville. The entrance is on the side of the building (facing Eastland Ave) so if you come here for the first time and look a little lost you are not alone! Once we did find the door we were greeted and seated right away in spite of it being a busy evening. The first thing I noticed upon looking around is that the hippie scale is off the charts here but the environment is comfortable (hey I'm not complaining).

Their menu features appetizers, sides & snacks, salads, entree bowls, tacos & wraps and sandwiches. They also always have a daily entree special, soups and sides. Everything on the menu is vegan unless you want dairy cheese on something then you can just tell your server. Our server recommended the spinach and artichoke dip as a starter so we went with that first. This was by far my favorite thing I had here. I am always surprised when I have something like a spinach and artichoke dip that traditionally will be made from mayonnaise, sour cream and/or cream cheese and this had none of those ingredients yet was still incredible! For an entree I ordered the buffalo grinder as a salad with tempeh. I also ordered the side of the day which was a medley of roasted vegetables. I did like the salad overall but I will say the the buffalo tempeh fell short. When I turned over the tempeh it was overdone on one side (almost burnt and a very dark brown) then the other side wasn't cooked enough. I figured that this must have been just the wrong choice of something to order because everything else I really did like. This is the only reason I am giving them a 3 instead of a 4 for an otherwise good experience. 

I would come back here and give this restaurant another chance to wow me, perhaps by ordering something else. However, I will say that I am the biggest fan of their sister restaurant Graze (see my review for them).

I decided to come to Carlucci's for a cocktail because of the fact that they had outdoor seating and it was such a beautiful spring day, plus it just so happened to be happy hour. I thoroughly enjoyed the scenery while sipping my cocktail. Needless to say, that is pretty much the only basis for my 3 stars. 

The food was extremely bland and "basic" to say the least. With each bite I thought to myself "I could make this 10x's better." However, I'm going to give them the benefit of the doubt in that I only ordered from the bar style menu during happy hour. I wouldn't recommend going to Carlucci's if you're looking to be blown away by food. I probably won't be back to have anything to eat. If you want to have a drink during happy hour from 4-6 and enjoy the weather, I would say go for it.

Wonderful, nice staff. Great (diner) breakfast, and very inexpensive. Cool location over-looking the nice Nashville skyline. We had fun talking to the locals. The joints just a cool, quaint little spot. Stopped in on our way to Memphis, and now we'll be stopping back in on our way back to Baltimore.
If your in the mood for great wings that are super crunchy and flavorful this place is your nirvana

This is probably my 5th visit to Nine Ting and once again, I left in a food coma. I got the hotspot this time and my boyfriend got the BBQ. Usually I don't think that's allowed but we came at a not so busy time and told the server nicely that I didn't want BBQ. We were immediately seated (first time that's ever happened; usually an hour wait during prime time) and we ordered a variety to foods. My favorite bases for hot pot are the tomato and the spicy soup bases. Depending on how many people you eat hotspot with, you can order the bigger pots with dividers, but since it was only me today, I got the mini bowl to my self. They also have a sauce bar with a variety of options. My favorite mix is peanut butter, sesame butter, chili oil, and minced garlic. 

I always order a variety of vegetables for my hot pot. Some of my favorites are frozen tofu, tofu skin, water crest, chitterlings, tripe, beef, Chinese yam, enoki mushrooms and corn. 

Service is also nice. Out waiter came back multiple times to check on us to see if we wanted more food.

On a road trip, found this gem thanks to Yelp. Want to add to the compliments. Some of the best Mexican food I've ever had. Fresh, tasty, and a wide selection, including many fish dishes. Highly recommend this place. Their parking lot in the back is small, but there is street parking. It's a one-of-a-kind place, although I hear they may be adding a second restaurant elsewhere. The owner walked through asking diners how things were. Wish there was a place like this in my hometown!

Again, visiting my favs in Tampa. Soho is top of the sushi food chain! My Uber driver confirmed my dining choice (but I already knew with my time in Tampa).

You walk in the door and you are most likely greeted with smiles positive energy from the staff.

The apps and sushi are over the top tasty. Tonight I had an app of a tempura mushroom cap stuffed w lobster salad, followed by Kiss Of Fire sushi roll.

Don't be fooled by the outside appearance, as a this spot is KNOWN for quality sushi. Highly recommended!

Went here for my birthday as I am a seafood lover. The service was good and the seafood was fresh and the presentation, eye catching. My food was good but the sauce could have been more seasoned, I've had better seafood sauce. I ordered the combo with a whole lobster, shrimp, Dungeness crab clusters with corn and potatoes. I would definitely go back.

This weekend I ate at Blush for the first time.  I live in the area but hadn't gotten around to eating there yet.  We sat outside on a beautiful day.  The patio is nice.  We had excellent service from Azucena.  I had the Cobb salad, my husband had the chicken BLTA, and my son had the California burger.  We also tried the Steak Bites appetizer.  All of the food was great.  It was my son's birthday so the restaurant provided a free dessert, a warm cookie topped with ice cream, that was fabulous.  We want to try dinner there also so I just bought a Groupon for Blush.

I came here on a Friday for lunch with a coworker.  We waited about 5 minutes to order and the food was out pretty fast considering the crowd.  Had the hot chicken platter which came out in strips and included two sides.  I thought the chicken was tasty and moist.  Best tasting slaw (wasn't slathered in mayo) I've had in a long time.  I would definitely come back to try some BBQ next time.

The elusive short review:

I'm spending a small amount of time on this review because we didn't spend much time at Two Bits. We were walking from Midtown to Bridgestone Arena for a concert and we needed a small and quick snack. 

We ordered water with a side of loaded tots. The tots were loaded with feta, poblano aioli, and chives. I wouldn't mind going back there the next time I'm in Nashville and trying something more substantial. They have plenty of pub grub and beer on tap. 

The place sticks out because of the video game theme. There are tables with game consoles. There are also arcade games. The best part of it all is that they're FREE to play! Even with a small wait, the time will fly by playing video games. The only issue was that one of the arcade games had stuck buttons. That sucks when it's a game that depends on timing. 

Two Bits is on a strip with many other bars and food places. We walked by the place a couple of times and it never seemed busy(We were there during the week). I hope this place gets packed frequently and sticks around. It's definitely the type of food/drink/dive/arcade place you want in your town.

Where do I start?  How do I even begin to express my disappointment.  Previously, this building housed a music venue/nightclub and I was very excited to see that a new restaurant was on its way.   The grounds appeared to be cleaned up, the exterior spruced up, and I could see they were doing some work inside.

None of that matters, however, when you walk inside the building and there is the pervasive smell of cigarette/cigar smoke wafing in from the outside bar area.   The decor is definitely improved and looks cleaner than the previous restaurant/bar. 

I was not greeted at the door as I entered.   Not a hello nor nod of a head.  I stood there for a few moments waiting for someone to acknowledge me even though there was only one table seated and one couple at the bar.  The waiter at the table with seated customers was giving his opinion on the state of economy and real estate in the area.   

 Finally, I was asked if I would like to sit somewhere.   

My waiter, although very nice, was unfamiliar with the menu and cuban cuisine in general.  When I asked if they had chicken and yellow rice, I was lectured quite nicely that chicken and yellow rice is not a cuban dish but that they offered paella which was cuban.  I didn't debate.

Rather than argue the point I continued to read the menu.  They did in fact have a chicken and yellow rice dish which I ordered.   The waiter then brought me a plate of cuban bread.  The bread was dry ~ seemed stale ~ and no butter was provided.  It was just sliced open.  
My meal arrived quickly.  The chicken looked deep fried.  The outside was dry and hard and the inside was worse.  Let me further clarify, if the chicken was roasted it was overcooked and on too high a temperature.  It was crusty without flavor.  How do you go wrong with chicken?  I couldn't eat it.  The yellow rice was flat with no flavor.  I ate the rice because I was hungry.

I did not eat the chicken nor the side of platanos which was cold and greasy instead of warm and carmelized.   My bill was over $18. without a beverage.  After a tip it was $22. and I left very hungry.  The waiter asked if I wanted to take my meal to go and I told him no.  I explained as gently as possible that I could not eat it.  He offered to rebate me 10% on my meal and I declined.

I am very disappointed as this would have been a nice weekly stop for me on my way home.

Hands down the best Thai food in south Philly. I will never order from anywhere else. They are so prompt with delivery and SO nice whenever you eat in. Their red curry is divine and so is their pad Thai!!

Always a great place to grab and go, take a seat with a group of your friends, or enjoy the evening air on the outdoor deck. Menu is bountiful with lots tasty options! The staff will be your friends if they aren't already! Stop in and have a bite, you'll be happy you did!

Mr. B's is located conveniently across the street from the Hotel Monteleone.  After the morning sessions for a conference held in the hotel, I stepped outside, walked across the street, and dined at Mr. B's for lunch.  I ordered the lunch salad and duck spring rolls.  The salad was delicious.   The mixed greens and salad dressing were great for a light lunch before another round of conference sessions.  The duck spring rolls were oh so delicious.  I could have ordered another two orders of it.  The spring rolls had a delicate balance of roasted duck and vegetables.   The restaurant was quite busy, and the service was smooth.  The place had a business dining atmosphere but laid back.   The hostess is very kind, and our server was quick and attentive.

On a recent visit to Philly with my vegan cousin, we happened to accidentally stumble into V Street completely unplanned. It was centrally located just 3 blocks away from our hotel, so we ended up eating there 3 days in a row, it was that good. 

The first day, we were just planning on getting drinks, and then ended up getting some snacks after realizing it was a 100% vegan restaurant. I ordered the Pico and La Brea cocktail with the activated charcoal, making the drink look pitch black. It tastes like adults lemonade and was refreshing and delicious. My cousin ordered the Jade Rabbit, and she was not a fan, as she thought it was way too floral tasting. We also tried the Peruvian Fries, which I highly recommend. They're definitely on the spicy side, but they're a perfect snack when you're drinking cocktails. We also tried their daily soft serve, which was a tahini soft serve with cherries. It tasted kind of like peanut butter, and we both really liked it. 

The second night we sat down for a full dinner. My cousin tried the Dan Dan noodles, which were definitely on the spicy side, but since she loves spicy food, she adored them. I ordered the smoked beet langos, which were probably my favorite thing we ordered the whole time we were in Philadelphia. The combination of the soft bread and the sauerkraut remoulade was so flavorful and delicious. If you're debating ordering them, definitely do. You won't be disappointed! 

We also stopped by for Saturday brunch, where we got the Byblos Bubbles cocktail (their take on a mimosa), which was bubbly and a little sweet, and basically the perfect brunch cocktail. We split an order of the okinamiyaki fries, which felt to me like a vegan poutine. Definitely recommend those! We also tried the Korean fried tempeh tacos, which I also highly recommend! It tasted almost exactly like a fried fish taco. We both inhaled them and seriously debated ordering seconds. We split the grilled avocado, with scrambled tofu soft tacos. The grilled avocado was delicious, and the tacos were also very pleasant. 

Vegan or not, this place is amazing.

The appetizers were great ! Loved the Tofu Hiyayakko - unlike anything I've eaten before ! The hot chicken buns were a treat too ! But the ramens were below my expectations - I ordered the lemon paitan and it seriously lacked flavor. the Spicy Miso was good - although I've had better Ramen. The server refused to help my friend that wanted vegetarian ramen options. The Mochi icecream was pretty good ! But am I going back - probably not !

Busting with activity on a Saturday night, this place has a great formula --- lots of wines "on tap," so you can try a little or a lot. They have limits outdoor (sidewalk) seating that my friend and I were lucky enough to nab.  The service wasn't exactly speedy, but they were quite crowded on the late Saturday night we were there. If and when I'm back in Indianapolis, I will definitely give it another shot.

Last night we ventured to the Harrison House after a long hiatus as our last experience was not that great. Well we now know why we haven't been back. I ordered the special which was the pancakes with fresh peaches and blueberries. I was disappointed when the dish came out to find that the pancakes were lathered in some sort of sauce (which it did not say on the menu). I went ahead and tried them and upon first bite I noticed that the bottoms of the pancakes were completely burnt. The bottom of my wife's reuben was burnt as well. I am not sure how they would let food like that come out to the table.

We decided to get dessert and the experience with that was the same. Both the Boston cream pie and the oreo cake were extremely dry.

We know know why we have not been back here in quite some time but we are definitely sure that will be our last time dining at the Harrison House.

After only having China King (yes, with a "K") in the neighborhood, China Hing (with an "H") was a refreshing break.  My usual dishes, Shrimp Fried Rice and Steamed Dumplings tasted cleaner, if that makes any sense.  The shrimp was cleaner looking too, and I think they have more shrimp in their rice than their competition.  
Drawback: we ordered catering recently for a group of friends and family, and while the food was good and delicious for a fair price, the guy at the counter didn't seem to recognize us when we went back a couple of days later for a regular, to go, order.  I know they see tons of people going in and out daily, but wouldn't we stand out?  Especially when you have a bald guy and a girl with curly hair ordering the food?  Ok, I guess we're not that memorable.  :) We'll still eat here, but we were hoping for an extra "Hey there" or "Hi" when we went back.  Minor complaint.  
We always order to go because we'd prefer to eat our dinner at home than there.  The ambiance just doesn't invite patrons, but that's not what we pay for.  The food is the focus, and as long as they are consistent in flavor and quality, we'll continue to eat there.

I tried ordering and I order for business partners, family, and friends on a daily basis. Probably around $1,000/mo. Tonight they declined to allow me to order because they didn't feel like delivering and claimed their driver was sick. Lol... next thing I know our neighbor is receiving rustys about 45 minutes later..I won't be back not one more time. Disgusting

Was a bit disappointed with dim sum today.  The shrimp in the shrimp dumplings were not fresh (mushy), some dishes were cold, and buns, custard were not the best in texture or taste.  The best dish was the XO stir fried rice noodles.  Will be a while before I go back.  Service was not the best either.  Took a long time for someone to get our drinks order or other stir fry requests.  Everyone is working so hard, no one smiles!

The first time staying here and I can't wait to leave this place it's beautiful don't get me wrong but you can not get service the screams at night was ridiculous when you walk you have kids screaming adults screaming at the kids then they run into you. The toilet was nasty when we came in and the shower i waited in line to get help with the waterpark only for him to brush me off. We tried to eat sit down after waiting 45 min to wait another hour and 15 min for no one to even wait on us so we had to go elsewhere and since we waited so long we had no food, behind on schedule and no one even noticed or cared. This place is understaffed needless to say.

Good stuff! After 4 visits we are still really enjoying this place. There is something for everybody I don't care for the floral aromatic foods but my does and she loved the Chicken Coconut Soup and the Thai Noodle Soup while I really enjoyed the Phad Thai and Merlion Noodles. My kids were split as well. One thing we all agreed was a 5 was the Love Wrap, I absolutely must have it every time and oh yeah the Thai Tea is good too.

This is the best burger in the city, hands down. I was back for a 5th time last weekend, and the food quality is still top notch. My one issue is that this place is tiny and on a number of occasions I have had other guests ask me how much longer I plan on staying. I'm not a straggler; I was with a party of 3 and we had only been there for 30 minutes.

You could say that this issue isn't the restaurant's fault, but I think it is to a certain extent. The hostess will always encourage guests to go find an open spot if they can, rather than managing all the seating and serving guests once a spot opens. Second, this is owned by Garces, who also owns Tinto next door. It would make a ton of sense to expand VW into Tinto's space.

My boyfriend and I went to Bank and Bourbon for 2022 Winter Restaurant Week. We had anticipated the restaurant would be packed, however, we had nearly the whole place to ourselves. As a result, the ambiance was intimate and quiet. We also had attentive and caring waitstaff. Our server spent time answering all of our questions and ensured we had an excellent experience. He explained that the restaurant is located in a historic building. The Philadelphia Saving Fund Society Building, where the restaurant is located, is regarded as the first International Style skyscraper built in the U.S.

For the appetizer course, we ordered the Pork Belly and Butternut Squash Soup. The Pork Belly was tender and had a nice smoky flavor. It was served with a cabbage slaw which was a perfect combination. The Butternut Squash Soup was also a hit as it warmed us up after our cold and rainy walk to the restaurant. You could easily taste the apple and nutmeg.

For the Entrée, we ordered the Sixty South Salmon and Hanger Steak. Both the salmon and steak were cooked to perfection. I particularly liked the creamed kale that was served with the steak.

Per usual, dessert was my favorite course. And unlike most restaurants where the dessert portions are tiny, these desserts were large. We ordered the chocolate mocha cake and apple-maple bread pudding. The cholate mocha cake was moist and full of espresso and chocolate flavor. The apple-maple bread pudding was served warm and was drizzled in a whiskey-caramel sauce.

Overall, we had an excellent experience at Bank and Bourbon. The ambiance, service, and food were stellar.

Had the Pupusa's  and the Street Tacos. The Street Tacos were a little smaller than in Texas but very flavorful. These were my first Pupusa's so I don't have anything to compare them to but what I ate I really liked. Staff is very friendly.

This review is comparison to cafes of the same nature in San Francisco, so take with a grain of salt: service was nonexistent. I went at 8 am on black friday. 
my experience, Wait for somebody behind the counter to notice you standing patiently and ready and finally recite your order. They will ungraciously toss you a coffee mug and pastry and hand you a table number if you ordered food from the kitchen. They don't seem appreciative of your business or interested in your well being. I was with my old fashioned (conservative) grandfolks and felt stressed that my grandma and I got our almond croissants immediately while my granddad had to wait several minutes for his croissant sandwich. I was shocked that the pastries weren't even offered to be heated up! A heated almond croissant is a world better from a room temp croissant. 

Onto the good. the space is large and spacious and the atmosphere was busy, polite, average noise level...we got in and out in under an hour. I absolutely was shocked that they offer bottomless coffee!! Most cafes are not like this! Most diners however are.... 
Almond croissants ARE all that, but they are sooooooooooooooo sweet. Way sweeter than classic french patisserie style. Also, they are much more vanilla bean flavored than almond liqueur flavored. 
Standard peerless coffee. Not bad. Wasn't burnt! I would go again and try more pastries and macarons and come back for the bottomless coffee! Yeehaw!
Awesome food and music. Try the collards and brisket then finished with a buttermilk pie.
This restaurant is very small, but the food is great.  I love it there.   Great variety and service!   Nice desserts and price is right.  Highly recommend!  My grandson loves the French toast.
Traveling through Indianapolis and ate here based on the reviews and the recommendation of our hotel.  We were not disappointed!  In the words of our 8 year old, "This meal is paradise!"

After a few disappointing dinners, my wife and I found a place that makes us glad that we moved to Tucson, and that place is Jax Kitchen. There is an amazing quality not only to the dishes but the service as well, and though the food can be on the pricier side, you won't care what the bill looks like by the time you're done eating.

I mention the service because it really is phenomenal. I'm not quite sure who our waiter actually was but several staff took turns taking care of us, offering us refills, suggesting entrees and appetizers, and even offering an extraordinary dipping sauce for the sweet potato fries that came with my entree. My only complaint is that I didn't know such a sauce existed and wasted a few fries with plain 'ol ketchup. 

It's a little dark inside Jax and seating is limited but if you're going to indulge in a night out, there's no better place to do it than Jax.

Bait House is an absolute favorite of mine. I discovered them several years ago and will always choose them over the regulars (Crabby Bills, Frenchies, etc.). The waiters are fantastic, atmosphere is fantastic, food is fantastic, can't say enough good about them. I highly recommend the spicy tuna nachos and their catch of the day reuban. Best restaurant at Clearwater Beach.
Delicious food, just got the basic Gumbo. So wholesome. So would recommend anyone to pay a visit

It's Olive Garden.. We all know it's not authentic Italian food, so what? Most folks come for the breadsticks. Like myself. Well I came for the pasta bowl special.. $10 for endless pasta. They serve you a dinner portion first, then a kid's sized 6oz portion for refills. This location isn't known for high quality service and never will be. My girlfriend and I came for dinner and the waitress asked my friend if she wanted to sample some wine. She said yes and I said that I wasn't drinking, while pointing to my protruding belly. The waitress proceeds to tell me that I can have red wine during my pregnancy. Ma'am, I know what I can and cannot have.. Move on. But she stood there insisting that I have a glass of wine.. Then my friend glared at her said that I wasn't drinking. Smh. Took 15 minutes to bring salad and breadsticks to the table. Whatever lady, just bring me my pasta. The service just was elderly senior citizens slow. Sheesh. No wonder they closed the location in Center City.

Upon entering the small and quaint Japanese restaurant, we were greeted warmly by the host who brought us to our table.

We started off our orders with chicken fried rice for the children, and for the adults, the following: sushi boat, Longwood Garden roll, sashimi salad, spicy salmon roll, eel roll, followed by three orders of fried ice cream. We had a long stroll in Longwood Garden prior to this visit, don't judge.

Let me start off by saying the salmon was incredibly buttery and creamy. There was not one gristle that could be found in that massive chunk of salmon. The octopus was deliciously juicy and chewy with a wonderful sweet fragrance that explodes with every bite. The Longwood Garden roll was a perfect marriage of sweet and savory and the creamy avocado and salmon balanced the sweetness perfectly. The spicy salmon roll was not the typical wimpy slap blah of salmon mush slapped on top of the rice, this was real diced chunks of salmon carefully mixed with tangy mayo and a generous squirt of spicy sauce. There were more sushi we had, but I'm salivating as I wrote this and have to stop. 

I was so impressed with the sushi that I decided to try the kids chicken fried rice, curious on what impressive feat they can conjure up. The rice had the perfect balance of egginess and savoriness and blended in perfectly with the white chicken breasts that were generously salted. Delicious. 

Lastly, we finished our perfect day with a heaping scoop of fried ice cream. The batter was thick without being too heavy, it had a wonderful spongey texture that soaked up the left over ice cream that had melted into the bowl. The ice cream itself was cream, but the batter was the star here. 

Overall, I highly recommend this place for quality sushi and sashimi. The fried ice cream is also a decadent dessert that cannot be missed.

I never had an order right when using the drive thru. My daughter-in-law went to Wendy's in Paoli, she asked me if I wanted something, I said large fry's. Well when she got home I tryed a fry and it tasted old, so I dumped the fry's in a dish and it was mixed with other food that we did not order. It made me feel sick it looked like garbage. I will not eat at the Paoli Wendy's again.

Great cranberry, walnut salad. So good that I ate there for lunch two days in a row. Love the quiet interior. If you are lunching alone it feels very comfortable. After reading the review from the guy from the South, I will need to work my way through the menu but for not I'm trying to stick to salads.

Stopped by for lunch today. The service was good and efficient. The establishment is pretty open, bright and clean. I ordered a few things because I'm greedy lol. The crab rangoons were really good, light and crispy. The ramen bowl was sufficient, but unfortunately the poke bowl was a miss. I've made poke bowls at home with much more robust flavors. Not, sure I'll return but glad I was about to support.
I love the Greek food here & the owner is wonderful.  All the food is made with love. Great local eatery!
I have been here twice, and have had a good experience every time.  The coffee is great, and you get service with a smile.  One of the best things is that it is not expensive, it is a great value.

Went here for my birthday dinner with my chicas! The decor is great. Its very aquatic and I like it! They have paper on the tables and crayons so you can doodle while you wait. 

The waitress we had was very attentive and sweet. She wasnt overbearing by any means. The runners were a bit confused but still happy and nice. Let me explain.... There were 3 of us. We ordered 2 of the same drink and a different drink. The runner came and placed the drinks in front of us. The glasses they gave us didnt match so we knew the order was mixed up. Not to mention, my friend and I both work in Hospitality. The runner told us the bartender told her which drinks were which. She consulted another runner and they had a pow-wow. Finally, our server came by and told them that we right. By that time, we had already switched glasses after tasting each others tasty beverages. No biggie. The girls were all nice and apologized for the petit faux paus.

Otherwise, everything was FABULOUS!!! The food was mind blowing!!! We waited a while between apps and entree but we doodled on the paper to keep us occupied. Nice touch! The dessert selection was slim pickens but the portions are HUGE. We decided against dessert tho so I couldnt tell you what it taste like.

Overall, a great restaurant with great food and great service that you can enjoy while having a great drink! Gotta love it!

I'm sorry we were such an inconvenience to you coming in 30 minutes before you close. I've been in the industry, and I even acknowledged the fact that they were closing soon, and said whatever is easiest would be fine. We felt like a burden on the staff, which unfortunately ruined the experience. It's a shame, since the crab cake was very good. Everyone has their off days, but the demeanor of the staff took it too far.
Great vibe and delicious food thus far!  Kale Salad was on point and educated server who was able to describe the restaurant perfectly!

We are still unsure exactly what happened, but all we know is that the service last night was bizarre:

- Sunday night, so it was very quiet, with 4-5 server ladies around, but we had to wait both to be seated and to pay, like we have never had to wait anywhere, ever.

- The lady who served us first introduced herself as our server, then when I mentioned I had a coupon to use, she said she was not our server...?!?!?!?!

- All the server ladies looked sleepy.

Colorado Omelet with pancakes was still good though, but that was just bizarre.

I really dislike writing negative reviews but be warned Cadiz now longer has a regular dinner menu contrary to previous reviews on this place. Small plates are expensive and not very good. The kitchen was painfully slow. Ouch. Be warned.

Love this place! Super authentic, fresh, flavorful food at very reasonable prices! It brought me back to being in Mexico with a delicious and expansive menu. The owner is very nice, and the place is no frills. I'm so excited this place exists in Arabi and there's a slice of authentic Mexican cuisine in the parish!

Had the best burger I've had in a loooong time tonight.  Delicious, fresh ingredients (even the iceberg lettuce I usually dislike) and holy mackerel, the place was SLAMMED and the one human who was bartending AND cooking did a remarkable job of both.  BECCA: You are an evil genius and one of the best chefs/bartenders I've ever seen.  Bravo, lady.  And thank you!!  We will be back.  

Also- Rev is a stone cold burger SLAYER.  And an awful nice dude.

This stuff was gooood. The fried chicken! sweet, spicy, and lemony. I also love the smashed cucumbers ap. the soups are yummy and they deliver to my neighborhood quickly and accurately. to be honest I've never been in the place (lol) so the only ambience I have to worry about is my house, which is just fine.

Jessie's  fruit sauces are amazing. This stuff should be marketed nation wide. It's good on so many items. Apricot is my personal favorite.  Try it on a grilled cheese sandwich and soup. One word heavenly.  Or just with chips using it as a dip. I promise your tastbuds will thank you.

Being a newbie to the location I wasn't aware you had I go upstairs to dine. The bartenders downstairs were extremely rude and unpleasant. The young lady acted as if I was bothering her when I asked about seating. However once I got upstairs the rest of the staff was friendly, helpful and tentative. Mr.Terrel was awesome and on time.. Thanks bunches!

Who doesn't like a good soft serve cone, or a chocolate chip blizzard?? I want one now just from typing this. Lol
