Dairy Queen is a staple in the ice cream industry. You know what you're going to get product wise, but it all comes down to customer service, cleanliness, and speed. 

This location has sub-par customer service. Sometimes you wait a very long time for someone to even take your order at the counter. All depends on who is working. There are a few employees that are on top of it and can get everything it in a timely manner. Then others are like sloths..... (see the movie Zootopia for a reference) 

The food is usually pretty fresh and the drive thru orders are normally correct. That's a plus. 

So to sum it up. Yes go to this location and love on some ice cream, but don't be in a hurry!!

Ahhhhhmazzzingggg!!!!

Everything is made from scratch and everything tastes out of this world!

The staff is super friendly and attentive!

Love

I have been coming here for 6 years. I have also been vegetarian for years and Tom's decision to turn plant-based was pretty exciting as I have been aiming to go vegan by the new year. This is my go to place in my neighborhood when I don't feel like cooking. The staff here is very friendly and helpful in making decisions if you are unsure what to order. My old standby is the sweet potato burrito. My new favorite is the carbacoa, a carrot and lentil based burrito which is well seasoned and has a nice mix of flavors. I also highly recommend the mushroom quesadilla (which is a special from time to time so if you see it get it!). A great place in a neighborhood with a ton of diverse, locally-owned options . Well worth a visit!

The place was throughly cleaned and the crew was amazingly good at customer service. The chicken was fresh and tasty as well. This gave me a great impression of the business and staff collectively that I just had to write a review!

My best friend and I decided to come here on opening day. Maybe because it was opening day the service was a little crazy and rushed and the workers were a little confused. I ordered the chocolate chip cookie dough and I fell in love with it! It tasted amazing!!!!! I decided to go back another day, this time the service was much better maybe because it was more calm and established. The two employees were so friendly and patient. They even took the time to let customes try samples because they wanted us to have something that we would love and enjoy. They were just super friendly and seemed like they enjoyed working! I decided to be adventurous and got the peanut butter flavor which was just amazing! I am trying to go for another visit to try a different flavor and I just can't wait!

Went for drinks a couple weeks ago, not a bad spot. Can't wait for the patio to open, it looks amazing out there. Being new to the area, this place was recommended by some coworkers. We will absolutely be back.

Sooooo, we got there early and got a seat outside.  That was the highlight of our evening.  I think I had higher expectations.  To  make this short: We weren't famished so no appetizers/first or second tastes.  Right to the main plate.  I had the trout and my husband had the pork.  Mine was fine, albeit quite bland.  He said the pork tasted fine; HOWEVER, the portions be far on the light side, his meat was over half fat.  Yes, a big thick slab of fat.  When he mentioned this to the waitress, she said she would pass that recommendation on to the chef but that the pork was cooked hours with the fat and it should be that way, and you could tell she wasn't happy about the complaint.  I get that it was cooked with the fat, but doesn't mean you want half your portion in fat, especially when the portion is quite small. Now, I am not a fan of HUGE portions, but they carry it to a whole new level.  The taste, portions and prices do not cohere.  If you want give it a whirl, go ahead, but don't say you weren't warned.  Who knows, maybe your experience will be better!  Cheers!

(NOTE: after I wrote this I got a message from the owner telling me they were using disposables due to COVID and were returning to real dishes next week).  I am not a bacon and eggs fan, but a friend picked this place so I was glad to go with her. I had scrambled eggs and toast which was good and my friend loved her food. My problem is they use non-recyclable plastic plates, cups and utensils for dine-in meals and styrofoam for their to-go. It is a very popular place so imagine how much landfill, non-eco friendly trash they are generating daily.  I will not go there again. There are too many other local places that have good breakfasts that care about the environment.
Very nice, fresh menu and very pleasant service.  A spot to add to the breakfast rotation list!    Thank you for the tasty grub and the excellent service.

We went for a dinner date and really enjoyed our experience. My husband and I split a delicious caesar salad with some of their complimentary bread. Both fantastic. We couldn't settle on 2 items so we went with 3. We ordered a small lasagna, a pollo pizza and a chicken marsala. We absolutely loved the pollo pizza. I enjoyed the chicken marsala. And we both felt the lasagna was so-so. It might be that we aren't eating much red meat these days but we wouldn't order it again. 

My biggest complaint is the seating. The place is pretty small. We had to sit outside on the patio and it was fairly humid. We joked that they should have a NASCAR background sound to accompany the sounds of cars whizzing down Jefferson Highway. When we go back, we'll definitely make reservations for indoor seating or wait next time.

Overall, our experience was a good one and the food makes it worth another trip back in the future.

A very good bowl of soup! Visited this location with my siblings. I had the miso ramen, which was flavorful, salty, and rich. The noodles were a perfectly chewy consistency and the chashu was fatty and delicious. I had the gyoza to accompany my bowl, which I highly recommend. They were delicious. Definitely coming back!
I was super excited when they opened only to be let down.Just another over priced mediocre doughnut shop. Its not worth the hype.

This is place is subpar for subpar
Mexican fast food joints. Definitely Mexicant rather than Mexican. Food prepared in view while you wait should be a good thing but in this case it made
Me throw up in my mouth a little. Same gloves on for multiple tasks. Finally washed hands and drys with paper towels he dropped in the sink. Greasiest gristly excuse for steak I've ever had and just sloppy sloppy sloppy. Top that off with relentless upsell pressure and a really lousy experience. Have been to the store in Conshohocken and had a good experience but this was deplorable.
High quality sandwiches prepared here, cant go wrong with the surf and turf choices. Probably the best restaurant located in Paoli, PA.

This place was freaking cool and definitely up my alley, however I was unfortunately there on Halloween and the place was an absolute madhouse. There was about a half hour wait to play a game and people breathing down your neck and distracting you hoping you would screw up and finish so that they could jump in. The bar was cool, the beer selection was very good, and I loved the divey vibe and all of the cool games. I hope to come back to Philadelphia and revisit this place because I had a lot of nostalgic things for me.

If carb comas are your thing, you've come to the right place. With only a handful of other bagel shops in Nashville, and the amount of hype surrounding Proper Bagel since it's opening, I was excited to finally try it. Even at 8:30 am on a Sunday, the line will be out the door. As soon as you walk in, you are drawn in by every kind of cream cheese you can imagine. I really struggled turning down the cookie dough cream cheese for a lighter option, but now I'm full of regret. Treat yourself! I ended up with a cinnamon bagel with the raisin and walnut cream cheese. Was the bagel good? Yes. Was it life changing? No. For the price, I was hoping for something just a little more over the edge.
Orders usually right. Only been disappointed once and they provided a replacement. Quick. Good. And friendly environment.

A highly anticipated meal that did not come up to expectations.  The mid- day menu is drastically cut back, making "choices" difficult.  Not wanting one of several wraps on offer (and wondering how a wrap is either "modern" or "fusion") - we went with a flight of starters - their hummus (okay, honestly, 10 stars on the hummus. FABULOUS!) - "flash fried" artichoke hearts - and their pot stickers.

Okay, it was going on 3:p.m. and shifts were changing, I get that.  But once my honey got her (wonderful, rounded, very tasty glass of white Burgundy) wine, and I got my "deconstructed" Bloody Mary - also a hit and highly recommended - I noticed that my drink was missing the stuffed olive garnish.  TRY and find the/a server...  Okay, finally got that corrected, then arrives the food.

Already talked about the hummus and if you miss that you are missing a small bowl of heaven.

Flash-fried artichoke hearts are a must miss item.  Fried is correct - but if those are house-made art-hearts I'll eat this review.  Flash those right back to the kitchen, along with the out-of-a-jug sweet chili sauce. This is NOT what I was expecting from Mosaic.

Now let's talk about the "Suckling pig with shaved celery and Thai peanut sauce" pot stickers. To the server who asked me how everything was, I herby apologize for being so brutally honest when I told her "these are horrible.". I try to be more objective, and kind in my remarks.

However, whatever the unknown goo was inside those pot stickers, it was insidiously tasteless.  "Horrible" was accurate.  Just don't go there.  To the pot stickers, I mean.  Oh, and shaved celery, in my world anyway, isn't a big old celery stalk sliced lengthwise in 1/2" thick slabs and pulled out of an ice-bath several hours later.

I have heard many, many good things about Mosaic from people who know and respect great food.  Alas, our experience today will not affirm those thoughts.

I would love to give it 5 stars but I can't. The French toast was underwhelming.  I wanted to love it but didn't. The eggs Benedict was good. The rest was pretty plain and not much to write about. We only had to wait about 30 mins. The server wasn't good at all. He was actually a bit of a jerk. He was constantly making comments about other employees at one point referred to his coworkers as "Beavis and Butthead". He threw a tantrum because a big party of 8 decided they didn't want to sit upstairs. All of which he was saying loud enough for customers to hear. He barely spoke to us directly but when he did he seemed really annoyed and was rather rude.

I have been to a great many Indian restaurants in this city and this new little gem in southeast Edmonton stands out from the rest. 

The food is delicious and you can immediately tell that the kitchen takes the extra effort to create authentic Indian dishes. Case in point was the insanely delicious coconut naan bread which has shredded coconut inside the bread, something I have never seen at any other Indian restaurant in town. In addition to the delicious taste, the presentation is superb and adds to the overall authentic atmosphere 

Service is also top notch. We were guided towards some items such as the milkshake (delicious) that would have otherwise not tried. The chef came out to chat and everyone was tremendously friendly. Food came out in a good time and everything was done with high professionalism 

This place was worth the drive from downtown. 5/5

We recently went here with my 2-year-old (which is no easy feat when you are 38 weeks pregnant). The ambiance was inviting and the night was quiet as we were in between lunch and dinner. Both women who were working were so polite and welcoming and greeted us right when we walked in the door. They brought crayons for my little one and water for me right away as we waited for our guest. 

The food was delicious. The curry and chicken tikka marsala along with garlic naan hit the spot. Service was quick and efficient, and the food is priced just right. Cheap even for the quality in my opinion! I brought Togo food home for my husband as well, to see his thoughts and we both agreed- we will be back and soon!

I got the strawberry flavor with fruity pebbles, chocolate sprinkles, marshmallow sauce and a brownie on the side. It was delicious! I would definitely recommend going here, they have a variety of options for both yogurt flavors and toppings and the customer service is great. Go get some healthy desserts!
One of my best sushi places in Reno. Service is very quick and also friendly. Yummy sushi!!! I highly recommend this place.
Cool concept, good beer! We had the poutine which looks delicious to begin with and was gone in minutes. Also would recommend the bacon wrapped jalapeños!
Just stared a job near hungry Greek tried it for the first time today.  Nice staff and good food.  I will be back

Love this place!  Creates a great vibe as you enter the vibrant tasting room!  The tastings are incredibly fun with a wide variety of 8 wines each.  The Lux Collection tastings were all delicious!  The NightOwl port combined with one of their truffles (which are made on site by their own pastry chefs) was incredible.  If you go for a tasting ask for Darlene.  She's knowledgable and very fun.  I don't have time for a full dinner review but needless to say, the 5 star experience continued for the rest of the evening.

I went there again with my friend from NYC and we both agreed it was definitely good food.  
They offer a variety of spicy levels from mild and sweet to really spicy.  I love spicy food so this place actually offers me the option.  I think it would be interesting if they offer a spicy curry challenge like they do in Brick Lane in NYC. 
Word to the weak stomached, order mild.
Good food and good service. I had breakfast here a couple times while staying at the Union Station hotel. Fairly pricy for breakfast, but it's an upscale place.

I'm a fan of Ted's. The bison burgers are really delicious and not necessarily easy to find anywhere else. I can't  come here without ordering the onion rings. One time the service was really bad, but because the food was so good we gave it another chance. The next time the service was much better (I would recommend going when it's not busy).

Excellent food! Moist chicken. Went on a date and everything was perfect. Mint tea was really good and I'm not a tea drinker. I liked seeing the chef in back cook...it added an extra element of authenticity and transparency. Excellent friendly and attentive service! Will definitely come back!

My wife and I were in SB for her birthday in July 2016 and we Yelped this place.  It had the highest reviews of the sushi places near State St so we checked it out.  The inside has the old, quaint house feel without AC but the cross breeze makes it comfortable.  If you are looking for a posh sushi place this isn't it.  This place is more casual and low key.  The staff was friendly and our food came out quickly.  I had the mango ice tea which hit the spot after walking in the sun down State St.   We ordered the mango roll and lion king roll.  Both were very fresh, presented well, and tasted excellent.  We would definitely come here again.
Should have been a check-in, but got too far away. Anyways, breakfast w/Friends. Torino's does their usual great job.

Good food. Impossibly slow service. I mean impossibly slow. A tad overpriced, but that is to be expected at a State Street bar I guess. For tapas I like Milk and Honey better and for Mexican and margaritas I like Carlitos.

I am not the biggest Ramen fan but this is a place that I have come back to twice. The ambience here is great, very family friendly as well a great date spot for a night out for dinner or a quick lunch with co worker. I don't eat any other meat so I got the chicken but my friend got the duck ramen and it looked soo good. I highly recommend any of the ramen dishes and you won't be disappointed at all.  Portion sizes were decently sized and the service was great. Truly recommend this place in the st. pete area if you are in the mood for some ramen.

A Starbucks is a ........ what it is.
I have my fav which is quite limited and I get the same every time.
Service is fast and friendly.
Easy in and easy out.

Stopped in for lunch for a friend's birthday.

 Cafe Linnea is a bright and light café that serves up French comfort dishes. They also over a Sunday afternoon high tea that looks to die for.

 Started the meal by ordering a Cappuccino. This drink was oh so Good. It was obvious that this place spares no expense high quality coffee. Coffee lovers will be delighted. 
For appy we all shared the Salmon Gravlax. It was a plate with delicate smoked salmon, rye Baggett and creme fresh. Also on the plate was a small pile of pickled beets. The combination of each ingredient was a like a party in my mouth and the creme fresh adds an unexpected brightness that leaves you wishing there was more even though the plate has already been picked clean.

The menu is small but each dish sounds so delicious its hard to choose just one. I ordered the Complete Gallette. Of all the dishes I tried today this was unfortunately my least favorite. The dish is like a tart only the crust is a simple buckwheat  open face crepe instead of a traditional pie crust. Inside is a combination of ham and cheese with a simple side salad of fresh greens dressed with oil and salt. I  felt this dish was lacking that flavor punch that it seemed every other dish we tried today had. It was salty savory with salty savory. If you are a big ham lover then this dish may be for you. One gal pal at our table order the cocotte. I tried a few bites and it was amazing. Definitely need to order that on my next visit.

We finish the meal by sharing three of the desserts. All were extremely tasty and packed an awesome flavor punch. My favorite was the pear and ginger cake. It was warm and moist with a spicy gingerbread like flavor with a slice of pear embedded in the middle. So wonderful. The lemon crepe was a simple crepe infused with lemon flavor and adores with tiny swirls of lemon rind. It was just light sweetened but full of flavor. Due to the simplicity of the dish I found it a little overpriced especially considering there wasn't any filling or further accoutrements with the dish. The last dessert we tried was the grape crepe. I have never had a dessert before with backed grapes. The dish wad spiced warmly spiced with cinnamon and possibly nutmeg. The grape reminded me of a plum dish my mom makes at Christmas. 

 Overall Id say this place offers unique options to the Edmonton culinary scene and I Can't wait to go back to try that again.

My family and I were out tonight trying to figure out where to get some dinner. My husband and I both pride in ourselves in trying to support local businesses and to try new places. Anyways we went here after seeing the reviews here. This place is off the dirt path. But it the food was hot and hit the right spot. My husband got a cheese burger and my child got one too. I got the chicken Gyro plate. Everything was made the way we asked. The owners were very friendly!

Decent pizza, but can't say I recommend it. Really nice atmosphere, good service the night we were there. It's sort of a local's place. I was brought here by a local, and might return someday. Have to try other dishes that are more traditional.

11/30 my boyfriend and I order fibbers off of door dash. He order salmon over alfredo and ate most of it saying how good it was. Woke up on 12-1 and was vomiting for 24 hours... now If that's not bad enough we reached out to fibbers and asked for a manager to report our issue. We received Matthew on the phone. Once he heard what was going on he became very Unprofessional  and started yelling and arguing with my boyfriend  saying they order their salmon every day receive it fresh everyday... my boyfriend said ok Matthew what your last name, I'm going to stop by the restaurant and I would like to see the daily Receipts's you claim to  order fresh everyday.  Matthew refused to give his last name and ended our phone call by yelling at him saying"go to small business court and sue us then" and hung up.  Not only is this unprofessional but disrespectful to us and the owners. I want justice and I want to speak to the owner!
Ate here after a Titans game. Arrived 5 mins before close and the staff was happy to seat us. Food was really good for a chain restaurant.

I really enjoyed this establishment. Has made my must go to list for Tampa.  I had the Pint and I thought it was a really good grilled cheese and the chips it came with were good also.  I had a couple of beers and they both were great also. There is a good choice to select from also.

As my wife says....it's a hidden treasure.  Great service wonder flavors.    Although this decoration are old....the place is great!!

Try the smoked trout and veal chop.  

And ask to meet Peppe!!!!
Love the historic vibe. Staff was friendly. Wings and salad special, thumbs up. Good beer selection. Check it out!!
1st Time here but Definitely NOT our Last.  Icing on Cake is that they are BYOB.  Quick service with a Smile.  Easy parking in surrounding area.

Our first visit at The Tomato Bistro was mainly due to the fact that the friendly owners/manager donated a certificate to a family benefit for a silent auction and we wanted to thank them personally.   Besides being all around really nice people, we were treated to a delicious menu mixed with delicious pizzas, sliders and small dishes. 

Yummy thin pizza, recommend the cheese fondue appetizer with soft pretzel, asparagus, sliced apple and grapes and kielbasa for dipping.  Want to go back to try the sliders.

Wait staff very friendly.   Highly recommend and look forward to going back.

Kathy L.
Excellent! Pulled bbq pork! Peanut butter pie! Macaroni and cheese! It's not inexpensive but definitely worth it. Their bbq has a vinegar base (I think).

I have eaten at both BR and Keystone locations. Food fair is consistent between locations, and it is price point appropriate. Service at both locations is outstanding. I have only ranked the Keystone location higher due to driving distance from my home. They truly have impressive consistency between locations.

I've had take out from here several times and their wings and chicken fingers are good but overpriced. The area where you pick up your food looks like an old cafeteria, but it suits the need of somewhere just to order and eat.  The bar area is a little nicer.  Half priced apps during happy hour (4-6) is decent and they seem to have a good beer selection there. I had the FWOT buffalo chicken sandwich and was a little disappointed the large piece of chicken I got was on a stale sesame seed roll and the chicken wasn't tossed in buffalo sauce like the chicken fingers- it only had buffalo sauce poured on top.

Talk about a nice porch....

HUGE selection of brews both local and abroad. Another flight, another enjoyable experience. (In some fancy-schmancy glasses, too)

Try the Brown Sugar Brown Cow Brown Ale. Goodness in a glass, my friends. Like a chocolate malt shake.... with 6.9ABV. 

The brisket BBQ wrap will not disappoint. And I think I got about 3 large potatoes worth of waffle fries on the side. Our sever, Brian, commiserated with us on the one downside: no Tabasco in the house. Wamp wamp.  

Enough TVs around you can catch a game, but not so many that you lose the cool-vibe ambience. And surprisingly not very crowded at 8pm on a Friday night.

I normally go here for dim sum once in a while, but the service has gotten so bad. We asked for two glasses of water and that took about 20 minutes to get. We ordered a dish twice, and it never came out.

I'm used to okay customer service at asian restaurants, but this is just ridiculous. When I paid the bill, I didn't put any tip since I have cash. The lady in the front said "the tip is on the table right?" Soooooooooooooo rude. As a customer, it's up to me to give tip or not. You don't need to remind me, that's an optional thing. I got upset and handed her the receipt, and she tried handing it back to me and "forcing" me to give tip. I was half tempted to not give tip at all, but that would be unfair to the servers. Never coming here again. Same food and better customer service at ocean harbour.

If I could give 0 stars I would!!  The past three times I've been here the drive thu has been closed.  One excuse after another.   Someone actually came on the intercom and said the cook left early!!  I don't know why I keep coming back to this location, I guess  bc it's the only one by me!  Just drove out of the drive through after sitting for over 10 min, it was 7:40, clearly they are open and yet unable to handle the one lone car in the drive thru. 
THIS LOCATION SUCKS!!

To answer some questions from the first reviewer here, same owners which are part of the family that run Darfon's on Elm Hill Pike so you'll see some similarities.  They reworked South Side to have a more casual, less upscale, more home style menu.

The service was fair.  Unfortunately I was told what the daily specials were and after partially overhearing it after I had ordered, I wished I had been offered the special.  I started with a lemontini which was on happy hour price of $4 and was good.

I asked what the soup of the day was and it was tomato parmesan bisque.  Hoping it was similar to the one served at Darfon's, I had to add it for $1 to my meal.  It was better than Darfon's version.  It was creamy, salty, chunks of tomato and lots of parmesan cheese.  Slightly spicier than Darfon's version.  So good I ordered another bowl to take to lunch tomorrow.

I had the NY strip steak with loaded baked potatoe and buttered asparagus.  The steak was good though it was the strangest shaped NY strip I have ever seen and it could have used some seasoning before throwing on the grill.  For all the saltiness in the soup, this was just the opposite.  As for the steak, I've never seen a NY strip that was less than 2 inches wide and somewhere between 6 and 8 inches long.

Baked potato and asparagus were good but nothing special or out of the norm.

Overall, a good meal.

As for atmosphere, it's rather small and you do have to walk through the bar which was small and pretty full but not crowded like the previous reviewer encountered.  Over half the tables were families with small kids.

My husband and I wanted to get a quick breakfast. We decided to go to iHop. If you go to this IHop, make sure you ask for Grant. When we got there, Grant greeted and seated us. During the ordering process he was  informative and gave pretty good suggestions. Once we got our food, he made sure we had everything even before we asked. I can't express enough how great his service was. I would say it's par or even better to fine dining service. The food came out quickly and we were pleasantly surprised. The omelet was a pretty large portion and fluffy, the hash browns had a nice crisp. The pancakes were pretty good. The French toast was a little bit burnt, but that's the worst part of our visit. We'd seriously come back just because of Grant's service.
Food is delicious, staff is great,  they have outdoor seating when its nice out, and it's a BYOB!

Tried to order local... 2:45 later we got a burnt pizza 95% blackened on the bottom. It was 75 minutes later than the estimated delivery time, and entirely due to the restaurant and misrepresentation of the delivery app. Will not be ordering again for a while. Please update delivery times and focus on quality, mamas.
I like pizza. I order 2 fry got two order of fry! Wow! Great business. Love it! Next time I take grandma.

While the jury is still out on their food, I like this place. 

We've been here twice now for happy hour. The happy hour is a great deal - micros are included, as are margaritas!

We've tried a handful of their appetizers - none really knocked our socks off, but the wings are pretty great - they're huge, and their house-made Crossroads sauce is good.

The Voodoo Chicken sandwich was great, just the right amount of heat, and bacon - can't really go wrong there! The Gorgonzola burger, however, was just so-so to me - the cheese was just too overpowering.

The service has been pretty good when we've come, and the atmosphere gets you in a mardi-gras mood.

I'd like to come back to try their in-house smoked meats. They also have a delicious sounding brunch on Sundays, including a $3 top-shelf Bloody Mary bar. I'll be back!

Ordered take out from here--mediocre to sub-par food quality and flavor.

Meats were overcooked, soups and curries were under seasoned, and oddly seasoned. There was some unwelcome bitter flavor in the tomyum. 

I DO NOT RECOMMEND.
The spinach dip was average, the atmosphere was modern. The oysters were really good. Some of the best I've had in awhile. We definitely will be back.

This is one of my new favorite restaurants in St. Louis. Locally sourced meat through Mac's Local Buys (the guy we buy meat from, too!). Amazing platings. Delicious food. When they first opened up, I think we went three or four times within a month span....they had turkey leg nachos on the menu which were both my husband's and my favorite. We'd like turkey leg nachos for appetizer, turkey leg nachos for salad, and turkey leg nachos for dinner.....and maybe turkey leg nachos for dessert! (We're talking four different orders here!) They are THAT good. Granted, I don't know if they are on the menu anymore, but yeah, look out for those.

Everything else we've had has been outstanding, too. We've taken our friends and family here. This place is a gem in the SoHa neighborhood. So impressed!
Great food, horrid service.

I ordered a lamb sandwich with cucumber, tomato and white beans.  The meat was nicely marinated and went well with the other ingredients. It even had a touch of spiciness to it that wasn't in my fiance's chicken sandwich. Contrary to Vince E., I liked the cornmeal dusted bread and thought it held everything together nicely.

I was not a big fan of the baba ghanouj. I like mine chunky, with bits of recognizable eggplant. This was blended to the point that it was too creamy - almost as if there was mayonnaise involved. There wasn't much eggplant flavor, and the only redeaming quality was that it came with more of the bread.

I'll probably go back again at some point in the future if the urge hits, but not for the baba ghanouj.

One of the best phos I've ever had! Houston has great pho and I've tried pho in many a places, cities, and countries and this is by far one of my favorites now. I got the filet mignon pho andOH MY so delicious!! And how it's served! The broth, meat and noodles are all served separately. The meat was filling,tender and juicy, broth was piping hot in a clay pot and plenty of noodles. I'd suggest to cook the meat to your liking first, take it out then add it to your noodles (in portions). I slightly cooked mine in the piping hot broth, took it out, added some noodles and divided my meat (in the pot and on the plate to eat separately).

Love that they have Angry Orchard on tap and $2 off during happy hour!  Tonight we got our usual, which is a Greek salad, split, and a large pepperoni pizza.  No complaints!  Consistently good food, consistently decent service.  We'll be back!

I have been here twice. The first time I came with my husband and son. We all split the devil crab appetizer, which is 1 huge devil crab. I had the cuban and black beans. The devil crab was (this is very difficult to say) the best I've ever had! The cuban and black beans were just mediocre. Second time I came with my mom and we both had a devil crab which is served with Crystal (hot sauce) butter, a delicious concoction. I will definitely be back for more!!

I am not a fried chicken expert. Not even a novice, after six irredeemable years as a vegetarian. But I wouldn't change a thing about our experience. Wandered in around 2 on a Sunday (Hattie's seemed to be the only hot chicken place that was open) no waiting and had the medium spice small. Nice even heat, not too spicy at all, and they provided lots of condiments to make it hotter yourself. I love the location & atmosphere too. There were other mid-twenties folks hanging out on the heated porch & the Falcons were on.  As to those who complain about the wait: I am certain the reason I loved my meal so much is the chicken was fried as fresh as could be. No sitting around getting limp in its own heat and losing moisture through steam. I would wait 20 minutes any time. Oh and cheap and good local drafts are a BIG+. I'm not the BYOB type ;)

I've ordered a few times and enjoyed the brisket and chicken. However, we ordered a meal recently and there was a dead fly in the mac and cheese. We called the restaurant and they seemed unbothered, they simply told us to file a complaint with Doordash, which we did.

Generic, but very fast service.

If this is your first experience with Indian food you will probably enjoy it and leave a glowing review like the ones you see here. However if you have had good indian before this will leave a lot to be desired.

I am assuming all of the awards aren't from this year or last because this was very bland --- tough to do with Indian food. 

Try Tashan, Tiffin, or Ekta instead.

Not what I expected from a place that just opened Not spacious not friendly things that are a must. The food was just ok. I hope things get better. I will try it again but as of right now I am not a fan.
Finally it is open! I had the cafe con leche and a guava turnover and I was in heaven. I can't wait to go back for lunch. Everyone was very friendly and I loved the decor. Great job!

After another thwarted attempt at getting into Ralph's for a last-minute dinner (I always forget how small that place is), my date and I strolled around the block to Dante & Luigi's.  The place wasn't too busy and we were seated right away.  The veal saltimbocca in sherry sauce was exactly what I needed (along with a glass of wine). The veal parm was bigger than my head!

The service was friendly, the seating was spacious and I enjoyed the Van Gogh replicas adorning the walls. It was unassuming, yet classy, and I'm happy to have added a new place on my list for date nights. It's easy to walk to from center city, but they do offer valet Friday & Saturday nights.
Delicious chicken bowl! Most students appreciate their late hours and decent prices. I also love the vibe and music! I am Definitely becoming a regular here.

I came on a Monday so I didn't have to deal with a long wait which I hear is an issue in the weekend....

The food is incredible, best biscuit and chicken sandwich I've ever had. Service was excellent as well. 
I think for the quality of the food the prices are appropriate. People complaining about it should stick with McDonald's. 
In short, if your in Franklin just do it. You'll be happy.

Nice vibe... good Italian food.  The wife always gets something different, but I always gravitate to the cannelloni.  Not a huge wine list, but really good selections.  We're not dessert people, but we have been tempted once or twice.  Still enjoy an after dinner espresso (served with a lemon twist, of course).  The place is small enough to get good personal service.  There is not a bad table in the whole place.  I think it's the same management as Il Bel Lago in Creve Couer.  We always get Carmelo... he makes us feel welcome and always give good advice on what's good.

I'm definitely not a vegetarian, but this is on the top of my lunch spot list. There is a line for a reason. My favorite thing to get is baba ganoush and it is out of this world. I usually order it on top of the house salad, and it comes with pita bread. I've also tried the baked tofu and greek salad, which have both been amazing. The hummus is also fantastic. You really can't go wrong here, I've never been anywhere close to disappointed. You can also pay with a credit card, which is a nice perk. 

If you haven't gone here and you work around University city/ are a student, then you really are missing out.

The red beans and rice was excellent, plentiful (they gave us a whole Andouille sausage to boot) AND inexpensive. It was only $12 for an entrée PLUS a side (we got red velvet cornbread and yes you read that right). Be sure to visit Sandi the bartender extraordinaire who will send you on your flight feeling right after a quick Bloody Mary shot!

Atmosphere gets 5 Stars
Service and Food get1 or less...

We were thrilled to know a new eatery/bar was opening near Vail and thought for sure it would be our new hang out.

I am so disappointed in Hot Rods.. the food is mediocre, the service is crappy and the cost is high. The atmosphere is definitely one of a kind, just wish we could say the same about the food.

Super busy all the time but extremely efficient. Ribs and salad are amazing. Never had bad food or service there yet. Highly recommend- seating always a problem, but what a good problem to have if your the owner.

The Best Baked Clams ANYWHERE Have come to the Clam Tavern from West Chester since the late 80s 
Staff is amazing as the food 
Great Date Place 
Family Celebrations or just dinner out
GO GO GO

If you're a serious hotdog fanatic, this restaurant will likely excite you, as it's obviously about hotdogs (my daughter enjoyed the Mac and Cheese hotdog).  I'm not a huge fanatic, but like them, so I got the regular hotdog.  It was fine, fairly basic tasting, nothing outrageously delicious, nor was the atmosphere anything to write home about.  It was just, fine.

We frequently order lunch from here and it's pretty good. Portions are large and you know the food is fresh because it's always slammed packed. A few drawbacks is that the sandwiches sometimes lack flavor. Everything is super expensive and I haven't tried 1 baked good that I would go back for 2nds. A sandwich,  chips, drink, and treat will run you an easy $20 a person for lunch.
Great and fun Irish pub in a perfect location. It's not worth writing more because if I'm ever in the area I'll be here with a smile on.

Finally made it back, and glad to see they got the kinks worked out. Sat at the bar for dinner. The service was great.  The timing of the courses was right, and the steaks were cooked to almost perfectly.  Happy I tried this place again.  Only drawback - I don't like having to give out my number when I get on the list for a table.

This spot is located and attached to the hotel we stayed at. So naturally we hit it up. Everyone is welcoming. The Shucker is a really cool dude popping them open with ease. The food is really tasty. Definitely recommend this place.
Very good sushi. I have been to a lot of AYCE places around reno and this one stands out. Good fish to rice ratio and the service was great. I'll be back for sure.

We had a nice late lunch and cocktails in a true New Orleans experience.  We ate in the charming interior courtyard.  The space has a happy decrepit quality that is the essence of the quarter.

The Pimm's cup was a real standout.  The muffelata was good, jambalaya OK (I wouldn't get it again).

We had a great time talking with our waiter (delightfully grumpy in a socially acceptable Southern way) and the couldn't-be-more gracious owner for 30 minutes about a variety of things - differences between SF and NOLA spumoni ice cream, post-Katrina NOLA rebuilding, and, uh, some other stuff (did I mention I was drinking?  I find waking up in NOLA works better with just a splash of bourbon).

We arrived at 5, before the dinner rush, and enjoyed attentive service. The ambiance is that which allows one to be dressed up or down and not feel out of place in either form.
 We ordered a large cheese pizza, house salad, and Caesar salad. 
 The pizza was good but nothing that blew my mind. Yes it was simple but if the sauce is right and the ratio of sauce to cheese is as well then a regular cheese CAN blow your mind... Personally I would have enjoyed a pizza from Costco more.
 The salads were well portioned, can't r ally go wrong there.

Stars are more for the service than Anything else
In my opinion, they have the best Mediterranean food in the area.  The inside is a little old fashioned but they keep it very clean. The staff are always friendly and helpful.

More Poke in indianapolis is always a good thing! At Moar you fill out your custom order on a little sheet and turn it in at the counter.  I loved my passion fruit black tea with mango jellies. I ordered the rice bowl with spicy tuna, pickled radish, eel sauce, seaweed salad, and fried onions. My major issue was that the tuna was shredded instead of pieces like other poke I've had. The consistency was gooey. My other thought is that if you're new to poke and not sure what you like, this style of ordering could be intimidating and maybe result in a bad order. I wish they had a couple of house bowls that you could order and know the toppings went well together.

What an interesting place to be. Local and organic ingredients and quirky decor make for an interesting visit. Love the menu of interesting combinations of flavors. A bit "up-scalish" but I feel out of place being casual :) This place is definitely is on my list for the next date night.

Visiting Nashville for work and needed a place to watch "El Clasico" . Google it. When I went to closest place to where I was staying at, although ok was definitely not a soccer game type of place. I saw Fleet Street Pub come up and so grateful it did! It was about a 20min walk but the day was perfect for it. The place is downstairs so cell service is pretty non-existent.  They have Wi-Fi but it wasn't showing up so you'll be away which works out! The match was a joy to watch there as the server Coree was super nice and attentive. She even put the sound on which makes such a huge difference. I got lucky to find some real fans, Erin and Nikki. Liverpool and Borussia Dortmund respectively but they wanted to watch this big game. No specials but good choices for beer drafts. I got the Blackhorse IPA (although not an IPA fan) and its flavor was delicious. They went with Guinness and coffee. Overall a great vibe and I'd go back! Too bad no games from now until I leave but next time. Check it out. They do serve food as well.

Four stars  for our nice waiter- Wes. Otherwise - yuk. Went for the Monday crab special. Had to return the first one because it was old and gray. Ick. Next one was okay but still old crab. Will not go back. By the way- my son's cheeseburger was great. So maybe you should order that. Very nice atmosphere and good wine.
The coffee cake is unbelievably delicious ! Best part of the meal. Coffee comes in a very large mug, and the omelette was huge! It was also very good. Was my first visit and would definitely return!

Out first stop on our Southside vacation was WEM. We arrived right at lunch time and choose here simply due to the fact they had a deal for a meal and a movie. Basically you could order any entree and get a movie ticket for $9.

The Old Spaghetti factory is located near the doors on Bourbon Street. It's a cute Italian eatery that include soup or salad, a loaf of sour dough bread with butter, and a bowl of neopolitan ice cream with every entree order. Score.

Our waiter was awesome and gave us great service.  I ordered the the seafood marinara dish and my husband had the seafood linguine with alfreado sauce. We both thoroughly enjoyed our dishes. We also really enjoyed the sourdough bread. It was warm and soft with a crispy crust and the garlic butter took it to a higher level.

Overall If your looking for some classic Italian eats this place will definitely give you that. Nothing too fancy just classic comfort food that will definitely fill you up.

Don't bother coming here to eat. Takes way too long took over an hour to get food and it wasn't even busy. Definitely not worth it. Peyton needs to check up on this because it wasn't impressive. Thanks for the waste of time.

Very good portion size for the money. Had the curry chicken which was $6.75 and I was given two very large pieces of chicken, a sizeable portion of rice and beans, plantains and cabbage. Everything tasted great. Highly recommend if you're looking for a cheap Caribbean meal.

So it's nothing too exciting to look at, inside or out but their food is good. 

I've been here quite a few times for breakfast and the Bloody Mary bar. I'm a sucker for a good Bloody Mary, and they have a great Bloody Mary bar. They have all the fixings which helps make a bloody go from good to great. Now don't miss understand, they don't have over the top stuff like mini burgers and chicken fingers coming put of the Bloody Marys or even bacon but the do have an assortment of olives and various pickled veggies and spices to add. Delish!

On my last stop for brunch, I had the eggs Benedict and my friend had the chicken and waffles. My eggs Benedict was good, I would definitely order it again. My only complaint was that the potatoes were over cooked which made them a little dry. That was the same issue with the chicken and waffles, great flavor but it was over cooked which made the chicken a little tough. We asked for extra maple syrup gravy and that fixed the problem and it was really tasty.  My breakfast has always been good, this is the first time I has items that were over cooked. 

I'll be back, great service, the food is usually pretty good and the Bloody Marys are tasty.  :-)

What is it with people and this place? We had a 20 minute wait outside when it was spitting rain and when we got inside the restaurant was only half full.  Making people wait outside when they're hungry only works for optics for so long. 

Sure, the fried chicken is good but the sides are terrible.  They actually served me canned peas (!) and the mashed potatoes were pretty mediocre.  The waiters were clunky and dropped things on the floor multiple times making loud slamming noises and it took way too long for our food to come out.

There are other places to eat fried chicken that treat their patrons better.  Next time I won't be back.

I came to El Rey who suggested this restaurant upon finding out the wait time for El Vez was over an hour. This restaurant is a more casual relaxed version of El Vez where you can still get your Mexican food fix at a better price too! You know you're getting quality because the same restauranteur Stephen Starr behind El Vez is the creator of this little gem too. 

I tried out the happy hour menu this time around and was not disappointed. I had a steak taco , a chicken taco and a fish taco ($1 each) with a side of empanadas and nachos. I liked the tacos and chicken empanada but the nachos were very underwhelming and I wouldn't recommend you try and instead opt for another taco or empanada. The horchata was good and refreshing and the tamarind drink quenched my thirst. Being of Mexican blood, I am a harsh critic when it comes to my Mexican food and overall the food was delicious, however not spectacular, and worth it for the price! 

Definitely a great place to come get your happy hour on!

One of our lunch staples. Great, unique sandwich selection. Price is competitive. Outdoor dining is great in milder weather, it's fun to watch watch the traffic, both foot and vehicular. Dinner oyster platter was HUGE and well worth the money.
The Green Pig was amazing! Also had 3 different tacos that were ok but for the price would not buy them again.

A group of us went there for the first time tonight.  We ran the gamut from New Yorkers to Puerto Ricans o Southerners and everyone enjoyed every single thing.  I am fairly sure that, between us all, we tried almost everything on the menu and everything was delicious!!!  My favorites were hands down the watermelon apple slaw and the cornbread.  We also sampled the cheese grits, greens, fried pickles, fried green tomatoes, fried catfish, brisket, ribs, desserts.... There was not one complaint and everyone agrees that this is one of the best restaurants in Tampa.
The food here is delicious! Brought a brit with us and he said the breakfast reminded him of home. Whenever we visit Philly we try and have a meal here, it does not disappoint.

I venture in Harry and David every time I'm at the outlets. I love the "foodie" type gifty things. There are many unusual things to choose, but I tend to window shop.  On my last visit there was an array of every kind of Moose Munch you can imagine, so I enjoyed the samples! That stuff is dangerously delicious!  Also they were sampling the Red Velvet coffee. It was ok. 

What we were blown away by though was the smell of the Banana Cream coffee in the bag. I felt if it tasted 1/5 as good as the smell I would be in heaven.  It was steeply priced at 13.99. They were running a special, 2 bags of whole bean coffee for 22$. We caved, bought that and the Toasted Coconut Vanilla. The coffees did not disappoint. The banana is the most scrumptious flavor I've ever tried and I've tried them all. I am a coconut fiend and while I liked the coconut, the Banana Cream was theeee star!

The staff was very kind and friendly. They told us they offer samples of everything in the store- no matter what! We were chatting with the staff and they were so personable & very enthusiastic of Harry & David!

Starbucks ain't got nuthin on Harry & David's incredible coffee creations

With all the blogger attention on this place I was really excited to check it out. Unfortunately it let me down though. I came with my parents who are not from a larger city and so to them $12 for a drink is pretty outrageous. I definitely felt they should be more around the $10 range but also if they are going to be priced like that they need to be good. They were just ok. Food was the biggest issue we had. I ordered the nachos which I was extremely happy with but my moms order came out wrong and the kitchen took so long by the time they brought it out we were already done eating and told them we didn't even want it anymore. The waitress then asked my dad if he wanted a box for his leftover fried seafood platter but all that was left on his plate was the breading. Literally there was so much breading on the items it looked like the actual food hadn't been touched after he picked out the actual pieces of fish and vegetables. I have never seen something so ridiculous and the manager mentioned she had issues with that and had a conversation with their chef about that dish before! Service was the biggest negative I heard about this place before going but our server was very personable. Bottom line, don't order the seafood platter and expect to pay too dollar for decent drinks.

I was so incredibly excited when I heard Shake Shack was coming to St. Louis. This was always a staple when I visited New York City and I didn't realized the founder had his roots right here in my city. I feel like they kept pretty tight lipped about the construction because all of a sudden it was already here! I waited in line the first day for an hour to have an early taste of glory. They kept us entertained in line with Bissinger's chocolates, strawberry mint lemonade, and custard. I ordered a single cheeseburger, the mound city double (special St. Louis burger), cheese fries, a Christmas cookie shake, and the local Pie O'My pecan pie concrete. The prices are more upscale than most burger joints at $30 for two people but when I tasted my meal it was well worth it! I can't wait to come back (and not wait an hour next time).

Absolutely AMAZING food! My boyfriend got the sushi roll and he said it was the best sushi he has every had. I ordered the tavern burger and added egg which was so good! (Make sure you get the bacon jam on the burger.) prices are higher than their other restaurant down the street (corner pub) but the atmosphere and what not are a little more high scale. first time here and we will Definitely Be back!

Ordered a large pizza with pepperoni, sausage and ham with 2 20 oz. cokes. Placed my order online at 8:02 PM and it arrived to my hotel at 8:35 PM by David. Pizza was quality , delicious and very filling. The online app was user friendly and the service was professional, friendly and quick. Very satisfied overall with this location and experienced no problems and issues. Great job Dominos!
My food took 30 minutes to arrive with cold toast. Meals took 3 times to arrive properly and the manager was not friendly. Avoid this restaurant at all cost and visit a locally owned restaurant.

This place has amazing customer service. Be patient because they are working on perfection. Every dish I've had from here has been amazing and im a local. We live right here in Ybor city. The customer service from our bartender/server and the management team was wayyyyy above and beyond! We will forever be faithful to this company and welcome them to ybor with open arms!

Food was crappy. Blooming onion was burnt to a crisp. Chicken sandwich was ok but the pickles were off. Weird sour taste. Staff was very nice. Place was kinda dirty. Doubt I would go back. Better choices nearby. Not worth what you pay.

Amazing atmosphere and food! Waiters and host were also great and very helpful. We recommend the sangria and spaghetti and meatballs. But everything we got was tasty. Sitting outside by the bay was a little smelly, so we sat inside. Good portions for good prices.
awesome! super cute outdoor/open counter and seating. very nice staff and very tasty coffee!!!! loved it

The ravioli pizza is an indulgence my body can only handle about once a month. The ravioli is big, fluffy, and stuffed with ricotta cheese - which would be fine on it's own but on top of yummy, doughy, cheesey pizza - it's just all too much. It's usually served with a pink sauce, but it's all too much cream to withstand in one sitting so I always ask for plain tomato sauce on mine. Delish!
Food was great! Listen to your server... pancakes are BIG!! We had one whole left. Everything including price were great.
Tacos weren't as good as expected from reading reviews. Carne asada had no flavor. Duck tacos were good. But I found a couple small bones in mine. Drinks were good. Waitstaff ok.
Don't do it. 3 out of 6 orders were wrong. Taco Bell has better food. Server did her best but this place was a total waste of money.

100% obsessed! I took my fiancé here for his birthday and we loved it. Neither of us had been before but from the looks of the menu, I knew it would be great.

When we were sat at the table we were greeted right away from Raphael (?). He welcomed us and offered us something to drink. He was perfect. He definitely set the mood of the restaurant and for our dining experience.

Next we ordered some wine and cocktails. Our server was Brooks. He was very helpful in going through the menu and explaining the concept of sharing . I loved the idea of getting many items and trying them all. I know my fiancé does because I always end up eating whatever he orders. 

Anyways we ordered: 
-kale salad
-brussels spouts 
-cauliflower
-crab cakes
-hangar steak w/frites
-cheesecake beignets 

I would 100% order every again except for maybe the beignets. They were great but just a tad to sweet for me. So go try it out. The menu is large, the portions are large, and the service is great. I promise you won't be disappointed.

Tip: valet because parking is complicated

The food was SO great here. And the beer with a really awesome happy hour price! I highly recommend the friend zucchini appetizers (they're pretty unique) and the fish and chips. So good. The service was meh but I was overall happy with my experience here.

The chicken salad sandwich is absolutely horrible! It is tasteless,bland, and small. It's not worth the money. The customer service is atrocious and try got rid of the only good salad on the menu. Avoid at all costs!

First thing's first, this is an American-style diner run by a Korean.  I was always skeptical of Asian serving American food but this place has definitely changed my opinion.  The interior is small but cozy, it's also pretty quiet and private for a diner.  

I ordered a "breaded chicken sandwich" with lettuce, tomatoes, mayo, cheese and fried onion.  The chicken was very fresh and crispy, so were the lettuce and tomatoes.  I don't know what set this apart from the other sandwiches I've eaten but it was good.  The sandwich was a good size and was $4.99.

I've also ordered  "spicy chicken cheese steak" from this place, which was great, I ordered extra spicy with everything on it (green & red pepper, mushroom, fried onion, cheese, mayo, ketchup, hot sauce, buffalo sauce)  all for $5.95.  Note that their chicken are chunks instead of teared strips that you would normally find in cheese steaks.

OMG. We had the tacos al pastor, chicken tacos, guacamole, a pitcher of the house margaritas, 2 other margaritas and the cucumber margarita. The food was amazing. The prices were good. What a great way to spend a Saturday drinking on a patio. Can't wait to go back. The staff was so nice and attentive

If I could give this place a half star, I would, but the description of "A-Ok" doesn't quite do it for me. It seems a bit TOO positive.

When this location was Tapioca Express, I think the service was just a little better - the girl that NEVER smiles and is always rude was still working there (and still IS working there), but there were enough OTHER smiling faces to make up for it. My first impression of the place (I got a milk tea with large boba/tapioca balls) was that it was over priced. I remember getting these delicious drinks all of the time in San Francisco when I lived there, and not paying so darn much (and definitely not getting a drink with SO much ice, like I did here). Then I had to remind myself: They can have their prices higher, because they don't have competition in this silly little town of Reno.

When they switched over to Nam Van, I gave them another try. I saw a few of the same faces, but the service seriously dipped - no one ever smiled, people were rude and rushed you, they didn't care to give explanations for the rising prices if you were curious about some items going up while others didn't - they just didn't seem to care that you were there, and definitely didn't want to talk to you.

NOW it's right in between. The cranky girl is still there, lips forever pressed into a line and never allowing the smallest smirk to pass... but there are a few other employees that liven the place up.

The crepes are good, but boring and uneventful; the best thing about the crepes would be the smear of Nutella, which can be done at home on your own (if you know how to make crepes). The teas and snowbubbles are good, but if you ever ask for them to double blend the blended snows, you'll get dirty looks. The pho leaves a little to be desired in that the broth is either bland or too salty, but the ingredients that came out with mine the two times I got it seemed to be a bit fresher than other locations. The other items on the menu that I've tried (squid balls, fried tofu, spring rolls, spicy tofu, and a few other noodle dishes) are all tasty enough, but there's better entrees in the same shopping center at CJ Palace or whatever it is. The spring rolls seem VERY fresh, though - I will give them that. The peanut sauce, however, is runny and bland. Sad.

Unfortunately, due to the grump behind the counter and only a few things being something to write home about, this place will probably never get a three from me. It's good enough to stop in when someone else I'm with wants it, or if I get a hankering for boba, but I'd almost rather just wait for a road trip to SF.

Coming in on a late Sunday afternoon allowed me to avoid the brunch crowd and finally give Marlows a try. With it being a Sunday, they were only offering a limited brunch menu that didn't have a ton to choose from. 

The server mentioned their flatbread of the day and we ordered that for our appetizer. It contained chicken, bacon and some sort of cheese that I can't remember. The flatbread was listed as an appetizer with no price on it as it is price daily since it frequently changes. It came out, tasted great but surely wasn't worth $10. Sure, I could have asked how much it was and I still probably would have ordered it knowing it was $10, but I would have expected it to be a little bigger for the price we paid. 

We placed our entrée orders and they took longer than they should have to come out. My chicken and waffles were terrific. The fried chicken was fried lightly and the inside of it was juicy and flavorful. The waffle didn't lack size and the pecan syrup that came with it was rich. 

My girlfriend enjoyed her burger. One bite in and she realized that the cheese wasn't offered on the burger so she asked a server for a slice and she would just put it on the burger herself. The server was very nice and offered to melt it for her and she gladly declined. The cheese was $1.50 up charge, which is steep for a slice of cheese. 

From the time we received our bill until the time we walked out of the door took roughly 15 minutes. That's way too long. 

I liked the atmosphere at Marlow's. It seemed smaller on the inside compared to what it looked like on the outside. It doesn't feel like a chain establishment at all (even though it is) and there are tons of TVs all over to watch a sporting event if that's what you please.

Ordered a simple margherita pizza from Revolution House but wasn't expecting it to impress me!  There was something about the fresh mozzarella - it was distinctly rich yet light.  Picture drinking skim milk regularly, and then you take that first sip of whole milk...oohh...that's exactly what biting into this pizza felt like.  The mozzarella was exceptional and the star of the pizza.  I appreciate the thin yet chewy crust. The tomato sauce was savory and tangy, just to my liking. Topped off with fresh basil. Muah!! Itsa greata pizza!  Quality ingredients shining bright.

We sat out on the sidewalk on Pride Day in Philly.  Nice outdoor setting. The servers were nice and checked on us regularly. Good for a bite if you're in the area.
Best sandwiches in all of NOLA! Highly recommend clooneys choice or chicken parm. Salads are delicious as well!

I really do like this place! It was my first time here yesterday and even though I only went through the drive thru, I felt like a valued customer. I got the #1 (What a burger combo meal) and it tasted amazing. Why I've never been to this place, I don't know, but I will be here more often!
Friendly staff.  Great bagels.  Awesome breads and good coffee.  Plus a nive atmosphere.  Best Bagels in suburban Philly.  Love this place.

This is one of your better choices for quality Mexican food on the NW side of Tucson with excellent value. 
The beans are super terrific!
The down sides are the place is small and crowds up very fast so go early and the parking lot is tiny, beyond that its a great place.

This place is a little Italian heaven. Great selection of cheeses, meats, pre-made deli food (chicken cutlets, pasta salads, etc.), olives.. really, anything you'd expect to find in an Italian market. Prices are good, for the most part. I always stop in for fresh ricotta. Store bought can't even compare.

Awful experience here today. . I have been coming here for years and always stop by when I'm back in the area. I brought my husband here for the first time and unfortunately they totally ruined his experience. He ordered a turkey bacon ranch sandwich on a sesame bagel. AKA the "TBR" on the menu. The woman at the counter was totally competent of what he ordered. She is ALWAYS friendly and thorough (and has worked here for years!) As listed on the menu board , the TBR is turkey, cheddar, bacon, lettuce, tomato and ranch. The only modification he asked for was no tomato or lettuce. The sandwich came out with TURKEY BACON and ranch dressing ONLY on it. He is the kind of person that won't ever say anything about a food mistake but I could tell he was very unhappy and encouraged him to request the actual sandwich he had ordered. (Especially because we paid almost $8 for it) The woman from the front counter register came over to the sandwich makers in the back and clarified that my husband was right and asked them to remake it. The second sandwich then came out some time later with .. Wait for it .. Regular bacon, ranch dressing and tomatoes ONLY on an everything bagel (not sesame as he asked for). It was clear that whoever was working making sandwiches today (around noon) had no idea what was going on and what one of the sandwiches ON THE MENU contained. It wasn't even worth saying something a 2nd time. Our lunch break was over and we had to leave .. And quite frankly you just can't fix stupid. The only saving grace was the consistently sweet and helpful front counter woman and my sandwich being ok. However, I'll seriously reconsider any urge to go here again after today.

I got to go order from this restaurant oh my g that was delicious brisket so good cook and tender, sausage was the best I had in Reno and sides Mac and cheese was good traditional coleslaw was so good and not too much saucey for defenetly recommend this restaurant specialt in corona period because everybody stay in home.

I wanted to eat here for lunch but they decided that they didn't want to keep the hours that are posted on their website. 

Now I work in the restaurant industry, and I know how it goes. You've had a slow shift and you just want to close up shop and be done. This is the wrong thing to do. I belive you need to do everything in your power to make sure that anyone walking thru your door has nothing but good things to say about your business. 
The excuse that they keep "European" hour is retarded. 
So in short, this restaurant with a perfect 5 star status, receives it's first ONE star review. 
Fuck you very much!!
Best Mexican we've found this far. Food is always hot and fresh. Service is great. It's our go to place for good Mexican .

Recently Hana has really been dropping the ball. Many of their well-trained staff quit due to internal issues, leaving a new group of hires that aren't as well trained to handle everything. Even food quality hasn't been that great. Their boba is really mushy most of the time. I used to eat here very often, due to it being a cheap and convenient option. But I've noticed myself coming less because of the declining quality of this place overall. If you order any of the rice bowls, I strongly recommend ordering it with extra rice and veggies. It is free of charge and you get more from what you're paying!

Shoutout to the Elisa who always has a smile on her face and is a great worker!!

AMAZING. Perfect leopard pattern on the bottom, airy crust, tastes like it's been fermenting for days (just overnight). Great, high quality ingredients, too. Good service, fast-eating atmosphere (no seats makes it a slight drag). Feels classic and unpretentious. Five bucks for a pepperoni slice is worth it since it is the best pepperoni slice I've had in a long time. I'm definitely gonna keep coming back.

Don't bother...
Overpriced undercooked poached eggs Stanley not worth the $14. We went for the softshell crab Eggs Benedict, which aren't on the menu anymore. Had Eggs Stanley instead, which was Eggs Benedict with fried oysters on the side. Oysters were way overcooked- I grow my own oysters on Chesapeake Bay and know how a fried oyster should be. And there was effectively no sauce on the dish, just a runny drizzle of something that had no flavor. I guess butter and fresh lemon are too expensive?

I am surprised at all the rave reviews after having eaten at Malaga... well actually, we got our dinners to go. We had Mariscada Malaga and Mariscada Salsa Verde, suppossedly two of their best dishes, and my husband and I both attest that these dishes were simply uremarkable. What's more, my husband even asked for bread and was told that it was in the bag. It was, in fact, not. I have eaten at a number of Spanish and Portugese restaurants and Malaga ranks at the very bottom of my list with regard to the taste of the food. I will never go back and my advice to you is to eat elsewhere. Try instead Spain in Newark, or Ria Mar or Portugese Fisherman, both in South River.

Delicious! I have only ordered take out from here but have truly enjoyed it. The Malai Kebab is so delicately flavored in a yogurt marinade that it makes for a wonderful, light meal. Samosas are delicious.

Smokin' Betty's has been open for just over one week.  I've been anticipating this place for two reasons: my good friend Brooks is working here.  Secondly, I'm always looking for a good BBQ sandwich.  My friend Jess and I headed out to check out this new establishment.

Usually I like to talk about food and drink first, but I have to talk about atmosphere.  The inside of this place looks excellent.  It's just a cool looking spot.  It has two levels of seating, with a bar on both floors, and really has the capacity to be a hopping place, in terms of coolness and the sheer numbers I'm sure it will be packing in shortly (after my review is read).  I recommend grabbing a seat upstairs, especially a window seat if available.  The service is excellent.  I'm not just saying this because Brooks was my server; all of the servers tag-team the tables to make sure that everything is taken care of quickly and efficiently.

The menu is impressive.  It's much larger than ones I've seen at "real" restaurants in quite some time. There are different sections, with appetizers, small plates, entrees, soups, and salads represented.  Lots of choices.  There was even a small kids menu with a few choice under $5! Really, it's a great idea and basically unheard of outside of chains.  There's an small plate of three sliders featuring three different types of BBQ: great for the indecisive.  

I decided to just go for the beef brisquet BBQ.  It was a really good sandwich, but not the best I've had.  Plus there's enough other great things on the menu that I'd try first before I had this again.  One downside was the tiny side of macaroni salad, especially because it was pretty good.  I also had a side of onion rings which were standard, but good.

Smokin' Betties boasts sixteen taps which are arranged in order on the bar from dark to light in terms of the color it pours.  While this order is a bit arbitrary and has no effect on actual taste, style, or ABV; I like it.  It's better than nothing at all.  All the beers are American craft brews. While most of the beers are "safe bets" and not very adventurous, there is good diversity and a lot of solid choices.  I went with the Yellowtale Pale Ale from Ballast Point, which was good. An easy drinking, light pale ale.

Bottom Line:  This place was very slow when I went in, but I suspect it will only be another week or two before it gets busy.  It's a cool spot in a good location.  The menu is massive and packed with good choices.  The prices are decent and there's a few good beers to chose from.  It's not perfect, but it's definitely worth a try.  I'll check it out again in the future.

I'd had Famous Dave's ribs at both the Boy's and Girl's club fundraiser they hosted outside their new building several weeks ago and at the Ciopino Feed. Both times they were ah-may-zing! But tonight we got to try some of the rest of the menu. The result? Awesome. Amazing. Fantastic. And this was just take out!! 

We got the chopped pork with two sides. The chopped pork was perfectly prepared, with just enough sauce, and cooked to perfect smoky perfection. I spent years living in North Carolina and this rivals anything I've had there. Just excellent. The chopped pork came on a nice piece of toast, which had a great buttery flavor to mix with the pork. 

The chopped pork meal came with two sides. The first one I had was the mac & cheese, which was outstanding -- southern style m&c flavor with a jalapeno kick. Awesome! I also had the wilbur beans, which were great. They too had a nice kick to them. 

We also got a rack of ribs with two sides (fries - which were pretty good and cole slaw, which was good, but a bit sweet). The ribs were excellent and plentiful. We still have some left. Perfect fall off the bone goodness. I like that they let you add your own sauce rather than dousing them. That's a really nice touch, especially since my wife doesn't really like sauces. 

Both meals came with ears of corn (really good) and corn bread muffins. These muffins are amazing. I could eat them for desert they are so good. Little muffin sized pieces of heaven really! 

The process of getting our take out was easy enough. The cashiers processed the line reasonably quickly (especially given that this place has been open such a short time) and explained how the sides and what not worked. Our order only took about 15 minutes, which was great. They even went over the order with me to make sure everything was there, which is a nice touch. 

One quick note--I spent about 20-25 minutes in there between looking at the menu, ordering, and waiting for our grub. In that time I spent some time wandering about (the place looks great) and happened to hear the bell that was being rung and the response from the waitstaff. After reading the reviews, I was expecting this to be deafening. It certainly wasn't. This place was jam packed, and the patron noise combined with the bell / waitstaff were not that loud. The reviews whining about the noise are SO overblown. What are you people? 100? Turn down the hearing aids old timers!!! Its not that noisy!! 

Overall, this place was excellent, and an excellent value. We will be back and back often. I honestly can't imagine buying ribs or bbq anywhere else after this experience. Definitely the best in town!

So, I'm in love with the staff, first of all. So friendly & so much personality! 

The food is DELICIOUS! I've tried the pork al pastor taco, the carnitas taco, and the shrimp and chorizo taco. The carnitas were my hands down favorite, while my husband adores the al pastor. My only qualms with the al pastor is that the flavor is so strong that is overwhelms the delicate flavors of the cabbage & tomatoes on the taco. The chorizo & shrimp taco is just a little spicy for me, but I'm a wimp when it comes to spicy foods. 

I've eaten the steak enchiladas which were also super delicious, but would have benefitted from a little more enchilada sauce. There was virtually no red sauce to be found. Not sure if that's a California style preparation or not, but I love my red sauce. More please! 

This is totally a 5 star place. I'm docking a star because I called in my order, came up pick it up, got all the way home & realized that they didn't give me the rice and beans that I ordered AND paid for! Not cool. I'll be checking my bag before I leave from here on out!

Loved this place! We came here after a hockey game in the area and we were a big group. Our server was wonderful, the food was wonderful, and the prices were fair. If I'm ever in the area I will definitely come back.

I remember the old Deep Dish Dijornos pizza from the grocery store being better than this. Slathered  in sauce. I was not impressed. Decent service but could seat more people with better seating. Although the place had awesome ambiance. I literally crapped myself when I walked in my motel room.
Salad is pricey but I was impressed.
Very tasty and flavorful. nice atmosphere, super casual, steaks are really good. I got the lomo saltado and it was delicious !! Would go again !!

Looking for an alternative from chain stores like Starbucks, Einsteins, or Dunkin Donuts before going to Tampa Zoo we drove by this rustic neighborhood spot.  What a treat!  Fresh homemade American breakfast food, some with a Cuban slant.  Wife and I had egg sandwiches on Cuban bread with fresh cut veggies, son got eggs and bacon and toast and when cheese was added by accident they made the whole plate again for free, other son had fresh biscuits and sausage gravy. Topped it all off with a Cafe con Leche.  Delicious!

Though I was tired from a long day of work, I was peer-pressured into heading towards Philly's gem for high quality restaurants: South Philadelphia.

While Im not the biggest Italian fan out there, the staff and the food transformed Italian Cuisine into an artistry. I wouldn't be surprised if God himself blessed me by making the meal. You may not think it would be amazing, with its small menu and location on a suburban corner, but it turns out to be one of the strongest restaurants I've ever experienced for an extremely affordable price.
 
Inside this quaint, cozy establishment lies a kind and caring staff, attentive to every detail in our meal and in their service.

Beyond just being timely with treating us at our table, they truly cared about the food they served. When my meal came, the waiter asked us whether we wanted cheese and pepper flakes on our plate. Soon enough, he delicately added it with a spoon. Tap, tap, tap. With each sprinkle, I felt as if it was love he was truly pouring onto the pasta. 

Now, the meal itself. Gnocchi and Seafood Stufato.The bread had a nice crunchy flavor and was well-made, filling me up after the second serving. The sauce in the stufato had a flourish of spice that what entrenched in the flavor of the calamari and shrimp. But the masterpiece: Gnocchi. My mind flew around the world as I tasted the truffle mixed with the spinach-infused gnocchi with mushroom and cheese. Within 5 minutes (I actually checked the time between me taking a photo and eating), I found myself licking my fork and scraping the plate to get the taste again. My mouth, salivating for more, kept telling me: "I'll be back or else I'll be making the worst mistake of my life." I cannot tell you have difficult it would be to describe how beautiful this dish was - Shakespeare would even be loss of the right words.

Come here. I swear it'll be worth it.

I really like Seamus for several reasons. 

1. They are great family-owned, neighborhood place. They take care of the people in the neighborhood and are a staple of everything Dogtown. 

2. The service is friendly and reliable. Every time I've been in there (which is a lot), I have been treated really well.

3. Beer selection: I love all of the drafts on tap. 

4. The food. I really like their steak sandwich and their wings. Their burgers are well-known, but I don't usually get them as I find them to be just ok.

To be honest I'm not sure why there was a lot of people sitting here. I think it's a popular & loyal spot for most of the bikers that ride in the area, but personally I wouldn't be back. The staff was VERY nice, nothing wrong with them at all. Everyone had masks on doing their part. However, what kind of dimmed my experience was when my table ordered a Spinach Dip appetizer and the Calamari. It came out, and I literally laughed out loud. It was basically a GIANT plate of chips that were definitely sitting in a bag somewhere (not warm or salted at all) and a SMALL .. and I mean SMALL container of Spinach Dip. The Dip was the same size as the dipping container for the calamari. It was absolutely humorous. For what the bill came out to, I was expecting a lot more with my order OR for it to at least be better. I could have purchased that at the grocery store and made it at home to be honest. It tasted like one of the spinach dips that comes in a frozen box. I was definitely disappointed with it.
