We didn't even order any more food cause if thats how the apps came out we were pretty fearful of what the rest was gonna look like. The calamari was also nothing to remember. Pretty much had no flavor and wasn't really that crispy or hot when it came to the table. I had the Key Lime Pie martini too, it was okay however it wasn't shaken long enough so I was biting pieces of ice as I was trying to drink it. Flavor was good but please shake that bad boy longer and harder! Lol 

Also, if you dont smoke cigarettes and hate the smell of cigarettes at the dinner table DONT go here. They allow smoking in the sidewalk section but all of the cigarette smoke from people blows directly back into the restaurant. Listen, Ive also smoked cigarettes for a solid 10 years of my life now and I still don't wanna smell no damn cigarette while I'm trying to eat a meal .. so I can only imagine what a non-smoker would feel like trying to eat here. Not to mention we were sat at a table that was in direct sunlight, so I was sweating the entire time as I was trying to enjoy any part of my meal and was basically blind from the sun. I know that they can't really help that the sun exists, I get that, but there was a couple of other tables open that they could've sat us. I understand most waiters are on rotation, I used to serve myself so I understand it doesn't always work like that, but I do feel as if they could've sat us at another table given the amount of tables that were open instead of sitting us directly in the sunlight on a hot day. 

Overall ... You can tell the place needs a boost. I do not blame the staff or anything. And I also don't blame the chef for how my spinach dip came out, I'm sure it has everything to do with management at the end of the day because that's usually the true issue behind everything in most restaurants. Please remember to tip well and big at this time. I just had to leave an honest review on my experience.

Friendly Baristas
Great environment
Excellent coffee
A passion for education
Great location.
A phenomenal check-in deal. 

There is plenty to brag about in this place. They've nailed it with ambiance and they are doing some great roasting in the back. Ask some questions and get connected. You won't regret it.

Our dinner was soooo delicious and our waiter (Jentzen) was exceptional! 
We'll be back!

There's always an appealing factor of a restaurant when you see outdoor seating in a Plaza and this was the case with Sab Cafe! I never got a chance to glimpse the inside of the restaurant because it was a beautiful day to sit outside. They have about 5 to 6 tables outside, located in the DTSP promenade across from the water.

BEEF FLANK PAD THAI $17: 4.5/5 (The go to noodle dish that never disappoints. Made with rice noodles, eggs, in sprouts, green onions and crushed peanuts). I feel like every restaurant makes their own unique Pad Thai sauce that is different compared to others. I know I have had a slightly better sauce compared to what they presented, but the Pad Thai sauce that was presented was a close second and I'd gladly come back. A lot of people believe the Pad Thai sauce is too thick ,but I disagree because there's nothing more disappointing than a thin layer of Pad Thai sauce that doesn't cover all of the noodles and it was the perfect amount! The sauce was the right amount of spiciness and we asked for American medium/hot and it was spciy, definitely had both of us gulping down on water. I recommend getting the Chicken for $15 compared to $17 for the Beef Flank. I advise saving a couple bucks and going with the Chicken instead and it probably would have tasted better as well! I would have liked the dish better if the Beef Flank was cooked a little less, making it more tender and appealing. 


TOM YUM CHICKEN $4: 3.5/5 (Hot and sour soup with your choice of chicken , tofu, veggie, and shrimp): There were a lot of veggies in the soup and I loved that aspect but very little chicken. You can choose premium choices like Shrimp for $5/cup but I advise sticking with the lesser expensive meat. Again, I know I've had better Tom Yum Chicken and would have liked a thicker brother with more of these flavors that are traditionally included in the soup: lemongrass, garlic, galangal/ginger, fish sauce, shrimp paste, etc. And prefer a soup with stronger flavor profiles. 

We really enjoyed our time here and loved sitting out in the patio area as the breeze blew away pesky mosquitos and the overcast day made it even more of a reason to sit outside on such a nice day. There's a lot of great restaurants in DTSP, but this will be one of my go to stops because the Beef Pad Thai flavors were tasty, really good and had great spices!

I flew into Philly from NH and the one thing I wanted was an Italian hoagie. The ones up in New England just pale in comparison. I spent a lot of time researching it on Yelp and ultimately ended up picking Sarcone's even though it was a pretty far walk (1.3 miles each way) mostly because they say "it's about the bread" because that is what I tell everyone up north. I have to say I'm a little disappointed and primarily due to the bread!

Most good Italians hoagies I've had have a thin chewy crust. This one had a thick hard crush that was hard to bite into and crumbled in flakes as I bit. Plus it was covered in sesame seeds which I'm not so sold on. The meat was good but at $9.99 for a medium the value was lacking.

It was a good sandwich but a bit of a disappointment given the effort to get it and the number of other options I walked past to get there.

Wow! What an extraordinary experience watching this restaurant outstandingly serving their customers. First, the food was wonderful. My wife and I wanted a light meal and ordered two 
Italian Wedge salads and they were  the best ever. Our server Kyle was so exceptional, you would have to go there to see what I mean. The entire staff is so friendly and the Manager, Austin, came by and discussed how they were able to satisfy customers take out needs during the shut down. This guy has some personality and should be promoted up the chain. But the most impressive thing I saw, except for the martini I had, was the way a young lady by the name of Amiah went about her chores sanitizing tables and chairs. She cleaned everything, table tops , bases and pedestals as well as the floors around the tables.  Very impressive. I complimented her on the way out and she said the management just wants to keep the customer safe. So go there have an epic meal, relax and enjoy the food and staff.

I stopped in here to meet a couple of friends for happy hour. I lived in Germany so I like trying German themed places. I went for the Bratwurst small plate and a glass of Lager. My bill was $7.95. I told the bar tender that I thought there was a mistake and he didn't charge me for one of the items. He said it's half price for happy hour. It would have been a good deal at the regular price. I felt a bit guilty paying only $7.95. The wurst was tasty and authentic. The garnishes were good too. German style sauerkraut and pickles. I was happy.

Fresh ingredients. The pesto egg sandwhich was pretty good. Not worth adding on the greasy hashbrown patty (and coffee) for $3.  The pancakes were nothing special, a little chewy.  For S8 you get three small pancakes, which was perfectly filling.  The kids split an order.  The brookie (chocolate cookie) was good, but not great. 

What I love is that they offer smoothies without yogurt or dairy.  I would just try one of those next time.  Great location right downtown with outside patio seating.

The 50/50 is the bomb. I've tried one or two of the other sandwiches and they're great too, but nothing beats the 50/50. I always go here with a plan to try something new and every time I end up getting the same delicious sandwich. The staff is friendly, the food comes out fast, and I'm always satisfied.

Of course, I had to go here for the muffeletta  sandwich. It was noon on Saturday and there was no line. A whole muffeletta cut into fourths was 14 bucks.  One quarter would satisfy any normal person (I had two).  One of the best deals in the city.

Go to this gas station and order the catfish poboy. Call me and thank me later. Get a half if you're one person...have them cut it in half. It was soooo much food! The fish was crispy and seasoned well. The wheat bread was delicious for the sandwich for those trying to get away from the French bread. Go forth and save a couple carbs and calories. 

Order at the console, pay at the register, pick up your post boy all in under 5 minutes.  Yumtastic!

You walk in and you get a wonderful aroma of old people it's so refreshing.  Nothing better than smelling the aroma of old people while enjoying an omelotte with pubic hair...simply ravishing!  If you haven't gotten the sarcasm here it is bluntly this place SUCKS!!!  Honestly I am saddened by the fact that so many people think this is good.  Please visit First Watch to understand what good breakfast is.  Also their French toast isn't horrible but in no way compares to the best that crown remains at Cracker Barrel.

This place used to be good but on 12/11/20 I ordered a cheese steak and old bay fries with ranch dressing and I was up from two o clock till the next day with food poison my stomach was aching and I thew up . Never again it seems like every since covid-19 everyone is cutting back on their food and quality of there food and the delivery driver was not friendly at all. So buyer beware of this place. I was a great customer until this happened and I will let everyone know how bad this place is. Do not go here I was in bed for two days dealing with this they use to be good do not know what happened zero stars and I was not going to leave a comment for this place but I had to warn everyone about this place.
Loved this place when it was in Fishers as EMiracle and today ate at the new Miracle in Carmel.  It was wonderful as always and plan to go back as often as I can.

I enjoyed my food! I got the fried catfish with Mac n cheese and green beans. Good catfish, but it was a lil salty for my taste, but flavorful. Mac n cheese was good, but 2 much black pepper. Green beans were very good! They gave me a roll...not good...dry and hard. I also bought a piece of lemon cake...pretty good. I will return.

Sorry Eagle. This place is not good. Thai basil was swimming in sugary sauce. The brown rice was mush. Sushi quality was hidden in sesame oil. Drinks were meh. Will not be giving these guys anymore of my money.

Welp, I've found my new favorite thai restaurant in the Circle City, knocking Bangkok to second place. 

I came here with coworkers on a weekday during lunch. The lunch specials menu is actually quite extensive. The best part: you can get meats, tofu, or just veggies as your protein in each dish - that leaves a TON of vegan/vegetarian options. 

We were immediately seated, as we came around 11:45am. The interior is very nice and classy feeling. Our host seated us and we were greeted for drink orders very quickly afterwards.

I ordered the Massaman curry with tofu, medium spice. Honestly, you get so much food. You get a nice starter bowl of soup. We then got a nice portion of rice, a large bowl of the curry, a simple salad (topped with a phenomenal, mouth-watering mustard-based dressing), and also a spring roll with dipping sauce. LOTS of food, especially for the price of less than $10 per person. I also ordered a plain iced tea, and for some reason, it was even better than a normal tasting black iced tea. 

Overall, a delicious place. I'll have to get back to try it during normal dinner hours to see how it compares, but its lunchtime menu and service blew us all out of the water.

As a giant fan of craft beer I'm excited to have a place with over 100 beers on tap right by my apartment! Awesome selection, including great local brews. Also got the short rib sliders and they were BOMBBB so yum, will definitely be back. I only gave it a 4 instead of a 5 bc they were slightly understaffed, but understandable as it's literally their first night open.

This is a cool place to visit. Old wood, lots of interesting pictures and decor hanging on the walls, with a main floor, upstairs, and bar seating options. 

They have a LOT of great beer choices, especially for craft beer lovers! The food is more like pub food but is also very good. You really can't go wrong with anything on the menu. The hot brown, tenderloin, and buffalo chicken sandwiches are fantastic. The fried Mac n' cheese is a must! 

The service is descent (I've been several times and sometimes it's great, sometimes it's OK...but the beer and food options make up for it!) and the place is kid/family friendly. 

Definitely recommend for a relaxed environment.

I've been super mindful of what public-facing employees deal with during the pandemic, but every now and then, you run into an employee who is just doing it all so wrong. In this case, my son and I went up to WingStop in the late afternoon, and it was set up for take-out only, understandably. There were two parties ahead of us, waiting, and one group had yet to order and was growing impatient. There was a crew in the kitchen of about 3, and two more employees came in around 5 p.m. The manager was sitting just out of reach, toying around on an iPad, in the area that was once the dining room. 

The customer ahead of us who had not ordered yet, challenged the manager. "Why aren't you helping up here?" The manager claimed that the business was not set up that way for her to help: she didn't have a register login. The customer persisted: "You could help pack orders, or get people their beverages?" The manager was polite, but ridiculous, and said, "I'm sorry, it doesn't work that way." Honestly, who knows what she was doing: she could have been playing Angry Birds, but she could have been making schedules or communicating with her corporate overlords, but really, whatever she was doing could have have waited until a less busy time. What manager puts computer work above customers? 

Two more groups came in to order, and two DoorDashers came in to pick up orders, and the manager continued to sit. The tension was palpable. Everyone just waited. And waited. And waited. I asked my son if he wanted to bail, but he explained that he had watched a TikTok video review of the establishment and the TikTokker said it was worth the wait.

The same frustrated customer addressed the manager again: "You're telling us you can't do a single thing to help?" The manager replied, "Thank you for your comment."

I could see there were a couple of cooks, along with a young lady who started getting beverages and packing napkins and such into the bags that were starting to come up front. But the star of the evening was a very harried young man who handled a little bit of everything on the front end: dispatching the orders to the Dashers, taking orders, assisting the cooks, making sure everyone had straws and napkins, and patiently explaining the sauce and spice options to anyone who had questions.

He was a thoughtful and impressive kid and is the reason why this place gets 3 stars instead of 2; if it were not for the manager, this would be a 5 star review, for the type of establishment it is. My son ordered wings with a spicy rub, and I went for the tenders glazed with Korean bbq sauce. We both got fries and a drink to complete the meal.

It did take a looong time to prepare the meal, and because we would have to use Olden Avenue during rush hour to get home (a congested unpleasantry even during the Plague Era), we opted instead to head over to TCNJ where we found an open picnic table behind Brewster dorm (where I lived for two years, many moons ago). It was such a nice night and I'm sure my newly-minted teenage son only tolerated my tales from the Lakeside dorms...and The Pit...but he tolerated them without fuss, and a bit of wing sauce smudged on his face. He said they were some of the best wings he ever had. 

My boneless meal was a perfect blend of sweet and spicy, a lovely marriage of garlic and ginger, and the fries provided a delicious carb-y base to sop up all the sauce. 

We were very happy with the food and have talked about going back again some time soon. We definitely will, and I will do so with the hopes of bumping WingStop up a star or two. Hopefully management gets it act together.

For starters the food was great. We ordered about 6 dishes and finished it before I could get a picture. Prices are low and fair. It is quite obvious that they are very short staffed. Two people up front and one cook bringing food. That being said, they did an excellent job running the whole restaurant. I saw a few issues where the two up front could come across as rude to some. However, they have no time to put up with people's petty complaints while running the place alone. I see it as completely fair, please treat your servers kindly, even if they are stressed. Lets also say they handled a hard situation with a solicitor very well, they kept him as close to the door as possible and honestly it took me a while to even notice the situation. Please be patient with food workers, and they did everything  professionally.

Great service as well as beautifully displayed baked goods. I bought a strawberry chocolate cake for my mother's birthday from here recently that was the hit of the party (not overly sweet but with distant flavors that did not taste artificial and it was beautifully decorated with a chocolate card) This is my new go to place for sweets!

It had been several years since I had been here, so I asked what I should order, considering I prefer my entrees not to be sweet, at all.  I was encouraged to get Chili Cheese Étouffée and Chipotle Alexio.  Both were excellent!  I will be back.  I also enjoyed a praline, as well.

Large venue and it was extremely packed and loud.  However, I had no problem getting to the bar and ordering a thirst quenching draft.  Two sizes of drafts were offered.  I opted for the more manageable small opposed to the behemoth sized mug growler.

Aside from the nice selection of draft beers, the food was delicious.  I ordered The Kanzler burger medium rare.  The burger was juicy; the balsamic onion and gruyere cheese added depth of flavor and the bacon top it off perfectly.

I sat at a table enjoying my drink and burger and, for shits and giggles, engaged in a game of jenga with my homie.

Good Times!
Food isn't that great. Bar is a little pricey. Should have went to the restaurant down the hallway. Nachos are awful. Not a good place.

Food was excellent and Freddie, our server, did a phenomenal job offering suggestions for what we might want to enjoy for breakfast! He has an infectious personality and checked on us an appropriate amount of times! Would definitely recommend this place if you are visiting! Side note: definitely join the yelp waitlist to cut your time in line shorter. It's a popular place for a reason!

Can I say cockadoodledoo on this site? Because that's exactly what I wanted to do after trying out Rooster for the first time. Cheesy, you say? I think not. Come on. How many really cool AND good breakfast/lunch spots have we really got? If you found one you liked, you'd want to sing about it too...

For the longest time, my only option for sating the gnawing hunger for a crepe was to be found at City Coffeehouse. Still love the place, but every girl needs a new adventure.

This place is tiiiiiiiny, but kind of like a music box you cherish. You always hold it close and don't care if it's just this little box only a barrette could fit into. You could listen to its music all day.

And I could eat every one of the crepes on the menu. My favorite, though, is the one with liquor poached cherries and melty chocolate. Now that I'm rollin sugar free, though, I'll take the roasted sirloin #3 with mushrooms, asiago and caramelized onions. Dear god!

The real icing on the proverbial sugar free cake, though, is the B.E.L.T. I'm a sucker for a good BLT, but one with an overeasy egg stuck inside, whose yolk runs like a golden sunset and whose skin is seductively crunchy....whose lightly greased surface melds with the bejeweled bacon, french kissing on its way down your mouth. Roosters everywhere are jealous they don't lay eggs.

Stopped by Eddie and Sam's on a Saturday afternoon. Location makes it a little more challenging for parking because who wants to park in the city lot across the street, pay an extra $10 just to eat pizza. Great location for business lunches during the week. We had a large group (around 20-25 people) and they accepted our call ahead. 4 Stars for overall experience. No one directed us to the counter to order- we just figured it out. It could have saved us 15 minutes and some confusion which is always useful when dining with a large group of kiddos. The garlic knots were the size of a softball. Pizza slices were huge and while I don't normally believe that bigger is better, this place delivers. The pizza was absolutely delicious.

Unbelievably happening place, with good reason! Their pitcher of premium margarita is served with glasses rimmed with orange salt! Delicious! And I can say that their tacos are some of the best that I've ever tasted, with the exception of their shrimp taco... the shrimp IS the best that I've ever enjoyed! This is coming from a SoCal woman who knows her fine street tacos! We look forward to returning... soon!

Wow !!  Had to wait for 1 hour for food after ordering ... Then had to request the waiter 3 times ... Finally we caught a different waiter, who said that it would take a other 7 mins .. It took another 20 mins for the food to come ...

The way food is meant to taste, this cafe/restaurant is a hidden gem. I literally struck gold all foods are farm fresh and you can taste it didn't know how flavorful nature could be until eating at The Turning Point. I had the Tropical Crunch who would have ever thought mango goes with waffles. It's a must try on my list

Giving one star for the mediocre food and another star for Groupon's good deal of $16 for two. Otherwise, bad service, extremely disorganized, not sure who is the server who is the receptionist. Waited 20 mins for our salsa and chips which came with our entree, defeats the purpose of an "appetizer".  Also, chips and salsa has ZERO SALT. Ordered the Blackened shrimp taco and nutty streak taco. The steak one is okay, but the shrimp taco is plain and flavorless. WOULD NOT RETURN.

I tried the 3-course brunch. turtle soup with sherry, catfish and bread pudding.
Everything is yummy! And the waitress recommended the biscuit as side, it smells good.

I haven't been to Brick & Brew for awhile but popped in for lunch with some friends today.  The menu looked great and the 3 of us ordered 3 different salads.  I had the Calamari salad which was delicious and had a yummy lemon dressing.  My friends had the Burrata salad and the Roasted Pear salad and they loved theirs as well.  

In a time where many restaurants are struggling to find help, we had wonderful service from our our servers, Danielle and her trainee Jen.  They helped us with our salad choices, provided us with water on the table and were just the right amount of attentive! 

Thanks Brick & Brew, We'll be back!

Came here for a birthday dinner with 11 guests. The service was snotty and they didn't work with me at all with the bill or bringing my own wine. Considering the $20 corking fee, they would have made a lot more money if they would have allowed my 6 bottles of wine, instead everyone had one glass since the cheapest bottle is $36. Friends had the Travelzoo voucher and they were treated poorly, even though I had called in advance to make sure it was ok to use it. $55 cake cutting fee is a little over the top, too. Won't be having any more big parties here! Staff needs to lighten up. I have to give credit to the food though, it was really good.

Last nights Dinner consisted steamed broccoli, old bay jumbo shrimp , Lemon butter garlic mussels, and Hot and spicy garlic Snow crab legs . Our server was very nice and very attentive. The security guard was very friendly and very open to our opinions and to even make jokes with me am I companion. However, I was asked to turn my hat  forward due to a dress code policy. I must say I was having a great time until I was asked of this. Really make me feel uncomfortable and out of place just when I was feeling very welcomed and happy to be there. I would like to visit this place during the summer hours to see how it is, and this time I won't wear a hat smh.

My boyfriend and I wanted to have a nice night out with our pups and wanted to come here because we heard good things and it was on our pub pass that we purchased. Unfortunately, because of the pandemic, we were not able to use our 2020 pub pass for most of the year and we still had the independent left on our pass. We called the independent ahead of time to see if we could use our 2020 pass still (even though it was January 2021) and they said yes that is fine so we were very excited! When we pulled up and finally found parking (parking is very limited), found a table, and sat down, they proceeded to tell us that we could not use our 2020 pub pass despite us calling an hour before and confirming that we could. We explained this to them and they did not care and told us we cannot use it. They also told us that where we were sitting was "not allowed" despite other people sitting and drinking there before us. I really wanted to sit and enjoy our time there but the experience left a bad taste in my mouth and I don't think we will be returning.

We didn't realize the menu here includes wraps, sandwiches, burgers and other appetizing choices as well as thier main attraction: wings! The place is spotless, bright and vibrant with very attentive service. Our handmade potato chips can definitely become habit-forming. The wings were hot and perfectly prepared, along with your choice of about 50 sauces from fruity mild to insanely scorching. Just a fun atmosphere with very good food for all aboard.

Very annoyed that every time I come through now it's a big deal to get extra chicken ON my cob salad. At first it was no problem I didn't even have to explain how to ADD CHICKEN TO A SALAD, then it turned into ME explaining to the order taker how to put my order in their system. Then it turns into "oh let me go ask a manager" all I want is chicken ON my salad, it's really that hard? Then my most recent visit yesterday apparently the manager said that I must be coming during night shift and the night shift managers do things differently. I DIDNT KNOW THATS HOW CHICK FIL A RAN THINGS. I pay to come to chick fil a for the SERVICE, for the chicken ON my salad. So please get your managers together and come up with a solution for this chicken on salad bs because it's not good for your business to have managers just doing whatever they want.

This was the best pizza ordering experience I've ever had...

Super fast delivery
Picture perfect food
Awesome cheat night
The women who seats you is a royal bitch. She's nasty to everyone. I'm done going there till they hire a decent person who doesn't through your bill back at you.
The food was very good. We sat at the bar and were attended to greatly. Def plan to go back as soon as possible.
Never worked soo hard for such little meat. I see why they serve the wings in dog bowls, because dogs eat bones. Never again.

They've got some great deals, but I'm sick of finding stuff in my food. Two years ago, it was a piece of zip tie in my soup. Last year, it was a hair in my buffalo dip. (Might I add that 2 bites in, we found the hair and sent it back, all they did was discount the dip 50%, so we still paid $5 for literally one bite of dip each.) And now, my to-go pizza has hair in it. I don't know what they've got going on back there, but 3 out of the last 6ish times I've gone, I've found something in my food. And there's absolutely no effort to make things right.

My family and I picked up an order from this restaurant on Christmas Eve and it was so good! After trying many sushi places around Philadelphia and New Jersey, this has been the best quality sushi that we have had. The service is also really good as the manager came out and talked to us and thanked us for dining with him. They also have really good deals and prices for such high quality sushi. I can't wait to eat here again and as a sushi lover, I highly recommend this place!!

What a mess. Ordered Togo, receipt was still on the machine when I showed up 25 minutes later so they had to make when I showed up. Go to Ollies to waste time. Brought me the wrong order, took three morons to find my food. 

Gave me a $7 off coupon that another moron couldn't figure out how to use. Card reader messed up. 40 minutes later leaving with rushed meal that they offered only apologies for. Stay off the weed Puccini's Carmel.

This was my second trip here.  Originally, we had friends tell us the food was pretty bad so we were cautious.  I had wings  and my wife had shrimp and grits.  I was pleasantly surprised by both.   we came back today and had a completely different experience.  I asked our server how the crab cakes were and she said the dish was changed and she had not had it .  I asked it it was bready and was told no it was not.  Well I got my meal and the crab cakes were 1. very small and 2. mainly filler     The side of mac-n-cheese was good, but served in a small ramekin , not much for $23  
My wife had shrimp and grits again, but now, the grits are fried !!!  They were terrible, dry and tasteless.   I have to say though  the server did warn us that they changed the recipe. 

My advice is 'eat before you come here'

The V cheesesteak was amazing!!! Couldn't even tell it was vegan!! Location needs more signage in the front of the shopping center but no other complaints here! Def with be back to true the other menu items!

Absolutely the best crab stuffed tilapia! My husband and I tried this for the first time tonight and we were thoroughly impressed with the service and the great food. The key lime pie was tangy and delish!! Great prices and wonderful selection. We will definitely be back!

Sat outside on the patio and since we got there early had our pick of tables it was like we had our own private patio! Love the atmosphere and the efficient service. Owner came out and personally asked us about our meal! Recommend this place a great find!

The lattes we ordered were pretty good and we agreed that the espresso is pretty yummy, the barista working was friendly, and it was clear that the coffee shop is a neighborhood friendly.  Overall a decent experience with good, smooth espresso. The decor is a little plain but some people don't mind that.

We wanted to have a day exploring Fishtown and a great day of adventures always starts with a great brunch! This is a belated review because this happened towards late summer, but we were particularly drawn to Kensington Quarters because of its affordable entrees. I got the french toast because I always find it to be the litmus test of brunch food, and this is among one of the most unique french toast I have ever had! The brown sugar mixture and the homemade cream as well as the long, kind of stiff toast made this particular french toast unique from other more soggy french toasts I have had. There is a ton of natural lighting and variety in seating along with affordable cocktails that I will be sure to try next time!

Love this place. Felipe was our server and he was amazing! I had the Arroz con polo and it was great. Lots of flavor going on. Margs were as well. Their guac was fresh as well. I love Mexican and this is now my favorite place in Belleville!

I was recently invited to this place by my friend because I have heard a lot of good things so I wanted to try it out, we got there and they sat us right away we probably waited five minutes. The waiter didn't come to our table for probably 10 minutes, then we decided to order our drinks and food right away since they took long to come, the drinks came out  fast but the food came out 50 minutes after we ordered it and they brought it out because we asked another waiter about our food , our original waiter never came back to our table, never came back to say sorry for the inconvenience or sorry for the wait, we ended up with another waiter to finish up our transaction. I gave this review two stars because the food was really good but I don't see myself going back to this place  it was just not right the time that we had to wait for our food, when the table behind us got there after us, ate and left and we were still waiting for our food

Very attentive and pleasant service. 
Ambience is cafe like. Salt and pepper Seafood appetizer was super peppery and needs a side sauce. Mongolian beef was the best in Tampa but that is not saying much as no one here knows how to make it.  Walnut shrimp was very good. Quest continues for fine Chinese.

I like Black Finn but they aren't doing anything unique enough to warrant 4 stars from me.  Further, I have only come here for game watching parties and happy hours.  I know that they have a dining room, a nice bar area, and a huge patio.  I've only walked by the dining room but it looks nice enough.  That being said, the patio and bar areas are really cool.  Most of the SEC schools have elected to hold their watch parties here so expect college football crowds taking over the bar on saturdays in the fall.  For me, that's fine but others may find it annoying.  The patio area is really nice with tv's every few feet and heaters on the ceiling.   What I like best about this place is that they put their flatbreads on the happy hour menu for m-f.  They are delicious.  

Someday maybe I'll dine here for dinner and if its good send up the upgrade to 4 stars.  

The real drawback for me though is that it is attached to a mall and getting parking is difficult on the weekends.

This is some of the BEST red curries I have ever had! I've never had duck in my red curry before and I would 100% recommend trying it from here! I also got the opportunity to try some of their fried rice which was also great! Perfect amount of veggies and perfect spice balance!
Yum, yum, yum!  Had the Arugula Salad and a half margherita / half house pepperoni pizza.  Pepperoni had a kick and it was great.  Awesome service.  Would definitely come again

Yum yum yum! Just when I thought I had totally given up on Philly cheesesteaks, Jim's swooped me off my feet with this one. The bread was so luscious and soft (I love bread way too much), steak was nicely chopped and super duper juicy, cheez whiz was just an awesome touch with to this sandwich. The amazing thing was that the juice literally was dripping out of the sandwich as I was eating it. So so good! I have not had a cheesesteak like this one (sorry Pats!). Will definitely recommend going back again and munch munch munch some more!

From the moment you walk into this place they make you feel as if you are an intruder.  No "How are you this evening?" or "Nice to have you with us.". Arrogant, curt and obnoxious.  Both the host and waiter acted as if they were doing us a favor by serving us.  A great combination to really piss you off.  The food is very good here however.  But it is no better than many other great Italian restaurants in South Philly.  

Don't waste your time unless you don't mind serious attitude!

First a warning...no reservations for small parties...I arrived with a colleague on Friday night at 7...and a potential two hour wait...fortunately they have a full menu at the bar...the wait is worth it! Local beers from tap. Really creative fresh food. I had the pulpo carpaccio as an appetizer...my colleague had the meatloaf...not your mom's meatloaf...and I had the seafood risotto...was expecting a small bowl with maybe a few pieces of lobster but got a lobster claw, shell filled with crab meat and two gigantic prawns...

Definitely a go to hip place to visit in Tampa!

We just went last night for my birthday dinner. The atmosphere was cozy, elegant, intimate, and romantic. The staff was very attentive. Our server was super knowledgeable about the menu: both food and drink, his recommendations were great! Started off with the crawfish dip and a couple of delicious French 75s. I had the Airline Chicken. I'm usually more adventurous when I go out and like to try new things but when I looked at the menu, the chicken was what stood out. Served with a mustard cream sauce and crispy brussel sprouts, it was AMAZING. So juicy and tender. I will have dreams about this chicken. And then there's the bacon fried rice. Oh lord it brought tears to my eyes it was so good. We finished off the night with a coffee and a glass of delicious (and organic) champagne. Yum! We will definitely be back when it's not cold and rainy so we can sit on the porch. Loved our night!

These were the best empanadas I have ever had.  My husband and I were arguing over which one was the best.  I loved the caprese one, he loved the mushroom one. The chicken and corn ones were great too. The salad and potatoes were delicious.  There was a great courtyard to eat in. We will be back.

I love a steak that I don't have to season! My filet mignon was perfect, no salt necessary.
I started with the baked brie which took an extra few minutes but was not necessarily what I expected. It was good but I think I would have been better suited with a salad. Like I mentioned, my entree was superb. The filet cut like butter and did not disappoint. The sides were also quite nice but, ironically, lacked in seasoning (macaroni and cheese; scalloped potatoes). Overall, a good celebration dinner for yours truly (college graduation). I recommend!
We went here to celebrate a birthday and it was great!!  Food was yummy... service was good... atmosphere was fantastic!! We will be back

Went here on a first date and it was a perfect balance between intimate and welcoming. Sat at a stool surrounding the kitchen so that was fascinating. All the food was delicious and the waiting staff were very pleasant. Very reasonably priced for the city.

This is one of the better burger joints in Delaware county. There are a couple zacs locations all over delco but this is the original. If you are looking to eat in beware there are only 2 tables this location is more of a takeout joint. 
 As far as the food goes the burgers are always fresh juicy and cooked to perfection. The patties are on the smaller side so I would recommend a double. Shoe string fries are very good as well.
 Service is really good! Friendly staff that works quickly so you never have to worry about a long wait. I would definitely recommend this as a must try burger spot

Awesome! The closest place 2 get paletas used 2 b a 30+ min drive to Nashville. Now with La Michoacana, I can have paletas by walking next door! Awesome ambiance, great scene, and an even larger selection of treats. U have 2 try the Mexican twinkie flavor!

I would leave 0 stars if I could. The food is good but they are always randomly closed via a note on the door. It isn't really in a convenient area, so I just find this very unprofessional and annoying.

Everything, and I do mean everything, on their menu is fantastic!

I visit Sessano several times a month.  Since day one the staff has always been friendly and welcoming.  I think I'm on a first name basis with all of them.

I've used them for catering both work and personal functions.  Just tell them what you want, how many you're feeding, and when you need it by.  They always put together PLENTY of food.  

Their award winning pork speaks for itself.  When I bring friends here for their first time, they always go for it.  Nobody has ever been disappointed.  

Fantastic food, great staff, and a nice place to sit and eat.  You can't ask for much more from your local sandwich shop.

So we came to vacation here from Michigan. We decided to eat outside of the resort for breakfast more than once and came to skidders. The best way to compare his place is to a Coney Island in the Midwest if you have ever been to one. That means it's fantastic. Both mornings we have eaten here we have gotten different breakfast each time, and each have been amazing. The service is quick and friendly, and the kitchen turnaround time is faster than many restaurants I've been to in such a long time. Whether you live here or you were just visiting on vacation in St. Petersburg, come try this place out, extraordinarily affordable (especially compared to the resorts) and so so tasty!!

Terrible, terrible service. Went in with a friend to try Ming's. We were very disappointed. The server, who may have been the owner, was unbearably rude and unhelpful. I am a customer who does not have overly high expectations and usually tip very generously. The server/owner did not speak English very well, so we made polite attempts to communicate clearly pointing to items on the menu while trying to ask questions. The server, a middle aged lady who spoke with authority did not seem at all interested in our business. She was brusque and abrupt. Not even the smallest hint of a smile, and her every answer seemed to be given with the attitude that having to speak with us was a great inconvenience to her.  Because she was so difficult to understand, I had to ask her to please repeat herself a couple of times. That did not go over well, and instead of trying to be helpful to a new customer she only made more of an unpleasant face and acted hostile and exasperated. I don't know how the food is but I felt like I was in A Jerry Seinfeld episode with an Asian version of the Soup Nazi. Fearful that I would wind up with her spittle or worse in my food, this lady being so hostile, I simply thanked her politely. My friend and I both left with a strange shiver. We went to Perkins instead where we have been many times before. I will never set foot into Ming's Tea and Coffee again. Bad, bad vibes.

I really enjoyed my Poké Bowl. Fish and toppings tasted really fresh. They had a good variety of toppings, but I've seen better in comparable places in the area. They have lots of kombucha/sparkling water/specialty drink selection as well. 

The staff was very kind and helpful as a first timer. The place also smelt very clean (great sign). The bowls are $13 each for 2 bases and 2 toppings. I usually get sushi rice, and was disappointed to not see it here. 

Parking was pretty easy for us, but definitely not a huge amount of spots. Overall, had a good experience but would love to see more topping/base options!

Fantastic service!
You can choose between bistro (bar) seating or the fine dining area. You can still get the fine dining menu in the bistro area but there are plenty of choices on both menus.
The lamb lollypops were delicious - the pesto was a nice touch.
The crab cakes had a spicy kick. Great for a little snappy appy with a glass of wine.
Te chicken mushroom Caesar  salad had great flavors and was plenty for one or two to share. Good wine list and   plenty of options for steak or small plates.
Good variety. Good westport option.

We were in town looking for good bbq. We almost passed right by it because it's a small converted house. We ordered the family meal of chopped pulled pork, chopped brisket, ribs, Mac & cheese, beans and corn bread. We added an order of sliced brisket. Everything was off the hook!  There was a TON of food, more than enough for 4 adults. We even took some with us to eat after we woke up from our food comas. The place is clean. You can see the smokers in the back. The staff are super friendly and checked on us regularly.  The only thing that I would say could use a little work was the Mac & cheese. I tasted more Mac than cheese. But overall our experience was great!  We will definitely come back the next time we are in Reno.

I wasn't wow's by this place. I went here based on the reviews, vegan or no vegan. First of all there's no public restroom switch really really stinks!
The service was sooo so! 
Lamb kebabs were super dry, not moist, and my husband said they didn't even taste like a lamb. 
Chicken momos - no no! We pulled them out of the wrapper which was slimy, so we drowned them in the Chicken Makhani sauce.
The Chicken Makhani was good! I'd go back for that!!!
Although burger was good my complete delivery order was wrong no American cheese not dressed they did not add ketchup and garlic mayo  Onion rings were cold

Tonight I attempted to order food from this restaurant despite the bad experience I had in the past. So I placed my order online, payment took off my card, once I got in my car and was on my way I received a call from the pizza hut stating We can complete your order because we don't have any product, when I was trying to explain my frustration the unprofessional young lady hung up the phone on me. Avoid this location if possible. The food is subpar and the service is very poor. Hope the owner or manager read these bad review and re-vamp his/her team, or the owner re-vamp the whole staff.

The food was great. The service was fast and kept checking on us. I had the lasagna and the wife has lobster ravioli. The house made lemonade was very good!  Enjoyed a great meal. We will be back for sure! The menu is limited but still has a good selection.

A colleague of mine and I decided to give Ulele a try and realizing that their lunch service was brand new, we thought that this would be a perfect opportunity to sample the fare and experience the restaurant.  I made a reservation on Open Table, and after reading some reviews, was a bit hesitant that our reservation time of 12:15 would be honored.  Have no fear...we were seated immediately upon arrival.  The menu is full of temptations.  That said, I ordered the meatloaf and she had the Gouda Grouper.  We also opted for a few additional sides.- the Jalapeno Cheddar Grit cake and Carson's Jalapeno Corn Beer Quick Bread or as I would like to put it- Ulele's take on a corn muffin.
We ordered and waited a fair amount of time for the meal to arrive.  We arrived and were seated at 12:15 and our meal arrived at about 12:45.  That is a bit of a wait for a lunch order, so we decided that a 2 hour lunch was necessary.  For those in a hurry, I HIGHLY encourage you to look elsewhere to dine, because if you cannot afford to wait, don't do it.  That said, they just began lunch service on Monday so perhaps they don't quite have the "quick service" routine down to a science yet.  Back to the food-
We were offered sparkling or still water, and we chose the still with lemon.  My lunch date was very happy with her Grouper entree, but was overjoyed with the grit cake.  She had two, so we shared.  They were nicely flavored and we added a bit of butter to top them off.  Her Grouper was served on a bed of wild rice with three sprigs of asparagus.  My meatloaf was very tasty, 2 slices were nestled on a nice serving of mashed potatoes accompanied by three sprigs of asparagus and topped with fried onions.  The mashed potatoes were described as "white popcorn cheddar" but I neither tasted nor noticed a resemblance to the description.  That said, the potatoes were good.  The meatloaf was presented as two slices about 1/2 in. thick each.  For the most part, very flavorful.  The corn muffins were delightful with just a hint of jalapeno, and sweetness.  I did not notice a beer flavor at all, so I just chalked it up to a very fancy description for a nice corn muffin.  We opted for no desert because our time was up.  The service was wonderful and attentive and I cannot wait to try the restaurant for dinner.  I give it a total of 4 stars for the combination of ambiance and presentation of the food and the overall flavor, though if I had to rate the food alone, I would probably give it 3 1/2 stars.  Looking forward to a trip to Ulele for dinner!

We walked in and were greeted by a messy dissheveled cashier who after giving us the up and down look, bluntly asked if we were ready to order. We ordered "the standard" with egg whites, light cheese and turkey bacon on toasted bagels. The bagels were dry, and by dry I mean flour coating your lips as you took a bite. Not what i'd expect from any bagel. The bread was very doughy definitely a difference between a regular bagel. If you want a dry, doughy piece of bread with Trader Joe's turkey bacon, make it at home with Thomas' and you're guaranteed a better experience. And this wasn't a cheap breakfast either. For two bagel sandwiches and drinks we paid close to $20. Personally, I prefer breakfast with a lot less attitude. I have no intention of returning and will be sure to SPREAD the word.
I had the best pizza of my life at this place. So so so good. My favorite part is the way they fold the crust. Nice sweet and tangy sauce. I want to eat it everyday.
Great food and drinks!  A little noisy but overall great steak! Portion sizes are very reasonable.

Okay so again, I'm not a huge BBQ fan, but my Boo is so we came here. I wanted the burnt ends, but they were all sold out by 2pm. Ended up with a pastrami sandwich that was the best ever pastrami on a lame piece of bread, but who cares because I am on a low carb diet and the meat was phenomenal. 

One star docked for everything being too sugary--the coleslaw was a diabetic hit 1 and then the fire pickles had no fire but all sugar and was a diabetic hit 2. It's just my preference to not eat everything that's not dowsed in sugar.

Service is lovely. Meats are delicious.

I always only get the vegetarian Pad See Ewe and I am never disappointed.  Not that expensive for a good sized portion of delicious Thai food.  It would seem like they do a lot of takeout, as there are always a lot of people who are coming in to pick up a to-go order when I am eating in, which can be kind of annoying since the counter to pay and pick-up is in the back.  But all in all, a solid choice if you want Pad See Ewe.

Has there ever been a more fitting name for a restaurant? The delicate care that each waitress has for their customers is unmatched in the Tampa area. Steak, eggs, pancakes, and home fries for $9?!? I haven't seen a deal like that since the Raegan administration. Quick service and great food for a low price? What more can you ask for? Well, you could ask for a lot of things, like a Chevy Silverado or a new pair of slippers, but that would be foolish to expect... because it's a restaurant. Yeah, but for real, go to this place. Yanks fans too so you know they're not weird or anything like that.

Always a first stop when I get to New Orleans. Donuts are fantastic but I am also lots to the chicken biscuit and kolaches. You really cannot go wrong with your food choice here. This place is very busy so expect a line. Dog friendly as they have tables outside. Snap parking selection adjacent to the building or you can find a spot on the street.

Had dinner here and service was awful. Our waiter neglected our table and spent more time talking to his friend at another table. Disappeared when we were done with out meal so I paid another waiter. Do not get the Stewed pork in the clay pot as the meat tastes awful with gelatin like meat and a mountain of rice.
The food and service were both amazing. Our waiter was very knowledgable about the different steaks. Recommend for a special occasion.

I used to go to this specific location when it first opened and had not been there in sometime now. On 6/30/15 I decided to go have dinner here with my wife and our nephew. Was not impressed at all, this place is in need of corporate assistance for sure.

There were well over 8 employees in this location at this time yet only 1 female on the front line and a male cashier that spent most of his time in the back chatting evidently. Now at this point a line started to form and this poor female got behind real fast and still NO help from others. She had to call for the cashier 3 times before he came up to take out money. Now after I sat down in a location that provided a perfect view of what was going on in the back I got up and left without even eating half my meal! Horse playing in the back, girl putting stuff down another's shirt then reaching down her shirt to retrieve it, a guy wearing food prep gloves with his pants sagging around his butt tucks his underwear in and adjusts his pants and goes back to food prep!!!!! WTF I was disgusted as hell by the fact the girls never washed their hands after the horse play and constantly on the phone.... I mean you are in food service industry pants should be worn properly and girls in cut off shorts should not be pulling/adjusting the legs down out of their crotch and then going back to food service WITHOUT WASHING your HANDS. Then this same girl comes out from the back makes the cashier step aside so she can get a drink cup for herself then heads towards the soda machine and steps in front of a kid says "sorry, excuse me" and gets her drink before letting a customer go first. 

This place is in dyer need of proper management for sure. All this was going on while a manager was doing an interview at the table behind me..... Sad Sad Sad.

Will never go back to this place again.

Love Cabana whenever I'm in Nashville! Our server, Natalie, was adorable & professional!!  She helped make our dining experience a good one!
My boyfriend had the fried chicken & his comment was "Scrumptious!" I tried it & omg...succulent & flavorful! Wow! If you like chicken, you gotta try this!  I had the grilled salmon over a chilled quinoa & arugula salad...I'd order it again!! Very tasty!
Back to Atlanta tomorrow but we shall return to Cabana soon!

The staff here are all so welcoming. It's fun to come here ! Even on my worst days, I always leave with a smile along with my shake, and tea in hand :) Their products are so good and healthy too! Very affordable and leave me feeling good due to their wholesome ingredients. Love their birthday cake and white chocolate raspberry protein smoothies as well as their tea bombs such as captain America and raspberry rush!

I was in Tampa looking for a Cuban place and came across this Bakery. What a huge mistake, first of all the bakery floor was really dirty, the witresss  wasn't nice at all, and most important the pastries were nastyyyyyyy...Tres leches old , capuchinos dry!!, and I had a jaiva "crab" croquettes OMG pure oil and no taste . Over all it wAs tremenda CACA..

Basically everything Claire O. said, I agree with.

I love sushi. If I could date sushi, I would. If I could build a person out of sushi rolls, I'd love her to death - literally, because I would eat her, and then she would no longer exist (except in my belly).

I love trying new rolls and Vic's menu had so many choices I didn't know what to do with myself. We ordered the Sansom Roll and the Ocean Brother, which were both amazing. I must come back to try the rest.

If you're looking for fresh ingredients and a great combination of flavor, try Vic. Definitely more than your average sushi joint. It's tiny and maybe unassuming from the outside, but you won't regret it.

Summer nights after the kids ball game is what ice cream stops like Dippy's remind me of. Plenty of hustle and bustle here. 
Ice cream is good but not great. Flavors are your standard fare with plenty of artificial colors and flavors.  It's early May and they've been open a few weeks and already they are having trouble keeping the place clean. Tables dirty, garbage cans full. 
Don't expect too much from your visit and you'll walk away satisfied. 
Good news is, the dogs loved it! Ciao!

I finally got around to updating my review even though it's been a few months. This time, I made reservations for 2 during a busy dinner time (7:30 pm). We were seated to our table fast--within 10 minutes of checking in (we checked in just a few minutes early).

The food was great, as expected. We ordered three small plates for $21. The Lutenitsa and hummus plates were delicious (I don't recall the third small plate). We shared the family-size Red Bass served in a poblano sauce. The fish was cooked beautifully the poblano sauce was not that impressive but paired well with it. We purposely ordered less small dishes because we thought the $60 family-sized fish would leave us with an excess of leftovers, but this was not the case. We were a party of two and this was enough food to be satisfied but definitely not family-size proportions. 

All in all, the food tasted excellent, the service was efficient, and our waitress was friendly.
We both had a filet mignon.     It was 3 pm. Service was great and the steak was perfect. No waiting.

We live right down the street and decided to try this place for the first time. Our server was a C- D+. She was friendly but forgetful (nicely put). We ordered a pizza, meatballs, and caprese salad. I asked the server if I was able to add chicken to my salad and she said yes. Anyways, the pizza came out first, then the meatballs. We waited for the salad and nothing. Maybe 15 mins after we were done, our server came up and asked if everything was okay. I asked her for the salad and she had the "deer in a head light" look. 5 mins after the salad came out, and of course no chicken, I asked her about it and she told me "we can't add chicken to caprese salad but we can add chicken to everything else." What?!? So i waited almost half an hour for you to tell me you can't do something?!? We end up getting a Cesar salad instead after we've been done with everything else. She seemed to be distracted with her other table. If you wanted to drink with your other customers, you probably should have someone else serve us. And I can't tell you who she is cause she never told us her name. Other than bad service the food is amazing.
Delicious authentic Mexican food! Don't expect chips & salsa or shredded cheese - this place is the real deal. So fresh & tasty!

If you have any concerns regarding the virus, this is not the place to go. Total disregard for safety. No masks. No social distancing. Tables packed together. Profit Over safety. Owner or manager didn't seem to care. Just kept packing the room.
VERY UNSAFE SITUATION

Went here for lunch today with my mom. It was sharp looking on the outside and inside.  Tables and floors were kept very clean, service was excellent and all staff was very friendly. I had a turkey club meal and my mom had a wrap and we enjoyed it all! Can't wait to come back and try breakfast here!

I had never really had Napolitan Italian food, and this was amazing! Flavors are exquisitely unique. Great cozy place that will soon become widely known for their authentic and delicious food.

Highly recommend it.
Chipotle has the same model everywhere and I love this place. Just walk in and order how you want your burrito, taco, etc. It's basically an assembly line for tacos.
The website and Yelp said they are open until 11pm and  we got there a 10:35 and they were closed.  Very disappointing!

I posted a negative review a month ago about food my wife ordered. I received a response from one of their customer service representatives that asked for details which I provided. She indicated that she would pass on the information to the th Shea's Office and I could expect contact in the next few days. It has been over a month and no word from anyone. I am not looking for a free meal but fully expected an apology which I have not received. When you order scrambled eggs you should received scrambled eggs not a substitute. 
Bill newton

I'll admit I was attracted to this place by the wonderful neon sign proclaiming the earlier oyster bar incarnation of the place. Unfortunately this is akin to selecting wine by the design of the label.  What is within, namely a diner-style spot with a few assorted Creole and Cajun standards plopped within a list of roast beef and club sandwiches, burgers, and the like, fails to inspire nearly as much as the enticing facade. A shrimp po-boy sandwich was perfectly fine, with a crunchy soft roll, mayo, lettuce, and a moderate amount of fried shrimp. I will admit I've had far worse and far better examples of this simple fare, but I give them points for the warm, toasty bread even if the rest of the sandwich was unremarkable, as it all-too-often can be. The service was less than fine, as I received sweet tea instead of the unsweetened I asked for (I know, I'm a Southerner so I appreciate the difficulty one has in failing to dump at least 5 lbs. of cane sugar into each gallon of tea) and rushed service which didn't seem warranted given the place was half-empty and apparently not understaffed. Failing to check on me until the meal was finished for some time didn't help matters, nor did the tepid old coffee and pecan pie (ironically, nuclear hot and chewy-tough from being zapped) which was immensely more pie and sugar than pecan. Of the decades of pecan (say it "pee-can!") pie eating, I have to say the maker of this particular pie was the most parsimonious pecan placer possible. Say that five times. Seriously, how can one slice of pie have the equivalent of one (or let's say 1.5) pecan in it?  Well, voila!  

See the sign, enjoy the sign, but if you eat here, heed the signs and try something  else -- and definitely avoid the pecan-less pie.
Amazing experience great food NY strip was perfect my wife got the gnocchi with steak she loved good service

Having tried several of the Indian eateries in the city we decided to venture out into the burbs. Pulled up this one on yelp and the reviews made it seem quite promising. Was not a let down either. Its a very well done restaurant and the interiors seem very well thought out with attention to detail, and very unlike a lot of the regular Indian joints. Really liked the feel of the place. The service was A-ok...not the best, but atleast they were smiling. Food was good, we had their lunch buffet. Seemed pretty standard to me, but the husband ate the chicken and was raving about it all the way home. So they do score points on their chicken being a winner definitely! Don't know if we'll make the trip all teh way back into the burns for it again, but if we find ourselves out there, we will stop by for more de-lish fare again!

Had a lunch at M&H recently and was a bit disappointed. Food and service were so-so at best. Will give it a try for dinner, but I am concerned this may be a tourist place that locals who know better avoid.

Was hoping for a great seasoned burger but it lacked in taste.  They do cook it to order which is great and the onion rings were outstanding along with the Service. Valet parking is really nice since parking is limited in the area.  Over all a decent meal but I'm still looking for that perfect burger.

Why 5 stars? Well did I tell you I was a vodka buff? We have been to this place several times since May of 2011 and not once have I had a BAD drink. I love vodka and the first time my boyfriend and I went, they allowed us to sample a lot of things. Needless to say, I had to drive us home that day, LOL. 

What I like about Sub Zero is that they have many selections and drink creations. I can always have my vodka in more ways than one, AND I can taste different ones. The atmosphere is diverse and relaxed (like I like it). I'm sorry that I can't tell you how the food is because we've always gone for an after-dinner drink or two, but when we do finally eat here, I'll let you know. I have not had bad service, the bartenders were always pleasant, and I always felt relaxed here. Humm..maybe it was the alcohol, LOL.

If you like vodka, this is the place to be. Although the drinks can be a little pricey, stick to the Vodka of the week and you will be okay.

I stopped in for lunch and had a surprisingly nice experience. Don't be foled by the exterior, the inside is quite pleasant. We ate sushi and Thai. The Thai didn't look as good as the sushi was. I got the lunch special: $11.50 for three rolls, which was a great deal. It was well presented and tasted fresh. 

My only complaint was the Thai dish came out a good 5 minutes before the two sushi orders. But not a big deal.

Steve's in center city is conveniently located close to city hall. It's not huge, but there's about 6 tables to sit at and a high top bar that wraps around two of the walls. I'm not sure if there's a bathroom, but we didn't see one. There are two windows for ordering- one for steak sandwiches and one for fries, drinks and miscellaneous items. 

We each got a cheese steak with whiz and fried onions and shared cheese fries with American cheese. They give you a large portion of fries and the sandwiches are about 12". I've had cheesesteaks from a lot of places in Philly, and Steve's (both this location and the one on Bustleton) never disappoints. Really tasty steak, a lot of cheese and onion, and great bread. They have a serve yourself counter with pickles, peppers, etc. If you're looking for a great cheesesteak and you're in the area--this is the place to go!

Yep. It's a bar on Bourbon, BUT it also can be a calm respite from the street. 
Yes there are still frat boys and wooo girls who patronize this bar. BUT the bar is spacious the drinks are affordable (beers, straight pours and basic mixed drinks only). The staff are on the ball and amazingly patient. 

I also like that the interior looks like it hasn't been renovated in decades...if you can discount the flat screen TVs that is. The bathrooms are a bit sketch. It definitely does have character.

Went in and had lunch with my boyfriend. Place is nice and staff was friendly. The pretzel app is sooo amazing! We did have the fried asparagus and didn't like It that much, just too much batter. But I had the Ahi Tuna app for my meal and the guac was alright but the tuna was delish! He had the Cesar chicken wrap and said it was good too. Overall great place to come and eat, good happy hour too. Would love to come have dinner there one day, would def suggest this place. Claudia was our server and was super sweet and knowledgeable on the whole menu. Will def be back!

Five of us came here on a Monday evening.  Our service was great, our server was very helpful and attentive but not overly attentive. They have all local beers on tap.  I wanted to try the huckleberry Collins and it was very refreshing, not too sweet. We shared the tempura green beans which were tasty and came with three different dipping sauces. I had the Gnocci and it was delicious. Everyone was very pleased with their entrees, which included the Cubano sandwich, the pork chop, the ribeye, and the steak and onion sandwich. Very good restaurant.

Whenever I'm in the mood for some Mediterranean food at work,this is where I head to for lunch. Always get the same thing, which is their Donor platter, which is tasty and rather large (ends up being two lunches for me). Maybe a bit pricey, but given that it ends up being two lunches for me, it's not really that bad. Service is always friendly. Not a real big seating area and anytime I've been there, it tends to fill up over lunch, so my suggestion is to try and get there a little early.

My review is a 3.5. We went here with a large group (12) in late 2016 to celebrate the visit of a friend (Kurtus J). We typically do dinner with this group 2-3 times a year on The Hill. Given than most have not been to Anthonino's Tavera (no one in our party could pronounce), we tried it. It's a fun place, probably good for 2-4 people, but the bar area was for too small for all of us to wait comfortably here. It's the aisle to the main dining room and offered limited seating. Service from bar was OK. The lighting overall here is WAY WAY too bright. It felt more like a cafeteria than a Hill restaurant. Needs more ambiance and a warmer feel (dimmer, more carpet, Italian Music, etc.) The bright lights and environment, made it feel a bit rushed. Maybe it's designed for young families (?), but for a group of adults trying to catch up on old times--there are 10 better options on the Hill. Toasted Raviolo were the highlight. Pasta as so-so to average. Service was OK. Prices OK. Many better Hill options. Hope they change the vibe here to get closer to the other great Hill spots. 

Location A
Food C+
Service B-
Ambiance/Lighting D+
Wine C+
Prices C+ 

On a busy night, entry area is crowded and not comfortable. Atmosphere to too bright at stark for our taste.

Came here a few days ago with friends in the evening. 

I ordered the gumbo and it was too salty. It came with a biscuit which was probably not homemade. Taste like Popeye's biscuits. I've tasted homemade gumbo by someone who grew up in Louisiana and his is 100 times better. 

I tasted a fried green tomato from my friend's dish and it was pretty good. Very hot (temperature-wise)! My friend also ordered a Bloody Mary (free refills) and she really liked it. Did not taste it so I cannot comment. We were told it's not freshly made. They use a Bloody Mary mix.

Our waiter was ok. It was semi-busy. 

Will not be returning back. Did not meet my standards (no surprise).
Fabulous lunch, the service was perfect and the flavors were amazing! Great beers too. My husband had the rabbit and dumplings and I had the braised beef sandwich. Sheer comfort food.
hmm sure their pork belly dish was good but then again, pork belly is almost always good. The restaurant felt really cramped and the price for portions...not worth it.

Needed to find a place to dine with my folks and my aunt and uncle inside the, "Inside" strip (E, SL, CC), so I picked this place as most restaurants you pay close to the same price for 1 dish as you can for AYCE, and tonight was seafood night $25.95, and $3 discount for locals w/ proper ID. 

I ate at this restaurant many years ago when it first opened and it was not impressive, which was strange as we used to dine in the old buffet which was across from this one, and that was always 4 to 5 stars. 

I didn't eat here for a long time, then heard it was good again, tried it and agreed. I ate here 2 more times and both times were 4-5 stars, that is if you got the dishes that always look the best and the ones you like.

Tonight really was impressive, we were quickly sat, and served, I went out to get a plate and saw the mushroom ravioli and decide to load up, I got about 8 to 10 of them, and most places that would be all you get for $18 (probably a couple less raviolis too), but then I added tortellini, a small serving of lasagna, a loaded baked potato, fresh medium rare prime, and grabbed my seat. Everything was 5 stars, even the potato was excellent! 

I was sufficiently stuffed, but it's kind of pricey, so you got to dig in and go for the uncomfortable stomach for a couple hours, so I grabbed another plate, and loaded up crab legs, mussels, and peel and eat shrimp. Again, all 5 star dishes. I was very shocked to have so many different dishes on such a high level! 

Service was great, all plates quickly cleared, server was available anytime for drinks, napkins, etc. 

Last I did desert, I again went for a belly buster consisting of cheesecake, butter finger something, flan, and mint chocolate chip gelato. The gelato was the star of this show, with everything else being delicious. Glad to see an old favorite come back to life and deliver an outstanding meal for my party of 5 with the greatest of ease!

I would give this over 5 stars if I could! Such a peaceful donation-based coffee shop and extension of the neighboring church, while the coffee drinks are names after Bible verses. This is a great spot to start your day, get centered, and reminded of what matters most.

Friends from NYC suggested this place so we tried it out and it was really good. I'm all about the crust but the sauce was amazing and the toppings were perfect. Seriously this was a really good pizza and I don't even crave pizza but maybe now I will.

Average food, way over priced. No liqour, butbthey will charge you a silly amount for their margarita mix if you bring your tequila. The food isnt terrible but nothing stands out either, on the whole a rip off

Bit over priced but most places on Bourbon are pricey.  They stay open late which is a bonus when arriving late to the hotel.  My fav here is the BBQ shrimp.  I've tried few other dishes but none were memorable except for the BBQ shrimp.  Been here 3 or 4 times and always sat at the bar.  Some of the waiters are cool to chitchat with and they'll give you some good recommendations on what places to check out.

Based on an adventurous kick my bf had and yelp reviews, I payed a visit to these friendly folks.

Order: scallion pancakes, chicken and cashew combo platter with wonton soup (mine), shrimp pan fried noodles (bfs order) 

Pros:
1. wonton soup was amazing! i looooove wonton soup! the broth was AMAZING! 
2. the spring roll that came with my meal was probably the best spring roll ive had in a long time! it even had whole shrimp!
3. food came out so fast! i didnt even finish my first cup of tea
4. staff is really nice, not annoying and bugging you every 2 minutes to check if youre ok. they alllll say bye when you leave, i feel like im leaving a friends house.
5. cheap! our total was $24! we had so much food!
6. the random one... i got a plate with compartments, you know like when youre 5 yrs old and everything is separated on your plate? yea one of those, i was waiting to see elmo on the bottom... 

Cons:
1. the dining area was small and kind of awkard... the table we got was uncomfortable. the man behind me kept moving back and forth on the booth i would get launched forward and back like every 15 seconds. it was so annoying
2. it was so quiet, i felt like i had to whisper...
3. we tried the pancakes bc everyone said they were amazing, all i have to say is ive had better. sorry.
4. no elmo on my plate =(

The very first time I had any Thai food was here, and now I can't get enough of it! I have only ever ordered the chicken pad Thai and it was/is delicious! Have yet to find any other Thai restaurants that top their pad Thai :).

I've been going to the other Crabby Bill's restaurants for years. Had no reason to think this one would not be good. 
Boy was I wrong! 

We had a dozen "PRIME" raw oysters and a dozen fried oysters. 
The raw oysters were so salty they burned all the way down. No one bothered to wash/rinse them. If they were PRIME I'd hate to think what the regular oysters looked like! These were tiny!   At $6.99 a dozen they should be good.... WRONG!!!!

Yes, we know about the month with an R in it thing but until now Crabby Bill's has never let us down. They sure did this time. 

The fried oysters were also small and they tried to hide it with a lot of breading. It didn't work. Then later I had a greasy coating on my tongue and mouth. Yuck! 

When we tried to tell the barmaid/waitress the problem she immediately called the manager over. He apologized but not without a comment to the effect, "well you did eat them all." 
Of course we did. We planned on paying for it so why not eat it? 
He said he would remove the cost of the raw oysters from our bill. We told him not to. He did anyway. We still left the money to cover them.

 Who knows if the "waitress" got it or the restaurant. That's their problem. 

We won't go there again. I'd rather take the long ride to Indian Rocks.
They know their oysters!

I love burgers. They're one of my favorite food's when prepared properly. My standards for a good burger can be a little unrealistic sometimes. But I will review this establishment truthfully as possible. Upon walking into this restaurant I was greeted by a cheery cashier who joyfully took my order, smile and all. I looked around and observed that the customer base seemed to enjoy glaring at me and the friend I was with. These stares continued for the entirety of my overall terrible experience. Mind you, there is nothing particularly interesting about the way my friend and I looked, just normal young people. My friend decided upon the "crunchified" Vegas Burger. I thought, "Eh, why not try the Philadelphia Burger?". I asked for it medium rare, my friend asked for medium. I sat in the tacky swivel stools and tried to ignore the eyes burning into the back of my skull. We waited for around 8 minutes, and then my companion graciously received his meal. Funny, I thought medium burgers took longer than medium rare to cook. Maybe I'm absolutely batshit crazy, but I don't think my burger should have taken 20 minutes longer than my friends to cook. But it did. 

I finally get my "Philadelphia Burger", and the first thing I think is, "This had better be a good fucking burger.". But it wasn't. It was bad. Not terrible, but definitely bad. I bite in expecting a medium rare, juicy, crispy on the outside, salty, cheesy burger. What I got was a WELL WELL done burger, completely gray, bland, and lame burger. I asked for Cheez Whiz because I love some Whiz with my meat. The cheese was stone cold, stodgy, and unappetizing. Please don't go to this location. Please.

I was in the neighborhood and decided to stop in for what I had hoped to be a Caribbean gem based on the high reviews but unfortunately I can't say it lived up to the hype. The restaurant is nicely decorated and with good music to set the ambiance. I decided to dine in and ordered the jerk wings, a beef patty and a ginger beer; but only the ginger beer met my expectations. The wings were good but relied heavily on a sweet jerk sauce that they were smothered in, the meat itself had little smoke or jerk flavor but overall they were good. The slaw that it's served with was surprisingly good; I'd eat that alone if I could order it. The bad was the beef patty to which I'd say you've probably had PB&J sandwiches that had more PB than this had beef. After choking on a few bites of pastry (where's the beef?) I asked the kind server if perhaps my fortune landed me with the odd patty with such little beef. She shyly agreed and went to speak with someone in the back and returned to say she was told "they don't make the beef patties and that the lady said I could buy another one but she couldn't give me another". I passed on the opportunity and recommended they check the patty vendor because it's not a good look for their restaurant. So all in all, I spent $23+tip for an excellent ginger beer, 10 fairly good wings and a beefless patty. The service was otherwise good but I'm not sure I'll be back soon. I wanted to like this place and support black owned local businesses, so I do hope they improve!

Being from Boston, we aren't allowed to purchase alcohol and walk around the city! We were visiting friends and family for the weekend because I was running a half marathon! So after the race we went to our friends house and she took us on a downtown New Orleans adventure! More like a celebration for finishing my 18th half marathon!! I was still amazed about how we were able to drink but when we got inside, there were many choices. At least 18 to choose from and of course we sampled about half a dozen flavors. I ended up getting the Kahlua Mudslide. It was delicious and it literally tasted like a mudslide but frozen! Next time I want to try a more fruity flavor like Peach Bellini.

This is -to me- the best place to eat Chinese food in the Downtown area. The prices are acceptable, no delivery fee (if you need to have it brought to you/work), the food tastes great (not as greasy as at the competition around) and the delivery guys are friendly and fast (yes, your food will still be hot when you'll open the box). It is cooked by 1st generation Chinese people who keep it as close to the culture as possible.
