I always order "shrimp with garlic sauce" and add fried tofu for $ 1.00 to it. Absolutely delicious! Full of shrimp, fresh vegetables and a sauce which couldn't be better. And the rice comes in an extra container, so you won't feel cheated on your size of the meal either. Really good, fast Chinese food.

I really enjoyed Big Storm Brewery! I visited on a quiet Wednesday afternoon as part of a brewery hopping adventure with my friends. There is plenty of seating throughout but I could imagine quite a bustling crowd on the weekend. The parking lot was a fair size and the building is well marked. In fact, there is a billboard across the street to help you find it. 

The interior was very nice and industrial based. The bar is kind of an island in the middle of the brewery with seating surrounding it. They have a large brewing area closed off by big glass windows. I don't believe they do public tours.

And as for the real reason we go to breweries...the beer was awesome! I had a Belgian flight which held a Single, Dubbel, Tripel and Quad. As you can see from the photo, they pack a hefty ABV! They were delicious and exactly what I was looking for! I will say that the Tripel had a funky skunky taste, but nothing was actually wrong with it. I absolutely loved the Quad! This combination caused me to forget how much my bill was but I believe it was $11 for the flight. Worth it in my opinion!

I'd definitely like to check out the Pasco location. I really enjoyed my experience! Since we were visiting for my friend's birthday, the bartender offered her a delicious Raspberry beer on the house. And they have free pub mix to nosh on while you drink your beers. Cheers!

A Luchador themed restaurant that seems to be all the rage at the moment. The ambiance was nice, the staff was very friendly, the margarita was super delish, but that's about it. I ordered the carnitas tacos and they were ok. There was a lot of fat left in the meat, way more than is normal. So, I don't know if they do that to make the taco look fuller or if they just don't know to cut most of that out. 
All in all, it wasn't a horrible experience, I would definitely return for the margaritas and to maybe try one of the other dishes.

In the mountains high above Santa Barbara, in what seems like the middle of nowhere, is a magical place that serves great food and drinks. An old stage coach stop from the late 1800's is the setting of this magical place. My friends and I were there on a Friday afternoon and there were people waiting outside for a table. Our reservations were for 1:30 pm and it was still croso if possible, I would recommend making reservations. The French dip, tri-tip sandwich, and ribs with onion rings on the side were what my friends ordered. The onion rings looked fabulous and my friends confirmed they were as were the sandwiches and ribs. I had the roasted vegetable salad and it was delicious. We had Cold Spring Tavern's bacon and asparagus quiche for breakfast that morning and it was the best quiche I had ever had. Our server that day was very personable and provided excellent service. My previous visit to the Cold Spring Tavern was about 23 years ago and the food was great then, so I am pretty confident the great quality is consistent.

Love Spaddy's.  My daughter and I love to stop and get our morning coffee here.  The Cafe con Leche is always perfect.  She enjoys the Heights Cold Brew, which is poured from the tap!  The menu includes many hot and cold specialties.  Cuban toast (with or without cheese) is always Hot, crisp and delicious.  Stop by and grab a cup!  You won't be disappointed!

Saigon restaurant is at the top of my list for great Vietnamese restaurants to dine at. I love it that they offer such an all encompassing big menu, but still do not lose the authenticity and flavor of their dishes. 

Here are my favorite Vietnamese dishes that I love to order here!

1. Soft Spring Rolls- they bring you a spring roll kit with rice paper, water for soaking, vegetables and meat so you can assemble it on your own! Very hands on cool experience! 

2. Vietnamese Pancake (Crepe)- I'm not always a big fan of omelettes, but when it comes to this Vietnamese egg dish, I certainly am! The pancake is a bit of a crunchy texture and goes great with shrimp!

3. Congee with Pork- I would love to eat this congee for breakfast every week if I could! This is the only place that I know of that serves the best congee. 

4. Wonton Noodle Soup (Hu Tieu Wonton)- I think this tastes better with egg noodles as a substitute. 

5. Bun Thit Nuong Cha Gio- Vermicelli noodles with grilled pork and egg rolls. 

My absolute favorite thing about Vietnamese cuisine is that they know how to cook grilled pork and make it actually taste good! I also think that they have the freshest vegetables available and it's great that they have a side of fresh basil and bean sprouts with a lot of dishes. I'd eat here every day if I could and would go through their entire menu!

One star for the portion size. For ~$10M for lunch and without drinks, we were all served kids' meals sized. We were all still hungry afterwards we all had to go to McDs to get burgers. However, the food is good and place is really nice. Awesome ambiance and friendly service! Most likely won't go back again.

I have been here a couple of times trying to give them the benefit of the doubt. I would hear people raving about how awesome "Port of Call" is, but i have never seen what the big deal was. I am a local and i try to eat at local restaurants, lived around New Orleans all of my life. Let me start with the burgers, they taste like someone opened a large container of ground beef, portioned a thick patty and threw on the grill. No seasoning at all, they ask you what your preference for how well done its cooked. Pick one level higher it tends to be on the more raw side of the scale. The way they make there burgers are typical from every other burger joint. Now to the steaks, i will admit in the past i had an great fillet, but someone brought it home and gave to me, it was seasoned good and cooked the way i like it Med Rare to Rare. The Salad was good, make with buttermilk so it was thick and had great taste. The last time i went there i got a rib-eye, my stepfather got the fillet, i went to grab for the A-1 (Which i never put on steaks ) and he was already using it. Neither steak had any taste just plain meat. My wife said her steak was ok but she was also drunk from the strong specialty drinks they serve. I would have given 3 stars, but the place is very tight for room so you will be elbow to elbow with everyone or standing outside, Parking is a tuff so good luck, i guess the experience of the place and people make it better. One thing on its own and it kinda sucks. I guess i would recommend someone to eat here if they were in the neighborhood, but i wouldn't recommend if they are more then 2 miles away.

Excellent meal. Excellent server. Wonderful evening!

Loved the House Plank - it was just right for four to share as an appetizer.

My filet was perfection, and the lobster risotto we ordered to share on the table was wonderful.

My only request is to please change where the red wine is stored; our bottle felt chilled when it was brought to the table.

Called and ordered a takeout pizza with the boss a couple months back. This is more of a takeout style place even though there is some limited seating of you choose to dine in. 

ATMOSPHERE:  Sort of a takeout cafeteria style joint that you would come across on a boardwalk or in a mall. Yet it is in a shopping center - and there is places to sit I would recommend take out.

FOOD: We ordered a pizza via take out. The pizza was a large pie with big slices and a proportional amount of sauce, cheese, dough, and grease. I found the pizza to be very good and would recommend it. Unfortunately I cannot speak to the rest of their menu but in terms of the pizza it was very good. 

OVERALL: I would recommend this place for a meal and a try. Nothing I saw or tasted would make me recommend to steer clear.
Alex the bartender gave me phenomenal service, Above and beyond. I wish everywhere I went people were this kind. AND the drinks and food were amazing. I was Absolutely blown away by the service.

All around a win!  Very nice decor inside, table linens, wall decor, and everything was clean.

My husband and I both had butter chicken, with different spice levels, and the portions were plenty.  To be honest if we could compromise on the spice level we could share a dinner.  The garlic naan and butter naan were both delicious! We will be back!

Thought the food was alright. I was disappointed to see that there weren't that many healthy options on the menu and my salad that I did get was very average! Overall great vibe thought and the costumer service was great!

Much better service for restaurants in Nashville,  a few miles from airport. I ordered my favorite Dish, Fish and chips, they didn't have the side to go with it, server ask if Fries were okay, I said was fine. It taste so hearty and I liked it. Plus I was hungry.

Had an amazing night with my lady here! 

Service was amazing, dang near bordering on overboard and yet never going over the line. Whatever we needed, it seemed like there was always someone right there. The 3 person jazz band was great (very talented!). They gave us a very sweet moment, without making us feel like that we were being called out to the whole room. 

Food was very good! The escargot was prepared in a way I've never had. Might have actually made a fan out of lady! Overall, our entire meal was fantastic! Obviously a more expensive place to dine, but the food and service is great. I'd love return on my next visit!

I was first introduced to The Corner through a Yelp Elite event and I told myself I had to come back. Funny enough I went back two days in a row.

Saturday I came to The Corner and got to experience the ambience of a notable Bluegrass band playing in the lower level of the establishment. It was a great time. Even though the place was packed service was timely and the servers were friendly.

I turned around and came back on Sunday to experience the brunch which was very good and again the service was great. I ordered the shrimp and red pepper grits with a side of bacon and the hibiscus mimosa. Everything was delicious, however, there wasn't as much kick to the grits as I would've expected and they were a bit stiff. The thickness of the bacon was very appreciated and the hibiscus mimosa was refreshing. 

I can't wait to try other things on the menu.
The food is excellent and the hospitality of the owners is even better. My favorite little gem uptown

Mac's Fish and Chips were alright. The fish was good and the batter was thin (which is good). The fries were not bad. They didn't serve lemons with their order (you have to ask for it). The malt vinegar came in a pitcher like container...so you'd have to pour the vinegar over your fish...lame. The tarter sauce came in a sample cup that was beginning to fall apart (that happens when you leave something wet in a paper cup)...I saw the tray that was already prepared with sauce, BAD IDEA. The place was cold but they had heaters. My boyfriend asked if he could close the door but they told him no. We probably won't be returning.

Things have changed here. Especially since the brains behind their establishment quit last year. They had a girl there that did all their booking, organizing - basically she ran the ship. She left and things went downhill quickly. 

The bottom line - there are bigger and better venues that have moved into Nashville. This place will also be a well known because they have been around for years. But if I were an artist, dj or anyone looking to book an event, this place wouldn't be on my radar.

And Hoagiefest has returned.

$3 for a Junior, $4 for a Shorti and $5 for the full-sized Classic.

The employees even got bright new shirts to mark this momentous occasion.

Fountain drinks remain 99 cents as well.

Yes, gotta have a Wawa.

I mentioned to the front desk at my hotel that I was thinking of going to James Joyce and he told me, hands down the best place to eat. I have to say that he was right....I ordered the Buffalo chicken sandwich and it was awesome! I have an allergy to shellfish so the cook personally came to my table to ask questions, made suggestions and explained how they cook their foods. 

The wait staff is awesome! Great conversations, patient and very helpful on the big beer list. I look forward to getting back to Tampa to visit this restaurant again.

Simply the best Chicken and Yellow Rice, hands down. For the price - around $6, you get a huge amount of quality food and fresh bread. It comes out within minutes and you're wondering how they get the chicken so tender and the yellow rice tasting so good!

The service is usually good and the place is like a moderate Cuban place, but for the price, the food is outstanding. I've been here no less than 20 times and I'm always happy when I leave.
French toast was amazing!!! Very nice wait staff. Green smoothie was delicious as well.

I came for lunch during Restaurant Week. This is a cozy place with attentive service and fresh, hearty food.

First Course: Warm Tostados w/ Chunky Avocado-Tomato Salsa
Ok... this is just chips and guac. The chips were tasty, well seasoned and the guac was fresh but it's nothing you can't get at a Chipotle. If I had known this, I would have tried something else more interesting on the menu.

Second Course: Roasted Eggplant Cannelloni
I am not a huge fan of eggplant but the flavor was not overwhelming. The eggplant truly substituted the noodle in this dish, even mimicking the "al dente" texture. The ricotta filling was rich and gooey, and the white beans made this surprisingly filling. The one thing that would've made this better is a big piece of crusty bread to sop up the sauce.

Third Course: Vegan Lemon Ginger Cake
I am totally not a vegan! But I loved this! The cake is a perfect texture, very moist but still dense enough to provide a delicious foundation for the pineapple and ice cream. The pineapple adds a tartness that counteracts the richness of the avocado coconut ice cream. Overall, it wasn't too sweet and was a great end to the meal - even though it's vegan!

Service- nice attentive and helpful in choosing pizzas for a large group

Fries- as delicious as they looked 

Pizza- yummy but the crusts maybe slightly undercooked. We may ask for them to be over cooked next time to get the crust a bit more crispy 

Eat in was CASH ONLY which we did not know, but they had ATM on site

This is my 3rd time in.   Still a major disappointment.   Food is just not good.  
Gumbo was watered down.   The scallops were rubbery, the veggies were perfect. 
Service never quality.  Even if they offer you free food just say no.   

Maybe for a drink and your okay paying 5.00 to park your car.

Went here for a pre-Valentine's day dinner.  We got there a little early, so went went upstairs to the lounge, which was really nice.  There were lots of televisions and different types of seating.  Drinks were pricey, but good and in line with the atmosphere.  Highly recommend!
  Our dinner was awesome, from the different breads, to the really good shrimp cocktail, (don't breathe out through your nose when you take a bite or you'll be sorry : ) to the fantastic steaks(ribeye and filet) and sides.
   I will have to say that the highlight of the experience was our waiter, Andy!  We can't say enough good about this young gentlemen.  He was polite, personable, professional, and accommodating.  He also walked us out and gave us a mini tour of the place, explaining some of the wall memorabilia and it's importance to Indy.  It was very entertaining and interesting!  I'm not sure what they are paying this guy, but it's surely not enough!  That was one of the best times we have ever had in a restaurant and I know we will be back especially for that reason!  Good food, good people and good times!  Oh yeah, make your reservations early, it fills up quick especially on the weekend and ask for Andy!

We were there as tourists. Although we ended up there spontaneously, we just took an Uber from City Park to a nearest Po Boy place, we got the experience we were looking for :) This is definitely a great place to try New Orleans food. It is small, it has seats inside and outside. It has many Po Boys options as well as Gumbos. No hype around, just local, just delicious and not overpriced.

Moreover, I prefer live conversations to googling. We asked a waiter about an origin of Po boy's name. He didn't remember and asked a guy in the kitchen, the guy didn't remember too. We were seating outside after our delicious meal waiting for an Uber, when a guy, probably the owner, came to us and told us the history of Po Boy! Isn't it the best experience you can get as a Cafe guest? And yes, the place is very affordable, that lefts no reasons not to go and check it out :)

A friend took me here for the first time saying they make the best cheesesteaks here. Obviously my friend doesn't know me very well... The lines were long and like a twisted maze with customers crossing over each other to order & pickup all within the same small 4 foot counter space. No one sure where any line started or ended, Rolls had sesame seeds on them and Fries were cooked in peanut oil. All I could taste were seeds and peanuts - I don't really care for either one. Not happy that the person handling out ready orders was only checking the receipts of people of color - "to make sure it's (your) order". Oh Okay, I will not be back.

As someone who never orders red sauce out, this place is the only thing I have found that comes close to Nonna's cooking on a Sunday!   The staff and service are good and with homemade, full-of-love food makes you realize you can't get any better!   It's a BYOB so bring a bottle and begin your conversation because it is always worth the wait! :)

Three generations of this family run this Italian restaurant with a wide variety of items to choose from.  Great wine selection, warmed, delicious, freshly made ciabatta bread with Rosemary olive oil starts the dinner.  My wife had the Salmon picatta and I the chicken Chris, both excellent.  Attractive, cozy atmosphere, great food and wine, reasonable prices and a very friendly staff.  Definitely a restaurant for SB locals to eat  again and again.  We will be back.

Good, creative food but on our second visit there, the bartender was so unbelievable rude that we walked out. And the more people we tell about it, the more we find that others have had the exact same experience! What is UP with that? Too bad; so few places like this in the immediate area. Not worth the abuse.

Terrible bartender with no customer service skills.  Tall red head bearded gentleman who wouldn't even make eye contact with me standing in front of him in front of the drafts.  There was no "I'll be right with you, please have a seat, or the waitress will be with you....absolutely nothing.  Other customers were experiencing the same. After 15 minutes I finally went to the other side of the bar, where another bartender was polite, courteous and professional.  Beer was decent.  The lack of service by the earlier bartender is the basis for this review and experience.

After an enjoyably evening at Winterhaven my son and I stopped by this location for a bite to eat. All I can say is Wow!! My son had the three chess stuffed crust and I had the deep dish pan pizza. The pizza here is fantastic and brings individualized pizza to a new level. The service provided by Keenan and Tina was attentive and welcoming. If you like pizza I heartily recommend that you try this location.

I enjoyed dinner last night at Mazara. The service was friendly and fairly quick, though the restaurant was only about 1/3 full. I tried the beer & cheese sound and Tutto Mara, both were wonderful. The bar area looks fairly nice too, but beer selection is limited. This is a restaurant I would try again.

So it's an institution and thus you come with some expectations. Not sure what was going on, but seated at the same time as the couple next to us, both ordered app and entree, but they had almost finished entree before our two cups of gumbo arrived. Waiters were apologetic but could not explain. Food was delicious, but there are plenty of delicious places in NOLA.

The owner replied back to my review and I can tell is a stand up guy who cares about running a good restaurant. 
                                                                                           Went on Monday for lunch with a friend. Food was decent, but nothing to rave about. They use grande cheese and quality tomato products, but the pizza didn't wow me at all. The service was good, but what bothered me was the owner of the restaurant sitting at a table in clear view of everyone dining there and when I was there, he didn't say hello to any customers at all. To me that's very rude. There are better options in Tampa for NY pizza.

First and foremost. This restaurant is NOT Mexican food. It's Tex-Mex style! Huge difference. I'm not a fan of Tex-Mex at all so that's why I gave 3 stars. Thanks for the gift card but I won't be paying to eat here again, not really my type of food.
Fried Chicken is sooooo good as is most of the food !  Service is sufficient for my tastes

In and out salad bar with sandwiches, soups and sushi!  When I crave a salad, I like it my way and there is no place better from work to grab what I want. Everything is always fresh and the sushi is simple, but a great compliment to the salad. Always friendly and always clean. Great to dine in or carry out.

A friend brought me in here for dinner. It was a favorite of hers because it was affordable and delicious. 

It is definitely both of those things. Affordable and yummy! They have a HUGE menu. I mean HUGE! We spent about 20 minutes just going through the menu. Take your time and really find something you want. 

The staff was great with guiding us through the many selections and helping point us to things that fit our cravings. 

I would absolutely come back here when I was in the neighborhood.

Some Fun funky new fresh energy in town! I like it !Being from San Francisco it is so hard to adjust out here in the desert. The playground has brought some great new energy downtown and that's what it needs!

The decor is great and the roof will  be even better when it gets a little warmer! Thanks Kade for bringing us The Playground!

A hip, hidden gem in the 'burbs. Clean, spacious old world decor; charming and quick service (super cute bearded guy); menu carefully crafted with passion and attention to detail. Try the bone-in selection jamon: they actually bring in a pig shoulder from Spain and slice it off directly for you. Prosecco is ON TAP. Think you're bored of hummus? THINK AGAIN. That ish has some magical spicy (but not too spicy for my weak mouth) addition like you've never had in hummus, son. No stale pita here. Chickpea Panella is this magical crispy salted square with a boar ragu that will throw down with your Nona's Sunday dinner ANY DAY OF THE WEEK.  12/10 A+++ would gorge myself again

My friends and I called just minutes before arriving at Harvest, and we were seated almost immediately. It is a modern/fine dining feel, but can be casual as well. There was live music playing on a Friday night. Our server was very engaging and personable. This restaurant is similar to Seasons 52, for the menu changes every 3 months with dishes inspired by season, but they have way more to offer on the menu that I can remember. The main difference to note is that they have a green concept with farm to table style using fresh and organic ingredients from over 70 local farmers markets. Not only that, but are eco-friendly in regards to using recycled products for other purposes in the restaurant. Also, each item on the menu is 500 calories or less, or slightly more as noted with a little plus sign. Aside it being healthier ingredients being put into your body, doesn't mean it is necessarily healthy. Plug in an app or two, a meal and dessert, drinks..you're looking at a 2000+ calorie meal. But who cares its dinner, and you're meant to indulge. So indulge..

All the food was proportioned pretty well. The flat bread was thin, but very large and came free with Yelp check in. It was yummy and shareable between 4 people. Spinach and Kale dip was creamy and delicious. I had the duck pot stickers, and I personally thought they were over fried and sort of bland. I did not care for the cranberry, and other sauce it was accompanied with. I absolutely loved the pumpkin ravioli. It is a sweet and savory dish, and very well balanced. Desserts are in shooter glasses and $3 each. Our server came to the table with a little tray displaying all desserts to choose from, always a great tactic. If you want one, which of course you do, she hands it to you right there. Genius! I'll take another. They are mostly a mousse, with a a little crumb or cake texture at the bottom.

The only negative was that the food did take a little longer to come out, but overall I thought it was a nice experience. I will come back again.

You're going to have to make a really phenomenal burger to get me to pay $15. I did not experience that on my visit...at all. Those sad, greasy, stale chips that accompany the overpriced burger should be removed from the roster altogether. The final straw? Those seats on the first floor that are so low you feel like a kindergartner when trying to eat.
CC is GREAT! Onion Rings are awesome! Fun atmosphere! $5 Rum Runners on Friday! Family fun and live music all weekend

I hit this place on a Friday night with some pals with no expectations other than to keep drinking after closing out the last bar.  The atmosphere was electric and the crowd was diverse to say the least.  Party girls, alternative peeps, thug wannabe's and goth kids all mixed together into a rowdy, happy bunch.  

This place is very casual and laid back.  You'll often find dogs sitting next to their owners at the bar (and sometimes on the bar), but no one bats an eye.  The tequila and rum selection is much more extensive than you'd expect at a place that offers PBR & a shot of well tequila for 2 bucks.  Try the Diplomatico rum, a Venezuelan rum (yeah, I know) that's smooth enough to drink straight on the rocks.

Pirate gear adorns the entire bar and its staff as well.  Nothing better than getting your drinks served by a pirate wench :) This place is a great joint to end a night on or start your Sunday at.

I think this may be a new favorite. To be quite honest, I didn't realize a view of the water existed like this without going closer to Geist. The view was relaxing, the drinks are good, and I didn't get to try any of the food, but everything that went by smelled delicious. This is definitely an awesome spot to visit in the Summer and Fall, and I plan to head back soon.

I was surprised! My hubby the carnivore really loved his steak. I had the salmon and it was great. I figured this place would be on par with TGIFridays or Applebees but it was way better. It was warm, excellent service (refilled my sodas jiffy on the spot) and hot food. Will go back!
I dont get by here as often as i would like too. Love the Greek salad and NY pizza. How fast does their mini train run?

This place is so cool.

I want to preface this review with I did not eat anything while here. The pizza is Chipotle style where you pick what you want and they bake it super quickly for you in a big giant oven. The food I saw looked delicious but didn't look like anything groundbreaking.

What WAS groundbreaking was allllllll the beer taps they had available to the customers. When you walk in you can see an entire wall of taps ready for consumption. All you have to do is go to the register, give them your card and get a bracelet. Holding the bracelet up to the beer tap allows you to choose whatever beer you want and fill up!

The beer is metered and however much you pour is how much you end up paying for. This is great because if you just want to try something, you can pour a teeny bit and just pay a teeny bit. If it sucks, you can proceed to the next tap and if it's good, you can go for it.

All places should have this beer tap functionality. It's incredible, and if you're in this area of Nashville, STOP HERE.

Nice enough bar. I ordered a burger medium well but it came out really rare. I'm willing to give them a pass as it was extremely loud and the bartender might've thought I said medium rare. The burger was still very good. The bartender was by herself in a packed house and everyone was getting there orders and drinks quick. Not bad willing to try again.

Best wings in the area without a doubt, especially the garlic Parmesan 
Bar area quite lively good selection of beers
If you want a bit more peace and quiet go upstairs or to the right bar

Good food but HORRIBLE SERVICE! Not only were we ignored in an empty restaurant but we were charged 18% gratuity for a party of five when the menu clearly said parties of six or more!!! When we disputed the bill and got ignored again! Terrible!

My husband and I went out for our Anniversary dinner last night. This place has an interesting ambiance- dark and reddish but fine for a date night. Casual and somewhat cozy.
 
Appetizers- filet egg rolls were good- cheesy, crunchy. Crab asparagus soup was creamy and tasty. Overall though, both apps were very salty. I couldnt even eat the croutons on top of the soup- tasted like a salt lick.

We opted to skip salads. Entrees: my husband had a bacon wrapped filet and I had the shrimp and catfish special. His was served over whipped potatoes and asparagus and mine was over a pancetta risotto. Again- mine was super salty- didnt taste my huband's. Mine was so salty to the point of I couldn't even really enjoy it. I just feel like if they laid off the salt it would have been a good dish. 

Dessert- the kahlua tiramisu which was the best part of the meal!

Exactly what I would come to expect from a bierhaus in its soft open. A little messy, but the staff seemed to be trying very hard to keep up with the challenges. 

My friend and I went the day after opening because she has been to the chain in Germany and her hometown and was antsy to try one now that it's twenty minutes away (she brought her dirndl in her purse just in case). The interior is humongous and fits the theme. Parking is a mess, but it seems as if the lot isn't complete yet. 

The family style seating is interesting, but it would be better if the hosts were more cognizant of who they were seating together. We (3 college students) were seated with a group of elderly women who didn't seem receptive to us sitting in such close proximity and stopped speaking to one another once we were seated at their table. The crowds seemed to be older. Because the restaurant is so close to so many colleges, I'd love to see outreach and themed nights geared toward younger groups to balance it out. 

They have a decent selection of vegetarian and gluten free options, which I did not expect from a meat-and-bread based Bavarian restaurant. I ended up choosing a small beer and a goat cheese pretzel. A little expensive for the amount of food I got, but it was pretty tasty. 

I'd like to go back and see how service improves once everyone settles in.

Well this is the original location. I was actually looking to eat something else but it seems there really isn't much good in Santa Barbara/ goleta.

Ladies at the register were ok, not good, not great.. Just ok. No smiles but not rude either.

However, they guy who gave me my food was friendly and polite!

Chicken Caesar salad is good, you can also have them put teriyaki sauce on your chicken (I did not). The dressing they use on the salad was just right.

Char burger is generally pretty good. I wouldn't recommend eating it cold the next day tho... Really is the best fresh lol.

First and foremost, this place is COOL. It's the Gulch! Get here early because a line forms quickly. When you walk in you immediately notice the cool atmosphere they are going for. Farmhouse industrial, maybe? 

The staff also look very cool. The vibe you get is that they are maybe trying too hard to be cool to the point of being aloof. We were there for 10 minutes before anyone came to the table and after that the service was pretty minimal. 

How was the food itself? Overall, pretty good, though there were some things that could be handled better. For instance, when you order a toast, the bread is a nice crunchy-chewy combo, so a *sharp* knife is required. The standard issue knife provided didn't... cut it (sorry, I couldn't resist). The fig and prosciutto toast, while appropriately named in the singular, should probably come with more than one fig on top. Prosciutto was just a whole mess, again, because there wasn't a good knife.

Overall, this was good but overpriced and service could have been a lot better.

I've been to Lotus Inn multiple times and have had a pretty good experience every time.  I always start with the sweet potato sushi roll...since I don't eat any fish.  It's not on the menu, but they always know what I'm talking about when I ask for it. The sauce they put on top is amazing!

For entrees..I've only ever had the sesame chicken and the pad thai.  The sesame chicken is good, very standard.  The pad thai was different than other pad thais I've had...it was pretty spicy! but overall still good. 

The inside of the place is a really cool vibe, with a large bar and nice interior. Would definitely recommend for a night out.

Cute place, great customer service, and delicious, inventive food! It is a bit pricey, but I feel it was worth it! 

We tried the seasonal pumpkin spice donut which had a flavorful pumpkin puree filling of some sort. It wasn't too sweet and tasted like real pumpkin - no artifical flavors here. I liked that it wasn't overloaded with filling!

We also had the hot chicken donut sandwich which was amazing! The spice/heat level was perfect and the slaw complemented the chicken very well. You don't even think twice about donut buns being a little unusual. 

We rounded out the meal with a matcha latte (with oat milk, yum!) and the nitro cold brew. Both were great! I'd love to go back and try the browned butter latte and the hot dogs, of course!
I love the cakes. They make them like I use to make mine . The variety that they have is truly amazing and I also love that the taste is constant every time I get one.

First let me say, because if you are like me and you like supporting business that 'give back' either via buying from local farmers, or are seasonal/sustainable, or donate, talent, or resources... you'll love the fact that Chef Colin has been very generous to local non-profits in the past through Roundabout Catering. 

As far as Roundabout Grill goes, it is a beautiful restaurant! It manages to tie in nature-urban themes and be classy and hip all at the same time. Two of the larger walls are covered with plants, they also have swinging chairs, incorporate logs into their features, have an open kitchen, and a 'closed off with bead strings' party section. Their tables have lovely rusty-classy wood tops.

The service was slow at times (but they were busy and had a private party going), but was exemplary otherwise. Our waitresses were super professional and polite. 

I had the House Pasta with the $5.00 Meal Salad. The Salad was huge! It came with 1/2 of a butter lettuce garnished with feta cheese, strawberries, roasted pecans, and apple strips. FYI it comes with what tasted like a mayo based dressing, so if you hate mayo (like me) or are vegan ask for a vinaigrette, but this was on me because I failed to ask what the dressing was! 

The house pasta was very good! The noodles were like longer macaroni noodles (about 3X the size) and cooked perfectly, they were truly delicious! The pasta was garnished with freshly grilled tomatoes, spinach, and huge cubes of rich and creamy mozzarella! The olive oil sauce was rich and tasty. My only criticism the pasta was just super rich - a little bit more of acidity to balance out the richness would of made it a 5 star dish versus yummy 4 star dish.  I'd still order it again :) 

As far as Roundabout Grill being 'vegetarian friendly' they have two meals that were vegetarian (one of the two were not vegan -maybe ask for no cheese?) and if I recall about 4 vegan/vegetarian friendly salads. FYI the warm beet salad looked and smelled amazing!

Definitely will be coming back!

Wow! That Reuben was amazing! I was so surprised the texture of the Seitan was SO LEGIT! I wasn't expecting that from seitan. It the mushrooms and seitan were just like the traditional Philly cheesesteaks I remember. And omg, those fries, flavorful and fried to perfection. Aside from being a bit pricey for the sandwich and fries, it was really tasty! Definitely recommend!

I love this place. The owner is super friendly, and even accommodated my friend who wanted just a few falafels with her chicken plate. I'm not sure he even charged us for this bonus little side, but how kind. While the pita's are microwaved back to life, the rest of the food definitely fits the bill. I had the gyro plate with most of the fixings from the small toppings bar, including jalepenos, black olives, green peppers, red onions, pickles, cucumbers, cheese, salad, lettuce, and an assortment of sauces. Portions are enormous for a beautifully low price. Everything is under $10 from a quick glance at the extensive menu.

Atmosphere-wise, it's a bit cool for the winter, but tolerable. The seating is reminiscent of most fast food joints with small group seating arrangements. There is a large flat screen near the counter if you need some entertainment.

There's plenty of parking around the back of the restaurant, conveniently away from the hectic traffic on Charlotte.

Definitely worth a try for the budget gourmet in town.

Really disappointed today and maybe I expect to much from BBD - I ordered the shrimp basket with onion rings and a side of Ranch Dressing with a Diet Dr Pepper - I got the basket and it was not like I am used to with a good amount of food it was far from that - The onion rings ok - NO Ranch Dressing - Dr Pepper was not diet and I check with the waitress and she had on the order DIET. Once again as I indicated that maybe I expect too much from BBD and I am used a good size portion that makes me full looking at it. Well I will not order any fish related items in the future - I will still be a BBD customer. Oh by the way I wish my waitress would have payed more attention to her station than someone else.

Ate at the bar and both of us had the burger and fries. One of the best burgers I've ever had and maybe the best fries I've EVER had! Got our food fast during Friday night happy hour! Our bartenders were very entertaining as well!

Mmmm delicious. Burgers are the best as well as the milkshakes. Can't wait to try the avocado burger next.
Does take a while for food to be ready though.
Also, when eating the burgers, get ready for some heart burn.
Worth it for me but it is really intense in that area.

I went here with a LARGE group for a birthday party - and the staff was totally cool with our boisterous crowd. We ordered pretty much everything on the menu, and it was all delicious. Pulpo and patatas bravas were the standouts. But so pricey! I would love to go back, but not too hungry and probably after pay day.

Really AMAZING restaurant. Across the board from arriving to departure, this restaurant delivers a fantastic experience.

Firstly, the place itself is right by the beach and you can hear the waves coming in. So, the ambiance is set. ( They have heaters to keep you warm )

Secondly, the food is delicious. The wine pairing is fantastic.

Thirdly, the service is on point. They are attentive and knowledgeable.

All in all, My wife and I got to eat at a few nice places in Santa Barbara and 
Caruso's was the best.

I haven't been to Cafe Tiramisu in a long time, and after this afternoon I certainly won't be back.

I was shopping in the 124 street area and decided to stop in for an iced red tea latte. Sounds simple, right? I walked in and sat at a table near the door. Over five minutes went by and no server had approached me. Maybe I was supposed to order at the counter? I got up, went to the counter, and the several staffers behind the counter were all being busy getting drinks and whatever together. One finally acknowledged me and after an inquisition about where I was sitting (I had to point out the table several times), she said she would be right back and went to deliver food to customers.

In the meantime, another server came along and said she did not see me sitting where I was. I had no idea I was so invisible. Made my day. I ordered my drink, paid, and was told it would be brought out to me. 

Fifteen minutes passed. At the 20 minute mark I went back to the counter and told yet another staff person that my drink had not yet arrived. He assured me it would be brought out to me right away. About five minutes later, the same server who I placed my order with and paid brought me my drink, and said they had almost forgotten me.

Invisible and forgettable. Wow.

The drink was good enough but my now my mood had soured to the point that I could not really enjoy it. Had my drink not come when it (finally) did, I would have gotten up and demanded a refund. It was about a half hour from the time I entered the cafe until I finally got my drink.

Interestingly, afterwards I packed up my stuff and used the washroom (which, by the way, was out of soap), and when I got out less than five minutes later someone else was already in the seat I had previously occupied and was having his order taken. I guess he was less invisible and forgettable than me. Did I smell bad or something? 

Seriously - the servers were friendly, but the service was not good on a number of levels here. I am very disappointed and it takes a lot to get me this upset over a customer service experience.

I enjoy this place for its intimate vibe, a rarity in UCity. It's a great way to get warmed up for a night out because most of the undergrad crowd isn't really attracted to the place, so you won't feel like you've been dumped into a 4Loco tank of adrenaline, filled with sharks - horny sharks. I usually get a few brews, a bite to eat, and then move to the other side of the river for much debauching and revelry.

All the food that I've had here so far has been tasty - nachos, wings, some kind of "Asian-inspired" noodle dish and a salmon steak. I usually dislike places that push the whole sustainable food thing, but this place does it without being too preachy - or at least they've not been too preachy to me.

The bathroom signs can be confusing. I don't know what the sex difference, if any, between a pointer and a setter. Someone enlighten me, because I might not be as clever as I think I am.

Finally, they consistently have a good selection of local brews on tap, and they always have Victory Pils - a big plus for me.

Kudos, White Dog Cafe. You're better than I thought you'd be.

Typically this was my go to diner on Saturday mornings but it's been a hit or miss lately. The management here are definitely not very friendly & always seem to have some type of attitude that you notice right when you walk in the door. Some waiters/waitresses are great but others not so much. Definitely a mixture of attitudes with the staff/management. I usually get a veggie omelette or waffles which always comes out great. I also love the eggplant parm sandwhich so the food is relatively good. Servers are usually quick & attentive as well. Only a couple of times I have had crappy service here. Overall, good food but poor attitudes amongst the entire staff.
Professional, friendly, helpful staff. Brewed, pour over and cold press options. Modern fresh look. Some outdoor seating. Loved it.

They said the wait was 45 minutes--it only ended up being 20 yay!  Warning:  parking lot is tiny and shopping center is popular!

Sat down, came prepared, since it's a BYOB.  Started w/ the meat/cheese platter--pretty good, but I've had better.  That said, everything was fresh and sliced thin, the way I like it.  

Then, the bread came out.  IT WAS THE BEST BREAD I'VE EVER HAD.  It was this garlic, parmesan LOAF.  Warm, toasty, perfection.  They offered us more, and we had to say no simply because it was delicious enough to be a meal, and no one needs that much bread.

I ordered the gnocchis and substituted a vodka/rosa sauce instead of the marinara that came with it.  I've never seen gnocchis like these.  They were like mini hotpockets--ENORMOUS for gnocchi size, but absolutely delicious--simply melted in your mouth.  Sauce was creamy and delicious.

My company got the eggplant parmesan and veal parmesan -- both were VERY happy with their choices, and one of them is very picky about his Italian food!  We would all come back, and hopefully, eat less of the magical bread so we have room for dessert next time!

As a Drexel student, this is the only bar on campus...wish it wasn't. MIkey's used to be Ecco Qui (they switched management) and man, do I miss the old place.

Their selection of beer on tap is not bad, but their food is sub-par. I've gotten the sweet potato fries which were pretty okay, the onion rings that made me throw up for three hours and a plain pizza which was burnt at the edges and soggy at the same time.

Waitstaff is also not anything to rave about.

The only thing I like is the beer selection and the fact that they have a patio - saves getting up from the table to smoke.

Very friendly and accommodating waitress. Lots of drink choices. Good was very good. Prices reasonable. Would have given 5 but my order came out wrong after very specific direction. The waitress did take the meal off the bill and offer for it to be remade. Very sweet waitress.
Food was average but the staff was poor.  The worst part is that the place was not clean at all.  Must avoid.

If I could give a negative rating, I would. We politely asked the hostess to be seated at a different table due to the table she seated us at being tiny and in a major walkway. Her response was to yell at my mother, "We're busy! That's all we have!" and storm off. Needless to say, we didn't stay. 

If this place plans to stay open, I'd suggest hiring professional people!

super good for brunch but kind of expensive! it's nice that it's byob though so don't forget that! I got the steak and eggs and could have definitely shared with another. Sometimes the wait is long but they have a whole area you can walk around and shop if you'd like.

We recently ate here after several years! They had some great choices on a Prix Fix menu for $39... Shrimp cocktail, soup or salad and delicious filet mignon! The service was attentive . Our server Brad made sure we had everything the way we liked it and helped with some suggestions! A wonderful meal! We will go back sooner rather than later!

We ordered from here as takeout order. The spaghetti and meatballs were dry, the meatballs looked like they were boiled only. The penne ala vodka was too salty. It had a lot of bacon pieces to it which made it worse. The pizza was expected to be at least better, but it wasn't. The dough tasted like if it was made with tap water and was not cooked all the way. Everything was Tasteless and if we can give a lower rating we would.

This place was a fantastic find! Bring your own tequila is a genius idea, and you can up the amount of it to your liking. Blood orange and mango mixers were just right...not too sweet or tart. We started with the mango chipotle guacamole & the queso fundido that is topped with homemade chorizo...I could have eaten just these two items all night! The guacamole was especially delicious...perfectly creamy and citrusy at the same time. 

As for main courses...I tried the tamarind braised shortribs, which was like a perfect pot roast that Grandma would make. It came with tiny little roasted potatoes and greens. Was a little more American than Mexiacn. Other dishes at the table included the salmon (beautiful texture), mahi mahi and shrimp enchiladas. We were all so full that we skipped dessert. Will definitely return!!! Just remember: cash only! Thanks Lolita!

This place was pretty busy for a Monday evening. They have so many cool options for snacks but being vegan I was a little limited. I went with the trusty mangonada and it is so good. Never had one? It is spicy, sweet, and salty (think tamarind candy) and sweet fruity goodness from the mango.

I highly recommend giving this place a try. There's something for everyone.
Went for Sunday brunch the other day. I got their breakfast burrito and it was absolutely delicious! They coffee was decent and the staff were pleasant.

Great energy, service, food, and cocktails - loved it!  Very creative menu that follows up w/amazing tastes.  Couple of dishes just ok and need a couple of more visits to bump to 5 stars.  This place seems pretty solid.

First...its a sports bar. Its not the Italian place that it used to be. My review will be based on what it is, not what it USED to be. 

The bar food is good. Wings, Pizza, Calamari is delish. 

They have a buffet on Friday,  and I enjoy getting a drink, some wings, and some tasty fries. You can't beat it for Hockession.

This was one of my favorite places to go when I lived in Santa Barbara. We were in town today and I wanted to take my boyfriend for a great cup of coffee and one of their wonderful pastries. It was late in the afternoon so we took a chance to see if they were open. The sign on the window in fact said they were open. We walked in and approached the cash register where there was also an open sign. The waiter came in and we said hello. He rudely pulled the open sign away and said "we are closed" never looking up at us or making eye contact. We asked if we can get a cup of coffee and he said "only espresso drinks" we said that would be fine and he said "to go only" never looking up at us. We got our coffees and left, but not before we told the waiter how disappointed we were in his approach and lack of service. And boy did my boyfriend give it to him!!! I had a restaurant for over 20 years and have been in customer service for much longer. I have never written a review before because I usually give people the benefit of the doubt. Maybe they are having a bad day or a sick child at home. There was absolutely no excuse for the way we were treated there today.

Me and my husband are moving to south Philly and we are so lucky to run into Kung Fu Hogies food truck which is just across the street from us. Since my husband is vegetarian, we always are actively searching and trying new vegie food. The people from Kung Fu Hoagies are sweet and friendly...this time we tried their pork bahm mi..they gave really good portion. The prok is made of tou fu and it feels very chewy and flavorful. We definitely will go back and try other options on the menu.

I've been to the Steer-In a handful of times. The very first time I was new to Indy (young and fresh off the U-Haul from Pennsylvania) so I ordered the BLT while everyone else around me ordered pork tenderloin sandwiches. My BLT was delicious but when those tenderloins came out it seemed I had made a mistake -- the Hoosier Tenderloin was the staple dish. Just so all you Hoosiers know, these sandwiches aren't a thing outside of the state -- gotta hook a new Hoosier up with the 411 on the local delicacies!

Since then, I've been back and only ordered the Hoosier Tenderloin. They have tons of other options, but as someone who is far, far behind on their lifetime tenderloin quota (lifetime grand total = 2), it seems silly to go with anything else. The breading on the tenderloin is the perfect thickness and has awesome crunch. The pork inside is moist and tender. The buns look like sheer golden brown perfection swiped right out of a fast food commercial. The side of fries doesn't disappoint, nor do the speedy soda refills! I also really like that while the tenderloin is larger than the bun, it's not one of those crazy, gigantic tenderloins that looks like it could benefit from a second bun altogether. It's not too big, not too small -- just right.

The Steer-In itself has a very old-time atmosphere. As if you stepped back to another era. It leaves you with the feeling that you're having dinner at your friend's mom's house. Warm, friendly, inviting. They're actually really quick there too and have a new iPad ordering system so you can pay (cash or card) right at the table, a change from before when you had to take your bill to the register.

Definitely worth a stop. I recommend the Steer-In for lunch and nostalgia any day of the week!

Had the best experience this morning at first watch !! Everyone was very friendly and attentive. I always have the best service  and breakfast here ... today I had the elevated egg sandwich it was delicious I didn't get a picture but it's worth ordering ! The waitress Tiffany was AMAZING and so sweet everything came out on time and our drinks were never empty! This restaurant gets 5 stars from me also the business was so clean even the restrooms !! Thank you first watch for another amazing experience !!!! Great job

This was our first time to Opryland Hotel - - simply to see the holiday decorations.  We decided to eat there to avoid the atroshish parking fee. (you get your ticket validated).  We both enjoyed the pulled pork sandwich.  At $19, it is expensive, however, I must mention that the portion was extremely generous, i.e. 1/2 lb. of meat.  Further, there had to be over 50 French Fries on each of our plates, along with pickles and coleslaw.  Our server kindly substituted my husband's fries for Mac 'n Cheese.  We ended up splitting one sandwich and taking the other home.  Wine is also a little $$$, but all in all, the food was delicious, and our server, Ryan was wonderful.  We'd definitely go back.  The décor is delightful, with large oak kegs, and very clean.

The place was understaffed and it was a hot day.  The people who had to work seemed worn out.  AC was enough, at least for the customers.  My bacon burger and one of my friend's bacon burger were cooked too much.  My avocado smoothie was good and another one of my friends liked the french fries, which weren't bad.  

I'm not sure how the seafood is here.  I was tempted to try, but I wanted to eat vegan because my friends are vegan and I wanted to be respectful of that since we went there because it was a vegan place nearby.

The interior decor is superb and very homely.  It is a nice local establishment to try to vibe up the 52nd St. business district with its neighbor next door.
Had a fantastic experience.  Amazing food and absolutely incredible service with Koree.  She is super attentive and made our visit exceptional.  If you come in, ask for Koree.
Excellent fresh bagels and their speciality cream cheese is delicious! Some of the best bagels I've eaten.

This is probably the worst Imo's of the entire chain.  I have had several negative experiences with this store while at work, resulting in delayed meetings, hangry co-workers, and cold food being delivered 45+ minutes late.  One event was a training where 30+ people waited over an hour for lunch.  We complained, no apology, no refund, not even a "kiss my @ss." 
 
Today was no exception, I literally made it as easy as possible for them to get this right.  I placed an order online (3 pizzas, 3 salads, 3 drinks) at 11:05am, called at 11:10am to confirm that they received said order.  I was placed on hold at least 5 times, then the manager got on the phone to say they couldn't find it, after being asked my name for the 5th time he found it.  I confirmed that it would be delivered at 12pm, and to call my cell phone to meet me in the lobby.  12:05, 12:15, 12:20... I call... "we're really busy." "Well when will it be here?"  "I don't know."  "Well is it going to be an hour?" "Probably not."  

12:45pm, my phone rings, they hang up.  I walk outside attempting to avoid any further mishap of having someone actually do their job.  Imo's has arrived... hurray!  NOT MY ORDER, delivering for someone else in my building.  LOL 

12:50pm, food arrives, cold.  "My boss said we're sorry, we get a lot of orders at lunch but I brought yours first."  So wait.... those other orders in your car are MORE than 50 minutes late?  LOL 

Dear "boss" - your store is a disgrace.  I gave it YET another chance, only to prove to myself that it was a poor decision.  Your staff is rude, you consistently screw up orders, and you're doing the Imo's chain a disservice.  You should close.  The only reason I'm making it worth my time to write this review and give 1 star, is that the order was mostly correct.  Cold, but correct.  

Imo's owner, if you ever read this - take action because this store is hurting your name!

Had brunch there Sunday.  Best biscuits and gravy ever...even better than mine (and I am a good cook, by the way).  The Bloody Mary was tasty and came with a full vegie garden. I cannot wait to go back!

Really cool, chill bar with a fun upstairs (tv, pool table, darts, and PHOTO HUNT!).  One of my favorite burgers in the city.  The mixed sweet potato and regular fries are great.  I was really excited to try the chicken tenders cordon bleu, but they were pretty disappointing, but most of the other stuff I've had here has been pretty good.  The only downside to this place is that it can be tough to get a table and if you are hanging out on the 3rd floor, you need to go downstairs to order drinks and food.

Impeccable service. Not quite there for the portion, for the price, for the region, and its missing Michelin star(s). You are left feeling hungry without having gone through an experience worthy of the hunger.

This is hands down my favorite sandwich shop of all time.  Never once have a had a bad sandwich from here. I've lived in Philly all my life and this is unquestionably the single greatest sandwich shop in the entire city and state. You have to get the fries with the truffle wiz, whatever sandwich you pick will be the best one you've had. I wish I could brown nose these guys even more but I don't know how.

Thai Chili 88 is a real gem for Turnersville. Their dining room has a great atmosphere and the service is decent enough considering the price you pay, about $5 for a dine-in lunch which comes with Fried Rice & an Spring Roll. Their Fried Rice is unlike typical Chinese affair, being not to oily, yet still very tasty. If you go, try their Drunken Noodles because it's fantastic. Definitely will be back again!

Very good lunch. Had the meatloaf which was very good. Nice touch of spice and moist 
The waitress was terrific would definitely recommend

The very very best bakery I've been to in years. I literally feel like I'm in France again when I bite into their wonderful pastries. Their chocolate almond croissants are really in a different league than all the others croissants in town.

I was surprised they also sold banh mi - the tofu banh mi is pretty good but their pork belly banh mi tends to be too fatty (I prefer less fatty pork pieces)

Osteria has one of my favorite happy hours in Fairmount and honestly the city. My favorite is the chicken liver pasta and all of their cocktails I've had have been amazing. The service is also really great and the servers are all incredibly nice and knowledgeable.

I was told this little shop had amazing sandwiches i ordered the number one "ham piled high" and added  some extra veggies. Right away the first thing I noticed was their good service. The sandwich was pretty tasty and they even brought it to my table. 

Giving this place 4 stars!!

This was our first night in NOLA .....what an awesome treat for anything Seafood...All kind of Steamed Combo Trays of local crabs,crawfish ,& shrimp. What a great place! Service was very accomidating and friendly. Full bar inside and 2 full rooms of tables . Also very close to the Crowne Plaza where most Cruise Ships Guests stay.. .We just came for our foodie tour and great Music!!

I have enjoyed the cuban food here many times, and have yet to be disappointed. Dishes are full of flavor and very filling! Black beans always delicious. Cuban toast with melted butter, a guilty pleasure. Service has improved over time. The location has always seemed odd to me, but this area can use more good, homey latin food like Cuban Breezes.

We were four adults, a 7 month old baby, and a three year old girl. After asking for the bill they included the %18 tip because we are 6 people. They counted the 7 month old baby!! I have not seen any resturant doing that !!! The waiter said, this is the rule and I am not the owner!!!!! I won't come again and I won't recommended it. I hate the idea of using loophole to take people money.

This place just opened up a location in Arnold and their wings are the best I've had in STL so I wanted to check the consistency between locations. I went with three of my brothers around 12:30 pm. 

The restaurant itself is in an excellent location and is beautiful. Nice and big with a big patio. The hostess was very nice and told us we could sit anywhere in the bar if we wanted, so we headed that way. We were greeted by our server within 2 minutes and she got our drinks (4 waters) quickly and returned. I ordered 12 wings and the chicken strip salad. My brothers ordered a Brett's Conglomeration pizza, the Sybergs Chicken Sandwich, and 12 wings. 

The food was delicious. My wings were spot on with the fry level and the sauce was plentiful. The salad was crisp and the chicken strips were warm and sauced perfectly. I love that they use provel cheese! The waitress was very friendly as were the managers that checked on us. 

The food took about 20 minutes to come out. The pizza took an extra 10 and came out after the rest of us were half done with our meals. I also ordered a beer when we ordered our food and I received it right before our food came out 20 minutes later. That seems like a long time especially since I never requested it be brought out with dinner. Also, I had to wait another 3-5 minutes after my salad came out to eat it because I had to wait for silverware. 

Overall the food is excellent, the staff are friendly but could be a little more attentive and the wait time for food is all over the place. And maybe it was an off day in the bar but if you plan on drinking more than one beer with dinner, maybe sit AT the bar. I will definitely be back for the delicious wings!

A chinese restaurant that does korean noodles better than its chinese noodles.

Good:
- Crisp pumpkin with salted egg yolk: not over-battered, lightly sugared
- Korean cold noodle: great noodle texture

Meh:
- Clear noodle with special sesame sauce (aka la pi): refreshing flavor, but the clear flat noodle texture is a bit stale compared to others I've had
- Braised pork neck bones: good portion for the price, not something I'd crave again
- Hot crisp fish: a signature dish here, not over-battered, a bit bland compared to its chicken counterpart (chengdu spicy chicken/la zi ji), generic fish inside the batter

Hard Pass:
- Braised beef noodle soup: bland broth and overcooked mushy noodles

Service: eye-rolling
The server reassured me multiple times that their Chinese soup noodles come with very al dente noodles before I decided to order their braised beef noodle soup. Al dente to people with no teeth maybe, because my family found zero bounce and chew in the noodles when it came. When we brought this up to that server, he brought his manager/an older lady, who simply justified that their noodle has always been like that and the server is new. Aight if your server didn't know what he was talking about, he could've simply told us he didn't know instead of straight up deceiving us about something and with full confidence multiple times. The lady disgruntledly took away the noodle soup after we insisted we don't want it anymore because it did not taste how they advertised. That's your customer service issue not ours. Save the attitude next time.

I have visited Crushcakes a number of times because it is incredibly convenient.  The food has always been good, but that is not what I am complaining about.  The service  is terrible, almost every time I go there.  This morning really made me hit the boiling point, and I really doubt that I will go back, despite the fact that it is 1 block from my office.  The woman at the register was obviously very tired and couldn't remember my simple order of a pastry and coffee.  She had to ask twice what pastry I wanted.  After she took my order, she began helping the person after me but had to stop because she started coughing on EVERYTHING.  I am just glad she had already handed me my scone because she coughed on all of the baked goods.  People in the food service industry should NOT go to work sick.  The owners/managers should definitely discourage this.  Then I started my long wait.  There was only one person who ordered a drink in front of me in line, just one, but I also had to wait until the person that ordered after me got their beverage, and then some.  I waited for 15 minutes for a latte.  There was no apology from the servers, no sense of urgency. At one point the woman at the register walked by me and said, "your latte is almost ready".  Great.  I can see that the baristo literally just started my latte.  So then I wait some more.  

At another visit, where I ordered online to try to cut down on the wait time during my lunch break from work, I still ended up waiting over 20 minutes for a to-go order due to negligence on the staff side.  I ordered online about 30 minutes before I went to the restaurant and made a note that I wanted no cheese on my sandwich and a side of salad dressing for my salad.  Apparently they do not read the notes because after arriving at the restaurant, and waiting 10 minutes for my order, I received what I ordered with cheese on the sandwich.  I had to send it back, telling them that there should be no cheese and salad dressing on the side of the salad.  I waited another 10 minutes for my sandwich to be remade.  When I finally received it, it looked like they had just scraped the cheese off the bread and still had no salad dressing for my salad.  I thought this would be my last time there, but I like to give people chances.  I am done, SO DONE.  

Also, why don't you try serving vegan and gluten free cupcakes on a regular basis? 

Oh, and one more bad experience there: I went in at 3 pm one afternoon to get a shot of espresso and they told me I couldn't be served because they had just cleaned the machine.  I am sorry, but aren't you open for 2 more hours? Maybe that should have been my last time there...

Lolita is a fun and casual Mexican restaurant that is BYO, no reservations, and cash only.  We have wanted to try it for a long time and finally stopped in and they had a table available.  Hubby ran to the wine and spirits store and picked up a bottle of tequila. They would not seat us until both of us were there but he was fast so I only waited a few minutes.  

Is it the best mexican restaurant in the city? Absolutely not.  Does it have amazing margarita mix? Yes!  We got the pineapple jalepeno margarita mix, which I have not seen anywhere else. I was a little hesitant about the level of spice, but the waitress said it is sweet at first and then just a kick in the back of your throat. She described it perfectly!  It was definitely a mild spice at the finish and not overpowering at all. This was definitely the highlight of the meal. 

They served hot and tasty tortilla chips with two kinds of salsa: tomato salsa with a medium spice level and a green salsa with a minty flavor. Both were awesome. So we were off to a good start.

Hubby enjoyed his two dishes: pork carnitas (came with four tortillas) and the pulled chicken tamale.  Those two dishes were a lot of food. He said that it was really good and he was definitely stuffed after.  

Being vegetarian, there are a few items that you can order and then you can substitute either grilled portabellas or tofu for a few of the dishes. I opted for two of the vegetarian appetizers. The beet salad with goat cheese was exactly that: beets and goat cheese. There wasn't anything special or wow about it.  Could have gotten this at Panera.  The other dish I ordered was the mushroom gorditas.  Great presentation and terrible execution.  The dish consisted of two breaded round disks (I think there was mushroom inside but I am not sure) that were dry and very salty.  I never think that dishes were salty and I was taken aback by how salty it was. I definitely do not recommend this dish.  

I was so looking forward to trying Lolita and was so excited to finally make it there.  Maybe my expectations were too high. But with so many awesome Mexican restaurants in Philly, Lolita doesn't rank up there for me.

My husband found this place on Yelp several months ago, and we thought we'd give it a try for date night. We've been there at least 2 times a month since! It's that good! Tiny interior with limited seating, but it is worth the wait (though to be honest, we have gotten lucky and have never had to wait. But if we ever did, it'd be worth it). The tuna dumplings are a must try item. If I could only eat one food for the rest of my life, Vic's tuna dumplings would be a top contender for my choice. I'm also a huge fan of the pepper salmon. I don't think you can go wrong with any of the rolls, either. We order at least 3 different rolls every time we go, and have loved every single one. It's a BYO, so feel free to imbibe. It's also right next door to Helium Comedy Club, and one block down from Capogiro (check my review for that glorious place as well), which is perfect if you want to make a night of it. I've been to a TON of sushi places, and Vic is my absolute favorite.

The best thing since sliced bread! 

My husband's exact words. He hit it on the nail for sure. 
Not only were they in compliance with Covid but the service was phenomenal.

The gentleman who took my order over the phone was kind and patient. He made sure they had what they needed for my order before confirming it. I was told 20 minutes and sure enough it was ready and still HOT by the time we got home to eat. 

The Brussels were yummy (a little over seasoned for my liking) but my husband LOVED them. 

It's really based on our palettes. Some things aren't for everyone right? 

Now that macaroni...... OH MY WORD! Best in the burg! The last place I ate macaroni was oak & stone and this definitely tops it for me. 

The Rich boy fish sandwich was so DAMN good down to the last bite! The shrimp were big, juicy and fried to perfection. Lettuce was fresh and the bun was so fluffy. 

My husband ordered the 1/2 chicken seasoned with Jamaican jerk and it  was JERKtastic! So flavorful and mouth watering. Not dry at all!

Lastly Desert, Bread pudding was moist and tasty. Lots of nuts and flavor. The brownie was soft and melted in my mouth. 

Overall great food, great service and great experience!

WOULD RECOMMEND!

Great spot, it really is, and I say this as a middle child. I was freezing and wanted something warm and boom, there I was with an excellent Reuben with special "sawce." As that brand new grill gets broken in, these will only get better...

Hands down best BBQ  in Clearwater:Largo area So good i don't even sauce them! People are great as I'm handicapped and they bring food to my car!!!!Sides are good too! Only complaint is they're not open weekends!Get there early as they only cook up so much and they have a great lunch crowd!

We took my mom here for her birthday and it was great!  BYOB.  Food was excellent, worth the money.  Very friendly staff.  Private room was having a party for a community group but other wise we had the place to ourselves.  Highly recommended!

Remember when Ed & Marge's Cafeteria was in the Indianapolis Chamber of Commerce Building?   They lovingly didn't want you to linger at their place, lest you didn't get back to work to keep the economy moving along.  That place has long since closed and in it's place is the new Sunrise Cafe.  They have gutted the place to open up a relaxing,  almost Zen like sophisticated  atmosphere of soft blues and beiges where one cannot help but stay just one more minute (or hour, or day for that matter) to escape the pressures of the day.  The staff is laid back and friendly.   I was in the mood for comfort food and decided on the Mushroom and Swiss Burger.  It was HUGE and JUICY!   The house made bun was very soft and delicious too.  I will definitely return.
I love the food. They are just very very slow. I've ordered food and drove 25 minutes to get there and still have to wait almost an hour for the food.
I love going to this place! My boyfriend and I have been therefore times since we moved up in June. We've had the paella, octopus, garlic shrimp, Spanish ham, and empanadas. Everything was DELICIOUS!
Went one time, that was enough for us. Just because they serve mimosa's doesn't impress me..and their iced tea was nasty!
The food was wonderful I recommend the southern plate or the the cajun hash browns. They offer a military discount as well

A wonderful experience. The food, the bourbon and atmosphere were briliant. Tom out server went out I God way to give us a great evening. I can't speak more highly of the place. You must give it a go.

Fantastic BBQ - very friendly staff! Very recently opened so think they are working out a few kinks but they have a nice patio area, are expanding their beers on tap and their smoky 'fruitwood' bbq is some of the best I have tried in STL. You will also see the owner making rounds making sure all customers are happy. Great addition to the restaurants in this area - I highly recommend.

Pretty typical Southern dishes.  I grew up in the South, so I suppose it's a bit more difficult for me to be impressed with the food because it's the kind I grew up on.  However, that said, everything was cooked to perfection.  This place is famed for the celebrity drop-ins and greasy comfort food.  I imagine breakfast is even better than lunch.

The menu has changed some since they first opened as they now offer smaller portions of some items at lower prices. Service is friendly but we've experienced several kitchen mistakes several times (incomplete orders, items left off plate) but the mistakes were quickly corrected.

If you are a fan of oysters, do not order them here as the 'popcorn' oysters are mostly bread with very tiny oysters. The grilled oysters the same, very tiny, not good.  Other items though are fine: Food quality and taste is consistently good; we especially enjoy their burgers. Free soft serve ice cream and coffee are plusses at the end of the meal.

Edit 3/11/2012 Looks like they took the word 'popcorn' out of popcorn oysters on their menu but I haven't been there to order them, but if they are regular sized oysters again then I will update my review and probably add a star.

Edit 3/25/2012 Was finally able to get back here and ond order an Oyster Po-boy, the oysters are back to regular size but they seem to be a bit stingy with the number of oysters in the sandwich. For about 12 bucks, I would expect a few more than 'just' covering the bread (if you get it 'dressed' you have to pull back the lettuce and tomato to see the single layer of oysters on there). So no extra star...

Had brunch here on a Sunday afternoon for our girl's bach party :) 

Cool interior, music and atmosphere, food were decent, drinks were good and service was excellent. There was no wait for the table, and a short wait for food and drinks.

- Bloody Mary: loved
- Country Fried Bites: greasy
- Eggs Florentine: good and enjoyed the spinach cream glaze and potato pancake!
- Parmesan & truffle fries: good

One of the guys who worked there came by, chatted with us and gave us a background of the establishment...cool and interesting...

Waitress was quick and efficient. She even bought our bachelorette a shot of drink, so sweet!

Tiger Lilly 2 continues the tradition of excellence established at its previous location.   Fresh, original and perfectly cooked dishes.   Many healthy choices.  Some of the best food in the Indy metro area.
Great bread bowl!!!! Maybe I could suggest digging deeper into the bowl to allow just a little more soup!

This was disappointing.  This used to be one of the bf's favorite Italian restaurants, but the past few dining experiences were just ehh.  This past trip basically wrote it off the list for him, and we've decided that we'll stick with Bartolino's for Italian.

1) Dinner salad - nothing special to rave about.
2) Capellini Carciofi - this was actually not bad.  It was not heavy like some pastas tend to be, but there was not much capellini in the dish.  While some ppl may find it great that the dish is FILLED with chicken, I personally wanted a balance of everything and was disappointed.
3) Chicken on special - Usually we assume that whatever is on special for the evening would be the best bet.  WRONG.  I'm still not sure how this dish is different from the other chicken dishes on the menu.  After looking at the menu again, it sounds just like the Picante Pollo or the Soto Chicken - charboiled chicken breast, topped with cheese, white wine butter sauce, and mushrooms (there might've been peppers).  The bf swore the mushrooms were from a can, and the overall appearance of the dish was not appetizing.  The side of pasta was also disappointing.

I feel like the Hill is overhyped and has been going downhill in the past few yrs.  All these places have been around forever, and maybe ppl just keep going for the sake of tradition.  BUT CAN SOMEONE PLEASE SERVE SOME BETTER FOOD!?!!?!

On the plus side, service here has always been great and when the weather is warm, you can sit outside.
Absolutely amazing popcorn. Like none other. Indy style and the chocolate sea salt. A true Indy style classic!!! Must stop for travelers.

Can we please get the hipsters out of the hospitality industry? The service was sooo sub par. Our server did greet us immediately but seemed annoyed while taking our order. You might be thinking "well maybe your a sucky customer". I've worked in restaurants through almost my entire 20's, I'm not difficult to work with. After he took our order he never came back. Not even with the beer I asked for. Someone else brought our food and someone else cashed us out. No one ever asked how anything was. Lame.

The food was ok. The ribs were pretty good, my b/f loved them. The coleslaw was tasteless and baked beans, fine. I'd take your BBQ needs elsewhere. Flemming's on 4th is pretty bangin'.

Good bagels, nice selection HOWEVER...asked for buttered and they gave Unsalted butter...yuk
Next time will bring my own.
Good food for the price but not worth the wait.  I have had better mexican food in Pasadena.

Nothing fancy about this place, but great quality. This a great low-key place to grab some good food, a couple beers, and catch up with some friends. The calzones are superb, and many options are available. There is a great beer list as well. Prices are affordable, and appropriate for the portion sizes. This place is keeping it simple, and doing it well.

5 Stars is not enough. They didn't have the full menu due to the Hurricane but we got a sausage and meatball pizza to go. So very good.
