Good food. Good drinks and huge beer selection.  More food than you could eat in a lifetime. But a chain so if you are into that...go!

Two words: BACON JAM.
I came here with my wife for a nice little brunch. It was busy, but you never felt crowded or ignored. The staff is amazing! Super friendly yet efficient and everyone gets served quickly. I had the Inclined breakfast sandwich and my wife had the Eggs Benedict. Both were delicious, but the bacon jam was phenomenal. It wasn't too sweet like a lot of versions are and had just a little kick off spice that I really enjoyed. The eggs in my wife's dish were cooked to perfection. I've been to places that only focus on breakfast that haven't nailed poached eggs like they have. If I have any thing I'd like to see more is maybe a bit more hollandaise on the eggs. Overall a fantastic meal.

Owney's BottomLine: Hey I'm drunk and I need some food....oh hey, pizza. 


Pizza is ok. Servers were cool, one was cute (bonus) and the crowd was from some post-apocalyptic world, except not run over by zombies, but by strippers and other sluts.

Needless to say I will be back for the beer and scenery, but I will eat elsewhere beforehand.

The staff is super super friendly, not obnoxiously so, just perfect. 

Waffle fries, chicken, hamburger and pork belly sliders were super.  My favorite was the pork belly, loved the blend of spice, vinegar and meat.   Had the Cuban libra donut.  It was not cloyingly sweet.  The cream was delicious.   I will be back.   Great ginger beer too.

This is a gem of a bakery. Gluten free or not this is a great place to get yummy baked goods in Santa Barbara. The breakfast sandwich and blueberry tart were delicious. My friend who has a gluten allergy was in heaven! Thanks for a wonderful experience!

Worst Chinese takeout. I've eaten at the restaurant a few times and it was very good. I tried delivery and was incredibly disappointed. First, they forgot part of my order and what they did deliver was cold, greasy and bad. Total bummer. 

I'd eat at the restaurant again (even though service is super slow). But I won't ever order delivery again.

Tony's used to have the best pizza and wings in South Jersey, but it's really gone downhill.  The pizza had this great tangy sauce that made it great, but they've since replaced it with a generic sauce that has no taste whatsoever.

Their wings used to be made in a great tangy wing sauce that wasn't overly spicy.  But once again, they changed the sauce, and now it's a fiery sauce that's absolutely brutal.  In addition, the once soft skin is now crispier - Something that I dislike.

Bring back the old Tony's, and I'll happy come back!!

Went and swung by this place to try. The pizza was really good with a nice and fluffy dough. The spicy wings and just enough spice to sweet ratio. The waitress Kayla did an amazing job very nice and helpful. 10 out of 10 would recommend. Was also nice to have $2 beers but don't know how long that deal is going for.

Just stood on line behind about 10 guys for the new Beef Kabob. First I was told it is not available and then on further questions, a discouraging "it will take about 10 minutes to prepare" with a push towards Schwarma which "also has beef". I have tried their Schwarma a few times before and was not really impressed with the dry chewy Gyro that they serve. So I decided to walk away. Not quite the experience I was looking for.

Needed to grab a late dinner and decided to try Mexican food as it was close by and had been wanting to try it out. DIL and I entered a larger than expected dining area with true Mexican ambiance. Ole! The brightly colored dining room, tables and chairs brought flavor ( no pun intended) to the restaurant and obviously delighted patrons of all ages. We ordered the appetizer combo but prior to that was served fresh piping hot tortillas with individual bowls of salsa. Salsa a little spicy for me (DUH Mexican food is not mild). The appetizer was good with a nice variety of samples. Could have used a little more sour cream with all the food. 

DIL ordered shrimp fajitas which was huge serving and looked fresh. She said it was very good. I had the shrimp wrapped in bacon atop a bed of Mexican sides. It was very tasty. One recommendation would be to take tails off shrimp. The way they are wrapped in bacon you cannot see tails are on there so you bite into it and have to take the shell out of your mouth. Once I knew it was easy enough to remove but a shocker to bite into. We both had sangria which was okay but not great.

Too much food so at least 1 more meal for each of us if husbands don't get to it first. 

I will definitely be back as the menu had lots of great choices and so many more to try.

I like California tortilla because it's different. You have Chipotle, a classic, and Baja Fresh, but this place is different. They have options like Korean BBQ bowl or chicken bacon burrito. The food is made to order with frwsh ingredients. Definitely make it a combo deal and get the queso on the side. They have a selection of hot sauces for you to try on the back wall. Food is made fairly quickly considering they have to prep and the staff are nice. Sign up for a reward card to get some good deals.

This is the best kept secret in New Port Richey.  If you ever want to have the best biscuits and gravy, then try this place.  It's not a fancy place, but it is clean and the food is fresh.  Most of the staff has worked there for years which should tell you something.  

Do waste you money at places like Denny's when you have access to real food and real people at Jimmy's.

UPDATE:
several years later and still making Jimmy's a regular event for breakfast. Chef Todd makes an outrageous western omelet...amazing. Staff is wonderful, etc. This place is the best!
This place is always a fun time. Great neighborhood place and Ryan is always friendly, and my favorite reason to visit. When him and Ashely work it's so much fun!

I really enjoy Seis Kitchen.  Each location has its own feel but the food never disappoints.  I think I've managed to taste each protein on the menu and can't give you a favorite--it's all good.  :). Go.
got a plain Cesar salad did not even think a Cesar salad could be bad. I was wrong. It was soggy and gross with olives that had pits. Yuck!! Will not be going back

I really personally did not like this place in any way shape or form.  I came here one night with some friends to play quizzo which is a trivia game and the experience was really just not good.  It is more of a sports bar which i completely understand because first there are like a hundred TVs so that's the main reason it exists.  I was however not impressed with the food by any stretch and the game itself was pretty bad because you could not hear the dude asking the questions because they had all the games on on high blast.  It was very noisy in here and well not a place I plan on coming back to anytime soon.  Just keep that in mind when considering coming here.

I had heard good things about this restaurant and it was even better than what I expected! Our waiter was friendly and helpful. The food was delicious. We started with the Mango Crab Rangoon and spicy edamame, which puts a fun twist on classic appetizers. I had the Blue Crunch roll and my friend had the Hot Popper. Both were creative and very fresh. There were so many unique rolls I can't wait to go back and try. Great selection of sake. I will definitely recommend this restaurant to others and I am planning on going back in the near future, especially on Sundays when they have drink specials and half price sushi!!

Fantastic addition to Armature Works! Amazing food and culinary experience provided by Chef and staff. Sarah our main server was outstanding. The charcuterie platter was filled with fresh, tasty cheese and accompaniments. The salmon and chicken entrees were light and prepared to perfection. The service is hands down some of the best in the city. This should be a "must try" on everyone's food list. Ambience is trendy and classy. Great at sunset by the water. Ready to go back!

Food is good, beer is tasty, staff is friendly, and decor is cool...only one complaint.  The music is way too loud, hard to have a conversation with the people at your table and difficult to even focus when eating.  We asked if I could turn it down a bit, even stating we didn't want to ruin the vibe, but just a little bit to reduce the obnoxious-ness.  We were told according to their manual it must remain at that volume.

There was nothing necessarily 'bad' about my experience at Bareburger, but nothing impressive about it either. It was just alight. 

It was nice to have two veggie burger options though (I tried the black bean burger, my boyfriend tried the sweet potato). But to add extra toppings is expensive ($2.75 to add a slice of daiya cheese is steep). The burgers were enjoyable but nothing to brag about. 

Beers are pricey too.

Lobster Omelet is delicious, with lots of lobster bits!Biscuits & gravy with over-medium eggs were delicious as well. The biscuits were a bit hard but flavors were good. Will definitely come back to try other items on menu next time we're in town
Ok they're good, but not that good. Tiramisu should be light and creamy. The one I got today tasted day old. They're also very expensive for what you get. I didn't try the cookies or cannoli.

Have signs on high tops requesting customers "bring their glasses and dishes to the bar." As a paying customer, this is absurd. After having an awful experience on my birthday with the most disrespectful & confrontational waitstaff, no response was received back from the owner as my family and I sent an email of what occurred. Poor customer service to say the LEAST. Would never recommend.

Don't let the line scary you away. It very worth the wait and standing. 

I went on New Year's Eve/Sugar bowl time so it was pretty packed around 11:30 when I arrived. I waited outside and inside for a total of 1 hour. 

Right when you walk in you can already feel the home cooking inside! They have the music blasting throughout the house and they have a open kitchen so you can see how they are cooking everything. 

We finally ordered two 3 piece and a side with butter beens, and corn bread! 

It took about another 30 minutes for the food to come out. But wow THE CHICKEN WAS SO JUICY, CRISPY, AND WELL SEASONED! The mac and cheese was pretty good and so was the mashed potatoes. 

The service could of been a little better but I can't blame them when they have a 100 foot line out the door.

I was looking for a quick healthy dinner and this place hit the spot! I love a place that offers healthy fresh vegetables, meat and yummy sauces. The strawberry Fresca was refreshing too, not too sugary and was light to taste. I will definitely hit this spot up again when I travel to Tampa.
Came here for Mother's Day and everything was amazing service was awesome I love how they gave each mom a gift. Thank you for making our Mother's Day special 2021
No masks were used by staff. This is unacceptable considering the uptick in cases. Not going back here.

If i could give this 3.5 stars i would for the sole purpose that although the food is SO good, both times we've been there the servers have been terrible. We were there about 2 weeks ago i cant remember the server, (younger bald guy) besides the fact that he didn't have much of a personality, he didn't know the menu when we asked about certain items, we never received our guacamole appetizer and he finally asked if we still wanted it after we already received our dinner. I'd likely still come back because the food and atmosphere is great but they need to train their servers better.

I love this place...in spite of the fact the service almost always sucks.  The tapas are bona fide...very similar to what I had in Barcelona, and the cava sangria rocks!  It's a very small place, and you grab a table or bar stool wherever you can get one (there's no hostess here)...but the food makes it SO worth the tedium of enduring the restaurant staff.  I've never had a bad plate here, but the Tres Leches Cake is incomparable...and the Patatas Bravas and Fritura de Mariscos also make the drive from East Tampa worthwhile.  Check out my blog for pics:  http://sweetpollyfood.blogspot.com/2010/02/pincho-y-pincho-ceviche-st-petersburg.html

Fantastic new, hip restaurant with a California vibe. I felt right at home with the fresh and well-prepared food. My large party of 8 tried many shared bites and entrees and they were all wonderful. I look forward to returning soon. Loved the avocado margarita, too!

I've lived in the FQ for a little over 6 years and one of the places I enjoy periodically is the balcony at Johnny White's Restaurant.  I've spent some pleasant evenings there on the balcony overlooking Bourbon Street.
On Wednesday April 18, 2018, a friend and I decided to have dinner out since it was such a beautiful day.  On the way to the entry I glanced up to be sure a table was available on the balcony.  The gentleman who is always out front working hard to drum up business for the restaurant was hard at work.  We just got ahead of two of his most recent recruits who headed up the stairs just behind us.  After reaching the top of the stairs, it appeared the wait staff was busy.  Thinking I could save some time I asked the "lady" behind the bar if we could sit on the balcony.  She smiled and said someone would be back to seat us.  For some reason, she became a raging smart- -? I decided it best to ignore her.  While waiting considerable time for a table, a lady and her party who had been seated spoke with the bartender asking to cancel her order as they had decided to leave the restaurant.  Shortly after, the couple who came up the stairs right behind me decided they didn't want to stay and left. I decided to wait and finally after a considerable time a young man came to seat me and my friend. There was a nice table I had observed being open at the corner of the balcony and I asked to be seated there. He informed me the table was being held for a larger group (4 max, I believe).  There were no other customers waiting to be seated and he wanted to seat us at a very small 2 person table which was squeezed between other small tables.
Having been irritated by the very rude woman bartender, seeing a seated guest and friends wanting to leave before their order arrived, watching a couple decide they didn't want to stay in that environment and being denied a nice available table I decided I didn't want to give my business or endure that negative environment so my friend and I left.
On previous visits I had a regular waitress who was always so pleasant and helpful.  I hope we still works there and I may return. In the past I always enjoyed my visits to Johnny White's even though the cook did not do the food justice.  Whoever the manager needs to apologize to the hard working man on the street who dutifully sends customers in while the bartender and wait staff send them out before being seated!!  I'll think twice before I return and will monitor reviews here to see if the problem bartender and wait staff are gone or retrained!!!!!!!!

Good was pretty good. Terrible service however. Our server, Leslie took a while to greet us and wasn't the most pleasurable. Had to ask twice for her to bring my sons apple juice & my order was brought to me incorrectly. It was kind of busy but not enough to be as flustered as she seemed. Hopefully she can receive some additional training & tips to improve.

Just stumbled in here, but it's a really awesome bar! Good mix of locals and visitors, so it's like not too weird, but also different from home. Everyone's super friendly. And they're watching the World Cup here!

Over ten minutes to receive our order, burgers were cold and they forgot to give us our fries (not checked until we got home), my wife emailed their company and asked for a reply and never received one. Lets hope the new Raising Canes puts them out of business.

From start to finish, this was, at best a mediocre dining experience.  When I called for a reservation, I let them know we had a birthday celebration.  I reminded the hostess again when we were seated.   Guess what....not even a mention from our waiter.  He simply gave us our check at the end of the meal.
Back to the food....it took well over 45 minutes to get our food after we ordered.  Just kept watching them bring dinner to other diners, including those who were seated after us.  Waiter said there were problems in the kitchen.  Absolutely not blaming the waiter.  
The food itself was, at best, like eating at a sizzler (which I haven't done for well over 30 years).  My filet was not just overcooked, but 1/2 of it was a big chunk of fat (unheard of with a filet).
Just a very disappointing meal and dining experience.

Seeing the great reviews online, I ventured over on a Monday for lunch around noon. The line was long, which to me indicated worthiness. The menu is pretty basic and really fairly priced. 
It seems to be owned by a married couple and I was immensely impressed with their efficiency of the cooking and handling the line.

I ordered the Cheesesteak with mushrooms & was disappointed with the taste. Let me be clear, it did not taste poorly. But it lacked flavor and did not "wow" me. I think the place would benefit from some cheese options. I think the cheese was white American and didn't add much taste to the meal. I think Cheddar would have added some real flavor to the sandwich. 

The amount of food on the sandwich was a bit underwhelming. I can't complain too much on this point since it was only $5.50; so it was a pretty fair price for the amount given. But, I think the menu could benefit from giving more options like adding extra meat to the sandwich or having a larger size offered. 

At the end of the day, the sandwich was alright, but it did not fill me up. I loved my interaction with the couple, and so I'll probably try something else from them in the future, but I won't go out of my way to eat here.

Pretty disappointed with the service and management that night. The manager argued with us when we requested to be seated like other tables (covid compliance). Instead of just accommodating us she made a rather large scene about it. After that brianna our server was accommodating at first but extremely slow with service the rest of night our drink stayed empty most of the night and we had to literally flag her down from her chatting with the other girls at what looked to be a mid restaurant host desk. Maybe they weren't staffed properly but it was frustrating. The star of the night though was Aldin, he was super friendly, and professional. Litterally saved the night! The best part was he actually cooked EVERYTHING perfectly.. One of the hibachi chefs i have had the pleasure of dining with.. If not for him this would be a one star review. So 5 stars for Aldin. The server didn't even offer to take our picture at the end of the night

Fair food, good steaks, service is hit and miss. The keep trying to put us in the half booth when asked for a booth and the place is 70% empty. Steaks are good, food is good, sometimes staff is iffy, unfocused.

Made a reservation on Monday for a group of 10 the following Wednesday. They said "No problem - we take reservations for parties of 6 or more." We show up and they say they don't have our reservation. The place is half empty and they refuse to move any tables to accommodate us. They tell us our only option is to split us into two booths of five. We ask again why a table can't be moved together and they say it's because of a reservation they had for a party of 5... ... general tone was dismissive and unhelpful and we went to a different restaurant.

The ahi tuna sandwich was good, but definitely overpriced for the kind of place they were.  The fries were under seasoned and got cold fairly quickly. The cashiers were not that friendly. I asked them about the calorie content of the fries only because their sandwich calories were posted and they just said "isn't it on the board?" when I told them it wasn't all they said was "oh, well we don't know, sorry" and were sort of rude. The other food doesn't seem overpriced, and the sandwich was good, but I don't know if I'd go back.
To go pizza place hands down! The backyard pizza is soooo good! Kids love there pepperoni pizza too!

We really liked this little place. The sandwiches were pretty big in size. They were very fresh and delicious. They play very nice background music. Very nice atmosphere. Our waitress was very friendly and attentive. We'd definitely return.
Oysters were fake, absolutely no taste. It was like they had preshucked them and just put them in shells when ordered. Tasted like tsp water. Ordered beans and rice, main ingredient was salt.
Absurd service. We got here for our 9:00pm reservation. 30 mins later and we're still waiting. I don't care how good the food is. This is ridiculous.

From what I can tell, this place has baked goods that will please everyone.  I came here and picked up a variety of items (doughnuts, danishes, etc.) for people.  Everyone liked what they ate.  I think I was a little bit disappointed with the cream filled doughnut.  Everyone has raved about it so much, I think I expected it to be better.  I think what disappointed me was the fact that I thought it would be a fresh (whipped) cream, but it was more of a sugary pastry cream.  It wasn't bad, just not what I expected.  I liked the fact that they had apple cider doughnuts without glaze, with glaze, and with powdered sugar.  The one without glaze was just the right amount of sweetness for me, but I thought it was lacking in apple cider flavor.

Overall, I think most people would like coming here or getting the pastries from here.  The service was very good.  I was surprised that they didn't have the most extensive cookie collection, but they more than made up for it in their pastries and other treats.  I would definitely go back there to pick up breakfast items if I have guests over.

So confused about the varying reviews - I was expecting a 5 star experience from the pics online and reviews but overall I'd say it was good, not great.

I had a Hyatt free night from a credit card so figured I'd use it for a staycation. The hotel is beautiful from the outside, the gym inside is amazing, and the restaurant (XIX) on the top floor is pretty deluxe albeit overpriced in my mind (kind of like the hotel in general).

Overall, I'd give more stars if it was a more cost effective stay for those paying cash, but I think for someone spending $400+ a night for a weekend stay there are far betters options in Philadelphia (although perhaps not as central of a location).

Recently booked a group dinner for 30 people at R2L.  Everything was amazing.  Best of all, while I was nervously waiting for the guests to arrive and escort them to the room, the manager, Yusef took the time to come and talk to me and put me very much at ease.

He is an asset to the management team as I have had less than stellar experiences in the past.

Great job!

Lea
Nothing wrong with the food, it was acceptable. The service was lacking, waited for refills way too long.

Terrible service!!! We went at a pretty slow time and it took forever for anyone to ask us what kind of drinks we wanted. Then we didn't get a refill after trying to hunt our waitress down for 10mins. The food was okay. Definitely would not recommend.

The Mac and cheese was awesome. When mixed with the gravy from the chicken it was a fantastic combination. It was a little spicy for my kids so they wouldn't each much more than the macaroni and cheese  and beef patties , but overall I enjoyed the food and would definitely eat there again.

We had a party of six this evening. Everyone was pleased with their pizza. Better than Blaze was the consensus. Limited selection of  beers (would have liked a dark beer), but pizza was good, if you like crispy crust. The herb-butter application prior to the sauce is a good choice.  Big benefit is easy parking - unlike Blaze in IV, where we just don't go when school is in session. 
All-in-all a good basic place at a reasonable price. Servers were good and conscientious, and place was clean and well-maintained.
Great food friendly staff and a nice place for a special occasion. Bring your family and friends for the best dining in the area.

Got a chance to stop by during the soft and grand opening. Even with a long lines, the service was fast and friendly. They did miss and upsize during the soft opening and a topping during the grand opening but overall, it was a wonderful experience. The flavors of the tea are strong so keep that in mind if you were used to more mild boba. The prices are on par with other boba places and frankly, the quality is better. I plan on doing an updated review later on. As of now, I absolutely recommend you check in this place out.

What a great place for salads. We sat by the counter top bar and watched them make them.  They wear gloves, clean their tools and run a tight ship. We had placed two separate orders and The manager noticed I was eating and my husband wasn't. He was genuinely concerned he didn't have his food. He showed ownership and that was great. Thank you.

Surprisingly good for what is essentially fast food pasta. The serving sizes were reasonable and not huge plates of pasta, which is a plus in my book. It was well-cooked and well seasoned. Food was coming out relatively quickly even with a line out the door, and the staff were friendly. The main bottleneck seemed to be those new-fangled computerized coke machines. Having only one meant that a line formed there pretty quickly and it took each person quite a while to make their selection and get their drink. Oh, and for really crowded days they do have a take-out option where you call it in then go to the front of the line to pick it up.

We were driving through Tucson looking for some good Mexican food. Yelp didn't let us down with this place serving up good, traditional food.  And those in Tucson know about it - it was bustling.  My companion had the President's Plate, which included enough for a table of 4! It had a tostada, birria taco, chile relleno, chicken enchilada and beef tamale. Everything was tasty on that plate (except the tamale, but we make those at home so I'm kind of picky).  The atmosphere is friendly and colorful and the wait staff pleasant and helpful. I find it hard to locate restaurants with good Mexican home cooking and reasonable prices. This is one of them!
I'm pretty sure once you enter the front door, you're actually in Mexico.  That's all you need to know to make an informed decision.
Seating can be a little awkward for dinner, but great bar. Best Old Fashioned in Tampa.

Had Biscuits on my radar for a long time now so I was glad to be able to get a chance to check it out. Located at the far end of Broad Ripple Ave  plenty of parking located in a strip mall would never guess this is a "mexican" breakfast joint.

Got in around 10:30 place moderately busy, nice decor, the add on area is nice, spacious grabbed a booth to get my grub on. Ordered the breakfast quesadilla, dining companions got the huevos rancheros, and chorizo skillet. I also decided on a side of spicy gravy to top it off. The verdict: Quesadilla was great, beans and salad not so much, the biscuits and gravy I would pass on, not bad just not worth it imo. Everybody was happy with their order, left full without breaking the bank.

Biscuits is a little out of the way for me but was pretty good, I'd hit this up on a regular basis if I lived closer. I'll keep this in my rotation next time I want a Mexican breakfast.

I heard a lot about this restaurant, this was my first time at Bungalow's and was looking forward to having the experience. Unfortunately, for lack of a better word, our waitress AMANDA was the epitome of inadequate customer service. After seating ourselves, at a dirty table, that she only decided to make a sorry attempt at wiping down only after we wiped it clean ourselves with baby wipes and didn't even apologize. she gave us one drink menu to share between the four of us. No water, that we had to ask for and didn't receive until long after our food arrived. Our small cocktails came with out stir straws and after asking if we may have some she had the audacity to tell us "cocktails don't come with straws", when people at the bar very well had straws in their drinks. I really dont care about anything you have to say after a customer asks you for something. As well, Never once did she come and ask if our food and drinks were okay, if we needed anything, nothing. The only thing she did adequately was bring us the check, of course. Never said thank you for coming have a good day, nothing. Might well have told us where everything was so we could get it ourselves, I'm sure it would have been faster and done properly and without the bad attitude. This was my first and last time at bungalow. Get a better service staff and maybe this place could be better.

I have called 22 times since my order was delivered today. 6 of which I was immediately hung up on! I will be contacting corporate. My son did not get his dinner tonight. My dinner was cold.! Door dash thankfully refunded my order, but I am extremely disappointed that this even happens especially since they know what is on the order and still mess it up.

We held a gender reveal scavenger hunt party yesterday, with The Cheesecake Factory being the final destination! They were all accommodating and Kim was the best server we have had there yet! She Did an amazing job tending to all 20 of us and could more than handle all of us and then some!!! Our food all came out at the exact same time and everything was hot and yummy!!! Kuddos to you Kim and thank you again for making my goddaughter's special day perfect!!!! The only complaint was the temperature of the restraunt. We did however tell Kim it was ridiculously hot and she alerted the manager. After that we felt the air start cooling so they must have adjusted the air. The service was definitely a 10 out of 5 and the food was perfect too! Go and ask for Kim and tell her the gender party sent you!!!

A surprisingly good buffet for the east side. Really good service. It was incredibly crowded during lunch, but the food was pretty tasty. Very clean, I just hope it lasts.....after all it IS the east side..

Not quite sure why there's so much hype around this place. I was told by a local that this was the best hamburger spot in town and I could not disagree more. 

Granted that it's COVID and there was limited seating outside, but it took over an hour to get our food even though we came at a very odd time (3pm I believe). Just be prepared for a long wait if you do come here. 

I ordered the cheeseburger and the baked potato and both were extremely underwhelming to say the least. I asked for medium rare but even then the burger was kind of dry and under-seasoned. The patty had a crumbly texture to it that I was not used to.  I also prefer my cheese to be slightly melted which they didn't do but that's just personal preference!

The baked potato was okay. I asked for the chives, bacon, and sour cream but again, not much flavor. My friend asked for cheese and she said it tasted a lot better so maybe I just needed the cheese. I wish that they used actual bacon though, instead of candied bacon. 

If you do come here, I do recommend there drinks. They have really popular alcoholic drinks but we opted for the non alcoholic one which was still amazing.
Excellent and interesting Thai food in a comfortable space and easy location.

Friday evening, no kids, no plans, just my wife and I with a hankering for sushi. Do we do the usual place or try something new? Well... I'd read an article about Cove recently and decided to check out their website. A beautiful, easy to read/understand, and visually appealing website, along with fantastic Yelp reviews... We decided to brave this hip new sushi place at 5:30pm on Friday night. 

First impression: "OMG This used to be that donut shop that I never got to try!!" Small but cute establishment, very inviting. Surprisingly, they weren't too busy yet... there was plenty of room for us to sit at the bar (our preference). We were welcomed with an explanation of how things work. Granted, we had scoped them out pretty well on their website and Yelp, so we knew what to expect - it was nice to have it explained very clearly and in a friendly manner from the beginning. 

Ultimately - instead of AYCE sushi, they offer set pricing for meals. Your choices are: 
1 Roll, 1 Appetizer, 1 Dessert - $13.99; 2 Roll, 1 Appetizer, 1 Dessert - $16.99; 3 Rolls, 1 Appetizer, 1 Dessert - $19.99. 
You can also add additional items ala cart, and can order items for takeout. Instead of spending $25 for AYCE and feeling "obligated" to shove your face with so much delicious food to make sure you're getting your money worth, you order a more realistic amount of food and don't feel the need to leave in a sushi coma with an enormous sushi bill. 

My wife ordered the muscles as her appetizer, which came out with a LOT of mayo sauce - almost too much. But otherwise good. You can choose baked or fried. 

The miso soup was good - good sized with fancy dried mushrooms on top. It was tasty! 

The roles were great! Honestly, my only complaint with the food is that the breading on the crystal shrimp was not what I usually experience with sushi. It had a weird breading that seemed to have bread crumbs - they reminded me of the shrimp you get at Popeyes or Long John Silver - not shrimp that belonged in sushi. That was my ONLY complaint with the food. Everything tasted fresh and well balanced ingredients - good fish to rice ratio. 

Throughout our meal, the sushi chef engaged in a lot of conversation with us. He was genuinely trying to make sure we had a great experience but it was almost overboard. He asked us what we did for a living, and was talking a lot about our community. He explained what sets Cove out from other sushi establishments in our community and how they want to stand out and support our community in a positive way. Their vision is more of a "fast and casual" sushi - providing quality food reasonably priced. While we enjoy a little conversation with our chef/waiter, it was almost too much and kind of awkward. There were times that my wife and I were in the middle of a conversation with each other, and along came the chef asking us random questions about our community. I'm sure over time this will become more natural and not as awkward, but it definitely made for an interesting evening.

By the time we left, there was people waiting for seats. They had several take-out orders. The food was great (with the exception of the shrimp as described above), the service was good and we never felt like we were waiting too long, and the prices were perfect. We left satisfied but not SUSHI FULL. It was a very nice feeling! We will definitely be back!

Front desk staff was excellent.  We had reserved two rooms and requested they be adjoining.  Upon check in they notified us that our they could accommodate our request but that the rooms were still being cleaned.  We were traveling with our 2 year old son and we needed to put him down for a nap.  When we explained our dilemma they were able to move to us to two different connecting rooms with no hassle.  Really appreciated the friendly and accommodating service at the front desk.

I haven't yet been when the music has really been my style but their pulled pork sandwich is a great deal if you ever find yourself starving on Frenchmen! As my local friend puts it, "the spice is just right." Drinks are strong, but when beer is $6-7 and a well drink is $7 it's an easy choice. The sweet potato fries were also right on point. I'll keep coming back to find some music I dig because the pulled pork is great.

These guys are trying way too hard to be trendy and failing just as hard. They are trying to force the fried egg on pizza trend, but the eggs were almost raw, and made the pizzas extremely soggy which was disgusting. I can not recommend this option if you are ordering the pizza. The cornbread gnocchi were very large and very dry, which is the opposite of what gnocchi should be.

We had the berry tart for dessert which was 3/4 soggy stale shortbread, should have been 3/4 fruit and a nice buttery crumbly shortbread.

The pizzas without the eggs were pretty good, but i didn't come here for pizza. We enjoyed the salad and the octopus the best and would eat those again for sure.

I got the enchilada al pastor. Its always good and flavor is on point. The taco al pastor though, I made supreme, but had little to no sour creme. Slightly disappointed but made up in the enchilada! The portions are slightly smaller than what I remember and usually when I dine in their other location, i'm stuffed. Maybe its because the to go container. The place was surprisingly busy on a Sunday night!

New Orleans has many great restaurants and Domenica is another to add to the list. A large noisy restaurant when I have been there. The food is very good but  a bit expensive thought expected given their location. I recommend happy hour for which is a good value.

Ok so today is my husbands birthday so I wanted to surprise him so we came here early for the happy hour to wait on our group to show up so we sat in the bar area and looked over the menu before ordering some happy hour sangria...another part of our party shows up and the waitress asks if we wanna be more comfortable sitting together so not thinking we say sure...she moves us to this back area of the restaurant and after we order more drinks and apps she proceeds to tell us that we aren't in happy hour area so drinks would be full price! Ok when you are moving a party from an area of happy hour don't you mention that before charging them!?!? This was the first mess up of the evening...I decided to be kind because it's my husbands birthday so we went on to food!! I give 3 stars because the food was pretty good...however when it came to the birthday surprise that was a hot mess I wish I could post a video because the server even acknowledges she has no clue what she's doing and she basically just pours alcohol over the dessert and serves it!!! Overall we will not come back!!! Note to self if you have a party of 5 or more you have an automatic 18% gratuity and then no separate checks!!!

Excellent food and Top Notch service!!!!

Wonderful date night place I definitely recommend!

I ordered omelette and it was over cooked. It was brown instead of yellow and the hash browns were very greasy and tasted old.  Last time I was here it was not any better.  Not coming back.  So sad it use to be very good.

Very cute environment, located in the Basement, one of the cutest hideaways..very attentive barista, probably helped that we were her only customers.  Very accomodating..coffee was ok but would come back for the local..

thought i would try someplace new and heard this resturant had opened.  have to say, waitress was attentive but the chefs seemed more inclined to visit with each other.  i ordered yellow tail, a fish i gage to see quality.  when they served me someother white fish on the third order, blatently different then the other orders, i placed this resturant on a do not touch list.  its affirmed that most fish is not what it seems from all news reports, but when a chef changes fish mid client, shame on you.

Love, love, love. Everything I've tried has been seriously delicious! Highly recommend the napa (grilled w/ prosciutto yum!), the buffalo, and the Hampton salad. Everybody that works there and at Rybread are very friendly which is a huge plus. Definitely give this places try!
Delicioso !!!! Food is amazing, staff is really friendly and they have a lot of seating space! Loved it !

Clean, and the service is friendly with reggae music playing in the background. Can eat-in at the counter with bar stools. Veggie special, which consisted of  rice and peas, cabbage and kallaloo, was on par with other Jamaican spots in the area. 

The veggie patties, which appear baked, not fried, are delicious. I get 2 b/c they're so dang tasty.

I was here for a bachelor party. There was 7 of us and they wouldn't even put us at a table together. We had to sit at two tables. They were Close but still , couldn't give us one table? I made a reservation ahead of time. They took forever to come around with anything good. We kept asking for certain things but got an attitude about that and us saying the  meat  ultra raw. I found the service to be poor and really not worth the price.
I was at the market one day looking for something to eat and I decided on Elysian. I ended up getting the Louisiana crab cake. It's really good, with fast service I would eat here again!
Bad service at the bar and forever to get a lane we waited 3 hours... Never got a lane and then left

We travel to Clearwater several times a year and always make it to Rumba for a meal. Stopped in for lunch after the Phillies game. The food is always fresh and the staff attentive. They specialize in grilled fish but not limited to with some nice chicken, beef and pork sandwiches/entrees. A must if your looking for something different and good to eat.
Probably one of the best modern Italian dishes you'll find. Coming from Italian fam that makes homemade gravy and meatballs that's hard for me to say. Ever changing menu that's always on point

Overall an enjoyable meal. Loved the gnocchi in the octopus dish but the tomato sauce was a little acidic and the octopus not charred as much as we like. "Sunday Supper" rice and meat dish was tasty but definitely needed the squeeze of lemon that we added too late. Melon salad very tasty but a little wet. 7 seemed mostly ignored - they didn't split the salad for her even though we said we'd be sharing everything.  Desserts were definitely the highlights for us. 

Would probably put this meal above Sidney Street Cafe but below Vicia and Billie Jean.
LOVE happy hours here! Best tacos in the Soho area... must try!! You will most likely need a reservation because it is usually always busy.

Delicious Nashville classic!! You cannot go wrong with the Tuscan fries--life changing. Also I'm not usually one to order salad out at a restaurant, but their kale salad with chicken is amazing. The kale is so finely chopped and the dressing is light and refreshing! They have awesome drink deals at lunch, as brunch cocktails are 2 for 1. Be aware of the long lines around that time, though. If going at peak times, I would be ready to wait at least an hour for a table.

Kyle is one of the highlights of our trip to St Pete beach every year. His bar service is top notch and always makes us feel welcomed and treats us as if we are locals.
We always make an effort to come in even if it's just to have a beer at the bar and chat with him. Hope he never quits and keep up the great service.
Also the softshell  crab is the best thing on the menu when in season.

Mirna's folded up after Labor Day. They had 1 waiter for 7 years who worked the entire place on weeknight's with a help wanted sign in the window for years. I'd eat there with my wife on either a Wednesday at 7pm or a Sunday around 6pm, and if there were three tables dining during those evening hours it was a surprise. I never was in there when it was busy

More than 1/2 of Jenkintown has folded up in addition to Mirna's, where businesses that have been there for years are now replaced by either Asian nail salons, Kick Boxing Gyms and Aerobic class rented spaces. So sterile and revolting with no character and no charm whatsoever. The borough has no identity and is looking worse along Rt 611 as each month passes. The dining scene is sparse and the service abysmal conmprised of amateur servers from place to place and hefty prices. An Asian luncheonette on West Avenue closed after just 6 months;(Jake's ). Service was an atrocity and the owner was a homophobe. The tiny French place across the street is now Southern cuisine with strange hours, a broom closet sized restaurant. Who know's what will go in there next. Marzano's is just fair ( still no liquor license ).  There is virtually no place ( DECENT ) to dine now on a stretch from the corner of West Avenue & 611 all the way up to Vintage Tavern in Abington, unless you consider Bella's good Italian. And they are closed on Sunday, the one day Italians like getting family together for dinner.  Once again, the town needs an identity as millennials have moved in to change the landscape with a brewery next to the Hiway Theater. And we all saw what happened to that previous owner. They closed up shop in the blink of an eye. I remember the bartender texting on his phone for 4 min after I sat down, totally oblivious to people who had just come in. Not exaggerating..the service in the county sucks big time.

Came on a Saturday night, wasnt as busy as we anticipated. 

Anyway, friendly service and quick enough. I got a caesar salad as an app which was different but still good. Our waiter was attentive. 

I normally get overwhelmed when menus are too expansive, which the grand luxe was and I probably could have made a better food choice but I digress

My bf got the korean fried chicken burrito, he said it was good, I tried a little bit and the chicken was tasty for sure.

As for myself, I got the chicken parmasean. It was okay, the pasta and sauce underneath seemed a bit dry, the chicken parm was good but I get the feeling it was nuked in the kitchen.

The best part was dessert, one of their options that takes 30 mins to cook, the flaky apple pie was superb! I really enjoyed it. 

3 out 5 stars. Service was fine... Food was just ok.

This place is incredible.  Best pizza I've had locally is at Brewey?  Is this heaven?  We had meatballs for appetizer as well and the sauce was on point.  My wife and I also had beer flights and the brews are really good too, highly recommend the groovy shade hazy ipa.

Enjoyed lunch at Jim n Nicks yesterday.  Pulled pork sandwich was on point.  The complimentary biscuits are delicious.  On the other hand the collard greens are a tad bit bitter.  Overall very please.

My first experience with Randi's was -ehhh ok. I ordered take out. Chicken Parm with Ravioli, Chicken Parm with Tortellini and Fett Alfredo. The good- portions were amazing and the chicken parm was awesome! The not so good- the flavor. The tomato sauce was bitter, I was definitely not a fan and although the Alfredo sauce was creamy and very cheesy like I like it- it lacked flavor. Maybe it was one cheese over powering another? I don't know. I will try other things here in the future but that's my assessment for my now.

Enjoyed sitting outside appreciating the jazz concert at this wonderful outdoor venue and tried the bignets which are made fresh to order and had an iced decaf which was nice. Plus they take cc!  Really lovely spot in the middle of the energy in Nola.

The food was so excellent that we went twice during our 4 day trip to Santa Barbara. You order at the counter and you find a spot indoors or outdoor. They had a salsa bar which is a definite plus. Service was great. I ordered the al pastor quesadilla twice! Omg it was so flavorful and plenty to share. Saw a friend order the seafood caldron, tasted it and had to order it on our next visit. The sauce was not spicy but so intense and flavors just exploded in your mouth. Plus for the price for a huge caldron it was crazy. The ceviche was huge and a definite order as well. Chips were endless. Parking can be difficult but nothing outrageous, plus it can be a nice walk after a Delicious meal. I'll be back when Visiting SB again.

If your inbox is packed full of Spams
And you've gained weight from Holiday Hams
Come straight down to Tampa
Because it's time to pamper
Yourself with some Eddie and Sam's!

My notes: Good concept, massive fan base, Lasagne Slice wasn't bad with pretty good crust, but overall, major disappointment, especially the shocking excuse for a grandma slice. Lovely girl serving tho. But it's FL so just for that tasty Lasagne slice, 4 star - if this was NY, not even close.

As you can see, I like the service, especially the adorable girl serving me, and it's extremely busy and good for people watching - although some of the people are a little rude to put it mildly. Parking is also a nightmare around here.

The pizza itself would be a 2 Star in New York City (or a 1 star for the Grandma and a 3/4 for the Lasagne), and a three-star in good pizza cities (Cleveland, Pittsburgh, Boston), or a 2 star in great pizza cities (Detroit, Buffalo), but Florida is so bad for pizza that I have to give it 4 and if I was going to rate it on the Lasagne slice alone, it might even get 5.

"Slice alone" came out as Sly Stallone in my voice dictation how awesome.

In any case, I quite enjoyed it although I'm quite sure in New York City it wouldn't be taken seriously except as a Manhattan tourist spot. I have to keep reminding myself this is Tampa and by Tampa standards this is actually really good pizza, the Lasagne slice and its crust particularly.

But work on your Grandma, seriously.

And I don't mean sexually.

Moved to Indy 2 years ago and have been utterly disappointed in the Chinese food options near our home, plus the fact we could find no place to deliver.

In steps Sichuan.  Had a fantastic meal across the board a couple weeks ago; amazing Singapore rice noodles, great soup, and lo mein, from our first order.  Looking forward to frequent re-visits and the fact they deliver leaves me even more thrilled.

Amazing service and even better food.  Only been in New Orleans 3 days so far and we hit this spot twice,  And probably will hit it everyday until we leave. I have to try the rest of the deliciousness on the menu. "Don't come here if you on a diets" says the owner, he is so right.

We celebrated our daughters 7th tonight. The restaurant was her choice (a neighborhood favorite).  Thin crusts are our choice of pie.  Tonight we tried one of the specials (The Koreantown).  We got kimchi on half the pie.  The sweet beef along with the salty pickles and creamy mozzarella were great pairings!
We also had our favorite salad there, the Bada Bing!  The flavors and textures are oh so right...almond shavings, Gorgonzola, dried cherries on top of lightly dressed greens is packed with flavors pleasing to the palate but still light and not "heavy".
The kids love the simple meat toppings. I don't care for their meatballs (mushy and mostly breading).
The waitress was very friendly and accommodating of two small children. Biff was sweet and gave us just enough attention to make 7 a great one!

I want to start off by saying, DON'T listen to others who review just because they can!! There's a review that starts with,"didn't even get a chance to sit down and eat." And she talks about how she'll never return because another party advised her party to leave. First of all, you can't review a place that you didn't actually eat at and base it off of 10mins that you waited to be seated (everyone waits to be seated at a restaurant)  people are ridiculous!! Another review talks about cockroaches in the parking lot?? Cockroaches are insects, they prefer to live in warm, dark, wet areas. OF COURSE they'll be around, but did you see cockroaches INSIDE iHop? No!
So i didn't let these nonsense reviews derail us. This place was AMAZING! My party of 4 was greeted immediately and taken care of by Sue, we had GREAT service and the food was delicious!! I'll definitely return!

So I am here for some work in the area. I left work pretty late tonight and their kitchen was already closed. Over an hour closed.. and the owner Lee made sure I had a meal. Hospitality like this is was drives a great business! Thank you for accommodating me while working in the area.  This is my second visit in two days and love the atmosphere and food!

Crabmeat cheesecake is amazing!!  

Charming spot right off canal where you can sit outside and people watch or sit inside in the elegant setting enjoying traditional nola cuisine.  I had the crabmeat cheesecake to start and the crusted tilapia for my entree and would definitely go back

Really liked the interior set up and décor. Tall private booths, with a sports and breakfast food theme, very clean. I got the pancake combo, the eggs were fine, bacon cooked perfectly, hash browns too greasy, but the cakes were super. Light, a little fluffy, and buttery, perfectly prepared. My wife got eggs benedict and said among the price levels places similar to this one, they are the best she has had in Indy. That's saying something because its the only thing she orders for breakfast. Fruit was fresh. Staff was great super friendly and on the ball. Service was quick. The place is really big so we didn't have to wait long to be seated. Prices are what you'd expect.
Great authentic food !! Call ahead because place is small  everything is really good even the noodles !!

I have been here several for both brunch and dinner, and both times my experience was fantastic.  My main complaint is the price - even though the quality of the food was very good, I'm not quite sure it was THAT GOOD (Cafe Ponte, for example, has lower prices on their food and I find that the quality between the two is comparable).  I imagine the extra $$ is for the view.  I can handle that. 

For the most bang for your buck (but still a huge chunk out of your wallet) is the brunch.  While extravagantly expensive (at that same price - or cheaper - you can go to the Wynn Buffet in Vegas and have the best buffet of your life), if you have the resilience and persistence of a person deadset on getting their money's worth (aka me) you can make this brunch worth the price. Things to do to get ready: 1) exercise in the morning or the night before to get that hunger up, and free up that stomach space.  2) But going to a buffet on a purely empty stomach is a big no-no. Be sure to eat a little something so that you can stretch out your stomach to fit in more. And 3) Get someone to DD because nothing gives you more for your money than bottomless champagne and bloody marys.

That being said, the all you can eat brunch is filled with tons of amazing stations: pasta station, omelet station, seafood station (raw oysters, shrimp cocktails, yum yum!), breakfast station, and an entire room filled with dessert. 

I would say that the brunch at Oystercatchers is a go-to must for anyone in Tampa.  It might not be reasonable to come here on a regular basis, but everyone should try this place at least once.

Deano's Beach Kitchen is a must visit place if you step foot on any of the surrounding beaches. We called a couple of cafes/restaurants to inquire on dine-in services since we are at the peak of COVID-19, Heather answered the phone, and her personality brought us in. The service here is impeccable! Mr. Dean's wife came out and introduced herself to us and made everyone feel welcomed. If you don't visit this place for the food reviews, visit it to be treated like family! Heather's personality brought us in, but the food is something I'd drive 8 hours to have again. 

The tropical nachos were amazing! Home made pineapple-mango salsa on top of real crab meat and shrimp, stacked with lettuce, tomatoes, and the holy queso cheese all on top of perfectly thin chips. The burger was well seasoned and the fries were to die for! The crunch and freshness of the fries tied this food review together. Everything was so great, I had to leave my very first Yelp review.

Not to be confused with bigger brother Del Frisco's Double Eagle Steakhouse (in other US cities), the "Grille" is not nearly the quality or experience and lacks an adequate price correction.  Not even close to a Bern's/SideBern's (Tampa) relationship.  Biggest let down were the steaks (turf).  Poor quality cuts and preparation.  Service was good, but our prepared meals sat for too long, as they came lukewarm.  Not a restaurateur, but thinking that using the established Del Frisco's name and brand is deceiving considering the "Grille's" product.  Then again... they got me once.

This was a great find.  We would have never found this gem without Yelp.  The great reviews gave us an interesting change.  So many items that you would only find here.  Unusual dishes like borsch cabbage rolls and piierski.  all excellent and not found elsewhere in Indy.  Plus, wonderful music during your dinner.

Service is impeccable. Food is tasty enough, though more expensive than it's worth. The Caesar salad was pitifully small for an $8 salad. The mozzarella impanata was tasty but it was really just fried mozzarella and only 3 triangles for $7. I didn't particularly care for the pomodoro red sauce. You can as good as pizza for less money a few blocks away at JJ Twigs.

We had a lovely Mother's Day brunch. Everything you could ask for, good coffee, great Bloody Mary, and delicious food. My favorite was the frittata and my husband had biscuits and gravy and 15mo had tastes along the way. Needless to say we were stuffed and unfortunately not able to make room for the donuts. However, it just means we need to go back again! Really excited for the addition to Lansdale.
I ask for philly cheese steak sandwich and they give me this nasty sandwich and it I told them it was nasty and she refuse to refund my money.

Excellent food. As someone who has been to Hawaii numerous times it fits the mold. Most of you have said it's an Asian flair which is true. However, if you have spent significant time in Hawaii like I have you'd know that's normal. Japanese and Chinese people are heavily invested in the Hawaiian economy and hence have added their style to Hawaiian food. It's all good.

I've only come here twice with expert Chinese foodie(s) such as Ming and Coty. Consequently, we've totally enjoyed our meals and tried dishes we might otherwise have never experienced! 

So, my advice is to find an expert Chinese foodie, bring them here, and indulge! Otherwise, you might end up with Americanized Chinese food which is often unsatisfying and rarely spectacular.

We, on the other hand, got to try fish stomach soup with strong red vinegar, Peking duck with scallions and plum sauce, whole dungeness crab, incredible fresh and tender pea shoots stir fried in garlic, and utterly amazing salt and pepper (and garlic and scallion) chicken wings with a spicy/salty/garlicky coating that also goes great with rice! Zowie! My taste buds are still on cloud nine!

Thanks Ming and Thanks Coty! Life is good!
Always a good time. Great Bartenders, delicious Bar food, good selection in drafts. Happy hour 7 days a week.

After seeing mixed reviews about this place, and not coming here for years, i decided to have breakfast here with my 3 yr old son.  I had full intentions of having the  breakfast buffet, but this isnt available on Wednesday, but in fact, only available on saturday and sunday.  Not a big problem, they have a large breakfast menu.  The prices were definitely on the low side, which was great.   My sone decided on the 3 pancakes, and the sausage, while i got 2 sunny side eggs with homefries and chicken breast (love that grilled chicken breast is an option since ive been trying to eat healthier).  

The waitress obviously didnt want to be here, but she was not rude, or even unconcerned with her customers.  She checked on us often.  

Now for the food!!!  

Pancakes-  they are on the large side. So 3 pancakes are a bit much for a 3 year old.  They were also very dense and chewy, instead of light and fluffy as anticipated.  The sausage was patties, and had decent flavor and was cooked perfectly.  

The eggs were a bit on the bland side, but most restaurant dont salt and pepper the eggs, so that was fine (thats why there is salt and pepper at the table, right).  The homefries were also on the bland side, and needed salt, pepper and ketchup, but, they had a nice brown cook to them, as expected for homefries.  The grilled chicken was seasoned, and while the taste was off putting at first, it wasnt bad, and also had a nice sear to it.  

The other reviews called into question the cleanliness of this restaurant, but from what i saw, this was not an issue.  In fact, i saw them cleaning several times while waiting for my child to finish his pancakes.  The silverware was clean dispite other reviews.  The tables and booths have normal wear and tear on them, and could be replaced, but seats were not torn.  Lighting was nice, and overall it was a decent experience. 

I dont know if i would come back anytime soon, but only because there are better breakfast options in town, but im not opposed to returning it a group of friends would say, "hey, lets go to Pottstown Diner".

A side note, as we were about to pay, the man at the register handed my son a spiderman toy still in the box and asked if he wanted it.  My son would never turn down a free toy.  Our total came to $15.53, which the guy rounded down to $15.50.  I just looked up the toy on amazon.com, and it is selling for $23.87, plus shipping.  So we both ate our fill at breakfast and got a $24 toy for $20.50 (after tip).
It's a "thing" here to put a newbie on the register.   Be prepared to wait and wait and then find out your order isn't yet ready!

We arranged a custom private tour for a family of ten, and it was honestly the highlight of our entire stay in New Orleans. Our guide, Luke, took us through the history and architecture of the French Quarter before leading us through the cemetery, and managed to keep us entertained and informed the entire time. We will definitely be calling French Quarter Phantoms the next time we are in town!

This place is cute but not overly noticeable.  Saw that it had good reviews so I had to check it out.  

The first time we tried to go it had about an hour wait.  Tried to go again today and it was still def busy, but we were able to get seated pretty fast.  It seems like this place is always pretty busy and can be a little loud.

When you walk in, it's not overly clear what you are supposed to do, so we initially stood by the door behind another couple, but were motioned to the back of the restaurant.  It would be helpful to have a sign indicating what to do when you walk in.  We were quickly given menus and got our order taken pretty fast.  Food on the other hand was a little slower.  They apologized however and said that they were slow because they were out of a lot of stuff.

We order the falafel plate for an appetizer and it was served with hummus and naan.  It took a while to come out but was overall pretty good.  For dinner I got the chicken kabob and my husband got the lamb kabob (he wanted the lamb shank, but they were out of that).  Food took a while and was pretty good, but could have used a little more spice. I wanted to ask the waitress for hot sauce, but unfortunately she didn't come back to the table to check on us so I wasn't able to do so.

We were done eating a good amount of time before the check came, but they ran the card pretty quickly.

Overall food is good, particularly the falafel, service was okay (not sure if it was lacking due to them being busy or bc it was New Year's Day).

Unbelievably flavorful and good food. Had the falafel plate - probably the best falafel I ever had - very moist and delicious. And also the chicken with herbs and potatoes like none other. There's also a lovely fresh clean yet also romantic feel here.  Definitely recommend. Plus we were there when there was live music on the street outside and people were dancing.

Best fried chicken in the city hands down. Their donuts are also fresh and fantastic. The chicken is super crispy, and every seasoning I try becomes my new favorite.  They have specialty donuts as well as the hot and fresh but you can't go wrong with either. They also now offer a chicken sandwich which is a seasoned chicken breast, cheese, pickles and a sauce. This sandwich is so much better than any other chicken sandwich I've had.

From the moment we walked in to the moment we left this was a great experience. Not being from Reno, I've found it difficult to find good food spots, with a good ambience, without being in a casino and this was for sure a win in my book! Amazing food, great setting and spectacular service. Will be coming back

Prices too high. $5 per street taco? These are typically $1 per at food trucks and $2 per at Mexican restaurants. Opted for burrito, which was good. Walked in wanting taco but didn't want to drop $15 to $20 on single person meal. Service was friendly.

French food is one of my favorites and I was coming into this place already knowing it was BYOB and that it only accepted cash from reading the other reviews. We had a reservation for 5 of us for dinner. We walked in with our red wine that we brought, and they quickly escorted us to our table. 

The important part of this experience was the fact that my father had flown in from Sweden and was meeting my boyfriend's parents for the first time so the noise level needed to be average or lower. Even as the place was getting more full and packed, the noise level wasn't to the point where we had to yell and we could hear each other's conversations.

We all ordered delicious appetizers, my Escargots were amazing. The last time I had them was years ago in Southern France, and I can tell you it definitely matched up to the competition. I ordered the pork chop which was so delicious and plated in a nice way. Our waitress (her name was Gianna) was very prompt, friendly and was making sure we weren't confused with the menu or the specials. This place could also be perfect for date nights, and I loved the big windows toward the entrance. 

I will definitely be coming back here. We all were very satisfied with our meals and the overall experience. I enjoyed the smaller atmosphere and it was quite cozy sitting there for dinner with dimmed lights. There was also no extra fee for opening your wine, even as it is BYOB. This is my new favorite place, so I will be back here very soon.
The highlights are extremely attentive wait Staff and managers as well as great decor. The food is good, but not fantastic. Two of our four entries we very good the other two were fine.

Marrakesh? More like MarraSHHEESSHH!! This place is the definition of northern African cuisine. From the time you step in to the moment they're all wishing you farewell it was such an experience! The workers are the most delightful people ever. The seating is comfortable and you're seated in a dim area. Great for date nights! Marrakesh is great at keeping to their roots because at some point you will use your hands to eat! (If you're not comfortable with that they also provide you with cutlery). The food honestly speaks for itself. So tender, well seasoned and cooked with heart. If I could rate this place more than 5 stars I would!! Only down side is that it is cash only so we did have to leave the place to go to an ATM. Other than that I would def recommend for anyone looking to try something new! 10/10 would be coming back here shortly!!

I have been wanting to try this restaurant for some time.  Devour Indy was my moment to travel down to fountain square and give it a try!  I LOVED everything about this restaurant.  A small Italian restaurant feel with lots of windows.  Automatically you felt at home and looking forward to the menu. 

Ordered from the devour menu and every new item delivered to the table was amazing!  Ordered the Bruschette Ricotta and my friend ordered the Garlic Cheese Bread.  The Brushcette Ricotta was simply perfection!  I will be back just to have this again!  The Garlic bread was good but the Brushcetta Ricotta stole the show.  I ordered the Caesar salad which was good!  No complaints just still thinking about the Brushcetta Ricotta!  
For my main course I ordered the Cacio e Pepe.  This was simple, cheesy, and delightful.  My only complaint was I wished the portion was a bit larger.  It was exactly what I needed on a snowy day.  We ended dinner with dessert which my friend ordered Tiramisu I choose the lemon cake, the Torta Della Nonna.   This was light, lemony, and perfect with a cup of coffee.  My friend said the Tiramisu was hands down one of her favorites!   We will be back for sure!!  
Got photos of the the appetizer and desserts.  Enjoying the pasta and forgot a photo

Alberta avenue needs more like this. Nice, not fancy sit down Columbian restaurant. Service was good. Three beef tacos $13. Made in house soft corn taco shell, roast beef (not ground), cilantro, onion, tomato. Red and green salsa on the side that were not spicy but very flavourful. Delicious. 
Arepa von todo (loaded) $9(!). Larger taco shell, roast beef, chorizo, cilantro, lettuce, tomato. Mayo and ketchup sauce (meh). Ask for some hot sauce. 
Also delicious. 
Coffee was not special but not bad.  
We'll be back to try other menu items.

Excellent grilled steaks , chicken & seafood . We have a group of 4 couples that have been going here for the NCAA Basketball Selection Sunday Show ... for years . Besides that , several of us have dinner here 2-3 more times a year . The service is outstanding & the food is great .. & .. there's plenty of it . The salad bar has more selections than you'll see anywhere .. & .. the blue cheese dressing is one of their famous " classic's " . I think I can confidently speak for all of us when I say , " We have the Best times & Delicious dinners every time we go to The Pub ".
Rice was undercooked and cold, chefs a bit slow, but wait staff was great.  Hard to find a consistent sushi restaurant lately.

Fun, happy employees make me feel happy too! They easily one-up Starbucks any day of the week on taste, service and price - plus they know how to make you smile. Also, you get an "extra" shot of espresso in your espresso beverages, so all you latte lovers out there take note. Plus, they make a macchiato the traditional Italian way - if you haven't tried it, check it out, I bet you'll like it.

This has been on my *To Try List* for months! Finally tried it and it's definitely worth the hype. 

Location: Decent street, could be hard to find parking but I caught someone coming out. 

Wait time: I came on a Saturday, early afternoon for brunch. No wait time which I was surprised at. 

Customer Service: Everyone was friendly from the moment we walked in, they were attentive and checked on us throughout our meal. 

Atmosphere: good music, great pictures, nice staff, this place is small but it's really a vibe. The owner did good with this spot. I'd love to see her branch off and get a second location with like outside seating as well. 

Food: I got the pancakes and turkey bacon. BOMBBBBBB!!! I don't know what they did to the pancakes but they were light and crispy but filling and huge. They may have been the best I tasted, shout-out to the cook. My friend got the shrimp and grits and she couldn't stop talking about them.

* the only reason I gave four stars is because they only offer half of their brunch menu on Saturday's, the full brunch menu is offered on Sunday's.   

Pricing: Listen I don't care what your budget is, they fit it! Lol They have extremely decent prices, I was surprised at how affordable they were. The atmosphere and Food is definitely a treat to yourself for these prices! 

This is a must try brunch spot recommendation from me, I will definitely be returning a couple more times especially on a Sunday to try the other half of the menu.

Schmooze unfortunately has closed, it's a shame this Classic themed New York style deli has closed. A lot of investment was made into the interior of the Resturant and the few experienced mature servers were a key part of the staff. The deli suffered from inconsistent, invisible leadership. I ate at the Resturant at least 4 times. The 'Classic BBQ pastrami sandwich special which was on the menu everyday and was great. The classic cold cuts and some of the deli condiments and soups were good. However the cooked food suffered tremendously from inconsistency of cooking, preparation and chronic shortages. I never once when I visited was aware of any management, leadership or someone who would survey customers on how their meal was. I could sense frustration on the part of the people who waited on me that things were not alright. They were always apologizing for the lateness of the food or the fact that meals were cooked incorrectly or were served cold. Again some things were good but it was very limited. I hope the resturant re-opens, please change the name. It the right place for the right geographic area and it will be a winner with the right leadership,
Best not-homemade fried chicken I've had in my life. We waited in line for a while, but it's totally worth it! I'd go for the tenders.

I went to Hinata with my fiancé for Valentine's Day. We were missing Japan after having to cancel our trip over Fall 2020.
There isn't a single thing we had that we didn't enjoy. Everything was beautifully presented and amazingly well prepared.
I will absolutely be going back and can't wait to share the experience with my friends when we start to go out together again.

The wife and I celebrated our anniversary this time around at Sullivans.  We had a reservation but was late due to traffic but the restaurant was able to accommodate us.  Excellent service.  Food was good. I got the 22 ounce and order it medium well but came out medium rare and had to be returned twice.  So it was comped as well as both our desserts and one double captain and coke.  So it was alright to me.  The manager was understanding and went out of her way to please us.   Will return to Sullivans.

Wen in on a Saturday afternoon and had lunch with my daughter and her boyfriend.  I just love their tomato soup with a grilled cheese sandwich.  It is such a friendly atmosphere.  We decided to eat inside because it looked like rain.  Got a cozy table in the side room and had a wonderful lunch.  The grilled cheese is made with two cheeses and they use garlic butter and there is some cheese grilled on the outside, the best.  The soup is thick and just right for dipping the sandwich instead of a spoon.  They give you one but why use is, just a wasted step.  If you want great soup, salad, and sandwiches, this is the place to go.
Great food, drinks and atmosphere. The enchiladas verdes were great. Add your name to the waitlist online before you head out and save yourself a long wait time for your table!

I've had nothing but an amazing experience here . You are warmly greeted as soon as you step into the establishment . The presentation of their food makes you want just about everything they are serving lol . Great tasty food with just the right amount of seasoning . If you are hungry don't worry you get a large portion to satisfy your appetite . I love the cleanliness & well kept both staff & place has .  If I was able to give more stars I most definitely would have done so . Keep up the GREAT job . By the way Vanessa is a sweetheart who goes beyond customer service satisfaction !!

I loathe Applebees...the only thing good here is the cocktails and those aren't that great. 

stay away, so many better places!

Mediocre food that is more expensive than it should be. With so many options in Conshy I'd be surprised if I returned.

Our server was the best part of the experience, very friendly.

Yay for lady chefs!!  This is a fancy date spot.  Had pork belly and foie gras pate appetizers, mmmm so good.  I had the filet mignon with gnocchi and mushrooms.  The gnocchi were great, the filet was melt-in-your-mouth delicous.  I hadn't had a good steak in a long time and this was cooked perfectly.  The stand-out dish from here was my baby's snapper.  Like a dum-dum I tried to talk him into ordering the flounder but I'm glad he went with his gut, becuase this was just absolutely delcious.  The mustard vinagrette made the dish I felt.  So good.  We got dessert (which means we loved this place)  which was pine nut tart with vanilla icecream and apricots.  I loved this, the icecream was homemade, tart was delicous, and it was just really really really really good.   We were the youngest people in the place I believe which is usually a good sign when it comes to restaurants (unless its Denny's early bird special).  Anyway this place is classy, love the atmosphere, love the food, would love to go back.

Great sushi! However, they have 3 different selections for rolls (hand roll, half and full). My one wish was that there was a number for each of those. If I had known that a full roll was 10-12 pieces I would've​ gotten the half rolls and been completely satisfied!
The chargrilled oysters we amazing. It is loud and busy so more of a quick in and out place than a lingering dinner. There was a wait at 11:00 am but the line moved quickly.

Slow service. Waited 95 minutes for the food. Food when it finally arrived was cold. Was doubled charged for items and had to have the check fixed. Would not go back and in desperate need of new management. 
Scottish Arms has better bottomless mimosa brunch and better food.

This is one of my new favorite BYOB places in Philly with its chic interior, friendly staff, delicious food and unbelievable price point.  Don't walk, but run to try this restaurant!!!!

Seven friends and I enjoyed doing the mezza, which at $30/person is a ridiculous bargain.  Since none of us had been here before, the mezza allowed us to try soooooooooooo many different Lebanese dishes and determine our favorites.  As we worked our way through the endless variety of incredible hot and cold appetizers, we had to keep reminding ourselves to leave room for the lamb and chicken kebobs.  Everyone in the group had a different favorite (e.g., stuffed grape leaves, roasted cauliflower, hummus, baba ghanouj, cooked lentils), but everyone agreed that everything tasted fresh and amazing.  We could not finish everything because of the generous portions, so the staff offered to wrap up anything that we couldn't finish to enjoy as leftovers at home.  Luckily did find a little room in our stomachs to enjoy the delicious Baklava (the bite-sized portions were perfect because everyone felt like they could squeeze in a bite but could not have ate anymore).

This place is just really greasy fast food. If you are in the mood for anything fried then just give Lucky Wishbone a visit. I got the chicken strips combo and it was pretty decent. Pricing wasn't that bad either for the amount of food you got. It is definitely worth a try for the average fast food junkie but if you're looking for something more exquisite look someplace else.

Stopped in for a sandwich while staying at the Harpeth Hotel. Four of us ordered and the staff was friendly and fast! The Turkey bacon was a generous portion on excellent fresh made sourdough! Tuna sandwich and roast beef were also excellent! Sandwiches came with a tasty pickle and delicious side salad. I would highly recommend stopping in for a meal if you're staying in Franklin or just visiting for a day! Excellent and reasonably priced food!

Fantastic food and service is steadily improving as they get their feet under them. The owners and servers are as nice as can be, and they anticipate their liquor license being approved soon. All in all, it's now the favorite restaurant in Mount Juliet for me and my wife - we've taken out or eaten there 5 times since they opened less than a month ago! The clean white decor gives a great ambience - I'd call it "fine casual."
