This is my favorite place to eat ever . I've been going there for as long as I can remember
Yum!! Super yum!! I absolutely love the ambiance, food & mimosas! Super cute, swanky shop with a great vibe!!

I like to think of myself as a small Chinese restaurant expert. I've had so many in my lifetime and they've all had their ups and downs. This place is by far my favorite. It's in a small strip mall and isn't much to look at, but their food is incredible. I truly love their chicken and broccoli almost more than I love anything. The portions are really good and they come in some great containers. I also love their chicken on a stick, but that's not for everyone.

This is a great place.  Food is great and a large wine list.  They have a lot of large tables.  Kinda small but that is not a problem.   They do not take reservations (traditional)  You can call ahead....say an hour or so and put your name on a list.  They take your number and they send you a link so you can see your progress and where you stand in line.  Then they send you a text when the table is ready.

The service was good and the food came out quick.  We started with the chips and salsa and a side of queso.  The queso was amazing, it's made with some white wine and was delicious.  I ordered the basket sample, everything was good but I didn't like the catfish.  Either way, I definitely recommend stopping by.

My boyfriend and I have been to this place twice now. The service is consistently good. Food comes out relatively quickly. They have yummy fresh drinks like tamarind or papaya. It's a pretty homey, family oriented place. Now to the food: I ordered the chicken enchiladas last time and they were pretty good, solid 4 out of 5. The second time I ordered the crispy tacos, and that was more like a 3.5 out of 5, but more so because it felt more like an appetizer to me. The crispy tacos were rolled up and fried, whereas I was expecting more like a fried flour tortilla that was nice and crispy and fluffy but an open taco. My boyfriends steak tacos however were pretty damn good. Overall We really like this place and will continue to eat here  The menu is pretty extensive so I plan on trying more things!

Went in search of some great Italian food and I was so disappointed.  Overpriced and not worth it.  Got some prosciutto which I hated and some meatballs that are not home made.  San marzano tomatoes where overpriced and not worth it.  Don't bother

Came here for a late night dinner on a Wednesday for the first time. We ordered the crab spinach dip and wow it was pretty amazing. I had one of the salads...can't remember the name but it was good. I mean the experience was just ok. Service wasn't really 5 stars.... More like 3. The waitress didn't really seem interested in us and was gone most of the time. Food was about 4 stars.  Maybe I'll come back.

I could be craving pizza and be walking by and STILL not go in again. I will say the ingredients are definitely fresh and service was great however the pizza is just plain not good. The crust is so thin that the pizza is cold within a few minutes and it was just a little floppy and bland. I wanted to love this place but with so many other pizzerias in the area I won't be going back.

We came here for Sunday Football and sat outside on the patio with our dog.  It was nice and shaded.  They had one working TV that they put on the requested channel for us.  The food was good, we all ordered wraps and french fries.  Only reason I give it 4 stars  is because the service was somewhat slow.  The server did acknowledge how busy they were with carry out orders(their wings seems very popular), and he was doing his best to accommodate us! We will definitely some back, we enjoyed the food, the ambiance, and seeing others order wings from afar made us realzie we need to roder some next time!

We sat for fifteen minutes and didn't get a chance to order.  We just left money and walked out.  As we were driving away, we finally saw someone come to our table.  We won't be back. Very disappointing.

This place really sucks. Ordered 2 of their chicken bowls...all we got was mashed potatoes with very little corn and drop of gravy some cheese thrown about on top but where the heck was the chicken. There was no chicken. This is not the first time they have messed up my order. last time I told them and they got mad. this time I didn't notice till I got home. not worth the hassle they won't do anything about it.

Amazing! I can't recommend Sugarpuddin's enough. The staff are great and the food is out of this world.

I recently moved to the area and I have seen Sugarpuddin's on my way home everyday. I finally called in an order from work today and, to be honest, I'm going to be doing that a lot more often. I ordered the Poplar Bluff Special (1/3 slab and brisket) with collards and coleslaw. This was, hands down, the best BBQ I've had in years.

They obviously care both about their food and their customers. I was greeted warmly as soon as I stepped in the door and they were the sweetest people I've talked to all week. And the food! I thought I would have left overs and I was very wrong. The meat was literally falling off the bone and smoked to perfection. The collards were exactly what I remember from my childhood and the coleslaw was better than that.

This was the perfect choice for take-out date night food. The fact that I was able to call ahead and just pick up a delicious meal (and one that I haven't had in years) earns it more than five stars in my book.
I've been going to black lab for a few years now and have never had a bad meal. I would absolutely recommend this to anyone who has not been yet.

I wasn't thoroughly impressed with Noodle Eighty Eight when I went, but I think they have a lot of promise. I ordered beef dumplings and honey vinegar chicken which came with noodles. The dumpling filling was just alright, but the dumpling wrapper was fantastically cooked and prepared.

The chicken was sweet but that's par for the course for most Asian chicken dishes. The noodles were clearly homemade, but mine were a little overdone. Still, a place with homemade noodles is somewhere I would want to try again, so I'm eager to return and try some more noodles!!

Awesome lobster rolls and boardwalk french fries. The fried pickles were okay but would have been better if they were spears and not long slender slices. The wait staff here was friendly as were the chefs. Will definitely return!!!

All I'm going to say is that I ordered here on a Grubhub whim without checking Yelp first. 

We ordered steamed dishes with sauce on the side. They were chicken and shrimp with broccoli.  Kind of hard to screw those up. 

The shrimp was ok, but the wife hated the chicken. I tried it, and it tasted like, well, not much at all. 

I wasn't even a fan of the wonton soup. I threw most of it out. Just off on the flavor.  I'm usually a big fan of the wonton soup. 

Positive was that the shrimp egg roll wasn't bad. I'm guessing they are really good at fried foods. 

Meh I've had better, that really sums this place up.

Had lunch here.  Without reservations, naturally we had a wait as it was very crowded even for a weekday lunch.  But worth the wait; food was very good.  Fresh fish cooked and dressed well.  View of the beach and ocean from the sheltered (glass walled) outdoor terrace certainly adds to the experience.  Only downside, all of the above are reflected in the upscale prices.
Took my mom here for her bday! We had the mahi sandwich and the lobster tacos. Both yummy! Lovely view! Go here

Came here with a friend and definitely the best food I had in Delaware! Service was good, Juliana's husband was the server and he was friendly and knowledgeable.  Food was great, the grilled octopus was delicious!   We had the special that day and it was good also.  Then we had tres leches, the BEST one I had.  I had tried it in other Peruvian places in NYC, but Juliana's beat them all.  Of course the $8 a slice was even more than some places in NYC.  But it was so good I had to order one to go, great midnight snack!

This is one of my favorite Chinese restaurants and all St. Louis. The food is very authentic the owner is wonderful and it always taste phenomenal.

Some of their authentic dishes like chop Suey blow everybody else's away.  

It's in the heart of you city and if you try it you'll like it.

Very good. I've consistently had both great service and food from this establishment. Recently, I ordered the Parilla Mexicana fajitas and the food was remarkably fresh and well seasoned. The seasoning of each one of the proteins was unique and individually distinguishable yet together they blended together quite well. I highly recommend this dish. Both the salsa and guacamole had great flavor and seasoning as well. The house margarita is lime heavy, which is personal preference of mine. Our, server was attentive but picked up on the fact that we were chatting and let us be. Good establishment here.

I really enjoyed this place during Fiesta!!!   I stopped in a few times and the staff was great.  Super nice and freindly even thought the crowd was big and demanding.    I didn't order the food but everyone who did seemed to be enjoying it, the prices looked good too.   I am excited to try Killer B's on a normal night and have a meal, I will update my review when I do.

First visit here. Ordered the avocado toast. The toast was cold and but the picante salsa was ice cold and overpowering with red onions and lime  juice..  2 lime seeds in my first bite. So.. I was enjoying my side order of  grits and  half way through my cup of grits I almost cracked a tooth.. there was a piece of hard white plastic in my grits. My husband's omelet was ok but not sure if we will be back.

I don't know know why I did not check this place out sooner. I have loved in the area for over 5 years now and just recently checked them out. The service is quick and the sushi is very fresh. They have some unique rolls that you can order but the best part is that it is BYOB. There's a wine store in the next shopping center if you need to run and grab some. They get pretty busy during the weekend for dinner so call ahead. They also do takeout if you prefer to eat your sushi at home. Definitely recommend this little gem. They have private rooms for private dinning. The rooms are so cute and looks like a great experience. The next time I come back with a large crowd were definitely doing the private room. Highly recommend this hidden little gem. High quality sushi at a great price in the middle of a shopping center! Who knew Bensalem had nice little hidden gems.

Good restaurant for the first night in New Orleans. The red beans and rice were great and so were the drinks. However, our server seemed so unhappy to be there, we would have preferred to eat somewhere else with better service.

Yeah, it's kind of expensive and obnoxiously trendy but I can't help it - I LOVE the fact that I can order a delicious bowl of fruit with lots of tasty toppings. The salads are also good (I haven't tried the noodles yet) but I am mostly excited about the fruit & honey. They also beat the whipped cream BY HAND, which I think is kind of silly since I don't think a hand mixer is cheating, but I appreciate the extra effort. The serving size is pretty hefty, so I could honestly just eat the fruit bowl for a light dinner.

Food is very good and if you don't like spicy its perfect. If you do like spicy just ask them to spice it up and they will. The homemade salsa is awesome with the chips and I never really liked salsa before so that's saying something! Menu is a bit overwhelming at first but plenty of options! A friend even asked for a special made burrito and they had no problem with doing that. The staff is friendly and basically the same people. Kids seem to love the place with the colorful chairs and booths too. I definitely recommend this place over Margaritas up the street.

A co-worker and I drove from the NW side of town purely because of the Yelp reviews.  We are always looking for good Mexican food.

Unfortunately, this did not meet the bar for good Mexican food.  It was okay, but nothing to brag about.  The Carne Asada was mediocre.  The rice was bland as compared to Guadalajara's (any location) and Little Mexico Steakhouse.

Aside from that, the service was horrendously slow.
Pizza was under cooked, they screwed up fried pickles (how is that possible?) and the place just felt generally unclean. Staff was attentive and the only good thing there other than the giant drafts.

Great weather and beach views were the order of the day.  Only the food topped it.  This place is known for their Grouper so we had to order the sandwiches.  I ordered the large Buffalo style with a side of fries and slaw.  And my wife ordered the regular with chips and slaw.  Both were delicious.  A Blue Moon and a glass of wine and we were in Seventh Heaven.  We can't wait to go back.

omg! One of our fabulous secretaries brought us all lunch from here. It was amazing! We were all silent while we were eating which tells you you know it was awesome. I had two fish tacos which were incredible! I'll def grab lunch from here on the future for sure!

This place is located in the new Asian food center replacing the once cluttered Asian furniture/souvenir shop. Ours realty well repurposed.

I've visited a number of times during my lunch break. They serve a solid poke bowl, it's a toss up between here and Oishii but I like the server here better.  While Oishii they are a bit aloof and unenthusiastic, I also enjoy the closed off atmosphere.  The prices are reasonable, they have an assortment of hard to find drinks and musubi.

Overall, it's a solid poke spot, would recommend and come again. I've been searching for one similar to those in California but that has still been an elusive endeavor.
We were in the area and found this little spot. Food was ok, service was ok. Area is a little rough. You might want to call your order in and pick up.
Thank you so much Dax for the great service!!!!! Super attentive and friendly. Plus everything was delicious

Beautiful views. Horrible service. Average food. Go for some drinks hang out with some friends watch the sunset. And don't expect anything else. Tried it three separate times over a year every time I got ignored and had bad service.

I took my boyfriend and my parents to Bobby's two weeks ago and I have to say I was very impressed!  Admittedly, I haven't been there for over a year because the last time I was there I didn't care for our server, but we were in Doylestown and I wanted to give it another chance.  When we walked in, this young gentlemen popped up from the table he was sitting at eating and asked if he could help us.  It turns out the guy doesn't even work there, but is opening up a wine bar across the way with the current owner.  He sat us down and came back after getting us water and started to talk about the menu that apparently was just updated.  He was so excited about the new asparagus soup offering that we ordered two bowls...it was fabulous!  Very fresh and perfect for the nice weather outside.  We waved him back and asked him questions about entrees to try and he suggested the pork chop, scallops, and his favorite, the salmon.  Everything was perfect...and the salmon was unbelievable.  Moist and perfectly done on the inside and the outside had this awesome bronzed crust that made it perfect.  My dad couldn't believe how good the pork was, so after quizzing our new friend, he went into detail about how the chef brines the pork to make the meat juicy during the cooking process.  After lots of great conversation, my dad told him he was a Yankee fan born and bred in the Bronx.  He lit up and talked about his relatives that lived there...he then insisted on buying our table an order of creme brulee to try,  saying it was just as good as anything we could get in the five boroughs.  It was good...although I have had better creme brulee in New York but didn't want to burst the bubble of one of the nicest guys I think I've met  "kind of working" in a restaurant.  

A great experience and we can't wait to go back!

I really wanted a crab cake today and since Trolley Square Oyster House is closed on Mondays, I settled in on big fish grill. I called in my order for crab cake sandwich and fries and was told it would be ready in 15 mins. 

I devoured the sandwich. The actual cake is small, sadly,  but full of lump meat and well seasoned. The fries were plentiful but not a fave. They become soggy quick in the to go containers. 

The 3 stars was for the ease of check out. There were two girls at the front counter. One was on a phone call and the other girl said she'll help you (motioning to the one who is obviously not available). I don't mind waiting, but I'm big on customer perception and associates should eagerly jump in to help out anyone at any time. 

Just my opinion. Food is good. That's not the issue. At all.

The sandwiches were tasty, but the bread was toasted a little too much, to the point of scraping the roof of my mouth. It made it unenjoyable to finish my sandwich. The mac and cheese is a must though.

AYCE fail. It was our first time and while we love sushi, we didn't think we'd eat enough to out-cost the AYCE dinner deal ($22.95 each). We'd order the seaweed salad and Jonathan roll (sweet and spicy) again in a heartbeat, but the Donald Duck nigiri and smoked salmon nigiri and a few of the other rolls were just okay. I like that they cut the rolls in small slices so they're easier to handle and dip as you please. Our meal totalled out just more than a duo of AYCE orders, so lesson learned. Wouldn't say it's the absolute best and freshest sushi in the world, but perhaps in Reno it's the best you can get. The rolls are the way to go (not the nigiri).

After many visits some updated thoughts.  Service is hit or miss at times. Expect a long wait for your food even if it isn't busy, don't order soda from the fountain it is always flat. Otherwise the pizzas are always excellent. Often out of vegan cheese so their vegan options are not always available.
Only been here twice. The yummy yummy crabby quesadillas inspired me to make my own one at home. Guess I will go for the happy hour on weekdays next time.

For those who know me, they are keenly aware that coffee and spirits play a vital role to my happiness and well being.  When I stumbled across Cafe Envie, I was just looking for a morning coffee.  But when I saw the full bar off to the side, I thought, maybe I am still wasted - drunk and seeing things.  I had to ask for clarification, and it was explained to me, that YES, they served all manner of coffee and YES they had a full bar.  I think I felt my knees buckle at that point.

So, at Starbucks, I would normally get an Iced Mocha, but I felt that I needed to push my boundaries a bit.  The barista / bartender suggested some rum in my drink and while I nearly jumped at the chance, I caught a lonely bottle of kahlua out of the corner of my eye.  I decided to go with that and it was love at first sight!

Of course they offer some scrumptious snacks and free wi-fi (everything you need at a coffee house).  And because this is a NOLA you can always enjoy a patio table.

So the moral of this story: More coffeeshops need a bar - JK!  But seriously, you never know what you will find when you stumble around (drunk or sober) - Cheers!
Best clam chowder and calamari around. Service is friendly and food is fresh. Bloody Mary is a tad watery tho

Wow! What a fantastic room upgrade. Too bad I only slept in it for 2 hours. :) The room was exceptionally clean and filled with amenities fit for royalty. Between the hotel staff and the quality of the room, they really know how to make you feel special.

My boyfriend has celiac disease so we wanted to try this restaurant. I heard rave reviews from a friend so we were excited to try it. We went on Black Friday and it was empty to our surprise so our service was super fast. But overall we were not impressed with the food here. He had a gluten free pasta meal while I had a regular gluten meal. We also shared gluten free calamari. We both agreed our meals and the calamari was just okay and definitely had better elsewhere. Maybe we will return if in the area but we won't make a special trip for it... sorry.
Burger bar. No tables. But you can go to bar next door to eat. The burgers are solid -- juicy, right amount of fixings, and delicious! I love the fries and the various dipping sauces.
Please don't spend your money here, they have been closed for about 2 weeks, because they can't pass health inspection due to roaches and mice.  Current owner also STIFFED employees pay.

We stopped in after visiting Bourbon Steak (where we decide not to wait)).  Grabbed a seat at the bar and Kyle took care of us.  He was awesome!  Great recommendations!  I will come back here and recommend friends do the same.  Hope Kyle can serve us next time!!

First time eating Russian food and was very satisfied with the delicious food. Everything we ordered from the stuffed cabbage, pelmini, lambplov,blinchiki, Kiev, syrnki, caviar bruschetta are all excellent. 
Will definitely go back.

Used to be one of our favorite restaurants. Sadly, this will be our last visit. Service was horrible. What a shame. Food was marginal. There was literally a tablespoon of potato salad on my Greek Salad. We will be cutting up our frequent diner card. Good thing we had a coupon for tonight.
Wonderful lunch spot! Shout out to Mitch and his phenomenal service and suggestions! Will definitely make a point to stop in anytime I'm in St Louis!

This is one of my FAVORITE restaurants, so how disappointed was I when we drove over 1 hour to get here, arrived 8pm and told they were closed. Website says 9pm. Please update your info so people are heart broken!

Tried this spot out based on reviews! Not too bad! We ordered one steak taco, the loaded fries with steak, one traditional elote and a grilled chicken quesadilla. I enjoyed everything, however I wasn't a huge fan of the elote, only because I think it had tajin instead of Chile powder, and it was a little too salty for my liking. We sat inside, it's very small, maybe 4 or 5 tables, and very warm. The taco was loaded, definitely used a fork to eat the rest! Flavor was there! The fries are awesome! We would probably get this again, but for takeout.

Management is terrible to say the least, first of all it took too long to get our food when it wasn't that busy at all, we thought that maybe the food would be worth the wait and  to our disappointment it was not, the food was terrible and for what it is, it was also way overpriced. This is just a fancy looking place with bad food, they really need to step their game up because they are not even on par with the rest of the loop restaurants.

We love this location as a nice option for when you want Italian food but don't want to commit to an Olive Garden or Giovani's but want more than Fazoli's.  I can usually get a couple meals, maybe a salad if I get the "Entree & Salad" special they're promoting at the time, rolls and butter, and cheese garlic bread for around $20.  Pretty decent deal.

A few of the menu items:
1) Pasta House Co. salad - good Italian salad (I pick the black olives out)
2) Lasagna - One of my go-to options
3) Spaghetti with Momma Tucci Meatballs - #2 go-to item
4) Cheese Garlic Bread - Decent option for only a couple bucks more
5) Tortellini - w/ peas and prosciutto (I think) in a cream sauce.  I used to like this but was very disappointed the last time I had it.  Seemed like it was all sauce and little substance.  Something about the flavor was missing.
6) My friend likes the Mt Vesuvius chicken, but I've never had it.
7) Cannelloni has always been good, but I'm left a little hungry if that's all I eat

I haven't had any of their pizzas yet, but I'm looking forward to trying it next time.
Was told by a friend that food was sub par. But I thought I'd give this place a chance. The burger was dry and chewy, and lacked even flavor. Don't know how they stay in business

We had a weekend stay in the hotel and had planned to venture out until we saw the brunch menu.  We had the avocado toast, cowboy eggs benedict and a cobb salad with the fried chicken.  Let me just say that the fried chicken was amazing!  Actually everything was amazing!  The bloody marys and selection of local draft beers made brunch even better.  We also wanted a place that had a patio, and this was the perfect spot. We returned for dinner, which included music by a couple of local artists, both of whom were really good. Enjoyed the music and the hamburgers were amazing!  Great venue for music and very good food!

An amazing place with great food. The pumpkin cheesecake topped a great meal. Order 2+ items per person to share. I think next time I'd sit at the chef's counter to watch them make the food. We would definitely go there again on a future visit to St. Pete's beach.

I stopped in for lunch today,  I got the steamed shumai and stir fried Udon with chicken.  Service was quick and staff was very friendly. The Shumai had little flavor, no shrimp whatsoever was inside of the dumplings and ridiculously small for the price . The Udon was a large portion for a lunch special and it also came with a house salad but,  the teriyaki sauce in my udon was super corn syrupy type of sweet and my mushrooms were undercooked. I gave two stars because of the price, Service and location (right up the street from my house) but I came for the food and it just didn't live up to the hype

I had not had Thai food for some time. My wife has it at least once a week. She told me how good this was and how beautiful this place was. I now totally agree. Food was most excellent and the service was fantastic. This place will be a regular with us.

Seriously some of the best sushi, and pretty well priced I've had in Tampa. Very intimate environment, low lighting, high ceilings, and a view of the chefs from just about any table in the room, and the servers are really nice--very patient when we asked about some more details on certain rolls. I really can't remember all the rolls, but one was a specialty spicy roll, a simple tuna roll, and another a rainbow roll. Their fish was fresh and the rice warm. 
Can't wait to come back here! Seriously, my mouth is watering just remembering and looking at my pics, ahaha!

Another chain restaurant that has good chef in the kitchen. You can feel it when the food comes out. They also has Wednesday night special for limited time. They are running a $9.95 6 oz sirlion with fried and beer. Such a good deal. 

I got special of the night. The selection of the meat has good quality. I have ask for medium rare. The outside is completely cook but the inside still see red less pink. This is very good skill from the chef. The middle of the did not feel cool too which make this well prepared over the grille. 

I also got sheared Ahi tuna. This is favorite from this restaurant. I like that overlay over Asian dressing slaw. It has every good thing with about the appetizer. I would recommend this dish to start. Overall the bar is good but only one person in the bar area make the attentive service is lack off.

When it comes to Mexican food, Que Pasa is my "Happy Place".  Not only is the food delicious, the portions are also generous.  Wait staff is amazing - both fun and responsive - clearly customer service is inherent in their training.  Often themed  happy hours (solid drink and food deals), particularly on Friday with a DJ, and drinks are spot-on.  Heck, writing this review is making me hungry ... do yourself a favor and enjoy this gem of a restaurant!
It's cool but the meat and cheese board is wack. Lots of beer and full liquor which is good. Live music sometimes and plenty of parking.
The steak quesadilla is good and so is the salsa. 3 meals cost $40 because they charge a crazy amount for the drinks. There is nothing special about the food here, just bring your own drink.
I've never felt the need to rate a restaurant in yelp before.  This place is amazing!  Food A++ Service A++

Stopped in for lunch, in from out of town for a conference. Had the best duck pastrami slider and bacon melt with marinated Brussels sprouts as a side. We sat at the bar, and the bartenders were super friendly and great conversation. The vibe was great. Music, decor all awesome. Very chill vibe. I live for places like this. You will not regret coming in here!

Wow so glad we tried this place!  A bit pricey and we had a long wait to order and get a table but well worth all of that!  Yummy food it's really terrific bbq.  It was a very delicious experience.  We will eat here again and buy a bottle of the bbq sauce to bring home with us!!!  Peace

So good! If you come here on the early side of lunchtime (around noon), the line is totally manageable and the service is always fast and efficient. I am partial to the small falafel sandwich - it's just enough food for me and it's only $3.50!! For those who need a bit more, you'll only pay $6 for the larger size. The falafel is crispy, flavorful, and fresh, as are the vegetables inside the sandwich. I go for the spicy which is balanced by the crispy cabbage. I also love the option of a wheat pita. This is the perfect lunch option.
Awesome service. Menu options where different yet fantastic. Like the setting inside. Wish I could have brought some back to New York.

I really wanted to like this place. But it's just too.... I dunno. Where to start... first of all, the space is far too small for the music. The music is good, but it's pumped so loudly through the speakers that you can't really speak to the person standing inches from you nor really enjoy the music itself. The layout kinda sucks, if you don't have a table or booth, are sitting at the bar, or on the dancefloor you're screwed. You're literally left standing in a 6"x6" space, being bumped into CONSTANTLY, in a bar that's way overcrowded and stupid hot. I'm glad there wasn't a cover because I probably would've been shittier. If I wanted that experience I'd go to a college town, not downtown Indy. That said, I'll def not be returning.

This is a great restaurant. The food is very good at reasonable prices. Take out is usually right on the money. We have never had a messed up order. When dining ij most of the servers are pleasant and efficient. My only real complaint comes from dining in and the time it takes to get your food. Simply put, it isn't a place to get a quick meal, at least for dinner.

Food was decently good. But I feel this particular location is understaffed. I would not recommend coming here if you have places to be. Coming in I had to wait some time to be seated and even longer to be checked out. The wait for being cashed out was uncanny. The guy who finally did help me was super nice though. And the service overall was good and friendly. Idk if it's just me and my paranoia, but I did feel uncomfortable after I heard some of the coworkers laugh when I came in.

My husband and I had dinner at the sacred pepper for the first time. The restaurant is absolutely beautiful! We had the meatballs as our appetizer and they were outstanding! Some of the best I've ever had, loved them! I had the filet mignon, medium rare and it was perfectly cooked. The only two negative things I could say is that the potatoes that came with the steak had no seasonings and were undercooked so I was a bit disappointed in that because I love potatoes and the music that they play in the bar area is way too loud! It felt more like being in a club than a restaurant. I would definitely eat there again and try something else but I would rather not have to scream over the loud music.

BJ's Restaurant and Brewhouse is a nice chain restaurant, especially if you are looking for a place to hang out with friends in a friendly and clean atmosphere. This location rates extremely high on service and cleanliness. The staff is friendly as well.
      Now - the important part, the food and beverages . This is a place that brews its own beers, don't go expecting a store brand. The root beer glazed ribs are wonderful, with a bit of a nip to them. I can also recommend any of their flatbreads. The California is excellent it has avocado and chicken on it, fantastic flavors! The Wisconsin cheese curds are tasty as well. For those who've never had the pleasure of eating them, cheese curds are like a small diced up mozzarella sticks only with cheddar.
    The sandwiches are phenomenal as well go with a burger , you cannot go wrong. Now, the desserts are what clinch the fifth star on this review. The pizookies ( a cookie Sunday) will make your tastebuds jump for joy. Also, take note this place is not a BAR and ... grill, no they cover all bases. Dessert is an example of this the coffee they serve is excellent ( and you're talking to a coffee snob). Go, take some friends and enjoy it all.

Just had a wonderful meal, FRESH is an understatement,sashimi that must have been caught this morning, and trust me I know my fish,we catch our own most of the time. My wife had the red curry that was out of this world, and ask about the Chef's special sushi or sashimi,(which I did not know about until tonite, fresh catch of the day asian style) they had fresh Hogfish,Wahoo,Mahi Mahi,Yellow tail and more, absolutely fantastic, if I hadn't gotten so filled up I would have tried them all. Also the staff is just as nice as pie with whip cream, have a question they have no problem answering it, it's really hard for me to get very excited over a restaurant any more,I've worked in the industry for over 35 years doing refrigeration,this place is clean and the fish is at proper temp. Thanks for a great meal!
Absolute best pizza in Tampa Bay.  No contest.  Bring a uhaul for that 24 in pie.  It's a literal delicious ufo.
Cheap tacos, good quality. Great toppings bar. I like the chicken tacos and chicken quesadillas.

I can't believe I never wrote a review for this place! I recently moved away from NOLA but I used to live in the Lower Garden District - walking distance to Lilly's. Lilly's was a great place to call in an order after a crappy day when I wasn't up to cooking or for pho when I felt sick. Normally I find banh mi sandwiches really underwhelming, but Lilly's helped change that (though the tofu banh mi was sometimes on the slightly salty side). 

Also, the folks who work here are some of the nicest restaurant staff in New Orleans. I remember one time when I stopped in for take out after a long and exhausting flight back to NOLA, and the lady gave me my order and said "WELCOME HOME!!!" How nice is that! 

When we return to visit, Lilly's will be at the top of our list for Vietnamese.

This used to be my favorite sushi restaurant in Reno! However, after my most recent experiences, I can no longer say the same. 

First off, this place is terrible at getting your order correctly. On multiple occasions we were given rolls that we didn't ask for.

Next, the wait was far too long. We went on a night that was semi-busy at the most. It took over an hour for a good portion of our order. Time is money and they wasted too much of my time.

Lastly, we asked to speak with the manager about the service and he attempted to blame everything on the deep fryer. Regardless, it should not have taken over an hour to get a few rolls out. 

My recommendation? Avoid this restaurant. Better places are Hiroba or Tha Joint.
This is a great barbecue restaurant that has a marvelous brisket that is to die for. The prices are reasonable and they have a good selection. Seating is outside only at this time or take out.

I continue to find myself going back to the Reef. The service is prompt and the various dishes I've tried I never been disappointed. I recently i've been on a diet for the past year and have lived off salads for lunch. I've tried numerous places and found that the Reef has an awesome House Salad that's reasonably priced. Oh and you must try the quesadilla's 
 The outside may be decieving, but the inside is warm and is decorated with a theme that fits the name perfectly.
 Mike...

Cute little place, I had the breakfast taco it was delicious with freshly squeezed OJ. The staff was super nice, although it was not on the menu they still made my boyfriend French toast. Great service.

Being in the neighborhood and having tried their food multiple times, I'm pretty confident I won't be going back.  Chicken Katsu is about the best thing on the menu but a thin breaded fried chicken breast is not that exciting.  Otherwise the sushi is WAY too big and definitely not fishy but very unwieldy and nothing great.  Rouse's is a better option for both sushi and gyoza because at Rouse's they're not deep fried - honestly, why do you need to deep fry gyoza?.  Beef teriyaki has some flavor but just okay, and chicken teriyaki is thin, tough, and lacking in flavor.  The side salad of iceberg lettuce is likewise uninspiring.

Apparently hot towels make a 5 star experience for many patrons, but this is a generic stretch of St. Charles and it's not a coincidence that most of the reviews here are from people outside of NOLA.  I like to support local businesses, but this is a difficult place to recommend if you're know and enjoy good food.

We have been to Eureka three times but we won't go back again. Each time the food has been very good but the service has been horrible. Today we waited fifteen minutes just to get our drinks and two out of our four food orders were wrong.  They seem to be doing fine despite the terrible service, so they have little incentive to improve.

Ok the bad reviews are from salty people obsessed with the whole mask thing and not willing to hear their flexibility.  The server wore a mask and asked us to let her know what we preferred.  We are from up North and enjoyed the "freedom" of deciding and not being forced or snarled at. The room is well spaced and ventilated, there is plenty of consideration so I just didn't see any disregard for anyone's safety.  
Now for the food, it was top notch and very flavorful.  We had the signature appetizers and 4 entrees and all were amazing. I highly recommend this restaurant, you just can't go wrong.  Also, try the specialty cocktails, they know how to mix drinks to suit your palate.  We will come back again when visiting this area for sure.

I have never understood Nashville's love affair with Las Palmas. I know several people who swear by this place (at any location) and I have always found myself disappointed in their bland, lackluster take on Mexican-style food.

Shredded chicken simmered in tomato sauce with peppers and onions...and then put in every single chicken dish they serve. It would be different if it were flavorful or something, but it never is. The beans are bland. Their sauces are the worst offenders- echilada sauces that are bland, cheese sauce that is overly runny and bland, salsa that could be confused for ketchup...if ketchup had no salt. I'm being glib but only because there some really great options for Mexican or Mexican style food in Nashville...and so many people still turn to Las Palmas.

If you really must have this food, have it made better at Las Maracas, OK Coral, or La Siesta. They are all better versions of Americanized Mexican-style food. And they're just as cheap, just as approachable.
The cutest place in Malvern for breakfast/lunch. Quaint, with a lovely staff.

I go there only to see bands that I like, it's not a bad place, and I truly miss the Old Rover. When Chef Joseph ran this place the food was truly excellent, now its pub grub, not bad but....

It's full of Neshaminy people and that's cool, my kids went there and I almost always run into someone I know there. 

Their waitstaff always seems agreeable but truly unexperienced . 

My big problem is the last two times I went there they ran out of soap in the bathroom. Now they have a nice clean looking bathroom with three soap dispensers but the trouble is not one of them had soap.

Headline: slow service and mediocre food.

This restaurant is inside the Marriott so it's unlikely that you will actually encounter it unless you happen to be staying here.  It has the usual bar food.  We decided to being the family for a final together.  What a mistake that was.

We started with the calimari appetizer.  This was bland-  the rubbery bits of calimari didn't really taste of anything.  A dash of salt would have worked wonders.

My main course was the Lancaster Chicken-  basically, an airline cut off chicken, lightly fried.  It w served on top of a bed of undercooked carrots and potatoes, and submerged in the saltiest broth I have ever come across.

Adding to these disappointments was the lackluster service.  Not bad per se, but very very slow.  It took over 45 minutes to get our entrees out.

Disappointing is one way to put it.  Do yourself a favor and seek sustenance elsewhere.

Had the Greek salad and Cajun dry rub wings.  The salad was great and wings were good too though I'll probably go for a different flavor next time.  The blue cheese for the wings is the best.  Chunky as good blue cheese dip should be!  There was only one waitress so as the bar filled up service was a little slow but she was working hard.  Bathroom could use a bit of a clean up but good place to go for some wings and a drink.  Prices are good.

So I was never a huge fan of BBQ....until I came here. My husband I stopped by the Shaved Duck for an anniversary dinner about a year ago.  It was completely packed and we almost decided to go somewhere else. I am super super glad we didn't. I had the BBQ pork on top of potatoes and I swear I almost died. My husband had the ribs, and for most of the dinner we ate silently. I swear people must have thought we were fighting because I could hardly put down my fork to speak. We topped off dinner with the bread pudding which is so deliciously sticky and sweet. I have since gone back and have not seen it on the menu. Sad face. I guess I am going to have to go back and try more desserts! (Happy face).
Try the avocado curry, with tofu and veggies spice level 3  the veggie rolls as well!

Finding good fresh sushi in the deep burbs is difficult but luckily not impossible.  Murasaki was a great little find.  It was quiet at the start but quickly filled up around 6.   We ordered the sushi dinner and found the fish to be very fresh and flavorful.  The Udon was ok but not as flavorful as I've had before but still good.  Kid friendly environment and very friendly staff.  Fried green tea ice cream came in a thick dough like crust and whipped cream, very tasty.  Will definitely be back to try some the other creative sounding rolls.

Where do restaurant people go after work, Grit is the answer!  Great service, friendly and helpful staff   We love to grab a drink at the bar for some good conversation and laughs. The smoked pepperoni pizza is the bomb!

So glad that Grit opened their doors, we know how difficult this business is and how nice it is to hear that people appreciate the effort and hard work it takes to run a restaurant / bar

Great job!
Tony and Geri Delia
On a Roll Deli
Eagle, Idaho

I was in the area with my sister, my bro-in-law and the bf to look at marble for a kitchen island.  Unfortunately, everything was closed on Sundays.  So when I saw Kermit's, we decided to check it out so our trip wasn't completely wasted.   

I got an everything bagel with plain cream cheese and my sister got the plain bagel with scallion cream cheese.  The bf got some coffee and a slice of cheese pizza.   While the bagels were just okay (NY bagels are incomparable!), the scallion cream cheese was very flavorful.  The pizza was delicious!  I can see why people are raving about Kermit's pizza.  That's the only reason to come here.

We also got the yo shorty cake, which was some almond cake with a weirddddddd raspberry cream in the middle and mousse and a strawberry glaze.  It was beyond gross!  No one could eat it at my house.  The raspberry in the inside of the cake was rotten or something.  We also got a vanilla cream puff for my mother.  She hated it.  The texture of the cream was super thick and sticky.

Pizza, yes!
Desserts, no..

Two stars for the gross aftertaste that cake left in my mouth

This place is the real deal. I'm not one to eat at the same restaurant more than once every few weeks, but this place has me as a repeat offender. Their daily specials usually include authentic down home Cajun cuisine and the price is always right. I highly recommend trying the crawfish beignets: they are to die for! Have tried almost every dessert and can't decide which is my fave cuz they r all great! Bread pudding, wedding cake, brownies, and cheesecake, just to name a few, yum! To top it off, their staff is always accommodating and enthusiastic. Rocksy's is truly a rare gem smack dab in the middle of Metairie and I hope they stick around for many years to come!
Real Chicago pizza and hot dogs! Best Chicago style pizza we found yet!house cab and Chianti are very good.

This place!!!! Love it!!! Amazing food whether you are vegan or not!!!! You would barely notice it's vegan because you are to busy noticing how amazing it tastes!!!! Great prices! Great service! And decent portions! Usually I get at least two meal out of my order!!!! I could seriously live there! Highly recommend the tots, the buffalo cauliflower bites, tacos and buffalo bean burger...oh and the kale brussel sprout salad!!! Please check them out! Meat eater and veggie water and vegan, all may happily dine together here!

used to be "da dawg's bollox" in a town where if ya want a bad meal u have to cook it yerself, my 1st visit to C's P was in the early 90's and it WAS amazing both quality of food / innovative service / ambience and worth every $. AN EXPERIENCE to be remembered. been back a few times in the intirim and each time it slipped a tad..... but NOW?

3 couples out for a birthday celebration, our personal observations:

past tense, USED to be.......
it's still good food TODAY..... but....
plenty of others do it REALLY good now...and not at VERY high prices like CP.....
where, if truth be told, they are a shadow of their former selves.
service is spotty...yes they still do the ARRIVAL at the table en masse for a group 'experience'....oooooh ahhhh!
however, the attention to details like water for the table, tidying up, drinks service, wine experience is NOT WORTHY of these prices,
did I mention how expensive the dining at C P is today? relative to what it was 25 years ago?
yes, it's THAT much, **130 bucks a head doesn't buy what it USED to. **(before tx/tip)
hmmmm, said dat b4 innit? and we were restrained and ordered modestly from the extensive wine list or that could have doubled or tripled.
still a beautiful building in a lovely neighbourhood on Washington in the Garden district, but as it's been said so many times before C P was about  more than excellent food...twas "an experience".
"not now, Josephine"

Rating : Meh. I've experienced better. (FROM THEM !) two stars

Simply amazing food that is fresh and flavorful. The bananas Foster Pain Perdu is a MUST. The bacon adds some savory to all that flavor of butter, maple syrup and rum. Absolutely dee-lish. And the Eggs Cochon the pork and that yummy biscuit. Simply divine. The portions are large and you definitely get full. 

Don't let the crowds scare you. It's definitely worth the wait. So good we went back the next day. And in this town of lots of yummy eateries, that's saying a lot.
Still love this place and the staff is very friendly. Happy to see some esports on the tvs here too. The best fried chicken in edmonton!

Recently moved just down the street from this place. Just stopped in for the first time and, wow, what a treat! I had the South Philly crepe, which was delicious, and the coffee was tasty as well. The real treat is Liza - owner and sole operator of the shop. She is incredibly sweet, generous, and full of fascinating stories. If you're up for great food and engaging conversation, this is the place to go.

I do agree that the space is a bit small, but there's no way it can lose points for that. Liza is just getting started, and what can you do but set up shop in a small place for a business that's operated on a small scale and is somewhat experimental in nature. Hopefully she can find ways to expand the space at some point, but take comfort in its cozy confines - there's a certain charm to that kind of setup that you can't find just anywhere.

In a sea of endless options for Mexican fast food, there's El Pollo Loco--which specializes in chicken. 

What do I love most about about this place? They have posole verde! If you've lived in Arizona all your life like I have, you're probably wondering why it isn't red chile-based, why it has chicken instead of pork, and if it is as miserable as a fail as Rachael Ray's sad excuse for posole. Yes there is a green one, it's very rare, very delicious and has chicken. Outside of here, I've only had it at one other place in the Tucson area. El Pollo Loco's is delicious, though very inconsistent; this is why I only awarded three stars. The first time I got it, there was so much hominy and chicken, it was awesome. The last time? It was mostly broth with a small handful of hominy, and maybe 10 small pieces of chicken, and it needed salt, lime juice, and green salsa to bring the flavor up. I suggest this place works on consistency.

Also, this place has Mexican hot chocolate, which I love.

Service can be spotty. I've always received the correct order, but the staff can be aloof and disoriented, and they can take quite a while on orders on occasion.

Overall, this is a solid lunch place for when you want something quick, Mexican, and chicken-focused.

Tasty food, good portions and a variety of menu options.  I went here with friends before work and was not disappointed.  The place wasn't crowded at all and we were seated immediately.  I saw pictures of the big bad skillet and thought it might not be enough food but rolled the dice.  I'm glad I did.  The combination of eggs, sausage, bacon spices etc. were spot on and it was plenty of food.  The biscuit was also really good.  Also, something that isn't a big deal but I found really cool was the squirt bottles full of blackberry jam in the table.  Number one, it wasn't little packets you had to open and two it was blackberry.  You never see that.  It's always strawberry or grape.  I know, not a big deal.  But I liked that.  Other people in my party got the grapefruit and some vegetarian options that were also good.  Parking was a cinch and the staff were very nice.  Highly recommend you check it out if you are in the area.  It was a nice change from the norm for me.

Always love coming here. Food is always good to great. Service is friendly and fast. It's a solid neighborhood joint, and they are great with kids. I haven't tried their breakfast yet, but I want to do that soon.

Husband and I went for an early Valentine's Day dinner.   We have been hunting for a bottle of Pappy Van Winkle for the past six years and had only just found out that Woodwork had some.
He finally tasted it and said it was just how he imagined (so the hunt continues)... huge thrill for him.  
The drink menu was amazing - tons of cocktails and wine options.  
We shared the frites and brussel sprouts to start.  The frites were covered in parmesan and delicious; I could have eaten three orders.  
I ordered the ragu.  The thick pasta noodles were perfectly cooked and the sauce was flavorful.  My husband had the fried chicken.. by far the best he's ever had.  The slaw salad on the side was also really good.  

By far one of the best meals we've had.  
Drink prices and food are high but comparable to any other restaurant of this level (high!)

Yes I'm giving it 5. The owner really does quality work and ingredients. Which is always welcomed to see organic being included more and wish other places would follow suit.  

Had an affogato with almond gelato and it was great. Just quality all around. Great strong espresso with out bitterness. The gelato is definitely tops and the flavors are very prominent. Like he doesn't hold back in ingredients in making them. Tried a lot of the gelato and honestly all good. I'm a big fan of Angelo brocato but I think I might have found my replacement due to the use of quality organic ingredients. Had the blueberry gelato for dessert and it was soooo good! 

Had a piadina which is an Italian quesadilla and it was good. I think I would have rather the breakfast one on a crepe instead though. 

Will definitely be back and will work my way through the menu. Awesome quality place and very cozy modern!

I love a good hoagie and I can tell you that Skyler's is the best in town! They're better than Wawa, Chick's Deli, Jersey Mike's, Gaetano's and dare I say it... they might even be better than Primo's in a way. I decided to try something new and I'm glad I gave this shop a chance. Everything was perfect from every ingredient right down to the friendly customer service! I was even surprised by the low prices for the quality you get. I don't want to give them any ideas but I would gladly pay double. The rolls were perfect and all of the fillers perfectly proportioned. I don't know how they do it but even the onions seemed perfect. I'm not always a huge fan of onions because they can be overpowering and the smell can stay on you. However, the onions here are light, crispy and delectable! I would recommend Skylar's to anyone and I will definitely be back the next time I get a hankering.

We went to Cafe Adelaide for dinner and arrived at approximately 7 p.m.   As we approached the unattended hostess stand, another couple was standing and waiting to be seated. We waited a few minutes and my husband entered the restaurant to find someone to seat the other couple and us. All of a sudden two young women come to the stand and scramble to seat the other couple and us.  Why are both of them away from the stand at once?   Then dining room was less than 50 percent full as we are seated.  Then the waiting began.  I won't go into boring time frames but I will say this was the single slowest service of food courses we have EVER encountered at any if the Brennan restaurant, I'll go as far to say at ANY restaurant.  We have been patrons of to Mr. B's countless times, at least a dozen times to Commander's Palace. We know the Brennan family has first class service.  

The servers were VERY attentive but the kitchen staff should be held completely accountable along with the manager. Two of the servers apologized explaining that "a large party in the back room" was to blame."  Great, the manager obviously was aware of a reservation for this large party, WHY did the manager fail to schedule their staff accordingly?  I hope that the two Brennan ladies that run Adelaide read this review because you are going to slowly lose patrons unless your staffing issues are solved.  It's a shame, the food was very good but the slllloooow service really damaged the experience.

I love the Goleta and Downtown Santa Barbara locations, but my experience at the Kyle's Kitchen in IV was disappointing. I ordered a side of fries, and it took a while to come out (not a problem because it was late at night) but they were cold when I got them. 

Not sure if they were sitting out for a while, but the fries definitely weren't fresh, so I probably wouldn't come again or would try to come during peak hours when the food has higher turnover. 

Go to the Goleta or DTSB location instead!
Hibachi Steak was raw, there's a big difference between rare and not even having any color on some of the steak. Had to cook it again at home. Beware.

Not happy. Ordered plain pizza and fries with whizz on side. A lot of the cheese slid off the pizza on it's way to me which made the barely edible pizza, inedible. The fries had whiz on the side AND on the fries. WRONG! Called to let them know and was promised fresh fries right away. Guess what........never came! I'll be dropping by after work tomorrow for a refund. I'll post the outcome
Good food, decent portions, but a big chunk of money for what you get. Come once for the experience, then do it at home.

I cannot grasp how this place is "Cuban" yet they looked at me weird when I ordered a colada. Is this only a Miami thing? We ended up ordering 2 cafe con leches which was mediocre coffee at best! My bf ordered the Muffaletta sandwich and I had the Cuban. I guess you can say I was disappointed because I'm used to the Miami Cuban way - pork, ham, cheese, mustard and pickles. I had no idea Tampa Cuban sandwiches were slightly different. They add lettuce, tomatoes and salami. By all means, it was a great sandwich, it's just not what I thought it would be so I left really disappointed. My boyfriend loved his though - and all of the pastelitos and desserts looked really delicious as well!

Nice experience, original setting, decent service.
Enjoyed all the side dishes and wine but not so much the over cooked steak.
Very good meal price.

You should go!!!

I will be a happy repeat customer. My fiancé and I genuinely enjoyed our dining experience from the skilled chefs to the expansive sushi menu.

I loved their appetizers -mussels.
Great burgers today!  Ice cold beer!  Awesome French fries!   May be my new burger joint!

The quality has gone down here.  I had the jambalaya appetizer.  Some rice was mushy and some crunchy.  The taste was okay once you put some hot sauce in it.  Had the hot smoked sausage po-boy.  It comes with steak fries which are great if you can get them hot which mine were not.  I would not get the hot smoked sausage again.  It was not bad but really nothing interesting about it.  I would have preferred an actual New Orleans hot sausage.  It confuses me why they leave the mayo out on the table all the time.  Isnt it supposed to be in the fridge?  I stay away from it. And the tables are always sticky.  I think this is the wood finish on the table but they maybe should cover the tables in that butcher block paper.  It just feels gross.

We ordered the mussels and fish taco. It looked beautiful and the portion size was perfect. But I'm more into eating my food than looking at my food. The mussels smelt like rotten fish but I hoped it would taste better than it smelled. I was disappointed as it tasted horrible and felt slimy as if I ate an uncooked snail. I thought the tacos were okay. I only took one bite and my boyfriend ate it and threw up. We spent $26 for food we didn't finish and got sick from. So it was not worth it.

Great cafe to grab a bite to eat while strolling the canal. The menu items are simple yet full of flavor. We've tried the vegan ministrone soup, margarita flatbread, vegetable flatbread, and vegetarian chopped salad. All were great and fresh tasting. Their homemade lemonade is also a must try, kind of addicting. And lastly the table side s'mores are a unique addition to satisfy your sweet tooth.

Nice addition to the canal walk with ample outdoor seating!
Shouldn't have gone the day after Christmas. It didn't seem ready to serve. Waited 45 mins. Would be a great place to stop after work or something for a burger.

Went with a group of friends and we had a separate room.   I was pleasantly surprised at how good the food was. I had the Shepherd's Pie which was quite good. I've often had it in Irish pubs in other places and it compares very well.  It was made with beef and had the traditional mashed potato topping. The description mentioned peas and carrots but it was short on them. It came with vegetables and extra gravy. Didn't need the extra gravy as there was plenty in the pie. Others I was with had the chicken pot pie and bangers and mash and really enjoyed their dish as well. It appears that many people come back over and over. It was pretty crowded but service was good. The menu has a nice variety in addition to pub food. It's a place worth a repeat visit.
Good cup of coffee and really yummy baklava! I didn't try the food, but it did smell good.

Very good restaurant. Great service with a varied menu. Mario the manager was very nice and our waitress was so helpful. This new Mount Juliet restaurant really wants to please and create generational customers.
15 minutes after being seated in our booth, and eye contact with two servers, no one had acknowledged us or taken a drink order. We walked out.

My fiancé and I came in last night (05/13/17) around 7-7:30pm. There were a few people at the hostess stand no one greeted us. Finally after the other staff cleared out we went up to the girl standing there ( I think her name is Cathy? Maybe) and told her we would like a table for two. She looked at us and walked away. Walked around the restaurant confused. Came back and said hold on I will be back. Walked up to the sitting area stood in front of a table for about 5 minutes. She came back and was like "uh we have to see if we have anything to accommodate you. But you can sit at the bar and order there. " she was making it seem like we were a party of 15. We were just two people. Give us a table with two chairs. It wasn't rocket science but she made it way more complicated. The place wasnt overly crowded. didn't let us know if there was even a wait or anything. Plus there was plenty of sitting at tables around the bar and a few in the seating area so I'm not sure why we weren't offered that. We never had a problem before but will probably not be back now.

First let me say: the wait is DEFINITELY worth it.

I love breakfast, so after I heard that it was a Nashville staple I had to try it. Especially since pancakes are my favorite food!

The 23 varieties made it hard to choose, but eventually I decided on the sweet potato pancakes. It sounds odd, but honestly these were the BEST pancakes I have ever had. The cinnamon cream syrup on top complemented the pancakes so well. 

We had to wait 50 minutes on a Monday morning, but I would do it all over again. This is a MUST, especially if it is your first trip to Nashville.

Maaaan if you're reading this you already know whats up...you already know fried chicken is the food of the Gods on the lower east side of heaven, smoking magical homegrown heaven super kush and shooting dice, jafeel?  These chickens were born in soft green fields of paradise, grazing on sweet corn and seeds, getting laid and squawking around happily.  
Donuts are straight blizzity blaze...Indian spiced cinnamon is like better than warm sex with the hottest most thickest and baddest girl from BET's Week In Review. Also dig the blueberry mascarpone.
I am mainly writing this review because of how bad the quality of the steak was. It was dry, thin and tough. There are better places in the area with a much higher quality of food.
Excellent hoagies and priced right.  Yes, it is a franchise but don't let that discourage you from trying this place.

This place is the best for happy hours! Prices are low and the drinks are yummy & strong. The service is fast and hospitable. Along with this, the overall design of the restaurant is fun and comfortable.
If you are in this area and a student, it's a great option for food and drinks during happy hour. If you are into tequilas and mezcal, they have a great variety with a range in pricing. They also have flight options so you can compare and contrast various types. 
I would definitely recommend for a good snack and delicious margarita!

I started to go to mikes deli recently over the last few months after a friend told me its the best for breakfast sandwiches. he was not kidding! i go there about 2 times a month or maybe 3 as i only travel for work 1 day a week usually. I normally get the sausage and cheese with egg on a roll. and its a huge sandwich. recently i got jsut pork roll and cheese on rye toast and it was HUGE! i loved it! The sandwich was unreal for the price. i had to each a few pieces of pork roll out of the sandwich to be able to eat it as a sandwich. There is no other place i go for breakfast sandwiches. cant wait to go get a lunch sandwich there. Mike is usually there in the morning and is very friendly and connected with the customers. he seems to know alot of them by name and asks about their family. The woman who is there is also super friendly and nice i just dont know her name. What a great place to go. I know they have a new customer for life from me.

Dave Jacob

This is by far the best Nico's location in Tucson! The food is always perfect, the place is always clean and the staff is friendly. We go there at least once every two weeks, if not more, and it's consistently a good experience.

Not a bad place to get food! It is right on Bourbon Street. They do make you sign in for covid purposes. I wanted the jambalaya pasta but didn't want the alligator sausage, sadly they couldn't remove it. So I got the shrimp platter instead. The portion was quite large! 
I wish the service was a little better given that there weren't many people on a Monday evening.

My family and I came here from California on a road trip. We were staying at the Best Western Inn, which is not even 50 paces from the steak house.

Upon entering the place, I noticed something that was a little alarming... The floor was CLEAN! If you have ever been to a Texas Roadhouse, you know there are barrels of peanuts in the waiting room, and small trash cans full on every table. People are encouraged to help themselves while they wait, and throw the shells on the floor. The floor was immaculate! I wasn't the only one that was hesitant to throw my shells on the floor... You could see people meandering around in the lobby with shells in their hand. This was very disappointing. This is one of the novelties of Texas Roadhouse. The floors at every other franchise I have been to have been COVERED in peanut shells.

We called ahead because we are veterans. There's no way I would take my children here and wait in the lobby without calling ahead. The average wait on a busy night is 30 to 40 minutes. A table was ready for us when we arrived.

On our way to the table, we noticed that this particular location was very cramped. Our greeter attempted to seat my one and a half year old at the end of our table, in arms reach of another family's food. We had to ask to remove a chair instead and sit the high chair in it's place. This seemed like common sense to me. We ordered waters for the kids, and margaritas for the wife and I. While we were waiting, I noticed there were TRASH PAILS on the table for the peanut shells! There were very few shells on the floor, and in the spirit of the roadhouse,  I threw all of mine on the floor, and encouraged the kids to do the same. Some others were following suit.

A new family came to sit down, and two of an existing group of customers had to get out of their seats so the new customers could get by. There was NO way they could squeeze by. The chairs had to be pushed all the way in to allow safe passage.

It was at this point, before we placed our order, that I heard another lady at the table next to ours talking about her steak. She had returned her first portion because it was too rare.  She ordered medium rare, and in her words, "It was still mooing at her". I saw her meat, and it was bright pink, soggy, and tore loose from itself in a shredding action rather than a tender, red, juicy rare steak. It was clearly cold and raw.

This lady was a portly woman, about two and a quarter, and her husband wasn't far behind. He had finished off his chicken and was grimacing at his wife's pile of cold flesh on her plate. It looked like something out of a horror movie, or worse, something Rocky just finished punching for an hour.

She sent her food back a second time, and the waiter was very apologetic, and hurried to the back with the cold dripping slop. You don't go to a steak house and order a hot dog, but It was at this point that I decided to order my steak medium well to be on the safe side. I figured it would arrive at the table medium rare, and that would be fine.

The poor portly lady's steak arrived for the third try, and... It was raw. She boxed it up and took it with her, no doubt to finish the cook's job at home herself.

My steak was presented to me on a nice hot plate, with fries and jack cheese on top. Then I saw it... The nightmare of every chef... STEAK SAUCE on the table. No self respecting steak house provides steak sauce unless a patron asks for it. A steak should stand alone on seasoning and inherent flavor brought out by proper cooking.

My steak was leather, with some shoe strings mixed in for good measure. It might have been gristle, but I wouldn't have bet on it. I am not one to complain (although I do like a tell a story here and there) but I had to tell the waiter how horrible the steak was AFTER I paid the check. She wanted to bring the manager over, but I told her no, that's why I paid it first. I don't want my check discounted. I just wanted the manager to talk to the cook.

The restrooms were not air conditioned. Enough said about that.

The service was good, and the rest of the food was great. The margaritas were not strong enough. They were more like smoothies. My wife ordered chicken and mushrooms, and her meal tasted great. For this reason, and for the good service, I give this location two stars.

We ordered delivery from here for the first time tonight.  

The service was quick and friendly.  Food was GREAT! 

I ordered the fettuccine that was homemade pasta, so tender and light, not a heavy dish.  The serving size was huge!  I couldn't even finish it all.

We are in NOLA for a conference and the Cafe' by the Square was right across the street from the conference hotel. We went for lunch. I ordered the tuna sandwich and my colleagues ordered the fried green tomato BLT. The tuna was prepared nicely and as ordered, and the sandwich was excellent. The report from my colleagues was that the fried green tomato BLT was also excellent. 

The service was great, and we were seated right away. The atmosphere was very nice. I would go back. Highly recommended.
Really, really excellent food. Best Latkes sandwich ever. Best falafel I've had in the city of Philadelphia. Beats the hell out of Maoz Vegetarian. The staff could be a bit cheerier though!

What a beautiful place and relaxing atmosphere. The accommodations are fairly comfortable, but it's the grounds that make this gem of a place special. (The food doesn't hurt either.) Get a massage from Vesalina if at all possible; it was the best I've ever had. Also, be sure to check out the gardens and chapels.

We had take out from here the other night (Chicken burrito, Steak Burrito, Chips & Guacamole and 2 Grapefruit Sodas) and it was FANTASTIC!! The mole sauce is killer and we get it on the side so we can slather each savory bite. Not to mention the prices are good also. Will definitely keep coming back!

Had an AMAZING breakfast this morning at The Griddle! We were totally sold once we saw the menu. We arrived just before 11am today and all the tables inside were taken, so our AWESOME server, Lexi, offered to seat us outside with the heater on. It was pretty chilly out today but we decided that we wanted to check it out bad enough to brave the cold. To our surprise, the heater worked GREAT! It was comfortable and we had the patio all to ourselves. We ordered the Wild West Scramble and the Gravy Train Potatoes. Everything was SO delicious and fresh and, again, Lexi was very nice and gave great service. On a side note, we witnessed a guest be very rude to her and she handled it like a pro. She rocks and made our experience a really good one: We will definitely be back soon!

Omg. Pancakes. This place was a great local find and now we always go on a Sunday. The service is kind and courteous and the food is all homemade. I don't usually go for pancakes but when you have seasonal ones like cranberries and pecans, or the normal offerings like chocolate chip and peanut butter, it's hard to resist. Other goodies include home fries, french toast, and the many varieties of omlets. When the weather is nice,  it's a bonus to sit outside. If you live around the area, please try this place once!

My uncle has made a reservation for eight people, but I brought a plus one and thank god they were able to squeeze in my main squeeze. The place is pretty busy, my party ordered two shoguns and it was delicious! From my personal experience, eating in the city is a hit or miss because you could be splurging on food that has very little substance (however, i digress).

I didn't catch my waiters name but the service was excellent food was absolutely delicious price was on point everything was 5 star, except one person ruined the whole experience Miranda I was so very disappointed with the way she was braiding her employee in front of customers me and my wife felt embarrassed by her blatant racism she said that's just how they "play"  You fluent in English and Spanish he didn't understand a word she was saying and talking loud and like he was a 5 year old wasn't going to help him understand, and common sense is if your employee makes a mistake right or wrong you sure as heck don't discipline them in front of customers let me make one thing very clear I am 100% going to fallow up on this with corporate on Yelp and to everyone who I come into contact with  belittling your employs is not a joke it's not a way to play around neither is racism

So...I realize that the Coronavirus is happening.  Businesses can't do their thing, has to be take out, blah blah blah.  I ordered two pizzas from Giordano's last night.  Went to pick them up, and they weren't ready to go, even an hour after I ordered.  No biggie.  I get it, lots of peeps ordering pizza to go!  Once it is finally ready, I get it and leave.  They did not include the peppers/cheese/plates that they were supposed to.  Again, no biggie.. I can probably dig that up at home.  Then I get home and see that my pizza is completely uncooked on the bottom...like, raw.  I can't even cut it and try to re-cook it.  I call the location to voice my concern, and I'm told all they can do is make me another one, which I'll have to drive 30 minutes to pick up, or put me down for a "free one" next time.  Next time doesn't feed me now, so I opt for the remake.  Head down, pick it up (after much wasted time and confusion) and go home.  Shocker...another uncooked pizza.  

Basically, I spent $40 on two small pizzas.  One was decent and one was not edible two times in a row.  Probably not going here again.

This is a friend's favorite restaurant, and she chose Brio as the location of our first tete-a-tete since I moved back to STL. I read many reviews here on Yelp beforehand, so I felt well-prepared, but not terribly excited.

We arrived around 5:45, and the happy hour was hopping. Not my crowd; I used to work at Plaza Frontenac, not hang with Plaza Frontenac. Plenty of seating in the dining room.

We ordered cocktails, mine was the Raspberry Mojito, and my friend ordered something custom. They arrived quickly, and although mine was good, I didn't taste any booze. Had I not had a few the night before, I might have pursued this with the waitress. The triangle crispy things were good, as was the warm sourdough. Even though I always eat the bread they bring out at restaurants, I just wish the industry as a whole would stop this practice. It fills you up, you're not hungry when the entree arrives, and you have all sorts of misplaced bullshit carb guilt. Why not bring out some vegetables and salsa or hummus? Just saying.

Per a suggestion from another Yelper, I joined Brio's rewards whatever and had the $10 appetizer coupon. We wanted apps from the light menu, which has appetizers and starter salads listed in the same category. The waitress would not accept the coupon for any of the starter salads, saying the computer would not accept said coupon for ANYTHING but a designated appetizer. Splitting hairs like this annoys me, especially when the food is so overpriced. $4.95 - $6.95 for a side salad? Really?

At this point, it was becoming obvious that the waitress, for whatever reason, had lost interest in us. I actually began timing how long it took her to come back to the table. Perhaps she saw two women talking and lingering over drinks, so thought we were there for the long haul. We weren't, but the slow-ass service saw to that. When my friend ordered a second drink, it took over 20 minutes for the waitress to bring it. I was scanning the restaurant to find another member of the waitstaff to fetch her when I finally spotted her coming our way. Was it busy? Yeah...but not that freaking busy. It became a game and a source of exasperated humor between my friend and I.

When we ordered, the waitress didn't tell us about any specials, so I have no idea if Brio even does specials. I ordered the Pasta Alla Vodka and my friend ordered the Roasted Half Chicken. Many reviews on this site mentioned the massive portions. My friend had a ton of food left over, and I had zero. I tried to keep it light with the bread and appetizers, so that I was hungry for the actual meal, maybe that's it. I do know this: there was not $18.25 worth of anything on that plate.

The disappearing waitress act got so bad that my friend spoke with the manager, who recognized her from many previous visits. He was incredibly gracious, apologetic, and comped all of the food on our bill, leaving us with the tab for four drinks.

Bottom line: food was fine, service was definitely lacking. I would go back begrudgingly, but it would be someone else's idea and I would try to steer them to another restaurant.

First time visit based on reviews.  While the Crispy Calamari appetizer was tasty - it was barely warm.  I ordered the Rib-eye special instead of my first choice crab cakes at the recommendation of the server who raved that whenever they have rib-eye special it's great.  Preparation was over cubes of venison sausage and root vegetables - which was tasty.  The rib-eye was not.  Mine was full of gristle and had a large section of fat (not marbling) in the middle.  I could barely cut through the gristle and tendons so either the steak knives needed to be sharpened or this was a bad cut of meat.  Could only eat about half the portion after hacking at it.  When the server came back I mentioned my issues with it and asked for a doggie bag - which in this case really would go to the dog.  She returned and said she gave my comments to the chef who said there was still a large portion of meat left.  So, I guess the fact that most of the cut was inedible didn't matter because there was some meat left around the fat.  In fairness, another in our party ordered the rib-eye special as well and his was OK - not full of fat and gristle.  So mine may have been a bad cut of meat (which seeing the large hunk of fat in the middle should have been evident to the chef) but frankly - even with a great cut not worth $36!  We ordered dessert - the flourless chocolate torte was tasty but must have just been taken from the refrigerator - it was very cold.  Made me think it was left over from the day before, and put in the refrigerator overnight to keep.  Overall just a fair rating.  Still, I'd be willing to try it again to see if it was just an anomaly with my beef dish.

I was so excited when I saw that a taco place opened near my office, even though I loved the thai place that was here before. That being said, I was so disappointed by this place.
