I ordered two of the "El Pastor" tacos. Al Pastor is like my favorite kind of taco EVER and aren't that common in the mexican places in Philly. Unfortunately, they were not very good at all.

There was a lot of meat, which is great, but it was really really dry. Like, kind of jerky-ish. And also had no flavor whatsoever.  Aside from the meat, my favorite part of al pastor tacos is the pineapple that comes on top, which wasn't as abundant as I would've hoped. Overall, the tacos kind of didn't taste like anything at all. 

Even though the tacos were disappointing, I got yucca fries on the side, which were pretty good. They were crispy on the outside and creamy on the inside.

All in all, I don't think I'd go back to this place, especially for the price.
The Poke is great and the staff are super friendly!  I loved the option to customize a bowl, the sweet potato noodles were so yummy!

A new, closer purveyor of the many splendoured Modern Times offerings. Been twice now and the menu has changed enough to make a flight a new and exciting experience. Great Cuban food in house and parking around the corner. This is a well-appointed and generously-tapped location.
Love the mom and pop feel of this place. The store also has very cool unique items that are fun to check out every time.

First time here and I was really pleased. Menu apparently changes frequently but the stew and burgers we had were superb and reasonably priced. Ambience was very relaxed with an eclectic mix of people and the wait staff was incredibly helpful, attentive, and polite. Absolutely planning on coming back.

Really now.  This place has 93 reviews.  Is anyone actually going to read this?  Anyway, I love this place and have been coming here since they opened. I have never been disappointed with the Brugge. Things that keep me coming back:  their own Belgian style beers, buckets of mussels served in a large variety of different flavorful broths, crisp frites served in cones with a multitude of housemade dipping sauces, the restaurant location and outdoor seating, the cool tables with the cone holes in them, and their beef Carbonnade stew and their Waterzooi fish stew on a cold Indiana winter day. Thanks Brugge for always being there for me.

Red Apple is no-frills, good take-out. The inside is grubby and sparse so don't eat in, and the bathroom looks like The Worst Toilet in Scotland, but their hot and sour soup is both actually hot AND sour, which is somehow tough to come by in this city. Moo Shu Pork is the best freaking thing on the menu and oh my god do they give you, just, a TON of it.
This is one of our favorite places!  Food is delicious, drinks are fabulous and bartenders are the best! We look forward to going there once a week!
Cute place, but the macaroon I got the other day tasted like it had been sitting out for too long.  Sorta conjured up the taste of shredded gym shoe soles.

I was so DISAPPOINTED!  This place was recommended by so many locals and friends. When I gave my feedback to everyone they said I didn't order the right thing.  If a restaurant is good it should not matter what is ordered it should all be good.  Being from California I was expecting so much more.
Great employees! Best brisket I've ever had! Would totally recommend if you are very hungry-- portions are big... definitely wanted to keep eating after I was full!

My husband and I came here today for a dinner. This was my first time here. We were greeted and got table right away. Very friendly staff. We were able to watch the cooking// creating process. We got hummus and kalaj for appetizers. Hummus was amazing, creamy and tasty, pita was hot and  delicious, kalaj was very good but very tIny.  
For my entree I got shish tawok , juicy Chicken breast seasoned to perfection.  Fluffy rice was very good, garlic sauce was super creamy and fresh veggies very tasty and crunch. I do enjoy a good crunch. 
My husband got mixed grill and enjoyed it very much. He said the lamb was super tender. 
This place is on our repeat list now. We will be back!

This is a little gem of a restaurant, well worth the visit. The owners are focused on making sure that every diner has a splendid experience. They are very attentive without being intrusive.

What we especially appreciated was that virtually every wine on the small but thoughtful wine list was available by either the glass or bottle, which allowed us to each enjoy our favorite choices, and pair each entree with its own wine.

We were debating between the pimento cheese and escalavida for an appetizer. We asked our server, who suggested that we opt for the shrimp quesadilla unless one of us was going to order the stuffed pasilla chile. We were awfully happy we took her advice; the quesadilla was cooked perfectly and wonderfully delicious.

My wife opted for the rotisserie chicken, which, while well prepared (including being deboned), was only made remarkable by the sauce. The buttermilk mashed potatoes were good, but not much better than she makes at home (granted, she is an excellent cook!). I went with the braised pork roulade, which was extraordinary. Great sear, tender and tasty. I practically licked my plate clean.

We were going to pass on dessert, although when our server informed us that there was apple & pecan bread pudding, we changed our minds. Glad we did. It was quite tasty.

If you live in Santa Barbara, you should frequent this place. If you visit, make sure to include it on your list of dinner destinations.

Not really sure about this location. I use to come here as a kid and I just ordered a root beer... that's it.... took about 15 minutes for them to take my order... and 10 minutes to bring it out..... not sure how you get a cherry coke confused with root beer... but I'm so thirsty I'll drink it anyway... no telling how a food order would go, so I won't chance it. Ima go next door to the gas station to get a root beer now.

My husband and I eat here once every couple of months. The servers are friendly, our order always comes out right, the food is between average and good. I lean toward the salads (the chicken and apple with dressing on the side is my favorite) and my husband usually gets a burger. It's a bonus for me that they have Angry Orchard hard cider on tap. Yum!

The only thing I don't like is having to walk through the gross cigarette smoke and always go home with the nasty ashtray smell in my hair.

Everything about this place says "we care" and it carries to the patrons who are equally friendly and courteous. 
It's hard to pick standouts since everything I tried on three visits was deliciously prepared and carefully executed.

This place hits every mark. The cheesesteak is really delicious - Amoroso roll, lean and tasty meat with perfectly cooked onions and gooey whiz. It's comparable to a Jim's steak more than Pat's/Geno's. So the steak is great but what really makes this place standout is that the experience is actually enjoyable. Other well-known places act like they're doing you a favor by serving you up a sandwich. Not at Sonny's where the service is friendly, the place is clean, the line moves, there's easy access to napkins, ketchup, etc. and there's a bathroom. All in all a great experience and even saw Sonny there, who obviously cares a lot about his namesake and it shows.
The food was not bad and the service a little slow, but I have had better experiences with Lebanese food in Tampa Bay.
We ate here on a Sunday afternoon and everything was great!  The food was fresh and delicious. The service was excellent!

Food: 3
Decor: 3
Ambiance: 3
Service: 3.5
Value: 3

Good steak and a good atmosphere considering the strip mall location. A little expensive though.

First time here to Skyway Café and I had a great experience. There is inside and outside seating available (both sun and shade) The prices are very reasonable with average of $9 to $10 or less! Huge portions. I love you because they have a little bit of everything in them and they have many to choose from. Service was good and you pay inside at the register. 

Special traditional breakfast options for $3.95 between 7:00-8:30. Located inside the plaza all the way over on the right hand side on the corner

I showed up for brunch with the Grandparents

Since they were paying and primarily focused on discussing my educational plans and career objective...I decided to order something I could shovel in my mouth between discussions regarding admissions, internships, lsats and the bar exam 

The Bistro Flatbread was a million times better than chewing on a twix for one of those much needed "moments"

The delicious combo of Bacon, Eggs, Arugula Pesto, Red Onion and Parmesan left me enough time to savor every tasty bite and respond with a diplomatic response!


SIMPLY DELICIOUS! 


I'll be back for lunch and dinner! :)

Big Firehouse Subs fan here. I have had Firehouse Subs in Carson in the past, but some how must have slipped my memory. We ordered online and I loved that you could select your time. I got the Meatball sub and it was so fantastic. The bread was perfect and not too soggy, the sauce had great flavor without being spicy, and the meatballs are some of the best I have ever had!! The sprinkle of Italian seasoning on the top of the cheese is a great touch. 

Our order was ready when we arrived with no issues! This was a great quick dinner on these crazy nights.

We ate here for a quick breakfast on our way to play tourist - our hotel was on the next corner. We were not disappointed. I had the tbm squagel. FYI - tbm = tomato, basil, mozarella. Squagel = a square bagel. The breakfast sandwich was awesome! I would definitely have this again (and I might..tomorrow!). The staff was friendly, and the prices were good. My breakfast sandwich and a large green tea were just over $5. My only complaints:  1) Our table was wobbly, which isn't fun when you have hot beverages on the table, and 2) my tea was so hot, I had to wait until I was almost done eating my sandwich to drink it. The food was five stars!

First time trying this place and really enjoyed it. It is a relatively small space with a small bar. The hh wine offerings are nice and they do a generous pour. We had the escargot, French cheese puffs and the cheese board. Escargot were great, cheese puffs just ok I'm my opinion and the cheese board was large and very tasty. We actually were unable to finish it. Would definitely go back.
My husband and I really enjoyed this restaurant. This is our first time in New Orleans and want be our last time. It was raining but it didn't stop us from trying this restaurant. WE WILL BE BAC

I have never been inside this place but actually discovered it during covid through uber eats. Once I'm ready to go back to going out to eat, they will be one of the first on my list. When food is still good after delivery, you know they're doing things right. Even fried food is excellent here whereas usually when you get something fried delivered it's soggy and greasy.  Highly recommend their popcorn shrimp, crab cakes, key lime pie and the list goes on. Somehow they even make broccoli that makes my mouth water!  I've now ordered from them about a half dozen times and they have yet to disappoint. Great job you guys!  I know how difficult it is to operate in the world of COVID, I work retail, and you guys are really killing it!  Thank you!!!

Today I took 3 kids with me to eat at one of our favorite family restaurants.   We not only had a wonderful, fun meal, we also had great service.  My server Kristin was extremely prompt with everything.  I never waited for a refill.  That's one of my biggest pet peeves.  Also, when we were done our meal she bagged up my food and brought me the check.  I was paid and out the door in under 5 minutes.  With two of the kids under the age of 10 it was a godsend.   Only minus I would say is not a huge selection of deserts.  Oh well, still a great night out just me and the three boys.

Been here once before and the service and food were good.  Just stopped in again and could get no service.  Only 4 other customers and the bartender made eye contact with me twice but never would come take my order.  Hate it, but they lost me as a customer for good.

Went here today and sat outside on the patio. Great selection of dogs and they can be grilled, steamed or FRIED. The fried pickles and tator tots should not be missed as sides for your dogs. Their original dogs are all 1/4 lb and you also have the option to "build your own." bonus was the special today on 2-for-1 beers!

Five stars for knowing what it is - and going above and beyond.

Before I start, understand this one star review is not about the food, but the customer service. I have been to this Chipotle many times over the past couple years. I have always had very good food, and great customer service. But today, I had a horrible experience at this particular Chipotle and I've got to say, I don't think I'm ever going back. 
After waiting in line with painfully slow service, I finally got to the counter and the two employees in the front were nothing but rude, slow, and lazy. I asked for soft taco shells as I usually get, and what I got was next to disgusting. Firstly, the two female employees were very rude, and kept stopping to talk, whisper, and laugh at me, and my order. I know this because they were not trying to hide their banter. She piled it too much and last second when rolling it and a horribly rolled tinfoil PILE, one fell open and spilled all over the rest of the tacos and they just laughed and squished them all together. When I finally get home to eat my tacos wrapped in a squished flat ball of tinfoil, the tacos were all over the place, and it was basically mush with a few tacos in balls.
Liked the signature wings and their ranch dressing.  Service was  good and got food pretty quick.  I recommend you try this place if you are in Indy.
Great bagel! A little expensive, but overall good service and good food. I got the whole wheat bagel with veggie cream cheese--amazing! Would definitely recommend.

Nice relaxing place to come for lunch or dinner. The front porch is a wonderful lunch spot on a warm sunny day. They offer a wide a wide variety of options and have always been pleased with the freshness and quality of the food. The fried green tomatoes are a must and defiantly recommend trying their daily specials. The bar area can be fun too, great place to watch a saints game. I have yet to experience the drag brunch on Saturdays but I will get there soon enough.
Amazing burgers! While it gets crowded and you need to wait, it's worth it. Everything is delicious, you can't go wrong with any choice!

Probably my favorite local spot. Always great service and great food. I like to dine for lunch and dinner. My husband and kids also love to eat at Terra Nova.
Love the wine country ambiance as well as the menu.
Love the Terra Nova salad with grapes, goat cheese and roasted red peppers. I have never been disappointed by a meal here.

We visited on Sunday about 11:00 am on a recommendation.  My group ordered Javier's French Toast, Biscuits & Gravy with Bacon, Bacon Cheeseburger, and Pancakes with a over-medium Egg and side of Bacon.

Result:
Server was OK, might have been better if she wasn't given such a big station.  She would disappear for 10 minutes at a time.  I blame the manager, wherever he/she was hiding during our entire dining experience.

-  French toast arrived cold with cold syrup and room temp margarine.  Server disappeared.  Wasn't fixed.  Taken off the check.  Left hungry.
-  Bacon Cheeseburger.  OK.  Only ate half.  There is a McDonald's in the parking lot if you want a better one.
-  Biscuits and gravy were good.  Bacon was good.
-  Pancakes were good.  Side egg and bacon was good.
-  Coffee is not good.  If you drink Starbucks Pike Place Roast, you will not like the house coffee here.  If you like the flavor of a Sanka instant coffee, you will be in heaven.

Bottom line:  Bar is open at breakfast.  Mimosa's and Bloody Mary's abound in the dining room.  Die hard's sit directly at the bar with mixed drinks and beer.  If you are inebriated, I can see how that would make the food more palatable.  If you are not, you eat at your own risk.  Basic eggs and bacon will meet expectations, everything else is average and below.

This little hidden gem just off campus has some great food to go with its great location.  I enjoyed the small breakfast we tried out while sitting on the patio, enjoying the last of the summer.  The food is tasty but not plentiful, especially with the higher than normal prices.

Beside the portions, I do have an issue with places that don't have table service (we were there in mid afternoon, before waiting staff started) PLUS add the tip to the total bill being paid upfront.  I'm not sure why this makes sense, but I'm at the counter paying for food that has yet to come (which I'll have to wait for, or run up to get) and being hit up for the tip already.  And even worse is the options that come up for the tip while paying with a credit card - 15%, 20% or 25%....for what!?!  

Ya, I know, this is starting to turn into a rant worthy of the opening cafe scene in Reservior Dogs, but I believe that the tip is based on the service one gets and should be decided at the end of the meal.  And if I'm serving myself, well....
We have been here multiple times. The food is always good along with the service and atmosphere. We will continue to come back.
Love the HaPenny!  They have lots of beer on tap (24) food and atmosphere is great an love the live music!  Karaoke on Wednesdays is fun too!

This landmark Tampa establishment sits in the belly of downtown Tampa in an old 3 story red brick building.  The architecture is fabulous.  The best part about this place, is the food menu is 3 steps above your average sports bar food.  The bartenders really know how to make great cocktails, & the mix of people runs the gamut of suit & tire downtown lawyers, University of Tampa college students, tourists, & blue collar workers.  Now, the downside:  The service is mediocre at best.  The servers are for the most part just short of being gorgeous swimsuit models, but their personalities are like the "ugly librarian".  Let me state I have frequented this establishment many times, & have had numerous female servers.  They all seem to act as if they'd rather be somewhere else than serving their customers.  I mean, I tip well above average, & am a pleasant person, not some loud mouthed drunk.  But, the only thing keeping this establishment getting 5 stars, is the serving staff.  Someone needs to train these ladies, that just looking good doesn't mean you do a good job.

This place was just okay.  

The customer service from the bouncers inside of the club were very respectful and peaceful.  

Other than that it's a pretty cool bar. Music seems to be a little too loud if that's ever a complaint to have.

Not a really fan.

Merchant takes itself a little too seriously.  We stopped in for a quick, to-go coffee and yogurt parfait.  Ten painfully slow minutes ticked by and I felt like I was watching a yogurt parfait making class as the staff went through the process of placing individual fruit slices around the rim of a plate, scooping perfectly shaped yogurt balls out of a tub with a fancy ice cream scooper, and then delicately drizzling honey in an artful swirl to top off the masterpiece.  I wanted to scream as I saw each new step in the complex process begin.  Come on people, it's just yogurt.  My time is far more important to me than a strawberry cut and fanned into a flower.

I am not gonna go into a long-winded diatribe about this terrific eatery. I just left an OUTBACK and the experience was sooo abysmal that it made me wonder why I didn't just go to Chop House in the first place. Never had a bad meal at Chop House. See you very soon.........

Gianna is a real delight! Delicious and not pretentious! While it looks like a "fancy" place, they welcome everyone. From the hostess, to the waiter, to other staff helping with our table, the service was exceptional. I ordered the spaghetti with mussels and my vegetarian friend ordered the lemon ricotta ravioli. We loved our options and raved about each! We also shared the ficoccia bread, which was a teeny but oily, but that's literally how ficoccia is made, so can't complain. One thing to note is that the restaurant may change their menu a fair amount.. for example, a lot of the options that we saw online are no longer offered. So, just keep that in mind when looking online. This may mean a bit frustrating, but this also means that their menu is fresh and constantly up to date. I also ordered the Trulia (?) drink and it was amazing! I love an Old Fashioned and it was just like an Old Fashioned or Sazerac, but with a hint of coffee at the end. I don't even like coffee, but it was delicious! Overall, Gianna was a great choice! Highly recommend.

Pretty good! It is quite expensive ($9 for a small/medium sized smoothie). I ordered the pina-Cado smoothie which was super bitter and not sweet at all. Maybe they forgot the banana? Haha. It tasted very healthy though. Probably won't be going back because the price is high and I could make one at home for cheaper than that with equally quality ingredients. Very friendly customer service though.

Stopped in late to give it a whirl. Name is a little misleading as you would think the main menu item would be wings. Not so as they offer quite a few other things as well.   Got 10 wings. Classic buffalo. So the wings were good size and meaty. The sauce was a little sweet for buffalo but wasn't bad. The wings were good but could have benefited from a hotter fryer or more cook time.  The place is clean and the price is right. Will definitely go back to try a few other things.

I am so glad that Mt. Juliet has another locally owned restaurant offering a great menu. We had dinner last night during their 3rd night of "soft opening" and like other reviewers have stated - its clearly a new business. I will not judge too harshly as this was the point of their gradual opening. The staff is very friendly and seems genuinely eager to serve. I believe the awkwardness will wear off as they get more comfortable. The décor is nice, but it is kind of loud and the main dining room seems cavernous (even though it is not that big). The music is a little too loud and last night they were playing newish pop country (think Florida Georgia Line and Luke Bryan) which didn't really add much to the ambience. But, I can overlook all of that if the food is superb. Problem is, it was not. I had the 7 oz filet (beef tenderloin) which was served with "stacked potatoes" and shredded brussell sprouts. The brussell sprouts were fantastic. The steak was good - maybe even very good, but not "wow" good. The potatoes had no seasoning of any kind and were as bland as hospital food. Also, there is no salt and pepper on the table and I didn't ask for it because I took that to mean the food wouldn't need it. For dessert, my bf ordered the cream puffs with candied bacon. It was not good. The puffs were cold (which the GM, who was very friendly) said they were supposed to be served that way - so what do I know - but I didn't love them. When I have had candied bacon before it is all about the sweet of brown sugar or maple contrasted with the salty of the bacon - this had a sweet coating, but it also had a large amount of pepper. The pepper was not good in concert with the sweet, and in my humble opinion should have been directed to the potatoes. 
All in all, I'll give them another try, but maybe for lunch when the potential financial exposure is not as great. I just didn't feel it was an $87 value and that is what we spent for two entrees, 2 glasses of house wine and one dessert. Still gave it a 4 because I have great optimism and I really want somewhere to eat in MJ besides chains!!

Ate dinner there a few nights back.  Excellent food.  Jalapeño shooters were great, fantastic sauce with them in shooter glasses.  Forgot the real name, but basically a salmon quesadilla (more to it than that) was rated superb by the two in our group that got that dish.  Great menu.  Would go again.

Food has the same consistency as other locations but the service here is excellent! Kate was very friendly and attentive. Hosts opened door for us upon entering and leaving. Definitely felt like they were going above and beyond to make our experience feel special

Don't you hate when the restaurant is slow and your server talks to the locals and doesn't give a shit about a new customer who just had Tabasco on his fries and his iced tea glass has been empty for 15 minutes ? Yeah me too !!

Great selection for college kids and late night eats 
Also fab to get delivery and they will add things like lighters or tp if you ask nicely! Love them and the nice guys working tonight...updated below.  They refused what I just claimed above so sorry to mislead you

UpdateWorst service ever on a large items totaling three dollars of which I had already over tipped and accountant for a special notation asking if they could be paid for that way. It was refused even though it had been done before and I was told I was a liar that that could've been possible. 

I don't make it a point to pay people to call me a liar when I know exactly what has been done for me before I have it in the notes. The manager was rude and argumentative even though I pointed out that not only had it been done before but that it was a pretty small price to pay to keep a customer that was placing a very large order regularly from them. 

Didn't matter to him at all all he wanted was his cash in hand. I told him if he was willing to get a terrible review for three dollars then that was a fair exchange and I will only be ordering because the guys to cook the food are usually in a good mood and do a decent job and the place has a wide selection of items available but not enough added to the menu that you can order everything you need without going to the store. 

So now that I've been giving a completely distasteful feeling and I'm hardly even hungry anymore except that I have not eaten in almost 2 days due to traveling across the country with the time difference jet leg etc. and this is my first experience back home with food ordering for $50 plus order?!?! Grrrrrrr!!!!

I'm extremely unsatisfied with their ruination of my faith in their ability to run a mini mart/delivery properly, and that it took me 10 minutes on the phone only to be forced into paying for something that I already paid for in the extra tip. 

Telling me you're not the owner of the business over and over again is not an effective tool for customer service assistance. I understand not everyone has clout to make whatever changes they want but if an action is already prior performed, I don't really want to hear that now it can't be again in less than a few weeks later. 

Pretty much spoiled my entire evening to have to deal with that whatsoever and I thought I was receiving a phone call from the delivery to be outside not to just be discussed over again, $3!!!!!  I should've canceled the order but I'm too starving to bother. Sorry been enough time that it should've been cut and delivered if they weren't so busy dealing with everything else and trying to call me about pettiness. In no way did I penalize the driver either as I said my temp is going to be lower and I added additional I didn't ask them stiff the driver for me to get free items? I said I'll pay U this and u allocate it. Because it's run through Santa Barbara menus app I have to complain to them that they were unable to help me probably because of their system so now it's two companies involved in the problem and I run a local business review Instagram about sb... it's all nonsense. It's too bad they're over run with drunk college kids and I'm not one so it doesn't sit well with me to be treated as some bother.

I went to Noche a few weeks ago for Center City Sips and wasn't too impressed. The drinks were alright, but the service is seriously lacking. I was meeting a group of at least 20 other people, so the first few of us asked for separate checks at the beginning of the night. Our waitress seemed nice enough but forgot who ordered what and ended up bringing an extra drink. It was still pretty dead at this point, and there were only four people at our table. 

I left the table for a little bit to talk to my friend by the bar and got a drink there. It was really hard to get the bartender's attention. She was more interested in talking to her coworkers instead of serving drinks. Even when I tried to pay for my drink not even a second after she handed it to me, she stared off in another direction at her coworker. 

We asked for our checks and our waitress combined them (thankfully only the table, not the entire group). She also charged some drinks at the sips rate and others at their regular price, even though sips wasn't over yet. We asked her to fix it, but the check she came back with was wrong too. 

I can't think of any reasons to return.

This is a cool little place to get a good bite and some cold beer. On a cool evening you can enjoy the patio. They have amazing fried pickles and make a mean ahi tuna burger. They have live music some nights. They have a lot of vegetarian options.
More of a coffee place that serves food. Breakfast sandwich on a bagel etc. Chic and very shabby. I'm not sure how much I'm dying to return but if Bitter Sweet is too long a wait it's worth a try.

Not at all impressed.  The burger was over cooked and pretty tasteless.  The cashier was not friendly or helpful.  Overall, very disappointing.  Truth be told, there is a Wendy's down the street and the new Hot N' Juicy burgers there are far superior to the one I had at Cheeseburger Eddie's.  Probably will not return for the burger, but would like to give the other fare a chance.
Great food, great price but the place is small and waiting times can be long.  Still a gray local place.

cant get enough of this place. the burger battle is a great way to spend your lunch time. Sneak in a cold Urban Chestnut then saunter back to the rest of the day. Good spot before Cardinal games and they are open late. if they have the candied bacon you have to try it.

Amazing food! If you're looking for something late night and something filling, or maybe just to soak up all the booze you've been drinking, highly recommend coming here. We ordered the basil soup bowl with the cheesy top and the hangover bowl and we both were very satisfied! Come to Buddha bowls and pack a bowl! Ps the staff is awesome, shout out to Daniel!

Very flavorful food. While I eat Indian food all the time I had never heard of a DOSA. I enjoyed my meal so much that once I returned to NYC I had to look for a restaurant which services it. Unfortunately it was not as good....
Long time Nashvillan first time to eat here it has always been packed glad we made the wait it was delicious  and we will be going back the rib eye was the best I have had.

This location has restored my faith in the franchise. When I give this location four stars, it doesn't mean this is the best food in Nashville. It means this location does exactly what a McDonald's is supposed to do. The staff is friendly and jovial every time. In six recent visits I have never received an incorrect order or poorly-presented food. The place is almost always busy but service is consistently prompt, with little to no wait time. Keep doing what you're doing!

I would give this restaurant zero stars if possible. The only good thing about this place is the friendly servers. I had a quesadilla which was so soggy I couldn't pick it up before it fell apart. I also had a side order of shrimp which was not only cold when it was supposedly "grilled", but it was tough, lacked seasoning and flavor. I wouldn't recommend this restaurant to my worst enemy...yes, it's that bad.

I visited this restaurant bcoz it showed on my search results and looked decent enough. What I encountered though, well let's just say, I wasn't ready for it.

The lunch buffet had a huge variety of dishes, which simply stuns you. And if that doesn't, then the taste of those dishes sure will.

A must visit restaurant!

I'm absolutely obsessed with this place. I finally made my way to this shop three weeks ago and I'm kind of ashamed to admit that I now go at least once if not twice a week. I used to be a Bing's fan but I've fully converted and haven't stepped in there since. 

The best thing about Chatime is that there are literally hundreds (maybe thousands???) of drink combinations so you will never get bored and can always try something new. I've had the roasted milk teas, the taro pudding tea, lychee black tea , milk chocolate and they are all super delicious. I am usually the type of person who finds one drink and sticks with it but I can't help but want to TRY ALL THE THINGS. I was surprised with how rich their flavors were - a lot of bubble tea places rely on sugar, powder and milk and the flavor is kind of an afterthought. Since you can adjust sugar, ice, and add-ins they make a point to start out with a really good liquid beverage so everything tastes authentic. I also love drinking the add-ins and Chatime makes it a point to fill the cup at least a quarter full of sweet, sweet tapioca (or other stuff). After I finish drinking the liquid part I'm always left with a whole bunch of boba to vacuum suck up with my face which is awesome.

I too wish they opened just a little bit earlier since I'd love to stop buy here and get a drink before I run errands on the weekends. Other than that I have zero complaints and I will be back until I have tried as many things as possible from the menu.

I've been to several of the steakhouses downtown Indy and Hyde Park is one of the best. I have been to devour at Hyde Park and I've also been to the restaurant outside of that, and both experiences were great. The steak is seasoned well, always cooked to the correct temperature, sides are plenty to share, and the service is great. I've tried the tomato soup, wedge, and ceasar salads, and each of these apps are very good. The side I will never not order again is the Lobster Mac and Cheese, I've lived in Boston and I have to say that Hyde Park Lobster Mac competes with New England lobster mac.  Overall, this is an underrated steakhouse that I always enjoy visiting!

Boy. This place used to be my go-to place. I haven't had sushi in a while and went to hit them up with my family a few times over a couple weeks (it was a bit crazy as we went for fun and celebrations during that period). Both times the service and quality of the food was a lot less than I expect. The sushi we received was shoddily rolled and the rice was a bit stale and hard, but it was still okay. 
The major turn offs of the meals were the service of the waitresses. She had this reluctant and narcissist attitude and I felt like I was begging her. She was really impatient with us and almost made us order right then and there and did not offer to come back later since she seemed soo busy. She would give us less straws and forks than we needed or requested and seemed really annoyed as she tossed us the two straws that she forgot. 
I used to love dining at this place and sushi is to be eaten as soon as it is prepared, but I would rather bring it home and save my appetite.

After hearing about there chicken sandwhich we strolled in to give it a shot and we were highly impressed. The chicken is cooked and breaded perfect a long with the spicy sauce its a hit. While we didn't try the donuts we did enjoy the iced coffee. The hype is real the chicken sandwhich is very good simple as that and holds it's own against other local competitors. Definitely will be back again!

Quaint small place on side street, but service & food is great! Ironman Omelette! It's too bad they don't have a nicer place with a view, however I will go back anyway. Probably so good because owner, a very nice clean cut guy, does the cooking!

The parking lot has some scary signs.  They basically discourage diners from parking there for fear of being towed.  I guess, in the summer time, Kelly drive visitors abuse the parking.  There is a pay lot across the street but why should I pay to park in this area.  

The other oddity is the fact that this place that specializes in breakfast does not offer pancakes.  Apparently it has to do with griddle space.  Each time I go I peruse the menu and feel as if the selection leaves something to be desired but I always find something interesting and I usually enjoy it.  

When it's warmer there is a nice patio for outdoor dining.  In the winter the single room diner is quite cozy.

Stayed here 8/24 for 3 nights. Love the hotel and the huge casino. Was not impressed with housekeeping services. They were too busy complaining about their jobs in the hallway that they overlooked our room. Took 3 more calls to get less than adequate service.
We attended a VIP dinner in the ballroom. My friend tripped over a loose outlet cover and was injured. The staff and EMT's were nice enough but the manager of the ballroom, already aware of this ILLEGAL HAZARD did little to accomodate. Nor did anyone follow up with us the next day or before we checked out. I referred this to my VIP host here in IL to make sure it gets resolved. It was a love/hate experience but I would probably go back.

Love the food and atmosphere! Fresh seafood and good cocktails. They have a bakery right beside the restaurant with delicious desserts. Nice little town with lots of stores and restaurants! Cool Greek people

Good old fashion dogs.
It's not fancy, the menu is classic, that is the charm!

Excellent Dogs (love the fact you can order "ONE" and they get you a dog!)  Condiments are on the side, mustard, kraut, relish, ketchup, all the usual suspects.

...Model Train Sets... (old and they run for a quarter, bring some)

Since 194X, it's a tradition, If you haven't been you have to go!

This is my favorite breakfast in St. Louis.  Every dish that I've had so far is top notch.  I'm trying to work my way down the menu, but they keep throwing in specials and I get sidetracked!  You can tell the management cares about every ingredient.  I see a few comments here about the space being small and crampy.  It's breakfast, people!  It's supposed to be bright and lively, just like the coffee.  It's not supposed to be a relaxing hookah lounge.  If you want to get a $15 breakfast for $9 and be happy the rest of the day, then this is your spot.

I was hesitant after reading some of the reviews but so glad I gave them a try. Yummy $5 martinis special, great bang for your buck combos. We had snow crab legs, dungeonous crabs, crawfish, raw clams. All the seafood were big and meaty. Try the sauces on the side. I enjoyed dipping the crab legs in the garlic butter sauce.

This review is only for happy hour.... however we talk about doing actual dinner there often.  

We really dig the bar & margs here.... great happy hour too - I believe it's 1/5 price on margs all Tuesday. 

Their chips & salsa bar with beans is delicious- which makes it hard to order food; I'll review once we do.

Whereas most resturants and bars in Center City gives off a modern, swanky, high class vibe, Oscar's is one if the few places that are divey, but hey, there's absolutely nothing wrong with a dive that serves cheap food and drinks so long as they're good, and Oscar's did not dissappoint.The chicken strips, crab fries, and pierogis were all bomb as well as the screwdrivers I ordered back to back. 

There was a bit of a wait before we could order, because it was super packed due to it being right after CDC Sips, and there was only one waitress. We didn't mind though, and I musy say she was really working the whole bar front to back, kudos to her!

Overall, Oscar's is a good hangout spot to grab a drink or a snack with friends.

Fresh pressed juices with a river view. Cucumber juice with kale spinach parsley and lemon is a favorite of mine. They also have various lemonades and limeades but have a bit too much sugar in them for my personal taste. A great stop after a run or a bike ride.

I found Stanley on the last day of my trip to New Orleans and was extremely disappointed to be leaving with only a single meal here. There is simply so much on the menu that you will want to try, I ordered the Club Stanley, which consists of Grilled Chicken Breast, Sliced, Ham, Smoked Bacon, Swiss Cheese, Lettuce, Tomatoes and Spicy Caesar Pesto Dressing on Toasted French Bread. I was a little unsure about the spicy ceaser pesto so I ordered it on the side, however that was quite possibly the best part of the sandwich. The sandwiches are not served with a side, so fries are extra however you are getting a quality sandwich and the fries are enough to share with another person. I really wanted to try their breakfast which they hype as the best in the city, and after seeing a few plates come out from the kitchen I have to think they are right. Everything I saw looked delicious, and their presentation for being an upscale diner was amazing. This was quite possibly the best meal I had during my trip to New Orleans, I will be back!

R2GO ("ready to go") lives up to its name, with fresh, healthy food ready to go. Either order a sandwich or salad from the menu board or select an individual entree from the freezer - think pot pies, soups, sides and more. This would be great for a quick meal stop.

I liked the selection of local artisan goods - both familiar and new to me. Of note: U-Relish, XChocol'art, Crazy Charlie's salsa, Endangered Species Chocolate, Best Chocolate in Town, Newfangled Confections and B. Happy Peanut Butter. Lots of goodies to stock up on!

There is a small counter area to sit and eat, if you wish. Parking is mostly just available in the front.

Here's a situation where different diners can sometimes have different experiences. Split decision in our family: half liked; half not so much. But since I'm the Yelp elite and this is my review... here is my experience. 

A very popular place but...

Felt unwelcomed most of the time and only got a smile at the end... you know that "please give me a decent tip" smile. 

Had to wait more than 20 minutes while a suitable table sat open. Clean and set but unoccupied. "Reserved" even though the party was not present. But for us it was a long wait on a hard bench and one that we had to ask for a parked stroller to be moved so we could sit. 

How about those complimentary fried chickpeas. Apparently they are only for most tables but not ours. Hmmmm. Even the kids splitting a burger got some. But not us. And not a couple of other "tourist" tables near us.

Dinner was actually tasty. The short ribs were well cooked, on the bone and, although not mentioned on the menu, basted with a tasty barbecue sauce. The mashed potatoes a bit bland. The veg was really well cooked and a pleasant mix of broccoli, zucchini, and asparagus. The salmon got good reviews. The seafood pasta, it was noted, was somewhat skimpy on the seafood. 

Service was minimal. This is a place run by kids so I guess that's to be expected. Best service seemed to be from the bus boy. 

As I said, the only smile was at the "pay your bill, give me a good tip, and let me turn the table". Well... two out of three is the best I could do tonight. 

But here's what really finalized my opinion about the lack of hospitality. A couple was being seated near us and asked the hostess about a corner table that had recently vacated. Rather than bus the table this girl told them it was dirty and their only alternative was where they were shown or on the patio. Really????????

Best Burgers in Saint Louis
Friendly and Courteous Staff
Gets busy in the weekends, so plan accordingly.

A-OK is exactly right. We ordered delivery, easy to place order and pay over the phone, pizza took 45 mins. The large pizzas were smaller than expected. The sauce was good. The crust was decent. They were decent pies. 

Food: 3/5 - average
Service: 3/5
Drinks are wonderful and deviled eggs are divine!!  The best I've ever tasted!!  I can't wait to come back and utilize the patio when it's warm outside.

Great Food!! Great Customer Service!!
The Rice Pudding is Delish
Lamb and Chicken Shawarma!!
Greek Salad is the best
Seasonal chef's tasting menu was incredible. Excellent service and great Sake recommendations

Don't forget to check in to receive their 50% off drink deal!! 

Really wish this place had opened sooner when I was still working in the area. This mini "food hall" offers a variety of good eats including bubble tea, poké, ramen, and bento boxes. But instead of individual vendors like in Chinatown Square, the same team runs the whole operation. 

I really like how the teas used are really fresh and flavorful -- some drinks even come with their own little satchel of leaves. They also have unique options like smashed taro (not taro syrup), red dates, and grape tea with cheese foam that you just don't see anywhere else in the city.

But the real star is the poké bowls. For just a little extra, you can create a custom bowl and it's 100% worth it. With your choice of base (rice, salad, noodles, etc.) along with two proteins and over a dozen toppings, the sheer amount of food you get is no joke.

Best gourmet pizza in town!
We don't normally go out for pizza. We were at the downtown Dunedin Mardi Gras festival and didn't want street food. We frequent Casa Tina for their heavy vegetarian menu so we decided to try their sister restaurant next door. The atmosphere is quaint and super romantic. The pizza is the best we have had in years. Just like Casa Tina there are many vegetarian options on this menu and they even use mostly all organic ingredients! We got the Posse's Pesto Pie and added the spinach and tomato. It was all so delicious. The wine selection is great also. It was a super busy night because of the festival and the service was fast and very friendly. We found out our sever was Tina herself and she is super bubbly and really puts her heart into her work. We will definitely be back very soon.

We keep coming back because the pizza is usually delicious, but they always mess up in some way, and tonight was no exception.  The email said to pick up our pizzas at 630, but we went late because they are never ready when we get there.When we got there they couldn't find the pizzas, but the cheese fries were sitting there.  The manager said they were crazy busy and backed up, but there was one couple eating there, and not a single pizza in the warmer.  Turns out they forgot to make them.  He offered to make me an extra pizza for free, that's fine, but I'd rather have one that I ordered for free.  I asked him if he was going to remake the cheese fries and he argued that they were fine, I pointed out how long they were sitting there and he said fine and threw them across the kitchen and said "We have to remake this guy's f###ing cheese fries."  This is completely unacceptable behavior.  When I first got there and they couldn't find my pizzas, he told me he was the new manager, and that he was going to make this place better.  He needs to calm down and take care of his customers.  To make this all worse, we paid for extra cheese, and there is barely any cheese on our pizzas, it's like eating crackers.  I've thought about writing yelp reviews before, but this is the first time I've actually done this, but when he threw the fries and said the f word, I knew I had to.  The service here has always been bad, but tonight's service  is unacceptable.

We went to this place today on a lark because we were nearby. And I have every intention of going again.
It's a small, casual place in a strip mall but it's very clean and the staff were all very nice.
 My daughter and I shared the Power salad and it was delicious. They put the chicken on my half as she's a vegetarian. She got the veggie burger and really liked it. She's had some really gross veggie burgers in her young life and stopped ordering them for a few years so I always appreciate a place that has a good one. I had a burger also, the one with the blue cheese and mushrooms, very yummy. 
 I took home personal pizzas for my husband and son and both liked what they got. It was a pleasant, unassuming surprise and worth checking out.

We eat at Grillsmiths often. We love the outside seating area with the TVs and they even have a separate area that is pet friendly which is so nice since we love to bring our fur friends out for the day often. They make us feel very welcome and catered to every visit. Our server Joey is so accommodating and attentive. I have only had excellent service here and highly recommend it.
Love this place. Can get pretty busy at times, but great food, atmosphere and staff! We often eat at the bar and Deana is the best! Attentive, makes great drinks and super friendly!
Food was ok, a bit over priced. Coffee was strong which was good. The wait is not so bad if u go early in the morning when they open

The pizza dove was excellent! The tomato sauce was not too sweet or too beater, it was perfect. all the ingredients were fresh. One of the best pizzas I have even had.  The service was fast, nice, and cordial and the ambient was good too. 

They need to work a little more in the gelato. It was little too sweet and the consistency was more like a regular ice. 

Overall speaking. A really good place to eat.

The boneless wings are sinfully delicious, good size and has the perfect breading for the right crispiness.  This is no low calorie food, but man is it worth it.  It's white meat chicken and still so yummy.  
The sauces are purchased separately and if you like it spicy, go for the suicide.  For me, I do not recommend any of the honey flavored mixes, and would just stick with the mild BBQ flavors.  We decided to go with $1/bag of celery and just used our blue cheese dip at home.  

They know how to cook, but I'm not sure if it's the Philly attitude, I sure as hell didn't feel the brotherly love.  So aside from the as a matter of fact attitude, this place is best for take out.  The store is quite old, never been updated, and cleanliness is a little questionable.  

To end on a good note, I've only always gone back for the boneless wings and would keep coming back.

COMFORT  FOOD!  Take a look at these handmade onion rings http://static.px.yelp.com/photo/oadmmq8SpTKvWbgcK_gJAg/l 

Really good bar food with a really good beer selection as well.  Service was a bit erratic on my visit, but the delicious food made up for it.   R.T. Weilers is definitely in my rotation now. :)

This is a cute little place on the water. The service here is phenomenal and the workers are very friendly. Good happy hour specials too - certain drafts for $3 and certain apps and sushi rolls for $5. Food here is good as well... Cheesy board, chicken tenders, conch fritters, fried shrimp all very good. Their sushi is okay - not bad but not anything to write home about. The only thing I would not recommend here is the queso, which tasted okay but it had a gloopy, viscous consistency.
Unique cocktails, attentive service, creative dishes, the buffalo stuffed morels with romesco sauve were perfect, the duck ramen noodles were also excellent.

Food is delicious though i wish the cooks were more consistent. The male cooks tend to cook better then the females. Just my opinion. Menu isn't always consistent but when they do have everything and the male cooks.... oh boy everything is delicious. The female cooks good it's just that you can tell who likes to opposed to who has too!
Very nice casual atmosphere, tasty salad. A little hard to find because it's tucked away in a residential neighborhood.
A fun little bar on Bourbon St. Drinks are reasonably priced and it's easy to get liquored up here. They also have some great bands that play in the evening. This was one of our favorites to come to.

This was my first time eating here. I ordered off grubhub and had it delivered. Delivery was quick, received my order within 30min. The delivery girl was friendly. I ordered their soul food - half baked chicken, collard greens, yams and cornbread. The chicken was tasty and juicy. The collard greens and yams were both delicious. The cornbread is huge and sweet but a little on the hard side. I would recommend and order again. Affordable prices as well! My meal was $10.25

Absolutely delicious!!!  The hot peppers were the perfect amount of heat and the portion size was excellent. I got the Jewish style grinder with everything and finished the entire thing in one sitting, I couldn't stop eating.

All delicious. I got a apple cranberry cosmo and the bison burger which were both outstanding. My boyfriend got the chicken wrap and that was also so delicious and doesn't have a tortilla wrap, it's more of a flatbread/naan. Different and delicious ! We will definitely be back. The free harvest flatbread for checking in on yelp was underwhelming though, skip the calories

My friends and I went to Cafe con Chocolate for our Sunday brunch.  We went in a fairly large group with 7 people, but were seated right away.  Our server was an adorable and friendly young lady who was very familiar with the menu and explained all the dishes to us.  There was no tofu or Japanese food that day.  I ordered a cafe con chocolate, breakfast burrito, and homefries.  Food was delicious.  Cafe con chocolate was delicious, and HUGE.  Only complaint was how slow the food took to come to our table, and how long we had to wait for the check.  I figure that they are only busy on-and-off and can't afford to hire another server.  I would come here again!  They seemed happy to have us there to keep them in business.

Ok so this review reflects my latest visit. My previous visits echo everyone's else's complaints about how long it takes to wait for their food. 

This time, I decided to do take out to avoid the wait. I ordered drunken noodles and the waiter on the phone said it'll take 10 mins. Awesome. I stopped by within 15 mins and surprisingly, it was ready. Everything's great so far. 

I got home and took the first bite- THE NOODLES WERE TOUGH AND HARD. The spices and tofu were all great but come on... It's a noodle dish and you decide to mess it up by either using old noodles that harden OR undercooking the noodles. Please get your life together, TAP Thai. 

Easy and fast take out service but terrible quality. Avoiding this place.

The day when taco bus was just "The Taco Bus" and when they had lengua. And when the location near USF no one believed me was really a Taco Bus...now finally has its sign. 3 stars simply because...where's my lengua? The burritos have shrunk and locations have grown. Why close St. Pete Central Ave too? Place has just become an ok chain. Good spot for late night after hours, sober up mode.
Very quiet , pricey for the food they make which wasnt even satisfying my taste buds. Could be better, maybe.

IF YOU LOVE GUMBO COME TO LEE'S!!

Lee's gumbo is quite flavorful and delicious. It is one of my favorite gumbos in the whole city and it's full of chicken, sausage, and shrimp. Lee's also serves poboys, fried catfish, lasagna, mac n cheese, and other various hot foods. The place doesn't look like much but they serve good food (esp. the gumbo) at reasonable prices. Everything is served in to-go boxes or cups. The large gumbo is $7.50 and is big enough for two people to share. 

Who would have thought that of all the wonderful restaurants in our city that Lee's would end up being one of my favorite gumbo spots.

This place is a gem in what looked to me, a Reno visitor, like an up-and-coming, trendy part of town. Indoor ambiance is extremely spare; it's tasteful, but one could say lacking in personality. Since it also didn't seem to have ac, we chose to sit on the patio. Our seating area was charming with market lights, lots of space and in view of a large smoking grill. The best thing we ordered was a ravioli special with broccoli, cheese and meat sauce. I'm not sure I've ever had better ravioli. Everything else was also really good, but more satisfyingly tasty than that off-the-charts, fireworks-on-your-taste buds ravioli. Overall a great selection of authentic Italian food with modern flair. I'll be back if I ever end up in Reno with time for a leisurely meal again.

This is GREAT takeout. I'm used to being spoiled by Cafe Bombay in Bristol whenever I want Indian, so I guess I was expecting...well, not this. Great food.

We ordered the samosa chat, which is smashed samosas with yogurt, chickpeas and tomato chutney on top. Deeeeelicious! It was sweeter than I thought it would be and this was definitely a pleasant surprise. Also, I ordered two thinking they would be small, like samoas, but in reality these appetizers could probably feed three people each. Whoops.

Also ordered the chicken madras and the dal tadka, which is stewed lentils. We chose mild spice level, and it was still a little spicy...which is great for me, since I love spicy foods (my boyfriend does not share my enthusiasm), but might not be so great for someone very sensitive to spice. 

The delivery guy was almost on time - he was almost ten minutes later than what grubhub suggested, and he promptly apologized for being late. No big deal, we're in an apartment complex and most people have trouble finding us, and the food was still very hot so no harm, no foul. I imagine the food tastes great the next day, too.

Very, very happy this place is here!

Based upon my lunch time visit, I was expecting a fabulous dining experience with my wife and our friend.  Sadly, all our entrees were improperly flavor balanced.  Maybe it was the chef's night off.

We arrived on Thursday evening and were seated promptly.  The room was very dark, relying mainly upon the natural light at the front of the restaurant and some dimly lit hanging lights that were more ornamental than functional.

Our service was friendly and efficient throughout the evening which started off well.  We put in an order for the Bacon Wrapped Apricots - tequila soaked apricots, hickory smoked bacon, jalapeno kumquat honey glaze.  These were tremendous!  There was a bit of sauce on the side that added an extra layer to the flavor!  Definitely get these!

We also shared the Foie Gras - sauternes, charcoal honey, espelette jelly, pistachios, country bread.  I really liked this, especially the bites where I got a whole pistachio.  The ladies thought it was good, but thought it a bit light on flavor.

I then ordered the "Toad in a Hole" - toasted brioche, egg, asparagus, prosciutto, roasted peppers, poached pears, shaved brussel sprouts, brie, truffle mushroom puree.  The way it was served, I ended up cutting up the entire serving first so that I could get multiple flavors in every bite.  Otherwise, there would be some bites that were mostly bread.  If you look through the ingredients, you can easily see that lots of flavor combinations made this a delicious meal.  My only complaint was that the tableware knife was too dull to cut through the prosciutto.  

Our friend ordered the Harvest Salad - endive, roasted beets, goat cheese mousse, portobello, blackberries, buttermilk vinaigrette, pistachio granola.  She raved about how good it was.  My wife agreed.  They both thought it the high point of dining.

And then the entrees came out.  

There was no balance to my Pork Belly - red chile glaze, bacon braised swiss chard, smoked onion rings, white bean puree, sweet corn relish, peach coulis, arugula salad.  Again, I needed to cut the meal completely because the plate was stacked high.  The pork was very salty.  The chard and arugula were clumped and had a more intense flavor than expected, overwhelming the rest of the ingredients.  The bites without the greens were overwhelmed by the saltiness.  It just didn't work.  I could see promise in that the pork was cooked tender and the plate looked rather nice, but the balance was wrong.

My wife had the Beef Brisket - sweet corn pudding, roasted creamer potatoes, heirloom tomato puree, baby carrots, hickory gastrique, pickled mustard seeds.  She found the brisket on the dry side.  

Our friend ordered the Fettuccini - crushed tomato sauce, roasted garlic ricotta, pancetta.  The restaurant does offer meatballs for another $3.75, but since our friend is usually a light eater, she passed and just went with the basic plate.  Sadly, the flavors were basic.  She thought spaghetti at home had more appeal than what she was served.  I get it:  If you want spicy, get the meatball.  But if they are going to offer a meatless version, then the flavors should stand on their own.

We finished sharing a creme brulee with pear sorbet and candied rice krispies.  The brulee was good, but the sorbet was teeth chilling cold (I wonder if they used liquid nitrogen?)  Uncomfortable to eat, and then it tasted like juice.  Not much flavor complexity.

I don't like writing negative reviews or down grading from excellent ones.  But I could see the disappointment in my guest's faces.  Since we traveled nearly an hour to dine, it is unlikely we will be back any time soon.  Maybe we were just a few years late catching this place when it was one of the best in town.
Rev #17

We had an AMAZING experience here. Everything our server recommended was amazing. We got the jalapeño cornbread, fried chicken dinner with the baked beans, mac&cheese and mashed potatoes. We also ordered the cucumber salad and bbq wings. The food was fresh and everything was homemade. The baked beans are more of a barbecue baked beans. The fried chicken was crispy and flavorful. The baked Mac was extra cheesy and a very large size served in a skillet. The lemonade and sweet tea are fresh and not fountain drinks like local restaurants. 

I want to add a separate note about our server Katelyn. She was super attentive although she was working the door and restaurant and had multiple tables. We felt like we were her only table with the amount of attention she gave us. She was super knowledgeable about the menu and when I overheard her speaking with another customer who is vegetarian she knew exactly what items to suggest. I thought that was amazing and great customer service.

I would highly recommend this place and shall return. They also have live music.

My friend chose to eat here as it convenient to her business.  I hadn't eaten here in years so .. hey, what the heck.

We sat in the bar for lunch as she commented it is noticeably quieter.  It was also noticeably HOT in there!!  Where was the A/C????  

Our wait staff was prompt and cordial.  We both ordered the chicken pot pie.  It was huge, had a nice golden crust and was served within minutes of our order ...  why and how was it ready so soon???  Anyway, it had large chunks of white meat chicken, not many veggies though and the few in it were kind of mushified together.  The crust was tasty and flaky.  The sauce/gravy in it was rather bland on real flavor and VERY heavy on salt!!  There was a small bowl of fruit on the side .. and the melon was rather mushy ... I'm thinking frozen fruit maybe???

Anyway, I wouldn't go out of my way to eat there again and they really need to do something about the temperature comfort level in the bar.  Very unpleasant.

After reading positive reviews, decided to give it a try when my little bro was visiting. As a fan of Cuban/Columbian cusine, I knew he would appreciate the food. 

Upon arriving, the decor really struck me. The exposed brick and large opened windows were very inviting on a hot July day. At 11th and Pine, this restaurant is smack dab in the middle of residential territory. But unlike many of the small restaurant counterparts, Mixto offers lots of seating both indoor and out. As such, there was no wait for a table at the prime brunch hour of 11:30am - much to stomach's pleasure.  

Although the drinks looked delicious, we opted out of brunch libations and chose to focus on the food. Feeling a a little unadventurous, I opted for the American style pancake breakfast ($9) which was served with two pancakes, chorizo, two eggs, and homefries - quite a value! My bro opted for the more exciting Gallo Pico ($11) which was delicious - a nice Columbain meal with rice, beans, and plaintains. Next time I will probably order it. And the bf, not embracing the brunch aspect of brunch, got the cuban sandwich ($9).

Overall we enjoyed the food and will be returning! Maybe I'll try out their mojito/margarita happy hour or stop in for dinner one day.

Jeannie has done a great job here.  I had her riff on Chicken and Waffles and it was excellent, my wife was jealous.  Service was knowledgable and efficient.  Food took a while, but it was a Friday night.

I always past this place on my way to my house and I finally decided to stop in, the smell of the smoked meat was overwhelming and I had to try some. I normally never eat red meat but the smell of the beef brisket sandwich was tearing up my nose. I ordered it and a side of mac and cheese, the mac and cheese I would pass on in the future, but I will be breaking my non-red meat eating habits every time I come to Tom's, the beef brisket was out of this world, and the portion was more the generous, the smoke flavor was present throughout the brisket but was not overwhelming, and the hot bbq sauce was a perfect combination (its not hot at all but with a little kick at the end). I would 100% back a decision to purchase a beef brisket sandwich, you will not be disappointed, I would just say stay away from the sides.

Nice quaint little brunch place, has good Bloody Marys. Unfortunately, the portions were small. The food was good but you will probably not have leftovers. Took a long time for service .. Server seemed a big confused and there were discrepancies between the menu and what the waitress brought out for sides/etc. Iced mocha was Delish!
Applebees was ok.  Best service I received was from Crystal who handles the bar area.  Service was excellent. Thank you

My wife and I have been to Nirvana several times in the last year and a half. They have always had consistently good food. I usually get the buffet when available, so I can try out new dishes. The buffet always seems fresh and has many different options. They have plenty of vegetarian and vegan options on the menu also. We like to sit out on the patio where there is a good view of the happenings of Magazine St.

I know you are thinking...why 3 stars?  There is always a wait to get in any of the locations, especially this one.  It doesn't matter ..any day that ends in Y..you are going to have to wait to be seated!!  I think the establishment is good, the service is usually average and the food is good too.  I am usually a weekender or Brunch goer , but a few locations are near where I work & train..so I will try & pop in at lunch.  I feel that if you wanna try it..go at lunch & do 'take-out'.  You will get an opportunity to sample some dishes and not have a long wait time.  

I feel that Philly has many great restaurants to choose from..so don't get caught up in the hype & try & force yourself to like it.  Take-out may neutralize some of those high expectations...

Went here with my gf a couple of days ago to try their crab for the first time. It was amazing! The flavor and the fullness in the meat of the pound of snow crab was awesome. Every piece was fresh and thick. We also had the gator bites and the mozzarella sticks as appetizers. They were also cooked to perfection and tasted great. This is a small restaurant on Gandy, and literally does feel like a "shack." It's got a great local feel and the servers were very friendly and helpful. No complaints here. Can't wait to eat there again!

Very good wood fired pizza, had the garlic knots which were huge so be careful when ordering !! I also had the garlic Parmesan and buffalo wings which were very crispy and arrived hot and stayed hot !!! The Woodfired pizza had sausage, mushrooms and peppers which was a great combo !!!! Crispy crust and plenty of toppings !!! I would highly recommend trying this restaurant also service was spot on !!!!

I really liked the ambience and coffee.  I dont eat a lot at once, so bite sized plates were perfect for me.  My friend and I enjoyed the service very much too.  It is such a cute place to be for a brunch.
Best. Pizza. Ever!!! New to town and ordered delivery and it was fast and super delicious! Also try the sea salt choc chip cookie... yum!

Popeye's is a great drive-thru style restaurant and it is tough to get this type of cuisine much better outside Louisiana. 

When's them crawfish comin'?
The place was clean, food was fresh, servings were generous and service was great. Nice alternative to the norm. We all had the Vietnamese selections. Great value. We will definitely return.

I've been going here steadily since I moved to the area the late 80s, and it's great to have a nearby place that serves reliably good Mexican food accompanied by a perfectly prepared Margarita. 

The updated menu has something for everyone, whether you're a boomer craving your favorite dish or a millennial foodie blogging the latest gustatory trends in South-of-the border cuisine. OK, maybe not the latter, but they do offer Poké Tostadas with Ahi tuna, avocado and chipotle crema--you get the idea. They even have special "gringo" tacos for resolutely old-school patrons. In this case I was in the latter camp, having been recently disappointed by a brand-new Mexican restaurant in Haddonfield (see my review of El Nopalito). So I went for my old standard combo platter: the Cancun, which is two tacos of any style, accompanied by an enchilada, refried beans and rice. Eschewing the malignant trend of wrapping everything in a soft shell, I instead opted for their delicately crispy corn tacos: one beef and one El Pastor (barbecued pork. In both cases the fillings were abundant and tasty, although the El Pastor was disappointingly dry.

We absolutely loved the dishes we ordered and really appreciated that the dessert portion of the menu has also been expanded. Churros were recently added and are just wonderful: a generous portion--freshly dredged out of the fryer--bursting with big, cinnamon-y taste. It was a fitting way to conclude a comfortable, familiar repast.

This is my first time ordering from this place, and it will be the last. Our order was placed at 615pm, and we were told it would take 40 minutes. I came in at 710 to pick up the food, and was told it would be another 15 minutes. There were 4 other people waiting on their orders, and all were told it would be another 15 minutes. I received my food at 750, 1 hour and 35 minutes after it the order was placed. The worse part of all this was there was no apology for the delay to any of the people who waited. Constant yelling could also be heard coming from the kitchen.

This is the first review I've written about a business, and I sat in my car after receiving my food to write this. 

Aside from that whole debacle, the one positive is that the place was clean. I haven't eaten the food yet, but if I don't write a follow up to this, you can assume it was good.

First thing, cash only. 

They have more than just donuts...brownies, etc. These donuts tho...yooooo...so good! My favorite was these blueberry cake. Soft, blueberry flavor in the middle that's bursting with flavor. The applesauce cake donut was amazing as well. I can only imagine getting these things fresh outta the oven!

As expected on an early Saturday afternoon the place was packed. Nevertheless, we were seated within 20 mins of getting on the waiting list. We had an awesome waiter by the name of Jason we had on a previous visit. 
We had our favorite appetizer the wild west shrimp. I rarely will eat spicy dishes but the spicy cherry peppers and garlic butter paired with housemade ranch dressing balances out the heat making this an enjoyable appetizer. I don't think I've ever had a bad experience with this dish. 
My 14 year old tried the prime rib. He was surprised  at the size of the fat "cap". once i trimmed it to his like he realized how succulent the meat was with a bit of the caramelized fat. I went with the 7 pepper steak salad. This dish was really good. The steak was cooked to a perfect medium rare. You would think with 7 varieties of pepper it would have a spicy taste to it but it was subtle pop that lingered a bit. My wife had the longhorn salmon on a bed of rice. As served it was good as is. She requested a side of butter garlic sauce which she used over her entire dish.  The salmon was seared to a nice crust and was flaky.  I was told it tasted as good as it looked.  Overall another great dinning experience.

My husband and I recently dined here and it was wonderful ! Everything was delicious including Filet Mignon au poivre , truffle fries ( a must at the Capital Grille ! ) , perfect mashed potatoes , etc... 
I wanted to try the generous pour and it was so worth it , delicious wines at a great price . 
But this review would not be complete without mentioning our server Mary - She was a joy , so warm and kind but a complete professional ! 
She made our night so special and fun - Thanks Mary and the staff at the Capital Grille for a wonderful evening ! 
Kevin and Tina M.
Love their crust. Crust is everything. You know it's good when a plain cheese pizza is satisfying. Love the atmosphere here too. Cool staff. I wished I lived close enough so I can get it delivered.

Found out about this place while browsing on Instagram. Really great presence on their page so needed to check it out! We walked from downtown and took about twenty minutes or so to get there. They're next to a brewery for now and had a spacious parking lot so I'm definitely driving next time. 
My girlfriend and I ordered the 3 smoked meat plate which included 2 sides. I would say it was enough for two people and their menu is pretty reasonably priced with a lot of different options to feed any type of foodie. I'm no expert with bbq but I definitely enjoyed the flavor of their food. The meat was moist and tender with their sauce complimenting the meat dish very well. The sides were also very delicious. I always have an impression that bbq is either too salty of lacks flavor but they knocked it out of the park with a great balance of flavor and taste. 5 stars 5 stars for them! 
P.S. they are also close to the dog park so there was a lot of cute dogs around the area :)

People reviewing this are buying into unnecessary hype. Overpriced, snooty employees, and mediocre food. 10$+ for a tiny piece of toast with avocado smeared on top? The food is average - the Acai bowl wasn't made correctly either and had the wrong consistency. People really buy into unnecessary hype. No combinations that are inventive or new.

When you first walk-in you are greeted right away by staff behind the counter. Great first impression for me. 

As I walk into the far back counter where you place your order, the aromatic smell of delicious Mediterranean food follows you. Every time I have come in here, I've seen the same 2 friendly faces. One takes the order and the other prepares your food. This location used to be Pita-Pit that served customized wraps so the prep area is pretty similar. With this said, whatever you decided on having will be prepared right then and there.

I grew up in the Philippines and surprisingly Shawarmas were quite popular there. So my very first visit, I ordered the Chicken Shawarma Wrap. Flavors were on point and the fresh veggies, garlic sauce and tahini made the wrap super tasty. I particularly enjoyed the side of vegetables that came with this. It was a cucumber and tomato type salad. The only thing that I was a little disappointed about was the actual pita wrap just broke into many pieces and was not able to properly eat my wrap as it should be. Not a big deal but if the restaurant is called "Wrap" It Up, I would expect a great wrap. Ever since then, I haven't ordered another wrap and instead opted for the platters. The platters are well worth your money. I have never actually finished an entire platter before because of how much food is given to you. The potatoes are seasoned well, and they practically melt in your mouth. The basmati rice is mind blowing. Cooked to perfection every time I come.

There is nothing special about the dining room area, typical tables and chairs with a soda fountain machine for refills. But this isn't a big deal to me. As long as the food is great and the dining room area is clean then I'm all about it. Not to mention the friendly customer service.

So really, my only flaw about this place is the pita wrap not holding up to its capacity. Like I said, I haven't tried the wrap again so maybe they have improved on this. Oh man... now that I'm talking about this -- I think that's where I'm going for lunch. I will brave this one out and order the wrap! What a great idea! This review might be updated pretty quickly depending on how this trip goes. Oh Wrap It Up -- Here I come!!!

From a person who has lived in Thailand this was by far the worst example of thai food in the US. The rice in both dishes was over cooked and mushy. The vegetable stir fry tasted like it was from a bag of frozen food. Both the pork and chicken were over cooked and chewy. To top it off the water tasted extremely metallic. I would never recommend this to anyone.

Oh my.. what can I say about Heidelberg Haus that probably hasn't already been said. This is THE GEM of the north east side for me. It's been there for over 30 plus years and obviously there is a definite reason they have been around so long. The pastries are all to die for. And so fresh. The selection is out of this world. The breads are just delicious and I can't help but to take some home with me EVERY time I visit. Their food selection of German items are all wonderful. I have never had a single thing I didn't like at Heidelberg Haus. And for me that is VERY rare indeed. They also have the LARGEST selection of gifts and novelties it takes an hour or two just to see it all. This place is very near and dear to my heart. It's been around forever and I sincerely hope it will remain here for years to come. It has become a bonding place that my teenage daughters and I like to frequent. We are always treated very well and made to feel welcome and completely comfortable. My only complaint is that if I go there more than once a month I'll pack on about ten pounds because when it come to their pastries and cakes I have ABSOLUTELY no self control. But I'm ok with that. People come from all over the state and as well as all over the country just to see this iconic establishment. Make sure you are one of those people. If you haven't done so yet then good lord what are you waiting for!? And sign the guest book by the front door to commemorate your stop in! :)

So...wow!   Started with Lemon Ricotta.  Citrusy and creamy on grainy bread.  Excellent.  Lasagna different from any other with Citrus Cream and Veal Ragout.  Then Chicken Marsala never before seen.  Side carrots and beets  perfectly done.  Dessert Apple Slab and Ice Cream Sandwich were fresh and homemade.  Perfect wine pairing with Pinot Grigio    As for the staff, the friendliest and most helpful I've come across.  Kudos to Tim and Jacob.

Wonderfully cheap and decent sushi. The restaurant isn't the prettiest, but this place is still awesome. You can get the dinner special with three rolls (18 pieces) , miso soup and a side item for 10 bucks. I normally get tempura vegetables. I definitely recommend. Get take out!
