I'm confident this will be a lively place to spend an evening meal most nights & am looking forward to coming back when the weather warms.

Yes, I am giving a fast food restaurant 4 star, in fact 4.5 star.

Seriously how could Popeyes in New Orleans be soooo good?!

Their Cajun fries have this delicious peppery taste, after adding their in-house hot spice, OMG that just turned sooo good. Their chicken was not overly fried either, perfect for my craving.

Servers were extremely nice... HELLO, southern people! I love your kindnes.

Conclusion: I love New Orleans' Popeyes. =D

My date and I dined in The Little Lion Sunday 7/9/17 and while the food was good the service was horrible. We arrived around 4:15 and did not receive our drinks until 5pm and food until 5:20pm. Our waiter forgot to input our order and when asked by the manager how was everything we expressed our disappointment and was told we would be "taken care of". We received a random free dessert, not of our choice, which we did not eat as my date is allergic to chocolate. Unfortunately, we spent most of our date expressing to each other how hungry we were and how long the drinks/food were taking. Overall experience was not good and the manager made it worse by offering a dessert that we could not even enjoy. I am not sure that I will be back. Very disappointing experience with the service we received.

Went here on a date and ordered sushi. They waitress said they were running behind because they ran out of rice and needed to make more??? Thought this was bizarre! When my rolls finally came out the presentation was awful and the taste was even worse! Worst sushi experience of my life! I also had crab dip and a Cesar salad as apps and both were very sub par. Wouldn't recommend this place to anyone and will never go back!

I didn't try Pat's or Geno's due to the poor reviews.  Service was fairly quick and friendly.  It was busy prior to a Flyers game.  I had the standard cheesesteak with american and it was really fresh, hot and good.  Pickles at the side stand were good also.  Had a terrible time trying to catch a cab back to my hotel after being dropped off.  It's in the middle of nowhere.  Be sure to plan ahead if cabbing it.
I saw they were open till 9:pm. Went there before 6 and they were closed. Very dissapointed in that they didn't change their hours on this website. Wasted gas and time

What a delight to find fabulous vegetarian options at a Cajun/creole place. They had at least 3 or 4 options to choose from. I thoroughly enjoyed my spinach and mushroom étouffée. The hot sauces on the side bar were a fun add-on. We were just stopping through sadly, otherwise I would be a regular.

Loved the atmosphere in here. Had to try the Peanut Butter burger on a dare. Not for me - but I see the appeal. Staff is friendly, almost a cheers-y vibe. Will definitely be back to try the rest of the menu. GREAT hurricane by the way!!
Great options for vegetarians, and I especially love their hot sauce! Friendly staff as well.

Solid three-star chain restaurant. I used to enjoy the Jamaican black pepper shrimp, but this iteration was only marginally preferable to hunger. The sauce was too sweet; no spices stood out. The black beans were dry, and the food was lukewarm when served. Service was great, drinks were good, and the tiramisu cake I took to go was solid, but I have no reason to come back for anything except their desserts.

The burgers are great. Bubbly and sassy bartender(forgot her name). A buddy and myself were cross country road trippin and this is a great divey little bar to relAx for an afternoon. Eat. Drink. Be merry.
The sauce on the pizza is always scarce to non-existent... even when you ask for extra. Its like there is just bread and cheese.

This place was amazing.  First time here but will most def be back. Staff friendly and food was just what I needed.  The sushi and noodle bowls were delish. Easy to find location, food was more than enough and very fresh.

The fiance and I went there for a late dinner on the recommendation of the employees of Buck's Coffeehouse.  I'm very glad as asked for their recommendation as the atmosphere was just what we were looking for, small but not too small and about as classic of a neighborhood bar as you could get.  

Service was friendly but not over the top and the food was excellent.  I picked the special sweet italian sausage with cheesy risotto and roasted peppers and it tasted even better than it sounded.  

All in all a great little place in a cool little town, we will be back.

This is one of the most unique places in Tucson! A beer & wine garden with food trucks in the parking lot! And right at the base of the Catalina Mountains. They have a wonderful variety of beers and wines, so you are sure to find something that you like. And the outdoor seating is great for small groups of friends or family to gather and enjoy our beautiful Tucson sunsets. Check out their Facebook page to find out what food trucks will be there each day. It will take me several dozen visits to try all of the beers that they offer! Can't wait!

So we were the first customer of the day with one person behind us. We ordered the chipotle chicken quesadilla, roasted poblano quesadilla without pico, a kids chicken taco, and kids quesadilla. Roughly 30 minutes later, we got our food... some of it... and my wife's had pico. 
They took back my wife's to redo it. I also had to go ask again for the guacamole and sour cream I had paid for. About 5 minutes later, the food rearrived, as well as my daughter's taco. 
My chipotle chicken was more like a salted Dobie sponge with not even a hint of chipotle. At least the guacamole was good. My wife's roasted poblano may have seen a roast once, but it was not. 
After this meal, I feel terrible, because this was our last lunch date for the summer. From now on, we'll stick with Mercado.

Came for the lakeside dining, beautiful evening. Apps were great (caprese, shrimp cocktail & long hots). Club music from tiki bar totally ruined the ambiance (let's talk about sex by salt n pepa, and s&m by Rihanna at 7:30p? Cmon). My husband ordered a steak & subbed risotto for mashed potatoes. Steak came out with the potatoes, server offered to bring out a side of risotto to fix it. When she came out with it, she asked for the potatoes back!!! I was FLOORED! She proceeded to scrape the mashed potatoes off his plate from under his steak!!! She said the cook asked her to. I was mortified, it was so awkward. And I felt bad for her, she's young and could tell she was uncomfortable doing it. That aside, entree portions were very small. I live 4.5 miles away & will not be returning anytime soon. UPDATE: as we were leaving, we recounted this to the hostess who said she'd get the manager. Our server then came out & in so many words admitted she lied about the chef story, and that she didn't know what to do about her mistake. This only compounded the awkwardness & now I really have no desire to return.
A hipster coffee shop in the beautiful Germantown neighborhood. Interesting offerings. Small parking lot in the rear. A good stop while exploring the place walking.

From service to decor to the food & drinks, you can't lose!
Likes: efficient seating and excellent service (very knowledgeable on menu), haunted??, bar tucked away in the back yet near skylight, pictures/photos and other antique decor, upstairs secret??
Dislikes: none
Return for: the Stuffed Mirliton, well-priced Pinot Grigio, and Etouffee

Great Happy Hour Spot!
Work outing - about 12 of us! 

We tried several items on the HH Menu! 
My two favorites are the hummus and pimento cheese.

The Bourbon Smash was excellent! 

Staff was friendly, but a super smarty pants. I think he was trying to be funny, but it didn't carry well.

Everything was fresh and had flavor. 
Pretty fast service - look forward to going back for dinner!
I've been here at least twice.  The food is average and the service ok.  They have a lot of different salsas, which is nice.  There is an area of outdoor seating that overlooks the highway.

Really awesome daquiries- not too sweet, and just "adult" enough. The food I have tried so far(it's a pretty extensive menu) has been spot on. In an age of the $16 lunch menu, I'm happy to have an affordable and delicious place in the neighborhood. PLUS THEY WILL DELIVER DAQUIRIES. This place might become a fiver soon...

Protip- the mix for the house special seems to change depending on who's working at the moment. I think the best one is way the owner makes it
My new favorite breakfast place. Blu's eggs are amazing and the coffee is very good.
This place is amazing! We tried all the ceviche and they were to die for. The combination of the flavors were so tastey! I was so impressed, we will definitely go here again!

We had a large party. The blonde manger on duty came off very rude to my family. The food was just okay. I had the wings, they were at least hot but the BBQ sauce just weak. The tater tots were barely warm. I wouldn't come back based on the level of service my family received from the manger. Our server was great for such a large party.

Well I am mixed on how I see this place ....  The meal was good as I got a 3 meat #6 dressed, with an order of fries and onion rings and a large drink for like $13 w/tax .... The hamburger was cooked right but they forgot to add my cheese

Both french fries & onion rings are extremely small no more than a handful in each bag but tasted well 

Soft drink was very thin almost watered down and the ice cubes tasted like atomized fryer oil taste 

Really minor things to fix

Went for the Happy hour after friends had highly recommended Luke. We were in town for a cruise so we flew in a couple days early. From the airport after flying for 14 hours we checked into our hotel and then bee lined it to Luke before happy hour finished. The bar was packed, but luckily a table for 2 opened up and we were seated with 45 min left. We started with 1 doz baked, 2 doz raw oysters, and a couple glasses of champagne. Baked arrived first and my wife was in heaven (she doesn't care for the raw ones) next the raw, these are plump  med. size gulf oysters, fresh as can be, simply wonderful !! We were going to order a bottle of the same champagne at the same time as I was ordering another 2 doz raw, but our waiter informed us that it was cheaper to order by the glass during happy hour. With 15 min left I got a call from my 82 y/o mother who had also just arrived in town with her 3 friends. I asked if she wanted some oysters and of course she said yes. Our waiter was great, after informing him that we needed  another 4 doz  raw for my mom and her friends he cleared a table next to us even though happy hour was almost over. All of us had a great time, the service, food, drinks, and atmosphere was as advertised and then some. The next day my wife and I decided to go back and we were seated at the same table. The manager recognized us and came over to chat, commenting that he had just seen us at the same table 23 hrs ago. NOLA has a lot of great restaurants and happy hours  to choose from and we think Luke  should definitely be high on your list to experience.

While our waiter was attentive and apologetic for our poor experience, this Applebee's needs to step up their game. Our order consisted of $85 of alcohol, apps and steaks all ordered rare. It took over an hour and 15 minutes for our steaks to be delivered. All were overdone; brown in color and tough to chew. The manager of the restaurant delivered new steaks and asked us if "these was better?" The 2nd steaks were an identical copy to the 1st steaks. We stated to the manager "no, these are still overdone." The manager then stated "So, that color of red is not to your liking?" At this point, we were frustrated with the rude comment but agreed to keep the 2nd steaks as we were hungry and it was getting late. We then requested the check. An $8 discount was applied to the bill. However, given the experience, we stated that we felt the discount was unfair. The manager came over and stated "Oh, so my discount not high enough for you?" We were appalled by the comment; it was distasteful to say the least! I strongly feel the manager should have handled every part of our experience differently. She should be able to recognize issues within the kitchen. Also, speak to your customers with respect! The comment: "Oh, so my discount not high enough for you?" really sent me over the edge and left such a sour taste in my mouth. Finally, if any part of the experience is poor, the manager should provide an apology. Were in no rush to come back, plenty of restaurants worth visiting for better service.

Hole in the wall gem! We both had the prime rib special and it was delicious. Great portions! Service was excellent. We were basically the only ones in there so it was a nice, romantic evening. The wine list could be more comprehensive and we should have been given steak knives, but those are my only recommendations. We would absolutely go back.

I went here for the first time with my husband to celebrate his birthday & it was amazing! We've both never been to a Brazilian steak house before so it was different & worth the money. Everything about the set up, the food, the drinks we ordered & the staff was perfect. I will definitely recommend.

I love love love this coffee place! Thank lighthouse coffee for that delicious caramilla drink. My new favorite. I usually go to the human bean but not anymore. This local business right here is the one to support. The staff is always so friendly to me, drinks are usually fast, and reasonably priced. I love that they have the loyalty program so make sure you ask for a stamp card if you like to go here often. Everything I have tried so far is absolutely delicious. Green tea matcha shake is one to try as well. I don't think you will be disapointed. I have not tried any hot drinks but I know one thing they definitely got my business.

After previously posting a bad review where we actually didn't get to eat, Nino the manager contacted us and made everything right. On top of that the food and service were excellent. Everything was very creative and made with fresh ingredients, definitely not your typical dinner place in Brandon. The atmosphere while modern is comfortable with a touch of organic old world.  Our waiter Roberto and the rest of the staff were on top of things and we didn't want for anything.  Nino was actively working with the staff and his high standards really show through. We will definitely be back soon.

Cochon--I couldn't pronounce it let alone know what it was. Sure glad I found out. Amusingly, cochon appears to have a negative connotation in French (http://dictionary.reverso.net/french-english/cochon), but I can tell you it is all positive in New Orleans!

We randomly happened upon this fantastic restaurant. How we got in without a reservation is unclear to me--lucky, I guess. Cute atmosphere that is rustic and elegant all at the same time. Small bar up front and a chef's table in the back that overlooks the open kitchen. Service was fantastic (there were a few folks tending to our table), yet casual and unintrusive. We started with the joy juice, which was a dangerously delicious moonshine-containing cocktail. I also sampled another orangey-bourbon cocktail that was quite tasty. They have an interesting bourbon list here, including flights, that I would definitely go for if I returned.

For food, I started with the crab-artichoke app. I LOVE blue crab, and this mix with tasty artichoke served in the top of a cleaned-out crab shell was fantastic! One of my companions got the alligator app, which I sampled--more breading/hot sauce than gator, but quite tasty all the same. For an entree I got the namesake cochon--deliciously spiced pulled-pork shaped into a patty and deep-fried; simply wonderful. Sides were tasty as well, with turnips, cabbage, and, of course, cracklins! Others got the ham hock and the brisket, both of which looked fantastic, and all were pleased with the offerings. I was very tempted by the oyster and bacon sandwich and it is definitely on my list for a return visit.

Unfortunately, I was too full for dessert, because if the rest of the meal was any indication, I am sure it would have been fantastic. Definitely a place to check out if you are in NO, and I would recommend this over the potentially more famous restaurant just down the street.

My experience at this location was terrible. I came on a Saturday at 8:30pm. There were 7 of us at the table. The waitress took about 15 minutes to come to the table and take our drink orders, which she did not bring out until the food came. Food? What food? They completely forgot to put my order in and when I was asked if I still wanted it the waitress replied "OK AWESOME!!" when I said "don't worry about it." Very annoying. Those who got food reported the food was OK. The watermelon margaritas apparently tasted peppery.

This place has great service and food
We had no idea if they were open or not so I called them and they welcomed us in before opening:) 
Very attentive and the food was tasty. We had the Panang curry with chicken and white rice and the Radna with chicken. Also some refreshing Thai iced tea 
It was our first time there and will definitely go back again.
Really good simple sandwiches that taste fresh. Their fries are outstanding with great daily soup options. We like to stop here on our way to Lucky Peak Reservoir.
Literally our fav place to go. Monica and Dom are the best bartenders there and we always have a good time! Recommend 100%!

My sister and I couldn't hang with the crazy deep line for brunch across the street at BL so we popped in to see what The Pub had to offer. Solid brunch menu and Smithwicks on tap. The Hangover Cure Bowl is a must. Really cool decor and fancy furniture that gives the place an authentic traditional pub feel. The place really opens up in the back with an area for darts and lots of standing tables and booths. Will definitely come back for their Happy Hour and beer cheese and pretzels

If you're in philly for work or play, you must come here. My coworker recommended it and explained that it's very well-known because of the Rocky movie. That wasn't enough to get me in the door, however, until he mentioned that every 15 minutes the waiters and waitresses take turns belting out opera songs in the dining area. SOLD!

The 4 of us arrived and were seated at a table in the main dining area. We ordered wine and calamari to start, followed by 3 pasta entrees to share. It wasn't the best italian food I've had, but the charming interior and opera-singing waitstaff made this one dinner I won't forget.

The decor is modern & fun. 
The service is prompt & attentive.
Here is a breakdown of what we ordered:
Diver Scallop - literally one scallop cut up & mixed w mostly pear, great flavors but tiny appetizer portion
Soft shell crab appetizer- delicious, perfectly cooked & nice size
Toro tartar- tiny size & filled with crunch filler, minimal caviar topping 
Eel fore gras appetizer - great flavors very rich & flavorful 
Wagu dumplings - very tasty if you like beef, tastes like comfort food
Duck entree - amazing! One of the best duck dishes I have ever had! 
Overall it was a nice experience, I would skip the scallop & toro tartar app because they were not great. Everything else was very tasty, perfect prep & presentation.

I've driven past this place a million times before finally trying it out.  And now I'm sad thinking of the million sonoran dogs I've missed out on.  They were great!  And food is cheap!

What is it about this style of Mexican food that makes it so cheap?  I spend more for less at Taco Bell and El Nene is far superior, I know it goes without saying.  Maybe that's a bad comparison but I think you get my point.  A few bucks here gets you a full belly of great Mexican food.  I can't wait to get back and try something different.

Ordered chicken wings and a small pizza. 3 wings out of the 20 were eaten when i opened the box. Frozen pizza at walmart will taste better than this garbage. Waited 1.5hrs for my order. All the sauces for my wings came spilled. Wings are the size of a baby carrot, dry as fuck. My order was only 28 but when he got here it was somehow 38. If you are staying at the Embassy hotel near nashville aiport, dont order from this garbage. Just go down staira and order food from the restaurant. Cleaner and alot cheaper than this bullshit. Stay away

I've been here several times. I gotta say all the ramen choices I've had are very good. Each ramen has different styles of noodles and broth default to them, and there is a rather wide combination of broths, noodles, toppings, etc. For a restaurant that is known for ramen there are a lot of opportunities for customization. I like the whole kernel sesame seed grinder and white pepper at every table, because I like a spicier nuttier flavor. Be advised though that the sesame seed oil is very potent, and I generally stay away from it. It's just a great place. Especially in the Fall and Winter.
I'd give it 6 stars if I could, the breakfast sazerac was the best sazerac I've had (and I've had a few). The lamb meatloaf was amazing, would definitely eat here again!

Out of the chain neighborhood style restaurants 54th has always been my favorite.  My last visit was definitely not up to par.  We went in specifically for the stuffed shrooms.  They were out of shrooms and calamari.  Very disappointing.  We ordered appetizers, salads and entrees.  All of the food was delivered at the same time with one of the appetizers delivered a few minutes after all the other food.  To make matters worse all the fries and one sandwich was cold.  I ordered a large salad and received a side salad.  The waitress was new and very uninformed.  She was extremely pleasant and learned more from us than whoever trained her.  It will be a while before I return to 54th st and it will not be this location.

This place is quite good and it better be, considering the well known and overpriced place about a mile north of there on the same highway.  Reasonable prices, very good food and an amazingly friendly atmosphere.  Only issue is the parking but we noticed valet parking when we went this past Sunday.  Please please please keep up the great work!

There's a lot to like about this tiny Korean kitchen on South Street. The simple menu, fair prices, and the fact that there just aren't a whole lot of Korean spots in South Philly. 

I really want to give BAP four stars but I can't just yet. I love bibimbap and the beef bibimbap here was alright. The beef was good, flavorful and tender. I've never seen broccoli in bibimbap before, which was fine. I just wish the portions were a little bigger; I was still hungry afterwards. And I think more veggies would've made it better. I'd like to come back to try the japchae and I would give the bibimbap another chance.
POOR CUSTOMER SERVICE & HORRIBLE COFFEE!! Owner was very rude and had an attitude for no reason. When I told her I would not return because of the poor customer service she said that was fine.

Absolutely horrible experience here. Multiple times we have gone and waiting in the drive through line for 20 minutes just to be told they're taking cash only when we get to the window. Not complaining about that but they should really let someone know that BEFORE the wait. Also on multiple experiences the food has been cold, forgetting items, soggy fries. I know its fast food so it already has a low standard but this Wendy's doesn't even meet that. Truly not a good experience they're lucky they are the only Wendy's in the area or else I would be going somewhere else.

My word.  The shrimp and grits were amazing.  I wouldn't recommend leaving without trying them.  The country fried steak Benedict was a close second choice but it wasn't as amazing.  I'd recommend getting a pitcher of Bloody Mary and spend the morning sampling the best dishes.

Don't go. Weird smell when you walk in the door.  Should have just left when I walked in, but ate there anyways.  Bad mistake.  Horrible food and service.  Went there because of the reviews, but they must have been done by their friends.
The food was good and the service was kinda of okay.The place was not very busy but the food took a long time to come out.

My review: from the waitress short responses and attitude to the order being wrong, not cooked, or cold/room temperature, forgetting an item until after the food comes and waitress is reminded.... to explain our experience to the gentleman checking us out and him shrugging his shoulders, taking our ticket and telling us the cost. I'm like really? Why rude? Why not apologize? Say sorry? Idk... something?

1st time: was good food about a year ago. This time so not a good experience that I don't ever wanna go back or give it another try just in case it was just a total off day for I don't know... everyone that worked there?

My tip... DO NOT GO
Large place overlooking the water. Relaxing atmosphere with sports on TVs. Next to Westin so I ate dinner and lunch here. Good food both times.

Lovvveeee Royal. They have the best vegan options around! I frequent Royal and have never had bad service or meal. 

Highly recommend the soba noodle salad and the tempeh club. Make sure you get some tater tots with vegan mayo on the side.

Had dinner here with several friends. For appetizers we enjoyed the Kale Tempura, Edamame and Shrimp Tempura.For dinner, we shared the Mexican Roll, Rainbow Roll, the Yummy Spicy Roll (wrapped in cucumber!!) and Tampa Roll. Everything was super fresh. The flavored Saki (peach and apple) were delicious and our favorites. Topped off with Friendly and fast service. We will definitely be back!

We've been coming here for breakfast on Sunday mornings for over 20 years. Large portions of excellent food at great prices? What's not to love? We travel a fair bit and this place has the best pancakes and coffee anywhere. My go-to hangover cure is their biscuits and gravy. Mmmm! The only thing that would make Kissin Cuzzins more perfect is if they served home fries. (I'm not a hashbrown fan although the hashbrown casserole is the bomb!)

Used to be really good !! Used to recommend people to go there but now I feel awful for talking about this place. It's just regular now. Nothing special. Foods were just ok.  loved their Pho and service at one point but will not go back anymore.  Couldn't find the server to ask for utensils. Didn't have the usual hot oil peppers among others at our table. Then once again couldn't find the service so we had to get up and go to the register and ask for one. The portions of foods itself was terrible.  Then when it was time to leave, the gave us a soup container  to pack our left over rice and stir fried chicken in. Yeah. That bad!! We are not planning on going back! Totally not worth it.

Well the wait was incredibly long [30 min longer than they said]. The food was avg at best! The portions were ok, nothing special, there was nothing on the menu that did not have a new age twist to it; in other words not authentic cajun/creole food!

Food was pretty good service was good too. I come here a lot of the time for mexican food and have never had a problem. My roommate says the seafood fajita was over powered by need flavor. But I said who gets seafood fajitas ha. Well that's it for now
This is my favorite place to get food in town. Good beer prices and great food the dragon fingers are awesome!

I was in the area late night and was craving for some Latino fast food. This place stays open quite late and they serve variety of foods including both fast food and actual healthy food. Food tasted good and servers were very nice and attentive

My wife and I came in for a date night. We were immediately greeted with multiple staff members. They have a wide variety of wine, liquor, and beer. We tried a couple of their speedily cocktails and they were phenomenal. We had a fantastic experience and will definitely be back. If you are looking for the perfect date night or celebration I couldn't recommend more.

Such a cool restaurant! We were not intending on coming here one Saturday night but everything else in the area had over an hour wait. You walk in and immediately catch the "old church vibe." Kind of weird at first but then it's fine after your first drink. Some ordered beer to drink and others ordered the chocolate cherry martini (yum!). We were able to get seated and served immediately.

We would recommend starting with the Artisanal Charcuterie & Cheese Plate and Cheddar Cheese & Ale Fondue as apps. SAVE THE REST OF THE CHEESE FONDUE for yours fries that come with your entree! SOOO GOOD! Thank me later for that tip.

All and all this place was kind of cool. It was nice to have dinner in a different environment than the typical downtown restaurant. I would definitely come back. I posted pictures of what we ordered!

This was the absolute WORST sushi I have ever had. Normally I absolutely love sushi and trying new sushi restaurants. So I had a very open mind.... until the food came out. The miso soup tasted like dishwater; no green, no pieces of tofu, just powdery water. Then my shrimp tempura roll was chewy and fell apart at the touch. It even tasted like it had been sitting out for a while. My boyfriend had similar opinions about his own food so we called over the server to tell him. I started off by telling him that I am a server myself and wasn't trying to be a dick, I simply wanted to express my frustration. I carefully explained what was wrong with each item and asked him to take it back. Keep in mind me and my boyfriend only took one bite each of our two rolls, along with 1/3 of the crab rangoon. Despite this however, the server came back and said he would still charge us "regular" price, $26, including the two rolls and appetizers. My boyfriend rebutted by saying the only thing he wanted to pay for was the crab Rangoon since we didn't eat any of the rest. The server took the receipt back to the manager to see what he could do. He returned moments later and said he could only take half off of all the items except the crab Rangoon and maki (which I barely touched), making the total $16 dollars. He justified this by saying we had "eaten" the other items, even though as mentioned before we had only tried a few pieces. Since after all how is one supposed to tell if something tastes bad without trying it? I have never written a review of any restaurant/ establishment before but sine this was the worst food related experience I have ever had, I felt compelled to do so. I would not recommend going here. Save your stomach and your wallet the pain and grab dinner ANYWHERE else.

II have been to Drake's a couple of times.  It's your classic sports bar.  It's a little too trendy for me, but I do like their food and the service has been very good.

I mostly go there when somebody I am dining with says they want sushi.  Despite over 10 years and dozens of attempts, I have not acquired the taste for sushi.  Drake's has a very large sushi menu, but also have burgers and chicken; go figure.  So Drake's is a good choice for sushi lovers and non-sushi lovers.  I will put a plug in for their sushi, at least the Ragoon Roll.  It was by far the best sushi I have ever had.  I'm sure that purists would not call it sushi since it is battered, deep fried and comes with awesome sweet chili sauce.  To each their own.

For the last 15 years, I've met a friend in Reno and stayed at the Silver Legacy.  The room prices were always acceptable, particularly with a Players Club Card, typically around $300 for a Thursday-Saturday 3 night stay (basic room with 2 queen beds). This year, the price has more than doubled to over $700 dollars, and not because of any special events.  This seems to have coincided with the ElDorado purchase of Silver Legacy.  At the Peppermill, which is in many ways nicer than Silver Legacy, my price is $335.00 for the 3 nights.  It's a no brainer, I will never return to the Silver Legacy as long as they maintain these inflated room prices.

Not a fan.  The fajitas were bland and the steak seemed as though it were steamed not grilled or even sautéed.  The tamales weren't good either. Very thick masa and dry pork.  

I wouldn't recommend it.

Pretty much once a month (or more) I crave pizza that I am either too lazy or too unskilled to make. I love making my own basil/mozzarella/red sauce pizza...but sometimes I want a pie that has a little flair.

There's newer pizza places in Indy and Carmel that someday I just might try...but for now, I'm perfectly content with Puccini's down the street.

When we go, it's always busy (dine in and carry out) but the staff never seems frazzled. Their newish bleu cheese wedge is fabulous, they have an ok beer/wine menu, and though we've never had their pastas...they look incredible.

As for pizzas, we pretty consistently order the Campfire (onion marmalade -- I could drink you), but the Veg Head is yummy, too!

They have calzones and a daily lunch special.

Fantastic beer list with a lot of local brews, great way to get a taste of Pennsylvania flavor if you're passing through the area. Even through the hell of Thanksgiving weekend, the bartenders remained cheery and made my long layover a little more relaxing. Beware that the kitchen closes at 10pm. I arrived just after 10 and they were so nice to get me some fries anyway. Unfortunately, the service was slow and the staff wasn't too attentive, despite their happy demeanor.

Happy Hour at R2L is where it's at - bites, beverages, and beautiful views make it worth a visit. I was pleasantly surprised it wasn't very busy, it feels like a crime that more people don't take advantage of a cocktail in the sky after a stressful day of work. There's no cover charge, no crazy rules - just come as you are and enjoy strong drinks from 4:30-6:30pm.

They offer happy hour dishes ranging from $2-10, beers for $4, wine for $7, and cocktails for $8. The food isn't mind blowing, but the drinks are strong and the crowd is fun and laidback. We tasted the fingerling potatoes, the flatbread, and the lobster mac 'n cheese. The lobster mac 'n cheese was VERY tasty, but for $10, you get a 2"x2" square dish sampler. I get it - it's lobster - but $10 for the amount you get is laughable. It looks like a condiment dish. The flatbread and potatoes were subpar and forgettable. I wouldn't order them again. 

The highlight of my visit was the sunset views of the city and the strong, delicious gin happy hour cocktail, the elevation. I had two over the span of two hours, and I was nearly falling out of my chair. 

R2L is a nice change of pace from the packed dives during center city happy hour. I'd be keen to come back for a different taste of their food and cocktail offerings.

Philadelphia isn't New York. I know in Philly I'm not going to find Ethiopian delivery at 4am. However, I've expected to find a suitable Dominican place - and until now, I really haven't.  Today, we found it. Parada Maimón is like any place in the DR you'd want to go after a day at the beach. Amazing seafood and all the typical Dominican food you'd want. It's BYOB, so bring your own Presidentes, but expect your fill of tostones, ceviches and chillo entero. ¡Que rico!
Finally a Greek restaurant with great ambiance and food! A new favorite in SB!
I ordered two separate chicken dishes to go. The food was ready in five minutes. In both cases the chicken was undercooked and near to being raw.

If you're looking for a cute neighborhood gem with good service and excellent Italian food, this is your place! Great outdoor seating with heat lanterns, easy to get to, free parking if you drive, and BYO to keep the cost in check! Cash only, tho...

3/4/17: Had an overpriced, bland, bacon, egg and cheese on a poppy seed bagel. 
Will not return.

We haven't been here in over a year due to COVID-19. Don't let the small parking lot dissuade you. Park across the street at Pep Boys and you'll be seated right away. We went midweek so not sure about weekends. The food was out fast. It was hot and delicious. Loved my Jack Benny and the coffee was piping hot and strong. The manager came by twice! Great service too.

I hate coming to this McDonald's. I don't even order full meals, just cokes here and there. I am always waiting in line, seems like forever. Staff is not friendly. Needs work on service and putting FAST back into fast food..
I love this place! Great food, great beer, and great atmosphere!! Sitting outside on the patio is my favorite. This place is a little pricey but I have never had a bad plate of food from here.

I was glad to return to Jimmy  G.s for a nice fat & juicy cheese steak last weekend. I was really looking forward to this because they are the only restaurant that posted my Yelp review big & bold across the wall.
Sadly however Jimmy G' is not the same. My review is still there, as bold as ever, except now my review is wrong!  The only serve chopped up meat on their cheese steaks. I prefer my cheese steak layered with slices of beef, not chopped up like baby food. And the roll is different and  the feel & weight of their cheese steak feels smaller.
 What a big disappoint!

Service was friendly and the food was excellent. Best poutine ever and if you
Like hot,  Nashville fried chicken strips will not disappoint.

Awesome place, good food, good beer and Sprecher sodas, yum! The pretzel is huge and tasty. We had the shaggy Belgian, fried chicken sandwiches between sweet waffles with pork belly. Fried chicken sandwich is also good, sauce is spicy but good. You have to try this place. Oh and did I tell you, my husband is awesome!

I cannot count how many times I have been in this restaurant.  When I worked at IOH, it was a favorite lunch locale.  Now that I work downtown, I still stop in when I am shopping in the area.  The honey chipoltle crispers are a favorite, as is the El Presidente.  If you go for lunch, make sure you have a full hour or you will not have enough time.  Soup and salad lunch is highly reccommended, as well.  They have a new pay at your table service if you pay with your credit card, which is really convenient.
This place really knows how to make an out of towner feel at home. Great chicken and even better sauce! Many thanks to the owner for the stellar service and friendly face.

FINALLY a great salad in philly. ok, so a great salad in manayunk, but i'll take what i can get.  philly/center city is salad challenged and i think i just found the best salad place ever.  i had the version with figs and goat cheese and then added chicken.  amazing.  lots and lots of goat cheese, fresh spring mix and delicious sliced roast chicken.  they have my favorite kind of balsamic (it's emulsified so kind of creamy) and for people who can't eat bread the side of homemade potato chips is a good option.  i wish i lived in manayunk just to get their salads!
The pizza is obviously New York Style.  The sauce is super taste and the mozzarella has great snap. The pizza is consistently delicious and reasonably priced. Love it.

We went for late lunch today and had a very good meal at a very good price.  Our waitress was very attentive, also. The light jazz and Sinatraesque music playing was a refreshing twist from most of Nashville's eateri

Food was really good!  It was empty when we walked in, which scared us, but quickly people came in.  Boil was quick and good!

Added bonus!  10% discount for staying at the Hampton!
Cool atmosphere and awesome hamburgers!! Rosemary potatoes are good also. If your craving a hamburger like we were, you need to go.

Chili's use to be my favorite restaurant. Changing their menu was the worst thing they could have done. None of the food appears fresh but seems frozen and pre made. I have a sensitive digestive system and none of the food settles well with me now. I have tried going back 4 or 5 times hoping it would be better. It wasn't. I know refuse to eat there any longer. Too many other good restaurants around. Looking for Chili's to close soon. So sad.

This place is great! The food was great! The service was great! The place was packed and standing room only, the bar staff was so friendly and helped get us a table , our waitress  even tho extremely busy was AMAZING!  We went out for a  girls night and work at a barbershop close we will be sending all our clients your way!!!

They reopened up derived new management.. this was our 3rd time there. They have daily specials, which is a pretty good price, $7.95 for a plate, ice-tea and soup. Todays (Friday)special, they had Carne Asada with rice n beans, fried fish plate and 2 chicken enchiladas with rice n beans, all come with tea n soup. 

We both had the Carne asada plate but they let me substitute my rice n beans for a salad. Steak was pretty good. 

I think their specials are different everyday. So for the most part it was good all around. Oh service was good n attentive.

This is our favorite sushi place. Not just in Santa Barbara - anywhere. Bummer they don't take reservations, but you can always put your name on the list and get a cocktail at good lion while you wait. Everything is fresh and delicious, especially the specialty sashimi's and anything with bluefin tuna.

Great neighborhood spot with fresh soups and a winning serving team.  Personal favorite is the Senegalese Chicken & Peanut Stew.  Choose the white rice option and you have a great winter meal in a bowl!

Been waiting for our order for about an hour. I can already tell this will be my first and last visit here. Waiters are rude, throwing plates in your table. All the reviews are true. Bad service. These servers look like they dont even want to be here. They have 4 sushi chef and they're saying because we have a big party, we're the last to be served. Really?!

(This is a review of brunch at Silk City.)

Brunch reviews are always tough, because I am typically not exactly feeling topital when I arrive, and the food becomes a kind of medicine, which is hard to review.  "Made me feel better" isn't the kind of glowing review I want to leave on Yelp.

And so while this was not my first trip to Silk City for brunch, it is the first time I've been coherent enough to really enjoy the food and describe it afterwards!

I ordered the chicken and waffles.  But not just chicken and waffles.  Three big pieces of thick, juicy fried chicken, each sitting on a slab of chipotle waffle, smothered in sausage gravy.

Sweet little baby Jesus wearing a tuxedo was this an incredible dish.  Just a little bit sweet... and just a little bit spicy.  Comforting but different, flavors I love in a combination I've never had, filling but not to the point I felt like I had just made a huge mistake.  

Our waitress (I forget her name sadly) was also the best-equipped I have ever seen to handle a group of eight hung over people.  She was all business, and without being pushy got the eight of us to order quickly and efficiently.  We weren't so badly off on this particular morning, but even if we were I feel like she could have gotten us in line.  I was impressed.

I also tried the truffled creamed chipped beef, and it was delicious.  Absolutely worth getting.  But I don't know that I will ever be able to order anything besides the chicken and waffles.  It's one of those.  

Well played, Silk City.  Well played.

So we headed to Sam's at old hickory lake because I wanted my friend to try a Bushwhacker during our trip and I felt that Sam's did them right. Plus we were escaping the crazy crowds on Broadway over the holiday weekend (and I mean CRAZY). We sat at the bar and had very good (and friendly) service from the bartenders. We actually ordered 3 Bushwhackers as my friend really enjoyed his and wanted to try the one with the peanut butter whisky. We also ordered the spinach dip which was also very good (and filling). The Laker game was on during our little stint at the bar which made us feel right at home. Nice relaxing bar at the dock on the lake.

Another Amazing Breakfast. Excellent service from Debbie who is courteous, upbeat and provided extraordinary service.
The food was prepared fresh with culinary expertise you would expect at a fine dining establishment in this casual, clean comfortable setting. Very reasonably priced and I consider this place a hidden gem.
Everything today, like normal was prepared exactly as ordered and tasted great.

Ok so as I write this there are 300 other reviews. So ill keep it short and sweet (much like myself)

Just go!  If you get one of the 3 basic flavors they are made to order. My dad and I split a vanilla lavender and all I can say is YUM. The cinnamon and spice options smelled deadly too.  They also have fancy flavors that are pre-made. 

I'm glad I don't live in the neighbourhood. I could see coming here with my little Saturday mornings and enjoying a coffee and donut tradition!  

And $6 for a half doZen seems totally reasonable, especially after that first bite.  Yummmmmm

I love this place and the ambiance is great. They have recently lowered their standards and people dressed poorly can arrive; which is a downfall; however the wait staff is knowledgeable and the food is amazing. The price is reasonable when you consider other comparably priced restraints offer food a la Carr instead of all inclusive (salad, bread, soup + enter). My favorite cut of meat is the chateau briand. To top it all off you can end your night in the desert room, a cool experience.

Quite slow considering no one is in line. Not very friendly either. 

Employees were NOT wearing masks while making sandwiches. All their oral and nasal droplets are on my (yes and yours too) sandwich.  Tossed my food away and won't be coming back.

When i rate fast food it is based on how it stacks up to other chains in the brand.  This one is bad.  10 pieces in the 12 piece bucket and the following picture is one of them.  And no, no one took a bite of the chicken before we got it, or after for that matter.  Just an indication that the quality control is lacking.


As far as chains go, well it would be like rating a MCDonalds.  If you haven't had KFC before, you are not really missing out on good fried chicken.  But, it is a very famous fast food chain and i recommend trying it at least once in your life.  Just don't go to this one.
Had absolutely no selection!  Service was sub par!  Most of the food was disgusting!  Would never recommend this place!  Avoid at all cost!

Japanese spot with customizable poke bowls. Choose your base, protein and toppings. Most of the proteins will be raw seafood with the exception of the chicken option which of course is cooked. I tried spicy tuna, steam shrimp and spicy salmon with the spicy tuna being my favorite.

I have always wanted to experience CST (Cold Spring Tavern) for Valentine's Day dinner, ever since I moved up here, (SYV) four years ago. I called and made our reservation in December because I knew they would book out early, they always do. Got them in, and then they emailed me back to confirm.  Which I appreciated more than a phone call.  With my business, email is the best way to reach me.  In any case Thursday night was a night to remember, and definitely a great story.  We got there right at 7pm and we were seated right away, I was excited because I finally got to sit in the room with the big window, and at a big 4 top table, overlooking the other diners.  Right away the scene of the room before us was captivating, there was a couple immediately to the left of our table who couldn't keep their hands off each other, a nearing empty bottle of wine on the table, and in between giggles, she pants, "this is the most sexually charged dinner," and now I'm giggling because its Valentine's day after all, I would hope if you were taken, you were doing the same...  and if not, same applies. In any case, the rest of the blue haired diners were exchanging judging mc judgerson glances to the naughty table to our left. And I get it, there was definitely an age gap, and different standards.  So I grabbed an "awesome" card, and went over to them, and told them, I thought they were adorable and that, I hope my husband and I are just as loving when we are 30 yrs older... they smiled we introduced ourselves. They laughed and thanked me for the card. And immediately the gnarly tension was lifted, and the couple calmed down on their PDAs.  We had Marcos for our server.  He was hands down professional and super calm when dealing with all the challenges that arose later in the evening. He also smelled really good, for as much running around he did. He had all of the tables in our room, and not sure how many more outside in the other areas. But there were,  8 tables in our little room alone, I hope I'm painting a picture, it was slammed, but still romantic and cozy.  I ordered the lobster tail and mushroom risotto ($60), my husband ordered the duck ($48), and our friend settled into her 10oz of filet mignon ($50) each entree came with a choice of butternut squash soup or salad, and a dessert large enough to share, which was a frosted sugar cookie, a fruit custard tart with market fresh berries, and a chocolate covered strawberry, which by the way were amazing. My husband got the scallop potatoes, so I could try them, because mine came with risotto, I didn't get an additional side. Best scalloped potatoes I've ever eaten anywhere.  During our dining  experience a young skunk walked by was spooked and 'pepe le pewed' all over.  Now it got interesting because one woman to our left, (different couple, than the smoochers) got up out of her chair so fast she knocked glasses over, made a scene about the smell and stormed out of the room.  Her husband begrudgingly followed behind her.  The kitchen was next to us, so we started to smell delicious garlic, shallots and butter, over the already skunky smell.  It was such an interesting smell, and thing to witness.   But after about 20 mins the only thing we COULD smell was delicious food being prepared and the skunk smell diminished.  To me I wasn't bothered by the skunk because 
A) we were in the woods in HIS backyard
B) we were in a historical landmark bldg (zero insulation)
C) it's Valentine's Day, and now we have an adventurous story to share later...  

Thank you Cold Spring Tavern for an unforgettable evening and you exceeded my expectations, above and beyond excellent meal. Also the long stemmed rose was a really nice touch.

I just don't understand why they can't get an order correct. I gave them two chances on uber eats and every time they are missing multiple items and getting the order wrong. I dined in here a few times and the service is always slow and communication is horrible. I asked for a chocolate shake they bring chocolate milk. The food actually wasn't bad it was tasty but the staff is just incompetent. On one visit the staff was sweeping under our table hard and fast while we were eating I always thought that was disgusting and you shouldn't be sweeping while people are eating. I gave this restaurant so many chances but after my last few experiences I have to say I won't be back and I recommend people stay away from this diner. There are many better options in Tampa. this is the bottom of the barrel for diners.

Both times I've been at Champps the service was horrendous and the food is basic bar food. First I sat at the bar and the bartender was barely behind the bar the entire time. Second time I went, I sat at a table in hopes for better service. 

We sat at the table for many minutes before given our menus. When the waiter finally came over with them, he immediately asked for our beverage order. I was glancing at the beer menu but only ordered a water before deciding if I was going to get a beer. After ordering my water, the waiter asked for my ID. Very creeped out by this and the waiter seemed mad that I did not give him my ID. Convo below.

Me: I'll just have a water please
Waiter: Can I see your ID?
Me: For a water?
Waiter: Well you're looking at the beer menu. 
Me: But I don't even know if I'm ordering an alcoholic drink

First time I've ever gotten carded for a water.

This place has gone downhill. Used to come here a lot when I lived in the area. Came back tonight. Chicken and bread sticks were overdone and hard. I brought the bread back and asked for another order since these were hard. The manager said she would bring them out to me. 15 min later,no breadsticks. I asked again and waited another 5-6 min. Then I asked for them to go because we were done. She bagged them up. Got in car drive away. Opened bag and I have 2 more breadsticks that are hard and dripping with grease. Also got fries as a side. There were about 9 fries on my plate. Won't be back. A shame I really liked captain Ds and it's the only one around.

Didn't expect Bibou to live up to the hype.  Surprisingly it did.  Copious wine bottles in tow we arrived for our very early seating.  When Saturday reservations fill up a month in advance, you take what you can get.  Really small restaurant, almost Little Fish small, but sharp and tastefully decorated.  Free parking for 3 hours in the large lot directly adjacent to the restaurant is a suburbanite's wet dream.

Thanks to group dining I was able to sample the hen stuffed with foie gras, gravlax, escargots, and a melon salad special they had.  All the apps were good, but the escargot was the best of the bunch.  Deliciously savory combination of fava bean and mushroom flavors with great presentation in a snail-esque plate to boot.  I enjoyed the gravlax more than the rest, who found it slightly salty.  Strange, since I'm generally a stickler about saltiness myself.  Finely diced trout and jicama with a bit of roe and lavender mango vinaigrette made it a great dish in my book.

Got to try both the halibut and striped bass dishes.  The cut of halibut was larger than expected, a pretty solid chunk of moist, perfectly cooked fish.  It came over spinach with white coco bean and chorizo ragout.  It was delicious, but probably not their strongest offering.  Especially when compared to the striped bass, which was out of this world.  Perfect sear, set over well paired morel mushrooms and a surprisingly flavorful oregano beurre blanc.  Melding of flavors could not have been better.  And then there's the pea and bacon flan, just as amazing in its own right.  Bright green with a distinct bacon undertone, a wonderful side for the dish.

We split the cheese plate.  All three were great, especially the goat.  I liked the Roquefort more than usual.  I always eat 90% of this on a cheese plate because I'm the only one that likes it in any group I'm in, and by the end I generally have a bit of an unpleasant acid burn feeling on my tongue.  Not so with this one, and the flavor was just as good as any other so I applaud Bibou's selection.

Got the sorbets and chocolate trio for dessert.  Both were delicious so be sure to leave room.

Chef came out after our meal to ask how everything was, a nice touch.

I would say that Livery is one of my favorite top 5 restaurants in Indianapolis. The decor, the food, the atmosphere, the service, all top notch. I haven't had anything I didn't like here. I would say their Pork Pastor is one of my favorites, along with the Red Drum. You can't go wrong with any of their sides or desserts. Always leave room for their dessert! The flavor of all the food leaves your mouth full of flavor. I love their patio. Their drinks are good as well, and you don't feel bad spending money on them because they all are made well.

Love this place. The food is great but what really rocks are the employees. Ordered a gluten free pasta dish just because I like it better than regular, and bread on the side, and they double checked with me making sure it wasn't because of an allergy. It felt like they genuinely cared and it made my day. I will absolutely be back.

I really appreciate that they have tons of vegetarian and vegan food options on the menu. They even have a plant  sign next to those dishes so it's easy to find. 

The kimchee fries are so good! Various veggie rolls (the Lombard was our fave), tempura, side dishes and more.

I first tried this chain of restaurants when traveling out of town. I am so glad they have a site here now! Everything is good, but I recommend the Kobe meatloaf. The menu and drink variety is impressive however and you won't find a bad choice on the list. 

The service is always good but I am sure this location gets very busy so allow time to enjoy a drink at the bar while waiting for a table if visiting at a peak time.

Inviting atmosphere and live music. What more can you ask for.
The Clam Chowder was very good! Great service!

Their tacos are cheap, fast, and AMAZING! Coming from San Diego, I obviously know how great tacos can be and this place is right up to par! I honestly crave these tacos EVERY SINGLE WEEK. I've tried their beef, pork, cow head, cow cheek, cow tongue, and cow eye and they are all SO DELICIOUS! 

As I'm writing this review, my mouth is watering and I instantly have the urge to just leave my place and get some at this very moment!

We ate here on a recent trip to Philadelphia (for our anniversary). The good reviews both here & on Open Table made it an easy decision. Unfortunately, we left here completely underwhelmed by the food and annoyed by the service. 

I'll start with the service. If you've read any of my previous reviews, you know that service is incredibly important to me. Therefore, this is going to sound insane, but the service was *too* good. It was so good it was actually annoying. We couldn't go 30 seconds without someone coming by to check on us, including some random woman (she did work there, just no clue who she was) who wanted to talk for about 10 minutes about someone named Ashley's accomplishments. I don't know who Ashley is, or if she thought I was someone else, but it was odd & uncomfortable. I put in the notes when making the reservation that it was our anniversary. Considering they had special menus printed with our names & dates, they knew it was our anniversary. I wanted to enjoy the evening with my husband, not talk to a stranger about how we're doing every 30 seconds. They had multiple people filling water & offering to get another glass of wine or a cocktail, They had someone come by to sweep up crumbs. If you get up to use the restroom, someone comes by to refold your napkin. I kept watching them do this, so when I excused myself, I folded my napkin myself & placed it on the table. But, I guess my napkin was too messy, because my husband told me they replaced it completely instead of just refolding it. Besides being annoying & unnecessary, I can't imagine how much energy & water they waste by using so many napkins. 

So, while the service was TOO MUCH, the food was completely underwhelming. I'll say that almost everything we hand was good, but nothing was great. And considering this was on all of the "best in Philadelphia" lists, I was expecting great. 

We did the House Menu (four courses each). To start, my husband had the Parsnip soup & I had the Black Bass Crudo. Both were fine. The soup was better than the fish. We finished both, but I'd never willingly order either again. I can't remember which pastas we had (the online menu has changed since December), but I do remember this was our favorite course. For our main, my husband had the pork & I had the monkfish. The pork was fine, but the monk fish was listed as "smoked monkfish, broccoli, potatoes, scallop". What I got was a decent serving  of fish, a few broccoli florets (that tasted like frozen, steamed broccoli), a few halves of small potatoes, and a pool of bright green liquid. The fish was fine (lacked in flavor, but nice texture), but the whole dish was such a disappointment. For dessert, my husband had an apple dessert & I had a chocolate one. Again, both were fine, but nothing special. 

The problem with this meal was that all of the food was simply fine. Nothing was exceptional, and for almost $300 dinner (counting drinks & gratuity), exceptional was expected.

Think wings to go, but so much better.

I've been wanting to go to this place for a few months but between the pandemic and being busy, I've not had the chance. Saturday evening I said I'm doing this, I walked in they had kiosks (you can also order on line) less than 15 minutes I was out the door (after putting in tip).
Pros:
Flavour variety (try the sweet tai basil), their boneless chicken is actually cut up breast (an appreciated rarity) and the dips were clearly thought out combinations. 
Spring roll and sandwiches (future review pending) look good. 
They do all of the major delivery places.

Cons:
Dipping sauce amount (to small, really tasty, but to small).

Overall I would definitely recommend and hell YEAH, I'm going back soon.

Kudos to Chef Jones (owner) for hitting this one out of the park!

P. S. FYI the fifth star because of biodegradable containers. You can never go wrong thinking about the planet.

I love Tria and it doesn't hurt that this location is right up the street from my house. It a great go to when the weather is nice and you want to sit outside and have some refreshing wine and/or beers with apps. Its a nice happy hour choice in the warmer months as well when its still light out at night and you just want snacks rather than a whole meal. Their cheeses are great as are their salads and brushettas from my experience. I will be back!
Hella greasy and overpriced. Standard French Quarter slice, I'd say. Won't be back unless in a super pinch. Ordering process was also super clunky.

This spot was a hidden gem, as I was looking for another restaurant, and saw this one next door to it. I decided to give it a try. The customer service was great. I started with an appetizer, the Bangers in Batter, with Guinness Gravy for dipping. Extremely delish!! I had never tried the British style Fish and Chips, and let the waitress know. She assured me that when it comes to their Fish and Chips, they don't play, and she was right!!  The haddock was enormous, and really good!! I'm so glad I found this wonderful establishment, and I will be back the next time I'm in the area..

Chatham Tap is just another wonderful restaurant/bar located on Mass Ave. I've wanted to go here for a while, but every time I've tried going, it has been packed to capacity. This obviously made me want to try it even more since it's clearly great and people truly enjoy it. The solution to this problem was going there for lunch on a sunny Sunday afternoon. We opted to sit outside in their patio area, comfortably located under an umbrella. We ordered Bloody Marys as they were recommended by one of our companions that is a frequent of the establishment and I was quite impressed by the cocktail. Chatham also has an expansive beer menu with draughts, domestic/micros, and imports.

For my meal I ordered the BLT sarnie, or sandwich for us lesser folk. When I ordered, the waiter made sure to get the point across that the bacon was thick cut, Canadian-like bacon. Apparently people are surprised by that and are sometimes unimpressed--how could that be? My superior BLT came with rasher bacon, lettuce, tomato, and mayo served on crispy toasted parisien bread. The sarnie came with homemade potato chips, coleslaw, or cottage cheese, but I was feeling frisky and subbed French fries for an extra $1.75. It was worth it. The fries were thick, crispy, and tasty. My BLT was around $7. My comrades ordered the hummus plate with pita chips for $7 and the green leaf Thai wraps, consisting of chipotle-apricot chicken with cilantro dressing, green leaf lettuce, and peanut dipping sauce for around $8. Don't be confused when the wraps come out with lettuce instead of bread like my friend thought was going to happen. Despite his complete confusion, he still enjoyed the dish. Definitely don't wait to try Chatham Tap!

We were seated right away ....no wait on a Saturday night !  maybe it was slow because of Labor Day weekend... anyway, they gave us chips & salsa right away, waitress was very friendly..... had to wait about 10 to 15 minutes for a margarita...but the waitress apologized and said she forgot... I can live with that because she looked kinda busy.

The food was good, hot and nice sized portions.   I don't think you'll get the best meal of your life here... but it was good.    I will say that the cornbread that came with my Tacos was pretty tasty... it was more like spoon bread because they spooned it out like a ball of mashed potatoes..... thanks to the waitress for suggesting the corn bread :-)

Hey, it's OK.

Had a bit of a Sushi-Jonesing the other night and yelp directed me to this place.  It was good and not overpriced.  Having their own parking is a plus but I can see where those spaces would fill up quickly (with Land Rovers and Benzes) on a weekend night.  After negotiating my way past the beautiful people, I was seated at the sushi bar.  Funny, I was the only one there.  Doesn't anyone appreciate the at the bar experience and checking out the fish personally?

I went with some Uni (shock there, huh) and a sushi/sashimi combo platter.  I'm guessing the old guy might be the owner but he was slightly annoying.  "Hey buddy, large Sake for big man".  Whatever dude, I'm only 5' 5" tall. The Sea Urchin was fresh but a bit too much rice.  The combo platter was plentiful and nicely presented.  Good stuff but nothing to blow my socks off.  The chefs seem to be just going through the motions rather than interacting with the customers and offering suggestions.  Who knows, maybe they don't speak english.

The service here is HORRIBLE. The hostess was extremely rude. They tried to sit us next to a window when it's 30 degrees outside like winter isn't here (hehe). There was a huge draft when we were seated and requested to be seated elsewhere. The hostess was extremely rude and straight up said "no we have reservations coming". As you see in the pictures the restaurant was almost empty. I even checked on open table and the reservations weren't even completely booked as there was open spots for 5:30 and we arrived at 5:20. Our waiter was nice and the bartender was alright. Asked for check and it took forever s Food was good as well but the service left a bad taste in my mouth and ruined the whole experience. It's a shame because Tierra Colombiana service is so much better than this place.

Service and food excellent!
Great happy hour hangout! 
Check out jazz night..... Fridays.

Excellent service! I always order 4-8 pizzas for
My crew online. Pizzas have always been made accurately. They are always fast, warm, and great tasting. Never had an issue with this location, and I've ordered probably 100 pizzas in last 6-8 months.

I hadn't been to the Victory brewery for years so when I happened to be in the area I had to stop by.  The renovated inside is pretty impressive.  High ceilings.  Nice woods.  Nice long bar with old copper kettle tops hung above the bar.  Some old Philly brewing memorabilia decorates the wall behind.

The beer selection is huge.  The had 26 options on tap, 3 on hand pump with an additional 2 bottle selections.  I'd say about half of the taps are rare or difficult to find beers so it's definitely a fun list.  I tried the Unity Kölsch which was a delicious example of the style.  I also did the Uncle Teddy's bitter.  Small 10 oz. (0.3 L) pours came in a  beautiful Victory glass at only $3 each!  In my mind Victory has always had some of the most consistently good beer in the region, especially their German styles.  Prima pils is one of the best pilsners you can get in America.  So, the beer alone is a good reason to visit.

They also have a huge menu.  I happened to be there on Wing Wednesdays where you can get 10 wings for $5 (or $5.50 if you pick another flavor not on the special menu).  The bartender recommended the Korean wings to me.  The wings were very meaty, crunchy on the outside and juicy on the inside.  The Korean flavor was a delicious way to go.  Sweet and sour with a bit of tang and kick.  These were some of the best wings I've had in a long while.

For two beers and wings my whole bill was $11.50.  A great lunch.

The first bartender was really attentive and helpful.  The second bartender a little less so, but they definitely both knew what they were doing.

It was also pretty fascinating to watch their special growler filling machine behind the bar.

A great experience overall.  Will try to come back anytime I'm in the Downingtown area.

I thought this place was ok. It is definitely an upscale brunch place. The tables are in there pretty tight, so If you're bringing a stroller it's a bit of a tight. My salad was good. Things are a bit expensive because of the high end quality. I found it to be ok but just not great. I'm not into overly fancy food though so that could just be me.

We just stopped by on a Friday night to meet up with some friends. We arrived around 10:45pm, and the place was already packed! We only came in for drinks since we had dinner already. 

This place sorta reminds me of Raleigh's (before it was burned down) and Blakes at Berkeley. Good times at those places.

I am not from the area, but I can imagine a lot of UPenn students frequent this bar since it is near campus. 

Free peanuts and a few beer selection on draft. Not bad. I love the ambiance :)

Nice to have Maynards open again. We made reservations for 6:30pm and was seated on time. Service was quick with water brought out when we were seated. 
We ordered crusty bread with the foie gras. The bread was warm and soft and the foie gras good. I had the Sonoran wheat ravioli. The sauce was very good with lots of corn but only 2 raviolis. We agreed our entrees were delicious, but the servings were small for the price. 
We also got told the hostess and server that we were celebrating a birthday and they acknowledged it but nothing special was made of it. Which was a disappointment.

Pretty good ice cream. It has a very soft texture, natural fresh ingredients. No mix-in flavors - the ice cream itself is flavored. Nice people working. They don't make their own cones - they are laser focused on making their ice cream great. The store has a nice courtyard that is dog-friendly.

The menu changes daily which is great.  And if you sit at the bar you can look into the kitchen, always fun.  We went on a Friday night without a reservation, but chose to sit at the bar, which I actually often prefer.

We asked what would be wheat-free and the server got someone to annotate the menu which was very helpful.  We got the mushroom salad, something else, scallops, and escolar.  The mushroom salad was awesome.  Crispy and flavorful mushrooms with creamy goat cheese on top of some bitter salad greens, a great combo.  The escolar was prepared with prawns and a buttery dill sauce.  The prawns were huge and super sweet.  Don't let the head scare you either because there is some sweet morsels to be found in there too.

I was super excited about this place, and while it was absolutely delicious, I will be frank-- it's expensive and the portions are extremely small.  Cocktails are also quite pricey at $10 a pop.  Good and creative, but pricey.  One of our servers kind of had a little bit of a 'tude, but whatever.  

Also, I get the local foods thing.  And I support it all the way.  I belong to a CSA, shop at a true farmer's market at least once a week, buy about 60% of my meat from a local source (and even more on the veggie side), and belong to a local food co-op.  This is how I choose to eat all the time.  But giving me this spiel and then telling me that seafood is your specialty, well, you can see how that doesn't quite jive.  Just sayin'.  Now maybe if you tell me that all of your seafood is sourced from small, independent, sustainable fisheries, or even a seafood co-op, I could understand a little bit better.

I might actually give 3 stars but the flavors and annotated menu bump it up to 4.

Note: Regrettably this placed closed in March 2009 but the owners are now cooking at the Avenue Pub on St. Charles.

This place really is ideal ... you get a meal that's way above average at a great price. The redfish sandwich lives up to the hype and it's $8.95, plus it comes with two generous and delicious sides (soup, potato salad, guacamole, etc.). Definitely check it out.

If I could do a two-and-half star review I would because Sauce is a definitively average pizza place. The only reason I went with two stars rather than 3 is because the place is very over-hyped. Whenever I would ask what the good pizza places in Tucson were, one of the first mentioned would be Sauce. My wife and I would drive by it constantly and we decided to check it out one night. Considering the great places we've found since (Zachary's, Picazzo's), we won't be heading back to Sauce in the near future.

I'm not a fan of the layout of the restaurant. It's self-seating which is a big problem since the place is constantly packed, and there's usually a considerable wait to order food. Of course, once you've ordered your food you have to hope that there's a table available to eat. I could get over the whole ordering and self-seating format if the pizza was worth the wait but sadly, it's not.

I like thin pizza but this is far too thin for my liking. Others might disagree but considering the price is a little higher than most pizzerias, I think the pizza should be a little thicker. The menu is also extremely limited. But they do serve mac and cheese as a side, which is a plus. It's not the greatest mac and cheese but any opportunity at indulgence is well-noted in my book.

I went here last night after I read on yelp that it was open until 11pm. The bartender told me that yelp was wrong and she gave us last call immediately for food and drinks, which was fine I was in a hurry anyway, but what she neglected to do was actually give us service. At all. She was focused on cleaning and didn't ask how our food and drinks were. She huffed and puffed like we were an inconvenience for being there so close to closing time. I am a bartender and I know that sometimes you can get someone 5 minutes before closing (we were there 25 minutes before closing). I give everyone, even last minute guests the best service they deserve. I was extremely disappointed. I used to love this place.

Ordered from here for the first time today. My food came within a reasonable amount of time. However, when I opened the box to eat the appetizer sample I ordered it was thrown together, there was a hollowed out potato skin in there (not sure why), my chicken fingers were torn in half and everything was cold. Pretty disappointed and confused about the random empty potato skin. Won't be ordering from here again.

We were coming through Tuscan with our pets to relocate to TX. We wanted good food and pet friendly. This place is great. I had the best beef steak Torta ever. The bun was fresh and soft. The steak was seasoned perfectly. Our dogs were happy to be with us and we did not have to worry about them. All four of us really enjoyed the food and they enjoy the local draft beer.

Five stars for Pho in Nashville. It's good by comparison to the West and East coast but great for Nashville. They have traditional beef broth and also serve chicken and vegetable broths. Happy to have found it.

All around great seafood bistro!  Waiter had the perfect balance of attentive but not annoying.  Food was fresh and delicious.  Great wine list.  High end but not pretentious.  Modern but comfortable atmosphere - cool looking wine wall.  Going back...

This place was great!!! It had really cute indoor and outdoor seating. All the servers seemed super friendly and the service was so speedy. The food was delicious; well seasoned tacos, delectable guacamole and yummy tortillas. I would highly recommend this place
It's Ihop. Not alot to say. Servers were watching us like we were gonna rob the place or something. Not the best experience....
I like the pho here, honestly been eating here since I was little so I'm happy nothing has change in the pho here taste like home!

Stopped by for a late night dinner by myself and sat at the counter. The waiter was super attentive. I ordered the La Plancha with the red sauce pot roast. It looks like a burrito covered with enchilada sauce. With sour cream and pickled onions.  It was soooo  good. Thought I would bring some home but I couldn't  stop. The meat inside was so tender and the sauce was to die for. Dreaming about it the next day is the sure fire way to get me back!
Walked in to the store, gave two different employees a chance to at least acknowledge me. After five minutes of watching them fill drive through orders, I walked out. Very sad experience.

Super clean, friendly staff and servers, and free chips and salsa.  I'm still amazed when a Mexican restaurant doesn't offer free chips and salsa with all the competition nowadays, La Parilla definitely delivered!

The carnitas tacos were simply amazing.  Even the refried beans were delish and I'm not typically a fan of refried beans.

The steak nachos were very good and most definitely should be shared.

Great sushi, quick delivery times outside of downtown West Chester (to my work), friendly staff and all around great experience.

I've had 1 order - a delivery order just consumed moments ago.  I picked the Any 3 Rolls: (Spicy Tuna Roll, Spicy Salmon Roll, Eel Avocado Roll) and a seaweed salad.  Portion size on the seaweed salad was great!  Overall flavor and texture were as they should be.  Very good seaweed salad.  All 3 rolls were excellent.  My only gripe is that the 3 packets of soy sauce weren't enough and I didn't have extra here at work.  4-5 would be better, but I'll make sure to ask for that on future orders.

I definitely recommend these guys!

Very hip and cozy spot, without a touristy vibe. This place has an incredibly large beer selection and will most likely have something for everyone's taste. Aside from the beer, the food gets a 10 out of 10. A wide selection of appetizers and in my opinion, they cook the best burger in Saint Louis! All in all, if you're looking for a good time, and astounding food at an affordable price, this is the place. I suggest going on Tuesdays.(2 dollar burger night)
Best soup and veggie dumplings ever! Food came out fast. Service was great. Definitely one of my faves!!

The champagne brunch buffet is overflowing with fresh seafood, prime rib, omelet station, pasta station, tropical fruit, cheese boards, salads - including seafood and gourmet, breads, substantial side items, There is a separate dessert room that is a favorite so save room. Excellent service and food are paired with a gorgeous setting with huge windows overlooking Tampa Bay. There is outdoor seating on the deck overlooking the bay and a firepit for a really special event.  A great experience for family or business. It is a favorite with adults and kids alike!  Bring your appetite!

If you're expecting Italian cuisine and a menu full of authentic options - this isn't the place to go. That being said, what they have is still delicious. I ordered the garlic bread as a started ($3) and that was really good. Then I had the eggplant parm for my main. The jam at the top was too sweet but the rest was delicious. Personally, I think it could've used a bit more of a kick in terms of spice. For dessert, I ordered the warm chocolate budino. That was delicious - rich chocolate flavor with salted caramel in the middle and the cool whipped cream on top.
