Aside from that, there are very limited pasta options - it's definitely more of a pizza place with a few other options. Overall, pretty delicious experience.

My favorite pizza place. 

I love a good deal and Jet's always seems to have one. Whether in those Val-pack mailings, rewards through Flocktag, or just random specials I have used it all to my advantage. I wouldn't work this hard if the pizza wasn't good, in fact, I just wouldn't even go. 

I always order the small deep dish sausage and cheese with turbo crust ( I love that you can flavorize the crust) and when I call in they already have my name in the system. This past time I visited I had a Flocktag reward so I got a large deep dish. When I went to pick up my order, it was messed up. There was a new person that originally took my order and didn't get it correct, but I didn't trip. The manager just made a new order and asked if I wanted to keep the pizza or they would have to toss it. I kept the pizza because I knew I had at least two friends that would eat it. Since I've become a patron at this establishment I've had orders messed up quite a few times, but the customer service that I received, whether calling in or in person, was good I won't lower my rating anything below 4 stars.

I have been here a few times now, and have been extremely pleased with a lot of their menu items. The chicken kabob is excellent (honeslty, though, I am a sucker for a charcoal grill) and the hummus is tasty.  The only thing I was disappointed in was the chicken shawarma.  It was just kind of dry and blah-tasting.  But overall, I can't complain., and they deliver, too!

I was craving breadsticks, and by god I was gonna get them. 
We pulled up to Olive Garden at 8:30(ish) and we're immediately sat in the bar area. 
Our waitress, Caryn, was super great. I wanted to order  one of the new green apple moscato sangria, but forgot my ID. (Guess I've got to come back!) 
We had the mozzarella sticks as an appetizer, which were pretty standard as far as chunks of cheese go. 
My soup, chicken and gnocchi was yummy as always, and the salad was rabbit food (in a good way, of course. Except that the salad had only two olives. Strange. 

I ordered the seafood alfredo, which was so yummy. I ended up taking half home for lunch the next day. 

We ordered zeppolis for dessert which came with a delicious raspberry and a chocolate sauce. 

All of the food was yummy. 

I feel like I need to comment on something else though. While sitting in the bar, I overheard quite a bit of discussion from the servers/staff. Every single conversation was friendly, and represented with a smile. I've never seen a group of coworkers in a restaurant work together so happily. Everyone seemed to get along and to be helping each other out. 
At one point, one young lady mentioned that she did something for the other because of how busy the other was. That's just good teamwork. 

Obviously this restaurant is run very well, and I will be returning.

Good flavorful food for area.  Lots of variety and able to accommodate larger groups. 
Be prepared to wait despite large seating area.  Noisy!

I had summer salad topped with grilled salmon which smelled a little fishy.  Others at my table had pork loin with chimmichurri, chicken divan and shrimps and grits.  Everyone else liked their dish.  

Service was awesome.   I don't think our water or ice tea  glasses were ever half way. 

I wouldn't go out of my way to try  but if I was in airport area I would come in comparison to other options.

I've been to Thai Orchid two times in the past 3 months.  Both times it was an overall superb experience.  Food was delicious and beautiful, service was courteous and attentive.  We will frequent this restaurant often

The food at the bar is good.... chicken tenders and mozzarella sticks are a stampede to order.... you will catch the owner, son and Brother working.... locally own and family owned catholic bar lol
Great variety of beer and spirits... they also do carry out beer and spirits.... I love his bar

The pizza here is so good! Huge slices for cheap! Best pizza we've ever had. Nice thin crust New York style. Very nice staff and clean environment. Hand sanitizer at the door. Left very full and satisfied.

Cute new restaurant in an area that definitely needed a cute breakfast/ brunch spot. However the food was average and the prices were outrageous. I live in the neighborhood so I was excited when Another Broken Egg Cafe opened but was quickly disappointed upon my first visit. When you arrive on a weekend, expect a wait with people standing outside in droves. Once you're seated you'll notice an average blah menu with extremely high prices and you'll experience average service. I will not be returning even though they are literally 3 minutes away from my house. I've been spoiled in South Tampa with delicious breakfast/brunch spots like Pinky's, Piquant, Tahitian Inn, and Datz so unfortunately Another Broken Egg Cafe will need to up their ante to survive here.

It had been several years since my last visit here and I was pleased to see the expanded restaurant and the large parking area behind the restaurant.  The service was a bit slow given that there wasn't a crowd.  But the food was great, typical N.O. seafood place with the standards.  Frying skills are top notch and seasoned well, not spicy but not bland.  We'll be back.

Had such an amazing experience here. The food was one mouth watering dish after another and i wanted more of all of them but was too full (We had ordered practically every non-entree dish on the menu and 2 of some) To top it off, a slipped glass at the end was cleaned up by the friendliest people I could imagine. They really didn't put out any bad vibes, just made me sit back while they took care of it and forced me to shake off the feeling dumb and enjoy myself. They were 5 stars already, this put it over the top.

Came here after visiting the CMHF. 
I'll start off by saying their chips and queso were really yummy. Not the best queso ive ever had, but solid queso. The chips were also really good. They had a different texture than most chips as they were much thicker and just..different? But I loved them.

We also got the Mexican street corn. It was not very good and you could tell they used cold mayo because the corn was pretty cold. It really just tasted like corn with mayo and there weren't many other flavors I could taste besides that.

The chicken tacos I ordered were good, but they weren't amazing. The corn tortilla they used was really dry. With that said, they tasted really fresh.

I liked this place, the food isn't bad, it just didn't stand out to me. With that said, if you're looking for a quick bite after visiting the CMHF then I'd recommend it!

A definite fave in the area!

Things I liked:
1. Shrimp in rice wine sauce. Mellow & tasty!
2. Mango chicken (a hold-over from their 1st restaurant, Sqaure on Square)..but just as tasty!
3. Friendly owner and staff!
4. You can park at the hotel right next door and they'll validate your parking slip (at least for lunch!). Very handy as parking in that area can be rather dicey. 

Things I didn't like:
1. Again, a tad pricey!
Love this place. Always yummy. Hubby and I get the lamb or chicken shawarma. Serving sizes are generally shareable.

So as beer guy, I am always excited and optimistic when a new brewery opens doors.
Schüssboom was long awaited.
There was hype.
There were delays.
This created more hype.
Then they opened, but without any of their own brews. (Sigh)
(Sigh again)
Then, heard they have their own beers on tap...
So now it was time for me to check this place out.
Beers? Mmmm, not bad. But with more competitive brews locally....
Food was excellent though...that's an after thought for this beer guy. But still held promise.
Back a few months later with some new Schüssboom beers on tap. And wow!
Beers are now a threat to other local brewers. Beer bait, pillow drops and IPAprés all have award winning potential.
And the food? Still insanely delicious!
The Schüss Poutine is out of this world.
I fondly recall days getting convenient store poutine in Canada (don't judge me) and then seeing the gourmet versions pop up at the likes of Depot only be dropped from the menu.
But Schüssboom is clearly after my business! And they'll get it (don't drop poutines )
It extremely difficult, maybe even double diamond difficult to deliver great food and great beer, but Schüssboom is shredding this run! Please keep it up (cowbell ringing, "Allez vite!")

My wife loves this restaurant for breakfast. She always orders the coconut french toast, it is unlike any french toast we've ever had or seen anywhere else. I really enjoy the eggs for breakfast and salads for lunch. Food is always fresh, service is always kind and prompt. Highly recommend! Hope they reopen soon, closed because of Covid temporarily.
I wouldn't know if the food is any good because we went at 2:15pm on a Sunday and they were closed. The sign on the door says 6am-3pm on Sunday, but the worker inside said they were closed?!

To say that The Grand Hall is stunning is an understatement. The decor, especially during the holidays, is beautiful! 

You don't want to miss the light show! It's projected on the ceiling every hour at night with different shows - The Beatles, Queen, Holiday Themed - all make the experience memorable. 

The drinks are great and be sure to get the loaded tots!

One of the best and most unique burgers I've ever had. Arugala, tomatoes, balsamic vinegar, and cheddar cheese on an obviously fresh and top grade burger patty. GREAT! The cauliflower and cheese was equally good. Very nice wine selection.
This is a keeper for us. It's in our neighborhood. So easy to get to. Service was great. Owner on site. Food delicious.

This place has been on my "to try" list for a while, and I used a dinner invitation as an excuse to pick up half a dozen cupcakes for dessert. The quaint shop is located on a quiet street, almost unassuming, but once you enter the premises, you see cases filled with cookie dough treats, cupcake varieties, and cookie/brownie displays. Their cupcake menu seems to rotate, so I really had no idea what to expect. I opted for strawberry champagne, red velvet, chocolate peanut butter, shamrock (mint), cake batter, and birthday cake. Each cupcake was decorated beautifully and so gorgeous to look at! Out of all of the cupcakes, the chocolate peanut butter was a clear winner for my taste buds. I don't care for peanut butter that much, but the chocolate cake was moist and the peanut butter icing was light and fluffy. I also enjoyed the red velvet, shamrock, and cake batter cupcake. I read rave reviews about the strawberry champagne, so this was the one flavor I was looking forward to trying the most. Unfortunately, the cupcake was a little too dry and the champagne icing was just a little too overpowering for me. At a little over $4.00 a cupcake, I thought it was a bit expensive, but my friends and I thoroughly enjoyed tasting a sample of each flavor. I would love to come back to try a more citrus based cupcake next time

Sunday evening dinner was nice. The vibe is so cozy, romantic, and inviting. We shared the surf & turf. I also had the pineapple martini. All had great flavor. The service was nice as well. They even split our dish on two separate plates instead of just bringing the extra plate out that we asked for. I kept a star because the steak was not medium as requested and our server left before we did but I still would highly recommend. Menu has several options that caught my eye and the martini was the best that I ever had.

Staff is always friendly and polite, delivery is also available and definitely convenient. Location is a little hard to get in and out of since it's at the intersection of three busy streets. 

The pizza is good, the sandwiches and wings are also good. I would not say it's my favorite pizza ever, but for a Friday night at home watching a movie, it's good for us.

They also have a small seating area if you just want a slice or just want to eat there.
Nyna was our server an was great.  She was on top of everything.  Great place to come.

The entire experience at this new hidden gem in Cinnaminson is amazing!  From the fresh Halal meat selections, Beef, chicken and Lamb to the wonderful side Basmati Rice, food is plentiful and reasonable. The owner/chef Asmad, really puts so much love into all aspects of his establishment and it shows.   I am so happy to have discovered the Baba Grill and am happy to a much needed venue to our local area! Welcome to the neighborhood!

Excellent food- great service!  Delicious New York perfectly cooked, delicious grilled chicken with the yummiest Parmesan polenta ever!!  Matthew our server was very attentive and great!  Thank you for a great meal, our first visit since we moved here, the Capital Cellars red blend was delicious too!

If you expect fine dining just off the Circus  Circus arcade, you have cine to the writing place -- that would be down the hall and around the corner at Ruth's Chris. If you want decent pizza or spaghetti at a reasonable price, you can do much, much worse. 

At $11.99 for "design your own pizza" or $10.99 for baked spaghetti and meatballs, you won't go wrong. This place will never win a Michelin Star. It's not even the best pizza in downtown Reno (that would be Piasanos for blocks down). But it is fast, filling, and good -- and well worth a visit.
Came for lunch and had the buffet. Excellent food, decent selection. I highly recommend trying it!
Best chicken in the city. Delicious sides and friendly staff. So glad Indy has a touch of the south

I am so glad I was able to get a reservation and experience Etch. This restaurant is one of the main reasons Nashville has been named a great American "food city."  This chef has a clear vision for preparing exceptional food, with high quality, local ingredients with diverse herbs and spices that tempt your taste buds cry out for another bite.  Every night there are specials worthy of your attention.  On the night we dined here we stayed with some of the old favorites. Roasted cauliflower, with a truffled pea pesto, Marcona almonds and a feta dip explode with flavor.  The Octopus was cooked to perfection, tender and tasty.  On the Entrees, the Cobia is not to be missed with brown butter, capers, olives, raisins, feta and Middle Eastern spices. The flavor combinations remind me of France, Africa and Spain.   The cocoa chili spiced Venison was grilled perfectly and served with sweet potatoes.  Wow.  For dessert, since it is peach season, the Peach Crumble Tart was an excellent choice.  There are lots of really good, affordable wines by the glass.  ...and there are some exceptional bottles for those with a discerning palate. Our waiter was knowledgeable, provided well thought out advice and was there when we needed him, but invisible otherwise - nice job.  To top all of this off, Etch offers complimentary valet parking.  In downtown Nashville, that is a big deal to me.   Best wishes to the chef and her team of professionals who make fine dining appear to be effortless. It is clear to me that everyone in this place watches the details and that is what sets Etch above most other places.
Omg... So good! We got the Taste of New Orleans was amazing. We will definitely come again. Everything we had was sooo good
Amazing food and service! The cauliflower and carne tacos were delicious and the service was excellent! Late night menu prices ($2 tacos!!) were unbeatable.

My first time getting food from here was awesome! Very fresh and seasonal. The Pork Bun was delicious. The Cod bun was so fresh and the homemade Tartar Sauce was phenomenal. With just the right amount of saltiness from the capers. They ended up giving us an extra salad and the tomatoes were easily the best tomatoes I've had in 2018. Greens were also incredible. The meal is a little bit on the pricier side but the quality makes it all worth it and you do not leave hungry.

This place has a fair amount of menu options so it is a good something for everyone.  My husband and son really enjoy the pho (me too) and I like that there is a variety for me.  The are very nice and are pretty quick in here too.    Thanks SK noodle!

Had the Cincinnati Dog with chili, onions, cheese and mustard accompanied by rings. But the bread didn't hold up to the chili all too well and got soggy and started falling apart. Think next time I won't get it buttered, just grilled.

Went here almost a year ago and really enjoyed it. The people working were happy and the menu had so many wonderful sounding options. Went back this week and sad to say both of those have changed. Menu is pretty limited and basic breakfast options. Nothing fun like before. Got a seasonal coffee, the pumpkin spice, and sad to say it's a sad excuse for pumpkin. Really want to support a local small business but when things fall short it's hard to want to come back.
This is the greatest nudie bar in the world.  Inexpensive drinks and friendly attractive dancers who don't hustle you.

Ok food, nothing special, it's a huge menu of all types of food, kind of like your poor man's Cheesecake factory.  Service was good, but not a place I feel the need to get back to.  The decor in the place seems to have been stuck in the 80's with random posters, plants, plywood walls.  I'm guessing it might be fun before a game to grab some drinks.

The Couch Tomato is a neighborhood staple, and they excel in serving Italian food that somehow doesn't make you feel like a beached whale lying in bed afterward. 

The cuisine is light and always features some kind of green. The flatbread pizzas are fantastic -- crispy and soft in all the right places. As for the menu at large, any item that contains the term "short rib" is going to be excellent.

They serve items with a wide variety of well-paired cheeses, and the upstairs dining area is fancy enough for you to feel comfortable bringing your parents in from out of town. 

Please note that you NEED to order the tomato bisque. I don't care if you don't like soup, or if a simple tomato-focused dish doesn't sound appetizing. You are wrong in both cases -- the bisque is thick and it eats like a meal. Here's a protip: you can order the bisque as a "pizza soup" and have them stuff it with bread and cheese. 

There. I just made your evening for you.

Have you ever been so excited and ready to try some of the most talked about famous philly cheese steaks.... TO BE SO LET DOWN.  NOT WORTH THE WAIT!!! A 30 minute or more stand in line around the building WAIT, for NOT the best thing i ever ate.  All of this sandwich was bland, the onions, peppers, and steak it lacked seasoning.  The place was packed and clean... I JUST DIDN'T LIKE IT! I agree with Nicole C. limited seating upstairs amd pretty BLAH FOOD. I was there 9-24-16 and it was a just ok.
One of the best loaded potato ever! It was so large, I ate it in 2 settings and still half of it left.

My centrally located pick for my birthday dinner with friends, and I'm not gonna lie, Crow's Next wasn't even on my radar until my brother started bartending there.  I read a few reviews and thought it sounded up my crowd's alley, so why not patronize those that pay my family member's bill, right?

Overall, I'd say The Crow's Nest is pretty appropriately labelled with 3 stars - A-Ok for this trip.  Would I go out of my way to visit again?  Probably not.  Would I stop by if I were looking for a bite in the area?  Sure.

For my entree, I ordered the mac n cheese, which was good, but when I make or order a mac n cheese, I tend to like the creamier, smack me in the face with some cheese varieties.  This stayed on the drier cheese end of the spectrum.  Good enough, but not my favorite.  I did try a bite of a friend's grilled cheese w/ bacon which was good and another's BAT (bacon arugula and tomato) that I had waffled back and forth choosing myself, and I should have gone with the BAT!  My husband ordered the pulled pork which he said was good, but the sauce wasn't his fave.  I'll chock that up to personal preference.

We didn't order dessert, because the offerings didn't sound all that appealing to me.  Perhaps the Pear Gorgonzola Bread Pudding would intrigue me more post-finicky pregnant belly.  I had read a stltoday review referring to some sort of chocolate-y bread pudding concoction that sounded awesome.  Alas, it wasn't on the menu.  Sad day.

The service - eh.  Our waitress seemed a little out of it, and the guys once or twice just gave up and ended up ordering beers at the bar which I never take as a good sign of service.

Perhaps a future visit will result in higher marks.

Omg the Hispanic employees literally screamed and yelled making obnoxious strange sounds the entire time I ate there

Laughing loudly amongst each other the entire time.

How unprofessional

My review is soley based on the bbq chicken sandwich. When i think of bbq chicken sandwiches especially establishments in the reading terninal, i think of smoked, grilled charred meat slathered in some kinda homemade sauce with a little kick to it. Bread toasted on the inside and served, ready to devour and barely finish. 

Well....this wasnt it. 

From the outlook things look promising based on everything else being sold in the display case. Sadly the sandwich wasn't bad, but not 6 bucks good. I've eaten my share of bbq and the chicken seemed average prepared and the sauce was...plain. I really didn't get a bbq taste....not like the kind you would get even at Famous Dave's....but this was Famous Frank...clearly Dave's little cousin from his estranged fathers side of the bbq family

I will give them another shot but the chicken sandwich needs work.

It's amazing how different one visit can be to another. I guess that's the testament of a good chef -- consistently good; not good sometimes, but bad at other times. I thought about this a lot during my second visit to Trang Viet Cuisine in Tampa. The first visit was so great that we couldn't wait to eat here again. But, this visit just turned into a disappointment and now I feel torn!

We arrived at Trang Viet on a Wednesday afternoon immediately after flying into the Tampa airport. This is not a vegan Vietnamese place, but they have a lot of vegan dishes!

I decided to try some new dishes and maybe this is where I went wrong. I started with the V3 Vegan Summer Rolls, which were filled with vegetarian fiber, fresh herbs, lettuce, and rice noodles. But, they had very little flavor. The peanut sauce helped, but they had little flavor otherwise.

For my entree, I ordered the V42 Vegan Noodle Stir-Fry with yellow noodles. This stir fry had carrots, broccoli, onions, and tofu with noodles in a light sauce. The problem was that it just wasn't very good. I just sat looking at my dish and wishing for something different.

Chris ordered what I ordered the last time, the V35 Vegan Lemongrass Beef Noodles, but this time he didn't like it.  He also didn't want to finish it because it lacked flavor. Where were the flavorful sauces these dishes needed?

We were both disappointed with our meals and with it being about 25 minutes from the airport, we felt like we went out of our way for nothing. Oh, and once again, the wine was pretty awful. Can't they just buy one good wine?  I'm not sure that we will return, but then again, with the lack of vegan options in Tampa, who knows. Sigh.

Ridiculous. A friend and I came here for Sunday brunch because First Watch was packed. Both of us had sleeveless shirts on (I'm female and he's male). A man came up to us at the hostess stand and told my friend that they require sleeves. That's understandable, if it was posted or if its for dinner!! There was no one in the restaurant at the time- hope they can stay in business because we definitely won't be going back.

Have taken out from here a few dozen times over the past eight months  The meatball sandwich, pizza, BLT wrap, crab soup, and turkey with stuffing sandwich are all great.  Never had a bad meal from here.  Highly recommend.

If nothing else, come here for the cocktails and the decor - it's beautiful inside! The bartenders have created a delicious cocktail menu that blends unique flavors together. Since we were just visiting, we relied on the waiter for some recommendations and boy did he deliver! The chili hush puppies were crunchy and spicy on their own but when you added the flavor complexity of the chicken liver mousse, the combination was fantastic. I was apprehensive at first but glad I didn't let that stop me from giving them a shot. For my meal, I opted for the duck and it was cooked perfectly. My friend ordered the ribs and they were massive! The asparagus and Mac and cheese were yummy compliments as side dishes. Definitely glad we stopped in for dinner!
Had to wipe the BBQ sauce of my face and fingers after leaving this place. Great smoked meats and wings. Very friendly staff. Wish I could eat there every week!

My family and I come to San Jose every week for taco Tuesday. This week we arrive to find a sign stating that the first basket of chips is complimentary but the following baskets cost money. Also, the tacos ($1 tacos) can have no modifications, including taking off cheese or lettuce. The price for the same taco subtracting cheese or lettuce is $2.50. We asked why and they said, it is hard for us to make modifications because the cooks can't manage to do it correctly and it results in sent back orders. The rudeness of the manager and waitress was ridiculous and we will not be coming back.

Giving crazy D's four star rating was tough for me I even took a whole day to think about the food. The experience was great everything clean everything in its place the gentleman at the counter was very patient and answered every question I could possibly think to ask him. This is the reason why I say my only hang up is the chicken while the portion size is huge practically being whole chicken breast, the flavor might be needing a little tweaking. Between myself and my buddy we tried three variations on their Nashville style chicken the flavors were crazy, hot, and medium while hot is exactly what I would expect the medium tends to be a little sweet and the crazy is actually not that crazy they sprinkle the fries with the Nashville spice as well, I also got myself a pomegranate soda and that thing was too good. Definitely worth another trip to check out the other sides and the rest of the flavors

The 3 stars is for the low quality of the food. Ingredients make the dish & they use low quality ingredients. Bagged tortilla chips, frozen cooked shrimp, pre made coleslaw & guacamole ect....The best recipes or chefs on earth can't make these items taste good. It is a sports bar with a dining room not a fast casual restaurant as advertised.
The service & sports bar vibe however were 5 star. The host was friendly & personable. & Our server was attentive, knowledgeable & professional . There are at least 50 TVs showing every game possible & a lot of great beer/drink specials.
I will definitely be back to watch sports, drink beer & eat fryer food, because that it what this place excels at.

Great view. Probably the best you will get in Apollo Beach. We love that we can take our dog with us and my daughter likes the live music. The food is...ok. I've never gone there for incredible food. Just a great setting and beautiful view. We will continue to keep going

Delicious food!  I've had some of the burgers, sandwiches, 4 Horsemen--everything has been excellent!  This place is on the ground floor of a high-rise apartment building down the street from me.  I would probably be here all the time except the food is not the healthiest (depending on what you order--but if I come here, I'm gonna order something fatty and meaty!).  The location is somewhat interesting and street parking can be hit or miss depending on when you come here (I walk since I live so close).  The staff is great and I wholeheartedly support the owner's restaurant venture!

Been telling everyone about this place. Bar None the best Mexican in town. Unassuming, quiet, and things are fresh.  Our complimentary chips and green sauce with avocado chunks were all made fresh. The guac is the best!  Honestly is heck of a deal and oh so good!

I'm glad they're in the neighborhood, but the place needs work. 

I've been to the Nolensville location scores of times and to this new one twice. The barbecue is good and the sides are adequate, but only 2 stars for 2 big problems: inefficient service and sky-high prices. 

There is only one register for taking eat-in orders. (If you're placing to go, don't wait in the big line; they have a separate to-go ordering station.) Therefore long lines form during lunch and dinner that could be averted with a more efficient setup that included another register. Furthermore, you have to cut through the line of folks waiting to get to the restrooms. This is also a problem at the Nolensville location.

Rather than handing you a number to place on your table, they scrawl one on your receipt. Some time passes and a server emerges from the kitchen, bellowing what sounds like random numbers until you realize there's something about the number 79 that seems vaguely familiar. By that time, everyone has looked up from their conversation to see what all the hollering is about. Then you look like a moron for forgetting your number, and the server has wasted time trying to track you down, which means other people's food is getting cold. It's a mess. 

Then there are the prices. I live in the neighborhood and am familiar with two other excellent BBQ places that are less than 1.5 miles from this location. One on 12South charges $9 for a pork platter with 2 sides and cornbread. One on Franklin Road charges $7.25 for the same. Martin's charges $12. Folks, I am here to tell you that while the BBQ here is very good, it's not 33% better than the competition and it's for dang sure not 65% better, so I'm trying to figure out why I should pay that much more for something of similar or better quality that I can get just down the street. 

As a parting thought, they don't vent the cooking smoke properly, so you smell like meat for the remainder of the day after going inside.

Always here and Idk why I've never written this review. Must be because i was always too busy eating my really good food or chatting with real cool locals and other moms from the area with our kids sipping iced chai lattes. Come here. Relax. Eat. Enjoy. Repeat often.
I actually have no words to describe how bad this place is. Too bad you cant give less than 1 star. My orange chicken bowl was a literal lean cuisine.

I love olive branch! Their food is always fresh and I appreciate that they deliver. However their prices on extras are starting to get a little crazy. Just ordered a side of ranch that cost $3 and got 2oz....that seems a little extreme to me. Will I go back....if course....will order extras....no way!
Good food and service.  Call ahead seating is great especially having a large family.  Great place to take kids because it's usually loud and no one notices if my kids get loud.

JJ Bootleggers advertised "20 minute lightning" lunch was a joke. 
During a busy workday, 6 hungry co-workers stepped out for a quick lunch yet ours actually took 45 minutes. Carly the surly server dished far too much bad attitude and curt remarks towards a group of people of color. Unsure if it was because we didn't order any alcoholic drinks during lunch or simply because we quickly wanted to place & receive our orders. Her smart assed comments came quicker than the food. Snapping at us: "does anyone else want something before I go to the back", is that all, etc. 
After 45 minutes with no food coming out of the kitchen, one co-worker needed to get back to work and asked to have her order togo. The server took the co-workers money and then asked if she still wanted her food... I guess Carly wanted my co-worker to pay for poor service. It even took about 15 minutes to get salt and pepper shakers (another co-worker had to beg the group at the next table for theirs. 
In the beginning, I thought this restaurant could be a big enough space for our end of year office party but the missing lightning and poor customer service put a stop to those ideas. Food just okay and service much worse.

I am a huge fan of Talayna's pizza.  Their pizza tastes great and the prices are very reasionable.  Growing up I had a few birthday parties where we got the monster pizza and everyone got to eat it... one piece will fill most up.  The ingredients seem to be very fresh.  I have never tried their pasta though so I cannot comment on it.
They are very nice, and has good service. They also have a stamp card to get free/discounted things!
Love this place!   You want something healthy.    You want something fresh.    You want something chock full of goodness/.   Come here and grab a bite.   You won't be disappointed.

Love this place!  Breaksticks are always fresh, people are always great!  I come in all the time and Tricia is always smiling and happy and always moving around helping other guest and talking with us, she is so nice.  The place has such a good atmosphere, we will be back!

Absolutely loved it! I had the real Jamaican ackee, vegan salt fish, dumbling, green banana, plantain and  yam! Washed that down with a wonderful very tasty glass of sorrel. The service was very warm. very friendly. It was like coming home. The prices are very reasonable. I say stop wasting time and get over there now!

Although they don't sport themselves a vegan restaurant, our waitstaff was able to accommodate us. We had excellent vegan mushroom pizza, Roasted chickpeas in their shells, olive selection, tomato salad, and fried cauliflower with herbs. I especially enjoyed the beer selection. Our non-vegan dinner companions house enjoyed their meal. It was a great place for vegans and non-vegans to happily dine together

Delicious chicken! I had the tenders, medium heat. They were spicy, but not too hot to handle. Perfect heat. Most of our group got mild, and they said they were just a little spicy. The people were so friendly and we were so glad we stopped by to try Nashville hot chicken!

I'm not sure who Elevation Burger wants to compete with, but I can't help but try to compare it to other burger joints.  It compares mostly favorably to Five Guys, and it is in the same price range, possibly lower, which makes me wonder whether they will survive.  First, they have a nice interior, it is much more restaurant-like than Five Guys.  After you order, you sit down and they bring you your food.   Second, their main ingredient, beef, is organic and grass-fed.  Much more expensive than regular beef.  And much tastier, by the way.  Third, they seem to have more staff than they need.  So their profit margins must be slim.  

I ordered a cheesburger with fries.  You can select from several toppings just like Five Guys.  I had caramelized onions.  Yum.  The burger was incredibly tasty and juicy and a bit greasy.  I like greasy.  The fries were matchstick, which I do not prefer.  They are harder to eat and since they have more surface area, they have more oil.  They are cooked in olive oil, which is ok.  They were cooked nicely.

The service was ok, but the people seemed to be not very happy.  At Five Guys, they are always loud and friendly.  The only thing about this place that will bring be back is the actual burger itself, and that is enough.
Chicken is inedible. It was supposed to be General Tso's chicken but tastes sweet instead of spicy. And the chow mein is disgusting. Do not eat here.

The best things I can say about the food here is that they offer lots of hot sauces, which given the absence of seasoning at least offers a flavor option. And, the oil in which they fried my food seemed fresh. The worst thing is that the food lacks seasoning: BLAH. At least the service is fast and the parking easy.

Divey bar, oversized bar food, the french onion soup lived up to the hype - It was basically a bowl of cheese. Beer list was typical for a NJ dive bar.. no microbrews except 1 Victory.  The portions were over the top large -- like the clientele.

Never have been to the tap house before but my friends and I decided to check it out for the $3 Yuenglings! Mark was our bartender who was so much fun! He suggested to order the Mac and cheese fries balls and the jalapeño poppers which were both so good! We also enjoyed some 41 mini beer shots. Thank you Mark we will be back next time we're in Ybor!

We have experienced many restaurants along the way from Kemah, Texas to Nashville. We have to say that  Fox's Pizza Den in Nashville was exceptional in so many ways. Not only did they have an outstanding selection of gourmet pizzas and additional Italian fare, they were pet friendly and were more than  happy to accommodate our fur baby to sit with us at their small but very 
cosy restaurant. In addition, they offer pick up and delivery to the surrounding areas. If we liv d here, this would a permanent place to go or order from. Would recommend this establishment to everyone.
Fantastic food at reasonable prices, especially considering the generous portions. Great atmosphere for dates or small parties.

Although this is a chain brewery, brewmaster Thomas Mercado always comes up with original brews that are some of the best in Nashville. The rooftop is a great place for tourist to view downtown and people watch, but there is no Happy Hour on the rooftop. When you're at the bar, be sure to ask for the Happy Hour menu...they don't give it to you unless you ask and they have some great happy hour specials.
Ok food, generiske portions, and the best viet to 4th of July fire work if you can time the seating...
It's a hidden gem and has amazing pho! Everything is super fresh, authentic, made to order, and the service is great. They have a big menu and fair prices. Definitely one of my favorite pho places.

I don't know what's with the bad reviews - we go here all the time and we are locals. It's a nice change from the only other bar in town that is smokey.  The only complaint I have is the fact that I got chilly mozzarella sticks once.  The food is always great and I've eaten everything from the mussels to the ribeye steak. My son loves the steak and egg burger. I haven't had the pasta bc I don't eat pasta.   The bartenders are always nice and attentive , the beer is cold and we had a great time a couple of weeks ago when we stayed for the band.  Which came on earlier and we appreciated it-

Met a friend here for lunch one day. I had the crab cake appetizer, it came with a roasted red pepper sauce and grilled corn and red pepper strips. They were more crab balls than cakes, not much coating on outside, but they were large in size and loaded with crab meat. Inside looked like tuna salad, they were flavorful and the grilled corn went well with them.  My friend had a Reuben sandwich and it was loaded with corned beef, she said it was really good. It was a good sized sandwich.  Great lunch, our server was friendly and checked on us regularly.

I've been going to this event for years and always have a great time. I do miss the days when they gave out the tokens instead of having the 'all-you-can-drink' wristbands, it seemed like a better value. They did offer pre-purchase tickets this year through Eldorado's website that saved you $6.50. I was excited to see Smashmouth on the stage but their sound guy must have been drunk because they sounded horrible! We didn't venture over to the other stage to check out any of the other music. We stopped by the Yelp booth for some swag and took a gander at the scavenger hunt. But after an hour of beers the task at hand was lost and beer was the only mission. By the end of the day I was toast but still managed to drink my Brew Brothers beer for checking in, good times! 8 hrs of beer drinking can really take it out of a guy.
The selection of beer they had this year was really good. I always like getting to try new brews to keep in mind for when its beer thirty.

I was there when BJ's won the Rib Cook-off for the first time. I tried the other guys ribs they were good then I came across BJ's stand, ordered some stepped out of line, took my first bite and OMG I thought my mouth and taste buds had died and gone to heaven! Best Ribs I've ever tasted! I didn't even finished what I had and got back in line. The young lady who helped me said good stuff she was right. I told her I was from the Bay Area and I needed ribs for the ride home and some for a few days she laughed. She tried to sell me some souvenirs, I turned down but told her if they won the cook-off I will return and buy everything she had offered. I bought more ribs to eat, we didn't get but 2 booths away when they announced the winners BJ's 1st place! I stopped turned around and the mad rush people were making to get to their booth was crazy! Another young lady was going to help us but I let the person behind me go first. She saw me with the biggest smile I congratulated them and said I'm back to fulfill my promise and mainly to buy the ribs that where flying out of there. I don't remember how much we spent I bought ribs, their famous BBQ sauce and rub some tee shirts I still have and some buttons. To this day I only use BJ'S sauce and rub. It's not sold here in the Bay Area so when more is needed it's all about the road trip to Reno, if you're lucky if you can.find it in a grocery in Reno or Sparks if not then it's off to the restaurant which we go to every time we're in Reno. I buy a case or two 6-10 bottles of the rub. I remember that little place they had that was always full to the new location, it's good seeing how far they have come I'm happy for the whole family and everyone who's supported them over the years! Oh I just bought a new smoker and you guessed right first thing I'm making is ribs coated with BJ's rub, oh oh think my propane ran out gotta put another tank on..

Excellent lunch all around. Have not been here in a while, and I like the new bright look. Very friendly efficient service in a quite busy lunch on a Monday. Had the very tasty snapper soup. The Sherry on the side was a nice touch that many often forget. Really outstanding order of Southern Fried Oysters with Chicken salad. A real Philadelphia Classic. The oysters were plump and the batter was crisp and tasty. The chicken salad had just the right amount of mayo. Will be back to check out the extensive raw bar.
Wandered in after walking around looking for a location to lunch. Waitresses were nice. Food was good. Chill bar.

WOW, love love love, Alice (pronounced uh-lice because they're fancy like that).  I pass it every day on my commute and I'm so glad I stopped in.  Now my wife and I go there all the time and have never been disappointed.  We frequently get the danish, crumb cake, sticky buns and chocolate croissant and they're always amazing.  The bread is delicious too, though very rarely we've gotten a loaf that's a little too crispy.  The foccacia and ciabatta are our favorites and the gouda loaf is good if you're in the mood for it.

The treats are so good, we took two danish home for my wife's parents, one for each.  Well, my mother-in law ate both before my father-in law got home from work that day and tried to convince us not to tell him

The inside is nicely decorated and very welcoming as are the people that work there (maybe saying they're nicely decorated sounds bad).  The owner also makes his own chocolates with all different flavors, so its always interested to see what he's come up with.  It seems like he's always trying new things, depending on the ingredients he can get, and will make almost anything if you order it.  We do miss the monkey bread with chocolate and my wife REALLY misses the chocolate cream puffs, but like I said, he'll make them if you order them.  Definitely check this place out if you're ever within 15 miles of it, you won't be disappointed (unless he's sold out).

Excellent experience! Met up with some friends here after they suggested it. After parking, walking up you see that they have nice covered outdoor seating. I have driven by here on days when no rain was forecasted and it is uncovered, and sometimes has live music. We sat inside and upon entering it was busy, a good sign for any restaurant/bar. The menu has a great selection of food, from fish or chicken sandwiches, burgers, wings, pizza, and many other items. I had the blacken fish sand. It was very tasty and served with lett/tom/onion, I chose tatar tots and they were nice and crisp. My son had the boneless bbq wings which he said were moist and well coated. My wife had a flatbread pizza which she said was one of the best she had. Our friends tried the prime rib which was served with aujus and it was a beautiful cut of prime and tender. They also had a meatlovers style pizza which was equally excellent per their comments, and too me, looked like the beat meat pizza I had ever seen! 
We also had mixed drinks and beer and found prices reasonable and drinks made well.
All in all a great food experience. We will definitely be back. I recommend you try them out!
Call ahead really isn't call ahead. Beware if you think you won't wait when you get here. Called an hour before as requested and still waited an hour when we got to the restaurant.
Great atmosphere! Great food!! Great drinks!!! Definitely will be back!! (Ask about the green tea shot. You're welcome)

I heard a lot of hype about this place, so I decided to give it a go.  Sadly, it turned out to be just that: hype.

I went about 7pm, and there were about 5 other tables in there. I ordered and then went to my table and waited. And waited. And waited. You get the idea.  Turns out that my burger took 40mins to come out of the kitchen.  The other groups of people were waiting just as long.  It may not seem bad if you go with a group of buddies and your drinking some rounds. But, solo or in a small group - 40mins is a lifetime for a burger. 

I mean really. How long does it take to make a burger?

It may just be me, but the size of the bun they serve is waaaay over- the-top. My burger tasted like a bread burger. The flavor of the burger completely gets lost by the oversize bun. The burger was dry, and slightly reminiscent of licking a piece of paper - no taste at all.

The only redeeming factor of this place were the fries.


In a nutshell: Overrated, overpriced, over-hyped.

Prompt, courteous service and excellent authentic Italian pizza, what's not to like? Prices are affordable and the place has great ambiance. Check it out if you love Italian cuisine or are just plain sick of crappy imitators.

Had lunch here today and was not disappointed. I really like the salsa. I had one chicken and one beef burrito. The chicken was great the beef burrito was a little dry, but still tasty. I will try something else next time. It wasn't as good as Miguel's, but it was still good.
Customer service is excelente, the food it's hot and tasty. I been going with my husband since we were dating like 3 years ago and we have never had a bad experience

We have now been there twice and I would give it four and a half stars for the food quality, but I would give it maybe two and a half stars for the service. While the wait staff was very knowledgeable and friendly, too much time was spent reciting menu intricacies while other diners  waited just to get the basics on the table. Once served, getting wait staff back to the table was a chore. Also, the back room, while charming, needs a bit more light. Most people were using their smart phones to see what was on the menu, and you can't really see what you are eating. That said, the ribs were great.

This place is great! Good beer and plenty of pinball. That's enough, but there is still much more to love.
I'm so glad this is in my neighborhood

NOTE: 3 individual visits, below is original, then 2 updates... Each visit a star has been removed, do the owners read these or care?  :-(

I "SO" wanted to give FIVE stars, and if I was just reviewing on my pizza, it would be! The pizza was GREAT! I've been searching for a great, thin NY style pizza, and they listened to my request, which is rare for a restaurant, and gave it to me slightly "well done/crispy". Thoroughly LOVED the pizza and would order again and again!

Now... The one star loss was due to the wings, something I was praying was going to be a knock-out... I'm VERY picky about wings, they must be "WELL DONE & WET"... which was how I ordered them... Sadly and to my disappointment, they were cooked, but JUST BARELY, and that grosses me out, slightly soft/rubbery skin is a complete turn off. I also asked for a MEDIUM buffalo sauce, which they have either MILD or HOT, I asked, "can you just mix Mild & Hot? He said "sure", but I was told as I picked up my to-go order, that's they tossed them in Mild and gave me a side of Hot... While the sauce was good, not the temp I was going for, and the wings weren't "wet" so I had to add the hot, so my mouth is currently burning. 

All in all, I'm THRILLED that they opened, and IN LOVE with their Pizza... and am willing to try the wings again, once more, and if they can't deliver then, I'd have to think hard about going back.

Pizza was SO worth it! 
Thank you Hampton Station!


UPDATE/ADDITION: (around 8/28-29???)
I'm so disappointed, had to take a star away... :-(
Ordered pepperoni pizza, along with my sister and I raved about how great it was... But it was SAUCE HEAVY and CHEESE LACKING... Very disappointing. Hampton Station... Please get it right, I so want to increase my rating to a 5 and support a neighborhood privately owned business.
Please... I'll try one more time, and hopefully it's "the charm"... and doesn't mean "3 strikes and you're out"!!! 

UPDATE/ADDITION 2: (9/11/2015)
I called FOUR times, no answer, went to voicemail... ???... I honestly thought they must have went out of business... I pulled into China Garden two blocks prior, and contemplated ordering there... but my desire for wings won... I pulled up, and SOaB!!! They were open!!!!???
Why would they NOT answer the phone??? 
I commented about calling 4 times and no answer, the waitress laughed and said "oh yeah"... Really?!? No apology, no... Sorry... WTF
I ordered a personal pizza w/pepperoni... Good pizza, but due to it sitting on the counter for 15 mins while wings got finished, it was cold and getting harder by the time I got home (1 block away). I ordered the pizza & wings at same time, was told 20 mins... When I returned 22 mins later, waitress brought me the pizza box and said "still waiting on the wings" they FINALLY came out 15 mins later. WTF?!? At least they were well-done (this time) but hardly ANY sauce... (Disappointing) 
I lIve ONE BLOCK away... Sadly, 3 strikes, your out... I'm through and seriously disappointed... I so wanted this place to BE awesome, offer GREAT service, and provide QUALITY, PROPERLY prepared food... They ONLY make 3 items!!!
Again, truly let down and sad :-(
Bye Hampton Station... You've pissed 4 people off who won't be back, or recommend you.
An excellent place for Chinese food, excellent service, friendly servers, and a welcoming place to be.

We had to run out and do something unexpected and while out decided to go by for a bit of a late diner.   It was our first time visiting and time of evening meant no wait and fairly quick service.    My hamburger was very good.  Burger meat was very hot, but the bacon was cool.  Maybe how it is to be.   Wife had BLT and she said it was very good.  Good sized portions.   Our daughter had Chicken Strips and fries.  She said it was good.   She is a lover of hot tea and had a cup.   She had a few choices to choose from, but she was not fond of the tea she had. New flavor she wanted to try and now she knows not fond of.  The French fry sides were very good.   Wife said the cole slaw was bland and she did not eat much of it
   The waitress was friendly and attentive

We craved Chinese, and found this place last year. Went back again with a group of 6, and found the food even better, service prompt. I don't understand why there aren't more people here, but it is off HWY 19, in a rather empty shopping center. But the food is wonderful, reasonably priced too. The salt and pepper shrimp were spot on. Mongolian beef was good too. One word of caution: share your entrees or make sure you have room in your refrigerator for leftover.
Great place to bring our 13 and 6 yr. old kids! Service was just what I would expect in the South - tremendous! Food was good too.

Fat Salmon is a good sushi restaurant. No major complaints except that maybe the food is a bit pricey. 

There is a lot of peculiar special rolls that go beyond the standard dragon, Philadelphia and rainbow rolls. There are a lot of vegetarian rolls options like the kimchi-ya and the tofuholic roll. These rolls were not bad but I'd prefer to spend money on seafood. $10+ is a lot for a vegetarian roll in my opinion.

Compared to the other sushi restaurants in Philly, the sushi here is great. Appetizers are good. Adequate beer selections as well.

Overall, I recommend Fat Salmon for sushi especially if you are a vegetarian.

Skip this place. Bad food, not worth the price or hype. Can't believe I needed a reservation for such a bad dinner.

I have to say, our waiter was fine. However, our table was near the kitchen. Wait staff were constantly walking around us. Not a big deal, except that they bumped our table over and over causing violent shaking and drink spillage, not acceptable at around $100 per person. That being said, on to the "food."

I had the iberville salad, akin to a house Caesar with bacon. Good, but not great. My date had the tomato salad, which was good. We also split the fried oysters, not bad. 

For the main course I ordered the 12oz prime rib. It came out cold. I told the waiter, he brought it back to the kitchen to heat it up. The prime rib came back over cooked, tough, and cold. I sent it back. 

My date ordered the fish of the day. It was a crusted seared drum. It was also cold. She however, managed to choke down 1/4 of it. The $40 fish was no better than a McDonalds fish sandwich, except it was cold.

The restaurant did not charge me for the cold then burnt prime rib. This was a far cry from acceptable. The whole meal should have been comped. What a lousy excuse for a "fancy" restaurant. Do yourself a favor, skip this place, eat at Krystal burger down the street, it will only cost you $5 and the food will come out hot.  

All in, I spent $100 for a glass of wine and a couple of salads. I understand a kitchen mistake, but not three at one table. What a joke.
Yum,alpine cheese, beer, and dirty mussels! We were going to go to the city but glad we stayed local

I preordered a large room with a bath tub. When I arrived they said they upgraded me. I was really excited. When I got to the room it was a small room with no bath tub. When I ask the front desk how this was an upgrade she stated that it had more room. I stated I paid extra for the bath tub. They then told me the actual situation was that the hotel was overbooked and that the room I reserved was not available. When I stated I ordered and paid in advance. They said there is nothing they can do. So the reality is that they downgraded my room, lied to me, and told me there is nothing I can do about it. Pretty much they ripped me off with a smile.

Yeah ambience at this place is really really cool. It's good for groups it's also good for small couples. The drink specials are really nice and very good options as far as draft or a bottle beer hey Siri read text message

Ok so I ordered the empress shrimp..... Hot and sour soup was ok. Fried rice was ok. Crab Rangoon was ok but the shrimp..... Not so good. This is what I had to pick off to get to the small shrimp. I did leave some (about half) on my shrimp so you can only imagine if I had picked it off entirely. It originally made the portion look huge. Little did I know it was mostly fried batter.IMG_3254.JPG

The lunch specials are amazing ! Great big portions with great big flavor ! The price is very affordable and you'll definitely want to come back to sample everything ! The menu is extensive and offers so many options.  If you've got a group or family dining with you spring for the whole fish! Impressive plating and so delicious ! Also I saw a family come
In and order DIY spring rolls.  I'm not sure if it's on the menu but it looked fun and cool.  The table was served raw this sliced marinated pork or beef and grilled it themselves at the table leaving the whole restaurant smelling terrific ! When the meat was cooked it was wrapped up in rice paper with noodles and veggies and I'm quiet positive,by the looks on everyone's faces as they feasted, that it was very excellent !

I've been to Southgate twice now and I'm not going to stop. 

1. GET THE WINGS. Large portion, perfectly crispy, spicy is pretty spicy and they're a bit messy,  but they give you wet wipes.
2. Skip the buns. They were ok, nothing to write home about,  and you can do better (Bing Bing).
3. Try the Korean 76, the Korombian Punch, or the p&p.
4. Skip the white sangria and the ritten in the stars.
5. The bibimbap and hwe dup bap (basically a tuna rice bowl/salad situation) are good,  solid sized portions. Tuna is super refreshing.
6. End with the misugaru cake- like strawberry shortcake but the cake is a bit denser and not too sweet.

Service was great and you can make a reservation through Yelp Seatme. Great ambiance for a date, to catch up with a friend, or just grab a drink and a bite at the bar.  I hope they stick around and I hope they slowly integrate more traditional Korean foods onto their menu (pajeun, maybe some Korean soups/stews for winter?)

This little place was more than charming and just what we needed after walking through Midtown. 

I had the Roasted Turkey & Avocado Sandwich and it was amazing! It comes with fries or you can select another one of their sides in place but the fries were decent. The sandwich itself is served on wheat bread with the turkey and all the typical sandwich regulars along with the avocado. I didn't get the name of it but there is a white sauce that has a touch of spice to it sitting in the middle of the table with the BBQ sauces. I drizzled this sauce on the sandwich and it exceeded all expectations. 

My friend had the Chicken Fried Chicken which I called the chicken version of Shepard's Pie. It actually has the mashed potatoes, gravy & onion straws in a big mound on the plate. I luckily got a little taste of this as well. It was definitely as good as it sounds. 

We were in a group of 5 and everyone got something different but all enjoyed their food. The music was entertaining. The singer was Juliette Irwin during our visit and she was pretty good. The waiter was on point the whole time and even brought club soda unexpectedly to the table because he seen me wiping as spot off of my shirt. Now that is paying attention to your guests! 

Overall, this place is what you expect when you go sit down for a meal with friends. Unfortunately, this is not always what you get. A definite must try when visiting Nashville!!

Good food, but usually very slow service. On an average evening visit, food takes about 20 minutes to arrive. The wait staff sometimes ignore people waiting to seated, despite having tables available.

They have a good selection of healthy foods as well as snack foods with gluten free options, smoothies, coffee, and teas with a friendly staff and artsy atmosphere perfect for studying, reading, or script writing!

I tried out Aki for All You Can Eat.  According to their sign out front, it is now 7 nights a week (before it was only on certain days.)  For $25, you get a laminated sheet of choices that include your standard apps, rolls, nigiri, and hand rolls.  Nothing was bad, but nothing was amazing (not that I was expecting this.)  I actually really liked the hand roll option, as you don't see this that often.  The nigiri was relatively disappointing, as the sushi was not properly cut, wasn't pre-seasoned with wasabi, and was just average quality overall.  

If you're a "fancy roll" fan (I am not, generally) the AYCE option probably isn't for you, as the rolls are only standard 1 or 2 item rolls.  If you like handrolls however, it's a good deal.  If you're in a fat kid that likes sushi mood (which I often am) then Aki is a solid option.

Went to lunch here to try the chicken tenders, they are indeed delicious! I chose the sweet sriracha and creamy garlic sauces, both were orange in color and rather creamy, a good combination when mixed together.I ordered the zucchini fries based on all the mentions here. The fries were under cooked and somewhat soggy, I expected better. The serving size was bigger than the tenders. I'll be back for the chicken for sure. The meal with soda was about $9.

This place used to be a standby for our family. We could count on them for cheap, healthy, consistently delicious eats. They changed their name, but management & staff were supposed to be the same, so we didn't think twice about hitting them up for dinner the other night. 

Sadly, the food was terrible the night we went. My vermicelli bowl was full of limp, way past edible green onions & iceberg lettuce that was brown & tasteless like it was from a plastic package the was past its "sell by" date. The broth just tasted like salt & they didn't bring fish sauce until I found a server to ask. But the biggest disappointment was the vermicelli. It seemed like spaghetti instead of rice noodles. Maybe we just caught them on an off night, but I'm in no rush to go back.

My partner heard they were supposed to be good but this was awful for us. He called ahead to see if they could do no onions, guy on the phone said he could so we went there. Get there and they sit us at a table with a family already eating. Weird but I'll give it a chance. Waitress gives us menus and leaves for a good 10 minutes at least. Comes back and asks what we want. Go to order and she says "onions are on the side is that okay?", When we asked for no onions. I stress that it's an allergy. She says oh everything has onions so this'll be hard but I'll ask. I say don't bother we are leaving and we leave.

Basically a no go if you have allergies.

The place and the donuts, especially the Strawberry Lavender donut, were wonderful. The only downside is the price of the donuts. It's bit is on the pricey side. We paid $15 for half dozen donuts. I wish the cashier told us that one of the donuts we chose is more expensive than the rest so the total price will increase. In addition, listing the ingredients in each donut will be wise just in case if a person has any food allergy.

Love the happy hour (Mon. - Fri. 4pm-7pm): half price apps and pizza. I love the Portabella Mushroom strips and my husbands fave are the Spicy Chicken wings. The brew house salad is also one of my favorites, even though it's not part of happy hour. We didn't have them this visit but if you are a fan of onion rings, you gotta try these, they are HUGE!! 

All the Trailhead beers are good but tend to vary a lot from batch to batch. This time around both the Missouri Brown and the Trailblazer Blonde Ale were very good. 

We usually sit on the porch and the wait staff is usually good - never had real great service but we usually are there during their most busy time (6:30ish) which I'm sure doesn't help. This time we sat at the bar. The bartender started off great with service but after awhile just forgot about us. 

I would recommend this place for really good food and happy hour but not for great customer service.

We were here on Mother's Day for my wife and daughter.  The restaurant was very crowded but the wait was pleasant with comfortable seating.  We should have called ahead to get on the list earlier.  We each had a combo meal and drinks and the food was delicious.  The wait staff seemed to be a little new but no real issues other than the apparent newness.

Would  recommend this restaurant to anyone looking for a good meal and nice atmosphere although it is in a strip shopping center type building.  The inside makes you forget teh outside. There was outside seating but as usual Tucson weather (blowing dust) precluded sitting outside.

Today I was hungry thinking about fried pork chops. So I went when I got off work. Ordered the fried pork chops collard greens dressing side salad peach cobbler extra crust. The only thing that disappointed me was the pork chops. There's a sweet taste to batter. I wonder what is in the 12js spice rub. No spice there just sweet. Everything else great
Really good, thin crust; killer happy hour deals. I've been eating my way up and down Passyunk and this is definitely my favorite pizza thus far.

Great customer service.  Shayna was our server.  She was awesome!  Made great recommendations!  We had the brushetta which was yummy.  The pizzas are brick oven goodness!  We had the don with added ricotta and mushrooms. So good!!  Hubbs had the tiramsu with he loved.  This is definitely our new pizza place.

I was jogging on Linebaugh Ave and saw a sign for Ethiopian Food. It's on! My wife and I LOVE Ethiopian food and Mitmita Ethiopian Restaurant did not disappoint. We came at the start of dinner hours so it was quiet (not a bad thing). The place was clean and the decor added a cozy feeling. 
Being that I'm vegan, I was happy to see that they have a full page in the menu with vegan/vegetarian options. We split the Buticha for an appetizer and it didn't disappoint. Flavors of garlic really popped as we mopped it up with the Injera. 
I ended up getting the vegetarian combo (red lentils, split peas, cabbage, collard greens and beets). They were all good and portions were great. My favorite was the red lentils and collard greens! My wife got the Kay Watt and loved it. Great portion size and the berbere came through. The extra juice from the meat was great to soak up with injera!
The food is quality but Athena made the experience all the more special. She took the time to get to know us and we had great conversations! 
I would hands down recommend this to newbies of Ethiopian food. We didn't get to try their traditional drinks this time, but there's always next time!!
Good family restaurant with friendly people and great dinner time specials. Exactly what you would expect from a family owned restaurant.

My girlfriend and I went here for a late breakfast today, and absolutely loved it. We tried both the sweet and savory grits and they were absolutely delicious and super creamy. We then both ordered breakfast sandwiches and were very pleased with portions they gave. The bacon was nice and big, and was cooked perfectly (not too crispy!). The atmosphere was very cozy and inviting. This is absolutely my new favorite breakfast place around Phoenixville!

So excited to have finally eaten here! I'm always a little intimidated trying new places, but this one is very straight forward. Birria tacos have been pretty popular on social media, and I've been wanting to try it out. Luckily for me, this place is just down the road from me.

They offer sit down ordering with a waitress and a walk up counter to go. There are pictures of most the food, which makes it easier to order.

The food is reasonably priced and comes out fast. 

I will definitely be going back again in the near future.
Ordered the ocean salad and other things to go. Ocean salad had no seaweed in it like I it was supposed too. Of course. Didn't know till I i got home

Best meal I've had in Nashville over the past few months. We split the octopus appetizer, a pork chop entree, as well as a bucatini entree.

Everything here was well worth what we paid (which I would personally rate in the $$ category). Our waiter was fantastic and it was a truly great experience. I highly recommend this restaurant.

First time here, a Friday night about 7:45. We were seated quickly in a great spot, party of 4. Business gradually slowed while we were there, as in people were finishing up and leaving, and not so many coming in afterwards. Over half of the AYCE bar emptied out after about 20 minutes.  Our drunks and apps came quickly. Apps were ok Combo plate and Mussels.  Ordered dinner 2 meals, & all u can eat sushi. Dinner plates-chinese food plate and single roll plate came quickly....no all u can eat yet. 5-10 min later, miso soup and cuc salad after we asked...still no sushi. 

Next the other meals are halfway eaten....still no AYCE.  Now we find out after asking again, the order was lost or not submitted. We wait another 10 min, while receiving apologies from the server and manager. 

The really sad part is after all that, and we were politely patient, the Sushi was not great, taste and cost combined was not worth returning even if the service had gone as one would expect. Turns out our server was in training, and that was what got the blame for the serious delay. However, they should have had a better eye on him, and the manager freely discounted the bill (not by enough I think, but I did not complain.) 

The Chinese food was good, however they said there was no fried rice. I don't know if that means they were out or just don't have it on the menu.

Love that young boy, seems like the food tastes better when he's there.
Saw the commercial, give that guy with the gauges employee of the year, he works register and grill lol

Perfect hidden gem! If you have a chance to eat here definitely do it! The food was amazing, service was great and a awesome atmosphere. My husband had the chicken n waffles with their home made gravy, it was delicious! I had the steamed shrimp which were absolutely perfect! It's hard to find a place to do steamed shrimp the right way, topped with old bay's seasoning. Add a beer and the total bill was under $30. Couldn't ask for better food for the price. Will definitely come back next time we are in the area.

I was horribly hungover when I was coming back from a dog park with my pup. I needed something hearty to fill me up for a very late lunch, early dinner. I couldn't fathom the thought of cooking. 

What I was craving was bolognese and these guys have an awesome pasta bolognese dish. Very flavorful sauce, meaty, and seasoned perfectly. It hit the spot and helped soak up any beer left in me. The portion was huge and I was able to enjoy some the next day as well. 

I of course also had to try out their mozzarella sticks and I approve. It wasn't the typical crumbly breading but more of a tempura batter. I know they didn't make them themselves, but they too were delicious.

I Have been to Ceviche countless times and have never had a bad experience. My favorite Ceviche location hands down is in downtown St Pete and the main reason for this review. The food is great as well as the service. You cannot go wrong with the Solomillo Segovia (Wellington), Patatas Bravas (potatoes with aoili), Morrillo De Cochinillo (pork shank), Atun Estilo Tartaro (ahi tuna) and for dessert the Almenrado (almond pastry with vanilla ice cream and berries). I only give this restaurant four stars because the thought of the immaculate service and quality improving...really excites me.

I adore this place, the food is excellent and the ice cream is divine. I've been in many times and no matter how busy it is (and the place gets packed!) the service is always excellent. The decor is great and I love the overflow seating in the bar, really well designed for the high numbers of customers that come through. Pro tip - if you're going to eat there on a Friday or Saturday night, make a reservation!!!

This is the worst!!!
How any restaurant can burn a brownie when they heat it up in the micro wave should be closed down.
Yuck Yuck Yuck....

I love this place and have for the last handful of years, so I am surprised by some of the negative reviews. I have always had: 1) great service, 2) excellent beers, 3) really decent pub food.  I don't know what else to say! Went here again yesterday after seeing a movie at the cinema, had a Scotch Ale and a Brussel's Blond, and both beers were excellent. I also had the Southwestern Caesar Salad with grilled salmon, and once again, it too was very tasty.  I was sorry to see that they did not have their special lamb burger on the menu, but our very nice new waiter told us that it was a special on Wednesdays now....In the past I have had the salmon fish and chips and, again, very tasty, and I have had the Santa Fe chicken sando, and AGAIN...very tasty.

El Pescador is amazingly delicious! The environment is very appealing with the emphasis on marine life.  You will discover great food and service! Also, my favorite meal, Pescador relleno con mariscos, is absolutely the most delicious meal I've ever enjoyed!
   The consistent quality is impressive as well. My fish is swimming in incredible lemony butter cream sauce! It's been exactly as wonderful on my last visit as it was on my first.  When you consider the prices, high quality food, great atmosphere, ease of getting a table and the fact that they give you three dips for the warm chips I can't imagine a more excellent Mexican food dining experience!
   I've been there 5 times and will return every time I visit Reno!

For some reason I decided to "treat myself" by coming here and spending $50. i ordered the sirloin, it was dry and bland and  the dish looked like something that would be served in a hospital cafeteria. nothing on this menu is worth the price. nothing on this menu is worth putting in your mouth. wow I really hate this place.

The service and chai is great but the prices are similar to the overpriced starbucks - glad that the hours are long and they have free wifi but compared to the atmosphere and quality of my choice #1 cartel coffee and #2 raging sage, this is my third choice.

Food was unique and executed very well; I had the pheasant scrapple which was super.  Decor is open with lots of light.  Pricing was fair and accommodated both big and small budgets.  I was there for Sunday brunch which also featured a live band.  I thought the sound was great, maybe a little loud if you were hoping to chat with friends, but the band (bluegrass) was perfect for the setting.

Parking is not great, but nothing unusual for the area.

Have never had a bad experience at Thai Orchid. They are always quick and delicious. The yellow curry chicken is my go-to, but I'm sure everything else on the menu is amazing! Best spring rolls in town.

Best bagel I've had outside of NJ. Had bacon egg and cheese on bagel. There is a large selection of bagels. Really fast cook and price is good. Will have to go back to try patties and the muffins. 

Bring cash since it's faster due to credit card machine taking forever. Maybe isolated incident.

Taj is under new management. The food in this long-standing Edwardsville Indian restaurant was always good. The service, however, was at best uneven. That has changed dramatically. While the food remains excellent, the service is now remarkable. In our most recent visit, for example, the server remembered accurately all the dishes we had ordered in a previous visit. The menu has expanded, including more vegetarian offerings, as well as goat, lamb, and lobster. It also includes dishes that reflect the influences of the chef and his wife who are from Nepal and Afghanistan respectively. Dining at Taj is now an altogether great experience.

Local cafe. Nice place to meet friends for a quite chat or to have a nice casual lunch. Like they say not Cha mama but your always at home. 
Happy birthday to Tasha a server there. 
Hope u have an awesome day

I have to start by saying I've eaten here before and it was always good...never great but good. But the last two times we have gone here we have been disappointed. Very slow service and the owner/manager seemed not to concerned with are problem, that was the last visit and we said we won't be back due to the very poor customer service from the owner. Now lets talk about this visit. The place was very quit and we sat down and ordered right away. Oysters they were not to bad very small not worth the $14. We both had po boys  Philly steak and cheese was good but to much pepper. The other one was a crab cake po boy it too was good but was a bit dry and we ask for a bit more mayo, we were charged for it. It also came we side of rice it was not good at all cold hard and dry. to sum it up the food we had was not worth the $55 we won't be back.......

Went out for Valentines Day dinner with my boyfriend. Service was prompt and our server was very friendly and knowledgeable. They have a feature cocktail called The Savoy Shuffle that changes; this is what I ordered as it was a special for Valentines Day and I was not disappointed. My boyfriend had the Old Fashioned and he enjoyed it as well. We split the oyster appetiser (4 piece) which was good. I had the Brisket - I would highly recommend. My boyfriend had the Steak Frites which was also quite good. 

The reason I only gave Woodwork 4 stars is because of noise level of how close the tables are together.

I would definitely return. Can't wait to try more cocktails!

I had no idea when I decided to check out Basically Burgers in Doylestown that I would be entering a dilemma that required me to chose between fidelity to Yelp's creed of honest no-holds-barred reviews, and my understanding of the Golden Rule of treating people as I wish them to treat me. 

My morality tale began as a walked the center of Doylestown Borough on an incredibly beautiful early August afternoon. Temperature 78; Carolina Blue sky; galleon clouds sailing their airy seas.  Perfect day. 

My destination was Basically Burgers for a simple late lunch.  Yelp led me there, and I had every intention of ordering their best offering loaded with fried onions, jalapenos, and pickled sweet peppers. No cheese today to keep some semblance of austerity. Arriving, I noted the tables and chairs were bare bone, and a black and white mural on the wall that I took to be Doylestown. I wondered if Crayolas would be available to color between the lines. Given the high level activity on the street, I was a bit surprised that this joint was quiet and three quarters empty.  Hhhmmm....

The folks in front of me on line were four seniors who could not decide what they wanted. I took the opportunity to study the wall menu and figure out how to put together my slider sandwich.  Too complicated.  When my moment arrived, I was facing a kindly woman who took pity on my apparent ignorance and asked a few simple questions to lead me through the order process. 

I sat at a small deuce near the front windows admiring the ant colony that Doylestown had become.  The old folks were double dating, and sat at a quad front and center in the main window, chatting about their Medicare. I felt an involuntary shiver run down my spine at the prospect of sitting there one day. 

The burger arrived, delivered by the husband owner chef.  He slapped me on the shoulder as he walked back to the kitchen, with a, "..hope it's hot enough for ya;" referring to the chilis mounded on top of the double disks, and making a bed for them to sit on, as well.  I took a photo to memorialize my favorable first impression. 

It is a shame when great expectations are dashed by poor execution.  This was it.  I asked for a medium burger, but received well done.
