Little juice left to mix with the pile of fixins, making the first bite experience (FBE) disappointingly dry and with no taste aside from the onion and peppers.  I moaned silently.  I took the ketchup table rocket and shot a long stream of thin red sauce all over the sandwich in an attempt to resuscitate it. Marginally successful, I ate the rest grimly. 

The wife, cashier, waitress came by a few times to ask how I liked my food. She was so innocent and earnest. I smiled weakly. When I finished, I wrote the tip you see elsewhere on the website. 

Now comes the dilemma. 

On my way out of the bathroom I walked past the kitchen, where the chef caught my eye and asked again about the heat of the jalapenos.  I had no qualms with the peppers, so I honestly said they were fine, but I have a high tolerance for heat, and could have used more.  He pointed at another burger in front of him in a red plastic basket. "5 Alarm Burger, if you like 'em to roast your mouth." He listed all the hot ingredients and took out a bottle of his secret hot sauce. He would not let me touch it, but his sly smile told me that he was very proud of the nitro inside. I told him I would have to try it next time (Ugh. Conscience pang). 

Then, he asked me if I was still hungry?  Well, I wasn't really, but where was he going with this line of questions.  "Yes. I could eat," as any good boy would say to his favorite BBQing uncle.  Next thing - he offered me the 5 Alarmer gratis because it was a misorder.  

I was caught; hook, line and sinker. He was making a generous offer because he enjoyed our exchange.  Of course, I took it with a big smile and sat down to devour another double.  This one was actually pretty good.  Much tastier with all the chili varieties piled on, and the secret sauce torching my tongue. Still, too well done for me, but mine was not to complain in the face of unexpected acts of brotherhood and random kindness. 

So, do I write the review I intended to draft after the first burger, or after the second?  Do I allow this real story to influence what I say about this eating experience?  Or, do I just lay it all out for you, and let you draw your own conclusions, and perhaps use it in your sermon next Sunday?

I was hosting out-of-towners who wanted to experience The Hill and got a reservation here.  We arrived before our reservation for 6 at 6pm on a Sunday, and waited 70 minutes to be seated.  Another group of four who also had reservations at waited over an hour told us the host was seating people as they walked in instead of honoring reservations.  When we were seated, our server greeted us by complaining he was having to wait in on additional table.  The food was excellent!  We experienced a similar wait to pay, and a $11 antipasto dish we didn't order had mysteriously showed up on our bill.  There's too much amazing food in the area for me to go back (I was so embarrassed I brought guests there) but if you go a) don't trust a reservation and b) check your bill.

I went when it was empty so can't speak for the wait.

Was a big, big A Full Plate fan so had high hopes. 

The renovation is definitely great. The atmosphere is ideal for a bar. I would like to be at a place like this every night, just on vibe/decor alone. 

My favorite at A Full Plate was promptly ordered: The Turkey Sandwich. They been really lax on the portion of cranberry aioli lately, so I asked for extra! A must. So I got to say, they changed this sandwich a ton which was sad. Used to be a ridiculous portion of turkey and the bacon was curled and crispy, but not it was more just like a slab of thin/fried ham. 
Still an excellent sandwich though, but if you had the previous one from A Full Plate, you could be disappointed.

Other than that,
 Grilled Cheese and a Tuna Melt to die for. The fries also, amazing. 

Order the grilled cheese and tuna melt and split both with your date/friend. You will be so happy you listened to me that you will want to meet me and buy me a free meal here :)

I'm a breakfast gal, I can have breakfast anytime of the day! Yolk  is one of my go to brunch choices. Located in iron works, parking is abundant. Make sure to join the waitlist which is offered here through Yelp to beat the crowds! Staff is always friendly and if may suggest try their iced coffee it's addicting!

Overwhelmingly large portions (must share) and EXCELLENT service.  We will be back before every movie at the Foothills Mall.  I loved that they talked to us at the table and brought us extra olives without us even asking!

I am always on the hunt for places that have good chicken fried rice and they have it! Often I find places that have small, over cooked pieces of chicken but this was not the case here. I do tend to like a lot of chicken so next time I will order extra but only because that is how I specifically like it and not because it was hardly present. 

I also ordered the crispy spring rolls which I could go without next time. I found them to have very little filling compared to amount of wrap used, making the inside kinda mooshy. 

I ordered take out for lunch but they do have a sign out front that states they are open for dine in and take out, please note they are closed on Mondays.

Horrible service and super expensive. I was waiting 25 minutes for a turkey & swiss sandwich. on top of it, the staff were dealing with a customer service issue while I was sitting and waiting patiently as my sandwiches sat on the counter. First and last time going there. RT 70 Marlton, NJ locatio.
Great white fish salad on perfectly toasted bagel! Quick service with a smile and reasonablely priced to boot!

I arrived to the drive-through and ordered three black and tenders, he told me they only had five pieces when I open my meal it was regular chicken tenders I drove back around to the window and he told me they didn't have black and tenders I asked him why he didn't tell me that When I placed my order and his only response was sorry we don't have that and offered no solution or to remake my order.
The brisket and pulled pork were old and dry. Chicken was dry. Ribs were tender. Service was very good.

I went here for lunch, it was a decent sized place. 

The hummus appetizer was ok but wasn't impressed with the shredded vegetables (not easy to dip in hummus). 

I had their soup of the day. I suggest a cup because the bowls are huge!!! Generous portions.

The cocktail menu was small and not very impressive. The waiter had no suggestions. They should improve this to increase sales.

Wowowow this was the best sushi I've had in Philadelphia by far. Umai Umai is located just off Spring Garden Street. Its modern and intimate decor matched its equally modern take on Japanese food. I could not have been more impressed! 

I came with a group of 5 on a week night. Umai Umai is a BYOB (!!!) so plan accordingly. We ordered fried calamari, seaweed salad, rock shrimp tempura, and the oyster and sea urchin shooters to start. The shooters were excellent; we were instructed to pour the contents of the shell into the shotglass full of sauce, chew, and then swallow. For dinner, we ordered the 4-8-15-16-23-42 (shout out to any LOST fans), Henrietta, Eternal Sunshine, Godzilla, and a spicy tuna. The Godzilla, which contained shrimp tempura, avocado, macadamia nuts, strawberries, and honey, was my favorite by far! I would definitely recommend any of their "designer rolls". All that we tried were unique and delicious!

Amazing Indian food! After having some very disappointing food in the city, I was hoping to curb the craving and this place did the perfect job. 

They have the option of buffet or a la carte. The location is a bit awkward i.e. it is located in a deserted mall and the decor is alright with indian music in the background. The service was prompt and very helpful. The food was excellent. They had 3-4 meat dishes and the same number of vegetarian options. They have over a 100 beers to choose from as well. 

I loved this place and is definately recommended.

Really delicious. The cassava bits are worth a try (very delicious). Can't remember the name of the main dish I got, but I do remember the after dinner drink: Hot chocolate and cheese or Chocolate con Queso. I think the cheese was mozzarella. It takes getting use to and the first bites will make you instantly regret this order or that the staff is playing a prank on you because you don't speak Spanish, but once you commit to it, it's pretty good. If you're wondering how to eat it, it's as you would think: Scoop out the cheese and eat it. Kind of like a soup. It's a good order for cold weather.

On a rainy weekend afternoon I stopped in quickly before my shift at work. Cup of beef pho was incredible. The portion was great! Super filling. Had a green tea latte as well which was pretty good. 

I was able to sit and read comfortably. The decor is delicate and sweet. I will definitely be back!

I have to agree with everyone else. Suggested to us by locals. Giant line across the street was ridiculous. Walked right in and sit at the bar for the best chargrilled oysters I've ever had. Staff was friendly and attentive. They gave suggestions and tolerated all of our bad jokes. Came back for more a few days later at the end of our trip! People across the street were probably still in ine. I can't wait to come back and visit.

In short terrible service, and bad food.

I asked the bartender for bottled beer selection, and she asked me to walk back to the cooler and check it out myself. (Of course in a nice tone)

Being disappointed by the beer selection, I ordered a Stella in tap. It was a little flat. (And what is up with a 100 IPAs on tap?? People do drink ales and lagers.)

A margarita pizza has tomato sauce and fresh basil, neither of which could be found here. There was a disgusting amount of frozen melted mozzarella though. 

Don't know if the bartender was busy, but I heard a gasp every time I asked for something. 

Never going back and making sure friends aren't either

This is one of my favorite places to eat, the Zingers are really good although they usually need extra sauce on the side. One problem I have is almost every time I come here I order French onion soup because I love French onion soup, but sometimes it is way too salty.

Like all the other photos posted here of the sage chicken and bacon waffles, I decided not to show the same thing and just give my review. I died and went to heaven and Jesus sent me back....good laawd this was off the hook. The chicken was super tasty and not overwhelming with the flavor or sage. Very moist and just plain delish. The waffles were nice and crispy and it had bacon inside (my favorite). Prices were more than fair. Service was good. My picky son didn't like the fresh pressed apple juice and I was going to just pay for it anyway but the server brought him oj instead and didn't charge us for it which was nice. I will be back here before returning home Thursday....thumbs up

I normally love Jimmy John's and I am usually pleased with how quickly they complete my order. My experience at this Jimmy John's can be described as a polar opposite from the norm. It took almost 20 minutes for me to receive my sandwich even though there was only two other customers in the store. I did realize that they had some delivery orders, and I understand that this could have an effect on how quickly they operate, however, I was very disappointed. They market their company as being "freaky fast" and my experience can be described as "surprisingly slow". I was also confused as there was an employee walking around with hands in his pockets while three of his employees very obviously struggled to complete orders. It seems that it would be appropriate to jump in and help, but instead he watched as the credibility of this store tanked.
Pdq is always a quick, easy, and (can-be) healthy option for dinner.  Their sauces are amazing. I wish they would sell them!

This place is on point. They're definitely really busy, but you have the option of ordering online. The chicken was moist and super flavorful. Even my two-year-old would eat it. It was delicious. Must try in Nashville.
Great tasting Italian food, with a great lively relaxing environment to enjoy a great tasting meal at. Joy was our waitress if you come here ask to sit in her section. Great service

This place is the Old Spaghetti Factory of New Orleans. Outside it seems like a small, authentic restaurant with typical NOLA/Southern food, but inside it is enormous. 500 seats! They do serve all the typical southern dishes, but we didn't like anything we tasted. The blackened alligator appetizer was good, but everything else was dry and flavorless. I loaded my food with the hot sauce (which was surprisingly good!) to add some flavor. 
We did love our server, Alex, though! He was very friendly and the best part of our dinner.
Worst service. Miami has restaurants with better fried chicken and we are not even southern. If you like fried chicken dipped in salt water, this is the place to go.

When the wife and I discovered our hotel didn't do a full breakfast, we went to Jeannine's three mornings in a row. The hotel staff had recommended it, the Yelp reviews were predominantly positive, and it was a short walk away. I came here with high expectations.

Jeannine's was certainly a nice (if a bit too cutesy) place but I wasn't wow-ed: 
-- Being a bakery, I was hoping for some fantastic scones (an old weakness). But Jeannine's had only very basic flavors (e.g. plain, blueberry, lemon) and the selection was the same every single day. I have come to expect more creativity than this. (local fruit? interesting combos?) But no. Yawn. I couldn't find one that appealed to me.
-- Many of their signature dishes rely on a slathering of hollandaise sauce, but I've just never been a fan (I'm a mutant, I know).  Plus it feels like cheating.
-- Prices are high here, yet food must be ordered at the counter (aka via a line). Seems like such a high-falutin' spot could afford some actual waitstaff.

That said, it wasn't terrible. My standard, two-egg breakfast used high-quality ingredients and was cooked just right. The setting was attractive, the coffee was good and the staff were reasonably friendly.  

The only food downside was the huevos rancheros special, which was super-boring and bland. (I switched back to the 2 egg breakfast on my third visit.)

Rating is tough. Between 3 and 4 stars for me, but since Jeannine's enjoys a golden reputation and a solid 4-star rating on Yelp, I'm feeling like they are overrated. 3 stars it is.

We stopped into Shoo Fry on a whim as we were walking home late at night. The poutine sign caught our eye and we immediately stopped. The goat cheese with pepper jam sliders were amazing and unique! Jerk chicken poutine comes with a mound of shredded chicken and you could tell everything was extremely fresh. The staff was up beat and made sure everyone was having a good time and received their food quickly. This is a great spot for a quick lunch/dinner or late night snack!

Usually the food here is ok, thou somewhat overpriced in comparison to the multitude of good seafood restaurants  in. this area .  I ate here today due to a friend's  grandson's request. I had the coconut shrimp appetizer which were good, fresh tasting . My entree was crab cakes topped with shrimp.  It was gross looking , super tiny slivers of slimy  crab  mushed together  topped by by 4 half raw shrimp .  Not even sort of close to being a crab cake,  & I have eaten many in quite a few restaurants . It tasted fishy & disgusting . $18.99 for this crap?  I will never go to Red Lobster again,  with so many competent seafood  restaurants around, they should be ashamed.

Note to Marlton Diner: even when you were at your best (5-6 years ago), you were never as good as this place.  My family ordered from all over the menu--from breakfast burritos with chorizo sausage to a French dip roast beef sandwich to stuffed French toast to a jumbo burger deluxe to roast turkey dinner. Everyone was very pleased with the meal and the service and left the table feeling full (despite not ordering any appetizers or desserts).  We all agreed that we should come back again, and soon.

The food here was pretty good. I'm vegetarian, and they had a whole bunch of choices for vegetarians. I went there pretty late and they were nice to accommodate us. 
Their falafels were delicious, but wasn't happy with the hummus. (May be they had a bad day). I've had better hummus and Mediterranean food. I come from out of state. 
The reason for 2 stars, is because of the way we were treated. Chef Maurice was initially kind enough to talk to us and explain the specials they had. And was raving about being the best (may be they are in that 50 mile radius). We were 3 people, and we wanted to order two appetizers , one entree and dessert. We are pretty light eaters and we weren't super hungry and also didn't want to waste food. 
But chef Maurice insisted that we order one appetizer per person, and was saying that it doesn't workout for them and stuff. Which I felt was a bit ridiculous. 
The exact words he said " people come here and share the food, and you guys tip only for the food you order, my men here won't like serving 3people and get less tips, if you're not hungry, then why not come next time when you are hungry". I felt that was a bit racist. 
That's not how you treat customers. If he can't deal with people ordering how much they want, and can't do business from that. He probably should be learning from the business running right across the street from him instead of raving about the best Mediterranean food and having 5stars etc. 
I wanted to walk out of that place, but my dad insisted staying back since I had driven 4 hours to get to Reno. 
Nonetheless we ended up ordering one appetizer and two entrees. And i left a pretty hefty tip even though we were insulted by him and the food was just above average. 
I wouldn't go back here because of the way they treat customers. And if anyone who's reading this, be prepared to be "not treated" well. 
They call themselves a fine dine, but I'm almost positive they have no idea what they're talking about. I've been to a lot of fine dines, and I know how they treat customers.

The staff is awesome here; they're so nice and welcoming! The food I would say is a solid B. The only critique I have is to rely far less on the fish oil. I can taste it in the chow mein, the vegetables, everything. The one dish I will never get again is the sesame chicken. It was scrawny little pieces of chicken overpowered by fried crap, and drowning in sauce. 
Great place for convenience. Okay for food.

The food which we received was good but not great. Our salad came after other things, and one of our ordered items did not appear at all, though it was on our check. Our waitress did take the item off the check (this took a long time) and did apologize.

Servers were friendly, but inattentive. I never did receive a drink refill.

The dining room was clean, with a mixture of high-back booths and regular tables. The booth I sat in was somewhat wobbly, so that every move made by the person in the next booth shifted the seat back about.
I love this place and whenever I'm on Davis Island I pop in. Great menu with a wide variety of items. I love the Field of Fruit with Salmon. Healthy and delicious.
Angelo was very nice and greeted me with a smile! Everyone was super friendly! Love the pizza but will now have to dine in!!!

They started with giving us 2 menus for 4 people without asking for our drinks while the restaurant was not busy (at the time) and then we waited 15 minutes to get waters...as it got packe just to get drink orders. We decided to order everything at once to stop the nonsense of waiting. Then they were out of 3 main dishes...one of which i came here for. Food was good but not enough MEAT. Had to ask for Sriracha twice!!!!spicy prom belly wasn't that spicy. And water...is it self-serve
Had the seafood dinner and I am seafood fanatic. Do not eat if you ever have had real seafood. Fake crabmeat does not do very well with me. However my husbands steak he says good.

You know that feeling you get when you drive up to a restaurant and there is no one in the parking lot?  Yeah, that was mine too but I trusted my Yelpers. Good thing!  This place is a gem in the middle of Belleville.  I tried  the Cm Tm Đc Bit for the first time and wow, I may never eat Pho or Bun again. Ok, maybe exaggerating on that but this dish was the phenomenal. If you mash the egg into the broken rice and drizzle fish sauce on it and the crisp pork, you are in for a treat. My waiter suggested I put the meat cake ( yes I said meat cake. Think of it as vietnamese meat loaf.  Mystery meat adds to the adventure ) in the fish sauce to soak with the slices of pork and pig skin.  Amazing. My favorite place in town now.
Had another pizza tonight and it was AWESOME! Thank you for being the BEST in the area!

Recently just found this spot and am amazed it's never ended up on my radar until now-- it's so absolutely delicious! So far I've tried a pepperoni Sicilian (cheesy heaven with light sauce on top of a buttery delicious dough), a classic NY style pizza which was absolutely perfect and made how it should be  and a cannoli. I'm now on a mission to try all desserts and food

this place is awesome.  very spacious, cool ambience, nice to sit among the brewing vats, plenty of windows, ,great location(bring change for meters, but plenty of spots).  Went to lunch today(4/30) with 4 co-workers.  
I have been a fan of the brewery since they opened, some of the best and more adventurous beer styles anywhere, and the adjectives used in describing the beer is part of the fun(dank, barnyard, herbaceous green stuff, fresh cut grass, etc..)  
Menu is fairly limited, no appetizers to share that we could tell, no big deal, I expect the menu will grow in time.  We all stuck with the tacos and there was not one complaint from anything.  I asked our server(Kenya) which was the most 'extreme' taco, she suggested the mushroom taco.  She was spot on with her recommendation, it was delicious.
My only 'complaint' is that the menu is kind of pricey, $9-10 for 2 tacos, not terrible but probably could have used one more taco on the plate to really satiate my appetite and wallet, but I certainly wasn't starving when I left. 
I look forward to this location growing in time and expanding their food menu.  No questioning the quality and taste of the beer, "it saul goodman".  I will definitely be back!  Nice work!

Went their for a aged steak on Monday 2/5/13 from Clearwater hooping to experience the unique aged steak and got good steak but nothing as tasty as my New York Wolfgang's Steakhouse experience even dough the prices wore high, i expected to get what i paid for. The main reason I'm writing this one star review is the service. The waiter was nice and polite but no connection with guests he knew his "speech" by hart when representing their pricey menu but was late with our focaccia bread for witch we asked the manager and another waiter/busboy who give us an answer like "The Cook its busy and it may take a minute or five"  than i lost my pittance while my $46 dollar steak was getting cold. The atmosphere is nice but in the restaurant like that I expected at least my friends $74 dollar steak to be served in a nice dish instead of plain cheap oval dish.Te tables are covered with a paper cloth witch i believe saves on laundry expense.
Overall One star for Service and Two stars for food and one star for cheap plates and paper tablecloth.
At the Presentation steak's look Big but when they bring it on your Plate they are almost half in size, I do understand that they lose size when grilling but not at least 40%  !!!!!!!

We had an amazing late lunch at this Bluewater Grill location with our Adored Grandson about a month ago. The weather was perfect for sitting outside, and we were lucky enough to snag seats at their indoor- outdoor bar upstairs. 

With a killer view of the pier and the beach, it is a premiere spot on the refreshed waterfront area where State meets Cabrillo.  Swaying palm trees frame a vista that made us feel like we were on a tropical get-away, without the hassle of boarding a plane. 

Top-notch, professional and friendly service provided the basis for a great dining experience.  As the designated driver, I appreciated the mix of fresh juices they whipped up for me, to add to the vacay vibe.

The kitchen kept us happy with fresh takes on seafood options.  Even 16 year old AG noted how well done everything tasted, and was presented. Dear Hubby and I shared an order of sand dabs and scalloped potatoes, with a crunchy slaw on the side.  Fabulously delicious!

Can't wait to return for the whole experience to be repeated.

Three stars due to the fact that we were misled by our waitress on the vegetarian dishes and also by the time it took to create a three ingredient bar drink. 

We asked our waitress for vegetarian options and she recommended the beets and cauliflower, so we ordered both. The beets came and we loved them!!! Guys...hours of vomiting later we discovered that there was bacon in the beets. Being vegetarian is not a dietary issue, it's a health issue. So disappointing. 

Further, having one drink arrive FIFTEEN minutes before the second did (for our party of two), was upsetting. On a Saturday night you should have a well equipped bar tender and bar back on duty. 

Last - this is not a destination as one thinks it is. If your name is Vista Ramen: do ramen well. Having FOUR ramen dishes is not enough. You must also succeed in sides and services. Tonight, that didn't happen. Happy to be asked back to prove us wrong.

Overall, food was excellent.  Tasty, fresh & eclectic.  5 Stars

BUT.....  service was abysmal.  Non attentive.  Had to ask for silverware.  Had to ask for water.  Had to ask for win refills (I bought bottles)... 

I almost walked out

Food is $$$$$$...... wine list is $$$$$$$$$.....  cheapest bottles are $70 range. 

Bottom line, when spending $200 per person (pre tip) it should rock.....  i spent $1,000 for 5 of us ..it didn't. 

I'll never return....

My first time here and I will be back! The steak was the best I've ever tasted and most tender! The tortellini was incredible! We were very well taken care of! My empty dishes were promptly removed and everyone working was really on the move ! Best customer service I've had anywhere! What a great experience! Happy early Valentines date to us !

One of the best when it comes to cheesesteaks here in Philly. If you have a friend from out of town and they want to try a Philly Cheesesteak, take them to Leo's. Forget about those other spots in South Philly. Take the drive to this place!
Loved it, makes me wish I lived closer! Great coffee and food in a cute cozy cafe, definitely worth stopping by!

Putting the word "Bear" into the name of your business and using a Bear paw print to market the name of your business will almost always catch my attention. Growing up in Michigan where Black Bears are part of the local culture - they are insinuated and woven into my psyche - which means I like 'em! Black Bears, Grizzly Bears, Teddy Bears...

As most of the other reviewer's mentioned - the interior of this place looks and feels like a Panera Bread. Even in my groggy, un-caffeinated state of mind early on a Sunday morning - I recognized this.

The layout, the fireplace, the placement of the drinks area - all like a Panera. Nothing wrong with that - it felt very cozy. And there is free Wifi.

They don't offer close to the same variety of a baked goods selection as Panera though. The guy at the register acknowledged this - but then also offered a "plus" differentiator for them - they have an actual grill in their kitchen.

The coffee was very good - I opted for the "Montana Blend." Good and strong.

If I had to do it over again, I would have stayed and tried some breakfast food, but my brain was not yet firing on all cylinders due to low caffeine levels. Will have to try it out for breakfast next year when I return for the next Scottish and Irish Music Festival!

We decided to go back to Bait to see if it was just as good as the first time we went or if it was a fluke.  It was just as good as the first time and I can't wait to go back.  As I've said before, make reservations or you will possibly have a long wait for a table.  They do not rush you at all.  Remember they have valet parking and when the weather gets nicer, they will have some outside seating.  We started out with cocktails (the pear margarita for me) and looked over the menu.

He decided to go with the Thai chili wings.  I did not try one but they looked outstanding and he said they were delicious.  I tried the oyster trio.  Three oysters prepared three different ways - black & bleu, spinach parmesan and roasted garlic & mignonette.  They were all good but I thought the last type was best.  My main was a special that evening, the Chilean sea bass.  It came with clams and fingerling potatoes.  Talk about melt in your mouth.  He decided on the lobster roll.  It came with French fries and was served the way they do in Connecticut - with butter.  We did do dessert which I believe was the lemon tart cheesecake.  Great way to end the meal.  

Would I come back here?  Of course, I need to try the seafood boil.  If you see me there, stop by and say hello.

TVs galore. Man, I am not a fan of this trend of putting TVs at the table. Don't we all complain that we don't talk enough. Yes, it's a sports-bar-eaque establishment and maybe I don't get that but it's a little too much. That being said the firepit is pretty awesome---I approve of that. Service here was spectacular especially considering how busy it was. I'm more likely to go to some place like Kilroys for a similar experience. (I'm not a fan of family friendly establishments when I'm downtown. I want to drink my cocktail in peace, thank you.) I think the food was a big overpriced for what it is. I think I paid $10.99 for three bourbon tacos and some waffle fries---none of which really hit the spot. My Margarita was decent but I don't know how one can mess that up. Overall not really impressed with the food and way overwhelmed by the TVs. Personally I'd go elsewhere but if the above floats your boat, you'll get lots of menu options and good service.

With such rave reviews I was excited to give this place a try for takeout. Unfortunately this meal left us underwhelmed and spiced out. Maybe we just got them on an off night, but the whole meal was fairly disappointing.

Garlic Naan- 1/5 very firm and chewy, garlic was raw, and flavor and texture were subpar
Milagu Rasam- 1/5 way too aromatic. The bottom third of soup was spices.
Gobi Manchurian- 5/5 delicious! Sauce had a surprising kick and cauliflower was fried and sauces to perfection. Our group's favorite item by far!
Basmati Rice- 5/5 perfectly cooked and seasoned!
Lamb Vindaloo- 3/5 sauce was good and surprisingly spicy. We ordered hot and it definitely delivered! Potatoes were great but lamb was pretty dry
Butter chicken- 4/5 sauce was incredible. Hard to go wrong with butter chicken but the chicken was extremely dry
Saag Paneer- 3/5 sauce was creamy and flavorful but paneer cubes were extremely dense
Vegetable Dum Biryani 1/5 We ordered it to be mild and this was overwhelmingly spicy. It was 80% rice with a few sparse peas and carrots. 

The overall theme of the meal was great sauces, too much spice, and overcooked proteins. I've had better Indian food in the area but I'm hoping we just got them on an off night.
Love this bakery. On the weekends they offer a delicious vegan brunch for a flat fee. They are very friendly and accommodating with small children. We love the upstairs library.

Took my in-laws here who came all the way from Japan. They gave us the driest meat I suppose because we looked like tourists or something. Could get better ones in the suburbs, maybe even Subway. Totally overrated or are just racist dumbasses.

I had heard nothing but good things about this new addition to the east end of Mass Ave and was happy to find that Mimi Blue doesn't disappoint.

The menu is simple...you pick your meatball (beef, classic, veggie, and turkey), then pick your sauce (bolognese, marinara, spicy cilantro, mushroom, and creamy). Our server was kind enough to give us samples of each sauce to try and all were very good. I ended up going with a mix of turkey and veggie balls with the cilantro and cream sauces. The turkey was very nice...not too dry either. I wasn't as satisfied with the veggie, but I think it's because meatless meatballs just seems sacrilegious.

We opted for sides of their Mac 'n Cheese and the roasted bell peppers. The nice thing about the sides is that you can choose to have your balls served on top of any side.

The restaurant setup is interesting with the kitchen window exposed to the general dining area. I'm not a huge fan of this layout as it can be a little distracting as a customer, especially when the GM and owner are standing about getting in the way of their staff. But, this is only a minor issue.

Overall, I think this is a great place for a date or to take friends out for a nice evening.

Village Whiskey is Philly's best burger....by far. They make the best hamburgers I have ever had, the prices are good, and the restaurant itself is a little cramped inside, but charming and decorated. The wait staff and bar staff are great and knowledgeable. Unfortunately, it's hard accommodate a large group here because of the size of the physical space. At lunchtime though while the weather is nice, there are some outdoor tables that can work for larger groups. The cocktails and the beers here are great. The whiskey selection here is impressive, bordering ridiculous. The duck-fat fries are great. Any of the house-made appetizers or pickled items are fantastic, I am partial to the pickled cherry tomatoes. The burgers are flavorful, juicy, perfect, delicious, and yum! Don't waste your money on the "whiskey king," I was accidentally given one of these on my 4th visit here...and frankly all that crap on top of the burger just ruins it. If you just get the plain burger for $9, with the basics that come with it, you will be impressed. Thats right, you can eat here on the cheap....a burger and fries is all you need to experience the best this place has to offer. I don't know about the other entree items other than the burger, and I don't really care to know about them either. As mentioned, the appetizers/snacks are a great if the burger and fries isn't enough food for you. Love this place.

day 60...

is it bad to admit that you drink all the left over au jus???

Went here for lunch with my boyfriend and his aunt on a Saturday. Dining room was cozy, service was good, and the food was affordable. Although there was a "bread bar" our server didn't direct us towards it or even mention it. Guess she didn't think we needed bread to go with our lunches? Also when we were there the women's restroom toilet was clogged. It hadn't been brought to their attention but was fixed within five minutes!

I'm not yet sold on Pier 48, but they have a few things going for them. First, the seafood is fresh and is flown in daily - a must in landlocked corn country. I've had oysters here multiple times (fresh and their char-grilled oysters) and they've been fantastic every time. What I'm not sold on are the drinks and the non seafood options. The cocktails are iffy and the bartenders don't all know how to make basic drinks (for example, a tender had to ask her boss how to make a sazerac) and the drinks are too sweet. They carry a lot of Deep Eddy if that gives you an idea of what I mean. The only meal I've had there really was the burger week special - a burger with lobster, Peanut butter, and some other stuff. This thing wasn't good. Peanut butter has no place on lobster. When I ordered I figured it would actually be a more savory peanut sauce (think African or Thai cuisine) but it was a literal smear of Jiffy (or, tbh considering the sweetness Peter Pan). I didn't even finish half. The burger meat itself was flavorless. 

I will return for oysters but I'll skip on the rest!

We had breakfast here today.  This place was recommended to my by someone in the neighborhood.  Bacon, eggs, potatoes, and toast for $10.  High quality bacon and the potatoes had peppers and onions in them.  

Great job!  

I will have to come back for lunch one day.

This place has service/ ethical issues.   First time I ordered thy added an $8 tip instead of a $3 tip...this time I ordered and paid for an 18" extra late only to come home and find a medium 15" pizza in the box.   Seemed like an owner might have even been working...  anyway I'm not ordering from here anymore unless the owner admits fault for this
The hype is real. Best fried chicken I ever had. Come when it opens and ask for Tasha. She is the best NA.
Nice Italian Restaurant along the Gulf Blvd. Our server was very good, very friendly and knowledgeable. She made us feel really special

Great lunch! 2 people in my party got the Cuban and raved about it. One person got the burnt ends sandwich and said it was excellent.  Brisket sandwich was great too. We got the nachos too and while a bit spicy they were delicious!
Service was great and the whole staff was super friendly!

After conversing with V where to go to dinner, we decided on Ikkyu. It is 10 minutes from my place, yet I didn't know it existed. V had high hopes on this place. Panda Express would have been a better choice. It wasn't that the food was bad, or the place was dirty, or the service lacked....but the food was average at best....V didn't enjoy her soup....my beef bowl was average...the Diet RC was good though! Don't get me wrong, the prices are awesome, and the food that I ordered was plentiful....I just expected more from the reviews I read. When I eat oriental food...even at Panda...it has tastes you can recognize and that are pleasing....what I had last night was about what I would have ended up with if I had cooked myself...I am a decent maker of food....and would have been thrilled to replicate thier meal....but I expect more flavor from a restaurant...it just wasn't there. I will go back with V, and try something else though, everyone deserves a second chance.

This place is a true gem! Has a great variety in Greek products for very fair prices! The owner has always been very friendly and accommodating 
to me! Very happy I can find all these products without having to leave Philadelphia!

I want to start by saying the ambiance of the place is great with live music and the decor is for a good date night BUT I was in disbelief to sit at high top table for a group of 4 we were all charged a instant gratuity that no one informed us of before placing our reservation. Plus what makes matters worse half of the group got sick from eating the food the next day.

Food was really good, we will be back.
Tommy and the rest of the staff were extremely helpful. We tried everything they recommended and it was good.

Wow. This place meets the hype hands-down. First off - I love the neighborhood south Philly Barbacoa is in. It's a super authentic and interesting street.

They are juicing fresh fruit outside of the restaurant and when you walk in you can see them pulling out huge chunks of Pork and lamb Barbacoa that's protected by cactus leaves.

We ordered a half kilo of the mixed lamb and pork. I think this is the best way to eat their tacos because they come with a fresh pile of tortillas, cactus salad, jalapeños, fresh onion, and cilantro. It also comes with two bowls of consommé, which was incredibly delicious and one of the highlights.

While we were waiting for our food, the man preparing the meats made a fresh taco for me with just the pork meat. It was insanely good, and an experience for sure.

Each item that came to our table was so simple but so perfectly executed. The pork and lamb Barbacoa was outrageous. The fresh corn tortillas were amazing. The hot sauces at the table were perfection. Nothing could have improved.

I will never come to Philly without wanting to come back. Easily one of the most satisfying and delicious meals I've ever had, all for $35.

They are not closed, just changed their name. 

I've eaten at a ton of Korean BBQ places and this one is by far top 5! So many choices on the menu for the bbq and a Korean side and sauce bar. A must do every time I visit FL.

Recently I went to the new Maple Hill Restaurant in Maple Shade, NJ. Until recently I didn't even know the New Maple Hill Restaurant existed.

Atmosphere: 
When I arrived around dinner time, it wasn't too busy. The outside is a cute, building with hanging lights. It reminds me of walking into a house versus a restaurant.

The inside has a small bar and a couple of rooms. It does echo, and you can hear every person's conversation in the diner.

Coffee: 
The coffee was good and brewed hot and fresh. It wasn't anything unusual, but it was good.

Food: 
The New Maple Hill Restaurant has plenty of options from all day breakfast, sandwiches, and dinner options.  It looks like a typical diner with simple options, but there isn't anything unique or special on the menu.

I decided to order off their specials menu: Pumpkin Pancakes! When they came out, nothing about them was good. They didn't look appetizing, and they were paper thin. It was shocking they were a special because I could have cooked better pancakes myself.  I found myself hungry afterward.

Service: 
Our waitress was friendly and friendly but came around. We could have used more refills.  Our food came out relatively quickly.


Overall Thoughts/Would I come back?

I didn't enjoy my food. If I go come back, I would definitely order something else.
The food was amazing, and Joe, our server was super friendly and fun to be around. All of the staff wore masks, and hand sanitizer is available throughout.

I have my reservations about Reno, but in any case I was here over the weekend at the Grand Sierra (along with 3000 of Nevada's Democrats who were here for the state convention-- fights broke out, let's leave it at that) cause the pops had a seminar for his Mitsubishi MU2. We had a party of 8 here and I was pleasantly, pleasantly surprised by both the food and impeccible service at Charlie Palmer.

Among the things ordered amongst our table was the porterhouse for 2 @ $85-- very supple and rich, the hawaiian tuna-- one of the best I've had, and I've had PLENTY of seared tuna...this is probably the safest bet on the menu, another had the crispy duck breast which didn't seem shabby at all. For sides, they have a proper variety from the usual sea scallops to a sashimi salad. Also, they have a large selection of sides including mac & goat cheese.

Service was phenomenal, we were seated within a minute, no complaints here.

I'd give it 4 stars but the past five times we've tried to eat there, they've been closed despite the message on the phone saying they are open.  

Tonight was the last chance.  They've lost our business.  Lousy way to run a business.

We held a 80+ person party at Amber.  The food was not bad but the service was horrible.  The staff and the owner's attitude is that they are doing you a favor by having you there.  We asked for more tea first they refuse to serve after some argument they told it will take 1.5 hours.  I understand there are not too many options for Indian food in Carmel but given the experience we had, I will not go back to the place and not recommend it to anyone.

First time we came on a Sunday. We got the fried catfish, Mac n cheese and collard greens...Also a sample of potatoe salad and the specialty lemonade.  Everything was delicious even after we heated up our leftovers the next day!  I vowed to return because the lunch special smothered pork chops, rice and gravy and candied yams were highly recommended by a co worker.  Went today for that lunch special and again everything is delicious again! My next trip will be for the ribs which seem to sell out quick ( a good sign to me :) Being that I'm not from the Tampa area I'm excited that I found an exceptionally excellent soul food restaurant! I will be a repeat customer and highly recommend this establishment to others! P.S...someone lied and gave a bad review on the candied yams because they are very good and remind me of my grandma's recipe

They have very bad customer service. Ronda is very matter of fact and rude. They want your money in advance but will not go out of their way to please the customer . I would not recommend using this business.

Authentic Mexican and great prices.  Margaritas mix is a little tart, but the food is very good,  I would like to see the atmosphere there be enhanced, they've got something just need to push a little more to compete with Casa Tina

Uncle nicks makes by far the best buffalo chicken pizza in this city! My second favorite is the Turkey Hoagie! Uncle Nicks is definitely worth a visit if you don't live in the brewery town area and if you do live here this is a place you should be eating at now!

Went for Sunday brunch with my brother and daughter. Each of us ordered the "eggs your  way". Two of us had the scrambled with bacon; one had over easy with sausage. Everything was delicious! Creamy scrambled eggs that weren't dry and overcooked- an unusual occurrence! Crispy bacon and perfectly cooked over-easy eggs. All came with super good red potatoes. Presentation was very nice and made it even more appetizing. Sourdough toast was a nice, unusual touch. Good coffee, very nice atmosphere. We weren't ignored and we weren't rushed either. Can't wait to head back and sample the cookies and sweets offered in the case!

Hands down one of the best sandwich stops to exist. It's so great to have a place on this side of town to enjoy. The staff gives off a terrific vibe. One employee in particular, Blake, sure knows how to make a spicy sandwich! Not to mention, the place is  always extremely clean. I will visit again and again. Love this place!!! 



P.S. The pickled popcorn is d-lish! Give it a try.

Their grilled chicken teriyaki bowl is the best! I really like how you can order ahead of time and your food is ready for pick up, really convenient. The workers are also really friendly. I've always driven by here and I had never noticed this place until now. I'm really glad a friend of mine brought me here.
Best local coffee place in Santa Barbara and Goleta. Very cozy and special treatment from staff. Whatever coffee you choose it's always great tasting. A definite stop when caffeine rush is needed!!

Lived up to every review and more. Went on a Sunday afternoon at 430. Waited in line for 25 min. The charbroiled oysters are an absolute must. Had the new Orleans medley which consisted of the jumbalaya(very good), gumbo (alright), red beans and rice (good). Soft shell crab was also very good, however if you aren't partial to salt this might not be the dish for you. An absolute must if in the French Quarter!

Really fun and different menu- we had four different appetizers bc they all sounded so great! In order of our faves:

Stuffed portabello- I coulda had 6 of these bad boys. So much flavor and cooked perfectly.

Buffalo cauliflower- wanna have deep fried chicken wings but don't feel like being a major fatass? Here you go.

Goat cheese balls- you had me at balls. And cheese. Oh and fried. Yes please.

Brie pastry- cheese? Good. Dates? Good. Pastry? Good. Together? 

Overall really neat space with fantastic music- I look forward to return
I was blown away by both the quality and quantity of the food we received. Simply an amazing place, though very busy when we were there.

This place is awesome, great beer selection and decent prices. And competing with a monster like the Foodery has to be rough. From what I saw the staff was quite friendly and knew a good amount about the beer in the store. However, the only reason I didn't give them 5 stars is because of the rarity of beers they do not have. Compared to the Foodery they have a selection you can find anywhere in the city. But, the cheap prices for this place will keep me coming back! 

Ps the cheese guy from the Farmers Cabinet relocated to the kitchen for Bottle Bar East. This dudes the best!! Whhazzup cheese man!

Um....wow. This place has the best burger I have had in a very long time, Maybe ever. The beer selection isn't anything fancy but what they do have hits the spot. I am always a fan of Guinness on tap.

The menu promises the Bob to have garlic, Worcestershire and soy sauce. Every flavor can be tasted in every bite without overwhelming the taste of the juicy beef. Add some mayo, onions, tomato and lettuce and you're in juice running down your arm heaven. This burger is not for the faint of heart! Keep your pantie  hose at home because you will get messy.

The staff were very friendly and attentive, however, the patrons were a little sketch. It shouldn't bother you if you don't mind hearing right wing bullshit. It was 5 o' clock on a Friday, so I expect the hardcore alcoholics are gone by the time more open minded youngsters start to come in.

We got the soup dumplings and pan fried dumplings (total was ~13)..prices are reasonable. I really liked the soup dumplings (crab). Usually I have to go to nyc to get them but this place has decent ones. Juicy and flavorful...comes with 6 of them. The pan fried dumplings were ok. I'd come back to try the other dishes since it's pretty cheap.

This place is basically where the old tea magic used to be, looks the same inside, pretty clean. Friendly service.

Only staying 1 night before boarding on a cruise ship, so wanted a restaurant within walking distance from our hotel. Decided on this restaurant for a party of 5. After a short wait, we were seated and all enjoyed our meals. From seafood to steaks, pork chops, Italian food. Such variety to please all. Service was great too.

We visited for dinner while on vacation in NOLA. In my opinion, our server made it extremely obvious that she didn't plan on giving us proper service being we were a group of 6 young people. 20% gratuity was added onto the bill. 

I ordered the spaetzle entree minus the quail eggs. It was pretty good, but tiny. Wouldn't recommend - it's not worth the price and isn't filling.

Thank you very much for great service! Calling to order was easy and the delivery guy was very polite.  Everything was packed with care, no smashed food or spills.  I'll be ordering from you guys again very soon!

As a first-timer, I went for the least spiciest chicken and it was delicious! So we know the chicken is wonderful, but let's talk side dishes: baked beans, Southern Greens, and Black eyed Pea Salad were all amazing. Finished off with delicious Sweet Tea and all at great value for money. Definitely is a "chicken dinner winner!"
the usual casino with all the likes of others..  just come here to lose a little money.

Dropped in like two weeks ago while visiting Florida.  Had the Jackson Street burger and cheese fries.  My waitress leann recommended them.  So good great suggestion from a great waitress.  Excellent service Excellent food definitely helped me enjoy my trip. I'll be back
Seriously when you go ask for Leann.

The wife and I have been wanting to try Rick's Reef for quite sometime, but every time we arrive it is PACKED...standing room only! (thats a good sign) We finally were able to come in on a Saturday afternoon during a "1 year birthday celebration" for Rick's. it was a small quaint, yet warm and welcoming group of people. We ordered onion rings and a couple of beers. The onion rings were....onion rings....but the beer was ICE cold...coldest beer I have had in a LONG time here in St. Pete. Then the owner walked by and asked if we had tried the salmon, which we had not. He said " I know a guy who knows a guy" and came back with a plate of slow smoked salmon.....now we are from the Pacific NW, born and raised in Portland, Or, we catch salmon on the rivers all day long, we KNOW salmon. This may be one of the BEST salmons I have EVER eaten. The only better salmon was a place on the Columbia River in Oregon served with fresh blackberry drizzle. 

This salmon had the perfect mixture of moist, but smoke and a true slow smoked crust that was unbelievable! He then said come back tomorrow for the slow smoked pork.....26 hours on the smoker! I never made it back the next day (long night!) We will for sure return to this hidden gem on the strip!
Not fully fried for chalupa supreme, cinnamon twist no sugar only cinnamon and biscuit very hard almost same as stone
This pizza is absolutely delicious! We love making Castrillo's our Friday night dinner.

We were seated on time which was good but it took us an hour just to get our apps then another hour for our meal.  Then when the food came out it was cold and bland.  We saw our waitress twice in 2 hours.  We had to get the hostess to open our wine.   The apps were delicious but overall it was a very disappointing experience and we'll most likely not return.

Always delicious. Always friendly. And they have grits, which is a huge plus to me. And they'll do half potatoes and half grits as a side on eggs. Only downside is putting the car at a meter. But the prices are low enough that the extra is no big deal. Cash only.

Had a bridal brunch here for a friend of mine about a month ago. They'll service was great and the food was even better! If you're there for brunch, I'd definitely recommend getting a side of grits with your meal - they were delicious. Also, they validated parking in the pinnacle garage for up to two hours!! Some people in our group didn't know this and struggled to find a spot.

Brought my sons here for a birthday party. They had a fantastic time. Lots of VR games and stations. They also have activities for the adults, full bar and the service staff was very fast and friendly. I loved that the owners and management staff was present in the building and helping out. I would definitely recommend coming here for birthday partys or even just to have a day out...
Meh!! Not all that. I went to this place because I saw it on Man Vs Food Nation. The minute you start serving pink chicken is the minute you should shut down. Spicy though, even the mild is spicy.

Came back with my family this time, I was praising how good the place was to my sister and she couldn't stop talking about it so we came with our brother and mother. My mom is very hard to please when we go out to eat but we knew she enjoyed seafood and this place gives you a bucket of it! My sister and I got a pound each of crawfish (I got shaking sauce/ extra hot, my sister got garlic butter/medium), I got an extra side of corn on the cob and red skin potatoes, they both come with 3 if you add extra sides, if not it already comes with one additional potato and corn. My mother got a pound of black mussels (shaking sauce/extra hot). She LOVES them, probably the first time we heard her say amazing things about her meal. My brother got the 6oz lobster tail, he really enjoyed it, the sauce was soaking into the meat and he ate it with his rice. We finished everything and left very satisfied! My family will be back.
The catfish platter was excellent start to my trip to the big easy. Definitely  a great place for dinner.

we were referred over to this place by a local , his exact words were "best food in town,check it out and if it disappoints you, il be here, and il buy you a beer. if you love it just thank me" so we took his suggestion, we were seated as soon as we entered. the service without a doubt was the best iv ever gotten, i even told the waitress that. she was amazing her name was JIMIKA, super friendly and helpful. and the food was great, large portions, no wait. the whole thing was a great experience . i will definitely be back. and i kept my word and thanked the local after!

Once again best vegan mac and cheese ever! It's the only thing that hits the spot. Also the Ocean protein was very good give it a try. All the food is very good though, and they are very nice here. :D

Love Zoe's Kitchen, but unfortunately the service was not the best in this location. Put in an online order and they forgot the sauces I ordered and I asked for my steak to be cooked well done. On top of that, I had already payed for my food o line and people walking in who ordered there, were getting there food way before me. Disappointed, I'd rather go the the new one in Murfreesboro. Food and service was awesome even when they're slammed.

When my wife said she was stopping here and bringing dinner home I had no idea I was about to have the best brisket I have ever had. And the ribs where amazing too. Mac & Cheese and potatoe salad ( have to say best potatoe salad in Tucson ) over all if I could eat here every day I would be very happy. Can't wait till tommorrow. After a long weekend of racing this place rocks.

Great coffee and quiche. Really nice menu with lots of options. Cool, relaxed vibe and kid friendly. Dogs welcome on the outside patio too!! Great addition to the SoHa neighborhood. We will definitely be making it a regular spot!
Great food, TERRIBLE service. I've been many times and particularly the night time staff is very rude and not welcoming.
Friendly, knowledgeable and go the extra mile to diagnose a problem and fix it.  I was very impressed and am a fan

I've been coming here for over a year,  at  first the experience was good since the pit boss and dealers were always nice. Not sure if under new management or they hired a bunch of new people, but in the last 2 week, I came here about 8 different days. Out of those 8 days, I was asked not to use my phone on 5 of those days saying it was against their policy. I took pictures with my phone and talked and texted on my phone last year, which is why they used to be my favorite casino.

However this time, they actually told me it's against policy to use the phone,  however when I wasn't using my phone and asked if I could use it. They said of course as long as I don't hold the game. 

I even was rejected from a pai gow table because they said I couldn't use it because it's against their policy, went to the tables right across from them, near the slot machines, and the pit boss over there allowed it. 

When I asked to speak with a pit boss during another occasion, the dealer kept saying that it is not allowed and refused to call the pit boss.

Usually when I ask about their policy on phones,  the general answer is that they are the only casino without a policy on phones, and allowed pictures to be taken,  as well as talking and texting on your phone.  As long as you don't hold the game or disturb other guests.  I had already folded my hand in this occasion and was simply texting my sister where I was at,  when the dealer said I had to stand up,  when the pit boss had already said it was fine. 

Ridiculous,  silver legacy needs to have better mannered dealers,  as well as a set policy, otherwise I would just stay at El Dorado or a closer casino.

Stop whatever you are doing, and get yourself to Yats and stuff your hungry face with some of the best and boldest flavors going today!  EVERYTHING here is magnificent!  Drunk Chicken is fantastic, Gumbo is rock solid, and that bread...THAT BREAD!!  Ahhhhh!!  Please go by and give them some love (and your money)!  This place is beyond wonderful, and you will not be served by sweeter people anywhere.  Tell Joe back in the kitchen that he ROCKS and that you are much happier having tasted the magnificent manna that comes from this place.  Really, folks, it's not to be missed.  Eat there, and eat there often!!

This is what I've been looking for since I moved to Delaware. I grew up working in a Pizza Shop in Philly. Yesterday we had the Turkey hoagie and Cheese steaks. They hand pick the turkey so it's not processed crap. It's fresh ! We went back again today and just tried the pizza parlor they have attached. The sauce is really good and on top it's a $7 pie. They have indoor and outdoor seating and the workers are very nice. I am a new fan but will become a loyal patron.

Delivery Review: 

I ordered a medium size egg drop soup and a shrimp fried rice. In my order request I asked "please add extra soy sauce and hot mustard". My order was delivered with zero of either. Great. Awesome. I'm the kind of person that needs both to really enjoy it. The shrimp fried rice was awesome! Even with no soy sauce or hot mustard. It was still cooked perfectly! Do not waste your money on the egg drop soup. It was without a doubt the worst soup I've ever had. I usually loveeee egg drop soup, and have never seen it get messed up. Today was a first. It had zero flavor. It's weird..it's like I'm eating thick water. No taste at all. There are 3 different people eating it, and all of us are confused as to how this is so bland. 
The portions are large and easily shared. 

Their delivery service was easy to use. I ordered through the yelp app, $7 delivery fee plus tip. $15 min order for delivery. 
I revived a message ("We're sorry, but your order is taking a little longer than expected. We'll text you when your pilot leaves the restaurant soon. Thanks for your patience!") after about 10 mins after ordering. I thought that was very nice. 
Would I order again? Maybe. Definitely not delivery. Maybe I'd order take-out...

I went by just for caramel corn, I can't find it near me and knew they had it. When I walked in the food smelled so wonderful that I picked up a 12 bone rib and potato salad for my husband and 2 hotdogs for me. I am not a rib person, but I ate one anyway. AMAZING!! My husband has not opened the box yet but he will be saddened to see that he only has 4 of the 12 ribs waiting for him! I keep getting in the box and eating another one and another one. Let me be clear, I am NOT a rib person. Until now! These are amazing, they fall off the bone, nice and saucy (of course he asked if I wanted them sauced, so if you don't like sauce you can get them without it) and they did not give me that smokey yuck feeling that a lot of BBQ gives me after I eat it. The hot dog was great, it was juicy, good size and fit the bun perfectly. It wasn't one of those dogs that is half the size of the bun. The potato salad is yummy, not too much mustard or mayonnaise. Caramel corn was all that I hoped it would be. He was pulling some meat balls out if the oven. Oh my, they looked amazing! He could tell I was drooling over them so he gave me one to bring home and try. They are home made and are their own recipe, so much better than any other meatballs I have ever tried. This place just might have changed my mind on BBQ. I will DEFINITELY be back and will spread the word!

Dissapointed!
 Johnny's has been in Reno forever and considering that, we felt our first visit would have been more exciting. The flavors were light and boring, the steak was way over cooked and the cannolini was filled with a meat paste that tasted and felt way over processed. The decor is nice and updated. Perhaps the food should be too. Just because it's been in Reno a long time, doesn't mean it's great.
Price was fair and the wine selection was great. But no beer on tap. Really? Want great italian in Reno? Try La Famiglia or the Tuscan Tomato.

This has to be one of my new favorite restaurants. Not only was the service great, the food was amazing. I tried their lobster Mac n cheese and crab cakes. Currently I have not been able to find better crab cakes in St. Louis. It is quite expensive but definitely worth it.

Being hundreds of miles away from home, where we don't have one of these, I was so happy to be back!

First off, awesome service! Our waitress was on top of everything. 

Food, was amazing! The lunch portion I'd perfect, so big and filling!

Drinks... amazing! Loved this place and we'll meet again soon!
Some of the best Chinese and Sushi i have had in downtown Indy! Great addition to downtown eating!

I was reminded of how much I love this place last night, when I had dinner with a few girlfriends for restaurant week.  I've been here for Easter brunch for so many years with my family (this is the place they want to go after driving 1000 miles to see me, if it's any indication of how great it is) but have not had a dinner experience.  Last night I remedied that, and I couldn't have been happier.

On a tangent, restaurant week is both a joyous time of year and at the same time nerve-wrecking.  Some restaurants really rise to the occasion, using this week as an opportunity to really showcase the best of themselves in the hopes of establishing new regulars.  Other places seem to suffer through it, putting out mediocre fare since they seem to be thinking people are coming in anyway, so I'll just give them something to shut them up and get me through this week.  I've had both kidns of experiences, and let me say Tin Angel took this chance ot show me everything amazing about themselves, and they will have a new regular.

The space is always nice to be in, with its exposed brick and cozy lighting.  It feels open and intimate all at once.  Our server was perfect, attentive, funny, conversational without being overbearing...she was what every server should strive to be.

And our food...oh YUM.  I chose the pescatarian (seafood) three-course meal as my choice, and I was not disappointed.  The appetizer was basically fried shrimp, which didn't impress me, but my dinner, consisting of perfectly-cooked salmon with fall vegetables and crisped arugula was DIVINE.  Melt in your mouth good.  My friends tried the vegetarian and carnivore meals, so I to sample butternut-squash and goat cheese raviolis (please tell me that's on the menu daily because I would bathe in it!) and a perfectly cooked and too-large-for-one-person steak.  And when our pre-planned desserts weren't available (which the server was honest about, bravo, we appreciate that) we were offered another option, which I really loved: an apple tart with walnut ice cream.  Not too big, too sweet, just a perfect end to the meal.

This place was perfect to sit with three friends and catch up and have great discussions.  From ym brunch experiences I can also say its a great family place as well (I recommend getting the biscuits with sorghum, WOW).  I truly adore this little gem on West End, and if you get a chance to try them during restaurant week, DO IT.

Apart from the sign outside (awfully garish) our entire experience here was wonderful. The decor is very upscale for Tucson, the wait staff was attentive and the food was absolutely fantastic. I highly recommend this one!!

Oh my goodness...
The very first time I came here I loved it...but I also only order drinks and their fundido dip. This past time that I visited here was just awful. For starters you are paying way too much for what you get. And in my honest opinion if the best thing on your menu in terms of taste and price is a cheese dip then you may want to re-evaluate what you are presenting to your guests. 

On this last trip I met two of my friends here for dinner one night. We walked inside and instantly could smell an odor. We opted to sit in the outdoor area and I immediately started to feel sick. I had a headache and was overall uncomfortable. We were sitting right next to what appeared to be a heating lamp that is mounted at the top of the wall. I thought I could smell gas coming from the fixture but when I ask our server he simply said he didn't smell anything and went about his way. 

Needless to say we left as soon as possible and it was literally a breath of fresh air stepping outside of that place.

Great Cuban food, casual atmosphere and good prices.  Please note, YOU SEAT YOURSELF, this is a very traditional Cuban cafe so they will not always sit you.  Highly recommend the carne con papas, puerco asado or steak sandwich.

This was one of the best meals I have had in my life. We did the 8 course tasting menu and ordered a few bottles of wine. Oliver guided us through service and him, his front server Kevin and the entire team delivered absolutely perfect service. Katelyn was our extraordinary sommelier and turned me on to some new wine I absolutely loved that I would have never chosen myself. I travel to and eat in Nashville often and Yolan is the best dining experience to date. I can not wait to return!

While the food and service are excellent (loved the chicken pad thai, mango rice + a very friendly & humorous waitress), the parking & location was a total nightmare. The restaurant is often overcrowded (the size of the restaurant is small) and waits can be an issue. Also, they leave the front door open, which allows cold air to fill the restaurant. Basically, once inside, it's easy to feel claustrophobic and chilly. 

Overall, the location isn't good at all. I'm sure college students love it close to their respective campuses, but it has a negative effect on the restaurant's ambiance and culture. 

However, the experience (once inside) is appreciable. A four-star rating if not for sub-par external criteria.

I'd rate this 3.5 stars for their prime rib (as decent as it is) sliced too thin to really enjoy and crab legs that really aren't worth the effort... but the quality of the food is really good, no matter which of the dozens of items they serve, but I always opt to find 'my faves' and tend to stick to them.   

The prime rib is really good but I like thick cuts and they won't serve it like that due to potential waste.  I can completely understand this, but I love shoveling huge chunks to chew on that melt in my mouth and sadly this doesn't fill that particular craving.  The crab legs are small and contain very little meat so if I want some kind of binge crustacean 'fix' I'd rather go to all you can eat lobster which is substantially more fulfilling, even though that buffet isn't as good as this one. 

I found the oyster Rockefeller and crab cakes worthy of giving 4, perhaps even 5 stars.  Next time I come back those are the two dishes that I will load up on for certain and will update my review when I do so.   The amount of actual crab in the crab cakes makes dealing with crab legs feel kind of silly.  They're loaded and taste wonderful, though there isn't any special sauces served with them.  

 For what its worth, the service and soda refills were timely and appreciated.

The only thing good about this place was the woman serving drinks and popcorn in the lobby. She was quick and attentive and so nice. 
You could hear workers in the theater next to ours cleaning and playing around extremely loud almost the entire time our movie was on. Seats and floor were dirty. Paint peeling off walls in the hallway. Tear in the screen was pretty annoying. And tons of random weird noises the entire movie.... maybe the AC? So loud people kept saying "what the hell was that?"

This has become my favorite breakfast place. The food is very tasty and you get a lot for your money. The staff  is outstanding, always pleasant and helpf, and the manager Dylan makes a point to remember customers and greet them when they arrive. The freshh squeezeD juice I is actually squeezed when you order it, that is fresh!

As an avid sushi fan - or perhaps rabid is more accurate - I was amazed and delighted to find H2G a block from my daughter's apt. The grand opening banners still up, we ventured in for a bite. The sushi is fresh, standard portions at prices that ought to make this place the most popular sushi stop in south phila. In fact, the only place i've ever seen a better deal is the Hibachi all-you-can-eat prices out in Downingtown. We did a selction of sashimi and a rainbow roll. 3.95 per three pieces of sashimi, $7.95 for the rainbow roll. Killer stuff. If you like fresh, well prpepared sushi and don't want to spend a small fortune to eat, this is the place! WOW.

It took us over an hour to get our food ! The "owner" Tony (at least he told us he was the owner) was completely unapologetic , he could not even say he was sorry for our wait. Sad to see such poor leadership to bad I was check the place out for a catering job I need done

Despite what the yelp page says from the business, the staff does not wear masks. Upon arrival, we were greeted outdoors by someone who wasn't wearing a mask, however with no distinguishable uniform or name tag, we thought it was just a patron being friendly. We were outdoors so it wasn't a big deal that he wasn't wearing a mask. 
   We were seated indoors, and noticed that the indoor space is quite small. Not more than six tables in a very small space sharing a full length bar. Ambiance was upscale and decorated quite nicely. We sat down and looked around and saw that no one on staff was wearing a mask in such a small intimate space. We were greeted by our waitress who was lovely and friendly. However, you guessed it, no mask. This gave us pause. Every staff member we saw in the front of the house was not wearing a mask despite still being in a pandemic with a very aggressive strain. So if the front of the house wasn't taking this virus serious, we can only imagine that the cooking staff were unmasked as well. 
    Unfortunately we didn't have a chance to try the food because the risk was too high of a price for us to take if the establishment and its staff choose to not wear a mask.
Kale Caesar salad is NASTY. Burgers are mediocre. Overall, no character in the restaurant and high prices for what you get.

This was a very cute little spot. Myself and my dinning companion had never tried it before but both like Greek cuisine - and I'm glad we walked in! The restaurant itself is pretty, nicely decorated, and clean. The wait staff is friendly and I love that a lot of the folks working there are related to the owners.
I got the lunch special - gyro wrap + greens and it was great! I got the chicken version and my dinning companion got lamb - both were well seasoned and dressed well. 
We were lucky enough to try the baklava for dessert and I'm pretty sure I'd go back just to sit and have another piece!

We were in Tucson to get same day passport service and needed a place that was an authentic latin place for good food. I am well versed in latin cuisine and this place is 100% authentic Mexican. The Pozole was homemade and fresh corn the carne asada tortilla quesadilla was awesome!!! The service was great too!

Had such a fun night with visiting family at the Christmas market! It truly is such a fun night time activity. Even with it being cold it's so worth it to walk around with hot chocolate and go ice skating!! Can't wait to come back again next year! 

If able I would recommend making a reservation for dinner at the cake bake for some drinks and a sweet treat!! 

And did I mention , free parking??

Have not eaten there for a long time. Went there yesterday and was not impressed.  Not much of a selection and for what it was, to expensive.  There was only 1 waitress for the entire place and she just could not keep up with refilling our drinks. The building could use a update also.

Burger Up is one of my top visited restaurants since moving here. The food never disappoints (unless delivered. Before COVID, I would visit once every 1-2 weeks, but of course, now I'm eating there once every 1-2 months. The Food: The Honey Dijon Aioli is one of my favorite sauces of all time. They nailed it and personally introduced me to the sauce. Would recommend 10/10.

This was an awesome experience in a nice comfortable environment. The portions are very generous and food selection is vast. Our server Abel is clearly employee of the month, every month! He was super helpful in giving us tips and recommendations. He was always close by on hand to cater to our smallest wishes at any given time. Do yourselves a favor and hit this place up!

My husband and I waited until they had been open for a while, hoping the negative reviews were due to opening challenges.  We really wanted it to be good.  Unfortunately, it wasn't.

We sat at the bar, the staff was friendly.  The only bourbon they had was Jim Beam or their well brand, the name of which I had never heard.  The drinks were fine, despite being made with diet Coke poured from a 2 liter bottle.The other liquor choices appeared very limited as well. We ordered the egg roll appetizer, they were over-fried, dry on the inside and greasy.    

Despite growing up in the 70s, we weren't fans of the Led Zepplin, Iron Maiden etc. rock that was playing (with commercials).
  
I ordered the "cuban", the brisket was moist but without much flavor and no smoke.  It was just OK.  My husband wanted the ribs, but at $32 a rack, he had the pulled pork sandwich instead, which was kinda just OK.  The fries were way over fried, mushy, and tasted burnt.  I think they may use the same oil to fry everything, and the oil smell followed us home, had to put my clothes right in the wash.

So, high prices and poor food.  I see that others have had a better experience.  Hopefully things may improve, as we really need a good bar-b-que place in the neighborhood.

Looked on yelp for a local restaurant that served manicotti as it's my son's favorite dish. Decided to try Villa maria after reading the reviews and we were not disappointed. We had a good basic salad served with delicious garlic knots. The manicotti was homemade and was huge. My son loved every bite that he could manage. There was enough left over for lunch tomorrow. This a delightful family run restaurant with good service and delicious food. Give it a try.

My husband & I stopped by on a Wednesday night & were quickly seated in the bar area. Our waiter, Tony, took great care of us! We had biscuits & blueberry jam brought to us w our drinks:) soon after our fried okra appetizer arrived. Yum!! I ordered the shrimp n grits & my husband had the fried chicken, both were good. We will def go back!

Our party of 4 adults +1 child only had 35 minutes before boarding at the other end of the concourse so we were in a hurry for a quick beer and a bite. Until recently we were not even aware of this place but made a mental note of it when we arrived in Tampa at a gate tucked into a back corner. We also discovered a smoking area that we didn't know existed. Anyway we were assured by the server that we should have no problem getting served and out of there in less than 30 minutes. She was true to her word! But just to be sure we ordered light, pretzels and chicken wings. I sampled the pretzel and sorry to say I wasn't impressed. They were obviously nuked and so they were rubbery. But my wife and daughter in law had the buffalo wings and they said that they were delicious. I had the porter beer which was wonderful. I'm giving it 5 stars especially because they got us out of there on time, the beer was great, and at least the wings were too. Next time through Tampa I'll be back, and given enough time will check out the smoking section for a cigar!
My favorite buffet. Good variety...always fresh.  Tried the buffet at the Atlantis and the Peppermill buffet is so much better. Always eat here at least once on our stay.

Cool little place right on the water. I believe you can even come by boat. They seem to have happy hour specials nightly with awesome prices. I had the BBQ pulled pork sandwich on bun with slaw. Everything seemed good and the prices are right. There was also a live band on Friday night when we went. Cool place to go with a group of friends or stop in for lunch, although it is hot since it is all outdoors, but a good majority is under the shade.
