Platter was really good. The sandwiches were average especially the gator po' boy.

As an avid admirer of anyone who spends time to make BBQ, especially in a place like Uptown I had been supremely excited about this restaurant from the moment I saw construction begin.  The only thing making this style of restaurant better was living on the same block.  Early on I was dazzled by the decor and tasty food.  The quality was quite high and there seemed to be a lot of care put into the food and presentation.  I must admit that I find the moniker "Shane-made" (versus house-made, etc.) to be slightly pretentious, though I really liked the sentiment that items were scratch-made.  

Attributable to higher-than-humble pricing, our visits have waned over time, though it's been a place where we'll regularly eat when we need a close restaurant and want something nicer.  Last night was one such occasion.  I must admit I feel badly for not previously writing a positive review for our various earlier visits, but I don't regularly contribute-- just for the exceptional visit (be it positive or negative).  Unfortunately, last night was quite a memorably bad visit.  

While pressed for getting food as the hour was later, and we were still working we ordered some food to pick up around the block.  The wait staff managed to put us on hold for an unreasonable amount of time (greater than 5 minutes) before having we had to call back to place an order.  As we ordered they seemed confused about the availability of a sandwich and had to trade off to another server.  This isn't a huge problem, though speaks of the lack of service that others have commented on.  The food was the real issue.

My sandwich was placed not only on stale, but badly charred bread with cold meat.  The cole slaw and potato salad sides must have been the last of a batch with the cole slaw being nearly rancid (and completely inedible) and the potato salad (very tasty) but comprised of more sauce than potatoes.  

With all his accolades, I find it hard to believe the quality control over these "Shane-made" offerings.  A nearly $30 sandwich dinner was really an insult to receive-- especially coming from a friendly neighborhood establishment.  This is a real shame as previously I was proud to bring friends and visitors there for a nice meal.  

***As a side note, should the owners ever read this, us neighbors would very much appreciate if they could help patrol patrons who illegally park in front.  This blocks our viewing when trying to leave and has caused several near-miss accidents.

$20 unlimited mimosas on Sunday's! Yes they will keep them bottles popping as long as you are there! Recently we went to brunch and I got the shrimp and grits they were delicious! Other friends in our group got the biscuits and gravy as well as the crab Benedict, all good! The ambience of the restaurant is also very nice. We didn't get offered the truffle popcorn while we waited but maybe next time!

Stopped in because my sister wanted a smoothie and I wanted something warm. She got the mango strawberry smoothie and chicken panini. I got the spiced chai with almond milk and herby chicken salad sandwich. Service was quick and polite. Both my sister and I loved our drinks and ate our sandwiches way too fast. I almost forgot to take a photo. Highly recommend for a delicious quick bite or drink...

One of the best pizza pick-up restaurants in the area. They're quick -- food is always ready in 10-15 mins. They're also open late, which is perfect when you get hungry late on weekends.
The people are friendly, and the food quality, consistency, quantity of toppings -- excellent
I've tried their pizzas, strombolis, cheese fries, onion fries, hoagies... everything awesome. Nothing negative to say about this place.
Drexel Hill Style Pizza and Joe's Pizza, are two of my favorite pizza/hoagie/cheesesteak places in all of Marple/Newtown area.
The only thing is parking really awful at Drexel Hill Pizza. You can't see backing out of the spaces, on West Chester Pike. The road is busy, unless you go late night for pick up, and people don't let you in when backing out. It is a very busy intersection of rt 3 and sproul.

I've been here twice. The food is always well prepared and tasty. The popcorn is so good I get cravings for it. It's just a yum yum place to eat. There is a good beer selection too. 
The room is a tad too dark. I like the Christmas lights but sometimes I want to see the person sitting across from me.

Talk about charm!!! This beautiful little gem hidden away in the New Orleans Lakefront Airport is an absolute must for every trip we take to NOLA. A note for clarification, we always eat in The Walnut Room for Sunday brunch, so this review is specifically for that.

Before we even get to the food and service let me just talk about this building!!! This airport has been renovated to retain the original art deco style and it is WONDERFUL. I feel like I walked into a scene from The Great Gatsby every time I go. It really adds to the ambiance that they play era-appropriate music, too. The ceiling in the airport lobby is not to be missed...how often can you say that, save for the Sistine Chapel? Then there's the view as you eat. This little airport is the landing spot for sports teams, celebrity personalities and just the Crescent City wealthy...so there's no telling who you'll see fly in or out!!!

The service here is always impeccable. The wait staff treat you like they have known you all their lives and the chef is HIGHLY visible. The staff make honest recommendations, and are SO professional in the meal service. It's really kind of nice to be in a place that still hold true to standards of an era that is all but lost. A large number of the wait staff have been there for YEARS, which says something about the management, I think, as well. They've definitely got a good thing going.

Now to the food...excellent. I am sad to read the review of the person who had a sub-par experience with the food. I feel like this must have been an off day, as I don't doubt their assessment, but on a typical day I can't imagine the food being on par with Waffle House. I tend to get Chef Leon's Crab Cakes (crab cakes with poached eggs and hollandaise) and, of course, the Brabant potatoes (do NOT miss ordering those...carb conscious or not, this is an occasion to cheat!), but I have also had the Eggs Boudin (poached eggs on patties of boudin sausage), the Shrimp & Grits, Grillades and Grits (can be an acquired taste for non-natives, but delicious!!) and the Lindbergh Omelet. I was not as big a fan of the omelet as the others, as I felt like the combination of crab meat and brie is better on paper than on the plate...it just wasn't as flavorful as some of the other dishes. Still good, but not my fave. The crab cakes, however...let me talk about them for a sec...the crab cakes are crispy on the outside and tender inside with deliciously delicate seasoning and nary a shell piece to be found! (Quite a trick, if you've never picked through lump crab meat) The eggs have been flawlessly poached every time, and the hollandaise is nice and rich and creamy. My son gets the Doolittle every time and polishes it off WITH potatoes every time. Now, he's a 15-year-old athlete, so his appetite is substantial, but this thing is huge. The husband usually gets a breakfast sandwich, which is "pretty good" but nothing Earth-Shattering. 

The service...has always been impeccable. Servers and hosts are always clean, tidy and smiling. They address the customers as Sir and Ma'am and are happy to small talk with you. They are very hospitable to special requests (my mom always asks for her biscuit to be grilled, for example) and my coffee is seldom below half-way. 

All in all, I can't recommend the experience of the Walnut Room more highly.

I am writing this from the toilet. this place was an absolute fucking disgrace. everything we ordered from here made us sick, and now our assholes are paying the price. both wings and fries were dry as fuck. save your money and go somewhere else instead. This place will make you shit your brains out

We've been going here for the past 4 years. The kids menu states that beverages are included with the kids meal. However, they've recently starting charging for my son's hot chocolate stating that it's a "specialty drink". Hot chocolate is listed with coffee on the everday menu. Nowhere on the kids menu does it state what drinks are included or not included. Emailed corporate and received no response regarding this practice.

I've been here 3 times now, and the food is reliably delicious.  The menu is diverse with something for any preference.  However, they need to work on their customer service.  Both times I ate at the front bar, it took more than 10 minutes for anyone to even acknowledge I was sitting there.  Each time I've been the servers seem to be more interested in standing in a cluster and talking versus tending to customers.  The service at the back bar was great though, it was a younger male bartender and I regret I cannot remember his name.  However, the kitchen is going a great job putting out delicious food.

Wow.  Went here for my 39th birthday last night.  2nd time eating here.  There were 6 adults in our party and we were seated immediately in a quiet nook as requested by my mother in law.  We all got steaks, but before that they brought us our popovers and little treats from the chef.   Everything was so good. I got the NY strip and it was like eating succulent butter.  It was the best steak I've ever had.  I also got the risotto tater tots and they were fantastic.  The rest of our party got various sides.  I wasn't a huge fan of the potato aligot,  but no one complained about anything.  Our server Daniel was warm and engaging and just seemed to be a real genuine guy.  I got to choose a free dessert for my birthday and got the milk and cookies.  So good!!   Our attentive server heard me mention my mother in law would probably like the opera cake and he brought her out one on the house.   This is the place to go in Nashville for exceptional service and food.  We will be back for years to come.

The food was absolutely fantastic, unfortunately the service was quite terrible. 

First of all, we showed up at 9:20, they close at 10 pm. They had dumped the tea. (I've worked in the food business before, we served everything we had up until the minute we closed, and we served people until our lights were turned off, even if we were "closed" before then). Why they dumped the tea a whole 40 minutes before they closed, I have no idea. So we ordered our food. I ordered a 10 piece naked wings (9-1-1 sauce), celery/ranch, and fries. Soon enough, the food came out, everyone got their meals, and I got my celery/ranch...so I kept waiting. Finally my wings were brought out, but not my fries. After everyone at my table was halfway done with their meals, my fries finally came. So I finally began to eat my meal. A few minutes later our drinks were empty. The waitress had not even once stopped by to check on us since my celery. It was the cook who had brought me my wings and fries. So we finally called over the waitress and asked for refills. She finally brought us refills and told us that this was the rest of the ice. Why they stopped making ice, a mystery to me. It was also at this point that we were able to ask for a fork so my girlfriend could eat her side salad. Why she didn't get the fork with the salad, I don't know. When we finally finished our food we called our waitress over again to ask for dessert. She claimed that they were closed and could not order anything else (and to be fair, it was 10:05, but like I said early, being a person who has worked in food services before, we served everyone everything; it's good customer service and it makes the customers want to return--declining us dessert is a great way to lose money). So we asked for our checks. Our checks came and we continued to wait for her to return. Finally she came back and took our checks. She returned with the cards of the two people that paid with card. They then noticed that she did not bring them a pen. Luckily one of them had a pen in their wallet and they were able to sign the receipt. After this, we finally left. 

We showed our waitress nothing but respect and she essentially ignored us the whole time. Everyone at our table enjoyed the food, but we were all very displeased with the service. I will not be returning to this location, and I love wings. I'll check out WingHouse next time I'm in Tampa.

I go to Adriatic Grill every chance I get while on Temple Main campus. The staff are nice and very friendly, we've become acquaintances. The food is delicious at a better price than elsewhere on campus. They have no issues changing orders or sandwiches to accommodate requests, and for this I thank them! 

When I was a student I went here every other day or more, and when I stopped by campus this week, I ate here again with the same great service and food!

Okay so I saw so many amazing reviews of this place so my friend and I decided to check it out. Off the bat it seemed very busy so it seemed that people did really enjoy it. My friend and I ordered some mussels and some crawfish we got the Cajun sauce with medium spicy, and some Cajun fries. Okay looking st the bag itself it seemed super overly oily. We shook the bag to get some of the actual seasoning on the food. Taking one bite and my mouth was already on fire....and I love spicy food. This not only was super spicy but it was flavorless spicy. So it really was spicy oil that hurt. Second, due to it excessively spice level for just MEDIUM it was not filling. On the other hand the Cajun fries were amazing. I probably wouldn't go back. 

Update!: so my same friend and I decided to give this place another try. Unfortunately at that time the crawfish were out of season so they had none but we decided to get the trifecta with extras sauce so the taste was a lot stronger and only mild spicy. We got the mussels and shrimp and some Cajun fries. Cajun fries were to die for like last time, and the seafood and sauce this time was amazing. Perfectly made. We will be going back soon for the crawfish


Alright update: they have just been under new management so they have been pretty busy. Yet still unorganized!!!! There was a giant party of people who ordered after me or I guess during when I order TO GO!  The front guy said it would be ready in 10 minutes. So I wait I'm not in any rush but I wait about 15-20 minutes before I go back and ask when my food is coming. He said oh... seems like they put the GIANT ORDER OF 15 or more people before my to go order of one. And I asked so I have to wait until all of those people get their food before I get my to go food?! He's like yeah I'm sorry. Yeah I'm not impressed.

I ordered take out from this little, unassuming restaurant that's located next to Cody's and LA Fitness. 

Although the owner was very friendly and my take out order was quickly prepared, I just thought it was ok. 

I ordered drunken noodles with chicken. It's by far my most favorite Thai dish. If prepared correctly, you can taste the subtle hint of the fresh basil. But instead what I got this evening was a noodle dish that was heavy on the Thai chili sauce. It wasn't bad, just wasn't as good as I'm use to.

Ok, today I'm going to whine a wee bit. I love Bruegger's. I loved Bruegger's for about 7 years when I lived in Franklin - I would get myself a ham and cheese bagel for lunch, and a plain bagel for my youngest to gnaw on/teethe on, haha. I missed Bruegger's oh so much when we lived in Tampa for 5 years and never found a suitable replacement for it. It was Bruegger's or nothing. So, we've been in Brentwood 5 years now, and I'm loving them again.
     My whine is the limited hours. I realize bagels tend to be a breakfast item, but my stomach dictates when I want a bagel and cream cheese. I am not a morning person AT ALL! And, i don't do breakfast? in fact, many times i don't eat anything until mid-day and its practically closing time for y'all by then!! I can't tell you how many times my family and I have wanted to nosh there, but we are too late. Bagels are a great food for athletes to eat, and my boys would be downing quite a few if you stayed open later. Even staying open til just like 7 PM would be a huge help and enable us to ingest more of your scrumptious morsels. We just want more of you, Bruegger's.

Went to Zavino for lunch with two co-workers.  I was pleasantly surprised how good the pizza was.  We shared two pies and a salad.  Everything was fresh and light.  Ate outside great experience, can't wait to go back!!

Delicious food & so charming ambiance!  Attentive service.  Went on a Mon night & the place was pretty full.  Always a good sign for a restaurant. 
Had their chicken Tortilla soup - yum! & an order of their Original Anaheim Chile Rellanos.   Both dishes were very satisfying!  
The restaurant was a marvelous history since 1922. 
Still family owned / you're in good hands.

We popped in the place on day one for the opening dinner unknowingly, and it was a complete disaster for service. However, the food was extremely tasty regardless of the wait.  I have waited a  couple months to order again to allow the place to settle in and not suck.

I just called to place a to go order and had to call three times to get someone to pick the phone up.  It was a treat for my lady as she was to pick the order up on her way home from work, and I had intended to pay for it over the phone. However, the girl that took my order informed me that they cannot process cards over the phone which I think is a complete joke. I'll wait another couple months I guess.

Great coffee, tea and food.  B/F and I were looking for something cafe-ish to do and  lazed away the afternoon here.  Nice ambiance.  Furniture comfy, layout conducive to people watching, plenty of games, magazines.  Will definitely be back.
Everything we ordered was amazing. Definitely have to try the bread pudding. Yasmin was an amazing server with the most beautiful personality.

This is such a great place to stop for food on the way to or from Indy, that it's worth it to stay hungry & wait for it instead of eating beforehand. Indiana people are not as familiar with this franchise as they are with KFC, which is a pity. Then again, that means more for me!! The red beans and rice is so incredibly delicious, you'll forget it's actually healthy for you. Their shrimp po boy is what my kid always orders, it's always delicious, as are all their sides, and of course, their chicken!! Get a split box of half spicy & half mild & discover what fried chicken tastes like when it actually has flavor.  It's in a truck stop, right off 65, so it's easy to get to, easy to get back on the highway. Call ahead if your order is large (they have specials on 15+ pieces all the time) and pick it up without having to wait.

I was a little nervous going in, despite the reviews, because down south we usually don't get our Cajun where we get our Tex-Mex. The service was great! Tevin gave us 5 star service. My mango frozen margarita was a 4.5. I'm from Texas so trust me when I say the chips, salsa and guacamole were even decent. My hubby had the fajitas which he thought was ok. I ventured out and ordered the Cajun seafood enchiladas with jambalaya on the side (you have a choice of beans/rice or jambalaya). The jambalaya was tasty, especially after I mixed it with the lump crabmeat sauce on top of my enchiladas. If I happen to stop by again, however, I probably won't order this dish again. Sautéed baby popcorn shrimp with no seasoning, huge chunks of green bell pepper and cheese is what I saw and tasted. Good thing I filled up on the chips, salsa and jambalaya (and margarita) because after a couple of bites I would have left hungry. Nice service and good drinks. Trust the jambalaya but try another entree.

Service was friendly, although a little slow to start. The beer list is fantastic. This was my first visit to the new Indy location and my second trip to a B-Spot. B-Spot's burgers just seem to lack SOMETHING. They have interesting creations but each end up a little lackluster leaving something to be desired. $4 for a small order of below average fries is definitely overpriced. The milkshakes are decent but nothing extraordinary. I'm underwhelmed and have had much better, high quality, creative burgers at other gastropubs in Indy.

This place looks a little gimmicky with the pink neon sign and the tufted velvet booths, but don't let that deter you. The food here is completely legit!  The complimentary salsas are just fresh and delicious! Get one of the guacamoles! The mole sauce is complex and delicious! The tamales, which I rarely eat at restaurants, because they are usually so disappointing, are fantastic! I've also had a few of the different margaritas on the menu and they are great with a Chile rim, and not cloying. Love the short rib enchiladas and the tacos arabes. I'm a fan of anything with morita chiles. Just make sure you make a reservation, because they are always packed!

The beer selection is great.  The food... Not so great.  Don't get me wrong, it was OK, I ordered the Texas melt which was supposed to be smoke brisket.  Find be a smoker in premises and I'll east my words.  Should have tried the shrimp po boy.

Average restaurant, average food, crappy service. Waited over 10 minutes for someone to even come to our table and say hi, then she didn't even introduce herself just asked what we wanted. Asked for a burger and steak cooked medium and both were over cooked. Not somewhere I would recommend to come.

Wow!! We absolutely MUST return here to try more! We tried the BBQ table for our first trip and it was awesome. We had the beef, ribs and spicy pork. All was great, but I liked the beef more. The little side dishes that come out are...interesting. Some I liked, some I didn't and two absolutely surprised me! The spicy cuttlefish and fish cakes were delicious and I NEVER would have guessed that until I overheard someone saying what they were. Anyways, it's a neat place and have great food with a nice staff. We will visit again!

I love this place! The food is great. I get something new every time I go and I have yet to be let down. The beer selection is excellent. The have a wide selection of craft beers which are always being swapped out, which is great for the variety and those that love multiple beers. Finally the service, it is always spot on. They are friendly and knowledgable, which are two key aspects I love. 

I highly recommend this place to anyone.

Full disclosure: I ordered delivery through a 3rd-party app. I am not basing this review on food temperature or presentation. The food just wasn't very good. Had the combo with an enchilada, flauta, and chile relleno with rice, beans, and a salad, plus a fajita taco, choriqueso, and flan. All of it was underwhelming--and no tortilla chips, to boot!

If you want tacqueria fare, El Taco Loco is a couple of blocks away. If you want entrees, Panchita's is practically next door, and La Mansion is just around the corner. All three are far superior. 

I've spent some serious time in Phoenix, Dallas, and to a lesser extent, Houston. I've had good Tex-Mex and authentic Mex-Mex. Most of the best Mexican food I have found here in Greater NOLA has come out of Kenner, so I was keen to give this place a try. I was sorely disappointed. Not recommended at all.

Sorry Chilango's; I've driven past and seen a good amount of business, so some people must think it's OK, but I'm not a fan.

I noticed this Fatburger location recently opened in my neighbourhood and after a long day, I figured I'd finally give it a shot. I have been to Fatburger in the past... but it's been so long I honestly couldn't even remember my previous opinion on the place.

Anyways, my first impression was that the menu was incredibly difficult to read. It's a fast food chain, so the menu board is above the cash registers... but for the life of me I couldn't figure out if you could get a combo, how much that would be, how much fries are on their own... etc. There's just way too much writing and it's pretty disorganized. Not so much a comment on the location, but the chain in general.

I finally went up to order a standard Fatburger with fries (and ended up getting a combo with a drink, which was a $1 discount according to my receipt). The total was a little over $13. In perspective, that's for a burger, fries, and drink... with no cheese or anything on the burger. Pretty expensive for fast food, in my opinion.

Anyways, in terms of quality: the fries were excellent, and you got a lot. Typical drink selection. As previously mentioned, the burger had no cheese (which I didn't realize until after I ordered and examined the menu further while waiting). The toppings were kind of meh... the lettuce was on the yellow end, as was the tomato. And the onions were chopped rather than rings, so they fell off everywhere as you ate. Lastly, the burger itself was REALLY GOOD, however, it was incredibly crumbly. Pieces of burger (and onion) were just falling everywhere as I ate.

Anyways, would I be back? Maybe... it's close, the fries are good, and I want to give their milkshakes a try. That said, it was expensive for fast food, and I probably wouldn't give the burgers another chance since they were so difficult to eat.

TO HOT!!  I'm not a Spicey eating person so his was not my favorite place for food. I will say they did everything right. Offered me another meal, and comped my meal and gave us a 25.00 gift card to return to try something else. Drinks are high in price and I think they should have a lunch happy hour everyone was nice. Place was clean service was spot on. If you like spicey foo I'd say give it a  try it

What has happened to this restaurant in the past 10 months,  there are not many hills in Florida but this place has gone way down hill!!  The last few times i was there always had the same margarita (Elderberry) last night it came green and the waiter who I've had several times said it's always green.  it's purple.  The guacomole had unripened avocado in it, (try biting into that) and the rest was watery with 2 litttle blobs on a 3 section plate.  I ordered the Soho Salmon salad, came with no arugula, was all baby spinach ( half wilted even with the salmon on the side.,  the salmon was a thin dried out piece of unedible, unflavored, fish.  The dresssing (which was from another salad the honey cilantro was sweet green water. no flavor unappetizing.  My friend had the ahi tuna wonton, the tuna was so overcooked there was no color to it! dry dry dry. We all ordered 1 drink each they were so bad,..Asked the bartender what color the margarita should be she said green,  called the restaurant today , they said it's purple. 
The outside seating for dogs has really changed the atmosphere of this restaurnat.  It started out a little classy and now it's gone to the dogs@
The wife and I walked 3miles from our Hotel to tease the  talk of the town! It was well worth the walk!!!!'

Ordered a pizza lastnight via Online ordering at 8:27 pm, and paid via Credit Card.  The order confirmation quoted 45mins.  Come 9:46 pm the pizza had still not arrived so I called the store...no answer.  I called back 3 more times with the same result...

We were looking to have Korean dinner for Wednesday night so we searched for a restaurant near us for the Korean food and seeing the reviews we decided to have Sa Ri One Grill Korean Restaurant. The restaurant was almost empty and we got the seating as soon as we checked in the restaurant. The restaurant is a fancy restaurant and it was amazing. We were greeted by our server Sang with the menus and water. We first got our Korean Appetizers which are served which includes Kimchi and Salad. After browsing through the menu we decided to order Kimchi Mandoo, Bul Go Ki Chicken and Dolsot Bibimboo with Chicken. The service was good and we got our food in 10-15 minutes. First we got Bul Go Ki Chicken and Dolsot Bibimboo. We really loved both of them especially Bul Go Ki Chicken which was tasty and delicious. After 5 minutes we got Kimchi Mandoo which were delicious and after having the other two dishes Kimchi Mandoo was too much to eat and they were too big. But all in all the food was delicious, tasty, hot and freshly cooked. Loved the ambience, good service and food.

I don't understand the hype about this restaurant.  I went twice in two weeks.  Second time I didn't want to go as I was underwhelmed with my first experience.  First experience was that it was overpriced for what you got.  We had the eggs benedict.  It was good but nothing to write home about.  Waited two hours for a table.  Second time was worse as we were rushed to order, eat and finish.  The waitress even said that weekends are busy and she needed our order after we had just sat down.  Meal was close to $100 for 4 people. Breakfast came out lukewarm.  Next time I'm in Boise I will be looking for a new breakfast spot.

This was our second visit, first was not very good and this one wasn't any better........

Watched a table of 6 up and leave because their food was no where in sight while tables seated after them were eating.
 Same happened to us, party of 7 and party of 2 seated well after our order was put in to the kitchen got all their food while we still waited. Had we not asked what was going on we'd still be there waiting. Only to find out they were now "plating" our food.

Food was ok, service not so much.
As the service continues to improve with shorter delivery times and the pizza and apps remain excellent, this location finally deserves a 5 star rating! Keep it up!

Cool vibe. Love that the wait staff worked as a team to provide awesome service. Our waiter was very knowledgeable of the menu and the history of the restaurant. Tried a few drinks off the menu all of which were on point. They have a rotating menu that isn't too overwhelming with choices. I loved the celery Caesar salad. I think I could have drank the dressing from the bottle. The sirloin was cooked to perfection. However, I tried the duck appetizer special and wasn't too impressed. Overly salted with little flavor. The cauliflower fried rice was also too salty for my taste. Otherwise a great restaurant. I'll definitely come back.
Great Happy Hour and was impressed with the staff, menu and the overall experience.  They just changed their french fries.  They are awesome!  Will repeat.
We loved this place. The list of specialty cocktails along with their vast menu. In the summer they have a fantastic outside area great for happy hours. Definitely will go back again and again

My daughter's BDay Brunch was saved by the Chef.
The food was great, however the Greeters were awful.
Management should seriously look into training the first face of your business.  Nine guest of a party of 10 in a non reservation  establishment should have been seated. Two more guest arrived and the Greeters refused to sit them at a table for 2 right behind us. We were told this restaurant that does take reservations, had this table on-a "30" minute wait!! No one  was ever seated during our meal.  Really Morrow!! WHY??? Please check other well established businesses before you set a rule that makes no sense.
The reason for a complete party is based on percentages. 80% is common and our party exceeded the norm,do a little research. Ok now the no outside cake to celebrate a Birthday on a Sunday. We were told your restaurant does not even serve desserts on Sunday!!! Really!!! WHY???? Again more research required--- have you ever heard of a "Cake Service Fee"?  Our server says lighting candles are a concern, however your staff sung Happy Birthday with SPARKLES 
MORROWS you really need to do better. When choosing a restaurant one is seeking a TOTAL and Complete Great and Wonderful Experience.
A one time great meal but  lacking in several categories does not generate a return visit.
Marketing 101 states word of mouth "can be" free good or bad advertising.  YOU CHOOSE...............

I love this little place. It's one place I stop when I'm in New Orleans. Great for a daytime beer drinking place. Food is decent and the wait staff is nice. I love this interior of this corner restaurant. They have a little bar in there that you can sit at and people watch at sidewalk goers and other passers by. I recommend it.

Went inside to pick up my lunch and noticed that all the customers dining were eating with NO lights on (Restaurant is probably trying to save money on the power bill, but there is a fine line to be drawn). Received my lunch "to-go", went back to work and started eating it. Chicken and green beans was horrible!! (Super, Super, SALTY), it was un-edible...I had to throw it away. The sweet and sour sauce was so "thick" with cornstarch it wouldn't even pour out of the little cup. Eggroll was put on top of the rice and was very "soggy" by the time I ate it (wrap it in paper of foil so that doesn't happen...ugggghhhhh). We have way to many GOOD Restaurant's to go back to this one.

This place has reeeeeally good food. So far I've had the burger with pulled pork and bacon, the chicken pot pie, the mac and cheese, and the chocolate cake. I recommend them all. The dining area is nice and cozy. Nice people that work and dine there. I will definitely be back.

This was my second visit to Fleming's and it was just as good as the first. This visit was an early birthday dinner for my mother. You cannot go wrong on Tomahawk Tuesday. There were 4 of us so we got 2 big steaks, 4 salads, 4 sides, and 4 desserts. 

The bread was warm and crusty. The steaks were cooked perfectly. Salads were cold & crunchy. The sides were great(mac n cheese, loaded baked potato, brussels sprouts, sautéed mushrooms). As expected, all of the food was great. 

The service was fantastic. Nick was our server. Attentive, courteous, and very personable. The manager, Alicia, also came over to check on how our evening was going. Not a requirement for me but it made my parents feel as though the restaurant and its employees valued the dinner they were having. 

Food can be great at a restaurant and lack service which can detract from the experience whereas great service can help to gloss over a less than satisfactory meal. Fleming's, for me, delivers on both fronts. The food was great as is the service I have received during my 2 visits. I will be back.

We popped in here for dessert but we will be back for the regular menu for sure! As visitors to New Orleans, we wanted some bread pudding, pecan pie, and chicory coffee! Yum. We called ahead since a lot of places are still shut and let me say--this was more than I could have hoped for. The staff was incredibly welcoming despite us just ordering dessert. Our sweet treats hit the spot! The building was quaint and served up a charming dose of the French Quarter decor. The bathrooms were top notch! As I have discovered in other places, they are quite often less than clean or modern. Not here. This place is top to bottom clean and safe but the wait staff is the cherry on top! So kind and attentive--I don't think my coffee ever really dropped below half full! The king cake style bread pudding was interesting and served up a good texture and taste. The pecan pie was just right.

My boyfriend took me out to Meme for my birthday dinner. I live down the street and pass it just about everyday. I haven't been dying to try Meme, but I figured since I'm moving out of the neighborhood I might as well. 
We started off with a beet salad and sizzling mussels. Both of these dishes were fantastic. The beet salad was a bit small for $10. For the main course I ordered the suckling pig and my boyfriend ordered the catch of the day. I LOVED the suckling pig. The last time I had sucking pig was in Segovia, Spain and this is exactly how I remembered it. Even though the pig was awesome, I don't really have any interest in going back because of the pricing. There are too many other restaurants that I am DYING to try!

This place has the worst service in Nashville. Don't waste your time, we were on the list and several people were sat before us. The staff and manager are completely clueless and have no business running a restaurant/bar.  As a native to Nashville this is a bad look for the city and the Gulch.
Really enjoyed this lovely place. The food was incredibly fresh and delicious. Would definitely recommend and try again :)
I don't give 5 stars too often but this place is pretty damn cool, great vibe, great people, great service. People from all walks of life. Not rowdy or loud just a very cool dive bar setting!

We went to Azteca with a party of six on a Friday afternoon and there was no wait. The chips and salsa were fresh, and our server was fast and friendly. 

If you are a vegetarian there are lots of options and even a vegetarian menu! There is also a lunch menu with smaller portions and cheaper prices with some vegetarian options. I got the lunch special with two bean enchiladas covered in red sauce with rice on the side. It was tasty. Everyone in our group enjoyed their food and the fajitas in particular were said to be good. 

They were very accommodating bringing to-go boxes and even to-go cups for our iced tea. When we asked for lemons she brought out a small bowl rather than giving us one lemon per tea, which is nice because once they refill the tea you always want more lemon.

Wow I've never had hummus so smooth and light, and pita so chewy and fluffy. 

Their platters come with hummus, one pita, and a side of cucumber salad! 

The hummus is easily enough for two people (imo) or, one person with a huge appetite haha. 

Their online ordering system was pretty seamless, and the pickup was easy.

Do you want to feel like you're eating "healthy" pizza without missing out on all the deliciousness? Grimaldi's helps me to enjoy pizza guilt free. How? First all of their ingredients taste fresh. If you don't believe me, just watch the guy spinning dough in the air like a globetrotter does a basketball. Second, the salads! You cannot go wrong with their salads, though my two favorites are the mediterranean and the caesar. Oh and a small is plenty for two. 

Their wine selection is nice too, plus, you can order a carafe if you don't want a whole bottle or a glass is just not quite enough. 

The service is excellent. It gets pretty crowded on weekends or when there is a good movie playing at Galaxy Theaters so my husband and I like to seat ourselves at the bar if the wait for a table is too long.

Great for big groups(we've been here several times with my husband's family at 10+). 

I need to say more about the pizza. It's made with a thin crust(again, good for the diet) and the sauce is oh so yummy with just a little spice to it. We usually get the pepperoni with kalamata olives and half jalapeños, but I would also recommend getting it with super creamy ricotta cheese. Oh and this is not the kind of pizza you want to order for take out as it tends to lose some of its "pizzazz" by the time you get home. 

Okay so I wouldn't go so far to say that it's diet pizza, but I am getting my veggies in with the salad and the crust is thin (less carbs!!) so let's just say it's pizza lite!

The servers at the Fenton, MO location are AWESOME.  And the food was downright amazing.  We loved it so much that we brought our robotics team in later that day.  They even made me a "birthday cake" out of a bandana and Tootsie Pops.  We just loved 'em.  They are so friendly and FUN!

I went in to this experience with no expectation other than the facade was pretty. Upon entering, there's no hostess or person to greet you,  to let you know the protocol to get a table. Approaching the bar, I was told to pick a table anywhere. So I picked a table in the courtyard(pretty weather with a lovely temperature), best part of the entire meal. The second best part of the meal was our server. He was prompt and attentive. The menu looks interesting and intriguing. The idea of using a sushi styled check box menu is fun, yet not needed for a menu that would easily fill half of an 8 1/2 x 11 sheet of paper. Next, someone needs to tells the kitchen, that restaurant is not sponsored by Morton Salt. Every item that was eaten had copious amounts of salt. So, we started with the radishes. Salted butter as a spread for raw veggies, not a problem tasted great. English peas were delicious seasoned appropriately, the cauliflower cream so yummy. Chopped salad with pickled veggies, at first was appetizing. Then we realized, that as we were encouraged to share our plates of food-tapas style- an additional salad was brought out that hadn't been ordered. Trust me one is enough. A salad vinaigrette should be used in moderation. I mean the restaurant took time to pickle their own vegetables, why not showcase them. Instead, the only taste to be found was an overly salted dressing that covered the beautiful colors and taste of the vegetables. Moreover, I'm not a fan of when a restaurant chooses to not list major ingredients on a menu(when a description/list has been given). So, we moved on to the Bolognese. No where on the menu does it mention fried chickpeas, at least I think it was chickpeas, there was at least a cup on top of the dish. The flavor of this item was similar to that of when you eat a Bolognese a day after it has been cooked by grandmother and then someone in the family, without any reason or tasting, chooses to re-season the sauce. The dish mentions spaghetti squash(it's puréed or whipped), it's not like the stringy spaghetti squash some squash connoisseurs may be used to. Either way, it won't matter what type of squash was in the dish because the only flavor that could be found was salt, salt, salt. There are culinary measures to correct these instances; though, I'm not sure those techniques are known to the kitchen staff. Sliding into the end of the meal, we selected the pork chop. I had real hopes for this item. It was the main reason I'd selected this location for dinner after looking over the menu. Upon arrival, the broccoli rabe looked charred(wasn't a great flavor-just burnt). The porkchop, which felt more like a pork loin, was not trimmed of it's fat. That is no a problem for me because that usually helps with flavor and holding in moisture. One bite is all it took to stop. It tasted like a salt. I stopped and that point my meal was over. My tongue started itching on the sides from all the salt. I hope this location gets some sense of salt levels with their food. They had some great products and wonderful platting. The flavors were just all over the place and need to reigned in. In closing, there may be another try here but I'm gonna need a bit to process all this sodium out of my body.

Best spring rolls I've ever had, and I've sampled quite a few. Fabulous dishes. One caviat: If you are even a LITTLE sensitive to spicy dishes and you see "Spicy" in the title, it's most likely they're using a chili sauce such as Sriracha. Make sure to be careful. I wasn't, and I paid the next day.

If by chance, you find yourself getting hungry while driving north on 170 St (maybe from a shopping excursion at West Ed), I urge you to take a right turn just before 100 Ave, into a little strip mall and venture into Island Cafe and Bistro. It is here that you will find many authentic Malaysian dishes that are just begging to be tried. 

Just recently, The Trophy Wife and I stopped in for lunch and were taken aback by their variety and can't wait to return. 

We started off with a spicy dumpling soup that in short, was simply amazing. I love a good soup and in my mind, this was one of the best I've ever had. Essentially, it was a spicy broth with dumplings. Nothing fancy-schmancy, just good ol' down home Malaysian goodness. If you order an entree for lunch, you are treated to a free order of Roti Canai with Curry sauce. For me, this was the first time I ever had roti. I suppose it's basically the Malaysian version of naan bread but lighter and flakier. Simply amazing! I could have stayed there all afternoon just snacking on roti. 
Next up was the Laksa Curry Noodles. I thought this dish was fantastic, even though I am not the hugest fish fan ever. It was a noodle soup (yay!) that had fish ball and fish cake, which I actually loved! Who'd have thunk it?
The wife had the Sambal Prawn dish and thought it was delicious; her favorite thing that we tried. 
For dessert, we indulged in their White Coffee Bubble Tea and the Ice Mochi Roll. We were told that the white coffee was a traditional Malaysian beverage (We actually had a hot one with our appetizer), and we absolutely loved it! The ice mochi roll was definitely an acquired taste (with a red bean filling) but I ended up enjoying it thoroughly. 

All in all, I LOVED the Island Cafe and Bistro. I'll admit that I thought the decor was unique in that they had flags of Malaysia interspersed with framed pictures of cars and auto races. To each their own, I suppose. 
Anyways, go to Island Cafe! You won't be disappointed!

love their beer selection here. its huge, and has a little bit of everything for everyone. i love the sours and the lucky charms they have here. this place is huge and has a great outdoor area. the service is pretty good too.

would come back again and enjoy some of the shows they put on - i see there was a stage.
It's awesome! We love this place! I'm vegetarian and they have so many good options and we have never been disappointed by any of the entrees we have ordered.

UPDATE: they're open at the new location in Trail dust town now! Open today! 12/7

Love this place. Delicious brunch and breakfast choice for east side Tucsonians! 

They are moving into Trail Dust Town across the street. Just a heads up.

I usually just stop in here on way back from the Shooter's Club to grab a quick meal.  They have a decent menu selection and generally have good service that is sometimes a bit slow.  The food is typically good and they offer good value for their portion sizes.  They have good sandwiches, pasta, burgers and the seafood is typically prepared well.  I wouldn't go out of my way to eat here but it is a decent family restaurant if you find yourself in this part of town.

The pho here is okay and is one of those things you order when you have a cold and it is February, but the mango milkshake, oh the mango milkshake!  It is a bit pricey, but it will change your whole outlook on life, especially if mangoes are in season.

My boyfriend and I just spent an entire day cleaning up my place for a visit from his parents.  We were dirty and cranky and finally I just said the magic words, "mango milkshake", we dove out of my apartment and down the street, got the milkshakes and sat on a bench in the school yard drinking them and watching the fireflies.  All was good with the world.

Getting in late to my hotel after a long cross country flight, I was famished. After settling in, I asked the front desk if there was anywhere to eat nearby and she suggested "the Diner" next door. This place is definitely a throw back to old school Diners. The wait staff was very friendly and suggested the hamburger steak dinner. I went ahead with that and within 5 minutes, my plate came out. Everything was good and tasted like something mom would make at home. They have all the comfort staples and after a draining day, I filled my belly to its delight.

My wife found this little spot and especially to be off the main road, it's doing well for itself. Normally you would expect a spot like this to sacrifice in taste, quality and so forth but I was impressed. The only reason why it doesn't get a perfect 5 stars, the last two times I ordered out, the meat was chewy. Didn't enjoy that to much but overall enjoyed the rest of the meal. The rice, noddles and veggies are not heavily salted as some Chinese spot typically do. Plan to go back when I'm around the area.
Of course there's a wait, but definitely worth it. We tried the East Nasty and B-roll for our first visit and hope to return to Nashville to sample the rest of the menu.

I've been on a "strip mall Mexican restaurant" tour as of late. I found myself in Plainfield for work the other day and thought i would give this one a try. I ordered the "huevos mexicanos", which was scrambled eggs with onions and peppers mixed in. It was served with a side of beans and rice as well as warm tortillas. It was by far the best version I've ever had of this dish. I spent around $7 including tip. The portions were so large that I had enough leftovers for another meal.

Sadly I could not buy coffee here because they only accept cash despite having an iPad as the primary cashier interface. I've helpfully pasted some solutions to this below and hope the owners decide to join the 21st century. When I asked why they only took cash, one person glibly replied "so you know how much you can spend" which implies to me that the management is incapable of managing their own money electronically, therefore requiring their customers to pay cash to compensate. 

Best of luck guys. 

https://squareup.com/
https://www.paypal.com/webapps/mpp/credit-card-reader
http://www.payanywhere.com/

After driving 23 minutes for your tacos, I experienced a lack of customer service and personality with your staff. During the pandemic, your staff should wear masks.  FYI, more than one customer, as we waited, complained of the lack of customer service. At this moment, we are at the Parsons location. My friends and I would never visit your location again.

Overpriced & inconsistent.  We have eaten here a few times and had a great meal the first time.  Unfortunately; the last two times have been unpleasant experiences.  Heat level is inconsistent - my husband ordered medium heat (mild, medium, hot, and Thai hot are the options) and it was so hot, it was inedible.  We don't mind spending extra money to have a great meal, but they are expensive and have meals that do not satisfy.  We will not eat here again.

Just go! The best fried chicken ever!!! Remember: call ahead, if you want it quicker. Chicken is cooked to order. Remember: ask for your heat level... Original or Mild or Medium or Spicy. Just go! Eat it hot there, and get some to go!

So we got a cab and went to WH. The food was the same as I remember, really bad and that makes it super yummy. Our waiter was good, the cooks were fast and I can't wait to go back. 

I wish we had a WH in Southern California!

Delicious soul - food great prices - friendly service 
If you're craving some home cooked food then you've come to the right place! The smells when you walk in make your mouth water! Definitely a must if you're looking to have a great dinner!

We decided to have Sunday brunch here on our last day in NOLA. We made reservations well in advance and requested courtyard seating. We arrived and were seated promptly. The service was excellent and the atmosphere was beautiful. Our problem was the food and where/how it was presented. I felt like I was collecting my food from a cafeteria. The food area was very industrial looking, unlike the elegant decor and architecture. The food itself did not live up the their reputation. I just read another review and they described it as "Cajun Golden Corral" and I have to agree. Definitely not worth the $102. (buffet and one drink) per couple.

Simple menu and fresh food. I like that they offer cabbage and avocado with the burrito bowls. The bowls and burritos are a large serving size and definitely filling. I'd eat here over Chipotle or any other chain. Local-ish owners. Staff always seems less than thrilled to be working, but still friendly with quick service.

I have never, in my 67 years,  been thrown out of a restaurant! Well... that changed last Friday night when 7 of us went to Bacio to celebrate my daughter 's birthday. The food was mediocre at best... (and yes Jay I too am Italian) the pasta was from a box ... not homemade as stated, and under cooked...and the serving sizes were very inconsistent... but mostly small.
Having said all that, we were still making the best of the night as we were enjoying each other's company. Until that is the owner started screaming at the large table right next to us! Ultimately the customer he was yelling at was thrown out by the owner! We all agreed that was bizarre... until a short time later we heard the owner screaming at a woman at ANOTHER table!  By now we were beyond appalled....as he threw out this woman also!
The owner saw my daughter looking at him in shock so he proceeded to push the woman's plate of half eaten pasta in my daughters face yelling at her telling her to taste it!!
By now we had all had it... my daughter told him she had no intention of tasting it.... one thing led to another... he was now screaming at all of our table telling us to get out of his restaurant!! He threw a pad at my son and told him to write his name down (also gave him nothing to write with!) so he would never take his reservation again! As if we would go back!
What put me over the top is he made my grandson cry!! So I told him he was a poor excuse for a man let alone a restaurant owner... so he pushed me!! He put his hands on me and pushed me!
Fortunately I raised my son to be a good man and exercise restraint when needed as he wanted to deck him!! The owner then calls the police telling them we were refusing to leave! All we were doing at that point was making sure we gave our waiter Ken, who was awesome, a great cash tip !
The police came and after a brief statement asked me if I would like to press charges against the owner for assault... I declined as I never want to see his face again in or out of his restaurant!
Please heed my advice(and The several other reviews that are similar.... NEVER GO THERE! If you need further proof... read not only other negative reviews... but the owner's crazy replies!

First trip to Tarpon Springs. Saw good reviews and decided to swing in. the menu was pretty limited but my husband and I decided on the Greek salad and one of the platters. it took a while for our server to get to us to order but they eventually made it.  My husband wanted a beer and asked for "one of the Greek beers" as there weren't any descriptions or options on the menu. Our server wrote it down and went on their way. My husband then commented that they must only have one Greek beer, because he wasn't given any options; the menu didn't list any specific beers either. After our drinks arrived I noticed our server smoking a cigarette outside on the sidewalk right outside the restaurant and right next to other dining tables. This was unsettling, and I kind of didn't want them handling our food after that. 

However, our food arrived promptly and was very good. I was surprised to find potato salad in my Greek salad, but it worked! The gyros were delicious as well and the pita bread was great. At one point we wanted more tzatziki sauce but our server was no where to be found. After a while they finally stopped by and we were able to ask for more sauce and our check. 

All together it was not the best experience. The food was very good but
it was the experience that will keep us away. I find it unacceptable to have employees smoking out front of the restaurant, ESPECIALLY when it is in the outdoor dinning area. I am sure there is an area behind the restaurant that they can smoke if they need to. If I would have seen then when looking for a restaurant, I would have kept on walking.

I'm very disappointed; I order over the phone the young lady couldn't understand  my order repeated atleast 4 times.
Once I received my $20 order food was cold,fish was small, bread/hushpuppies hard as bricks, didn't receive any garlic-butter sauce. 
Waste of time and money!!

Despite the location of the hotel I absolutely adore the Ritz-Carlton and I have stayed here are a couple of times
Every time I room is immaculate and very charming and beautiful I love the breakfast and that shopping boutique near the courtyard 
I spent $90 on a robe for my son and when I got it home sadly it was way too small for him. 
I just gave it away. 
The room is so pretty I've stayed in two separate ones one was a sweet and another time I got to see Stephen Spielberg's wife in the elevator

I think the food is great and at night in the piano bar they have dancing and drinks the crowd is a little bit more older 
So I ended up going into the French quarter instead to the carousel bar
I would definitely stay there again
 There is convenient shopping with a local CVS drugstore and a foot spa are a couple of doors down which I always visit when I am in New Orleans
The staff at this particular hotel are very very nice!

We've eaten here before and have always enjoyed the service and the food has been great. But this evening the service was in disarray and food soso. 3 people came up to us to take our drink orders. Once things were straightened out or drinks came we placed our order I asked for a deluxe Texas burger with Mayo on the side, my daughter had a opened face sandwich with a Caesar salad. Well the Caesar salad was a handful of lettuce thrown on the plate with a dribble of dressing on it. Hmm where was the care, where was the parm cheese, where was the croutons? Very disappointing. Our entrees arrive no problem with my daughter's but I get a burger with onion and cheese. So I asked about the bbq sauce, onion rings lettuce and tomato as well as Mayo on the side. Our waitress states "you didn't ask for the deluxe so you don't get it. So now you want it". She just walks away. I have no idea if she's coming back with what was left off or waiting another table. She eventually came back with a piece of lettuce some shriveled up bacon and 1-2inch thick sliced tomatoes. Still no bbq sauce and no Mayo. Tried to get her attention a couple of times but she ignored us. It would seem that be we were bothering her from the moment we got there or she had a bad shift and some of her "heat" was being taken out on us. If you're a waitress/waiter you are there to serve people. When you get a new table it's a new group of friendly people looking to you to guide to the best food. I used to waitress and yeah there were jerks but not everyone is a jerk and shouldn't be treated so. She was rude and disrespectful be ware of the staff.
Best burgers and fish n chips in town. I love the eclectic menu. My friends from out of town always insist we go there when I pick them up from the airport.
I saw the pizzas coming out if the oven as I was ordering and they looked yummy but my crust was over cooked and not soft. The bottom of the pizza was do crispy it was like a chip.
This place is great.  Was visiting from out of town and stopped in. Reasonable prices friendly people. Highly recommended.
This place is amazing! Good service and good food. It's been very consistent. Everything I've gotten here has been so delicious. I would suggest it to anyone.

Worst restaurant experience I ever had in my life. We were forced (!) to move from our seats to another table with no explanation or any apologies. Not even a "please" word! The server was super nervous for some reason that we were not aware of and forgot one of the drinks completely and ignored me couple of times. Food was not good either. Overpriced and tourist trap by all means. I really don't understand good reviews for this restaurant.

I ordered from Jalisco via Grub Hub. My food never came. I called the restaurant. The woman who answered snapped at me so rudely ("You know this is a restaurant?! Why would you call and play like that?!") like I couldn't possibly have ordered something, or maybe she thought I was plsying a joke. I contacted Grub Hub and they canceled the order. I wish I could say if the food was good or bad but I can say with certainty the service is awful.

I don't know what the rage is about Chick-fil-A, maybe it's me, I just don't get it.
Don't get me wrong, I like my chicken, but this is just blah. Is it a better choice than a burger? Absolutely! But there's no real flavor to it...
We got the grilled chicken sandwiches & the kids meal chicken nuggets.
My husband liked it. Definitely better chicken than McDonald's and Subway!!
But not better than Arby's chicken pecan salad sandwich!

Real Mexican food. Will definitely go back. Had tacos and burritos. Excellent!
Also had their pizza.

Schenk's Family Bakery on Veree Avenue in the Fox Chase neighborhood of Philadelphia, has been in the flour, water and yeast business since the early twentieth century when their first generation started baking in Germany before immigrating to Germantown  and opening their shop in 1938. Both the family and the bakery have moved around, but always remained Philly centric. Their recipes travelled well.

Today, their storefront is small and lined with glass display cases and shelved walls, all full of their classic cookies, doughnuts, cupcakes, custom iced cakes and amazing pound cake. My small sample of half dozen doughnuts (glazed, vanilla iced, cinnamon sugar and powdered sugar) were all fresh, lightly yeasty and full of sweet flavor. They were perfect for accompaniment with hot coffee. 

The vanilla pound cake was dense, moist and was solidly superior to any commercial effort I have eaten. Better even than Starbucks, which has been on my pedestal for a long while. It would have been great heated with a scoop of ice cream, but stood unapologetically on its own. Why they loaded it up on three sides with copious amounts of white icing is a mystery. It was truly an amazing sugar coating, but unnecessary given the quality of what it covered. Diabetic overkill. 

That shelf of large Eagles playoff cakes looked great and gave comfort that they would be the hit of any party or cold afternoon tailgate at the Linc. Unfortunately, the sweetness would not be enough to change the outcome of the game to come.
Another Chinese own Japanese restaurant.  I give it to them that they try to be trendy.  Service was fast.  Food is ok.  No complain

Gary (husband & part of my dining "trio") and I enjoy eating here because they have a super salad bar with lots of variety & some substance. They also have delicious deli meats and sandwiches, and other choices (wraps, soups...) as well.

We opted for one all-you-can-eat salad bar ($7.50), one side salad ($3.99, that interprets as one visit to the salad bar) and one New York Yankee sandwich ($8.59, and the most loaded sandwich they have, per the cashier. Figures we'd pick that sandwich, oink, oink!).

The sandwich was served with warm and very tender pastrami and corned beef and Swiss cheese on rye. VERY good and very large. It comes with chips and you can substitute them if you want something else (might be a slight up charge). I realized after we left that this sandwich did not come with a pickle! I love deli pickles (hey, I grew up with real hardcore deli foods in NJ & NY, including pickles stewing in a real pickle barrel!). 

PICKLED ABOUT THE PICKLE DILEMMA:
So I was curious and I just called them and said, where's the pickle with the deli sandwich? And I found out I missed the boat. Or at least the pickle. They stopped putting them on the plate. They can be found lurking on the salad bar--all you want to eat! And no one told me. So the pickles are still lurking there. So I'm telling you, you fellow pickle lovers! (I know, I sound silly and I'm just being playful about it.)

We ended up taking it home as tomorrow's dinner. Gary enjoyed the terrific salad bar, with many veggies, pastas, olives, beets, eggs, artichokes, nuts, granola, dried fruits, breads, desserts, these really super flatbread crunchy crackers (health-foody and fab), and a billion other choices on the long salad bar. Something for everyone. That salad bar is a very good value and the vibes at this Jason's are friendly and nice. Oh, and they have free soft ice cream for those who may still have an inkling of an appetite left after enjoying Jason's Deli delights. HUMANE TIP: Remember to tip the busboy; there is no regular table service except someone carries the food to you when it's ready. Those folks work hard clearing those tables and work long hours.

This place is definitely touristy but the food is good! The building is old so the AC leaked and the waiter cleaned it off with what seemed to be sponge mop which grossed me out a tad and the room is a bit tight hence only 4 stars. It's worth going to if you're on bourbon and looking for a good meal.

The food was ok. I usually enjoy my late night buffalo wing craving  here. But our server, Justice was one of the worst servers if not the worse server I've ever had. I've actually had her a couple of times before, and she was never great. Hardly smiles, not very friendly, poor attitude, doesn't greet her customers and  just seems to do the bare minimal. The last time we were there, we waited nearly 20 minutes after we were all done eating to get our checks. Which we actually never received. I had to get up the table to find her sitting in the bar, conversing with the bartender,  and ask for our check. The first couple times I thought that maybe, she just had a bad night and that she was off her game, but lately I just came to the conclusion that she just doesn't care about her job and it shows. I normally leave a 20% or more tip on my check even if isn't the best service or meal, since I used to wait tables. So I'm really lenient and sympathetic when it comes to service knowing a lot could go wrong, and it's not always the servers fault for bad service . But  there's really no excuse for her poor work ethic that our table, all previous servers/food industry employees felt that she didn't deserve a tip. So we all tipped well bellow our usual 20% that I felt she didn't even deserve. I normally don't write reviews yet alone a review with more than one sentence. But I felt Justices' performance was so poor that it needed to be said. Hopefully management take this review as connotation to improve as I'm probably not the only one who feels this way.

Novel idea, definitely a cool spot.

It is absolutely impossible to sit down at Starbucks and enjoy a cup of coffee with my wife and two toddlers. This is a fact. The kids melt down after gnawing on a piece of banana nut bread for a minute or two, and we leave amidst a series of judgmental stares and the occasional sympathetic smile from another mom whose been there.

This is a place where you can meet your adult friend and share a cup of joe while the kids happily play nearby. There's a pretend kitchen with lots of accessories, and little play fort, a ton of books, building toys, train table, carts for pushing...even a little baby friendly zone. 

I know a lot of the other reviews criticized the price and amount of toys. I definitely think that issue has been rectified. The price was very reasonable, and the amount of toys and quality of toys could not possibly leave anyone wanting.

As for not being able to bring in food from outside, I think that's ok. They serve food, they're an establishment that has to make money...and while I can't speak to the snack quality, the coffee they serve is great, so who needs to bring it in?!?

If you're looking for a place for a play date where you can enjoy some adult time, I definitely recommend giving this place a try.
Great New York style pizza.  Fast service and depending on who is working it can great or average service and the 1/2 price Monday 12 in is a deal!
Delicious!! Most tasteful and fragrant rice I've ever had, and the most savory garlic naan.  The staff was friendly and welcoming, wish I lived closer, I would come here all the time!

What happened to this place? I used to eat here frequently 10 years ago before I moved out of town. Loved the BBQ chicken pizza. Now the restaurant has slipped considerably, and is in need of some TLC. the pizza is less than impressive and huge selection on the buffet was meager. I suspect that was due in part to the fact that no one was coming in for lunch, which I found very odd  for the time of day, this place should have been rockin. I tried again a week later and had the exact same experience.

We're not members, but were invited by a friend. Both my wife and I thought the food here was incredible. We had a couple different appetizers and shared three small plates. Everything we had was creative with impeccable attention to detail in both preparation and presentation.

A bonus is the bar. The service at the bar is awesome, and they have a great variety of drinks and a knowledgeable staff. We just told them the kind of drinks we like and they hooked us up. They even have live herbs growing behind the bar to use in drinks and food. Amazing.
I love this stop. I tried the earl grey latte with a hint of lavender and it was perfectly done. The chocolate mousse was the perfect amount of sweetness for a nice treat.

I have been a fan for a long time with FWOT i love their cheese fries and also their chicken fingers, i usually try and tell lots of people about this place and to try it. Its a comfortable little place and i know the next time i eat there i have to get something else besides chicken fingers and cheese fries haha.

I've stuck by my word on Bakersfield being the best taco joint around UNTIL we visited here. La Mulita is easily just as good, if not better, than any taco joint I've been to in the city - and that's almost all of them! Their tacos are VERY generous. I had the pastor and could honestly only finish one. Best pastor taco I've ever had. I also like that you get a side - and I will never stray from those incredible sweet potato wedges with aioli for dipping. My fiancé and I wanted to go back the very next day! 

Also - margaritas. The margarita is smaller than most but the taste is SO fresh and strong. Easily one of the best I've had. 

Service is another very important thing to us and Irma was hands down the best we've had in a long  time. She was the absolute sweetest and VERY helpful. We will 150% be back here!

So, I deleted two previous bad reviews for this place because I gave it another shot (6 years later) and it was better than we remembered.  The pizza we got could have used another 3-4 minutes in the hot part of the oven but we'll order it extra well done next time.  My only complaint are the fries...why don't pizza shops make their own hand-cut fries?  They are so much better and if you have the right slicer they aren't difficult to make.  We'll probably return but my only request is better fries.
The best chicken burger in town. Was s not surprised as I usually order a donair, but thought i would try something different. His icy and thick meat. 5 stars and underrated for the chicken.

Lobster sandwich for lunch was amazing! Kyle In the bar is a great bartender. Fun, easy going and makes it happen. 

During my 2 day stay in Clearwater I came to the restaurant 3 times. My last time on Sunday I ordered the mahi tacos, they were quite bland and tortilla was cold. I should have sticked to the lobster sandwich. Definitely recommend the lobster sandwich. Server was blah, probably hungover. Go to the bar and sit with Kyle for great decide :)

Definitely one of the best restaurants in South Jersey. Ceviche and agnolotti were out of this world delicious BUT the only reason I'm not giving this restaurant 5 stars is the price. $5 for bread and butter seems unreasonable with some of the entree prices being as high as $56. Some of the nicest restaurants in Philly don't make you pay for bread! Otherwise service is exceptional, atmosphere makes you feel like you're in the city, and food is great. Definitely a must try.

Good and Bad experience this morning: 

Good:
I go this Wawa frequently due to the convenience of location. Usually I go in for a quick cup of coffee because it is the best, and always fresh! (guess it is hard to mess that up). Customer service at the counter is ALWAYS great! 
Bad: Today I ordered a scrambled egg/sausage burrito with avocado, (which i have ordered from other locations with no issue) and I am extremely disappointed with how it was prepared. The wrap was simply a mess. Initially I thought "ok they were in a rush...ill eat it with a fork and knife when I get to work" , but after opening it and noticing that it was a WET sloppy mess, with more salsa then eggs and NO AVOCADO, i couldn't even eat it.

I am a huge fan of Wawa, specifically this Wawa, because of the customer service, but I will not be ordering from their deli anytime soon. 

I hope this review is read, and the message gets out to the employees that are prepping food to SLOW DOWN, and make the food like they would be the one that has to eat it, like the other Wawa locations do.

Thanks,
Christina

Sarita's has a plain and even "tumbledown" exterior and interior appearance (a dive?). The waitress was friendly and helpful. I ordered the Steak Tacos, and they were simply delicious. My partners remarked that their orders (flautas and the Steak Plate) were also very good and enjoyable. The appetizer chips, cheese sauce, and salsa were also quite nice. I would recommend this place and certainly return. RJT
I feel like taste of the dough better than little ceasars ,but little ceasars I'd also way cheaper. The buttery crust is good but sometimes the pan pizza is too oily.

When we approached, we saw a woman sitting alone in the dining room so we had low expectations for the place. Upon reaching the counter, it took ten minutes for the cashier to take our order... the donuts are really lacking for me in proper density and sugar balance. The chocolate frosting is deeply overpowering, as is the glaze on the toasted coconut, so much that the taste of the coconut vanishes.

Also - I ordered a chai and the cashier had to walk from the kitchen to our table to ask me three different questions (hot or cold, size; etc), which is petty to mention but it was annoying. I am glad to have satisfied my curiosity but there's a Dunkin Donuts up the road which has never failed me.

Great traditional food and excellent service! We ate char broiled oysters, blackened gator, jambalaya, fried catfish, and rice and beans! It was our first night in New Orleans and it was a great first meal!

Ordered take out:
Crunchy crab roll 
Shrimp and avocado roll 
Futomaki 
Fried tempura vegetables 
Very affordable price for the quality of the food. Would def come back.
Such great coal oven pizza and at a great value in comparison to other neighborhood spots.

It was ok.

First, the service was a little weak, i.e., the waitress had too many tables. Also, you should always just drop the check off without asking at this type of place.

Second, my hot roast beef was served lukewarm.

Third, I make better homemade french fries so I was not really impressed by the "Daddy Fries".

It was inexpensive and the portions were large so I will probably check it out again.

The food is delicious however as of late the portions have become very stingy.  Service is extremely slow and you will be waiting for your food for a while.  If you aren't starving and have time to chit chat, this may be the place for you.

Great customer service and food. Got the Dubai mixed grill and mixed grill platter. More than plenty for 4 of us. Lots of different kinds of meats. Huge portions. Plenty of dipping options. Perfect rice. Hummus appetizer was quite filling itself. I dont know what the garlic sauce is but it's so good. Also got Turkish coffee shots complimentary. Very nice. Nice decor.

My third or fourth time here. Haven't loved a meal yet. The food is just ok to me. I'm always let down. The lighting is kept so low that it's difficult to read the menus. The A/C is always too cold for my liking. No more cheesecake factory for me.

I think this is the best OJ's in Edmonton.

My friends and I used to go here all the time when I worked nearby. The staff got to know us, and even offered us a "service" discount. The place can get pretty packed, but the servers are always on top of things. The food is also really good.

Portion sizes are massive and the food is fresh. I love love love their dill dip with fries.

This location has a couple pool tables as well as a nice deck. I like how big the restaurant is. It feels very spacious, but is awesome for people watching. If you manage to get the big booth on the top level with your back facing the door, you will enjoy hours of people watching.

Also try their brunch on Sunday mornings -- yum yum!

I was in Tucson on Saturday for an event for my company and decided to stop in after seeing a lot of good yelp reviews. It was a good decision! Great food & very prompt & positive service. I would definitely recommend this restaurant.

Just ate the most delicious rib eye cheesesteak, because it was Calvin's top recommendation from the kitchen. Couldn't have enjoyed it more. Tender, well seasoned rib eye, perfectly baked, crusty bread and peppers and cheese to top it off. Great service from the bartender too -- introduced us to the wonder of grapefruit bitters in a High Life (so much better than you'd probably think it could be). 

They serve food here until they close -- which is 4AM. Come on by and say hi. I think you'll be pleased -- or at the very least, not disappointed.

OMW! This place is incredible! Doesn't look like much from the outside but wow the food is authentic and reasonably priced! Great flavor! Definitely recommend if you are looking for a great lunch in Hendersonville! Staff was very friendly!

I tried the Bulgogi Asada bowl today, and it was by far the best food I have eaten at the food court.  The meat was well flavored and the ingredients fresh and nutritious.  The service was friendly and the restaurant looks clean. I hope this place sticks around!
My first visit to Hina Hot. The food and service was exceptional. We will visit again.

Nice place, very good food. My only 3 star reason was a poor waitress service. Extremely slow and our 2nd round drinks were made wrong. We sent them back and 15 minutes later they came back wrong again or just sent back the returns.  The bar was 15' from us. We could see it all transpire why service was slow. iPhone was more important. We flagged down another waitress and told her. She immediately made our drinks, but 1st showed us the bottle, on the 2nd round and it was the wrong vodka. It was some odd name and flavor. 
Our food came out and all was well.  Next the original waitress came by us and was at desk. Another waitress came to her and asked for help and she said no I'm going on break. This is why the 3 star and it would have been a 2 but our replacement waitress figured out what was wrong and we understood.

We went here for dinner on our vacation. Our food was very good and the service was exceptional! It was a very nice dinner. Our steak was very good and we tried quail for the first time and it too was good. We even had our 10 year old and she was felt very welcomed. We would definitely recommend this for anyone looking for an upscale, off the beaten NO path meal.

Blew in on my way south, was going for BBQ in Murphysboro but road construction caused me to change routes. I was surprised how busy BOB was at 2:00 PM, but it was Friday. Service was quick and food was tops as always. On the way out I gave a thumbs up to a member of the management team.  MJ came over and remembered me from the last time as was there months ago and we had a nice conversation, this kind of personal touch adds another layer of high quality customer service from the top down.
