Most places don't take the time to make a customer feel appreciated. To me that means a lot.  Did I mention how good the foodbwas

This is our second time in four days visiting this restaurant and both times we were not impressed. We had eaten there for both lunch & dinner service and even though not slammed it took FOREVER to be seated, once seated it took FOREVER to be approached for our drink order or even just an introduction.  My coffee cup had something on the inside of the glass and the salmon with mashed potatoes were drenched in oil, looked ugly to eat and made us sick! The restroom was out of soap on Fri and on Mon it was still empty... coincidence I would have guessed but now I think not! The service was fine once it got going and the cheesecakes are always delish other then that this place has been removed from our list of fav places to eat when visiting Boise.

After having a good steak at The Mill, I went to Outback Steakhouse with my colleagues. I haven't been to Outback in a while and was curious to try  it again as I love steaks. 

I went for the Outback Centercut Sirloin. Normally, I am a Ribeye guy but the waitress recommended it as an Outback signature dish. I asked for light on the seasoning as I love the taste of steak just seasoned with salt. But I was curious about the seasoning and so I compromised with a light amount. 

Since I joined my colleagues late, the bread was almost over. I was a tad disappointed that I had to remind the waitress about the bread. 

When the steak arrived, what I got was mostly  medium or medium well with a touch of  medium rare in a small portion. 

But what was worse was the steak had a rough texture. Tasted like a very cheap cut of steak. The exterior had a burned leathery texture like it was overdone. The light seasoning ended up being a tiny saving grace because as much as I don't love seasoning, it added some taste to a steak that lacked any on its own. 

When the waitress asked how the food was , she started to walk away right away as if the question was some obligatory "g morning" you would mumble to  a stranger as you pass him by. Next time she came around, I told her about my steak. She kind of did a half hearted "oh is there something you want me to do ?" and I replied, "Not really as I will just finish it even if I am not happy about it" as I dont like to waste food. She seemed relieved I wasn't demanding an exchange and said "oh well, the objective is to finish the steak , am i right?" and tried to pawn her lazy response off as a joke. 

Oh, and the evening parking is bad. It was full and it would be nice if they put up a sign out there that you can park at the Carrabbas opposite the restaurant (I had to call my colleagues to find that out as they were inside and were able to ask the waitress).
Delicious food and wonderful service. Devonte and our host really took care of our party. House-made cannolis we're everything. Try the filet mignon if you get a chance!

Definitely meh.  A 20 minute wait in line for ordinary soy-sauced stir fry dished out cafeteria style.  I did it once a few years ago and wasn't impressed, and tried it again yesterday for a second opinion.  Normally I wouldn't have waited in line for that long but had to see what the fuss was about.  Curiosity satisfied, I won't be back--and I really don't think food like this is worth standing in line for.  Serious about quality Chinese food?  I'd recommend nearby Yen Ching.
Best veggie pie in town and that $5.00 menu is insane.  The portions look like regular size to me.

Kim Cameron, Valencia, CA
I used to eat at Silvergreens all the time while I was attending UCSB. I like the BBQ Chop Salad, and the Chicken Ranch Sandwich. They make a killer breakfast burrito too (but, The Cantina's are better)! Everything was always fresh and delicious!

I was really excited to try this place and it did not disappoint. From the décor to the ambience and especially the food everything was great. We had the warm dinner rolls with black garlic butter, the octopus and the butternut squash to start.  There were so many flavors that popped and worked together harmoniously to make a delicious bite.  The food was flavorful, unique and beautifully presented.  Only knock is that a thicker part of the octopus was a little underdone for our liking. The njuda carbonara was absolutely perfect -- cooked al dente, rich but balanced, spicy and a perfect amount of salty guanciale to bring out the flavors. Probably our favorite dish of the night.  The spiced chicken was succulent and flavorful with a delicious crispy skin.  Between the two of us we were easily satisfied.  We'll definitely be back to try more.  It seems that there are certain staples on the menu with other items that rotate.  They also have an extensive wine and cocktail menu and a pretty good selection of draft and bottled craft beer.  Excellent meal, highly recommend for a special occasion.

After reading the mix of reviews I decided to try this place out for myself, glad I did! I had the lasagna and it was delish! The service was great, quick and waiter was a pleasure. Go early as on my way out it was extremely busy around 6:30. I will definitely return on my next visit back to Nashville.

A tiny restaurant in the back of a wine store makes for some interesting conversations. 

If you are claustrophobic do not come here or bring a group and request the group dining area that is out in the open. There are lots of seats at the bar and a few tables for 2 tops or 4 tops. We're bar people so that's where we went for a light snack and drink before dinner. We went around 6pm on a Saturday which I thought would have been more packed but it wasn't bad at all. 

We were able to find a corner at the bar and ordered the chef's cheese plate special. For the amount of cheese and etc you get doesn't justify the $ amount but ..you are in 'South Tampa'. Regardless, if you're already here you're ready to drop some $ so DO it! I did the Spanish Trail flight and left tipsy (job done check). We always forget that this place is here but venture back to it every couple of years. =)

This pizza is the best in the area. Taste similar to New York style pizza the sauce & cheese is excellent good quality thin crust. The house salads are served with precision I prefer black olives on mine & Romaine Lettuce. I am from philly & I  very impressed by their pizza quality. We Philadelphians are very selective about food. Pizza is delicious overall.

I ordered take out sushi for the first time and feel that it was a total rip off. The lady on the phone said $8 per roll with 16 small pieces. We received small rolls with only 5 pieces. She claimed that she said 6 pieces but we doubled checked while still ordering on the phone. $40 worth of sushi was barely enough to feed 1 person. I wont be eating here again. The only good thing was that they gave us a full refund (we did not eat any of the food, so we deserved a full refund). 

There are too many 3/4/5 star reviews from this place on yelp that make this seem like a decent sushi spot, but do not be mistaken. Unless you have been here before and understand that the food you buy will be way overpriced and not satisfy your appetite. Go eat somewhere else.

Columbia is by far my favorite restaurant. We've been to several locations and love that each environment is a little different but the delicious Cuban food and ambience is the same. 1905 salad is so delicious. Love the history and of course the wonderful service.
Went for Mother's Day and it was great. We were a big party and they had a limited menu but we really enjoyed ourselves and the food was delicious.

Moved from New York a few months ago and have been having a hard time finding good wings. My sister and a few friends stumbled upon this place and I am BEYOND pleased! I ordered wings and OMG so good!! Our server, Sydney, was amazing! We live not even 2 miles away and will DEFINITELY be back!
Energetic, loud, fun, and great food. Oysters are so fresh and the cocktails are strong.

We are from Los Angeles and this is our first time in New Orleans. This is hands down the best meal we had so far. I recommend this to whomever is in town to go. Its in the warehouse District and I will bet my last dollar it will give and place in the French Quarter a run for its money.

This is the best food in downtown Clearwater. It's always delicious and is far healthier than anything else in the area. The staff are consistently friendly. Prices are in line with quality food. Personally, I love the wild-caught salmon and the carrot-raisin muffins. The salmon is always crisped just a bit on the outside and slightly rare on the inside unless you ask them to cook it a little more for you. Take their chocolate pudding and truffles home with you.

This is a fast food "chipotle concept" for Greek food located next to Bentos.  The staff is helpful and friendly.  The establishment is clean.  The food is fresh. You pick from a pita or a bowl then you pick your protein, sauce and toppings.  Simple yet tasty concept.  We couldn't pick what protein to get and the person taking our order let us try it before ordering. The food portions are big. The baklava cheesecake was tasty and they have a few other dessert options as well! They also have a variety of sides to choose from.  I got the standard French fries which you can never go wrong with French fries but there is a variety of other things to try. I will definitely be going back when in St.Pete and need a quick bite to eat.
Everytime I order from this place my order is sent to me incorrectly. Tonight I ordered jalapeño poppers (7.00) and  the order only contained four small poppers.

Horrible every time I come here the big lady thats a manager is very rude and mean to costumer and employee its not just once of twice its every time I come she's very mean to everyone. And I feel bad for the employees. And other customers I'm pretty sure her name is Rebecca. All the other employees are great. And nice its just her and I'm not the type to complain but its every time I come in and I do not like how she treats her employees it is not a good positive work environment and makes everyone in a bad mood.

Lots of happy hour specials, huge oysters, and overall great food. I'm normally not a big fan of crab cakes but these were too good. I came in with a party of 11 and my food didn't come out till everyone was almost done eating ..which was fine. The server messed up EVERYONES tabs and didn't fix it (there were 5 different checks not 11). He said he is used to the "old way" of doing things which is putting everything on one tab..... "you guys are all friends you can fix it" I'm a waitress and I would never say something like that. Maybe I just didn't understand his humor? Food was too good to let the server ruin my experience (even though I didn't understand his way of doing things).

Great food, in a great portion size. Salmon is awesome. No disappointment. My server is great conversation also. Ordered a chai latte. It was really good as well. Cool spot. Dinner, coffee, tea, cocktails and beer. If only my bf was here we would be happy having beer and coffee at the same place with good food.
They are no longer at their original location at 16th Street and 30th Ave. I have no idea if they're still in business

Love the food here. In my opinion it's the best Chinese/ Japanese place in the area. The decor is nice on the inside, great and welcoming service and the food is amazing. My gf and I order sushi and food here all the time

I can't believe I've lived in Tucson for 10 plus years and never ate here in til today. Fresh tortillas made here and it's delicious. I eat it with there tasty salsa. Shrimp ceviche is made fresh as well, so it took 20 minutes , well worth it. I had chicken fajitas and it came with beans and zucchini and corn, so good. My  husband got the Chili con carne that he liked , and he also had a Michilada that he said was excellent! This place is now our favorite Mexican Restaurant. I can't wait to go back.

Kona Grill is one of the nicest atmospheres and menus I've seen more experienced...
This is a beautiful place to sit and enjoy a meal.

Given the number of restaurants that have been at this location, it appears the Shack will be on a long run. Good, tasty food and a prompt staff that's on top of things. While it's a bit noisy for some business activity, most who come are there to enjoy the food.

I love going to The Palms and getting cheap, decent drinks and the salad bar.  As was previously mentioned, the croutons are very tasty!  It is a good deal for a steak as well since you cook your own.  The bartenders and waitstaff are all locals and great!  I do not recommend going late on the weekends as people get a bit out of hand, see note below. 

*Beware, on busy weekends like Avocado Festival and New Years; people get very drunk and it gets crazy in there. I turned around on a very busy evening to find a very drunk patron rifling through my purse! The owner seemed concerned until he realized it was one of his regulars. He felt the guy was harmless.  I handled the situation myself by going to the guy and telling him the cops were on the way. He left in a hurry.

I unfortunately won't be coming back to this Bully's location. I had an extremely unpleasant experience with an employee Courtney. She gave me an incorrectly made meal for my to-go order and I came back to the store to replace my meal and she made me pay for it!!! So I paid about $45 total for what should have costed me no more than $30. Naturally, I wanted to get my money back somehow so the next time I got a to-go order (~2 weeks later) I kindly spoke with the manager, Miguel, who promised to speak with Courtney about the incident and give me a call back the following day and find a way to make it up to me. He never called me back and therefore I never got reimbursed. Luckily, there's another Bully's just down the street off of Sierra Highlands :)

Oh dear sweet jesus just go eat there. I want to die every time I'm there because I know my life won't be as good after my sandwich is finished. There are options for everyone. You gotta go. You gotta.

Tsunami does not have the best Sushi in West Chester but they have the distinction of being the best place to get Sushi in West Chester. The staff is  friendly, the portions are generous, prices reasonable, and I have almost never left there without receiving something for free. If Tsunami had a bar, I would eat there every other night. The staff is great, and it is a place worth patronizing. The quality of the fish has only been getting better recently, so it's absolutely worth the time.

A fine place to grab a Hoegaarden and catch the game on the numerous flat screen TVs. Beers were brought promptly and we were left to our own devices until our pints neared empty at which point our waitress reappeared.
Montecito and Mesa Burger are the best here!!! Their sauces and fries are so fresh and filling at the same time. Must try if you're in Santa Barbara!!

Ate there today with 13 men.  Great parking lot. They were really busy even with the rain.  Food was good. Service was lousy.  Coffee was 2.19 per cup and refill after you ate and ready to leave.  Guys real unhappy about that.  One guy ordered salad but never received.  My club was very good.  They just not set up to handle large groups.  Beautiful building. One guy ordered burger well done.  Had three people inspect before the cooked him another and it was just right.

Tex Mex kind of place. Portions are huge. Next time we will share.
Small place that is comfortable. Definitely on my date night list now.

I use to LOVE this place. However, the last three times we have been the service has been horrible, the salsa taste like tomato paste and the food is terrible. They use to be really good however, I sent my food back since it was ice cold came backs till cold and flavorless. I guess zapatas or sinsenior next time

This was my first experience at this place and it'll definitely be my last. A coworker of mine kept trying to get me to check them out and I'll admit, on their social media the pictures of their food did look very appetizing. So we went on a Sunday around 1:30ish. The line and wait at this time wasn't too bad. When I got to the window the girl taking my order gave me a huge attitude for no apparent reason. She was mumbling, I had a hard time hearing her and she would give me dirty looks as if I did something. I just brushed it off as another girl with a stank attitude. Anyway, my coworker got her food and we tasted her egg roll. Let's just say they were nothing to rave about. No outstanding flavor, not mouthwatering, they were just...okay. I got my cheesesteak and we left. When I got home I opened it and it was drenched in hot sauce. It looked absolutely disgusting and I knew I wasn't going to like it...I was right. Again, nothing special. Too much hot sauce, the bread tasted like it was old and doughy. It just wasn't good--like at all. A huge waste of $12. My coworker also said that it wasn't what she had expected either and she had been very excited to try them out. So needless to say, please save your money or go elsewhere like Delesandro's and get you a real good cheesesteak or if you want a good egg roll you're better off going to any average pizza or Chinese store. The "Better" Box is overhyped, overpriced, and basic asf. Seriously.

Great location, great decor/ atmosphere, great bartender, great food,(I engulf the 20oz steak almost weekly) and great patrons.  Pricing is great and I've been there many times.
A great escape/ decompression from the rigors of night-life work & a great hang-out spot.
Huge selection of beers & liquors, nice menu, and some seating by the sidewalk for a smoke.  Courtyard can seat about 50 people, and the bathrooms are clean.
Check this place out!

I've been here twice now and both times the card reader is down so you have to pay cash and they don't provide a receipt, hmmm. Anyway, the place is usually warm inside and even though it was 85 degrees outside, it was cooler than inside. We had a beef sandwich which overflowed with meat and was delicious.  My husband had 2 meats, the pork and ribs and they were pretty good too.  I loved the collard greens.  It's pretty but doesn't compare to Texas bbq!

Sadly, we never made it to the meal as we arrived to an empty restaurant at 5 pm and were seated at a horrible table and asked if we could move, but were told no because the restaurant was expected to fill up with people that called for 6 pm reservations.  This must be a new thing as I thought reservations were to reserve your time/table NOT an actual table location within the restaurant.    We decided to leave as they definitely did not make us feel welcome, especially as first time customers.  To say the least this was one of the most bizzare experiences I've ever had at a restaurant.  It will definitely be our first and last time!

As someone whose family hikes to Lansdale to eat at Greater India (scrumptious cuisine) every time we want Indian food, I was very excited that an Indian Restaurant was coming to Red Hill.
We went for the lunch buffet and were disappointed to find that children were the same price as adults ($10) which seems a bit steep. Kids 10 and under are free at Greater India.
Since I knew my children would not eat that much, my youngest 2 ordered off of the childrens menu (about $6 ea) instead of getting the buffet.
The food was good, but chicken was the only meat option on the buffet (no lamb or beef) like what we're used to.
I must say, that although the food was good - my family and I will still travel to Lansdale for the Greater India buffet. 
The bill for 2 adults and 3 children was $50. At Greater India my entire family can eat the buffet for $35, not to mention the food is better.
I think Sawaii is on the right track and with a few improvements could really be a great restaurant. 
Improvements:
1) more buffet variety (less chicken dishes)
2) a lower buffet rate for children
3) Explanation of what's in the dishes on the buffet so people know what they're eating.

I love most things Hawaiian and was very excited to learn about Solid Grindz when I moved here two years ago.

I tried the big kalbi and bang shrimp plate. The kalbi was overcooked, but that shrimp was delicious - crispy, creamy, a little sweet. The mac salad was spot on with the creaminess and seasonings - not soupy or anything! I didn't know what to expect with the beans, but they had the standard bacon/smoked flavor; I paired this with my kalbi and rice and it was almost the perfect bite, maybe I could have used a little bit of kimchi, but it's not like I didn't enjoy my lunch.

SG is located very close to the Air Force base and it gets packed fast. The parking lot is a complete cluster, and small, so be careful when you pull in, there's just a bit of wiggle room. The dining room is small/medium sized due to its location in a tiny strip mall. Orders get cooked fast, so you're not waiting too long whether you're dining in or take-out.
Out of all the spots for some Korean fried chicken, decided to try this spot. One of the good ones, get it with the sauce on
The food was delicious and large portions. Service was quick and the meals were different than your traditional Chinese restaurant fare!

The last time I was at Beyond Bread, they did not serve breakfast but the do now!  I had to head back to Phoenix early in the morning and I am happy to say that my friends rallied despite their hangovers and we all came here for an early breakfast.  The bacon, eggs, bread, everything was so tasty and that makes this my number one spot for hangover breakfasts in T-Town.  From the patio, you can dine and take in views of Mt. Lemon - something I take for granted living in Phoenix now.
This is our go-to pizza. It's unbeatably delicious. We get no garlic butter on crust and fresh garlic and basil as toppings.
Great new find in Media! Excellent nachos... I was too stuffed to eat the pickle brined fried chicken with mac-n-cheese I ordered, but I took it home and it was still delicious.
This was such a delight to eat here!  Homemade pasta, wide variety of choices and great service.

Wow. We just asked the server if she could bring us drinks. Direct quote "I'm sorry, I don't have time. I have 5 people waiting at the bar". I get it - you are busy - but you don't EVER tell a customer you don't have time for them. Especially when you just brought drinks to the table next to us. #worstserviceever #wontcomeback

BYOB whats not to love!?...I absolutely have to rave about this place. I had dinner here tonight, anyone that wrote a bad review obviously was not in the same restaurant I was in. We had amazing service, we sat outside in the back. I ordered the penne Sofia Loren and it was spot on, the sauce and broccoli were exceedingly delicious and perfectly seasoned when it came to the table (as it should be). I then indulged myself with the dark side of the moon chocolate cake. I should advise anyone ordering this to have someone help. This is definitely a chocolate overload, but I enjoyed it. I would come back in a heartbeat!

Ok.  Yum.  Not sure how I missed this place these past few years.  Now, with North End BBQ and moonshine closing I may have found my new porkopolis.  1st off, it's right on the Monon which makes it difficult not to stop by while trying to burn calories on my bike... let's call it a reward.

My wife chose the carnitas tacos.  A big hit.  Very well flavored and came with an array of sauces.  I'm always excited to see a menu section labeled, "Choose your meat."  I did the pick 2 and absolutely loved the fatty gristle and slightly charred ends of the brisket and the very tasty pulled pork.  I had corn bread and their VERY tasty sorghum Brussels sprouts.  Sweet and salty... yum!!

This place is an utter joke. I don't care how good people say the fried chicken is here. Service is so below par, it is laughable and you feel you are being punked. The day I went with a group of 8, on a Tuesday at lunchtime, I kid you not, they were out of 65% of the menu items. Either you cose your doors if you can't afford to order product or get product trouble-shot to your establishment. It was truly the biggest joke I have ever experienced in a restaurant. 

A lot better dives and fast food restaurants than this joke.

Thai Spice is my favorite Thai place in Indy.  The staff is very sweet and attentive.  The drive from downtown is a bit farther than I would normally go, but  it's always worth it.  My recommendations are the Thom Ka Gai soup and the Panang Curry.  If you can get your dinner mate to order Panang Curry and you order some Padd Thai and steal some of their sauce, it's EXTRA good!

I was very excited at the prospect of takoyaki and okinomiyaki in Philadelphia, but sadly this place just doesn't cut it.  I've never been to the place itself, but they were one of the vendors at the Night Market.

I arrived at the market around 6:30 and immediately stood in line at Maru. They weren't even cooking food at this point because they were "waiting for something."  So I made my rounds and came back not much later.  The short line was painfully slow, when I looked at what was going on there was some white guy making about 6 takoyaki at a time rather than using the entire pan.  I've been to Japan where I've seen them quickly make dozens at a time to a golden brown perfection.  This was inefficient and undercooked.

For some reason I kept on waiting and after 30 minutes I get to the front--only to find out they are out of octopus!  The ONE dish they are supposed to serve and they are out of it after about 10 people.

I know the night market is busy, and not the same as a restaurant, but this gross mismanagement of time and ingredients proves to me that I do not need to be going here.  Combined with all these reviews of undercooked, poor quality food leads me to believe Philly won't be seeing Kyoto street food anytime soon.

Our ride on the Steamboat Natchez was in October 2011.  We still laugh about it to this day.

Four of us purchased tickets for the daytime jazz cruise with lunch.  We were pretty excited for the experience - we all love jazz music.  And food.  And anything New Orleans.  I believe we each paid about $30.00 for the daytime cruise with lunch.

We sat on one of the decks for a few minutes and listened to the announcer talk about the buildings around us.  Again.  And again.  I kid you not, we heard the man say "To your left, you'll see the old Jackson Brewery" a minimum of 10 times.  I started to think he was a recording just being played over and over again.  

Eagerly awaiting the start of the music, we went down to the dining cabin to eat first thing.  The food was mediocre at best - the portions were good, but almost everything was lacking flavor.  You're in New Orleans!  Really you expect something that is going to blow your mind.  It was highly disappointing.  And we heard nothing but the droning on of the announcer, who by now I was positive must be a recording.

After eating, we went back up to the deck to sit in the sunshine.  Still, the announcer continued, pointing out all of the visually stunning (sorry, sarcasm) barges lining the river.  I get it - the Mississippi is a river used for many industrial purposes.  I didn't care about the scenery, I was just happy to be on a boat on the Mississippi.  And because I didn't care about the scenery, I really didn't care to learn where the different barges were from.

Finally, one of us said "Has anyone heard any jazz music?"

We all looked at each other.  Surely this was some kind of joke, right?  How can you have a jazz cruise without jazz music?

Then, finally, the announcer stopped talking.  We had reached our turnaround point.  It had been an hour of his monotonous drivel.  We had all tuned it out and just tried focusing on the sunshine.

Then suddenly - JAZZ!  Glorious jazz!  We all smiled at one another and breathed a sigh of relief.

But it was extremely short lived.  

Before the musicians could even get out 6 notes in their song, the announcer was back at it.  Telling us the exact same things he had already told us on the way down here, but now we were able to see things from the opposite side of the boat.

We heard no more music for the rest of the cruise.  And we were still convinced that the announcer was a recording, until some kids ran by us on the boat, and over the PA system came the thundering warning "NO RUNNING ON THE BOAT!" 

By this point, we were all laughing quite hard.  We were trapped on a jazzless jazz cruise with a man who loved to hear the sound of his own voice and so he would not shut up.

As we passed the Jackson Brewery once more, the haunting words were spoken again: "To your right, you'll see the old Jackson Brewery."

The announcer's closing message was this, nearly verbatim:

Thank you for coming on the Steamboat Natchez.
That's the Steamboat Natchez.
Tell your friends.
Steamboat Natchez.
That's the Steamboat Natchez.
Tell your friends.
Thank you.
Steamboat Natchez.  
Tell your friends.   
The Steamboat Natchez.

Maybe there's a secret room somewhere on the boat where you can hear some decent jazz.  I don't know.  We never did find it, but we'll always have these memories, and those are priceless.

LOVE LOVE LOVE IT!!! The gumbo here is much better than many others I've been too. Everytime I visit NO I stop here to grab a bowl. I ordered the Chicken and Okra Gumbo.. I posted a pic also and of course it was awesome. We were seated rather quickly and we had a party of 8. The food is also affordably priced so that is a bonus. Some places charge $12+ for a bowl of gumbo and its not that great. Here It's under $10 and hits the spot. Must try if your coming

Came back after being gone for a year to what use to be my favorite pizza place. I was told to find my table in the back room which to my disappointment was in front of the men's and women's restrooms. I sat down without complaining because the restaurant was full. 

Just after my pizza arrived, the staff came into the backroom where I was seated and started deep cleaning and shutting down the room. While I appreciated the fact that they were cleaning the room, turning over chairs and putting them on tables while there were numerous parties still eating made a lackluster atmosphere even worse. Couldn't they just wait until the room was at least half empty? Or better yet shut down part of the room and clean it? 

The worst part was when one staff decided to clean the women's restroom. It was 4 feet from my table where I was eating and she propped open the door with a dirty water bucket and proceeded to clean it with chemicals. The worst part was she went off and left the door propped open for the remainder of our meal. 

Good pizza but I will not be back.
no es buena, la pizza es tarta de culo y huele a tripa de pescado

Mediocre food, waiter was rude, he treated a new hire waiter like dirt.  I had the fettuccine alfredo with chicken, it had no flavor, the garlic bread tasted like burnt plastic. Probably will not be back.  I guess I should have looked at the reviews before I went there, according to them, I should have ordered the toasted ravioli or the pizza.  Cost $70 for 3 of us to have pasta dishes, iced teas and no appetizers.

Saw this place while driving on Page and was excited by the name and the prospect of another great Korean restaurant in the area.  Tried it one time, ordering the Red Chicken Gangjung (fried boneless chicken pieces in red gochujang based sauce), a Spicy Beef Bulgogi bowl, and Popcorn Mandu.  The order was done right on time and the lady who handed me the bag was very sweet and made sure I knew to keep the bag open so that the chicken would not get too soggy.  That said, during the ten minute drive home it did get kind of soggy anyways.  I can't fault them too much for this under the circumstances, but it does take away some of the appeal of the dish.  The chicken is essentially just fried chicken pieces in thick sauce with a side of rice. The quality of the meat was very good and it was cooked right, but I found the sauce much too sweet and cloying. The rice is white rice topped with a small splash of soy sauce and some little droplets of fried batter. It looked interesting but really was not a very creative way to dress up the rice. There were no veggies or pickles either of which would have made the combo much better.  The Bulgogi served on rice did have some veggies mixed in which was good, but again much too sweet and lacking any BBQ char.  Finally the Popcorn Mandu.  Not sure if these mandu (meat dumplings) were house made or store bought and dressed up (I suspect the latter, but not sure). They were fried and sauced with mildly spiced mayonaise and some melted cheese.  Not bad, but also not very interesting. This dish needs additional seasonings and maybe dry toppings to add some spark. I would not mind trying Fire Chicken again, but given the choice I much prefer  O Wings down the road on Page for Korean fried chicken, and for other dishes I prefer Sides of Seoul (also down the road on Page). I hope this assessment spurs Fire Chicken to up their game and provide some real competition to the korean food landscape in STL.
Food and service were fine. The place was filthy. Dirty table, dirty seat, spots on the silverware, sticky menus and food stuck to the glass. Disgusting.

I had a reservation on a Friday night. The waitress we had was excellent, and friendly. Things turned strange when a small, doughy roll was served to only those who had ordered a dinner entree, and not to those who ordered salads, soups, or appetizers in lieu of an entree. We asked for more rolls, and she advised us we would have to purchase for $1.50 each. We said, no, it's not even that good. We expressed our displeasure with this policy. Moments later, our entire table was served a roll. I commend them for doing the right thing here.

 I ordered the  French onion soup which had the classic taste and was good. I also had the beet salad with goat cheese and arugula. This was disappointing, as it was very heavy in beets and very skimpy on goat cheese and arugula. I left 1/3 rd of my beets because there was nothing else left to balance them out. 

My husband had the crab cakes which were very good, but the cantaloupe/cucumber soup over sorbet was way too sweet to eat as a first course. 

They have a very good beer list. The prices for drinks were reasonable.  

I think I'll keep trying different restaurants if I find myself in that neighborhood. It may be best for drinks and appetizer.
.

Lucky 13 is a cool place to hang out and it's very family friendly.  The pizza is just OK, nothing to mind blowing.  Like the rest of the reviews, great toppings but poor crust.  Also, the pizza is always way under cooked so we have to ask them to leave our pizza in longer so it comes out piping hot and completely cooked through.  Sandwiches are ok, salads are pretty tasty.  Not our first choice but not our last.

tried this place after getting a haircut at my new barbershop...all I can say is amazing... Great service... Clean establishment and food was absolutely amazing... I had the Philly cheesesteak which was one of the best I've had in Florida... If you haven't check this place out yet make sure you head over and give it a try

It felt like a sweet escape from busy Carrillo and crowded State street 
I like how they make the atmosphere feel cozy country style, but still comfortable in modern pleasure
Date night, friends hang out, or family gathering are all good :)

Despite living in the area for over 20 years - we have never been to the Liberty Bell.  Avid breakfast junkies that we are (HE rather than ME) we decided to try it out.  We were greeted and seated immediately and the place was full for a Wednesday morning.  Tables, booths and a sit and eat bar offers plenty of seating options.  well lit and decorated with liberty bells and classic red white and blue theme. Food served properly and hot, no way these plates sat under a heat lamp for more than a second!   A sure pick for a cheap eats place - plenty of menu specials coupled with blackboard specials to boot.  Got out of there with full bellies for just over 10 for the both of us (not counting tip) The high point I have to say as a tea drinker was the full pot of steaming hot tea in addition to my cup.  Tea drinkers are often overlooked as coffee is usually top dog - having the pot and being able to top off and refill my tea was a HUGE plus and greatly appreciated.  Stop in to the Liberty Bell, one of the finest diners in the area, you won't be disappointed.
It's about time we got a sushi place. Staff is friendly, good quality food. A bit pricy for sushi.

My family went there for lunch.  We experienced good food, good service and a great atmosphere.  We went early enough on a Sunday - we had the place to ourselves when they opened!  It was a wonderful view on a beautiful day.  Definitely recommend if you want a nice experience.

I heard they just opened up here on Grant Rd and Oracle, they were previously serving in the Tohono O'Odham swap meet. Was bored staying home so decided to come here for take out. Got the Parillada (1 lb meat + fixing) for $23 and one goat taco ($2.50 +$1= $3.5). We were allowed to choose hot to 3 types of meat for the Parrillada so we picked Carne Asada + Carnitas + crispy Tripas. She did ask us what tortillas we wanted, we said flour so we assumed we were getting tortillas with the paradilla but when we went home no tortillas to be found. I guess they forgot it, no worries, we got our own tortillas at home and put the meat in. I mixed in a little of the carne asada, Tripas, and carnitas in one taco and it was good! They asked us if we wanted the Tripas soft or crispy so we said crispy! Crispy Tripas is good just a little greasy. The carne asada is ok, could be better if they had wood/ charcoal grilled it. The goat taco was good, the meat was tender, it is an acquired taste, so if you don't like gamey meat maybe this is not for you since it cost $1 more than regular taco. The lime provided was tiny and dry, hardly any juice coming out but no worries, we grabbed some lemon from our backyard and we were good to go. I'm glad to support local mom and pop shop during this difficult time, will you?

This is the time I went here and the food was so delicious. The staff was very friendly and I never ate garlic naan which I ate here it was awesome. I suggest this place for everyone and I will be there next time when I visit clear water.
This chicken right here was yummy! Tasted like grandma's chicken! Full of flavor and cooked to order! The music is live so you can dance while you wait!

Went with 2 of my adult kids and my parents to the Christmas buffet.  It was a bit pricey, $65 a a person, but the food was amazing.  They had such a large selection, lamb, turkey, prime rib, grilled chicken, bbq ribs, grilled shrimp, peel and eat shrimp, sushi, crab claws, not to mention all of the sides and desserts.

The staff was amazing.  They were very friendly and the service was fantastic.

While the it is a bit pricey, it was nice to have such a large selection of food choices and not have to clean up after the big meal.  It is very likely my family and I will be back.

Such a peaceful setting in the middle of a garden and around century old cabins.  Food was very fresh despite small portions.  The experience was well worth the price tag. It's recommended for those who are seeking a unique atmosphere and quality. Bread baked in a flower pot was a unique surprise.

I've become a regular at The Abbaye. Crafty, innovative pub food with an excellent rotating craft beer menu. We are suckers for the Seitan Cheesesteak. It's a contender for the city's best vegetarian cheesesteak. The staff even recommends it for carnivores. The Chimay-marinated seitan adequately resembles steak, but it brings deep layers of flavor to the table that simply aren't present in a run-of-the-mill cheesesteak. Their homemade seasonal veggie burgers are always a home run. While I've also developed an addiction to their crispy thin-cut fries, I recommend you pay the upcharge and order the sweet potato fries. Not only are they the best in the city, but the portion could feed a small nation.

I'm not a huge fan of buffet style restaurants.  Not sure if it's because I am a major germaphobe and cringe at the fact that 500 people before me have reached into the same bin to get spring mix, or maybe it's because there are so many places to try before resorting to Sizzler.  On my visit here, I was kicking it with the Grandparents and this was their choice for dinner.  My suggestion to get sushi instead got a hard no!  

Brittany was our server and I do have to say she did a fantastic job.  By the time I went to make my salad and came back the food was already out.  She made sure to check up often and bring extra napkins, sauces, and waters.  In addition to the salad I did notice they have a small taco bar and a pasta station for those wanting other choices.  I liked that they had over 5 options of lettuce including kale but the cleanliness of the salad bar was not very kept up.  Salad dressing was everywhere, mixed in with others and the spoon handles had food all over them.  As far as stocking up toppings those were neglected as well.  

Its Sizzler not a fancy steak house.  The salad bar needs some loving.  If you already decided to eat here, the service was really good and hopefully it will be a lot cleaner as well for other future customers.

I recently made a trip down to Tucson for business, but arrived early. I'm not familiar with the area, but I happened to pass by Buffalo Wild Wings and figured I'd have lunch while I waited. The service is good here; my drink was never empty for long. The food is good! Best wings I've had (and I've had a lot)! The noise level is loud, as there are a lot of TVs for people to watch their sporting events. However, it wasn't so loud that I couldn't have a conversation with someone. Overall, it's a good place to grab lunch. In and out in an hour or less.

Excellent restaurants must have four prime elements: cuisine, ambience, service and location. This restaurant ranks high in terms quality of food or cuisine. But, they are missing some obvious conditions. The condition of the business is substandard in that they are not keeping up with needed repairs where walls need painting woodwork and doors need repairs and cleaning, there is only one bathroom for both woman and men which is grossly inadequate and the bathroom looks in need of refurbishing because the walls and floor looks filthy bye to age. They had a beautiful 2nd location on South Virgine which they closed unfortunately.

The Cheescake Factory is located at the International Plaza Mall off Westshore Blvd and Spruce Street right next to the Tampa International Airport. Aside from being the employer of Penny from the Big Bang Theory, the Cheesecake factory is famous for a large variety of over 20 pies that they serve. They also have a 10+ page food menu with food of every different type from Italian, Japanese, Thai, Chinese, American, Mexican, and other regions. I was dissapointed that the Cheese Cake factory got rid of the Thai Chicken but I recently  enjoyed Bang Bang Chicken & Shrimp with Curry,  Peanut, Chile, Coconut, Sautéed Vegetables, and steamed white rice.  

For Dessert, my favorite cheesecake is their Caramel Turtle Cheesecake. Other honorable mentions for best cheesecakes include: Adams Peanut Butter Cup Fudge Ripple, Hershey's Chocolate Bar Cheesecake, Chris' Outrageous Chocolate Cheesecake, Reese's Peanut Butter Chocolate Cheesecake, Chocolate Mousse Cheesecake, and Strawberry Cheesecake. The Cheescake Factory also serves 9 different kinds of specialty cakes and 4 different ice cream desserts. Sometimes my office orders a couple pies for everyone. I really like how the pies are precut with plastic in between so that slices can be easily taken out. I Look forward to my next visit!

There is plenty of parking available in the mall's private parking lot. Our server was friendly, quick, and courteous, and we got our food in a timely manner. Usually the wait times are kind of long to get in here because it is such a popular restaurant. It's better to check-in, go shopping, and then come back when you are notified that you can be seated instead of waiting around and being bored.

We love this place. Super nice people. The due traditional Italian well. My step son loves the ravioli and they added meatballs he was in heaven. They do the best Cesar dressing, I like the tangy version and they nailed that. Chicken parm is great. Desert selection was awesome. We did the rainbow cake. Can't say no to that.

I had the pleasure of eating at Matt & Marie's last Wednesday while visiting Philly.  I go to Philly a good amount from NYC and always looking for a good lunch spot.  The place right away gives you an upscale sandwich shop feel. Super clean and crisp looking.  The staff was super friendly and inviting as you walk through the door.  They walked me through the options and I decided to go with the Uncle Guys' Turkey sandwich.  I love the personal touch they give you as they make your sandwich to tell you about the ingredients in the sandwich.  The price seems perfectly reasonable for such a high quality sandwich.
I sat down at the communal table and inhaled my lunch.  I couldn't eat it fast enough, it was one of the best sandwiches I've ever had, I also bought some dark chocolate milano's that they sell at the cashier counter! A nice touch if you ask me!
If I worked in the area I would see myself having lunch there most days.  Such a nice change from the usual sandwich shops.  The high quality of ingredients really makes a huge difference.
I highly recommend everyone in the area to stop by and order up some deliciousness!

Two visits prior and hit or miss. I now think it all depends on the waiter. We had an excellent waiter Martin who got us the lettuce wrap with shrimp blackened now not on the menu. The black and blue chips and pot stickers were great. We stick with appetizers and no entrée for the best of everything. Oh and they do have Moscato wine (we were told last time not available and its always been available). Great visit this time thanks to Martin.
Cute little place! Very welcoming.  The kids just wished they had more flavors. Reasonably priced also.  We will return!

Stopped in for a late dinner.  Really nice looking bar/restaurant.  They also had a nice outdoor dining area.  The service was great and pretty quick.

I was pretty happy that I was able to grab a Miller High Life.  It's my favorite major brewery beer.  They have cans, pretty good.

I got the fried green tomato grilled cheese.  The sandwich was very big.  Delicious thick bread, with rich, creamy cheddar, arugula and a nice big fried green tomato.  It was filling and completely delicious.

Great place, good service and delicious food.

I just ate the most perfect spicy gluten-free veggie pizza from G's. The deliciousness caught me off guard. Perfect crust. Perfect hot n spicy swirl drizzled on top. Wasn't even expecting to write a Yelp review for this place, but here I am. Excellent customer service from Yancy. 5 star experience.

10" Gluten Free Crust. Light Cheese. Regular sauce. Mushrooms, Black Olives, Jalapeños. Hot-n-Spicy sauce drizzled on top.

I will never eat at this location again. I went there on Halloween night to get food after trick or treating. The night manager is always unprofessional. He was giving out free food to people he knows. Telling the employees to cancel Uber orders because he didn't want to do them. Someone had a baby in a car seat in the kitchen on top of a box and they have roaches all around the drink station and front counter area. This is very discussing they need a hole new night shift including the manager. And they have the nerve to have the inside open 24 hours now. They can't handle that at all I waited 40 mins for my food and it still wasn't right. I was told I couldn't get a refund because I didn't have a receipt when I was never given one in the first place.

I really wish they had the option to give them no stars because they are horrible.
The kimchee fried rice is off the chain! I knew I piced the right spot when the restaurant was filled w\ Korean's enjoying hot pot. I will definitely be back. This place is worth eating thru the menu

I've been a fan of Blue Sky Bagels for quite a while.  I've been eating there since the location quit being bruegger's bagels.  

My favorite bagel is the Salmon Filet.  It is always delicious.  That is one thing about BSB, they are very consistent.  The Asiago I got today, tastes identical to the one I had 2 years ago, as far as I can tell.  Same with the flavored cream cheeses.  One way to tell how "economical" a location is, is the number of high school students that go there.  If you accidentally hit during the local lunch time for the high school, it is packed.

This place is delicious and inexpensive.  Usually, the service is pretty fast, too.  I'd say that is the only inconsistency.  It seems that the staff has a bit of a high turnover, and if you catch them training a couple at once, things slow down (quality does not go down though).  At worst, this is a minor complaint.

I'd say the biggest issue with the location, is that a few of the parking spots that look like they are part of BSB's parking lot, are owned or managed by a parking company.  I've gone in and come out after lunch to a parking ticket.  So, just be very aware.   I think the signs displaying this information have gotten a bit larger since then.  I think this only occurs on the weekends, as well.  

So, if you want a filling, delicious meal, head here.  That it is very inexepensive is just a bonus.

I read this in another review and it is so true. It's a great place, but your GPS will lead you astray. It thinks you are there when you are still on the highway. I got there prime Sunday brunch time (about 10am), and the seats were packed. However the bar/counter was almost empty, so I was able to sit there immediately. Others waited in line for several minutes, because they apparently don't understand the concept of eating at a counter. A mother with a couple of small kids seemed to be under the impression that it was a part of the waiting area. But that's purely a customer flaw. Prompt service despite the crowd, good food, and great prices particularly for the Carmel area.

Not sure how I haven't reviewed Bamboozle yet. We come here every couple of months and we just got takeout a few days ago.
This isn't a typical Vietnamese place, it's more fusion.  As a vegetarian this is a great place for both me to find something to eat (yay tofu) as well as my boyfriend. He loves their pho. My usual go to is the red curry with tofu... so good. We usually split a couple of their fresh rolls (peanut sauce.. mmm). Perfect. 
The reason for not the full 5 stars is because I once ordered the Udon noodles in miso broth. Unfortunately it was like eating a salt lick. I am sure that was enough sodium for 3 days. (Looking back, I should've returned it). Also, for some reason they often want to put us at a small table right in the middle of the walkway when they're much better tables available out of the way. We just started asking if we could have another table. All is good.
What an amzing meal again at Solstice. You can not go wrong with anything on the menu. The service is impeccable as well. Will keep going back many more times.

I had dinner with a friend at this incredible restaurant. Usually when you go to a brewery, you expect bar food. Not at The Depot. The salad had pinenuts, dried tomatoes, Parma cheese with fresh green--not that bagged stuff; it was the best dinner salad I've had in a long time. I had the scallops, as did my friend. They were cooked perfectly and served with coconut rice, which was delicious. 

The beer flight was second to none. The waitress told us the brewer is the Co-owner who trained at the International Brewing Academy in Munich. He is the real deal! We also noticed a display case with all the awards his beer has won.

Recess is simply outstanding.  an amazing culinary journey with thoughtful preparation, as well as unique and  pallet complimenting flavors.  presentation is also not lacking, but again, those flavors.  A short but sweet review here.

Recess is a must dine at establishment.  great vibe, great staff, amazing experience.  Would come back tomorrow in a heartbeat.  Such creativity going on in that kitchen.  You can feel the love in every dish.  Outstanding experience.
Fresh, clean, delicious food . Staff was super polite and friendly . I def go back with more friends . I enjoyed every bite of my food . Spicy tuna was delicious

Best Chargrilled Oysters I've ever had.  We happen to live close to Oyster Heaven- Hoggs Island, Tomales Bay, etc.....and growing up Asian, or Pacific Islander, or whatever the hell I am we grew up over here in the bay area eating oysters to become the hornballs we are.  Everytime I've been to New Orleans I've always went to Felix's or Acme in the French Quarter and I could honestly say nothing on that side of 'Merica has anything on Drago's.  It's so good that even in the Bachelor Party of 14, we each ordered our own plate of 12 each....THAT'S 168 frikin oysters.  We probably put them Gulf Oysters on the Endangered Species list.

BTW, I gave Drago's 4 and not 5 because the different lobster dinner that each guy had wasn't anything spectacular.  BUT DAMN THEM CHARGRILLED OYSTERS! WOW!!!!!!!

I went to the Kove for dinner on a sunday night. The place is quite visually appealing and provides a decent atmosphere. The waitress was friendly albeit a bit nervous but I didn't mind. I had the plain pizza which was decent for a bar pie. My wife got the crab cakes which she enjoyed but I was pretty surprised that they came with no dipping sauce or remoulade. I wonder what the thought process is behind that. My father in law had an audubon burger and my mother in law had a fish entreé which they both seemed to enjoy. 
              My major bone of contention is with the beer selection. They are definitely attempting to make craft beer available but it looks like the selections were picked by someone who is on the outside of the craft beer culture. The most appealing thing I could find was a Sam Smith's oatmeal stout which was 6.50 for a bottle. Way too expensive and will never compete with places such as the pour house where you can get the same thing for almost half the price. As far as the rest of the beer menu, how about some double ipa's, imperial stouts, barleywine's, barrel/oak aged beers? They list Goose Island on the draft menu. Goose Island makes like 50 different beers, so that being listed as Goose Island tells me nothing. If this place stepped their game up with the craft beer, I guarantee that customers would come in droves. There are plenty of incredible craft beers that are widely distributed and readily available. So this was a major turn off for me as well as the open bible on the table by the exit. That's just inappropriate. Obviously they are working out the kinks, but overall it wasn't bad. I hope the owners take heed to this advice: Differentiate yourself with a truly great selection of craft beer, and they will come. Craft beer is a huge trend and it is growing exponentially. It will make your establishment truly succeed.

Food was great while catching up with a dear friend. It's Alishah's service that will keep me coming back. She was amazing! Super friendly, knowledgeable and great recommendations. You go girl! Lobstah Trap is lucky to have you.

For my appetizer, I ordered the crab bisque, it was the best crab bisque I've ever tasted! It was creamy and not too overpowering. It was amazing! We also ordered the Chophouse house salad, which was a little disappointing for a $9 salad. It seemed like it was just iceberg lettuce you buy in a bag with tomatoes, bleu cheese, and bacon. 

My husband and I split our entrees - I ordered the sea bass and he ordered the filet. For a steakhouse, I was surprised they only prepare their steaks "Pittsburgh style" and I realized I wasn't a fan of the charred taste, I felt like it took over the whole steak. We ordered the steak with the fried lobster, a little on the salty side, but very flavorful. The sea bass was probably my favorite of the night, the roasted garlic added was a nice touch. With our meals, we ordered the loaded baked potato which was delicious! Fully loaded is what you order and fully loaded is what you get.

No complaints here! My wife and I enjoyed our first date night without kids since last year / pre-covid. Very fine wine selection - they offer flights and even better, tastings! I was able to enjoy nine different tastings of vinos - mostly Italian, but some French, German and Portuguese. My wife enjoyed a sparkling wine flight followed by a glass after. We didn't order food except a cheese/charcuterie board which also didn't disappoint. We will definitely be back to try more wines and definitely more food sampling's. It's a must for a nice date night or casual night out with friends!

I was a fan the first time I had Company Burger.  Soon after they opened, I got a burger and fries to go and that it was oh so-so.  After friend after friend giving rave reviews, I decided I had to go back and see what all the hype was about.  Ever since, I've been hooked.  You walk in to order at the front counter, give them your name, the grab a seat just like any good burger joint.  I have to say that I am not typically drawn to the type of burger Company  is (I put it in the classic diner burger category), but man they do it better than anyone.  The meat has a wonderful flavor, they use a very traditional gooey American, toast wonderful buns to perfection, put the perfect amount of extremely thinly slice barely grilled red onion right under the cheese and serve it up piping hot.  My complaints are consistency (sometimes they overcook their meat leaving much to be desired in the way of flavor) and their fries (which just aren't very good).  Despite the claim that they are double fried, I tend not to believe them.  Only a few of the bunch are edible (but that's probably a good thing on some level).  The onion rings are definitely the way to go.  They array of sauces is a plus (try some garlic mayo on your burger... mmmmm......).  This place is greasy and filling, but it's delicious and exactly what it should be.

I love Pizanos. They make a very good pizza and the price is low enough that I can stop by once every week or two for a treat. On Wednesdays they have the bacon cheeseburger pizza by the slice for the special and it is fantastic. I usually go for happy hour between 3 and 6 because the slices are much cheaper. I definitely prefer Pizanos over Pizza Reno or Noble. The atmosphere is a little more upscale as well, which adds to the experience for me.

We have been loyal customers of Tha Joint for years. When 2 Tha Joint opened it gave us more opportunity to go enjoy their delicious sushi. This location is near downtown. It's somewhat easy to get as it is on Plumb Lane. It's spacious and has a private room for big parties. They offer great deals...especially the free sake with All You Can Eat. They have one menu... no lunch and dinner menus. You pay one price for All You Can Eat. Service can be hit or miss but he sushi is always spot on. The rolls are not huge... which is nice for easy one bite pieces. My all time favorite roll is Tha Twister followed closely by Tha Wingman. An absolute must order are the mussels. I have tried others sushi restaurants but always find my way back to Tha Joint because they offer the best.
I felt like I was dining at a 5 star steakhouse this morning, excellence at its finest.

Good value - large overall portions for the money. Management or the cooks have improved since the other reviews. My New Orleans Eggs Benedict were excellent. Hints of lemon in the hollandaise, the andouille smoky, and the star, the poached eggs were perfectly runny with creamy gelatinous whites. Only minor takeaway was the muffin base was not crispy and was a little soggy by the time I got to it.

The side of ranch potatoes were crispy and not oversalted.

My Mrs. had the Wisconsin Scramble (sans cream cheese) and being a lite eater, found it light and fluffy, but ate the whole thing, so it must have been tasty. The pork sausage was tasty, tender, also not over salted, or overcooked, and with good sage flavor.

Two entrees, coffee were $25 even. Service was attentive, and cheery, Alexandra was reading her customers correctly as to pace and service tone, and her tip from us reflected that.

We will be back for more lazy Sunday brunches. The wait was not too bad, 10 minutes, and they have separated the seating from the cashiering since the last reviews.

The best you can say for this place is it's....OK.  I've only been here a couple of times because I can walk here when I have to take my car into Central Tire a couple of blocks away.  

Both times the food has been edible, but not great.  That's the best I can say for this place, it's OK but will never knock your socks off.  

I had the waffle combo breakfast I think it was called with coffee.  It was eggs, bacon, sausage, stuffed hashbrowns, and half a waffle.  In my case I 86'd the sausage and ordered all bacon because I don't like sausage (make whatever double entendre joke you want at this point).  

The bacon was good, I'll give them that.  Also, my waiter Emmet provided me with excellent service, so I have no complaints about that.  The coffee was also good.    

Their stuffed hashbrowns consist of 2 layers of shaved potatoes with sour cream, green onion shavings, bacon bits, and cheese in the middle.  It might sound appetizing but it's a little bland for my taste.  I'll eat shaved potatoes but everywhere they serve them I always find they have no taste.  Even in this case all the fillings didn't help too much.  Edible but underwhelming.  

The waffle was....meh.  I suspect it was microwaved toaster waffle rather than something made from scratch which again is edible, but nothing that would inspire you come here regularly.  

The worst part about the whole thing is the eggs.  It was pretty obvious the cook just half assed the job and poked the spatula around the grill a couple of times instead of thoroughly rotating around like professional chefs do to make scrambled eggs.  But the piece de resistance in their eggs is that it was obvious they make it with that fake egg like substance from a carton instead of real eggs.  Much like the shaved potatoes, these are very bland - even the addition of a layer of cheese and salt and pepper doesn't really help these eggs.  

Again, edible but uninspired.  Instead of imitation egg like substance I'd suggest using real eggs.  I mean, with a volume discount how much more expensive can they be then the fake egg like substance from a carton?  

I once met an ex-manager from IHOP and he mentioned to me that IHOP at least blends real eggs together with the carton imitation egg substance.  Not sure why Ricky's can't just at least do the same thing.  

So, to me, Ricky's is what it is.  When you have to take your tires into Central Tire for repair, it'll do to have breakfast in while you wait for the phone call your car is ready, but nothing that would inspire you to come here regularly.

Excellent food with friendly service.  The restaurant is small and the parking is a joke, however, these are minor compared to how good the food is and how fast/hot it is served. My only hope is the consider moving to a larger location (not to far though). Five star in the low budget, no frills, great food category.

En route from Columbus to Chicago, I decided to meet with my friend, Paul from Guam who I haven't seen in a decade.  Luckily, he moved to the midwest for an orthodontics residency.  Anyway, as I was yelping Indianapolis, MacNiven's caught my eye because they serve haggis and veggie haggis as well, and decided that this be the place for me, Paul, and Amish to dine out on our first night.  

I was excited because Chicago does not have restaurants that serve haggis on a regular basis.  The only time I had haggis in Chicago was at the Robert Burns supper at Martyrs.  But...the haggis was not too good here.  It was a bit too mushy and wet.  While the veggie haggis tasted just like chilli.  So the only thing going for MacNiven's that night was that they served Belhaven and Tennet's.

Stopped here on a recommendation. We were in the area for a trade show. What a gem! Our server Joann was fabulous.  The food was perfect.  The Cesar salad was the best we have ever had. The French onion soup was delicious.  My meal of chicken zingara was a delight. Wish I had room for a dessert.  Definitely worth the trip.

- Best scallops I ever had
- Outstanding shrimp
- Very good BBQ chicken appetizers
- House-made potato chips
- Good linguini
- Great friendly service, although a little slow, but that's OK when you're with friends

Really good bbq as recommended by a work colleague during a trade show.  Wanted something good for lunch and he took us here.  BBQ was worth the wait with the line being out the door.  I ordered the shredded chicken with the chili beans and fixings as well as the slaw.  Very tender and moist.  Beans were so awesome with the cheese.  Slaw was different than what I had eaten before.  It was more like a salad.  All in all this was a great and affordable lunch.

Delicious food and great service!  I knew it was going to be real good just from the smell of it in the parking lot! The food was sooo flavorful and freshly made as we ordered our meal. The nice guy was joking with my son and making us feeling like we were regulars already! Great hospitality!  We will definitely be going back there again! By far one of my favorite places!

I have been here before, and it has always been good.  Yesterday we went and I just absolutely love their mac and cheese, the best I have ever tasted.  The vegetables are good too.  I had the fried chicken and he had the fish, which were both good.  

Your eyes can be too big for your stomach and you walk out full.  The staff is great and they work hard at refilling your drinks and clearing tables.  Good home made cooking.

I was excited to try this new place. I did the chef special $60. The food was alright. The fishes were good but uni wasn't the best I've had. The rice with fish was amazing. Shrimp tacos I had were super good too. My waitress could've tried to look happier doing her job and not talk while I was talking when asking about a dish on Yelp. Other than that it was fine.

This is an unfortunate review.  I think chows has good food however chows offers terrible customer service .  We order from there all the time and chows constantly has leaky bags !  You have to be especially careful.  Saturday we used Grubhub to pick up and true to form the food arrived in a leaky bag.  The poor driver from Grubhub was so apologetic and we told her that this has happened before.  We tried to call chows but it was busy .  The driver called to Grubhub and it was immediately taken care of.  15 minutes goes by we receive an angry call from the lady at chows who is especially rude and argumentative.  She said it was the drivers fault.  We politely said  NO it's your fault and we told her how we have ordered before and your bag is always wet and leaking.  She continued to argue on the phone.  Customer is never right at chows.  Attached is the picture of our food on the ground and chows offers to refund half of the money! Ummm no thanks chows.  Good thing grub hub cares about their customer, maybe you should take a page out of their book!  Maybe I should charge chows with the labor cost to wash my sidewalk, door and floor at 9pm !!! Buyer beware , bring a plastic bag and check all the lids !

I've been a customer of Pete's Famous for about 2+ years now, ever since I moved to Philly/Center City. It's only a block and a half from my place, and the pizza is very good. The reason I am giving this review only 2 stars is not because of the food, but because of customer service, or lack thereof to be more specific. On my way home from work tonight, I placed an order for pick up just before  8pm - a single, large Margherita pizza. The person on the other end said it'd be about 15-20 minutes. At 8:16, I arrived to pick up my pizza. After paying, the cashier said it would be "another 2 minutes." That 2 minutes turned into another 17 minutes! It's not like they were super backed up with orders, so I'm not sure that my order had even been relayed to the kitchen when I called.

I did not have a problem with the waiting. Well, ok, maybe just a little bit of a problem. But I'd have been perfectly fine if the person that rang me up and told me I'd have another couple of minutes to wait  had checked on my order and let me know what the hold up was for. But she was too busy texting on her phone to seem to care.  When my pizza was finally ready at 8:33, there was no "sorry for the wait" or anything.

Note to employees who work in establishments where there is a tip jar on the counter:  Tips are not automatically given just because there's a cup sitting there with a couple of dollars and some change.  Act like you actually give a crap about my business, and learn how to use phrases such as  "Thank you" and "I apologize". Little things like that really do go a long way in my book.

In summary, I still think the pizza from Pete's Famous is good, but perhaps it's time to give some other pizza places around here a shot at my business.

Love this place.  Reno/Sparks does NOT have very good pizza places...except Big Apple.  Fresh ingredients make their pizza stand out (homemade mozzarella!).  The owners have always been very helpful and friendly.  They even have a toy box for my kids to play in!

Wife and I went to Flying Pie Pizzaria in Meridian. On a Saturday about 3:00 with only two tables occupied at that time. 

 We sat at a table and waited for a waitress for well over ten minutes just for someone to offer us a drink or anything. Finally after about fifteen minutes . We decided that was our first and last visit to this Pizzaria.

Very disappointed. This is our 3rd time here and each time it has been worse than before. The beer is definitely more tailored to the hoppy but there is usually something for the lighter beer drinker to enjoy. We ordered the wings and French dip, pretty basic fare but it sounded good. The wings were very bland, despite being told they were very spicy and had a great kick to them, and had been cooked sometime previous because they were very dry and very tough. My girlfriend was not impressed with the small amount of meat and the large amount of onions on the French dip. The fries were very undercooked and tasted like old grease. We were never asked how the food was or if we needed another beer. Needless to say we left hungry and regretting our choice to come here for happy hour/dinner.

This place is awesome. We just got into town and went there because of the reviews and we were blown away. There was a long wait for a table but before we were about to leave the hostess gave us a heads up that a few people were about to leave from the bar area. We sat at the bar and had some great cocktails. The ambiance is warm and quaint. We ordered food from the bar and the bolognese was amazing (2 people recommended it) my sister said the smoked fish fritters was so good. The chef came out to greet us. We love this place and everyone gave us a fabulous experience.
The fish sandwich was disgusting. Could bring myself to try!  Errs are good but will not be back!!!

Cool spot in Armature Works with great menu items. Had the mussels, which were the best ones I've had in the Tampa Bay area. The 007 salad, absolutely blew me away, and the NY Strip dinner. Needed a little more seasoning for the steak dinner which is why I gave it 4 stars, but other then that a great experience. Cool atmosphere and great decorations.

I have been to this place a handful of times and it is always the same, I am not sure why I return. All I have gotten is a plain bagel toasted with some smoked salmon on it. They charge me the full price of a sandwich for this $7.54. The bagel fits in my hand. I have uploaded a picture to show this (with a bite taken out I was hungry before I realized how small this actually was). This was not worth my money. It was bland. Yes I am plain, but I have had some really good smoked salmon before, this hasn't lived up to that. Im sad about it because there isn't really another place that has this option, but I just can't validate spending that much money on something that I need to go somewhere and get something to eat right afterwards.

Arrived late, 10:30, no problem, sat at the oyster/raw bar so we could enjoy the playoffs. We were greeted and table settings placed, ordered our cocktails- smoked old fashioned served table side off a smoking wood board, great flavor- the chocolate bitters added to the flavor. Despite us sitting at the raw bar, warm towels were then presented- nice touch ;) 
We were late night so we ordered the most delicious oysters- mucchi(sp?) from the west coast & an east coast selection. Beautiful briny fatty flavor- who doesn't love a salty fatty oyster?!!!
Ordered the lobster bisque on a cold night- rich- would have preferred less short-fingered claw meat but rather the real claw- but oh well. Brussels with onion and bacon- WOW- I am trying to figure out how to report that flavor. Lobster tacos up next- sweet lobster house made corn tortilla shell with 60/40 mix corn to flour making corn he shell hold together nice, not crumbly like a full corn shell. Fresh greens to top it off. Godiva cake to finish. 
Overall great service- even better people watching- real housewives of Tampa Bay or 'paid' dates, or just reg peeps being fab for the night. Either way, it was fun- we will be back - be ready to spend some $$&$$$
A lot to like here - fun atmosphere, nice cocktails, great craft beer selection, excellent comfort food with an emphasis on fried chicken...really good fried chicken.
Busy place, much needed here.  Great food great service!!!  Wish they had more parking, but I guess from a business POV that's a good thing.

Breakfast is decent and reasonably priced
Nice spot for a quick breakfast on a Sunday morning before church.

This is definitely the best brunch restaurant in Pinellas. Food is phenomenal. Service is fast and cordial. The signs on the walls will keep you entertained while you wait for your food. Highly recommended.

DEFINITELY my go to spot for non-American food!!! I find that I crave this place sometimes. I got the Lamb Shawarma on Gyro Bread which I actually had to physically look at once I took my first bite because I couldn't believe how good it was, fried calamari which was super crispy outside and moist inside..didn't care for the dipping sauce though, Combo Platter which was yummy and served as lunch the next day and Baklava. Boy oh boy is their Baklava good!! I've been to other places where they give you this miniature piece that is supposed to be dessert but theirs is HUGE! not to mention the quality is far superior than other places I've tried (I've eaten a lot of Baklava in my day). Overall, DEF worth the order!

Best breakfast sandwich and pastries in Indy- Hands Down. 

I have been coming here a few times a week since they opened and am impressed every single time. Highly recommend Raspberry walnut danish.

Food is delicious and plentiful!  I split the penne primavera and a pizza with my sister and mom.  It was some of the best pasta I've had in a long time!  The service was prompt and the staff is extremely friendly.  I will definitely go out of my way to go back!!

Oh how I've missed this place since moving out of Prospect Park to Wallingford. Yesterday I was back in PP and got myself 2 orders of wings to get my fix. One mild & one zesty garlic. Gonna freeze em & enjoy during the week.

We accidentally ended up here for lunch after seeing the advertised lunch specials on our way to get pizza. So glad we ended up here instead. We ordered the paneer makhani and chicken korma lunch specials with veggie samosas to start. Everything was so flavorful. The lunch specials are a real deal - for $20 we were full and happy.
Kind service, flavorful traditional Indian flavors, and a killer lunch deal. Definitely worth checking out!

Sonny's was great, just what a Philly cheese steak should be.  Service was fast, place was clean and the cheese steak with cheese wiz was perfect.  We also tried the cheese fries and onion rings which were good also.  Cheese wiz over provolone hands down.

Frankly, I've NEVER had bad produce or meats from this store. Quality is second only to Henning's and I am not going to travel 5 extra miles to get there.  Seafood can be steamed fresh for you, the clerks remember you, and the prices are great. I only gave 4 stars because they run out of specials on a regular basis. Otherwise I don't shop anywhere else.

We loved it. The food was delicious. The Pakora was perfectly fried. The Rogan Josh and Karahi were excellent, especially the green peppers in the Karahi. The Naan and Kulcha were warm, toasty and crispy. The service was also top notch. They were very friendly. Our water was always full.

Look, don't come here. It sucks. Drinks are weird, like who's ever heard of these things, not a single Cosmo on the menu? It's too crowded, the people are dumb and no one had on boots. It's super easy to find with it's neon signs out front, but stop. Don't do it. The music is not cool at all. I didn't hear FL/GA line once. The bartender is a dork and super hard to talk to. And what's with the art on the walls? How are you supposed to get a good selfie without the glow of a bud light sign?




(This place is awesome, SHHHH... but if you're looking for anything like above stay on Broadway and leave this joint to the oddballs.)

Came here on the way to SB Bowl concert. Parking  is not so convenient and difficult to fine. You'll inevitably have to wait in line but the wait is so worth it. We had special, tacos, cheese enchiladas. All were delicious, including homemade corn tortillas.

I like.that they have added some things to their menu .The slow roasted ham and Swiss has.become my new favorite. Catherine the manager is so sweet and always on top of things. I usually get the same thing but from time to time i switch it up and recently tried the BlackBerry Mojito iced tea , boy was it refreshing . I'd also like to give special nod to Avery he's always so friendly and goes out of his way to be helpful. Great job dude :-)
Amazing Spanish food ! Get the basics like rice and beans , plantines, chicken !!! So good! Staff is so awesome ! Very nice !

Heard that this was a fantastic restaurant in New Orleans. When we arrived, I soon realized this wasn't the restaurant I had seen pictures of or read about.  The newly renovated decor is terrible...a bad 80's rendition of pastels and grays. The menu is completely new so we couldn't order what we had been hoping to.  The food was just ok...nothing to write home about but we couldn't get over the ambiance of the restaurant. It felt like we were in a diner. Unfortunately, we won't be back.
