This place needs help or something. Went in for dinner about 8pm. It wasn't too busy but the staff left us standing at the door for a good 10 minutes. Once we we were seated we had chips before we had anyone offer to bring us a beverage. I ordered iced tea & my husband ordered a root beer. We placed our order for food at the same time we ordered our drinks. When they brought out our meal we had to ask for silverware and napkins. That was the last time we saw our server. There were only 3 tables in our section with diners at them but the whole time during our meal not one server checked on us even though they were blatantly standing around chatting with people. Dude walked by our table multiple times with my empty tea glass sitting on the edge of the table! The food was sub par as well. I left no tip as no one in that place earned one. If you stay at the Grand Sierra and are looking for good food,  go to the buffet. The cantina in no bueno!

This place is great! Ability to join the waitlist on Yelp is definitely the future of dining and the service is great! For its price point, you really can't beat this place. Great ambiance, awesome Biergarten, good selection, house-made products. How can you beat that at 20$ a meal including a beer??? Simple. You can't. Check it out! 5 stars for its category

If I could give zero stars I would. Went through the drive through while driving through the area. Order was not complicated. Frisco burger meal, no tomato, and a 5 piece chicken tender meal. We get our bag and pull away when I realize there is only one meal in the bag. I pull into the parking lot and go in. Let them know we didn't get our other meal. Made the mistake of not checking the meal we had received at first. Get a couple miles down the road and realize the first order is completely wrong, isn't the correct sandwich at all.

We went to Casa Grande for the 1st time  4/17  upon entering the hostess was very friendly, our waiter was wonderful and made suggestions.  Our meals were excellent and we were well cared for during our whole dining experience.  The food is fresh and the presentation is very nice.   The decor inside is very warm and inviting and YES we will go back and would recommend to friends/ family

Was very excited to try Havertowns new upscale pizza pub. 
Walked in and sat at the empty bar and was greeted by a nice looking bartender, after delivery draft lists and menus she started yukking it up with coworkers about the slow Saturday and her boredom. It took her over 10 minutes to turn from her fascinating convo to ask us for our drink order. 

We ordered the chicken and hot pepper pizza well done and the butter milk fried chicken sandwich with fries. The pizza was not cooked well done but the peppers were hot and the flavor was awesome. The fries were seasoned with a little bit of a dry rub and cooked to perfection. There homemade ketchup had a hint of BBQ sauce that was delicious.  The chicken sandwich had a great carrot slaw on it. Was great. 
After hearing a few other patrons comment on the specials we turned to see a board full of menu additions that our terrible bar tender did not mention, she also never checked back on us after we received our food. 
The place has a comfortable atmosphere. good beer, bourbon, and whiskey selection. 
Food was great but service was quite poor and disappointing, especially for sitting 2 feet away from the server at the bar. 
Will defiantly return, hopefully to a more attentive server.

One of the few things I miss about Tucson is St. Mary's Mexican Food..The green corn tamales are amazing the best I ever eaten The prices are very reasonable in price and most of all delicious. Very friendly family oriented.  I can remember them from many decades back.

Best waffles this side of Belgium! Seriously, they are amazing. They come with a dark chocolate whipped cream and chile syrup. And the waffles have the perfect density: kind of light. Hard to describe. Just go there and try one. Their take on biscuits and gravy is also brilliant! Small menu, but so creative. I love this place.

Continue to love Crabby Bill's. 5-day trip to FL and have been here literally 4 times (lunch and dinner x2). 

So good - especially the oysters - and really enjoyed everything from ribs to grouper to crab cake to stone crabs. Service is excellent, from the front of house to all servers and this place has a fun, friendly vibe. Yay Crabby's.

I was here with a party of 10 for my friend 24th birthday.  Their tapas were all right. 

I recommend this place for drinks with some friends amongst a crowd of classy dressed people.  Other than that, their food really stunk.  I had gotten their NY Strip Steak With Sauteed Mustard Greens and Blue Cheese Butter which was not good.  I asked for medium rare and it came out medium well.  Not only that, the NY strip steak was salty as if they were masking how old the steak may have been?  Not sure but if one is to pay $24 for a steak, you would assume that it would be at least good.  The potatoes were just potatoes at least they got that right.  If you screw up potatoes, then you suck.  I got a glass of their cheapest red wine which wasn't bad.  It was called De Bortoli Merlot.  Just Merlot.  Whatevs.  We had a taste of all the tapas which is never filling.  The tapas were okay, nothing special.  If you want great tapas, you should go to Amada's, which is the best tapas place in Philly in my opinion.  Overall, if you wanna just a casual drink, small talk, and look cool then I guess come here cuz Rittenhouse is nice but food sucks.  Eat Ramen.  Save Money.
Wonderful experience - we were 11 with kids and they seated us quickly without reservations. The food was excellent and the setting elegant. A true New Orleans gem.
I have loved this place for 25 years. Cozy inside with great salads and sandwiches. Love the roast beef sandwich, charbroiled chicken, greek salad, and the chicken salad.

For a fast food sandwich and salad shop good quality salads or excellent the sandwiches have a good amount of meat and other toppings there bread is much better than some well known sub shops been there many times see ya shortly thx Bob!

I really enjoyed the jambalaya pasta here and we also ordered a half order of Rockefeller oysters. This place seems to be a chain and honestly reminds me of The Red Lobster in Chicago lol. When on Bourbon street I would totally stop by for another meal.

I used to love Panera. This place has fast and efficient staff. The food quality is good and the bakery is diverse. All that aside I probably won't come here anymore. The menu seems to get less appealing every time I come back. It all started when they got rid of the asiago bread. Why would you get rid of that?! It was your best bread! Anyway, if it comes back; I'll come back. Until then, adios!

We really wanted to like this place as it was our only food stop in St. Louis. They ran out of ribs which was fine since in was late in the evening but we got extremely sick after our meal. I would give this place another try if I could get their ribs.
Brazil Arts Café is a great restaurant. The chimichurri sauce is so good. The steak is lean and tasty. We came here for lunch and loved it.

On our first night in St Pete, using the Yelp score as a guide, we tried Oishi last night via a delivery and was terribly disappointed with our food. 

Our order arrived without any soy sauce, forcing us to drive to a store to purchase some. 

The spicy tuna roll was flavorless, like cruise ship buffet sushi. The smoked salmon sushi did not melt on the tongue. It was chewy and tough. 

In short, it was a small order that left a big negative impression.

Meh. Maybe it was just a bad Thursday evening before Easter.

It wasn't late when we arrived but wasn't primetime either.
8:30ish.

I love a Chicago dog. I ordered 2. I was so disappointed.
My poppy seed buns had the texture of typical squishy white bread soaking wet apparently from the wet relish and a sopping wet dog.
 
She got the breaded chicken sammie - she was fine with it.

Fries could have cooked another minute or two as they were served wimpy, wimpy, wimpy.

Chatting afterwards w/ my friends from the Region agreed with my experience - they haven't been wowwed yet either.

The absolute worst experience ever! People talked and side commented during the entire show. A guy even answered his phone during the movie and responded, "I'm at the movies". Dude! Really?!?! We had one waitress serving the entire theater. I asked for ketchup from 4 different people on 7 different occasions before actually getting it and by that time my fries were cold! The staff came to attempt to pick up my bill, more than they were there to service me. Then I exit the theatre and the manager is having a conflict with a customer and called the police! Everything occurring outside of the movie was far more drama filled than the movie I was supposed to be watching. On the contrary, the food was good, prompt, and hot when I received it. However, the service just sucked horribly! I will not be back again under any circumstances! Ever!

The tri-tip was so delicious I had seconds. How I was able to ingest two hefty portions is beyond me. I have no regrets and my full belly sustained me just enough to do without dinner and breakfast. I almost bought a third tri-tip sandwich and was going to stow it in my carry-on. Cold Springs is definitely a spot I will return to during my next visit to central CA.

X Frenchy's saltwater Cafe is very phenomenal. Jordan was a very excellent server. Jordan  told us    about the fresh seafood that we can get.   Which were coming back to get the next day. Everything was just really good.

The best pizza on the beach. Best service and the freshest ingredients try one of their specially pizza like the deluxe . Please try the chicken parmesan is very fresh the breading Superfresh flaky the chicken very moist they have the best Italian food around. Married to a true Italian I know Italian when I taste it!! You're going to love it. tell your friends. You won't be sorry.

This Chipotle is just ok, which is disappointing because it's the closest to my house. I appreciate Chipotle because it is filling. That being said, every time I go to this particular Chipotle, it's not a great experience. Unlike other Chipotles that give large portions of each topping, if you do not ask for more of whatever you are getting, you will be left with a half empty bowl or a puny burrito. After asking for extra on 2-3 things, it starts to get uncomfortable. I've also asked for lemons a couple of times, which most others have sitting out in the drink area, and been given straight rotten lemons. They were in little cups, so I could just throw them out, but not good.

The one positive thing is that there is usually little-to-no line. So I can be in and out in 5 minutes.  But if a longer wait will give me a better experience, I'll go elsewhere.
Really good food and fast service.  The alligator sausage was my favorite followed by the red fish.  Our waiter Ponce was very helpful.

I have had two really excellent experiences at the CCF recently! The first one, was a delish brunch on Sunday! Peach Bellini + Monte Cristo French Toast. Does it get any better than that? I think not! You have to try the french toast! So delish. 

I brought my brother and his girlfriend here for a dinner & we had a great time. Our server Isaiah, was amazing! He gets a big shout out. He made our whole dinner experience great. More peach bellinis & laughs all around! Thank you for making our time together even better! We love sitting outside & the food is always great!

Found this place via yelp by the reviews and it being outside the city. The staff is super friendly even when they are soo busy! The food was amazing! I definitely recommend the raw oysters if you are an oyster fan! Their crawfish is VERY authentic and delicious. My husband had blackened halibut and it was also to die for! Will be coming back!!
Better than Chipotle..  no seriously. Well priced really fast service for food that's great. Will definitely come again.

My fiance and I took a trip into New Hope for the day and needed a place for dinner. We live off of Yelp reviews so we picked Italian Cucina. By no means were we disappointed. The food was amazing. We couldn't stop talking about it even as we were eating it. We had a shrimp app that was in a slightly spicy cream sauce. I loved it she thought it was just OK. There were six very fresh and very large shrimp. We were told it was enough to share I wouldn't entirely agree but that's just me. Also it was i think $18 which is really over priced for what we received. We both got pasta dishes that we awesome. As I read in another review someone felt the lobster ravioli were store bought...I would like you to bring me to the store that sells ravioli where when you cut them open large chunks of lobster claw fall out. I had these little cheese pockets ( not raviolis) that were also very good and were topped with their home made sausage. The sausage tasted home made and was also very good. It was BYOB so for us that's always a plus. They even offered to keep our left overs in the fridge over night because our room didn't have one. The owner came out and chatted which I thought was a really nice touch. The big let down for me was I was at a table that was seated directly in front of a window AC unit. The only reason I was OK with this was because there was a heat wave and I had already come close to passing out earlier in the day. This place definitely has our vote!
Had the east Nashville breakfast sandwich. It was great.  The place needs a better exhaust system, Though.

I absolutely love Mix. Their cookie classes are amazing! And so much fun! Their sweets are also very very good and I recommend them whenever I get the chance! Their workers are always so nice and their place is clean!

Our hotel was on St. Charles, so it was really close to Jimmy J's Cafe. We walked in and was greeted by a friendly bartender/hostess/takeout person. The restaurant is tiny and every table was occupied. We waited outside for maybe 10 minutes before a table opened up. Our waiter was wonderful. All the servers were wonderful, actually. My husband ordered the fried shrimp & oyster po-boy and I had the French toast Monte Cristo. The food came out promptly and it was good. By then the line had started to form outside and we realized how lucky we were to have avoided the long line (we were there right at 9am on a Friday). We had a very nice experience. Service was friendly and prompt. The food was very good (not super special, but good). Overall, we thought the visit was special. I would go back again and try some of their other offerings.

So.... this spot in NOLA is a must for breakfast and brunch. We walked here from our hotel on canal street and were not disappointed... the only disappointment was that we couldn't come back a second time while we were In town. Get here early cuz it's poppin. I had the combo Benedict with the special and one with smoked candy bacon. Wifey got the Migas. Next time in town we will be back

I love Liberty Bell, best breakfast in town but today I doubt I will go back, during this pandemic I worry about health and not ONE server, or the owner, or the busboy was wearing a proper mask!!  I cannot take a chance of the best breakfast being my last! Done with Liberty Bell for the foreseeable future and you should be too!! Let me give them a bit of advice, the mask goes OVER your MOUTH and NOSE!!

Nice casual atmosphere and very reasonable prices. Good service and food. Fish tacos were great but little messy....just right amount of heat. Big juicy burgers and plenty of fries. Will be back when in area...lots of newer stores and shopping there.

There are worse experiences than eating at Long John Silver's. 

For example, getting poked in the eye with a razor blade. That's definitely worse. 

Oh, and I remember when I had my foot amputated. That was way worse. 

That said, there are few dining experiences as aggravating and sensory-jarring as dining in a Long John Silver's restaurant and this particular location in Castleton on Indy's Northside is one of the better locations in Central Indiana. 

Now then, it may seem weird to even review a fast food joint but there are those certain experiences that just call out for a review. 

What's the Long John Silver's experience like? If you were to combine the unapologetic sterility of McDonald's with the soul-crushing ambience of a Burger King and toss in a pinch of middle school cafeteria warehousing, then you'd have an idea what it's like to dine in a restaurant where you're subjected to the almost constant ringing of a dinging bell that signifies another drive-thru customer and a floor that is almost always bathing in those little crunchy pieces of batter that you love but that make you look like a six-month old still trying to figure out the whole hand-to-mouth motion. 

Here's the sad thing. I actually kind of like Long John Silver's. It's kind of like the Wal-Mart of restaurants, because you leave saying "never again" but eventually you get the craving and find yourself back in there smooshed together with other diners while your kids wear their silly little pirate hats. I almost always order the two-piece chicken plank combo that comes with a side and a drink. I almost always upsize the drink. It's a cheap meal that tastes cheap, but the truth is I like the chicken, love the hush puppies, and am even a fan of the iced tea. 

The crew at the Castleton location is pretty solid and almost always outgoing and friendly, but there's simply no mistaking this to be a remarkably unpleasant atmosphere and almost stunningly unfriendly to wheelchairs. 

While they do have a couple wheelchair parking spots, their ramp could use a little work (I've actually fallen on it) and there's a modest incline to get into the restaurant. The restaurant itself really only has one truly accessible table and you'll know it because they clearly identify it that way. It also happens to block the aisle should you have a large wheelchair. I tend, on the other hand, to sit at a back booth that allows me prop my legs up and stay out of everyone's way. Unfortunately, as happened today, this can lead to you getting blocked in with no way to exit the restaurant. 

Can you say fire hazard?

The really strange thing is that this design is after the big Long John Silver's renovation. Um, really. You couldn't have consulted someone on ADA law with your nationwide renovation?

On the plus side, the bathrooms are now fairly wheelchair friendly as before you simply couldn't get into them at all. 

By the time I leave Long John Silver's, my nerves are shot. The constant dinging is a major irritant and talking employees increase that sense of non-stop noise. On this particular day, it was worsened by a noisier than usual crowd and an overwhelming desire to abandon ship.

There were many times when I didn't know if I should eat or laugh! The headliner of the night was Jimmy Yang and oh boy oh boy was he FUNNY. I think the combination of food and laughter was weird but I had a great time, although next time, I would probably just order drinks. I wanted to focus more on the comedian but the food was good nonetheless! I got the chicken chipotle paninis with a side of fries and it was great! There is a 2 item minimum and water does not count! One star less just because I think it would've been better if we had some sort of button or some type of system to call for service if needed instead of the waiters/waitresses coming over to check on us at random times. It's not their fault but I would've liked it I could watch undisturbed. Consider it a suggestion! Overall, great experience at this place and would go again if they book awesome headliners like Jimmy!!!

Food is great, if you aren't getting it to go. Brisket was dry, bun was soggy due to the moisture from a non-ventilated lid. I would highly suggest keeping the bun separate in wax paper instead of including it with the hot food. I picked up the order for several of my coworkers and myself, staff I encountered was curt and rude. They had enough of an attitude where I doubt I'll be back.

Can't believe I haven't reviewed this place. I know it has been a while especially after my dad passed away. He used to take me here all the time. We do a combo pizza with wings, steak fries and some ranch. Pizza is loaded with ingredients and thin crust the way we like it. The wings are a bit small but they pack flavor. Steak fries are nice to have since not many places do them anymore. The interior is a bit outdated but it is what it is. Kind of homey actually. It's dark and simple like a bar. Doesn't have all the flashy décor like some newer places but who cares? I came for the food. Oh they do take a while with your food. Best to place your order ahead of time.

Came here for dinner and a show (The Full Monty). Good ambience and good food. The Server (Carlos) was great and attentive (not overly). Salad bar was fully stocked and they had a good selection of wine and desserts as well. Will definitely return.

Wow. What a relaxing, flavorful, and enjoyable meal.  This membership-based restaurant does take non-member reservations, and we were able to easily get one on a Thursday for the next day.  But that might not be a great sign for business.  Anyway, you enter an unmarked door, like going into a 1920's speakeasy.  It was surprisingly light inside - not eye hurting bright, but I was expecting dark wood and very dim lights.  Everyone we encountered was extremely professional.  I thought at first that our waiter was going to be stand-offish, but after he warmed up very quickly and wound up being pleasant and chatted quite nicely.  I'm guessing that our fairly early 6 pm Friday reservation, and being his first table, probably took him a few minutes to get into mode.

The amuse bouche (peppadew stuffed with goat cheese) was both savory and slightly tart, to cleanse and prep the palate for what was to follow.  We ordered a couple of mocktails, simply asking for the wife's to be sweet and sparkly, and mine to be citrus.  The bartender, a the waiter also indicated, went above and beyond.  The accompanying pictures show the results.  Mine was a simple grapefruit base, that came straight at you, and the wife's had a deep fruitiness with a dense egg-white meringue atop.

Rangoon starter had Maine lobster, Fresno sweet chili, and cilantro.  The Rangoon were smaller, but heartily stuffed with large amounts of lobster in the cream cheese.  The sweet chili was lightly drizzled on top, with most of it thankfully poured around to apply as desired, since it packed a pretty good heat.

Another starter/explore item we got was off menu and suggested by the waiter when we asked for some.  It was truffled tater tots, and they were awesome.  Whipped potatoes formed into tot shapes, battered ans dried, with truffle oil having been mixed into the potatoes.  And the serving was huge (and only $7).

The wife's main course was the turf (6 oz black angus tenderloin, winter medley of vegetables, beurre rouge).  It was butter tender and highly beefy, with the vegetables fresh and crisply blanched and spiced.

My scallop cioppino (bay scallops, purple potatoes, sea beans, tomato-fennel broth, lemon snow) was an explosion of savor.  I especially enjoyed the mix of multiple items in the broth, making it almost a stew if it were a thicker gravy instead of broth, and that the scallops were smaller so that there was a decent amount of them.

Finally, dessert was split between us - a gooey brown butter cake, topped with scotch caramel, and bacon-sage caramel corn.  That was some great caramel corn, atop a pretty good cake.

Disappointed. Food was still good, portions a little different, but understandable and not drastically different.  The disappointing part was the in dining experience. Before covid, used to enjoy coming here for a night out in a very hip and fancy atmosphere. That's no longer the case. The restaurant was brightly lit, tables were scarce and spread out, and at least a 1/4 or the restaurant was dedicated to barrels of supplies (20-30 buckets of soy sauce in clear sight) and take out orders scattered everywhere.  Obviously no longer interested in making this a memorable dine in experience. It's a shame. Won't eat here again, but perhaps takeout. Like I said, disappointed.

We should have turned around and left right away. They tried to seat a party oF 8 at a table for 6. Then we must have made them mad when we asked to be set at a larger table. There were several tables open too. The waiter  was not good at all. He never asked if we needed more drinks, when we asked for another pitcher of sangria he never brought it!  The salad and bread were great!!!  But our entrees were just ok. When he brought our check he put it all  together when it was obvious we were 4 couples. Frustrating!  We come down every January and will be sure to not visit there again. The couple that recommended it  were embarrassed at the service.
I always get the same things on the menu so can't speak to all the food but the chicken tempura, starburst rolls and cheesecake makimono are amazing. The raspberry lemonade is also a great pairing.

All I can say is, AMAZING!!!!!

There are already a tremendous number of pictures about this restaurant so I'll spare you another. I just recently found this restaurant on Yelp. It's a but out of my way for a dinner/lunch, but I'm totally planning to make this a regular spot. 

What have I eaten thus far? Cassava fries, potato salad, perimayo corn, 1/4 chicken, and the chicken & rice bowl. I get everything medium spice and it suits me well. The flavors are unreal.

Regarding the staff and restaurant. The staff is incredibly polite. You approach the counter, place your order, and they bring it out to you. They don't skimp on the appearance of your food. They use real ceramic plates that are bequtiful and quality silverware. It has a very nice feel to the place and not something that is cheap. They'll also take your plates when you are done. If you need to go boxes, they have you covered. 

I absolutely love the gem of a restaurant. It is a must try for everyone.

Oh, Longway! I am so happy you exist! Longway has the feel of a true local's spot right smack in the middle of the French Quater. I frequent during Happy Hour when I can enjoy a $5 Moscow Mule with a sampling of delicious treats. The calamari is next level! It's definitely the best friend calamari on this side of the Mississippi. Seriously, you can't get anything like it in NOLA. 

The staff here is amazing. Everyone is friendly and makes you feel at home. Longway gets pretty popping on the weekend so check it out if you're looking for great food, drinks, and atmosphere on your night out. They're open late too! They also have a beautiful courtyard which I plan to hit up more frequently once this Summer heat dies down. 

I'm a big lover of all of the owner's other establishments (MeauxBar, Sylvain, Cavan) and Longway Tavern certainly did not disappoint!

This is a great place to pick up something to go.  Sometimes I stop over here to pick up food before going to one of the craft breweries in Reno that don't serve food.  They give you plastic cups to take sauce with your bowl, but it is better to add sauce directly to your bowl before leaving.  The reason I say this is because you never take enough sauce with you.  There are a lot of options for bowls and generally I take the traditional option.  Very filling and worth checking out.

Booked a last-minute stay for a night this past weekend via Yelp. Very easy to book online, and I believe if you book through Yelp, you get a complimentary upgrade...don't quote me on that though. 

Loved the room. Every room comes with a gigantic tub and a TV in the bathroom. Also comes with a Keurig. Stunning views of the Santa Catalina Mountains. 

Will be booking here for a longer stay soon...check this gem out!

I would definitely recommend this place! We were headed somewhere else but saw the sushi sign and decided to switch plans. 

We had a small bowl of Tom Yum soup which my fiancé devoured leaving me only to have a taste. It was a winner for sure and just enough spice to make me happy without overwhelming him. We also had the seaweed salad and two sushi rolls. 

The Valentine roll was off the charts. Fresh, simple, and the presentation was fitting as the pieces were put together to form little hearts. Awe! When leaving I noticed they had specials on the board by the entrance that were not on the menu. Next time we will be reading those first, they looked pretty unique which is what we look for.

I've been to Molly Maguire's for lunch and brunch. Both times it was delicious. I especially liked the squash soup I had for lunch. I love the atmosphere. It feels just like an Irish pub. I will definitely be back.

Delicious. The ribs are really good. My husband had the meatloaf and garlic mashed potatoes - SO GOOD and I really don't like meatloaf. To top it off, our waiter, Jeff was the best! If in the area - definitely stop in for some great food, great service, and great music. And ask for Jeff - you won't be disappointed.

I've only ever had mediocre service at Ms. Tootsie's.  I don't think it's the fault of the waitstaff either. They try, and some are better than others, but I think there's a management problem that makes the experience inconsistent.  The food is delicious, the restaurant's nice, but the dining experience has always made me anxious.  It's too overpriced for even amazing soul food, but the wait is often too long for that price, among other things.  Many times the phone just rings after several attempts, but when I get there it's empty.  I'm really annoyed when they don't put cornbread in my takeout - it's a staple and comes with the meal.  They also play with portion size when they're having a party upstairs.  It's as if I'm expected to understand their shortcomings as a restaurant.  Since we were both (hubby & I) usually annoyed upon leaving, we don't go there anymore. Hopefully, they'll get it right one day.

If what Chefs Donald Link and Stephen Stryjewski cook at Cochon is reflective of authentic, Louisiana cuisine, then I want to eat Louisiana food for the rest of my life.

Located inside a former warehouse, the interior is a wonderful combination of rustic and modern, with plenty of wood, exposed bricks, and large glass jars. The overall vibe is convivial and welcoming, and the open kitchen certainly adds to that lively atmosphere.

For drinks, I tried Tin Roof Brewery Voodoo Bengal ($5), which is a nice American Ale with a rich, hoppy taste, and a slightly sweet, caramel-like aftertaste. Nola Brewery Hurricane Saison ($5) is a wonderful Belgian-style farmhouse ale, with a nice balance of malts and hops.

The food. Ah, the food! Where should I start? The idea behind the restaurant is to honor a Cajun tradition of whole-pig boucherie. The pig is served smoked, pressed, cured, and shredded, with dishes that manage to be both inventive and respectful of the tradition. But there's a lot more than just a pigfest at Cochon.

Among the small dishes, the baked artichoke-stuffed crab ($12) was flavorful and delicate, and the chicken and andouille gumbo ($6) rich and earthy.
But the fried alligator with chili garlic aioli ($10) was just fantastic! Perfectly fried, the morsels of alligator were surprisingly juicy and tender[1]. A revelation.

For entree, the braised pork cheeks with sauerkraut potato cakes, goat feta and pears ($12) were as good as they sound, with the sauerkraut and pears providing a nice, tart contrast to the rich, almost sweet pork cheeks.
The Louisiana cochon with turnips, cabbage, and cracklins ($23) is slow-stewed suckling pig served as a crisp, delicious patty.

Dinner for two came down to $95, all included. A real bargain for the best dining experience of my dreadfully short visit to NOLA. Can't wait to come back and try the fried rabbit livers with pepper jelly toast!
--------------------
[1] Compared to other places, Cochon uses only alligator shank for this dish.
Just a simple, really good neighborhood pizza joint in a strip mall with nice guys behind the counter. Food is good but nothing special.

Bad experience. Yesterday I was in the mood for BBQ. I usually go to Baby Blues but I just didn't feel like making the drive. Instead, I decided to stop past Dekes. Such a mistake. All I wanted was a 1/2 pound of brisket. I placed my order and returned home. Well the first thing that threw me off was that there was a great deal of sauce already on the brisket. Most places usually put the sauce on the side. Not a big problem with that though. Then I figured out why it was completely drenched in sauce. There was little to no meat, all fat. If I wanted a plate full of fat I would have ordered that. No wonder the guy at the counter told me they were "making it a pound". Even with a pound I had about 1/4 pound of meat. It was all fat. So disappointed. Waste of time and money.

There was only one employee visible in the entire arcade, bowling and bar area.  I spent 60.00 to load two game cards with 85 credits each.  Just about every game my husband and I played were 5 credits just to begin the game and another 5 credits every couple of minutes to continue playing?, up to 13 credits per game.  It usually took at least 10 - 15 credits per game, just to figure out how to play them?  Needless to say, our 85 credits went very fast.  My husband had played a game that earned him 1000 bonus points, and I played a game and earned 40 bonus points plus another game that I won 100 free tickets?  I asked the only employee that was behind the bar if he could explain to me the difference between, credits, bonus points, and tickets?  He said that the credits were for playing the games and that the tickets were to get prizes, but he could not tell me what bonus points were for or how to cash them in?  I feel ripped off!!! I walked over to the prize area to see if I could use our bonus points to get a prize but nobody ever came over to help me. I waited for about 20 minutes before finally leaving without a prize, and 1040 bonus points on game cards that I will probably never use again!  I was very dissappointed

Speedy seating and service. I had water and my order taken promptly. Servers are all attentive and observant. I ordered the pork buns and crab/pork dim sum. My first time to have either and SO YUMMY!! Delightful flavor and prepared well. So yummy and cheap! Cash only but there is an atm in the entrance way.

On a Stone Crab claw mission! 

When visiting Clearwater in March, I was determined to feast on some Stone Crab Claws, living in New Jersey - we just don't have them. After convincing my friends, who are clearly not foodies, and love chain restaurants, that we needed to come here and pick up some things for our hang out day at the pool! 
Easy to find, small non assuming storefront, until you enter. Truly impressed with the selection of local fish, shell fish and STONE CRAB CLAWS!!! I was lucky to visit in March, as the season runs from October to May. They had a variety of sizes and prices, all pre-cooked and ready to eat. They were delicious with a clean fresh taste! We also had some Jumbo Gulf Shrimp that they steamed and cooled for us, also perfectly cooked, and very fresh. 
Added bonus they carry J.J. Gandy's Key Lime pies and cookies, another place I wanted to check out in Palm Harbor, but met resistance from my non foodie friends. After trying the pies and cookies, a trip to Palm Harbor is in our future. 
Ward's is a must-do for fresh Florida seafood! I'll be back next year, have my Stone Crab Claws ready for me!!!
Food was good and pricey.  I wont be ordering and soda anytime soon. They wanted $3.29! No thank you.

I walked in here by mistake.  But, make no mistake, I will never make that mistake again.  It was once a cajun-type place and I thought it still was.  But, I decided to sit anyway.  I had the ALWAYS LOVELY Veronica with me, so you should know that I aim to please her (so I enjoy reciprocity from her later on, if you get my point).  We stood there for a few minutes until the listless slug behind the bar motioned to us to sit wherever we wanted.  Not surprisingly, there were MANY empty tables.  After sitting, we were delivered menus by the barely-able-to-speak bartender.  We ordered two soft drinks, and placed our order.  The twenty minutes waiting for our food were spent watching the enormous room dwindle to about 5 patrons total.  Our sloth-like bartender finally arrived with a black bean/sausage concoction that must have been sitting on the pass the whole time because it was no more than 60 degrees.  I told the bartender we would like it warmed.  She asked if it was too spicy.  ????  hello?  We also had a rice dish that was mediocre on its best day, surrounded by fries that were more limp that a quadriplegic's cock.  Of course, we had to request utensils from the bartender.  Poor Veronica then had to walk our empty glasses for a second pour to said empty-headed bartender.  When the black bean debacle was brought back, it was warmed to a scorching 61 degrees.  We ignored it ALMOST as much as the bartender ignored us.  I apologized to my beauty for this scarring event and begged for the check so I could RUN back to work.  And I offer my recommendation to all of you to similarly RUN if anyone ever suggests lunch here for you
New fave place! AMAZING SERVICE. great food. Great environment. Get the Turkish beer and baklava for dessert! Feels like you're on vacation somewhere trying new and delicious foods! Cheers!

You would think it was a dive bar or friends-only bar when you drive by, but Carollo's has AWESOME Italian food.  You get a great salad, garlic bread and entree if you're going Italian.  It's about 20 minutes away, but we stop in whenever we're in the mood for good portions.  I recommend the Gnocci!  Few seats in the dining area, but it's usually only 50% full anway.

Awesome Greek Salad was large and contained a nice mixture.  Staff was attentive and very quick to serve the lunch entree. My guest had the turkey sandwich which looked incredible.  Very pleased and will return to Triumph!  Kudos to restaurant for a great job!

We ordered redfish, blackened chicken and bread pudding

Total check came out to be $46 with taxes 

I would say a lil pricy as compared to the quality of food! 

The place had great reviews thats why we stopped here 

I would say its a lil over rated. Chicken was normal and so my red fish. Fish was a lil more mild (as compared to original red fish) but still not bad, i had a good time 

Casual dining experience is great and our server was solid too! 

Bread pudding dessert was the highlight of our experience (made me rate it 4 stars) its a MUST TRY!!! Loved it
Arrived at Clear Sky at 8:15 pm.  This busboy looking guy told my party and me that they were closing early cause they weren't making any money on super bowl night.  Seriously.  So, won't be back.
Very expensive takeout!! My first time and last time going there. 2 dishes was $30!!!! Wow.

We went for dinner service and we were not disappointed! I ordered the lamb kabob and my wife ordered the vegetable kabob.. Both entrees arrived to our table hot and fresh. The lamb was tender and flavorful along with the rice and salad that came with the meal. The vegetable kabob was  flavorful as well and was grilled to perfection. Overall, the service was timely and our server was attentive and professional. I highly recommend this restaurant!

The burger I had here was top notch. I had the Morning After. It appeared to be made from completely fresh beef patties right there in the restaurant. At least, that's how it tasted. I also tried the loaded tots, which were also good. Service was with a smile.

For the past 10 years I've been coming here a few times a year. All I've ever ordered here is chicken pho with chicken slices, Vietnamese spring rolls, grilled chicken skewer, and the combo veggie delight. They also have slushies and teas, and all I've ever gotten is mango slushie with coconut jelly (sometimes I will do a quick stop just for a slushie). If you during their busy hours, be prepared to wait. Once my order has been taken, I have never waiting more than 10 to 15 minutes for my food. I can never get over on how great the service is.

Simply the best Pizza in the world. Great ingredients and inspired flavor combos.

We ordered the cheeseburger style pizza and the sesame seeds in the crust plus special sauce were so creative. The seeds added such a good flavor, too. 

We also had the smoked bacon and red onion pizza which was equally decadent leading me to believe that the entire menu is the same high quality pizza masterpieces. If you really love pizza, the could be a world class favorite.

Stopped by here on the good reviews, missed the place twice as they only have a small sign that says diner.  Very easy to miss.  Walk up only too find a note that's says only cash or check - and I never carry either so I just turned around and went back to my car.

The sushi burger its the best ever!!
a lot more to explore, amazing manu 
i will go back.

I love this quaint little shop!!! Locals who had a dream! A great addition to the Delco area!! Great atmosphere, amazingly friendly owners, great for connecting with others or a place to chill on your laptop. Free wifi is available. I'm not a coffee drinker, however they make the most amazing Chai Tea, I refuse to go anywhere else. Their smoothies are also phenomenal as well, made with no fillers, all real fruits and juices. Most amazing brownies ever, made in site! Super Family Friendly!!! They also host small private events, great for book clubs, breakfast clubs and more. Breakfast, lunch and Dessert Trays for catering available as well. So much better then your run of the mill chain coffee places. This is surly an up and coming hot spot! A true diamond in the rough! I'm excited to watch them expand and grow! Don't forget the daily  fresh baked pastries 

AND  live music nights!!

Frankly, we were disappointed. 
We had just stayed at Atlantis and had a crackerjack Eggs Benedict at the Blue Parrot Cafe there the day before.  The Hollandaise sauce here was bland by comparison.
Ingredients, generally, were very good -- tasty eggs, excellent bacon and sausages.
But, Service was puzzling.  Very slow and hit-or-miss. The restaurant was not especially busy, but we had to wait a very long time to locate and catch our waitress's attention to remind her about requested condiments and ask for more than a half-thimbleful of pancake syrup; which translates to cold food.  Sub-room temperature eggs=Blech! Our waitress even apologized for slow service and we overheard a manager doing the same at an adjacent table.  Whether the seat of the problem was the kitchen or the serving staff does not matter to me if I am paying the bill.
Prices were slightly higher than a standard eatery.  That would have been fine if service was up to the same standards as decor and ambiance, which were good (except for the distracting large TV screens that have become the bane of  American eating out -- we are seldom permitted to dine any longer due to smartphones and omnipresent large screen TVs.)

The salads & the pizza was outstanding. I was surprised when I tried to order our pizza over the phone to discover they do not take phone orders. I had to come "in person" and wait for it to be prepared which was an inconvenience.

Been enjoying delicious, hot pho at Saigon for more than 10 years, starting at their Lafayette Rd location.  Service is always friendly and efficient and food always reliable and reasonably priced.  One of our go-to restaurants for a quick, filling meal.  Banh-mi sandwiches, potstickers snd goi rolls always hit the spot.

I can't decide if I like this place so let me break it down based on my last visit there.

Plus 2 stars for putting on my Habs game on a recent Saturday night (no Oilers game on, relatively empty bar, plus it was Habs-Leafs - classic Canadian rivalry). But minus 1 star for repeatedly forgetting to put the volume back on (think: at least half of the period gone by!).

Plus 2 stars for the friendly waitress who even squeezed in a last happy hour drink for us just as we arrived. All smiles and willing to ask the manager about putting the Habs game on for us. But minus 1 for the worst poutine I've had in a while (photo to be uploaded soon). Crinkle cut fries that look just like McCain fries (including the "baked" not deep-fried look), gravy that tasted like it was made from a grocery store powdered packet, and grated cheese. The horror! I don't think this was clearly communicated on the menu because I would never have ordered this poutine otherwise. If it was on the menu, I apologize - it's just that they feature so many kinds of poutine on the menu (including a smoked meat one that my friend had that was deemed equally sub-par) that I assumed they had to have cheese curds - why else would you showcase the variety?

So, would I come back? Probably... but it wouldn't be my first choice.

Omgggg this place is amazinnggg.  Get anything off that grill and feel free to go for any of the signature dishes or specials.  Everything is fresh and well prepared.  Even the sides are soooo gooood - cilantro lime rice and black beans oh holy moly.  My favorite is the matrimonio - grilled skirt steak and chicken with chimmichurri.

Meh.

I'm not sure why it's a four star.  Bland Mexicajun.

We came on alumni weekend and it was 25min wait.  Stand by the door...they "call" your name with a whisper.

I had the chili verde pork with home fries and tortillas.  The pork was dry but tasty.  The home fries tasted like toasted boiled potatoes.  The tortillas were bland and dry as well.  The coffee was old (?) and bitter....and I really don't like my ladies that way either.

My GF had the fried chicken and waffles.  The chicken batter was BLAND! But the chicken was moist.  The waffles were the exception to the entire breakfast....very tasty.  Get the waffles!! 

Oh!  Do try the beignets!  Not NOLA, but it's was a nice snack before the food came.

I get that they were busy and things may have been rushed...but I have zero reason to come back or recommend them given the other places to choose from in the area.

What a cute little restaurant! I love the atmosphere! It's like you're sitting in someone's kitchen. The place is filled with cookbooks, art, and canned goods, to give the feeling of a kitchen. Food was amazing and I appreciated the fact that they let me know what soup was vegetarian and that they specifically didn't contain chicken broth. Plus they make some of their own baked goods, which were the best I've ever had (sorry mom) I'm going to make this a regular place to stop at.

All you really need to know is that this place has THE best donuts in Indy. I'm not sure how they do but it is consistently amazing and fresh. The raspberry and lemon filled are my favorites but honestly, they are all good. It is cash only!

I had my first Pho experience today, well my first Vietnamese food experience in general. After reading some yelps about the local restaurants, I decided that Pho Hoa would be a safe introduction into the world of Pho. I checked out their online menu and then I went down and got some take-out. The women at the counter were super friendly. 

I got home and opened the bag and delicious aromas filled my kitchen. My honey loved his chicken Pho soup. He has a cold and it was just what he needed. He loaded in the jalapenos and made it really spicy. 

Me, on the other hand....I really wanted to love my seafood Pho soup, but I just didn't. The shrimp were bland, it had imitation crab meat which I loathe, and some other form of tasteless white mystery seafood. 

I don't know, either I am just not as adventurous as I'd like to be, or I just ordered the wrong thing. I love Chinese, Japanese, and Thai food...  I mistakenly thought I would love Vietnamese food just as much. But, I guess I'd be willing to give it another shot.

Saturday evening, looking for dinner after a long day of shopping and thought we'd check it out... parking lot was empty which was in our favor because everywhere else was an hour plus wait. Went in and was deafened by over-the-top-loud rap music being blasted by a DJ. Took our seat and got our glasses of water but couldn't even discuss the menu options with my husband because it was SO loud. So we left... If that's your thing, check this place out! We weren't fans. And I REALLY wanted seafood... the Mexican restaurant next door was happy to oblige!
The ambiance is lovely and the beignets are even lovelier...i thought the food was even better than cafe du mode....beignets were on point and the breakfast sandwiches big enough to spilt

Burger, maybe a cocktail, but definitely a shake. That's a recipe for a good time at Farmer & the Cow. Our team has made a couple trips out to Wilmington in recent months and every time, Farmer & the Cow comes up. And never, let me emphasize, never, gets shot down. Their burgers are hearty, and I haven't heard a single complaint from the group about their orders. I've personally tried Mr Gandolfini and Morning Glory and I have no regrets. I will have to add, it is a good amount of food so while I 127% recommend their fries, a salad might be an option to consider if you're looking to save room for dinner. Especially if you're ordering the Paul Rudd. This fantasmical shake is a bacon lovers dream. Also, peanut butter. If you don't love it, we just can't be friends, I'm sorry. That said, I can assure you we'll be stopping by next time we're in Wilmington - you should too.

I think Tampopo tries to create a mix of asian bento box, noodle soup house, with asian fusion flare. We've been here a couple times - have tried the udon, the tampopo house special spicy noodle soup, sushi, and a few other things. 

Overall, the udon was probably the best out of everything we've tried. The noodles are chewy, the broth is tasty, and you can get it with shrimp tempura which comes out decently crispy (as long as you don't let it soak in the soup too long). T

he tampopo house special noodle soup packs some kick, but the broth doesn't seem to be nearly as flavorful as the udon broth. We tried one of their "special" fried chicken sweet-n-sour looking thing - was unfortunately a little let down - just kinda tasted like faux-chinese orange/sweet-n-sour chicken. 

It's not too far away from where we live in University City, and it's not a bad option, if you're in the mood for some quick/accessible chinese/korean/japanese food - but if you're really looking for some GOOD chinese food - just make the trek to chinatown.

I came here with coworkers around 12:30 on a Monday afternoon and the place was packed. There are 10 tables in the restaurant and it's buffet style. The best item I tried was the prik khing chicken and the green curry chicken... All items come with chicken BTW. There are no other meat options. The food is pretty good, however there are limited options to the buffet and things run out quickly. I wouldn't recommend coming here between 11:30-2:00pm.

Terrific venue and service.  Good drinking place but skip the food, e
xpensive and tasteless.

I loved Poké Munch! The food was very fresh, the rice was warm and well cooked, and there were lots of add in choices including Mango and pineapples for vegetarians for customization. I did just have the vegetarian bowl that was on the menu, and didn't customize. The quantity is very generous and there is literally a pound of tofu in the veggie bowl. One small issue I had was that because they pile the bowl so high, it is difficult to mix it all together and you end up eating the bottom layer by itself in the end.

You have to rate this place on the bier, which is very good. This was my first visit to a brewery only location and I was not sure what to expect.
Rocky at the door was very friendly and gave me the run down of how the place was laid out. 
The tasting area was large and inviting. So many awesome things can be done is such a cool space. I look forward to seeing what events take place in the future. A bit more seating would be nice and a place to sit your bier down, but it was not a big deal at all. It's not like you are going to sit and drink bier after bier. (well maybe)
I loved the blonde and amber. I am just not an IPA fan, but I keep trying. I liked that we were able to enjoy a pint for $4.50 and a growler to go for $12.00.. 
For those of you who don't know, when you get a growler you can get it refilled at ANY brewery. They just have to put a sticker on it. Refills at Flat12 are $8.00

Good place! Definitely worth a shot based on the price and service.

I ordered the chicken and beef shwarma

Mikey likey but check your bill . Last 2 times here they overcharge me and make a big deal out of correcting the problemz.
Service is slowwwzzzzz. Which was confusing as there wudnt and other customerz.  Seemz some peeps order ahead .
Staff seem rudez and bothered by the customers

The food is excellent but this Marlton location is so understaffed that it's a long wait before the food comes up. Even when they are not very busy. 15 minutes from kiosk entry to deliver food. Management needs to increase their staff. 

Otherwise food is excellent

My family was in town and we needed a place to eat at 7:00 on a Tuesday near the Kimmel Center.  Of course that was not an easy task but luckily we found CiBo.  The staff was friendly and very welcoming.  The food was great.  We had the crab cake, steak, chicken parmigiana, and the tortellini special.  All the dishes were great.  We will definitely be back.

I enjoyed this place. The Devil Crab Arancini was delicious and the service was great! The ambience was great for the nightlife. I will say this place is a bit expensive but very modern. I will definitely be back but next time it will be for brunch! I heard they have a great brunch selection on Saturdays and Sundays.

Very good, authentic Taiwanese and Chinese food. Having lived in Taiwan for several years it is a pleasure to be able to savor the tastes from my past. I have always found the service to be very good too.

I feel like a three and a half star rating doesn't do this place justice.  Every time I visit this place I have such a memorable experience.  It is a great place to escape reality for the night with a large group and socialize with family or friends.  

I can't put my finger on it but in about the last two years, the quality of the food here has definitely improved significantly.  I wasn't too crazy about the food here if you asked me three years ago.  The burgers are a major highlight for me and the chicken tenders tossed in Jameson BBQ with Hot sauce are great.

Come in here and have a pint of your favorite draft, maybe a shot (or a few), grab some great food, relax, and mingle.

And of course, have a designated driver or request an Uber, if you've had one too many!

I was in the mood for a Violet Hour-worthy drink; one carefully crafted by a mixologist, with small batch bourbon and homemade bitters and stuff like that. I was surprised when my roommate suggested Pi in the Central West End, but she assured me that the drinks are amazing, as is the pizza. I have to admit, I was a bit skeptical about the pizza, since I'd sampled some from their truck at Winter Green back in December and wasn't overly impressed. However, I'd heard owner Chris Sommers talk at the Launch event last month about how Pi cooks with local ingredients, composts, and uses salvaged and Earth-friendly materials, so I was intrigued and decided to give it a try. 

For those of you who haven't visited the Central West End location, make sure you look pretty. I had had a tiresome day of work and was wearing my favorite grey cords and my glasses; my hair was messily tied back in a ponytail and my shoes were more like winter boots. I haven't felt so underdressed or unglamorous in a long time, among the well-coiffed, heeled, and skirt-clad women that crowded this restaurant. But that was quickly forgotten when I saw "Old Ransom Gin" on the alcohol menu, scrawled in chalk above the bar. I don't even know that many places in Chicago that serve this masterpiece!

The cocktails on the menu entice you with ingredients such as Lillet, rhubarb, orange bitters, and sazerac. But then the bartender (more about him later), instructed us to tell him what we were in the mood for. Oh-so-Violet Hour! I said, "gin," and my roommate said, "bourbon," and the bartender was off! My drink involved my beloved gin, ginger liquor, and ginger simple syrup--so ingenious!--and my roommate's was this bourbon, caramel, chai-spiced dream. We did not know the exact ingredients at the time though...

While the antipasto platter was tempting, we started with Pi's deconstructed garlic bread. The bread arrives warmed and naked, accompanied by a roasted head of garlic and sweet butter, which allows each diner to choose her ideal amount of garlic. It's such a simple concept, almost peasant food-like in its presentation, and yet Pi's garlic bread is light years away from the overly-toasted, sopping yellow stuff that most restaurants serve. 

Our bartender described Pi's menu as "very diner-friendly," which means that they are very flexible; even deep dish pizzas can be half South Side and half Bucktown (sounds like my life in Chicago!). Luckily, my roommate and I both adore anchovies, so we got the Mission, which includes berkshire pork sausage, red onion, and hot red pepper flakes in addition to those delectable little fish.  Despite being from deep dish and stuffed pizza's homeland, I prefer floppy, fold-over, NYC-style slices. However, Pi's cornmeal crust and balanced amount of cheese won me over.

At the end of the evening, our bartender revealed the contents of our drinks and told us about his rescued Grayhound. I regret that I've forgotten the dog's name, because it was cute, but our bartender's name was Jamie Corona. "Like the beer!" he smiled. I explained how my name, when formatted for university emails, is 'Molson,' also "like the beer." "I LOVE Molson!" Jaime exclaimed. REALLY? The man who had concocted  a perfect gin and ginger cocktail loves Molson? "I grew up in Detroit," he added. It was a bizarre moment that nearly shattered my super-foodie experience, but I let it go and decided that yes, in St. Louis, your mixologist can express his love for cheap Canadian beer, and somehow, it's charming.

They use Fiestaware here!  I love nothing in my kitchen more than my Fiesta dinnerware.  So that obviously captured my heart pretty quickly.  I visited during lunch and had one of the very reasonably priced lunch specials.  Salad served with the largest lunch sized portion of flatbread ever.  Seriously.  It was the size of a large pizza.  Now the nice thing about Fiesta! is that you can sure cram a lot into their salad bowls and the lunch salad was certainly overflowing.  The raspberry vinaigrette dressing added the extra kick the salad desperately needed.  I don't know why but the salad really lacked flavor.  I blame the cheese.  Mozzarella cheese on salads is not overly flavorful to me, but no biggie.  The salad is plentiful with olives, croutons, red onion, and cheese galore.  Flatbread was just so-so.  It also lacked in the flavor department and was pretty greasy.  I could fold each piece in half without much breakage-meh.  I would like to try their regular pizzas and some of the pasta dishes sometime.  The pizza at the table next to me looked pretty awesome.  Staff isn't overly friendly, especially the fella that seats you.  It's clean AND they have local brew selections on tap from Sun King.  I will give it another shot for sure.

As a side note, they appear to be closed between 2-4PM (at least from what I could gather from posted hours on the door) which sort of seems like a better time to do maintenance work that involves having the main door open in winter during a good portion of lunchtime, causing big baby patrons like me to be forced to wear my coat during my meal.  Call me crazy.

You'll need to put your traditional (or ill conceived "californian") taco and mexican food notions aside.  This is probably the real taco.  The marinated meat is served on hand made (fresh!) corn tortillas.  I HATE corn tortillas... but I loved these.  That should give some testament to how truly delicious these are.

If you're looking for more, you won't find it.  Meat & a tortilla.  That's it.  Get two and prepare to probably want a third but decide against it because the line is too long.  Don't beat yourself up over it though because you don't want to over do it on your first visit.

Finish your Negra Modelo and dish to your friends about your latest accomplishment and enjoy the Santa Barbara weather as the Super Rica tacos sit contently in your tummy as your taste buds savor the memories.

Super, super delicious breakfast food! I had the Croissant French Toast and it was the best sweet breakfast I've ever had. My fiancé had an omelet and said it was really good too! We sat outside so we had an awesome view of the State House and people watching. We will definitely be back to try more!

However, be careful if it's your first time, the coffee they offer you while you wait for a table is not free!
The pizza was great! I loved the vegetarian options! Our server was great and friendly. We were in and out in a timely manner for a Friday night.

Watch them make your beignets! So light and fluffy. Sit outside and watch the street cars, look at the cemetery, wonderful porch to enjoy. I wish I'd gotten the name of the young man who took our order, he was so sweet and enjoyed a bit of the sunset with me. Two tour guides recommend going here to try their beignets! Great feel, fully staffed, clean, looks like the locals go here.
We are regulars of Hailey L. who is our favorite...tonight we had the pleasure of "meating" (get it) Ginny and Jenna. What a great team. You girls are awsome.

Excellent pizza. Got the three meat pizza and the sausage was really tasty! Pasta was pretty boring though. The bread they bring after you sit down is great though. So in general the food was above average.

Very cheap drink specials!

Service was excellent. Quick, funny, and friendly.

We had a chance to grab their happy hour prices which are available for every table in the house during HH times (not just limited to bar seating).  We tried the Dragon, Crazy, and Washington Ave rolls which were good but not amazing.  Glad we only paid the HH price of $5 per roll and not the standard $9-$11.  The service was fine although the waitress was less than enthusiastic.  Nothing bad here, also nothing spectacular. May I recommend Izakaya Ren just west of here a few miles for a much more delicious experience.

The Mango Margarita was about as good as it gets. Guacamole was five star could be some of the best if not the best I have ever had.  The item that made Mr Baja stand out was the Calamari.  I've only tasted one other calamari dish ever that would rival the Baja Fish version.  Worth the trip just for the Calamari.  The salsa's were nothing great, The shrimp cocktail is full of fresh flavors and had plenty of shrimp. They serve a Shrimp in a green sauce that was very original and flavorful.  If you have a chance to visit it's worth the trip.  We will go back again to try additional dishes but so far this spot gets a thumbs up!

The food is good.  I'm not sure why there are gnats flying around though which is a turn off from wanting to eat there.  Last time I went there were 5 employees and not one picked up a rag to wipe the dirty tables.  I wiped my own table.

Yo Sushi is so good! We had such a nice waiter. Our little daughter wasn't feeling well and had a gross incident at the dining table and the waiter ran quickly to give us something to help clean up the mess. Okay sorry for the story.

Back to the food. It was a rotary style sushi bar. It's where they have a belt machine that is kind of like a train where they bring you the sushi and all the prices are on the menu. There are no surprises here you get what you can pay for or however you want to budget for it. The sushi is so fresh and delicious. We also ordered a bowl of Tempura Ramen it was really good. The broth wasn't too salty but it was good.

The atmosphere is very European cool...the food options are vegetarian friendly.  I had the eggplant schizal sandwich with the beet salad and my husband had the falafel sandwich with the macaroni and cheese.  They were both terrific.  We like a hoppy IPA and only IPA on tap was okay, not great, but good.  Service was prompt and attentive.  The future plans will put this on the map with the additional restaurant space and outdoor areas!

This place is too cool. Love the atmosphere. The decor is really funky - trombones, figurines and even a stuffed armadillo holding a beer bottle. The food was tasty. We had drunk chicken, red beans n sausage, jambalaya, and the white chicken chili. All served w rice. I'll be back again.
Ok, place is really cool, great ambiance, bartender was also very nice. The pizza simply wasn't worth $25+ dollars. WAY better options for pizza elsewhere for less.

What a beautiful establishment. My fiancé and I were looking for something new and stubbled upon this gem. I drank their margarita, it was perfectly balanced and tasty. Their Lamb chops perfectly tender and juice, but go for the duck carnitas. Those duck wings were fire! I'll be back soon.

I loved the food here! I had the pad see yew which they had a funny name for and my boyfriend had the green curry. The roti that came with his dish was SO GOOD! I loved the shimp chips and we got a lychee drink that was too sweet but my bad for not asking for less syrup. There was a beautiful dog inside with his owner when we went and everyone loved him so this place is definitely pet friendly. Service was great and the place is very modern.

For the eclectic semi-fast food market, this place is probably the best in the area. That being said I hope this place gets more customers! I think the location isn't in the best parts of town, they would do much better downtown but I'm assuming the rent isn't cheap down there.

Service is lovely, food is surprisingly delicious and incredibly flavorful. Their collard greens are probably the best in the area, cooked to perfection. And their waffle fries are crispy, starchy potato gold. Cover them in cheese, chili (beanless!), and onions and you won't be disappointed!

And yes, awesome. I was recently on a business trip to New Orleans.   A Friday night fire/urgent matter at work had me and a coworker rushing to fix it . . . so we got to dinner on a Friday night in New Orleans around 8:30.  NOT the best timing, but the wait was only 30 min.  Not bad.  But we spotted 2 seats at the bar, so there we went, since we were grumpy and hungry.  I had oysters, we shared a crab cake to begin with.   EVERYTHING I ate outside of the hotel and the Convention Center was fantastic (and the Convention Center wasn't that bad at all - and they fed us for a week). Dinner - mine was scallops atop mashed potatoes.  Seriously, you can't go wrong with seafood ANYWHERE in New Orleans. I WAS NOT disappointed at all. The scallops were lovely, and the mashed potatoes did not seem to be overflowing with cream and butter - which was nice for my waist line. She had some sort of local fish - and that was her kick that week.  Fantastic!  

Our work group had a dinner seminar there - not sure how it went, but I am sure they ate well!

Our bartended/waiter was nice - very attentive at first - then, not so much. But her - we were all tourists.

All Fixed. Owner looked at the review and lowered the prices. I went back got the same thing and it was normally priced. Thanks Peter W. for taking my review to heart and making the adjustment. My apologies for taking so long to update my review.

Excellent food (whether fillets or sirloin), wonderful service. Hadn't been in years and am glad for opportunity to revisit. Interesting mix of younger, older and in-between people, all seemed to enjoy their food and their company. Try it out for a first time visit, and revisit if you've been there before. Did I mention excellent food???

So... This place has okay food. Most of it isn't interesting and the wraps are below par. The salads are good enough. Very expensive for what they give you. Honestly, their coffee is possibly the worst coffee around. I think it's only extremely busy because it is the only viable option on Campus for coffee. They have beer though, that's a plus.

Yelp doesn't have you write a title for your review, but if they did, I have a good one:  Lost in Translation.   To begin with, I can't for the life of me remember whether the name of this restaurant is Shu Feng or Feng Shu or Fu Sheng or Sheng Fu (you need to know: I often write my reviews offline, then copy them in).  Besides that, what's funny about this restaurant is that each of my three visits has been made more interesting by a lack of English communication.  For my latest visit, I sat down and ordered the same thing I had the time before, the House Special Chicken lunch special.  After a couple of minutes, the woman I have deduced is the owner walked up to the table and I swear, said "Do Dee Do Dee Do Dee Doo Doo Dee Do."  I thought I was in a dream.  I just looked at her and said, "What?"  So then the waiter walked up, she said something to him in, uh, Chinese I guess, and he turned to me and said "How spicy do you want your chicken?"  How was I supposed to get that out of Do Dee Doo Dee Doo?  My wife always laughs at my inability to understand people with accents, but after this, I might just tattoo American Dumbass on my forehead.

Later, when I was about done with my lunch, another woman, who is kind of an assistant/bus girl, walked up with a pitcher of ice water.  I had about half a glass of soda, but no other glass on the table.  She asked if I wanted water.   I said "I had soda" and she looked confused and troubled.  I guess she was going to top it off with water.  So I just said "No water, thank you."  Satisfied, she left.

So how was the food, you might ask?  Strangely, it seems stylewise like kind of standard Americanized Chinese, like you'd get at China King or some other suburban strip mall place.  I'd rate it as good or better than any of them, but considering the lack of English spoken here, I'm kind of surprised it's not more, well, foreign.  The prices are fair, the place is clean and the food os very good, so I'll be back for sure.  Maybe next time I'll venture off of the lunch specials and try something more unique, like the Do Dee Do Dee Do.

I'm very impressed with this place.  Everything is fresh, local and cooked to perfection.  The pasta, all made in house, tastes like it was brought in from Italy, as does the salami.  Excellent chefs who actually care about the quality and presentation of their dishes, they take pride in their craft and it shows.  A bit pricey for Reno....but I understand why....this type of talent costs and is worth paying for.  So splurge a little every now and then your taste buds will thank you!

As we walked away from the honky tonk towards the Nissan Stadium, we overheard some top 40 tunes. Naturally, we quickly turned back around, and ran towards the music. 

The name is misleading, but the place is great! Multiple above-ground floors with lots of room to hang and dance. Spacious two-tiered rooftop bar is perfect on those warmer nights. There are couches and high-top tables with umbrellas, perfect for groups looking to lounge. 

Located at the end of the honky tonk, the rooftop here is the perfect place to get a picture with the entire strip in the background while you enjoy Top 40 hits.

As a born-and-raised New Yorker with bagels as a standard part of my diet, I can't say Proper Bagel has REALLLLL bagels...but they have really good round shaped breads that resemble bagels!

Put it this way...they try...and they're good. I had the bacon, egg, and gouda sandwhich on a spinach everything bagel (these don't exist in New York), with a side of sweet potatoes and an iced coffee. You can tell that the food is high quality.

What I really liked about this spot was their vegan-friendly options, since some of my friends have dietary restrictions. There's not much seating so grab a seat while you can!

We love pizza and have tried A LOT of place on the Main Line.  Paisano's is the best of the bunch.  Not too think, Not too sweet.  Not over loaded with cheese or sauce.  We drive the 20 minutes (40 round trip) for pick-up because it IS that good.
Only wish their full menu was online.
Weeks later, I'm still dreaming about this place. I had banana, honey, and almond butter on a biscuit and I'm telling you, as weird as it sounds, I'm dieing to go back!

Stopped in for lunch with a friend and went back for dinner on date night. Lunch dumplings are delicious. Lunch portabella bun was hearty and filling with a great combination of flavors. The tiny bucket of skinny fries with the bun was a nice touch. 

At dinner, we ordered the papaya salad, dumplings, and street corn for starters. The papaya salad wasn't too spicy like it's served many places in stl.  Dinner dumplings were incredible and I could've used the sauce on everything. Our table raved about the street corn.  I ordered the crispy duck as an entree and loved it. Crispy skin, tender duck, just enough heat in the sauce to give it a nice kick and great flavor. 

Staff was accommodating and friendly. We will definitely return.

Totally awesome.
High-caliber, high-quality preparation with all the delightfully oily spiciness you could want from Szechwan cooking.
A variety of price points that will enable you to make it work within budget. For example, I splurged a bit and got both the Dan Dan Noodles ($7.95) and a lunch special ($8.50), but the noodles alone could have sufficed. A comforting bowl of slightly spicy, nutty deliciousness.
I loved that the folks dining here were from all walks: blue collar, white collar, Asian, non-Asian. Really just great food that will appeal to anyone who is down for a bit of spice.
Great staff too! All around very friendly, pleasant and accommodating.
Just about perfect.

TLDR: Overall, great Cuban restaurant! The portions are HUGE that we had left overs to bring home, service was great, food was delicious. I will definitely be coming back in the future!

Came here for restaurant week with a friend, and we sat outside. It was a cool day (66 degrees) but it did not feel cold at all! They isolated our area with a plastic curtain so we had some privacy.

Service was GREAT. They called me a day before to confirm my reservation and sent me a text the day of to remind me to let them know if I was here. The servers filled up our waters in a timely fashion. 

Drinks:
Non-alcoholic Mango Mojito - If you are not a fan of drinking, I would recommend trying the non-alcoholic Mango mojito! It was my first time. It tasted like sweet mango juice.

Appetizers:
Mamá Amelias Empanadas - We ordered one Chicken De La Casa and one Beef Picadillo. Both were very good and fairly large! The beef one has olives, which I'm personally not a fan of the flavor, but the beef itself was good.

Pineapple Guacamole Cubano - Plantains were delicious with the guacamole. The pineapple in the guac provided a sweet ting to the guac. Highly recommend!

Entrees:
Ropa Vieja - Large portion! the braised beef was absolutely delicious. The portion was so large that I actually had left overs for lunch the next day! Highly recommend.

Paella Mixta - DELICIOUS. Highly recommend! It looks so pretty too. This was a very flavorful dish with shrimp, ham, and asparagus. The garnish was the perfect finishing touch.

Dessert:
Cuban Flan - I love flan, and this did not disappoint! The vanilla cookie was a nice complement.

Churros con Chocolate - If there's anything you need to try, get this!! There's apple sauce inside the churros, which was a nice surprise. The churros were coated with a lot of cinnamon and when dipped into the chocolate dipping sauce, it was the best flavor.
Service and staff were excellent food, not so much. Hot pastrami sandwiches were over salty, French fries were salty and tasted old, salad was iceberg.

Really solid brewery. Has a very nice atmosphere inside. The menu is interesting and everything I have had so far has been really good. The beer is very well done. I've tried about 10+ of their beers and haven't been disappointed yet. Friendly staff. Great system online for reserving cans when they're released. Can't wait to see more cans coming out of here

Walking in I was greeted by a friendly hostess and I told her I was looking for a friend who'd already sat down. Wandering through this restaurant is tough as the layout makes you feel like you're in a lab rat's maze. The aisles are narrow and there are twists and turns at nearly every table so although I could see my friend making it to her was a bit of a task.

The beers on tap were excellent and the service speedy. I ordered wings  and inquired how hot their "wings of fire" were, the server gave me a bit of a shrug, perhaps she wasn't a spicy-food-fan, so I opted to split my wings between that at the garlic Parmesan. I found both to be pretty good. I wouldn't really classify the "wings of fire" as such but they did have a good spice/flavor to make up for what they were lacking in the scoville scale. All in all this joint is A-Okay, nothing amazing but certainly not too shabby either.
We've been craving the prime rib since we left! Too bad we were visiting from out of town!

Living out in Catalina, there are not a lot of choices for delivery and let's face it, at the end of the day who wants to cook? Wouldn't it be nicer to just make a phone call and have dinner delivered? 
So, we ordered Domino's. We have lived out here for about 2 years and have sporadically  ordered from them, each time we are disappointed. But time and time again, we want delivery so we give them another chance. Well this is it. Not only did we get our pizza delivered late ( we live, LITERALLY, 3 minutes away) we also got the wrong pizza 3 times! Are you kidding me?! The service and business has gone down the drain without hope of repair. 
If you value your health and want a quality pizza, do NOT order from here, there are WAY too many choices in the Tucson area to eat this crap.

We were in NOLA to drop our daughter off at college at Tulane and were looking for a "locals" place for quality Cajun. We found it at Chef Ron's. The gumbo was mind glowingly good, and Chef Ron himself checked up on us during our lunch. I can't wait to go back next time we are in Louisiana!

First time to Indianapolis. Looked for a local place that the locals go. Let's just say you won't be disappointed. This place was happening. Great breakfast or lunch anytime of day. I had the protein plate. 4 eggs to order and two meats. Added hash browns it was awesome. I will defiantly be back durning my current stay and if I'm ever in the area.

I don't give 5 stars often but really found no reason to drop them down to a 4. Got here around 930 on a Sunday and was seated right away. Staff was friendly and attentive, prices were reasonable. Pretty big inside, we were seated in the main dining area but there looked to be two other rooms for larger tables.
