I ordered the special crab cake Benedict and had to try the cinnamon bun pancake (just a single), my husband ordered the over the boarder skillet and everything was delicious. I am not a huge sweets person but the cinnamon bun pancake was SO GOOD! see pictures! Will definitely be back

Salty, spicy, sweet and good. This has been my favorite lunch or dinner spot for chaat, dosai and curry since the demise of  India Chaat house years ago. Loved it when it was Udupi. Love it still as Passage to India. You can go as hot, fried or light as you like. Idli, pav bhaji, pani puri. Lightly fried cabbage and deep fried hot peppers.  Love that it is 100% vegetarian. When I have taken carnivores, not one has complained about the lack of meat. I suppose it is, in part, due to the fact that eating here is much more adventurous than the standard indian buffet joint. I have eaten here for lunch and dinner and the weekend dinner buffet is a treat. They have Indo-Chinese, Gugarati, and chaat nights on the weekends. Stock up on the ingredients to attempt the dishes yourself at the grocery at the end of the hall or just pick up some music or a dvd. This place is great.

Over the past couple months working in Philli I've become a regular here.  Just a fantastic intimate place, with no pretentiousness. Seafood dishes are phenomenal, chefs specials superb, service fantastic.  All in all, one of the best places for a meal in the city.

The most important thing I have to put here is, a corn dog, is a corn dog.  There are no great corn dogs, or gourmet corn dogs (I'm sure there are bad corn dogs, but I can't imagine what you might do to a corn dog to lower its quality).  So, that bubble above your head that is filled with dreams of some fantasy corn dog, I'm popping it.

I had two veggie corn dogs with french fries.  I ended up throwing out most of the second dog, and only consumed every crumb of the dirty, bottom of the barrel fries because I apparently hate myself to some degree (eating the entire first corn dog supports this theory).

However, I am not going to hold this place completely at fault.  Everything I ate at the Reading Terminal Market had a weird taste, so maybe things might have be different if I had met Fox and his son elsewhere.

I also didn't get to try the funnel cake, which might have changed my mind about things.  It also might have taken this rating down a star.  The lady who took my order was very pleasant, so that has to count for something.
I love this place. I have never been able to find a good Chai anywhere until I came here. The staff is always really friendly and always happy to see me.

I love the Patterson House. I especially love their delicious doughnuts. I get them every time I go.  Of course, all the food there is very yummy. They actually make bar food taste good. 
As for the drinks, some of my favorites are the Maisy Day, Pimms Cup, Cooper's Bright, and the Juliet and Romeo. I am definitely looking forward to the new fall menu that will be coming out very soon. 
One flaw of the PH is that on occasion , such as the weekends, it tends to get a little loud in the quaint space. I'm afraid I'm yelling at the people sitting at my booth. 
I hope the PH becomes a permanent fixture in Nashville.
Trident Grill is simply amazing. The pricing is reasonable. Every thing was terrific and tasty. The crew was really pleasant and service is wonderful. Trident Grill - So good!
Hospitality is wonderful. Saag paneer with garlic naan is one of my favorites here. I even did a catering order and it came out amazing. Daal makhani, gobi mutter and paneer tikka are also wonderful.

We went in and got seated right away on a Saturday evening around 6:55pm. We waited 15 minutes and still no server. I watched another group get seated and within a minute they had a server come and take their drink order. They were a party of 3 and we are a party of 2. Jorden who was supposed to be our server never showed. So we left. Should have known something was up with all of the empty tables. Done with them.
The cheesesteak was delicious!!! One of the best cheesesteaks I ever ate! The fries were delicious!  Definitely will be coming back when craving a cheesesteak!!
If you're into the hipster crowd then this place is where you need to be. Long lines, crowds, slow Internet, etc. Good local spot or many but not me.

After a bad experience in the past ( terrible food and mediocre service) I gave it another try with coworkers and was pleasantly surprised! We got the Spanish fries which are soooooooooo goood lol and a great portion size, we split three orders among 9 of us! l and I ordered a chicken quesadilla for the happy hour which was just pretty standard, tasty but nothing to rave about, good size and would recommend for the happy hour price about $6 I think. The wait staff was fine and we were seated downstairs which I was unaware they had, there is no music, really dark, looks like something they gave up on , and kind of depressing down there. So the lights, music and general atmosphere was lost. So Spanish fries were the highlight of the night! I would go again for those alone and the location/area but the experience in total was average.
Lovely restaurant. Food was great, large portions. Waited about 10 minutes to be helped by the managers who eventually became our server. Margaritas were great, very fresh.

Went to this donair shop thinking I would have a delicious donair, was I ever wrong! Awful meat, soggy pita, vegetables that looked like they fell on the floor, cheese tasted like plastic! As someone whose eaten at over 30 donair shops in Alberta this was hands down the worst! Fast forward 3 months and I'm willing to give them another shot as bad experiences are sometimes not the norm. Anyway I order through skip the dishes and 90 minutes later driver calls and tells me owner gave him 10 bucks to not deliver order because it's late and they are cleaning up kitchen and order was processed but unfortunately my food will not be delivered. People take your money and run, Swiss donair is the best alternative
They get an extra star for being a vegetarian/vegan restaurant in meat happy Missouri. The food was good, but expensive for what you get. I'd check it out again to support vegetarianism

The food was a mixed bag, some dishes were good, while others were either too salty or too bland.  However, the real problem with this restaurant was the overall dining experience: Not only was the decor very dated (which is not necessarily a big problem) but the place was really filthy and is in dire need of a thorough cleaning. I am usually not sensitive to such issues but this was too much for me!
Nothing crazy about it. Ok food with ok drinks. Sports bar/restaurant. I won't go unless I have to. Easy parking. Not too crowded.
Great cappuccino! This coffee shop has a good vibe for studying or catching up with friends. Beautiful minimalist decor. The outdoor patio is shaded for days when the weather is cool.

Probably my favorite Chipotle location near me because the staff already knows my name and what I like to order, plus, since it's one of the newer locations, not that many people know about it so it's less crowded than the other Chipotle's I've been to.

This location is a bit difficult to find because it's not visible from the street and the only way to get here is by driving here so if you see the CVS, it's behind that.

Great service with great attitude and they don't skimp on the burritos. Most Chipotle's get 3-4 stars (unless it's the 86th St Chipotle in Brooklyn, that place sucks).

Parking: Lot
Price: $7+
Wait: Little to none

I'm sorry to say this but the last few times I've been there the food is not up to par. Is actually dried out and the salad is usually limp and skimpy. When they first opened it was an excellent value

Our first visit at Bouchon was amazing!  Hunter was one of the best servers we've had.  It is appreciated that he was as knowledgeable as he was about the items on the menu & which wine went with the excellent Chanel Island Sea Bass, over a bed of vanilla scented risotto with fresh peas from their local farmer's market & lobster chunks.  The duck breast is the best I've had in a LONG time!  Finishing our dinners off with their perfectly made Creme Brule, & Chocolate Chip cookie dough bread pudding was a perfect ending!  Looking forward to our next dinner there!  Thank you & compliments to one chef from another!!  Dr. Robert's Bakery

The food is great so is the service. They have a sweet and sour chicken that is out of this world. It's more like a spicy sweet and sour. But it is good. The beef noodles are mouth watering good. Prices a little high but well worth it. You won't leave hungry, the portions are generous.

Remarkable flavors, huge menu, prompt service whether dine in or take out, and the prices match the portions. I have nothing to suggest for an improvement.

They're performing very well in spite of COVID, and I will definitely return for a third try and more. It makes me very thankful to have restaurants this great available during this time, so thank you, Royal India!

We had here dinner on Sunday. The staff was extremely friendly, and was checking on us many times, every time noticing that we had nothing to eat on the table. The waiting time for the food was excessively long although in the restaurant there were just two more parties at the same time. I was disappointed to realize that the lemonade was made by dilluting sweet sirup (I don't know, perhaps it's a standard procedure in some restaurants but if you charge 15$ for  a dish...); we had to send one of the 'lemonades' back because the proportions of water and the sirup were clearly too much on the side of the sirup. My meat pie was really delicious, but my husband and son complained that their meat dishes were too salty. Perhaps we got there on the wrong day but most probably we won't give them a second chance because it was simply overpriced.

After years of passing by this bakery I finally went in and discovered they have the best donuts. Not only are they inexpensive, they are huge. If you have not been to Goleta Bakery now is the time to give it try. They are located in Old Town Goleta in what should be deemed a historic building and are family run.

I really wanted to like this place, however I have found that the best way to describe it is mediocre. 

I ordered a 1/3 (their smallest) burger with all the fixings, fries and drink. Total bill with tip was $23.   Bun was soggy, but the ground beef was ok. Not good enough for $23. Not even close. 

I should have taken the hint when the Yard House and twigs were packed and this place had two tables at 6:30 at night. 

Service was fine, locations in the village was poor. Too far away to enjoy the fountains or anything else. 

All told the dining experience was worth $10 not $23.

Did not enjoy this place at all. Service was bad, burger was way over cooked. When asked how our food was we told them it was over cooked, instead of offering to make us something else they offered us a shake...we already had one. Do not recommend.

The inside of Bongo Java gets crowded pretty easily, but outside on the deck and patio, there are plenty of tree-shaded tables.  Most afternoons, the tables inside are too close together and the volume is too high for me to get work done, although the deck outside is a great place to hang out or do some studying.

Of course, Bongo Java's organic coffee is exceptionally high quality, and the bagels are good, but the hummus plate leaves something to be desired.  The line can get pretty long, so customers should be prepared to have some patience.  If you have trouble finding parking, just keep driving down Belmont Blvd. away from Magnolia Blvd. - I've always had luck finding a spot across from the church.

Beau was the barista tonight and unfortunately Cartel has dropped Finca Alaska Bournon (FAB). What a real disappointment, easily one of the best espresso shots in Tucson.

He pulled the Black Market for me and it is more fruity than usual, I think they've changed the varietal or they've modified the roast profile.

On the pallet this is very smooth, a faint table lemon, syrupy Orange Muscat and a cocoa finish, this time not bitter at all.

Character held throughout the temperature range with no modulation.

The pull was tight on the doppio estratto, my count in my head was 17 seconds. Volume was spot on.

Three words: CHILEAN SEA BASS - yummy and highly recommended. The ambiance . the people . the food = fabulous. The CHOCOLATE BENTO BOX leaves chocolate lovers speechless. 

The one qualm: the layout is a little wacky so during our 2 hour dining experience to the left of Big-bellied Buddha, we saw at least 2 people trip down the invisible stairs... ouch!

It's also a little noisy which makes it difficult to enjoy conversation ;)

For my first time eating here it was really good . The Asian Wanton Salad was awesome. I had a great server Natalie. Who had me try the tomatoe soup & some cheese bread. Both are great, but better when u dip the cheese bread. I will definitly be back.

I discovered this downtown dumpling place due to Downtown Dining Week and wow, I had no idea what to expect but I am a complete fan. I'd give it 6 stars if I could. Their specialty is the soup-filled dumplings that are exactly what they sound like: little dumplings filled with a bit of meat and a burst of delicious warm pork broth. 

The regular pork soup dumplings are smaller and easy to pop in your mouth, but the pan-fried pork or shrimp and pork dumplings are larger so it's a bit more challenging to figure out how to eat these without getting soup all over you! (Maybe those of you with bigger mouths can eat them in one, but I sure can't.) In terms of flavour I personally prefer the pork and shrimp, because I'm a big shrimp fan, but they're all delicious.

In addition to their soup dumplings, they do the sandwich style bao buns: a sweet steamed bun filled with fried chicken, or fried tofu, or pork - all these are delicious also, but probably similar bao can be obtained in other places in Edmonton (such as 99St Kanto) whereas as far as I know, the soup dumplings are a specialty that only BaoBao makes like this. Their spicy wontons were pretty delicious too. Basically, I've been going here at least once a week since discovering it ... so if you haven't tried this place out yet, please do!

One caution: due to popularity, their soup dumplings do sell out. So, safer to stop by for lunch if you absolutely must try them, or call to check in advance.

The Legend is located in an east side neighborhood called Irvington. Irvington is named after the author Washington Irving, so you can guess how the restaurant chose its name. 

The Legend offers a menu of traditional American dishes such as meatloaf and chicken, but of very high quality and in a fairly upscale atmosphere. They generally have specials that venture beyond traditional American cuisine. The prices are a bit expensive in my opinion, but you certainly can't complain about the quality. There is a beer and wine bar attached to the dining room, and it is a great place to hang out. They sell a lot of micro and local brews, which are always popular with the patrons.

Food was better than I expected for Bourbon Street. We were seated quickly on a busy night and our server was very friendly, suggesting good items on the menu. I really enjoyed the Shrimp Ya Ya and my Shrimp Creole.
Amazing duck Vietnamese tacos! The fire pits outside are cozy and inviting as well. Great spot for dinner with friends.
Loved everything about the Drag Brunch. Amazing experience, bottomless mimosas and great food!

Great service. I was seated right away, and ordered within a few minutes. I had the Chicken Vindaloo, basmati rice, and naan. Everything came out hot and super fresh. The Chicken Vibdaloo wasn't all that spicy, so keep that in mind when ordering, but it has excellent flavor. I definitely left super satisfied and with leftovers. Will be back!

I never thought I would use "flavor profile" and "bagel" in the same sentence, but I've gotta say the flavor profile of this bagel sandwich was amazing. The tomato jam was a surprising needed addition, but all of the ingredients are so complimentary! I also tried their sweet potato, which i was so glad my roommate made me try--such a yummy side! I can't wait to go back for more.

I have to give this place a solid 3 although I really wanted to give more. The whole premise of a burger place is the burger, right? They should know how to time it so the burgers are cooked to the right temperature. My dining companion and I both ordered ours cooked medium and both came out well done. We were starving or else we would have sent them back. The brisket is absolutely delicious.  I love that there are lots of options and that the business is health conscious. I'll give it another try sometime, but I was definitely disappointed.

Ribs were good. Fries were good. Grits were good.... Beef brisket was literally terrible it tasted like wet beef jerky... Sadly they really only have ribs, sausage, and beef brisket on the menu so one out of 3 meet options was bad....

Price is good for how much they give you but don't get the brisket. Seriously, go to Sunny's BBQ before you do .....

My good friend and I have been wanting to try this place for a few months now and we were extremely impressed. The two working the lunch shift we went to today we're really nice and gave quality service. I got the Classic Melt and my friend got the Korean BBQ sandwich. Both were something to come back for!

I just ordered for the first time in maybe 10 years. A friend at work had ordered the Italian sausage 3 pepper pizza and it was awesome!  Tonight I ordered for myself Italian sausage, onion and black olive.  It was GREAT!  Not better than premium pizzas but very very good.  Got a medium 3 topping with garlic sauce for $15.  Very good, Dominoes!!!

Thought I was buying great crab cakes. They looked good. "Best in town" according to label. $10 each. Restaurant price for a market item. What a disappointment. Stuffing balls. All bread, no flavor. Maybe, maybe a teaspoon of crab, each. I've bought sea bass, salmon, scallops here, all good. But would NEVER purchase the crab cakes ever again.

We loved this restaurant. Great homemade pappardelle and a classic oil and vinegar green salad. We had a nice Montepulciano for a perfect family style Italian restaurant in the Old City. You can't do better!

Season 52 is awesome! Good portions, healthy and fresh food. I went today for lunch. And had the grilled trout with veggies. It was delicious. Well cooked and light. It was pretty busy for a Tuesday but my food came out at decent time. It is always good to eat here.

On Sunday, January 31st while closing, "Executive Sous Chef" Nathan was dumping water and grease right down the alley. (No grease trap in sight anywhere on the premises.) Nathan cursed up a storm and argued that it was "just water". He then decided to enter the neighboring business, make a scene in their shop, slam their doors, and toss some of their patio property across Macklind Ave. (All while on the clock, very professional!) Nonetheless after the incident on January 31st, a brand new grease trap appeared behind their business on February 2nd. I thought it was "JuSt WaTeR"? Even upper-level management tried saying that the mess was "water frozen over from the night before", when it never dropped to freezing temperatures. It's a shame when the businesses don't respect the neighborhood they belong to. The neighbors thank you for finally properly disposing of your waste!

Our first time here. We sat outside which was really nice they had fans and a breeze however that flies seem to find us. The service was awesome we had drinks and salsa almost as soon as we sat down. The food came very quickly and I must say was the best part of the whole experience. My daughter got a " Zesty Diskada"  and I got the "Cinco" tacos. The food smelled delicious, however it was so hot ... temperature... that we had to wait before fully enjoying it. I am not saying that this is a bad thing in any way in fact it's a positive because the food came out really hot.   
I've heard they're famous for their margaritas and as much as I wanted one I declined. But I will be back...!! And we will definitely be back and bring out of town family with us. The food was that good!!!!!

No frills.  Mary is nice.  Atmosphere is meh.  Breakfast was meh (I judge a breakfast place largely on their home fries).  Suggestion?  Throw some onions and peppers in there and a bigger helping would be good.  Also, Heinz ketchup makes a difference.  I liked the serve yourself coffee machine.  Place was clean and warm.  Neighborhood is safe.  Try for yourself ;)

First time visiting this place and I am SO happy with it. It's on the river front so I can't wait to go back when it's warmer and eat some food by the water. While I was waiting for my food to be done, I got the Oreo cupcake and it was fabulous! For lunch I got the V-Steak, macaroni and cheese, and the sautéed southern greens. Everything was so wonderful, and hands down the best vegan Mac and cheese I've had yet. The cheesesteak was so meaty and flavorful and the greens were perfection. I also got the rose quartz drink which I wish it had more of the floral syrup in it because I couldn't taste it much, but it was still so refreshing so I didn't mind! It's decorated with cool record covers and news articles and art, and I'm pretty sure it's a black female owned business so I will always 100% support that! I can't wait to come back!

I Wish I could give a better review but I was very let down. When I got my food, it wasn't hot. First I tried the rich which was over cooked and basically just mush. The macaroni salad was bitter and didn't taste like regular macaroni salad at all. The chicken was flavorless but the sauce was decent. There were also lots of moths flying around as well as a big stink bug walking around by our table. When we told the cashier, she said she was too scared and made the manager come sweep it up with a broom. I will not be going here again.

Overall,  I had a nice experience here. I agree with other reviewers that the service was slow (especially when it was not at all crowded). I overheard other tables complaining about the time it took to receive both food and drinks. It took us awhile to receive our drinks as well, but the food came out in a timely manner, and it was delicious! We enjoyed the bruschetta and two flatbreads. I really liked the ambiance of the outdoor patio, and the live band was fun. I think if they find a way to speed up the drink service, this place will be top notch!

Delicious! Great service and good food! I had the sopes, they were delicious and super authentic. My husband had some enchiladas and he enjoyed them. I can't forget to mention their courtesy chips and salsa... that salsa is the best I've tried among all the Mexican restaurants in the area. I'm glad they opened this new spot with an outstanding service. Another thing we liked was the ambiance, it was not busy but usually some restaurants have their music too loud. Good job El Fogón!

I used to come here quite regularly after it first opened up about 10 years ago, and I was pleasantly surprised to find it still open on my return to Tucson. So I came in, expecting to experience the same high quality experience as before. 

The menu is more or less the same, I remember seeing the Monkey Man, Green Dream, and Eat A Peach on their original menu. The prices are pretty similar too. They have always been a little steep price wise. However, if you compare them to their closest competitor, Jamba Juice, and factor in how much better their smoothies are in comparison to Jamba's sugar bombs, you might find the cost negligible.

That said, I ordered my favorite smoothie, Eat A Peach. It tasted wonderful, but it was a little sweeter in comparison to what I remember. Must be the peach juice that they use. Or it could be possible that my tastes have changed since then.

At any rate, I can safely say this is still a solid location. It's not the type of place that I would go out of my way to frequent, but if you happen to be in the area, I would highly recommend giving it a visit.
Favorite Mediterranean food in the valley. Hummus is great and so are kebabs. I always get the kebab sampler and it's amazing. Rice, pita, and dolma are great sides!
Awesome spot, outdoor seating near water, lots of parking. Good food, not huge selection and bit pricey. Beers are amazing, always a great selection!

ambience: good. a bit cramped, but in a charming sort of way. very very busy for lunch. don't expect to get a seat.
service: you wait in line to order food but it's friendly. 
food: excellent!! love the food here. very very yummy. been here a few times and has never disappointed.

the only reason i'm giving 4/5 stars is because i do feel it's a bit pricey for a soup/salad joint where you can't reliably get seats.

I live right across the Square and have been meaning to try Parc for awhile, but every time I pass by it has been so crowded it put me off. I finally found an afternoon and around 2pm the crowd was significantly less. Had a great seat by the window. The service was impeccable and my water/ wine glass was never empty. I had the french onion soup to start. Bread inside lightly crispy still and the onions cooked perfectly, the broth was very flavorful and the cheese was crisp and melted. Dare I say though, that there was too much cheese? Nah never mind there can never be enough cheese. The wine carafe 12 oz was an adequate red blend. The mussels were really out of this world. First of all the portion size was huge! Probably around 24+ mussels, I was very surprised. And super flavorful with herbs, onion and garlic. Certainly some of the best mussels I've had in awhile. I was full to bursting after but had to order the creme brûlée and I'm so happy I did. I am a creme brûlée snob after visiting Paris 10+ times, and can say it is superb and made me feel as if I was back in the City of Love. Above and beyond in every way, Parc, I will definitely be back!
Great service, food tasted average but better than other options in the near by area.

I tried out the village bar a week ago and have been wanting to write this review ever since. I love neighborhood bars, and this one had the feel of a good one. As soon as you walk in the back door, you can smell the beautiful aroma of burgers and fries that makes your mouth drool a little bit. The wait staff, especially some of the waitresses that have been working there a while, are extremely welcoming and accommodating. The bartenders and cooks are engaging and efficient. If you're a smart person, you'll order a "better burger". I had a side of fries and washed it down with a beer on tap. At such a cheap price and comfortable environment, I can't imagine waiting too long before I go back. Thanks Village Bar for opening my eyes to a whole new world of enjoyment!
Great sushi. Great service. What's not to like? I'll definitely recommend this gem to friends and family.

Came in on Father's Day after church and was hesitant because of the line. Since the pizza was good the first few times I'd visited we decided to wait it out. Got to the counter and "Scott" the shift manager began to complain how everybody wanted pizza today and how he wished they didn't all come at one time. Being a manager of a franchise myself I reminded him that it was a good problem to have. Then when asked what I wanted and I told him wanted whole wheat crust he said I'd have to wait because he'd have to go to the back to get it. He continued to ask the next person in line what they wanted...who just happened to be my husband. Well he also wanted whole wheat so he didn't have a choice but to go to the back now. I was shocked that he was planning to just skip me knowing the line had already backed up behind me. Then when I told him I wanted the Athenian but had a few changes to it he acted as if I was ignorant and begin telling me that what I wanted was NOT the Athenian pizza and I needed to make it more clear. Basically all I did was switch the sauce and the crust! He was extremely rude and disrespectful to me and acted as if I was a bother to him. When checking out i asked the cashier who he was which is when I found out he was the shift manager. I had a coupon for a free pizza which I did use and told the cashier I would not be coming back again! His customer service skills were horrible. I continued to hear him speak harshly to others in line once we sat down. I also have noticed that the place is not being cleaned well. To be new a new location it is a shame to see the service and the environment so poorly managed. Hope the owner begins to look into these issue otherwise I don't foresee this business lasting long in such a great community.

Driving through Nashville to Chicago, looking for a healthy option. Found this gem. You'll drive up thinking your in the wrong place (it's across the street from the children's museum) but in the International Medical Group building. You'll be eating with people on their lunch breaks from the medical group, but worth the food! Lots of organic, vegan, and gluten free options. We had the balance bowl and it was delicious!

First time trying this place! Located in the centro ybor district area, this great find hit the spot! 

There are a few sushi places around here, but this is more of a Thai and noodle bar. 

Atmosphere is casual and inviting, with a big semi circle bar and tables around it. Staff was very accommodating and friendly and good came out quickly! (However, we did come around 4:30pm on a Monday, so it wasn't too busy). 

We started off with a Roti appetizer and the curry sauce was very tasty! The roti was thin, flaky, and crispy! Perfect!

It was a cold day so the noodle bowls hit the spot! I had the Thai curry bowl and the sauce was awesome. A creamier curry. My husband had the Thai boat Noodle and the soup was savory according to him.

We both shared the Asian BBQ Pork Belly was yummy! You can choose either lo mein noodles or rice noodles with this entree.

All entrees were good portions! Everything tasted authentic since the cooks are actually Thai! That helps!

Brook was super friendly and helpful! She recommended the Thai tea and it was delicious - it's more of a dessert type drink with whipped cream, but was perfect ito compliment the dinner. 

For dessert lovers like me, there wasn't a dessert menu, hopefully in the future we will see some sticky rice with mango or some additional sweet Thai items, but for now, the Thai tea is a delicious alternative!

Update: third time here! Today (7/14/17) was phenomenal! It's a busy Friday night and we were in and out in 30 minutes! Our food was ready immediately after appetizers! Food was again delicious!!!! All I really need here is more dessert options, I love the Thai tea but I'd love some sticky rice mango dessert (hint hint) :)

First time visiting The ROW.. LOVED everything about it.. food, drinks, staff and atmosphere over the top!! To
top it off, great country music.. Can't wait to return the next time we are driving thru Nashville..

The hamburgers at Paradise Park are GREAT!  Tastes like a burger you would make at home.  All the toppings are fresh and the meat is MEAT.  I highly recommend this place.  It looks like a dump from the street, but the food is so so good.  I am so glad we decided to eat here. as it was our last day in Nashville.
One of my favorite places to eat. Great atmosphere and the baked goodies are delightful. Give it a try when you are downtown.
Delicious donuts and plenty of flavors to choose from. Helpful workers. A little tucked away so wouldn't know about it unless you are referred by someone.

This is a breakfast staple in the Tampa Bay area. Formerly called "J. Christopher's," this breakfast joint serves up a variety of familiar breakfast platters as well as unique options like duck bacon.

I have been a regular patron to this establishment for the past two years, and I keep coming back for more. Personal favorites include the duck bacon and the route 66 skillet. Pro tip: add goat cheese to anything you order.

The interior is a little overwhelming at first, meaning that it resembles a giant dining room with very little partitions between tables, offering little for those seeking privacy. There is a separate room immediately to the right, and I've noticed that the temperature tends to be a little on the cooler side, so I generally try to sit there or at the bar area. Pro tip: Bar area is first come first serve.

The service is capital. I haven't met a server who wasn't on top of his/her game.

Restrooms have always been clean and well-kept.

They also offer a rewards program, so be sure to ask about that.

Duck bacon:
I have never heard of duck bacon before coming to this place. It sounds like it might be odd/gamey at first, but rest assured that the "bacon" is very meaty, slightly lower in fat than pork bacon, and much better than turkey bacon.

The food was delish, I ordered the Salmon a la parilla, and my other friends ordered the enchiladas with shrimp and fish.  My absolute fave was the side of creamy poblano rice with the enchiladas.  

The reason why I'm not giving a higher rating than 3 stars was because the service was pretty bad.  Our waiter took a while to take our orders and seemed very pretentious.  On top of that he decided to take all the cash and not seem to think giving back change existed.  So we had to awkwardly ask for our change back, and definitely did not deserve a good tip.  However, the other guys that served the food were pretty funny and nice, and were able to hold the super hot dishes bare handed, hands of steel! But to sum it all up the food is great, and hopefully you don't have a waiter like we did.  Sorry I don't remember his name, but it was a saturday night on the second floor.  His name is obviously forgettable though.
At the recent food truck awards they were my winners. The poutine and Italian Ham sandwich were excellent. Can't wait to see them at future events around town.

My new favorite Poke place!

So my daughter and I just stopped here to try this place. I learned that this place has been here since November, but we didn't know. Every time I Google Poke in Reno, only one place comes up. I found this place on yelp (have I mentioned I love Yelp?) after reading other yelpers descriptions I'm looking at the menus, 12 ounces of fish for $13-$14 seemed  too good to be true. Also with an amazing number of toppings that are included in that price. 

When we first entered, there were two smiling faces to greet us: one male and one female. They explained a little bit about my choices and then asked what base we wanted. We chose Half mixed green salad and half white rice. Then we chose three scoops of salmon and three scoops of yellow tail (They have four other proteins to choose from: shrimp, ahi tuna, spicy tuna and scallops) We had Ponsou sauce, seaweed salad, dried seaweed, edamame, crab, scallions, tomatoes, tobiko, cucumber and topped with Furikaki. They have six other sauces and quite a few other toppings. We did add avocado for $.50. It was a quarter of avocado. 

What is really amazing is the size of this bowl. I was able to split the bowl with my 15 year old-daughter, 6 ounces of protein each, and the toppings were so generous that we both walked away full and satisfied. All I can say is wow. Where has this place been. I regularly Google for new poke places, this place does not show up on Google. I question them about this after eating that wonderful poke ball. The girl said that her boss is never there when the Google people call to get the place listed. I let her know that I would've been going there for months if we would've known about this place.

Great price, great quality, great workers... What else could you ask for!

2013/052

In my nearly 2 years here, I've only been outside of Nashville's city limits *twice*.  The most recent time was because friends brought me to one of their favorite places.

Clean, modern interior. Dark tables. Pretty popular with the locals.

I don't remember seeing the owners, but my friends seemed to know him well enough to ask about him. 

Food is Asian fusion, and the flavors were definitely prevalent -- except in the salad. I started with the side salad, which was rather bland. I think it was finely chopped, marinated carrots on top of a few leaves of iceberg. But the dressing seemed to be missing. I didn't feel the need to return it, as I really am not much of salad person. I just eat it sometimes as medicine.

I was hoping for the salmon teriyaki, but when I asked, I found out they remove the skin. I love salmon skin (which I know some people are weirded out about eating). I consider my salmon incomplete if it's not available.

Instead, I had the "chicken taco" -- taco in the sense of a soft tortilla, rather than the crunchy, folded up kind. In contrast to the salad, the flavors were bursting. The chicken was not entirely seasoned, but the toppings definitely were. I detected a mixture of julienned daikon and apples with lots of kimchi-like seasoning. Not too much a fan of daikon. Had half of the daikon portions, and all of the apple part of the topping.
The food is good, but they are rude and snobby af!  It's a bad look for the vegan community.  Seriously, every time I interact with the owners the snobby and miserable.
You will tell yourself you're not gonna get the shrimp and grits on top of your filet mignon... but you will... and you will love it.

Came for the Bills Backer Bar and had a good time this past Sunday.  The bar area had multiple TVs including 1 projection screen size.  Other customers were pleasant and we all seemed to get along despite the Eagles crushing our beloved Bills.  Beers were cheap--Blue Lights for $3 and Genny Cream Ale (a personal favorite).  Wings were actually pretty good--I've still been searching for good wings down here in Philly.  We placed an order and received 8 wings (not sure if that was the number we were supposed to receive) but they were flavorful, saucy, and had a good amount of meat.  Will definitely be back to cheer on our Bills but not sure if I'd go here for any other reason!

I've been stopping by here recently before a regular gig I have in Ardmore.  I went for the first time on a recommendation I got after randomly popping into some sort of picture frame/random decor store around the corner to ask about cheap places to eat close by.   The man there said he'd been having some "great experiences" at Firinji so I decided to go check it out.

The guy who owns the place is really friendly, as are his staff.  Maybe a little too friendly, even--I'm not surprised his background is hotel management.  Too friendly is of course better than not friendly enough.

The place is set up essentially like a fast food joint, although not quite as fast.  It's never been busy at all when I've come but I could see there being a problem with food preparation time if there was ever a long line.  The foods all seems to be quite fresh but since it's also reasonably priced I don't think you're getting free-range organic chicken here, either.  Everything I've had, including the lamajhoun wrap (not sure if I'm spelling that correctly) and veggie burrito, has had an appealing taste.  On my first visit I had lentil soup that was especially good--I've never had lentil soup that was pureed into a uniformly smooth texture so that was also a bit of a novelty.

What I struggle with the most at Firinji is that the combination of ingredients is rather odd.  It can't seem to decide whether it's serving Middle Eastern, Mexican, or American food.  This was most notable in one of the Kumpirs I ordered.  There were so many different things on it that it just made no sense.  One feels a bit of unease when confronted with the combination of pico de gallo and hummus, or yogurt in a burrito instead of sour cream.  You can combine a lot of these things together and the result won't taste "bad" but I really wish they would make their menu a bit more cohesive.  I'd really like to see some kind of "Middle Eastern plate" with hummus, baba ghanoush, dolmas...as well as some more entrees that were more consistent with respect to the melding of ingredients and flavors.  It's also important to mention that customers are equally encouraged to build their own wrap/kumpir/etc. combining all these different ingredients as they wish.

I've gone there for a few weeks consistently and may try out some other places in the area before returning.  On the whole though I'd say it's a good bet.

Bonus: they also have free wi-fi.  The unsecured "guest" network didn't work for some reason, but the owner gave me a password to the secured one.

I am a person of Jamaican descent and sometimes you can get good Jamaican food OUTSIDE of your own home. Not in this review. Ron's is cafeteria Jamaican food at best. Everything was super SALTY! I per chased ox tails, curried goat, and jerk chicken. PROS-OX TAILS were tender. CONS-they were very small. The very end of the tail. salty and the gravy tasted like a doctored version of the real thing. The best gravy however of the three. PROS- GOAT was tender. CONS- goat was SALTY. No other veggies in the pot. If they added a carrot or some potatoes it would have helped with the saltiness. Would have been the best gravy if it was not so salty and inedible. I threw it away. PROS- JERK CHICKEN was a good serving size. CONS-Not enough jerk flavor. They need to marinate the chicken in the jerk sauce. It was just plain bland. The worse part is they added some cheap barbeque sauce on the chicken and called it jerk sauce. HORRIBLE! Ruined the entire meal! If you get the jerk chicken DO NOT get the sauce! Cabbage was BLAND! Beans and rice a big disappointment. A poorly made version with poor ingredients. Tasted like minute rice. The give you a lot of rice and beans especially in the extra large serving of ox tails. The meat to rice ratio was just unfair. I felt cheated. I will not recommend!

 There was a short wait considering the place was crowded. It looked like organized chaos. The servers were clean, in uniform and their heads were netted. GOOD. They were pleasant also because the masses were kind of difficult. The cooks were dressed in chef whites. Nice touch. Well stocked variety of drinks and desserts. Very clean.  I left thinking I have found my new Jamaican cuisine home. NOT!  THE FOOD WAS JUST BAD. REALLY BAD! BAD!

I am giving them 2 stars just because they are new. We had problems with our orders. Seating is not for people with children, short, heavy, older, arthritic or a person deep into their cups. All tall bar stools limited short chairs for parties of 2. Those seats not for women in shorts or a dress. The chairs are straw type and snag clothes.
My wife is Greek so we are very hard to please. This place rocks!!!! Come check it out. Also very nice and friendly. Appears to be family run.

Ever since Charlie Karp passed on and this place was sold to current owners it's gone down hill. I remember the prime rib diners .This place will never match it.Somebody should be calling John Taffer and Bar Rescue

D/B/A doing business as Old Manhattan & Mama Rosa's. 



Wow I got to revisit my TMJ pain trying to eat this chewy piece of pizza.  Sauce is good so maybe pastas would be better.  But I wonder if they recycle all the pies from the night before and microwave the dough to reheat this mess.

By the way this restaurant goes d/b/a by mama Rosas also and manhattan grill.
Excellent burgers and exemplary service by Kyle, even during the craziness of GenCon!
I've been to Chicken's Kitchen twice. The food has been hot & tasty each time. Today I had the braised oxtail. They were perfect!

I stopped by today for happy hour, and there was plenty of seating available. It was self seating, and order at the bar. The bartenders working today were both very friendly. I ordered the oolong infused bourbon and the Chinese city wide. The oolong infused bourbon retained the bourbon flavor and wasn't overly sweet. The beer and shot in the Chinese city wide were both very smooth. I would order them both again. The total bill was $20. They don't take card for less than $10.

My boyfriend and i live right next to Umai Umai, so we always go there for their incredible sushi and amazing atmosphere. We tried Domo tonight looking for another good sushi place in the neighborhood and were VERY disappointed! The food was no where near the same quality as Umai and the service was even worse! Nothing tasted fresh at all and the lights were so bright i felt like i was in a high school cafeteria. we showed up around 8:45 and the entire time we felt like the staff was trying to get us to leave so they could go home. We sat at the bar so we could watch the 2 guys make sushi, but not even halfway through our meal did they make us move to a table to they could "clean" the sushi bar at 10:30 pm. We did not have a good time and we will never go back. Umai is the best sushi north of ben franklin. period. Domo is no where near the quality and experience you will get at Umai Umai!!!
Awesome. Eats was great. Super service, clean, attentive staff and tasty delicious food. We will be going back.

By other half loves to come to Outback - while I stick with preferring more 'ethnic-fare' he sides with a baked sweet potato and salad w/honey mustard ;)
* On Wednesdays there is a 2 for $25 option we've been digging lately. You can share either a small version of an appetize or a dessert and 2 entrees for this price. This makes things more reasonable than the usual steak prices.

Food - My preference has always been the Outback special: 6 oz. steak w/a greens salad (w/vinaigrette) & green beans. Hubs digs the same w/a baked sweet potato and side salad w/honey mustard. The Ahi tuna on crispy won tons and the chicken quesadillas are our favorite appetizers!

Atmoshere - The Outback in Brandon upped the ante! The new decor and more 'chill' mood opens up the space and gives diners a more quaint feel than the hustle and bustle of the bar area - should you choose a more quiet surrounding.

Overall - we come back, it's a great place for dinner

Only set back: parking. That parking lot for all of the  businesses in the plaza gets crazy!
Rocked out a delicious Cubano as the sun was setting.  Great view of the gulf without breaking the the bank. Super-helpful wait staff (genuinely glad I was there).  Great spot!

This is my favorite casino on the row. 

There is always a cool show gin g on I. Their awesome theater. When you go there for a show you can get 1/2 priced food by the way! It also has a stage that they can raise and lower. 

Besides that they have all the best games. I swear if you want to play it they have it. Not just slots and tables, they also have virtual tables for roulette, blackjack, etc.

They do have their own parking lot that is a bit tricky to find and it's down a few one way areas so that is frustrating. However if you do the enternece is right next to the theater and food areas. Speaking of food it's delicious. We have had the Italian place and been to a few bars for work functions and happy hours. I have yet to be disappointed with the Eldorado specific food. 

They also have a Starbucks! Which for me was the cake topper. 10/10 would recommend.
Fresh delicious pizza at a great price! Dough came out nice and crisp and all the toppings were great quality. Will for sure stop by again when I'm in the area!

Good things about Joe's:
- Organized service system (great for the lunch rush)
- Cheap pizza

Not-so-good things about Joe's:
- Pizza is average to below average
- Servers are hot/cold -- never know if they'll be friendly or snappy with you, though they're not really mean

We went to NECTAR for a birthday celebration, and the experience was just okay. 

While the interior of the restaurant is beautiful, the service was subpar. Upon being seated, we were ignored for nearly 20 minutes and only given food menus (all other tables surrounding us also had drink menus). When someone finally did come over, they hurriedly jumped to asking if we were ready- no greeting- and when we inquired about a wine list (something they're known for) we were met with a scoff and asked to show our IDs, which is fine because we're both in our mid-twenties, but the smugness on part of the waiter was unappreciated and unwarranted.  

My sushi was just fine, nothing special, and my partner said his pad thai was pretty good. We were in agreement that the best part of the meal were the edamame dumplings, and while they were extremely rich/creamy, they too needed something a bit more to set off the flavor/counteract the creaminess. 

I was given my wine with my entree, another symptom of the rushed/hectic service, and felt totally unwelcome to relax and enjoy the experience. 

Overall, a disappointing experience, particularly for a birthday. We probably won't be back, which is a shame, because their menu is varied & intriguing.

The worst burger that I have purchased in years! I ordered take out. This use to be my favorite burger place. Burger was cooked beyond well done. It was charred on one side. It was almost inedible.  After a couple of bites the rest was thrown into  the trash.  The French fries were barely cooked and were the opposite of the burger. They were limp and soggy. Unfortunately I do not live close or I would have returned all of the food. There are too many other burger places close and you are too expensive to serve food like this. I will not be spending any more money here as this has happened before.

Went there on a busy Saturday around 5:30 pm. We were informed of a 45-50 minute wait, which was expected. After finally being seated at around 6:30, we waited patiently for our server who eventually came over to take drink orders. We got our drinks in a timely manner, and it was all down hill from there. Appetizers taken to the wrong table RIGHT NEXT TO OURS! Waited 15 minutes for appetizers again, 15 more minutes for bread, 20 more minutes for our salad, another half hour for entrees, 15 minutes  for the check, after having plates removed . Bottom line...the manager came over to apologize, though we never complained, and took 20 dollars off our check. That saved this from being a 1 star review. Bad day at Carrabba's...and it was our first time ever going.

While waiting to be seated another customer came out and said the food is amazing, she said if you eat meat, get the bacon and not the sausage, and My boy did just that and I got the SHRIMP AND GRITS, DAAAAAMMMNNN!!!!  BEST SNG I've ever had!!! We Loved it so much yesterday (7-321) We're about to go back as soon as I get done with this review... And the staff was VERY FRIENDLY AND THEY ALLOWED US TO SIT AND LET THE HEAVY RAIN STOP BEFORE WE LEFT WITHOUT A PROBLEM.  A MUST DO IF YOU EVER COME TO NEW ORLEANS..

Service, really bad!  We ordered take out for dinner, sat and waited 15 + minutes, after watching two couples come and go with their food, I asked about the status of my order.  First the blank stare, then she turned around and grabbed my bag off some shelf it had been sitting on and tried to tell me it was not cold from sitting so long.  

there were three girls working the counter, only two couples that came in to order food during the time we were waiting for our food.  Why would you bag up my food then stick it in some shelf far from the front counter?  Do you seriously think I want to pay for cold soggy food?  Did not offer to remake it so I asked for my money back and left.  Bottom line- no customer service skills & too busy chatting to do their job.   Too bad, I liked the food.

I went to Levis Hot Dogs one night and had a combo with the fish cake and hot dog.  The hot dog was not hot and the fish cake was only so-so.  I ordered pepper hash on the combo and only got a teaspoon of the flavorless condiment on it. I also tried a Potato Knish. It was the worst knish I have ever had.  The potato was flavorless and the dough was thick and heavy and it seemed that the knish was sitting in a steamer all day. Disgusting!  Not at all my memory of what the REAL Levis Hot Dogs were like back in the day.  But the real disappointment was the attitude of the owner who was yelling at the workers and rude to some customers who seemed to be taking a little while to decide. And then I heard him murmur something to a worker that "these cheap old farts" never order any sides to make it worth my while! And they look at the nostalgic candy but never buy any!" I would NEVER go back to a food establishment where the owner does not seem happy to be there. The food, service, knowledge of the staff, and owner attitude was absolutely horrible!

We come and we wait over 15 minutes to be served. Then the girl (blonde long bob, was in a referee suit) comes and serves us, very short and not sweet. We order. Then a while later I request a drink  again and she takes my order. I decide to not tip her since she was rude and not hospital at All. She then proceeds to tell me to " have a great fucking night" and keeps hackling me to leave the bar, I was APPALED. I get kicked out because I didnt tip? I'm a bartender myself!!!!I finally tell her she is a bitch and that why I don't tip her and she kicks me out. I never was disorderly or out of control. I was simply a nice patron who was abused. I will NEVER COME BACK HERE. And will tell everyone this place is HORRIBLE.  I talked to a "manager" and she handled nothing!  Just kept saying " well Jen is a manger so we can't really do angthing" if your manager is treating people like that then they should be fired.

SUPERB experience there last night. It was crowded, but we were seated immediately and menus were delivered, drinks orders taken at once. Our waitress explained "how it works", then followed the plan to every detail. Food comes out as it "hits the window", sizzling hot, nicely seasoned and perfectly cooked. Great variety for all appetites. Our server was so attentive, we felt as if we were her only table. She even brought us a complimentary dessert (cinnamon ice cream with fried 
wontons dish), and I tipped 40%, which I rarely do. We'll be back. Only downer to me was acoustics of interior -- concrete floor, metal ceiling, you can hear every conversation in the room. Management, there are easy ways to deaden acoustics with ceiling-hung banners/upholstery, etc.

I'm here on Saturday March 13 2021. The new place is horrible. So loud. Lacks the cozy fun Mexican feeling. 
Sadly I think they're understaffed that's why I asked for napkins three times and still don't have any. Salad served with no utensils.

Ladies, come for the meat and the other meat.... man meat! It's a sports bar that serves awesome meaty items like pulled pork, brisket and hotdogs. And with this meat will be served a heaping pile of fries or tater tots. No plates. Just the mountain of food on a giant piece of paper. This is a recipe for a man magnet. Seriously, I was the only girl in the place. (FYI... I have a boyfriend so I won't be going for the other meat. But, hey, gotta spread the word to the single ladies).

My brisket was quite good, but I didn't get enough sauce. I like my meat slathered in the stuff. This girl ain't counting calories. I would have asked for more but......

Service is a little slow, but word on the street is that this is how it's always been. 

Must say this is my fav chill hangout spot in SoBro. Bonus points for windows that open during warmer weather.

Still 3 star as the dinners were good, however I ordered Gluten Free chicken Marsala with GF pasta and extra mushrooms.  They upcharged me $6, it was $3 for GF pasta and $3 for mushrooms, so my dinner was $29. At what point will restaurants realize that having a gluten allergy should not cost more, as a box of GF pasta is $1.98 and had 1/4 of the box with this dinner.  Someone who is GF will not eat bread, so it should be a swap.  In general, the marsala doesn't have enough mushrooms.  The mozzarella and tomatoes was ok not great, so next time we will pass on it.  The cappuccino was outstanding and we loved it.

Our favorite breakfast spot in the area, and we have always had a great meal here.  The menu is pretty standard, but the specials on the board are always great and varied as well.

It's the kind of place you would expect to see on DDD.  Be prepared, however, to wait for a table as the place is always packed when we go regardless of the day.

Staff hardly acknowledged us. We stopped in for our lunch break, and a to-go order of a sandwich and salad took over 15 minutes to put together. When we finally opened the bag, we'd received the wrong sandwich altogether and the salad had no dressing on it. Way too expensive for what you get (even if you get what you actually ordered). Bummer.
One of the BEST Cuban sandwiches I've ever had. Looking forward to their new location. Please deliver to Nora!!

After standing at the counter going through the menu, you will probably find yourself overwhelmed with delicious Venezuelan food options. You will want to try everything and will be indecisive. Not a problem... do what my hubby & I did and get the Sampler plate. This is more than enough food for two, and it's only about $16. The food is awesome. There wasn't a single item that I didn't like. Also, the woman working the counter was telling us about the Venezuelan tamales in plantain leaves, and now I have to make a return trip just to try those, because they sound fantastic.

Tastyyyyyyyyyyy.

I initially saw the pairing of "seafood and sausage" and imagined that this place was mostly for casual fair -- basic oysters, maybe some homemade sausage, but nothing all that elevated. Those options seem to exist here, but they live in tandem with a more expressive, elevated menu which is worth your time. It is creatively planned and carefully executed. 

After a long, cold day of watching my football team lose a bowl game, we started with the poutine with crawfish. We ordered it mostly because it sounded fun and strange (poutine in the south?). But I cannot describe to you how thoroughly my partner and I "mmmmmm'd" at each other once we dug in. It was greasy and salty and rich and delectable. We didn't even eat it all! We boxed some of it up for the next day because it was just that worth it. 

Entrees were equally flavorful. I ordered the porchetta. DO NOT BE AFRAID OF IT. If you ever thought to yourself "Well I like the taste of pork but not the texture of it. It is also hard to cut" then go for some porchetta! It was crunchy and crispy, but also tender and held together. Think about succulent. This porchetta is succulent. 

We ate at the odd counter-space that seems to be installed in several sections of the restaurant. It was not only ok, it was great! I felt like our service was faster and we were seated more quickly. Don't second guess the small space.

Fantastic lunch place! We stopped in after going to the beach. Everything is incredibly fresh! We started out with the calamari appetizer. Perfectly crunchy, accompanied by a delicious marinara sauce and fried zucchini, carrots and cherry peppers. 

My brother and I ordered the lunch special with half panini and half salad and soup. Both the buona salad and pasta e fagioli soup were great! The baronessa panini has grilled chicken, pesto, red peppers, goat cheese and arugula. Perfect combination of ingredients and toasted to perfection on the panini grill! 

One of the best lunch places we've been to a while! Great sized portions too.

The food is really really good the biggest problem is that they tell you every time your food will be out in 20 minutes but expect to wait MINIMUM an hour and a half. They need to hire more people and answer their phone so your not waiting.

I was seriously disappointed in this place. I went in and ordered an açaí bowl but informed them i had a banana allergy and needed to make sure there was no banana in my bowl and they said they were "unable to make it with no banana," and proceeded to watch me leave without ordering a thing. I've had açaí at multiple places with no banana & they always inform me it takes longer to make but they'll do it, safe to say i won't waste my time at soho again.

I LOVE Olive Garden and occasionally go with my family for lunch or dinner. This particular Olive Garden SUCKED! We went in around noon (myself and my two boys). The restaurant wasn't full and we were happy about that. The girls in front sat us down immediately. We sat and sat AND sat waiting for someone to even say "we will be right with you". After awhile the waiter comes and says has anyone gotten you drinks? I tell him NO. After about 10 min another waiter comes and ask us what would we like to drink. We get our drinks and another 15 min of waiting for anyone to take our order. The waiter then comes and says "Sorry, they gave me extra tables knowing I was busy".  After placing our order the wait for the food is ridiculous. We finally get our food and can you believe it was fu*** ing horrible. The chicken gnocchi was watery. My son's platter combo look like it was meant for a 3 yr old very little portion ( mind you it was almost $12 dollars). My other son's flatbread pizza was not hot. I'm beyond pissed at this point. He comes back after a long while and says do you guys need anymore drinks. I tell him yes please, it's been awhile and they are choking on their food with no drinks (sarcasm because at this point I don't care). I will NEVER return to this Olive Garden again. The service and food 2 thumbs down!

The best lunch spot in Marrero, possibly the westbank. The prices are awesome. We got 3 poboys, and a large onion ring for 25 bucks. Roast beef is as fresh as it gets. Atmosphere is the best thing about the place, everyone is treated like family. Nina takes the time to know all her customers, and it truly makes for the best of experience.
This is my go-to take out spot. I highly HIGHLY recommend the Sweet and Sour Fish soup!

This is a special place. I was at the soft opening and have been back several times since.  The food is great. So far our favorites include the pizza, salads and fish tacos!  
Our severs have all been friendly and helpful. Shout out to Calvin, Michael, Peyton and Christine.  
The bartenders are great and made everything perfectly.
The property lovely and sitting outside is relaxing.  
Yes, the Barnyard Crafthouse & Eatery is new. They are working through some glitches.   I will be happy to wait and be patient as they do, because we need a place like this in our neighborhood. I plan to be a regular there, and gratefully welcome them to Tanque Verde Valley.
I truly appreciate that they're open until midnight. The food was good too. I ordered the Flame Broiled Pork and they got it ready pretty quickly.
Ate here yesterday and fell in love!! Best coffee for a low price. Great grits and eggs!! My boyfriend loved the Monster!! I will comeback for my next stay in Nola!!
overall a good place but I ordered some pizza's on a stick and hotdogs on a stick but I finished my bubble tea while waiting for them & wanted to order another one service could be a little quicker .

This place is killer. I mean really I'm a Grilled Cheese fan, but these guys are like ninjas. What Killer Poboys did for poboys, and Dat Dog did for hot dogs these guys are doing for Grilled Cheese. 

We went in Saturday night and it was busy but not crowded. You order at the counter and they bring your sandwiches out very quickly, probably 5 minutes or less. i ordered "The Juice" which is roast beef and cheese and my SO tried "The Cheezy BET" with bacon and egg. Both were stunning in simplicity and flavor.  There were several other sandwiches on the menu that I thought were worth a try and the beignets looked delicious as well. 

The only complaint I had was that the place is not in my neighborhood and I told one of the owners that, and he said cryptically that they were "working on that". So if you haven't tried it yet. Go Now!
How nice this little place was!  Just beautiful inside and the dishes were fantastic.  Lots of outdoor seating as well.  Will definitely return.

We were on a mission to find really good bbq here in Tampa. But sadly mission bbq is not the place. The decor and everything was ready great, service was good, but the food was lacking. 

This restaurants honor the military and all vets. Around noon they'll start playing the national anthem and request that everyone should stand in attention. It's a great way to remember the great country we all live in. 

Now onto the food...let's start off with what we order. We got ribs, a steak special, brisket, pulled pork, side of Mac and cheese, side of slaw and it came with corn bread.

The meats was decent. Lacking some flavor that we would need to use bbq sauce to fix. The ribs was falling off the bones, but some parts were just over cooked. The steak we asked for medium raw, but got medium well. The brisket was suppose to be juicy, but that wasn't the case here. A friend of mine thought it was too dry to finish as well. Pulled pork was just pulled meat...there was no sauce to it...we had to add the bbq sauce and mix it around. 

The sides was the best. Mac n cheese was amazing. The slaw was good. I enjoyed the sides way more than the meats. The corn bread though was just super dry. 

I had way better bbq at other places, but if this is the only option, I guess it's decent enough.
This is one of my favorite places to go in this area. It is definitely a great date night spot. The buffalo prosciutto pizza and the pork belly fries are a must! Never a disappointment.

I was quite impressed with the decor here.  The restaurant is extremely clean and very modern looking.  My lady friend and I decided to go for a visit last night after hearing about their tempura banana dish.  We love fried banana dishes so this was right up my ally.

It was a Monday night at 9PM.  So, I wasn't that surprised that the place was fairly empty with just a few people sitting at the bar.  They attended to us reasonably quickly and let us sit wherever we liked.  We ordered two hot green teas and the tempura banana dish.  

The tea was good.  The banana dish arrived beautifully displayed with a small dish of ice cream.  I ordered mango ice cream to go with the banana.  Either the mango flavor was very strange or we actually had lychee ice cream.  I'm not sure.  Either way, the ice cream was good but different tasting. 

The service was good and our tea pot was refilled when it was empty.  For $10 it was a good evening dessert and tea outing.

Stumbled on the place by serendipitous chance and was not disappointed. Prompt service, friendly and full of excellent suggestions. I arrived with a GRUMPY toddler (late lunch) and they brought a "busy bag" for little guy with goldfish crackers and fruit chews. I ordered the Not So Nasty 1/4 lb elk burger and was amazed. The bun was fresh and delicious and the meat was lean, well-seasoned and cooked to perfection. The 1/8 lb kids burger was perfectly sized, too, and came with a PILE of their excellent waffle fries. The final bill was less than $20, which was a total shock, given the location and quality of the food. I've paid more than that for lunch at Panera and not had as much food!

I forgot to write my review 

OK when we got here I was like this place is a whole in the wall from when you walk into place I don't want to eat here from the beginning so as we were seated the waiter smelt like a homeless person  so when we had got your food I find a dead roach in my food 
So I don't not recommend you guys eat here this is not the place!!!

I've been a repeat customer for years butI bought a quart of vegetable soup and the beans were inedible because they were like little stones!! I went back a week later and simply mentioned to the "CHEF" that I had to throw the food away he said I was mistaken because he sold a gallon to someone who didn't complain!

My family and I so wanted to love this place as we heard great things, and are always looking for a great Italian restaurant.  I am sad to say, the food was terrible.  There was a party of 9 of us, and all agreed, food was awful.  Even the 10 year old would not eat his.  His meat lasagna had no pasta in it.  I did not believe him and tasted it and checked it out, and it was only meat filling and cheese.  Almost no entrees seem salted or seasoned.  Not even a tiny bit..  The fettuccine alfredo was tasty, but all other entrees were bland, tasteless, not even worth eating.  The fettuccine with sausage had overcooked, nearly burned, sausages and zero seasoning.  My cappellini with shrimp that was supposed to have a garlic butter sauce had no garlic, and no butter.  Sauce was actually just moisture - I assume left over from the hot pasta.  Adding salt to it did make it edible, and the shrimp were nicely cooked, but, again, no flavor.  The asparagus ravioli were hard, did not taste like asparagus at all, and, again, just no flavor.  Very, very odd.  The polenta appetizer was good, was seasoned properly.  The Caesar salad was poor, seemed like bottled Caesar dressing, no anchovy or lemony flavor, and croutons so hard they shredded the roof of the mouth.  The dessert of tiramisu was good, as was the cheesecake.  Again, really wanted to love this place.  Service was friendly and attentive, but we will never go back as we could have had better food at Olive Garden, and that is not a restaurant I care for.  They need a real chef in the kitchen.

This restaurant has come a long way since it first opened! The portions are a lot larger now and the service is quicker. The carnitas are delicious and the margaritas rock! It's a family friendly restaurant but also a great place to go with friends! The outside seating area is a bonus because there aren't a lot of places in Downingtown with that! The homemade salsas at the table are all very good!
Just finished having lunch. Food was good and the young lady who served me was extremely polite.

Very old school vibe. Tight aisles around all the tables which made it difficult to get seated without bumping someone at the table next to you. Service is excellent. Cocktails before dinner were medeoker  at best. Wine selection was good. 

But the main reason its getting a 4 and not a 3 is because the steak was amazing. Great cut of beef. juicy and tender with awesome seasoning.
This review is long overdue! I've been coming here since It opened with my family and it always meets our expectations! Mellow Mushroom always puts out great food and the best service.

Well I do love their mushroom burrito bowl! Fresh ingredients, nice staff, delicious food and it's quick! I need their recipe for their pickled onions! Never had their tacos but my friend really enjoyed them!
Do yourself a favor and go try out this restaurant!! Every single item on their menu is amazing!!!

Say HALLAJUEH Mascoutah, you now have a WONDERFUL barbecue restaurant!  It's on the side of the American Legion (across from the high school).  The meats are glorious, the sauces are stupendous, and even though it wouldn't matter with the first 2, the sides are damn good too!

I had the brisket meal with red beans and rice and fries for my 2 sides.  The brisket was fall apart tender and MOIST!  The flavor was VERY good.  The have 3 different sauces:  sweet, tangy, and spicy.  Our favorite was the tangy.  The spicy sauce is a sweet sauce.  If it were tangy, THAT would be most awesome!!!

My husband had the pulled pork sandwich with potato salad and baked beans.  He said it was all good, with the meat and sauce being the best part.

The service was STUPENDOUS:  very friendly family run place.  Get out there Mascoutah and support this business.  Spread the word so they get enough business to stay with us!
Your typical in-n-out :) right next to the freeway for an easy way to get there. Great burgers, fries, shakes. Get the animal style french fries.

The Texas Meat plate is delish!  Beef Brisket is tender and savory.  The pork ribs and bbq'd sauce are so tummy.  Also the salad is great.  Service was great and the servers take personal interest and are friendly.  Great place!!!

Pad Thai is wicked! The staff are so sweet. Dine in or Take Out, service is quick and the food is super tasty. The ambiance is really nice, the price is right and they are really accommodating for gatherings. They even let us drop off a birthday cake early and provided what we needed without a cutting fee.

They should call it flavored rice with boiled chicken, instead named it biryani. 

You are better off cooking rice with salt and turmeric

We decided to visit Taqueria Doña Maria because we got a menu in the mail and everything looked delicious. I couldn't even decide what I wanted to try because it all looked amazing. Two things gave me a great first impression: the decor and cleanliness of the restaurant, and the presentation of the food. Wow, the food looks great. It LOOKS great. My daughter and I both ordered chicken chimichangas while the rest of my family ordered various tacos. The server came off as cold and aloof. I felt very unwelcome. We didn't even get a smile though we're a pretty friendly bunch. Once I got my gorgeous chimichanga, I happily bit into it and...there was no flavor and no spice. I drowned it in the hot salsa and it was still flavorless. I am told that the tacos were much the same. As my (Hispanic) husband put it, "this is Spanish food dumbed down for non-Spanish tastebuds." I really, really wanted to like Taqueria Doña Maria, but I just can't. Even without heat, I can't even wrap my mind around how flavorless food is even possible.

Huge portions for little cash. Decent cuts of meat for the price.  I'm from Idaho and the baked potatoes fully loaded almost made me see god...both in taste and as my ventricle slammed shut.  Very good. Not good for you though!
I've never had issues with this location. They've always gotten my order correct and the food always tastes fresh!

I feel bad leaving this review, but I gotta be honest. Pros- clean restaurant, attentive and polite staff. Cons- flavorless food. I know it's "north" Indian  food and meant for the US palette, but it was just not very tasty. It lacked spice and didn't seem very authentic- looking at you biriyani. I ate at the buffet with other Americans that really liked the mild taste, but If you really like spicy Indian food, I think you will be disappointed
Excellent food for what I'd consider to be well-priced. Shocked for the quality of food that it was only $80 for a charcuterie board, 2 glasses of wine, and two entrees. Definitely coming back.

I have been at the restaurant twice, both of the times food was not fresh. Theirs is fairly expensive food, but doesn't commensurate the price. You can charge even more, at least provide freshly prepared food. You lost a customer for forever!

Probably better for tourists than as a place to make your new regular spot (I was living about an hour away and only in Philly sporadically so I liked getting to go somewhere different.)  It is right in downtown Philadelphia, offers a unique experience which I always look for while traveling, and in both of my experiences, great food and service! It is a little pricy, but again great if you are traveling or for a special occasion.

You have to splurge a little on the dessert, get the little mini camp fire for your table and roast your marshmallows for the fondue!  So good, and so much fun!  I have never seen that anywhere else. That was our favorite - also tried the chocolate truffle heart cake, and a chocolate espresso milkshake. If you have to pick one, go with the fondue plate to share - delicious and you get a lot more. The cake is very, very small. 

I went for mainly desert both times so the only food I tried was the southwest caesar salad and mac and cheese - happy with both but definitely recommend the mac and cheese! 

Wanted to try the specialty coffees and chocolate martini, but there is only so much you can take in one sitting! They do offer those though.

I see others posted that this place was great for kids, which I can understand given the menu, but both times I went were on dates, and we were looking for more of an up-scale place.  On Valentine's day, we got just that (I assume because no one had their kids out), but the second time we went, there were a lot of kids (running around), the place was very very crowded and hard to walk around, and I definitely wasn't as happy with the atmosphere as the first time.  So the vibe of the restaurant is a little confused - if you are looking for a quiet, romantic place, I would suggest only coming here if it isn't a busy time.

So I have a backlog of reviews to post, but skipped through the rest to post this. WHAT A JEM!! This is the perfect execution of a farm to table eatery. There are so many who attempt this concept and miss, but Boca NAILED it. The decor, the music, the service and THE FOOD. Oh, the food. Their version of the shrimp and grits was by far the best I've had. Ever. Anywhere. I was torn between their smoked chicken entree and the S&G and asked my server for his recommendation -- thank you Darius for steering me this direction.
Do not get the strawberry ice tea! It tastes like bubble gum, not strawberries. Horrible, chemical flavor. I had one sip and asked to exchange it. They would not. Not the best customer service.

This was our second visit to The Southern and it was better than the first.  It seems to make a big difference what you actually order.  
It was happy hour till 6:00 and drinks were $1 off.  We shared the $5 Fried Green Tomatoes which were excellent.
My wife ordered Chicken Fried Chicken which came with greens, mashed potatoes (instead of Mac and Cheese) and country gravy.  It was very good.  Chicken was tender and greens perfectly cooked.  Also reasonable at $19.
I ordered Prime Ribeye, and selected my cut from the whole Ribeye.  At $3.50 per ounce, it cost $40.  Unfortunately, it was quite fatty and not really tender.  I was disappointed.
It is in a great location, just across from the Schermerhorn.
YOU GUYS. They have something here called "Crunchy French Toast." It had oatmeal and almonds on the outside. I think it was deep-fried. I will dream of it for the rest of my life.

Kwok's is definitely a hidden gem in Reno.

My boyfriend and I came here on a whim the one night - we sat on the patio since the weather was nice and enjoyed a couple of beers.  The first thing we ordered were the pork belly sliders.  I will pretty much eat anything stuffed in a Lotus bun, but these were exceptionally good.  The sauce was a perfect mix of sweet & savory, and they added some crunchy veggies for freshness.  We also ordered the sweet & sour pork, beef broccoli, and some fried rice, which were all super flavorful and delicious!

My favorite part of Kwok's is the quality of the ingredients.  The meat is never gristle-y, the veggies are always fresh, and the sauces aren't weird colors.  Also, the service is absolutely amazing!  We can't wait to come back and try more from Kwok's!
Best pizza in the city! Well thought out ingredients and on a different level from the competition.

Solid new option in the area for work lunches. So far I have had the lemon, basil and buffalo chicken salads. Both equally good.
