The grape side salad is very delicious and the broccoli one is enjoyable as well. The lemonade is good and the "chick meal" comes with a full sandwich, not just a half which is nice. Each meal comes with a small cookie. But, do yourself a favor and get the big one too because they are good and not too sweet.
My dad and I came here while we were in New Orleans. The crawfish bread was delicioussss and our server was super nice and pretty

Just enjoyed s relaxing, enjoyable meal, we had the brisket and Caramelized onion sandwich and baked cheese starter. So dang yummy. Sitting on the front porch of this old house while dining was so cool. We really enjoyed the setting, the atmosphere. Really chill.

If you want to wait in line for over an hour due to poor planning and organization of table seating by severely undertrained staff with poor customer service orientation for basic chain restaurant food that is mediocre at best, then by all means give this place a chance.  However, New Orleans is culinary food haven with so many amazing restaurant options.  Save your time and money and try a different place that will offer you superior food and service!

Get a real and delicious dinner somewhere else before you head there!
We did mistakenly the exact opposite. We wanted to grab a drink and appetizers here but were disappointed. The service was slow and the food was mediocre. We ordered the chicken and fish tacos and both tasted the same, filling and without distinct flavor. For some weird reason the chicken here tastes like tuna, did not make any sense.
We would always return for drinks since the outside patio is relaxing and the perfect spot for a late summer night in Nashville.

Absolutely loved our experience at Hemingway's! We came here for drinks and the menu here is just SO COOL! Each drink has a unique description (no ingredients listed) but the bartenders will help you if you want to know more.

We then stayed for dinner and omg are we glad we did! We tried the duck pontine, Korean chicken, and the chicken dumplings. Everything was amazing and I have no complaints about the experience. We plan to come back when we return to Nashville

Went here late night on a Saturday.  Just to grab dessert but ended up with appetizers and dessert.  It wasn't crowded.  We were seating immediately.  There is a thing at the table to order but the waitress came over within a minute or so.  She was very nice and attentive. She actually came by a little more often than I'm used to.  We had the sampler app.  Everything on it was fine.  Nothing special.  It was out in about 10min.  Nothing too spectacular no issues we used the thing at the table to pay which I love being able to do.

This was the worst steak sandwich I have ever tried in my life, it was all dry bread and the cheese was not even melted. I took one bite and complained to the lazy girls working their who basically turned their backs on me and I then proceeded to throw the whole sandwich.... I wouldn't have that to my dog... wish I had read the yelp reviews before I bought

Awesome service and very fast! Went to a Krystal close to my place and they refuse to honor my coupon. Their excuse was "oh we were told not to honor any coupons yet." Funny thing was I was there yesterday and they honored my coupons. Bunch of lazy workers. 

Not this place though, I pull up my coupons and they honored right away. Service was so fast too! Before I can text my wife I am bringing home Krystal, they were already done. Wish more places was like this!
Fresh, clean, healthy, delicious. Highly recommended. Chicken salad and açai bowls are especially good.

The Ruby Slipper was just around the corner from the apartment we rented in the Warehouse District on Magazine Street. I highly recommend reservations, since any time we passed by it in the morning, we saw very long lines. We waited around 20-25 minutes then were seated at the bar. The place is very cute, has a nice ambience and friendly bartender who waited on us. Because we were at the bar and the restaurant was busy, our service was a bit slow. I had the Southern Breakfast which included two eggs, grits, bacon, biscuit and fried green tomato. It was good, not great, and I take umbrage at being charged several dollars more for the simplest of breakfast plates over what one would pay at a local diner or Cracker Barrel. However, I understand this is in a tourist area, so they could probably charge even more. Our entire visit lasted about 1 1/2 hours, so it was good we had a flexible schedule and weren't looking for a quick breakfast to get us on our way for the day.

Amazing good... Was surprised. First time eating there. Perfect blend of flavors and spices in dishes... With out the spices blurring or walking on the other flavors. That gave their food a more complex and interesting flavor experience. Decent presentation. I would suggest to anyone. Worth the money with great food and good portions.
Great atmosphere. Drinks are good and reasonable.  Wings and Buffalo shrimp awesome.  Grouper bite special was great, not too heavy on the breading and nice size chunks.

I get excited for Joanie's, the pizza is great. It only missed 5 stars because inside seating feels a little cramped, but outside the seating is nice. Sometimes they have outside seating in front making it dog friendly as well. They have open mic and bands, I even once did karaoke there, though I embarrassed myself it was fun. Make sure to check this place out.

We wad the; Beet salad, roasted asparagus, Gulf Shrimp Boil and Chicken Cofit. Dessert was sticky toffee pudding and blueberry cobbler.

All was delicious, I love the seasonality of the menu, many dishes showing the bounty of spring. Staff was great

I was just amazed to find a vegan deli in the middle of Reading Terminal Market. I couldn't believe my eyes. They make all their meats and cheeses from scratch, and sell them by the pound. Ham, capicola, pepperoni, SCRAPPLE of all things (but of course, when in Philly). Swiss, provolone, cheddar, mozzarella...it's taking all my will power not to jump back on a plane and take a pound of everything.

They have a small menu so you can try their goodies right there. I had to get the reuben and see how it compared to my favorite reuben back home in LA, at locali.

It was unreal. It's easily one of the best sandwiches I have ever had. It was so fun eating this decadent mess in the crowded Reading Terminal. Made with their own corned seitan, thinly sliced and piled high, and swiss cheese, it was a work of art. I still love my locali reuben but Luhv's is the new reigning sandwich.

I also bought a brookie to take home with me. It's a brownie and a cookie and it is delicious.

Next time, I'll have to come back at the beginning of my trip so I have time to experiment with their meats and cheeses, and I suggest you do the same if you're from out of town.

We went for the music and the dancing. And it was good. La Touché plays short sets, mostly slower Cajun music.  It's not rousing but it is a pleasant ambience.  You won't be driven uncontrollably to your feet so relax if you don't care to dance. 

We ate and drank for a few hours. Our server was very attentive and most congenial. We never really waited for any parts of our orders.  It was a fairly busy Friday night. 

People who ordered mixed drinks felt the bar served more "mix" than drink.  Three tall Long Island teas should have been more "affective", so to speak. Same for margaritas and other specials.  The Abita beers were good.  Stick with beer or wine. 

The food was ok. Appetizers, red beans, gumbo, ribs, seafood platter were all plentiful and.....well......good.  Unlike some other places, there's nothing we had that you gotta' have here.  The dessert pecan pie was excellent. Pass on the bread pudding and root beer float.

Finally, be prepared to pay a whole bunch for your drinks (especially) and meal in a large, open, barn-like setting.  I definitely recommend Mulate's for big groups.  There were many there and they can handle them well. If you are 2 or 4, it's really okay.  We had fun.

YES!!! We were in town and looking for a local breakfast place to swing by. We were not able to go inside and eat (we had dogs with us) so we were looking for a place that also served up a take out option. This place came up on our search - and they have a Drive Up window - that made it so easy to pick up the food!!

We called to order our breakfast and the lady that answered the phone was very sweet and pleasant. We ordered a turkey sausage and cheese omelette and a second cheese only option. Both with toast and home fries. 

Upon driving up to the window we were greeted with a smile, paid for the food and left. 

YUM!!! All of the food was delicious and flavorful. We will definitely be back when we are in town again. 

This is definitely a must visit establishment.

I am currently staying at the resort now, upon check I was greeted by a very friendly and helpful staff. When I got to my room I found it to be an ADA room, it was nice but not what I would have asked for. The next morning I had kindly asked if I could move rooms, I told them the reason and Tate at the front desk could not have been nicer and more accommodating. I was in meetings all day upon my return my bags had been moved to my new room. Everything was taken care of and Tate also give me a beautiful upgrade for the mistake. (I never asked for an up grade for the mistake). I could not be happier with the room and the resort, the entire staff has been so kind and friendly, I would recommend this resort for anyone coming to Tucson. When you find the front desk and others though out the resort to be so professional you know it comes from the top, this is a very well managed resort.

Came for dinner and enjoyed the food. The restaurant is very laid back.The food was great and the wait staff was excellent. The ambiance was nice. I had several small plates and found them to all be delectable! The place was completely transformed from the prior restaurant that was there, Tangier.

The food was good. The lamb buns were great as well as a shrimp dish we tried. I also tried the kimchi but was not a fan, the waiter was great and took it off of the bill. The shrimp and pork dumplings were to die for! 

Service was great and the food was served swiftly. This place is one I have to visit again.

I enjoyed this place so much. They have such a wide variety of food and the majority of it is pretty tasty. Of course there are some foods that are a bit bland because it is a buffet. I had a delicious brisket, "make-your-one" pasta, and the passion fruit sorbet is amazing. The price is average for a buffet in town.

My husband and I used to live in Conshy and El Limon was our go-to spot. When we bought our house in Ambler and found out they were opening a new location here, we were pumped! Never had a bad meal and the staff are always so nice!! My favorite are the steak tacos on corn tortillas with a side of refried beans and rice. Their salsa has a great kick to it and great flavor. My husband loves the chicken burritos, which are huge, with tomatillo sauce. I think we order take out here at least once a week. Absolutely delicious and will continue to come back!

I love this place!  My family eats frequently at Bread and Butter Café and it's always delicious.  We've been going there for over 18 years, since they were in their old location nearby, and we've never been disappointed.
We always TRY to save room for dessert because they have the BEST pies, but often we have to take a slice or two home with us because we don't have room.  You've got to try their pies!

I don't know what has happened to this location,  but the service has really deteriorated.  At least two employees saw me and never acknowledged me.  Cashier just tossed my order at me and turned on her heel.  The only reason why I have two stars instead of one is because the food is good.

I know expecting much from a fast food restaurant is not allowed but the service here is pretty poor, even for fast food. They are ridiculously under staffed and It is management's fault. Theses workers are working their butts off and so backed up. I think waiting 30 minutes for fast food is unheard of. And too top it off they are completely out of chicken and turning people away because they are too busy. This place needs some h

Ninja is my favorite place in New Orleans to have sushi. I have been a customer here for 15 years. The rolls are larger than most sushi bars. It's a laid back place and prices are reasonable try the Goma miso roll its excellent. Their fish is always the freshest.
Service average, food terrible! Poor grade beef in fajitas, colleague and I both really felt awful for hours after the meal.

Gave it a star because the bar it self is very nice and the food was ok, but the service was horrible to put it in a nice way but I have other choice words about it. The waitress forgot about our beer had to ask for it again. The food runner brought out our food. The waitress didn't even come and ask us if we needed anything or if everything was ok. Not until we completed our meals and cleaned up and pushed out plates out of the way did our waitress then come over. And by that time we were very annoyed. If it wasn't for the atmosphere it self I probably  wouldn't of even given it a star.

My cousin decided to have us try Fado and it was absolutely amazing.  The food is very authentic and the atmosphere and staff were exceptional.  If I lived closer I would go every opportunity available.

Royal House! Amazing ambiance and experience. 


Our waitress was Destiney and she was lovely! Best waitress that we had while on our trip. Destiney! Remember the name.

Sampan, I adore you.  On our way to a different restaurant for a food fest we tried walking past Sampan. Failing, we popped in to see if they had a table for 2 with immediate seating, a rarity.  Just like that we were seated at the high top kitchen section. 

What an experience! I've been to Sampan and the graffiti bar countless times but being seated where we were was an absolute blast.  The precision was mind blowing. We must have watched 100+ orders of Brussel Sprouts and Bao buns be created with perfection.  We were so impressed by the speed, the attention to each dish and the energy everyone that oozed from the 10+people had in such a small amount of space!

We ordered mostly from the Happy Hour menu.  (HH on a Saturday, ftw.). The specials offer a scrumptious glimpse into the abundant menu.  We ordered the edamame dumplings, the edamame dumplings, and the edamame dumplings.  Each order comes with 4 dumplings in the most flavorful broth. I should have ordered more to be honest....mmm.  Another standard, the Brussel sprouts. The portion size is plenty for 2 to share but there are never any left. These soy glazed sprouts are done perfectly and thinking back we should have ordered more.  I also ordered the spicy tuna crackers and the chicken bao buns.  If you're reading this, I'll help you get started...BUNS, DUMPLINGS, SPROUTS, REPEAT.

Completely full, I had to try the sushi dessert, pb ice cream that was wrapped in a rice crispy treat and served with a chocolate sauce.  Yum!!  Artistic and adorable!! (See Pic)

Long story short Sampan has had my heart since day one. Their food is consistent, the happy hour menu is the best I've experienced in the city and the service is always top notch.  I've always experienced knowledgeable servers who are so helpful with menu navigation.  They even offer a vegetarian menu, just ask...Sampan, perfect in my opinion!

Minus one star because there are times when they are out of things that (i feel) they shouldn't be out of... also the wait... they have been in business far too long to not have figured out a way to make things go faster.

The food never lets me down... i keep tryig other places to give a fair shot but they just don't compare... i recommend the jerk bbq, mac n cheese, cabbage, oxtails, pretty much all the chicken, the yams... that's all first hand.

Basically... don't waste time with the fakes.

Terrible service. Didnt even stay to eat. Came in alone was ready to order the waitress said to give her a second but she decided to take some one else's order who she sat afterwards. Her response was `if you had patience.` Last time I checked you attend in the order arrival. Never going back. Nothing worse than bad service.
This is our pizza spot for delivery. Usually pretty quick. Have had some issues but seems normal for pizza delivery. Food is good.

First time trying rolled ice cream and I loved it!! A little expensive but delicious. And everyone there was very patient with my indecisiveness, definitely recommend if you are looking for a rolled ice cream place to try! Got the hazelnut chocolate with some add ins and it was great

Don't see what the big deal is about this place. The menu is small and the food was ehh. The meat on the tacos were too Smokey for me. I will say the nachos are on point but he three tacos I had. I don't ever have to go back.
We really love this place for a date night. Their wine is great...join their VIP group!  Food is pretty good, as well. We always have steak when we go. Haven't been disappointed!

I really wish there was 3.5 star option, but since it's only been open a couple of weeks I decided to give it the benefit of the doubt and give it 4. I think it has a bright future once it works out the kinks.

This building has special memories for me...I saw every Disney movie as a preschooler in this theater and I remember the staircase. The concession stand and the popcorn was against the left wall of the restaurant area. The front bar is where a full size replica of Herbie the Love Bug stood when I saw that movie.

If you're not suffering from depression or your meds are spot on - you'll love the dark decor. It's really dark, especially when breakers are still flipping. Seriously though I actually appreciate the fact that they found an ambiance that allows for conversation at normal levels and doesn't require escalating your volume like so many open restaurants with concrete flooring requires. Don't valet - the red shirt valet company has abused more cars than a Blues Brothers film and refuse to be accountable. We also had three brown-outs so clearly still a lot to work through as the entire infrastructure where the restaurant gets rebuilt.

The cocktail menu looks fantastic; I remember the name of one we tried was the "When Rande met Cindy" but both were craftily prepared and a great start.

We started with the "bread and butter", and "the Pig and the Peach" and they were both fantastic. I was really skeptical about butter as an app but they definitely make it worthwhile. The Pig and the Peach was a perfect combination the salt in the various porks and the sweet of the fruits.

For entrees my wife had the Walleye and had the French Onion Frites. The walleye dish was fantastic for her; it was very light and the beans and almond really made for a nice flavor profile. If you order this make sure and mix the dimensions into a single bite; the walleye seems to be poached so not a ton of flavor in the fish by itself. I wanted to something heavier and the French Onion Frites was the perfect entree for that. I saw another review that really abused this dish - bear in mind that yelper rated Calypso Cafe with 5 stars so you really shouldn't take her seriously on any review. So the ribeye isn't wagyu. So what. it's a great meaty bite to the crouton, onion, and cheese and it is a fantastic bite!!! It's worth a couple of extra miles running to order. The frites with it were crisp and salty like they should be. I got the house steak sauce and it's WAYYY too sweet - almost shouldn't be called a steak sauce.

For dessert we had a bit of let down - we ordered the Caramel Corn and the Chocolate. The caramel corn was the better of the two but I thought the Profiteroles were pretty chewy, they should've been lighter. On the Chocolate the mousse was phenomenal but the Bouchon was hard as rock. We literally couldn't cut into it so it went uneaten.

The service was great although we knew are server from Pinewood Social so she was already well trained by the Goldbergs before showing up at Sinema. We met Q who is the transplanted manager from another restaurant and he was super nice, really understands wine because he immediately recognized what we had brought with us!

We'll definitely be back once things have settled down and we've been able to work through some of the other new restaurants in Nashville.

Super dissappointed. Went in for dinner (a late dinner) and it wasn't really busy. All the servers were at the front counter. 15 minutes passed and no one ever came to our table or even acknowledged we were there. A group came in after 15 minutes and were seated behind us. They were served immediately and still no one came to our table. We actually left without ordering anything. No one said anything to us on the way out. Worst service I think I have ever had. :(

First visit here but more than familiar with local competition. Get the oysters, they're on point. Po boys were far above average, just shy of excellent. Little too expensive, oysters and shrimp piled high and fried well but stingy on the sauce. Still, go and get it.

Wonderful neighborhood spot on the Near Eastside. I love the staff and the menu has enough options to keep things interesting on multiple visits. Pizza is pretty good and I love the firecracker chicken poppers. Great selection of beers and harder options and the loaded Bloody Mary is the stuff of legend. I am there every Thursday night for trivia night at 9pm and always leave happy (happier when we win for sure).

Everyone at our restaurant LOVES this place!!! After a long day working, we order the 28inch extra extra large pizza for everyone to share and believe me, one slice is equal to 2 normal slices!  We have tried the meat special, pepperoni, veggie, broccoli/tomato, and combo pizza (half/half) all of them delicious!! 
Normally we don't stray from the 28inch pizza because its never failed us but one day we all got different items off the menu. A few of us got cheeseteaks, panzarottis, fries, and assorted sandwiches...all good. There was one small mistake on one of the orders and they were not only prompt in correcting it but corrected it in a friendly manner.
Their delivery service is both quick and courteous!
If I could, I would order numerous of the 28inch pizzas for a party even if there was an extra charge for deliveries to NJ!
I tried taking the leftover pizza in my car once and the box wouldn't even fit in my car!!
I'm surprised there aren't more great reviews, love this place and will continue to order!!!

Sadly a one star for the company's human values. I have come to this icon spot of New Orleans every time I have visited New Orleans. Sadly today aug 4, 2020, because of COVID, Hurricane Laura, etc. I got the answer " we are not responsible for your needs" when I requested a restroom. C'est la vie, I don't complain. However I am sad for their values down the drain don't expect me to come back for anything else besides first time experiences.

Came here for the free WiFi... Stayed for Happy Hour

$3 domestics/$4 imports

It's an alright spot. People are cool, talkative, friendly... who wrote the bartender handbook with rule #1 must be a dick?  This place didn't read that book.

They have a small beer selection; shock, widmer, bud, stella, ranger and firestone.  Wings are $5 at happy hour but they're small and not very "meaty".

Prob be back for the internet and brew.

I have no idea that Penang is Malaysian and Cambodian?!

I love to eat at Penang because they have my favorite food: Chow Kueh Teow a.k.a Kwetiau goreng.
What I like from penang is the quality of food are never change, no matter how busy they are during weekend or dinner time!

The only small thing bothers me is the food is greasy when you order take out!

This place gives me the best bohemian vibe straight out of the movie RENT. There's mix match chair, couches with quilts and throws on there. There're board games for groups and books for single. I felt like I walk right into my hippie best friend's home. Now the food was even better! I got the quesadilla with the blue corn chips. Did I mention mostly everything is vegan!!!!! This is a place where after you finish eating, you don't feel in a rush to leave. I really wish I could give this vibey divey a 10

It was nice to see the riverbank and hear about the history but it was super hot and the kids would have been just as hoot without the tour. The staff was very nice and friendly. Get a seat in the shade it helps
Very good food.  Great salsa and chips and staff is very accommodating!  Good margaritas.

Phrank on the third floor is the guy you need to go see! Restaurant had phenomenal seafood and great drinks!!! But Phrank was the best bartender/server we have had ever. Go see him and go to this restaurant!!

Love the food, love the atmosphere, and love the staff!!!! Great place!!! Their Short Rib Tacos are Fire  And Madi, behind the bar, does a great job with the drinks. I highly recommend you stop in and try it, you have fun for sure!!!

Pros: very good drinks and food (Hummus was the best I tasted in the US, surprisingly), friendly service and hip decor. Also, prices were very reasonable.

Cons: at least on a Tuesday evening, it was virtually empty. We got all of our plates at once within 5 minutes of ordering - not exactly the right way to keep a 2-3 hour night out going. I assume it's better on weekends though
Food and Service is outstanding! Been here multiple times over the past year and it is ALWAYS consistently great. Best Asian food in the area!

I went to Pudge's because one of my fellow Yelpers had check-in there. I was curious and the steak sandwiches looked great! So as soon as I found the time me and my husband were off to check it out. 
The young lady at the counter took our order. We decided on a large cheese steak hoagie and a large pizza steak and a order of Pudge fries.  Everything came out within 15 minutes. 
I wanted to eat some of the fries in the car (while they were hot). They were delicious! Real potatoes cut thin and fried crispy and seasoned just right. With a side of creamy dressing to dip them in. Next time I go, will definitely be getting them again!
The sandwiches were Huge!  The rolls, nice and fresh. Lots of tender steak! 
I would definitely recommend Pudge's to all of my steak sandwiches loving friends.  
The only thing I would advise is whatever extra you want on your sandwich,  you need to tell them, like Mayo, Onions,  cheese etc. If it doesn't say it on the description they do not put it on your sandwich nor do they ask.  This is no fault of theirs,  but a oversight of mine. 
When I got home I put Mayo, ketchup etc. on my sandwich and it was great.
I will be back to try more great sandwiches in the future!
Absolute best steaks in STL and super affordable! I make sure to go here at least once a month!

Just wanted to let you know what happened at your location in Sparks, NV on E. Prater Way and Sparks Blvd. last Thursday 7-9-2020 about 5pm ish.  I stopped to get fries and burgers because you're just down the street from me.  When I got home I dumped what was supposed to be french fries on a plate.  What came out was some fries, some of your waffle cut potatoes, some I don't know what and a piece of I'm not sure that had a bite taken out of it, you could see teeth marks!!!  Gross ans disgusting.  

I would give this minus stars if I could!

Also your french fries taste terrible.  If you blindfolded me and put several brands of fries out for me to taste I could pick your fries out every time.  They have a very unpleasant taste.  No matter how much time between visits, they have a funny taste.

If I hadn't been tired I would have got back but I waited till the next day.  I had the garbage in a zip lock bag.  I went in about 11am the next day and asked for the manager, a somewhat unkempt guy walked out and said he was the manager, I explained what happened, he didn't seem to concerned, and showed him the baggie.  He looked at it and basically dismissed it with the comment 'so' and wanted to know what I wanted him to do about it.

I asked him what he would do if he received that for his order, he didn't really seem concerned.  I asked if he really thought that was acceptable, well he guessed not, did I want another order.  I said no not hardly, well what did I want, did I want my money back?  I said actually yes I did. so he refunded the price of the fries.  And said is that all.  No apology no I'll talk to the employees, no nothing.  You really have a problem with that store.  Most of the employees there are that way, they couldn't care less about anything but their cellphones!  Their attitudes leave a lot to be desired, and I know several people that say the same thing.

We will never go in there again.

After reading all the reviews it's clear the owners do not care at all.  It's very clear the employees and the poor excuse for a day manager doesn't.

I usually go to this place and I like it. But today I ordered rice bowl, chickpea, vindaloo and I asked the lady to put minty cilantro sauce instead she served tomato ketchup. It was a take out order so I noticed it when I got back home. Secondly it had a hair in it too.  I would highly recommend the owner to ensure that the servers dont mess up the orders and also to maintain the food standards.

WOULD NOT RECOMMEND - No Service

Entered the restaurant and there seemed to be confusion among the staff, trying to figure out who will seat us. One of the waiting staff out right stated that they got the last guest so someone else can have them. 

After being finally seated in the middle of the restaurant, we noticed that staff seemed to be aimlessly wandering the establishment not really helping the less than a quarter full restaurant. After about of 10 minutes of sitting at the table with no waiting staff offering us any water, coffee - so we left. 

If you want a nice breakfast experience seek elsewhere.

Service was horrendous. Was seated about 15 minutes after my reservation time (not too big a deal) but then after that my party waited an additional 20 minutes just to have our waiter come introduce himself and take orders for drinks. Food was good- I had the lobster bisque which I would definitely recommend, and one of the men I was with have me a bite of his steak which was delicious. Even though the food was good, it wasn't worth the price, especially since the service was awful.

After attending a Yelp event we got my kids a pizza to go. We purchased a custom pizza with BBQ sauce on wheat crust, with vegan cheese, chicken, spinach, artichokes,  onions and bacon. We also ordered the Caprese Appetizer and an extra cookie. 

The Caprese was the bomb. It is fresh mozzarella, tomato, basil, balsamic glaze, with pizza chips. I would definitely get this appetizer again. The balsamic glaze with sweet red peppers is amazing. My kids feel in love with the chocolate chip cookie. It is soft and chewy with lots of chocolate chunks. 

There is only one size of pizza which is more of the European personal size. At this amazing quick pizza chain you get to choose your crust (Wheat, white, or gluten free), choose your sauce, and choose your protein and vegetables. Toppings are not extra. Keep in mind if you over top your pizza will not cook through. Customer service is amazing!! The cost for the pizza is $8.95. 

Plus they also have a frequent Pie'er program that I recommend you join.

Nice charm to the place.  Can only speak to what we ate. Pickled veggies were good.  Fried green tomatoes were okay but the pimento cheese on top wasn't right.  Bone marrow dish was raw and when we pointed it out to the waiter, he assured us it was cooked correctly.  Pasta with mushrooms was really bland and unappetizing.  Just over cooked brown pasta in a brown sauce with brown mushrooms.  You couldn't cut through the mushrooms they were so rubbery.  Meatloaf was decent, but not special.  Plus it was served on mashed potatoes and then they put roasted fingerling potatoes on the side.  Just an odd choice.  Daughter's cheese pizza had huge chunks of tomatoes that were so sweet they tasted candied.  Inedible.  Happy hour drinks were overpriced. $100 bill for three people and then had to eat sandwiches at home afterwards.  I know we should have said something.  If it is one or two things that just aren't quite right, but the place has promise, we give them a shot to fix it.  But when we can tell the chef/kitchen is just in over their heads with the ingredients and most of the meal is a mess, best just to quietly pay the bill and scratch it off our list of future dinner options.

This restaurant was the best unlimited meat Korean BBQ in St. Louis!!!!!

Open kitchen, bright inside, and very clean!  All the food was delicious and service was great too! 

I'm Korean and I will highly recommend to anyone that loves Korean BBQ.

Crab legs are all the rage these days and as a connoisseur of sorts I have to say Hot N Crazy crab is my favorite that I've had in Tampa. They are well priced the seasoning is well balanced and not overly salty like a lot of places. They also have a great lunch special. They have great customer service and a clean inviting atmosphere.

We came here based off many suggestions from locals. Let's just say they did not disappoint! We went for taco Tuesday which makes all the tacos $2. We got the fried oyster, duck, the Carolina, and the calypso taco. They were all beyond delicious. Our server Daisy was welcoming and informative as well. I suggest stopping here if you can. It's well worth it. Out side seating  was nice and shaded too!

Incredible dinner! Outstanding service! The Chana masala was rich and flavorful. The coconut curry was like candy
The naan was cooked to perfection.
This is not your standard greasy Indian buffet...high quality
I'll be back

I think they have closed down. Sole friends and Friends and I had arranged to meet for happy hour but when we arrived the doors were locked and all the patio furniture was gone. We checked their hours and their Facebook page and both indicated that they should be open. Called the phone number and it went to a full mailbox. Yikes! Not a good sign

2 starts are for customer service. Everyone was very friendly. Lack of starts for the meal. A large sub & a drink for $17 is a pretty penny to pay for the small amount of food. Ordered the artichoke & paid extra to add mushrooms. Disappointed in the portion of the sub to begin with but then when I realized the main ingredient on it was gobs of Mayo with a few artichokes & covered in cheese I was throughly disappointed overall. I would not recommend this meal. Maybe they have other options that are more bang for your buck or at least a decent portion. Sorry guys, this is a no for me.

I had dinner here, which was definitely solid. The menu is pretty innovative, and although the food was not the best I've had, it certainly was tasty.

- Tuna tartare - I'm a sucker for ahi tuna, and the avocado, hint of spice, and the chips were quite good.
- Truffled beef tartare - I'm also a sucker for truffle. Truffle on anything is good to me, but the parmesan was great.
- Bleu mango salad - The sweetness of the mango went well with the fresh vegetables, and the crunch of the cashew. This dish was a bit on the sweet side though.
- Truffle mac and cheese - See above. But serious, this dish rocked.
- Pan seared jumbo sea scallops - My scallops were perfectly done, and the bacon cheese grits were delicious. Oh, and add a decadent lobster sauce on it? Yum.

Yes. So I guess you now know my weakness for truffle. But seriously, try it out. I didn't have brunch here although I think I will, nor did I party here either... but it seems like a fun space (did have a flight of port though...)

Came in to grab a salad for dinner. Was in a hurry to get back to work. Slowest service I have ever had at a StL Bread Co. They were completely disorganized behind the counter putting orders together. Bumping into one another, couldn't seem to pull it together. The kid at the counter was particularly rude as well. I waited 30 min for a carry out salad! For such a nice area and great location, I can't believe they haven't staffed this location better.
the worst possible place to eat in Oldsmar. It is so dirty and the food is disgusting. I wasn't expecting a gourmet burger but at least something I could eat. Yuck!

Decided to join a friend for a late bite to eat..930pm..sat at the bar...and it was not busy at all, however waited for bartender to inquire if we wanted to order anything, rather than ask she chose to socialize with a a group at the opposite end of the bar and busy herself with stocking glasses etc..so I then asked another server who just happen to walk by from the dinning side..what time do you close, her response was we close at midnight..finally the bartender comes over to help the server, I said excuse me , may we order a couple of appetizers, her reply..sure just a minute, as I thought Iv been sitting here for 15 min with no acknowledgment at all, I could see if the bar was busy, but there was nothing going on. So my friend and I just sat there, I should have followed my first mind and just left and went else where..but decided to see if the service would get better...NO!!! it was worse, so as we waited and the bar back cleaned and restocked the bar..he then decided to set 5 dirty glasses next to my friends drink clearly in our area where we would be eating. I apologized to my friend and said Iv eaten here a few times and I have never had such crapy service. So I asked the bartender for a refill on my drink, she says ok..she continues to busy herself with the other group at the end of the bar needless to say the refill was on the back burner..so to top it off, two ladies from the smaller group walk over , one puts her  hand on my friends shoulder and asked if I was her date, and she wanted to compliment my date on how beautiful she was, and then said please don't think im weird, I work here.....really ! I thought wow!! then she asked could she get us anything ??My friend then says how about a refill on the drink...then she looks at the bartender and she says she is taking care of us, I thought umm no your not...we were made to feel as though we were an inconvenience for her and never did she ever ask or check on us for what we wanted , we had to stop her every time for drinks, to place our order, and to ask for refills...by then I gave up and cancelled the order , as my friend asked for manger and express the dissatisfaction and poor service. As my friend spoke to the manager, the bartender then looks at my friend and I and says well I can just give you your food order to take with you and cancel it so you dont have to be charged...I responded by saying no thank you..as if that was suppose to make it ok..I didn't want the food, drinks, etc ..with that type of service and behavior, I will make sure that Black Finn is on my not list of places to grab a bite to eat.

After flying from one coast to another coast, my friends and I were so hungry and we were looking for a place to grab a bite to eat. The only thing opened that time (close to midnight) was Midtown III. Hmmm...don't want anything heavy....so I ended up sharing a turkey club with chips with one of the friends. This place is okay: definitely, more like a diner style. It reminds of like a Dennys...there's a cocktail lounge/bar in the back, so if you ever feel like drinking, head to the back to have a drink at the bar.

The food at this restaurant is superb!  My favorite dish is Chupe de Camarones, but everything else that we've tried has always been delicious.  And for a before dinner cocktail, try the pisco sours.

The ambience is somewhat brittle and off-putting, but the food more than makes up for it.  Try it today!

I'm liking this place less and less.  
Service wasn't as good today, there were many more people than at previous meals.
Also, the food overall while good, we didn't feel was as high quality.
The only one we really liked was the seafood dukbokki.

Wow! I didn't expect it to be so big!  They have a nice deck for spectating, listening to music, having some drinks and eating hot food.  If I remember correctly there are about 16 courts and each row signifies skill level. 
I'm always looking for an alternative to exercising at the gym so I'm glad my friend invited me out to see his league in action. I can't wait to sign up for the spring league!
They are located next to the Ponchartrain Center-you cant miss it. 
I parked in the first lot a saw but there are huge parking lots on both sides.
 Don't be a fool like me and think that there was going to be a paved area once you enter-its ALL SAND so wear sand appropriate shoes:)

First time here - their ribs were smoked perfectly, the pulled pork was perfect, but the cut of brisket was below standard. The sides were okay. It's a good place to bring young kids; a very casual atmosphere.   Don't expect anything more than the basics.

I have been to ramen places all across the country and this one ranks up there when it comes to ambiance and flavor. The space is nice and bright and there is plenty of space for large groups. Only thing I wish it had was a broader variety of menu options when it came to appetizers and dessert.

Lives up to the reputation! Came here wanting to try famous New Orleans oysters and wanted to avoid Acme crowds. Yelp and tour guide approved.

LOVED the char-grilled oysters, flavorful and fresh. Was worried "butter breadcrumb" combo would make it too greasy but they were not overwhelming at all. Could not believe how good the red beans and rice were-- actual mystery. Thought it'd be the weakest link in the "bayou platter" trio of jambalaya and etouffee, but was our favorite. 
Etouffee was like a cheesier creamier jambalaya And a bit bland, but much better after Tabasco and lemon. Jambalaya is much fresher than expected.
First time having hush puppies. SO GOOD. (Fried cornballs with jalapeños for the other non southerners)

Fat juicy raw oysters yummy too but that is less particularly special if you're used to good oysters. 
Skip the po boy-- got a oyster and shrimp one bc didn't want fried seafood with fries. but really forgettable-- probably not fault of the restaurant and more about the concept. Get more oysters instead, cheaper and way better!
Great little vegetarian restaurant tucked away in Huntingdon Valley. Hummus, tehini, falafel, salads, soups, and smoothies. They are gluten free. Also they do catering.

Incredible food. I moved from Oakland, California several years ago and never thought I'd find another vietnamese restaurant that matched the quality of the one I used to frequent out there..then I discovered House Of Pho. Beautiful ambience and decor inside as well and our waitress was very helpful. I have to try more on the menu, but their beef noodle pho soup and grilled pork are absolutely out of this world. I've been to several vietnamese restaurants in the area and this one is my favorite. A bit expensive for the grilled pork plate but still highly recommended.

It's been awhile since I went to a Cracker Barrel 
I love breakfast but they are always packed
But not for dinner and covid 
So I went for

Fried catfish
Hush puppies
Corn bread
Mac and cheeses
Greens
Berry tea

All were awesome 
Really hit the spot 

Friendly people 
Not busy

I was so excited to visit this place when it first opened.  Since it has I have been there several times but I agree with previous reviewers that it leaves much to be desired and my experiences have always just been meh.  While out celebrating we stopped in here last year and decided to splurge on a bottle of Veuve.  On top of not knowing what it was the server didn't know how to serve it (including setting our glasses on the floor :S ).  We left shortly after.  But since then I have returned for other celebrations and fundraisers and still leave with a blah taste in my mouth.  The dj's are never quite as good as we hoped and just overall service is not great.  I can't say I won't be back but it is far from my first choice downtown especially with all the new great places around.

2013/024

Whenever I eat out solo, I always ask for the check as soon as I get the food. I also ask for my dessert to be served at the same time as the main meal. I personally just want to be checked on once, and getting everything all at once cuts down on the servers having to deal with me. :D

The servers at Cinco de Mayo were extremely fast and got me my check and dessert at the same time I got my order of 4 taquitos. They still asked me mid-bite how my meal was, but I expected that. 

The taquitos were okay. They weren't overly seasoned. I added the salsa from the complimentary chips to flavor it some. And I should have read the menu better -- I always assume that plate lunches would include rice. This had neither beans nor rice. But I was okay with that, since I eat rice every day. And I hate beans.

The salsa wasn't hot, but I appreciate the flecks of fresh cilantro. I did enjoy the cheese served with the taquitos. I don't know if it was Oaxacan style cheese, or just your typical mozzarella. 

The flan was delicious, especially since it came drizzled with chocolate sauce and came with a maraschino cherry.

Sadly, my go-to drink of horchata is not offered here.

Lots of seating -- booths and tables.

I have attempted to eat here multiple times; and was disappointed each and every one of them. The number one thing that really upset me was the utter  disrespect from almost all their waitstaff. The hostess was rude, telling my elderly father after asking her if we could wait for an outdoor table to "wait until those people outside are done then you'll get a seat obviously". That was our final straw, no more blind pelican for us! The only thing that kept us coming back was the scenery.

We went to see the improv group. Our first time there. Very casual and comfortable atmosphere. Limited menu. I enjoyed my Cesar chicken salad and my husband enjoyed his apple turnover / ice cream dessert. The group was OK. We had a few laughs. I would go back but would try one of the many other restaurants on Bridge Street instead of eating there.

I bought the iced caramel cream not expecting too much, but boy, it was probably one of the best iced drinks I've ever had. My only complaint is the paper straw which falls apart after like 3 big sips! Definitely better than Starbucks' Caramel Frappuccino. The ambiance of the shop is quite nice and feels so quaint. The music really matched the atmosphere and I like how the doors were propped open to give the shop a more airy feel. I did some reading here and it was quiet enough to focus, but not too quiet which is good. I like the ambient noise. A minor qualm I have is the lighting in one part of the cafe where the fans are running under so the brightness of the light alternates and it's a little distracting when trying to read. But overall a good experience here!
This pizza does WONDERS for your colonic health.  Enough said.

The location for the restaurant is really great. Right off of Kelly Drive, with a view of the river. It was much too hot this past Friday, so we opted to sit inside. The decor is just all over the place. There was a wall clock and a fan that were not plugged in...not sure what the deal was there. It really had no theme. Exposed ceiling, industrial, but not Italian at all. The music they were playing was ODD. Someone apparently likes Blink 182, because that was all that was on when we went there.I had looked online to preview the menu and beers. When I arrived, the menu in person was different. No biggie, but I had already scoped out which beers I wanted. The server was VERY nice and by far was the highlight. We ordered the two cheese and two meat plate. This was a great choice, except the chef left the PLASTIC wrapping on the spreadable cheese. Luckily we saw it before we ate it! Next was the Blue crab bruschetta. This came in a mason jar along with 4 pieces of bread. For 15.00, it was just an obnoxious price, because there was little to no crab...just filled with peppers and oil. Big ouch on that. We also ordered the Margherita pizza. This place prides itself on fresh tomatoes, yet the pizza came out sitting on top of a large opened can of tomatoes. Yes, yes...i know that it could be for ambiance, but it gave mixed signals. The pizza was not to my personal liking. The underside was charred, the top was chewy and not done. The sauce was also VERY sugary. Since neither of us ate it, the server inquired, so I was kind, but honest. It simply was not made to my liking. She offered another entree, but at this point, most of the menu is pizza and I simply did not want another poorly made one. We then had the Whoopee pie and an espresso for dessert, these were decent. I honestly thought that they would have comped the dessert, but they didnt and I am not mad about that. I had the option to replace the entree and declined. Caveat emptor! More on the bad: The parking lot is a tight hot mess, the fruit flies buzzing around the drinks and beers were annoying, seeing one of the cooks eating a slice of cheese while making a pizza was downright gross, and the above meal was almost 100.00. This was in NO WAY a meal or restaurant worth that price tag. If you go, avoid the parking lot, better yet, just avoid the place altogether.

Ordered stromboli's here three times, three separate times and disgusted to say that EACH one had hair in it. Called to talk to anyone about it and there was no one who would assist me. Loved their food otherwise else, just disappointed in the quality.

That secret sauce is what makes this place specials. 

I always get the combo because I want a little bit of everything. Combos come w wings, fried rice, salad, and a drink. Wings are pretty good, lots of different flavors. Fried rice w extra secret sauce is my favorite. The salad is your typical salad you get at an Asian restrauant. 

Extra cost for extra sauce! 

Staff is super friendly, fast service, small place but there's always been seating available (in and out).

I've eaten here multiple times and each time it is delicious! The food tastes very fresh, and if you like spicy then this is the place to go. The service is great, everyone here is so friendly. I definitely will keep coming!

I have not been very happy with the yogurt here. The yogurt itself does not seem to have a lot of flavor.  There are two sizes of cup, both much larger than I want.  And perhaps my expectations are wrong, but it seems awfully expensive for what you get, about $0.50 per ounce. 

I have been here twice, but I'm not planning to come back.
Had the spicy chicken panini with a kale pineapple smoothie, YUMMY. Place is clean and they are quick

Hit or miss- sometimes good, often pretty poor. All too often they don't have the staff there, or just walking in late. I wouldn't suggest anything that should be fresh, seems like most of the dinners come out of the freezer. Get a hard liquor on the rocks and you'll be buying two for the size. Great place to sit outside during the summer and have some beers and appetizers but not a good dinner.

Always a great place to get pizza! 

Idaho pizza co was the first pizza establishment my husband and I tried when we first moved here. We have never been disappointed by their quality of food. We always seem to lean towards their specialty pizzas and they are all very good. I very much so enjoy their wide variety for salad bar options as well. 

I will say however, for this particular establishment, be prepared for a few things when ordering take out (which I primarily do). If you are ordering delivery and it is around the "dinner time rush" expect there to be about an hour and a half wait for it to be delivered... at first this was a major disappointment to me... until you go to pick up your pizza. 

The staff is constantly working their tails off! The last time I visited this particular Idaho pizza, I didn't want to wait for the delivery.. so I thought I wouldn't be lazy and I would just pick it up. I'm so glad I did, it opened my eyes with how hard the staff is working to provide everyone their food on time and as quickly as they possibly can. 

If you're in the area and want to try this location. Just don't be discouraged. Your food might take a little longer than expected, however, the staff is doing their absolute beat.
Yum! This sushi house is always fresh, lively and doesn't disappoint. Food is fantastic and the owners warm and welcoming.
Wow! Awesome food. Awesome margaritas. Fresh ingredients. Reasonable prices. Come on Tuesday's if you like $10 pitchers that you get a solid 5 drinks out of. Wow!

I have always loved Chava's. It's one of my favorite Mexican Food places. I have literally had almost everything on the menu at least once....but a couple of things stands out as my favorites. The fried fish tacos, the chicken chimichangas, steak nachos, the wings and they have THE BEST chips and salsa!! 

I had to check them out during this whole curbside pickup life...to see if the experience was going to be the same...well as far as the food...since I could go in!! I was absolutely impressed!!! The pickup area was super clean and sanitary and the food tasted exactly how it did in the restaurant (huge plus)!!!

They have officially retained me as a customer!!

The food really is about as good as I've tasted in Louisiana, and there is a decent selection on the menu.  They let you pick how you want your fish prepared, and it doesn't matter which one you pick because it's all amazing.  Make sure you wear a jacket if your a guy, and get there early to get seated.  If I had to come up with a complaint; they wouldn't make a mint julep for me.

Second time eating at 5th and Taylor. Both times I have left thinking this little hipster want to be restaurant is so over rated. No matter what don't order steak! I've never seen my husband leave behind meat. The service is subpar for the level of restaurant it portrays to be. Nonetheless, the food is not worth $$$

It was a happy day when Martin's finally reopened Uptown after Katrina!  We love going there for lunch - not the cheapest place, but the food is good and the service is excellent.  I know nothing about wine, but when I am entertaining I know I can go in there, tell them what I am serving, and have them select something that my guests rave about.  Makes me look as though I DO know something about it!

I find this place absolutely delicious. My most memorable dish was the scallops, which I got all to myself as I dined with two vegetarians. The tapas style lends itself to experiencing twenty-plus different tastes in one meal. You probably will not be full by the end of your dinner, though, unless you show up with a fat wallet. Be prepared to pay at least $10 a glass for the cheapest wine, as it all seems to be imported from Spain. I'd recommend making reservations early in the week because this place is packed nightly. I'll definitely head back with some meat eaters when I get the chance.

Little known secret is there are happy hour specials after 10pm Sunday through Thursday. $3 beer, $4 sangria, $5 wines and $2 tapas bites. This might be the best way to explore such a fantastic restaurant if you're on a budget.

Big flavors come on small plates.  The bacon wrapped dates were ones I would absolutely take out on a date again. the roasted red peppers stuffed with crabmeat were packed with flavorful love.  Beautiful colors and presentation as well.  Sit at the bar overlooking the kitchen, and watch the magic unfold.

This place has a classy and relaxed vibe.  It reaks of sexy, clean, fun.  Gotta go, they just brought dessert!

Always enjoy this place.  Great draft selection, fair priced wines by the glass, and a " different" menu that will inspire you to think a little before ordering. Good food, great location for theatres.

This place was horrible. They completely messed up my order and then refused to give me my money back. They told me the next day that they would take care of my order but then refused to honor their agreement because the employee that promised to correct the order was not at work that day. I would never do business with these people plus the food was not good. The spinach and feta cheese with dough was burnt. The man on the phone was completely rude and agressive.
Despite the high prices, we ordered take out spinach salad with chicken. Got a measly amount of chicken. Next morning, we both had diarrhea. Not going back.

With Valentine's Day approaching I called a couple of guy friends to see if they might be interested in taking our ladies out for a special dinner on the Saturday prior.  My friend Steve agreed to join my wife and me so I asked him for a dining suggestion.  He mentioned that he had not been to Marsha Brown's in quite some time so I phoned to secure reservations.  They must have some great software reservation system because I received an email confirming our reservations almost immediately which included two follow-up reminder emails and an additional reminder call!  I have also noticed that I am now on their email list notifying me of special dining events. 
 
I had dined at this establishment many years ago.  All that I had remember that it was an old church that had been converted to a restaurant.  Looking at the menu online I could see that they specialized in Cajun stile cooking and steaks.  I also to a gander at the reviews on Yelp and seen that recent dining reviews had been favorable. 
 
Knowing that parking is terrible in New Hope I was happy to see that they offered valet parking for $10.  Walking in we were promptly seated and handed menus by our server.  We started with a round of cocktails while we looked over the menu and the specials for the evening.  The cocktails arrived promptly which was good for I needed a drink.  After all it was Saturday night!  Our waiter gave us a few minutes to decide upon appetizers.  We started with oysters and a slab of bacon (must be a Cajun thing). 
 
With one drink down I reviewed the room.  Since it was once a church the room is very cavernous and loud.  Up in front is a rather large wall painting indicating that it was no Catholic church.  Everyone seemed to be enjoying themselves dressing up for their dates.  After all I sure a lot of the patrons were like us celebrating Valentine's Day. 
 
Since this was a Cajun restaurant I decided to go with the Jambalaya. With a few glasses of wine and some good conversation I really did not notice what everyone else ordered for their entrees.  Upon finishing our meal the waiter appeared and inquired about our meal.  As it turns out Steve's wife had ordered the special Beef Wellington.  As it turns out the pastry coating was undercooked (doughy) and the beef was raw with an ice cold center.  She explained that she was trying to work her way through it but could not.  Our waiter was very apologetic and offered to send it back.  Losing her taste for the meal she no longer wanted it.  And besides everyone else had finished so our waiter had taken her meal off the bill.  After sharing a couple of deserts and coffee our waiter returned with the bill and reminded us that the Beef Wellington was taken off the bill and the deserts were also on him.  So in our book he did us right!

Amazing food! I came in on a whim, and I am so glad I did! I ordered off of the lunch menu. I came in with my mom so we were able to try almost everything on the lunch menu between the two of us. The portions for the lunch menu are perfect for you to try a little bit of anything and still have some left over! The server was perfect. She was attentive but not hovering, and was very friendly. It's a nice atmosphere

Never disappointed by the service and quality of the food at this Saladworks! Everyone here is so friendly and helpful, it's really appreciated!! I really have no clue how they have anything less than 5 stars, you guys rock!!

Staff is nice and that's why they got three stars. Prices went up too much. The chicken isn't even that meaty. God knows I love the spices and red beans and rice. Abhorred by the prices -I got the popcorn shrimp. $2 gets you 75 cents worth of shrimp. Happy they threw in a biscuit.

*Restaurant Week Review only*

Cash only BYOB in the heart of Rittenhouse.

Ambiance: Small, cute hip and noisy. The noise level is actually quite high -- you have to talk very loudly for your party to be able to hear you - I was straining to hear my boyfriend across the table and vice versa. 

Service - 3/5: Service was a little slow at times with initially receiving our menus, and then in finishing up dessert and waiting for the check. I know it was busy, and he did seem to be one of the only ones waiting on tables, but walked by our table 4 times before I had to stop and ask him for the check.. and i try not to be that person. 

Food 3/ 3.5 out of 5
This was a little hit or miss for me. The seared haloumi was good, and enjoyed pairing the savory  cheese with the sweetness of the candied dates and fig compote. His arugula goat cheese salad was pretty good, but nothing mind blowing and just a tad over dressed , just an opinion. As for the entree, I ordered the pappardelle pasta because I'm in love with good homemade pasta but it was a bit underwhelming. The texture of the pasta was great, but it was not flavorful. I don't know if it's just me but I do like salted pasta water or a little flavor. So I tried pairing it with a bite of mushrooms, arugula and sunflower seed to try it all as one single bite which was much better, but still just a tad bit.. bland :( I feel terrible saying that, but my honest opinion. My boyfriend ordered the seared ahi tuna, which was great. Really really great. It was one of the best seared tunas I've seen, barely seared on the outside and nice fresh tuna raw on the inside. The truffle emulsion was amazing, something I'd never think to pair with tuna and it really worked. Lastly the dessert was a sampling of a bunch of different desserts-- I was kind of surprised they didn't ask for preferences, allergies or anything -- but anyway we had a cinnamon apple rice pudding, chocolate cake and some sort of panna cotta. Overall all of them were just okay, nothing standing out.

Overall I left a bit unimpressed, but loved the ahi tuna.
Great selection of fries and sauces.  I love fries and this place was heaven.  Definitely like the bison burger, it had a cleaner, leaner taste.

Finally got the chance to try out Tony's, I've been passing it for months and always hoped to! The restaurant itself is gorgeous, with ceilings that are designed to carry music throughout. The night I dined in, there was a fantastic slow jazz band which was a perfect background for a perfect dinner. 

We are oyster fiends, so we started with Blue points and their complimentary house bread. The blue points were lovely and fresh - my only complaint was the lack of house mignonette (just cocktail sauce and horseradish). The bread was fantastic and fluffy! 

We bought a bottle of wine to share, our server was clearly still learning the ropes but he did well in checking on us regularly. He did fumble the specials but it wasn't a huge deal. For entrees we ordered a New York strip steak and the Chilean sea bass. The steak was definitely the star but both were wonderful. One downside of the night was that the restaurant was out of nearly everything. We each wanted different entrees initially but they were out of them. Because we know there are supply chain issues currently, we didn't see this as too big an issue. 

Overall it's a lovely restaurant for a date night or intimate celebration. Thanks for a great night, Tony's staff!

Wayside is a hidden gem and I'm so glad i discovered it. Their cheese steaks and breakfast is perfect, never been disappointed with anything from here and everyone I've introduced to wayside also loves it. I definitely recommend them

Had breakfast here. The hubby got a great shrimp and andouille omelet with cheese and potatoes that he loved. I got simple eggs and bacon and was able to sub out hash browns/biscuit for a great fruit bowl. Easy to have a gluten free breakfast and if you're dairy free you can work it out

I have been eating here since I was able to drive. I use to sneak out at night and drive 45 mins just for this place. The food is to die for. Chicken strips and fries. Gyros you name it. One kind tip, do not go here on the weekends at 3 or later. This place gets a seriously packed crowd. I mean packed. People park across the street to eat here when the clubs let out and the cops are usually there with their lights on driving around making sure fights don't break out.

The deep dish square pizzas are the BOMB!!! I use to live in Michigan 10 years ago and use to get this pizza on a regular basis. Now they have opened a few Jets locations in Indiana I feel right at home.

The food was... hell I can't even recall what I ordered. It was that unimpressive. Oh I now remember that I had shrimp and pasta with a crab cake.  I could have just had the crab cake. Certainly not the best crab cake I've ever eaten but it wasn't bad.

Closed Down! I am highly disappointed that I  joined their waitlist online and drove all the way to the location to find out they are closed down. Their status online says "Open". I'm not sure if they are re-opening at some point... but a nearby business told me that they close down two weeks ago.

The pizza was better than average, but didn't blow me away either. My real beef with Empire is their delivery procedure to hotels. 

I stayed at the Hyatt Regency, a 900+ room hotel a short drive from Empire. Being a lazy traveler for the night sounded great, and pizza was ordered. The disappointment lies in the fact that rather than bring the pizza to your room, they call you ahead of time and have you meet them in the lobby. If I wanted to put on respectable pants and shoes I would've gone out to eat. Then, of course, despite my commute to the elevator (literally 100+ steps) and the ensuing 9-story descent I still beat the driver to the meet-up spot by a few minutes. In an effort to avoid any opportunity to be a provider of great service, our driver didn't even offer napkins (or paper plates), which I'd say is fairly standard when delivering to people that are at a hotel.

In hindsight, I should've just gone out to Pi Pizzeria.

The Saints and Sinners walking tour was one of 3 I took during my short trip to NOLA, and it just so happened to be my favorite.

At $30 for 4 people with a Groupon, I know you get what you pay for, and I wasn't expecting much. But the tour was much funnier and more informative than I had imagined!

Our tour guide, Justin, was enthusiastic and witty. He spoke loudly, clearly and was very animated while telling us stories and facts about the past. Great job, Justin!

The tour starts at the Voodoo House and ends in Jackson square. You get a good look-see of much of the French Quarter. There's also a much appreciated pee/drink break halfway through the trip.

Absolutely worth it! Just remember to bring cash to tip at the end. (My friends and I forgot about this and only had $10 between us. Justin, if you're reading this, we love you and you're worth $183,929. But we only had a ten. We're sorry. Please forgive us.)

Very awesome tour! A definite must if you're in NOLA and looking for something interesting to do.

Had an amazing time eating at Joyland. It's adorable and everything I could hope for after months of drooling over their Instagram posts. Perfect food to make your stomach happy, your taste buds smile and leave with the same grin on your face. 

Staff was as friendly as the name would imply and the music selection inside is worth noting for being nothing less than amazing. We sat indoors but outdoor seating was just as cute and inviting! Will be back if ever in Nashville again :)

IF YOU WANT THE BEST BURRITO/ BREAKFAST BURRITO/ TACOS ETC YOU HAVE EVER HAD IN YOUR ENTIRE LIFE AND WILL EVER HAVE IT IS MANDATORY THAT YOU VISIT HONEST TOMS. 
Sorry for internet yelling but it was necessary. 

I have been coming here since it opened and I will continue to come here even if I move away. I live in fishtown now and make the short trek there often. I have even biked from the gayborhood to Honest Toms. 

Anyone who thinks this place is just OK must have had their taste buds shaved off of their tongue at birth.

My husband and I love the Gyro here. It's super flavorful and delicious and the gyro sandwich is stuffed full of meat and toppings. I really like how fresh all their ingredients are, and the owner and all the staff have always been very kind. This is definitely our go-to spot for a quick and tasty Gyro meal!

We had a phenomenal brunch here--I'd recommend the bloody marys, the Tennessee sipping cream and the shrimp and grits. They had a live music trio, and great service--the managers came by to check on us and chat. I'd love to go back.

Let me start by saying, this review has nothing to do with the bar side of the business. Sole exception being staff of course who are friendly, polite, and attentive.

As far as food goes though, Lucky's by far has the best burgers I've ever eaten. I couldn't tell you what they're doing differently here, but their beef has so much flavor packed into it that it's unreal.  I've been to the Manayunk lucky's a few times now, and had them at the annual Philadelphia burger brawl a few times too. Every burger, every time, has been exceptional.

Suffice to say i'm a big fan, my most recent trip to lucky's had me eating a breakfast burger, removing the bun, and just chowing down. The fried egg was fantastic, nicely seasoned with a bit of pepper kick to it, and as aforementioned- the beef was heavenly as always.

Drinks are relatively affordable, and the upstairs atmosphere is extremely chill, i can't think of a better place to wind down a night, There's something magical about the upstairs here.  Something amidst the dim edison lights just connects with me, lucky's feels like home.

There are few places that i swear by, and lucky's is certainly one of them.

Flavor & Presentation 5/5   |   Speed & Service 4.66/5   |   Pricing & Portions  4.5/5

Overall  4.75 / 5

We're greeted at the door and seated ourselves on the patio. After twenty minutes had still not been seen by a waiter. They walked past us many time and just ignored us. Finally gave up and left. Have been here plenty in the past but are now very disappointed.

JRP is a legendary establishment. I have been coming here religiously for the last 15 yrs! I am a bit of a chessesteak snob and Johns is one of 3 spots in the city where I will order a cheesesteak (its also my fav!). I'll only order a cheesesteak when John himself is workin the grill. The man has the magic touch and he has more pride in making a cheesesteak than anyone else in Philly period! Its seriously not the same sandwich if someone else is making it- John is a master! 

If Im not ordering a cheesesteak, than I usually getting a Roast Pork or Beef or a Chicken Cutlet Parm (w/ extra gravy). JRP is truly a quintessential Philly sandwich spot for the people! For me, it doesnt get much better than housing one of their sandwiches while sitting outside on a nice day!

Oh man. We ended up here because it was one of the only places still open at 9:30p near our hotel. I'd had myself all prepared for Mexican (margaritas and tacos are just sometimes what a girl needs), but that place ended up being closed. A sports bar would not normally be my second choice, but at this point we were desperate.

Our party of 7 sat ourselves at a high top. And things went downhill from there...

I thought for sure it was going to be a tough one when our waitress had trouble taking our order. She did not bring us menus. She had no idea what beers were on tap. She actually brought one of us over to the POS for help figuring out what the choices were and inputting the drink orders! She apologized so many times, saying it was only her third day working there. Why are you working the evening shift alone if it's only your third day?? Grrr...

But that was the worst of it. Once we obtained menus and put in all the orders everything went fine. We told her up front that it was going to be separate checks, which I'm sure helped her a lot. She should have thought to ask that herself, but NBD. When the drinks and food and checks came, everything was accurate and we had no problem settling up.

The food was good not great. Everything was decent except for the boiled egg on my salad (see photo). Bleh. The rest of the salad was unimaginative but edible. (Remember how exhausted and desperate we are by this point in the evening.) Other people's meals came with fries; I tried a few and they were pretty good.

All in all, I think this is a typical local watering hole. You don't come here for fancy food or expensive cocktails; you come here to have a beer with your bros. It did that job well enough.

Along with the rest of the reviews, I have never seen such horrible food. The food had no hint of authenticity & the owner was didn't even acknowledged it. I don't even think they deserve that 1 Star. I think the only reason they are getting any business is due to lack of Indian restaurant around the area. I'll give this restaurant a hard pass.

CONSUMER BEWARE!!!! RAISED PRICE ON TAKEOUT ORDER FROM GOOGLE ONLINE PRICE AND REFUSED TO ADJUST/HONOR. We ordered from here as we always do and were surprised to see our order was $10 more than the online price. I politely mentioned this to the manager who was ringing me up. He said I must be mistaken and wanted to see how I found the prices I saw. So, instead of just taking my word for it he insisted I take 5 minutes of my time to show him. I showed him the online menu powered by Google and he said it didn't matter because he would only honor the PDF File available on his website. He restated the raised total to me and at this point I had to buy it (screaming young children in the car and a hungry wife). It wasn't so much about the money as it was the principles of good business. The customer is always right. 

As I said before we have ate here several times because the food is slightly better than good. Yes, not great in Thai terms but closer to Chinese take out. (We have had authentic Thai, this is Americanized Thai). However, is one of the better ones on the southside. The last few times we have been there the customer service has been not very pleasant. Greeter was rude and white manager rude as well. 

None the less we will NEVER eat there again or recommend to anyone. If money is not an issue to you and you like condescending staff this is your place. THERE IS A BETTER, MORE PROFESSIONAL, MORE AUTHENTIC, AND CHEAPER THAI RESTAURANT THE NEXT LOT OVER. We will be going there from now on since this is how Thai Spice treats its loyal customers.

If you like a smoke filled bar with a sketchy crowd and terrible food. Go here. The food was all frozen, fried, etc. The live music was good and the beer was cold but overall bad experience. Will not return. There are other options in the area offering the same atmosphere without the smoke.

My boyfriend and I stopped in for lunch on a road trip and we couldn't have picked a better spot to eat! Since we've been vegan I have not found a cheese that I have liked but the v steak here was one of the best things I've eaten, the cheese sauce was perfectly creamy and melted and the flavor was on point and the vegan steak was just right. The staff was super friendly and helpful and we will be stopping back in on our way back

The quintessential brunch spot in Nashville, you'll want to hop on line and wait for Biscuit Love again and again.
Once you get inside order up at the counter and the food comes out lightening fast. 
Why is this place worth the wait? *Lily.* A biscuit French toast with lemon mascarpone & blueberry compote whose bold and delicate flavors mingle with a perfectly crisp and buttery biscuit to create an unforgettable meal.
Or if you're feeling savory, the Princess hot chicken biscuit sandwich scream Music City as well.
They have some of the most tempting options such as gertie - biscuit with chocolate gravy, peanut butter, caramelized banana jam, & pretzel crunch....and hummingbird family reserve - drop biscuits filled with pineapples & banana jam topped with pecans & cream cheese frosting which make me want to have the whole experience next weekend! 

Pro tip: parking in many lots offer your first hour free at the Gulch location

One of the worst sandwiches I've ever had. Ordered the 'chicken supreme' sandwich. When I got back to the office and opened it up I was shocked. The chicken was burnt black. It was cinders. I broke the chicken opened and it was in cinders. I was in my work uniform so I couldn't go back there because I was pissed. I would have lost it. For any deli to give out a product this bad is unfathomable. You will want to avoid this toilet at all cost. This place should get negative stars.

The best Indian restaurant in Santa Barbara. We drive from Santa Maria for the amazing food and great service. The restaurant service team is fantastic and makes you feel welcome. 

A must try if you are in Santa Barbara.

My boyfriend and I were in the area and hungry and decided to try this place, it was small but man is it a gem!!! It was early for dinner (4:45pm) on a weekday so not very busy inside, so we expected it to be quick good service and they did not disappoint.  The server was very nice, helpful being that we had not been there.  We ordered pasta and it was just amazing...Full of flavor and spice! Definitely worth it.  We live completely across the city but would drive out of our way for this yummy place again!
Although this place is nice and clean I find it too expensive. The bumper cars are fun but 5 bucs for 3 mintues come on now.....

Had a great workout this morning and found this cute coffee hidden in the west side of town. Instead of going to Starbucks in the same parking lot, check out this place instead. Very small, good for a personal convo, Has their own coffee (what it's not tinker ) and sells local merch. I got an iced latte with salted Carmel and oat milk. $6 is too much but it was delicious.

Ribs are overhyped. Decently seasoned, but not tender and nothing special. Sweet potato fries were hot and good; I just wish there wasn't so much sugar on them. Corn was good. Had an overall average bbq experience.

Terrible experience. I ordered eggs benedict with fruit no bananas. When I got my breakfast the fruit had bananas, not a big deal but the waitress should've realized right away that wasn't right. The hollandaise sauce was two different colors and didn't taste right and the eggs weren't cooked all the way.  My waitress didn't ask how my meal was and both her and the manager looked at the napkin with the bananas on it and just kept going. The entire wait staff and manager are more focused on talking to the regulars then caring about the other customers.

It's been a long time since I've been to Chili's and I'm happy I came back. The food and drinks are both on point. It's rare to find a place that gets both right. My new favorite Chili's drink is the blueberry pineapple Margarita. Fellas don't let the big feminine glass stop you.
