Update from my previous review.  We hit RR monthly, at least.  Food is still solid, and they are doing a lot more local stuff, which is great.  The staffing issues seem to have been resolved, staff is pleasant and prompt.  Some of them still know little if anything about the beers they have.

My primary complaint at this point is the beer.  Whoever orders their kegs has a real hop fetish.  Hey, guess what, not all of us are hop heads.  The real shame of it in my eyes is that they have 30 or 40 taps, all with mostly US micros, but a LOT of the beers have too much crossover - there might be 3 or 4 beers on draft of a given style at any one time that are really similar to each other.  That's a real shame.  Want an uber IPA or two on draft?  Sure.  But free up a couple of those taps for different styles for different beer tastes.  And always, always have at least one good old traditional American lager/amber ale on...New Belgium Fat Tire would be a solid choice.

The primary motivator for me to go to RR is the food, not the beer, and that's a real shame.  Mix in some traditional Wit beers, a few Belgian style doubles or triples, some good, malty, chewy beers, and I'll be happier.

Absolutely love this place. Everything that comes out of the kitchen is delicious, from the oysters to the farmhouse platter to the larger entrees. Kip and his team are extremely attentive without hovering, make great drinks and are wonderful company if you do feel like chatting. I'm here a few times a month and the consistency of the food and service is incredible.

This place truly made me feel like I was taking crazy pills. So much so that I did not even make it through the line to have their coffee. At first sight, I thought this place looked like a great spot to sit down for a cap (which was my intention). There was a little bit of a line (8-10) which did not discourage me but gave me faith that this place may be worth the wait. So I wait. Then I wait. Guess what I do next? Fine, I'll tell you, I wait. Now I start looking around and I notice that their staff seems to be working quite hard. However, what is God's name are they working on? It has been 10 minutes and I have not seen a single person move up in the line. Finally, my girlfriend comments on how absurd this is and I start venting. I honestly thought I was going crazy. How can these barista's be so active without serving a single coffee while the line continues to grow? I really wanted to give 1 star but I have not even tried the coffee. I would say give it a shot but if there is a line, no matter what the size, be prepared to sip on a tall glass of fresh Nashville air and not a coffee.

Seems like a pretty authentic atmosphere.  Even though the service wasn't great (the waiter kept coming to our table every two or so minutes asking if we were ready to order or if he could take our plates when we were still eating, etc.), the food was great.  A friend and I had the fajitas for 2 with steak & chicken.  They were delicious, and there was enough fajita toppings for about 4 people!  I would definitely recommend it, and I will be going back!
I am in love with their food. Bagels are always amazing. Parking sucks and ordering can be intimidating if you've never been there before.

I like this big restaurant that's just west of the border of UNR. Apparently lots of college folks flock here (which makes sense) since they have daily specials. I like the fun atmosphere with the random trinkets scattered along the walls. Service was great.

My friend and I enjoyed a couple cold brews and I had a burger. If you're looking for a unique bite, try their Jiffy Burger. Yes, there is peanut butter in it--not sure if it's Jiffy as implied in the name of the burger, but it's there. Now, just imagine: bread, beef, and peanut butter. It's actually not bad. I mean, it's worth trying but I'm not sure if I'd get it again. You might have one of those moments where you're just like, "ohhh, this is interesting," and then just finish it. The fries were typical--but the good typical.

I'd definitely come back again if friends wanted to! The parking lot could get tricky (could be more spacious) so beware if traveling in a caravan of sorts.

Dinner at Luvi is absolute poetry. Each dish that you consume here will make your taste buds sing. Both the food and the chef will create an unforgettable experience. In a city full of delightful restaurants this is a perfect gem, with its rare sake selection and flavorful dishes it makes for an experience you will want to repeat time and time again.
Chicken Noodle Soup is $5 but there wasn't any noodles and barely any chicken. Just chicken broth with carrots. Very disappointed for the price :[

In Reno we wanted  some vietnamese food,  we Yelp it  and it had some good reviews compared to other restaurant in town.This was a winner me and husband decided to try this place. We came in nice man sat us down their were some social distancing we can see when we come in so that's was good and everyone that came in and staff all had their mask on.

I order coconut juice thinking it would be a coconut because I saw the picture outside but it came in a can and it was $5 I'm like wow it's Reno should be reasonable prices right and we order large pho with everything. The large pho was not  compared to the  Bay area out here their large was like a small and they didn't have much meat or noodles in there and the large pho with everything was $12.95 . I order the large bowl to share with both of my kids when it came I was like wow that's not going workso my husband had to share his pho too. My husband was still hungry after that,the pho broth did not taste like pho and I'm Vietnamese I'm just in shocked , the owner was really nice and I spoke to him in vietnamese too , nice man but the food and used so work and portions too for the price.
Great experience maybe I need to try something different then pho next time if I come back will see when I'm in town

Buen Provecho!  I have now been to Maya Quetzal a few times and it is definitely one of my favorite restaurants on fourth.  The food is 100% Chapin and the simple and fresh flavors reminded me of my trip to the country of eternal spring.  The thick homemade pupusas are riquísimas and the sauce for the pollo pepiano has just the right amount of spice.  The staff is friendly, courteous, and you never wait long for a meal.  Maya Quetzal is a great find!

Other than the smallness of the restaurant and the relatively  higher noise level as a result, I love this place. Had the coconut soup (yummo!!) and the Pai thai. You can ask to have it as spicey as your pallet allows.  The staff were accomodating and attentive. Loved the fact that it is a BYOB.
It was our pleasure to be welcomed by Crystal! The atmosphere was inviting and cozy, the food was so enticing, we had to have seconds! We got "rolled up" at Happy Fish!!!

Typical Chinese food, nothing at all special. Food quality used to be consistent but has been all over the place over the last couple years. Delivery service is pretty lacking, driver is rude (ordered dozens of times with coworkers). They will often 'forget' items from the order and then refuse to redeliver them or offer compensation. They never send chopsticks...

I called in an order on a busy night- apparently the secret is out about Angelo's. My husband came to pick up and waited for a while. He was given the wrong order and then another pizza tat was not quite what we specified. What made all the difference was the level of attention he got. They even called to apologize and offered to make everything right- for a very busy restaurant (or even not so busy one) that is truly an amazing thing. We were very touched that our patronage was appreciated. That given with the dedication to to the quality of ingredients and pride in preparing everything from scratch is such a rare thing these days. We usually get the Big Lou- a white pizza with onions and sausage. The Margherita is amazing. We're looking forward to exploring the cheesesteaks and cutlet sandwiches next. And it's always wonderful to support a small family business.

Amazing!
We had Frank as our server.  He was awesome.  He has a serious exterior but gave perfect polite professional service. 
We ordered the gumbo as a starter.  It was great. 
The main entrees were cooked to perfection.
I had the gulf shrimp and greens.  It came in a nice cast iron small serving pan.  The shrimp were a good size cooked perfectly.  The greens were fresh and bright green. The sauce was so delicious.  I was thankful to have bread to soak it up! 
My husband got the red fish.  It was so flakey and flavored amazingly.  It was served on top of a vegetable potato mix.  
The atmosphere was a nice relief from the noise of bourbon.  
The entire evening was great and memorable.  
We will be back and we will be sure to ask for Frank.

I aways enjoy this establishment. The seafood here is above average and so is the wait staff. There crab legs are delicious. Your bill can ran up really fast as everything is per order. I love this place I hate the way I've heard they treat their eait staff
Customer service SUCKED! The hype was not real what so ever about these sandwiches LOL

I was looking for a sandwich and soup type place and just happened to stumble upon this place. I ordered the soup of the day and a strawberry salad and loved every bit of it! The atmosphere inside was very relaxing...local art on the walls, very quiet, nice customer service. I have no complains! Would definitely go back again.

Is there a 2.5 star option? The fries were okay but nothing to write home about.   Lots of fancy salt options and dipping sauces, but the wow factor wasn't there for me. It seemed like a brilliant concept for the tater state but I left feeling underwhelmed.  One fry I won't be trying again.

I was exited to come here.
Atmosphere was like casual downed hungry cat- ish.
Attractive looking bar as well.

First thing we notice. Silver wear is spotty. Visibly clearly spotty. 
 
Menu. You can tell they are trying topical " now days" burger place.

We ordered shrimp poboy sandwich,humberger( can't remember what it was something with blue cheese in it ), lulu buger which is lamb.

In general, it's all bland. Not enough seasoning.
Serving Poboy on chabata - ish bread is probably not so good idea.

Lulu burger, I ordered as medium. Inside was cold. Like fridged cold.
It's not hand shaped patty. Not sure frozen or just mechanically shaped.
But simply not a good burger.

French fly that came with burger was so what ever.
It did seems like fresh cut potato. But not crispy, not hot, not enough seasoning.

Burger was most ok one. barely noticeable amount of blue cheese.
Wasn't bad. But just ok.

So we had 3 entré, 2 wine total of over $60 of what ever burger made us little sad.

I wanted to love this place. 
Unfortunately their food was not even close to what I was expected.
It's just another ok food with big bill restraint.

Always a solid choice for lunch. At the bar now and it is packed on a Wednesday at noon.  I come here specifically for the Prime rib which is served with mash potatoes. It is full of flavor and you will eat every bite. Jeremy was a very informative, and positive bartender. His knowledge of products was superior. The Champagne by the glass is a must and served in proper glassware. Everything is solid here. Everything. 5 stars everywhere.  Did I mention they sell Champagne by the glass. Actually from the Champagne region of France. YUM

What a beautiful place! The restaurant and bar is both very clean and very pretty. The pizza was absolutely delicious and prepared quickly! The staff was very patient while I was overwhelmed with all of the options!

So just moved to the area and giving all tge local shops a try. I really enjoyed their pizza and Chicken Cheesesteak.  Large 2 toppung pizza and a sandwich for $25 no to bad. I did take out. Food was ready and hot. Ill be back

Very disappointed in the customer service skills here. Long story short, one entree for our party of eleven came so late the rest of us were done eating; the server said "don't worry about it" - we thought meaning it would be comped but it was on the bill. Music so loud you couldn't hear the server's announcements or have a conversation with someone across the table and the server's response was that the manager wouldn't do anything about that. Food was average. Too many better options for me to think about returning here.
Amazing Margeritas!!   The guacamole and chips are great.  The older location is fun but both locations have the same food.
This is a true Pizza Mecca. Up there with the pizzeria legends like Frank Pepe's. The spinach & tomato is the best topping option and the signature plain is just like heaven, I'm sure.

If you can deliver cheap, delicious Sushi to me, I love you. Sole reason this place gets 4 stars. Don't get me wrong, I've enjoyed other menu items, but the Sushi is what keeps me going back. Most Chinese take out places in the area are decent, and fairly similar in quality, but SUSHI, man, SUSHI. I will say, if Mei Fun is one of your favorite dishes like me, it's not very good here. Only thing I can really say I don't like from here. Try Lucky Wok for that. (also Aston).

Went here for lunch on a weekday. It should have been a key indicator that the restaurant was empty at 1230. I did not enjoy the pre formed Hamburger steak covered with canned gravy with canned mushrooms. Neither did I enjoy the instant mashed potatoes covered with canned gravy. Not exactly an appetizing lunch. I felt sorry for the waitress for having to serve the food.

I get take out from My thai pretty often and it is a great neighborhood spot. 

I had always been a loyal orderer of chicken pad thai and when i moved to the neighborhood I have to say I was disappointed by My Thai's pad thai. The pad thai is pretty bland but if you are in the neighborhood there are no other thai places that close so its worth if it you are having a pad thai craving.

After being bored with their Chicken Pad thai, I decided to try and new thai dish and ordered the red chicken curry and I am so glad I did. The Red Chicken Curry here is amazing. They give you a nice size portion that is difficult to finish for one meal. I am not a person that likes spicy food and whenever I order the curry and ask for it to be mild they are always able to accommodate me which I always appreciate.  For spicy food lovers, I have ordered with people who enjoy spicy food and they were also very satisfied with their meal.

This is a good neighborhood spot to grab take out from. They also have a sit down restaurant inside which never seems to be too crowded,

I have had 2-3 bad meals here over the last couple of years but today was by far the worst. Ordered the special buttermilk fried chicken sandwich for lunch (was not good, and I'm not a picky eater) it turns out when I got the bill it was $19 despite all the other comparable items on the menu being $10-12. Not cool. Also the soup was gross. I don't recommend eating here.
Had Crêpe,parfaits here. Coffee au lait is a must try for Mew Orleans. My friends had omelet, French toast. The foods are good. The waitress had a good attitude.

What an unfortunate experience! I'm a somewhat regular customer at Mikimotos and to first have them hang up on me then the manager on duty takes her sweet old time coming out when a waiter who has waited on us serval times tell her to come out. When she does finally appear, she has NO IDEA how to handle a customer issue, she starts messingl with the phone and studdering.

Just because you are under new management doesn't mean you can treat your old customers like shit.  If you can't handle the business bring on more staff!

All I can say is fuck you Mikimotos

I wrote my prior review of Barcelona a year ago, and my enthusiasm still stands. I am including a photo from my most recent sit at their gorgeous bar, where I enjoyed THE most delicious tapas, and some delightful wine suggested by the sweet bartenders. 

I have quite literally been dreaming of the bacon-wrapped dates (not figs, as I mistakenly wrote in my original review) since my last visit, and this is coming from someone who has not historically been a bacon nor a date fan. Unreal goodness.

Great shopping here for any of the race weekends, memorial day cookouts, graduation parties, picnics, church pitch-ins and as part of my weekly shopping trip.   Large selection of spices, cocktail mixes, coffees, teas and creamers, parties items in numerous colors of tableware and decorating supplies. One of my favorite items is the selections of small 1-2 oz. cups for Jello shots or Gazpacho. Or the tumbler size glasses with lids for preparing individual servings of dishes from salads to desserts. 

GFS carries a large selection of fresh to frozen meats, vegetables, desserts, breakfast foods, frozen lasagna's, stuffed shells, hamburgers, brats, hot dogs, chicken wings to cocktail mixes and juices. It's not a wholesale store but the prices are comparable with smaller packaging. No membership required.

I returned to Adams after many years and found it to be rather mediocre.  Nothing stood out as exemplary, although the food is not bad.  Basically, I think it is rather overpriced ($11 for 3 small pieces of catfish/$18 for 6 pieces, 3 hushpuppies, a side, and small cup of coleslaw), and the seasoning was not that good.  It does have some atmosphere (some vintage tintype ads and old tools) but nothing out of the ordinary, and they also do not have any desserts or a very large menu.  I got the onion straws as an appetizer, and while they were good, they were laden with grease, and there was no "wow factor" to them.  They do serve steak fries.

One appetizer they have that few other restaurants have is fried veggies.  They may be good, but I cannot speak for them.  In Belle Chasse, there are other seafood places, like Lil G's and Salvo's that do have larger menus, but Adams is harmless.

Also, they do have rather limited hours (usually 11-2 for lunch and 5-9 for dinner) compared to many other restaurants, so it may be prudent to inquire about specific hours (I am not sure which days they are only open for lunch or only for dinner).

A bit pricey but worth it for the flavors! I grabbed a carry out order on grub hub. Super easy and straight forward. I parked the car right outside and was able to quickly pop in and grab my lunch. You don't even have to interact with anyone if you don't want bc they have a carry out tower to grab your meal from! 

Grabbed a O Miso Healthy. Super flavorful, fresh. I'm not a huge chicken person but this chicken was moist and flavorful. Well worth it! A bit of umami, spiciness and all the chicken goodness. It's a bit messy so grab a few napkins to wipe the deliciousness off your face. I grabbed a fresh pressed juice which rounded out to $16. Again not horrible but also not super expensive. Going to put this on my list of places to drop by when I'm in town!

This place is very close to where I lived. It's hidden in a small shopping village of montecito. It's an Italian cuisine.  My favorite here is their calamari and their Sicilian pizza... we dine here with my friend but mostly I always call in to order and pick it up.. it could be packed here in some days . Small place but amazingly classic with modern touch beautiful place...some of movie stars dine here mostly the one that lives here...check it out if your here In Santa Barbara.

Great prices for affordable home styled food served by someone's mum:). 

The place feels like an old school diner on the side of a secondary highway. The room and everything in it looks to have been there since the 70's but it's all endearing and the place is remarkably clean. Our server was a sweet lady who was very happy to serve us. 

I got the house omelette which was under $10. I loved the pan fried potatoes. Our meals were simple and well made. They reminded me of something I might get when visiting home. 

Our first experience was a very nice and I'll be coming back quite a bit.

The service is great but the food is blah. Chicken tastes like processed chicken. The shrimp tastes pre frozen. The meatballs are rubbery/frozen and definitely not home made. You're better off eating frozen Bertolli dinners than you are this.

This was a truly essential stop the morning after nursing a bottle too heavily the night before. Wild Eggs offers a long, comprehensive and distinctive breakfast and brunch menu appreciated even
by someone as myself, who always opts out of breakfast. Clean joint, vast seating (indoor and outdoor), and a nostalgic retro bar as a centerpiece. Our waiter was definitely a morning person (as it should be, I guess) at a morning breakfast restaurant.

What a great addition to the Mont Clare community!  I'm sure as they grow (they haven't even been open a year yet) they will become a community staple!  Their location is great -- right along the river with on-site parking!  We cannot wait to check them out during warmer weather. 

This is such a great family spot-- in fact, my husband and I had left our kids "at home" and each commented how we couldn't wait to bring them back.  

We started with the dry rubbed wings - given the recent wing shortage, we were super impressed with how huge the wings were (and delicious to boot!).  

My burger was amazing - I ordered it as a turkey burger and there was just so much flavor.  I wasn't a fan of the fries, but the burger was worth every bite, every calorie.  My husband did the Nashville hot chicken sandwich and found it HOT.  It's a favorite "dish" of his and this was among the spiciest he's had.  He liked it but didn't love it the way I loved my burger.  He also found the side salad to be very average.  We would both probably just go with the standard side of chips going forward.  

The beer/wine list was limited - I know they're using local brews/wines, but as a wine addict, I wish there were a few more options.  Same with the brews, I was looking for a little more variety.  

All in all they're doing okay, and three stars means we will give it another shot for sure!

This was a once in a life time experience. I typically go here for great Chinese food, and I am sorry to say that is all you can expect from this place. Unfortunately, the Poor customer service was so bad it might be a first here on Yelp. 

Get some popcorn and pull up a chair: 

So this place has an online ordering system where you can also pay online. Great, right?  So I get there feeling efficient like I'm gonna walk in, say my name, and walk out without having to pull my wallet out and deal with paying and stuff. 

I get stopped by the cashier saying "you didn't pay, we need to swipe your card". I politely point to the big notice at the bottom of the order slip saying "order is PREPAID..."  They reluctantly let me go but now I'm feeling like I avoided getting conned. So off I go ready to take the food home to a hungry family

Then my phone starts blowing up. Two calls and finally a voicemail saying I need to pay the bill. I figure, ok simple misunderstanding I'll call when I'm done eating. Then another call which I finally take. I'm told the online ordering website run by BeyondMenu never pays the restaurant and so I need to give them my card details so they can charge me (again). This smells fishy so I say "I'm happy to pay, but I won't pay twice". If BeyondMenu credits the charge I'll gladly pay you. Get this - The restaurant asks if I can call the website to see if I can get them to credit me! Now I am a back office employee?  (Come to think of it, I often see employees chewing a wad of rice and stir fried goodness as they work). Imagine - "hi PayPal, the merchant says you never pay them. So could you please credit me the money so I can pay them?"

I then get many more calls at home by the restaurant and the waiter (!) for a total of THIRTEEN calls (see pic) saying it was urgent that I fix this tonight, because I should've gotten an email proving the credit was applied - (Granted I did get an email from BeyondMenu, but it never said the credit was applied). I assure them when I get the time I will check that my card was credited and I'd be happy to come in an pay for my meal. Not to mention this is my personal time with family, my moms over, etc. I don't plan to put everything on hold to fix the restaurants broken B2B ecommerce deals. 

So I finally get stern with the guy and say when I get a moment I will call my card and confirm the credit has been applied. I end making good on my promise and now you know too!

oh hi mad mex!  i love you! 

mad mex is great because they have vegan options and can put daiya on anything. if you're in university city and want a burrito, or some chips and guac but dont want to spend a ton this is a go-to for sure. 

MM is moderately priced, nothing super fancy, and nothing authentic. but delicious nonetheless.  it has a lil bit of a rowdy atmosphere (think college kids).   they have margaritas that are seriously over 1,000 calories a pop *stay away* 

once i forgot my ID and they wouldn't let me in -  i wish that wrinkles were a valid form of ID but they aren't (the bouncer did NOT think my joke was funny).  hey i get that strict tip - no hard  feelings - but  i did have to ride my bike back home and get my passport.  (i had an expired license at the time and was waiting for my new one!)

i try to come here once in a while because mexican food is my weakness.  its def more chain restaurant than hipster and more college aged than grown ups but that's cool.  i always have a good meal there. 

thanks for all the vegan options, clearly labeled menu, and very informed staff.

I still find myself dreaming of the oysters. Everything at Cochon is incredible, from the cocktails to the appetizers to the main courses. This was, by far, our best meal in New Orleans. I'd highly recommend both the Louisiana cochon and the fish -- and, of course, the oysters. The amazing oysters...

Very authentic Cuban food.  Everything was excellent from the garbanzo soup to the flan.  The menu is extensive so there is something for everyone.  Service was great and the restaurant was very clean.  My new go to restaurant serving breakfast, lunch and dinner.

Checking out some of the ladies at the counter is enough to whet your appetite for a long time to come. Some of the hottest hotties in IV work here. And for good reason: South Coast Deli is simply the best sandwich maker for miles around. Their portions are substantial and tasty. And in my experience, salubrious. Yes, they do cater to vegetarians.

Dined there last night with a friend.  As mentioned by other reviewers here and elsewhere, the service is  rushed, the entire meal was 45 minutes, and the server, Owen, is a little pushy/over eager. Having dined here several times, I wanted to like the place but it has become apparent to me after last nights experience that there has been an inexorable decline in the quality of the dishes.  The vegetable entrees, including kale and mushrooms, were not served at the right temperature.  The spicy tofu was good.  The smoked carrots were vastly different this time around. Whereas previously the carrots were tender, thus time they were crunchy from undercooking.  When I first came to vedge years ago what impressed me was the care and ease with which the staff combined seemingly disparate ingredients. My experience this time around was an oily culinary cacophony.  

Who knows, maybe the restaurant ownership has changed hands?  Plead bring back the vedge of yore.

My husband and I recently held our wedding rehearsal dinner for 20 people at Percy Street. The team there was super responsive to all our pre-event questions/concerns, and, the day of, went off without a hitch! The space was ready. Service was impeccable and attentive, as it is during dinner on a normal night. And the food was fantastic. We had the Lockhart - basically one of everything on the menu - and the meats were moist, sides were appetizing and portions were large. Everyone left stuffed and my, now, mother in laws, is still raving about the key lime pie!

this is the best restaurant i keep coming back to.. a hidden gem.. black cod just is vooked perfect always just melts in your mouth.. salmon so fresh and amazing ... service is very friendly..  usually get free complementary plates ...  the deep fried bananas with icream to top of it off sends you home very happy
Good burgers. Excellent service. Gluten free bun was not good but server was aware of gluten sensitivity and suggested that the chips were fried in a fryer with other items containing flour.
One of our favorite places! Best egg flour soup in Tucson!! We have tried a few different entrees and appetizers and they are all delicious! Fast and friendly service!

I'm not much of a gambler, so its just as big a surprise to me that I found myself in Reno for my birthday/holiday weekend. Never one to say NO to an adventure (People who say YES have more fun!), I happily checked into the Peppermill Casino-Resort-Spa and after reading Yelp reviews, simply had to try out Chi.  Calling down the day of, we had no problems getting reservations at 8 pm on a Friday night.

We arrive at our appointed time, greeted & seated immediately.  One glance around and you can see the ambiance my fellow Yelpers have described: upscale, elegant Chinese decor surrounds you, with beautiful crystal chandeliers hanging above each table - sending out scattered, diffuse light. If I were on a date I would love the low, complimentary lighting in this place - but alas, I was having a lovely dinner with family.  Our glasses were immediately filled with water, after first being given the option of still or sparkling, bottled or tap. Next, our delightful server Lily arrived with compliments to all of the ladies at the table on their beauty and assuring us we were to take our time and enjoy our dining experience. Intrigued by their specialty cocktails, I tried to the Ginger-Lemongrass Cooler - a vodka, simple syrup topped with ginger beer and slices of fresh ginger.  It was light & refreshing - a perfect summer cocktail. 

After happily "cocktailing" for a bit, we moved on to the appetizers - choosing the appetizer combo plate to sample a little bit of everything. It arrived seemingly minutes later, with steamed pork pot stickers, cream cheese crab puffs, BBQ sweet ribs, fried spring rolls and a curious fried spring roll with a whole shrimp inside.  Every bite was delicious - the pot stickers being my favorite. They were perfectly steamed, with just a hint of crust where they were flash fried for a few seconds before plating. The pork was sweet and flavorful, hardly needing any dumpling sauce because it was so tender and juicy. Next came the BBQ sweet ribs - a bit awkward at first, I'm not usually one who enjoys eating with her hands in a nice restaurant, but then Lily appeared with hot, almond-scented towels to clean our hands. Her timing and service was this impeccable all evening. Messy, but tasty, shortribs devoured, I decided to try the fried-spring-roll-with-a-shrimp-tail-sticking-out. It wasn't anything I recognized, but the blend of vegetables wrapped around the shrimp, then covered in a phyllo and fried golden brown were excellent, especially paired with the spicy mustard. The fried spring roll was as expected, possibly a low note to end on, but I attribute that more to my adoration for the other items rather than its lackluster performance. 

After enjoying our appetizer selections, we decided to share the Peking Duck and Chicken & Shrimp Pad Thai among the table. None of us were famished after our yummy starters, so we thought this would be a good option to try a few different things.  Boy, the portions are so large we probably could have just ordered one! Again, minutes after ordering our selections arrived - their kitchen is either psychic or wonderfully efficient. Our pad Thai arrived in a presentation similar to a Cobb salad - each layer of toppings was beautifully displayed in rows atop the traditional flat noodles in tangy peanut sauce. I deftly mixed the peanuts, sprouts, generous fried egg, shrimp and chicken into the pasta while Lily began preparing the Peking Duck. Arriving sliced and laid out on a platter, the large pieces of duck are beautifully glazed with a crispy outer crust. Borrowing a pair of chopsticks from the table, she expertly unfolds the "pancakes" (for those unfamiliar, they are more like crepes than fluffy buttermilk pancakes), slathers on a bit of the spicy, sweet Peking sauce and then adds vegetables and slices of duck, folding each back up like a lovely little Peking duck burrito and placing them on our plates.  The whole presentation was fascinating and fun - with Lily explaining each step with her lovely accent, comparing this to how her family makes the dish at home. Each bite was just as delicious - the sweet but tangy sauce, the light crepe-like pancake and the slightly crunchy crust on the juicy duck, all blended into a wonderful meal. And don't forget the pad Thai! It was perfectly spicy, peanut-y and delicious, with large chucks of white meat chicken and shrimp, all beautifully blended with the flat noodles and fried egg. We simply couldn't finish each tasty morsel, so Lily graciously boxed up the leftovers for a late night snack after some gambling...

Now, you might ask: How does it get any better? Well, here's how: some members of our table qualified for the very prestigious (ahem) over-55 discount of 10%, but our sweet Lily discounted the entire bill 10% - a lovely surprise ending to a scrumptious meal.  If I were a Reno regular, this would definitely become part of my regular rotation.

I absolutely LOVE the food...buutttt I am not a fan of the service I've received here. I have only had one decent server the few dozen times I've been here...all the others have been rude and lack knowledge of the (food) menu. I've ordered the royale a few times and sometimes I've been given a side of crack fries (like the menu states it should), and others time I've been told that I only get the fries that come on the sandwich.

Really wasn't thrilled with the quality of service at this location. Food was OK, but nothing to rave about. Very average chain restaurant fare. The pretzel with dip appetizer was good. Cheese sauce was very bland, but the other two dips were delicious. The pecan crusted salad was not very tasty. It was also very bland.

I was asked if I'd return to Applebees. The answer is a wholehearted....NO!

This place was so much fun, with friendly service, lively music and delicious dishes! We came in early to escape the heat and were able to grab a seat at the bar as we waited for our table. They let us sample their bloody mary's while we waited. We also got to enjoy the live music while sipping our lemonade and then were seated when it came time for our reservation.  Service was very friendly and accommodating.  Definitely order the etouffee omelette! It was my favorite dish.  My group also had the duck hash (also a hit), shrimp and green tomatoes po'boy and chicken-n-biscuits. It was a great start to our New Orleans trip.

I love going here! Their menu is amazing with so many crazy creations to concoct! I love all the varieties and flavors. It's awesome. Can I just say that dipped cones are beautiful and I'm so glad to be alive. Love their huckleberry burger. Their burgers are on the thin side, but it didn't put me off. Their soda creations are unique, fun, and delicious. I will come here until I die.

Only getting one star because you have to assign a number of stars worst service ever 16 year old kid disrespectful! I waited over 2 hours! 2! I then was put on hold multiple times so I came in to the store. The 16 year old still disrespectful! Yelling back and forth! Never have I dealt with this from a pizza delivery place. Walter the owner should fire him on the spot!

There was only one server so I made sure she knew I was seating "outside". After 15 minutes, no one came to get my order and I ran out of time to have breakfast before my flight. I know business are struggling for workers but just don't open or say you cannot take anyone anymore because you are low on staff. Specially at an airport where time is of essence.

This is a good place to check out once while in the city. There are an inordinate # of places to it. It may not be for everyone, though, because it is extremely crowded and hard to find a place to sit. I'd say it's worth seeing if you don't mind big crowds...

Why a place that specializes in crepes only has one crepe cooktop I have no idea. It took 25 minutes to get one. Completely inefficient system. The eggs were very over cooked. The fruit side was frozen melon and blueberries that had no flavor. The staff seemed confused and annoyed to have to be working. On the scramble the cold cheese they put on top was never melted and again the eggs were over cooked and they charged $.75 for each add on which was just like a couple leaves of spinach and a few chopped onions. Ridiculous. The side salad was just a few leaves if mesclun with a raspberry vinaigrette. No options for dressing, that's just what you get. If you're not going to give options then maybe use something a little less specific. And just leaves? I mean add something else. At least some other veggies. I can't see a reason I would ever go back.

Great food. Great location. Located right on Gulf Blvd, it was an easy walk from our beach house rental. The blvd has sidewalks on both sides and clearly marked pedestrian crossings at the nearby intersection and just near the restaurant itself. 
We were a party of 9, so we had to wait for a bit, but the hostess was very attentive and kept us updated. The live music kept us entertained. He played everything from Bob Dylan to Elvis to Darius Rucker. 
The only reason for the loss of the star was our server/service times. She seemed overwhelmed even though it wasn't super busy. She was very nice, just not around the table often and the food took a long time (45 mins from order to table). 
When the food did arrive, it was somewhat inconsistent in quality. Our Margherita pizza looked and tasted delicious. My daughter's pizza had numerous bubbles that cut down on the taste.
For adults, they featured a decent range of local and big brand beers. They also had flavorful cocktails. 
What was good was really good, our experience was just inconsistent.

Best BBQ and Best Mac and Cheese in St. Louis, hands down!  The brisket is absolutely insane, it melts in your mouth!  The Mac and cheese is a white cheddar Mac and cheese, literally voted best in STL by the RFT.  You have to hit this place up.  It's the best!!

I stood in front of the counter for 7 minutes at a nearly empty location (Nashville, Thompson Lane) before any of the staff acknowledged that I was even there. They walked past a total of 6 times without bothering to say "hello" or "is there a chance you'd like a sandwich?"

From the start walked in you know service wasn't as great but you know it's whatever. It's like Denny's on Sunday morning packed so I couldn't expect anything more. Our server stunk like cannabis and that wasn't very great. They forgot an order which include both a drink and the food. Had to grab a servers attention by whaling our arms and even then had to wait a good 2 and a half minutes. The burger is okay it would've been great if it weren't to include a whole slice of raw onion which isn't as appealing as an aftertaste in my opinion but hey I'm not other people so that's you to decide. In reality the bacon is all the same they are just different shades and disintegrate into your mouth because they were over cooked.

This is a great example of a seafood store. 
The staff is very knowledgeable and very helpful. 

They have a nice selection of fish and other seafood. 

They crab cakes are very good. If you like crab cakes then try these. 

They can be a little pricey but I have never been disappointed.

Found Izumi after passing by on a whim. I just recently moved to Philly and got off of work early and decided to stop by. The service was excellent and it was the servers first day. Being a chef it is hard to find a place with great service but is is more difficult to find a place with great service from a new server. Sushi was exceptional. I have had sushi in Tokyo, Yokohama, and Hiroshima, and it was a pleasant reminder of how great sushi should be. Two thumbs way up. Check it out

Wonderful food, great service, attentive owners and chef. The only issue is that the tables are too small for all the wonderful foods we ordered, lol :)
I recommend the glass noddles, Bronzino, and the dumplings. Best Thai food I've had in a long time... possibly ever.

Breakfast here is not as impressive as their subs, but it's still good. Carefully cooked and hand crafted breakfast makes it feel and taste like a home cooked meal, because it pretty much is! 

I ordered a sausage, egg and cheddar sandwich on half a sub roll. It was tasty and made to order. 

I got to meet one of the the nice lady's son's. Talking to them this time around I found out that all of them have taken culinary arts to enhance the Deli. 

I'll be back again. I'm glad I was told about this little gem.

Fantastic Italian,  hand made pasta, excellent service and the quaint feel of an authentic Italian restaurant I once visited in Amalfi.  If I could I'd dine there every night. What a great find in this little town.

Part 1 of my search for the BEST BLOODY MARY IN NASHVILLE: 

After seeing a RIDICULOUS bloody mary on IG, I was super stoked to find out it was being served in Nashville at The Flipside! So off I went for Sunday Brunch with a girlfriend in tow.

The restaurant is located in the very popular 12 South area of Nashville, where traffic and parking can be a pain. On a Sunday around 11AM, I was able to find street parking in one of the side neighborhoods and avoided having to pay for parking. Woohoo! 

The decor reminds me of a trendy diner-style. Lots of retro posters and decorative pieces lined the walls. Very cute and casual. Service was also good. They were attentive to our needs and checked in multiple times.

Now, for the star of the show: THE BLOODY MARY, also called "The Big Fix," which consists of a large mug of Bloody Mary with a pickle on the side, full strips of bacon sticking out of the top of the glass, a stick filled with fried chicken cutlets and tots, and TWO snow crab clusters ($25). The pictures online didn't do it justice. This thing was impressive. The Bloody Mary itself was actually quite good, could be a tad spicier for me but overall not bad. The high points was the super crispy bacon, tots and drink itself. Average was the crab legs which were served very cold. The legs had great flavor but the body  was very bland. The bad was the chicken cutlet which tasted like cardboard, could do without that. 

**They also have a great Saturday/Sunday brunch 2-for-1 deal on the regular Bloody Mary's, bellini's, sangria's and mimosa's that all looked excellent. Available between 10AM - 3PM.

Also worth mentioning is the Tator Tot Nachos, which is as awesome as it sounds. It includes a mountain of tater tots topped with melted cheese, bacon, avocado, tomatoes, jalapeños, and green onions. As a non-cheese eater, I didn't even mind it because everything else was so good. 

Overall verdict: WORTH IT! I would come back to try the rest of menu and even get another Big Fix!

Ordered a Wok Bowl by recommendation with salmon, teriyaki sauce, and lo mein noodles. I asked for no cashews which still came on my food but rather than send it back I just brushed it off. The flavor was great and it was a lot of food but I personally think $21 was too much for it.

Found this restaurant on yelp because we needed a vegetarian friendly place to eat. First impression was a bit shocking because it looks like a whole in the wall whither only outdoors sitting. However it was a great experience, weather was great, the decor in the alley is cute and the food so delicious. The beet hummus is yummy! The sweet potato soup great! I have the pork mofongo it was delicious and totally different to a typical mofongo. Extremely recommend it!!

What a pleasant surprise!  I was stopping by Home Depot for some condo stuff when I noticed Rocco's right in front.  Smelled so good so I went to yelp to check on the reviews.
I ordered spicy sausage with peppers and onions and it was so good!  great sandwich.  Really good bread.  service was nice and quick.  Made it an extra worthwhile trip to Home Depot.

Everest opened a new downtown location this week, so it was necessary to visit. I'm a big believer in supporting Downtown locations, even if my visit to their Manchester Road location wasn't the best. 

Upon entering, we were greated with a friendly "namaste" (is their an angry namaste? OK, I'm back after Googling Sanskrit swear words, back to the review). We were seated -- word of warning here, they've got the tables packed in very tightly. 

The buffet was pretty much a mirror image of the Manchester Road location -- chicken korma, veggie korma, mustard greens (completely wonderful and not just for soul food), some other vegetarian options (kidney beans and lentils come to mind), a spicy chicken with bone (that is its name, really!), daal, chicken and vegetable soup, GIANT pieces of naan, zucchini pakora, and of course, my nemesis from the other location, tandoori chicken. 

The tandoori chicken was way better than my experience at the other location, but still not spicy or burnt as I like it. Oh well. 

They also have mango pudding, salad, raita, and a wonderfully super spicy red chili chutney. 

I'm going to say the food was a solid 3 stars, the service 4 stars (very friendly throughout and prompt with the check), the decor was mixed (half is very "Indian" feeling, the other half, a bit plain). The seating is just too cramped. 

I might have given them 4 stars, but also like the Manchester Road location, they do not include mo-mos on the buffet. I just don't get it. Maybe it's an cost issue, but it truly bums me out.  So for that and cramped seating, I'll say a solid 3 stars.

Since the management change  in December, there has been a lack of bagels!!! This is a bagel store!! Really. How do u have no poppy?? 
The bacon changed to shoe leather with pepper. 
The coffee area was pushed in front of the food pickup area. Way too congested. 
Bring the old manager back. Stop cutting corners and improve your customer service PLEASE. sincerely a 15 year customer.

Very impressive new entry on the ever expanding Oak Street scene of cafes, restaurants, shops and general funky places. While housed in a historic building DTB is its own self, respectful of Creole cooking but not afraid to chart its own culinary course.

In honor of the Tricentennial go for the Louisiana cocktail, a tasty riff off a Sazerac rye. For a darker taste the brown sugar Old Fashioned was surprisingly good and not as sweet as it sounds.

We did a mix of small plates and entrees. Thumbs up for the fried cornbread--a bit of heat, lots of crunch. The gumbo is dark and favorable--a wonderful roux that includes the chef's potato salad rather than rice. Sounds a bit odd I know but try it--it really balances the roux. The salad is fresh fresh and highlighted with bits of cheese, bacon, spices--light yet filling.

I believe I would order the Louisiana Rice Bowl every time I come here--everything about the dish, from the browned rice, the Tasso and the grilled shrimp. Just a perfect new Creole dish.

The dessert choices are limited but excellent: creative, beautiful presentation. The strawberry shortcake sounds boring but not here--do it: like many items the inventive approach just stands out. This place is close to a 5 but in New Orleans that's a tough number to reach.

Basing the review on my only experience, hoping to make it back to the St. Louis area sometime soon for another shot so I can satisfy the creole junky in me. Don't recall name, but I tried the andouille sausage/pork burger and it was excellent. The marmalade gave the sandwich a great twist. My fiance tried the beer battered burger and was disappointed. Separately, the ingredients were tasty, but everything put together was a greasy mess. There also was hardly any cheese sauce to be found. One thing I wish was different was portions/menu setup -- be nice if there was a side gumbo option (or a gumbo/sandwich combo) rather than having to pay $9 just to try the gumbo.  Really wanted to try a sandwich and gumbo, but wasn't going to drop $17 to make that happen.
Another great omelet (Colorado) today. The service at this location is consistently good. Thanks Barbie!

Absolutely love this place! The pho is superb and has just the right amount of broth, meat, veggies, and rice noodles. I love the brisket but the veggie is equally as delicious! The staff are so kind and friendly. This is one of my favorite places for pho in lil' ol' Boise!

I used to do nearly all my grocery shopping here.  However, in the last two or three years I have noticed that going there has more often caused me to leave feeling annoyed or frustrated.  Whether it is by them not honoring their advertised prices, even when it is valid and you have the flier in your hand, or the store creating limits on sale items and not clearly posting thr limit or the price you will pay if you exceed the limit Or being charged for more items than you purchased.

I can't think of a shopping trip that I have made there in the last 6 months where I haven't been annoyed and felt ripped off when I looked over my receipt at home.  After too many trips like that, I just can't see shopping at Schnucks.  I think I need to stick to Fresh Thyme, Aldi and Target.

The interior was very cute and really liked the long bar counter.   Hope this place sticks around for awhile because I really want to try several of their drinks as well as a few other pies.   


I grabbed two pieces of pie for takeout (Caramel Apple & the Butterscotch Bourbon)
I ate the Butterscotch Bourbon with an hour of picking it up.   I am not a huge fan of Bourbon but that being said it was still one tasty piece of pie.   The crust was a bit soggy and wish it a some crisp to it.   The Bourbon flavor was there but without the BITE which I appreciated.   

The Caramel Apple sat on my counter overnight and became my next days breakfast. :)   I heated it up in the microwave a bit and must say it was a delicious piece of pie.   One of the better apple pies I have eaten.  I will say I wish it had a tad more caramel flavor but the sugary top crust and the apples were done very well.   I had it with ice cream.
I love the latin food which is not over priced for lunch or dinner . Very close to work and close to downtown . You dont need reservation and has outside seating .

No need to sugarcoat this. My friends and I went here last night absolutely trashed. 2 cheesesteaks and 2 chicken cheesesteaks were ordered around 2 am. It was fast, hot, and pretty good. I thought 10 bucks was a little excessive though. I'll try them sober to see if my opinion stays true.
Tried the gumbo. It was watery and had little flavour. The service was also unfriendly from our waitress (Caucasian female with light brown hair). I wouldn't recommend it!
Great place to grab breakfast, always full of people and very fun environment. Big portions too.

When my husband and I arrived we thought this was going to be fast casual by having the title street food. It is a casual sit down place. I had taken my husband to Saigon a few years back and it was a bit too authentic for him. I thought this might be a good reintroduction to Vietnamese food for him. We got the pho as an app. I got the chicken bun as my meal. He got the steak bahn mi. I got an avocado smoothie. Overall, my main criticism would be that things are too bland. We had leftovers from the bun and pho. I could see if you only got the bahn mi with it being small but the pho and bun are filling. The overall quality is good. I really liked the boba in the smoothie it was so soft and not underdone like many boba are at places. We wanted to try the waffle for dessert but we're full and had to catch a movie. Overall, I knew this wasn't going to be totally authentic but it was a good start to those unfamiliar with Vietnamese cuisine.

Average. The sushi really wasn't that good. My friends order came out wrong twice. Her edamame had sugar on it instead of salt, and she ordered a salmon roll, but was given a shrimp roll. Service was slow. Sushi just wasn't that great. Shrimp roll barely had shrimp in it. And the spicy crab roll tasted funny.

Me and my friend went here and we had to wait 45 minutes for our food to be brought to our table while the couple next to us came in at the same time, got there food, are and then left and another couple proceeded to come to that same table get there food and leave all while we're still waiting. We made the decision once we got our food and it was WRONG! The waitress took the food away from the table with an attitude came back and told my friend he had to pay for the food even tho neither one of us ate anything. He refused and ARRESTED him. NEVER AGAIN WILL I EVER GO THERE AND I WOULD RECOMMEND YOU DON'T EITHER!

Was taken here for an interview dinner. Pleasant location down by the lake near the Marina. I'm not much of a seafood person to be honest so I wasn't thrilled with where they'd picked at first but the food is actually pretty good. I don't know about climbing two flights of stairs to get to the restaurant (and I didn't see an elevator for those who might need one) but the view is nice. 

The service was friendly and efficient; I have no complaints there. The food took a little while to come out but it was lunch rush. Portions were extremely generous. I suppose it's a good seafood restaurant, but I don't really eat the stuff, had the catfish instead which was decent.
Used to be very good when they first started. Over the last 3/4 months, quality has really deteriorated. It is now probably one of the worst places in town. Horrible biryani and buffet.

These guys are really friendly, and consistently serve great food. Prices are more than fair, good value for the healthy  portions. Can't beat a combo plate or gyro sandwich combo. Always fresh and delicious. Love the mango tea as well!

Haven't been here in almost a year. Decided to come back and give it another shot. Now: it's Friday prime time but we went in to give it another shot. Told it would be a 30 minute wait. Ok we will sit at the bar. Ordered drinks from the bartender who was sloppily dressed with wrinkled clothes and unkempt beard and decided to chat with the couple next to us. Turns out they had been waiting 40 minutes for their food.  that factored in to whether we would order food. Then, the manager showed up and apologized after the bartender brought the husband's food. That was our sign that this place has seen better days. I won't be back. Disappointing. Fail.

Best bagels in Tampa. Nice soft middle and crunchy outside, plenty of variety. Cream cheese is awesome and there are tons of flavors to choose from. The eggs are all freshly cooked on a griddle and they sandwiches are great. The only thing I wish is it was closer to my house

I order this online due to COVID-19 and everything went smoothly. It was the first restaurant out of quarantine. The online ordering process was easy, even told me when my food would be ready, and the pickup process was contactless and clean. I got the spicy Cajun, special Juicy sauce, and lemon butter flavors: 3 bags per pound of seafood boils which hit every palate spot on my tongue.

We had a delicious meal at Quinoa! My fajita was perfectly cooked and my vegetarian sister had lots of options to choose from. Jack, our waiter, was very knowledgable, personable and friendly. Will definitely come back!

Francophile here! This lovely café is my new favorite spot. The menu is authentic, the ingredients fresh and the wait staff is attentive.

I ordered the Omelette du Soleil, which was deliciously cheesy and savory. The hash browns were crispy and crunchy and I recommend the flakey baguette over the toast.

I love the music selection! From TV on the Radio to Belle & Sebastian right into The Notorious B.I.G.! The only other place I've ever heard that is on my ipod. 

Also love the iced Irish coffee with whipped cream on top - just one has me buzzed as I write this!

Lots of big open windows and free wifi. The clientele and staff are a nice break from the tourists.
Came to soft opening night in Indianapolis and food was amazing, people were nice, love the new wall decor!! They also gave us a free goodie bag when we left with a sweatshirt and coupons inside!

What a terrific diamond in this regentrifying neighborhood on N4th.  Not trendy, not a fad, not touristy.... it's a local community place where you are treated like your part of the restaurant family; even for us our of towners.

Had some challenges selecting just one plate as there were so many interesting dishes to try.  Just means we need to come back over and over again.

Our server was so helpful in our decision making.
I had the El Beit which was awesome.  Its-- eggs with shaved Cauliflower, zucchini, tomatoes, onions, pesto parsley sauce, topped with diced potatoes, artichoke hearts, string beans & asparagus, arugula salad drizzled with whipped feta & yogurt dressing with a side of pita.  

My honey enjoyed the Poulet Roti, French baguette, marinated chicken, sautéed onions, mushrooms, tomatoes, arugula, avocado, potatoes, pickles & roasted garlic aioli.

No one rushed us and we were treated very well considering we were the out of town newbies (former NYCers).

While relaxing and finishing our beverages we joined a conversation in progress with Gabby (one of the dynamic duo owners of this husband/wife team).  Ended up spending an hour sitting outside taking with both Gabby and his honey Natalie as they greeted and spoke/hugged their customers.  A new home away from Bucks County for a great meal.

Very cool little restaurant/bar on the side
Of a hill. 
Venison Tri Tip sandwich
Was so good, could cut it with a fork 
Chili 
Service
Not sure about other customers but great pizza for the area...great beer and burbon selection plus they give military discount.  Staff very friendly!
Excellent Mongolian grill the service great and the food is superb.  I strongly recommend this restaurant.

Stopped in for a late breakfast/early lunch. While parking was a bit tight it did not take long to find a spot. Once inside we realized one must first make the line, order your food and then find a table. If you are dinning in you will get a number for your table and they will bring out your food to you. It was a bit busy but luckily this did not affect wait times. 

I got a breakfast sandwich, i went with a bacon, egg and cheddar. I also got a cafe on leche (sweetened) with some sparkling water. Honey got a Cuban as well as an empanada. I thought my breakfast sandwich was good, it's hard to mess up a breakfast sandwich. The bread was very fresh Cuban bread but somehow I longed for a crunchier bread, maybe a bit more pressed? Honey felt the same about the bread used for his Cuban sandwich. In regards to his sandwich over all he thought it was an ok Cuban. He said it wasn't the best Cuban he's had in Tampa. He did enjoy his empanada. 

Overall the vibe is cool at this establishment. The cafe con leche was phenomenal and I'm not even a coffee drinker.  Next time I would like to sample some of their pastries, I was just way too full after that breakfast sandwich. I recommend checking this place out.
Great venue. Lots of TVs for game day, great appetizers (and food did not look bad either), dogs allowed upstairs and good amount of street parking.
Best sushi in Santa Barbara for sure, Luis was so kind and helpful I am for sure coming back again...it's a super chill restaurant with a very friendly staff

Four friends and I had dinner at The Block this weekend. We met there around 6:30 on Saturday and had to wait about 15 minutes for a table. We waited in the bar area and were very happy with our cocktails. 
   Once we were seated, we ordered 2 appetizers, the Ale & Cheddar dip with house-made pretzels and the brussel sprouts.....you heard me, a brussel sprout appetizer. Don't turn up your nose, it was fantastic! It will make a believer out of you. Seriously. We also demolished the pretzels and dip, stopping just short of licking the bowl. Which, by the way, one of my friends has been known to do in a restaurant.
   We all ordered a different entree: fish special, rib-eye, sirloin, scallop salad and a hamburger. Again, we were all very happy, except for a small mishap with the burger. There was a bit of inedible gristle in it, which my friend mentioned to our waiter. He apologized, manager came out and apologized, comped her dessert. Aside from the gristle, the burger was really good, cooked exactly as described by Jason, our waiter. I had the walleye, which I wasn't sure I was going to like, but I'm trying to eat more fish, so, what the heck. It was delicious. Cleaned my plate, which I usually don't do at restaurants because I like leftovers.
   We each ordered a different dessert. The best was a potted chocolate with toasted marshmallows on top. Coming in a close second was a brown sugar-coconut ice cream. Apple tart was also good. Our two least favorites were a dried cherry-chocolate bread pudding (a bit dry) and the chocolate-bacon ice cream (too much chocolate, not enough bacon).
   Although the place was busy, our service was good. Jason, our waiter, was extremely knowledgable and did not steer us wrong on any of his recommendations. 
All of us were pretty happy ladies when we left. I know we will be back!

Went to Distrito for lunch today with a few co-workers and everything was delicious! There was a group of 6 of us so we got a few plates of nearly everything to try. The guac is some of the best in the city tbh. We started with the Ensalada De Jicama and then had a series of things including the chicken enchilada, the short and mushroom flatbreads, the queso fundito (which is a cheese dip with pulled duck meat #yum) and the mahi mahi tacos -- which were fried to perfection. Everything was so fresh and amazing. I'll definitely be returning.
I love this place. Great miso soup, sushi, bento boxes, and friendly staff always.  I haven't tried any of the Korean specific foods yet, but I'll be back for bulgogi.

I love this juice. I've been getting two at once sometimes - made fresh, and fun flavor combo suggestions.

Also like the rewards program. It's pricey but healthy.
BEST BAGELS EVER!!!  The cream cheese is also really nice!  I had the pesto flavor.  YUM YUM!!
Our group of six hold a birthday dinner here. The price here is not cheap but the service and taste are totally worth the price. The wild boar bacon is really memorable.
Good Food, great service, great prices. Salsa bar is great! Highly recommended. Three locations conveniently located.

This used to be our favorite breakfast spot in Tucson so it's unfortunate that I never wrote them a positive review when I still felt that way. After two subpar experiences in a row though, I can no longer recommend it. On my previous visit, the food was simply subpar - the eggs weren't cooked well, the hash browns were raw, and everything had a dull flavor to it, in contrast to the freshness I remembered from prior visits. Today was the final straw though - short staffed, they managed to not even bring us two glasses of water before attempting and failing twice to make an adequate burrito; first they put the wrong ingredients in it, then a second one was thrown together with eggs that had not been cooked fully. My corn bread waffle was admittedly quite tasty and it's possible that the old spirit of the restaurant still resides there, in which it prided itself on flavorful local ingredients and unique breakfast creations. Unfortunately, given the relatively high prices on top of the aforementioned experiences, I will be avoiding until further notice.

We went here for lunch with the company and oh men, I never thought it was this big! It was a Wednesday and so we were expecting it was jampacked and so we had the reservation made. I was told you can't make reservation by calling, rather by doing it online, so take note of that. It was good we made the reservation because true enough, it is jampacked.

I like the menu because it offers a lot of variance in it. I suggest coming in with something in mind to eat because with a long list of their menu item, I would bet it will take you a lot of time to decide.

I always go with a salad for lunch and I've never had a salad with fish on it so I got the blackened salmon salad and it kind of met my craving for it. I wish they could have the option of having a different dressing on the side and not something that is already mixed. It will be good also to have a variety of greens to choose in there. I did like the caramelized nuts in the salad, it kind of complimented the saltiness of the salmon.

Overall, my experience is great. The service was fast and our server was overly kind.

I was told also that they have a good dinner menu here, especially with their microbrewery. I've seen the bottles of beer on every table so I kind of like got curious as to how good their beer is.

A coffee shop is only as good as your last visit. It's Saturday morning, I have been sitting in the drive thru for 15 minutes and haven't moved. I think they are waiting on Juan Valdez to roll up with his donkey with the next shipment of beans.

The experience was awful. Our server took our order and then forgot to input it into their system, it then took 22 minutes for her to realize it wasn't put in. She took our order again and then it took another 40 minutes to get our food. Yes it was a little busy however there were at least 5 other tables that were sat, orders taken, and then received their food all before us. We watched them come in at least a half hour after we were seated. When we finally attempted to pay their network went down and the manager proceeded to tell us it happens all the time and she has had to comp many orders because of network failure but refused to comp our order and made us wait until the network came back or we paid cash. I wish I could give less than one star. Also half of our burgers were incorrect or cold.

Bacon Cheeseburger - 4 Stars
Croquetas- 5 Stars

Good beer variety on tap. 

A true Gastropub. I felt like I took a step back in time when I walked through the door. 

The burgers are great and I highly recommend the cheeseburger with both cheddar and jack cheeses. Then add bacon to make it perfect. Ditch the fries and go for croquetas.

This location has a large, clean seating area and very friendly service. Unfortunately, the food quality does not match. The vegetables are not fresh; my cucumbers tasted really weird, as if they had been left in plastic for too long, and some of my spinach was wilted. Considering that this is a salad place, the vegetables should be much fresher. Also, I'm not really a fan of how finely the vegetables are chopped, especially in comparison to whole spinach leaves. The whole wheat rolls are very dense and kind of dry. I won't be returning anytime soon.

I always thought this place would look like an "old fashion dinner" with lots of fried food and was I wrong. Came here on a Sunday morning there was a long line of people waiting outside to be seated so I assumed that meant the food must be good or there is no other place open at this time. We decided to go on the wait list which was approximately 20-25 minutes. The wait  to sit seemed shorter than the time we waited for the food but the food was great. I love that I can order just one piece of French toast or pancakes and not be forced to eat a full plate. I ordered one French Toast topped with chocolate chips (fantastic), the smoked salmon (not too salty) and a pink grapefruit mimosa. The waitress was very friendly and definitely knew the menu. great place for breakfast, the burger in the lunch menu was also good and if you like Bloody Mary's you should try theirs. I found this place to be very loud so if you're looking for a quiet, conversation place this may not be your to go spot.
Ordered my food at 6:58. Got my food at 7:23. My order was wrong and my onion rings were cold. Got my money back and don't plan on going back anytime soon.

A very small Italian restaurant which serves up very generous portions at very reasonable prices.  And it's BYOB, so bring any bottle of wine you like and there is no corkage fee.  Very crowded quarters, too, so if you don't like literally sitting next to a stranger, this place ain't for you.  And it's cash only.

Was the food spectacular?  No, but all of it was very good.  Servers were indifferent and barely made eye contact (and also sloppily poured our wine) but otherwise, they were prompt and efficient.

Lobster ravioli was excellent and the homemade tiramasu was not too sweet and very light.  Everything else we tried hit high marks in flavor.

A solid choice.

Hands down the best Indian food in Reno. One of the best restaurants period! The tandoori is terrific! The Naan is out of this world. They have a number of vegetarian choices as well. I would recommend to anyone looking for something that is different from the typical American food and sushi spots.

Worked for this Dictator, tyrant Chef for a week decided it wasn't a good fit, parted ways. This asshole has the nerve, to "mail" my check out, so he says. Now today is Wednesday he says he mailed it Friday, do the math. I don't think it's fair when someone thinks it's funny or cute to play games with money that you have worked for because they have hard feelings. What an ass, I  have a family  yet he plays games and laughs b ecause he has the upper hand over the little man. My friends and I will be out to boycott and picket this racist establishment.
The atmosphere was inviting and the staff was extremely friendly. I ordered 2 donuts and a kolache to go and they didn't disappoint. If I'm in New Orleans again I'll be sure to come back.

I'm a California girl and this was my First time having TN bbq-it did not disappoint. I am not much of a Carnivore but I became a ravenous meat eater on our visit! Loved the bbq sandwiches m, sides m, hot sauce and they made a great whiskey sour! Great service and atmosphere too. Can't wait to go back... I keep thinking about that sandwich! We are moving to Nashville soon And this will definitely be a staple place to eat!

Great food, great service.  And, great views.  It ain't cheap folks, but you get what you pay for.  Everything, from the bread to the desert, was perfect.  Looking forward to returning and trying other dishes on the menu.  Unless you can devour a huge portion, entrees and pasta dishes can be split.  Or, when can't finish the generous portion, you can take home, which is what I did.

Stopped in for lunch today with my coworkers.  We're from out of town and this was the best rated chicken shop within walking distance of our hotel.  I ordered the Hot Chicken Po Boy with the Nashville Hot heat level, which is level 3 out of 4, 4 being the hottest.  I guess our food was taking a while to cook (we hadn't noticed) because our server Aubrey apologized for the wait and brought us a free order of fried pickles which were bomb.  They were only lightly breaded so you could still taste the pickle and not feel like you're clogging your arteries.  My sandwich was much larger than I expected.  I had really wanted like a large breast on a bun style sandwich but they didn't have one on the menu so I settled for the po boy.  It was still good though and the macaroni and cheese I had on the side was amazing!!  My coworkers both had the chicken and waffles, one with no heat and one with level 2.  They both said it was better than Roscoe's which is the famous chicken and waffles joint in Los Angeles where we're from.  I don't eat chicken and waffles but I know that means it was good!  Our server Aubrey came by again to let us know they accidentally made an extra macaroni and chicken waffle cone and offered it to us complimentary.  We tried it and it was delicious!  I actually wish I had ordered this over the sandwich, even though the sandwich was great too.  Apparently the chicken in the waffle cone was the same level of heat as my sandwich but it tasted much hotter oddly.  I like a medium kick but can't eat ghost peppers or raw jalapeños, and the level 3 was just fine for me.  Great food, great service, great experience!

For those complaining about a line in the drive through and indoors yes, there is typically a line but that's because everything is so good and they don't make it until you order it! If you don't want quality food go to McDonald's. Love this place! Took my parents from out of town here and they now have wanted to come back multiple times. Great place! Good portion sizes. Excellent quality of food.
Was down in clearwater area visiting family.  Staff was friendly food was fresh and would defifinilty come back here again when I'm in the area.

I was craving brunch on a Monday and I've been meaning to check this place out as the menu has a lot of creative options. Unfortunately, the meal was nothing to write home about. 

I should have known it was going to be a subpar experience when the hostess handed me the silverware and the menus and pointed to the stairs.  We sat ourselves upstairs at the bar. The vibe was really awkward.The music was quite low so all you hear is clanking of forks and the occasional hand dryer being used in the restrooms. The waitresses were huddled at a corner table talking amongst themselves. The bar was unkempt, the cooler doors smudged with layers of greasy fingerprints. It just seems like no one cares about this place.

We had the fried green tomatoes, which were good and the only redeeming thing about my experience here. The biscuit and gravy was 100% cold. I would have asked the servers to nuke it in the microwave but they were far in their corner, clearly didn't want to be bothered. The fried livers were soso and the duck waffle had no duck. 

No one cares here. It seems like at one point they did but now it's just a restaurant that has aged ungracefully, lost its sparkle. Oh well. The search for good brunch continues.

My family and I came in this morning and it was a great experience! Liza was our server and she did a phenomenal job. She was so friendly and attentive to every need. She was so good with our daughter that loves talking to everyone. She never seemed overwhelmed and always had a smile. The food was great too. We will be back next weekend and requesting Liza!
Good service and fun diner. We enjoy the Sloppy Joe's and burgers with a chocolate malt. The prices are really affordable with a good selection of diner items.
Super speedy service. Solid breakfast basics and coffee at great price.  Full menu served all day too I believe.

Great little restaurant! Seems to be pretty authentic thin crust Italian pizza. They have Coke products, so that's the first plus. 

We were seated quickly and ordered three build your own pizzas. Mine was garlic butter, prosciutto, and artichoke - I tried to recreate the best pizza I had in Italy. It was not the best I've had, but definitely solid. They were not generous with the prosciutto but I get it. The garlic butter was totally delicious. 

The biggest drawback is that the food was honestly overpriced for what it is. I've had fantastic pizza for half the price of this place. I assume they have to have high prices to afford their location, but it's high enough that I'd hesitate coming back again.

Wow. I paid a visit based upon great reviews on Yelp as well as that "other" review site. This was my first experience with Ethiopian cuisine, and it was outstanding. Previous reviews are spot on. I opted to start with an order of vegetarian sambussa. Great flavor, perfect for two or three people, but too much for one. Ye Bag Watt was a delicious entree--spicy, but not hot. Each accompanying side dish was tasty, and the flavors were unique in the best possible way. Thanks to other reviewers, I went easy on the injera. Even so, I felt bad, as I could not finish my food. I opted for hot tea, and it was both fragrant and delicious. A very nice way to end the meal. 
I will add that the lady serving me was exceptionally helpful and gracious, even when I told her I left my wallet in my hotel room. "Come back in one or two days, I know you will be back." (I of course dashed back, got my wallet and paid right away)
I encourage locals and visitors alike to visit. The place was virtually empty on a Monday evening. Restaurants like this deserve support.

My wife and I were looking for a new place to try for a date night and we were really in the mood for Italian.  This place really fit the bill.  The servers were friendly and helpful and the food was delicious.  Highly recommend the Sicilian Chicken if you are looking for something spicy.  After appetizer, entrees, desert and a beer, we were surprised to see how reasonable the total bill was.  Portions were very generous, so you definitely get your money's worth.  Happy to say that we have found our go to restaurant for local Italian food!

I'm ashamed I lived in Wynnewood for so long before trying this place. Sometimes you're not looking for some artisan flatbread. Sometimes you just need 1 good classic pepperoni slice, a cheesesteak, or a chicken parm sandwich. This place will satisfy the craving!

I don't write a lot of reviews but this one is the most friendly lunch place in Fairmount. Their salmon sandwich, Cobb salad with sesame oil dressing are my favorite! Very reasonable price. Very friendly family.

I was really looking forward to dining here due to the high ratings and comments. The staff seemed like they wished they could be any place else and it carried through. the variety and costs are both good, but the food was on the bland side. Minimal options for appetizers and bodega like atmosphere without the camaraderie and banter typically found in this type of neighborhood joint.

Easily the best Indian food in Tucson!!!
I'd also say this restaurant is in my top five places to eat!
I had the chicken tikka masala and my wife the lamb  roghan josh.  Both excellent!  Great complex flavors and the right amount of heat.  I've never had a masala this good before!  I've had the usual creamy buttery tikka masala but they take it to a whole other level!  Highly recommend!!!
I plan on returning weekly and trying everything on their menu!
One of the best steaks I had, great mash potatoes and fries. Also loved the strawberry lemonade. My wife and I will come back again. The only problem service too slow.

Sushi Nara is a great sushi option on this side of town. I'm usually skeptical of sushi in landlocked states but I was very pleasantly surprised. I've been here twice and really enjoyed my food each time.

Tried this place on a whim a few months ago figuring it had to either be great or awful. Glad to say it was great. The catfish is good and the turkey and dressing tastes home made. They also have real mashed potatoes; a must for me. If you're in the area give this place a try.
