Come here for brunch and leave your diet plans at the door! 
I think this place is all about brunch. It does get crowded, so be prepared, but brunch means you'll get to try their "Monte Cristo" and "Chicken and Toast." And you won't feel like restraining your mimosa intake. The weekly breakfast menu is smaller; although, the pastries just might make up for the lack of diversity since the cronuts and scones are top notch.
One menu misstep in my opinion is the "Veggi Beni," and the "A.M. Relleno" could use some tweaking. I thought the texture of the "Veggi Beni" was all wrong. The egg, hollandaise, and vegetables made for a slippery mess. The "A.M. Relleno" needed more mole sauce and spice (I couldn't taste much of that poblano), and could have been kicked up with some protein, maybe steak. 
On a recent visit, the friendly bartender mentioned that they wanted to create a boutique vibe, and when I thought about it, I did kind of feel like I was in eating in a small, organic beauty store-turned-restaurant. But the crafty decor is appropriate for the crafty menu, which I don't have too many complaints about.

Went to this restaurant last night about an hour before closing.  Service was fast due to NO ONE being there.  The food was typical Cajun/ Creole with some other added flare.....see their website for more details.

Beef cheek or pork shoulder the way to go. Service was tremendous similar to the experience we had at their sister restaurant Cavan. The outdoor garden made it fun to jump back and forth while waiting for the next course and a drink in our hand. Also had the champagne and fries - pleasant surprise.

Stopped on our way back north, so glad we did.
Staff is wonderful and our breakfast was delicious
I got the Cheesesteak.  It looked like a cheesesteak.  They sold a lot of pizza while I was there.

THE BEST CHINESE FOOS HANDS DOWN!!!!  

My wife and I have been ordering takeout from Asian Kitchen for the past few years.  The food never disappoints, is always fresh, and the orders are always correct!  Never had a bad meal.  The owners are super friendly and amazing people!
Mediocre food with terrible service, we won't be going back again any time soon!

If I could give this place more stars I would!  We arrived in the off season.  Doug was there alone, which was fine as customer flow was slow.  We ordered a mahi sandwich and a burger, fries and pasta salad.  Doug was pleasant, friendly, efficient, professional and welcoming.  Everything you look for in a restaurant!  The food was all fresh, cooked to perfection and uber flavorful!  We tipped 40% if that tells you anything :-)  We were more than satisfied...it is always a hope when you find a little hole in the wall place that it be this awesome :-)

We dropped on a Friday night without reservations and was able to snag a spot at the bar. The restaurant had a good amount of patrons despite the beginning of the summer shore season.   
My husband was over the moon with the beer selection and enjoyed talking to the Victory brewmaster that was there that night, the bartenders were spot on with their knowledge of the food and cocktails.
Husband was busy ordering the beer flights, while I was perusing the menu.
I was so excited to try the roast bone marrow, but alas, it was not meant to be. It was sold out and i was informed that it would take another two days to be put back on since the bones are brined for that long= sounds delicious!! I then moved on to the a couple of the Cape May Salts- it was brought out with an array of sauces, a house made migonette, hot sauces and the standard cocktail.  Yum! 
Pig tails with fennel agrodolce- this was in interesting dish- very gelatinous and greasy, full of flavor but I wouldn't order it again. (We have puppies with docked tails which completely grossed me out when I made the correlation) 
Beer fat french fries- you really couldn't go wrong with this choice.

There is a private room above the bar that can be rented out for parties. It over looks the restaurant and kitchen area. It was just a interesting way to incorporate the use of space.  I like that you can purchase the kitchen a six pack to thank then for their hard work, although I hope they aren't drinking and cooking at the same time!

The only annoyance were the neighboring restaurant employees stopping in and grabbing a beer during their breaks. There seemed to be an endless stream and I did not like hearing complain about working.

All in all, Alla Spina has some growing pains but I'm glad to have them in the neighborhood. We would stop in their again and great some eats and drinks. Be sure to check out the tile work leading into the bathroom!

I can't rate the food because it hasn't arrived yet. Our order was placed at 7:45 pm. It is now 9:45 pm and still no food. I called twice and the hostess said "sorry, we have a lot of orders". Our expected delivery time was 8:45. The hostess didn't have an answer when I asked why they never updated the delivery time. I would have canceled if I knew I'd be waiting over 2 hours to eat dinner. At this rate, I will be in bed before the delivery arrives. This is the worst delivery experience I have ever had.

The building is really neat and sets expectations high.  The service was pretty good and they had plenty of options for dinner.

For nearly $30 a person I expected a little more wow factor I guess.  There wasn't anything food or drinkwise that stuck out at me or made me think "I'd like to have that again!". 

There were no issues with the food or visit just nothing that we ordered made this place special.  There location is pretty cool.  After dinner make sure to take a stroll down the river walk.
The best pizza I have had in years!! Very friendly service and fast delivery. I would seriously come back to Spring Hill for this pizza.

The food is excellent - healthy, organic and deliciously prepared. The wide range caters to all taste buds from vegan to burger lovers. Gino, the soup man, outdoes himself with the daily choices. And, the tomato soup is available every day. Keeping up with the latest food trends, they even offer jack fruit as a meat alternative in more than one dish. I love the South Reno location in the shopping center on South Meadows and Double R.
Been on my list of places to try and finally made it in!!!! I LOVE the thin crust can't wait to return!! Great staff also!!! GO BEARS!!!
Everyone can get exactly what they want. We love this place! Multiple locations makes it easy to never miss out when in St. Louis.
The grouper sandwich is my favorite thing to get here! We always have fast and great service. Servers and bartenders are very attentive and the drinks are amazing!

We eat here nearly once a week
Highly recommend the egg rolls the rooster sauce wings and the Brussels sprouts and the shrimp tacos are freaking awesome. 
The guys are really nice.  Can get a drink at the bar. No kids though unless you sit out front.

Absolutely delicious dessert bar selling sweet  treats galore and some with an alcohol pairing.
Swah rey pronounced "soiree" has an artsy and whimsical decorl which you can see throughout the store.
You can't miss this made from scatch treats storefront which looks more like a sweet boutique.
They have samples available and their best of the best is layed out all in front you.  With a variety of mini cupcakes and cake slices to choose from your sweet treat fulfillments are only a choice away. Having difficulty choosing, buy a variety box of your choice. Dont forget to pair your dessert with a shot of something alcoholic like wine or go the non alcoholic route and choose a coffee.
There is so much to choose from here. My personal favorite was the cookie dough and funfetti. But they had cool flavors like strawberry lemonade, pancakes & bacon, and chocolate salted caramel just to name a few. Don't want to give all the sweet surprises away but this dessert bar also sells sugar cookies, pretzels,  cream pies, dessert bars and they even have a treat for your 4 legged friends.
Service here is also super friendly so that's an extra plus so stop by with your pup and you both get some treats!

Hello everyone, 
I would like you all to know that Flamestones is back open and they have ALL new furniture and decor and most importantly noted, are all set up for fine dining at a distance inside. I visited last night and was soo happy to see my friends Nichola tossin up the fine Liquor and wine behind the bar, Allison serving up the best service at my table and Emil running around over seeing everything from the front of the house to the back so to speak.I had STONE OVEN FLATBREAD WITH STEAK & BLUE CHEESE which was nothing less than Awesome along with a cocktail (or two) from Nick. PLEASE GO and experience yourself. Tell them BOSTON TODD sent ya !

My husband and I received a gift certificate from our HOA last year because we had the most decorated house in our condo association. We have been sitting on this for awhile, but luckily - we FINALLY got to try it out.

On Saturday, we decided to order take out. We ordered the bruschetta trio, a 12'' Don pizza and a 12'' Arugula with Prosciutto pizza. We followed the prompts to order online, as we were ready to get home from a busy day. We showed up at the establishment to pick up our food and was greeted by the nicest hostess. She redirected me to the take-out counter and they quickly ensured that I was taken care of.

My perception of the establishment was that it was very clean, well lit, and crowded! ALL GOOD signs. We were looking forward to our dinner and couldn't wait to get home. While some people think bringing pizza home may not be the best option (I'm a pizza snob), all of the things we ordered were absolutely delicious.

We will 100% be back with our family and friends!

Café Mosaics is a nice restaurant with a nice vibe. Unfortunately, the product doesn't match the pitch.

To the point: the food is boring, standard fare. I find that much of it is simply lower-quality, pricier versions of the food I eat at home. It's certainly edible, but there's much better. I'd go as far as to say that it's my least favorite vegetarian fare that I've had. Being a vegan in the area, however, I've spent a fair bit of time there, and I've found that the menu does vary in quality. Sandwiches are great, breakfasts bland. Save room for the vegan chocolate cake too. My recommendation, however: go to Friends & Neighbours next door and have their Vegetarian Sandwich.

Before moving to Edmonton, I asked a vegan friend from here about vegetarian dining. He said "there's nothing that great here, but for lack of better options, people go crazy over average food." While this isn't a fair generalization (see the deliciousness of Padmanadhi, Langano Skies, ...) I now realize he had Café Mosaics in mind. He did have a point though: take a first-timer here and they'll enjoy it. However, why settle for worse?

I have a call in to the Manager and will be contacting corporate offices tomorrow. This is the worst Waffle House ever! Ordering by phone was not exactly friendly but I thought they might've been busy. I was told food would be 5mins. Went quickly to find that their waffle machines weren't signing well so I waited. It was 8pm and the place was empty. The floors were filthy and at least four tables were a mess. The counters were not clean and there was food on the floor.

After three waffle attempts and an incident where part of my order almost walked out the door in another take out customer's bag... my order was finished and half cold. I paid and went home to find that my eggs were not included and an order of bacon was missing. I called to ask for them to make the missing items and returned.

Not only had they not cooked the missing items, I was told that I hadn't ordered them! The clerk Dajuana was rude and yelling! When I responded, the racist waitress says "You people all think you can come here and talk to me like this!"  I reminded her that I was the customer and that I was only one person but that didn't stop her from screaming at me, refusing to tell me who the manager was, and practically refusing to order the remaining food items on my behalf. She cooked herself food, told me it was shift change time and yelled that she is a child and shouldn't be spoken to like this because she has a parent! I was shocked by such bad behavior and the cook and other waitress seemed amused.

I will never go back to this Waffle House and I will not stop contacting the manager, district managers and corporate offices as long as this waitress works for them.

We were really looking forward to having good Indian food.
The signature curry was watery and bland- told our waiter that when he asked and told some manager when he asked, but alas, nothing.  why ask if you aren't going  to make it right?good wine ..
Plenty of other places to eat...

I love Qdoba. This one is close to my job and is the reason I'm here often. I stop in for breakfast quite often. It's pretty quick and clean and I have even seen the managers checking the temperatures on the food to make sure they are adequately being kept at a safe temperature at all times. I learned about that in my Sanitation class for Culinary School and am amazed how little I see it happening in places. 

The morning staff recognizes my face and tends to know what I want when I get there.That's the old school way of things - when food service people remember faces and orders. It reminds me of a diner. The queso here is always good and hot (which I can't say the same for all Qdobas around the city...I've had some that tasted like cheese water). The ingredients have little to no cross contamination (you know I'm always checking for that) and although it's busy during lunch time and has a small interior, they have outdoor seating for the spring/summer months and there's hardly ever been a time I wanted to dine in and couldn't find anywhere to sit. 

The downfall is the parking lot (if it's lunchtime). It can get crazy and busy and there might be a fight for a parking space, but if you can get around that, this is a great Qdoba to start your morning or your afternoon with !

I just ordered take out. I'm speechless! We ordered Ribs, Brisket, BBQ Beans, Fries and Cole Slaw. Amazing. The meats are seasoned perfectly and you don't need sauce. However the sauce is incredible. South Tampa has new best BBQ in the South!

My review is for the cookies.  I had the double chocolate cookie, pecan shortbread, and chocolate chip.   The pecan shortbread was the best of the three and I'm so glad I didn't get more because I would not have been able to stop myself from devouring them all.  Plus, they're one net carb per cookie so you can have a few without being totally overcome with guilt.   They're $1.75 a piece currently and if you buy 5 you get the 6th free.

I also purchased several cupcakes but I'm honestly just not a huge fan of almond flour cakes so I can't hold that bias against them.  The frosting however was superb in texture, albeit a little less sweet than I'd normally enjoy.  

I'd go back repeatedly just fort the cookies and I'm hoping to try some bread from there soon.

On Valentine's Day 2009, I had one really great meal (Red Robin) and one really terrible meal (see my review of Lorenzo's). Granted, I love me a good cheeseburger and fries and that's really difficult to mess up. But the service combined with the superb burgers has made me a fan!

We got to Red Robin about 45 minutes before we were scheduled to catch a movie. Upon being seated, we let our server know that we were in a hurry and he took care of us! He placed our orders immediately and even offered his recommendations on how the burgers should be cooked ("Do you like it with a little bit of pink, or with a lot of pink?"). We got our food in record time and the burgers were cooked exactly how we asked. Perfecto!

Although it shouldn't be a tall order to go to a restaurant and get the food you asked for in a timely manner, it is a problem for many restaurants (again, see my review on Lorenzo's). But our time at Red Robin was exceptional, especially since our server was really young (couldn't have been more than 20 years old) and handled our requests with ease. I actually got on the Red Robin website a few days later and praised his performance. The manager actually called to confirm his receipt of my letter and thanked me for the feedback. You don't get that too much these days.

Yay to Red Robin! I look forward to going back again soon!

Parking is odd and setup to help you ding another car.
The food was below par. 
The staff was very friendly. But the prices I think are steep based on the food quality. While I would expect some greasy food at a Meat and 3 I would question why everything is so greasy. So this company takes it up a notch and adds pepper to their food. I guess that counter balances the grease. How can you get carrots greasy?

Regardless, you can go. But don't be shocked. You have been warned.
A hidden gem in Northern Liberties. Amazing atmosphere inside and out, amazing food, and great prices! This place is a must! The staff is friendly and it's a byob.

Almaz really is a small cafe.  Walking it, i had to ask if food was served beyond the delicious looking pastries, coffees, and smoothies promoted at the "bar" area. The restaurant features loft area dining for roughly 8-10 people, in addition to the cozy first floor seating.  My selection was prepared in a satisfactory time period and delivered to me as I sat in the window and people watched.  I thoroughly enjoyed my veggie combination and Keye Wot (beef stew), which I surprisingly ate completely....  Now I'm filled and ready to sleep!

I'm Indonesian but am not from Philly. I came by to get a few things to bring home.  I know they jacked up the price just because I am not a regular and there is no price list.  I didn't appreciate that.

Food is good and authentic.  Get the soto betawi (Indonesian food).

This is a relatively new establishment on the Santa Barbara restaurant scene, and I couldn't be happier!  For Santa Barbara, the prices are relatively inexpensive, about $16/person for entree + soft drink.

The menu is simple and elegant, coordinating appropriately with the restaurant's "farmhouse chic" decor.  The service was quick and friendly, especially for a Sunday morning brunch.  My girlfriend and I arrived around 10:30 or 11AM and didn't have to wait at all.  This, I imagine, is due to its status as the new kid on the block.  (Jeannine's, on the other hand, had a massive line out the door.)

My girlfriend had the fig French toast and I had their rendition of biscuits and gravy.  The French toast was very good, not too sweet like one often finds French toast.  The biscuits and gravy were also delicious.  The biscuits, unlike the traditional Southern biscuit, were thin and crunchy and topped with a piece of fried chicken and drizzled in a jalapeno bacon gravy.  The gravy only had a hint of jalapeno, barely giving your taste buds a kick.   I really enjoyed it!  The dish also included two eggs and country potatoes.

We will definitely be taking our boyfriends back here for brunch again!  Kudos on the new establishment!

Try #2 7/21/16:
After receiving a very nice message from the owner in response to my prior review (below) albeit a belated response, the owner offered to buy my meal if I let him know I as coming, but instead decided to try this place again on my own dime with hopes of actually getting to try the food. We came in at 7:22pm, were immediately welcomed and told to have a seat where we liked. We chose inside since it was so hot outside, and our server came right over with menus. Our server was super nice and was able to answer our questions about the wing sauces and the type of fries they serve. Food came out pretty quickly. I ordered my wings extra crispy and they came out perfectly. The Tingle sauce was just hot enough. The fries (shoestring cut) were crispy and had a seasoning on them that was good - seems like paprika, sugar, salt... It was good! My hubby didn't care for it though. The chicken tenders were super crispy, very good, but just a bit too much black pepper. The ranch and honey mustard were ok-good, and I'd like to see a teriyaki sauce offered. Overall, our experience was very good, it was 1000x better than our last experience. Yes, we got wet naps! We'll come back. I bumped this place to 4 stars. 

Prior review: 
Was looking forward to trying this new restaurant in Westchase, however, despite there being lots of waitstaff standing around, and after being told to seat ourselves in the outdoor patio area, no one came to wait on us! So we left.  Not only that, but several servers had come out to the patio out three or four times, while literally only caring one or two drinks in their hands at a time, but never came to wait on us. It was somewhat busy inside and outside, but by no means packed, and there were tons of dirty tables both inside and outside with lots of tables waiting for their checks. It's obvious this place is poorly managed. It's a shame because Westchase is a great place to be.

The marathon burger is the best vegan burger I have ever had..... ever. Even my carnivorous friends opt for the marathon. House-made ketchup is also delicious. You may have to wait for a table during peak hours, but you can usually grab a spot for 2 at the bar. The  decor is simple/clean.... like a really fancy picnic. It fits the menu/vibe, and I always like to support restaurants who buy local and organic when possible.

The only reason this place does not get 5 stars is the service. I have several friends who work there who are awesome..... so my service has been great for the most part. However, I have a number of friends who had less than stellar service.... a shame considering what a great place this is. It's pretty hit or miss though so I wouldn't let that stop you from going..... it's worth it for the marathon burger.

The drinks are a lot more bitter than the other Starbucks in the area. When there are a lot of people, there is no rush to make the drinks; most of the employees take their time and if you are in a rush, this starbucks is NOT the place for you.

I thought this place was just okay. The service was very good, personable and fast. The food was a little hit and miss though. The portions were also small on the pasta sampler. A little too much salt on the food, so I left hungry and finished my evening elsewhere.
Cool pub with good beers and the Kale salad was great.  I liked the vibe, the food was fresh and the beers were cold.  Nuff said!

I was excited to try the okra gumbo with healthier options amidst the typical market, French quarter fare. Unfortunately, I was disappointed. $15 for 12oz of mediocre rice and okra with a few shrimp and turkey sausage. The "toast" was 2 1/4 pieces of bread. In all I waited 20 mins for the to go order while the family had eaten from other vendors and started back on the journey. Not what I expected from the other great reviews. Bummer

Was there last night with friends.. Atmosphere was great, mixture of ages. Decor was so nice felt like I was in a modern cabin.  Bathroom was so clean and it smelled like vanilla bean.  Staff super friendly and the prices are not expensive... A live band was playing and they were great. Definitely will come back with friends also great place to host a party. Wish I would have taken a picture so you can all see how nice this place is.
Best in Nashville.  Fantastic steam buns and you can build you own ramen bowl.  So good we went back two days in a row!

The food is delicious and reasonably priced. The best deal though are the fried wings. I never thought I would order wings from a Chinese place but this is my jam. I order them any time I have friends over to watch The Ohio State Buckeyes. Buy a few wing sauces from Publix or BW3 and treat yourself right. You CANNOT beat the price.

Stopped in for their lunch special: Stromboli, Breadsticks, and a drink for $10. Now, I've been on a real pizza kick these last couple of weeks, and I regret to report, I was underwhelmed by Wise Guys. 

First things first, I felt very awkward ordering...almost like I was bothering the person at the front counter...I'd never been here before, and since I love to eat local, I was excited to try! I was just asking questions about the menu when a woman came up from the back and began speaking OVER me to the customers behind me..wait...what?!?!

Alas, I continue ordering and after I get my total and wait for what I was hoping to be a knock my pants off stromboli, I get back to my desk at work to begin my meal...and I take a nice big honkin bite into a cold stromboli...oh man. Now, I just ate around the middle (which was the cold part) and that wasn't bad, but it wasn't great either. I want to go back and try just getting slices next time, but hopefully in the future the service staff won't look at me like I have four heads and a dog flying out of my ear...

Loved the burger! My husband loved his also. The sweet potato fries were awesome and the service great. i don't know why people are giving this place a hard time this is waaaaay better than baileys range if u ask me. Also a great beer selection. I must say this is the best burger I have had in Stl so far.
So give it a try and if there is something wrong just ask the waiter or tell them what u need....it's not rocket science. It's just a good burger.
Great atmosphere. Amazing food. The veal saltimbocca was flavorful, but not too salty. We shared and eggplant tower appetizer that was in a garlic and oil sauce. BYOB, so it is relatively cheap.

We came here at around 8pm and waited for maybe 15 mins, which wasnt too long, but it was odd that the hostess didnt take anyones names and was seating people out of order (even the same sized parties). Anyways, not a big deal. We had the dinner menus. The chicken/andouille gumbo was amaaaazing. Crawfish gumbo was also delicious. The cajun shrimp plate was okay, the shrimp tasted and looked like the frozen ones, the jambalaya was great. Praline ice cream was great to top off the meal. Service was nice.

We were visiting from Knoxville, Tn. We were staying at a hotel not far from this resturant. I and my son really wanted breakfast food so we stopped at Ihop express and we really didnt have the patience to wait for 25 minutes for food so we were already HANGRY, LOL ! So my husband saw this resturant right across the street and said lets go eat there. I really didnt want to eat here because my taste buds were set for eggs and pancakes ONLY !! 
I'm so glad we gave this resturant a try it was fast and delicious. I normally have to ask for a to go box...I ate everything on both my plates. The waiter gave us his best when it came to customer service, He was amazingly nice. Inside was very clean and if u go during the fall/winter tell them to sit u in the back away from the door. Because when that door open u can feel the cold breeze, We were in the back and I felt warm in the area we were assigned to. If I ever come back to the Nashville area this will be the only mexican resturant  I will eat at. They do have Vegetarian options, I had the vegetarian plate and super super delicious ! Im a very happy customer.

Iv tried this place for the second time. First time I got a burrito and the second time I got the fish tacos a plantains. The only thing I felt was made well were the plantains. Iv made plantains before there isn't much to them. Though they could have over cooked them but they were just right. The taco and burrito were just average. I wouldn't get them again. The tortillas are not as fresh as I prefer. The place is a bit cold and service was ok. My boyfriend got the side order of fries- they came out cold and even if they were hot I'm not sure how tasty they would have been. Not a fan of this place.

So my friend invited me to this spot. I was a little skeptical because the reviews seemed very 50/50. However my friend said he gives the food a 5 out of 5. 

So we get there and it's sort of self serve-ISH. You order your food, get a buzzer and when it goes off you go and grab your food from the window. There is a bar (doesn't appear to be fully stocked), but has enough options. 

I ordered the Chicken Fajita Taco -- SO GOOD! It's funny because I don't personally eat tomatoes and blue cheese crumbles, but I left it all on there and took a bite and it was SO good! I added a little of the hot sauce on it (They hace sauces on the table). My friend ordered some sort of burrito that didn't LOOK appetizing but it's his favorite. 

We also tried all of the desserts: Cinnamon churros, Oreo churros and another item that I can't pronounce. The Cinnamon churros are SO GOOD! The Oreo Churros are pretty decent but I have to be in the mood for them because I'm not an "Oreo eater" lol. The 'other' dessert I won't be buying again though. It's basically a thin piece of hollow bread with cinnamon/sugar on it and it comes with some icing. I would've better preferred just a bread knot that dips in icing. It was just thin for no reason lol. Try the churros though! 

The atmosphere was great. TVs and music. Friendly vibes. 

The reviews I previously read were many complaints about the service BUT I had a great experience with their service. I was there until they closed and a rather large sized family came in and didn't get their food until closing time and the cook made sure to tell them not to rush and take their time. He was very polite. i just so happen to notice him bringing out their food and telling them to take their time. So I was pleasantly surprised being that the reviews said different. 

One of the young ladies even came and grabbed our trays.

Wanted to try this place so went on Friday and we liked it very much. Not fancy but the food was very good with  a kick. We will bring friends next time .
It's BYOB AND THEY SERVE A POT OF NICE TEA .

Have come here a couple times and every time I am just not impressed with the service or fancy pants coffee. First time I went to buy coffee for a friend and the girl helping me, while very nice, did not know anything about their coffee, while the roast master or whatever he's called was talking to his girlfriend and drinking his own coffee. If I feel like mediocre way too hot coffee I'll go there again but until that day I'll be going to less pretentious cafés.

We've eaten here several times since the new owners took over the previous "Thai Smile 2" and it is SO much better.  We love the new decor and everything we've had here is great.  The tom yum soup is delicious and the pad thai is the best I've had in the city (other than Thai Spice in Greenwood).  The red curry, laad nar and pad seuw are always great.  We can't wait to go back and try everything on the menu!

Food=3 Stars Service=2 stars which makes that 2.5 stars 
I've never felt sooo rushed to order food.  The waitress seemed like in a hurry.  I told her it was my first time here and she didn't give me enough time to look at the menu and literally pulled the menu from my hand to turn it over and tell me to order this and that.  WTH?  As I was browsing through their menu, I felt sooo Rushed! 

We quickly decided on the seafood pancake which was big and thick but I was a little overwhelmed with the big pieces of green onions.  I mean if you're an onion lover go for it.  It wasn't bad though.  For sushi, we got the sweetheart roll, red dragon, and crazy roll.  The sweetheart was the best out of all.  The other two were just alright. 

At the end when we paid the check she brought it out and left, came back a minute later and saw that we weren't done writing the tip and total, then said "Omg you're still not done yet?" Geeeeez lady.  She was so rushy rushy.

Nothing special.  Atmosphere struck me as somewhat cheap.  Most of the food was decent, but none of it was great.  The Spanish sausage reminded me way too much of the packaged major-brand sausage you can buy at your local Wal-Mart.  Don't come here expecting food that resembles something you'd actually get in Barcelona.

On the plus side, the service was attentive.

This place is rock solid.  Stopped in for a bite with a friend on a Saturday and there wasn't an empty seat in the house the entire time we were there.  I usually get the brussels sprouts and the Diavolo but this time opted for the cauliflower and The Joey - sausage was seasoned perfectly.  Food comes out straight from the oven. Service has always been friendly and engaging.  Great spot for a pizza!

Why did I end up here? Oh right, because I relinquished control to a group of guys out on the town after a conference... It was a Thursday evening, late at night, and the place was dead. Surprisingly though it proved somewhat impossible to get a drink without actually going up to the bar (apparently the staff had enough of serving tables for the night?) 

a cross between a hooters and a creepy catholic school girl fetish, the 'uniforms' are either the best or worst part, depending on your point of view. food was pretty standard fried fare and they had some beers for sale. nothing too special here. at least hooters has that amazing chicken sandwich going for them (though I still don't go there for a plethora of other reasons).

Hilarious sidenote, as we were leaving I snapped a shot of their thermostat which had a setpoint of 63 degrees F. It was a brisk 71 in that place for sure, but no chance of 63.

Love love love their pizza!!!!  Hunter is awesome!!! The person above who complained....I think the Tahoe thin air has affected her brain cells!! Jammin' Jamin is a great bartender So excited they opened another WGP......they are the BEST in Reno

I've heard so many things about Morrows so it was a must that I try. This was my first time after months of attempts due to the high volume of traffic this place gets. So let's get this review started. The atmosphere is awesome. When I stepped in our heard the voice of Jagged Edge on the radio, I instantly began to rock and sing to the music as we waited for a table. Standing in the front I noticed how small the space was, so the wait could take longer if you have a large group. Luckily for me I had a party for two so I was seated in less than 5 minutes on a Saturday evening. The service and staff was great, very friendly, attentive and welcoming. I tried the chargrilled oysters which were stuffed with crabmeat and the crawfish pasta. The oysters were the star of the show! Seasoned to perfection and they were big. Now as for the crawfish pasta I was disappointed. The fried fish that was on top was delicious but the pasta sauce was runny and not creamy at all. I could taste a lot of butter and pepper. If it was creamier I would have been blown through the roof because it was filled with crawfish. Overall I enjoyed the experience and would come again to give it another try.

Maybe my expectations were too high due to the chef's table hype, but I thought the tacos were just decent! 4 of us ordered a 1/2 kg of barbacoa, and it comes with all the sides and 12 tortillas to make your own tacos. I felt like the meat was a little dry and lacked much flavor, but it still tasted good! We came at 10am on a Saturday morning, and there was no line.

Beware they are cash only!

I reserved the small patio area at the Rusty Nail for an engagement party I was throwing for some friends. When I arrived 30 minutes early, the manager and bartender were already outside and came right over to introduce themselves. In true New Orleans fashion, the weather was not cooperating and there was a storm that was likely to hit right as friends were supposed to arrive. Luckily, they had already thought ahead and reserved some space inside for us in case the weather did take a turn for the worse. We decided to take them up on their offer and move our small party inside. The guys were so awesome and even set up an extra table for us and covered the piano in the back so we could put food on top. We had a wonderful time celebrating the engagement and were checked on multiple times throughout the evening by at least 4-5 different staff members. Everyone was so kind and helpful and although I was sad we were unable to make use of the beautiful patio area, they were on point and able to accommodate us regardless of the weather. I will definitely be continuing to frequent the Rusty Nail often and I recommend them to everyone, whether you are looking for a place to have a gathering, or just looking for a chill place with good vibes to grab a drink.

-Rubbery lobster tail
-Extremely over cooked meat
-Shorted our ice cream and green tea
-Servers acting like "zombies" 
-Small, overpriced plates


This is the first review I have ever written.  I registered with Yelp to specifically write this review.  When a dining experience is this inexcusable  that I have to go out of my way and take time out of my schedule to warn others to rethink their decision to go to Benihana's, that should be your first warning!  My wife and I ordered from the six course menu.  She had the steak and lobster tail. I had the teriyaki combo - chix, steak and shrimp.  The steak which we both ordered rare was cooked well done.  Plates were about $40 each and were supposed to be six courses.  I was handed the check immediately upon finishing my main course.  We were not offered green tea or ice cream (both items part of the meal).  Our children's meals were brought to the table about half way into our main course.  Honestly, at the risk of loosing you, the readers, interest I'm going to stop now.  It was our first and last time to a Benihana's.  I was under the impression we were going out for fine dining.  Isn't that the image Benihana's promotes?   I've had MUCH BETTER meals at the cheap buffet for $25 vs $120!  Save your time, money and frustration - eat ANYWHERE ELSE!

The atmosphere is casual and the music is pleasant.  You can actually carry on a conversation and hear each other--so nice to dine and visit at the same time. The food is very tasty. However, you would not want to be in a hurry because this is not fast food.  

Typical New Orleans menu but I'm Metairie. Yeah!
Really good food! Amazing service. The server Paulina was so nice and welcoming to me.

The food is very good. I enjoy the service, at times it could be better but when it's busy you have to understand the servers can't spend as much time at each table. My daughter and I really enjoy coming here, to me it's a real nice addition to the Blue Bell area.

Their motto is "Brunch born in New Orleans," which is disrespectful to New Orleans. We had a group of 3 at 12:00 pm on a Tuesday. We were seated right away. The hostess was so nice.

Here's what we got:
- Boozy Iced Coffee ($10): Not worth it.
- Nola Style Iced Coffee ($5): Fine.
- Hot Chocolate ($4): Not worth it.
- Seasonal Beignets (Peaches & Cream) ($7): These came after our entrees, so they took this off the bill without us even asking, which was very nice. However, they were terrible and not anything close to resembling beignets from New Orleans.
- Sweet Heat Chicken & French Toast Bites ($14.50): The "French toast" was actually croutons. They looked like croutons and once we stuck our fork in them, or rather, stabbed our fork in them because they were so hard, they tasted like croutons too. The chicken was very good. But the French toast was far from
French toast.
- The Peacemaker (Corned Beef Benedict & One Tomato, Two Tomato Benedict) ($16): We preferred the Corned Beef Benedict over the One Tomato, Two Tomato Benedict. Both were lacking though. 
- Classic Buttermilk Pancake ($2.50): Did not taste like a pancake. I don't know how to explain it, but all 3 of us tried it and agreed.
- B.Y.O. Omelet ($10.50 + $1 for every extra ingredient, so $12.50): The omelet was good. The biscuit was hard.

It took a long time to get our drinks and our food. The food sucked. We were so disappointed in this restaurant. We would never go back.

A group of 8 of us dropped in for a late dinner on the Saturday Dec 29th.  The restaurant was not too busy, 3 or 4 tables, and we waited for about 10 minutes to be seated. My husband and I ordered a Veggie Burger (no Mike's sauce) with salad (dressing on the side) and the Bruschetta (no parmesan) to share. The burger came with Mike's sauce, the salad came with dressing, the bruschetta came with parmesan and the ketchup that I asked for at time of serving arrived after we were finished.  When the waitress checked in with us and we indicated the order issues, her response was 'okay' and a blank stare.  No apology or offer to fix the meal. It could have been either a kitchen screw up or waitress error but regardless, it was an unsatisfactory response and we won't be returning.
Staying at this hotel for the second time. I really love the view of the ocean and how close it is to the beach.

The full rack of ribs was amazing. They literally fell off the bone and melted in your mouth. The pork steak was equally amazing and not something I've ever seen before. The fried corn and bourbon apples are delicious. The baked beans and fried were good but not great.
I just had Mama's cabbage salad, so good!  Our server at the bar was great, best server experience we've had yet, cordial, attentive and professional.
Sadly overrated. The impossible burger was so bland.

I give this restaurant an A for atmosphere. The food was ok. The pizza was not the best- a little doughy the crust. I expected a better tasting sauce too. The salad was ok, which is saying a lot- I give it a B+. I'm picky about salads! I would go again and try something other than the pizza!

Very cool hidden gem in Brandon! My fiancé and I love the number of beer choices they have and the staff if always very friendly. It can be slammed on the weekends, but there are usually one or two bar seats available during high tide.

Great atmosphere, service and margaritas. The chips and salsa were terrific as well. We ordered two types of tacos -- the tortillas tasted homemade and were super tasty as was the shrimp. The three star rating is based on the brisket tacos which were awful. There were large chunks of fat vs lean meat in our tacos which made them inedible. The manager comped our brisket tacos which was very kind, but fingers crossed that they get that issue fixed. We will go back again.

This place is a hidden gem.  This place is so tasty and very unique. 
All but once has the food and staff been great.  
The one bad experience I had was not a deal breaker due that I have had so many great meals served to me here.  I would recommend everyone try this place and see for your self.  You will be back.
This place is awesome. Really great and friendly service, good food and a fun atmosphere.

I had a lovely dinner with friends at this quaint Indian restaurant in the heart of center city Philadelphia. The atmosphere was warm and welcoming and the serve was impeccable. The unique drinks were like a work of art. The crispy spinach app with a yogurt sauce melted in my mouth. And for all the vegans and vegatarians the gobi mutter was out of this world. A dish where cauliflower, potatoes paired with the beautiful spices of Indian cuisine danced on my taste buds! Highly recommended for dinner lunch or brunch on any day of the week. Outside seating available is an additional plus! 

B Saunders

Best and cheapest seafood on the beach. Service is usually great, but bear in mind that even in the off season they can have a wait for dinner. I've been going there for years- love the crab (all of it), mussels, shrimp, and clams. 

They also have a mighty selection of bottled beers, more than most beach seafood places. If you don't like shellfish, try their salmon. Veggies are also almost always just right- they don't taste like they've sat in a steamer tray for hours.

Gumbo is made on site and it- what's the word? Oh, yeah. Rocks. It rocks. Scallops, shrimp and other seafood bits, and they don't scrimp on it. It's also not at all salty, which can be a problem with soups.

Anyone who says this food is just average is probably getting their seafood fried, or not getting the seafood at all. That's fine, but don't expect great things when you take a fine piece of fish, roll it in batter and fry the hell out of it.

After 3 visits to zpizza I usually go at 11:30 or 12:00 for lunch, as they have lunch specials. I waited 15 - 20 minutes for 2 slices of pizza (mind the pizza slices are cooked to go). A sandwich and a ceasar salad . These two items should not have to take 15 minutes of my lunch time, as I ordered to go. Only one staff member was on duty, being 11:30 you would think the business would want staff on hand for the lunch hour rush. Throw 2 slices of pizza in a container, make a sandwich and cut lettece should not take a whole 15-20 minutes. 
Irritating to deal with . For paying $13.00 dollars service was horrible.
Heavenly Apple+Gorgonzola Salad. The Bianca Pizza was amazing. Definitely coming back!

Came to grab a bite to eat before the movies and wasn't sure what I was in the mood for  but definitely not the loud echoing atmosphere.  
Place is clean with-a somewhat friendly younger staff 
I got the ahi appetizer which tasted very good served   with nice crIsp veggies. Then got the fish and chips meal which was large portion and tasted alright. 
I love good fish and chips so I critique them hard- these were light flakey cod a decent batter that was crunchy but bland and oily.   Food came out pretty quick and was hot I think they are a bit pricey for the atmosphere 

May come again to try other items but not if I want to have a conversation with the person I bring.

Two stars only because the food was good.  Otherwise not a very pleasant experience. Service was extremely slow and the wait staff was very inattentive. Sat for about 40 min waiting for food to come and when asked for a set of silverware we had to go to the hostess stand to receive. Again had to go to the hostess stand to ask for our check when we waited another 30 minutes after done our meal with no acknowledgment from the wait staff.  Food was good but staff was not.

New to the area, I listen to what friends and coworkers recommend so off we went to check out a local favorite for dinner.  We'd been there once before for lunch and decided we wanted to check it out at night.

The only challenge that evening was trying to find parking, which, coming from NYC, I find more challenging in Philly than in the Big Apple, but we were lucky enough to finally get a spot right in front of the restaurant.

We were greeted and sat immediately by a friendly staff member.  We ordered our margaritas and appetizers and checked out the menu.  While the patrons kept pouring in.  

Mexican and Texas BBQ are divided, we all went with the Mexican fare and ordered Carnitas Tacos, Seared Ahi Tuna Tacos and Shrimp Tacos.

All the tacos are served Mexican 'street style' on small tortillas, so those expecting the bell style, forget it.  

The Carnitas (pork) were succulent and with a squeeze of lime, very tasty and perfectly accompanied by cilantro and raw onions.

The shrimp and seared ahi tuna tacos were also a big hit, although a white fish would be more welcome on fish tacos as the fleshy tuna just doesn't quite cut it for this dish.  With the lime juice and accompanying condiments it's just not as complimentary as say a sea bass or even codfish.

The ambiance is great.  Casual diners and locals gathering for conversation and some bar games during the reverse happy hour packs the place, but our service was friendly and attentive.

Looking forward to the weather warming up again so we can sit outside and people-watch while dining at this very hipster locale.

This the first time i visited tampa bay i wanted to try out different pizza. saw it on yelp i went and try them pizza and got tell you'll i lefted taste those was one of best pizza i had, people work there are real friendly and nice, they got real nice service will visit again when i come back to Tampa bay.

We were only in town for a day and wanted to get the most of our time and boy did we get it with this place! 

Happened upon the restaurant while driving around town and decided to stop by since it seemed like a nice little place and we were all starving!

We parked the car across the street and as soon as we stepped out we could smell the food and oh my lord was it amazing! There wasn't much of a line since it was well after lunch and quite a bit before dinner. 

There are 4 of us in our little family and we all got something different. We sat ourselves and the food was out within minutes!! Such great service! 

Everything we got was absolutely amazing! The brisket and ribs are the best I have ever had (and I've had a lot). Not a huge fan of potato salad usually but somehow I could not get enough of theirs! 

This is hands (and feet) down the best little discovery we've ever made while walking around cities. Fast and super friendly service and AMAZING food!

I have came here a few times and decided to make a fair judgement after the third time. The meat and seafood are decently seasoned. Although for the life of me I don't understand why the rice isn't fully cooked.... If you can't make rice in a pan use a rice cooker. I mean these days you can practically put anything in a rice cooker or a slow cooker. So for all or nothing. If the meal includes rice and it's not properly cooked it's a no go for me, since it's a part of the meal

Very, very good food.  However the service was awful.  We (there severn of us) arrived at approximately 11:20, only ordered one appetizer and then our meals.  We got the appetizer quickly (smothered fries, excellent). It took quite a while for the server to come back and take our order.  She finally did, we got our food and once we finished eating, had to track her down to get our checks.  There were other tables who came in at the same time or after and left before us.  We finally got our checks at 12:50.  Won't be coming back here for lunch.  Would do carry out possibly, but it will be a while before we go back.

Cafe Osage is seriously goals. I love the feel, decor and warm feelings this little cafe oozes. I typically come here with girlfriends for brunch and then we pop over to bowood. Everything we have eaten has been delicious. Drinks are always generous. Their bacon is spot on and one of my favorites. Not too lean, too soggy or overly crisp. I've tried all of their French toast and hands down their summer berries one is my favorite. The oatmeal is so so and I'd avoid that next time. Simple breakfast is literally simply perfect. I love their tea, lattes just everything!  You will not regret coming here!
Ordered their 2 piece white chicken meal with a garden salad, yellow rice and black beans as sides. Meal was very good. Tasted great. Meat serving was a little low. Price good. Good service.

This was one of the worst customer experiences that I've had at a restaurant. My husband and I evidently pulled in the exit instead of the entrance. The sign said " Private drive- No thru traffic". It should have said "Exit Only". The guy at the window (I'm assuming he's the owner)immediately yelled at us when we pulled to the window to order. At first, I thought he was trying to get his message across in a teasing manner. He even stated that he almost called the police. (Who does that!?!?!) I should have left then, but I placed the order. A few minutes later, he shoved our food at us. Needless to say, he doesn't have to worry about me coming in the wrong way again, because I'm Never Going Back!

Also, the pulled barbecue was just mediocre and the white beans were the worst I've had. My family was not impressed!

Just got back from Roberto's.
I have been going there about once a week since they opened this location.
Poor parking, but i can walk from my house, and job, and they are open 24 hours.
Frendly service, great food, great prices.
I get the Cali bureto, or the number 6 combo plate.
 (chicken tacho and chicken enchilada, rice, and beans)
Or sometimes both.
But today, in the middle of the afternoon i had to endure some agressive panhandling  right outside their front door.
I don't know why the employees did not ask him to leave, or call the police to have him removed.
I won"t be going back, ever.
And i don't think you should go there, ever.

I will take Mas Tacos over BAJA BURRITO any ol' day!  You must try the fried avocado taco or the quinoa and sweet potato taco.  The tomatillo sauce, red cabbage, cilantro on top of the sweet potato and quinoa. Totally yummy.  The brick and mortar restaurant is not too fancy, but the food makes up for it!  Oh and it is pretty reasonably priced for a yummy lunch!  GO!!

Bagels are fresh and service is quick. Had the Asiago bagel. Also a good place for a quick lunch. Staff are nice and friendly but a little quirky. Lobby area needs help with cleanliness but maybe they were just busy. Prices fair but not cheap.

This is definitely my favorite of the steakhouse chains that I have visited (Texas Roadhouse, Outback, etc.)

Had the shrimp and crab "Surf and Surf" dip appetizer and it was amazing. Came with a huge pile of perfectly seasoned flatbed. Definitely hit the spot for this Atlantic Ocean Boy.

For my main course I had the 6oz sirloin and grilled shrimp. The steak was average but the shrimp was 10/10, supple, juicy, and amazingly seasoned. I also had the Mac and Cheese (also 10/10) and fries(they were ok).

We shared dessert even though we were massively full. We ended up getting the chocolate lava cake which was pretty good but I wish the lava actually leaked out like it was supposed to .

Our wait staff was very vigilant and right on top of our needs. Constant water refills and checking in to see if everything was tasting amazing.

Awesome experience 9/10. Will be back.

Ordered out some breakfast. I was really looking forward to my French toast. When I was going to eat it I found a little fly! I was okay one what ever, then I looked at the lid of the to go box, and there was like at least 10 other little dead flies! I will never eat there again! Totally grossed out!
Always great food and excellent customer service. Great people and comfortable environment.

idk who tf i talked to on the phone but i was just calling to ask what time you guys closed and whoever was on the phone said "around 8...but we might close early, so don't get your hopes up" and then hung up on me. get yoself some new employees jesus christ

Stopped in for lunch on the Fourth of July. 
It is located in a run down office Park area so kind of offputting but we persevered and went in. And I'm glad we did. 
Got the lunch special -two rolls for $8.95 with miso soup and salad - it's a great deal. 
Each roll has eight pieces and they will customize them at your whim for no or a minimal charge. For example I deleted cream cheese and added avocado to one roll/ they were very accommodating. 
Great attentive waitress. 
This is very far from where I live but I will visit again. The sushi was fresh- mine was cooked, my husbands was raw, so we had a pretty good spectrum of sushi and he enjoyed his as well. 
Good job!

i've been here a few times with no major issues, except for yesterday. there was a worker who i believe was finishing up her shift and had her two kids at a table waiting for her to finish. which is cool i get a hardworking mama, except one of the kids ran around the restaurant the whole time. the little kid approached our table and kissed my little girl on the mouth. no warning. and proceeded to come back twice to do this yet again. i stopped the last two times, the mother/worker witnessed it and did nothing, said nothing, you know how inappropriate that is? the same kid also pointed and laughed at other people and was in everyone else's faces while trying to eat. not sure why the mom didn't say anything to her kid or why idk management didn't step in. very unprofessional!

The worst experience I've ever had at a chain that I love from when I used to live up north. Me and coworkers got there at 11am because we had to drive from the other side of town we needed a somewhat faster sit down lunch. The food took forever to come out (about 55 minutes from when we sat down), seems like they were short on staff, and because of it food was at the temperature of when it's been sitting out for a while, sauce on the chicken was all dried up from sitting and not being brought out right away, he forgot the rice the comes with plate and still came around to see how things tasted and was still missing my rice. We were so late that just wanted to go containers and waited another 10-15 minutes when we just decided to go to the front and talk to the hostess to get our checks because we really had to go. She explained to us that the system was down and everything had to be done manually, we didn't feel comfortable leaving our credit card numbers to be charged later on but we had no other choice. Our complaint was why didn't you tell us before you sat us down, server knew what was going on so why no informed us and let us decide if we can stay or not. Manager did not care she just wanted the money and move on. So unethical and I would never go back here again.

Awesome authentic Thai food!! The curry is great and has lots of flavors. There are different spices to pick from too with any dish you order!! Highly recommend. Only giving four stars because sometimes they're kinda slow but it's a great place to grab some auntie Thai food!!

The best Indian food in Philly. No contest. (I'm a vegetarian, so I can only speak from that perspective--I'm guessing that, since this is Mughalai food, that the meat must be even better.)

This isn't health food. Be prepared for tons of very, very buttery sauces and vegetables cooked to peak tenderness ... and then some. Everything is melt-in-your-mouth incredible.

I'd recommend coming for the very reasonably priced lunch special ($7 for two curries and a naan!) My favorite entree, however, is the special Makhani aloo gobi, which is different from the regular aloo gobi. The sauce is exquisite. 

The naans are also great. 

The real standout, however? That mango cheesecake. You must try the cheesecake. The yumminess reverberated across every desi cell in my body.

I look forward to trying some of their other dishes, but I'm very happy with what I've had so far. 

Also, the owners are super nice and friendly. It's a family restaurant. I feel like they definitely try to get to know their customers.

What Wash Ave. has been missing.  Given St. Louis's French ties, burlesque is definitely an appropriate fit on this street corner. The dancers and hostess are energetic and the food is great and the drinks are strong. Looking for a great time?  Come to the Boom Boom Room!

Randomly found this location while working in Trenton and very lucky I did. My wife and I LOVE Puerto Rican/Spanish foods and this place delivers. Small place but service and atmosphere was great. I had the pernil and my wife had a "stuffed" plantain. Both were tremendous. And the desserts...Outstanding. Would highly recommend.

Listen, this place is one of the best in St Louis. Get yourself a gyro sandwich or salad, if you like sweet alcoholic drinks, ask for the space kitty, and enjoy the patio. You don't be disappointed. Staff are all genuinely sweet and helpful and the food slaps like a mothafucka. Take ya girl here and it'll fix your marriage okay.
Love this place. Don't let the line up scare you! Get there early for the good treats!
Great tasting authentic Mexican food. Music is on point and the ambiance takes you right to Mexico.

I love this place when even the Cesar Salad is a reason enough to eat there you've 
stumbled upon something special. The staff is fun and attentive .I love the atmosphere
and I meet great people every time I dine here .It's the place to be downtown to socialise,enjoy a full bar ,and a fabulous meal!

BYOB! Unfortunately we didn't know. 

The food was so good we could have been eating in a restroom and it wouldn't have hurt the review. 

I recommend the empanadas, beef though, way better than the chicken one. 

Also the black bean soup, kind of plain but the flavor makes up for it. To die for!

Ropa Vieja was great as well as the Arroz y Polo (stuffed chicken)

Best meal we have had in a long time, way better than Cuba Libre!!

Very low quality food. The only reason I am giving it 2 stars is because the server was very nice. The shrimp I got were absolutely so undercooked and the lowest quality shrimp I have had. My boyfriend said his country steak was too greasy and not what normal country fried steak is supposed to taste like. The only thing I enjoyed was the croissant. I felt gross from the food here afterwards. I heard people say how good this place was and I did not agree at all.

This place was so awesome! We came here as our "fancy" night during the bachelorette weekend and all the staff was great. We called in to get a reservation and they were more than accommodating. I got the young chicken and it was absolutely delicious! The crawfish jus definitely was the perfect touch to this dish. We finished off of course with the banana foster and bread pudding. The banana foster is a must try and the bread pudding was really good but not sure if I would recommend it over the banana foster. It's a pretty good size for both though. This place is awesome!

Love this place, great neighborhood sports bar and restaurant. Bartenders are attentive and make sure you are taken care of. I've been here twice in the last week to catch the NBA finals game. Both times they had great deals. I went on Sunday and they had 8$ mix well pitchers. Food was good too. Their wings are cooked well done which I love. I like my wings with crunchy skin they have a variety of sauces that you can have them tossed in but I got mine dry. Jalapeño poppers were what I expected but the fries were a pleasant surprise. Seasoned well, no salt and pepper needed.

Love the people and the food is amazing!! My stay in Nola was 3 and a half days and I made sure I went here twice the food was that great got the same waitress both times and she was the sweetest lady love her. The food is super cheap and the taste is amazing. Definetly worth every cent and more! Highly recommend this spot.
Everything here is outstanding. The sushi, appetizers and drinks far exceeded my expectations. Really excellent waitress as well.

The food was very good and was ready when promised.  Only reason it isn't a 5 star is because I ordered take out and no utensils were given and the spring rolls weren't very good but the krab Rangoon and lo mein were excellent.

Cool vibe, good location for tourists, but utterly underwhelming food and drink. We were really looking forward to it, as it was our first stop in town after a long drive and online reviews were quite promising. Had fried pickles, Mac and cheese with hot chicken, and hot chicken salad. Absolutely nothing outstanding, unique, or interesting about any of it, unfortunately. Standard at best. Fine if that's what you're looking for, but there's so much more good food in this town.

Excellent, fresh food. Service was so polite & fast. 
Big size meals. So glad to find a restaurant open past 10 on a Saturday night!

OMG! Have you ever been given food and thought about asking that person to marry you?
 I got the bacon turkey sandwich and it was the best thing I've eaten in a long time. 

Also if you like them on yelp they will send you a yelp deal. That is very cool.  This place is just good bottom line!

Having lived out of the area for a while, something I would always crave is a Tarpon Springs style Greek salad with potato salad. Getting a Greek salad elsewhere typically meant just a normal salad plus feta. Calling this a Greek salad was always a big disappointment to me.Where was the yummy potato salad???  I would suggest or mention this fact while in New England and it always seemed like a pretty foreign concept to people, but I am a firm believer that Florida's Greek community has it right when it comes to salad. Pile on those potatoes please! 

As a fan of this style Athenian Garden is my go to place for Greek Salads. They are consistently great with a perfect balance of crisp lettuce, tomato, kalamata olives,  beets, onions, green peppers, pepperoncini, feta, herb oil+vinegar dressing, and of course knock your socks off potato salad.  I've tried many others in the Pinellas area,and I always and think to myself, why keep on searching? Athenian Gardens has me covered. 

Besides my obviously high regard for their salad, the falafel sandwich is always outstanding here. The fried crispy chick peas, yogurt tzatziki and warm buttery pita always taste delicious together. My dinner companions rave about the chicken or lamb souvlakis as being great too. And often they will have very reasonably priced dinner specials which include a free glass of wine and creative different entrees such as octopus, crab stuffed shrimp, or local red snapper. ( Plus almost everything on the menu comes with the above-mentioned incredible Greek Salad!) 

Athenian Gardens has multiple locations throughout the area and this Largo location on Starkey is their newest opening. It tends to be not so busy as compared to their more established restaurants and that makes it easy to get in, and the service is always very attentive and the food comes out quick. I guess that is one advantage of it not being super busy. The plaza is on the left just before the intersection of Ulmerton and Starkey if you are heading northbound, and the restaurant has many booths, tables, plus an entire other side featuring a full service bar and high top tables I never see full. Lets hope people starting going here as the Greek food is excellent, and I don't want this to be Largo's best kept secret anymore!

Oh my googly goodness! I am just in awe at the amazing food this place is serving. Everything was delicious! Total deliciousness. I'm still craving their food and unfortunately I don't live anywhere near them. It is a definite must try place if you love southwestern food. Staff is super friendly and the food, WOWSER!! So tasty! Such fresh food and amazing flavors. What more can one ask of a food place? Oh, cocktails you say. They have those as well!! And those are also on point with excellent liquor selection and perfectly blended margaritas! I am definitely going back when I am in town.

The best pizza I have ever had in Tucson!  I had a meatball ricotta roasted red peppers and Caesar salad!  My Aunt had a cheese less garden pizza and that was amazing too!  Who knew a pizza without cheese could be good!  I will be back next time I'm in town.

Hummus was ok. Greek salad was good. It's BYO which is nice and the owner gave us some cake. The cake was the best part. I really like Greek restaurants but nothing here really excited me. Btw , the cake came from a bakery near Fort Dix.

My family seemed to like it. But the food made me feel sick all day and I didn't love the ambiance. The service was terrible. The girl that took our order was insanely rude and disconnected. I think I just need to avoid restaurants on Cherokee St..

Positives: good food.  
Negatives: contrived theme bar vibe, password is a hassle, poor value.

The last time I was here I craved an old school gin & tonic.  The server mocked me for this simple drink request. Then she brought me something with cucumbers instead- it wasn't good. Thank you annoying server!

Early-ish on a Friday night, my sister and I were early for our reservation but they sat us right away. They had a great list of cocktails and food, we each had the Elvis Rum Punch and the fish sandwich with fries, both delicious! The lighting is cool with the strung round bulbs across the ceiling, would definitely need to come back just for drinks to enjoy it more. And also for brunch! Only down side is their happy hour, 4-6? C'mon guys, let's be reasonable here..

I have been back a couple of times to La Tapatia.  I would have to say, the food has gotten better!  The service is much improved.  If you do not want to drive out to Kuna, it is probably the best option for Mexican in Boise.

I really want the cocktails to impress me at Sangrita, but I've been there twice and I'm still "meh" about them. 

What I'm not "meh" about is the food. The tacos are great, although they are so stuffed they could use a second corn tortilla so that the taco doesn't disintegrate as you eat it. The sides are what get me - the elotes and the black beans are chock full of flavor. These are not the dry, boring sides that usually accompany Mexican food.

The inside seems a little too dark, but the patio is lovely - just off the Broadripple beaten path that it's both convenient, but not too loud/busy.

Going to be a long one. 

Sat in the bar at a two top with a friend of mine for dinner this week. We both wanted a little bit of everything, between the two of us with drinks, our meal was $110. I thought cost was reasonable given everything we could try. I recommend doing a taster tray of the charcuterie and cheese and spreads. (Duck prosciutto and fig jam is genius and the cured salon, A Plus) I do think the tray it arrives on is monstrously large for the amount of food, it took up way too much space on our small table. We were able to fit a few things, but what frustrates me is having a kid come by to drop off some other things we ordered and not offering to problem solve and rearrange the table. This poor 14-16 year old runner just stared at us to figure it out while he stood there with our next two plates. This is the same kid who said to the table behind us "I don't know" when asked about the sauce. My only suggestion here, help him get more comfortable with speaking to guests, or don't have him run food. 

Becca did a great job organizing our order and stretching it out. I appreciated having different plates brought out a different times. We also got great protein recommendations from both Becca and John to add on to our meal. I would love to see a serving size ratio on the menu. Like "good for 2-3" or "4-5". So when I bring friends back, we don't have to argue over the last piece of tuna. Haha

Please expand on social media. Instagram story new dishes. As a 28 year old, I rely on that to make decisions on where I will spend my money. I have lived down the street from Divvy for over a year, and that was my first trip. This restaurant is the coolest concept. I'm giving it 5 stars because I want to see it succeed in Carmel. I'm leaving feedback because I genuinely care. 


Food: 

Starters: vegan cheese ball, duck prosciutto, cured salmon, rustic bread, all great.

Mains: Brussels sprouts, caprese salad, scallop wontacos, baby lamb chops, seated tuna, solid choices.

Finally decided to write a review for this place since I am constantly telling people to come here. They have the BEST veggie burger I have ever had (and I've had a lot)! They make it themselves in-house and it is full of flavor with a great texture. Paired with the fresh bun, steamed tomato and mixed greens it is absolutely perfect! I'm not the type of person who orders the same thing every time they go somewhere, but I haven't been able to stray away from this burger. I will say that it's not for everyone though, it has a softer consistency than a regular burger, but that just makes me like it even more. Don't say you don't like veggie burgers until you try this one!!

Stopped by my favorite Japanese restaurant. I love this place. Fresh food, good service, clean bathrooms. Due to Covid they are taking every measure to follow the rules but make you comfortable at the same time. No silver wear but plastic . Only had about eight tables occupied so the food came out fast. I'm always finding myself ordering the same thing from food to drink so I tried some new things on the menu and was not disappointed.

To some people M&M means those delightful little candies there are so addictive for many folks.  No, I didn't say S&M. That's an entirely different subject!   However, for fellow Yelper Nando F. and me it means Martini & Meatball night at Anthony's Coal Fired Pizza!  So if you are looking for info about chocolate candy, or S&M you can skip this review.  Otherwise read on.

So the two of us stopped in this Wednesday night around five and the place was just getting going. Nando arrived first and I found him sitting at the bar flirting with the pretty bartender.

So here's the deal with M&M night.  Any kind of martini you want is $5.  It's sponsored by Double Cross Vodka so that will be in your drink.  Other than that there are no restrictions.  And the glorious meatballs are free.  They are a slightly larger than a golf ball and served with a little red sauce and a dab of ricotta cheese on the side.  They are delicious and you can have has many as you want.

As we munched on meatballs we perused the menu.  Numerous fellow Yelpers had raved about both the wings and the pizza so we decided to order both and share.

I'm usually not a wing guy but these bad boys changed my mind.  A small order of 10 pieces goes for $9.75.  These delicious morsels are lightly tossed in olive oil, garlic, rosemary, and maybe another herb or two.  Then they are stacked on top of slices of delicious focaccia and buried under a pile of perfectly cooked caramelized onions.  I know, I know this sounds incredibly good and it is.  For a guy that usually doesn't like wings these were fantastic.

Next out was the Broccoli Rabe & Sausage Pizza.  We ordered the large 16 inch pie for $19.95.  These are thin crust pizzas baked in an 800 degree oven.  This one was cooked perfectly and we enjoyed every bite.  The toppings are well distributed over the pie and the amount of toppings is great.  

It's not often you get a truly fine meal at a chain restaurant but for me, and I believe Nando agrees, we had a four star experience.

Adorable quick and tasty place for sandwiches and salads made with pork or chicken gyro (using locally sourced meats)! The food was hot, fresh, tasty and cooked to order. The staff were pleasantly enthusiastic about the food, and the place was clean. No sticky tables! Simple self-serve station for water, etc., but they do offer beer and wine as well. The sandwiches are pretty large and filling! The bread is home-baked and is amazing! You can smell all the aromatic cooking herbs when you walk in! And, it's so affordable!!! Can't wait to return!

I enjoyed this place.  Mrs. Yelper and I went here for a quick lunch during the work week not knowing what to expect, and we were pleasantly surprised.  This is a lovely little café tucked away in Creve Coeur.  It had a bit of a lunch push happening, but things moved at a nice pace, and we didn't have trouble grabbing a table.  

The menu was good.  Nothing heavy or artery-clogging; sandwiches, wraps, salads--and they had plenty of options.  I settled on a Veggie Wrap with Salmon, and it was quite nice.  Looking around the room, I saw what a lot of the other plates looked like, and it seems as if I'd be satisfied with most anything they had prepared.

My only regret is that I chose to forgo dessert, even though their beautiful display was screaming to be sampled.  If their sweets are half as good as they look, I'm sure I'll walk out with a smile.  However, that will be a trip for another day.

I ordered some food from here thru Uber Eats the Chicken & Shrimp Steak and the Tilapia platter with asparagus an Mac n Cheese. The food was very fresh an still warm considering it came from Germantown Ave to West Philly. Now as for my food the steak was lacking substance very little in my roll for $14.00 an the shrimp were small an it didn't have my mushrooms. As for the fish platter they called an said they didn't have anymore Mac n cheese bummer  settled for the rice then called back an got fries. The fish was good, asparagus alittle overcooked for me but I loved the fries very good. Will try other selections.

I loved this place, but the other day i ordered  s and s chicken to go, they were nice enough to put sauces in the bag for me, but when i got to the park to eat.. no fork, and the fried rice.. looked like a wad of mush, and tasted just as bad..... i will give this place another shot, but im concerned.

I have had many meals at La Pena and what it comes down to for me with a 5 star review is freshness, consistency and local flaver, time and time again.

I've had a variety of the menu choices, the tacos, burrito, sopa and torta..and all are fanstastic.

The only mis-fire for me were the fish tacos.  The fish was over-fried for my liking..  not a crime.

One word of caution..if you ask for spicy here...you are going to get it.  The owner likes his hot peppers, and does some magic with them in his spicy pork and spicy chicken.  YOWZA.

Usually go to another Chinese take out a bit closer to my house. See this place advertisements figured I would try their food. Better than good. Great food great service and very efficient safe take out window. My new place to go. (We have gone back 2 more times)

I have attended a few events at this Restaurant and thought the food was good. So In planning my friends Bridal Shower I recommended it. We spent A LOT of time and money on this shower to make sure it was exactly like the Bride to Be imagined. Unfortunately, the staff and managers turned out to be extremely rude and I'm now really surprised that people even chose to have their events at this place . I ordered and had a custom dessert delivered that cost over $100 and the staff member brought it to the wrong party room and that party ate it ! I understand mistakes happen, so I approached it nicely. However the response I got was being passed from one person to another when they realized what they did and than the manager flat out said " We aren't paying for anything. We aren't giving you any money. We aren't being held responsible." They also threatened to get a lawyer, which sounds a little funny. Are they that tight for money? All the money we spent there and they can't even own up to and pay for their $100 mistake? We never signed any contract saying they would not be held responsible for anything lost or damaged, so technically they should be taking full responsibility without question. Im more disgusted by their treatment and poor response than them carelessly throwing away $100 of mine. I will never recommend this restaurant or eat there ever again, neither will anyone who attended the event, or anyone I have already shared this story with.

Suburban classy... I like this place, seated immediately on a Sunday at 5:00pm isn't bad at all. 

You have other choices on Baltimore pike but for a different experience we tried Charlie Brown and actually liked it.

Two picky kids enjoyed the free (with yelp check in) firecracker shrimp which is probably a spin off on bang bang shrimp at (bonefish grille) but let's just call it the younger version, shrimp are tinier... yet tasty and they do give you a lot. 

Food came out fast. our Waitress was new but she was fast, couldn't tell she was new.

very cute giant booth we were seated in, not too noisy...

I had a garlic crusted steak w mashed potatoes, great! that was after two Delicious Margaritas... yum!

everyone enjoyed their meal they are more expensive than famous Dave's or miller ale house but it is more classy.
