Definitely try this place - best to go on a Tue or Wed for early lunch to avoid a huge line. We sat at the bar and the bartender gave a us great overview of the menu. I was very happy with our experience and it was by far my favorite Jambalaya and Gumbo of all that I sampled in NOLA over 4-5 days. The food had plenty of heat where it should have and in other (appropriate) cases we had access to ample hot sauce. The Shrimp Po Boy was a winner - dress it yourself. Our fried chicken as part of the sampler was small, but very good - if I had been able to go back, I'd try the fried chicken.

Love the location, ambiance, roomy bar, happy hour, pups on the patio, classic bike night, the suds (always The Blonde), and rail pints of said suds. Food can be hit or miss (especially the burgers), but the beer battered fries and beer sponges are always delicious. A buddy of mine also swears by the fish tacos. The crew is also pretty accommodating. A favorite watering hole.

Yesterday dinner was only our 2nd time here. All 5 meals we ordered were spot on. We used to live in Thailand and food here is definitely authentic! We ordered papaya salad, tom yum tale (seafood), soft shell crabs, chicken krapow and mango with sticky rice. Definitely worth going to from Wilmington, DE!

Amazing restaurant. We had the Veggie Pho, the Pad Thai (Recipe from the owners home town) and the chicken curry. Everything was delicious. The restaurant doesn't have alcohol which didn't matter. We had a pot of tea and really enjoyed our meal.
Highly recommend this place!! Everything was cooked to perfection! We are carb loading for tomorrow's Clearwater marathon... loving every single bite!

OK, its on the beach, had live music, good food, happy service, and its just a fun place.
This review is for the overall experience, not for gourmet food.
It's the overall experience that makes this a great place.
If I was rating food alone, its exactly what you expect, a solid 3 star.
but put 3 star food with 10 star atmosphere and you have a great location.

One if the best Asian restaurants around. Staff is incredibly friendly and the food is amazing. Order the jerky papaya salad and the beef chow fun and you won't regret it. The beef is so tender and the dish is so well flavored. I hope they stay open forever.

I've tried their Garlic Cheesy Bread topped with minced garlic, Megan's Chicken Parmesan, Blind Hawaiian and my friends and I created our own pizza. Which was pretty cool, just for additional costs. It was worth it the price was not expensive like I thought it would be.
Delicious and authentic. I eat a lot of sushi and i'm very picky. This place is good sushi.

No better way to start a Saturday than brunch with your girls are an incredible restaurant. I was a little disappointed that you couldnt call or use Yelp to make a reservation ahead. 

It was a 40-50 minute wait around 11. We walked over to market district; there are many cool spots. We walked back around the time, and were seated. Very cute and clean restaurant.

Jasmine was our server and so sweet, very knowledgeable on the menu and setup of that restaurant next door. Tinker coffee is in house as well as an espresso bar. Vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free options are available. There were a lot of options but I went with the Nano...OMG was it absolutely delicious and unlike anything I ever had. So tasteful, fresh eggs over easy, hot tomato sauce, savory meatballs, with toasted ciabatta.

I can't wait to come back and try everything on the menu.

I've been to Katie's several times for lunch and dinner. It's a good spot, no doubt. Sunday Brunch is all the rage, and as much as I love a good brunch on the weekends, this is one I hadn't experienced until this past Sunday.

First tip: if you're okay with sitting outside, make sure to tell the host(ess) that you would like to sit outside. Saying "first available" doesn't communicate "inside or outside" here. 

Pros: The bottomless drink selection is pretty good. For $14, you can enjoy several Bloody Mary's, Mimosas or Sangria. The food menu also provides lots of options. 

Cons: They must have been having an off day, but it was enough to deter me from returning for Sunday brunch and definitely makes it to the list of "just eh" in my books. 

I was totally okay with the wait, but it annoyed me to see the tables outside stay open when I said we were fine with first available. After being seated, I learned why outside wasn't the best option. The heat? Nah... That is something this New Orleans native can handle. It was the service. We literally had to ask for a glass of water four times before the server came through. She kind of glanced our way and dropped quirky one liners to let us know how busy she was, but didn't have much time to check in. No big, we don't need much attention as long as you take the order and bring us our food. However, it would have been nice to let her know the quality of my dish.

My fiancé's Chicken and Waffles were pretty tasty, plated well and a generous portion. The gumbo is also good.

My end was unfortunate. After asking for a recommendation on the benedicts, I went with the Eggs Cochon. The plating was pretty scattered and bare with a few grapes that probably shouldn't have made it out of the kitchen. 

The Cochon was poorly seasoned (which is a shame since this is a headliner for Katie's) and the English muffin was so hard that I couldn't even cut through it with a knife. 

As I've said, it may have been an off day, but Katie's only gets 3 stars from me. In the words of Gordon Ramsay, "Damn damn damn."

Horrible customer service. Ask for 12 tacos no lettuce, get them home, all 12 tacos have lettuce. Call to let them know and have new made get hung up on, call back ask for manager and she is very rude. Go get tacos and they are talking about the phone call like I did something wrong not vice versa.
great food and great for large groups! Read my full Nashville blog here: https://reagans-reviews.blogspot.com/2021/11/i-went-to-birmingham-and-nashville.html

My family and I went on a recommendation for the prime rib and we were extremely disappointed! It looked and tasted like no other prime rib I ever had before. In fact, it was almost like shoe leather! To add to that, the waitress was not terribly attentive. They may be good for breakfast but they are sorely lacking when it comes to dinner.

Nice place.  Bad Music.

Came here the other night for a few drinks.  Impressive beer/liquor selection.  Fair prices.  Friendly, knowledgeable staff.  Didn't eat but the food definitely looked good.

Only gripe was the terrible music that they were playing.  Picture BLASTING Foo Fighters, among other bad late 90s music.  I do like 90s music, just not what they were playing and at volume they were playing it.

My wife and I tried this new restaurant for a date night. We are thrilled that a fantastic Mexican restaurant opened up in our area. I highly recommend this place. I had the Burrito Loco which was fantastic the salsa tastes very fresh the cilantro tastes very fresh. We will be back for sure to try some different dishes. The service was very good also.
This place is a dive with a great ambiance and chilled vibe.  I ordered an egg burrito with chorizo.  The tortillas were homemade along with the anejo sauces.
The band was great. A couple is hired to dance. Don't worry about any signage about drink minimum. Bartenders likely to ignore you. Bring your own booze and tip the band.

I ate here when it first opened, my pasta had more grease on it that what would be left from a pound of bacon.  Just ate lunch there.  Salad was ok, but since we weren't regulars the service was bad.  We were never told about the specials, saw the waiter once but of course was very friendly when he came with the bill.  I really don't see why anyone would eat here.

First time trying Korean food so I was a bit nervous but this place was soooo delicious! I can't wait to come back and try the soups when it starts getting cold! Our server was also so sweet so that's always a plus. :)

I called up today to reserve a table for 6 for lunch. The guy on the phone said no problem, there was plenty of room. 

We showed up right on time and waited at the door for someone to seat us. Unfortunately there was nobody working the front. Looked around a bit, but couldn't find any employees. So we waited. And waited. And waited. 5 minutes standing in the doorway and nobody showed up. 

At that point we walked in toward the bar to see if we could find someone to ask if we should just sit or wait, but we couldn't find a single employee. So bizarre. Anyway, we wound up leaving and eating at the falafel joint across the way.

Not the best experience!

The only reason I'm giving this review 3 stars is because the service was not at all what I had expected. From the looks of the restaurant I would have expected for this to be a 5 star service level. My date had taken me here for a surprise birthday dinner and while the food and view was breathtaking, the lack of service would definitely be something that would prevent me from coming back. 

Our server, whose name we found out was Justin, from our dinner receipt at the end of the meal, must have been having a bad day or was too exhausted to work. I've never once had someone ask me if I wanted my birthday dessert, that was definitely a shock, especially when it was suppose to be a surprise. We were not greeted with a warm hello and to be quite honest there was less than minimal human interaction with him. I had more interaction with the host throughout my entire meal. 

The hostess however was exceptional, I never got her name but she was a brunette about 5'6. Honestly I would come back just for her hospitality. We had a reservation for a ocean view table but it wasn't ready at the time so we just sat at a regular table. The hostess however took it upon herself to help move us to the ocean view table as soon as one opened up even after we told her it wasn't necessary. She knew it was my birthday and she definitely did all that she could to make it special and I definitely thank her for it. 

I wish I could have gave this place the 5 stars it deserves but my experience here this time definitely did not earn it. Although I had a bad experience, the manager Katie offered to invite me back to give them a second chance and was very professional with the conversation that took place the morning after my meal. I'm definitely hoping our next experience will get the 5 stars this place deserved because the food was exceptional, the hostesses were exceptional and the management as well.

My husband and I had the unfortunate opportunity to eat here last night. We were seated at the same time as another couple at the other end of our table. 5 minutes after we all ordered, the couple next to us received their drinks. 10 minutes after that they received their food. I then asked our server if we could please have our drinks - and he then brought them over. After asking several times about our food (a long 40 minutes after seating) we received it. While the broth and noodles in my seafood pho were fairly tasty, the rest tasted very bland. My husband's shrimp fried rice was also severely lacking in flavor. I feel just based on the delay they should have comped a drink but they offered nothing. We will not be going back.

Stayed in a hotel near the avenue cafe.  Delicious cocoa cruffin (we had surmised it was a cross between a croissant and a muffin, whatever it is, it's yummy), fresh squeezed juices and strong espresso.   Great breakfast spot.
OK tasting takeout Chinese food. Standard menu options to choose from. Reasonable prices.

We went here in the recommendation of a local shop keeper. I'm not a fan of meatloaf. I don't care for the mealy quality often produced by the binder. That said, the menu description was interesting enough that I was compelled to give it a chance. Best decision I've made in a long time. Salsicca, ground turkey, spinach and red peppers with a chili sauce topping was nothing short of amazing.
The Oatmeal Stout and Pecan Brown Ale are both outstanding. We're on our way to becoming regulars.
This place is the wosrt place to get a steak.It`s a 5 star slop house.Worse off is the employee`s look like they are on dope.Eatin a frozen dinner from a dollar store is far better than this dump.

My husband and I have been on the hunt for awesome tacos in Tampa and we have finally come across a couple places that hit the mark. Loli's is one of them!

We tried to visit Loli's a couple of times before our third visit but it was closed every time. Closed on a Sunday and closed on a holiday. I guess I can't blame them. If you're that good, you can be closed whenever you want to be closed!

When we finally made it there (the third time), it was around lunch time at noon on a Friday... and it was mayhem. Lines of people inside, lines of people outside, cars pulling in and out, people picking up to go orders. WOW! This place is popular. And now I can see why.

I ordered two tacos, one was al pastor and the other was carnitas. I really enjoyed the al pastor tacos because there's nothing like a slice of pineapple to counteract the tangy sazon of the pork. Yum-o! The carnitas taco was good as expected. Cilantro and all the fixins on each of my tacos! I also ordered a sope with ribeye. The ribeye was okay. The sope was missing some salt. No biggie. Next time, I will add the salt to it! ...And likely choose another meat topping. My hubby ordered a lengua sope and it was AWESOME. I will definitely come back to order the lengua.

Folks here speak Spanish and English. Service is fast. Not much in the way of seating but I saw many people sharing seats at tables. A few people came in alone and befriended each other at a larger table in the center. Gotta love it. Any way, of course I plan to return and try out everything else on their menu. Super excited!! :-)

Fantastic!  The atmosphere is so welcoming with a warm and relaxing ambience from wooden decks and brick walls.  The menu is robust and so are the portions.  Have tried several items over the last few months, all superb.  Bar upstairs is a hidden g

if you like apple bees then you will love this place, food was so,so.  but they do have a vast selection of brews that apple bees does not have...  customer service little slow,  but in all fairness they were very busy....

I mostly come here for the $2 PBR Tall boys and the star tots.

They have great food and strong drinks, but something always feels little off to me when I come to this bar.

Sexyman and I visited Phil's Deli and Market to grab a quick breakfast before a day of fun activities. He's been there several times so he knew that this would be a good spot for us (he always chooses well...and in every way!). They offer extensive breakfast and deli items (including healthy options) and they have a good sized market inside also. You can purchase breads, canned goods, etc. Really convenient if you're out of something and you're in there picking up something to eat/drink. Killing two birds with one stone is the name of the game, people!  

I ordered The Diesel (egg whites, sauteed mushrooms, jalapenos, and gouda cheese on a whole wheat wrap). He ordered something similar but on whole wheat toast. I am still talking about that wrap and it's days later. I need to order it again for picture purposes. I ate it so fast that I actually surprised MYSELF. They have an area where you can dine in, watch the news and shoot the breeze with other customers, which is what we did.

I hate to discount other Yelpers reviews, but giving one star due to the owner not wanting to heat up a can of off-the-shelf Progresso soup is ludicrous. I don't ask the cashiers at Rite Aid to wash my hair for me because they sell shampoo. Just saying.

Any establishment that has a hands-on owner that genuinely cares about his business earns an extra star in my book. Phil is warm, welcoming, and he takes pride in his place. It was a pleasure to meet him last weekend. 

Support local businesses and give Phil's Deli and Market a try. Your local Wawa will be okay with it :)
The sandwich they are known for IS good...it's the only thing I've tried and it'll probably stay that way. Why fix what isn't broken?

the food was amazing. Staff was friendly and very helpful. I ordered the seafood platter and it was delicious. I will come definitely come back and be sure to let my friends and family know about this place. I ate here once before when it was the older restaurant so this place has def upgraded and came along way. I would recommend this to anyone who would like something new that tastes great and don't want to be let down.

I love New Orleans style food. Since my husband is from New Orleans we had to try this restaurant. The drinks were fantastic. We had the charcoal-grilled oysters. Crawfish etoufe and Boudin stuffed pork tenderloin. I am giving it 4 stars because the etoufe was too spicy for my taste. Overall, great service, drinks and food.
I've been here about 5 times and prior to that I've never had creole. This tiny place is an absolute gem. Great service, amazing food, and they are quick to get your order ready.

Came here on a Saturday night.  Waited an hour.  Started with a sampler of a dozen oysters.  They were so-so.  The Arugala and Endive salad was large and quite good.  My companions both ordered the grouper with a chimichurri sauce.  This was delicious and expertly prepared.  I ordered the Fishermans stew.  I generally order this whenever it's on the menu.  The flavor of the broth was terrific - loads of fresh fennel.  There was not a lot of seafood in the stew.  Three shrimp, four muscles, a few calimari rings, and a small piece of fish.  It was mostly tomato and fennel.  Stews are hearty and this was more of a soup.  I pointed this out to the waitress and they brought out additional seafood - more shrimp and calimari.  I was full after this and was appreciative of that gesture.  Maybe this is just how the chef prepares this dish and if so, I would not order it again.  Ambiance is festive and service was excellent.  I would definitely go back.

Had an hour between my massage and class so I thought hitting up Big Sky would be a good idea. I had made a reservation but was late. They respected the reservation and I got a good table by myself. The soup and salad were good and really filling. The iced tea was tasty and the service was excellent.

Today I tried the Sgt Pepper and Sausage. Each ingredient on its own was outstanding. Three types of peppers, fresh Italian Sausage with a marinara that's not to sweet. Piled on with mozzarella and Parmesan cheeses. I highly recommend grabbing a slice from Love and Pie.

I have eaten at Luke's for years.  It's been decent but always over priced, in my opinion.  It was convenient and on the way home.  But now I have to say sandwichs there are not what they used to. Last week  I tookout a small sausage sandwich with hot peppers and a bag of fries: well over $10.   When I got home and looked at the sandwich I couldn't believe it.  Pitifiul. Looked like a dried up frank with a few peppers on it.  Just terrible. Bread was ok.  Overall sandwich experience was not worth the money.
Don't think I go there for awhile.

This is the best BBQ I've had in Tampa so far.
I've tried Jazzy's, Selmon's and a few others, all of which were deeply uninspiring.

I had the "Everything Platter" which has a piece of chicken, sausage, shredded beef, shredded pork and pork ribs. A meateater's wet-dream!
The ribs were the best thing on the plate; the other meats were okay.
Cole Slaw is a little too sweet, and the mac and cheese is average.

Next time I'll just order a slab of ribs I think.
But at least there'll be a "next time" which is more than I can say for a lot of the other rib joints in Tampa.

Sit by the bar if you can! We got a half dozen raw oysters and half dozen chargrilled oysters. Both were mind-blowingly good!!! The guys served my raw oysters straight up. He opened the shell and slid the oysters one by one to me. No plates, no ice, just fresh juicy raw oysters! The chargrilled oysters were very tasty, too! 

If you're looking for a nice sit-down restaurants, Felix's is not a good choice. But if you're up for some real fresh oysters and plan to be in and out within half an hour, you'll be glad you come here.

Love the super Emma, their blended iced coffees are also so good. Best when hungover. Always take my friends here when they visit. The wait is always insane but typically worth it. Sex on a bagel is my second favorite

This place is pretty good, but has the potential to be way better. 

First off, if you want people to come in, maybe give them enticements like happy hour specials. It amazes me that they are trying to compete with Trolley, but don't have any happy hour specials. Even Mikimotos next door has them and it is owned by the same group so it doesn't make any sense. 

My other complaint is that they took the garlic soy flank steak salad off the menu. This is literally the reason why I came in. It was sooo good and it is sad to see it go. 

However, this place does have some things going for it. They generally have a good beer selection. Also, they have complimentary bagel chips with garlic butter which are super good. The last time I went, when I found out they had betrayed me by taking the best dish off the menu, they did have a brisket sandwich special. It was very good. 

I have hopes that this place remains good, but continues to work on improving and drawing people in.

The staff made an instant impression on me as especially friendly and attentive. I ordered water with my drink; the bartender refilled it twice for me, then came out from behind the bar, on a crowded Saturday night, to get my water cup from me and refill it, after noticing it was again empty. 

Also, the pizza is excellent, and there was a great band playing. Great atmosphere.

Well, off the top, they've apparently taken down the "NO YELPERS" sign mentioned in several other reviews, so that's a good start, anyway.

My food was OK. I had the burger and curly fries. The burger came with one of those newfangled brioche buns, but something was very wrong - the top of the bun had been slapped with oil or egg or something, *after* baking and it was wet and greasy. I'm not sure if was the normal egg wash, or something else, but it had clearly been applied after the bun came out. You couldn't pick up the burger without all your wet fingers wet, and the top of the bun quickly became soggy.

Other than that, the food was good (although I was hungry, so that always adds a bit of bias...).

My server, Dana, was very friendly and provided just the right amount of attention. The bartender was also pleasant.
Hidden gem close to University Medical.  Don't be worried about the size and look.  Great food and an awesome staff.  Quintessential New Orleans faire with a twist.   Will be back!

I grew up in a little town in Hawai'i and lived a very sheltered life. So much so that when I came to California I thought that Taco Bell was real Mexican food since that's all I knew growing up. 

Tacos are one of my favorite things to eat. So I was really skeptical when I came to Lily's for the first time and found that all you got was meat on a small corn tortilla. I think I might have even laughed when a friend told me that these were "authentic" tacos. 

Hands down, this place makes the BEST tacos I've EVER had! Who would have thought that a taco didn't need cheese, lettuce, sour cream or tomatoes. 

They have a really simple toppings bar with a variety of hot sauces, radishes, lime, cilantro and onions. I always load mine with a mixture of the hot sauces and top it off with radishes to give it a nice crunch. 

Sure I've seen some SBCC students sneak a bag of pre-shredded cheese every now and again...seems like a great idea especially since I'm a cheese FIEND at heart, but honestly...these tacos are so good they don't need cheese at all.

Great little spot hidden from the tourist in busy downtown Phila.  Had a fabulous Vodka and Arugula Martini and plan to go back an sample the other creative cocktails.  Fun decor, while sitting at the counter you can always find the writers names hidden within the letters on the wall.  Upstairs is whimsical and cozy, and comfortable in the blue highback sofas.

I finally got to check out Topgolf!!  AND I was part of a group event so had the added benefit of food variety and unlimited drinks. 

I highly recommend coming here for a group event, it was a lot of fun and the servers were attentive. The food was phenomenal and plated beautifully. 

The heaters worked great so I was warm... there were clubs at every bay, and as a lefty, I was glad to see there were some for me. 

I have no complaints, it was a great time.

This was such a great experience the best service ever! Its like they were reading my mind. Id want to ask something and they tell me before i can even speak. My water cup was never not full. But the food was amazing cooked/prepped to perfection.

I cant believe I haven't written a review for Vintage! I have been going here for food, drinks, and birthday celebrations for about 7 years. We are always welcomed, by the staff, served good food and drinks and always leave having had a great time.The pulled pork sandwich is a favorite, the Garlicky cajun shrimp app is so so good, the mussles are great, and the best part is dipping the bread with the delicious butter in all the yummy sauces. I love love the cheesecake and the chocolate lava desert too. Can't wait till my next visit.

I don't know if someone was listening earlier to my complaint about not having sausage, but they've added Smoking Goose Sausage to the menu! I'm highly impressed. 

Thanks so much, Cafe Patachou for listening and for supporting other local businesses. You're #1 in my book.

Went for Sunday brunch last week. Fabulous! Will definitely return.  Waited about 30 minutes, which was acceptable, (I'd been warned.)  service was friendly and efficient. Portions were generous. Four of us ate for $73 which included tip.  Cash only, btw.

The hamburgers are great.... and it is a great place to watch a sporting event. However, on Friday nights, you might as well be at Chuck E Cheese's. They have an extra room that kids are running around and screaming in. But some of the kids get out, and their oblivious parents let them run wild around the main seating area. I would give this place a better rating if not for this.

It was close to 7:30 on a weeknight and since they close at 8, one staff was mopping the floor and the other was cleaning up.  I like the toasted subs so I've never been disappointed with one from Quiznos.  

The staff finished up and washed their hands and asked what we would like.  I decided on the 9 inch mesquite sub with chicken, lettuce, tomato, onion, cheese, bacon and ranch dressing.  With groupon in hand, I had to pay 60 cents for the tax and we took our meal to go.

I was disappointed with the sub.  The bun wasn't nice and toasty and a little bit soft likely from too much ranch dressing they put in.  I should have asked light on the dressing as I don't like too much sauce on my subs.  I won't get this sub next time.

Still a decent location and service so it wouldn't prevent me from going another time.

Stopped in on a Saturday night with 5 friends and they were able to accommodate us with no wait although it is a very small restaurant. Service was great and the tacos were delicious!! The shrimp had a kick to it and they do not skimp on the meat. A friend ordered the coco-ñada which we all agreed was very very good. Would have been 5 stars except it was very very warm in the restaurant. I'm not sure if they were having issues with ac or if it's normally that warm.

Why 4 stars? 

While the servers are nice, it took forever to get extra plates and our order of tortillas that come with the fajitas.

And the cheese can be overwhelming and artery clogging.

Don't wast your time and 10 bucks.  More hype than sandwich.  A little less meat than Pats next door but cheese wiz is authentic and onions tasted juicy.   Hold on ... Where's the beef?  Wow two lightweights.  No parking.  At $11  don't waste your time at pats either not gonna make me as happy as Jersey mikes or even wawa.

King and I Thai is a small close bet setting restaurant. It has a relaxed vibe that offers a nice drink selection in addition to great food! There are several veggies options here which I love and definite must have for me. Sitting can be quick depending on what time you arrive and your party size. Definitely an establishment to visit at least once whether you live in St. Louis or just visiting. Enjoy everyone!

Really delicious, but it's more of a slider than a burger. Think the regular McDonald's hamburger in terms of size.  Good fries, good sriracha mayo.

It's like they take the Miller Lite slogan way too seriously - great taste, less filling.

My husband and I went to dinner here for our 5 year anniversary . We were very pleased with the service the staff and the whole atmosphere. Gary was the best manager that night we went. He made sure everything was top top perfect for our date night. I got rib eye and my husband got filet mignon. Both were very delicious and tender loved everything we ordered. We are Very very pleased and we will for sure be returning.

Yes.  The service was relatively slow.  It was not busy day, the house was not full at all.  However, people who came later than us, served by another waitress, already placed their order when the waitress just put our drink on the table.  I had a side salad and 1 minute after the waitress put it my table, our entrees arrived.  Seriously?! I had to finish my salad in 1 min so that I can enjoy my hot entree in a freezing day?!  I had Masala Chicken. it was very salty.  I won't come back to this location again.

Excellent vibes. I want to hang out here. Just had biscuits and gravy with a fried egg and a black & white cocktail. Put me right. I've also had the burger for lunch and the pot roast at dinner. All good! Can't wait to come back and see what else they come up with. Oh yeah the almond croissant was excellent too. I'm really happy it's in my hood.

Adding to this review. The lattes are delicious and the ham and cheese croissant is super good. Once I had the chicken with accoutrements and it fed me for 2 days! I am saying this again. I really dig this place. The Hungry Pigeon is like going to a friend's house who happens to be an excellent chef and baker and loves to have people over.

First thing first the atmosphere and decor of Autograph is amazing. It is intimate without being too dark and claustrophobic, and artistic without being kitschy. Our dining area was the "autograph" area, with each booth containing a beautiful framed photograph, but each unique area of the restaraunt is worth checking out.

Our waitress was not just extremely nice and sociable, but she completely understood each dish, and was easily able to describe in detail the ingredients, flavor profiles, etc. 

Onto the food though. Absolutely worth the bill. We started with the Grilled Octopus and the Gemelli. If you are getting one dish in this building make it the Gemelli. Absolutely to die for. Few places I've been to have pasta (house made) so delicious, and the lobster bisque emulsion sauce with peas, mushroom, and sundried tomatoes made the dish heavenly. The Octopus was nothing to scoff at though, and the pimenton sauce it sat in was, as the waitress said, "so good you could bathe in it". 

For our entree my wife had the Veal and I had the braised short rib. While the short rib was perfectly cooked, I wish I ordered the veal. My God I could eat that every day. Each element on the dish led to one of the most perfectly balanced plates I've had out. We also ordered a side of the Truffle Mac and Cheese. It was not bad at all, though I wish they really put some big truffle shavings in there, as I couldn't really discern  any truffle. Besides that though the meal was all around phenomanal. We will be back for the Gemelli if nothing else (but we will definitely be eating more then just that, the gnocchi looks awesome)

Just ate at Asuka and it was the best sushi I've ever had. Very fresh fish. Best service I've ever had. A little hard to find but when you get here it is worth it. Nick is the best waiter I know. Very nice place I will be recommending this place to everyone I know
Finally open but not as good as the other one.  Myself and friends were not impressed.  Half a menu and chairs tight for movement.  Probably won't be back.

It is what it is! A dive bar. Cheap drinks, cheap (but surprisingly good) bar food, and music. Daily beer specials. Staff is attentive and you can always get a drink when this place is busy. One of the go to places in Edwardsville area - and they have live music and open mic at times.

My wife and I recently visited 18 On The Rocks while vacationing from Chicago. We had our four children all of whom are under the age of 7. We ordered them 3 kids meals which come with a drink included. We asked for kiddie cocktails to which the waiter replied that they had cool strawberry dacqueries for kids. We said great and he brought them out. When the bill came we were charged $5.00 for each drink! Keep in mind I had a domestic bottled beer that was $2.50! We explained that we had thought that the kids drinks were included with the meal and the waiter explained that the dacqueries were not part of the kids meal package. It would have been nice to know that as the drinks cost about the same as each meal. He felt badly that he did not explain that to us prior to ordering. He said that he would talk to the manager. The manager did not even come over to the table. The manager just said that the drinks were not part of the kids meals! Now we didn't even get the benefit of using the drinks that should have come with the meals! I do believe that it was an honest mistake on the waiter's part. However, the manager should have realized the mistake and corrected it. We would have really enjoyed this place but for that incident. Because of the manager's ignorance I would have to say that I would advise people to stay away. Every other place we visited in the area really catered to families and could not have been nicer. The way the management handled this at 18 on the Rocks was very surprising to us to say the least.

Superb food.

Slightly cheesy decor - trying a little too hard to seem "authentic".

But seriously superb food.

And they stock Bluecoat gin!

Chinese food tends to be hit or miss for me, all too often you'll ask for extra spicy and the food comes out bland.  Enter Jay's - Most Excellent Cafe.  I sometimes go into my office on a Saturday and thanks to GrubHub - I have ordered delivery from Jay's roughly five or six times.  The food has always been completely to my liking.  spicy, crispy, yummy, flavorful in every way.  As a 20 year vegetarian I appreciate the meat free choices.  I've had spring rolls, fried veg dumplings, the Chinese pizza and General Tso's Tofu - extra, extra, extra  spicy.  Everything was cooked to perfection and delivered piping hot.   I would recommend Jay's to anyone who loves delicious Chinese food and is in the Cherry Hill area.  (Get the Chinese scallion Pizza.....get two!)
You have to try their homemade food.  Awesome.  And then for desert try the triple chocolate cake with vanilla ice cream.  To die for.

Delicious good, wonderful service!   We stopped in a little after 10 a.m.  and there was a line to get in but the line didn't take long, they cleaned tables as soon as people got up, but did not rush people. Kiki was our server and was great, very personable, good at explaining menu options and making recommendations and very friendly. The other staff that also waited on us (brought out the food, topped off waters) were also all friendly and helpful. Just a great team with a good vibe. 

The food was really really good. I couldn't decide between the lemon corn cakes and the beer biscuit, but fortunately they also have a single lemon corn cake option so I got one for the 3 of us to try it. So good! The side of lemon meringue?custard? was so good, I could just eat that by itself with a spoon. :) The side of blueberry (sauce? jam?) was also really good, we tried each separately on the corn cake and mixed together and all options were good!

The powerhouse potatoes were delicious (potatoes, tofu, cheese, ___, & ___). My biscuit was really good, my egg was just how I like it (firm white, runny yolk) and the chili mayo and salsa were nice sauces to add. I'm veg so I got the black bean patty instead of the meat option, and that was the only meh thing in the whole meal (it was more moist/mushy than I prefer, but with the sauces I still ate it all). My aunts loved their orders, too (garden skillet w/ avocado, and the special California Benedict).

I will definitely be back for breakfast again, and looking forward to trying their lunch menu, too!
The sweet potato fries keep me coming back!! The food is great and the atmosphere is suited to buy casual for lunch but just fine in sweats and a hoodie. Love this place!

(Note:  Regular at this location since 2012.)

Why 5 stars?  

--Well crafted and delicious beers with many that rotate monthly/seasonally.  They have a dozen or so great beers on tap to choose from so I always have something that I like and that I'm in the mood for.

--Food is usually great.  There's an occasional miss but the servers/mgrs/chefs resolve without any issue.  I've had one miss in the last year but I'll give them credit for being innovative in the attempt.

--Great service.  Servers and management are friendly and attentive.

--Great with kids.  They just *get* kids!  The kids' food comes out with our drinks which means Mom and Dad can hold an actual conversation.

I've recommended this place to friends, colleagues, and visiting business partners from out of town - even for big business events and celebrations.  They've never been disappointed.

Our latest visit was no exception.  Our server, Nick, was super friendly and knowledgeable of all current food and beer offerings.  He was double-duty as a bartender and still checked on us regularly.  I had the Burger-of-the-Month which was cooked well and very juicy and flavorful!  As a healthy balance, I opted for "greens" instead of fries, which was a generous and fresh side salad.  My wife had a premium salad that she really enjoyed.  The kids tore through a pizza.  All left quite happy!

This was my third time here with my boyfriend. First time, we were both pleasantly surprised. The uni and scallops were amazing and the Dungeness Crab spectacular. The second time, they were out of uni but the two dozen fresh oysters made up for it! We had clam chowder, a lobster roll, and Dungeness Crab again. It was the best meal my boyfriend and I have ever had! The crab was flakey and fresh and probably the best crab we'd both ever had (we eat crab a lot.) THIS TIME HOWEVER, we came for our anniversary and got oysters, uni, and Dungeness crab. The scallops under the uni were warm and questionable but still good enough to eat. The oysters were fresh and good. When we got our 3 lb crab it was smaller than expected. We got an old rotten crab that had a bad aftertaste. It was 2 lbs at most. We didn't complain and just asked for our check, when our waitress was picking up our plates she dropped melted butter and crab juice all over my boyfriends jeans. She looked down at it and just said "I'll get you some water for that." WHAT?! An apology would've sufficed, which we did get when we were about to leave. It just seemed insincere and like she wasn't taking responsibility for her mistake. I work in a restaurant so I understand how it is, but I always apologize to paying customers when I'm at fault. Very disappointing for my go to seafood place.
Best Mexican Restaurant on 4th and it's a hidden gem. The food is traditional and you can't beat the prices for downtown.

I have been here a couple times, and now know what to look forward to. The soup is definitely a shining star. The hot red pepper oil spots floating on top are spectacular and make the soup sing. The little crispy rice noodles they serve on the side are a heavenly crunchy accoutrement to the soup.

Here is where life gets confusing. I mapped this out last time to make sure i get this right next time. They have a number on the menu that is both Pad Sew Eee (spelling is completely botched) and Drunken Noodles. Everytime, I am convinced it is Pad Sew Eee that i like. NO, it is the pefectly noodley delicious-ness that I happened to order once that is Drunken Noodles. I highly recommend this dish.

I have tried a few appetizers, but honestly, save yourself some time and just get the soup and some delicious entree.

Best breakfast for celiacs.
My wife is not a celiac but she really enjoyed what she had. 
Congratulations for this great tastes.

I travel all over for work. I live in t south where good BBQ is everywhere. I was reluctant to try this but based on the reviews I did. I got a pleasant surprise, very good brisket. They also have a nice arrangement of different sauces. I would recommend this place. I had lunch.

Cozy spot in downtown Wilmington. I read some good reviews about the place and decided to stop in for some breakfast. My fiancé had the chip beef----it was delicious (though I normally don't care for that kind of dish). I had the sunrise platter with turkey sausage, turkey bacon, 2 eggs and French toast. Everything was absolutely scrumptious. Our check was equally appealing. Both meals were less than $13. The staff is also very friendly and attentative.

I went to Taco Maya this weekend and had a chicken burrito. Size wise, I would put it on the same scale as a chipotle burrito, only 100% better tasting. Definitely get their queso on your tacos/burritos. I thought it was fairly priced considering you get a side of chips and salsa, too. I would say the service was so/so. They seemed alright, but the guy at the register seemed unhappy to be there. Inside the  restaurant is cute with Mexican decor and a variety of booths and tables. It was clean and I overall enjoyed my experience there.

My son and I had breakfast here when we visited UC Santa Barbara. It reminded me of places I'd known in the 50s-70s on trips to LA and San Diego. It was friendly and efficient. The coffee was more than decent. The food was ample, fresh, and well prepared. The service was timely and cordial. I'll make a point of returning for breakfast when in the area.

Great food is often overshadowed by not so great waitstaff and a TERRIBLE seating system. Don't bother coming here on a weekend morning. It's just not worth it. They cram as many tables as possible into a small space and the service is slow. If you run out of coffee, you'll be waiting a while. The worst part of Sabrina's though is the way they do seating. It seems like their policy is always changing. A couple of years ago, you could not be seated if your whole party wasn't present. Now I see people all the time camping out at tables for half an hour while the rest of their party wanders in. For me, the food does not make up for the lack of service. The food is not consistent, and I find that often details of my order (what kind of toast I order, "no onions", etc.) are ignored or forgotten. The food is pretty expensive for what you get. I don't go here unless I have friends who are really into it.

Ordered 3 chicken strips and received portions that were about the size of the business end of the plastic fork. Seriously. I asked if I had gotten a child's version in error and was told that the portion size has been reduced. I noticed the price has not been. No attempt was made to satisfy the customer. It was a "not my problem" response.
They use a hot air conveyer belt for an oven like dominos does. Sorry, if you don't have a real oven it tastes like bread with cheese and that's what you get. Guru my foot.
Thank you Thai Corner Cafe for the delicious dinner! Food was awesome and your contribution is appreciated! Saint Mary's loves you!

I went for happy hour on a Thursday around 5 pm.  We went to the wine cellar area of this establishment.  They had half price appetizers from 5-6 pm.  I decided to try something new after my friend told me about an espresso martini the waterwheel has on their menu.  It was yummy and filled to the brim!  As an appetizer, I ordered the crab meat martini which is lump crab meat served to you on a bed of greens with marinated cucumber and onion slivers.  The crab meat was quite tasty --- you could tell it was a good quality of meat!  The bartender was attentive, polite, and helpful with suggestions.  A very enjoyable experience for my first visit.

Awesome food red beans n rice, gumbo  and fried catfish was our meal, loved it!!!!!planing another trip very soon with this restaurant in mind Nick " Dominic" was the best owner/server, we will b back

Dirty diner and horrible service all the way up to the owner. 

It seems that the customer is never right at this place. We've been here a few times - simply because of the geographic location. Bad food, bad service and the worst attitude in the management I've ever seen at a restaurant.

Go to the Green Street Grill in Downingtown, or one of the many places in Phoenixville, if you're looking for brunch. Many other choices in the area if you're looking for lunch or dinner.

Stay away.
Solid burger, Benedict, and crispy potatoes. I only wish they salted the crispy potatoes more and accompanied it with a dipping sauce of some sort.

Beware,  there are 2 Picasso's very close to each other!  If you are meeting with friends make sure they specify where you are meeting!

I've come here a few times for Latin dancing on Tuesday nights.  

They serve alcohol and coffee drinks and have light snacks in the evenings.  I believe the sangria was a special for Tuesday night,  but it was so good! I've tried a few of the coffees and loved them also. 

My only complaint would be parking.  I avoid garages as much as I can and that's really the only parking available in this whole complex. When I did come out of the garage into the complex I was right next to Picasso's though,  so that turned out well.

Great food and very friendly staff. The outdoor seating is great and comfortable. The beer selection is on point. They offer so many sizes, short, pint, growler to try different beers it ends up being a really great experience to try something new. Will be back soon for sure!

Holy moly, I love the family style servings here! The duck wings were very unique, tender, and sweet  Also, I definitely recommend the Japanese eggplant because you get a blast of sweet flavors. We also got the pappardelle, which I don't recommend. The sauce was creamy and rich, but the noodles had a poor texture.

Should have listened to other Yelpers. This pizza was probably among the worst I've had...and I've had a lot of pizza. Cheese was barely melted. Had to throw it in the oven after it was delivered to finish cooking it. Pie was huuuuge, but still...not worth it. Pizza Hut is better, and that's saying something.
Food is great but who put one bathroom per gender in a restaurant that seats 100+ people? Total fail.

Great food atmosphere too casual date night and I loved the lobster bites appetizer. The aged steak was insane and I recommend this for a great food experience. The staff was very prompt and extremely on point
Super chicken nachos sooooo delicious ! Strawberry lemonade also so so good! Customer service very attentive

First cheesesteak in Philly did not disappoint. I almost went to Gino's or Pat's, but wanted something the locals recommend. Ordered with onions and sharp provolone. Absolutely incredible and highly recommend going here.

Kinda tired. Breakfast menu is good as are the cocktails. However the dinner menu is TIRED! Change the beef option. Used to dine at Culina often however we rarely ever go any more. No more open table reservations and a tired menu result in less patronage from us.

We stopped here for lunch on a Saturday after reading all of the great Yelp reviews.  We had a very nice meal.  My husband would have liked his sandwich to be a bit spicier, he complained to me that it was a little bland, but my blackened mahi tacos were spot on.  Our waiter was great and the patio was a very pleasant place to kill some time. We will definitely come back here again.

A friend told me I should check this place out on my trip.  The line was not too long, I'd say we waited about 20 minutes to order.  The food came to our table shortly after... About 10 minutes. 

I shared the Famous Ferdi Po'Boy (it's a pretty big sandwich).  It had roast beef, ham, debris and sat in au jus gravy. It was good but not something I would order again.

I also tried the Red Beans and Rice. It was okay. I had better in the French Quarter. 

I had a side of the potato salad which wasn't very good. 

All in all, I don't think I'd recommend this place to my friends visiting NOLA.

First off, let me say, this review is only based on the beer and service, I see many reviews for the poor food (which I can't comment on since I didn't order food), but I thought the service was great! 

I went to SB with a group of 12 others to celebrate a friend's birthday. The birthday boy suggested we hit up IV Loop because that was the thing back when he was at UCSB (oh yeah...we were a group of about 12 26-27 year olds, but we're all Asian so we looked like all the other barely 21 college students in the area LOL). We bought 3 pitchers and the owner asked if we wanted chilled glasses or plastic cups (it's like he knew we were planning on playing flip cup). We asked for plastic cups so we can play flip cup on the tables outside. The owner was so nice about it! He even came out with a pint of beer for the birthday boy on the house, made him down it, then stayed for a minute to cheer us on while we played flip cup! 

Great beer selection, various size choices, and super cool owner!

Their tacos are delicious! I was not too fond of them my first visit, but I think they just had an "off" day as the taco was very bland. But I came back and I am so happy I did! 

The tacos are (usually) very fresh and flavorful - and for only $3 each! I eat two and am very satiated and full. My favorite tacos are: chicken, spicy carne, sweet potato, and the tilapia. 

I have yet to try the sides or soup, but I have only heard great things about them. 

They only take cash or check, so be prepared. They do have an atm on site, but I'm assuming it has a decent fee. 

Order your food at the front and grab a table and wait for your name to be called. For those of you wanting to drink, try out their lime or seasonal margarita for a yummy treat or the Paloma for a refreshing drink. 

You have to order your drinks separately and go to the bar. However, I try to snag chairs at the bar that will allow me to order food and drink at the same time (you'll still have to walk up to the front to grab your food). 

Ample street parking too!

Come check it out!

I know. Yeah it's hard to image a 5 star...but I can't find anything I did not throughly enjoy this night. Ok, I could say that it would have been just a bit better to have more olives included on the humus dish...yummmm. This night, a Tuesday, found myself sitting at the bar in front of the wall of windows looking out foot traffic passing by. A nice glass of red wine top it off nicely.

I usually have the mahi-mahi tacos served with rice & beans, NEXT FAV is the Veggie sandwich! But you really cannot go wrong with anything on the menu!

My husband LOVES Franks for breakfast!  I am not a big breakfast eater... but I can get 2 eggs, toast, and hashbrowns for $2 at Franks! 

Don't go for the customer service! The servers are busy and have the "get in, eat, and get out" mentality... but hey, this place is small and they want to make some money!  Don't plan on sitting around here.  Food comes fast, is good and there is plenty of it.  It is definately not the "cleanest" of restaurants... Outside or inside is good- but don't plan on bringing more than four people or it may be a pain.

We decided, on a whim, to order a pepperoni pizza (we had actually gone there for happy hour).   The pizza we had was probably the best pizza I've had in many years - and I have eaten lots of pizza.  Wow, too bad there are not more places like this.  Service was impeccable.

We were here at 5:00 on a Friday and the place was dead. There were two other tables and one guy in the bar. There was no sushi available, there was no chef. The best part of this restaurant was the salsa. There were three and they were each very tasty. The margaritas were weak, and chillie rellenos was soggy and tasteless. I will not be back.

This place is a must when leaving or returning from MSY. It's places like these that make you want to move back to the craphole that the greater New Orleans area is.  You can't beat the affordability of the seafood as well as the quality. We had raw oysters, a few crabs, a poboy, and blackened alligator. It was all fabulous. It's a hole in the wall place that is next to a fresh seafood market. The decor and ambiance is lacking, but that's not what you are there for. The bathroom is cramped and stinky, try to avoid. The service was fine.
 I'll be stopping by this place to/from the airport from now on.

I got my food delivered from Uber eats, nothing wrong with the delivery service. But common guys your sending food out like this during a pandemic that looks like trash and not what's ordered? Ordered side of guacamole for 2.25$ and get like a 1/4 of a slice avocado lol what the hell? The two tacos were also sloppy and kinda lacking for the price. Plantain chips also tasted stale.

Perfect pizza. I have only had the Square but I've been to dozens of the best pizza places (apizza Scholls, amodern, all the New Haven spots, and many more) and this is my favorite (tied with Apizza scholls in Portland and Delancey in Seattle- both different styles). They are nailing it here.  My only issue is that I don't live right next door. I'd volunteer here just to be around this pizza if I could.

I visit Reno once a month for work, and usually wander around town with my coworkers looking for places to eat. We were walking downtown and this place caught our eye, as we walked by the plates looked very tasty, so we decided to step in. It was totally worth it. The menus are visually stimulating and even when we where really not that hungry, we tried the food. I, as always, WAS hungry, so i ordered the all you can eat special for 25 bucks, it includes entrees and unlimited rolls, so it definitely was worth it.  I tried like five different sushi rolls and they all were absolutely great. The portions were good, the flavor was great, the appetizers were awesome, and i definitely will come back to this place again.

I had a great plate of chili rellenos, rice and beans.  I liked how the food was fresh and a little different than a typical Mexican restaurant.  I tried my daughter's chorizo nachos and they were amazing!  Friendly and prompt service - I will definitely be back!

Got to the airport nice and early, decided on a cup of coffee. Despite the line I decided to grab a cup from River City. Mistake! I only bought a bottle of water and a small drip coffee, the cashier said she didnt hear mthat i ordered a coffee so had to wait for my cup. She wasnt happy about me! Then the dark drip was empty and the gal behind the counter was very unpleasant when i asked if there was any more! I didnt feel that a small drip coffee and a bottle of water was an extremely difficult order but the looks on the workers faces sure made it seem that i had asked the world. Won't bother next time!

When it comes to taste, I would give these folks a 5 star. Honestly, fantastic coffee, brewed to perfection. It is their customer service and friendliness which is lacking, hence the lower score. Most recently, I purchased their groupon which states you will receive a punch card for 10 visits, with each visit worth $4. Upon redeeming my groupon, I did not receive the punch card and when I asked questions felt as though I was talked down to. I was handed a cell phone by the employee to speak to the manager whom I asked how this was going to work if I don't get the punch card and I was hung up on. I'm not exactly thrilled with this experience whatsoever. On top of it, I was charge .50 cents still (reason unknown) as I have frequented this establishment now on a more than weekly basis since they opened and have never paid more than $3.95 for my medium decaf mocha (it's under $4!).
I was very disappointed in the boiled crabs and shrimp- pure quality and the place was dirty

I had read this is one of the restaurants you needed to try in Boise so after the wonderful vigil last night to support our community we headed over to enjoy dinner together. The portions were generous and the food was tasty. My daughter who has experience in Korean food said it was good but not totally authentic. The service was most excellent with an energetic and passionate server and the food hit the spot! Some of the side dishes that come with your meal like the eggplant was absolutely delicious as well as the tofu. It is wonderful to have a restaurant like this in Boise.
Very clean diner. Solid breakfast and great lunch options. Nice portions, service can be a little slow during peak times but not dreadful.
The food and service were both excellent here. My wife and I will be back whenever we are in the area. The hot chicken was great.

I hate to change a review to lower it (this is my first time), but in this case, it is necessary. True, a place like this is necessary in this area, and the decor is fabulous. However, Tela's really needs to follow through. Having been to the original Four Barrel and having had it at other coffee shops before, the coffee is honestly depressing here.  I don't know if it's untrained baristas, or its horribly watered-down, but their coffee is downright not good. It doesn't taste like Four Barrel at all, and for the amount of amazing lattes I can get elsewhere in the city, I probably will never get one here again.

This is a speciality "market", but the prices are too high and the portions are too small.  The breakfast burrito is minuscule. Also, I hate ordering something like a breakfast sandwich and getting nothing else with it!  Come on-- throw a piece of fruit or a couple greens on the side or something to make it seem more like a meal. 

I have been here about five times now, and honestly plan on avoiding it unless completely necessary, which really pains me.  They definitely have some work to do.
12 minutes! Thats how long it took from the time I hung up the phone until I was enjoying this delicious food. Food is delicious, affordable, and great variety. My new go-to north of Spring Garden.

This place has the best lemon/lime margaritas around! The tequila is excellent, and you can tell that the lemon/lime juice is squeezed fresh. Their guacamole is chunky and delicious! You can almost eat the guac appetizer as a meal! Their complimentary chips & salsa are pretty tasty as well, chips are not greasy. Some of their menu items are over-priced for what you actually get, but everything is still tasty. The atmosphere is great as well, but sometimes it can get loud in the evenings.

Although Pei Wei isn't my first choice for Asian cuisine but when it's the closest thing I have when I am in the Westshore area, I will take it! I ordered the Chicken Pad Thai there and for some reason, I enjoyed it more than I thought I would. It is a good mix of flavors but you can tell it's not Thai authenticated Pad Thai flavors but it was still good! I always enjoy getting the Pad Thai at Pei Wei and is probably the only thing I get as everything else is kind of iffy. Service was okay, I had take out. Order, take and go! This visit was good.

I WILL NEVER ORDER FROM THIS PLACE EVER AGAIN!!! I placed my order at 1 PM and was advised it would be an hour before I would receive it. 2 hours later, I'm still waiting for my food so I call back. The person who answered said it would be here in 1-15 minutes. Another hour later, I'm still waiting for my food so I call back. The cashier tells me they were at my location but someone else had a problem with their food. What the HELL THAT HAS TO DO WITH MY FOOD? Nothing. The idiot delivery person took my food back with him and never attempted to contact me ONCE! The cashier tells me they would have to make another and it would be a while. I waited for him to make some type of concession: it's on us, let me throw in a free dessert, something. HELL, AN APOLOGY would have been nice. I didn't even get that and when he did not, I WAS DONE!!! I DON'T THINK SO, BUDDY. You can't make anything for me. You can shove that sandwich UP YA ASS!!! This company will not get a DAM dime from me!!!

Love places like this. We got the donuts hot from the belly (dont even know where you make donuts...oven? Pan? Lol) anyway the donut is better when it is cooled off. It has a more light and cakey texture unlike the onces I like from Dough. Still very good. I ate the cinnamon brown suger ones. People like to work there. You can tell they are happy employees. A place that takes care of their workers deserves my patronage! Good old school 80-ies music to complete the federal experience. Love it!!

This place is great.  Good drinks, too.  It is good every time we go.  Sitting in the bar area is not so fun for a meal, but that's a small gripe.  It's a joy to eat this food.  And to drink the tequila.

The tostadas de ceviche are always worth it.  Any of the ceviche, really.  Also  good is the salmon with mole.  Although, this would be better with salmon from Alaska.

This place is honest and filled with talent.

Stumbled upon this little hidden gem and decided to stop in and grab a bite. The restaurant has a real old school diner feel complete with red and white checkered tablecloths. We were greeted warmly by the waitress. The menu was pretty standard seafood flown in fresh daily. The sauce from the crawfish boil was delicious! And you can adjust the spice level to your liking. The soft shell crab fried just right. The staff were all very friendly and they worked together very well. Would definitely come back to this spot.

Food all tasted the same.  Huge portions but so so good.  Spinach in salad was not clean, had large stems, and had some mushy leaves near bottom.  Light raspberry dressing was thick and plopped out of container into salad.  Macaroni and cheese was really good.  Food was way overpriced for quality.  Will not return.
Good wing deal but they weren't that good. Breaded and drenched in grease. The basement has a bunch of cool games to play.

This was our first time here and we loved it! 
The drinks were delicious and fresh. The food was amazing! I had shrimp queso and tacos. I can't wait to try more! To top it all off, the bartenders, Julio and Diego,  went above and beyond for us tonight! This is definitely our new "go to" Mexican for many reasons and we can't wait to bring our friends here.
Very clean inside, despite how the exterior looks. Service was nice, the food is good, and the portions are hefty for the price!

Joey Bs never disappoints. My husband and I try to stop here whenever we are in town.  We have yet to have something we don't like. I recently ordered the buffalo chicken salad. Ummm... Yummy! I couldn't stop eating. Our wait staff was great and food came out warm.

Disclaimer: I am not a member. However, I was seriously considering getting one if I had an awesome experience.

Obviously, great cocktails and tater tots. So fluffy, hot, and melt-in-your-mouth truffle heaven. Definitely get those. 

However, the entree plates were pretty underwhelming for the price point. We got the Amish chicken and pistachio-crusted duck, but both were lackluster. Absolutely no wow-factor at all. Everything was served rather cold and their foie gras with the gelatinous "chicken sausage" left me wondering if it was some kind of culinary joke.

Intimate decor and ambiance, but the windows were quite drafty so I felt cold the entire evening. That was rather unpleasant. 

Given the price point and business model, I feel the staff could use more training. My waitress was friendly and kind, but she wasn't very knowledgeable about the menu. In addition, the staff were dressed too casually. The male staff wore button-up shirts at least, but the female staff were basically in what could pass for pajamas. Management must be going for some laid-back work culture, but it doesn't jive with the atmosphere. I don't know how I feel about dining at a place where the customers are (mostly) dressed to the nines while the servers are dressed like students. If I'm shelling out my hard-earned dough for a luxury dining experience, I expect impeccable service. (This reminds me of where I've had the best service by far in St. Louis: Sydney Street Cafe and Tony's)

Bottom line: If you're looking for great drinks, you can easily go to Taste. I entertained the idea of getting a membership just for the tater-tots, but I'll pass.

Below average Chinese buffet.  A handful of chicken dishes in different sauces and some greasy pizza and crab rangoon.  Dubious sushi bar and  a few sliced fruit and pudding for desert.  For $10 you are better off ordering something you like from a decent Chinese restaurant.

Our Uber driver suggested Biscuit Love Hillsboro instead of The Gulch to avoid the ridiculous line. It was definitely a ProTip. When we got inside, there was a bit of a line, but nothing like what we saw as we were leaving (it was around the corner and down the block a bit). 

Firstly, the staff were phenomenal. I ordered a Bloody Mary, and when the cashier checked my ID, he mentioned that our birthdays were close - I'm from the Northeast and really not used to friendly conversation, and it was a really sweet, funny exchange - a great start to a brunch experience. 

Secondly, the atmosphere is darling. Super instagrammable, if you're into that kind of thing. Also, they have a choice of sparkling and still water that you can serve yourself - it's the little things that make a difference. 

Lastly, the food - I got the egg plate. It was no frills, just the way my Mum makes (actually Mum, if you read this - your breakkie is way better, obviously, I know it's made with love). The bacon was cooked perfectly, and the eggs and grits were great. 

I'm glad that we experienced Biscuit Love, but I'm not sure that I would return - it was a fun time, but I'm not entirely sure what the hype about this place is...

We used to go to Affton Cafe. Really wanted it to be great, but the service and food was up and down. New management has really increased the level of service and consistent quality of food. Give it a chance and support family owned local businesses!
Wow this was an awesome lunch. Italian beef was tasty. Mouth watering with giadinera on it. My husband ate Mama's Special 9" pizza. Amazing. Love the Provel cheese authentic to St. Louis pizzas.

Just went before a game for a drink but ate the queso which was good. I gave 4 stars because I got 2 drinks, margaritas, but they were both made different.  One was lime juice then my next was sweet and sour mix only.
Had an awesome brunch here with a family member. The service was good, the coffee was good, and the food was good. Definitely recommended. I wish they opened a little earlier, but otherwise great!

AMAZING! My favorite restaurant in Nashville! Have been a fan of Ethiopian food ever since I've tried this place! The marinated lamb is my favorite dish here but all the meats are amazing! Very affordable and great service! HIGHLY RECOMMEND!

Tried this place out recently for brunch.  It's an all you can eat buffet with various food and drink stations at the mid $30 mark per person with booze included.  The alcoholic beverages included bloody marys, mimosas, white and red sangria.  

Food options were diverse from some token Mexican items, salsa/guac, chips, the normal breakfast foods (eggs/bacon/sausage/French toast/pancakes), and there were other options including meat carving stations and steamed crab legs and shrimp.  The dessert options weren't as plentiful as there was fruit and some breads to dip into the chocolate fountain that seemed to be sputtering all over the table.  Overall not a bad option if you're looking for an all you can eat type of meal with some booze included.  The quality of the food is decent and buffet grade.

Solid cheesesteak!
More like a 3.5 but definitely above average.
I would prefer a better roll. I would guess it was an amoroso or Lucio's. 
Cheese was mixed in well and steak was fresh but prolly frozen.

I've been going to Sister Muhammad's for a very long time. Before the remodel, and they've always had GREAT food. The best Fish sandwich/hoagie in Philadelphia hands down...
I give it 4stars because not only is the food good, it's clean, service is good, and did I say they have the Best Fish Hoagie in Philadelphia?

We tried to visit last week on a Wedneday and arrived there at 9:00 p.m. The hotess told us they were closed. We clearly could see the sign for the hours and it read that the store closes at 9:30 Mon-Thur. When we questioned the hostess, she lamely answered " sometimes we close early". We didn't want to waste our time arguing about this but we did see others coming in after us!  We were outdone! Codys owner or management needs to speak to their staff about correct customer service and not being selective as to who comes into their establishment.

I'm stuffed. Totally, uncomfortably, regrettably stuffed. You might ask me if I'm so stuffed why would I decide to sit in front of the computer and writing a review? I should walk it off or do some exercise or something. Yes, that would be the healthy thing to do but I didn't say I was health-smart and I need to write things down when my memory is still fresh.

Some odd years ago when Ms.Tootsie first open, I came here all by myself to try out this then new establishment in the near edge of Broad and South. I was the only non-Black person in the restaurant and even though it was a bit intimidating, the waitress I had made me felt right at home. It was excellent food, excellent service and excellent ambiance, honestly I don't know what have kept me from coming back all these years.

After I don't know how many renovations, I'm back again with a friend. The place has done well for itself, With dark wood tables and white plush chairs and banquette, it reminds me of exotic resorts in St. Tropez or Bahamas, places that I've never been. The roomy, luxurious bathroom is hidden behind cushioned wall. Red glassware lined a cube shelf installment. Right next to the buddha statue, a church podium and saloon doors separates the next door bar lounge. My favorite artist Jill Scott's newest album playing in the air. I'm already in love with this place.

The servers are as friendly as ever if not friendlier. There are smiles, they act like they've known me even though I'm sure that I've never met them before. I remembered having Ms. Tootsie's Famous Ice Tea with a huge take away cup with slices of orange, melon and watermelon inside, so when I reordered it and see only a slice of watermelon atop a glass stemware, I was a little disappointed. 

After ordering, a plate of hot corn muffins and strawberry butter were brought in front of my friend and I and they were delicious. It's rare that I can find cornbread better than my own but theirs were fluffy soft and mildly sweet. Not overpowering and with enormous fresh taste. I wish there were more strawberry flavor in the strawberry butter and I wish I was having waffles but it works out well enough.

For appetizer, the boyfriend and I decided to have catfish and fries. To be quite honest, the appetizer section of the menu is strange considering they are almost all fried items with fries, qualified to be entrees in most diners. The catfish fingers were glorious. Soft catfish wrapped inside the most delicate crust. The Louisiana remoulade that accompanies the fish is slightly sweet and sour which elevates the catfish into something completely heavenly. The fries are meaty and crispy, tossed with cayenne pepper and mixed spice, think a spicier version of the fries at Burger King. The drawback is, after sharing this appetizer with my boyfriend, I'm already full.

My boyfriend ordered fried chicken (a breast and a wing) with black eye peas and candied yam for entree and I had the ribs with cabbage and rice and gravy. The chicken here were fried hard, I've never been a fan of white meat except in boyfriends. I find breast, especially fried, is usually too dry. The black eye peas is earthly and sandy with subtle pleasing flavors. The candied yam can almost qualify as a dessert, the already decadently sweet yams drizzled with a caramel sauce, how is this a side dish? I got three meaty and large ribs with a rich, yummy BBQ sauce. I like my cabbage on the softer side but the ones here were very well done. I like my rice on the softer side as well, and I like the gravy to be a bit runny so that it can cling and mix to the rice a bit easier. 

Overall though, the food is great, the environment and staff inviting. We couldn't finish the food and we have to ask for boxes. All the better, I love leftovers. I will definitely try to be back more often. LivingSocial or not.

The modern blue glass decor is wonderful, with a spectacular walk-in wine cellar.  The seafood was excellent as well and can be enjoyed with a view of Tampa Bay.  

If you're staying at the Westin, it's a no-brainer.  If you're in the area, definitely a place to consider.

i go here at least twice a month with my girlfriend and the experiences just get better and better every time. the owners are beyond friendly and the food is amazing. all of their sandwiches are to die for and the breakfast menu is all kinds of delicious. they grow a lot of their vegetables themselves and they don't shy away from answering any questions regarding their food. 10/10 would recommend!
Food was excellent. We will definitely begin to eat here regularly. Yummy!! Restaurant was clean and the staff was very courteous.

It was Saturday evening on me and my girlfriend'a second anniversary. After much deliberation on what restaurant to go to, we finally decided to try this nice little place. Came in to what looked like a small cheese shop and we were asked if we wanted to sit in the garden. I was confused because I did not see any seating outside but decided to see what happens. We got led outside then through a passage that went around the restaurant to the back. It was dark and very enchantingly lit. Looking up there was a leafy tree with huge leaves and a clear sky. The middle of the garden was covered in pebbles that added a nice touch to the atmosphere. In the corner was a small fountain that produced a calm trickling sound. We ordered one of the cheese samples, the prosciutto wrapped dates, and the passyunk. The cheese sample was great but it was the condiments that really made it. The toasted bread was the perfect texture and the jam that came with it went great with the cheese. The dates were stuffed with a tart cream-cheese like cheese and had a satisfying combination of flavors. The passyunk, a cheese pasta which stood out from your typical Alfredo type dishes. The service was great and the decor, especially the water pitcher (comes in a stopped bottle), was very nice. I would definitely come back and try more of the cheeses, they have an amazing selection and are glad to help you choose!

Establishment was closed on 1/23/20 by the health department due to rodent droppings and a dead mouse in the kitchen. Reopened a couple of days later.

Download Washoe Eats app for health department inspection reports.

*Update: Get the n ew crispy chicken sandwich.  It's about 2,000 calories of pure delish-SHISH-NESS!  Boo rah!


Thank heavens they now deliver!  Formerly Joey's Stone Fired Pizza.  They kept the pizza recipe, which is awesome.

Now they've expanded the menu and deliver nearby, which is what a pizza place needs to do these days to survive.  Especially in a residential area. 

I had the Italian burger with mozzarella and a basil tomato.  Portion was huge, burger made in-house from ground beef, and hand-cut fries were outstanding.  Crispy with a nice thickness.  I could definitely see getting those fries smothered in their tomato sauce with cheese or something.  Yum.

The Caesar salad could still use a little more dressing.  Good flavor, but it's lacking a little punch.

Otherwise, the prices are reasonable and the quality is excellent.  I love their pizza and now can enjoy an expanded menu and delivery.  Glad they're still around in a slightly new incarnation!

I'm glad I went well after the hyped died down.  There was a small line on the day I decided to go.  I was happy to finally try Bobby's Burger Palace and I was not disappointed.  

It was difficult deciding on which burger to order.  I narrowed it down to three burgers and my final decision was made at the register.  I ordered the Dallas burger, sweet potato fries, and a dark chocolate milk shake.  The Dallas burger comes with coleslaw, pickles, BBQ sauce, and Monterey jack cheese.  I was dinning inside so I was given a number to place on my table.  The server comes out with your order a item or two at a time.

The hamburger was very moist and had a good beef flavor.  The toppings went well with my patty.  The sweet potato fries were very good.  I was a little skeptical at first because sweet potato fries is an item that most establishments mess up.  My fries had a nice crunch to them.  The honey mustard horseradish sauce was sweet and tangy with a little kick from the horseradish.  My milkshake was thick.  To be honest, the ice cream tasted like Breyers. I was expecting a homemade, artisanal, ice cream.  Especially from an Iron Chief.  Five dollars for a milk shake is not cheap!    

The decor of the restaurant has a sixties look to me.  They have long communal dinning tables therefore there is little intimacy.  Bobby's burger palace is a nice option when you want something besides Five guys, Jake's Wayback, or dare I say fast food.

So good, massive portions. 

Musts: scallion pancakes, Dan Dan noodles, spicy cucumbers.

1st we went in to order and the employees didn't even acknowledge that we were there finally another customer told us they were only taking orders via their app because they said that they were too busy strange only 3 customers in the place so we ordered on the app waited 30 minutes for the 2 burgers fries and drinks $33 we should have left like the 4 other customers who came in after us that after being ignored walked out. The food was not really that good the fries were cold and nasty, I would suggest if you're thinking about going to this place just go a short distance past them to Wendy's and get a much better burger at a much lower price. Oh and the foul language from the one employee and them talking about the people who walked out because "they were too lazy to order from the app" maybe the lousy employees who were too busy discussing how much better life was in Norway and talking loudly using foul language should have used that time to wait on customers.
