So glad we stopped here on the way to that big thing in the desert!  Entering the restaurant feels like you've stepped into a bright, beautiful desert oasis--rain even falls from the ceiling!

I always order green curry at every Thai restaurant I visit and the curry at Cafe De Thai sets the bar very high.  The vegetarian curry was flavorful and gently spicy with lots of fresh veggies and tofu.  I practically licked the plate clean hoping that I could remember it as I lived on granola bars and cup o noodles for a week at Burning Man!

The drink menu was impressive and our server recommended the drink of the day--a homemade soda that was bright and fruity without being too sweet.  I ordered one and my partner had to have their own after tasting my drink!  LOL!  

Service was top notch and everyone was super friendly and attentive.  My heart and belly were both full after dining at Cafe De Thai.  Thank you so much for a "last meal" to remember!

The food was delicious and the customer service was awesome. I would definitely recommend the place. I ordered through the website. It was easy and they called me within 30 minutes to pick up my order.

Pricey AF. I only ordered one cheeseburger combo, and a double cheeseburger no combo l, got charged for two combos. Didn't realize till after I paid and got my food.

Nothing like In -N- Out. Don't know why everyone says that. Is it just cause the thousand island on the burger? Idk.

I won't be back

During the light-fair couldn't avoid visiting the Reading Market daily. Particularly this Puerto Rican place....
The food amazing, I felt like eating food cooked  at home... the rice was tasty..
The prices are ok....
Just some attitude from an employee.... not enough to not comeback....food worth it.
About 20 taps with great beers in each. That is as good as it gets. Good environment, lots of room too. I would definitely come back again and again.

Run of the mill bar in Conshy. When I was there it was overly crowded, which seems to be the norm there. Personally I don't see what the lore is but some people just love this place. I found myself waiting and waiting and waiting to get a drink from the bar. Thats not really my style since I can just go to the GAP and get drinks right away and not feel like a sardine.

Bottom line; Seems to have its own "cult" following that I just dont get. If you like crowds and slow service, give it a whirl.

Family run. Good Wine. Authentic Food. Out-of-this-world Lemon Cake. Amazing. Will go back all the time. They might get sick of seeing my face. Can't say enough about the amazing service and great experience I had.

Nice place but I wouldn't make a special trip to hang out here. It happened to be next to our hotel so we gave it a try. I ordered the ahi tuna:  it was served lukewarm with a lump of rice and a salad that was essentially a heap of lettuce and not much else. I hear the pizza is good; kind of hard to mess up pizza though.

It was a Saturday night and we did not have a reservation but we were able to get a table which was very nice! A little hidden gem. Atmosphere was nice. Service was attentive and the food was very good! We did have a slight hick up with an allergy and they brought food out with the known allergen but quickly replaced the meal with a new plate. We ordered the truffle fries for the table and everyone said they were great, including the kids. My husband ordered the fish and chips and said it was soggy so maybe not their specialty. My mother in law had the rib appetizer and said it was fabulous. So, I think there are lots of good options to choose from on this menu. The staff makes you feel very welcome and that your business is appreciated. We will return!

Saturday night. Warm. Sat on the patio. Great vibe, wait staff was really nice. The owner stopped by the table to chat. Food was authentic with large portions. It's been a while since we ate there but it's back on our radar screen. A perfect pick for a good summer night dinner.

This place is beautiful , modern and new . Super clean and has a pretty upscale vibe to it . They have extremely good lighting too . I know that sounds random but good lighting is important to me ... The Margarita pizza is definitely one of the better ones in town and cooked in a pizza oven to perfection. The salads and Everything is really fresh & the staff seem friendly . What's not to like ? The prices . It's hella expensive here but you get what you pay for . 
I would also recommend sitting at the bar top if you are looking to catch up w/ a friend or on a date because it's more intimate and you don't have to sit at the tables that are so close together and listen to other peoples conversations . However I would recommend it to others and totally can't wait to come back !

After waiting quite a while to be greeted, the two girls at the sports bar hardly made eye contact and were incredibly rude. We watched many other patrons be greeted almost immediately, and when finally asked if we wanted to order, the servers acted as if we were an inconvenience. The food and drinks may be good but I never got the chance to find out. If you're looking for a personable experience, look elsewhere. Bummer.

big fan of this place.  plenty of beers on tap good service even on busy nights.
lots of fun to be had here

My darling wife and I made a reservation through YELP and enjoyed a wonderful evening at this classic French Quarter restaurant.  We arrive about ten minutes prior to our reservation and we directly seated.  Jonathan was our waiter and the absolute definition of professional.

We started our delightful evening with an order of Mcilhenny Oysters and Escargots Orleans. I had to try their Turtle soup so we also order a cup size for tasting.  All three of these were outstanding and we would highly recommend you try them.

We complimented our food choices with a wonderful Sauvignon Blanc and Pinot Noir, both by the glass.

Our entre selections were the filet (for her) and the prime rib for me.  Both were prepared perfectly as we ordered and the filet was so tender you could literally cut it with a fork.  Wonderful taste.  It has been a long time since I have eaten prime rib so I was excited to select it as my entree. As I mentioned it was prepared perfectly and I savored every bite.  The only thing I would do next time different would be to order the 12 oz instead of the 16, because that was a LOT of meat.  I guess my enthusiasm overcame my judgement in selecting the size.

Having such a wonderful meal of appetizers and entree's we passed on desert but next time we plan to order the Banana's Foster and share it between the two of us.  Maybe choosing only one appetizer instead of two.

If you have an opportunity to enjoy an evening at Dickie Brennan's, don't pass it up.  Restaurants like this don't come along often and we are so glad that we chose it for our evening.

i do LOVE Enoteca!! Downstairs @ Goose the Market ........i usually don't quote (or drink much wine)  but 
Wine and beer by the glass at the Goose: introducing the Enoteca

Visit the Goose's cellar where the Enoteca is now open!

In Italy, the neighborhood enoteca is where wine is stored, bought, and consumed. In Indy, the Goose's new Enoteca is a casual place to drink wine.
i love the HUGE communal tables!!

Lovely decor, warm atmosphere, and really great service every time .  Great place for vegans !My favorite dish is the Tornado tofu and veggie sushi. Yum! Fresh veggies that are steamed perfectly . Tofu was crispy and the coconut curry was very flavorful . Our waiter tonight was soooo helpful and knowledgable . Veggie summer roll and miso soup are yummy ,too. They have a vegetarian section so it's easy to navigate the menu.
Fantastic salad and rubyn!! Christina with hair flower is an awesome server! Excellent service!

The food here is fantastic! The drinks are just as good. The historic space is hip and open. Unfortunately the entire experience is marred by the poor service. I mean, I understand and even appreciate hipster aloofness to a certain degree, but this is your job! Please care.

This is easily my favorite local Mexican restaurant and having eaten there with Mexican friends who agree I feel compelled to write a glowing review. I've eaten here at least 5 times since I discovered it only a year and a half ago and I tend to order the same thing when I find something I like but their Chile Rellenos are not to be missed as far as I am concerned- you can get them in any of the combination plates and they are actually cooked the right way (in my opinion) Poblano chiles filled with melted cheese I make mine filled with jalapeno cheese but this is as close as I can come to the perfect one in a restaurant since their sauce is so good. Their burritos, steak fahitas, chimichangas, guacamole and flan are fantastic. In fact, according to my friends they've never had a bad meal here so you can proceed with confidence. This is a local favorite of mine and I've eaten in at least every Mexican restaurant in this city.
This Moe's is beyond generous and very clean. They always make sure my food is just how I like it. Adding on to that, their employees are just Divine and lovely.
Empanadas are Delicious! I always go here when visiting Santa Bárbara. You must try you won't regret it!

I really enjoyed my experience here. We came for a later lunch after day of holiday shopping so we arrived famished. Next Door is a beautiful establishment and I love the decor. The service is friendly and attentive. You have every option from vegan to gluten free to meat entrees. I'm excited to come back when it warms up a bit to seat outside. From the other reviews I've read that's an experience in and of itself.
Although Blue Bell isn't exactly a hot spot for thai food, this place is amazing. Pretty much every dish on the menu is consistently fantastic. Personal favorite is the massaman curry

A lot of places in Indy claim to have have the best tacos in town. I had yet to see a real competitor for that title until I visited this place. It's so quiet and unassuming. I got so distracted by all the delicious goodies in the grocery that I almost forgot about the restaurant! I ordered the Carne Asada tacos (3), it was the most flavorful meat I have ever tasted. I was surprised that the ketchup and mustard bottles were actually truly delicious green and red sauces. Dear god the red sauce was spicy, but ohhhhh so good. The green was flavorful as all get out! I honestly cannot even believe how delicious everything was!! I would give them an extra star if I could!

Much better than Largo store. Mashed potatoes are hot and spicy gravy has a little kick, and it's delicious. Mac-n-cheese is creamy and it has actual seasoning on top. Southern chicken tenders are perfect, not greasy. I'm glad I gave Joella's a second try, all thanks to Dakota.  I'll be back with my family.
Wow! The beignets coffee, people watching and street jazz are the best anywhere.  Don't leave New Orleans without enjoying this place.

AMAZING!!! had my first po boy in new orleans here...and i loved it! the soft shell crab po boy was delicious. i came back a second time during my visit and tried the alligator, but i wasn't such a fan of it. 

this place is a MUST if you're in the french quarter or any other part of new orleans!

I was super hungry and my friends were trying to go to dive bars, so I wasn't allowed to get a burger at Bishop's and this is where we ended up.  

The address is a little weird here, as the entrance is on the backside of the Philadelphian on Fairmount.  They have a nice little courtyard with tables and umbrellas, and allow smoking but don't provide ashtrays.  It seemed we were the only people there under 60, and since it was Yom Kippur they had a fully kosher menu addition.

I got chicken fingers and fries and an Amstel light (p.s.  cheap beer selection), but unfortunately everything was a little over done.  Plus they mixed my honey mustard with the BBQ sauce which creeped me out because I really hate (cheap) BBQ sauce.  My friends really liked their meals (western omelet, bagel w/ cream cheese and lox, and a french onion soup).

The service was really good, even if our waitress was new and very unfamiliar with the menu.  We were seated immediately and they kept offering us bread and water.  

I think I'll try this place for breakfast (the omelet looked fantastic!), but not again for dinner.

Such a treat! We got to sit at the bar. Loved the bartender/server. I think his name was Neal. Such a nice guy. This dinner was fantastic. The steak was cooked perfect, came out on a hot plate sizzling. Creamed spinach was nice and went well with my buttery ribeye. Excellent flavor. My hubby loves shrimp and the shrimp were gigantic and the sauce was nice. We probably didn't need the chocolate cake but why not. Life's short. Glad we did. We had a fun night out. The interior of the Restuarant was gorgeous as well. Thank you! We will be back.
Pretty good. It reminds me of an upscale and hip restaurant in LA, which Tucson has very few. Is a good place to go with a friend or on a date to split a salad and split a pizza.

I have ordered pizzas from this Imos several times in doing business with them. I ordereda deluxe pizza Online for the first time and when it was delivered it was overloaded with cheese. I called them about it and they told me that at first I could get another pizza. Then I receive a call back from the manager and he told me that I should have  specified light cheese when I ordered it online.

I have never ordered a deluxe pizza and had to specify like to eat before. They always have had a very perfect blend of cheese and sauce. The manager then tells me that he is not going to send me another pizza. In the first place I didn't ask for the pizza I was making them aware of the overabundance of cheese. His attitude was so nasty that I told him I would never do business with them again. He told me "that's fine go somewhere else". For a business trying to succeed this not the way to make a customer happy. I will never do business with them again. Neither will my family or anyone else I can talk to about it.

This place has come in clutch so many times by being available via UberEATS! 

I absolutely have enjoyed how prompt my food arrives and the great quality it's in upon arrival. I manage a team overnight and we sure do enjoy good pizza. 

Thank you for always being available. The only other thing I've tried was a chicken sandwich and house salad. Really good!

I have passed by Lubeley's many times but never actually stopped until one day whne I saw that they had Pumpkin Doughnuts. I figured I would give it a try, however i was a little disappointed because they were all out (it was 5:30 so I give them that). I decided that I couldnt leave empty handed and picked up a couple other doughnuts. Overall I wasnt that impressed, the doughnuts were average, the icing was actually the best part very good. I didnt have a chance to try the cafe, so I cannot really speak for that.

Did a 3-course dinner tonight and all 3 courses are highly recommended ... 1. Chargrilled Oysters ‒ Drago's invented and popularized these, so you definitely can't go wrong.  2. Lobster Marco (pictured) ‒ extremely good.  Make sure you top it with the crabmeat.  3. Brownie a la mode ‒ a little dessert delight, probably was an overkill but it was good.

It was a 45 minute wait, but we'll worth it. I usually will leave if it's that king of a wait, but since we were in no hurry, we waited and shopped around. The food is served family style, meaning whatever you order, everyone gets to partake in, so you get to have a little bit of everything. All you can eat for about $20 a person, plus your drinks. Kids are a little cheaper. I can't remember how much tho bc we didn't have kids. I highly recommend this place!

If you're familiar with employees who get so hype over seeing their friends as customers to the point that they stop and make conversation, this is one of those places. Nothing wrong with small chatter, but if it disrupts your work flow and you have other customers waiting while you're fraternizing, rather obnoxiously, then it's a problem. 

Food-wise, quality varies but never to the point of no return. However, something hard was in the brown rice that could be dried up or something else altogether. Tables are also usually dirty, I don't have a problem cleaning them myself, but others might. Hence the one time, a customer approached me and my friends and suggested we complain. The manager, however, noticed and gave us coupons so that was nice.
Service was excellent but food was not... I got the boudin grilled cheese. It was the driest sandwich ever! Drinks were good though. Very small menu

Dined solo at the bar as an out of towner. Service was quick and friendly. It's a bit loud, but since I was alone, the noise level didn't bother me as much as if I was trying to converse with others. I ordered the nacho mommas - yikes! It was a lot of food for one person and I should have probably gotten something else. The nachos had good flavor though and were yummy so I guess no regrets.

Eh. We went here for brunch on a Sunday because of its proximity to where we were to be later that day. I ordered one of the specials for the day - pumpkin spice waffles -and he ordered french toast. The waffle seemed as if it had been nuked in the microwave (i.e. it was floppy instead of crispy) and both our dishes were drowned in hot syrup. Yep, came to the table in a syrup soup, so-to-speak. It was way too sweet. The french toast was mediocre. Neither of us came close to finishing our meals. However, the the Bloody Mary was nicely made and spicy. We will not be returning for food, but maybe afternoon drinks only.

Overall Value:  We came for a birthday dinner for my mom, and splurged on a really nice dinner.  The food was fantastic, but it gets a bit too pricey for dinner for my frugal tastes.  That said, they threw in a bunch of free dishes and the service was amazing, but I'll probably still limit myself to restaurant week (which is a 5-star value) and lunch in the future.

The Food: High quality tapas at a high price.  I'll just give blurbs about each to keep it short (-ish), in the order of what we enjoyed most. 
Pernil Asado ($18): OMG the crispy skin on this pork.  It's a must get. Super fatty in all the right ways, and perfectly balanced by the white beans/arugula to cut some of the richness.
Empanada ($12): Oh my, a surprise hit!  I almost didn't even bother ordering this, and we ended up getting a double order.  The super crispy shell with the incredibly flavorful interior (spinach, manchego, artichoke) was amazing - best empanada I have ever had.  
Manchego ($9): I could drown in that truffled lavender honey.  
Chorizo ($10): two skewers of 3 pieces each come in an order, and we got two orders.  Very bold flavors in the grilled chorizo - my mom wasn't a fan even though she normally likes chorizo, but my wife and I really enjoyed it.    
Mixto of cured meats ($17): I love spanish cured meats.  I'm a little spoiled because you can get a whole package of acorn-fed Iberico in Spain for like $5, but we aren't in Spain, and this brought back good memories.
Garlic Shrimp ($12): Very garlicky and flavorful, and served with bread which is great to soak up the garlic oil goodness.
Pinxtos de pollo ($15): Good flavor on the chicken and crispy sweet breads, although the rice was a bit bland (didn't really get much saffron).
Huevos rotos ($11): Interesting that they use potato chips for this.  Good flavor combination but maybe a bit too salty with the serrano and chips without enough else to balance it out.   
Croquetas de jamon ($7):  Super crispy exterior and flavorful.  An old standby for tapas. 
Patatas bravas ($7): I think I enjoyed the lunch version of these more, where it is more like fries with the spicy sauce.  These were good, but the dinner version is more of a small bite.  I guess I'm basic.   
Calamari a la plancha ($10): It was very tender, but a little bland.  My dad is Greek and not impressed.  
Caulilini ($9): Sweet stem cauliflower a la plancha.  It was fine, just not overly flavorful and bit forgetful.  

Space and Pace: Made reservations about a week in advance for a Saturday evening (initially nothing was available when I looked online, but I called and they found some space for us).  This place was packed!  I love the interior - really cool Andalusian-style lamps throughout.  It was a bit dark inside, but very atmospheric (made for some dark pictures of the food - sorry!).  I love this interior.  Definitely a great way to spend the evening, and the dinners are not rushed - you can have a long, fantastic meal over several courses. 

Service:  Great service.  The waiter divided up our many many tapas into three courses to give the meal some structure and let us pace ourselves.  As I mentioned, they also gave us a few extras as well.  Top notch, notwithstanding the crowd.

Went in to order 2 banh mi and a thai tea to go. A minute after I placed my order, my thai tea came out and I could not make this up. I told them to put it in the fridge because I don't want the ice completely melted and diluting my thai tea. I guess they made my thai tea fast because the banh mi was expected to be made in like 10 minutes. I waited for my banh mi for over  30 minutes. How? The place wasn't even busy. The man making the banh mi has his own space where you can see what's being made from a transparent glass. He calls the host and words are being exachanged for about 5 minutes. I had a hunch that something was wrong with my order but the host handed me the bag of banh mi and said thank you and have a good day. I didn't think anything of that because what can go wrong with banh mi, right? Wrong. When I arrived home, there were no vegetables in the banh mi. No cilantro, pickled vegetables, jalapeños, cucumbers. Uhm. At this point, I'm furious because now it clicked in my head. The man in charge of making my banh mi must've ran out of vegetables and told the host but that (trying so hard to keep my composure right now) host* failed to tell us. Who even does that? Like I'm not gonna find out about this. Maybe she thought I wouldn't have came back for vegetables. Wrong

The reviews were spot on. Order the ceviche. If there are two, get any fish and shrimp dish. Recommend the shrimp 
culichi.

Went here with my friends for lunch and "mid-day margaritas". It wasn't that busy so we were able to get a table pretty quickly. Didn't care much for the decor...it just seemed like a typical Mexican restaurant. 

I ordered a chicken quesadilla, an order of cheese dip for the chips, and a small watermelon margarita. The food was good, but nothing special. The margarita was pretty strong for a small amount...I had to keep sipping my water to get the strong taste out of my mouth.

I'll probably come back mainly just because my husband wants to try the food here.

Today it was my first visit at this place. I visited always one other Pho place before.
It is really a great restaurant and food for a good and reasonable price.
The service was really great - fast and friendly. We got the tea (for free) immediately. The food was served within 10 minutes.
My Shrimp Pho was delicious and the shrimps were not cooked too much.
The ice coffee was fresh prepared. The price for a Pho and coffee was around USD 10?

This place is amazing! Everything was so delicious from the bread and olive tapenade they bring you when you sit down to the prosecco. You have to get the pasta filled with Gorgonzola, pears and walnuts! It's a great date night spot. We will definitely be back!

We thoroughly enjoyed the food, atmosphere and outstanding service at this fun little restaurant. We love to eat out and we're pretty picky, but the cocktails, wine and food did not disappoint. The mackerel crudo and sweet corn tartlet were especially delicious.

Stopped here out of convenience and refusal to eat BBQ before a concert at Bridgestone . I was pleasantly surprised. Nice, local farm to fork type food. Really good cornbread. Got the hot chicken dish. Was not expecting a complete half chicken but that's what it was. More "expensive" food than I would expect from being that near the strip. Not gimmicky like most food around the area.

We had dinner here 20 Dec on a whim. We've always enjoyed Emeril restaurants. This visit completes our chase of having dinned at all the Emeril restaurants. The hostess was very nice and were seated with very little waiting. I like the team approach. We had two folks tending to our table. Excellent service! Started with the bruschetta and a glass of holiday eggnog. The bruschetta with fresh mozzarella cheese! amazing! The eggnog was just ordinary. It didn't have much liquor in it. We ordered the ribeye cap and scallops for dinner. The scallops was very good. The ribeye? well, it did say "ribeye cap with truffle oil. I did not expect to just get 4oz of steak, (maybe 5oz) with a spoonful of spinach. It was good, a little overcooked but tasty. I get it that its truffle season but this dish just doesn't cut it.  Overall, it was a great dining experience. Unfortunately it was getting late and we decided to pass on the banana cream pie (but we always get it, and it's delicious) Come here for the food just not  the steak. #NOLA #Emerils

I thought I'd give it a try one more time after not being pleased with the brisket several months back and try the chicken.. GROSS! It looks like it taste. Picture buying frozen chicken at the store and warming it up in the microwave. Ugh. What a waste of 14 bucks.

We stumbled upon this great restaurant and were drawn to the patio seating to eat and people watch. We shared the small charcuterie plate with a glass of wine each and it was a meal! It was so delicious, am still dreaming of it! For dessert, had to try the churros with chocolate dipping sauce--to die for. Will be our new "regular" place!
Great coffee, cute place, good service, reasonable prices... Quiet little hole in the wall for a date or study session.

Stick to the classic flavors here- cinnamon sugar 5/5, and even the famous maple bacon is 4/5. blueberry is also good at 4/5
wasn't a big fan of the coconut, wayyy too sweet! Overall Duck Donuts is best fresh and certainly is indulgent. Iced coffee was ok, but free refills made up for it.
Called and asked for manager had no idea I was a customer. Spent 21 plus dollars for only a 12" pizza with no sauce and undercooked. My receipt shows she's full of it.

We've been here twice now and I love the atmosphere. Definitely has that Ladue old money feel to it without being pretentious. They have a small tasting menu for $55 which we will try if they have stuff on it we want someday. My husband has gotten the Gumbo and I gotten the Truffle Risotto and the French Onion soup as starters. I will definitely go back for the soup, it was so rich and tasty. The Gumbo was full of meat and broth. The risotto was very rich and had healthy supply of mushrooms. My husband got the short ribs special with grits which he loved. I got the Duck from the menu and then a special. The portions were huge. I've never asked for a take home box from a fine dining restaurant before but I had half of my duck left and I certainly wasn't going to leave it behind. It was actually great the next day. The second visit we saved room to try the Bananas Foster dessert and it was great too.

I had a celebratory brunch here Sunday with my best friend and I was disappointed. Eggs Benedict is usually my brunch go to and I like to think of myself as a hollandaise connoisseur, but Harvest has ruined what I previously thought unruinable.   Their take on Eggs Benedict is short ribs topped with poached eggs and hollandaise sauce.  That is not Eggs Benedict.  Disappointed, I ordered the bacon egg and cheese sandwich which was very good.  But it was $12 which is a little ridiculous since I could have made myself the same thing at home for like 30 cents.  And the "side of fruit" it comes with is like three slivers of pear.  I'm glad we had ordered a side of the potatoes, though they were a little bland and lacking salt.  Grapefruit and pomegranate mimosa was decent, nothing special.  Service was subpar.  We had to flag down our waiter to ask him for water, to take our order, and to bring us the check.  Quite frankly, if you're looking for a brunch place in University City, Tap House is only a few doors down and a much better option.

The greatness of this place may be lost on you unless you are really into food from all aspects. If you are someone with a sophisticated palate and your bucket list does not go beyond Michelin 2 and 3 star establishments, you will likely disavow The Habit as a legitimate contender for a solid meal. It is a small, nondescript greasy hovel which most people would drive by if they didn't know any better. But if you are like me and look beyond fine dining for the real story behind great food, there is a lot to like here. 

This particular location in Goleta is the original Habit burger stand established in 1969. It is a less well known but just as important institution in the So Cal burger genre along the lines of In-N-Out. And while In-N-Out is still my favorite burger, The Habit has better add ons so I can be happy eating at either and maybe even both in the same day!

The story here is a tasty charbroiled burger at a decent price. The chargrill taste does add another dimension to the burger which is a nice touch. Their fries are solid and crispy but the newly found show stopper for me on this visit were the Tempura Green Beans. Who knew? I also love that they have a condiment caddy at the window stacked with 3 free kinds of peppers: sliced jalapeños, whole pepperoncinis, and tiny whole mexihots that are full of heat and make you sweat. Those little addictive add-ons are awesome!

The menu is a bit more expanded than a typical burger chain too since they have a Santa Barbara Burger (Sourdough plus avocado...really fantastic!) and also things like chicken sandwiches, Ahi tuna sandwich, Tri-tip sandwich, and a veggie burger(!) which almost seems blasphemous at a burger joint. No one around me ordered those things so I can't really vouch for any of them. And seriously, if you come to The Habit and order a veggie burger you probably deserve to be choked out and put in the back dumpster while waiting for your order. 

Don't miss this little gem of a burger stand if you are in the area. There is a small parking lot in the rear which is a pro tip recommendation as parking is tough to find on the street. And don't miss those hot peppers. Nothing completes the foodie look more than to have rivulets of sweat and burger juice running down your face while seated under the awning of a 1969 original.

Gia Nina's is by far the best Italian restaurant in the area.

The eggplant parm is so good that I've gotten it two of the three times we have ordered from here.  The eggplant cutlets sandwich a layer of seasoned ricotta and are covered with sauce and mozzarella.  The accompanying pasta always al dente, which I find impressive and unique for a delivery dish.

Their pizza is fantastic, balancing the right amount of toppings with a delicious crust.

Tonight we tried a couple of their sandwiches.  I couldn't test my husband's tuna hoagie because it was made with carrots in the tuna salad (food allergy), but he reported that while it fell short of being the best tuna hoagie he's ever had, it was certainly tasty and probably the most interesting.  I ordered the roasted pork sandwich with sharp provi and broccoli rabe.  Just like the pizza, the toppings were just the right ratio to the meat, and the meat was juicy and flavorful.  Both were served on homemade rolls.

There is only one problem with Gia Nina's: we can't manage to narrow down our choices on the menu because everything has been so good!

Favorite place to eat in Tucson. Phenomenal food and margaritas, I highly recommend the chipotle shrimp or carnitas tacos. I've been here over 20 times and have never had a bad experience with the food or the staff. They have a great happy hour menu as well.

Love The General. Food is excellent. Burger is above par. Sushi is superb. Bar area is super classy - bar tenders are nice, and the small plates are really good.  Can't say enough about this upscale addition to the Conshy-PWM area. Beautiful renovations on this great historical building - thanks for keeping it going!

Walked in and we were seated quickly. The waiter was very nice and gave us a few minutes to make our choices. The hamburger and fries were sooo delicious, so were the balls made of alligator. The sloppy roast beef sandwich was so so.. missing something but wasn't sure what.... Very generous portions.
Outstanding pizza! Well worth stopping in when you are near Clearwater beach.

This is straight up my favorite of the new taco places in STL.  They don't have a huge menu, and it isn't a standard sit-down joint.  The place is tiny and usually pretty packed; but the staff is very fast, friendly,and efficient.  and the food.  THE FOOD.

Get a pork taco. Just do yourself  favor. Do it. Because you will love it.  It is spicy and sweet and tangy and juicy.  I go by here all the time and just get one or two tacos to go and eat them on sidewalk in the Loop.  

their quesadillas are good, too, and some of their sides are excellent.  and if you want something more Korean, they have a Gogi bowl (a spicy veggie stir fry topped with a fried egg) is really excellent.

I STRONGLY recommend Seoul Taco, whether it's their food truck or their restaurant.  They are cheaper than other newer taco places and have less of the frills, but their food is far and away higher quality.  they are committed to just making really awesome, simple food.

Waited one hour for food.  The food was decent  but nothing amazing. Overheard multiple other customers ask for their food and complain about wait times too. The place is not ready for prime time. The table next to us received a 30 percent discount for their long wait but this was not offered to our party. Would bet  they are no longer in business in a year. Most likely less. Owners were at the bar the entire time and did not once step in to help or talk to customers.

They don't take reservations, but somehow turn us away at 6:00pm when we arrived with a party of 8.  We can't accommodate you is what we are told. And as we depart, we see a steady stream of diners arrive. I am more than happy to take my business elsewhere.

Enjoyed my first visit to Oyster House! Their selection of fresh oysters is worth of the namesake, and I definitely look forward to hearing about any happy hour offerings on my next visit.

Came in on a Friday lunch around 12pm, and as a table for two, we were seated immediately. Didn't have to wait, and the service was relatively speedy.

I had the New England Clam Chowder (about $8 for a cup or $12 for the full bowl), and it was delicious. I like that they have the packaged oyster crackers to accompany any soups or sides you get. For the entree, I had the grilled salmon salad (~$15), which was excellent. The salmon was seared, warm, and paired well with the yogurt based vegetables underneath.

Overall- great environment and great food. A bit steep on the pricing, but that's what you expect for center city seafood!

I had their fajita bowl which was very good.   Their cocktails, however come up short.  I had their cucumber martini which was only filled half way up the martini glass which is less than a third martini (think of how the martini glass is shaped).  Same with second drink.  Too expensive at $10 for a cocktail with only 1/3 contents.  Other than that, the bowl was great.
Good lite Italian fare with a fresh decor to match

Sun King Wee Mac on tap, great burgers, good fries, and very clean bathrooms, -- what is not to like?   The only complaint is the games on the table send the message that you should expect slow lousy service and they gross me out (how many grubby hands of thousands of customers touch those things?).  Please remove those things from the table and let people who want them ask for them.

Service is slow.  There dies not seem to be a responsible adult in charge and I've had to hear the young staff use profanity within ear shot of those in the dinning area.   My fries are usually cold and if I order something "special order" it is usually wrong.  On a positive note, the lobby is usually clean.

The Chophouse was a pretty good steakhouse. The service team was amazing! The crab bisque was creamy. We've never had a fried lobster tail so we decided to try it. It was still pretty tender, and the breading was tasteful but just too much for a lobster tail. I really liked the chargrilled crust on the steak. We're glad we got the Cajun seasoning as it may not have had much flavour otherwise. We ordered medium but it was closer to medium rare. Overall a good experience.

Came here for our 2 year anniversary and it was amazing. The food was delicious, we had the heirloom tomato to start and then the pork chop and the chicken entree and both were phenomenal. Our server Sasa was great! The manager Lowell was also very hospitable as well, he was very kind and always checked on us to make sure our dinner was going well. I definitely recommend this place!
I had really low expectations when I walked in... And this place is even worse than I expected . Do yourself a favor and go elsewhere ...

Visiting from Texas and was looking for a spot to have breakfast other than the hotel, so to Yelp I go! Nick's popped up and after reading the menu, we decided to check the place out. So pleased!!

The brunch menu pretty much covers anything you want..from eggs Benedict to waffles to steak to burgers. We opted for omelettes and we are not disappointed! The portion sizes are huge! Nobody in my party finished their plate...we were too stuffed! Even though the place was packed, service was super quick! Out waitress, Gwen, was friendly and happy to answer my many questions.

The place was clean. Staff was friendly. Food was fantastic. You definitely get more for your money here!
One of my favorite restaurants in Indianapolis.  Great options for vegetarians, vegans, and meat eaters too!  The service is always fast and friendly.  I come here every time I'm in Fountain Square.

Being at the beach I was hoping the seafood would be fresh. Fried calamari was probably the worst I ever had. Crab stuffed grouper sounded amazing on the menu but I was also disappointed. I could barely taste the blue crab and the grouper, other than the center, was a little tough. Staff was courteous and seemed to be hustling but there were several delays.

FANTASTIC FRIED CATFISH!!! My first time visiting on the behest of a neighbor, and she was correct, the fish is unbelievable. I purchased a fried catfish platter with steamed broccoli with garlic and a kiss of lemon, yum! I let my mother, whom is very hard to please, try a piece if the catfish, and all she could say while salivating was " ummmmm this is very good". I gave 4 stars because I wasn't a huge fan of the macaroni and cheese, although I saw a gentleman buy a large container of it. I told a friend of mine's about Soul Kitchen and she said her and her husband go there often. I will definitely be a repeat customer. Just WOW!

Ok, first off how can a Public House bar not serve a Bloody Mary? Second, how can the bartender admit they make the BM with a mix?  Third, how can you be out of BM mix and actually admit it? Fourth, why not fix all that with some tomato juice and vodka and whatever? But no, "We are out of Bloody Mary mix, sorry."  -- ridiculous --

Tamara has done it again. A great addition to the food scene in downtown Dunedin.

The seafood omelette is fantastic, but come hungry.

Featured picture is the Skillet Fries.

DEVINE.  Got the Rico, the most popular item for lunch. It was piled high with pulled  pork - a very generous portion. Super tender and juicy. Underneath was thick melted cheese and a delightful plantain patty.  Soft avocado sliced topped it off with a creamy Dressing drizzle. The side salad had a beautifully sweet mango dressing, not a vinegarette, full of fresh juicy flavor.

HIGHLY recommeded!!

No wait to get in which is always a plus at any restaurant.  Excellent food .  I ordered the Fried green tomato BLT and the wifey had crab cake Benedict.  Yummy. Like to thank our waiter, Antonio, for doing an outstanding job. Be back soon Stella!

One of the best restaurants in West Chester.

My fiance and I come here often and love it every time.  The food is always delicious and they change the menu around so we get to try something different every time we eat here.  

They tell you that each dish is meant to be shared but you could eat it by yourself.  We usually get three or four dishes and share them.  

It is also BYOB so that is always nice.

Quick 
Cheap
Good
What's not to like
Green chili pork is excellent!
Going back to try more.
I just wish they didn't use those aluminum pie plates for some dishes that deserve far better.

We stayed for 3 nights and had a wonderful time. Spring for the larger deluxe rooms if you can. Excellent bar and restaurant on first floor; nice complimentary continental breakfast. Valet parking is adjacent to hotel and free. Walking distance to New Hope shops and into Lambertville, which is a short walk over the Delaware River. Very friendly staff, and the inn has a long storied past. Highly recommended!

Just inside of a Korean market hides this gem know as Dosi Rak or  in Korean this the a word for a lunch box with rice, sides and a main course being meat or veggie.  Gal bi or Korean short ribs are one of my favorite Korean dishes and Dosi rak does it really well, nothing beats cooking it fresh at a KBBQ place but if you're looking for a Togo option especially in these Covid times, you won't be disappointed.
The Bulgogi is also really good and a very common Korean bbq item.  If your are new to Korean food and like beef, you need to try Bulgogi which translate to Fire meat.
Staff at Dosi rak is friendly and helpful
Food pricing is pretty normal for Korean food
Food it really good.
I highly recommend and I hope you enjoy Korean food as much as I do!!

This place was great! My friends were in search of a good bagel and we were not disappointed.  The bottomless bloody Mary bar was a bonus.  Awesome staff, (shout out to Misty!) awesome atmosphere, awesome food. Definitely on our list to stop back!

I saved macros for you Smokin' Pig! First, I need to mention that this place is a million times better than Mission BBQ. Now that I've said my peace, on to my review. 

Confusion. The ordering process with the two registers and the food out in the front is confusing. The little girl running one of the registers was noticeably frustrated. Upon ordering they didn't tell us to look for a number on the receipt, causing more confusion. 

The smoked turkey was bland and tasted previously frozen. It may not have been. I thought I would get the negative out first because hold your butts guys! The side dishes. FFS!!! This Mac N Cheese, the baked beans, and the corn bread are all worth switching sides from Franky's in Clearwater to here. I think there should be a plate that's like - Macaroni and cheese base, brisket, sauce. I'm going to do that next week. With a side of two pieces of cornbread.  And some beer. Because beer. 

The sauces were aight. The spicy could be spicier. The original was alright. The light one was mustardy, and it's just not my fave. Spicy is where it's at. 

I will update as time goes on. Now that I know what to do when I get there things won't be so awkward. I look forward to an ongoing relationship with your Mac and cheese and brisket.

2.5

It was late and my friend and I were a bit tipsy - we needed food.  We were walking around Philly and we stumbled upon this place. The place is standard diner - the decor is corny and it's really just a diner.  I ordered some two egg special with turkey bacon, toast and hashbrowns. It's was good, nothing really special though.  It did do the job of satiating my hunger and I didn't have a hangover the next morning.  The service was okay and the prices weren't bad.  2.5 since it was convenient and it wasn't too bad.

Obligatory Huge Ethics Disclaimer: an immediate family member of mine works here.  While we were eating, he was not working. He was seated with us.  I pride myself on my honesty. I'm the type of guy that will hurt the feelings of loved ones for the sake of self-integrity (sometimes known as "being an A-hol"), but this definitely bares mentioning.  I'm not sure if we got special treatment or not because I've only been here once.  I don't usually mention the service in a review anyway.  Unless it is bad. (it was not)

Ok, now that we got that out of the way.

This is the exact type of place that Tampa has so desperately needed, for years.

Finally something original and local that isn't a beach-side tourist-trap!

And, what, they brew their own beer?

I don't know the exact history, but it looks like they took an old building no one wanted anymore and gave it NEW LIFE.  I love the design of the place, brick, huge windows, high ceilings, it's gorgeous.  AND it's right on the river/bicycle trail (Tampa has bicycle trails now?!)

We got a wild sampling of the beers.  They were just OK.  They seem to not want to rock the boat with the beers here too much.  They are solidly done, but they are very "safe".  Not much of anything outside the box, nothing to rock the boat.  If you're not usually into craft/microbrew beer, you will probably LIKE the beer here.  If you ARE into heartier/bolder/hoppier beers, you should come here for the food and go to Angry Chair for beers afterwards.

We got a variety of apps (see photos), they were all unique and relatively excellent.  I don't even like oysters, but I loved what they did with them here.

As far as the main course, I loved what everyone at the table got!  The steak was probably the best thing I tasted, it was excellent.  I didn't get steak because I wanted to get something more uniquely "Florida" (can get a good steak just about anywhere in the US if you know where to look!).  

Big mistake on my part.  I got the Yellow fin.  The presentation was gorgeous, nice, deep, purple-red rare center.  That is exactly how I like it cooked.

But.

It was very very very very bland.  Absurdly bland.  It tasted like nothing.  The pumpkin seed crisp on the outside of it, tasted like nothing.  I was very disappointed.  

I actually used the salt shaker, something I never do.  I don't even remember the last time I touched a salt shaker.

For dessert we got the duck bacon/ice cream thing.  It was FANTASTIC.  Be sure to share though, it's sooooper rich.  I can't imagine one person taking it down.

Overall I was impressed. I'll be back next time I fly thousands of miles in from the tundra of the 49th state.

I won't be getting the yellow fin though.

The restaurant located at a quiet spot from the state street. The atmosphere is cozy, unpretentious, modern, artsy, just amazing. And the service is definitely great, you get just enough attention that you feel importation but not disturbed frequently.

We only ordered two dishes to get a taste, it turned out we feel quite satisfied afterwards. The two dishes are the risotto and tuna salad. Risotto is rich but not cheesy, the salad is so refreshing with the fresh raw tuna and fruit-juice-like dressing. It was absolutely a five star dinning experience.

the pizza might have tasted good if each time you took a bite you didn't get a mouthful of flour. lift up the pizza and it's caked in flour. breadsticks were good. like others have said, it's run by kids and very slow lacked customer service
Love this local smokehouse! Great flavors on the meats and the various sides. We enjoy the sweets too! Cane sugar sodas and desserts worth saving space for (try the smoked chocolate chip cookies)!

What used to be our favorite northside eatery is now going on our NEVER again list.   You now have to circle the entire to get to the hostess who then takes you to a near empty bar.   We're told the soup is cream of potato.   Then server comes back and says they've switched the soup already to ham and rice.  It's 2pm.  You switch soups at 2pm?  Then I notice my favorite sandwich is no longer on the menu.  The Ruben.   I guess they don't serve 1,000 island dressing as an option so it was easier to just the sandwich.   The appetizer was below average.  Can't wait for the tenderloin.  Hey, Chef Ramsey, I think I have your next kitchen nightmare right here.

I want to commend Doug and his staff of servers! They efficiently served a group of 121 students and adults. They were organized and very helpful.  Our drinks were always full and they constantly checked up on us if we needed anything at all.  We received excellent value for the money we paid.  Thank you all for taking such terrific care of us!

Yesterday was our 1st time at the Coop. I have seen the name all over IG, so I was excited to see them on Grow Financials promo list, giving the kid and I a chance to try this chicken.

It's only 8 minutes from my house so I will definitely add this place to the list of go tos for when I'm not in the mood to cook or for a lunch outing with my daughter.

The chicken is good!! It came in a cute, sturdy box with fries, sauce and pickles. The tenders are big, legit big, like double the size of your typical fast food size tenders. Fries are better quality then you'd get from a drive thru too. I love dipping tenders in sauce and their sauce was yum!!! I actually may even suggest maybe sizing up just a tiny on the sauce cup...I mean with tenders that big I definitely need more sauce. 

If you are looking for a unique tender, something different in the tender category, something different then the common chicken places, I feel like this place could be where to find what you are looking for. The seasoning on the tenders was like a dry rub. A little messy, but it was a different, satisfying taste to the tender. It didn't feel like I was getting a chikfila tender from a local spot, it felt like I came to a place that is setting themselves apart amongst what they specialize in. King of the Coop is worth stopping by to try!!

I came to the city to play a little poker at the River Cree. It was definitely an enjoyable atmosphere to play in.

Annually, I play in poker rooms all over Vegas, unlike many poker rooms this place felt new & fresh. Usually when the poker room is a cordoned off space on the main floor, the slot machines are overwhelmingly loud to the point that you can't hear yourself think. That wasn't the case here at all. The music played in the background but wasn't overpowering. 

The players were all very friendly. It was like playing in a large home game, as everyone was catching up with everyone else.

The pit boss & dealers were also very friendly & very professional. The desk had a digital photo frame that slowly displayed pertinent information for upcoming tournaments & scheduled events. Compared to many things I've seen, I thought it was a classy presentation.

I will definitely return. :) In fact, I can't wait! :D
Good food, excellent wait staff, great prices.  Definitely a nice addition to Magazine St.
Great spot. Laid back atmosphere with great service. They have their own fishing boats so the food is fresh. Great happy hour specials.

The food is not good at all!! I thought it would be a great choice since it was on Diners, dives & drive ins. The food is disgusting!!  The food tastes like it was microwave food warmed over, nothing fresh, homemade or delicious. It was an awful choice. The staff is not friendly and service was barely adequate which is amazing because the food is so bad. So sorry I thought this place would be good since it was on Food Network. The one star is because my sister liked the hot chocolate.

Worst meal ever. Potatoes were cold. Ordered eggs over easy-received eggs over hard. As far as the biscuits and gravy-gravy good but the bottom of the biscuit was hard as a rock. Bacon was good. Should have gone to City Diner as I had originally planned.

Excellent breakfast. Long lines to eat here but I used the yelp live wait and it helped our timing. Waiting for a table is not bad as the city life is all around you. The menu has lots of great egg items and several gluten free options.  I had a scramble with chorizo and it was fantastic. I nibbled off other plates of chocolate chip pancakes and beignets!

Every time we order they always get our order wrong and the customer service is very bad. There is a lady that takes orders in the front she is very rude and was not listening to us about our order being wrong. It took us 10 minutes over the phone just to order because she was putting us on hold over and over again and not complying. I do not recommend this location and we will not be coming back.

One of the best places around here for breakfast and pastries. They have the best egg dishes. Nice clean place and helpful friendly staff. They have to have patience because there's so many great choices. Never disappointing!
Great customer service, friendly atmosphere and the food is great. Staff sanitize menus after each customer.

Homely atmosphere. The food is a tad bland for my liking (and unlike traditional Korean food) I could sense they wanted to lower the sodium level overall for a healthier diet. Nonetheless, this is the place to go if you want Korean street food!! Staff is really friendly and they make you feel welcome.

This place has really taken a nose dive. The food quality is really hit or miss and the service absolutely sucks. The food here used to be amazing and we would dine here often. You can definitely see how the thriving Nashville economy has effected this restaurant. Good help is hard to find and these guys are scraping the bottom of the barrel. Nothing but tattoos, piercings and shitty millennial service. Taking these guys out of the rotation for now. I hope they can get their act together.

Fantastic service! I was being a pain and taking forever to order because I was indecisive and they were super cool about it! I also ordered a kids quesadilla and they didn't even question it. Just overall a great experience and I think a lot of other restaurants could learn a thing or two from chipotle!

Their policy of waiting until all parties are here to be seated is ridiculous.  No other restaurants in Chinatown require that you arrive with EVERY single party. Hence, you could spent a lot of time standing in the wait area looking kind of dumb while others walked past you.

Their food isn't worth all the hype. 

Much better food elsewhere!!!

I have a new food craving: the hawaii five-o roll. Warm coconut battered shrimp, cream cheese, avacado and mango. Pure heaven.  
This is hands down my favorite sushi place in nola.  As a Vancouver native and 7 year veteran of San Francisco, I know my sushi, and this place has high quality fish and innovative tasty rolls.  Loud music and club atmosphere: I don't care one way or the other.  The sushi is amazing. End of story.

I wanted some pizza tonight and this place delivered. So I checked the website. The Dali pie had some good flavor. I was pretty disappointed with the Veggin Out pie. Most of the toppings were good. Sadly they put the basil on the hot pie in the box. By the time I got it... The leaves were mushy. The crust required ranch and hot sauce to go down. Overall it wasn't a bad meal.

My friends and I came here for brunch twice on a 4 day trip to Nashville. The service was flawless, and the food was so delicious! The biscuits are the best I've ever tasted, as well as the grits, AND the jalapeño bacon ugggghhhh so good!  
The Blood Orange Mimosas and the Bloody Mary's were awesome!
Amazing food, service and atmosphere.  Next time I'm sitting the at the bar and ordering there.
Really cool spot, the waffles are really great but their coffee is what really does it for me. Perhaps a little pricey however but a great treat!

This place is a hidden gem! We started going to this place on a recommendation from a friend.. we always get pizza and it's always delicious. We recently tried their pasta wings and calzone and let me tell you they where amazing! Their young waitress by the name of ALEXiS is awesome she is very sweet and attentive always checks up on us to make sure we are doing good and have everything we need.. the only thing is that they do take a bit to get your order out to you but I think it's because everything is made fresh and that's perfectly fine with me.

The service is so outstanding here. The food is somewhat eclectic, although when their ideas work, they are amazing. I'm more comfortable with traditional/known menu choices, but I have to admit this is a safe place to try new dishes.

Best sushi in Indy hands down.  The portions are generous, prices are fair. Several sets of our friends who live out of town ::always:: ask to go here when they come to visit.  I've even gotten snapchats of them eating sushi in their car when they are passing through Indy when they weren't able to see us. Sakura has had the same staff for the decade I've been going there, which I believe is a statement, too. Sakura is a must go.

I've been to Amada several times in several seasons and have always had a fabulous time.  The food is brilliant, the service is friendly without being smarmy or intrusive, and the drinks are interesting in both summer and winter. (Delicious sangria.  Truly delicious, but this is really a summer drink. )  It's not cheap but it's not unreasonably expensive given the quality of the experience.  It's a tapas restaurant so they do small plates but they're good-sized small plates, not a tablespoon or two.  The salad wrapped in serrano ham with figs is celestial.   I've never done the tasting menu, it's too much fun to choose.

The food is good but waiting for it is another thing. We usually go on our lunch break and sit at the bar expecting faster service, not the case. In my last visit we waited 40 minutes for an order of sweet potato fries and edamame.

Coffee is okay but food is gross. Tastes like it went through the microwave! Took really long to prepare only to look and taste like something that came from a gas station. So disappointing. The place next door is DELICIOUS though!

No one who works here wants to be working.  And it shows in the messy floor and tables.  Waited 15 minutes to order while the employees were busy with their own gossip.  My order was rung up wrong.  The soda machine was out of all the syrups except for one.  Not one customer seemed happy when I was there.  I would never eat at this location again.

Myron was a great server!!! We had came to indy for the weekend and this was our last night dinner was excellent the manager was very tentative. Recommend the sweet potato casserole amazing! It happened to be veterans day they don't have a military discount, but the manager bought our meal.  It was a very nice surprise. I will be going there again

We went to Sushi Rose to celebrate my sons 14th birthday, and it was his first time trying sushi! 
It was a Monday night, so we expected it to be busy as they have the free beer/sake included with all you can eat on Mondays. We didn't receive several appetizers we ordered, the server didn't tell us what most of the rolls were as they usually do, and we didn't receive a few drinks we ordered even after we were told "I'll be right back with that for you". 
It was busy, I get it, but still pretty unacceptable. 
Giving these a 3 star because this isn't typical of the service we usually get.

Amuse bouche done right. 

   Lady Mary and I were visiting Longwood again, trying to capture some great daytime photos, and stay for the lights at night. This requires one to spend the better portion of the day at the Gardens, which is far from a problem.  One does, however, work up an appetite taking in all that gorgeousness; Enter 1906.

   The crowd of plebs and dirty children in the Terrace didn't look like something in which we were interested, so we decided to see if there was seating available in the restaurant. We didn't have a reservation, but were seated promptly regardless of that fact. For an appetizer we tried the onion soup, which was made from locally grown, organic vidalias. It was a clever play on a very traditional french onion soup; one which added a little cream to finish and a very small amount of heat via cayenne. The soup course was creative and well executed. 

   If the dear reader will permit, I'm going to go on a brief tangent. Every menu has what I've termed 'sucker items'. These are menu options which are rarely the best , but frequently the most expensive items on the menu.  There are a few words that run the 'sucker item'  flag right up the pole; among them are 'medallions of...' 'an 8oz. filet', and the worst offender of all...crab cakes. They are intrinsically forced to have filler, which makes me wonder why on earth they push the $30 mark on menus. The only dark spot on our otherwise sunny visit to 1906, was our waitress trying to push a $27 crab cake entree on us. No thanks sister, you'll not fool this limey that easily. 

   Back on course now...sorry (straightening my tie). A much better value seemed to exist in the pork tenderloin, at $19/ plate.  The pork itself was cooked perfectly, and the rub was an attempt to elevate traditionally bbq flavours...it succeeded. The pork was joined by some more of our onion friends from the previous course, now in ring form. Each was filled with greens & grits.  I am a huge fan of taking staples (like onions, greens, and grits), and finding a way for them to make sense on a gourmet plate. This very transformation happened beautifully in our meal. The chef has good knowledge of ingredients, can execute, and has a bit of creativity...definitely worth a go. 

   Lastly, we went (unbeknownst to us), on member appreciation day, which afforded us a 20% discount.  The whole meal was $53 including tip.  I'd be happy to re-rate at five stars if we can please take the huck finn-ness out of the ordering process. Overall, a strong 4 stars. Lady Mary and I will be back.

A friend wanted to take me out for dinner to celebrate my birthday so we came here. I chose this place because of its proximity to another event I was attending later. The reviews seemed "iffy" but the location was convenient for me, so I went with it. I called to see if I needed a reservation for that evening and was told it wasn't necessary. I arrived around 6pm on a Thursday and the restaurant was completely empty. There were a few people at the bar but we were the only table seated the entire time we were there. This also gave me pause--I considered leaving but I'm glad I stayed. We started with the oysters and truffle fries for appetizers. Both were great choices! The oysters were fresh and served with cocktail sauce and vinegar. The fries were amazing and went perfectly with the aioli sauce. For dinner we had the lamb chops, shrimp flatbread and Caesar salad. The salad was huge, the flatbread was flavorful. The lamb was over cooked (I ordered it medium and it was mostly brown throughout) but it was seasoned well. I didn't care for the sauce that came with it but I enjoyed the beets that I got as a side. For cocktails we tried the industry sour which was horrible and apparently gets sent back frequently, and a bourbon, ginger, maple syrup drink (I forget the name, grandmas cocktail or something) that was very tasty
Bismarks!!!!!!!!! Baked and not fried. The ladies are so amazing and friendly. Spacious. Go here instead of Starbucks, support your local businesses.

Im new to Tennessee and i love Hibachi grills, so i made plans for my girlfriends birthday. I have to say this is one of the best hibachi grills ive been to.  We had a lot of fun and the food was amazing.  I had the new york strip and shrimp,  she had the filet and shrimp.  Both were very delicious and cooked perfectly.  Will definitely be going here more often.

From the outside, this place looks a little dingy, but looks can be deceiving.
The food was fresh, tasty and really well prepared.
Each item we ordered came out to us quickly, but not so fast as to overwhelm us or not allow us to finish the last item.
The wait staff was attentive but not oppressive.

Definitely plan to become regulars here.

The food is always great here, the problem is even when they open they are out of ribs. It's a bbq place how do you not have ribs at 11:00 am? Usually we come at dinner and they are out of Brisket and banana pudding.

I LOVE THIS PLACE! The food is always great and the service is as quick as you need it to be. The donuts are as awesome as expected, but I was surprised how delicious the sandwiches are. The Tuscan chicken panini is off the hook good. Can't wait to get my next fix!!!

I am highly disappointed with Blondie's.
Today was my first post Covid visit and I am saddened to see how irresponsible Blondie's staff has been.  The servers bringing food to the patio are not wearing masks at all.  The tables have not been cleaned appropriately between customers, and they are not spaced 6 or more feet apart.

The chef is a real ding dong, but holy crap is the food good. Go for brunch if you can. They regularly update the menu and use local ingredients. Also, they provided meals and aid to folks in need around the neighborhood during Covid, so you should go there based on the fact that they're just good people. Enjoy!

My boyfriend took me to this little romantic hidden gem for Valentines dinner.  We went the day after to avoid the crowds around town.  If you are not looking for the place you are going to miss it.  It's tucked away in the shopping center so make sure you google the address and then keep your eyes open.  The iconic Italian archway at the door will help you recognize the entrance.

The place is pretty cute.  Elegant bar to the left at the entrance way and then to your right is a small intimate room with a few booths lining the tables and some tables chairs in the center of the room.  We were greeted and sat right away in a booth.

We were asked our drink order right away which was nice and given menus right away which was nice but that was kind of the end of "right away".   It took well over 15 minutes to get the break and oil and about 20 minutes to get two glasses of wine.  I'd say it also took about 30 minutes to place the order. When all was said and done we were probably sitting in that booth for an hour before we had dinner in front of us.  My boyfriends steak was perfect although he would prefer less of the balsamic on top (noted for next time).  My cioppino was decent.  I have had better and probably would not order it again.  Funny thing - I have never had a cioppino with actually baby octopus in it before.  I can't tell you if it was good or not because I couldn't bring myself to try it.  

The prices are higher than most but not astronomical.  Despite the slow service I would give it another go because the food and ambiance was worth it.  I think that they were short staffed.  At one point our waitress had a family emergency so the manager took care of us the entire time.  That would be the only think I'd say they need to improve on - staff a little better so we don't wait 20 minutes for wine.

If you are looking for a semi-upscale romantic Italian/Steak place this is the right spot for you.

GO HERE !!!!
This restaurant has just changed owners last week. Luckily there is only one other review so far. 

The person taking over is chef Suhel Anwar. He makes the best Indian food I have had period. I have been following him around for about 8 years or so ever since he worked at the meat department at International Bazar. Back then he used to prepare one dish...biryani. 

His biryani is unmatched. I have tried it at tons of places all around the country and  have yet to find another king. It is moist and flavorful. To me it's the single dish that showcases the masterful balancing act that spices preform in Indian cuisine. 

Let us not forget everything else on the menu. Homemade paneer, fall off the bone goat, deserts to die for, chai tea with true flavor. I can not say I have a favorite here as everything is so good. My usual order is just to make whatever he feels like that day. A few things that are always good are the goat curry, malai kofta, and palak paneer.

The nan is always fresh and usually too hot to hold. It comes in several varieties and you can also get roti. If you go here for the lunch buffet you usually get a fresh basket (but if not you can always ask for it).

Onto the experience of dining here. I usually find Indian restaurants to be cold and impersonal. Suhel goes out of his way to make you have an extra special experience. His staff is quite small right now so he might get stuck in the kitchen at times. At any rate tell them that you herd of the place from me and you will be treated as family.

As most other Indian places they have a lunch buffet and they also have a Friday night dinner buffet.

Man, I'm so excited that Suhel once again has a restaurant. Overnight I now have a new favorite restaurant in Indianapolis.

I was looking forward to some excellent sushi based on the reviews I read, but I was unimpressed. I tried the New Philly roll; shrimp tempura and Kobe beef. I was not a fan but my BF thought it was ok. The spicy tuna was my least favorite of all spicy tuna's I have had, way too spicy and tasteless. My BF had this skirt steak that was advertised as an entree for $28, but the portion was more like a tapas meal & left him hungry. The steak was very good, I just think they should increase the size for the price. 
Overall Azie had a great atmosphere and the service was fast and friendly, just too expensive for what you get.

I'm starting a search for a great sandwich places in CC but sadly, I can't say this is one of them. 

While just walking around for lunch, I was drawn to this place because of its bright colors and advertisement of healthy eating. Looking at the menu, I was stoked that I had many choices and that the price was cheap. They carry sandwiches, wraps, soups, salads, and smoothies. A regular sandwich is just $3.95. You can also get a combo (with chips, soda, or a smoothie) and it's still less than $7 (see pic). 

I got a sandwich and smoothie combo. The "Raindrop Smoked Turkey", which comes with lettuce, tomato, smoked gouda and sun-dried tomato pesto was so-so. It came out a lot smaller than I expected and I was not a big fan of the bread. The lettuce and tomato were fresh but the sun-dried tomato lacked flavor so I didn't really notice it was there. What bugged me most about this sandwich though was that the smoked turkey was very salty (I don't know how healthy that can be) so I'd skip this sandwich and try something else. The regular sized wrap here is also pretty small. 

What I did really enjoy about this place was the smoothie! You definitely should try the "Mango Mania", which has passion fruit mango juice, strawberries, bananas, and pineapple sorbet. Great flavor and consistency. 

Also, this place doesn't have seating except for two small tables outside. If you are going to eat here, expect to bring it to-go.
Still one of my favorites. Always great service. Although my diet restrictions are limiting my selections at the moment, I was quickly able to find a great meal choice.

I walked in and was the o my customer there. I ordered chicken and broccoli and nothing else. 

I patiently waited 25 minutes in the booth. The chef could see me and so could the lady that took my order. 

I went up after the 25 minutes and the lady approached me and asked if I was ready to order.

Now they made the food and it's utter trash!

Stay away from this place!

I've never had a bad experience at J Bucks, but I've never really had a remarkable one here, either. It's one of those places that I avoid, unless someone really wants to meet here. 

Don't get me wrong, the bartenders and servers are all very nice. The beer selection is fine and they even offer a decent happy hour. It's just the fact that J Buck's is always crowded and I don't really understand why. There are so many other great happy hour spots in Clayton, why would you stick around at a mediocre establishment?

Maybe it's the clientele that irks me. Usually it's full of people who want to be "somebody" but didn't get the memo that the A-listers don't hang out at J Buck's. It's kind of sad. But not sad enough to get more than three stars from me :)
Love it love it love it. Food was wonderful. Paella was outstanding, matches anything I have had in Barcelona. Service was very attentive. Plan to make this a twice a month stop or more!

This is my favorite taco joint! This is real authentic Mexican food makes me feel like I'm back home. I live close by so I'm guilty of making it a frequent stop and the fact that it's so freaking delicious doesn't help. I think I'm addicted to their food.

Very enjoyable experience. The venue is small, so if you're going to visit, they take reservations--make one. The service is top notch. The quality is superior, and for their location, their prices are very reasonable.  We were in and out, but not rushed. Would definitely visit again.

Finally a spot in SB with GREAT and affordable cafe style food!  I got the Rolex and the Burger and they were both unlike anything i've ever had.  This food is so good, you would be stupid not to try it!  Well done gentlemen

Revising my last review of 2 stars to 4 stars. I went back after a couple months of a hiatus bc I really do love their food. The service was a lot better and the food on point! The Esane sausage and Malaysian noodles are still my favorite Thai dishes in town!

Lovely outdoor dining among the planters and benches. No wait for a table when we arrived at 6pm on a Saturday night. 
We shared the appetizer sampler platter and Crispy Choo Chee Salmon. The fried spring rolls were the best I've had in recent memory. White meat chicken satay was flavorful but had no discernible peanut taste or peanut sauce. The fried tofu and fried chicken dumplings were kind of bland, but the sweet chili dipping sauce helped. 
In our main dish, the abundant salmon pieces were individually fried, which we appreciated. Veggies were just-right crunchy: green beans, green bell peppers and sliced onions.  The dish wasn't too spicy.
The service was excellent, the portions large, and the food was extremely fresh. All of which made it easier to overlook my unmet expectations and give it four stars instead of three. We will return for another try.

Kinda hidden which only adds to its charm. Designed after classic speakeasy. Hamburgers are INCREDIBLE.  The bean soup amazing. Drinks are fantastic!  Highly recommend the Old Fashioned.  Staff is very friendly.  Patio in back to hang out on nice.

Considering all the great reviews written in here, I was bit surprised that this place was just an average meal place. Food was ok, service was ok, atmosphere and location are also ok. Price was ok too. No major complaints in this place. Perhaps I was expecting more of a 'Nashville' style in this place.

My husband and I came for lunch today. It was his first time here. I've been several times and I've been raving about it. He ordered a cheesesteak wrap and sweet potato fries. The fries were super good... The wrap not so much. He found three bay leaves in it.... Not at all a pleasant thing to bite into. He said it just didn't taste that good either. They did take half off his meal due to the bay leaves, which was nice of them. 

My Chinese chicken salad wasn't prepared as listed on the menu (no wonton strips, and it had candied pecans which I am fairly sure it didn't list on the menu) but it tasted really good. It'd have been even better with wonton strips though. 

I'm a little let down today and now I probably won't get him to come back with me!

The restaurant is a nice intimate hideaway filled with amazing food! Don't let the exterior fool you, inside is a hidden gem of wonderful flavors. 

The location itself is fairly small, but that works to its advantage as it lends a nice intimate feeling to every meal. 

Parking is a bit of an issue during the day, they only have a limited parking lot behind the location. However in the evenings (after 6), you can park at the office building next door. 

Getting back to the food, the pad thai and pad lao were flavorful without being over powered. The Tom Young soup was a perfect blend of flavors and spice. 

The green curry over the coconut rice is quite simply yummy. To change it up, you can go with the sweeter, but spicier red curry too. 

Combine all of that with some salad roles to get you started and I had a wonderful meal!!
We ordered from Oceana Grill via UberEATS, which was fast and convenient. The New Orleans sampler was quite good (4 stars). The burger was really sad (2 stars at best). Alligator po boy was ok.

After few visits, it turns out that there's nothing strange about patrons love for Strangelove's. It's a beer-centric bar, of course, with about 20 drafts on tap. There's something for every taste. Couple of weeks ago, I had one of their specials. Portobello sandwich and it was anything-but-basic sandwich, very meaty, and inspired. 
The service, is always on point, and prices can be on the higher side but its worth the tasty food. 

Tips... tips... tips:
- Remember, there's always happy hour. They are fun and inexpensive. 
Weekdays 5:00pm-7:00pm. $4 select drafts & house wines, and $5 well drinks. Sundays:3:00pm-5:00pm.
- Weekdays lunch 11:30-4pm: 10% off lunch bill to all Jefferson staff and students. 
- Be prepared to wait for a table on weekends. So be patient.
- Street (meter) parking are available, if founded. However, there's a parking garage just across the street.

Four solid Yelps.

If I could give it 0 stars, I would have. The food was cold or room temp. Most trays of items were either empty or long lasting remnants were inside. The owner cooked me up some spareribs but everything else was awful. The egg drop soup smelled like toilet water and I ate one rib and that was it. My friend only ate some mushrooms and half of a room temp egg roll. The owner said they turn the burners off 2 hours before they close.  The water we drank tasted stale and old. 

When we went to pay, I said I would only pay for one. The woman at the register started yelling at me and said I must pay for both of us since we both sat down. I tried to explain calmly but she went nuts and made me pay $24 for 1 rib and a few mushrooms that were eaten. I have never been so disrespected as a customer ever and I've never been to a more disgusting Chinese buffet in my life. DO NOT EAT HERE. 

Shame on them. They will get someone sick by not keeping the food hot and fresh.

Reasonable price.....delicious....

don't forget to order beefstroganov ($18)  and mocha parfait.

What I had:

Split Pea Soup: um...yummy
Arugula Salad ($7): love it
Beefstroganov ($18): Tasty
Broiled Crab Cakes ($26): there are 2 jumbo crab cakes which you can ask them to split for 2 dishes......my mom shared this dish with my dad.

Last week I stopped in with friends because I thought the place looked cute. I started with a cup of the chicken noodle soup, served Luke warm at best it was a thick and gelatinous. I'm certain it came out of a can, which is very disappointing because I lived chicken noodle soup. I had the eggplant Parmesan for my meal.
