Booths is a fantastic little place. It has almost everything you could possibly need (for cheap!). I often get bacon and lunchmeat from the stand at the far side of the building. It's high quality, affordable meat. The baked goods are awesome. There is also a stand with Polish goods. I've gotten a few dozen pierogies here and they are much better than Mrs. T's (duh!). The crabcake stand is solid, as well as the cinnamon roll stand.

Different types of fries were tasty though we may have gotten the bottom of the batch (thin and short).  Ordered the lettuce wraps with seared ahi was heavenly.... good selection of local beers.  The experience that gave its extra star was our server.  She was cheerful, helpful, and honest!  Nice atmosphere.

I've been eating here since I was a child, 30 years. Growing up it was always a blast for the family to come here for dinner with the live bands blaring! While the live bands are a thing of the past, the food is still authentic Italian.
We try to eat here 2-3 times a month as the food is spectacular and the prices are more than reasonable.
Please try it at least once. I swear you won't find any better authentic Italian food anywhere.
Absolutely delicious!!

We made a reservation for party of 8 for Sunday brunch.   The buffet was all amazing!  I loved their omelette station with Cajun crab omelette.  The Bloody Mary's were the perfect blend of spices.  If you can grab some while they're out, my most favorite dish was the roasted sweet potatoes.  Yum!  Everyone should have brunch here.  Not to mention the gorgeous vine covered patio, picture perfect
Amazing. Awesome service, wonderful sandwiches and just a charming deli on the water. Highly recommend the Cuban and the chipotle chicken Gouda sandwich.

This was amazing! We happened to stumble across this while walking down Central and were amazed! The staff was super friendly and worked very hard. I got the tempeh taco with as many toppings as possible. It was divine! They make the corn tortilla fresh right in front of you! The tempeh was perfectly cooked and well seasoned. My husband got the burrito and he said it was better than Chipotle! Thehave a really good pineapple habanero salsa to go with their chips. Yum! We are so happy to have found this and can't wait to come back for more!!!

Amazing! 

We went there on a Friday at 830pm to find a 45 minute wait. Such good news to hear that a place like this that is only in their 'soft-opening' phase to be so busy. We lucked out and was able to sit at the bar which is just as good as any seat in the house. 

They did a wonderful job remodeling and Chef Ramon has produced some of the most amazing dishes. We tried 5 different items and dessert. DO NOT FILL UP, eat dessert! 
 
The ceviche is fresh and makes you want to go back for more and more. Loved the Tamale and the carmel crepe dessert. 

The decor is fabulous...

This is my new hot spot for date night. SB needed this and I hope for success!

Food was sooo good they definitely did not disappoint. I had the fricassee chicken and curry goat and my husband had Jerk chicken. Nothing else needs to be said everything was seasoned well and very flavorful! Will be back

The little corner spot is known for having the best burgers! I tried one and it was great! The all beef patty was thick juicy and hot. The lettuce, tomatoes, pickles were cold crisp and fresh! The cooks take pride in what they do. The have a small menu and limited condiments. They make you feel welcome and are very friendly and courteous. I will make another trip there and try out there breakfast. Glad I'm staying just down the street.

Really good pizza and great service in a super-casual environment. They have pizza by the slice (which I didn't try) and baked us up a custom pizza with a perfect thin crust and super fresh toppings (even the green peppers were fresh and still had a crunch, which was a nice surprise).  We'll definitely be back here. Only negative thing to say was that the door to the men's single bathroom didn't lock or even latch shut.

I wouldn't recommend this place. We went for the jazz brunch and could barley hear the music and they didn't even play the whole time. I even made a reservation over a month In advance and requested to be seated near the jazz band. Was placed at the farthest table away. Food was average - nothing to write home about. Staff was great but I will not be back.

This is a tough place to get a reservation-popular & deservedly so. The entrance is to the bar area, with a stairway leading to the restaurant area. It's not particularly big or fancy up there. 
The menu offers dishes of varied sizes. Many plates can be shared. There are also large plates for two: tonight's grilled fish (for 2) was a 2-lb bronzino. Since I was alone, I ordered three dishes; all were terrific. I started with Maryland crab on toast. It was surprisingly big & filling. They are known for their toast dishes. I then ordered the jack with avocado from the "Raw" section. I then had a medium-sized dish of tagliatelle with lamb ragout. All very tasty. They make their own gelato, and I love good vanilla (bean) ice cream. It was very good. 
Service was friendly, attentive & efficient.

This was by far the WORST service me and my husband have EVER received from a restaurant . We don't get to have dates very often due too the fact we have two children under the age of 3yrs old. And my husband had simply asked for a side of mayo with his fries, she forgot, so we asked again, she then proceed too say "well do you want a 5 gallon bucket of it"..rude. Who says that?! Whether we were all of 90lbs or 350lbs, or it was a cheat day on our diet. The fact that her judgments were cast on us was beyond rude and unexplainable . We will never go back here due too the the service. Thanks Holly (that's her name) , for ruining  our date.
Great food! Great outdoor space! Friendly bar tenders! The outdoor space and fire pit make it possible to enjoy on cool fall nights. My kids love their menu too!

Reading the reviews expected better.  Perhaps the chef had a bad night. Fish cakes appetizers were small and from the frozen section of your neighborhood Asian grocery store. My seafood lover lacked flavor, needed both heat and sweetness. I didn't get the chili sauce at all. I have been to many Thai restaurants, both in Thailand and here in the states.   I know good Thai food. This was unexpectedly disappointing.

What an incredible brunch spot. I had a "biscuit flight" which came with four different types of biscuits and four types of spreads. It was phenomenal. The coffee was free flowing and good quality and the the space itself had an inviting vibe. I'm sad that I'm leaving St. Louis because otherwise this would become a regular brunch spot.

Went there with my mom while visiting NOLA to watch the pelicans vs Rockets game ( go rockets) amazing place and the staff are nice and friendly. I got the Chicken pizza and it was absolutely DELICIOUS 10/10 recommendations

Tried their chicken pho here one time because pho ga thanh thanh across the street was super crowded. Their pho ga was disgusting, from the dipping sauce to the chicken broth. It looked so plain and white, not appetizing at all. The broth taste more like artificial broth you get from a can. I had their Ha Noi style noodles from them too and it wasn't good at all. Well next time I know Not to cheat on my go to chicken pho spot.
During the spring and summer time it is great sitting outside and watch people walking by Rittenhouse Sq. the mussels are very good and the ambience is very Parisian.

JoAnn provides a wonderful personal experience that is equal to her fine dining experience.  The fried oysters were the best I've ever had anywhere, and the roast duck nearly as great as my favorite french restaurant in Palm Beach FL.
Everything we ordered was perfectly prepared and everything was special.  The fried green tomatoes and the etouffee appetizer were off the charts.  Two of us had the duck and two had the drum fish and everyone was happy.
We liked the three course $45 deal a lot and enjoyed all the desserts.  The creme brûlée was equal to the many I've had in Paris and the pecan pie crispy and not too sweet.  
The wine lists includes the perfect choices for a great meal.  JoAnn, we all look forward to visiting you again soon.
Used to have the most delicious burger! Today it was two dry patties, terrible, what a shame

Absolutely love coming here. I always come for happy hour during the week. Their crunchy L.A. roll is my all time favorite. I've always had good service and no issues with our order. I am a frequent flyer! 
Also took my boyfriend here and he won't stop asking me when we can go back. LOVE IT!

Writing this review and wishing I was at King of the Coop right now ! All I got to say is WOW ! I was so impressed with this spot! 

We ordered two Chicken Sandwiches the King Mac & the Nashville Hot Sandwich! They were amazing, cooked to perfection ! Amazing Sauce ! The crispiest fries ! Hands down amazing food! The Mac and cheese on my Sandwich was so delicious, I had to get an additional sauce.

Let's also not forget that they make their own pickles ! I am not a pickle gal at all ! But when I tell you these things were awesome I am not lying to you. 

The place is super chill, minimal seating, but who cares the food is BOMB ! The prices were super reasonable and the staff was friendly and very knowledgeable of their food. 

Going back like tomorrow ! :) Enj

This takeout spot has been a Tucson institution for years and rightly so. They know how to fry and that includes keeping the oil fresh and the smell acceptable. We had the shrimp, steak fingers, chicken giblets, and onion rings. All came with a mild all-purpose cocktail sauce. While I couldn't tell you what animal those fingers came from, they weren't bad. Everything else was really good. Have to go back for fried chicken, Cole slaw and more of those crispy onion rings. While there are a couple of small metal tables at which at least one group was eating, this is take-out food and deserves to go to the park or backyard for a picnic. We took it home, but weather permitting, next time it's outdoors with a thigh in one hand and a cold one in the other.

We recently had a Celebration of Life luncheon for about 16 people in one of their private rooms upstairs ( where we had 2 nice restrooms right outside the room). Everything was just what we wanted. The historic nature of the location, and the  room itself was a key reason we chose the Inn. The room had very nice light, & had 2 fireplaces which made for a lovely ambience. From the moment we started dealing with the staff ( Banquet Mgr. Dayna, & her assistant Megan) we were very pleased with the attention to detail, including dealing with our diverse & significant food allergy issues ( nuts, gluten, ) and dietary restrictions ( vegan, vegetarian). That alone is usually a challenge but both assured us that the chef could adjust and they provided excellent options for us.  All of the food was delicious,served at the appropriate temperature and at the same time for our group. None of us had ever eaten there before , and based on our experiences, will most definitely be coming back. The food from salad through an exceptional desert was WONDERFUL! We had a very attentive , efficient, and pleasant server, Christina, and she absolutely took care of our group not only in terms of the food but also in terms of the details we had asked for in the room. 
We simply could not have asked for a better experience for an emotional day and I am so thankful that the Washington Crossing Inn clearly is very customer service oriented, has a talented chef, as well as a staff that cares.

Item tried:
1) black bean enchilada 
2) shrimp tacos 
3) mucho nachos 
4) pineapple canela margs
5) Jalapeño margs 

All items were great. Inside look is very good and they have outside booth in COVID times.

I am very impressed with this place. It has great food and even better service. After asking the waitress that we were on a schedule the waiters appeared to work as a team and it was wonderful to see how they worked together to get our bloody Mary's, OJ and food out quickly.  The grits were the highlight of the breakfast! Can't wait to get back to New Orleans and Café Adelaide!

I really enjoyed my afternoon visit to Vault.  It was a Sunday afternoon and we were just at the relatively nearby Crossing Vineyards for a wine tasting when they mentioned the wine served at Vault, a newer microbrewery in the area, was from that vineyard.  Because we were just there for fun and are much more into beer, we stopped asking about the wine and started asking more about Vault.  Our host gave us directions, a warning to follow the speed limit in Yardley borough, and we were off!

Vault is a very cool looking place made cooler by the fact that they left the vault of the bank building they now occupy in operation, except now it holds riches of beer.  We had a sampler and enjoyed all of the beers but I preferred the Extra Pale Ale and my husband enjoyed the  Chinook IPA.  We also ended up ordering a very delicious flatbread that was made in what I believe was a wood burning oven.  The pizza was crispy and tasty and the varied, abundant toppings on the Prosciutto Fig pizza really hit the spot.

We didn't stay for too long, but we definitely plan to make the trek back in the near future, especially if we can time our visit for one of the weekend nights when they feature live jazz.  Plus, my husband is dying to get one of their very fancy stainless steel growlers.  They are definitely something out of the ordinary in and of themselves and if they're an excuse to visit Vault again, I'm in!

I am definitely a fan of the delectable desserts, CUPCAKES! who doesn't like cupcakes?

The first time I was introduced and tried CrushCakes was in the Carpinteria location. The small from outside of the restaurant was what enticed me to come in, also my co-worker knew the manager. The cupcakes are on the moist side which is important when it comes to cupcakes.

I was also lucky enough to try the Santa Barbara location. As far as the food on their regular menu (breakfast) the food is just okay. I probably won't eat lunch of breakfast here again, I will just come for the cupcakes.

As it started to snow, I naturally wanted soup. Of course I turned to Yelp and landed on this restaurant in Chinatown, which was walking distance from my hotel. Sooooo glad I ended up here!! 

I ordered the braised sliced beef noodle soup with hand pulled noodles on a whim, as I normally don't order beef soup. I thoroughly enjoyed every...single...bit!! The food arrived to the table quickly, and upon first glance I knew it'd be amazing. Great portion size, great taste...great everything! I'd highly recommend this spot for a quick, comforting meal at a reasonable price. 

Can't wait to visit this place again on my next trip to Philly.

***Cash only!

Think: cozy.  Located on a back alley in a cute historic downtown Zen Den is full of small charm like it's rhyming name suggests.  It's quite a large newly refurbished space (which it doesn't look like from the outside).  Inside there's lots of wooden surfaces, books, some restored furniture, overstuffed everything, and lots of quaint artifacts and nick-nacks.  It's early now so its just ~40something guys in running gear but I assume a bunch of SUV moms will be in here after dropping off the kids at school.  The barista was very nice.  She didn't know what to do with my foursquare coupon but was gracious about it.  She also fixed the wifi and asked if I was okay with the music (Pavement Radio on Pandora (which is okay with me)).  My tip: there's free parking down the street and the fantastic la columbe coffee starts a buck - not bad at all!
Never again will I order from this place.  Rude service with bad attitude.  A Chinese woman in the phone was a straight up b@\÷#.

There aren't any Korean options in close proximity to where I work, so I gave Rice & Mix a try. Ordered a custom bibimbap bowl for lunch take out and it really hit the spot.

Service is amazingly quick, serving sizes are ample, and everything was well cooked and delicious.

Whenever I get the hankering for some Korean food while downtown, I know where to go now!

This is my favorite fried chicken place in central jersey.

i always call up the owner and tell him to put fresh stuff into the fryer b/c I bring 10 people from work with me. Their potato wedges are good but there chicken tenders are the best. not as greasy or stale tasting as KFC or Popeyes.

they have good kabobs as well.

btw, this place is 100% halal.

For Tourist:  This is a large seafood store where locals mainly pick up food to go. However, they do have tables if you want to sit and eat, no table service.  A wide variety  of fresh, boiled and fried seafood, chances are Cajun's has what your looking for.  1st, their Gumbo is some of the best in the city.  It's made very close to how locals make it at home..  Not restaurant style with mostly okra and stewed tomatoes.
At Cajun's you will find a nice brown roux, plenty of shrimp, crab, hot and smoke sausage.  2nd. Their PoBoys' sandwiches have generous amounts of seafood or meats on them.  The fried shrimp w/ lettuce, tomato, pickle, hot sauce and ketchup and light mayo. Yumm.  As a seafood shop, they sell plenty of fresh seafood, the boiled crawfish and crab are well seasoned but not too spicy. Cajun's will give u a nice taste of New Orleans seafood.

The hour was 10 pm. The day was Saturday. The feeling was hunger. DeSano Pizza was the answer! Anyone who knows me knows that I am a connoisseur of all things cheesy (food and jokes) so DeSano fits right in with this love. I had previously picked up a pizza to-go and been happy with it and this was my first time dining in. DeSano serves up authentic Neapolitan pizza in a casual setting in the Music Row area of Nashville. They have a parking lot (can I get an amen?!) and the interior is quite spacious with long wooden tables and benches. 

The large menu is displayed in the lobby area near the entrance and you order from a cashier before having a seat. They bring the pizza right to you once it is ready. Our cashier was honestly high as a kite which didn't bother us really but as far as professionalism goes, not the best (hence, minus one star from my otherwise glowing review). 

The San Gennaro rocks my socks....the combination of the sausage, caramelized onions, buffalo mozzarella and peppadews (brand of small sweet red peppers) is a marrying of all the best flavors on one pizza. The wood-fired crust is delicious and completes this perfect pizza. My boyfriend and I finished a whole pizza by ourselves!

The food is great, the atmosphere is fun/casual and this place would be good any time of day. I'd come back in a heartbeat and this would be a fun place to come as a group since you can bring wine to share with no corkage fee. You will not regret indulging in this delicious pizza!

I love this restaurant and have been eating here for 10 years. I do not live close to it and it would be probably easier for me to go to the city and eat, but I always come here. The food is really good if you want to eat sushi or chinese or they even have a fantastic Thai Style Chicken Fried Rice. The owners are usually working when I go in and are super nice. The restaurant is really clean and you can always find people in there even on the slower days of the week which confirms how good the food is. If you live in the area I suggest trying it!

Food is exceptional. However, service is extremely slow from the moment you walk in the door. There are more people waiting for tables than sitting at tables and wait times consistently exceed 30 minutes. Even once seated, the service does not pick up and you will easily be waiting for your food for 30-40 minutes. We have given this location a few chances and this has consistently been our experience.

Discovering Watami was one of the best things that could have happened to us! Their sushi is amazing, staff is kind and wonderful, environment is clean, and the price is great! Best all you can eat sushi in Indiana!
Terrible service, sever was absent, forgot food and drinks, obviously the place didn't have enough staff loud obnoxious trivia night

Order: meatball stromboli: wonderful toasted garlic butter hoagie bun, meatballs, sauce and mozzarella.
Service: Owner and staff bent over backwards for just a carry out and even provided me with a free drink while waiting. I felt like I was part of their family just during my short wait.
Rave: Thank you and will be back soon for more first time food adventures!  Cheap and amazing bites and did I mention you are supporting local?!
Neighborhood: East
My guess is that you have never had a really Philly Cheesteak. This was one of the worst I have ever had. Might as well use steak ums. So disappointed

I was really hopeful for this place after reading their website, but as my motto states, I am still looking for good Mexican Food in the northeast.

The Margaritas were OK, nothing great, nothing terrible.  The star of the visit was probably the Guac, but the homemade salsa was disappointing.

My wife had the enchilada and was disappointed, not much flavor or spice.  I had a special, shrimp in chipotle sauce, which was also disappointing.  Bland, overpriced food.  Luckily we used a Restaurant.com certificate so we saved $25.

The waiter was very nice, but that does not make up for everything else.

The food is delicious. 
North Third converted me from the traditional obsolete (JK) beef patty to an Ahi Tuna burger. Do you find the sound of an Ahi Tuna as a burger somewhat questionable? Then you haven't lived life. The fish tacos and fried eggplants will have you coming back for more. 

And if you carry Golden Monkey, then you have a great beer selection. 

Wanna take someone out for a first date, but you fear awkward silence? Don't fret. The provocative interior decors (not for the prudish innocent souls) will be your ultimate wingman. Enjoy.

Hands down has to be the best Korean restaurant in South Jersey & dare I say it, in Philadelphia also. The spicy chicken dol-sot bi bim bap is AMAZING. Sometimes I have dreams about it. Their side dishes are usually pretty tasty, & the service is very friendly. The wings that they have are not that good.. Too much breading & the sauce is sticky icky. 

In all a decent restaurant with pretty good combination sets & great tasting food.

nice place, friendly service (besides the waitress my friends and i got), and good food. got a few antipastas that came out after we got our food. i got the cheddar pierogies, they were cold but still good. kind of pricey for 3 pierogies with specks of broccoli.
  also, having it shoved at me by the waitress wasn't the best experience either. waitress didn't come to check on us until we had to find her and ask for the checks. sat us, a party of 4, at a dirty table. guess she didn't bother to check if it was clean or not.
  anyways, the other folks were very friendly, kind, and full of smiles, especially the woman at the front desk! she was incredibly sweet. going to be coming back again since i'm positive that there's got to be a great server here.

I decided to try this place because I'm always and ever on the lookout for good Indie coffee joints to frequent.  Good location (across from Banner Bank Building).  Fun little upstairs loft with comfy leather sofas, chairs and a couple of tables.  The layout of the place is strange...there isn't really very much seating downstairs and even with the loft, there still isn't much.  And, what is there, isn't terribly convenient--we sat upstairs in the loft on the sofa, but there was nowhere to sit our coffee (they're called coffee tables for a reason, yo!).  The coffee?  In a word?  Meh.  You'd do better by going to any number of other coffee houses downtown (Java, Dawson's, Flying M--to name a few).

I do not like hamburgers very much. They never impress or excite me. Farm Burger impresses and excites me! The staff knows every item of the menu and will recommend great things to try. The chili mayo is amazing and adds a great Asian zing to it similar to spicy mayo used on sushi! 10/10 one of my favorite burgers I have ever had.

Went on a random Tuesday afternoon and the place was packed- for very good reason. Everything here was great- we had my 2-year-old in tow and scored the little short bench-table in the front corner, which was perfect for him. The muffelata was great, but I really wanted to steal my father's BLT- which was really one of the best I'd tasted. The toddler had the little mini-pizzetta small plate, which he thought was a little personal-sized toddler pizza (I took a taste and it was great, too)... 
Perhaps the ultimate highlight of the meal was the Pancetta Mac & Cheese- omg- this was so good it should have a warning. 
After eating, I got a sandwich to go for my SO at home, and then had to stock up on some of the homemade cookies, some bacon chocolate covered almonds (I liked them, but thought they were a little too cocoa-tasting and not sweet enough, my SO loved them) and some bacon pralines (I loved them, my SO thought they were too sweet for his taste)
I need to go back sometime to get some of the meat here so I can cook up something incredible on the grill at home...

Usually limoncello is our safe spot: a reliably always yummy place to eat. Today was a bit disappointing. The servers were great and always attentive. We only ordered the calamari for a light lunch to share. The breading was great and light, but the squid was very over cooked. It was like chewing rubber. We have had it before and not had this problem, so hoping it was just a random midweek lunch thing.

I dont live close to a panda express, therefore i enjoy it when I can. 
Classic orange chicken and beijing beef with half noodles half white rice, is always a good choice. 
The teriyaki chicken is also recommended. Wish the restaurants would allow limited seating. Taking food home and having to reheat it, is not ideal. Hopefully soon.

I love Prohibition Taproom! Great service, very neighborhood/local spot type of feel. Dim, cozy, low-key. 

I loved their gnocchi, mac and cheese, and their hand-cut fries. 

This is a good place to grab a drink with co-workers. It has a chill vibe for conversing and enjoying food/drinks.

First Freebirds in the world... The world was never the same. Great burritos here. Lots of varied clientele and a friendly staff to boot. The funny change about this location is that instead of moody gringos making your burrito it's run by real Latinos. They made me a superb monster burrito and I think it was cheaper than most franchise locations. There was however a bit less of a selection on things like tortillas, salsas and shredded tortilla chips for fillers in the burrito. Still an amazing burrito joint and worlds better than the bafflingly bad chipotle.

I came back to Joe's after a long absence and wasn't disappointed.  The breakfast food was good for the price.  The atmosphere isn't authentic, but it's a great place for a laid back Sunday brunch with time to linger over the paper.

5 stars for Five Guys!!!  This has to be one of, if not the best place to get some really good, cheap, quick food.  I hear can people whining, "I've heard it's greasy?"  Well, yeah, it is.  But you don't compare 5 Guys to some West Coast juice bar, a nice place you take your significant other for an anniversary dinner, or even a "gourmet" joint that serves up $30 Wagyu burgers.  Yeah, it's a chain; but as chains go, this one is pretty darn good.

Five Guys is counter service, and while the staff only has limited interactions with you, they're always friendly and efficient about what they're doing.  TONS of toppings for your burger, and with the exception of cheese and bacon, they're all free!  I'm pretty vanilla when it comes to my topping selections, but it's nice to have the option if I'm in the mood to upgrade.  I usually opt for the Bacon Cheeseburger; The Wife sticks with the Little Cheeseburger.  Don't let the inclusion of "little" in the title fool you, this is still a good-sized sandwich!  Also, a regular fry is plenty to share as they're always spilling over into the bag.  Finally, don't sleep on the free peanuts!  It's not like you're going to Five Guys specifically for them, but they're a lifesaver if someone is starving and needs a quick snack before your freshly made brown bag of goodness is ready.  If you're looking for a quick lunch or dinner, or are just feeling really casual, spend a few bucks more here, rather than some other fast food; you'll be glad you did.

Yay! Finally a good fast/casual noodle place in N Pinellas Woo hoo:) My husband brought me home the Mi-So Spicy Ramen and considering Ramen doesn't usually travel well I was impressed.  My husband ate his on site and really liked it.
It came with lots of noodles, very well seasoned/flavorful broth, and a great piece of crispy seared pork.  They also have Pho, Poke and lots of other cool options.  As long as you go in with the expectation of solid/tasty food (not this is the best noodle house on the planet) I think you'll enjoy.  Hope they stick around!

Some of the best food in town, certainly the best ethnic type food in the area. We had some appetizers that were awesome (crab Rangoon, spring rolls) and one that was so/so (salmon roll special). 

The entrees were the best food I had in a while. I got the Lobster King which was lobster in a chu chee curry sauce, which is red curry with coconut milk..? I think. I have never been a curry fan and always hated the smell of curry. I now realize what I thought of as "curry" was like comparing a frozen TV dinner lasagna to good Italian food. The lobster tasted sweet and spicy but neither one was overpowering. The veggies went perfectly and although my mouth was burning it was a "good" burn. The person I was with had the Lemon Grass Flank Steak which was cooked perfectly and so good he got one to take home. 

The only downside was the service. It wasn't perticularly busy and yet it took a while to get refills on drinks. The server also seemed, disinterested almost? It's hard to describe but it was bad enough the next time we just got take out. 

The downside to that was I was told 20 mins for the food. No problem, ran some errands and got there 35 mins after calling. Then waited another 15 minutes for the crab Rangoon. WTF? When I got there I was surprised it wasn't done already and was told its the crab that was taking longer then expected. 50 mins for crab Rangoon?? It's crazy. The girl was super nice and polite but even making that by hand would take less time. I'm not sure what exactly was going on but it was a bad excuse. Just tell the truth, someone forgot to put the order in, etc but don't tell me absurd tales of the magically uncookable Rangoon.

Watch Out!  Antioch Location:  Food poisoning from spinach enchiladas. Very sick for 2 days. When I called them they wanted to know why I did not call sooner!!!!!   Well ..... because I had food poisoning!!!  
Will never go back. Tooooo bad, at one time this was my favorite place to eat.  Times change....must move on.  Again, Watch Out!!!!

Loveeeee this place... This was my first time here and although I don't see myself going here on the regular because most times when I head out for dinner I prefer for my food to be cooked for me versus me having to cook the food myself, lmaoo. Because if that was the case I would stay home and cook in my own kitchen lol. But as far as going here for a date, something fun or different. I would come back here for sure!!!

From the moment I walked in the door the customer service was amazing until the minute I walked out. Everyone who I came in contact was very pleasant!!! Which is how it should be when you are out spending your money. But not every business understands that. But this place for sure gets it

I walked in and was greeted by the hostess with a smile and warm welcome. Who then showed me to my seat by the window. The only two complaints I have are that maybe the inside could get a little touch up on the interior. And second my table have needed to be wiped one more time before I was seated there. It looked like some droppings of food was still left of the table. Other than that no complaints.

So it was a Monday around 1:30pm I came and figured I would take advantage of the lunch special they had. Which I got the "3 meat option lunch special" so I was able to choose 3 different meats, a salad, soup and white rice. Everything was delicious!!! The soup was great and well seasoned, the salad was very delicious the meat was great besides me burning some because the meat is very finely cut. But it was all great. You get a nice bowl of white rice.  

I was stuffed and I had food to even take home. I had order the spring rolls and Japanese chicken as appetizers and both were very good also. I did add on broccoli, which I did not like the flavor of. Whatever it was seasoned with was a little to much. But the broccoli itself was very fresh. I also Sade's s'mores for dessert which you can't go wrong with

I had my daughter and her friend with me as well. And they loved the food and everything about the experience.

One thing I loved is that every person one the staff seemed available to help. And they were moving around often but not as often as it would become annoying. To help clear the tables to make room for you once you finished with a dish or anything. So I never had a messy table or had to wait to my waiter to come clear something. Everyone there was very nice and willing to get anything you may have needed. 

The experience was great and I will for sure be back whenever I want to do something different.

Thank you guys for remembering what customer service is all about

Ordered two meals and two desserts tonight for delivery. The meals were great! Very good and would totes order again. Hubs dessert came perfect but I was missing my brownie bites and only got the ice cream :( I wanted my chocolate fix!

What you do when you love hot chicken and you are looking for something vegan? You could put hot sauce on a carrot OR you can race down to Joella's Hot Chicken and get yourself some Vegan Hot Chicken. I was sold after I learned it started with J-O-E and I had to have it. Also, the one lady on 90-Day fiancé works at one which is why I googled it and why I found this place to begin with! That show has never steered me wrong!

I will say the Vegan Hot Chicken didn't look all that appealing as it lacked a sauce. It could have been breaded so it had the crunchy layer that held the sauce and heat. I ordered the tweeny which was between medium and hot and it definitely could have been hotter. The spice levels are vastly different at these places and some medium means Hot AF and some medium means it has black pepper on it. There needs to be an industry standard!!!! I feel I could have ordered the hottest one here as I was only 2 levels removed.

The Fries were think and absolutely delicious! So fresh, hot, and crispy! The vinegar based cole slaw went nicely and I could have totally made a Pittsburgh style sandwich with the fries/slaw combo! Yinz know what I mean?

They also had a sampler of 5 tenders at 5 different spice levels which I totally would have been on board with for my first trip, but it was only real chicken. Also, I think they had 6 heat levels, but one may have been plain. I didn't look that far down on the list.

They had Boylan soda which was Ok and did the job of wetting the whistle after a long drive. If you're into craft soda, then you'll probably like it.  I'm a Coke Zero snob (trying to quit) so it wasn't my favorite.  Lots of people seemed to be getting take-out too, so it's good for that.

I'd come back here if I was in the area, order the hot and see if they can add some extra sauce to make it wet.  It's a nice fast-casual joint, the staff was helpful in helping me decide as I told her it was my first time.  She said I'd like it and I should call her Nash-stradamus cause she was right.

This is the spot. It's the type of place you want when you want crawfish, spicy, flavorful, affordable and good. I got 1 lb crawfish, 1 lb shrimp, 1 fried turkey wing, 4 potatoes and 2 big beers. The seasoning on the crawfish and the potatoes was so delicious! Definitely worth the drive. The atmosphere is simple and comfortable and you can tell that people who live here come here.

Came here when visiting my son. It was ok. Staff was very nice and looks like a fun place to hang out. They had excellent COVID protocols in place, so I felt safe eating there. The food was just average which is why I only gave it 3 stars.

Well first off, the place always seems to be dirty. I get that customers can leave their trash for the staff to clean but they aren't very attentive. I ordered the cheesy pig and fries, the bacon was way too hard to even bite into. The fries were literally crumbs and hard ones at that, also pretty cold. I could barely bite into any. I told the cashier and he offered me new fries but that took another fifteen mins. While I waited I noticed they have food waiting to go out for about five mins before anybody even realizes there's anything there. I guess that's why all the food was cold.

I have the first boy from China to be adopted in the state of Louisiana . After finishing our "over priced meal ( $58. I had salad w/ goat cheese. $11.; gazpacho ,$7,&$7 margarita. With husband's entree, $58.   Obviously, designed to be a casual outside dining spot. Inside, a bit " over done", using faux antique mirrors, combined with 21 year olds  blasting profanity. Obviously, acceptable, as no one attempted to subdue their foul mouths. So do not let decor fool you. "Elegant", they are not. One of my two best friends, growing up in Mobile, AL., birthday is today. I detest selfies of myself, as the Alabama sun has left a permanent impression on my smiling face. Asked bartender. So " bored", pic caught him staring towards our beloved Esplanade Ave. The manager humiliated in a way I'd never had done to me before. I'm not 21. Taught school 30.yrs. Only child about to leave for LSU. Husband is quiet. Still have that part of ALA that likes to chat with strangers. Remember young wife's aunt adopted in Russia. Young husband mentioned he knew some who adopted from Ghanghou. I said..( TOPS issues),& he said,"I've heard." I was voted "Most Gullible", Who's Who." MANAGER was STANDING behind me, making faces.!!!!!!!!!! This has never(!!!), happened to me in my life!!!! Do NOT dine if over 35, or accompanied by individuals 35 & under. Cannot believe humans behave in this manner. Such as that off a ten year old.

Love this place! Our server Victoria and her team kept our table happy the entire night. The food...calamari, bruschetta, truffle fries, eggplant pizza, bake ziti, Mac and cheese all delicious. The desserts and coffee outstanding. Bring a bottle of wine (we did 2016 Staggs Merlot) and enjoy your night!

Very impressive smells if you ever walk by!I don't know why it took us forever to try the food, but while some people might feel like it's not enough food... it's certainly good food and pretty heavy/rich. I love the brisket cheese steak. The meat was just cooked perfect and was so flavorful. The little potato sticks on top with the sauce was pretty messy and fell off quite a bit, to the point I used a bunch of napkins and really appreciated they had wet napkins for you. My food seemed heavy enough and well-portioned. Loved the bread-  - something about it was very delicious and complimented the brisket so well. It's nothing like regular ol' hoagie roll at all! Some sorcery...
They have bottled soda, which is very nifty. Not sure if they have canned... they're allowing dine-in, however not too sure about now since covid issues seemed to have recently escalated. Either way, 10/10 I'd come back for more.

Oh how I have missed In-N-Out!!! I moved to the Midwest, and unless I'm willing to drive 6 hours one way, I'm pretty much out of luck. But on my recent trip to Tucson to visit family, I had to insist on coming here! This was the first stop right off the plane, and I couldn't have been happier! Yeah, we arrived in the evening, and it was busy, but it really wasn't terrible. The staff was nice, and didn't rush us to place our order. 

The food was fresh, and everything I remembered. I got a regular burger, fries and drink, but it was cooked perfectly, and absolutely delicious! I really wish I could have gone back one more time before we left, but the memory will hold me over for a while. All in all, it was a great experience.

I didn't love it. It was a nice experience. Really interesting flavors. Different. But I wasn't blown away. There wasn't one thing on the menu I thought I HAD to have again in my life...we had the burrata...good but not Katie's pizza amazing. We also had the butternut squash. It was different than anything I've had before in my life so much that it threw me off being cold and spicy but I wouldn't eat it again but glad for the experience. We had the chicken and gnocchi. The chicken was really super rich but I could do as well with chicken from straubs at home. The gnocchi was loaded with crab and flavorful but not powerful...prefer the gnocchi at Olive and Oak. I loved Niche and I love Brasserie. Not a fan of Pasteria so I'm not surprised about the latest. Maybe I'm just old school Gerard Craft...did like the atmosphere and service! And the rolls but the butter wasn't what the reviews rave about and bread and butter are life!

Tabboulee is this household's hot spot for this area. Quality food that's fast from a team with excellent people skills. Definitely recommend anything with the curry sauce and/ or the hot taziki sauce.
Love this dinner. Friendly staff. Great ppl good food. Always treated so nice by staff. Great for breakfast lunch or dinner.

I would say I felt like this was more 3.5 but I can't bring myself to say I'm a fan... with an exclamation point! Overall, this was a typical experience relative to other Nashville spots - nothing outright horrible but nothing that makes me want to come back for seconds.

Happy hour is strictly in the bar/lounge area. However, you can order one of the happy hour drinks to your table. Not sure how much it costs you though but considering the cheapest regular cocktail is $14, I highly doubt you'll get it for anywhere near the low low happy hour price of $6. Perhaps the pro move is to eat, drink and save a few dollars by dining in the bar/lounge only and then move to the dining area once you get your fill of the happy hour offerings.

I didn't drink because I was more interested in spending my money on food. I heard so much rumbling about the Crispy Brussels Sprouts and Spicy Tuna Crispy Rice that I felt an obligation to order them.

The Brussels Sprouts were an easy standout. The vinaigrette was the MVP. The acidity kept the dish bright and easy to eat by itself. It is one of my favorite preparations, so much better than the classic bacon preparation. This is easy to share with others so you can save room for other dishes.

The Spicy Tuna Crispy Rice ate like a weird gimmick that catches a bunch of attention because of its Instagram-worthiness or the popular components - Sushi! Spicy Tuna! Sriracha! Crispifying anything! This was all hype and no substance. Spend less money on a spicy tuna roll at a decent sushi place if that's what you're looking for.

Outside of trying the hyped dishes, I ordered the Hamachi Marrow. This tasted good but when you think about the fact that each piece is $7... it's tough to swallow.

I tried some of the Pork Adobo Fried Rice. The taste was okay but it was very one-note which rendered itself forgettable.

I had a half piece of the Unagi Foie nigiri (a two-piece dish) and I don't think I got any foie in my bite so I can't speak to that element. The unagi was very, well, unagi-ish. If you don't like the fattiness and the sauce, you're not going to like this dish. The weird thing was that our waitress tried to sell it by saying that the unagi sauce breaks up the fattiness which I don't understand because unagi sauce is salty and sweet and not acidic. Perhaps the yuzu marmalade was supposed to be the element to cut through the fattiness but I must not have gotten any of it in my bite. Despite not getting to taste the full piece as intended, I have to say the worst thing about this dish was that it was like ordering a souffle, except we were not warned about the wait. It was ordered during the first round of orders. But this dish only appeared after a second round of orders were placed and came to the table. That was extremely disappointing.

A different dish was ordered and we saw it basically making the rounds to every other table in the dining area before it finally made it to its rightful destination - our table. How is this such a problem? Isn't there an indication of the table? Or do the runners not know what table is which so they opt to ask every table before asking the waiter who placed the order?

The upside on the service was that my water cup was never less than half full. I literally would take two small sips and someone would come by and pour some more water in my cup. Of course, I'd rather have it this way than having to gesture like I'm in a desert to a waiter across the room.

Despite eating what amounted to three and a half pieces of nigiri, a scoop of adobo rice and a scoop of Brussels Sprouts and no alcohol, I was paying close to $40. If you go with a big group of undiscerning eaters who like to share and don't have a budget, this would be a good option.
Great service from Christian! Delicious food and BOGO as well. Busy day today, Mothers' Day. Well orchestrated staff. A little noisy, but tolerable.  Check it out!

My company hosted The Cheese Shack food truck today for lunch, They were very friendly and the bruschetta sandwich was honestly one of the best sandwiches I've ever had. It was served on the most amazing bread with a sweet balsamic drizzle. It was hot, crunchy, and made my taste buds sing until the very last bite! My only disappointment was that the mac and cheese balls were so popular that they were sold out by the time I got out there (I was one of their last customers for the day), but I can't wait to try them next time!
The usual fare at this Delaware original chain outlet.   We ordered 2 Capastramis and two Bobbies.  Both met the usual Capriotti standards.  It's nice to have one closer to home.
The owner is in there making pizzas by himself and they were outstanding! Definitely get some food here!!

This is a great addition to the neighborhood. Ordered seafood ramen and pork ramen on respective visits, and they were both excellent. Their fried rice side dish is so unique and flavorful, nothing like the generic fried rice you usually get. And their chicken Katsu is delicious, this coming from someone who normally doesn't like chicken. It's definitely a neighborhood-type establishment so don't expect fine dining, but the food makes up for it. I'm looking forward to trying some non-Ramen specialties in the future.

My first experience-I was thrilled bc I've only heard wonderful things and as a Nashville native this was refreshing, due to the influx of new (everything really) restaurants. 

We went with a birthday party-party if 13. They accommodated and the service was beyond excellent. The waiter was attentive to each and every person. Coming around to each of us individually-made our big group feel small and completely manageable. 


This is for the VEGETARIANS- get the Black Kale: Curants, Marcona Almonds, Lemon, Parmesan and EVO. I don't know what kind of magic they put into this kale salad but it's there. Next, get the Risotto Tater Tots ASAP. Pure genius! Lastly, if you haven't had a enough cheesiness from the risotto get the macaroni gratinèe and please, please, please add the roasted jalapeños. The crunchy panko with the roasted jalapeños-perfection.
Great BURGERS! Stop by or call ahead. Service was Awesome! When they a have coupons it helps make dinning out an easier choice!

Sometimes Yelp hits the head on the nail and other times, it misses the boat. Unfortunately, Yelp has missed and has lead me to a place where BBQ is average at best. 

Four of us ended up here one late lunch or early dinner and ordered the Lancaster, which consisted of a whole chicken, brisket, 1/2 rack ribs, six pieces of cornbread, 1 lb slaw, fries, mac and cheese, and collard greens.

The biggest letdown was the brisket because there was hardly any smokiness to it. On top of that, it was pretty dry, most likely because it didn't have enough fat on it. The ribs were pretty good, not completely fall off the bone but decent enough to get on a regular basis. Fries were meh, mac and cheese was nothing special (penne pasta, no crust, no texture), collard greens were overly bitter because of lack of seasoning, and the cornbread was dry. We also didn't get any butter with our cornbread, and when we asked for it, they gave us extremely cold butter that was unspreadable. 

All in all, not the greatest experience.

In town with friends doing the cheesesteak trifecta.
When the meat slightly varies from joint to joint, I think Tony's wins hands down with their bread. (They also accept credit cards)
Total Package.....Tony Lukes!

I have heard that Acme Oyster House is the place to go to in New Orleans for good oysters, and the place didn't disappoint at all.  The line and wait was really long, but that's to be expected for a well-known restaurant on a Saturday night.  We fell in line at about 5:30 and got in around 6:45, so I'd arrive early.  I'd also grab a drink and wait in line if it seems like it would be a long wait.

I ordered a seafood etouffee with fried crawfish tails (an additional $3.99 that's so worth it), and we collectively ordered two dozens of the renowned char-grilled oysters.  The etouffee itself was full of flavor and the amount of seafood was plentiful.  It was even better when the crawfish tails were added, so I highly recommend the addition.  The char-grilled oysters were just as good as everyone says.  The sizes varied but were large in general, the oysters themselves were fresh and cleaned well, and the flavoring was on point.  It's really no wonder that these oysters are the restaurant favorite and an order that everyone recommends.

Had the BEST hot dog today. Ate the Desert Dawg and it was a good thing I was hungry. Grilled hot dog topped with beans, bacon, potatoes and homemade relish, the whole nine yards. So good. I will definitely be back. Russ honors veterans with a free soda. Plenty of parking.

Food and service were great!  Cindy, the manager, was awesome- very friendly and inviting and gave great advice on what to order. We also had a great experience with our waitress Rebecca, and the bartender Lexis when we had after-dinner beers.  Even though we were there late and closing duties had started, we never felt rushed and they made us feel welcome to stay as long as we wanted.  (The beer was also great!)

I've visited Athens several times now and have been impressed every time.  First of all, everyone here is so friendly! I always feel very welcomed.  Most recently enjoyed a chicken gyro with delicious side salad but have also tried the lamb souvlaki and been rather delighted with how yummy it was.  Also recently tried the "Athen's Famous Avgolemono Soup," a traditional Greek soup with chicken, rice, eggs, and lemon juice.  Lemon juice, Megan? You ask.  That just doesn't sound like it belongs! You proclaim.  I asked the same thing.  And the second I tasted it all of my doubts were dashed.  I could probably eat an embarrassing amount of this concoction.  Unfortunately for me, the bf ordered the soup, already knowledgeable of its tastiness, and I didn't want to interfere.  Next time, I'm totally getting my own bowl.  Or swimming pool.  If they have that.

Would've liked to have tried the food. Don't bother trying to eat a late lunch here. They don't believe in it and we waited for 20 minutes with tons of empty tables in view but these were reserved for dinner and were told we came in between lunch and dinner so... that's a problem. Ok- so close your doors after 2pm! Came in at 2:30. Would've taken an hour max to eat. Yet somehow that's infringing on your dinner hours and ??? Finally told us after waiting 15 minutes there was only one table we could have- unfortunately the customers had paid and were still sitting. The one table? No thanks.

Terrific restaurant! We went here on a whim and plan to come back! I got the Lamb Dumpakht, which is baked with bread over top, similar to potpie. They said it was the house specialty. It took a little longer to cook than other dishes, but it was worth the wait!  Amazingly flavorful lamb and delicious bread to go with it. The staff was lovely and very accommodating when we had to leave quickly for a show. I can't wait to go back and eat here again!!!

Dirty inside restaurant and bathrooms.
Weird issues with staffing and closing early.
Food isn't good like it used to be decent years ago. I wouldn't recommend this place.

Had a wonderful dinner at Mr and Mrs Crab, they go the extra step with social distancing and ensure you are seated apart to make you feel safe. Our server/bartender Sam stepped up and made our night special. The food was good and fresh, we had the snow crab, lobster and shrimp combos. The seasoning was spot on, the atmosphere was good. Had a wonderful time, highly recommend!

Great concept, okay food, too pricey for what you get, and rude staff. 

I love the "design your own food" concept like Chipotle, and Blue Coast Burrito, but what you get for the cost and quality leaves much to be desired. 

When I went it was staffed by kids who were very open about their disdain for their job. Wish Mount Juliet would get a Chipotle. My money would be better spent there on quality food from quality ingredients at a fair price. 

Clean.

I'm currently very disappointed in Pearl Diver. I had long been anticipating its opening and couldn't wait to check it out. But there's definitely some kinks that need to be worked out (as several other reviewers have already pointed out).  First the Pros - the inside of the restaurant is gorgeous. Positively awesome, special, amazing attention to detail, super comfy seating, too, by the way. I definitely felt as though I were sitting in a cafe in Havana. I have no issue with ordering at the bar (although it can indeed leave you alienated from your group for 15 minutes or so, but still not a biggie). The prices are comparative to other trendy bars in Nashville. The bartenders and staff clearing tables were all super friendly and lovey.  

Now the things that gave me pause: I tried the platter of food samplings and it was decent, but not particularly exciting. Pretty basic fair dressed up with spicy dip options and dressings. The best offering I tasted was a bite of my friend's burger, which had a nice kick to it, but again nothing special. IF I go back I'll try the Cubano Sandwich, which may win me over. As a few others have stated, many of the drinks are fairly weak - yummy but mostly fruit juice and in the case of one drink I ordered, a large piece of fruit took up 50% of the glass, so that was disappointing for the $14 price tag. The exception to this rule are the dark rum drinks which packed a punch. The Mai Tai is somewhere in the middle. 

There were some major service issues including:  When the shared food items came to the table there were no plates, no silverware and our party of four was provided with two pair of chopsticks and one single napkin. These are tiny things BUT they also get really old really fast when you have to stand in line at the bar where everyone else is trying to get drinks in order to flag down a bartender to get utensils so your party can eat and then return to the table where your food is now lukewarm. 

My biggest problem with Pearl Diver was the way the door was handled. Upon my arrival at 6:20 pm, a line of four girls (my being the fifth) was held outside the door and refused entry due to the need to create a "calm ambience" inside the restaurant and also something about helping the bartenders "keep up" which made no sense unless they were having a staffing issue at the time. However, once we were let inside (a mere 10 minutes later), we discovered that Pearl Diver was HALF EMPTY... bar seats, a booth and a huge L-shaped seating area that spanned half the front side of the restaurant were all empty / unoccupied and four bartenders were at the helm. The patio wasn't busy either. I really don't know what the issue was unless PD is trying to establish a perception of exclusivity by making sure there is always some type of line outside the door (I did notice when two more people walked up, the door gal let two people in and so on and so forth). Perception is awesome, guys, but when your clientele begins its evening with a negative vibe, they are less likely to return. . .or they might just walk away after a few minutes in line once customers realize they're being kept outside purely for show.
It's Tijuana Flats! If you enjoy hot sauce, well than duh you will love this place. I personally enjoy hot sauce. The norrito bowl is delicious.
I gave this place another try. It has gotten a lot better than the first visit. This place is better than all the dim sum restaurants in Philly.

My husband and I came here on a Sunday afternoon for lunch. We were greeted by a very friendly, young hostess, probably the "teenage hostess" referred to in a previous review. She was kind, welcoming, very personable. The service was great. Our waiter was attentive, informative, and patient with us as we decided what to get. The sangria and mimosa we started with were tasty! As for the food, my husband and I ended up getting the seafood linguine, and the pasta and seafood were very well cooked and the lobster sauce was delicious! Highly recommended.

This hotel reminds me of that "turn of the century" grand style and elegance.  The location is awesome, in the heart of the city center and right on Walnut Street.  The set up is very odd, however, with the registration desk on the 19th floor adjacent to the XIX Nineteen restaurant.  From the palatial windows, you get a breathtaking view of the city.  The concierge desk is on the ground floor where you are greeted by a grand sweeping stair case.  The floors are some type of aging mosaic petit tile flooring, which are absolutely beautiful.  And an extra nice touch is all the beautifully displayed orchids.  

The health club is awesome.  I high recommend taking advantage of the spa services at Pierre & Carlo Salon & Spa and it's nice to be able to visit The Shops at Bellevue.  And the ball room is truly amazing.  Hotel staff is good, too.

The guest rooms are huge and formally decorated.  The rooms have all the typical amenities plus nice designer toiletries.  The wallpaper is a little colorful and has a Victorian feel to it.  I just feel like the rooms are a little worn and tired and could benefit from a refurbish.  In spite of that, I had a very nice stay.
Awesome burgers, good beer selection, really great bartender and cozy atmosphere. Its never packed, so I hope it sticks around!

We had the pleasure of attending a wedding at this venue. Beautiful for sure! The lily pond and wisteria courtyard was dreamy in the sunset and the setup was very nice between the ceremony and reception. There's also a nice view from the hillside that includes the ocean, but it's not far from downtown at all.

I hear rooms go for $2000 a night here, but there's a great discount in limited quantity if a block is reserved by the wedding party. The rooms are separated into distinct buildings like a quaint little village and it really is cute. 

If you're in the market for a wedding venue, I have no idea how much this costs, but it's definitely worth looking into if it's in your budget.

This is in Carmel and is a really nice store.  The staff are friendly and were quite helpful.  I didn't spend as much time sampling this trip as I would have liked but it was a pleasant experience.  Vine and Table hosts many events and I was there to get my tickets for the Whiskey and Fine Spirits expo held at Montage.  A great event, yes a bit pricey, but when you have the opportunity to taste $1000 a bottle whiskey and $200 bottle bourbons it pays for itself.  The food at the event was great also.

We stumbled across this grocery while walking around the French Market area. This an old fashioned Italian grocery dating from when the neighborhood was largely populated by Italian immigrants. We ordered the half mufaletta. Large enough for the two of us to split. Basically an Italian hoagie. Italian meats and cheeses with a savory olive spread. The roll was round and topped with sesame seeds. Fresh and delicious. They have seating and bottled beer as well. This sandwich was a welcome break after all the Cajun and Creole food typical of the city.

These drinks are PHENOMENAL and witty ("Chai-d Car"). The drink menu is impossible to beat and extremely diverse. I suggest going with a group and everyone ordering different drinks to try several different items on the menu -- Or just go by yourself and stumble home. There is a drink for anyone on the menu and the staff was very friendly.  

To be honest, the first time I came here I was disappointed that I could still see outside the window. The atmosphere is definitely like a ski lodge -- They have a "fire place," logs, the walls are painted to look like a ski slope, and they play Winter Olympic clips which is great, but then you can look out the window and see there is no snow and you are still in the great city of Nashville.  

I think I also ate them out of Salmon dip, but if they found some fish hiding somewhere, I suggest ordering it for sure.

Stopped in for hot chocolate and dessert after seeing an ad on Snapchat. The beignet flight here was delicious. The three we got were s'mores, raspberry and matcha filling. Being so used to Cafe Dumond and Morning Call, this was my first time eating filled beignets. They were sweet but did not overdo it. The ambience is good, warm, and dimly lit which is perfect for the winter season. Don't forget to go to the booth to order the beignets and other baked goods-- they don't really come to take your order like one would be used to at Cafe Dumond and Morning Call. For the beignet flight and hot chocolate, it was around $14, which is a little overpriced but worth the experience.

This Companion is close to work, so I dropped in the other day for a sammy. My first thought was - it's SMALL! It gets super crowded at lunch and is also small. I wouldn't want to eat in unless you want hoards of people around and people watching you eat and begging with their eyes for you to finish already so they can take your table. Parking is actually ok since there is a side street that is easy to park on and walk since it's on the corner. 

That being said, Companion has awesome bread and sandwiches. I love the cocktail party - brie, apples and apricot marmalade on some sort of walnut bread. Toasted. YUM!! It doesn't come with anything but you can make it a bag lunch easily. The soups and entrees come with a roll or bavarian pretzel on the side. I highly recommend the pretzel. They are so good! I buy them in Schnuck's or Straubs frequently. Warm them up and they make a great snack. Companion also has local products like Fitz's. It's pretty quick once you order to get your food. 

I was pleasantly surprised to see that the foil they wrapped my sandwich in kept it really warm when I got to work and was ready to eat it. I also got a frosted sugar cookie, which I didn't like much. The frosting was kind of gummy tasting and the consistency of the cookie wasn't great. That being said, there are a lot of cool designs on them. 

This is definitely a primo sandwich stop!

Seriously the nicest folks! From the bartender to the cook to the other patrons, I always feel like a regular when I walk in, even though I barely make it once a year. I'd come by more often if I lived in the area but I always consider it a treat if I find myself in the position to pop in. Always a pleasure!
Everytime, for years this has been a reliable place to get good and authentic mexican food!

We go here ever few months to get our fix of great Chinese food.  In my opinion better than Chinatown's in Philly and DC and totally rivals New York.  The food is very consistent and the service is wonderful.  Even if we haven't visited in months, the wait staff always recalls my favorite dish.  I cannot express in words how great the Honey Citrus Chicken or the Rainbow Wild Pepper Chicken tastes.  Wow, some of the best meals I have ever ordered.  Tonight, we also decided to try the Mei Mei Chicken.  Very tasty, but might be better as an appitizer.  Can't wait until our next visit!!!

This place is under the radar and you should be going.  I frequented the Fishers location for some Korean flavor and was nervous how the transition would be to Carmel.  Nonetheless, I'm pleased that Miracle is an established Carmel joint.  Their sushi is always well done.  The service is friendly.  The Rainbow roll is definitely my sushi roll go-to in the north suburbs.

I had a pulled pork taco with pickled red cabbage on toasted paratha bread. My wife had a chicken chorizo with Brussels sprouts slaw. Both were wonderfully tasty.

The chips with salsa verde side were lightly toasted, flaky paratha bread. Very nice!

We will definitely eat here again!

Toppers Pizza - not quite top notch.

I happened upon Toppers Pizza quite by accident.  I was planning to visit another "newish" spot (http://www.yelp.com/biz/blaze-fast-fired-pizza-indianapolis?hrid=BVKe1oPjHbbBuBs1yvtq2A), but the line was snaking its way out the door.  My companion and I decided to stroll across the street and ran right into Toppers.

The pizza was good.  Nothing to celebrate with a parade in the street, but certainly worth a try.  There are a variety of menu options and topping choices.  The space is very small with only one 4-person high top table, about 6 bar stools, and a couch/conversation nook.  I assume Toppers wants you to take your treats to-go.  

I would recommend Toppers if you just want something quick, easy, and relatively reasonably priced.  But, don't make a special trip.  This is definitely a "because I was in the area and kind of wanted pizza" spot.

What a comfortable and relaxed atmosphere. The food is very well prepared. The prices a really reasonable. The staff is very friendly. Everything about this seafood restaurant wants to keep coming back.

Such a great market! It is so unique and such a fun place to take out of town visitors! The take and bake meals are an easy weeknight go to meal. The patio is a great spot to enjoy a glass of wine and one of their awesome subs! Prosciutto and mozzarella is my personal favorite! Don't forget to grab a canollj to take home too
The thin crust pepperoni pizza was so good we went back the day next day and got more! I'm picky about my pizza and this place is AMAZING. It has to be the sauce that makes it so good.

I stopped in here with a friend after visiting someone in the hospital for a few hours. We came in and it was packed! We lucked out and were able to get 2 seats at the bar! The service was prompt even though they were sooo busy (I believe it was a lighting play off game that night) we got some beers and talked for bit then got an order of wings. Those wings may be some of the best I've ever had! My only mistake was ordering only 10 wings. I wish we had ordered more, but that's ok, as I'll be visiting my friend in the hospital for at least the next 2 weeks, so Hattricks, here I come!

Really tried to like this place. 
Went back twice believing I might have caught them on an off night for the brisket.
I'll give credit where it's due however and the only reason that this isn't a 1 star review. The smoked wings are extremely good. 
With that said, I've ordered the Brisket here twice several months apart and both times it was dry/overlooked and without much flavor. Get the feeling they cook everything in the morning and serve it throughout the day rather than cook fresh all day. 
Sides were also just ok. 
Everything on the menu is on the upper end of price for BBQ establishments as well. Actually, they're probably the highest in the area.
Owner is great, very approachable and always onsite. 
Just wish the food was a high quality as the idea behind the restaurant

Vegan done wrong. We ordered two different vegan tacos and were disappointed by both. First off the kitchen "mixed up" the order and put mixed veggies on one of the tacos that was supposed to be only tofu and cheese. Which would have been fine if those veggies were seasoned at all. Everything we had, from the house made tortilla chips to the hash browns and all the fixins for the tacos, was severely underseasoned. No salt to be found anywhere, let alone some garlic or onion or some black pepper. The tacos were also poorly plated, you can see from the photo that they just laid the tortillas on the plate and dropped the ingredients on with no thought as to filling the tacos evenly. The avocado was also sliced all sorts of weird, not consistently sized. The tofu was nice and crispy but also incredibly bland. We didn't get the opportunity to tell our server, as they only came around to ask how it was when we were finished eating. For the price, we can make the same vegan meals at home - and remember to add salt.
Great restaurant with plenty of vegan options! Love the roasted veggies

Love it!  Sit in Johnny's section and make sure he gets you a "Happy Ending" when you're all done.  I need a monitor next time... I can't be trusted with an all you can eat sushi dinner that is so good, fresh, and fun.  Haven't tried the other location - this one is intimate and really clean.

Holy almost NOLA....fantastic menu, great prices!    The food arrived and I was so excited to eat I forgot to take pic.  Then dessert came and almost made the same mistake.   My daughter and I split char-broiled oysters, crab cakes, and grilled shrimp in a cream sauce I'd like to layer myself in.   My go-to desserts are creme brûlée and bread pudding...they had the bread pudding and it is one of the best I've ever had.   Hot, thick with yummy sauce and great whipped cream.   We will be back.
Just got here from Northern Virginia, this place is amazing, unbelievable pizza, great ingredients, can't go wrong, if you don't like this, please tell me what's better

I just wanted to say that coming here made my weekend. Definitely one of the best experiences I've had at a Firstwatch hands down. Not only did they seat us fairly quickly for being crowded, but we were in a bit of a rush and the waiter moved heaven and earth to put our food order at the top of the pile of orders. We received three breakfast dishes in less than 15 mins. To me...that is amazing. And it was a packed house that morning! Not only that, but all of our dishes tasted great. The smoked salmon eggs Benedict were delicious. The salmon was fresh and the eggs Benedict was perfectly done. All on top of crisp piece of ciabatta bread...perfection. Then there was a refreshing pile of greens with lemon vinaigrette on the side as a palatte cleanser. My companions ordered the avocado toast (also one of my Firstwatch favorites) and the market hash. They enjoyed their meals as well.

But that wasn't it. Nick (we had to get his name because he was beyond awesome) set the bar super high when it comes to customer service. We were stunned by his kindness and his generosity the whole morning. If you come here for breakfast you will not regret it. That level of care from the staff and over all quality of food will have you more than satisfied. It will be the perfect start to an amazing day.

I'm updating this Diner to 5 stars, this is one place I have been going to more then few times. 

There's so much to enjoy about coming here for breakfast, private parking lot, so you can park your vehicle, and there's always a lot of space. the inside is so roomy with a lot of room to sit. it's quiet. The service is on top of everything. No matter what I order. it's always out within 5 minutes. their server is always back at the table asking me if there's anything I need and keeps pouring me a cup of coffee. Without asking. 

Their breakfast menu is huge, with so much to choose from. from breakfast specials. to eggs, omelets, french toast, stuffed french toast, reasonable prices. good quality coffee, 

I had the breakfast special this morning. It was two pieces of French toast two pieces of bacon. French toast was a nice size and bacon had a crisp. And was definitely filling. Basically that is all you need. To enjoy a good breakfast!! 

I will have to give lunch a try hear one time. Probably just as good as the breakfast.

I ordered the pastrami sandwich with Brussel sprouts and Mac and cheese. The pastrami sandwich was flavorful and not too fatty. The Brussel sprouts were seared to perfection with a slight kick. The Mac and cheese was savory with a light crust. For dessert we ordered the peanut butter pie and chocolate cake. Both were delicious and a great way to end a great meal.

Stellar beer. Solid food and the worst slow(I'm busy but I need to ignore you for now) service. 
Busy lunch time visit. Probably could have used an extra server. I will go back because the beer was so good but if I order food I'll just get it to go. Again, it was quality but as more brew pubs come on line in the area this place will suffer due to inattentive service.

Love this place. Usually have the Reuben or the pastrami sandwich.  Both solid. Their brownies are also very good. Honestly would've been 5 star but for two issues: (1) the ordering can be tedious. There's usually a long line at lunch hour, the credit card machine has failed a number of times (making the line worse), and then you have fight past the people at the register to pick up your food when it's ready; and (2) the price is a bit high considering the pricing of nearby competitors.

A dinner of tonkatsu, manga comic to read [backwards!], and a nice hot bowl of miso soup after work. Splendid!

This eatery is reminiscent of the izakayas I used to go to frequent in Japan, in that it provides food for the everyman without and pretentious accoutrement. Perfect for the after work meal.
We walked here from Frenchman Street to find it closed at 1230 on a Wednesday.  Call ahead to make sure Kayla' s is open before making the trip.  Sorry we missed it.

We went for lunch. The door was locked. We watched people dining and looking at us like we had 3 heads. After banging on the door the owner I presume came out and said they were out of bread besides one. Lock the door? No sign? Never had a chance to try do to poor planning!

On a visit to Indy I was able to stop here to buy dinner before heading back to Louisville. Worth it? Yes, times a million. This place is as authentic as you can get. The owners and staff are all from Jamaica and they know what they're doing. Traditional jerk chicken cooked on a grill, freshly cooked plantains, rice and peas, and delightfully baked patties. In addition to the world famous Jamaican jerk style chicken, they have other traditional dishes and some unique creations. Curried goat or chicken, oxtail, escovitch fish, brown stew chicken, and jerk ribs! Nom nom.

On this visit I got jerk chicken, curry goat, and some patties to go. Chicken comes with mild, hot, or barbeque jerk sauce - made in house. You are able to get most of the meals in a half or full size order and they come with a side. Either size is sure to fill you up and satisfy those taste buds. 

Took the meals home to my Jamaican husband and he was really pleased. If it was any closer he would have gone back the next day. Guaranteed!

Deep dish style is wonderful. Service is extremely poor, never a manager in sight and place seems to be run by inexperienced and/or poorly trained staff, as well as being routinely understaffed especially on Wednesday evenings for the popular wing-night.  I enjoy eating outside whenever possible and they do have a nice patio, however, it seems there could be a better mix of two and four seat tables (rather than the large round ones they have) that would make additional seating possible. 
This place would easily be four stars with a better patio arrangement, five if they had better customer service.

First time visiting, the Pho was great!  I've had Vietnamese soup in many places all over the country. This definitely was a great place in this area it is the best one. Great atmosphere clean. We loved it thank you
A very nice little diner - well worth the trip. My wife and I each had tasty omelets with excellent home fries and toast. Very good prices.

First impression on a Saturday night is that the place was empty. That's never a good sign for a good restaurant. There was live music which was mediocre. The service was very good but I would hope it would be when the restaurant is empty. The choices are very limited for a vegetarian, I didn't realize it was  centered around beef. In 2017 to have such limited selection of vegetarian offerings is sad. My husband ordered a seared tuna appetizer and for $17 he got 8 tiny pieces. I mean tiny! That was not worth it! One good thing was that they had gluten free pasta, but it was undercooked. I ordered a tomato Florentine soup and the waitress asked the chef if it is gluten-free he said it was. Well, it wasn't because it had pasta shells in it. What?! How does the chef not know his soup has pasta in it?! I have no plans of returning here. Highly disappointed.

So far this is my favorite Thai place in Indy!  I have tried several and this is the best.  The flavors are great, the service is good and the portions are perfect!  You can't beat the lunch specials that include soup and a spring roll.  I was stuffed and took home left overs!  I'm already salivating thinking of my next trip back for some more masaman curry....

I am definitely not a seasoned yelper, but I feel compelled to write this review in hopes that the management at Caffe Nonna will read. My Husband and I have lived in the neighborhood for close to 5 years now and Caffe Nonna has always been one of our go-to weekly spots for dinner. Over the past couple months we have noticed some pretty strange changes ( almost complete change in wait staff, slow slooooowww service, and most recently a menu that boast ***no substitutions** with far fewer options, and cold sometimes soggy food). sadly these changes have pretty much stopped us from coming. The staff at Caffe Nonna used to be super cool, attentive, and knowledgeable. Now it is completely clear that nobody working there knows what's going on whatsoever. Not to be rude but every waiter we have had since May has been slow, borderline rude, clearly doesn't know the menu, and to put it simply- just plain awkward. The food is no longer as good as it used to be and comes out either all at once or with close to 30 minutes in between. Every time we have come since I'd say May- some sort of my order has been wrong, and tonight it happened again. I casually asked the waitress that brought the food to our table if the kitchen could add the topping that was missing to my pizza. She just ignored Me which was odd.. literally no response.
